title: 레너드 마이어스: 가정에서 합리적인 사람이 되십시오 (골로새 3:18-20)

ko.text: 남편들이 기억해야 할 이런 말이 나옵니다.
흔히 더 균형 잡힌 결정을 내릴 수 있습니다.”
이 자리에 계신 남편 분들은 이 말에 공감하실 겁니다.
이와 같이 행동하는 데는 여러 가지 성품이 관련되는데요,
우리는 그 본에서 무엇을 배울 수 있습니까?
먼저 첫 번째 질문을 생각해 보죠.
그는 다른 사람의 한계와 상황을 고려해 줍니다.
합리성이라는 특성에 대해 어떻게 알려 주는지
이처럼 다른 사람들이 알 수 있게 해야 합니다.
그러니까 우리가 자신을 합리적이라고 생각하는 것이
우리가 합리적이라는 평판을 얻고 있는지가 중요합니다.
“이런 것들 중 하나와 관련하여 죄과가 있게 되었다면,
그는 자기가 어떻게 죄를 지었는지 고백해야 한다.”
곧 가축 떼에서 어린 암양이든 어린 암염소든
암컷 한 마리를 속죄 제물로 가져와야 한다.”
그런데 7절에서 여호와의 합리성을 볼 수 있습니다.
“하지만 그가 양을 바칠 만한 형편이 안 되면,
죄에 대한 죄과 제물로 산비둘기 두 마리나
그런데 11절을 보면 그분은 한 걸음 더 나아가십니다.
어린 집비둘기 두 마리를 바칠 만한 형편이 안 되면,
고운 가루 10분의 1에바를 속죄 제물로 가져와야 한다.”
이처럼 여호와께서는 이스라엘 백성 개인의 경제 상황에 따라
각주를 보면 그 점을 알 수 있죠.
속죄 제물로 고운 가루 2.2리터를, 아마도 제사장에게
새 두 마리를 바치지 못해도 걱정하지 마라.
여호와께선 이 가난한 이스라엘 여자가 가져온 재물을
다른 부유한 사람이 가져온 재물만큼 소중히 여기셨습니다.
이 가난한 여자가 얼마나 행복해했을지 상상해 보십시오!
귀한 손님을 대접할 때 쓰는 가루여야 했죠.
따라서 여호와께 다른 사람만큼 드릴 수는 없어도
자신의 가장 좋은 것을 드려야 했습니다.
나를 위해 최선을 다할 거라는 것을 나는 알고 있다.’
여호와께서는 우리의 한계와 상황을 이해해 주심으로
일부 형제 자매들은 양이나 염소를 바치는 것처럼
비둘기 두 마리 정도의 봉사를 드릴 수 있는 사람도 있고요.
어쩌면 어떤 분들은 과거에 그런 봉사를 드렸을 것입니다.
마치 고운 가루 2.2리터와 같은 봉사라도 말이죠.
형제 자매들에게 지나친 기대를 해서는 안 됩니다.
그 예를 누가복음 22장에서 볼 수 있습니다.
예수께선 베드로가 곧 그분을 세 번 부인할 것을 알고 계셨죠.
당신이 돌아오거든, 당신의 형제들을 강하게 하십시오.”
베드로의 믿음이 없어지지 않도록 기도하신 겁니다.
형제들을 강하게 해 줄 것임을 확신하셨습니다.
베드로가 세 번 부인할 것을 아셨는데도 그렇게 하신 거죠.
이 내용이 어떻게 예수의 합리성을 보여 줍니까?
베드로가 처해 있었던 상황을 고려해 주신 것입니다.
그가 앞으로 할 일에 대해 확신을 나타내셨습니다.
스플레인 형제가 토요일에 그 점을 강조하셨죠?
우리는 그들에 대한 확신을 나타내야 합니다.
다른 사람들에 대해 합리적인 기대를 하십시오.
어쩌면 그들은 우리가 잘 모르거나 온전히 이해하지 못하는
어떤 어려움을 겪고 있을 수 있습니다.
“형제들이 하지 않은 일에 대해 판단하는 것보다
그들이 한 일을 칭찬해 주는 것이 훨씬 낫습니다!”
합리적인 사람은 참을성 있고 친절하고 부드럽게
또한 다른 사람의 한계와 상황을 이해해 줍니다.
여호와와 예수께서는 정말 좋은 분을 보이셨습니다.
또 우리는 사람들의 좋은 점을 보고
우리 모두 매일의 생활에서 우리가 합리적이라는 것을
모두가 알 수 있도록 최선을 다해야겠습니다.

en.text: Our text comments today
highlight this point about a husband.
Notice it says:
“Although he cannot always do
“as she [that is, his wife] asks,
“he often arrives at a more balanced decision
by consulting her.”
Well, those of us who are husbands
know the truthfulness of those words, don’t we?
Now, there are a number of qualities
that this statement may bring to mind.
And one of those qualities
is the quality of reasonableness.
That’s a quality that all of us need to display.
How would you describe a reasonable person?
What examples of reasonableness
do we find in Jehovah and Jesus?
And what can we learn from their example?
Well, let’s first consider that description.
Our publications have stated
that a reasonable person is patient, gentle,
and kind in his dealings with himself and with others.
He takes into consideration
others’ limitations and their circumstances.
Someone with a reputation of being reasonable
is flexible when circumstances warrant it.
It’s like that husband that we just mentioned.
When he is reasonable as he consults with his wife,
he’s willing to listen to her and, when appropriate,
to go along with her wishes.
Now notice with me at Philippians 4:5
the inspired counsel about this quality of reasonableness.
Please turn there in Philippians chapter 4,
and notice what the Bible tells us in the A portion of verse 5.
It states:
“Let your reasonableness become known to all men.”
So others should see us displaying this quality.
Another translation renders the verse:
“Have a reputation for being reasonable.”
So notice, it’s not so much how we view ourselves,
whether we feel we’re reasonable,
rather, it’s how others see us —how we are known,
if we have the reputation of being reasonable.
When you think about it,
reasonableness attracts, doesn’t it,
whereas unreasonableness tends to drive away?
Well, now that we have that description,
what examples of reasonableness do we find in Jehovah and Jesus?
Let’s consider Jehovah’s example first.
And if you turn with me to Leviticus chapter 5,
let’s look at an example of his reasonableness
with the nation of Israel.
Leviticus chapter 5,
and notice there in verse 5 to begin.
It says: “If he becomes guilty as respects one of these things
“[talking about someone who’s committed a sin, it says],
then he must confess in what he has sinned.”
Verse 6: “He will also bring his guilt offering
“to Jehovah for the sin that he committed,
“namely, a female from the flock,
either a female lamb or a young female goat, for a sin offering.”
So that was plain.
But notice Jehovah’s reasonableness in verse 7:
“If, though, he cannot afford a sheep,
“he must bring to Jehovah two turtledoves
or two young pigeons as his guilt offering for the sin.”
So that was reasonable on Jehovah’s part.
But Jehovah took it a step further.
Notice verse 11:
“Now if he cannot afford two turtledoves or two young pigeons,
“he must bring as his offering for his sin
a tenth of an ephah of fine flour for a sin offering.”
So notice, Jehovah was reasonable in what he expected,
depending on the Israelites’ financial circumstances.
As we read verse 11, you may have wondered, ‘Well, what’s a tenth of an ephah?’
Well, our footnote helps us.
You notice what it says?
“A tenth of an ephah equaled 2.2 L
(2 dry qt).”
Notice this image of an Israelite woman.
She’s of very limited means, and she’s holding out
—possibly to give to the priest— her sin offering of two quarts of flour.
It wasn’t much, was it?
Here in Leviticus, it was as if Jehovah was saying:
‘If you don’t have enough for a lamb or a goat, that’s OK.
‘If you don’t have enough for those two small birds, don’t worry.
Just bring me two quarts of flour as your sacrifice.’
Well, imagine how happy a poor Israelite like this woman would have been
that Jehovah valued her small offering
just as much as one of the costlier sacrifices
presented by her wealthier neighbors!
But did you notice an important detail there in verse 11 about the flour?
The flour that the needy Israelite
was to offer wasn’t just any type of flour.
Did you see there in the verse?
It was to be fine flour,
such as that used to prepare a meal for an honored guest.
So though the poor Israelite couldn’t give as much as others,
the little they offered to Jehovah was to be their best.
In effect, Jehovah was saying, ‘I realize you can’t offer as much as others,
but I know, I know, that you’re going to give me your best.’
What’s the lesson?
Jehovah displays reasonableness
by taking into consideration our limitations and our circumstances.
You know, some brothers and sisters can offer
in their service the equivalent of a lamb or a goat.
Others can offer the equivalent of two turtledoves or two pigeons.
And perhaps in the past, some of us
were able to offer the same in our assignments.
But right now, because of our circumstances,
because of limitations, maybe we’re not able to.
Well, what do we know about Jehovah?
He graciously and reasonably accepts our best
in his service even if that’s comparable
to two quarts of fine flour.
What a reasonable God we worship
and a good lesson for us to be reasonable
and not compare ourselves with others
or to expect more than we should of our brothers and sisters!
Now, what about Jesus’ example?
He set an example in reasonableness
by being patient and kind in his dealings
with his disciples despite their shortcomings.
Let’s notice an example.
Turn with me to Luke chapter 22,
and let’s notice an example of Jesus’ reasonableness.
Luke chapter 22
—the setting is shortly before Jesus’ death,
and he’s aware that Peter is soon going to deny him three times.
So, what did Jesus do?
He encouraged Peter.
Notice verse 32.
Jesus said: “But I have made supplication
“for you that your faith may not give out;
and you, once you have returned, strengthen your brothers.”
Notice the encouragement?
Jesus said: “I have made supplication for you.”
In other words, Jesus prayed in Peter’s behalf
that Peter’s faith not give out.
And then he told him:
“Once you have returned, strengthen your brothers.”
Jesus expressed confidence that Peter,
after a short lapse, would return to faithful service
and he would strengthen his brothers
—and that despite the fact, you notice in verse 34,
Jesus told him, ‘You’re going to deny me three times.’
Now, how does this account show reasonableness on Jesus’ part?
Well, you may remember what Jesus had said sometime earlier,
as recorded at Matthew 10:33.
He said: “Whoever disowns me before men,
I will also disown him.”
Now, that was a strong statement,
and Jesus could have applied that to Peter.
But demonstrating reasonableness, Jesus didn’t reject Peter.
Why?
Because Jesus knew that there were going to be
extenuating circumstances.
He was willing to forgive his repentant apostle
and express confidence in what Peter would do in the future.
So the lesson?
We should look for the good in our brothers.
Brother Splane highlighted that on Saturday for us, didn’t he?
Despite their imperfections,
we should express confidence and faith in our brothers.
We should be reasonable in what we expect of others.
Who knows?
They may be facing challenges that we either don’t know about
or that we don’t fully understand.
One Watchtower stated this:
“How much better it is to commend our brothers
for what they do than to judge them for what they do not do!”
Like Jesus, let’s be reasonable when love calls for it
and circumstances warrant it.
Well, what have we considered?
A reasonable person is patient, kind, and gentle
in his dealings with himself and with others.
He takes into consideration the limitations
and the circumstances of others.
Reasonableness attracts,
unreasonableness tends to drive away.
What excellent examples we have in reasonableness with Jehovah and Jesus!
Remember the fine flour and the need to look for the good in others,
expressing confidence in them.
So as we go about our day,
may we look for opportunities
to let our reasonableness become known to all men.

cn.text: 关于做丈夫的
今天引述的《守望台》文章这样说
“虽然丈夫不可能每次都按妻子的意见去做
但丈夫和妻子商量后
就能作出比较合理的决定。”
我们做丈夫的都非常同意这句话，是吗？
这让我们想到做丈夫的应该有的几个特质
其中一个特质就是通情达理
这是我们所有人都要培养的特质
那么，通情达理是什么意思呢？
耶和华和耶稣怎样表现这个特质呢？
我们可以怎样效法他们呢？
首先，什么是通情达理？
我们的出版物提到一个通情达理的人
对人对己都会有耐心，表现温和和仁慈
他知道别人能力有限
也会考虑其他人的情况
有这种特质的人
能按照不同的环境做出适当的调整
就像我们刚才提到，一个做丈夫的
如果他表现通情达理的态度
他就会跟妻子商量，如果可以
他就会听妻子的意见
我们来看腓立比书4:5
提到通情达理这个特质
请翻开腓立比书第4章
让我们一起来看看第5节的前半部分
这里说
“要让所有人都知道你们通情达理。”
所以经文说
要让所有人知道我们有这个特质
有些英文译本也说，要有通情达理的名声
请注意
这里不是说我们自己觉得自己通情达理就好
这里强调的是别人的看法
别人是不是也觉得
我们是个通情达理的人呢？
你是不是也觉得，通情达理的人很容易亲近
不通情达理的人，大家都会躲得远远的
现在我们已经知道什么是通情达理了
那么耶和华和耶稣怎样表现通情达理呢？
我们先来看看耶和华怎么做
现在请你看利未记第5章
来看耶和华怎样对以色列人
表现通情达理的态度
我们从5:5开始看
经文说
“假如有人在以上任何一件事上担负罪责
（这里说的是一个犯罪的人）
他就要承认自己犯了什么罪。”
第6节说
“他要为自己犯的罪
把抵罪祭的母羊献给耶和华
也就是用一只母绵羊羔或母山羊羔
献做赎罪祭。”
这里说的很清楚
但请留意耶和华多么的通情达理
第7节说:“但他如果没有能力献羊
就要为自己犯的罪
用两只斑鸠或两只雏鸽做抵罪祭献给耶和华。”
看上帝对以色列人真的是通情达理
“如果他没有能力献两只斑鸠或两只雏鸽
就要为自己犯的罪
用十分之一伊法的上等面粉献做赎罪祭。”
你们看，耶和华还考虑到以色列人的经济能力
他的确是个通情达理的上帝
11节提到“十分之一伊法”是什么呢？
来看看脚注就可以知道了
脚注说，十分之一伊法相当于2.2升
请看看这个以色列人妇女的图片
她很穷，拥有的不多
她拿着赎罪祭物要给祭司
她献上2.2升的面粉
2.2升的面粉一点也不多，对吗？
在利未记里
耶和华好像在说
“如果你没有能力献上绵羊或山羊，没关系
如果你没有能力献上2只小鸟，也没关系
只要献上2.2升的面粉当赎罪祭就好了！”
你能想象那些很穷的以色列人
听到了会有多高兴吗？
虽然这个妇女献的跟那些有钱的邻居献的相比
显得微不足道
但耶和华还是很重视她的祭物
11节有一个跟面粉有关的重要细节
就是那个面粉可不是随便的面粉都可以
你看到经文怎么说吗？
一定要是“上等的”面粉才行
就是招待尊贵的客人时使用的上等面粉
虽然贫穷的以色列人
不能像别人一样献上那么多
但他们献给耶和华的一定要是他们最好的东西
耶和华好像在说
“虽然你没有办法献的跟别人一样多
但我知道，你一定会把最好的给我。”
我们学到什么？
耶和华愿意做出改变
他会考虑每个人不同的能力和情况
有些弟兄姐妹做的服务
好像是献上一只绵羊或山羊
但另一些弟兄姐妹
就好像献上两只斑鸠或两只鸽子
也许我们以前在岗位上
可以为耶和华做很多事
但现在环境和情况有所改变
我们就没办法做那么多了
那耶和华怎么看我们呢？
他仁慈体贴又通情达理
只要我们献上最好的
就算只献上2.2升的面粉，他也很愿意接受
我们崇拜的上帝是多么的通情达理
我们学到:我们不要拿自己跟别人比较
也不要对弟兄姐妹要求太高
那耶稣呢？
虽然门徒一再让耶稣失望
但耶稣还是很有耐心、很仁慈地对待他们
耶稣多么通情达理啊！
我们一起来看一个例子
路加福音22章
我们来看看耶稣怎样表现通情达理
这段经文的背景是
在耶稣去世前
耶稣知道很快彼得会3次不认他
那么耶稣怎么做呢？
他鼓励彼得
请看32节
耶稣说
“可是我已经为你恳切祈求，免得你信心尽失
你回头以后
要帮助你的弟兄坚强起来。”
耶稣怎样鼓励彼得呢？
耶稣说
“我已经为你恳切祈求。”
也就是求耶和华不要让彼得失去信心
耶稣还说
“你回头以后
要帮助你的弟兄坚强起来。”
耶稣对彼得有信心
他知道虽然彼得一时软弱
但后来一定会继续为他服务
也会鼓励其他弟兄
虽然耶稣知道这些事
但34节耶稣还是对彼得说
“你会三次说你不认识我。”
你们可能还记得在马太福音10:33
耶稣在更早之前曾说过
他说，“谁在别人面前不认我，我也会不认他。”
这个措辞非常强烈
耶稣也可以用在彼得身上
但因为耶稣十分通情达理
所以他没有否定彼得
为什么呢？
因为他知道到时彼得的处境一定会很困难
耶稣很愿意原谅悔改的彼得
也相信他以后会忠心地崇拜上帝
我们学到什么呢？
我们应该看弟兄们的优点
就像斯普莱恩弟兄前几天的演讲提到的一样
虽然弟兄姐妹都不完美都有缺点
但我们还是应该对他们有信心
不要对他们有过高的期望
也许，他们遇到的困难是我们无法了解
也无法完全体会的
有一篇《守望台》文章说
“称赞弟兄做得到的事
比批评他们做不到的事，还要好！”
所以要通情达理
要知道每个人的情况都不一样
要表达对他们的爱
那我们学到了什么呢？
一个通情达理的人
会有耐心也会待人温和仁慈
对别人对自己都是这样
他知道别人能力有限
也会考虑其他人的情况。
通情达理的人很容易亲近
不通情达理的人，大家都躲得远远的
耶和华和耶稣就是通情达理的好榜样！
要记得上等面粉的故事
还有要看别人的优点，要对他们有信心
希望从今天开始
我们要让所有人都知道
我们是通情达理的人

we’ve made dramatic adjustments
to our activities all over the world,
including how we meet, how we preach,
and even how we associate with one another.

with the changing conditions.

and we want to commend you for your obedience to theocratic direction.
We love you all very much and want to keep you safe
while helping you to maintain a good spiritual routine.
As we think about what happens next,
it’s important to remember that we’re not all experiencing
this global crisis the same way.
In some parts of the world,
the coronavirus is just beginning to spread more quickly.
In other places, outbreaks appear to be somewhat contained for now,
and governments are already easing restrictions.
So how will this affect our theocratic activities?
Well, as things open up in various regions,
we’re going to be guided by the principle
in Proverbs 14:16,
Proverbs 14:16,
where it says:
“The wise one is cautious and turns away from evil,
but the stupid one is reckless and overconfident.”
In this pandemic, recklessness and overconfidence
have literally cost people their lives.
But as the proverb says:
“The wise one is cautious.”
So we’ll continue to take a cautious approach.
In general, we’ll allow more time
after the government loosens a particular restriction
before we resume a theocratic activity.
This will allow the organization to monitor the impact
that any lifting of restrictions has
on the spread of the virus.
The Coordinators’ Committee of the Governing Body
recently shared some valuable principles
with Branch Committees around the world
to help guide them as governments ease restrictions
related to the spread of COVID-19.
We’d like to share three of those points with you now.
We are confident that obediently holding to these principles
will not only save lives
but glorify Jehovah.
First, out of respect for our Creator,
we place a high value on life.
Some governments may choose
to lift restrictions and reopen businesses,
in part for economic reasons.
But simply put,
our decisions are motivated by love,
not money.
So we’ll continue to make the safety of our brothers a priority
over personal convenience or preference.
Ecclesiastes 7:12 says this,
Ecclesiastes 7:12:
“Wisdom is a protection
“just as money is a protection,
“but the advantage of knowledge is this:
Wisdom preserves the life of its owner.”
So, in harmony with that,
our aim has been and will continue to be
to make wise, balanced decisions that protect lives.
As an example, back in March we made the decision
to hold the Gilead graduation with no invited guests present.
That was a big change.
But that one decision protected so many lives here at Bethel in New York
and among those who would have been guests.
Little did we know that just a short time later,
New York would become an epicenter of the pandemic.
We thank Jehovah for helping us
to make that wise decision!
What’s the lesson?
Because we place a high value on life,
we need to follow direction
even if it seems overly cautious
or means significant changes in our theocratic activities.
That obedience will help to keep all of us as safe as possible.
In the following video, note how this has proved to be the case
for the brothers in South America,
where the outbreak of COVID-19 cases
has surged in recent weeks.
We’ll hear from Brother Anthony Carvalho,
who serves on the Brazil Branch Committee,
and from Brother Jaime Tamayo,
who serves on the Ecuador Branch Committee.
Their reports show the benefits of obedience
even if at first we don’t understand the reasons for the direction.
The outbreak of COVID-19
has already taken tens of thousands of lives in Brazil,
and so we’ve come to appreciate
how the early direction
we received from the organization
was a real protection.
One example is a sister who is a medical doctor.
She said that when the branch office
gave direction to suspend meetings at the Kingdom Hall,
she honestly did not agree.
There weren’t any confirmed cases of COVID-19 in the region,
and the local government had not ordered any restrictions.
So she felt the brothers might be exaggerating the threat a bit.
But then she reasoned on how Jehovah had sometimes given his people direction
that didn’t make sense from a human standpoint,
and so she decided to obey.
Well, shortly after congregation meetings were suspended,
the government put restrictions in place.
COVID-19 began to spread rapidly in the region,
and sadly many have died.
Our sister said that she now sees
that the direction from the organization was a real protection.
She related,
“Seeing how Jehovah is caring for us in a loving and tender way,
“even on an individual level,
has increased my confidence in him.”
Well, this is just one example of many here in Brazil,
where we have truly seen the benefits
of obediently following theocratic direction.
There is no question that the early direction
we received in Ecuador saved lives.
For instance, one publisher, Fabricio,
started to have some flulike symptoms,
but his doctor told him
that it was the common flu
and not COVID-19.
Still, Fabricio followed the instructions from the organization
to stay home if you have any symptoms of illness.
Later he said, “All in our family agreed
“that it was important to follow these instructions
since they were given to protect us.”
During the following weeks,
he and his family didn’t allow anyone into the house.
Even when relatives came to visit them,
they received them outside the house to maintain a safe distance.
Around the same time, meetings at the Kingdom Hall were suspended.
Well, several weeks later,
Fabricio tested positive for COVID-19
and so did three family members.
Fabricio’s family are so glad that they followed the instructions
received from the organization.
They maintained distancing protocols
even without a positive diagnosis of COVID-19.
This protected the lives of others,
including their extended family and the congregation.
This really helped us appreciate
the wisdom of suspending congregation meetings when we did.
Doing so prevented the spread of the disease to others.
What a powerful example of how our obedience to direction
is a protection and a blessing!
Our second principle is based on Romans 13:1, 2:
We must listen
to the governmental “superior authorities,”
who are permitted by Jehovah
to care for certain functions.
The importance of listening to these authorities
is emphasized in verse 2, where it says:
“Whoever opposes the authority
“(or, according to the footnote, whoever ‘resists’ the authority)
has taken a stand against the arrangement of God.”
We know that these authorities exist by God’s permission,
and it’s his will that Christians be subject to them,
as long as what they require doesn’t conflict with his law.
News reports are filled with stories
of people ignoring the direction from the authorities
or even protesting against it.
But rebelling against secular authorities
constitutes a rebellion against God.
We love Jehovah,
so we respect the authorities.
We also listen to the authorities because we love our neighbors,
and we’re concerned with how they feel about health and safety.
We know that many people
out of concern for possible infection
are anxious about interacting with others.
Following safety guidelines from the authorities
and adjusting our activities
shows that we really care about our neighbors.
And this can even contribute to a good witness being given.
Here’s an example of that:
In one European country,
local officials visited our branch office
to check on what we were doing to slow the spread of the virus.
When the officials learned that we were holding
all our meetings by videoconference
and had already been in lockdown for over two weeks,
they were amazed!
One of them asked,
“Did you know beforehand that all of this would happen?”
The brothers explained that we’re a global organization
that puts a high value on human life,
so we were following developments on an international level.
That enabled the brothers to take the steps needed
to keep everyone as safe as possible,
even ahead of guidelines from the national and local governments.
The officials were impressed.
Doesn’t that beautifully illustrate
how our obedience reflects favorably
on our organization and our God?
It brings to mind the thought at 1 Peter 2:12.
When people become ‘eyewitnesses of our fine conduct,’
it brings glory to Jehovah.
The third principle we want to share is this:
Do not develop a casual attitude.
As this situation stretches on month after month,
it can be hard to stay vigilant.
We might be inclined to relax,
lower our guard,
especially as certain restrictions are removed.
However, Proverbs 22:3 reminds us:
“The shrewd one sees the danger
“and conceals himself,
“but the inexperienced keep right on going
and suffer the consequences.”
So we need to remain cautious and be ready for additional outbreaks.
Many experts say we may be dealing
with the spread of this virus for some time
until the successful treatments and vaccinations
become widely available,
possibly in 2021 or beyond.
This means that the adjusted arrangements
we have in place for congregation meetings,
assemblies, and the field ministry
may need to continue for some time.
When we do begin returning to our normal arrangements,
it will be a gradual process,
in accord with what we read
in Proverbs 14:15:
“The naive person believes every word,
but the shrewd one ponders each step.”
You can be assured
that we will prayerfully ponder each step
and adjust our meeting and service arrangements gradually.
And, of course, we’ll monitor the situation closely
and reinstate certain restrictions if additional outbreaks occur.
So as you face the days ahead,
keep in mind the three principles we’ve talked about:
(1) Place a high value on life,
(2) listen to the authorities,
and (3) guard against developing a casual attitude.
We know that this pandemic has hit some of you very hard.
You’ve lost jobs and income.
You young ones have had your schooling interrupted,
and you haven’t been able to be with your friends.
And tragically, a number of you
have lost family members and friends in death.
Some of you may feel like Job,
who faced one tragedy after another.
It pains our hearts to see what you’re going through,
and we’re praying for you every day.
It’s been a difficult time.
Yet, in many ways,
all of this has been training for the great tribulation ahead.
What we’re learning now about how to adapt our spiritual routines,
to support one another, and to be obedient to direction
is building us up and equipping us
for even bigger challenges in the future.
It’s been very encouraging to hear how our brothers around the world
are helping one another during this unique time
in human history.
Your actions are bringing honor
and praise to Jehovah.
Our brothers and sisters from Brazil and Ecuador
send you their warm greetings.
And on behalf of the Governing Body,
we thank you for all you’re doing,
even under these difficult circumstances.
Please know that we love you very much.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting®.

ko.text: 그리고 외딴곳에 대해 들려 주실 겁니다.
각 이야기는 충절의 다양한 부면을 보여 줄 겁니다.
두 분은 앙골라 지부에서 봉사하고 계시죠.
그럼 도밍구스 형제는 어떤 일을 하시나요?
많은 사람이 진리 안에 들어오고 있어요.
낙원 같은 곳이라고 할 수 있습니다.
네, 현재 앙골라에 있는 전도인 수는
일곱 살, 여덟 살, 아홉 살,
백성을 돌보시는 걸 볼 수 있었어요.
왕국 전파자 학교를 위한 시설이 더 필요하고,
앙골라 사람들이 성경 진리에 대해 보이는 사랑입니다.
그 결과 어떤 왕국회관들은 무려 14개 회중이 함께 사용합니다.
이러한 상황 때문에 전도인들과 장로의 회가
얼마나 많은 조정을 해야 할지 상상해 보십시오.
모든 주말 집회를 빠짐없이 열기 위해
어떤 곳에서는 아침 6시 반을 시작으로 하루 종일 집회를 연달아 엽니다.
평일 집회의 경우 어떤 회중들은 오후 일찍 시작해야만 합니다.
이러한 집회 시간에 맞추어 참석하려면 우리 형제들이 직장을 잃을 수도 있습니다.
집회 날에 한두 시간 일찍 퇴근할 수 있도록 고용주와 대화를 나눠 봅니다.
그 후에 늦게 시작한 집회는 밤늦게까지 계속됩니다.
장로들은 모두가 최대한 유익을 얻도록 협력하죠.
왕국회관에서 가장 멀리 떨어져 있는 회중에게
편리한 집회 시간을 선택할 우선권을 줍니다.
그렇게 하면 먼 길을 오가는 형제 자매들이 느끼는 부담을 많이 줄여 줄 수 있죠.
왕국회관이 꽉 차면 밖에서도 앉아야 합니다.
자기 자신보다 다른 사람의 필요를 먼저 생각함으로 사랑을 나타냅니다.
유지 보수와 청소를 할 시간을 어떻게 계획합니까?
모든 회중은 왕국회관 운영 위원회의 지시에 긴밀히 협조하여
건물을 항상 깨끗하고 안전하고 쾌적한 상태로 유지하기 위해 노력합니다.
여호와께서 질서와 평화의 하느님이심을 증거하고 있습니다.
융통성 있게 왕국회관을 사용하는 걸 보니까,
전파 활동에 대한 앙골라 형제 자매들의
열심 있는 태도도 아주 인상 깊었습니다.
또 거의 전파되지 않은 구역에 있는
정 형제는 한국 지부에서 봉사하고 계시죠.
기쁘게도 저도 그 일에 참여할 기회가 있었습니다.
다른 두 명의 형제와 함께 작업을 했죠.
젊은 형제들과 양심적 병역 거부가 생각나는데요.
군인이 건네주는 군복을 받지 않겠다고 거절하고 있네요.
그리고 이 사진에서 볼 수 있는 것처럼,
법정 같은 곳을 거친 게 아니군요.
이 사진을 특별 파이오니아가 보냈다고 하셨는데,
이 사진 속의 형제를 기소할 때
호별 방문에서 그 남자를 만난 겁니다.
그 남자는 사진 속 형제의 이름까지도 기억하면서
이 사진을 전해 주라고 했다고 합니다.
이 사진은 우리가 찍은 게 아니죠.
헌병 수사관이 찍어서 보관하고 있던 게
여호와께서 칭찬해 주시는 거란 생각이 들었죠.
충절을 지키기 위해 최선을 다하는 형제들을 보시고
그 형제는 현재 장로로 섬기고 있고,
형제는 이 사진을 보게 될 줄은
사실 형제도 그 수사관을 기억하고 있었어요.
그리고 발표된 책도 한 권 받았는데,
그 사진을 보고 다들 반응이 어땠나요?
항상 유쾌하고 미소 짓는 아버지만 보다가,
자기가 아버지를 많이 닮았다는 걸 알게 됐죠.
자기가 사진 속에 있는 것 같았답니다.
사진 속에 있는 것 같다고 했는데
그 말은 여러 면으로 정말 맞는 말입니다.
사실 정 형제도 사진 속에 있고
저도 있고 우리 모두가 있다고 할 수 있죠.
학교에서 기 경례를 하지 않을 때나,
거짓 종교 축일에 함께 참여하지 않을 때나,
직장에서 그런 일들에 참여하지 않을 때
낯선 동양인 얼굴을 한 우리 가족은
우리가 길을 걸어 가거나 가게에 가면,
좋지 않은 대우를 받은 적도 있었어요.
그래서 나 자신, 내 자리를 찾기가 힘들어요.
심지어 많은 사람과 함께 있을 때도,
여호와의 증인의 그런 큰 행사에 참석해서
세계 전역에서 온 형제 자매들을 보는 게
아무도 외모나 그 밖의 차이로 판단하지 않았죠.
많은 형제 자매들과 가까워진 것이 큰 도움이 되었죠.
그 형제들과 나중에 많은 형제들이 보여 준 본은
아, 도밍구스 형제처럼 전파 활동 데스크요.
그런데 차로는 갈 수 없는 곳들도 있습니다.
그래서 회중은 특별 전파 활동을 조직해서
어떨 때는 강에서 몸을 씻으며 봉사하죠.
두세 집씩 있는 외딴 구역에 가기 위해
여기서는 형제들이 여러 시간 차를 타고 가야만
주민이 몇 사람 밖엔 살지 않죠.
전파하기 위해 노력하는 걸 보니 놀랍네요.
칠레 구역 중에 가장 먼 곳인가요?
칠레에는 이 지역보다 더 외진 구역도 있죠.
남아메리카 서쪽 해안에서 약 3200킬로미터 떨어진 드넓은 바다에
주민이 8천명도 채 안 되는 이 외딴 섬에서도
하느님의 왕국의 좋은 소식이 전파되고 있습니다.
외떨어져 있는 것처럼 보이는 이 구역에서도
전도인들은 여호와의 조직이 적극적으로 지원하고 있다고 느낍니다.
영적 양식을 폴리네시아 토착어인 라파누이어로 번역하고 있습니다.
전 세계 다른 형제 자매들과 동일한 영적 양식을 받게 됩니다.
이 번역 팀은 영적 유익도 얻고 있죠.
칠레 지부의 영적 프로그램을 함께 즐기고 있습니다.
여호와께서 저를 사랑하시고 제게 힘 주신다는 걸 느껴요.
여호와께선 섬에 있는 우리 모두를 돌봐 주시죠.
또한 칠레 지부는 로빈슨크루소섬에 있는 왕국 전도인들도 지원합니다.
이 섬은 칠레 본토에서 600킬로미터 남짓 떨어져 있어
비행기를 타고 외딴 공항까지 간 다음
그 섬의 주거 지역까지 가려면 또 배를 타고 들어가야 합니다.
파도가 너무 심하지 않을 때에만 갈 수 있죠.
이러한 어려움들이 있지만 우리의 형제 자매들은
시기적절한 영적 양식과 LDC 지원, 양 치는 방문 등을 계속 받고 있습니다.
여러 해 동안, 로빈슨크루소섬에는 5명의 자매들밖에 없었습니다.
덕분에 2명의 독신 장로들이 섬으로 이주할 수 있었고,
이제 전파 활동과 양 치는 일을 돕고 있습니다.
이곳까지 온다는 게 정말 만만치 않지만
전도인이 8명인 이 회중도 1년에 2차례 순회 감독자의 방문을 받습니다.
그 동안 이 충실한 형제 자매들에게 영적 지원이 충분히 베풀어지죠.
도시에 살든, 시골에 살든, 또는 심지어 이런 바다 한가운데 있어도
전파하는 사람들과 좋은 소식에 반응을 보이는 사람들은
영적으로 부족함 없이 돌봄을 받고 있습니다.
그 결과 이들은 전 세계 형제 자매들과 연합하여
우리의 위대한 하느님 여호와를 찬양하고 있습니다.
지부에서 정말 많은 노력을 기울이고 있네요.
지부가 이 특별한 섬을 돌보기 위해
칠레에서 순회 감독자가 방문하는 또 다른 곳이 있는데요,
방금 보신 곳들이 가장 외딴곳은 아니에요.
우리가 몇 년 전에 방문한 곳이 있는데요,
그래서 지부는 한 부부가 그곳에 갈 수 있도록
혼자가 아니라는 걸 알게 해 주셔서 고맙습니다.
우리는 거대한 영적 성전 안에 있는 거죠.
그분께 꺾을 수 없는 정성을 바치는 것,
그 결과 언제나 그분이 기뻐하시는 일을 하는 것”이죠.
시험에 직면했을 때 충성을 유지하는 모습을 보았습니다.
계속 여호와께 꺾을 수 없는 정성을
“새벽의 날개로 멀리 날아가 가장 먼 바다에 거할지라도,
여호와께서는 우리의 충절의 행동을 보고 계시고
박수 소리가 여기 한 500명은 있는 것 같네요.
또 한 번 믿음을 강화시켜 주는 프로그램이었습니다.
이 땅 이곳저곳에서 벌어지는 일과 경험을 보면 참 놀랍습니다.

en.text: But now, we’re moving to a part of our program
we’ve truly grown to love.
It’s entitled The Inside Story,
and Brother Trent Lippold will be our host.
So let’s give Brother Lippold our attention as he presents this:
The Inside Story.
Welcome to another edition of The Inside Story.
Today, we’re going to meet four guests from three continents,
representing the 148th class of Gilead.
We’re going to hear stories of isolation,
a remarkable gift, and obedience.
In each case, we will see different faces of integrity.
Curious?
Well, let’s meet our first guests then,
Salvador and Isabel Domingos from Angola.
Welcome, Isabel.
Thank you.
Please, Salvador, welcome.
Thank you.
Yes, again, welcome.
So you’re both from Angola, serving in the branch.
Sister Isabel, what is your assignment in the branch?
I work in the Translation Department.
I do composition for one of our vernacular languages.
OK, which language is it?
I work with the Chokwe language.
Chokwe?
Yes.
All right. How do you say “Watchtower”  in Chokwe?
Kaposhi wa Kutalila.
But, you know, Brother Lippold,
we don’t need to learn the language to do composition
because it’s a technical process.
Well, thank you for learning to say “The Watchtower”  anyway.
Good.
And Brother Salvador, what is your assignment?
I work in the Service Department with the Preaching Needs Desk,
and I also give support to the branch office.
OK, the Preaching Needs Desk in Angola —what’s the preaching like in Angola?
Well, the preaching work in Angola is wonderful.
We have been seeing the fulfillment of Haggai 2:7.
Jehovah is “shaking the nation.”
Many people are coming into the truth.
And since people respond well to the good news,
we usually say that Angola is a paradise
for all publishers but especially for pioneers.
OK, so He’s “shaking” Angola.
Yes.
So how many are coming in in Angola?
Well, right now we have
more than 165,000 publishers
and more than 720,000 Bible studies.
Seven hundred and twenty thousand Bible studies?
Yes, more than that.
More than?
That is absolutely amazing!
Yes.
Isabel, with the kind of growth that you have in Angola,
what touches your heart about this?
What touches me most is seeing young ones come into the truth
—young ones who are at seven, eight, nine, ten years old.
They start studying the Bible.
They start going to the meetings,
and many of them without their parents,
and they make progress in the truth.
They start preaching with the congregation.
They get baptized.
And some of them, they start working as auxiliary pioneers.
So this is something amazing to see.
This really touches my heart.
That’s beautiful, yeah.
And Salvador, for you, when you look at the growth,
how does it affect you?
What touches you?
Seeing how Jehovah has been blessing
the work in our branch territory, it’s something amazing.
For example, I remember when I was invited
for the first time to attend a meeting.
That meeting was held in a brother’s home,
and we used a bedroom
as a place to hold the meeting because we were under ban.
But sometime later, since more people were coming,
we needed to move from that bedroom in the same house
to the dining room.
And some months later,
with more people coming
(there was a little bit more freedom),
we needed to move from that dining room to the courtyard.
Same house?
The same house.
OK.
And from that time on, many congregations in Angola
started using courtyards of brothers’ homes
to hold meetings.
But now the situation is completely different.
So seeing the transition
from the courtyard of a brother’s home
to a nice Kingdom Hall
built with the help of Jehovah’s organization
is something that touched my heart
—seeing how Jehovah takes care
of his people by means of his organization.
That’s beautiful.
So, what is the situation like with Kingdom Halls in Angola?
Well, right now we have many congregations
that are sharing one Kingdom Hall.
For example, in one Kingdom Hall with one auditorium
there are 10, 11, 13.
Even right now, we received information about a Kingdom Hall
where there are 14 congregations using it.
So we have a huge need for more Kingdom Halls in Angola.
Would you say that’s one of the biggest needs right now in Angola?
Yes, since many people are coming into the truth,
theocratic facilities are a big need in Angola.
We need space in Bethel; we need more Assembly Halls;
we need a facility for SKE,
and especially Kingdom Halls.
OK, yes.
And we have a video that shows
the big need for Kingdom Halls that we have in Angola.
You will enjoy seeing this video.
OK, excellent. Let’s watch it.
On the southwest coast of Africa sits Angola
—home to lush jungle hillsides,
vast desert plains,
and tropical Atlantic beaches.
But even more beautiful is the love that the people of Angola
demonstrate for Bible truths.
The growth rate of Kingdom proclaimers
has vastly outpaced Kingdom Hall construction,
with some Kingdom Halls hosting as many as 14 congregations.
Imagine the coordination challenges this creates for the publishers
and for the bodies of elders.
To accommodate all the weekend meetings that must take place,
some begin at 6:30 in the morning
and they continue to be held all day long.
For midweek meetings, some congregations
must start early in the afternoon.
Supporting these schedules
could potentially jeopardize our brothers’ employment.
Therefore, they prayerfully negotiate with their employers to get off work
one or two hours early on meeting days.
The later meetings that follow can last well into the night.
The elders cooperate
so that everyone can get the best.
They decide that the congregation
that stays far from the Kingdom Hall
has priority to choose the right time for them,
so that they can feel comfortable because of the distance.
Once the Kingdom Hall is full,
the congregation spills outside the building,
forming lines at the windows.
In all cases, our dear brothers and sisters
lovingly put the needs and welfare of others ahead of their own.
With the building in constant use,
when do the congregations schedule time for maintenance and cleaning?
It takes careful coordination
under the direction of the Kingdom Hall Maintenance Committee
to ensure that the building stays
clean, safe,
and very comfortable.
Our brothers and sisters in Angola
are “aglow with the spirit” and cooperate
together in beautiful ways,
providing a witness to all onlookers
that Jehovah is a God of order and peace.
Thank you. I mean, that was very, very interesting.
When I look at the flexibility and the cooperation
of the brothers and sisters in Angola with the Kingdom Hall,
I will appreciate whatever meeting time our congregation is assigned.
It’s just so beautiful to see the spirit
of preaching in Angola.
Many brothers “step over” into unassigned territories,
and others go to seldom-worked territory
to help congregations with fewer publishers.
That is why, for example, Brother Lippold,
last service year
we had 20 new circuits
—last service year.
Twenty.
Yes.
This service year, from September until now, we have already . . .
Should I hold on?
. . . we have already 97 new congregations.
Ninety-seven?
Yes.
That’s almost a hundred new congregations in just a few months.
Yes.
That is a tremendous, tremendous spirit,
just to see the obedience of the brothers and sisters in Angola for preaching.
What a beautiful example for all of us!
Well, thank you both for being here and sharing these experiences with us
and the spirit of the brothers and sisters in Angola.
Thank you.
Thank you so much.
Let’s introduce our next guest.
It’s Brother Ho Chong from Korea.
Welcome, Ho.
Thank you.
Nice to have you on The Inside Story.
Thank you very much.
So Brother Chong, you are serving in the Korea branch.
And what is your assignment?
I work with the Legal Department.
And last year, our branch renovated
the historical museum of our branch,
and I had the privilege to participate in the project
—especially working with the “Integrity” section of the historical museum—
with two other brothers.
And we had very encouraging experiences.
Very nice.
Integrity, Korea
—we think of young brothers and conscientious objection.
Is that what the “Integrity” part of the museum is about?
Yeah.
To renovate the section,
brothers and sisters were invited to donate
meaningful historical artifacts.
So we received a lot of valuable items from them.
One of them was very, very special to us.
What was it?
It was a photograph
that we received from a special pioneer brother.
This is the photo.
Very interesting.
Brother Lippold, what do you think?
What is this picture, and where was it taken?
Well, it obviously looks like at a military —some kind of military place.
It looks like a young brother.
He’s being offered a uniform,
and this is him refusing the military uniform.
Yeah, that’s right. It was in a military camp.
It is not a reenactment; it is a real situation.
Brothers in Korea were forcefully taken to the military camp for enlistment,
sometimes from home and sometimes even from the Kingdom Halls.
And as we can see in this picture,
they were forced to take arms to be a soldier.
So this is not—
He has not been brought from court or anything like that.
Right on the spot he has to take his stand for Jehovah.
Yes, that’s right.
So you said that a special pioneer sent the photograph.
How did he get the photo?
Actually, this photo was taken in 1988
by a military police investigator.
He wanted to use this photo as evidence
to charge this brother.
But he was so touched by his firm standing,
he kept this photo for almost 20 years.
And in 2007,
the special pioneer visited him during the house-to-house ministry.
He gave this photo to him, even recalling the name of the brother,
and he said, “Please give this back to him.”
Wow!
So when you received the photograph (you and the other two brothers),
when you saw it for the first time,
what did you think?
We all just agreed that it is a gift.
It is a special gift from Jehovah.
Without him, it is impossible.
Just the existence of this photo is impossible,
and it has been kept for almost 20 years.
And then through the special pioneer, we have it.
It’s also impossible.
Why did you feel so strongly that it’s impossible?
We didn’t take this picture.
The investigator took it, and he kept it.
And now we have it.
But the timing is also very important
because it’s after the two monumental decisions
in the highest courts,
and then all the imprisoned brothers were released,
and then we now have this photo.
So this was just last year in 2019?
Yes.
So we thought that Jehovah was commending
all the brothers who did their best,
according to their Bible-trained conscience,
to keep their integrity.
And Jehovah was saying:
“I still remember your integrity. Thank you so much.”
We felt that way.
It’s very powerful.
I can feel that also.
Were you able to find the brother?
Yes, we did.
He is now serving as an elder.
He has three children.
He never expected that he would see this picture.
He knew that it was taken.
He knew the photograph was taken?
Yes.
And he remembered the investigator
because he was favorable to him,
and he relayed one encouraging story about him.
The investigator, for his work,
attended the convention in 1988.
Our convention?
Yes, for his work.
And then he received a book.
Do you remember the book,
the Revelation  book?
Yes, and he gave this book to this brother.
In the camp?
Yes.
And he said:
“Maybe here you may be relaxed.
“Maybe in prison it is more severe.
Just enjoy this book.”
That is unbelievable.
Yeah. So he missed the convention but . . .
. . . he got the release.
Yes.
That’s quite a story.
So, what happened when the photo was shown?
What was the response of his children?
They were all surprised at this.
The eldest son was surprised
because his father was always happy and smiling,
but he was so serious in this picture.
So he was able to understand
how determined his father was in order to keep his integrity
And the second son found out
that his father looked very similar.
So the two looked alike, the younger son and the father.
Yeah. So he found himself in this photo.
So all the family members
were able to visualize what it would be like in keeping integrity.
And it was really encouraging to all of them.
Well, I think it’s really true
what the younger son has said about seeing himself in this picture
because in many ways it is him in this picture.
And it’s you in this picture, and it’s me in this picture.
It’s all of us
—when we take our stand for Jehovah and when we’re loyal to him—
whether it’s a young person in school not saluting the flag,
or not participating in a false religious holiday
with worldly relatives,
or at work (again not participating in things)
taking a stand for Jehovah.
So, really, Ho, this is a gift for all of Jehovah’s people
to remind us of what it means
to show our integrity and be loyal to Jehovah.
Thank you very, very much for sharing this with us.
Thank you very much.
Well, let’s meet our next guest.
He’s from Chile, and his name is Allen Kim.
It’s nice to have you on The Inside Story.
Thank you very much for inviting me.
So, Brother Kim, you were born in Chile and raised in Chile?
Actually, I was born in Chile,
but I was raised in Brazil, and then we moved to Chile.
And my parents are Korean.
OK.
Did you speak Spanish when you came back to Chile?
I had to learn Spanish, yes.
When did you come back to Chile?
I was about 14 years old when I moved with my family.
OK, so, what was that like —fourteen years old, you speak Portuguese
and then coming to Chile and having to learn Spanish?
It wasn’t easy at first
because Chile is not a country
that was used to receiving many foreigners.
So just seeing our family,
an Asian-looking family,
caught much attention in Chile.
So when we were walking on the streets
or going to a store,
many people used to look at us, point at us,
and also talk about us.
We had some bad experiences also.
Hmm.
So as a young person, how did that make you feel?
As a teenager, you know that it’s not easy to receive
that kind of treatment in some places.
And also added to that,
you have to be acquainted with their food
—it’s a new place, a new culture.
So you have a problem of identity
because you are in one country,
but you have another culture, you were raised in another culture.
So it wasn’t easy to find myself—my place.
So sometimes even among many people,
you can feel a little bit isolated
and that you don’t belong anywhere.
Hmm, that’s interesting.
Probably a lot of people (a lot of brothers and sisters even)
can relate to what you’re saying, sometimes feeling that way
and not being sure where you fit in for various reasons.
What changed for you?
Yes, a big help was association with brothers and sisters.
I especially remember that our congregation was invited
to attend a special international convention
in Chile in 2003.
And that was a very special moment
because it was my first time
at such a big event of Jehovah’s Witnesses
and seeing brothers from all around the world.
No one was judging you by your looks or having differences.
Just being there and seeing everyone happy and united
—that was a very big moment for me.
And I could understand well that this is really Jehovah’s organization.
This is the place I should be.
OK, we have a picture here of you.
This is at the international convention?
That’s right.
That was the same year that we arrived to Chile,
and it’s my family attending at that location.
OK, very nice. You’ve changed your hair since then.
Yes.
So you found your place now in the congregation
and things really started to progress for you?
Yes, as I started to progress spiritually,
I would meet many brothers and sisters.
That was a big help for me.
For example, I remember one single brother
that was from our congregation, a Korean brother raised in Chile.
He went to MTS,
and he was assigned back to our congregation
with another Chilean brother,
and, well, just seeing their example
and later many other brothers’ examples helped me
to find my place in the organization.
So the congregation, was this a Spanish congregation you were in?
It was a Korean congregation.
OK, so you’re in a Korean congregation,
and you had a Chilean-Korean brother assigned to your congregation
together with a Chilean brother.
Did he speak Korean?
Yeah, he was learning Korean when he arrived.
He had to learn.
So the three of you, then, you found that you made a good partnership.
Yes.
A really positive influence on you —that’s absolutely beautiful.
So you’re working at the branch now in Chile?
Yes, I’m working at the Chile branch in the Service Department.
I help in the Preaching Needs Desk.
OK, a bit like Salvador then, the Preaching Needs Desk
—what’s the preaching like in Chile?
We have many places, remote areas,
especially in the southern part of Chile, where territories are very big.
So brothers have to (sometimes they have to) travel for many hours by car.
There are even places that they can’t reach by car,
so the congregation has to arrange a preaching campaign
that can be days —seven days—
of walking, sleeping in tents,
and sometimes even washing themselves in the river.
And they try to reach those places,
remote places, with two to three houses.
Wow, that sounds exciting!
The first photograph you’ve brought for us, where is this?
This place is called Aysén Region.
And in this place, the brothers have to drive for many hours
just to reach a small town
where a few people live in these remote areas.
Good. In the next photograph, where is this area?
Well, this is a southern part of Chile;
it’s called Araucanía Region.
And many people live there,
especially people that speak Mapudungun.
They also have many remote areas
that the brothers have to walk to reach.
OK, and the next photograph you have, I mean, that’s quite appealing.
Yes, this is one of the most remote areas
in the most southern part of Chile,
and the brothers also arrange to preach in those places.
This is called Torres del Paine.
Very nice.
It’s amazing to see the efforts that the branch is making
to reach these really remote areas in Chile.
Yes, brothers and sisters are working hard
even to reach a few people.
So we can say that they are doing a good work.
Good, yeah.
It’s very, very remote in these places.
So is that—?
This is in the most southern part of Chile.
Is that as far as you go?
Actually, this is not one of the most remote areas.
We have other places that are more isolated than that area.
I brought a video that I want to show you.
Do you want to see it?
Yes, please.
More than 2,000 miles of open ocean separate Easter Island
from the west coast of South America.
Yet, even here on this remote island
with less than 8,000 inhabitants,
the good news of God’s Kingdom is being preached.
And the publishers in this seemingly isolated field
feel the full support of Jehovah’s organization.
This Kingdom Hall and translation office was built in 2016.
Here five brothers and sisters
work to translate spiritual food
into the native Polynesian language of Rapa Nui,
ensuring that local publishers receive the same spiritual food as their brothers
and sisters around the world.
Translation personnel receive benefit from Bethel spiritual programs
despite being two time zones away
from the branch office in Santiago, Chile.
Here in the middle of the ocean,
I feel how Jehovah loves me
and gives me his strength.
Jehovah is taking care of all of us on the island.
The Chile branch also supports
Kingdom publishers on Robinson Crusoe Island.
Although much closer to the mainland,
just over 400 miles away,
it’s more challenging to reach.
The journey involves a flight and then a boat ride
from the isolated airport to the inhabited part
of the island, which can only be traveled
when the seas aren’t too rough.
But despite these challenges, our brothers and sisters
receive constant and timely spiritual food,
LDC support, and shepherding.
For years, Robinson Crusoe Island was home
to just five spiritual sisters.
With the help of the LDC, a small Kingdom Hall
was remodeled and a two-room apartment was added.
This made it possible
for two single elders to move to the island,
where they now assist with preaching and shepherding.
Although traveling here is not for the faint of heart,
this congregation of eight publishers receives a visit
from their circuit overseer twice a year.
The visit lasts for two or three weeks each time,
providing extra spiritual support to these faithful ones.
It doesn’t matter where you live,
if you are in the city,
in the countryside, or even in a place like this
in the middle of the ocean,
Jehovah is with us.
Those who preach and those who respond to the good news
receive abundant spiritual care,
resulting in a unified worldwide brotherhood
that praises our great God, Jehovah.
That’s beautiful, Allen, to see the efforts that the branch is making
to care for brothers and sisters on such remote islands.
And I thought it was interesting as well that,
for example, on Robinson Crusoe Island,
the circuit overseer will stay there for two or three weeks
because it is so isolated.
Most of the time he spends two weeks
just to encourage the brothers that are so isolated,
and sometimes he even spends one additional week
(almost three weeks)
to combine with a circuit assembly.
OK, very nice, very nice.
So it’s a nice arrangement that the branch has
to care for this particular island.
Yes.
And there’s another island
that circuit overseers from Chile are visiting,
and that’s the Falkland Islands.
In this area, we have an arrangement
to send a circuit overseer
to encourage the brothers and sisters.
That’s amazing, very nice.
I mean, you brothers in Chile,
you’re not afraid of remote places, that’s for sure.
Yes.
Actually, these places that we just saw
are not the most remote areas.
We have one place that we also reached a few years ago,
and that’s Antarctica, as you can see in the photo.
You’re kidding me.
You mean the branch in Chile has supported the work in Antarctica?
Yes.
I imagine it’s very difficult to get there.
Yes, it’s very hard
because first we need permission, and we have to fly.
So the branch has to make
some arrangements to reach a couple in that area.
Very nice. Well, thank you very much, Allen.
Thank you for sharing this information with us
and helping us to see that even though we’re isolated,
we’re not alone.
Do you really feel like Chile is your home?
Yes, of course.
As you can see, Chile is a beautiful place
with many good brothers and sisters.
Also, it really doesn’t matter where we are physically.
If we are with Jehovah and his organization,
we are in the great spiritual temple.
So we can feel—
Wherever we are, we can feel that’s our home.
Beautiful.
Thank you very much, Allen, for sharing that with us.
Integrity has been described as ‘wholehearted love for
‘and unbreakable devotion to the Person of Jehovah,
so that his will comes first in all of our decisions.’
And our guests today have shown us different faces of integrity,
like obedience and cooperation
in preaching and meeting together
and maintaining loyalty when you come face-to-face with tests.
And if you feel isolated
or are literally geographically isolated,
you can maintain unbreakable devotion to Jehovah.
The psalmist wrote:
“If I would fly away with the wings of the dawn
“to reside by the most remote sea,
“even there your hand would lead me
and your right hand would take hold of me.”
Clearly, Jehovah sees our acts of integrity,
and he loves us for it.
Please join us on another edition of The Inside Story.
You would think that we have about 500 here in the audience.
But that was again a faith-strengthening program.
It’s amazing, some of the experiences
and things happening in various parts of the earth.
What a treat that was!

ko.text: 마음이 크게 감동되어 다음과 같이 말했습니다.
“그분이 길에서 우리에게 말씀하시면서 성경을 온전히 열어 주실 때에,
이처럼 마음을 감동시키려면 어떻게 해야 합니까?
듣는 사람이 생각해 보도록 만드는 질문을 하고
둘째, 올바른 일을 하는 이유를 생각해 보도록 권하고
하느님의 성품과 우리에 대한 사랑을 강조할 수 있습니다.
청중이 자신을 검토해 보도록 도와주는지 생각해 보시죠.
영원한 생명을 얻기 위해 여러분은 무엇을 해야 합니까?
“가서 당신의 소유를 팔아 가난한 사람들에게 주십시오.
그러면 하늘에서 보물을 얻게 될 것입니다.”
이처럼 여러분은 여호와를 섬기는 데 방해가 되는 것은
무엇을 해야 할지 알려 주기는 했지만
우리는 영원한 생명을 얻기 위해 무엇을 해야 합니까?
한 부자가 그와 비슷한 질문을 했는데
“가서 당신의 소유를 팔아 가난한 사람들에게 주십시오.
그러면 하늘에서 보물을 얻게 될 것입니다.”
그 부자는 어릴 때부터 모세 율법을 잘 지켜 왔습니다.
하지만 예수께선 그의 부족한 점을 발견하셨죠.
우리는 이렇게 자문해 볼 수 있습니다.
여호와께서 내가 가진 모든 걸 포기하라고 하신 건 아니지만,
그중에 여호와를 섬기는 데 방해가 되는 것이 있는가?
직장 일 때문에 집회에 참석하기가 어려운가?
물질에 대해 끊임없이 생각하고 있지는 않은가?
영원한 생명을 얻는 것보다 더 중요한가?’
질문을 통해 청중은 스스로를 검토해 볼 수 있었죠.
성경 말씀을 적용해야 할 대상 가운데 자신을 포함시켜서
좋은 동기를 갖도록 도와주는 것도 필요합니다.
성경의 가르침에 대한 사랑에서 우러나와 행동하도록 도와주어야 합니다.
이제 한 가지 실연을 통해 그 점을 생각해 보겠습니다.
흡연, 과음, 마약 사용 같은 나쁜 습관을 피해야 하죠.
그런데 아직 담배를 못 끊고 계시죠!
끊고 싶기는 한데 잘 안 돼요.
조금만 있으면 끝이 올 거라는 걸 모르세요?
흡연, 과음, 마약 사용 같은 나쁜 습관을 피해야 하죠.
그런데 나쁜 습관을 극복하는 게 늘 쉽지만은 않죠.
담배를 끊지 않으면 아마겟돈을 통과하지 못하니까요.
우리가 매일같이 열심히 일하는 이유가 뭐죠?
여호와를 사랑하고 그분을 기쁘게 해 드리고 싶은 마음이 있으면
또 여호와께서는 흡연 같은 나쁜 습관을 극복하도록
만약 담배를 피우고 싶은 생각이 들면
언제든 도와 달라고 여호와께 요청할 수 있어요.
이제 도움이 되는 성경 원칙 다섯 가지를 함께 살펴볼까요?
여호와를 기쁘시게 해 드리는 방법을 생각해 보도록 도와주었습니다.
사람들의 마음을 감동시키는 가장 좋은 방법은
하느님에 대한 사랑을 갖도록 도와주는 겁니다.
그분과 가까워지고 그분의 벗이 되고 싶어질 것이며
영원히 찬양하고 싶은 마음을 갖게 될 것입니다!

en.text: Jesus’ teaching reached the heart.
Luke 24:32 records the reaction
of some of his disciples following a teaching session:
“Were not our hearts burning within us
“as he was speaking to us on the road,
as he was fully opening up the Scriptures to us?”
When we teach, how can we reach the heart?
We can (1) use rhetorical questions to help our listeners think,
(2) urge listeners to examine why they perform good works,
and (3) highlight how Bible principles and commands
reflect God’s qualities and his love for us.
In the following example, does the speaker
help the audience to make a self-examination?
What’s one thing you must do to gain everlasting life?
At Matthew 19:21, Jesus said to a rich young ruler:
“Go sell your belongings and give to the poor,
“and you will have treasure in heaven;
and come be my follower.”
Clearly, you must cut out of your life anything
that interferes with your worship of Jehovah.
Were the words accurate?
Yes.
Were you moved from the heart?
Probably not.
Although the speaker told us what we needed to do,
he didn’t help us to examine our own feelings on the matter.
Let’s watch him try again.
What’s one thing we must do to gain everlasting life?
At Matthew 19:21, we find Jesus’ response
to this question as posed by a rich young ruler:
“Go sell your belongings and give to the poor,
“and you will have treasure in heaven;
and come be my follower.”
Although this man had kept the commandments of the Mosaic Law since his youth,
Jesus detected that something was missing.
Each of us does well to ask himself:
‘What might Jesus detect about me?
‘Although Jehovah doesn’t expect me to part with all of my belongings,
‘is there anything in my life that interferes with my worship?
‘Does my job prevent me from attending congregation meetings?
‘Do I catch myself thinking about material things
‘when I’m engaged in sacred service?
‘Material things may be valuable,
but are they worth more than my everlasting life?’
Well done!
The rhetorical questions helped us to examine ourselves.
Also, instead of using the personal pronoun “you,”
the speaker showed respect for his audience by including himself
as one who needs to apply the counsel of God’s Word.
In order to reach the heart,
we must also appeal to good motives.
In other words, we should motivate our audience to act
because they love Jehovah, fellow humans, and Bible teachings.
Does the Bible teacher do that in the following demonstration?
The question asks: “What do we need to avoid?”
Bad habits, like smoking
and abusing alcohol and drugs.
That’s right, but I noticed you’re still smoking.
So, what do you need to do?
I know I need to quit, but it’s not easy.
Well, we’ve been studying for over a year.
How much more time do you need?
How much time do you think is left before the end comes?
Did the teacher appeal to proper motives?
No.
Instead, he tried to pressure and shame the student.
Let’s watch a better way to motivate.
The question asks: “What do we need to avoid?”
Bad habits, like smoking
and abusing alcohol and drugs.
That’s right.
Of course, it’s not always easy to give up bad habits.
But what can be a powerful motivator?
Well, I’ve got to stop smoking so I won’t be destroyed at Armageddon.
Actually, there’s a stronger motivation.
Why do you get up early every day to go to work?
To provide for my family.
I do it because I love them.
Exactly!
In the same way, strong love for Jehovah
can help you to break habits in order to please him.
And what does he provide
that can help you win the battle against smoking?
Holy spirit?
Yes.
Anytime you have the urge to smoke,
you can freely call on Jehovah for his help to resist.
Let’s now consider five Bible principles that will help you further.
Not only did the teacher appeal to good motives
but he also helped the student to think about how he could please Jehovah.
When we do our best to reach the heart of our listeners,
we’ll be appealing to the best of motives: love for God.
Love for Jehovah will move them to draw close to him and become his friends.
It will motivate them to praise him,
not just for a short time but for all eternity!

cn.text: 耶稣的教导能打动人心
门徒在听过耶稣的教导后有什么反应呢？
路加福音24:32说
耶稣“在路上对我们讲话
向我们清楚解释圣经
那时我们的心不是像火一样燃烧吗？”
我们在教导时，可以怎样打动人心呢？
第一，我们要善用问题
帮助听者省察自己的想法
第二，我们要促请听者
分析自己行事为人的动机
第三，我们要强调圣经中的原则和诫命
怎样反映出耶和华的特质和他对我们的爱
接下来，我们会看看
这个讲者有没有帮助听者自我省察呢？
我们需要怎么做才能够享有永生呢？
马太福音19:21
耶稣对一位年轻的官长说
“要去卖掉财物，分给穷人
这样你就有财宝在天上
你还要来跟随我。”
所以，你必须要舍弃
一切会影响你崇拜耶和华的事
他分析的正确吗？
正确
那你受到打动了吗？
可能没有
虽然这个讲者告诉我们要做什么
但他没有帮助我们省察自己的想法
我们再给他一次机会吧
我们需要怎么做才能享有永生呢？
我们可以在马太福音19:21
耶稣对一个年轻官长说的话找到答案
耶稣说
“要去卖掉财物，分给穷人
这样你就有财宝在天上
你还要来跟随我。”
这个官长从小就遵守摩西法典
不过耶稣看出他还需要做一件事
我们每一个人都应该问问自己
“耶稣会希望我怎么做呢？
耶和华没有要求我们放弃一切财物来崇拜他
但是有没有什么
会影响我们跟耶和华的关系呢？
我会因为工作的关系没有办法参加聚会吗？
我在传道和聚会的时候
心里还是想着赚钱的事吗？
财物是很重要
但是它会比永生还要重要吗？”
非常好！
善用问题可以帮助人留意自己的想法
而且讲者在演讲中没有指责听众
他说的是“我们”，而不是“你”
也就是包括他自己
所有人都要听从圣经的劝告
为了打动人心
我们需要帮助听者培养正确的动机
换句话说，我们希望他们是因为爱耶和华
爱别人，爱所学的圣经真理而采取行动
你觉得下面的这个圣经老师做得怎么样？
这一段的问题是：“我们要避免什么？”
要避免恶习
例如抽烟、纵酒或滥用药物
没错
那你为什么还在抽烟？
你觉得你该怎么做？
我很想戒烟，但是没有那么容易
好，我们都学了一年多了
怎么还戒不掉？
末日很快就来了，你觉得你还剩多少时间？
圣经老师有打动学生的心吗？
没有，他只是训斥学生
让对方感到难堪
他怎样做会更好呢？
这一段的问题是：“我们要避免什么？”
要避免恶习
例如抽烟、纵酒或滥用药物
没错
不过想戒除坏习惯不是一件容易的事
那为什么我们要努力这样做呢？
我得赶在哈米吉多顿之前戒烟
不然就会被毁灭
其实，还有一个更重要的理由
想一想你为什么每天那么辛苦工作呢？
我辛苦工作，当然是因为爱我的家人啊
非常好！
同样地，如果你爱耶和华，想让他高兴
也会努力克服恶习，对不对？
耶和华看到你努力戒烟
你觉得他会用什么方法帮助你呢？
嗯......赐我神圣力量？
对，不管什么时候你的烟瘾上来了
你都可以随时祷告求耶和华帮助你
接着让我们来看看五个能帮助你的圣经原则
这次老师努力打动学生的心
而且帮助对方想一想
怎样做才能让耶和华高兴
我们努力唤起听者对耶和华的爱
鼓励他们做耶和华喜悦的事
就是尽力打动他们的心
对耶和华的爱可以推动人亲近上帝
成为上帝的朋友
而且这也会推动人一生一世
永永远远赞美耶和华

ko.text: 가장 큰 영향을 미친 사람으로 여깁니다.
그들 중 일부가 쓴 성경 기록을 보면
예수가 실제로 어떤 분인지 알 수 있습니다.
“그는 큰 자가 되고 가장 높으신 분의 아들이라고 불릴 것입니다.”

예수의 적들도 예수를 죽이고 싶어 하는

방문을 원하는 시간과 장소를 선택할 수 있습니다.

en.text: Many people regard Jesus
as the most influential person in history.
But is he Almighty God himself?
Or was he simply a good man?
Many people personally met Jesus,
and some of their accounts are found in the Bible,
revealing who Jesus really is.
For instance, an angel spoke to Jesus’ mother about her unborn son
and said: “This one will be great
and will be called Son of the Most High.”
When Jesus was being baptized,
God’s own voice confirmed Jesus’ identity:
“This is my Son, the beloved, whom I have approved.”
What did his followers believe?
When Jesus asked who they thought he was,
Peter responded:
“You are the Christ,
the Son of the living God.”
What did Jesus’ enemies say?
Those wanting to kill him explained why:
“According to the law he ought to die,
because he made himself God’s son.”
What did Jesus himself say
about his identity and relationship to God?
He told his followers: “The Father is greater than I am.”
Even after his death and resurrection, Jesus said this about his future:
“I am ascending to my Father and your Father
and to my God and your God.”
The Biblical record makes it clear that Jesus is a distinct person,
separate from God Almighty.
In fact, the Bible teaches that although Jesus
is a powerful spirit creature in heaven,
he is still subject to his God and Father.
Still, God has given a special assignment to his Son:
to bring everlasting life and happiness to all humankind,
just as God originally purposed.
What else does the Bible say about Jesus?
Did Jesus really perform miracles?
Why did Jesus die?
Will Jesus return?

ko.text: 그때는 이스라엘이 이집트를 떠난 지 1년이 지난 때였습니다.
이 책은 145년 동안 있었던 일을 다루는데,
이집트에서 노예 생활을 하던 이스라엘 백성을 구출하시고
자신을 숭배하는 방법에 관해 가르치신 기록이 나옵니다.
1장에서는 이스라엘 백성의 수가 급속히 늘어났다고 알려 줍니다.
히브리인을 때리던 한 이집트인을 죽였기 때문입니다.
대변자인 형 아론과 함께 파라오에게 여러 차례 가서
그러자 여호와께서는 이집트에 열 가지 재앙을 내리십니다.
그분은 나일 강물을 피로 변하게 하시고,
개구리가 이집트 온 땅에 가득하게 하시고,
또한 마지막 열 번째 재앙을 내리셔서
처음 난 것들이 모두 죽게 하십니다.
결국 이스라엘 백성에게 이집트를 떠나라고 말합니다.
이집트에서 나온 이스라엘 백성이 가는 길을 인도하십니다.
하지만 여호와께서는 파라오와 그의 군대가 홍해에 빠져 죽게 하십니다.
모세와 이스라엘 백성은 여호와께 승리의 노래를 부릅니다.
곧 너에게 내 능력을 보이고 내 이름이 온 땅에 선포되게 하려는 것이다.”
그 말씀대로 하느님의 이름이 널리 알려졌습니다.
사탄을 비롯해 여호와를 대적하는 모든 자들에게 경고가 됩니다.
그들은 광야에서 지내는 동안 주로 만나를 먹습니다.
그곳에서 하느님께서는 이스라엘 백성이 철저히 순종하면
그분께 “제사장 왕국과 거룩한 나라”가 될 것이라고 약속하십니다.
24장에서 모세는 백성에게 계약의 책을 읽어 줍니다.
그리고 그 밖의 신성한 물품에 관해 다룹니다.
제사장의 옷과 임직식에 관해 알려 줍니다.
금패에는 “거룩함은 여호와께 속해 있다”라고 새겨져 있었습니다.‏
춤을 추고 노래를 하면서 금송아지를 숭배합니다.
산에서 내려온 모세는 금송아지를 태우고 바스러뜨려 물에 뿌린 다음,
여호와께서 자신의 이름과 특성을 선포하시는 것을 듣습니다.
하느님의 영광이 장막에 가득 찼다고 알려 줍니다.
여호와께서 어떻게 교만하고 오만한 자들이 치욕을 당하게 하시고,
앞으로 하느님의 왕국이 가져올 구출에 대한 믿음을 어떻게 강화해 주는지

en.text: An introduction to the book of Exodus.
Exodus was written by Moses
in the wilderness of Sinai in 1512 B.C.E.,
a year after the Israelites left Egypt.
The book covers a period of 145 years,
from Joseph’s death in 1657 B.C.E.
to the construction of the tabernacle
in 1512 B.C.E.
Exodus tells how Jehovah
delivered the Israelites from slavery in Egypt,
how he organized them into a nation,
and how he taught them how to worship him.
Exodus has 40 chapters.
In chapter 1,
we learn that the Israelites have increased at an extraordinary rate,
causing Pharaoh to subject them to harsh slavery.
Chapters 2 to 4 relate events around Moses’ birth,
his adoption by Pharaoh’s daughter,
and his flight to the land of Midian
after killing an Egyptian who was oppressing a Hebrew.
Many years later,
Jehovah commissions Moses to lead Israel out of Egypt.
In chapters 7 through 10,
Moses, using his brother Aaron as spokesman,
repeatedly tells Pharaoh to send Israel away,
but Pharaoh refuses to do so.
Jehovah responds by bringing ten plagues on Egypt.
These include turning the Nile River into blood,
covering the land with frogs,
and inflicting boils on man and beast.
In chapter 12, God institutes the Passover.
He also brings the tenth and final plague
—the death of the firstborn.
A humiliated Pharaoh, whose son is among the dead,
at last tells the Israelites to leave.
In chapter 13,
by means of a pillar of cloud by day
and a pillar of fire by night,
Jehovah leads his people to freedom.
In chapters 14 and 15,
Pharaoh foolishly pursues the Israelites,
but Jehovah drowns him in the Red Sea
along with his military force.
Moses and the Israelites then sing a victory song to Jehovah.
Did you know?
Through Moses, Jehovah told Pharaoh:
“For this very reason I have kept you in existence:
“to show you my power
and to have my name declared in all the earth.”
God’s name did become widely known.
Even 40 years later,
the people of Canaan, including Rahab of Jericho,
recalled the events at the Red Sea.
More important, Pharaoh’s humiliating end
serves notice on all who defy Jehovah, including Satan.
In chapter 16,
Jehovah provides the Israelites with manna,
which becomes their main food during their wilderness trek.
In chapter 19,
Moses ascends Mount Sinai,
where God promises that if the Israelites strictly obey Him,
they will become to Him “a kingdom of priests and a holy nation.”
In chapter 20, the people witness thunder and lightning,
the sound of a horn, and smoke coming from Mount Sinai
as God gives the Ten Commandments.
In chapter 24,
Moses reads the book of the covenant to the people.
They respond:
“All that Jehovah has spoken we are willing to do.”
Chapters 25 to 40
deal largely with the priesthood,
the construction of the tabernacle,
the ark of the covenant,
the lampstand,
and other sacred items.
Chapters 28 and 29
focus on the attire of the priests
and the installation of the priesthood.
The high priest’s attire includes
an ephod and a turban with a golden plate.
Engraved on the plate are the words
“Holiness belongs to Jehovah.”
In chapter 32, while Moses is on Mount Sinai,
the people make a golden calf and worship it
with dancing and singing.
When Moses returns,
he burns and crushes the idol,
scatters the powder on the water,
and makes the Israelites drink it.
In chapter 34, Moses, again on Mount Sinai,
hears Jehovah declare His name and attributes.
Chapter 40 tells us that the pillar of cloud
covers the completed tabernacle,
which fills with God’s glory.
As you read the book of Exodus,
note how Jehovah can humiliate the proud and arrogant,
observe how he uses the humble and meek,
and see how his deliverance of Israel
strengthens our faith in our future deliverance
by means of God’s Kingdom.

cn.text: 出埃及记是摩西在西奈旷野写的
时间是公元前1512年
也就是以色列人离开埃及一年后
这本书涵盖了145年的历史
从约瑟去世，也就是公元前1657年
直到圣幕建成，也就是公元前1512年
出埃及记告诉我们
耶和华怎样拯救以色列人摆脱埃及的奴役
让以色列成为一个国家
并且教导他们怎样崇拜他
出埃及记共有40章
第1章提到以色列人人口大增
而且增加得特别迅速
于是，法老强迫以色列人做奴隶
压迫他们
第2到4章的内容包括
摩西出生
他被法老的女儿收养
后来他逃到米甸
因为他杀了一个虐待希伯来人的埃及人
许多年后
耶和华派摩西回去，带领以色列人离开埃及
第7到10章
摩西和他的代言人，就是他的哥哥亚伦
多次要求法老放以色列人走
但法老不肯这样做
于是耶和华在埃及降下十场灾殃
其中包括让尼罗河的水变成血
让埃及遍地都是青蛙
以及人和动物身上长毒疮
第12章
上帝设立逾越节
他也降下第十场，也就是最后一场灾殃
把埃及所有头生的都杀死
法老无能为力，他的儿子也死了
最后他不得不放以色列人走
第13章
耶和华白天用云柱
黑夜用火柱为以色列人引路
带他们离开埃及，摆脱奴役
第14和15章
法老愚蠢地追赶以色列人
但耶和华击溃了法老和他的大军
让他们葬身红海
后来摩西和以色列人向耶和华唱出胜利之歌
你知道吗？
耶和华通过摩西告诉法老
“我让你活到现在
就是要向你显示我的力量
让我的名字传遍天下。”
上帝的名字果然广为人知
40年后
住在迦南地区的人，包括耶利哥的喇合
都知道在红海发生的事
而且，从法老的下场我们可以看出
凡是跟耶和华对抗的人
包括撒但最终都会一败涂地
第16章
耶和华提供给以色列人吗哪
这是以色列人在旷野流浪的主要食物
第19章
摩西登上西奈山
在那里上帝承诺说
如果以色列人完全听从他的话
他们就会属于他
成为“祭司的王国，圣洁的国族”
第20章
上帝在西奈山上颁布十诫
当时人民看到雷电交加，山上冒烟
听到有号角声响起
第24章
摩西向人民宣读立约法典
人民回应说
“耶和华说的一切我们都愿意去做。”
25到40章讲述跟祭司有关的安排
以及怎样搭建圣幕、制作约柜、灯台
和其他神圣物品
28和29章重点记述祭司的袍服和就职礼
大祭司的袍服包括圣褂和包头巾
包头巾上系着纯金的牌子
牌子上刻着“圣洁属于耶和华”
摩西还在西奈山上
人民却造了个牛犊像，并且向它下拜
还狂欢作乐
摩西回到营中
就把牛犊像用火焚烧，磨成粉末
然后把粉末洒在水面上，叫以色列人喝
第34章
摩西再次登上西奈山
在那里，耶和华宣告他的名和美好特质
第40章
圣幕完工后，被云彩遮盖
耶和华的荣耀充满圣幕
你读出埃及记时请留意
耶和华会使骄傲自大的人蒙羞
他会任用谦和的人达成他的旨意
耶和华拯救以色列人的事迹让我们坚信
未来上帝一定会通过他的王国带来拯救

title: 알렉스 라인뮬러: 억울한 일을 겪었을 때 (사무엘상 20:30)

ko.text: 파킨 형제는 모든 걸 잘 준비하기 위해 최선을 다했습니다.
그런데 선교인 모임 후에 노어 형제는
조직을 좀 더 잘했어야 했다고 강한 충고를 했습니다.
몹시 낙담한 파킨 형제는 나중에 아내에게
“이제 짐 싸서 가야 할 것 같다”고 말하기도 했습니다.
하지만 그때 파킨 형제는 자기가 잘못한 것이 없다고
아마 여기 계신 모두가 이와 비슷한 경험을 한 적이 있으실 겁니다.
오해를 받으면 처음엔 화도 나고 배신감도 들고
한동안 기운이 빠지게 될 수 있습니다.
남들이 나를 무능하고 영적이지 않은 사람으로 볼까 봐
나 자신이 완전히 부정당하는 느낌이 들 수 있습니다.
그런 일을 겪을 때 우리는 어떻게
여호와에 대한 충성을 유지할 수 있습니까?
그는 불공정한 일을 겪을 때의 심정을
게다가 이 시는 하느님의 영감을 받은 것이기 때문에
오해를 받으면 당장 자기가 옳다는 걸
증명하고 싶은 마음이 들 수 있지만
그렇게 하는 건 별로 도움이 되지 않습니다.
겸손하게 맡은 일을 계속 충실하게 수행해야 합니다.
예수께선 ‘지혜가 그 결과로 의롭다는 것이 증명된다’고 하셨죠.
많은 경우 상대방이 틀렸다는 걸 지적하기보다는
계속해서 충실하게 일할 때 사람들의 마음을 얻고
여호와께서 도와주실 수 있다는 걸 왜 믿을 수 있습니까?
그분은 예수를 창조하신 뒤 모든 걸
예수는 여호와께서 그들을 어떻게 대하시는지 보셨습니다.
그런데 사탄이 여호와에 대해 거짓 비난을 했습니다.
그분의 동기 즉 사랑에 의문을 제기했죠.
얼마나 많은 피조물이 사탄의 거짓말을 믿을 것이었습니까?
이 쟁점들을 해결하기 위해 즉시 조처를 취하셨지만,
이 쟁점이 다 해결되는 데는 많은 시간이 필요했습니다.
그러면 우리가 다른 사람의 오해를 받을 때
‘여호와께서는 나무랄 데 없는 자들이 겪는 일을 알고 계십니다.’
그분이 네 마음의 소원을 들어주실 것이다.”
다윗은 여호와의 사랑과 보호를 확신하라고 말하고 있는 것입니다.
그 점을 확신한다면 다른 사람의 말에 더 잘 귀 기울이게 됩니다.
또한 자기 견해를 고집하거나 방어적이 되지 않을 수 있죠.
어떻게 자신을 안전한 곳으로 인도하셨는지 노래했습니다.
누가 여호와보다 우리를 더 잘 보호해 줄 수 있겠습니까?
다른 사람이 우리에게 무슨 말을 하더라도
그분을 의지하면 그분이 너를 위해 행동하실 것이다.”
다시 말해 여호와의 인도를 따라야 합니다.
그분은 요셉과 한나와 다윗에게 그러했던 것처럼
우리를 계속 인도하고 축복해 주실 것입니다.
여호와께서 그의 손을 붙들어 주시기 때문이다.”
너의 공의를 대낮의 해처럼 빛나게 하실 것이다.”
이처럼 여호와께선 상황을 바로잡으실 수 있으며
자신의 사랑을 우리에게 확신시켜 주실 것입니다.
여호와께선 그런 것에 영향을 받지 않으십니다.
우리의 문제를 바로잡아 주실 수도 있다’고 설명합니다.
그분이 그렇게 하신다면 모두가 분명히 알게 됩니다.
하지만 모든 문제가 그렇게 해결되지는 않습니다.
그들에 대한 평판은 생애 중에 온전히 회복되지 않았죠.
따라서 여호와께서 문제를 바로잡아 주실 때까지
마음이 상한 상태로 있는 것이 아니라,
지금 마음의 평화를 누리기 위해 노력해야 합니다.
“여호와 앞에서 잠자코 있고 그분을 간절히 기다려라.
계략을 성공시키는 자 때문에 속상해하지 마라.”
계속 속상한 상태로 있어서는 안 됩니다.
억울하게 부당한 충고를 받았다는 생각이 들면
자신의 양심을 위해서라도 잘못된 걸 분명히 짚어야겠죠.
기도를 하고 들은 내용을 잘 생각해 본 뒤
적용할 수 있는 부분은 적용해 보는 것이 어떻습니까?
모든 충고에는 어느 정도 유익한 점이 있죠.
많은 경우에 오해를 해결하는 유일한 방법은 시간뿐입니다.
여러 해 전에 한 형제가 그런 말을 한 적이 있습니다.
“하느님은 자신에 대한 비난이 거짓임을 증명하기 위해
우리의 동기도 오해를 받게 되는 경우가 종종 있지만
그 정도는 기다릴 수 있지 않습니까?”
여호와께 초점을 맞추면 오해를 받아도 기쁨을 잃지 않을 수 있습니다.
여호와께서 여러분의 마음을 아주 잘 알고 계시며
때가 되면 문제를 바로잡으실 것임을 늘 기억하십시오.
파킨 형제의 체험기는 이렇게 알려 줍니다.
‘약 6개월 뒤에 노어 형제를 다시 만났을 때
그는 자기 방으로 우리를 초대해서 식사를 대접해 주었죠.”
여호와께서 파킨 형제의 마음의 소원을 들어주신 것 같죠?
파킨 형제는 그때 이후로 노어 형제와 친한 친구가 되었습니다.

en.text: Have you ever been misjudged?
When Brother Parkin was serving
in Puerto Rico, it happened to him.
Brother Knorr came down from Brooklyn
for the very first international convention
on the island.
It was an exciting time for everyone,
and Brother Parkin did his best to get everything well-organized.
But after the missionary meeting,
Brother Knorr assumed that transportation
had not been arranged for everyone to get back to the hotel
—although, in fact, it had.
And later he gave Brother Parkin some strong counsel
about being better organized.
He even said that he was disappointed in him.
Well, Brother Parkin thought:
‘That’s it. I’m out of here.’
And he even told his wife later to start packing.
But at the time, he says that he didn’t argue with Brother Knorr
or try to justify himself.
Yet, he admits that he did feel misjudged
and was upset afterward for quite a while.
Has something like that ever happened to you?
Likely it has.
It usually happens to all of us at some time.
When others misjudge us, we might initially get upset,
feel betrayed, or become discouraged for a while.
We might worry that others don’t see us as smart enough,
strong enough, spiritual enough.
And what they said may threaten our whole identity.
So when something like that happens,
what will help us to stay loyal to Jehovah?
Open your Bibles with me to Psalm 37.
The writer here is King David,
and he well knew what it was like to be upset by injustice.
But more important, what he wrote is inspired of God,
so we can trust that it can help us.
Let’s start reading with verse 3.
He says: “Trust in Jehovah and do what is good;
reside in the earth, and act with faithfulness.”
When someone misunderstands us,
our first instinct may be to prove ourselves right,
but usually that isn’t very helpful.
David says we should focus on Jehovah and keep doing good.
Be faithful, be humble, continue caring for your assignments.
Jesus once said that “wisdom is proved righteous by its works.”
And many times, it’s our works over time
(instead of trying to straighten the other person out)
that win back their heart and our reputation.
Why can we trust Jehovah to help us in these situations?
Well, remember what happened to him in the garden of Eden?
Jehovah based everything in creation
—his entire sovereignty— on love.
After he made Jesus, they made everything else together.
As each new angel and human was created,
Jesus saw just how Jehovah treated them,
and that made him love Jehovah even more.
But then, as we know, Satan slandered Jehovah.
He didn’t challenge his position or power;
he challenged his motives—God’s love.
Now can you imagine how hurtful that was to Jehovah and Jesus?
And this raised all sorts of questions.
How many others would believe Satan’s accusations?
What would happen to Adam’s offspring?
How would Jehovah’s reputation be cleared, and so on?
Now, Jehovah is the Almighty,
and he took immediate steps to resolve those issues,
but it has taken a lot of time to resolve them.
So if someone misjudges us,
do you think Jehovah knows what we’re going through?
He sure does.
He knows exactly what it feels like.
And as David says later in verse 18 in this psalm:
“Jehovah is aware of what the blameless go through.”
Let’s read verse 4.
He says: “Find exquisite delight in Jehovah,
and he will grant you the desires of your heart.”
David is urging us here to find safety in Jehovah,
because when we feel safe,
it’s easier for us to hear what others are saying to us
or be less inclined to push our own views or justify ourself.
In other psalms,
David talks about how Jehovah brought him into a place of safety.
And really, who makes us feel safer than Jehovah does?
If we are in Jehovah’s place of safety,
then we can hear almost anything without becoming defensive.
Verse 5:
“Commit your way to Jehovah.”
David says: “Rely on him, and he will act in your behalf.”
In other words, let Jehovah lead you.
Once we fully commit ourselves to Jehovah,
we won’t feel lost or abandoned when we have setbacks in life.
We know that he’ll continue to guide and bless us
just as he did Joseph and Hannah and David and others.
Verses 23 and 24 of this psalm say:
“Jehovah guides the steps of a man when he finds pleasure in his way.
“Although he may fall,
“he will not be hurled down,
for Jehovah supports him by the hand.”
Verse 6:
“He will make your righteousness shine like daybreak,
and your justice like the midday sun.”
So Jehovah will either vindicate you
or, at the very least, reassure you of his love.
He knows our motives and intentions,
so if a relative or friend or an overseer misjudges us,
Jehovah will make his own decision.
The Watchtower once said that if Jehovah wants to vindicate us in some matter,
he can do so at the proper time.
And if he chooses to do that, it will be obvious.
One translation says in this verse
that it will become as clear as “the noonday sun” that you are right.
But not all situations get resolved in that way, do they?
We love to hear those stories about Joseph and Hannah and David,
where the underdog ends up on top.
But what about Mephibosheth,
Jeremiah, or the apostle Paul?
Were their reputations ever completely cleared during their lifetime?
So it makes no sense to hold on to hurt feelings
until Jehovah vindicates us.
It’s so much better to resolve the matter now.
Notice verse 7:
“Keep silent before Jehovah and wait expectantly for him.
Do not be upset by the man who succeeds in carrying out his schemes.”
The bottom line is that we can’t stay upset.
What, though, if we get counsel
that doesn’t seem to be 100 percent correct,
like in Brother Parkin’s case?
Of course, if you’re accused of something serious, you should speak up,
at least to satisfy your conscience.
But more often,
after you pray about it and think about what was said,
why not just apply what you can?
Most counsel has at least something that we can benefit from.
And if there is something that still doesn’t seem to fit,
then wait “patiently,” as the footnote on verse 7 says,
for Jehovah to clarify matters or make things right.
In most cases, the only way for misunderstandings to get cleared up
is with the passing of time.
I like this quote from a brother years ago.
He said: “If God has been willing to wait six thousand years
“for his true character to be made manifest,
“should not we be able to wait a few brief years
“to have our motives and lives, now so sadly misunderstood,
cleared of every misconception?”
That’s the key, isn’t it?
Focus on Jehovah,
and we can be happy even when we’re misunderstood.
Always remember that he knows exactly how you feel,
and in due time, he will act in your behalf.
How did things turn out for Brother Parkin and Brother Knorr?
Well, in his life story, Brother Parkin says:
‘The next time Maxine and I saw him (about six months later),
he invited us to his room and cooked a meal for us.’
Well, it looks like Jehovah gave Brother Parkin
“the requests of [his] heart,” right?
In fact, he told me recently
that he and Brother Knorr became the best of friends.

title: 우리의 조직이 이루고 있는 일들—고난의 때를 위한 사랑의 마련

ko.text: 자신이나 가족이 응급 상황에 직면하거나 큰 수술을 받아야 했던 적이 있습니까?
그랬다면 정말 많은 스트레스를 받았을 것입니다.
‘여호와께서 병상에서 우리를 붙들어 주실 것’이라고 약속합니다.
신체적, 감정적, 영적 지원을 사랑으로 베푸십니다.
한 가지 방법은 병원 교섭 위원회를 통해서입니다.
전 세계에는 약 2000개의 병원 교섭 위원회가 있고
1만 6000여 명의 형제들이 그 위원회에서 일하거나 그 일을 지원합니다.
우리는 환자가 하느님의 법을 어기지 않고 치료를 받을 수 있는 방법에 대해
의사와 여호와의 증인이 합의점에 이르도록 돕는 역할을 합니다.
한번은 두 형제와 함께 아주 큰 병원을 방문한 적이 있었는데요.
게다가 전화선으로 연결해서 듣고 있는 다른 의사들도 있었죠.
우리가 강당에 들어서는데 한 의사가 우리에게 이렇게 말했습니다.
하지만 준비한 프레젠테이션을 잘 마치고 질문들에 대답해 주고
몇 가지 의학 자료도 전해 줄 수 있었죠.
이 문헌들은 전문가들의 주의 깊은 심사를 거쳐
이 논문들을 병원 교섭 위원 형제들에게 제공하면
형제들은 그러한 논문들을 의사들에게 보여 주면서
이것이 효과적이고 문제 없는 무수혈 치료 방법이라는 것을
이제 의사들은 피와 관련된 문제를 환자 스스로 선택할 수 있고
의사들이 그러한 선택을 존중해 주어야 한다고 생각합니다.
그리고 이제 의사들은 꼭 피를 사용하지 않더라도
우리 외과의들은 새로운 수술법에 정말 놀랍게 잘 적응했어요.
최신 기술을 사용해 이제는 수혈 없이도 수술을 진행하죠.
우리는 여호와의 증인 환자의 의견을 존중하고
큰 수술을 받아야 할 상황이 생기면 스트레스를 받게 되고
수혈 문제를 포함해서 신속히 결정을 내려야 할 일이 많습니다.
하지만 병원 교섭 위원회 마련 덕분에
제때에 도움과 위로를 받을 수 있습니다.
작년에 저는 정말 힘든 시련을 겪었습니다.
그러다 약 1년 전에 식도암이라는 판정을 받게 되었습니다.
“짠!” 하고 암을 없애 주시지 않는다는 걸 알고 있어요.
그렇게 해 달라고 기도한 적은 한 번도 없습니다.
저뿐만 아니라 우리 가족을 위해서 말이죠.
때때로 병실에 가 보면 아픈 환자를 보기 위해 가족과 친구들이 와 있는데
그중 가장 강한 사람은 병과 싸우고 있는 환자인 경우가 많습니다.
바로 환자 자신이 모든 사람을 격려하면서 이렇게 말하죠.
시편의 말씀처럼 여호와께서 그를 붙들어 주시는 겁니다.
저는 입원해 있는 동안 병원 교섭 위원 형제들의 도움을 받으면서
이 마련이 진정한 사랑에서 우러나온 특별한 마련이라는 걸 알게 됐습니다.
또한 그 형제들과 사랑을 주고받은 것은
우리가 병원 교섭 위원들을 지원할 수 있는 두 가지 방법이 있습니다.
최신 사전 의료 지시 및 위임장을 작성하여 소지하고 다니는 것입니다.
치료를 받기 전에 담당 의사를 찾아가 미리 협조를 구하는 것입니다.
우리를 위해 바쁘게 일하는 수많은 형제들을 생각하면
또한 여호와께서 우리를 사랑으로 돌보신다는 걸 분명히 알 수 있습니다.

cn.text: 你或亲友曾面对过一些紧急情况
需要接受手术或某些治疗吗？
如果有，你一定知道这有多不容易
诗篇41:3说
“他卧病在床，耶和华会扶持他。”
耶和华不是用神迹把我们治好
而是在身体和感情上给我们支持
让我们能继续忠于他
其中一个方法是通过医院联络委员会
今天，1万6000多个弟兄
在世界各地大约2000个医院联络委员会
服务或负责协调
他们会提供什么帮助呢？
我们的工作是
协助医生和耶和华见证人达成共识
用不违反上帝法律的方式治疗病人
有一次
我跟两个弟兄去一个大医院
到达时，有25个医生在等着我们
另外还有一些医生连线参加会议
我们一踏进会议厅
一个医生就对我们说
“欢迎来到我们这个狮子洞！”
的确，一开始真的不容易
但我们还是顺利完成了报告
回答了他们的问题
也给了他们一些医学文章
这些医学文章
都必须经过一组医生仔细筛选和审核
以确保内容准确可信
我们把这些文章
提供给医院联络委员会的弟兄
然后弟兄会让医生看这些资料
跟医生解释
让他们明白
采用不输血疗法是可行而且有效的
医生现在都明白
病人在血的问题上有权自己做决定
明白他们必须尊重病人的决定
他们也看出不用输血
一样可以治疗病人
我们的外科医生
很愿意尝试不同的治疗方法
他们在手术过程中运用新技术
这样就不需要给病人输血了
我们应该尊重耶和华见证人的意愿
怀着开明的态度治疗他们
紧急的医疗情况令人担心
而且当事人往往马上要作出决定
其中包括跟血有关的问题
医院联络委员会的安排
能在适当的时候给人安慰和帮助
对我来说
过去的一年真的很难熬
之前我被医生误诊
不知道问题到底出在哪里
大约一年前才被确诊得了食道癌
我知道在这个邪恶的世界里
耶和华不会弹个手指，说
“你的病好了！”
我知道他不会这样做
我也从来没这样求过他
我求的是安慰
不只是为了我自己，也是为了我家人
我的祷告果然得到了回应
我求上帝
这些弟兄就出现在我眼前了
上帝给我的完完全全超乎我的想象
“他卧病在床，耶和华会扶持他
他生病的时候，你会为他更换床铺。”
当你看见一个人卧病在床
跟疾病搏斗，亲友都围在身边
而最坚强的人却是躺在床上的那个人
你就看到这节经文应验了
很多时候是这个人在鼓励别人
告诉他们
“不要哭，没问题，不会有事的。”
可见耶和华真的扶持生病的人
我在住院期间
得到医院联络委员会的协助
让我感受很深的一点是
这些弟兄做的一切完全是出于爱
最重要的是他们深爱耶和华
很感激他给我们的福分
我们拥有的健康
弟兄对我们的爱
以及我们对他们的爱
这一切实在很宝贵
我永远难忘
我们每个人也可以做两件重要的事
尽自己的本分
（1）确保你已填妥
最新简易版的预立医疗指示卡
（2）进行任何治疗之前
确保医生明白并支持你的决定
我们多么感激医院联络委员会的安排
以及许多弟兄不辞劳苦照顾我们
这证明耶和华多么爱我们
多么关心我们

ko.text: 학생들이 받은 5개월 간의 집중적인 성서 교육이
모든 분을 위해 제가 말씀드릴 내용의 주제는
우리 출판물에서 찾을 수 있는 일반적인 정의는
그리고 예수께서는 자신의 한계를 아는 면에서
겸허에 대한 여호와의 생각을 아주 잘 알고 계셨습니다.
예수도 그 점을 잘 알고 계셨죠.
“겸허하게 네 하느님과 함께 걷는 것이 아니냐!”
예수께서도 겸허하게 하느님과 함께 걷는 것이
단지 선택의 문제가 아니라는 걸 아셨습니다.
예수는 우리가 따라야 할 완벽한 본이므로,
학생 여러분과 그리고 우리 모두에게 도움이 될 것입니다.
예수께선 자신의 권한에 한계가 있다는 걸 늘 인식하셨습니다.
그 내용을 보면 야고보와 요한이 어머니를 통해
왕국에서 특별한 지위를 얻으려고 한 것을 볼 수 있죠.
그들은 어머니가 예수께 이렇게 말하게 했습니다.
내가 해 줄 수 있는 일이 아닙니다.
그 자리는 내 아버지께서 선택하시는 사람들의 것입니다.”
사실, 예수께선 사람들에게 선물을 많이 주셨죠.
또 많은 사람을 고쳐 주시기도 했습니다.
한 과부의 아들을 부활시켜 주기도 하셨죠.
왕국에서 두 번째와 세 번째로 높은 자리를 주는 것은
자신의 권한 밖의 일임을 알고 계셨습니다.
그런 일들은 우리가 적극적인 태도를 가지고 할 수 있습니다.
하지만 우리의 권한 밖에 있는 일들도 많습니다.
예를 들어, 아내라면 가정 내의 많은 일들은
자신이 아니라 남편이 결정해야 한다는 걸 알고 계실 겁니다.
자신이 아니라 장로의 회가 결정해야 한다는 걸 알고 계십니다.
또 우리는 베델 부서 내의 많은 일들이
감독자의 승인을 받아야 한다는 걸 알고 있습니다.
나중에 지부 위원회에서 섬길 분들도 계실지 모르는데요,
지부 위원의 권한에도 한계가 있다는 걸 알게 되실 겁니다.
지부 위원이 처리할 수 있는 일이 있고,
우리 모두는 우리에게 권한이 있는 일들과
우리 권한 밖의 일들이 무엇인지 잘 분별해야 합니다.
만약 우리에게 권한이 있는지 없는지 확실하지 않다면,
일단 하고 보자는 태도는 좋지 않죠.
예수께서 자신의 권한의 한계를 인식하셨다는 두 번째 예가
그렇다면 우린 더더욱 한계가 있지 않겠습니까?
우리는 어떤 문제들에 대해 말할 때
