ko.text: 이 사실을 되새기는 것은 매우 중요합니다.
첫째로, 사탄은 여호와께서 우릴 사랑하지 않거나,
우리 봉사를 가치 있게 여기지 않는다고 믿게 하려 합니다.
우리가 여호와께 소중하다는 사실을 되새겨야 하는 두 번째 이유는
살다 보면 힘든 상황이나 나쁜 일들이 생기기 때문입니다.
자신이 사랑받을 가치가 없다고 느끼는 형제 자매들이 있을 수 있습니다.
왜 여호와께서 이런 상황을 허용하실까 의아해하죠.
여호와께서 우릴 소중히 여기신다는 걸 기억해야 할 세 번째 이유는
불완전성으로 인해 부정적인 생각이 들 수 있기 때문입니다.
어떤 분들은 과거의 잘못에 대해 자책하면서,
나 같은 사람을 사랑하실 수 있는지 의문을 품습니다.
자신이 무가치하다는 느낌에 계속 시달리는 분들도 있죠.
무가치하고 사랑받지 못한다는 느낌을 갖게 만들죠.
나는 여호와의 사랑을 받을 자격이 전혀 없다는 느낌이 들어서
그분께 더 많은 봉사를 드리려고 노력했습니다.
하지만 봉사에 아무리 많은 시간을 바쳐도,
나 자신의 부족한 점만 보았던 거죠.’
‘나는 사랑을 거의 표현하지 않는 가정에서 자랐습니다.
이전에 형성된 자기 비하 감정이 있어서,
고통을 겪을 때면 그런 감정이 되살아납니다.
회중 장로로 섬기는 일을 그만두었을 때
하느님과 가족과 회중의 형제들을 실망시켰다는 느낌이 들었습니다.’
이런 느낌이 든다면 여러분만 그런 게 아닙니다.
여호와께서 여러분께 관심이 있으신지 어떻게 알 수 있죠?
첫째로 이스라엘에 대한 여호와의 감정을 생각해 보고,
둘째로 복음서에 기록된 한 사건을 살펴볼 겁니다.
이집트에서 노예로 일하며 심한 압제를 받았습니다.
여호와께서는 그들이 고통 속에서 부르짖었을 때,
“그들이 온갖 고통을 당할 때에 그분도 고통스러워하셨다.”
여호와께서는 백성들의 고통을 보셨을 뿐 아니라,
여호와께선 그들의 고통을 보고 부르짖음을 들을 때
동정심을 느끼시고, 행동하지 않을 수 없었습니다.
갓난아기에 대한 어머니의 사랑에 찬 관심을 생각나게 합니다.
아기가 울면, 어머니는 관심을 갖고 동정심을 느낍니다.
사실 그 점이 이사야 49:15에 이렇게 잘 표현되어 있습니다.
자기 태에서 낳은 아들에게 동정심을 느끼지 않을 수 있겠느냐?
나는 결코 너를 잊지 않을 것이다.”
어머니가 아기에게 젖을 먹이고 돌보는 일을 잊어버릴 수 있을까요?
슬프게도 우린 아기를 돌보지 않은 어머니에 대한 보도를 듣기도 하죠.
자신의 종들에 대한 여호와의 부드러운 동정심은 매우 놀랍습니다.
그것은 우리가 상상할 수 있는 가장 부드럽고 자연스런 감정
즉 아기에 대한 어머니의 동정심보다도 훨씬 더 강합니다.
이사야서의 다른 구절에도 잘 묘사돼 있습니다.
“네가 나의 눈에 소중하여 내가 너를 존중히 여겼고 내가 너를 사랑하였다.”
여호와께선 그들에 대한 자신의 감정을 분명히 표현하셨죠.
그분이 여러분도 따뜻하게 사랑하신다는 걸 확신할 수 있습니다.
현재 어떤 시련을 겪든 또는 과거에 어떤 시련을 인내했든
여호와께선 너무나 소중한 여러분을 잊으실 수 없습니다.
여호와께선 여러분이 기울이는 과거와 현재의 노력을 유의해서 보십니다.
여호와께서 자신의 백성을 지원하고 위로하겠다고 어떻게 약속하시는지
“너희가 젖을 빨고 허리에 안기며 무릎 위에서 귀염을 받을 것이다.
어머니가 아들을 위로하듯이, 내가 늘 너희를 위로할 것이다.”
사랑 많은 어머니가 아기를 무릎 위에 놓고
우리에 대한 그분의 사랑이 얼마나 크고 부드러운지 감동적으로 묘사하십니다.
충실한 종들에 대한 여호와의 감정을 보여 주는
예수께서 예루살렘 성전에 계셨을 때 어떤 일이 있었는지
“예수께서 눈을 들어 부자들이 헌금함에 예물을 넣는 것을 보셨다.
그때에 한 가난한 과부가 가치가 아주 적은,
작은 동전 두 닢을 넣는 것을 보고 말씀하셨다.
저 가난한 과부가 그들 모두보다 더 많이 넣었습니다.
그들은 모두 넉넉한 가운데서 예물을 넣었지만,
저 과부는 궁핍한 가운데서 자기가 가진 생활비 전부를 넣었기 때문입니다.’”
“생필품이 부족한 사람이나 생계를 이어 가기가 어려운 사람을 가리킬 수 있다.
이 단어는 그리스도인 그리스어 성경에서 이 구절에만 나온다.”
그 과부는 자신을 부양해 주던 남편을 잃는 슬픔을 겪었습니다.
“과부의 집을 삼키는” 종교 지도자들이 판치는 환경에서 살아가고 있었습니다.
품꾼이 단지 몇 분이면 벌 수 있는 돈 밖에는 헌금할 수 없었습니다.
우리 출판물에서는 과부가 성전에 헌금한 동전이
8렙돈으로는 참새 두 마리를 살 수 있었는데,
참새는 식용 새 중엔 가장 값이 쌌죠.
과부는 참새 한 마리를 살 돈의 절반밖에 없었는데,
한 끼 식사를 하기에도 부족한 돈이었던 것입니다.
하지만 그 과부와 과부의 헌금은 여호와께 소중한 것이었습니다.
예수께서는 과부의 헌금이 부자들이 한 헌금보다 더 많다고 하셨죠.
과부가 헌금함에 넣은 작은 동전 두 닢은
부자들이 넣은 돈과 섞이게 되었을 겁니다.
그 동전 두 닢과 그 과부가 여호와께 얼마나 소중한지 알지 못했을 겁니다.
다른 사람들의 생각이나 과부가 자신을 어떻게 여기느냐가 아니라
여러분도 상황 상 여호와께 드릴 수 있는 것에 제약이 있을지 모릅니다.
그 밖의 어쩔 수 없는 상황으로 인해,
봉사에 많은 시간을 바치는 것이 어려울지 모릅니다.
자신이 드리는 봉사가 “가치가 아주 적은, 작은 동전 두 닢”처럼 느껴질 수 있습니다.
하지만 우린 가난한 과부에 관한 기록에서
우리가 여호와를 위해 한 일 하나하나를,
그분이 눈여겨보고 소중히 여기신다는 점을 배울 수 있습니다.
잠깐 동안 지난해에 여러분이 여호와께 드린 봉사를 되돌아보십시오.
별로 한 게 없다는 생각이 드십니까?
불완전한 우리 마음은 여호와께서 그 노력을 기뻐하셨는지 의심할 수 있죠.
특별히 희생을 치르며 봉사한 적이 있지 않습니까?
여호와께서 가난한 과부가 넣은 동전 두 닢을 눈여겨보시고 가치 있게 여기셨다면,
그분은 여러분이 바친 그 시간도 유의해서 보시고
우리가 그분께 드리는 모든 것을 소중히 여기십니다.
우리가 그분의 왕국을 지원하기 위해 드린
아주 작은 정성도 기억하시고 상 주실 겁니다.
여호와께 여러분이 소중하다는 두 번째 증거였습니다.
현대에 하느님께 매우 소중했던 한 사람의 예를 생각해 보겠습니다.
피나 자매는 알바니아의 남부 해안에 있는 작은 도시인 블로러에 살았습니다.
열심 있는 복음 전파자였던 피나 자매는
험한 산들을 오르내리면서 성경을 손에 들고 봉사했습니다.
시간이 흘러, 블로러에 더는 회중이 없게 되었고,
여호와께서 자매가 기울인 노력을 보지 못하셨을까요?
형제들은 블로러에서 정신이 좀 이상한 노인이 전도를 하고 있다는 말을 들었습니다.
다들 자매가 전체주의 아래 오랫동안 하느님을 믿다 정신이 이상해졌다고 생각했죠.
하지만 당시 80대였던 피나 자매는 전혀 그런 게 아니었습니다.
얼마 후에, 형제들은 피나 자매가 건강이 악화됐으며,
책임 있는 형제를 만나고 싶어 한다는 걸 들었습니다.
그 대화를 나눈 지 얼마 안 되어,
피나 자매는 충실하게 지상 생애를 마쳤습니다.
여호와의 조직의 지상 부분으로부터 고립되어 있던 그 여러 해 동안,
여호와께서는 피나 자매의 노력을 보지 못하셨습니까?
자매가 최선을 다해 충실히 그분을 섬기는 것을 보고
여호와께선 여러분이 그분을 위해 기울이는 노력도 눈여겨보시죠.
오늘 내용을 통해 우리는 무엇을 알게 되었습니까?
살면서 겪는 힘든 상황이나 나쁜 일들,
하지만 여호와께서 자신의 종들을 매우 소중히 여기신다는 걸 잊어선 안 됩니다.
이사야를 통해 이스라엘에게 하신 말씀에서 알 수 있었죠.
여호와께서 여러분을 따뜻이 사랑하신다는 걸 확신하십시오.
현재 어떤 시련을 겪든 과거에 어떤 시련을 인내했든
여호와께선 너무나 소중한 여러분을 잊으실 수 없습니다.
또 과부에 관한 누가 21장의 기록에서 알려 주듯이,
상황 상 여호와께 드릴 수 있는 것에 제약이 있을 순 있지만,
여호와께선 우리가 그분을 위해 하는 일 하나하나를,
특히 어려운 상황에서 하는 일을 눈여겨보고 소중히 여기십니다.
그분은 우리가 왕국을 지원하기 위해 드린
아주 작은 정성도 기억하시고 상 주실 겁니다.
그리고 현대에도 우리 조직에는 여호와께 충성을 증명한,
그러한 훌륭한 본들 가운데, 피나 자매가 있었죠!
여러분이 여호와께 소중하다는 사실을 결코 잊지 마십시오!

en.text: Our theme for this month’s program is
“You Are Precious to Jehovah.”
How vital it is
that we remind ourselves of that!
Why?
Well, let’s consider three reasons.
First, Satan wants us to believe
that Jehovah doesn’t love us or value our service.
He wanted Job to believe that.
But that was a lie in Job’s day, and it’s still a lie today.
A second reason that we need to be reminded that we’re precious to Jehovah
is because of negative circumstances
or events that have taken place in our life.
Severe illness, advancing years, injustices,
mistreatment, a difficult family life, or other situations
may cause some brothers and sisters to feel that they’re just not worth loving.
Some may question why Jehovah allows those things to happen.
Finally, we need reminders of how Jehovah feels about us
because our imperfection can cause us to have negative thoughts.
Some may still punish themselves for past mistakes,
doubting that Jehovah has forgiven them
or that he could ever love them.
Others wage a constant battle against feelings of worthlessness.
One Witness wrote:
“Satan has done an excellent job of making
“even those who love Jehovah feel worthless and unlovable.
“. . . I never felt worthy of Jehovah’s love,
“so I tried to do more and more in his service
“as a way of earning that love.
“. . . So no matter how many hours I spent in the ministry,
“or how many people I helped, I felt it was not enough.
I saw only the lack in me.”
One brother stated:
“I came from a family that showed little love.
“I was belittled, teased, and laughed at.
“So, early in life I felt worthless.
“I still carry entrenched feelings from my past
“that beat me down when I experience calamity.
“When I stopped serving as a congregation elder,
“I felt like a failure as usual
—to God, my family, and my brothers in the congregation.”
If you’ve experienced such feelings,
you’re not alone.
So how can you be assured of Jehovah’s interest?
Let’s examine three lines of evidence
that prove you’re precious to Jehovah.
First, we’ll examine Jehovah’s feelings for the nation of Israel.
Second, we’ll reflect on an event recorded in the Gospels.
And third, we’ll consider a modern-day example
of one who was very precious to God.
By the end of the 16th century B.C.E.,
millions of Israelites were enslaved in Egypt,
where they were severely oppressed.
In their distress, the Israelites cried out to Jehovah.
How did he feel?
Turn with me to Isaiah 63:9.
The A portion reads:
“During all their distress
it was distressing to him.”
Did you notice?
Not only did Jehovah see their troubles
but he felt for his people,
and he was moved to act in their behalf.
Isaiah 63:9 goes on to say:
“In his love and compassion he repurchased them.”
Jehovah couldn’t see their suffering or hear their outcries
without feeling for them and doing something about it.
That may remind us of the loving concern
that a mother has for her newborn child.
When that baby cries,
the mother takes notice
and she feels for her child.
In fact, notice how this is expressed at Isaiah 49:15.
It reads:
“Can a woman forget her nursing child
“or have no compassion for the son of her womb?
“Even if these women forget,
I would never forget you.”
It’s hard to imagine a mother forgetting to nourish and care for her nursing child.
That baby is helpless
—day and night it needs its mother’s attention.
Sad to say, however,
that we hear at times of such maternal neglect.
But what did Jehovah say to reassure the Israelites?
“I would never forget you.”
Yes, the tender compassion that Jehovah felt for his servants
was immeasurably stronger
than one of the most tender and natural feelings we can imagine
—the compassion a mother normally feels for her baby.
Jehovah’s feelings for the Israelites
are summed up in another expression in the book of Isaiah.
Please read with me Isaiah 43:4:
“For you became precious in my eyes,
you were honored, and I have loved you.”
Jehovah clearly expressed his feelings for his people.
As one of Jehovah’s servants,
you can be sure that he also loves you most tenderly.
No matter what trials you’re facing now or have endured in the past,
Jehovah sees you and he feels for you.
When you hurt, he hurts.
You’re far too precious to Jehovah for him to forget you.
He remembers your past efforts,
and he sees your continuing efforts to please him.
Notice how Jehovah promises to sustain and comfort his people
according to Isaiah 66:12, 13:
“You will nurse and be carried on the hip,
“and you will be bounced on the knees.
“As a mother comforts her son,
so I will keep comforting you.”
What a heartwarming scene!
Imagine a loving mother carrying a baby on her hip
or bouncing him on her knees.
In this way,
Jehovah touchingly illustrates the intensity
and tenderness of his love for you.
Just as Jehovah loved his people, Israel,
he likewise feels that you are very precious and dear
—never doubt that!
A second example of how Jehovah feels
about his faithful servants can be found in the Gospels.
Let’s read what happened on one occasion
when Jesus was at the temple in Jerusalem
at Luke 21:1-4:
“Now as he looked up,
“he saw the rich dropping their gifts
“into the treasury chests.
“Then he saw a needy widow drop in
“two small coins of very little value,
“and he said:
“‘Truly I say to you that this poor widow
“‘put in more than they all did.
“‘For all of these put in gifts
“‘out of their surplus,
“‘but she, out of her want
“‘[or as the footnote says, “poverty”],
put in all the means of living she had.’”
The study note for verse 2
in the New World Translation of the Holy Scriptures
tells us that the Greek word for “needy” may describe
“a person who lacks the basic necessities of life
“or someone for whom life is a great struggle.
In the Christian Greek Scriptures, it is used only here.”
Just think about the widow’s circumstances.
Not only had she experienced the grief
of losing her husband, her provider,
but she also lived in a religious climate
dominated by leaders who,
according to Luke 20:47,
would “devour the houses of the widows”
rather than help such vulnerable ones.
That widow was so poor that her contribution to the temple
was what a laborer might earn in just a few minutes.
Life wasn’t easy for her.
In fact, Jesus said that she
“put in all the means of living she had.”
Our publications have stated that the coins the widow contributed
were likely two lepta.
With eight lepta, a person could buy two sparrows,
which were among the cheapest birds used for food.
So the widow had only half the amount needed
to buy one sparrow,
hardly enough for a single meal.
Yet, both the widow and her contribution
were valuable to Jehovah.
Jesus said that her contribution was greater
than the contributions of the rich.
When she put those two small coins in the treasury chest,
they would be mixed with what the rich had put in.
To imperfect human eyes, they might seem lost, buried.
Yet, this precious widow was the one Jesus singled out for praise.
When the treasury workers came across the coins,
they wouldn’t have known how precious the coins and their donor
were to Jehovah.
But God’s view was the one that really mattered,
not what other people thought
or even how that dear widow viewed herself.
Like that widow,
you may find that circumstances limit
what you can contribute to Jehovah.
Age, infirmities, or other circumstances beyond your control
may limit the amount of time you’re able to spend in the ministry.
You might feel that your efforts are like those
“two small coins of very little value.”
Still, we learn from this account of the needy widow
that Jehovah notices and he treasures each act done for him,
especially when we do it despite difficult circumstances.
For a moment, think back on your worship of Jehovah during the past year.
Some of you may feel that you accomplished little.
Your imperfect heart might cause you to wonder
whether Jehovah was pleased with your efforts.
However, did one of the hours you spent
require a special sacrifice on your part?
If Jehovah took notice of the widow
dropping in those two coins and valued her contribution,
don’t you think he also noticed
and valued what you did for him during that hour?
Jehovah values every gift, no matter how small,
that springs from a heart motivated by love.
He remembers, and he’ll reward
even the smallest contribution given in support of his Kingdom.
That’s proof of how Jehovah feels about you.
Finally, let’s consider a modern-day example
of one who was very precious to Jehovah.
It’s the experience of Sister Areti Pina.
Sister Pina lived on the southern coast of Albania
in the town of Vlorë.
She was baptized in 1928 at the age of 18.
There was a strong congregation in Vlorë in the 1930’s,
and Sister Pina was a zealous evangelizer
who climbed up and down rugged mountains,
preaching with her Bible in hand.
In time, a congregation no longer existed in Vlorë,
and Sister Pina lost contact with the brothers.
Yet, she kept preaching faithfully on her own.
Do you think her efforts went unnoticed by Jehovah?
Well, years later, word reached the brothers
that there was an old, senile woman
who was reportedly preaching in Vlorë.
People thought she was crazy for keeping faith in God
during years of totalitarian rule.
Yet, Sister Pina, now in her 80’s, was anything but senile.
When the brothers arrived at her home,
Sister Pina invited them in,
but she seemed somewhat reserved.
When they explained that they were her spiritual brothers,
she had no reaction.
After a few minutes,
Sister Pina started firing questions at the brothers:
“Do you believe in the Trinity? What is God’s name?
“Do you believe in hellfire? What happens when we die?
What about the earth? How many go to heaven?”
The brothers answered each question.
“Do you preach?” she then asked.
“Yes,” said one brother, “we preach.”
“But,” she responded, “how do you preach?”
“We preach from house to house,” replied the brother.
“Now I know that you are my brothers!” she exclaimed.
“Only Jehovah’s people preach from house to house!”
Through her tears, Sister Pina stated:
“Jehovah is wonderful. He never forgot me!”
Sometime later, the brothers were notified that Sister Pina was ill
and that she wanted to meet with one of the responsible brothers.
When he arrived, she asked in part,
as she gasped for air,
“Has the book of Revelation been fulfilled?”
The brother responded, “Yes, Areti, most of it has.”
Sister Pina said: “Now I can die in peace.
I needed to know how close we are.”
Shortly after that conversation,
Sister Pina faithfully finished her earthly course.
What do you think?
During all those years of isolation
from the earthly part of Jehovah’s organization,
did Sister Pina’s efforts go unnoticed by Jehovah?
Absolutely not!
Just imagine Jehovah’s joy
as he watched her faithfully doing what she could in his service.
Do you think that Sister Pina was precious to Jehovah?
Without a doubt she was.
Well, your efforts in Jehovah’s service do not go unnoticed by him either.
Like Sister Pina, you are precious to him.
So, what has this consideration helped us to realize?
We may have to contend with Satan’s lies,
negative circumstances and events in our lives,
and our own imperfections.
But we should never forget that Jehovah highly values his servants.
We saw that in his words to the Israelites through the prophet Isaiah.
You can be sure that Jehovah loves you most tenderly.
No matter what trials you’re facing now or have endured in the past,
Jehovah sees you and he feels for you.
When you hurt, he hurts.
You’re far too precious to Jehovah for him to forget you.
The account of the widow in Luke chapter 21
can assure you that although circumstances
may affect what you can contribute to Jehovah,
he notices and treasures each act you do for him,
especially when you do it in the face of difficult circumstances.
He remembers, and he will reward
even the smallest contribution given in support of his Kingdom.
And what beautiful modern-day examples we have in the organization
of brothers and sisters who have proven their loyalty to Jehovah
and are precious to him, like the example of Sister Pina!
Dear brothers and sisters, please,
never forget that you are precious to Jehovah!

cn.text: 这个月的主题是
“你在上帝眼中非常宝贵”
我们经常提醒自己这点非常重要！
为什么呢？
我们来看看三个理由
首先，撒但巴不得我们相信
我们是一文不值的，上帝并不爱我们
他就是希望约伯这么想的
不管是在约伯的日子还是在今天
这样的说法都是骗人的！
其次就是，也许我们的生活不尽如人意
我们可能有严重的疾病
身体越来越衰弱
受到不公平的对待、受虐待
不快乐的婚姻生活或有其他不容易的情况
这些都可能让我们觉得自己不配得到别人的爱
有些人可能会想
为什么上帝会容许这些事发生？
所以我们需要经常提醒自己
耶和华很珍视我们
最后一个理由是，我们都不完美
因为不完美，我们都会有消极的思想
有些人可能因为之前犯下的错而不断自责
认为上帝不会原谅他们，上帝也不会爱他们
有些人则在不断地跟自己消极的思想搏斗
一个朋友说
“撒但曾经成功地骗倒一些爱耶和华的人
使他们相信自己一无是处、不配人爱
我觉得自己不配得到耶和华的爱
所以不断多做上帝的工作，希望赢得他的爱
但无论我花了多少个钟头传道
或者帮助了多少人接受真理
我还是觉得自己做得不够多、不够好。”
一位弟兄说
“我在一个缺乏爱心的家庭里长大
家人看不起我，戏弄我，取笑我
所以我从小就觉得自己一无是处
每当我遇到重大打击
过去那种自卑的感觉
就再一次狠狠地折磨我
我不再是会众长老的时候
以往的感觉又再次涌上心头
我觉得自己辜负了耶和华，辜负了家人
辜负了会众的弟兄姐妹。”
要记得，有这种感受的人并不只有你一个
那怎样才能确信上帝关心你呢？
我们会看看三个上帝珍视你的证据
首先
我们会看看耶和华对古代以色列人的看法
接着，我们会沉思福音书中的一个记载
最后，我们会看看一位现代忠仆的例子
她在上帝眼中也非常宝贵
在公元前16世纪末
几百万以色列人在埃及饱受压迫，受尽奴役
以色列人遭难的时候，向耶和华哀声呼求
耶和华有什么反应呢？
请打开以赛亚书63:9
经文开头就说
请留意，耶和华不只是看见他子民所受的苦
他还感受到他们的痛苦
想要采取行动帮助他们
经文接着说
是的，耶和华看见他子民的苦况
听见他们的呼号
他绝不会无动于衷、袖手旁观
这让我们想到妈妈对刚刚出生的婴孩的爱
孩子一哭，妈妈就会听到
然后马上冲到孩子身边照顾他
以赛亚书49:15也有类似的描述
经文说
我们很难想象母亲会忘记哺育自己的孩子
婴儿没有自理能力
时刻都需要母亲的照顾和爱护
遗憾的是
有些妈妈的确没有好好照顾自己的孩子
但请留意耶和华对古代以色列人的保证
耶和华说：“我也绝不会忘记你”
耶和华对他子民的怜悯超出我们的想象
远比人间最亲切的感情
也就是比母亲对孩子的怜爱更加强烈
另外，圣经在以赛亚书43:4
也描述了耶和华对古代以色列人的爱
耶和华说
耶和华清楚表达了他对子民的爱
你也是上帝的仆人
你也要坚信耶和华一直爱你
无论你遭遇过或正在面对什么难题
耶和华都清楚知道，也感同身受
你痛苦，他也难受
你非常宝贵，耶和华绝不会忘记你
他不会忘记我们曾经付出的一切
也不会轻视我们现在的努力
请留意以赛亚书66:12,13
耶和华对以色列人保证
他会一直支持和安慰他们
经文说
多么感人的画面！
想象一下
一位慈爱的妈妈一会把孩子抱在怀里
一会把孩子放在腿上，逗孩子玩
耶和华用这么温暖的场景来说明
他对忠仆的关心和爱护
耶和华这么珍视以色列人
他也会非常珍视你！
千万不要怀疑这一点
接着是第二个证据
我们会看看福音书中
上帝关心他忠仆的一个例子
这件事发生在耶路撒冷的圣殿里
当时耶稣也在场
路加福音21:1-4说
英语精读本圣经在第2节有一个注释说
翻译成“穷”的希腊语词是指
“缺乏生活必需品的人
也可以指生活非常艰难的人
在《希腊语经卷》中
这个词只出现过这一次。”
请想想这个寡妇的处境
她本来有丈夫可以照顾她，但她的丈夫死了
她不但要承受丧夫之痛
还有可能被宗教领袖剥削
路加福音20:47描述
这些宗教领袖不仅没有帮助穷人
还“侵吞寡妇的房子”
这个寡妇非常贫穷
她在圣殿捐出的钱
是当时的工人用几分钟就能赚到的
可见她的生活肯定非常艰难
耶稣说
这个寡妇把“她赖以为生的一切，全都投进去了”
我们的出版物曾经解释说
寡妇捐的两文小钱差不多是两雷普顿
八雷普顿可以买两只麻雀
当时，麻雀非常便宜，可以用作食物
寡妇投进去的两文小钱还不够买一只麻雀
还不够吃一顿饭
穷寡妇和她所捐的在耶和华眼中十分宝贵
耶稣说，这个寡妇所捐的
比富有的人捐的还多
两文小钱投进钱箱后
就跟富有人投进去的钱混在一起了
一般人根本不会注意到，也不会在意
但耶稣特别称赞这个穷寡妇
清点捐款的人不会想到
这两文小钱和捐钱的人
在上帝眼中是多么宝贵
所以，真正重要的是上帝的看法
其他人怎么看，这个寡妇又怎样想
都不重要
就像这个穷寡妇一样
你可能受环境所限，能为耶和华献出的不多
有些基督徒可能因为年老体弱
或其他无法控制的因素
只能用很少的时间传讲上帝王国的好消息
你可能觉得自己所做的
就像两文小钱一样没什么价值
我们从穷寡妇的例子可以学到
耶和华不仅会留意
而且非常珍惜我们为他付出的点点滴滴
特别是我们在不容易的情况下献出的
回顾过去一年的服务
你可能觉得自己做的并不多
你可能会想，耶和华会看重我做的吗？
但请你想想，你献给耶和华的时间中
有没有任何一个小时
是你必须额外努力才能献出的呢？
如果有，你大可以放心
既然耶和华非常珍惜寡妇的两文小钱
耶和华也一定十分重视
你在这一小时里为他做的事
无论我们献上的礼物多么不起眼
只要出于爱心，耶和华就会非常看重
我们为王国所做的工作即使微不足道
耶和华也不会忘记，他一定会奖赏我们
寡妇的记载证明，你在上帝眼中非常宝贵
接着我们谈谈第三个证据
这是一个现代的经历
让我们看看耶和华怎样表明
自己非常珍视阿蕾蒂·皮纳姐妹
皮纳姐妹住在阿尔巴尼亚南岸的发罗拉
她在1928年受浸，当时她18岁
在1930年，那里曾有一群会众
皮纳姐妹是一位非常热心的传福音者
她拿着圣经，沿着崎岖的山路，在山区传道
后来，在发罗拉没有会众了
皮纳姐妹也跟弟兄们失去了联系
虽然如此，她还是坚持不懈地独自向人传道
你认为耶和华会珍视这个姐妹吗？
过了很多年
弟兄们听说在发罗拉有一个老奶奶
有人说她头脑有点糊涂
在极权统治下，皮纳姐妹仍然忠于上帝
人们因此都以为她疯了
虽然皮纳姐妹已经80多岁了
但她的头脑十分清晰，一点也不糊涂！
当弟兄们到了皮纳姐妹的家后
皮纳姐妹请他们进去她家
但她却一直保持沉默
弟兄们告诉皮纳姐妹他们都是她的弟兄
皮纳姐妹听了还是毫无反应
几分钟后，皮纳姐妹突然问了好几个问题
“你们相信三位一体吗？上帝的名字是什么？
你们相信地狱永火吗？人死了会怎样？
地球最终会怎样？有多少人会到天上去？”
这些问题，弟兄都一一回答了
皮纳姐妹又问
“你们会去传道吗？”
一个弟兄回答说
“我们都会去传道。”
皮纳姐妹问：“那你们怎样传道？”
弟兄说：“我们挨家挨户传道。”
皮纳兴奋地说
“现在我知道你们真的是我的弟兄了！
只有耶和华的子民才会挨家挨户传道！”
皮纳姐妹哭着说
“我真的很感激耶和华！
他一直都没有忘记我！”
过了一段时间后，皮纳姐妹病了
她很想跟一个负有职责的弟兄见面
后来，弟兄去找皮纳姐妹
当时皮纳姐妹呼吸已经很困难了
她费力地问
“启示录的预言应验了吗？”
弟兄回答
“大部分都应验了。”
皮纳姐妹说
“现在我可以安心地走了
我需要知道我们离终结的日子有多近。”
过了不久
皮纳姐妹就忠贞地走完了她在地上的人生
你觉得呢？
虽然有一段时间皮纳姐妹跟组织失去联络
只能独自传道，但耶和华忘记她了吗？
绝对没有！
耶和华看到皮纳姐妹尽己所能地向人传道时
他一定非常开心
你觉得皮纳姐妹在上帝眼中很宝贵吗？
这是肯定的
你尽己所能地为耶和华服务
他也一定不会忘记
你们跟皮纳姐妹一样
在上帝眼中都是非常宝贵的
我们今天学到什么呢？
我们可能因为撒但的谎言而受苦
或生活不尽如人意
还要跟自己不完美的身心搏斗
但千万不要忘记
耶和华非常非常珍视你
我们从耶和华通过以赛亚先知
对以色列人提出的保证，可以确定这点
你可以放心，耶和华充满温情，他非常爱你
无论你现在正面对什么难题
曾经应付过什么考验
耶和华都看在眼里，疼在心里
耶和华非常珍视你，他绝对不会忘记你！
穷寡妇的记载让我们确信
即使我们因为某些原因
不能为耶和华做很多
但他还是非常珍视我们为他做的一切
特别是在困难的情况下做的
我们为上帝的王国所做的工作即使微不足道
耶和华也不会忘记，他一定会奖赏我们
今天，在我们的组织里有很多感人的经历
他们像皮纳姐妹一样，忠贞地为上帝服务
耶和华也非常珍视他们
亲爱的弟兄姐妹，千万不要忘记
你在耶和华的眼中是非常宝贵的！

titles.en: Leonard Myers: You Are Precious to Jehovah
titles.cn: 伦纳德·迈尔斯：你在上帝眼中非常宝贵

ko.text: 이렇게 가슴 아픈 일이 생길 거라곤 상상도 못했죠.
아니면 위험한 상황으로 가고 있는 걸까요?
톰 형제는 제가 잘못하고 있는 거라고 말할 수도 있었지만,
전 형제 마음이 어떤지 다 알 수가 없죠.
여호와께 의지해야 한다는 걸 깨닫게 됐습니다.
정말, “여호와께서는 마음이 찢긴 자들에게 가까이 계십니다.”

en.text: I, Steven, take you, Emily, to be my wedded wife.
I, Emily, take you, Steven, to be my wedded husband.
I had no doubt our vows were forever.
Nothing could have prepared me for the heartbreak.
I never expected her to be unfaithful
and unwilling to work things out.
I felt humiliated.
How could she do such a thing?
I was embarrassed,
and I didn’t want to talk to anyone.
I read somewhere that time would help me heal
and just to stay busy.
It seemed to work.
But I was constantly reminded of what I lost:
our spiritual goals,
the hopes and dreams we had
—all destroyed.
I didn’t want to dwell on the hurt,
but I just couldn’t ignore it.
Was I really coping?
Or was I leaving myself open to even more pain?
Brothers and sisters, we’re going to talk about marriage today.
If we turn to Ephesians chapter 5, . . .
I was angry, but not just with Emily.
I was angry with everything.
Steven! Steven!
Hey, let me stop by tomorrow.
What I had to say,
I wouldn’t have blamed Tom for judging me,
but he didn’t.
You’re right, Steven.
I can’t understand how you feel.
But you know who can.
Do you remember Psalm 34?
I think verse 18 says it best.
Can you read it for us?
“Jehovah is close to the brokenhearted;
he saves those who are crushed in spirit.”
Isn’t that a beautiful scripture?
Take advantage of Jehovah being that close to you,
and include him in everything.
Jehovah is  a loving Shepherd.
When we hurt, he cares.
I knew this, but in a way, I’d forgotten.
I realized I hadn’t included Jehovah
in the ways I tried to cope.
Staying busy was important,
but I needed to draw closer to God,
not push away.
And when I did,
the real healing began.
Even though the pain is still there,
Jehovah sees the tears;
Jehovah feels what I feel.
It is getting better, slowly,
because “Jehovah is close to the brokenhearted.”

cn.text: 我，史蒂文
愿意娶爱米莉为合法妻子
我，爱米莉
愿意嫁史蒂文，以你为合法丈夫
那时我以为我们会天长地久
我从没想过会发生这种事
我的妻子居然会对我不忠
她甚至不想弥补我们的关系
我觉得很丢脸
她怎么可以这样做？
我不想要跟任何人说话
有人说，要保持忙碌
时间会冲淡一切
这看起来好像有用
可是，有些事情总是会提醒我
我们曾经想要一起扩大服务
但现在却不可能了
我不想一直这样消沉下去
但是我心里还是很痛
可是，我现在做得
真的能让自己好起来吗？
还是我会让自己更痛苦呢？
各位弟兄姐妹，我们怎么让婚姻更幸福呢？
〔请打开圣经到以弗所书第5章......〕 - 我很生气
我不光生爱米莉的气
我看什么都不高兴
史蒂文！史蒂文！
明天去你家看你，可以吗？
我告诉汤姆我的感受
他一点都没有责怪我
史蒂文，你说得没有错
我确实不能完全明白你的感受
但是你知道谁可以完全明白
在圣经的诗篇
34:18对你很有用
请你读好吗？
“耶和华亲近心碎的人
拯救心灵伤痛的人。”
这节经文告诉我们
耶和华很想亲近我们
所以遇到考验时，不要忘了他
耶和华是充满爱心的牧人
我们受伤，他也非常难过
这些我都知道，只是我一时没想到
我发现我一直想靠自己来克服伤痛
没有倚靠耶和华
的确，保持忙碌很重要
但我更需要的
是亲近耶和华，不是远离他
当我这样做，心里的伤痛才开始好转
虽然偶尔还是会难过
但耶和华都知道
他不会忘记我流过的每一滴眼泪
我的情况越来越好
慢慢地变好
因为“耶和华亲近心碎的人”

titles.cn: 耶和华拯救心灵伤痛的人

title: 후안 파블로 제르메뇨: 여호와께서 삶의 의미를 찾게 해 주셨습니다

ko.text: 돈 걱정도 없이 사는 것 같았습니다.
저 사람들은 어떻게 저렇게 잘 살까?’
저는 범죄와 폭력이 많은 동네에서 살았어요.
늘 좋은 충고를 해 주려고 하셨죠.
몇 년 동안 도장 사람들과 지내면서
시간이 지나면서 저도 마약을 팔기 시작했죠.
저도 그렇게 될 수 있다는 생각이 들었죠.
우리 삶에 왜 이렇게 문제가 많은지
그 친구들도 알았으면 좋겠다는 마음이 들어서
제게 더 이상 마약을 팔지 않아도 된다고 했어요.
프로 복서가 되게 해 줄 테니까
여호와께서 제가 삶의 진정한 의미와 목적을 찾게 해 주셨어요.

en.text: When you’re little, you just want to be happy.
But sadly, my father had a problem with alcohol,
and no child wants to live through that.
One day, my family from the United States came to visit us.
They looked so happy!
The way they talked, it was as though they only had fun
—a good life
with no economic problems.
I was shocked.
I asked myself, ‘How can we live
in such poverty while their life is so great?’
That was the life I wanted for my family.
So when I was nine years old,
I left my mother and the rest of my family
to cross the border into the United States.
I lived in a pretty rough neighborhood.
So I joined a local gym to learn how to defend myself.
The trainer, Leo, was like a father to me.
He always tried to give us good advice.
Raymond was part of the boxing team.
He was a good friend.
We got along really well.
He respected me, and he looked after me.
After several years of being around Raymond
and the other members of the team, I felt really comfortable.
To some extent, I admired him
because I could see that he was really doing well,
because Raymond was selling drugs.
I knew that it wasn’t right.
But in time,
I began to sell drugs as well.
Raymond was in a drug deal gone wrong,
and he was murdered.
I said to myself, ‘This could happen to me too.’
It had been six years since I had seen my mom and my siblings.
My mother was studying the Bible with Jehovah’s Witnesses.
It helped her to cope with a lot of suffering.
It brought her peace.
She was so happy.
I began to realize that this was what I really needed.
I also thought about my friends at the gym.
I wanted them to understand why life was so hard for all of us,
so I returned to the United States.
But they weren’t interested.
My trainer, Leo, told me that I didn’t need to sell drugs anymore;
he could make me a professional boxer,
and I could help out my family in that way.
He even gave me the nickname The Bible Boy.
But I realized that that was just a temporary solution.
What I was learning was going to help me forever.
I was determined to serve Jehovah.
I returned to Mexico.
I started to study the Bible and take it seriously.
I began to view Jehovah as my Father
because he helped me to find real relief from my pain,
to have peace—a tranquility that makes you feel
accepted, loved, and wanted.
I have enjoyed an incredible life serving Jehovah.
Decades later, my father was baptized as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Jehovah has been so kind to me,
my family, and my siblings.
Truly, I have no way to repay Jehovah for the life he’s given me.
I’ve had so many blessings in my life: a wonderful wife
and great friends,
including those that I serve
alongside of in Bethel.
I’m not on my own anymore.
Jehovah has given me a life full of real meaning, purpose,
and so much happiness.

cn.text: 每个人都想要有一个快乐的童年
但我没有
因为我爸爸有酗酒的习惯
没有人喜欢
这样的童年
有一天，我们的亲戚从美国来看我们
他们看起来好快乐
他们之间的互动充满欢笑
好像
没有经济压力，过着幸福的生活
我们家过得好辛苦
但是他们看起来好快乐
我希望跟他们一样，也可以有快乐的生活
后来我9岁的时候
我离开了我的妈妈
和其他的家人
越过边境去了美国
我那时住的地方，环境很不好
所以我加入了一个拳击社，学习保护自己
我的训练员叫做李奥
他就像我爸爸一样
他教了我们很多事情
雷蒙德也是拳击社的
他是我的好朋友
我们相处得非常好
他很尊重我，也很照顾我
跟拳击社这些朋友在一起的这几年
我感觉他们就像我的家人一样
其实，我还蛮羡慕雷蒙德的
他因为贩毒赚了很多钱，生活过得很好
我知道这样是不对的
不过后来我也跟他一样开始贩毒
有一天
雷蒙德去交货的时候
他被人谋杀了
我心想，下一个被杀的可能是我
那时，我已经有6年没见到妈妈和弟弟妹妹了
我妈妈正在跟耶和华见证人学习圣经
这帮助她应付很多难题
学习圣经带给她内心安宁
她变得好快乐
我现在知道，这才是我真正需要的
我想起了我那些拳击社的朋友
我觉得
他们也需要认识圣经
知道为什么生活有那么多难题
所以我回到美国去找他们
但是他们都不感兴趣
我的训练员李奥
他告诉我，我不用再卖毒品了
他会帮助我成为一个职业拳击手
这样我就能赚钱，照顾我的家人了
他甚至给我起了个别名，叫做
圣经小子
但我知道这不会真正解决问题
圣经才能够帮助我
所以我下定决心
我要崇拜耶和华
我回到墨西哥
我开始学习圣经，改变我的生活
我把耶和华看作是我的爸爸
因为他帮助我、安慰我，让我不再感到痛苦
有真正的内心安宁
我感觉自己被认可、被爱、被重视
崇拜耶和华让我的生活更有意义，也更快乐
许多年后
我的爸爸受浸，成为耶和华见证人
耶和华一直很照顾我
也照顾我的父母和弟弟妹妹
真的，耶和华给我太多，我永远也报答不完
耶和华赐给我很多福分
一个非常好的妻子，很棒的朋友
包括那些跟我一起在伯特利服务的弟兄姐妹
我再也不是孤单一个人了
耶和华给了我一个人生目标
让我过有意义的生活
我现在真的很快乐

title: 말루 모크: 여호와께서 우리를 받아들여 주실 거예요

ko.text: 우리 가족은 자연과 함께 많은 시간을 보냈어요.
제가 계속 진리 안에 있게 도와 달라고
제 심정을 담아 편지를 많이 썼습니다.
저는 아무도 보고 싶지 않을 때도 있었지만,
제가 할 수 있는 최선을 다했어요.
지금은 엄마랑 같이 여호와를 섬길 수 있어서 정말 기뻐요.
저는 늘 다윗왕에게서 많은 걸 배워요.

en.text: My name is Malu Mørch.
No one can imagine
how much Jehovah has helped me.
I was raised in Sisimiut in Greenland.
My childhood was wonderful.
We were very often out in nature.
In the summer, we sailed.
And in the winter, we rode dog sledge
and we went hunting and fishing.
When I was a child, I was very close to my parents.
I was a “daddy’s girl.”
He called me “My Beloved,”
so “Beloved” became my nickname.
It has been so wonderful to be raised in the truth.
The greatest gift that I could get
is to know Jehovah through them.
When I was nine years old, my parents got divorced.
It was terrible.
I saw how my siblings were hurt.
It cannot be explained how— I mean, we were very wounded in our hearts.
When my parents divorced, my father was disfellowshipped.
It was very hard to be separated like that.
I missed my dad a lot.
When my mom started to drink,
I also felt abandoned.
Because I knew what she had been doing, I was not surprised when,
after some time, she was disfellowshipped.
But, of course, I felt very hurt and sad.
I supplicated Jehovah to help me stay in the truth.
The pioneer sister who studied with me helped me a lot.
She studied with me and sometimes took me
in the ministry and invited me to dinner.
When I was about 12 years old,
my father came back into the truth.
I was very happy that it finally happened.
I began to have a good relationship with him again.
We sailed a lot, drove snowmobiles, and rode dog sledge,
and my father and I watched movies in the evening.
I remember that when my dad heard that I was going to be baptized,
he shed a tear, and I could see that he was proud.
When I was 15 years old,
my world fell to pieces.
My father committed suicide.
It’s difficult to describe that my father was suddenly gone.
I can’t understand
why he would do such a selfish thing.
I missed him a lot.
It was like my heart was stabbed.
I was also very angry at him.
I wrote a lot.
And I wrote many letters to my father
about things that I wanted to tell him.
I also cried out to Jehovah in long prayers.
I love Psalm 34:18
about Jehovah being close to “those who are crushed in spirit.”
That was how I felt.
And the thought that Jehovah is close to them
comforts me a lot.
I also did all I could to go to all the meetings,
even when I didn’t want to see anyone.
Even if I had cried before the meeting,
I went anyway.
One month after my father’s death, I got baptized.
I got baptized because I loved Jehovah.
When I was nine years old, I had promised Jehovah
to serve him for the rest of my life.
My relationship with my mother is much better now.
It is great to serve Jehovah together with her now.
We preach together every Sunday,
and I always look forward to going in the ministry together with her.
When I was 18 years old,
I began to help in the remote translation office.
Later, I started pioneering.
I have always learned a lot from King David.
No matter what circumstances he faced,
whether bad or good, he used them to draw close to Jehovah.
Jehovah has helped me to overcome
challenges through the congregation,
giving me “power beyond what is normal”
and taking me in as his daughter.

cn.text: 我叫马卢·默克
如果没有耶和华，就没有现在的我
我在格陵兰长大，是大自然的孩子
童年过得很快乐
夏天我们会玩帆船，冬天就坐雪橇
也会去打猎和钓鱼
小时候，父母非常爱我
爸爸常常叫我“宝贝”
所以“宝贝”就成了我的小名
父母给我的最好的礼物
就是帮助我认识耶和华
这真的是一件很幸福的事
在我九岁那年，父母离婚了
我受到很大的打击，我姐姐和弟弟也很受伤
我没办法形容我们受到的伤害有多大
父母离婚后，爸爸也被开除了
跟爸爸分开的日子，我真的好难过
我好想他
后来我妈妈开始酗酒，我感觉好像被抛弃了
我知道她做的是什么事
所以当她被开除的时候，我并不惊讶
但我还是非常难过
我恳求耶和华让我不要放弃真理
我的圣经老师给了我很大的帮助
她是一位先驱
有时候会带我出去传道
也会邀请我一起吃饭
12岁的时候，我爸爸重新被会众接纳
他能回来，我真的太高兴了
我们又回到了从前
我们一起玩帆船、骑雪地摩托车、坐雪橇
也会一起看电影
我告诉爸爸我要受浸的时候，他流下了眼泪
我能看出他有多么高兴
可是没过多久，我的世界就塌了
我爸爸在我15岁那一年自杀了
他的死太突然了，好像是晴天霹雳
我真的不明白他为什么做那么自私的事
我好想他
我的心好像都被撕碎了一样
我对爸爸真的好失望
我写了很多日记
把想要对爸爸说的话都写了下来
我也常常哭着向耶和华恳切祷告
耶和华拯救心灵伤痛的人
这就是我的亲身感受
一想到耶和华离我很近，就给我很大的安慰
我也尽一切努力去参加聚会
甚至在我不想见人的时候也是一样
有时我刚刚哭过，可是我还是会去参加聚会
我爸爸去世一个月后，我受浸了
我受浸是因为我深爱耶和华
我九岁的时候就向耶和华承诺
我要永永远远崇拜他
现在我跟妈妈的关系非常好
我们一起崇拜耶和华真的很幸福
每个星期天，我们都会一起传道
我总是很期待，跟妈妈一起传道的那一天
我18岁的时候，开始在远程翻译处服务
后来我开始做正规先驱
我从大卫王学到很多
不管他遇到什么情况，顺境还是逆境
他都当作是亲近耶和华的好机会
耶和华通过会众
帮助我克服了许许多多的挑战
也收留我，把我当作他的女儿
还赐给我“非凡的力量”

titles.ko: 말루 모크: 여호와께서 우리를 받아들여 주실 거예요
titles.en: Malu Mørch: Jehovah Will Take You In
titles.cn: 马卢·默克：耶和华收留了我

ko.text: 그때 제가 세 들어 살던 집의 주인이
여호와의 증인과 성서 연구를 하고 있었습니다.
그분에 관해 더 배우고 싶었기 때문에
아들은 제가 꼭 참석했으면 좋겠다고 말했습니다.
남녀노소 할 것 없이 모여 있었습니다.
진정으로 기쁨과 만족감을 느끼는 걸 보면서
‘이게 바로 내가 찾던 거구나’ 하는 생각이 들었습니다.
그리고 초대장 배부 활동이 있을 때마다

en.text: I came to Greece as an immigrant when I was just 16 years old.
Because of that, I never felt safe
with people around me.
At that time, I was renting
an apartment from a man who was studying the Bible
with one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
One day I joined the study,
and the brother invited me to the convention.
I was very cautious at the beginning, but the brother seemed trustworthy.
I always had questions about the true God,
and I wanted to learn more about Him, so I decided to go.
I received an invitation
from my son to attend
the convention of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
He was getting baptized at that convention,
and it was important to him for me to be there,
and so he asked me to go.
Even though I was very active in another religion for 30 years,
I went in order to please him.
I learned the truth after I supplicated God with all my strength
because I was really lost.
I asked for answers to questions
that were yet unanswered.
And God answered me.
Jehovah gave me the answer to my prayers when I found this.
This invitation, “Deliverance at Hand!,” was the answer to my prayers.
Arriving there, at that convention, I observed the crowd—many people.
Starting right at the parking lot,
everything was organized; people were entering in an orderly manner.
Inside the Assembly Hall, everyone was very organized,
well-dressed, very loving.
And when the convention began,
I saw such spiritual food that I had never seen in my religion.
Thirty years in a religion —I thought I knew a lot,
but I didn’t know anything.
So I decided to study.
When I arrived at the convention, I started watching the people.
Their faces were smiling.
They seemed to be happy.
There were men, women, and children from different races and nationalities.
When they sang, I could sense their true joy and unity.
For the first time in my life, I felt very safe.
I was not in fear of being taken advantage of.
Also, what I learned at that convention
drew me to the true God.
I thought, ‘If all these people
‘are truly happy and feel really safe being part of this organization
‘—Jehovah’s organization—
then, indeed, this is what I was looking for.’
I went to the convention on Sunday.
I was really warmly welcomed by all the brothers and sisters there.
I listened to all of the morning program,
and at noon, I recognized the sound of the truth.
I was sure it was the truth.
I decided to become one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
and I became one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
I got baptized in 2017, and now I serve as a pioneer.
My first study was the following Wednesday.
I was happy to get to know Jehovah.
Now I am one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
and as much as I can, I participate in the invitation campaigns.
I really hope that it helps many people to be delivered.
I started attending meetings right after the convention.
I started a Bible study, and eventually I got baptized
as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
My mother, one of my brothers,
and my two sisters are now serving Jehovah as well.
Later on, I got married to a faithful sister,
a very good wife, and we serve Jehovah together.
People need to feel safe,
and I know for sure that Jehovah’s organization is the safest place you can be.

cn.text: 我16岁的时候移民来希腊
因为我是个外国人
我担心自己被别人欺负或被别人利用
那个时候我租了一个房子
房东刚好正在跟耶和华见证人学习圣经
有一天，我加入了他们的讨论
然后，那个弟兄就邀请我参加大会
刚开始，我有一点犹豫也很担心
不过他看起来很正直很诚恳
关于上帝，我其实一直有很多问题
我很想多认识上帝
所以我答应他，就去参加大会
在2016年，我儿子给了我一张
耶和华见证人的区域大会邀请函
他会在这个大会受浸
他希望我去
因为受浸对他来说非常重要
虽然这三十年来我都有自己的信仰
但是为了让他高兴，我还是去了
我本来很空虚
因为很多人生的问题我找不到答案
后来我就很努力地跟上帝祷告
上帝真的回应我了
耶和华给我的答案就是
让我收到这张“得救在望”区域大会的邀请函
这就是我要的答案
到了大会场
从停车场开始
一路上我看到了好多好多人
一切都安排得井井有条
每个人都非常守秩序
会场里的人也都规规矩矩的
穿的也很端庄，每个人都很友善
节目开始后
我听到了很多我从来没有听过的圣经真理
我信教信了三十年了
我以为我什么都知道，但我其实都不知道
所以我决定开始学习圣经
我到了大会场
我开始观察我身边的人
他们的脸上都有笑容，看起来好快乐
他们来自不同的国家、不同的种族
有男有女，有大人也有小孩
他们唱歌的时候
我感觉到他们真的很快乐、很团结
这是我生平第一次感觉到很安全
在这里，我不用担心被别人利用、被别人欺负
而且我在大会里所学到的
让我更想进一步认识这位上帝
我心里就在想
如果这群人真的那么快乐
跟他们在一起我又有安全感
快乐和安全感不就是我一直想要的吗？
那我是不是该成为他们的一分子呢？
我去参加了星期天的大会
弟兄姐妹都非常温暖地欢迎我
我很认真地听完早上所有的节目后
我发现这就是真理的声音
我非常确定，这就是真理
后来我决定成为耶和华见证人
而我也真的成为了耶和华见证人
我在2017年受浸，现在是个先驱
大会后的星期三我就开始学习圣经
我很高兴可以认识耶和华
现在我也是耶和华见证人了
我也努力多参加分发邀请函的特别活动
我真的希望可以有更多人收到邀请函
大会结束后
我开始参加聚会而且也开始学习圣经
我继续进步
后来我就受浸成为耶和华见证人
现在我的妈妈，还有一个弟弟
另外两个妹妹
也都是耶和华见证人了
后来我跟一个忠贞的姐妹结婚了
她是一个很好的妻子
现在我们一起崇拜耶和华
每个人都需要有安全感
而我确定只有在耶和华的组织里
我们才会得到真正的安全感

titles.cn: 找出珍宝般的人

title: 존 에크란: 여호와의 손길을 느끼고 있습니까? (이사야 66:14)

ko.text: 누군가 성서 연구를 하고 싶어 하거나
집회에 처음 참석했을 때 그런 생각이 들죠.
우리나 형제 자매들에게 좋지 않은 일이 일어날 때는
어떻게 여호와의 손길을 느낄 수 있을까요?
지금, 다들 제 손이 잘 보이시나요?
손이 아직도 붙어 있다고 생각하실 겁니다.
곰곰이 생각해 봐야 할 때도 있습니다.
여호와에 대해 알고 있는 어떤 사실을 근거로
그분이 “행복하신 하느님”이라는 점에 대해 생각해 보죠.
여호와께선 그 모든 나쁜 일을 보시면서
우리는 고통받는 형제들의 소식을 들으면 가슴이 아프죠.
지진에 관해 듣게 될 때 말입니다.
‘여호와께서는 이 모든 일이 일어나는 걸 아시면서 어떻게 행복하실 수 있을까?’
행복하실 수 있는 많은 이유 중 세 가지와
그분은 우리를 위해 신세계를 열심히 준비하고 계십니다.
어떤 생각을 가지고 계신지 잘 보여 줍니다.
“‘내가 너희에 대해 갖고 있는 생각을 나는 잘 알고 있다.’
너희가 미래와 희망을 갖게 하려는 것이다.’”
그러니까 여호와께서는 이 모든 일을 지켜보고만 계신 것이 아니라,
예수와 하늘의 천사들과 함께 왕국을 위해
물론 우리는 지금 하늘에서 무슨 일이 있는지 볼 수는 없지만,
얼마나 분주하게 일하고 있는지 상상해 볼 수 있습니다.
우리가 연례 총회와 봉헌식 준비에도 많은 일을 하는데,
현재 하늘에서는 얼마나 많은 일을 하고 있겠습니까?
생존자들을 위해 꼭 필요한 깨끗한 물,
거기서 그분의 손길이 작용하고 있다는 걸 압니다.
네, 여호와께서는 우리를 위해 활동적으로 일하고 계시기 때문에 행복하십니다.
우리는 고통스러운 일을 보더라도 행복할 수 있습니다.
지금 우리를 위로하실 수 있기 때문입니다.
여호와께서 우리 미래를 위해 일한다고 하신 후에 말씀하시죠.
“너희는 나를 부르며 와서 나에게 기도할 것이고,
나는 너희의 말을 들어 줄 것이다.”
너에게 행복한 미래를 가져다 주마’라고 하신 것도 감사하죠.
“앞으로 모든 게 좋아질 때를 생각해 봐.
여호와께서 이런 상황을 다 바꿔 주실 거야”라고 하면,
그 친구가 이렇게 말할 때도 위로가 됩니다.
그분은 우리를 위로하고 돕고 싶어 하십니다.
어린 아이를 대하는 부모의 예를 생각해 보겠습니다.
무릎에서 시뻘건 피가 흘러나오는 걸 보고는
하지만 부모가 보는 시각은 다르지 않습니까?
무릎이 까진 것은 까마득한 일이 되어
아이가 기억조차 못 할 걸 알기 때문이죠.
현재 우리가 무슨 일을 겪고 있든지,
우리가 그 고통을 기억조차 못 할 것을 아십니다.
우리가 영원히 살게 된다는 것도 알고 계십니다.
우리도 남을 위로하고 도울 수 있습니다.
신세계로 가려고 힘쓰면서 서로 도와야 합니다.
여호와께선 행동할 적절한 때를 참을성 있게 기다리십니다.
“주권 쟁점에 계속 초점을 맞추십시오” 기사에 이런 좋은 말이 나왔죠.
여호와의 주권의 입증이라는 매우 중요한 쟁점을 잊어서는 안 됩니다.
여호와의 주권을 지지한다는 것을 나타내야 합니다.”
이런 일을 겪지 않을 것을 아십니다.
주권 쟁점 문제가 완전히 해결될 것입니다.
우리 형제 자매들과 많은 사람들이 겪는
한 남편은 아내가 숨을 헐떡이며 괴로워하는 걸 봅니다.
그 순간 우린 신세계로 바로 가는 버튼이라도 있다면
“여호와의 종들은 그의 손을 알게” 될 것입니다.
여호와의 주권 쟁점에 계속 초점을 맞춰야 합니다.
이제 세 가지 요점을 복습해 보죠.
주위의 모든 고통을 보면서도 행복할 수 있을까요?
우린 여호와와 예수와 부활된 기름부음받은 자들이
지금 신세계를 열심히 준비한다는 것을 알기에 행복합니다.
위로하고 도울 수 있기 때문에 행복합니다.
또한 우리는 참을성을 보일 수 있어서 행복합니다.
우리는 여호와의 주권 쟁점 문제에 초점을 맞춥니다.
우리가 항상 여호와의 손길을 느낄 수는 없을지 몰라도,
분명 우리는 그 사실을 알게 될 것입니다.

en.text: Sometimes, I think all of us would agree
that it’s easy to see Jehovah’s hand
when things are going well
—when we get a court victory,
when someone’s health improves,
or maybe when someone really asked
to come to study the Bible with us and they’re at our meetings.
But it’s harder to see Jehovah’s hand when we see bad things happen
either to us or to our brothers and sisters.
So we may wonder, ‘How can we see Jehovah’s hand
when bad things are happening?’
Well, you can see my hand right now, right?
But if I put it away, you can’t see it.
Now, do you assume that because you can’t see my hand
that I don’t have a hand anymore?
Well, no.
You reason on the fact that since you see the rest of me,
and there’s probably still my hand attached.
So likewise, there are times when it’s easy to see Jehovah’s hand,
and there are other times when we have to reason
on what we know about Jehovah in order to see his hand in action.
So let’s consider one thing.
What do we know about Jehovah
so that we could reason that his hand is in action?
Well, let’s reason on the point that he is a “happy God.”
Now, how does Jehovah stay happy,
seeing all the bad things that are happening?
Maybe you’ve wondered that. I know it’s crossed my mind.
How does Jehovah stay happy
when he sees all the suffering that’s going on?
And frankly, he sees all  the suffering;
he sees everything going on.
I know how I feel, and you probably know how you feel
just when you read about what’s happening
to our brothers in Venezuela or in Russia
or with all of the hurricanes
and earthquakes that we’ve had in recent times.
And we see the suffering
not only of our brothers and sisters but also of other people,
and we consider,
‘How can Jehovah stay happy when he knows all of what is happening?’
Well, let’s consider three (I’m sure) of many reasons
why Jehovah can stay happy even though he knows all the suffering.
And then we can see how that could benefit us as well.
First of all,
his hand is hard at work preparing the new world for us.
And I think Jeremiah 29:11
really covers how Jehovah feels
about the future for us.
At Jeremiah 29:11, he says:
“‘For I well know the thoughts that I am thinking toward you,’
“declares Jehovah, ‘thoughts of peace, and not of calamity,
to give you a future and a hope.’”
So Jehovah is not simply just watching events occur.
He’s actively working on the solution.
He, along with Jesus and the heavenly angels,
is working hard on the Kingdom.
Now, we can’t see into heaven right now,
but I want you to just imagine all the activity of the angels,
the resurrected anointed brothers,
and Jesus working hard on making preparations
for Armageddon and the new world.
Just think of all the work we’re doing just to prepare
for the annual meeting and dedication.
Can you imagine all the work going on in heaven that is there?
I mean, how far along are the new scrolls?
How are our basic needs as far as clean water,
food, and homes going to be provided for the survivors?
So while we can’t see into heaven,
we know that his hand is there.
So Jehovah is happy because he’s actively working right now
to make things better for us.
What is the lesson for us?
We can be happy when we see the suffering around us
because we know what Jehovah and our brothers are doing up there
to prepare for the new world.
A second point about how Jehovah can be happy
is that he can comfort us right now.
He is happy when he can do that.
In verse 12 of Jeremiah chapter 29,
Jehovah continued after saying that he was working on the future (he says):
“And you will call me and come and pray to me,
and I will listen to you.”
So I love this point because Jehovah is saying,
‘Don’t worry; I’m taking care of building a better future for you.’
And we appreciate it.
If we’re going through some trial —some difficulty—
and a good friend of ours reminds us,
“Remember things are going to get better in the future;
Jehovah is going to change this; it’s going to get better,”
it is comforting.
But it is also comforting (like Jehovah says here in verse 12)
when the person says, “What can I do for you right now?”
And Jehovah is saying right now, ‘Come, pray to me.’
Jehovah is there to comfort and help us.
We could kind of illustrate the way Jehovah feels
by thinking about parents and how they deal with a small child.
Have you ever seen a small child, maybe two or three years of age,
and they fall really badly and scrape their knees badly,
and they are screaming in pain?
There’s this red liquid leaking out of them.
They are distraught.
In fact, in that child’s mind,
he may think: ‘This is the end of it. This is the end of my life as I know it.
‘I’m never going to recover from this.
I’m going to die.’
But for the parents, of course, their perspective is different, isn’t it?
But they comfort the child; they help to take care of the skinned knee.
They comfort them, and they tell them: “You’re going to live.
It’s going to be OK. It’s going to be all right.”
And why can the parent have that view?
Because they know that in a few hours maybe
(at least in a week or so),
the child is not even going to remember that skinned knee.
It’s going to be just a very distant memory.
Well, Jehovah also knows that whatever we’re going through right now
—whatever suffering we may be going through now—
that soon in that new world, we aren’t going to recall that suffering.
And he knows that he can solve any problem we’re facing
as easily as we heal from a scraped knee.
He knows our whole eternal lives are ahead of us.
So he comforts us; he listens to our heartfelt prayers.
And like a kind parent, he’s telling us
(through our brothers, the Bible, and holy spirit),
‘You will live.’
Jehovah is happy because right now, what can he do?
He can comfort us and help us.
Well, what is the lesson for us?
We can comfort and help others.
We’re, really, kind of all in this “lifeboat” together,
trying to make it to the “new-world shore,”
and we can help one another.
Third, his hand is patiently waiting
for the right time to act.
Jehovah is waiting patiently
for the complete vindication of his sovereignty.
I really love what the June 2017 Watchtower  article
“Keep Your Eyes on the Big Issue” said:
“Let us not become so absorbed in our own lives
“that we lose sight of this big issue
“—the vindication of Jehovah’s sovereignty.
“And let us appreciate that our role in this vital issue
“entails remaining faithful
even under difficult circumstances.”
Isn’t that a beautiful quote to think about?
Jehovah knows that by his being patient now,
he and all his faithful servants will never have to go through this again.
The issue of sovereignty will be completely settled.
Don’t you admire Jehovah’s patience?
I mean, to watch all that is happening
and to have the self-control to wait for the appointed time
is truly an example of patience in action.
When we think about the different situations
our brothers and sisters and others face
—when a mother, for example,
watches a handicapped son struggle to walk or to talk
or a husband watches his wife struggle to breathe—
we want so much at that moment
to press that big, red, “start-the-new-world” button now.
But when you have that feeling,
remember our text for today:
“The hand of Jehovah will become known to his servants.”
What is the lesson for us?
We need to be patient
and keep our eyes on the big issue of Jehovah’s sovereignty.
So let’s just review those three points.
How can we see Jehovah’s hand
and be happy when we see all of this suffering around us?
Well, we can be happy knowing
what Jehovah and Jesus and the resurrected anointed
are doing right now to prepare for the new world.
And we can be happy because we have a role
in comforting and helping others.
And we can be happy being patient,
knowing why we’re being patient.
We have our eyes on that big issue of Jehovah’s sovereignty.
We may not always be able to see Jehovah’s hand,
but we can be sure, as our text for today says,
that Jehovah’s hand is there, and it will become known.

cn.text: 我想，有时我们会觉得
生活过得一帆风顺
是因为耶和华伸手帮助我们
例如，我们在法庭上胜诉了
或是某个人的健康状况好转了
又或者，有人愿意跟我们一起学习圣经
而且来参加聚会了
但当坏事发生在我们自己
或弟兄姐妹身上的时候
我们就可能觉得耶和华没有帮助我们
这时我们可能会想
耶和华的手在哪里呢？
你们可以看到我的手，对吧？
但当我把手放下来，你们就看不到了
不过，你们会因为
没有看到我的手就认为我没有手吗？
当然不会！
因为你们看得到我的手臂
所以可以推测出我的手其实还在
同样，有时我们比较容易看见耶和华的手
但有时，我们必须好好思考
才能看出耶和华的手一直在帮助我们
所以，让我们想想一件事
为什么我们能够确定
耶和华的手一直在帮助我们呢？
圣经说耶和华是“快乐的上帝”
为什么呢？
耶和华看见这么多坏事不断发生
为什么还能快乐呢？
也许你想过这个问题
我也想过！
耶和华每天看见这么多坏事发生
他看见地上的所有苦难
看见地上发生的所有事情
那上帝为什么还能快乐呢？
当你知道在委内瑞拉以及俄罗斯发生的事
或是最近飓风和地震造成的灾害
你一定很难过
有这么多的苦难发生在弟兄姐妹身上
也发生在其他人身上
我们就会想，耶和华看到这么多坏事
为什么他还能保持喜乐呢？
原因有很多
但现在让我们谈谈其中三个
我们可以从中学到很多
首先
耶和华正辛勤地为未来的新世界做准备
在耶利米书29:11这节经文告诉我们
耶和华希望我们有怎样的未来
耶利米书29:11
耶和华说
“我很清楚我想要为你们做什么
我要赐安宁，不是降灾祸
要让你们有前途有希望。”
所以，耶和华不是眼睁睁地看着事情发生
其实他正积极地采取行动，指引事情的发展
他和耶稣还有天使们
正在为未来的新世界做准备
当然，我们看不到天上正在发生的事
但我希望你们想象一下
天使、复活到天上去的人和耶稣
他们在天上正努力地为哈米吉多顿
和未来的地上乐园做准备
再请你想一想
光是准备年会和新的世界总部的呈献礼
我们就已经忙得不可开交了
那么，何况是天上的工作呢？
也许他们正在写新的书卷？
在为渡过大患难的人准备生活必需品
可能是干净的水、食物还有房屋
虽然我们不知道天上有多忙碌
但我们知道上帝一直在工作
耶和华一直勤奋工作
他想给我们一个更好的未来，所以他很快乐
我们学到什么呢？
虽然我们看到世界充满各种灾难
我们还是能够保持喜乐
因为我们知道
耶和华正在为未来的新世界做准备
第二个原因是
耶和华能为我们带来安慰，所以他很快乐
每当他安慰人，他都会很快乐
耶和华说完他为将来的新世界做的准备后
在耶利米书29:12，他继续说
“你们会来呼求我，向我祷告，我也会垂听。”
我很喜欢这节经文
耶和华好像在说
你放心，我正在为你准备一个美好的未来
我们非常感激耶和华，是吗？
如果我们正在面对一些挑战、难题
一位好朋友提醒我们
“情况会越来越好的，耶和华一定会帮助你的！”
这真的很安慰人
如果朋友说：“我可以为你做什么呢？”
这也很安慰人
耶和华也同样说
“来呼求我，向我祷告吧！”
耶和华随时能安慰和帮助我们
耶和华会怎样安慰我们呢？
我们可以拿父母对待孩子的方式来做个例子
你看过大概两岁或三岁的小孩跌倒吗？
他的膝盖受伤了，伤得很严重
然后他开始嚎啕大哭
接着他发现他的膝盖流血了
他开始乱想，然后说
“糟了，我的伤口不会好的
我快死了，我真的快死了！”
但父母会这样想吗？
不会！
他们会安慰孩子，在他们的伤口涂上药
温柔地对他们说
“没问题的，你很快就会好起来的。”
为什么父母会这样想呢？
因为他们知道不久后，伤口就会愈合
孩子也会很快忘记曾经受伤这件事
同样，耶和华也知道
现在我们面对的伤痛很快就会过去
因为新世界就要到了
到时，我们就会忘记这些伤痛
就像伤口一定会复原一样
耶和华也一定会解决所有难题
他知道我们有永生的希望
他会安慰我们，也会垂听我们的祷告
就像慈父一样
他可能通过弟兄姐妹
圣经或是神圣力量对我们说
“你会永远活着！”
耶和华非常高兴
因为他现在就能够安慰和帮助我们
我们学习到什么呢？
我们好像在一艘“救生艇”上
奋力向着新世界的岸边前进
所以，现在我们必须互相安慰和帮助
第三个原因是
上帝一直等待指定的时间来到
到时他就会采取行动，维护他的至高统治权
我非常喜欢2017年6月刊的一篇《守望台》文章
题目是〈专注于更重要的事〉
文章说，千万不要因为专注于自己的难题
而忘了全力支持上帝的至高统治权
我们面对逆境仍对上帝忠心耿耿
就是拥护上帝的统治了
这句话值得我们好好想想
耶和华知道，现在他耐心等候
将来就不会再看到他的忠仆受苦受难了
到时，至高统治权的争论会被彻底解决
我们很感激上帝一直表现耐心
上帝看着这么多坏事发生，却要表现自制
等候指定的时间来到
这真的不简单，实在让我们感到敬佩！
请想象一下
一个做母亲的，看着自己伤残的儿子
费劲地走路或说话
一个做丈夫的
看着自己连呼吸都很困难的妻子受尽折磨
看到这么多人面对这么多难题
我们多么想现在就按下通往新世界的按钮
如果你也有这样的感觉
请记住今天的经文，经文说
“耶和华要向自己的仆人显示他的力量”
我们学习到什么？
我们要有耐心
将焦点集中在上帝的至高统治权上
因为这才是最重要的
好！
我们来复习一下今天的要点
我们怎样看出耶和华的手在帮助我们
而且我们也能保持喜乐呢？
首先，我们知道
耶和华、耶稣和复活到天上去的人
正在为将来的新世界做准备
其次，我们也很高兴
因为我们有机会安慰和帮助遭遇患难的人
最后，我们也很高兴的原因是

专注于更重要的事

耶和华会显示他的力量，伸手帮助他的仆人

title: 증오가 가득한 세상에서 진정한 사랑을 찾을 수 있는가?

en.text: I am full-blooded Cherokee.
We were Indians, but yet we couldn’t be Indians
in the white man’s world.
And now you’re telling me I’ve got to go fight your war.
I was drafted during the Vietnam era.
When I got out, I was very angry at the government.
I heard about this militant group of natives
who were fighting for their rights.
Protesting was a way of letting people know
that we were not going to stand for this any longer.
I grew up in Ireland in a family of ten.
We were Catholic and very poor.
At 16, I joined the army.
At school, we learned all about nationalism
and the 800 years of fighting between the English and the Irish.
When the conflict started in Northern Ireland,
that had a tremendous effect on our lives.
When I saw something happening
and I saw foreign soldiers
killing my people, fellow Catholics,
I felt I had to engage
and defend them against the British establishment.
My wife started studying.
I said: “They are coming here and are going to Christianize us and civilize us,”
and “Don’t bring those Bible-toting white people around me.
I don’t want their religion.”
After Nancy started studying,
she decided to get baptized.
So the sisters said, “Are you taking her to the assembly?”
And I told them; I said, “Nah, I’m going to stay home.”
So the sisters, you know, said,
“Well, who is going to watch the baby while she’s getting baptized?”
I said, “Oh, yeah, maybe I should go.”
The way they treated each other with respect
—one wasn’t on this side and the other on this side.
They were all together.
They didn’t just walk by and ignore me.
They brought people over and introduced them to me.
They spoke with sincerity.
I thought: ‘This is the way the world should be.
This is the way people should live.’
I’m currently serving as an elder
in the Illinois River Cherokee Congregation of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
I have the privilege of teaching these ones who have moved here
to learn the Cherokee language so that they can teach them the good news.
There is no other love—nowhere.
This love is genuine.
I was in a car accident and nearly died.
I started to drink because I couldn’t cope with my situation.
I did expect that my comrades in the Republican movement
might have come to help us, but they didn’t come at all.
I was studying the Bible three weeks with one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
He was very English, and his wife, so English.
I wouldn’t have chosen them to have come into my house,
but they did, and they were lovely.
Nobody came to see me—only the brother.
He would come regularly.
And that to me was a godsend
—that someone cared about me.
And I thought: ‘Wow!
Everyone who is fighting for justice in the world needn’t fight.’
And that went right through my heart.
Sometimes when I meet ex-British soldiers in the truth,
I say to them, “We’re in the same army now, brother.”
The only place we can find love and friendship
and companionship is in Jehovah’s organization.

cn.text: 我是印第安人，是切罗基族
我们在白人的世界里处处受限
不能做真正的印第安人
越战爆发时，又被迫上战场为白人打仗
之后我离开了部队
我非常愤怒，痛恨政府！
当时有一个由印第安人组成的激进团体
为印第安人争取权益
我们会通过示威来抗争
让政府知道我们不是弱者
不会再让他们压迫我们
我在爱尔兰长大
我们家有十个人，都是天主教徒
我们家很穷
我在16岁的时候加入军队
在学校，我们接受爱国主义教育
也知道英国和爱尔兰
在长达八百年的时间里一直冲突不断
北爱尔兰和英国爆发冲突
我们的生活受到很大的影响
我看见周围发生的一切
看见那些天主教同胞被外国士兵杀害
就觉得自己必须站出来保护他们
对抗英国政府
我妻子开始学习圣经
我对她说，他们是想改造我们
要把我们变成基督徒
那些白人传教士最好离我远一点
我不会信他们的宗教
后来我妻子南希决定受浸
姐妹问我，你会跟她一起参加大会吗？
我说，不会，我不去
姐妹说，那南希受浸的时候
谁帮她照顾宝宝？
我说，啊对啊，那我得去
我发现他们很团结，而且会互相尊重
不会只跟肤色一样的人来往
不少人会来跟我打招呼
介绍新朋友给我认识
没有把我晾在一边
他们很真诚
当时我想，人跟人相处
本来就该这样
世界本来就该是这个样子！
现在，我在切罗基河会众以长老的身份服务
有些传道员很想向说切罗基语的人传道
所以就搬了过来
我很高兴教他们我的母语
他们表现了真正的爱心
这在任何地方都找不到
后来我出车祸，差点死了
我不知道该怎么面对我的处境
只好用酒精麻痺自己
我以为我那些爱尔兰共和军的兄弟们
会来看我们
但他们一个都没来
我和一个耶和华见证人学习圣经
学了三个星期
他是个地地道道的英国人，他的妻子也是
按理来说，我根本不会让他们进我的家
但我很喜欢他们，还是让他们进来了
那阵子，他们常常来看我
这是个意外的礼物
没想到还有人在乎我
圣经让我明白
我们不需要为了争取公平正义而拿起武器
我的心被深深触动了
有时候我会遇到一些弟兄
他们以前是英国士兵
我会对他们说
我们现在是同一阵线，并肩作战了！
这个世界上只有耶和华的组织
能让我们找到真正的爱心和友谊

title: 프란시스쿠 리베이루: 교도소에 들어가 자유를 얻었습니다

ko.text: 저는 진리 안에서 태어나, 열네 살 때 전도인이 되었습니다.
하지만 그 후 일 년도 채 못 되어 전도인 자격을 잃었죠.
열대여섯 살부터 도둑질과 마약 밀매를 하게 되었어요.
교도소 안에서도 나쁜 짓을 많이 했죠.
그 안에서 저랑 싸우지 않은 사람은 없을 겁니다.
뭔가 웃을 일이나 기분 좋을 이유가 생긴다 해도 잠시뿐이었죠.
수감돼 있다는 현실을 깨닫는 순간, 기쁨이 사라져 버리거든요.
갈수록 상황이 악화되는 게 제 자신 때문임을 알게 됐습니다.
그러고 나서, 므낫세에 관한 기록이 떠올랐는데,
자기 자녀를 제물로 희생한 사람인데도 여호와의 용서를 받았죠.
저도 희망이 있고 용서받을 수 있다는 걸 이해할 수 있었습니다.
재소자를 만나러 온 사람들 가운데 형제처럼 보이는 사람이 있었어요.
혹시 여호와의 증인이냐고 물어보았더니, 그렇다는 겁니다.
그때부터 교도소 안에서 성서 연구를 했습니다.
거기선 낮에 일하고 밤에는 교도소에 돌아왔습니다.
그런데 그때 전 다시 나쁜 습관에 빠지기 시작했죠.
이대로 가다가는 마약 때문에 죽을 것만 같았습니다.
차라리 여기서 도망가는 게 낫겠다는 결론을 내렸습니다.
다시 변화하고 여호와의 도움을 구하고 집회에 참석하기로 결심했어요.
종종 마약을 피우다 이렇게 울며 기도하곤 했죠.
당신의 이름을 아는 사람이 마약을 사용해서는 안 되는 거잖아요!”
우리 집 근처에 있는 왕국회관에서 집회가 열린다는 걸 알게 됐습니다.
제가 법적으로 어떤 상황에 있는지 연구 사회자에게 밝히지 않았습니다.
장로들과 함께 만나는 날, 형제가 몇 가지 질문을 하잖아요.
그 질문들을 다 검토했을 때, 형제가 저를 쳐다보면서 이렇게 물었습니다.
“왜 이 질문을 하는지 아세요? 사도행전 5장을 같이 한번 보시면 좋겠네요.”
그래서 아나니아와 삽비라에 대한 기록을 읽었는데,
그들은 땅을 팔아서 돈 얼마를 감췄고, 그런 행동 때문에 죽었습니다.
그들은 사람한테 거짓말을 한 게 아니라 여호와께 거짓말을 한 겁니다.
그 순간 정신이 번쩍 들면서, 제 상황을 밝혀야 한다는 걸 깨달았죠.
저는 자수하고, 도망 나온 교도소로 돌아가야 했습니다.
그래서 연구 사회자에게 그렇게 하겠다고 말했죠.
교도소 정문에 도착했더니, 경찰관이 저를 보고 변호사냐고 묻더군요.
저는 탈옥수인데, 남은 형기를 마치려고 돌아왔습니다.”
제 어깨에 있던 무겁고 커다란 짐을 여호와께서 내려놔 주신 것 같았죠.
그분이 이젠 정말 저를 도와주신다는 걸 느꼈습니다.
교도소 안에서 몇 달 동안 전도인으로 지낸 뒤, 전 여호와께 헌신했습니다.
침례받는 날 교도소 밖으로 나와 침례를 받을 수 있도록 허락을 받았죠.
저는 침례를 받고, 그날 저녁 교도소로 돌아갔습니다.
얼마의 시간이 흐른 뒤, 저는 석방되었습니다.
제가 여호와께 대한 사랑을 나타낼 수 있는 최상의 방법이었습니다.
사실 저는 교도소에서 오히려 자유를 얻었습니다.

en.text: I was born in the truth.
And when I was about 14, I became a publisher.
When I was still 14, I was no longer a publisher.
I became a thief
and a drug dealer when I was a teenager
—around 15 or 16 years old.
When I was older, I was arrested.
I did a lot of bad things inside prison.
I basically fought with everyone in there.
Anything that would make us smile
or any reasons we had to be happy in prison were short-lived.
Your joy is gone because reality hits that you’re in prison.
When I saw that I was the reason that my situation
kept getting worse and worse,
I knew I had to change.
I asked Jehovah for help.
And then I remembered the account of Manasseh,
who sacrificed his own children,
and he was forgiven by Jehovah.
That account really helped me to understand
that there was hope for me
and that I could be forgiven.
And then one day during inmate visitation,
I saw a brother inside there.
And I asked him if he was one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
and he said that he was.
That’s when I started my Bible study inside prison.
After studying for six months,
I was transferred to an open prison
where I could work during the day and return to prison at night.
Then that’s when my situation hit rock bottom again.
My situation was so bad that I came to the conclusion
that it would be better to escape from there because if I didn’t,
I would die because of so much drug abuse.
And that’s what I did.
At the first opportunity I had, I escaped.
After I escaped, I was determined again to change,
to ask Jehovah for help, and to go back to the meetings.
I would smoke, cry, and talk to Jehovah all at the same time:
“Help me get out of this situation because I know your name,
and a person who knows your name can’t use drugs!”
Some time later,
I found out about a group of brothers and sisters
who met at a Kingdom Hall near my house.
That’s when I started attending the meetings again.
I stopped using drugs with Jehovah’s help.
And after some time passed,
I expressed my desire to be a publisher.
Up to this point, I hadn’t told anything to my Bible teacher
about my current situation with the law.
So on the day we considered the questions,
he asked the questions, right?
And when we were at the end of the consideration,
he looked at me and asked me just like this,
“You don’t have anything to tell me, do you?”
Then he said: “Do you know why I’m asking you this?
Turn to the book of Acts chapter 5, and let’s see what it says there.”
So I read the account about Ananias and Sapphira,
who sold some property but kept part of the money,
and because of their actions, they died.
It wasn’t that they had lied to men,
but they had lied to Jehovah.
It was at that moment that I realized
that I needed to tell him about my situation.
I had to turn myself in,
so I went back to the prison that I ran away from.
So I told my Bible teacher that was what I was going to do.
When I arrived at the front door of the penitentiary
and the police officer saw me,
he asked if I was a lawyer.
I was well-dressed and had a tie on.
I told him: “No, no, Officer.
“I’m a fugitive,
and I came back here to serve my time.”
I felt as if Jehovah had taken a huge weight off my shoulders.
I felt that he was now truly helping me.
After being a publisher for a few months back in prison,
I expressed my desire to make a dedication to Jehovah.
I received the privilege on the day of my baptism
to leave the penitentiary and go to the baptism location.
I was baptized, and at the end of the day,
I went back to prison.
After some time had passed, I received my freedom.
Making the decision to turn myself in and go back to prison
was the best way that I found to show my love for Jehovah.
It’s for this reason that I have come to the conclusion
that being imprisoned brought me freedom.

cn.text: 我从小就学习圣经
在我14岁那一年
我成为一个传道员
但也在同一年
我失去了做传道员的资格
我到了青少年时期
大约15、16岁时
我开始偷窃和卖毒品
几年后，我就被警察逮捕了
我在监狱里还是做尽了坏事
基本上，我跟里面所有人都打过架
在监狱里
任何会让你感到开心的事都非常地短暂
因为你知道你没有自由
你还是被关在监狱里
后来我的情况越来越糟糕
而当我知道这一切都是我自己造成的
我就知道我该改变了
我求耶和华帮助我
之后我就想起玛拿西的记载
他用火焚烧自己的孩子，献给假神
但耶和华还是原谅了他
这个记载真的帮助我看出
我在耶和华眼中还是有希望的
耶和华还是会原谅我的
有一天
我看到有一个很像弟兄的人来探监
我问他你是耶和华见证人吗
他说是
从那时候开始
我就在监狱里学习圣经
学习圣经六个月后
我被转送到另一个监狱
在那里，早上我可以出去在外面工作
晚上再回到监狱
不过，我又开始做坏事伤害自己
我的情况越来越糟糕
所以我开始想要逃狱
因为如果我再不离开那里
我一定会吸毒过量而死
后来，一有机会
我就真的逃走了
逃跑后
我又再次下定决心要改变
我求耶和华帮助我
我也想回去参加聚会
我一边抽烟，一边哭着对耶和华说
求你救救我！
因为我认识你
我也知道认识你的人不该吸毒
有一天
我看到一群弟兄姐妹
聚集在我家附近的王国聚会所
所以，后来我就重新开始参加聚会了
有了耶和华的帮助
我成功戒除了毒瘾
过了一段时间
我跟长老说
我想成为一个传道员
但其实我没有跟任何人
包括我的圣经老师说
我从监狱里逃跑的事情
我记得那一天
长老和我快要讨论完问题时
他看着我，问我说
你没有什么事瞒着我，对吧？
你知道为什么我会这样问吗？
你看使徒行传第5章
我们看一个记载
我就打开圣经
那里提到亚拿尼亚和撒非拉说
他们把卖掉自己土地的所有钱都捐出来了
但是他们说谎
他们因为自己的行为被上帝处死了
这件事情的重点是
他们不是欺骗人而是欺骗耶和华
读完经文后
我好像突然清醒过来了
我想我必须告诉长老我的情况
后来我就跟我的圣经老师说
我想要回去自首
回去那个我原本逃跑的监狱
当我到了监狱门口
一个警官看到我
问我说：你是个律师吗？
因为我穿着西装打着领带
但我告诉他：不是不是
其实我原来是个囚犯
但我之前逃狱了
现在我回来认罪了
我终于感受到耶和华在帮助我
他把我肩上的重担都拿走了
在监狱里
我成为未受浸传道员几个月后
我就向上帝祷告说
我要献身给他
我得到监狱的批准
在受浸那天
离开监狱到大会场受浸
受浸结束后
他们就把我送回监狱了
过了一段时间后
我被释放了
想想当初
我决定回到监狱

en.text: Absalom quickly organized
a full-scale conspiracy for the throne.
He forced his own father,
King David, to flee for his life.
While David was traveling through Bahurim,
Shimei began walking along a mountainside.
Ugh!
You bloodguilty man!
Why should this dead dog,
Shimei, curse my lord the king?
Let me go over, please,
and take off his head.
What happened next, Nathan?
Well,
David wasn’t so quick to act.
Leave him alone!
Perhaps Jehovah will see my affliction
and will restore goodness to me.
Mephibosheth
—his grandfather had tried to kill David.
When David became king
and asked Mephibosheth to the palace,
he must have wondered why.
Here is your servant.
Mephibosheth,
do not be afraid,
for I will certainly show loyal love to you
for the sake of your father Jonathan,
and I will return to you all
of the land of Saul your grandfather.
And you will always dine at my table.
What is your servant,
that you have turned your attention
to a dead dog like me?
Come.
David, Saul, and their army
returned from striking down the Philistines.
The women of all the cities of Israel
greeted them with a celebration
of song and dance.
The women began singing,
“Saul has struck down his thousands,
and David his tens of thousands.”
The only thing left to give him
is the kingship!
From that day on,
Saul was always suspicious of David.
Jealousy controlled Saul
and ruined his friendship with David
and with Jehovah.
David was popular, good-looking,
physically strong, a talented musician,
and he had been anointed as the next king.
Here is my eldest daughter, Merab.
And I will give her to you as a wife.
Who am I to be son-in-law to the king?
Other men would have used this opportunity
to boast or to promote themselves.
Some just couldn’t understand
why David wouldn’t take more credit.
David,
you’re the finest warrior we’ve ever had.
Haven’t you earned the right
to accept some praise?
But who really trains me for battle?
Who rescues me from the sword?
Jehovah is my Rock; he should be praised.
What is any man next to him?
David was sick.
Absalom saw this
as an opportunity to seize power.
Like his father David,
he had many gifts.
He was born into a wealthy
and powerful family.
He turned heads wherever he went,
and he relished the attention.
Men would come to the city gate
so that the king would hear their legal case.
If I were appointed judge in the land,
every man with a legal case
or judgment could come to me
and I would see that he receives justice.
You are from the royal house, my lord.
My mother too has royal blood.
It seems that I was born to lead.
But God will do what’s best for his people.
Absalom seemed
to be interested in the people
who came to David,
but he was only interested in himself.
The ark of the covenant
was finally brought to Jerusalem.
David and the people danced and celebrated.
Has he forgotten that he is king,
dancing like a common fool?
How glorious the king of Israel made himself
before the eyes of the slave girls
of his servants,
just as an empty-headed man!
My celebration was before Jehovah.
Michal did not love others
as much as she loved herself.
David was faithful to Jehovah for decades.
But then he let his guard down,
and he coveted a married woman.
Bring Bath-sheba to me.
David and Bath-sheba committed adultery,
and she became pregnant.
To hide their sin,
David secretly ordered
Bath-sheba’s husband to be killed.
And he hurt the God
who had done so much for him.
On the run from Saul,
David’s men came to see Nabal,
whose sheep they had protected.
They asked only for what Nabal could spare.
David didn’t wait to react.
Everyone strap on your sword!
David took action,
but he didn’t seek Jehovah’s direction.
Still, Jehovah intervened
through Nabal’s discerning wife, Abigail.
My lord, let the blame be on me.
It is Jehovah who has held you back
from incurring bloodguilt
and from taking revenge.
You will have no regret in your heart.
Nabal was senseless,
but he was still David’s Israelite brother,
and he deserved to be treated lovingly.
David had become provoked, and Abigail
rescued him from making
the situation much worse.
Praise Jehovah the God of Israel,
who has sent you this day to meet me.
The Amalekites kidnapped
the wives and children of David and his men.
And his men became very bitter.
You!
Our families were never safe here.
You led them to their death!
“Life for life,” David—you should be stoned!
Patience, patience, please
—Jehovah may yet rescue them.
We don’t know.
David looked to Jehovah for help.
David fought the Amalekites,
rescued all of the kidnapped Israelites,
and recovered all of the flocks
that had been taken.
Jehovah protected us
and gave into our hand the marauder band
that came against us.
David could have given the spoils of war
only to those who trusted in him,
but he shared with all.
It was as though they had never wronged him.
I’ve escaped from the camp of Israel.
Many have fallen and died.
Even Saul and his son Jonathan have died.
How do you know?
I stood above him and put him to death.
Teach all of our people this dirge
for Saul and Jonathan:
“Saul and Jonathan,
“beloved and cherished during their life.
“How the mighty have fallen
and the weapons of war have perished!”
Not once did David
mention Saul’s hurtful acts.
To David, the assassination of Saul
was an unrighteous act,
and David could never rejoice over that.
Here I’m dwelling in a house of cedars
while the ark of the covenant
of Jehovah is under tent cloths.
Do whatever is in your heart,
for the true God is with you.
But I had spoken too quickly.
David.
Nathan.
Go on, Nathan. What is it?
This is what Jehovah says:
‘You are not the one
who will build me a house to dwell in.’
David’s son Solomon would build the temple.
But David didn’t feel sorry for himself,
and he didn’t try to push ahead
without Jehovah’s blessing.
David knew God’s will, and he rejoiced in it.
Later, he gathered
a vast amount of materials
so his son could build.
David had been pursued ruthlessly by Saul.
He and his men faced hunger, fear,
and threat of death.
It’s Saul!
Today, God has surrendered
your enemy into your hand.
Let me pin him to the ground.
David could have ended his trial
then and there,
but he was a man of love.
Do not harm him.
It is unthinkable from Jehovah’s standpoint
that I should lift my hand
against the anointed of Jehovah.
Despite all that Saul had done,
David left the judging to Jehovah,
whom he loved and trusted.
David was on the run from Saul.
His friend Jonathan,
Saul’s son, hatched a plan to protect David.
But could David really believe Jonathan?
After all,
Jonathan was second in line to the throne.
Only David seemed to stand in his way.
Saul had betrayed David.
Might Jonathan do the same?
Could David put his life in Jonathan’s hands?
May Jehovah do that to Jonathan
and more if I do not disclose it to you
and send you away in peace.
And I swear never to withdraw
loyal love from you and your household.
May Jehovah be between us forever.
David loved Jonathan, and he believed him.
That trust saved David’s life.
Abner had been chief of Saul’s army.
He pursued David in the wilderness
and supported David’s rival
after David became king.
So why was Abner coming to see David?
My lord the king,
make a covenant with us.
We now support you as king
because Jehovah has promised us
salvation by means of your hand.
I will make a covenant with you.
Thank you.
David trusted Abner
and hoped that he would now remain loyal.
But Joab saw things differently.
What have you done?
You know Abner!
He came here to fool you
and to get to know your every move
and find out everything that you’re doing!
Be careful.
You know the law:
‘You must not hold a grudge,
‘and you must love your
fellow man as yourself.’
Joab’s distrust grew into vengeance.
He later killed Abner.
Those who hate expect the worst,
but those who love never lose hope.
When Jehovah chose David to be king,
he had already rejected Saul.
Even so, it wasn’t yet Jehovah’s time
for David to begin ruling.
Waiting wasn’t always easy for David.
He became a fugitive running for his life.
Even his own men once threatened to kill him!
Twenty-two years had passed.
Finally, he became king over all of Israel.
True, King Saul and even some
of David’s friends abandoned him,
but David endured it all.
Jehovah had never abandoned David,
so how could David ever give up
his love for Jehovah?
When David was anointed as king,
he couldn’t have imagined the tests
that would come his way.
But love helped him to face all of them.
David saw that without love,
we become jealous,
get puffed up,
behave indecently,
look for our own interests,
and become provoked.
Love helped David to be patient,
to be kind,
not to brag,
not to keep account of the injury,
and not to rejoice over unrighteousness.
Instead, love helped him
to rejoice with the truth,
to bear all things,
to believe all things,
to hope all things,
and to endure all things.
David faced many trials.
But love was equal to all of them.
When David comes back to life,
he, like love itself,
can live on forever.
