title: 제프리 W. 잭슨: “그리스도께서 우리를 위해 죽으셨습니다” (로마 5:8)

ko.text: 이제 특별한 아침 숭배 프로그램을 시작하겠습니다.
베델 가족뿐 아니라 전 세계의 수많은 우리 형제 자매들과 함께
성경에 근거한 영적인 내용을 나눌 수 있어서 정말 기쁘네요.
어디서 시청하시든 이 프로그램을 즐기시기 바랍니다.
주 예수 그리스도의 죽음을 기념할 시간을 기다리고 있습니다.
먼저 아침 숭배를 위해 오늘의 성구를 낭독하겠습니다.
교습 위원회 보조자인 데이비드 셰이퍼 형제가
믿음 때문에 투옥된 여러분은 내일 아침이면 처형될 거라는 말을 듣습니다.
과거에 일부 형제 자매들은 실제로 이와 같은 상황에 직면했습니다.
그들 중엔 그 마지막 밤에 가족과 친구들을 위로하고
강하게 하려고 편지를 쓴 사람이 많았죠.
나치에게 처형당하기 전날 밤에 가족에게 편지를 썼는데,
그 편지에는 그의 용기가 잘 드러나 있습니다.
제겐 아직 생각을 바꿀 시간이 있습니다.
아! 제가 주를 부인하고도 이 세상에서 다시 행복해질 수 있을까요?
이 세상을 떠난다는 것을 확신하시기 바랍니다.”
오히려, 시간을 내서 사랑하는 사람들을 격려하는 편지를 썼습니다.
믿음을 포기하지 않도록 힘을 주고 싶었던 것입니다.
예수께서 땅에서 인간으로서의 마지막 밤을 어떻게 보내셨는지를
자신의 죽음과 관련해서 무엇을 알고 계셨습니까?
그들은 그에게 사형을 선고하고 그를 이방 사람들에게 넘겨주어
조롱하고 채찍질하고 기둥에 달아 처형하게 할 것입니다.
그리고 그는 셋째 날에 일으켜질 것입니다.”
그분은 자신의 죽음에 관해 무엇을 알고 계셨습니까?
방금 읽은 성구에서는 네 가지 점을 알려 줍니다.
첫째로, 그분은 자신이 유대교 지도자들에게 넘겨져서 법정으로 끌려갈 것이고,
아마도 신성 모독죄가 포함된 죄목으로 유죄 판결을 받을 것을 알고 계셨습니다.
둘째로, 그분은 자신이 “이방 사람들”, 다시 말해 로마 사람들에게 넘겨져
그들에게 가혹한 대우를 받을 것을 알고 계셨습니다.
셋째로, 기둥에 달려 처형될 것을 아셨습니다.
마지막으로, 자신이 셋째 날에 부활될 것도 알고 계셨습니다.
예수께서는 자신의 죽음에 관한 일부 세부점들을 알고 계셨고,
그런데 그분이 알고 계셨을 점들이 또 있을까요?
그날 밤에 그분이 알고 계셨을 또 다른 세 가지 점을 생각해 보시죠.
첫 번째 점을 알아보기 위해, 요한복음을 찾아보겠습니다.
여러분 중 한 사람이 나를 배반할 것입니다’라고 분명히 말씀하셨다.”
그다음에 26절로 가 보면, 계속해서 이런 내용이 나옵니다.
‘내가 빵 조각을 적셔서 주는 사람이 바로 그 사람입니다’라고 대답하셨다.
그리고 빵 조각을 적셔서 가룟 시몬의 아들 유다에게 건네주셨다.”
예수께서는 사도들 중 하나가 그분을 배반할 것을 아셨고,
예수께서 아셨던 점이 또 있는데, 같은 장 38절을 읽어 보겠습니다.
닭이 울기 전에 틀림없이 당신은 나를 세 번 부인할 것입니다.”
그러니까 예수께선 베드로가 자신을 세 번이나 부인할 것을 아셨습니다.
예수께서 아셨던 또 다른 점은 요한복음 16장에 나옵니다.
“여러분이 각자 자기 집으로 흩어져 나를 혼자 버려둘 때가 옵니다.
따라서 예수께선 나머지 제자들이 그분을 버리고 도망할 것도 아셨습니다.
네, 그분은 자신의 죽음에 관해 무엇을 아셨나요?
예수께서는 자신이 곧 재판에 넘겨져 박해를 받고 처형당할 것을 아셨을 뿐 아니라,
또한 배반당하고, 부인당할 것이며, 버려질 것임을 알고 계셨습니다.
여러분이 예수였다면, 이런 상황에서 어떻게 하셨겠습니까?
자신을 실망시킬 사람들과 함께 있지 않고 혼자 있는 편을 택하지 않았을까요?
‘내가 겪을 안 좋은 일에 신경 쓰지 말고 내일을 위해 혼자서 기도하면서
그 모든 안 좋은 일을 겪게 될 걸 알면서도,
그분은 제자들을 피해 혼자 있지 않으셨습니다.
오히려, 그분은 사도들과 이 마지막 유월절을 지키기를
말하자면, 예수께서는 부정적인 일들 때문에 “집회에 빠지지” 않으신 것이죠.
놀랍게도, 이 모든 일을 아시면서도 예수께선 충실한 사도들을
앞으로 닥칠 일에 대비하도록 도와주고 싶어 하셨습니다.
예수께서 마지막으로 사도들을 격려하신 말씀이 나옵니다.
그분은 참으로 놀라운 비이기적인 사랑을 나타내셨습니다!
예수께선 시간을 내서 사도들의 발을 씻겨 주셨는데,
심지어 배반자 가룟 유다의 발까지 씻겨 주셨죠.
사도들은 그 비천한 일을 하려고 나서지 않았을 뿐 아니라,
예수께서 발을 씻겨 주기 시작했을 때도,
아무도 그분 대신 그 일을 하지 않았습니다.
누가 가장 큰지 논쟁을 벌인 것을 보면 그 점을 잘 알 수 있죠.
이 모든 일에도 예수께선 분명 사랑을 나타내셨습니다.
사도들의 잘못 때문에 그들에 대해 부정적인 견해를 갖지 않으셨습니다.
사도들을 지켜 달라고 하셨을 뿐 아니라
나중에 그분을 믿게 될 사람들도 돌봐 달라고 하셨습니다.
그분은 그 모든 부정적인 일들이 아니라,
사람들을 강하게 하고 그들을 위해 기도하는 데 초점을 맞추셨습니다.
오늘 저녁엔 여호와와 예수께서 우릴 위해 보이신 사랑에
온통 정신을 빼앗길 수도 있는 그 순간에도,
사도들이 앞에 놓인 일에 대비할 수 있도록 그들을 참을성 있게 도와주셨습니다.
물론 오늘 밤이 우리 생애의 마지막 밤이거나
우리가 내일 처형되는 건 아닐 것입니다.
하지만 예수께서 그 마지막 밤에 나타내신 사랑을 어떻게 본받을 수 있습니까?
우리는 이렇게 하기로 결심할 수 있습니다.
형제 자매들이 우리를 실망시키는 경우가 있더라도 결코 그들을 포기하지 마십시오.
우리가 어려움에 직면했을 때에도, 계속 다른 사람들을 강하게 하십시오.
여호와와 그분의 사랑하는 아들 예수 그리스도에 대한
“예수께서는 제자들을 위해 기꺼이 생명을 바치셨을 뿐 아니라
매일의 생활에서도 자신보다 그들의 유익을 먼저 생각하셨습니다.
예를 들어, 예수께서는 몸이 피곤하거나 감정적으로 괴로울 때에도
그분은 사람들에게 받을 수 있는 것이 아니라 줄 수 있는 것에 초점을 맞추셨습니다.
우리는 그리스도인 형제들로 이루어진 유일한 참종교에 속해 있으며,
우리와 함께할 새로운 사람들을 초대하기 위해
그에 더해 우리는 ‘믿음으로 친족’이 되었지만 무활동이 된 사람들을 돕는 일에
우리는 그들에게 우리의 집회, 특히 기념식에 참석하도록 격려함으로
우리는 무활동자들이 여호와께 돌아올 때 여호와와 예수처럼 기쁨에 넘칩니다.”
그러면 이제 오늘 계획된 성서 읽기 범위에 주의를 기울여 보겠습니다.
“무교절 첫날, 곧 관례대로 유월절 제물을 바치는 때에,
그러자 그분은 제자들 가운데 둘을 보내며 말씀하셨다.
그러면 물동이를 메고 가는 남자를 만날 것입니다.
그리고 그가 어디로 들어가든지, 그 집의 주인에게 전하십시오.
유월절 식사를 할 방이 어디입니까?”라고 말씀하십니다.’
그러면 그가 잘 갖추어 준비된 큰 위층 방을 보여 줄 것이니,
그래서 제자들이 나가 도시에 들어가 보니 그분이 말씀하신 대로였다.
내가 당신의 집에서 제자들과 함께 유월절을 지키겠습니다.”’”
제자들은 예수께서 시키신 대로 하여 유월절을 준비했다.”
“저녁이 되자, 그분이 열두 제자와 함께 가셨다.
그들이 함께 식탁에 앉아 먹고 있을 때에 예수께서 말씀하셨다.
곧 나와 함께 먹고 있는 사람이 나를 배반할 것입니다.”
그들은 근심하며 한 사람씩 그분에게 묻기 시작했다.
나와 함께 그릇에 손을 넣는 사람입니다.
‘사람의 아들’은 자신에 관해 기록된 대로 떠나갑니다.
그러나 ‘사람의 아들’을 배반하는 그 사람에게는 화가 있습니다!
그 사람은 차라리 태어나지 않았더라면 자신에게 더 좋았을 것입니다.”
그분이 빵을 들어 축복의 말씀을 하시고 떼어 그들에게 주며 말씀하셨다.
또 잔을 들어 감사를 드리고 그들에게 주시니,
“이것은 많은 사람을 위해 쏟는 내 ‘계약의 피’를 의미합니다.
나는 하느님의 왕국에서 새것을 마시는 그날까지,
더는 포도나무에서 난 것을 결코 마시지 않겠습니다.”
끝으로 그들은 찬양의 노래를 부른 다음 올리브 산으로 갔다.
오늘 바로 이 밤에 닭이 두 번 울기 전에 당신은 나를 세 번 부인할 것입니다.”
“주와 함께 죽는 한이 있어도, 저는 결코 주를 부인하지 않겠습니다.”
그리고 베드로와 야고보와 요한을 데리고 가셨다.
그리고 조금 앞으로 나아가 땅에 엎드려,
가능하다면 그 시간이 자신에게서 지나가게 해 달라고 기도하기 시작하셨다.
그러나 제가 원하는 대로가 아니라 아버지께서 원하시는 대로 하십시오.”
그리고 돌아와 그들이 자고 있는 것을 보시고 베드로에게 말씀하셨다.
한 시간도 깨어 있을 수 없었습니까?
유혹에 빠지지 않도록 깨어 살피고 계속 기도하십시오.
그분은 다시 가서 기도하며 같은 말씀을 하셨다.
그리고 다시 와서 보시니 그들이 자고 있었다.
그들은 그분에게 무슨 말을 해야 할지 몰랐다.
그분이 세 번째로 돌아와 그들에게 말씀하셨다.
이제 ‘사람의 아들’이 배반당하여 죄인들의 손에 넘겨집니다.
그분이 말씀하고 계시던 바로 그때에, 열두 제자 중 하나인 유다가 왔다.
그리고 수제사장들과 서기관들과 장로들이 보낸 무리가
칼과 몽둥이를 들고 그와 함께 왔다.
“내가 입을 맞추는 사람이 바로 그 사람이니,
그를 붙잡아 잘 끌고 가시오” 하고 미리 신호를 정해 놓았다.
그런데 곁에 서 있던 사람들 중 하나가 칼을 뽑아
대제사장의 종을 쳐서 그의 귀를 잘라 버렸다.
칼과 몽둥이를 들고 나를 잡으러 왔습니까?
내가 날마다 성전에서 가르치면서 여러분과 함께 있었는데도
그러나 이것은 성경 말씀이 성취되기 위한 것입니다.”
그때에 제자들은 모두 그분을 버리고 달아났다.
그런데 벌거벗은 몸에 고운 아마포 옷만 걸친 어떤 젊은이가
그는 아마포 옷을 버리고 벌거벗은 채로 도망갔다.
그들은 이제 예수를 대제사장에게 끌고 갔다.
그러나 베드로는 그분을 멀리서 따라가 대제사장의 집 뜰에까지 들어갔다.
그리고 집 수종들과 함께 앉아 불을 쬐고 있었다.
예수를 죽이려고 그분에게 불리한 증언을 찾고 있었으나
사실 많은 사람이 그분에게 불리한 거짓 증언을 했으나
또 어떤 사람들은 일어나 그분에게 불리한 거짓 증언을 하며 이렇게 말했다.
“우리는 이 사람이 ‘나는 손으로 지은 이 성전을 헐고,
그러나 이에 대해서도 그들의 증언이 서로 일치하지 않았다.
그러자 대제사장이 그들 가운데서 일어나 예수께 물었다.
이들이 당신에게 불리한 증언을 하고 있지 않소?”
그러나 그분은 잠자코 계셨으며 아무 대답도 하지 않으셨다.
여러분은 ‘사람의 아들’이 권능의 오른편에 앉아 있는 것과
하늘의 구름과 함께 오는 것을 볼 것입니다.”
이 말을 듣고 대제사장이 옷을 찢으며 말했다.
그들은 모두 그분이 죽어 마땅하다고 정죄했다.
그분의 얼굴을 가리고 주먹으로 치며 말하기 시작했다.
법정 직원들도 그분의 뺨을 때린 뒤에 그분을 데려갔다.
대제사장의 하녀 하나가 와서 베드로가 불을 쬐고 있는 것을 보고는
“당신도 저 나사렛 사람 예수와 함께 있었던 사람이군요.”
당신이 무슨 말을 하는지도 모르겠소” 하고 부인하며
곁에 서 있는 사람들에게 다시 말하기 시작했다.
그런데 잠시 후에 곁에 서 있던 사람들이 다시 베드로에게 말했다.
“당신이 갈릴리 사람인 걸 보니 그들과 한패임이 틀림없소.”
그러나 그는 스스로 저주하고 맹세하면서 말했다.
그 즉시 닭이 두 번째 울었다.
그러자 베드로는 “닭이 두 번 울기 전에
당신은 나를 세 번 부인할 것입니다”라고 하신 예수의 말씀이 생각났다.
분명 이 성구들이 우리가 오늘 기념식을 위해 마음을 준비하는 데 도움이 됐을 겁니다.
마치기 전에 중앙장로회가 여러분 모두를 사랑한다는 걸
어디에서 기념식을 지키든, 어떤 어려움을 겪든
여호와께서 여러분 모두를 풍성히 축복하시기를 진심으로 바랍니다.
오늘 기념식에 참석하려는 우리의 연합된 노력이
그분의 아들 예수 그리스도께 영예가 되기를 바랍니다!

en.text: Welcome to our special
Morning Worship program
for the most important day of the year.
It’s a real privilege this morning
not just to speak to the Bethel family
but to be able to share some Scriptural thoughts
with the majority of our dear brothers and sisters
right around the world, including you
wherever you may be this morning.
All of us are looking forward with excitement to this evening,
when we unitedly remember the death of our Lord Jesus Christ.
But first, let’s start by reading
the scripture text selected for today.
We’re going to ask Brother David Schafer,
a helper to the Teaching Committee,
to read for us this morning.
Please, David, let’s have the scripture text read.
Tuesday, April 7, 2020
—the Memorial date after sundown.
The text is taken from Romans 5:8:
“Christ died for us.”
Thank you, David.
Imagine, please, that you are in a prison cell.
You’ve just been notified
that you will be executed in the morning because of your faith.
There is no further means of appeal.
The decision is final.
How will you spend this last night?
What will you do?
What will you think about?
Some of our brothers and sisters in the past
have found themselves in this challenging situation.
Many of these used their last night
to write letters to strengthen and comfort
their friends and relatives.
For example, consider the courageous words
written by one young brother to his family
as he awaited death at the hands of Nazi persecutors.
He wrote: “It is already past midnight.
“I still have time to change my mind.
“Ah! could I be happy again in this world
“after I had denied our Lord?
“Surely not!
“But now you have the assurance
that I leave this world in happiness and peace.”
Notice, this dear brother didn’t use
that final evening just to focus on his own hardships.
Rather, he used part of that evening
to encourage those whom he loved.
He wanted to strengthen them
so that they wouldn’t be overwhelmed
by the sad news of his death.
Well, with these thoughts in mind,
let’s now think about how Jesus spent his last evening
as a human here on earth.
To start with, let’s ask this question:
By the time of that evening,
what did Jesus know about the circumstances of his death?
To answer that question,
let’s read together what’s stated in Matthew chapter 20.
So if you turn with me, please,
to Matthew 20:18, 19,
Jesus said:
“Look! We are going up to Jerusalem,
“and the Son of man will be handed over
“to the chief priests and the scribes.
“They will condemn him to death
“and hand him over to men of the nations
“to be mocked and scourged and executed on a stake;
and on the third day he will be raised up.”
So on that final evening,
what did Jesus already know about his death,
and what would he have been thinking about?
These verses that we just read
mention four things.
First of all, it tells us that he knew
he would be handed over to the Jewish religious leaders
who would take him to court and find him guilty of a crime,
perhaps one including the charge of blasphemy.
Second, Jesus knew that he would be handed over
to “men of the nations” (in other words, the Romans),
and that they would violently abuse him.
Third, he knew that he would be executed on a stake.
And the final point,
he realized that he would be resurrected on the third day.
So on that final evening,
Jesus already knew some of the details concerning his death,
and these would have weighed heavily on his mind.
But were there any other things that he already knew?
Yes.
Let’s consider another three facts that were on his mind that evening.
The first one we’ll notice
if we turn to the book of John this time.
In John chapter 13,
we’re going to start by reading verse 21:
“After saying these things, Jesus became troubled in spirit,
“and he bore witness, saying:
‘Most truly I say to you, one of you will betray me.’”
Now if we turn across to verse 26,
it tells us that Jesus continued to say:
“‘It is the one to whom I will give the piece of bread that I dip.’
“So after dipping the bread, he took it
and gave it to Judas, the son of Simon Iscariot.”
Jesus knew that one of his apostles would betray him,
and he even knew who his betrayer would be.
Now for something else that Jesus knew,
let’s read verse 38 of the same chapter
Jesus here said to Peter:
“Will you surrender your life in my behalf?
“Most truly I say to you, a rooster will by no means crow
until you have disowned me three times.”
So Jesus also knew that Peter would deny him three times.
And for another point, let’s turn to John chapter 16
Here, speaking to his apostles, Jesus said:
“Look! The hour is coming,
“indeed, it has come,
“when each one of you will be scattered to his own house
and you will leave me alone.”
So Jesus also realized that the rest of his apostles
would run away and desert him.
So, what did Jesus have on his mind that evening?
Not only would Jesus have been thinking
about his upcoming court trial, persecution,
and execution but he also knew
that he would be betrayed,
denied, and abandoned.
Now, if you were Jesus,
how would you have reacted to this knowledge?
Perhaps you would have preferred to be by yourself,
avoiding those who would fail you.
You might have thought,
‘It’s better for me to spend the evening in prayer
—preparing properly— without these negative distractions.’
Just think about it:
Despite all these negative things,
Jesus didn’t hide away and stay by himself.
In fact, he told his apostles that he “greatly desired”
to celebrate this last Passover with them.
In other words, he wasn’t going to “miss the meeting”
because of these negative things.
Amazingly, even with all these things on his mind,
Jesus focused on how to help his faithful apostles.
He loved them, and he wanted to prepare them
for what was about to happen.
In fact, in John’s account,
five chapters are devoted to Jesus’ final words
of encouragement to his apostles.
What an amazing, unselfish love Jesus showed!
Just imagine, Jesus took the time
to wash the feet of his apostles,
even the feet of his betrayer, Judas Iscariot.
Not only were the apostles unwilling to do this lowly service
but when Jesus started to wash their feet,
not one of them stood up and offered to take over.
Yes, they had a real problem with their attitude.
That was further shown by the fact
that they had an argument that evening
about who was the greatest among them.
But do we see the evidence of Jesus’ love in all of this?
He didn’t give up on them.
Jesus didn’t allow these failures
to cause him to have a negative view of his apostles.
Instead, he commended his 11 faithful apostles
and even made a covenant with them to be part of his Kingdom.
Isn’t that truly amazing?
Additionally, Jesus earnestly prayed to Jehovah
not only to watch over those apostles
but also to care for those who would later believe in him
—that includes us today.
Despite all the negative things on his mind,
Jesus focused on strengthening others and praying for them.
What an expression of unselfish love!
This evening, we’ll be focusing on the love
Jehovah and Jesus expressed for us.
But as we meditate on the events of Nisan 14,
let’s also remember how Jesus proved his love
for his apostles by not giving up on them.
Even at a time when his thoughts would have been focused
on the excruciating death that lay ahead of him,
he patiently helped them
so that they could deal with what was about to happen.
What lessons can we learn from this?
Well, this may not be the last night of our life,
and we may not expect to be executed tomorrow.
But how can we imitate the love
that Jesus displayed that final evening?
Here are some things we can all be determined to do:
Don’t give up on our brothers and sisters,
even if at times they seem to fail us.
Continue to strengthen others,
even when we are facing difficulties.
In this way, we will also prove our genuine love
for Jehovah and his loving Son, Jesus Christ.
Now, David, let’s have our comments read.
“Jesus was willing not only to die for his disciples
“but also to live each day in a way that put their interests ahead of his own.
“For instance, he met with his followers
“even when he was physically tired or emotionally distressed.
“And he focused on what he could give to others,
“not on what he could get from them.
“We belong to the only true Christian brotherhood,
“and we enjoy spending as much time as possible
“inviting new ones to join us.
“However, we are particularly interested
“in helping those who are ‘related to us in the faith’
“but who have become inactive.
“We prove our love for them by encouraging them to attend our meetings,
“especially the Memorial.
“Like Jehovah and Jesus,
we are deeply moved when an inactive one returns to Jehovah.”
Thank you, David, for reading for us this morning.
Now we’re going to turn our attention
to our scheduled Bible reading for this morning.
“Now on the first day of the Unleavened Bread,
“when they customarily offered up the Passover sacrifice,
“his disciples said to him:
“‘Where do you want us to go and prepare for you to eat the Passover?’
“With that
“he sent two of his disciples and said to them:
“‘Go into the city,
“‘and a man carrying an earthenware water jar will meet you.
“‘Follow him, and wherever he goes inside,
“‘say to the master of the house,
“‘“The Teacher says:
“‘“‘Where is the guest room where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’
“‘“And he will show you a large upper room, furnished and ready.
“Prepare it for us there.’”
“So the disciples went out,
“and they entered the city and found it just as he said to them,
and they prepared for the Passover.”
“On the first day of the Unleavened Bread,
“the disciples came to Jesus, saying:
“‘Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?’
“He said: ‘Go into the city to So-and-so and say to him,
“‘“The Teacher says: ‘My appointed time is near;
“I will celebrate the Passover with my disciples at your home.’”’
“So the disciples did as Jesus instructed them
and prepared for the Passover.”
“After evening had fallen,
“he came with the Twelve.
“And as they were reclining at the table and eating, Jesus said:
“‘Truly I say to you, one of you
“who is eating with me will betray me.’
“They began to be grieved
“and to say to him one by one:
“‘It is not I, is it?’
“He said to them:
“‘It is one of the Twelve, the one dipping with me into the bowl.
“‘For the Son of man is going away, just as it is written about him,
“‘but woe to that man through whom the Son of man is betrayed!
“It would have been better for that man if he had not been born.’
“And as they continued eating,
“he took a loaf, said a blessing,
“broke it, and gave it to them, saying:
“‘Take it; this means my body.’
“And taking a cup, he offered thanks and gave it to them,
“and they all drank out of it.
“And he said to them:
“‘This means my “blood of the covenant,”
“‘which is to be poured out in behalf of many.
“‘Truly I say to you, I will by no means drink anymore
“‘of the product of the vine until that day
“when I drink it new in the Kingdom of God.’
“Finally, after singing praises,
“they went out to the Mount of Olives
“And Jesus said to them:
“‘You will all be stumbled, for it is written:
“‘“I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered about.”
“‘But after I have been raised up,
“I will go ahead of you into Galilee.’
“But Peter said to him:
“‘Even if all the others are stumbled, I will not be.’
“At that Jesus said to him:
“‘Truly I say to you that today, yes,
“‘on this very night, before a rooster crows twice,
“you will disown me three times.’
“But he kept insisting:
“‘If I have to die with you, I will by no means disown you.’
“Also, all the others began to say the same thing.
“So they came to a spot named Gethsemane,
“and he said to his disciples:
“‘Sit down here while I pray.’
“And he took Peter and James and John along with him,
“and he began to feel deeply distressed
“and to be greatly troubled.
“He said to them:
“‘I am deeply grieved, even to death.
“‘Stay here and keep on the watch.’
“And going a little way forward,
“he fell to the ground and began praying that,
“if it were possible, the hour might pass away from him.
“And he said:
“‘Abba, Father, all things are possible for you;
“‘remove this cup from me.
“Yet, not what I want, but what you want.’
“He returned and found them sleeping,
“and he said to Peter:
“‘Simon, are you sleeping?
“‘Did you not have the strength to keep on the watch for one hour?
“‘Keep on the watch and pray continually,
“‘so that you do not come into temptation.
“‘The spirit, of course, is eager,
“but the flesh is weak.’
“And he went away again and prayed,
“saying the same thing.
“And he came again and found them sleeping,
“for their eyes were weighed down,
“so they did not know what to answer him.
“And he returned the third time and said to them:
“‘At such a time as this, you are sleeping and resting!
“‘It is enough! The hour has come!
“‘Look! The Son of man is being betrayed into the hands of sinners.
“‘Get up, let us go.
“Look! My betrayer has drawn near.’
“And immediately, while he was still speaking,
“Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived
“and with him a crowd with swords and clubs,
“sent from the chief priests and the scribes and the elders.
“Now his betrayer had given them an agreed sign, saying:
“‘Whoever it is I kiss, he is the one;
“take him into custody, and lead him away under guard.’
“And he came straight up and approached him
“and said, ‘Rabbi!’
“and gave him a tender kiss.
“So they seized him and took him into custody.
“However, one of those standing by drew his sword
“and struck the slave of the high priest, taking off his ear.
“But in response Jesus said to them:
“‘Did you come out to arrest me
“‘with swords and clubs as against a robber?
“‘Day after day I was with you in the temple teaching,
“‘and yet you did not take me into custody.
“Nevertheless, this is to fulfill the Scriptures.’
“And they all abandoned him and fled.
“However, a certain young man wearing only a fine linen garment
“over his naked body began to follow him nearby,
“and they tried to seize him,
“but he left his linen garment behind and got away naked.
“They now led Jesus away to the high priest,
“and all the chief priests and the elders
“and the scribes assembled.
“But Peter, from a good distance, followed him
“as far as into the courtyard of the high priest;
“and he was sitting together with the house attendants
“and warming himself before a bright fire.
“Now the chief priests and the entire Sanhedrin
“were looking for testimony against Jesus
“in order to put him to death, but they were not finding any.
“Many, indeed, were giving false witness against him,
“but their testimonies were not in agreement.
“Also, certain ones were standing up
“and bearing false witness against him, saying:
“‘We heard him say, “I will throw down this temple
“‘“that was made with hands, and in three days
“I will build another not made with hands.”’
“But even on these grounds,
“their testimony was not in agreement.
“Then the high priest stood up in their midst
“and questioned Jesus, saying:
“‘Do you say nothing in reply?
“What is it these men are testifying against you?’
“But he kept silent and made no reply at all.
“Again the high priest began to question him and said to him:
“‘Are you the Christ the Son of the Blessed One?’
“Then Jesus said:
“‘I am; and you will see the Son of man
“sitting at the right hand of power and coming with the clouds of heaven.’
“At this the high priest ripped his garments and said:
“‘What further need do we have of witnesses?
“You heard the blasphemy. What is your decision?’
“They all condemned him as deserving of death.
“And some started to spit on him
“and to cover his face
“and hit him with their fists and say to him:
“‘Prophesy!’
“And slapping him in the face, the court attendants took him.
“Now while Peter was below in the courtyard,
“one of the servant girls of the high priest came.
“On seeing Peter warming himself,
“she looked straight at him and said:
“‘You too were with the Nazarene, this Jesus.’
“But he denied it, saying:
“‘Neither do I know him nor do I understand what you are talking about,’
“and he went outside to the entryway.
“There the servant girl saw him and again began to say to those standing by:
“‘This is one of them.’
“Again he was denying it.
“And after a little while,
“those standing by again began saying to Peter:
“‘Certainly you are one of them,
“for you are, in fact, a Galilean.’
“But he started to curse and swear:
“‘I do not know this man of whom you speak!’
“Immediately a rooster crowed a second time,
“and Peter recalled what Jesus had said to him:
“‘Before a rooster crows twice,
“you will disown me three times.’
And he broke down and began to weep.”
We’re sure that those verses have helped
to prepare us for the Memorial this evening.
But before we finish,
we’d like to assure you that the Governing Body loves you all.
Wherever you may be this evening,
no matter what challenges you may face,
it’s our heartfelt wish
that Jehovah will richly bless you all.
May our united efforts to be at the Memorial this evening
bring praise to our loving heavenly Father, Jehovah,
and his Son, Jesus Christ!

cn.text: 欢迎大家在这个最重要的日子
收看这个特别的早晨崇拜
很高兴能在今天早上
跟大家分享一些圣经的内容
今天的早晨崇拜不光是对伯特利家庭讲的
也是对全世界大部分的弟兄姐妹讲的
也包括你在内
我们所有人都热切期待
今天晚上要举行的耶稣牺牲纪念聚会
现在，我们会先读出今天要阅读的经文
我们请教导委员会的助手
戴维·谢弗弟兄为我们朗读今天的内容
戴维，请你读好吗？
4月7日星期二
日落之后举行耶稣牺牲纪念聚会
基督已经为我们而死
罗马书5:8
谢谢你
请大家想象一个情况
你因为信仰的缘故被关在监狱
明天早上就要被处死了
你没有办法再上诉
这已经是最终的判决
你会怎么度过这最后一夜呢？
你会做些什么，又会想些什么呢？
过去
有一些弟兄姐妹就曾面对这种艰难的情况
其中的许多人在这最后的晚上
写信鼓励和安慰亲戚朋友
来看一个例子
一个年轻的弟兄，他在被纳粹党处死之前
在最后一个晚上写信鼓励他的家人
他说
“现在已经过了午夜，我还有时间改变想法
唉！
如果我放弃信仰
即使活在这个世上，又怎么会快乐呢？
但现在我确定
我离开这个世界时，内心是快乐安宁的”
在最后的晚上
这位弟兄没有把目光集中在难题之上
相反，他用了他最后的时间鼓励深爱的人
好让他的家人不会因为他的死而过度悲伤
那耶稣又怎么样呢？
他在被处死前的最后一个晚上
是怎么度过的呢？
首先，我们来考虑一个问题
关于这个晚上耶稣要面对的事情
他已经知道了哪些呢？
为了回答这个问题
我们一起看看马太福音20章的记载
请打开圣经
耶稣说
“看！现在我们上耶路撒冷
人子会被交给祭司长和抄经士
他们会定他死罪
把他交给外族人戏弄和鞭打
在木柱上处决
第三天他会复活。”
在那个最后的晚上
耶稣已经知道关于他死亡的哪些细节呢？
刚刚这段经文告诉我们四件事情
第一
耶稣知道他会被交给犹太的宗教领袖
这些领袖会把他带上法庭定罪
罪名可能也包括亵渎上帝
第二
耶稣知道自己会被交给外族人
也就是当时的罗马人
被他们戏弄和鞭打
第三
他知道自己会被挂在木柱上
最后，他知道自己第三天会被复活
在这最后的晚上
耶稣已经知道了这些细节
这些事重重地压在他的心上
那么，还有别的事是耶稣知道的吗？
有的
我们来看看另外三件压在他心上的事
第一件事是什么呢？
请大家打开约翰福音13章
我们会看第21节
经文说
“耶稣说完这些话，心里难过起来
就公开说
我实实在在告诉你们
你们有一个人会出卖我。”
现在我们跳到第26节
耶稣继续说
“我蘸一块饼给谁，就是谁
耶稣就蘸了一块饼
递给加略人西门的儿子犹大。”
所以，耶稣已经知道他有一个门徒会背叛他
而且还知道这个人是谁
耶稣还知道些什么呢？
我们来读13:38
在这里耶稣对彼得说
“你愿意为我牺牲生命吗？
我实实在在告诉你
鸡叫以前，你会三次不认我。”
所以，耶稣已经知道彼得会三次不认他
还有一件事，耶稣也已经知道
我们看看约翰福音16:32
耶稣对他的使徒说
“看哪！时候要到，其实已经到了
你们会被分散，各自回家，留下我一个人。”
这里说
耶稣已经清楚知道
其他使徒会抛弃他逃走
所以，那天耶稣心上有多少事呢？
耶稣不仅要面对即将到来的法庭审讯
迫害和死刑
他也知道在那天
使徒会背叛他、不认他
甚至离弃他
请想想
如果你是耶稣，你会怎么做呢？
也许你只想一个人待着
远离那些会让你失望的人
你可能会想
我要彻夜独自祷告，才能做好准备
不受到这些负面的事影响
但耶稣不是这样
虽然有这么多负面的事
他却没有离开人群一个人待着
相反地，耶稣告诉使徒
他十分渴望跟他们一起过逾越节
换句话说
耶稣没有因为负面的事而错过聚会
真的很了不起！
即使心里有这么多事
耶稣还是想着怎么帮助他的忠心使徒
耶稣深爱使徒，所以他想帮助使徒做好准备
单在约翰福音，就有五章的内容
记录着耶稣在最后鼓励使徒的话
他的爱很伟大、很无私，对吗？
想想看，耶稣花时间为他的使徒洗脚
甚至也包括加略人犹大的脚
耶稣的使徒不但不肯做这种卑微的工作
当耶稣帮他们洗脚时
甚至没有任何一个人愿意起来帮忙
他们的态度真的有问题，对吗？
这也是为什么他们在耶稣要牺牲的那天晚上
还在争论谁是最大的
你看出耶稣深爱使徒了吗？
他没有放弃他们
耶稣没有因为他们的缺点
就对他们有负面的看法
相反，他称赞11个忠心的使徒
甚至跟他们定下了王国之约
这样的爱很伟大，不是吗？
除此之外，耶稣热切地向耶和华祷告
不只是为了当时的使徒
也为了后来跟从他的所有人
包括今天的我们
尽管有这么多事压在他心上
他还是专注于鼓励别人，也为别人祷告
耶稣表现了多么无私的爱！
今天晚上，我们会特别留意
耶和华和耶稣对我们的爱
但当我们沉思尼散月十四日发生的事时
要记得耶稣怎样对他的使徒表现爱心
不放弃帮助他们
尽管耶稣知道
他很快就要以非常痛苦的方式死去
他还是耐心地帮助使徒
好让他们能够应付将临的考验
我们可以学到什么呢？
虽然今天不是我们人生的最后一天
我们也不是明天就要被处决
但是我们可以怎样效法耶稣向使徒表现的爱呢？
有几件事情是我们可以努力做的
就是不要放弃我们的弟兄姐妹
即使他们让我们失望
要不断鼓励别人
在我们自己有难题的时候也要这样做
这样，我们就能表明
我们真的爱耶和华和他的爱子耶稣基督
戴维，请你读《守望台》的评论
耶稣不只乐意为门徒牺牲生命
在平时，他也会先考虑门徒的需要
……他关心的不是自己能从别人得到什么
而是他能为别人做什么
我们属于真基督徒的大家庭
很愿意多花时间邀请人参加聚会
不过，我们也应该特别关心
停止聚会或传道的基督徒
因为他们跟我们“亲如一家”
我们很爱他们，所以会鼓励他们参加聚会
特别是耶稣牺牲纪念聚会
看到这些弟兄姐妹回到仁爱的天父耶和华身边
我们会跟耶和华和耶稣一样非常高兴
谢谢你，戴维，谢谢你的朗读
接下来，我们会聆听今天要阅读的经文
无酵节的​第​一​天
也​就是​人们​按照​惯例​宰杀​逾越节​祭牲​的​那​天
门徒​对​耶稣​说
“你​要​我们​去​哪里​为​你​准备​逾越节​的​晚餐​呢？”
于是​耶稣​派​了​两​个​门徒，对​他们​说
“你们​进​城​去，会​遇见​一​个​人​拿​着​一​个​水瓶
你们​要​跟着​他
他​进​哪个​房子，你们​就​对​哪个​房子​的​主人​说
老师​说
“我​跟​门徒​一起​吃​逾越节​晚餐​的​客房​
在​哪里​呢？”
他​就​会​带​你们​去​看​楼​上​一​个​宽敞​的​房间
里面​家具​齐全，布置​整齐
你们​就​在​那里​为​我们​准备​吧。”
门徒​出去，进​了​城
发现​情形​正如​耶稣​对​他们​说​的​一样
他们​就​把​逾越节​的​晚餐​准备​好​了
无酵节的​第​一​天
门徒​来​问​耶稣​说
“你​要​我们​在​哪里​准备​逾越节​的​晚餐​呢？”
他​说
“你们​进​城​去​见​某某​人，对​他​说
老师​说：“我​的​时候​快​到​了
我​要​在​你​家​里​跟​门徒​过​逾越节。”
门徒​照​耶稣​吩咐​的​去​做
就​准备​好​了​逾越节​的​晚餐
傍晚​时分，耶稣​和​十二​使徒​一起​来​到
他们​坐​下用餐​的​时候，耶稣​说
“我​实在​告诉​你们
你们​当中​有​一​个​跟​我​一起​用餐​的​人
​会​出卖​我。”
他们​就​忧愁​起来
一​个​一​个​对​他​说
“不​是​我​吧？”
耶稣​对​他们​说
“是​你们​这​十二​使徒​之​一
他​正​跟​我​一起​把​手​伸​进​同​一​个​碗​里
正如​圣经​说​的
人子​要​离​去，可是​出卖​人子​的​人​有​祸​了！
那个​人​没有​出生​倒​好。”
他们​还​在​吃​的​时候，耶稣​拿​起​饼​来
祷告​之后​就​掰​开，递​给​他们，说
“你们​拿​去​吃​吧。这​指​的​是​我​的​身体。”
他​拿​起​杯​来，祷告​感谢​之后​递​给​他们
他们​所有​人​都​喝​了
耶稣​说
“这​指​的​是​我​的‘立约​之​血’
是​要​为​许多​人​流​出来​的
我​实在​告诉​你们，我​绝​不​再​喝​葡萄酒
直到​我​在​上帝​的​王国​里​喝​新酒​的​那​一​天。”
最后，他们​唱​了​赞美歌，就​离开​那里
前往​橄榄山
耶稣​对​他们​说
“你们​所有​人​都​会​离弃​我
因为​圣经​上​写​着
我​要​打击​牧人，绵羊​就​会​四散。
可是​我​复活​以后，要​比​你们​先​到​加利利​去。”
彼得​却​对​他​说
“就算​其他​人​全都​离弃​你
我​也​不​会​离弃​你。”
耶稣​对​彼得​说
“我​实在​告诉​你
就​在​今天，这个​晚上
鸡​叫​两​次​以前，你​会​三​次​不​认​我。”
彼得​却​坚决​地​说
“就算​我​必须​跟​你​一起​死，也​绝​不​会​不​认​你。”
其他​人​也​都​说​了​同样​的​话
他们​来​到​一​个​叫​客西马尼​的​地方
耶稣​对​门徒​说
“你们​坐​在​这里，我​去​祷告。”
他​带​了​彼得、雅各、约翰​一起​去
他​非常​苦恼，极其​难过
就​对​他们​说
“我​心里​非常​忧愁，几乎​要​死
你们​要​留​在​这里，不断​守望。”
他​稍​往​前​走，跪​在​地​上​祷告
祈求​如果​可能，就​让​那​时刻​过去
不要​临到​他
他​说
“爸爸，父亲​啊
对​你​来​说​什么​都​可能
求​你​为​我​撤​去​这个​杯
可是​不要​照​我​的​意思，只要​照​你​的​意思。”
他​回来，看见​门徒​睡​着​了，就​对​彼得​说
“西门，你​睡​着​了​吗？
你​连​守望​一​小时​也​做​不​到​吗？
你们​要​不断​守望，不断​祷告，免得​陷入​引诱
心灵​固然​是​热切的，肉体​却​是​软弱​的。”
耶稣​又​去​祷告，说​的​也​是​同样​的​话
他​再次​回来，看见​门徒​又​睡​着​了
因为​他们​困​得​眼睛​都​睁​不​开​了
他们​也​不​知道​怎样​回答​他​才​好
他​第​三​次​回来，对​他们​说
“在​这样​的​时候
你们​还​在​睡觉，还​在​休息！
够​了！时候​到​了！
看​哪！
人子​要​被​人​出卖，落​在​罪人​手​里​了
起来，我们​走​吧
看！出卖​我​的​人​快​到​了。”
耶稣​还​在​说话
十二​使徒​之​一​的​犹大​忽然​来​了
有​一​群​人​带​着​刀剑​棍棒​跟着​他
他们​是​祭司长、抄经士​和​长老​派​来​的
出卖​耶稣​的​那个​人​
事先​跟​他们​约定​了​一​个​暗号，说
“我​吻​谁，谁​就是​你们​要​的​人
你们​要​拘捕​他，把​他​押​走。”
犹大​直接​走​到​耶稣​面前，说​了​声
“老师”
然后​非常​亲切​地​吻​他
他们​就​抓​住​耶稣，拘捕​了​他
有​一​个​站​在​旁边​的​人​拔​出​剑​来
向​大祭司​的​奴隶​砍​去
削​掉​了​他​的​一​只​耳朵
耶稣​对​他们​说
“你们​带​着​刀剑​棍棒​出来​捉拿​我
像​对付​强盗​一样​吗？
我​天天​在​圣殿​里​教导​人，跟​你们​在​一起
你们​却​没有​拘捕​我
不过，这​是​要​应验​圣经​的​话。”
门徒​全都​抛​下​他​逃跑​了
有​一​个​年轻人
身上​只​穿​着​一​件​上等​细麻衣，跟着​耶稣
那些​人​想​抓​住​他
他​就​撇​下​细麻衣，光​着​身子跑​了
他们​把​耶稣​押​到​大祭司​那里
祭司长、长老、抄经士​全都​聚集​起来
彼得​远远​地​跟着​耶稣，来​到​大祭司​的​院子
就​跟​仆人​们​一起​坐​在​火​边​取暖
这​时，那些​祭司长​和​整个​公议会
​都​在​找​证词​来​指控​耶稣，要​把​他​处死
但是​没有​可​用​的​证词
有​许多​人​作​伪证​诬告​他
他们​的​证词​却​各​有​出入
又​有​几​个​人​站​出来，作​伪证​指控​他​说
“我们​听​他​说​过
我​要​拆毁​这​座​人​手​所​造​的​圣殿
三​天​之​内​另​建​一​座​不​是​人​手​造​的​殿。”
但是​在​这​一​点​上，他们​的​证词​也​各​有​出入
大祭司​在​众人​当中​站​起来，问​耶稣​说
“你​没有​什么​要​回应​的​吗？
他们​作证​告​你​的​事，你​没有​听​到​吗？”
耶稣​却​还是​默不作声，一​句​也​不​回答
大祭司​又​问​他​说
“你​是​不​是​当​受​称颂​者​的​儿子​基督？”
耶稣​说
“我​是
你们​会​看见人子坐​在​大能者​的​右边​
带​着​天云​来​到。”
大祭司​就​撕裂​衣服，说
“我们​还​需要​证人​吗？
你们​都​听见​亵渎​的​话​了
你们​认为​怎样？”
他们​全都​判​他​有​罪，应该​处死
有些​人​向​他​吐​唾沫
把​他​的​脸​蒙​住，用​拳头​打​他
对​他​说
“先知​你​说​吧！”
差役​把​他​带​走​时​还​打​了​他​耳光
彼得​在​下面​的​院子​里
大祭司​的​一​个​女仆​来​了
见​彼得​在​取暖，就​盯​着​他，说
“你​也​是​跟​那个​拿撒勒人​耶稣​一​伙​的。”
彼得​却​否认​说
“我​不​认识​他，也​不​知道​你​在​说​什么。”
他​就​走​到​外面​的​门厅
在​那里，女仆​见​到​他
又​对​站​在​旁边​的​人​说
“这个​人​跟​他们​是​一​伙​的。”
彼得​再次​否认
过​了​一会儿，站​在​旁边​的​人​又​对​彼得说​
“你​的确​跟​他们​是​一​伙​的
因为​你​是​个​加利利人。”
彼得​就​开始​赌咒​发誓​说
“我​不​认识​你们​说​的​那个​人。”
立刻​鸡​就​叫​了​第​二​次
彼得​想​起​耶稣​对​他​说​过​的​话
“鸡​叫​两​次​以前，你​会​三​次​不​认​我。”
他​就​忍​不​住​痛哭​了​起来
相信这些经文
能帮助我们为晚上的纪念聚会做好准备
在结束之前，我们想让你们知道
中央长老团非常爱你们！
不管今天晚上你在哪里
不管你正面对什么难题
我们都衷心地希望耶和华大大赐福给你
愿我们为今晚聚会所做的一切
都能为耶和华和耶稣基督带来荣耀和赞美！

ko.text: “용기를 내십시오!” 특별 지역 대회가 기대감 속에 열렸습니다.
아홉 개 나라에서 온 대표자들이 밤낮으로 잇달아 도착했습니다.
대표자 모두는 현지 형제 자매들의 따뜻한 환영을 받았습니다.
우릴 숙소까지 데려다 줬어요. 모든 게 잘 마련돼 있었죠.
여러 부서의 형제들이 1년 반 전부터 이 행사를 준비했습니다.
대표자들은 현지 전도인들과 야외 봉사를 하면서,
지부 사무실은 다양한 관광 코스를 준비했습니다.
문화도 배우고 영적인 유익도 얻을 수 있었습니다.
성구들과 하느님의 이름인 테트라그람마톤을 볼 수 있었습니다.
아름다운 카르파티아 산맥 지역을 관광하는 코스도 있었습니다.
그곳에 전시된 예술품과 역사적 유물을 관람했습니다.
스비르시성에서 90명 정도 되는 형제 자매들이 준비한 춤 공연을 즐기기도 했습니다.
대표자들은 지부 사무실도 견학했는데, 각 부서에서 하는 업무를 알아보고,
그들을 위해 특별 프로그램을 준비한 베델 가족과 교제를 나눴습니다.
우크라이나 여호와의 증인 역사를 다루는 동영상을 보여 주었습니다.
대표자들은 큰 격려를 받았고, 많은 사람이 감동의 눈물을 흘렸습니다.
동시에 대회가 열릴 경기장에서는 준비가 한창이었습니다.
이 경기장 전체가 여호와의 충실한 종들로 가득 차게 될 순간을 기다리고 있습니다.
우크라이나 지부 위원회는 여러분 모두를 따뜻하게 환영하게 되어 기쁩니다!
말이 서로 달라서 대화를 나누긴 어려웠지만, 서로 안아 줬어요.
대회 프로그램은 우크라이나어, 영어, 러시아어, 러시아 수화,
대회는 모두가 시련에도 불구하고 용기를 내도록 도와주었습니다.
우리 형제 자매들과 함께할 수 있었고,
어려울 때도 용기를 내는 법을 배울 수 있었던 즐거운 시간이었습니다.
여러분이 내린 결정을 결코 후회하지 않으실 겁니다.
하느님께서 함께하신다면, 아무도 우릴 대적할 수 없습니다.
우리의 편이 우리의 적보다 많기 때문입니다.
제가 감동받은 것 한 가지는 따뜻한 후대를 받은 것이었어요.
이곳 형제 자매들이 나타낸 친절과 후대를 많이 배우고 돌아갑니다.
여호와의 조직에 속해 있다는 또 하나의 증거죠.

en.text: In July 2018, a long-awaited event took place
in Lviv, Ukraine:
the “Be Courageous”! Special Convention.
The delegates were arriving from nine different countries
at all times of day and night.
Even so, all of them were warmly welcomed by local brothers and sisters.
When we got here, we were picked up and everything was just perfectly organized.
For about a year and a half,
brothers in various departments were preparing for this event.
We are confident in Jehovah’s blessing and support.
The delegates also worked with local publishers in the field service,
inviting the residents of Lviv to the convention.
The branch office organized different excursions.
Tours in the ancient city center enriched the delegates
not only culturally but also spiritually.
On some buildings, they could see Bible citations
and the Tetragrammaton of God’s name.
Outside of Lviv, tours included visiting the picturesque
Carpathian Mountains region.
The delegates also visited three castles,
in which art and historical exhibitions were on display.
In the Svirzh Castle, they enjoyed a dancing program,
in which about 90 brothers and sisters participated.
In the branch office, guests learned about the work done by each department
and got acquainted with the Bethel family, who had prepared a special program for them.
The evening gathering program consisted of songs, dances,
and a video about the history of Jehovah’s Witnesses in Ukraine.
It encouraged the guests a lot.
Many of them were even moved to tears.
At the same time, preparations at the stadium were underway.
We are waiting for the moment
when this whole stadium will be filled with faithful servants of Jehovah.
It’s a special privilege for the Branch Committee
in Ukraine to warmly welcome all of you!
We couldn’t speak the language.
You could barely say any words to each other, but the hugs and—
You could feel the love, and that’s why it was so special.
The convention program was held in four languages: Ukrainian,
English, Russian, and Russian Sign Language.
It helped everyone to be courageous despite any trials.
A special time for me
was to be able to be with my brothers and sisters
and learn to have courage despite difficulties.
The peak attendance at the convention
with 255 being baptized.
May Jehovah richly bless all of you.
You will never regret the decision you made today.
If God is for us, no one can be against us.
So put your trust in Jehovah
because there are more who are with us
than against us.
I can say one thing that stood out to me is that it taught me hospitality
at a level that I’ve never experienced before.
The way the brothers and sisters have been kind to us and treated us
is a lesson that I’ll bring back with me.
We can see that love.
It’s just another demonstration that we are in the true religion,
and this is Jehovah’s organization.
So it’s all thanks to him.

cn.text: 期待已久的“要鼓起勇气！”特别区域大会
在乌克兰的利沃夫举行
来自九个不同国家的大会代表
出席了这次的大会
无论他们何时到达
当地的弟兄姐妹都在机场热情地欢迎他们
一下飞机就有人来接我们
一切都安排得井井有条
弟兄们花了大概一年半的时间来准备这次大会
耶和华一定会帮助我们成功地举行这次的大会
代表们跟当地的弟兄姐妹一起传道
邀请人参加这个大会
利沃夫是乌克兰的历史文化中心
代表们也参观了一些名胜古迹
有些古老的建筑物上雕刻着圣经经文
以及上帝名字的四个希伯来字母
这些活动不仅帮助他们了解乌克兰的文化
也强化了他们的信心
此外，代表们也欣赏了喀尔巴阡山脉的壮丽景色
他们还参观了3座城堡
城堡内有艺术和历史展览
在斯维尔日城堡
他们看了一个舞蹈节目
由差不多90个弟兄姐妹一起表演
代表们也参观了乌克兰分部
有机会了解一下各部门的工作
也认识了伯特利家庭成员
伯特利家庭也为代表们准备了一个特别节目
为代表们准备的迎宾晚会的节目
包括歌曲、舞蹈
和一部介绍乌克兰传道历史的影片
代表们很受鼓励，甚至感动得流下眼泪
在同一时间，弟兄姐妹们
继续在大会场做最后的准备工作
我们一直很期待看到整个会场
都坐满亲爱的弟兄姐妹
乌克兰分部很荣幸能够举办这次大会
我们非常欢迎你们！
虽然我们不会说乌克兰语
但弟兄姐妹的拥抱，让我们感受到温暖的爱
大会节目以四种语言进行
分别是乌克兰语、英语
俄罗斯语和俄罗斯手语
大会激励我们在患难中表现勇气
能够跟弟兄姐妹们聚在一起
学习怎样在逆境中鼓起勇气
我真的很开心！
这个大会场的最高出席人数为
有255人受浸
愿耶和华赐下厚福给你们
你们绝不会后悔今天作出的决定
既然上帝与我们同在，就没有人能反对我们
要信靠耶和华
因为与我们同在的比反对我们的多得多
乌克兰的弟兄姐妹非常地热情好客
我实在是太感动了！
他们表现的爱心和仁慈让我印象深刻
所以，我也想用同样的方式对待其他弟兄姐妹
我们可以感受到弟兄姐妹之间的爱心
爱心是正确宗教的标志
这个组织的确是受耶和华指引的
我们真的非常感激他

en.text: Around the world,
Jehovah’s Witnesses show unfailing love.
In the next hour,
we’ll hear reports that highlight
real-life examples of such love.
We’ll consider how economic hardship,
natural disasters, and political upheaval
give us the opportunity
to show our unfailing love toward our brothers.
Later in the program,
we’ll see the immense support that’s given to special preaching campaigns
and to the construction of places of worship.
All these examples will prove that Jehovah’s organization
lives up to the words of 1 Peter 2:17:
“Have love for the whole association of brothers.”
Additionally, many of the reports will highlight
not only brotherly  love but also neighborly  love.
We do this by going to extraordinary lengths
to preach despite many challenges.
To get us started,
let’s see some examples of unfailing love in Africa.
Specifically, we’ll be talking
about how our brothers thrive spiritually
despite challenging economic circumstances.
We now have the privilege of getting reports
from Brother Paul Rahajanirina,
who serves on the Madagascar Branch Committee;
from Brother Baston Nyirenda,
who serves on the Malawi Branch Committee;
and from Brother Robert Elongo,
who serves on the Congo (Kinshasa) Branch Committee.
First, Brother Rahajanirina,
how have our brothers in Madagascar
experienced brotherly love?
Thank you, Brother Rahajanirina,
for sharing those beautiful examples
of brotherly love.
Next, let’s travel to Malawi to speak for a moment
with Brother Nyirenda.
Brother Nyirenda, how has the organization
shown love to our brothers in Malawi?
Thank you, Brother Nyirenda.
We’re happy to see how Jehovah not only provides spiritual food
but also makes it easier for us to consume it.
We now focus on our brothers
in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Brother Elongo,
how do economic circumstances
pose a challenge for our brothers there?
Brother Curzan,
the economic challenges are quite noticeable
in connection with conventions
and assemblies.
The majority of our brothers have to travel on foot,
or with bicycles, motorcycles,
and even trucks to reach the convention sites.
They simply do not have enough money
to arrange for other means of travel.
Once at the convention site,
the visiting brothers stay in the homes of local brothers.
In some cases, the branch has provided tents
so that brothers who may already have
people staying in their house
can also have guests stay in their yard.
But despite these logistical challenges,
close to 800,000 brothers and sisters
attended the regional convention in our branch territory.
The brothers love conventions very much,
and they always look forward to the next one.
But hospitality is needed also when it’s not convention season.
Sometimes political instability
requires our brothers to relocate to stay safe.
And when that happens, examples such as this sister’s
show the evidence of the unfailing love in our brotherhood.
My husband has passed away,
and I take care of three children
and nine grandchildren.
I have a full house.
It’s challenging to provide even for our basic needs.
A conflict broke out in the Kasai region,
so brothers from that region came all the way
on foot with no shoes
and only the clothes on their backs.
When I saw how many there were
and in what state,
it broke my heart.
But I prayed to Jehovah,
so Jehovah gave me courage and boldness to take the brothers in.
I decided to host three families in my house.
I had no foam mattresses for those 18 people.
All I could do was spread a piece of cloth
on the cement floor of the house for them to sleep on.
As the house has only one bedroom and a living room,
I asked the brothers to sleep in the bedroom
and the sisters with their children to sleep in the living room.
My love for Jehovah and for my fellow Christians
motivated me to take the brothers in.
I received many blessings
because the organization —Bethel—
sent food: flour, rice, oil, and clothes.
I was selling charcoal,
packing it in smaller bags to get some money to feed all of us.
Since Jehovah helped me in many ways
—even with my small business, and that we all lived together
without any disputes—
it was clear evidence of Jehovah’s support.
Everything that has happened has touched my heart so deeply.
I want to remain faithful
to Jehovah God’s organization
right up to the end.
I have many friends among the brothers and sisters
who sought refuge in my house.
These friends help me and tell me,
“Keep your love intact to the end.”
I look forward to seeing the brothers and sisters who sought refuge here
—who came empty-handed—
in the new world, in Paradise.
They will have a house and eat to their heart’s desire
without any problems.
When convention season and political upheaval happen to coincide,
arranging for accommodations for everyone can be challenging.
This happened in 2017.
The brothers near the convention site
were already housing the brothers
who had been displaced because of the fighting in their home region.
Still, arrangements were made
to accommodate those coming for the convention.
For example, some brothers
asked their non-Witness neighbors
to accommodate their guests
—and they did with pleasure.
And the visiting brothers made sure
to share the Kingdom message with their hosts,
with many positive results.
Very touching experiences, Brother Elongo.
Thank you for your fine report.
Thank you very much.
Next, let’s go to Asia.
We have with us Brother Yasushi Wakabayashi,
who serves on the Taiwan Branch Committee,
and also Brother Maurice Raj,
who serves on the Myanmar Branch Committee.
As you may know, Asia has recently been struck
by several natural disasters.
We want to start by asking Brother Wakabayashi,
What kinds of natural disasters
have the brothers and sisters
experienced in Taiwan?
Well, we have experienced many typhoons and earthquakes.
For example, an earthquake in 1999
killed some 2,400 people.
Although large earthquakes have not been very common,
we did have a magnitude 6.4 earthquake
An apartment building where a sister lived completely collapsed.
Thankfully, she was not home when the earthquake hit.
Another earthquake struck last year.
But it was so encouraging to see how much our brothers and sisters,
in the midst of disaster, value spiritual food.
My wife and I are currently working as translators
at the Amis Remote Translation Office in Hualien.
Amis is an indigenous language
spoken in the eastern part of Taiwan.
The earthquake struck around midnight of February 6th.
We heard very loud noises and people screaming outside.
Furniture fell over, and all my belongings were on the floor.
Brother and Sister Ruan ran into my room
and gave me a pair of shoes to wear.
I was stepping on broken glass as we fled outside.
All we had were the clothes on our backs and a bag.
Losing everything was hard on us emotionally.
However, the most important thing was,
not to focus on what I’d lost,
but how to resume the supply of spiritual food
—to continue to translate spiritual food for the Amis people.
We decided to move the translation office
to a Kingdom Hall close by, where it was safe.
The brothers and sisters all wanted the translation work to continue,
so everyone cooperated to get things set up at the office.
One brother even asked me: “Do you need a car?
“We can lend you one so you can commute
from your home to the office.”
Before we could agree,
he drove the car to where we were staying
and gave us the keys.
Many brothers and sisters sent things without asking us.
They sent many clothes,
meeting bags, ties,
shoes for my wife
—almost everything.
We had something new to wear every day.
This gave me a sense of urgency
to resume our work as soon as possible,
to translate our publications, and not to set things back.
We were able to resume our work at the RTO
just about a week after the earthquake.
The congregation arranged to witness to the victims at the shelter
the same weekend after the earthquake.
Some asked me:
“You are also a victim, and yet you are comforting others.
Why?”
Because I believed when I comforted others,
it brought me comfort too.
The love and zeal the brothers displayed
in such difficult times deeply touched our hearts.
The brothers and sisters are always very quick
to help when a natural disaster strikes.
For example, during the recent typhoon,
a tree fell on a sister’s house.
She later wrote to us about the events that followed.
She wrote: “As soon as you found out that my house
“was badly damaged by a tree —yes, immediately—
“arrangements were made not only to visit us
“but also to fix and rebuild.
“It has been a great witness
“to all my unbelieving family members,
relatives, and neighbors”
—a great example of unfailing love.
Still, while it is good not to presume
upon the love of our brothers,
sometimes the brothers and sisters
can be reluctant to ask for help.
For example, after a typhoon,
an elder called a sister to ask if she was doing OK.
She said: “I’m fine. We can manage.”
But actually her roof had blown away,
which to me would not really qualify as being OK.
So congregation elders have encouraged our brothers and sisters
not to be shy but to accept the help
that they are offered by the organization
as a reflection of Jehovah’s love.
That’s such a good point.
After all, we’re living at the end of this system of things,
with all that it entails,
and Jehovah asks us to trust in him.
Thank you for that report, Brother Wakabayashi.
You are welcome.
Next, let’s speak with Brother Maurice Raj
of the Myanmar Branch Committee.
Brother Raj, what Scriptural principles
have guided our brothers in Myanmar
to show love during natural disasters?
During one of our circuit visits, it started to rain heavily.
According to the news on the radio,
many of the roads in the area had collapsed;
and there were reports of landslides in Hakha,
the next congregation in our circuit.
The distance from where I was to Hakha was 65 miles.
Despite the dangerous conditions,
my wife and I decided to walk to Hakha.
I received a phone call from the branch.
They requested
for the Disaster Relief Committee to go and assist
the brothers in need in the disaster areas.
The committee prepared food and other supplies in a nearby city.
The road was very muddy,
so the trip took a long time.
It took four days to reach Hakha by foot.
When we arrived in Hakha, we discovered
that some of the brothers and sisters lost their homes.
So I met with the congregation elders,
and we arranged to make shepherding visits on these families.
It brought me joy to see that they were comforted through Jehovah’s Word.
Once we arrived in Hakha, we arranged to distribute
the food and other provisions that we had brought with us.
After that, we started a journey together to help other congregations.
It was a very difficult time for the brothers.
One brother said: “Because we were running low on food,
“our family was planning to eat just one meal per day.
“But now with the relief committee’s help,
we can eat all three meals.”
The brothers were so happy
and were really thankful to Jehovah and his organization
for their loving support.
The trip was quite rough,
but we felt that Jehovah supported us in wonderful ways.
In some places, the roads were very bad.
Sometimes we had to cling to the edge of a cliff.
We had to climb up very steep mountains
and then climb down steep mountains.
We even had to cross streams with strong currents.
I knew that I couldn’t give up,
so I kept saying to myself:
‘This is for God’s Kingdom. This is for God’s Kingdom.
Keep walking.’
That helped me to continue on my journey.
To provide the congregations with the supplies,
we walked 120 miles over four days.
God used us to show to his people
that he never abandons them
and that he really cares about them.
Knowing this brings such joy to our hearts.
It was such a wonderful privilege
for me to be involved in this relief work with Jehovah
in behalf of our brothers and sisters.
Well, thank you for sharing that excellent example
of showing unfailing love for our brothers.
Thank you, Brother Raj.
Next, we visit Europe.
Brother Jasin Ali serves on the Albania Branch Committee,
and Brother Lars Kassholm, on the Scandinavia Branch Committee.
First, let’s speak with Brother Ali.
The Albania branch
oversees the work in Kosovo,
where a preaching campaign
was recently arranged.
Brother Ali,
why was there a need for a preaching campaign in Kosovo?
The publisher-to-population ratio
in Kosovo is the largest in all Europe,
with 1 publisher to more than 8,700 inhabitants.
This means that quite a number of cities
and villages are seldom preached in,
and many others have never received a witness.
When this preaching campaign started,
almost one million of Kosovo’s population
had never heard the truth.
While many people in this territory have a religious outlook
and have heard of the Bible and about Jesus Christ,
many often connect religion with some of the atrocities
that were committed in recent political conflicts in the region.
Numerous families have been personally affected
by the war of the 1990’s in Kosovo,
and in many cases, they have lost loved ones in death.
So it truly was an expression of love
by the brothers and sisters who answered the call for help
with this campaign.
When we heard about the campaign,
we thought about how wonderful it would be
if at least 200 volunteers would come.
We were thrilled but also really nervous
when we found out that over 600 volunteers were going to come.
As soon as we heard about the campaign
being organized in Kosovo,
we were very excited and really wanted to take part in it.
Our limited income meant
that we would have to calculate the cost carefully.
Also, because I lost my sight,
the adjustment to a new environment preaching in villages
obviously would not be easy for me.
I was offered a scholarship
from a university in Tirana.
But my mind was made up,
and my goal was to take part in this campaign
and to give my best to Jehovah.
Since I serve at Bethel,
I used my vacation days
to come here for the campaign.
This campaign has been
an answer to my prayers.
It was like Jehovah was saying:
‘Keep trying.
‘You have brothers and sisters
who are supporting you.’
I have worked with brothers and sisters
from all over the world on this campaign.
The sacrifices that they have made to come here
have been a real source
of encouragement to me.
I understood how much appreciation
the volunteers were showing
for the opportunity from Jehovah
to support the campaign.
I was deeply touched.
If I could use all the words in the world to describe the joy
this campaign gave me, they wouldn’t be enough.
Now I have seen with my own eyes
my worldwide family,
and I feel in my heart the love and care
that they have for us.
As you heard, the campaign had a profound effect
on the local publishers.
But it also had an impact in the field.
For example, one day a group of publishers from different countries
were having lunch in a local restaurant.
They noticed that a group of policemen
that were having lunch in the same restaurant
were often looking over at them.
So two brothers decided to approach them
and start a conversation with them.
One of the officers said that he had seen the publishers in the city
and knew all of them very well.
Then he added:
“You are doing a very fine work.
“If everyone did the same work as you,
there would be no more need for a police force!”
This campaign resulted
not only in the formation of new groups and pregroups in some areas
but also motivated the local publishers.
It’s amazing to see how initiatives like this campaign
can be an expression of both brotherly and neighborly love.
Thank you, Brother Ali.
Next, we turn to Brother Lars Kassholm in Scandinavia.
The Scandinavia branch office oversees,
among other places, the work in Sweden.
How have recent world events
shaped the preaching efforts in Sweden?
In Sweden, meeting refugees in the ministry
has been common for many years,
and we have had foreign-language congregations for decades.
However, in 2015,
over 160,000 refugees arrived in Sweden.
So over a period of two years, the Service Department approved
forming 45 new foreign-language groups
and pregroups in Sweden,
so today we have over 90,
plus a number of foreign-language congregations.
Even in small congregations,
the brothers have worked very hard
to invite refugees to the meetings.
This has often resulted in Kingdom Halls packed to capacity.
Thousands of refugees come to Sweden every year.
Some of these are sent into different refugee camps
around Jönköping.
I came from Burundi
as a refugee because of the war.
I came to Sweden when I was 17.
I came alone.
When you come as a refugee, you are a stranger.
You miss your family, you miss your friends,
you miss everything.
They need hope, they need the truth,
and Jehovah has given us the privilege to give this to them.
Many of these camps were in isolated areas.
Sometimes when you visited them, there could be
three or four different nationalities in the same room.
Some of the friends also learned a few different greetings.
Before setting off, we downloaded videos in up to 30 languages.
Sometimes we connected interested ones with brothers
who spoke their language through video calls.
When we did not receive permission to preach at the camp,
we had to find other methods.
We tried to invite people
to a meeting in Swahili,
and more than 50 people came.
We had to borrow several child seats
and ask many of the friends to help.
I feel that Jehovah has helped me to become more open-minded
—much more patient and empathetic.
There were long days,
and sometimes you were tired in the evening.
But when you looked out and saw your brothers and sisters
making the same sacrifice,
that motivated you to continue.
When you saw the way they accepted the truth,
how it formed and transformed them,
it was worth all the effort.
Although many of us from Sweden are known as somewhat reserved,
when we meet a person who has lost everything
—everything, even his family and friends—
it really touches our hearts.
Today, our territory reminds us
of Jesus’ words at John 4:35:
“Lift up your eyes and view the fields,
that they are white for harvesting.”
While Sweden is one of the most secular lands in the world,
with the influx of refugees,
we now have territories filled with God-fearing people.
These people are very often very disappointed in their religion,
so we are now happy to help them
by offering them a solid hope for the future
and giving them a meaning in life.
Of course, it takes an effort to study the Bible
with someone in another language.
But to be used by Jehovah in this special way
brings us even closer to him.
So we are very grateful to Jehovah
for this opportunity we have now
to help refugees in Sweden.
We appreciate the brothers and sisters in Sweden
for setting a good example of neighborly love.
Thank you for that report, Brother Kassholm.
We’ve now come to North America,
and we’ll be talking with Brother Anthony Griffin,
who serves on the United States Branch Committee.
And we’ll continue focusing on neighborly love.
Brother Griffin, you mentioned to me earlier
that you’ve seen a pattern,
a pattern of what it takes
to show personal interest.
Can you tell us a bit more about that?
Absolutely.
When you talk to brothers and sisters
who have progressive Bible studies
and who have successfully aided new ones to serve Jehovah,
what you’ll notice is that patterns begin to emerge.
One of the patterns is that they prepare
before they go out in service.
How does that help?
When you’re prepared, you’re more relaxed,
and thus you’re more friendly when you present the good news at the door.
Another pattern is that effective Bible teachers—
They think, they pray, and they act
on the personal needs and concerns of Bible students,
whether those needs are physical
or emotional or spiritual.
It’s kind of what—
It reminds you of what Paul said at 1 Corinthians 9:22.
He said that he became
“all things
“to people of all sorts,
so that [he] might by all possible means save some.”
So this means that inside
every successful Bible teacher
is a heart that is filled with love for people.
And it’s this love, this outstretching love,
that has motivated some to learn a new language.
Some have moved to a foreign-language congregation
in order to help and assist more to learn about Jehovah.
As an example of this, I’d like to introduce you
to Sister Sally Giltinan.
Sister Giltinan did not allow anything
to stop her from showing neighborly love.
Just prior to my baptism,
unfortunately, I became critically ill.
I was eventually told that I had two hours to live.
The doctors insisted that I have
a blood transfusion, and I took my stand.
There was no question that I was willing to die for Jehovah.
But the question to me was, Was I willing to live for him?
And I became all the more determined
to use my life to serve Jehovah.
So obviously, I lived.
It motivated me to really be focused on the ministry.
I began regular pioneering when I was 17.
It’s been a privilege
to study with people who were Baptist and Catholic
and Methodist and Episcopalian
—some were Atheists, some were rich, some were poor.
There were five parents that came with their children,
and there were 13 children.
I was in such a supportive congregation,
and there were so many young pioneers who had the energy
—those couples were so important to me.
When my husband and I got married,
we were in a rural congregation in Virginia.
Eventually, we wound up in the Spanish territory.
With so many migrant workers,
I just wanted to be able to talk to them.
It was a challenge because I didn’t speak Spanish!
I never let that stop me,
so I learned enough to get my foot in the door.
While I didn’t speak Spanish, I spoke the language of love
—Jehovah’s love— and that’s what they were relating to.
And I would work so hard to prepare for Bible studies.
And the goal was not just to teach doctrinal truth
but to teach them to know Jehovah.
I would take some Bible students to visit other Bible students
so they could encourage one another.
Eventually, the brothers determined that they could hold a meeting.
We thought 20 or 25 would come.
Eighty-two people came to the first Spanish meeting.
It was such a joyful day
to watch them associate with each other.
It was a family, and it continues to be to this day.
For 35 years, David and I have driven separately to the meetings.
We generally take two different cars to pick people up.
I usually have a car full of people that I’m bringing.
He will often have people he’s picking up.
If I’m going to teach people
to know Jehovah and to love him,
it begins with me.
So if my heart is filled with love
for Jehovah and for people,
hopefully it will show.
Obviously, you try really hard to teach the truth.
I think that, if anything,
it’s been the language of love.
I wanted so much for them to feel that love
that Jehovah showed me in the beginning.
So showing personal interest by applying Bible principles
—it really does work!
And this can be demonstrated in many different ways.
For example, in Los Angeles, California,
there was a brother who was in a coffee shop,
and he noticed a man who was reading a newspaper.
So he approached the man, and he simply asked him,
“Is there any good news in there today?”
So that led to a conversation,
and the man brought up something that concerned him.
He was concerned about his young daughter.
So the brother asked him,
“Can I show you something on the website
that might assist you in helping your daughter?”
So he showed him one of the Caleb and Sophia videos.
Then after further discussion,
the man wanted to know where the Kingdom Hall was.
So the brother took him right back to the website
and showed him the address of the local Kingdom Hall.
What was the result of all of this?
That man who was reading the newspaper at the coffee shop
is now one of our brothers.
And his daughter?
She’s making wonderful progress in the truth.
Well, thank you, Brother Griffin,
for sharing those beautiful experiences
about showing personal interest.
Let’s now talk for a moment about how our brothers
faithfully care for our places of worship,
which essentially is an aspect of showing love for Jehovah
and our fellow brothers and sisters.
This takes us to Oceania,
where we have Brother Kegawale Biyama,
who’s joining us from the Papua New Guinea Branch Committee,
and Brother Abraham Lincoln,
who serves on the Micronesia Branch Committee.
We turn first to Brother Biyama.
What need for places of worship
currently exists in Papua New Guinea?
Currently, we need to construct
22 new Kingdom Halls
and renovate 26 existing halls.
Because of the increasing interest shown in the field,
most of our big congregations in our main towns have had to split.
Attendances at those congregations’ weekend meetings
are generally double the seating capacity
of their existing Kingdom Halls.
So when a new Kingdom Hall is built,
the brothers and sisters do all they can
to support the LDC brothers who have come
from afar to assist with that building.
To accomplish the construction work here in PNG,
there are many challenges.
Sometimes there is no road,
so the brothers and sisters
have to carry all the materials
to the site to build a Kingdom Hall.
Sometimes it’s hard to travel to other areas for work
because we leave behind our family and our friends.
When we work on a Kingdom Hall, everyone in the congregation helps us.
They cook for us
and support the work on the site.
In one congregation, they gave everything they had to support the work.
They wake up early in the morning
and walk down the mountains,
bringing food with them.
It takes them three or four hours.
They come onto the construction site,
and they cook food.
After the construction team eats,
they clean up
and they walk back.
It takes them three to four hours again,
so around 9:00 p.m. or 10:00 p.m., they arrive home.
Sometimes it’s hard for them
because they have their own family to support.
It’s a huge sacrifice that they’ve given to come and support this work.
At the same time, we get encouragement at the meetings
and when we are out witnessing.
Some give encouragement to help us do this work.
Then we go out on the weekends to swim and play.
In that way, we meet a lot of brothers and sisters,
and they become as family to us.
When brothers and sisters give everything to support us in the work,
this encourages me to give my best to do this work.
Construction is hard work,
and there are many challenges.
But you will receive many wonderful blessings.
You will learn to trust in Jehovah,
and also you will be happy doing this work.
It’s fascinating to see how the outpouring of love for Jehovah
can be manifested in not only practical ways,
such as by cooking food for our brothers,
but also how it can motivate the brothers
assigned to the construction project.
Yes, and the love we see is not limited
to the construction of the building
but extends to the upkeep of the hall as well.
Many passersby have stood in front of the Kingdom Hall property
to take pictures because of its well-kept look.
That really shows how our love can be a great shout of praise to Jehovah.
Thank you, Brother Biyama, for that good report.
And while some places have a huge need for Kingdom Halls,
others require similar effort
because of the remoteness of the location.
Brother Lincoln, the island of Tonoas
is part of your branch territory.
How did the brothers there
show how much they treasure
their places of worship?
The brothers take seriously
their responsibility
to maintain the Kingdom Hall,
as was visible in a recent renovation project.
With the assistance of local and international servants,
this small congregation of 31 publishers
was able to complete the project in only 11 weeks.
Our island of Tonoas is very beautiful.
But many people have no jobs.
Previously, the Kingdom Hall was very small.
Even though we endeavored to clean inside and out,
there were many things that were in bad condition
because there was no money —not enough.
It was no longer suitable for a sizable group to worship Jehovah there.
We were very happy when we heard
that Jehovah’s organization would help us
with the Kingdom Hall in Tonoas.
We are grateful for the way Jehovah’s love was clearly manifested
and for the love of our brothers from distant lands.
There were difficulties that we experienced when the materials
arrived in Chuuk from Guam.
We received the materials,
using a flatbed truck to take them to a barge to be transported
from the capital island of Weno to Tonoas.
Upon reaching Tonoas,
it was very difficult to unload because there is no dock.
We used a motorboat to carry the materials
from the barge to the drop-off point
so that it could reach the job site.
On our island, people do not view construction as being women’s work.
But with the help of the brothers who came from distant lands,
they really helped the sisters to understand how to use the tools.
Many villagers would kind of mock them:
“Look at those Jehovah’s Witnesses going to work.
That’s not supposed to be women’s work!”
But our sisters ignored it
because of their deep love for Jehovah;
they walked, singing our songs
so that they would not hear others mocking them.
Today, we are very thankful to our God, Jehovah,
and to our brothers around the world
because of their love and hard work on behalf
of our new Kingdom Hall.
It really is a beautiful building for Jehovah
and for people in Tonoas to see
what love Jehovah’s people have among them.
As Hebrews 6:10 plainly tells us about Jehovah’s promise,
‘he will not forget the love and hard work’
his people performed on our behalf.
Though we can see how deep the Pacific Ocean is that separates us,
because of Jehovah’s love for us,
it feels as if we are very close together as a family.
It took the action and efforts of many involved
to complete this renovation project.
Through this action, the brothers and sisters
showed how much they value their Kingdom Halls
as places where we can go
and “give thanks to [Jehovah] in the great congregation,”
as stated at Psalm 35:18.
A lot of love goes into building each Kingdom Hall,
and you highlighted that well.
Brother Lincoln, thank you very much.
Thank you.
We have one more continent to visit, and that’s South America.
There we have Brother Douglas Little,
who serves on the Bolivia Branch Committee,
and we also have Brother Geraldo Meilsmith,
who’s on the Brazil Branch Committee.
The friends in South America
set a great example of reaching out
to the many indigenous peoples,
so we’ll be focusing on that for the next few minutes.
Brother Little, what does the branch in Bolivia do
to reach remote populations
with the good news?
Well, Brother Curzan,
Bolivia has dozens of indigenous languages
spread throughout the country.
Some of these languages have over a million speakers,
and others, only a few hundred speakers.
So when Acts 1:8 speaks about witnessing
“to the most distant part of the earth,”
we feel that we need to do our part.
One way that we reach out to these populations
is through campaigns.
Once we have established
that an area or language has potential for growth,
we look at how we can give that field more permanent support.
For example, we encourage pioneers
to take up the challenge of learning an indigenous language.
And when pioneers from other countries
write expressing their interest in serving in Bolivia,
we include a recommendation of an indigenous language group
they could consider serving in.
And to give you an idea of what it’s like,
we would like you to meet these two sisters who came here to serve.
My parents were in the international construction work before we were born.
And we didn’t know it as we were growing up,
but they were planning on someday
moving to another country to pioneer.
My name is Jessica.
My name is Mariah.
We’re from the United States.
And we’re serving in Beni, Bolivia.
We had our doubts at first about moving to another country.
When you’re pioneering in this area,
you’re in the sun a lot.
You’re either walking or riding a motorcycle
or sometimes a bicycle out in service.
Also, you are adapting to a new culture
—a new culture and new ways of eating
that are different than what we’re used to.
But once we got here and we started going out in service,
we met the brothers and sisters and we fell in love with Bolivia.
Once, we were preaching by boat,
and we arrived at one indigenous community.
And a man on a motorcycle came,
and he started picking everybody up and collecting them.
And we were worried at first.
We thought that he didn’t want them to listen to us,
and so he was taking them all away.
But it turned out in the end that he was the son
of the chieftain there in that community,
and he was gathering everyone together
so that they could all listen to us.
It’s something that you would never really get to do back home.
Moving here has helped us
to see Jehovah’s hand
more directly in our life.
We’ve gotten to be part of activities
that maybe we’ve heard about in a Yearbook
or maybe we hear about on the broadcast,
but getting to live those activities makes us feel very happy
and closer to the organization as well.
We get to see
how Jehovah is moving the organization in the last days
to reach as many people as possible.
That really drew us a lot closer to Him
because we were forced to trust more in him than in ourselves.
So put the car in motion,
and Jehovah will bless you.
Jehovah has richly blessed
all these efforts of our brothers and sisters
to reach out to the indigenous populations.
To give you another example,
a caravan of 11 four-wheel-drive vehicles
with 62 brothers and sisters
went to the remote Izozog region,
where the people speak Bolivian Guarani.
They were able to bring with them the recently translated Teach Us  book.
And as the brothers and sisters went door to door in each small village,
the villagers would walk by
and tell them not to forget to visit their houses too.
Some were so excited to receive the brothers
that they didn’t want to risk not being home when they came by,
so they brought their chair to their neighbor’s house
where the brothers and sisters were already visiting
and sat down to participate in the discussion.
Thank you, Brother Little, for sharing that with us,
and we wish Jehovah’s continued blessing
on the preaching work in Bolivia.
We’ll now travel to Brazil to speak with Brother Meilsmith.
As in Bolivia, the branch in Brazil
has made concerted efforts to cover remote territories.
Can you tell us a bit about that,
Brother Meilsmith?
When we graduated from the School for Kingdom Evangelizers,
to our surprise, we were assigned to the Sateré-Mawé field.
This is an indigenous language spoken in the Amazon rain forest.
It was a challenge for us because the assignment
was about 4,000 kilometers (2,485 miles) away from our home and our friends.
My name is Alex, and this is my wife, Rosane.
We’ve been serving in this language
for about a year and a half.
We wanted to put into practice right away everything we had learned.
But how could we do that if we didn’t know the language?
All we heard was blah, blah, blah; I couldn’t understand anything!
We know a sister who’s a native speaker, so we asked her for a lot of help.
We wanted to be able to know enough to at least be able to preach
and understand a little bit of the language.
We noticed that the Sateré people
would come into the city and then go home on a crowded boat.
So we and some other sisters decided to go with them.
We were a little nervous,
and we didn’t know where we were going to spend the night
or even if the people would allow us to stay in the village.
But they were very loving and received us well.
Some even offered for us to stay in their houses.
Since we didn’t know the language very well,
we decided to learn just one presentation
—to teach them Jehovah’s name.
We showed God’s name at every door.
Some of them were really surprised.
They had a Bible;
they had God’s name right there in their Bible,
but they didn’t know that Jehovah is God.
It was exciting for us to see them learning Jehovah’s name for the first time.
Who would want to learn a language
spoken in the rain forest by only 10,000 people?
But we know that Jehovah loves all sorts of people.
He wants even people who live
in isolated places, like the rain forest, to know him.
I’ve fallen in love with the people, the assignment, and the language.
It’s a beautiful language.
Even with all the sacrifices we’ve made materially,
we’ve never lacked anything.
And I think that going through the experience of living here
has strengthened our confidence in Jehovah.
It’s helped us to not rely on our own strength.
We’ve really seen how well Jehovah takes care of us.
That’s such a good point.
The love we show is ultimately an extension of Jehovah’s love
for those with a spiritual need.
Thank you for your report, Brother Meilsmith.
And that concludes our travels
to visit our brothers and sisters around the globe.
Do you remember the different examples
of brotherly and neighborly love we’ve seen in the past hour?
We saw how our brothers and sisters in Africa
show love by helping each other to cope
with difficult economic circumstances.
When we visited Asia, we saw the love
shown during times of natural disasters.
In Europe, preaching campaigns
were used to share the good news.
We saw examples from North America
of how personal interest can reach a humble person’s heart.
And a lot of love and effort was put into supporting
construction, renovation, and upkeep
of places of worship in Oceania.
And finally, in South America,
we joined our brothers and sisters as they went out of their comfort zone
to preach to indigenous and remote populations.
In the first talk of this convention,
the chairman promised that this symposium
would make you feel proud
to be a part of our international brotherhood.
We’re confident these examples had that effect.
Still, each one of us needs to ask himself:
‘Am I doing my part?
‘Do I show unfailing love
toward my brothers and my neighbors?’
This is what Jehovah requires of us.
Although our circumstances may differ,
when we do our utmost to display love in daily life,
we prove that we are taught by Jehovah, our Father,
whose “love never fails.”

cn.text: 不论什么情况
世界各地的耶和华见证人
都努力表现爱心
在这个专题节目中
我们会看到一些真实的经历
看看弟兄姐妹在物资匮乏
遭遇天灾
和饱受战乱的地区
怎样不断表现爱心
另外我们也会看看
弟兄姐妹怎样全力参与特别传道活动
以及热心支持组织的建筑工程
这些经历显示
我们的确在实践彼得前书2:17说的
“爱整个弟兄团体”
另外我们也会看看弟兄姐妹怎样克服困难
付出极大的努力帮助人认识真理
弟兄姐妹用行动表明他们不仅彼此相爱
也爱不是信徒的人
首先
我们会看看非洲的弟兄姐妹怎样表现爱心
那里的一些弟兄姐妹虽然经济条件不好
但还是快乐地崇拜上帝
我们很高兴跟保罗·拉哈雅尼里纳弟兄连线
他是马达加斯加分部委员会的成员
另外有巴斯东·尼伦达
他是马拉维分部委员会的成员
最后是罗贝尔·埃隆格
刚果（金沙萨）分部委员会的成员
保罗
马达加斯加的弟兄姐妹
怎样感受到基督徒大家庭的爱心呢？
马达加斯加是世上最穷的国家之一
百分之80的人一天收入不到2美元
许多人连医药费这样的基本开销也负担不起
马达加斯加分部一直和中央长老团保持联系
让他们了解这里弟兄姐妹的最新情况
这样其他分部就可以向我们提供协助了
例如，法国有一群做医生和护士的弟兄姐妹
组成医疗团队
来这里义诊好几次
他们不怕天气炎热
道路崎岖
从一个村落前往另一个村落
弟兄姐妹得到很大的帮助
举例来说
一些年迈的弟兄姐妹听力不好
也没有钱到大一点的城市就医
医疗团队就直接去他们那里
