ko.text: “내 백성이 ... 생명의 물의 근원인 나를 버렸고,
자기들을 위해 ... 물을 담을 수 없는 터진 저수조를 팠다.”
‘이스라엘 백성은 그렇게 많은 걸 보고 경험했는데도,
어떻게 여호와를 떠나 다른 곳에서 지혜와 도움을 구할 수가 있지?’
우리에게 경고가 되는 교훈점을 얻을 수 있을까요?
오늘날 우리는 여호와께서 그분의 조직을 통해 베푸시는
전 세계에 있는 우리 형제 자매들이
여호와의 조직과 지금처럼 가까웠던 적이 없다고 말하는 것을
우린 생명을 주는 진리의 물을 그 어느 때보다 풍성히 공급받고 있죠.
여호와와 진리의 순결한 물을 떠나 가치가 없는 것들을 추구하죠.
그런 일이 없도록 어떻게 해야 할까요?
오늘 일용할 성구 해설의 처음 세 문장에 유의해 보셨나요?
“사탄 마귀는 우리가 여호와의 인도를 받을 때
생명을 얻게 된다는 것을 알고 있습니다.
그래서 우리가 그분의 음성을 듣지 못하게 하려고 혈안이 되어 있습니다.
또한 우리 자신의 ‘믿을 수 없는 마음’도
여호와의 인도를 잘 따르는 데 방해가 될 수 있습니다.”
‘믿을 수 없는 마음이 여호와의 인도를 따르는 데 방해가 된다’는 표현에서
우리가 잘 알듯이, 여호와께선 솔로몬을 축복하셔서
그가 순종하는 데 필요한 걸 다 주셨지만,
결국 솔로몬은 그분과의 좋은 관계를 잃었습니다.
시작은 좋았지만 무슨 일이 생긴 겁니까?
오늘 해설에 나온 것과 같은 일이 벌어진 것입니다.
여호와의 인도를 따르는 데 방해가 되었습니다.
사실 여호와께서 솔로몬에게 주신 지침은 매우 분명했죠.
그 예로 신명기 17장을 들 수 있는데요,
왕은 정기적으로 율법을 읽고, 베껴 써야 했습니다.
‘왕은 자기를 위해 말을 많이 소유해서는 안 됩니다.’
“또 그는 아내를 많이 두어 마음이 빗나가는 일이 없게 해야 합니다.
은과 금을 아주 많이 소유해서도 안 됩니다.”
말과 아내와 은과 금을 많이 소유하지 말라고 했는데,
신명기 7:3, 4에서도 여호와께선 ‘나라들과 결혼 동맹을 맺지 말라’고
‘그들이 다른 신들을 섬기게 할 것’이라고 말씀하셨습니다.
“솔로몬 왕은 파라오의 딸 외에도 많은 외국 여자를 사랑했는데,
그들은 모압과 암몬과 에돔과 시돈과 헷 여자들이었다.
여호와께서는 전에 그 민족들에 대해 이스라엘 사람들에게 이렇게 말씀하셨다.
그들이 너희 가운데로 들어와서도 안 된다.
그들이 분명 너희 마음을 기울어지게 하여
그들의 신들을 따르게 할 것이기 때문이다.’
그런데도 솔로몬은 그들에게 빠져 그들을 사랑했다.
그의 아내들이 점차 그의 마음을 기울어지게 했다.”
자기도 모르게 아내가 700명에 후궁이 300명이나 된 게 아닙니다!
여호와의 지시에서 벗어난 나쁜 결정들을 내렸고,
그러다 결국엔 여호와로부터 완전히 멀어지게 되었습니다.
그런 결정들을 내렸는지 우리는 알 수 없지만,
어떤 일이 있었을지 짐작해 볼 수는 있습니다.
솔로몬이 파라오의 딸을 아내로 삼았다는 내용이 제일 먼저 나오는데,
어떻게 여호와께서 그에게 모든 지혜를 주시고
그런데 그 일은 솔로몬이 파라오의 딸을 아내로 삼은 이후의 일이죠.
그는 ‘여호와께서 축복하셨으니, 괜찮다는 뜻일 거야’라고 생각했을까요?
사실, 솔로몬도 자신의 결정에 문제가 있다는 걸 알았는데,
역대기하 8:11은 그가 아내를 위해 따로 집을 지었다고 알려 주죠.
외국인인 파라오의 딸은 그곳에 살 수 없었습니다.
모압 사람들은 여호와의 적이었지만, 다 그런 건 아니었죠.
예를 들어, 다윗이 사울왕을 피해 다닐 때의 일을 기억하실 겁니다.
그는 모압왕에게 자기 부모를 모시고 와도 되겠냐고 물었고,
실제로 모압왕은 다윗의 부모를 보호해 주었습니다.
기록을 보면, 다윗이 은신처에서 지내는 동안 내내 그렇게 해 주었죠.
솔로몬의 할아버지와 할머니를 보호해 준 것입니다.
다윗의 용사들 중에도 모압과 암몬 사람들이 있었습니다.
그러니까 모압 사람이 다 나쁜 건 아니었죠.
솔로몬은 다윗의 용사들이나 모압에 거주했던 조부모를 통해
나중에 왕이 된 솔로몬의 아들 르호보암을 기억하시죠?
솔로몬이 왕이 되기 전에 태어났다는 겁니다.
‘이집트 아내도 있고 암몬 아내도 있는데, 여호와께서 날 축복하시는구나.
이 법은 나한텐 적용 안 되나 봐.’
성전 건축을 위해 시돈 사람들이 많은 양의 목재를 가져오게 했습니다.
후에 솔로몬도 그들과 계약을 맺어 성전을 위한 나무를 베게 했습니다.
혹시 솔로몬은 이런 사업 관계가 계기가 되어
처음으로 시돈 여자들을 소개받고 아내로 맞이한 것입니까?
여호와의 집을 짓는 이 신권 임명을 완수하는 데 틀림없이 도움이 될 거야.’
하나만 더 얘기하면, 헷 여자들도 있었습니다.
밧세바의 남편인 우리아를 죽게 한 일을 기억하실 것입니다.
우리아는 헷 사람이고 다윗의 용사 중 하나였습니다.
그러니까 솔로몬의 어머니는 헷 사람과 결혼했던 것입니다.
혹시 솔로몬은 밧세바를 통해서, 또는 밧세바의 이전 시댁 식구들이나
다른 누군가를 통해 처음으로 헷 여자들을 아내로 소개받은 것입니까?
솔로몬의 생각을 정확히 알 순 없지만,
우리는 그가 자신이 처음에 내린 결정들을
어떻게 합리화했는지 추리해 볼 수 있습니다.
솔로몬은 그러다가 결국 여호와로부터 완전히 멀어지게 되었습니다.
솔로몬이 아내들을 늘려가고, 부를 쌓고, 말들을 모아가는 기록을 읽는 건
차가 충돌하는 과정을 슬로 모션으로 보는 것과 같습니다.
우린 그 차가 어떻게 될지 보이는데, 솔로몬은 보지 못했죠.
따라서 이런 자문을 해 봐야 합니다.
책으로 쓰여져서 다른 누군가가 볼 수 있다면,
그 사람은 나에 대해 어떻게 생각할 것인가?’
네, 우리의 마음은 믿을 수 없습니다.
우리 마음은 여호와의 분명한 지시를 어기도록 스스로를 합리화하려고 합니다.
여호와의 축복을 받고 있는 것처럼 보이기 때문에,
또는 다른 사람도 같은 결정을 했고, 결과가 좋아 보이기 때문에
자신이 내린 결정을 합리화할 수 있습니다.
“마음을 다해 여호와를 신뢰하고 자신의 이해에 의존하지 마라.”
“자신의 이해” 즉 자신의 지혜에 의존하지 마십시오.
우리는 결코 “생명의 물의 근원”을 버리지 않게 될 것입니다.
우리는 그분의 인도를 통해 영원히 유익을 얻을 것입니다.

en.text: Jeremiah 2:13:
“My people . . . have abandoned me,
“the source of living water,
“and dug for themselves . . .
broken cisterns, that cannot hold water.”
Now, we often may think,
‘How is it possible that Jehovah’s people
‘—after all they saw, all they experienced—
could leave Jehovah and look for wisdom and support elsewhere?’
And yet, it happened over and over again.
Is there a lesson and a warning for us?
Well, yes, there is.
Today, we appreciate so much all of the spiritual provisions
that we’re receiving from Jehovah through his organization.
Travel all around the world, and our brothers and sisters
say they have never felt closer to Jehovah’s organization than they do now.
We’re receiving life-giving waters of truth as we never have before.
But even so, just as in Jeremiah’s time, some of our dear brothers and sisters
are leaving Jehovah or have left Jehovah
and the pure waters of truth and pursued worthless things.
How can that happen?
How do we make sure that does not happen to us?
Well, did you notice the point in our text comment, the first two sentences?
It says this; it says: “Satan the Devil is intent on neutralizing
“the lifesaving guidance we receive from Jehovah.
“Moreover, our own ‘treacherous heart’
could interfere with how well we respond to Jehovah’s directives.”
Now, when I think of the statements
—“treacherous heart” and ‘how we respond to Jehovah’s directives’—
I cannot help but think of Solomon.
Now, we know Solomon’s account, how Jehovah blessed him
—gave him everything he needed to be obedient—
but Solomon ended up losing his precious record with Jehovah.
He abandoned “the source of living water.”
Now, Solomon started off so well.
What happened to him?
Well, exactly what our text is talking about here today.
He allowed his treacherous heart to interfere
with Jehovah’s directives.
Now, the directives that Jehovah gave Solomon were very, very clear.
Look at, for example, Deuteronomy chapter 17.
And as we remember, as the king, he was supposed to read this law
on a regular basis and write this law on a regular basis.
Deuteronomy 17:16, 17
—it says: “However, he [in the context, it’s talking about the king]
should not acquire many horses for himself.”
Verse 17: “Neither should he take many wives for himself,
“so that his heart may not go astray;
nor should he acquire vast amounts of silver and gold for himself.”
Do not acquire horses, wives,
vast amounts of silver and gold.
Solomon did all three.
You look at Deuteronomy 7:3, 4,
and there Jehovah says: ‘Do not form marriage alliances
with the nations because they will lead you astray.’
What did Solomon do?
Well, look over in 1 Kings chapter 11,
and look at verses 1-3.
First Kings 11:1-3—it says:
“But King Solomon loved many foreign women
“besides the daughter of Pharaoh:
“Moabite, Ammonite, Edomite, Sidonian, and Hittite women.
“They were from the nations about whom Jehovah said to the Israelites:
“‘You must not go in among them,
“‘and they should not come in among you,
“‘for they will surely incline your heart to follow their gods.’
“But Solomon clung to them and loved them.
“And he had 700 wives who were princesses
“and 300 concubines,
and his wives gradually inclined his heart” —just as Jehovah said.
Now, how did this happen?
Solomon did not just fall into sin.
Solomon just didn’t, in a moment of weakness—
He didn’t just wake up one day and realize, “Oh my word,
I have 700 wives and 300 concubines!”
If he did, Solomon had more problems than we thought he did.
No, Solomon was an intelligent man.
This was a man who was blessed by Jehovah with wisdom.
How did he deviate so far?
Well, it was a series of decisions —one after another—
that differed from Jehovah’s directives
that somehow he was able to explain away,
rationalize away, until he was completely alienated from Jehovah.
Now, we don’t know
what was going through Solomon’s mind or how he made those decisions,
but even from our limited perspective,
we can see how that could have happened.
For example, he starts off talking about the daughter of Pharaoh.
Now, he took the daughter of Pharaoh as a wife.
But, interestingly, in 1 Kings chapter 3,
it relates how Jehovah granted him all the wisdom and blessed him.
Well, that was after he had taken the daughter of Pharaoh as a wife.
So is it possible that Solomon thought,
‘Well, you know, Jehovah still blessed me; this must mean everything is OK’?
Now, Solomon knew something wasn’t quite right there
because at 2 Chronicles 8:11,
it says he had to build another house for her.
She couldn’t live in the house of David because of the Ark.
It was holy.
She was a foreigner and couldn’t live there.
He knew something wasn’t quite right.
But he was able to make the decision and rationalize it away anyway.
It says that he loved the Moabite women.
Now, as we know, the Moabites were enemies of Jehovah, but not all of them.
For example, you may remember that when David
was on the run from King Saul,
he asked the king of Moab
if he could bring his father and mother
—David’s father and mother— there, and the king of Moab protected them.
And he did so the whole time that David was in the stronghold, the account says.
So that means the king of Moab
protected Solomon’s grandparents.
We also remember Ruth.
Well, Ruth was Solomon’s great-great-grandmother,
and she was a Moabite woman, and look how well that turned out.
And also men from Moab and Ammon
were part of David’s mighty men.
So they weren’t all bad.
So was it perhaps through David’s mighty men
or maybe from his grandparents, who stayed in Moab,
that he was introduced to some of his first wives from Moab?
It talks about Ammonite women.
Well, we remember Solomon’s son Rehoboam, who later became king.
He was born from an Ammonite woman.
And, interestingly, he was born before Solomon became king.
So, again, is it possible
that Solomon reasoned: ‘Well, Jehovah is blessing me.
‘I’ve got an Egyptian wife and an Ammonite wife.
Maybe this doesn’t apply to me like it does to everybody else.’
What about Sidonians?
Well, we know the Sidonians were famous for their craftsmanship.
They had outstanding abilities as loggers and lumbermen.
In fact, Solomon’s father, David,
used the Sidonians to bring lumber
in great quantity for the temple.
Solomon later established contracts
with the Sidonians to cut trees for the temple.
Well, was it through, possibly, some of these business relationships
that he first was introduced to some who became his wives?
Could he have reasoned: ‘Well, you know, marrying these Sidonian women—
‘Well, that will help ensure that Jehovah’s house is completed.
This will help me fulfill my theocratic assignment.’
And just one more: What about the Hittite women?
Well, we remember Uriah.
David committed adultery with Bath-sheba
and had Uriah put to death.
Bath-sheba became Solomon’s mother.
Uriah was a Hittite and one of David’s mighty men.
So that means Solomon’s mother
had been married to a Hittite man.
So is it perhaps through Bath-sheba, through her former in-laws,
or perhaps through others that Solomon was introduced
to some of his first wives from the Hittites?
Now, we don’t know what Solomon was thinking,
but we can see how it was possible for him
to begin to rationalize some of those early decisions
until he found himself on a slippery slope,
completely alienated from Jehovah.
So, what’s the lesson for us?
Well, we read this account of Solomon
—accumulating all of those wives, all of the riches, all of those horses—
and it’s like watching a car crash in slow motion.
We know exactly where it’s heading, but Solomon didn’t see it coming.
So the question we have to ask ourselves is,
‘What would the reaction be
‘if somebody was reading my life story right now
—the decisions that I am making day to day right now?’
You see, our heart, too, is treacherous.
Our heart will try to cause us
to rationalize away Jehovah’s clear directives.
Sometimes we may rationalize a decision
because we see we’re still getting blessings from Jehovah,
or maybe we rationalize a decision because we see
how it worked out for somebody else
or what somebody else is doing—dangerous.
So, what do we need to do?
Well, we need to do what Solomon said and should have done himself.
If you turn to Proverbs 3:5,
let’s turn there together, Proverbs 3:5.
It says: “Trust in Jehovah with all your heart,
and do not rely on your own understanding.”
“Do not rely on your own understanding” —on our own wisdom.
“Trust in Jehovah”; follow his direction.
And if we do, we can be assured that we will never abandon
“the source of living water,”
but rather, we’ll benefit from his guidance for all eternity.

cn.text: 耶利米书2:13说
“我的子民……
不但离弃我这活水的源头
还为自己挖了……
破裂而不能储水的池子。”
我们可能会想
以色列人已经看过
也经历过耶和华所做的一切
怎么还会离弃耶和华呢？
很可惜
这些事一而再，再而三地发生
我们可以从他们身上学到什么教训呢？
今天，我们受到那么多
来自耶和华组织的教导
我们真的很感激耶和华
世界各地的弟兄姐妹都觉得
从来没有像现在这样
与耶和华的组织这么近
因为我们收到的圣经出版物
比以前更丰富
可是，就好像耶利米的日子
今天有些弟兄姐妹
也与耶和华渐行渐远
有些甚至离弃耶和华，去追求无益的事
怎么会这样呢？
我们怎么做才不会跟他们一样呢？
请留意今天《守望台》的评论
《守望台》说
“［魔鬼撒但］竭力使我们分心
不再将耶和华的话放在心上
此外，我们也可能受诡诈的心欺骗
没有完全按照耶和华的指引去做”
讲到受诡诈的心欺骗
没有按照耶和华的指引
我就想到所罗门
耶和华大大赐福给他
他应该很容易服从上帝的指引才对
但最后他还是失去了
跟耶和华的宝贵关系
他离弃了活水的源头
所罗门开始的时候做得很好
但后来发生了什么事呢？
他跟随自己诡诈的心
而没有听从耶和华的指示
耶和华给所罗门的指示非常清楚
请看申命记第17章
身为一个君王
所罗门要常常阅读并抄写上帝的法律
“可是，王不可为自己增添许多马匹。”
第17节继续说
“王不可娶很多妻子
免得他的心偏离正道
他也不可为自己积蓄巨量金银。”
经文说的马匹、妻子和金银
所罗门他都有很多
如果你看申命记7:3,4
这里耶和华说，不要跟外族人通婚
因为他们会使你离弃我
那所罗门怎么做呢？
让我们看看
列王纪上11:1-3
“所罗门王除了法老的女儿以外
还爱上了许多外族女子
包括摩押人、亚扪人、以东人、西顿人
和赫提人的女子
关于这些国族
耶和华曾经吩咐以色列人，说
你们不可以跟他们来往
也不可以让他们跟你们来往
因为他们一定会诱惑你们的心
去崇拜他们的神
所罗门却非常爱她们
他有700个妻子，都是公主
还有300个妃子
他的妻妾逐渐使他的心离开了上帝”
他的结局就是这样
怎么会这样呢？
所罗门犯的罪并不是无心之失
也不是一时软弱
他不是某天突然发现
“我的妈呀
我居然有700个妻子，300个妃子！”
如果是这样，他问题可就更大了
所罗门那么聪明
又有耶和华赐给他的智慧
他怎么可能还会不服从上帝呢？
其实
这是一个又一个没有按照耶和华指示的决定
所导致的
所罗门总是有很多借口
而且常常把自己的行为合理化
直到最后他离弃了耶和华
我们不知道所罗门的心里到底在想什么
才做出这些决定
但我们可以根据圣经推测
他大概是怎么想的
举个例，所罗门就娶了一个埃及人为妻
她是法老的女儿
有意思的是，在列王纪上的第3章
经文提到耶和华赐福给所罗门，给他智慧
是在他娶了法老的女儿之后才发生的事
他可能会想
“欸，耶和华还是赐福给我！
娶埃及人没问题吧？”
所罗门其实知道他这样做是不对的
因为历代志下8:11说
他另外建造一个宫殿给法老的女儿
她不能住在大卫的王宫里
因为那里有约柜，是圣地
所罗门知道，娶法老的女儿不对
可是他还是合理化自己的行为
经文还说，他爱摩押女子
可是摩押人是耶和华的仇敌
虽然不是全部都是
也许你还记得
当大卫在逃避扫罗王的追杀时
他请求摩押王保护自己的父母亲
也就是大卫的父母亲
而摩押王也确实这样做了
圣经的记载显示
大卫王住在山区的时候
摩押王一直保护他的父母
也就是一直保护所罗门的祖父母
再来，我们都认识路得
路得是所罗门的曾曾祖母
她也是摩押人，后来她崇拜耶和华
另外，大卫手下的勇士当中
有些人也是摩押人或亚扪人
所以他们不都是上帝的敌人
所罗门有没有可能是通过这些勇士
或是他在摩押的祖父母
认识了这些摩押女子呢？
圣经也提到一些亚扪女子
我们知道所罗门的儿子罗波安王
他的妈妈就是一个亚扪人
有意思的是
所罗门还没作王之前
罗波安就已经出生了
所以，所罗门有没有可能因此认为
“我娶了埃及人和亚扪人
耶和华还是赐福给我啊！
这些法律对我不适用。”
那西顿人呢？
我们知道西顿人以手工业著称
他们的伐木工人和木材商也远近驰名
所罗门的父亲大卫
也用西顿人运来大量的木材
用来建造圣殿
所罗门后来就跟西顿人订下合约
请他们为建造圣殿砍伐木材
所罗门有没有可能因为这些人
认识了一些西顿女子
后来娶她们为妻呢？
所罗门可能会想
“也许我娶了这些西顿女子
就能确保耶和华的圣殿能顺利完工
这样我就能完成耶和华的吩咐了。”
最后一个例子是赫提的女子
你还记得乌利亚吗？
大卫和他的妻子拔示巴通奸
还把乌利亚送到前线，害死了他
拔示巴是所罗门的妈妈
而大卫手下的勇士乌利亚是个赫提人
意思是，所罗门的妈妈
曾经嫁给一个赫提人
所罗门有没有可能通过拔示巴
和她前夫的亲戚
或是其他人
认识了一些赫提女子呢？
我们不知道
我们也不知道所罗门是怎么想的
但我们可以看出
所罗门可能为自己找借口
合理化自己的决定
以致他跟耶和华的关系越来越疏远
最后他离弃了耶和华
我们在这里学习到什么呢？
我们看到所罗门娶了很多妻子
积聚了大量的财富和很多马匹
这就好像看车祸的慢动作一样
我们知道结果会怎样
但所罗门却看不出来
所以，我们每个人都该问问自己这样的问题
“如果现在有人正在读我的生平故事
看到我每天做的决定
他们会怎么想呢？”
其实，我们的心非常诡诈
虽然耶和华的提醒很清楚
但我们可能会合理化自己的决定
因为我们可能跟所罗门一样
觉得上帝还是赐福给我们
或者我们看到其他人也做了类似的决定
而看起来没什么问题
如果我们这样想其实很危险
所以，我们应该做什么呢？
我们应该按所罗门说的话去做
虽然他自己没做到
我们一起看箴言3:5
箴言3:5
在这里经文说
“你要全心信赖耶和华
不可依靠自己的聪明。”
不可依靠自己的聪明
不要以为自己很有智慧
要信赖耶和华，听从他的劝告
我们这样做
就一定不会离弃活水的源头
而会永远从耶和华的指引得到益处

en.text: Just a few months ago,
most of us had probably
never even heard the word “coronavirus.”
Now the words “coronavirus” and “COVID-19”
have become an all-too-familiar part
of our vocabulary.
With the world facing this pandemic,
everyday life for many of us
has been disrupted in ways we might never have imagined.
And, sad to say, in just a short time,
this disease has taken the lives of thousands.
We know you are concerned
about the well-being of our brothers and sisters,
especially those living in lands
most directly affected by COVID-19.
Well, in this report, we’ll hear from responsible brothers
in Korea, Italy, and the United States
to find out how our brothers and sisters
are doing and what steps are being taken
to assist those facing this serious health crisis.
But before we hear from those brothers,
please let me share some thoughts with you.
The spread of this disease
is distressing, to be sure.
But we’re really not surprised to see the world
in the grip of such pestilence, are we?
Jesus made it clear at Luke 21:11
that pestilence would be part of the sign of the last days.
And in Revelation chapter 6,
the ride of the fourth horseman
includes mention of “deadly plague.”
So the events unfolding around us
are making it clearer than ever
that we’re living in the final part of the last days
—undoubtedly, the final part of the final part of the last days,
shortly before the last day of the last days.
But while the situation is serious,
as Jehovah’s people, we do not need to panic,
and Isaiah 30:15 tells us why.
Let’s read that together.
Isaiah 30:15:
“For this is what the Sovereign Lord Jehovah,
“the Holy One of Israel, says:
“‘By returning to me and resting, you will be saved;
“‘your strength will be
in keeping calm and showing trust.’”
Jehovah has always guided and supported
his people in times of distress.
So we have good reason to do just as this verse tells us:
‘Keep calm and show trust’ in Jehovah.
And, in turn, Jehovah will give us strength.
As we’ll see in these reports from around the world,
Jehovah has given us Bible principles
to help his people make wise decisions,
even in very difficult circumstances.
Let’s begin by speaking with Brother Reino Kesk,
who serves in Korea.
Thank you, Reino, for joining us.
You’re welcome.
It’s a privilege.
But we ask, Brother Kesk,
how are the brothers in Korea
doing right now?
Although there is fear
throughout the country, our brothers are in good spirits
and they really are endeavoring
to apply the good counsel at Isaiah 26:3
by fully leaning on Jehovah and by trusting in him.
That’s very good to hear.
How has the coronavirus pandemic
affected the congregation meetings
and field ministry in your branch territory?
Well, we’ve had to stop holding meetings
at the Kingdom Halls and also stop public witnessing.
At first, the brothers were a little bit confused when this happened
because of the suddenness of everything.
But once they were informed about the reasons for these steps
that had to be taken and also when they understood the need
to apply Romans 13:1
(to cooperate with the “superior authorities,”
or the government officials),
they understood immediately and started to put into practice
the recommendations and the suggestions that were given.
And they were so thankful for these good suggestions,
recommendations, from the organization.
Well, those are big changes,
but no doubt the obedience and cooperation
of the brothers has reflected favorably
on Jehovah’s name.
But what has helped the brothers
maintain their peace of mind during this time?
Well, the friends are still keeping a very good spiritual routine,
which is helping them, and all of us, to stay calm
and to keep a proper perspective of matters.
As far as meetings are concerned,
the brothers are either meeting together in small groups
or they’re using videoconferencing programs
so they can keep in touch and enjoy the meetings that way
—and also JW Stream.
They’re also more flexible in their ministry.
They’re writing letters, they’re texting their return visits,
they’re conducting Bible studies over the telephone,
they’re calling their family and friends to see how they are (to talk to them),
and they’re also calling former Bible students
to see how they are and are able to witness this way.
But one other thing too I might mention,
and that is, that the brothers are really trying hard
to be balanced in how much time they’re spending
watching news reports and reading about them.
In fact, it’s important, of course,
to stay up-to-date with things that are going on,
but our brothers have found that constantly watching
news reports and updates
can also increase undue,
or unnecessary, anxiety.
For a certainty, we can imitate the faith
of our brothers in Korea and their determination
to maintain good spiritual routines during this time.
Thank you very much for joining us for this report.
It’s been a pleasure.
Thank you.
Now we’ll go to Italy with Brother Greg Cicciù.
Thank you for being here, Greg.
I’m glad to be here, Brother Lett.
Thank you.
We know that our brothers in Italy
are facing many of the same challenges
as our brothers in Korea and in recent weeks
have had to face some especially difficult conditions,
including a nationwide lockdown.
Can you please tell us how our brothers are doing in Italy?
Well, some of our brothers have contracted
COVID-19 and, tragically,
as of March 16, six of them have died.
The vast majority of our brothers are fine.
We’re praying for all of them, especially those
who lost dear loved ones in death.
We’re very glad to hear that most of the brothers are doing well,
but our hearts go out to those who have lost their loved ones.
The news media has reported on the many restrictions in Italy right now.
How have our brothers been looking after each other
despite these restrictions?
Well, the brothers really miss associating together in person but,
thanks to Jehovah’s blessing, they’re doing well spiritually.
As Jesus said at John 13:34, 35
that love for one another would identify his true disciples,
well, we’re seeing this love in action here.
True, government restrictions prevent us from leaving home freely,
but the brothers regularly keep in touch by phone or other electronic means.
The result is that many are reporting that through this situation,
it’s actually drawing our brothers closer together.
That’s very encouraging news.
Please tell us what the elders are doing to shepherd the brothers.
In addition to providing for physical needs where possible,
the elders are videoconferencing
with individuals and entire field service groups
to share Scriptural encouragement so that no one feels isolated.
Each one receives emotional and spiritual support.
Many are expressing a renewed appreciation for their dear shepherds.
For example, one sister wrote,
“I feel protected, like when a hen gathers
her chicks to protect them from a predator.”
Another brother said, “I feel Jehovah’s love through my elders.”
Just as Isaiah 32:2 says,
our elders are really proving to be “a hiding place from the wind,
[and] a place of concealment from the rainstorm.”
How very encouraging!
We’re excited to hear how Jehovah
is getting you brothers through this difficult time.
Our prayers will continue to be with you.
Thank you very much, Brother Lett.
Now we’ll go to the United States and speak
with Brother Harold Corkern, who serves in Wallkill, New York.
Brother Corkern serves as a helper to the
Publishing Committee of the Governing Body
but is also a member
of the United States Branch Committee.
Thank you for being with us, Harold,
and we look forward to hearing from you.
Thank you for the opportunity, Brother Lett.
Why don’t you tell us how the brothers
at world headquarters and other
United States Bethel facilities are doing?
Well, there’s no question
that we’re going through some challenging times
because we’ve never experienced
a health situation like the scope of this one.
But on behalf of the Branch Committee,
we’re very happy to report that the Bethel family is coping well.
And commendably, they have displayed the “wisdom from above,”
being “ready to obey” as described
in the book of James 3:17.
And likewise, our brothers in the field
are quick to respond to direction from the branch office.
That’s very good to hear.
Can you explain what practical steps
the brothers are taking to avoid spreading the coronavirus?
We’re taking very seriously the guidelines
that we have received from medical and government authorities
regarding steps that can be taken to prevent the spread of the virus.
There are some basic reminders, such as regular hand washing,
not touching the face, avoiding hugs and handshakes,
and making sure to disinfect regularly surfaces that are often touched.
And if someone is sick, they should stay home.
So we have emphasized these basic reminders
not only to our fellow workers here at Bethel but also to those in the field.
Those are very practical reminders.
Even I’ve been greeting my brothers
with an elbow bump instead of a handshake.
Can you tell us what other measures
have been taken to keep everyone
as safe as possible?
Well, as a precaution for the Bethel family,
for our brothers in the field, and for our neighbors,
no tours or guests are permitted
at our Bethel complexes at this time.
At the direction of the Governing Body,
no guests attended in person at the recent Gilead graduation,
and the Bethel family was directed
to watch the program from their personal rooms.
Now with growing concerns,
the most recent precaution that’s being taken
is that the Bethel family has been directed
to not leave their respective complexes
for any activity
—that would include shopping,
social gatherings, and meetings.
And we’d like to emphasize that this
is a precaution to protect the Bethel family,
because we do not have an outbreak at this time,
but we’re being extra careful to protect them.
And we will monitor this latest restriction
on a week-by-week basis
to determine how much longer it should continue.
Now, as far as the field is concerned,
we have directed that all large theocratic events
throughout the U.S. branch territory should be canceled until May 17.
Many of the adjustments you’ve described
have no doubt been challenging.
How have the brothers responded?
We’re happy to report that they have responded very well
to the precautions that have been provided.
And we’d also like to say, Brother Lett,
on behalf of the Branch Committee to you dear brothers on the Governing Body:
Thank you very much for your loving direction.
We can certainly sense your loving concern
and your tender affection.
So thank you very much.
Well, thank you very much, Harold.
I’ll be sure to pass that appreciation on to the other brothers.
We’ve looked to Jehovah for help in making these decisions.
It’s encouraging to see how willing and cooperative
our brothers and sisters have been.
Thank you very much, Brother Corkern, for sharing this update.
You’re very welcome.
As you’ve seen from these reports,
with the situation changing day by day —sometimes hour by hour—
many adjustments have had to be made.
Now, in some cases, the Governing Body
has provided specific direction
on how these adjustments should be put into effect.
But many decisions have been left
to those who are most familiar with local circumstances:
Branch Committee members,
circuit overseers, and congregation elders.
To you faithful spirit-appointed men
serving in these capacities,
we’d like to say this: We trust you,
and we are confident
that you’ll prayerfully evaluate the facts
and local circumstances
and follow the direction of the “superior authorities.”
And we know that you’ll do all within your power
to stay in touch with the congregations.
You will do so on a regular basis
by phone or videoconference as necessary.
We’re also confident that Jehovah’s spirit
will guide you and give you the mature judgment
needed at this time
to apply Bible principles properly
and to provide clear direction.
As for the rest of us, whether the direction we receive comes
from the Governing Body, the branch,
our circuit overseer, or the elders,
we want to follow that direction closely.
It can serve as a protection now and, really,
if we think about it,
it’s good practice as we head
into even more turbulent times ahead.
Before we conclude, we’d like to share a few thoughts
about the upcoming Memorial
of the death of Jesus Christ on April 7.
There’s no virus or pandemic in the world
that can dampen our appreciation
for what Jehovah and Jesus have done for us
or weaken our determination
to observe the Lord’s Evening Meal.
Our gathering to commemorate
that important event is more than a tradition;
it’s a command
recorded at Luke 22:19.
Let’s read that together.
Luke 22:19:
“Also, he [Jesus] took a loaf,
“gave thanks, broke it, and gave it to them,
“saying: ‘This means my body,
“‘which is to be given in your behalf.
Keep doing this in remembrance of me.’”
So will we ‘keep doing this in remembrance of Jesus,’ as he commanded?
Absolutely.
But how we do so may vary
depending on our local circumstances.
If it’s possible in your area,
we encourage you to meet with your congregation.
You can be sure that the elders
will take practical measures for the benefit of all those attending.
Of course, in some areas,
local circumstances created by COVID-19
may prevent you from meeting as a congregation.
In that case, you may receive direction
from your elders to meet in smaller groups;
to use videoconferencing, like Skype® or Zoom;
or if none of those options are possible,
to watch the program on jw.org®.
How thankful we are to Jehovah
that he’s equipped us to be able to “drink the milk of nations”
as mentioned at Isaiah 60:16,
which includes the wise use of technology!
Regardless of the specific arrangements involved,
we all want to prepare our hearts
and do whatever is necessary
to obey Jesus’ command
to celebrate the Lord’s Evening Meal.
Just think for a moment about Jesus’ sacrifice
and what it means,
especially in the light of this global health crisis.
By means of the ransom, Jehovah has made provision
to completely eliminate problems
such as pestilence from the earth
—not just this one viral pandemic
but all sickness and death.
Admittedly, the events we see around us
are now creating “times hard to deal with,”
just as the Bible foretold.
But these events also remind us
of how close we are to seeing
a complete solution
to all these problems forever.
We want you to know that the Governing Body
loves you deeply
and will keep you in our prayers.
Our brothers in the United States, Italy,
and Korea send their warm love and greetings.
This is JW Broadcasting®
from the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

en.text: The universe is vast and awe-inspiring.
Earth and life on it are amazingly complex.
How did it all get here?
The Bible book of Genesis says that there is a Creator.
But the account is often misunderstood or even dismissed as a myth.
Is what the Bible says about the origin of the universe plausible?
Scientists estimate that the universe is 14 billion years old.
This implies that the universe, including earth, had a beginning.
The Bible agrees.
Genesis 1:1 reads:
“In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.”
The account does not say when or how the universe began.
Rather, it focuses
on the creative process that took place on earth
over six periods of time, which the Bible calls days.
Were these six 24-hour days, as many believe?
No.
The Hebrew word used in the Bible for “day”
can refer to various lengths of time.
Genesis even summarizes
the six days of creation as one day
—“the day that Jehovah God made earth and heaven.”
Each “day” in Genesis chapter 1
must have spanned extremely long periods of time.
The account’s perspective is also important.
The writer describes the creative periods
as they would have appeared to an observer on the earth.
Had someone been there, he would have seen events
that started in one period
and then progressed into the following periods.
Light penetrated the atmosphere
to reveal alternating day and night.
Earth was covered with water,
and vapor filled the air.
The dense clouds lifted from the waters that covered the earth,
forming an expansive sky between them.
Water receded to uncover dry ground,
and the first plants appeared.
The atmosphere cleared further
to reveal the sun and the moon.
God created living creatures in the sea
and flying creatures above.
And in the last period,
God created land animals and humans.
In harmony with the Genesis account,
the Bible says:
“Of course, every house is constructed by someone,
but the one who constructed all things is God.”
The Bible does not speak in scientific detail,
but its account of creation is logical and reasonable.
The Bible also offers logical and reasonable answers
to other important questions.
Does our planet exist for a purpose?
What is the meaning of life?
What does the future hold?
To see the Bible’s answers, go to jw.org®
or fill out the online request for one of Jehovah’s Witnesses
to visit at a time and place convenient for you.

en.text: Anita and I came here to Honduras
as missionaries as single people.
And Anita came here one year before I did.
I graduated from Gilead in 1974.
I was so excited!
But on the flight to Honduras,
a feeling of loneliness and anxiety overpowered me.
I was sitting there all by myself.
And I thought, ‘What if they forgot that I am coming
and nobody is there waiting for me or they never got the information?’
One night shortly after arriving in my assignment,
suddenly my bed started to shake.
And I thought, ‘What on earth is going on?’
I had no idea because I had never experienced
an earthquake before in my life.
But then I heard a voice:
(that means in English) “Joseph!
Come on down quickly!”
So I came down,
and I saw my dear friends Ramon and Melody,
who came from their house to check on me.
I was so happy to see them, and I gave them a big bear hug.
I almost cried because of their hospitality,
friendship, and love for me.
When I stepped down from the airplane,
I saw a group of people, and I realized:
“They are my brothers! I am not alone.
That’s my new family, and they are waiting for me.”
Forty years have passed since we arrived in Honduras.
But Anita and I realize that the love and the hospitality
and the friendship of the brothers has not changed.
And we appreciate that very, very much.

또 어떤 자매는 큰딸을 돌봐 줬어요.
저희를 사랑한다는 걸 느낄 수 있었습니다.
그들이 여호와를 본받고 있다는 걸 알 수 있었습니다.
그래서 이 조직이 여호와의 조직이라는 확신이 들었죠.

en.text: The reason I immigrated here
was to earn more money and more freedom,
but my life was only work and sleep.
I once thought,
‘This is not the reason I came here;
this is not the life I wanted.’
But what could I do?
The life that I was pursuing
did not bring me true happiness.
My husband’s sister started taking me along to the meetings.
The brothers and sisters there
were very welcoming to me.
My wife started studying the Bible first.
I saw her becoming happier and happier studying the Bible,
and this motivated me to start studying the Bible with her Bible teacher.
She lived far away, but she was never late.
She was like a mother
and cared for us like her children.
In our studies, we were making huge progress.
But we didn’t expect the huge challenge that lay ahead.
When my youngest daughter was born,
the doctor told us she had congenital heart disease.
She needed immediate surgery.
When we were facing this challenge,
the brothers and sisters were right by our side
continually assisting us,
helping us to find a doctor,
and interpreting for us,
even though we were not yet baptized.
On the day of the surgery, a congregation elder and his wife
drove to pick us up and brought us to the hospital.
They also stayed by our side until the surgery was done.
A couple came to the hospital and brought us food.
Another sister helped to care for my older daughter.
We really could feel that the brothers and sisters
really loved us, just like family.
My wife and I, along with our two daughters,
are very happy to be worshipping Jehovah.
I realized that the love shown to me by the brothers and sisters
was in imitation of Jehovah.
It really helped me to see that this is truly his organization.
This is the life that we had been searching for.

cn.text: 我移民来这里的目的就是
希望有更多的收入，还有
更多的自由
但是，我的生活只是工作跟睡觉
我曾经想过
这并不是我来到这里的目的
这并不是我想要的生活
可是我又能怎么样呢？
我之前所追求的生活
并没有让我感觉到真正的快乐
我的丈夫的妹妹找我去参加聚会
那里的弟兄姐妹非常地欢迎我
我的妻子，她先开始学习圣经
我看出我的妻子在学习圣经的时候
她越来越快乐
那这也推动我要开始学习圣经
跟她的圣经老师
她住的家离我们比较远
但是她都没有迟到过
她就好像母亲一样把我们当作孩子看待
我们在学习方面有了很大的进步
但是我们没有料到我们将来
会面对如此严重的考验
当我的小女儿出生的时候
医生告诉我们她有先天性的心脏病
需要尽快做手术
面对这个挑战的时候
弟兄姐妹一直在身边扶持我们
帮助我们找医生
还帮助我们做翻译
虽然当时我们还没有受浸
手术的那一天
会众的一位长老还有他的妻子
开车来接我们去医院
他也一直陪我们
到手术结束为止
当时有一对夫妻
来医院探望我们时给我们带来了食物
另外一位姐妹还帮忙照顾我的大女儿
我们真的可以感受得到弟兄姐妹
真的很爱我们
就像我们的家人一样
我还有我的妻子
我们很开心可以跟两个女儿一起崇拜耶和华
我看出弟兄姐妹他们对我表现的爱
是效法耶和华
这让我看出这真的是上帝的组织
这就是我们一直想要寻找的生活

titles.ko: 없어지지 않는 사랑을 회중에서 나타내십시오—외국인 거주자들에게
titles.en: Display Unfailing Love in the Congregation—To Foreign Residents
titles.cn: 总要在会众里显出爱心——对外地来的人

title: 없어지지 않는 사랑을 회중에서 나타내십시오—연로한 사람들에게

ko.text: 얼마 전까지만 해도 하루 종일 봉사하면서
그런데 몸이 아프면서 봉사를 많이 못 해 슬펐어요.
지금은 힘이 없어서 예전만큼 많은 일을 못 해요.
빨래도 해 주고 식사도 챙겨 줍니다.
형제 자매들이 와 주면 저는 기뻐서 이렇게 말하죠.
형제 자매들은 빵이나 과일 같은 걸 가져와서
또 어떤 날은 음식을 해 와서 다 같이 식사도 하죠.
제가 해설할 내용을 큰 글씨로 써 주죠.
하지만 여호와께서 언제나 제 곁에 계시니까 괜찮아요.
지금 전 전시대 봉사에 계속 참여하고 있습니다.
여호와께선 늘 저를 잘 돌보고 보살펴 주세요.

en.text: Some time ago,
I could spend entire days
talking about Jehovah in the ministry.
That’s why I was so sad when I got sick,
because I was used to being out in the preaching work.
I feel like I don’t have the strength to do
as much as I used to.
But Jehovah is so great.
He puts into the hearts of his people
the desire to visit me and help me.
They’ve cleaned my house.
They even washed my clothes and prepared my meals.
It makes me happy to see them arrive,
and I tell them: “It’s so good to see you.
Here you go, have some coffee.”
They bring me tortillas and fruit,
and they say to me: “Take them. They’re for you.”
They prepared food, brought it over,
and then we ate it together.
I loved that.
I felt so protected, as if I were surrounded by my children.
The sisters really help me.
A couple of days before our meeting,
they write out my comments in big letters.
Then I can practice them over and over again.
That way, I can give a comment at the meeting.
But then I am sad when the brothers leave.
I wish they could always be by my side.
Then I remember Jehovah is always with me.
Some time ago, I was in better health.
I could still go out in service.
But the brothers and sisters have come to my aid.
I’ve been able to go out in public witnessing with the carts.
I continually see Jehovah’s support and protection.
It really touches my heart.

cn.text: 以前我能一整天在外面传道
帮助人认识耶和华
生病以后，我没办法像以前一样常常出去
这让我很难过
我的体力衰弱了很多
能做的很有限
不过，耶和华很爱我
他让弟兄姐妹来探望我、帮助我
他们帮我打扫
帮我洗衣服，还帮我做饭
每次他们来，我都很高兴
我会对他们说
“你们来真好
来，喝点咖啡吧。”
他们会送我玉米饼和水果
跟我说:“这些送给你，慢慢吃。”
他们会准备好食物
然后带过来跟我一起吃
我觉得很幸福
他们像我的孩子一样
有他们在身边我觉得很温暖
姐妹们给我很大的帮助
她们会在聚会前几天
把我想说的话用很大的字写下来
我反复练习
聚会时就能发表评论了
弟兄姐妹回去后
我觉得有点孤单
我希望他们陪着我
但我会提醒自己
耶和华一直都在我身边
前一阵子，我的身体好点了
我又能出去传道了
弟兄姐妹都热心地帮助我
我也能参与展示架的传道工作
我感受到耶和华一直在帮助我、扶持我
我真的很感动

titles.ko: 없어지지 않는 사랑을 회중에서 나타내십시오—연로한 사람들에게
titles.en: Display Unfailing Love in the Congregation—To the Elderly
titles.cn: 总要在会众里显出爱心——对年长者

title: 없어지지 않는 사랑을 회중에서 나타내십시오—과부와 아버지 없는 아이들에게

ko.text: 그날 아침은 어둡고 날씨가 좋지 않았어요.
남편은 큰딸과 함께 성서 연구를 하러
그런데 남편이 사고로 목숨을 잃었다는 소식을 듣게 됐죠.
그날 밤 저는 정말 위로가 필요했지만,
날씨가 좋지 않아서 아무한테도 연락을 할 수가 없었어요.
우리 조직의 출판물을 읽으면서 위로와 힘을 얻으려고 했습니다.
형제 자매 세 명이 우리 집에 찾아왔어요.
작은 집단의 형제 자매 일곱 명이 더 찾아왔어요.
맨발로 한 시간 반이나 걸어서 온 겁니다.
우리 가족은 정말 큰 힘을 얻었어요.
저희 마을은 미신을 많이 믿기 때문에,
여호와에 대해 나쁘게 얘기할까 봐 걱정이 됐죠.
형제 자매들이 저희에게 보여 준 사랑과 지원 덕분에,
큰딸은 잘 성장해서 지금 베델에서 봉사하고 있고,
작은 딸은 저와 함께 행복하게 여호와를 섬기고 있습니다.
형제 자매들이 정말 큰 사랑을 보여 주었다고요.
최선을 다해 우리 딸들을 영적으로 잘 키웠다는 것도요.
“생활하는 데 필요한 게 있으면 뭐든지 돕고 싶다”고 말씀하셨어요.
남편을 잃었지만, 형제 자매들의 친절 덕분에
절망에서 벗어나 희망을 되찾을 수 있었죠.
우리 가족은 그처럼 큰 시련을 견딜 수 있었습니다.

en.text: It was a dark and gloomy morning,
but my husband and my daughter took their bicycles
and went out to care for their Bible studies.
That evening, around 5:00 p.m.,
I was waiting for them to return,
but instead,
I received a message
that my husband had died
in an accident.
That night, I really wanted to receive comfort,
but because of the bad weather,
I couldn’t tell others about the accident.
That evening, my two daughters and I
tried to look for strength and comfort
by reading our organization’s publications.
Unexpectedly,
even despite the bad weather,
three of our brothers and sisters visited our home.
They rode their motorbikes over two hours through the heavy rain.
At around midnight,
seven more brothers and sisters from our small group
came to our house by foot.
It took them an hour and a half
to walk barefoot through the rain and mud
in the dark to reach us.
Our family was strengthened
by the brothers’ and sisters’ visit that night.
Because our village was very superstitious,
I worried that the death of my husband
would bring reproach to Jehovah’s name,
so I prayed about this matter to Jehovah.
The next day, many more brothers and sisters
from our neighboring congregations visited our family.
Rather than reproach,
the love of the brothers brought glory and praise to Jehovah’s name.
Thanks to the love and support that our brothers and sisters showed us,
my oldest daughter is currently serving at Bethel
and my younger daughter is happily serving Jehovah with me.
In the new world, I would like to tell my husband
of the unfailing love the brothers and sisters have shown our family
and how I trained our daughters
to continue to progress spiritually to the best of my ability
with their help.
One elder said to me,
“We are more than happy to assist with your material needs.”
Although I have become a widow,
such kindness helped me to overcome my despair
and renew my hope.
The love of our brothers and sisters
enabled our family to endure this tragedy.

cn.text: 我记得那天早晨
天阴沉沉的
但我丈夫和女儿
还是骑自行车去教人学习圣经
到了下午5点
我正等着他们回家
没想到我却听到消息说
我的丈夫出了意外
已经死了
那天晚上
我真的很需要有人来安慰我
但是因为天气不好
我没办法出门找人商量该怎么办
于是，我和两个女儿阅读组织的出版物
想要从中获得安慰和力量
出乎意料的是
尽管天气那么糟
还是有三位弟兄姐妹
冒着风雨来看我们
他们在大雨中骑摩托车两个多小时
才到我家
到了半夜
我们小组的七位弟兄姐妹走路到了我的家
为了来看我们
他们光着脚在泥泞的道路上走了一个半小时
那个晚上
我们一家人从弟兄姐妹受到了很大的鼓励
我们的村子特别迷信
我很担心村民会因为我丈夫的死
而羞辱耶和华的名
于是我向耶和华祷告
第二天
又有很多附近会众的弟兄姐妹来看我们
结果，耶和华的名不仅没有被羞辱
还因为弟兄姐妹的爱心而得到荣耀和赞美
全因为弟兄姐妹的爱心和支持
我们才能渡过难关
现在我的大女儿在伯特利服务
小女儿和我在一起
也快乐地崇拜耶和华
在新世界，我想告诉丈夫
弟兄姐妹怎样一直对我们表现爱心
我也会告诉他
在弟兄姐妹的帮助下
我怎样继续竭尽全力教导女儿们亲近耶和华
一位长老对我说
“我们很乐意在物质方面帮助你们”
虽然我失去了丈夫
但是弟兄姐妹的爱心帮助我克服伤痛
让我再一次看到了希望
弟兄姐妹的爱心
确实帮助我们从失去家人的悲痛中
走出来

titles.ko: 없어지지 않는 사랑을 회중에서 나타내십시오—과부와 아버지 없는 아이들에게
titles.en: Display Unfailing Love in the Congregation—To Widows and the Fatherless
titles.cn: 总要在会众里显出爱心——对孤儿寡妇

title: 없어지지 않는 사랑을 회중에서 나타내십시오—인도하는 사람들에게

ko.text: 그런 지역들은 치안이 좋지 않아 매우 위험하죠.
봉사할 때 무장한 갱단원들을 쉽게 볼 수 있는데,
형제들은 정말 신경을 많이 써 주고
저희 곁에 계속 같이 있어 줍니다.
또한 많은 형제들은 건강상의 어려움을 겪고 있죠.
하지만 형제들이 늘 저희 곁에 있다는 생각을 하면
계속 순회 활동을 할 힘이 납니다.
형제들이 보여 주는 크고 작은 사랑은
계속 여호와를 위해 일할 마음을 갖게 합니다.
이 모든 어려움에 잘 대처하도록 도와주는 형제 자매들에게

en.text: In the circuit work, we visit several poor communities
in the city of Rio de Janeiro.
One of the challenges we face here is security.
In these communities, there are a lot of conflicts and shootings
between rival drug cartels and between gang members and the police.
It’s common for us to see armed gang members when we’re preaching,
and often they are taking drugs.
When we’re visiting the congregations in these communities,
the brothers really take care of us and don’t let us out of their sight.
They’re always thinking about our safety because we’re not locals,
and it’s possible that some gang members may not like us being there.
Most of these communities have a lot of steps to walk up and down,
and many of our brothers have physical limitations.
However, just knowing that our brothers are always close by
gives us the strength to continue serving them in the circuit.
All of these acts of love, whether large or small,
really motivate us to keep working for Jehovah.
We owe a lot to the brothers and sisters
for helping us get through all of these situations.

cn.text: 我们探访的地区是里约热内卢的几个贫民区
这里有很严重的治安问题
贩毒组织之间、黑社会帮派和警察之间
常常发生冲突或枪战
传道的时候
我们常常能见到拿着枪的帮派分子
他们通常都吸毒
我们探访这些会众的时候
弟兄姐妹非常照顾我们
因为我们不是本地人
一些帮派成员可能不欢迎我们
弟兄姐妹考虑到我们的安全
一直陪在我们身边
这个地区有很多台阶
而且一些弟兄姐妹行动不便
这对他们来说很不容易
但光是知道他们在我们身边
我们就有力量继续在这里把工作做好
弟兄姐妹不论用什么方式表现爱心
都让我们受到激励，更想为耶和华服务
他们帮助我们克服这里的各种困难
真的非常感谢他们

titles.ko: 없어지지 않는 사랑을 회중에서 나타내십시오—인도하는 사람들에게
titles.en: Display Unfailing Love in the Congregation—To Those Taking the Lead
titles.cn: 总要在会众里显出爱心——对带头的弟兄

ko.text: 공사에 참여한 지 이제 열두 달이 돼 갑니다.
여러분에 대해선 길에서 전도하거나 집을 찾아온다는 것 밖엔 잘 몰랐죠.
여호와의 증인들도 이런 공사를 하는 줄 몰랐는데,
전 세계에서 건축 공사를 한다는 걸 알게 됐죠.
이만큼 일이 잘 진행되는 현장은 처음 봅니다.
현장이 아주 깨끗해서 흠잡을 데가 없어요.
여러 가지 방식으로 공사를 진행할 수 있다는 것도 배웠어요.
현장 작업자 대부분이 자원봉사자라는 걸 알고 깜짝 놀랐습니다.
확실히 사람들을 훈련하는 데 많은 시간과 노력을 들이더라고요.
기술을 가르쳐서 필요한 작업을 할 수 있도록
그렇게 시간을 들이고 훈련시키는 게 정말 대단하다고 생각했습니다.
이 사람들이 다 자원봉사자라고 하니까 제 말을 믿질 않았어요.
이런 좋은 공사 현장이 있다는 걸 밖에다 얘기해도
여자 분들이 굴착기와 덤프 트럭을 운전하는데, 보기 드문 광경이죠.
하지만 많은 여자들이 실제로 공사에 참여하고
심지어 아주 거친 작업들까지 해내는 모습이 정말 멋집니다.
현장을 돌아보니까 남자들 못지 않게 일을 잘 하더라고요.
솔직히 어떤 면에선 더 나은 것 같습니다.
모두들 어찌나 친절하고 편안하게 대해 주시는지,
다들 하나같이 정말 좋은 분들만 계셨습니다.
“안녕하세요?”, “수고 많으시죠?” 하고 어딜 가나 인사를 받았습니다.
여기서 일하고 퇴근하면, 평소랑 기분이 달라요.
여기 처음 왔을 때 다들 연기하는 줄 알았어요.
항상 즐거워 보이던데, 그건 불가능하다고 생각했죠.
네. 제가 여기 온 지 8개월, 9개월쯤 됐는데 언제나 그랬어요.
그렇게 오랫동안 행복한 척할 수는 없죠.
매사에 긍정적인 사람들과 함께 일해서 아주 좋았습니다.
부정적인 뉴스나 소식을 듣고 보면서 살다가
이곳에만 딱 오면 저도 모르게 미소를 짓게 되더라고요.
어떻게 이렇게 빨리 잘 짓는 거죠? 정말 굉장합니다.

en.text: We’ve been working on the project
almost 12 months now.
I had a limited knowledge
of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Occasionally, they knock on the door.
We only see one small part of you
when you’re coming around the streets
and you’re knocking on doors.
I didn’t even know they did
these sorts of projects.
Then I’ve learned that they’ve been
all over the world doing these, the same sort of thing.
I’ve never been on a site that’s as well-run as this one.
The cleanliness of the actual site
is, you know, impeccable.
It seems a very, very well-organized site.
The planning of the whole thing . . .
Yes.
. . . the walkways, the routes in and out
—it’s all been exemplary.
It’s been an experience
—a good one, I might add.
It’s opened my eyes to a lot of different ways of working.
When I found out that most of the people on this site
were volunteers, I was quite amazed.
It was very clear that Watchtower
put so much time into their people
in terms of bringing them on, putting the skills in,
and making them capable of doing the job that they wanted to do.
And that training and that time,
it was just superb to see.
This fellow sitting next to me,
when I explained to him, you know,
that volunteers were working here,
he didn’t believe me.
And everyone we speak to, there’s just no chance they would believe us
as to what we see and what we experience —which has been good.
You’ve got ladies driving
diggers and big dumpers.
And it’s not very often you see that.
Construction is still a male-dominated environment,
but to actually come on-site and see the number of women
that are actually operating the plant and actually involved
in the cold-face construction, it’s fantastic.
It proves that they’re able to do as good a job and—walking around this site
(I’m going to be honest with you) —probably a better job in many instances.
It’s amazing how everyone
is just really nice
and just seems so relaxed
and are just genuinely really, really, nice people.
You always got a “Hello.”
You always got a “Goodbye.”
You always were asked how you were doing.
When you go back home, you feel different.
You don’t have that feeling
—that stress—on top of you.
We came here the first time,
and it was almost (to my mind) like a film set.
Everyone seemed happy all the time,
and it didn’t seem possible that it could happen.
Yeah, and it’s just continued for the last
—what?—eight months, nine months since I have been here.
And it’s always happy, and no one can fake that.
It’s great to see people that are just really positive about everything,
which in a sometimes negative society
when you pick up the papers and look at the news—
It’s just when you come here —it’s just—it puts a smile on your face.
It’s just been a warmer,
friendlier experience.
All the health and safety
and the briefings—they’re all still done.
How can you build so fast and so accurately with such quality, though?
And that’s what’s blown our minds.
Most of the people on-site don’t have the skills when they first come here,
and they’re doing work as good
as some of our guys who’ve probably been employed six or seven years.
The communication has been fantastic.
It’s a two-way conversation when problems arise;
it’s not always a fight over money.
It’s just working with each other.
There’s not an argument over everything.
If something is not right, you work together to get over the problem.
To see everyone here together
all striving for the same goal is fantastic.
I think what’s made it great for us, working with Watchtower,
is that everything they want to do, they want to do it right.
And they do everything with passion and energy,
and it’s something that we like to do ourselves, as well.
I’ve built The Gherkin in the city; I’ve built Wembley Stadium
—big projects, big status—
and we’ve pretty much seen the cusp of other professionals out there.
You would not know the difference.
And being volunteer and nonprofit (I would say),
it’s been absolutely incredible to see, really.
We’ve learned how to work together with other people on-site;
we’ve learned how to work with people that haven’t been in construction before.
Just keeping it honest and straightforward sort of solves a lot of problems.
We wish it would be like that everywhere else,
because, you know, it’s unheard of, really.
We’ve learned more on this site than we’ve learned on any site
about working with each other, probably in 23 years.
I’ve had an enjoyable experience working with Jehovah’s Witnesses.
If there was a chance
to come up with another project,
I’d definitely be more than willing
to want to get involved.
I wish all sites could be like this because my life would be a lot easier.
You need to get people to come to this site;
there would be a definite difference
in the way people perceive Jehovah’s Witnesses.
It’s certainly opened and broadened my mind
to what Jehovah’s Witnesses do.
And what’s changed my opinion of your organization most
is that you do exactly what you preach, and I mean exactly:
you’re friendly, you’re forthright, you’re very truthful.
I’ve never been on any other project like this,
not at all.
I just wish all construction sites were like that.
It would be a nicer place to live and work.

en.text: When Job was at his lowest point in life,
three of his companions came to offer him comfort,
and they failed miserably.
But what if their situations had been reversed?
What would Job have done?
He said, as recorded at Job 16:5:
“I would strengthen you with the words of my mouth,
and the consolation of my lips would bring relief.”
Today, more than ever,
people need encouragement and comfort,
so we should always aim to be upbuilding and positive.
What does that take?
We need to cultivate a positive view of our listeners,
limit negative material,
and make good use of God’s Word.
Why is it important to cultivate
a positive view of our listeners?
Because our viewpoint
will be reflected in our teaching.
Let’s watch an elder giving
a local needs talk with the theme
“Cultivate the Habit of Being Punctual.”
How do you think he views his audience?
The elders have chosen this theme
because many just don’t seem to understand
the importance of punctuality
and have the habit of arriving late for meetings.
In this talk, we will answer these questions:
How does being late show
a lack of appreciation for Jehovah’s provisions?
And when you are constantly late,
how is this inconsiderate of others?
The speaker seemed to be irritated, didn’t he?
Because he didn’t have a positive view of the audience,
his approach was critical, not constructive.
Such a talk wouldn’t be very motivating.
Let’s watch the elder try again.
Notice how a positive view of his audience affects his teaching.
The elders asked me to commend you
for your efforts to be punctual.
Our theme, “Cultivate the Habit of Being Punctual,”
was chosen because as busy, imperfect humans,
we all have a challenge to be on time for meetings.
In this talk, we will answer these questions:
Why is it important to be punctual?
And what are some practical suggestions
to help us arrive on time?
Did you notice that he first commended the congregation?
The speaker believed that his audience
wants to be on time and please Jehovah,
so his approach was positive,
focusing on how to be punctual,
rather than how to avoid being late.
This made his talk upbuilding.
A positive view of our listeners
is also important when we’re in the ministry.
If we believe that behind every door
is a potential fellow believer,
we’ll preach with enthusiasm.
To be upbuilding and positive,
we must also limit negative material.
Of course, life in this system of things
has negative aspects that cannot be ignored.
However, when teaching,
we should include negative material
only when it serves a useful purpose.
For example, the introduction of a talk
may call for us to discuss the failure of human rule,
reports of crime and violence,
or the shocking prevalence of immorality.
But if we were to consider such things at length,
the effect may be depressing.
The overall tone of the talk should be positive.
When in the ministry, we sometimes start a conversation
by raising a problem that’s on the minds
of those in our territory.
However, the purpose of our visit
is to share the good news of the Kingdom.
So at an early point in the conversation,
we should try to direct attention
to refreshing Bible truths.
How do you think the publisher does in the following demonstration?
We’re making brief visits to help people manage their stress.
Does it seem to you that people are
more stressed today than they were in the past?
Hmm. I think people are more stressed.
Crime is getting worse and many people are afraid.
Many people feel pressure to make ends meet.
Then there’s the very real threat of nuclear war!
I’m not interested.
The conversation ended
because the publisher spent too much time
talking about negative things.
Let’s watch her try again.
We’re making brief visits to help people manage their stress.
Does it seem to you that people are
more stressed today than they were in the past?
Hmm. I think people are more stressed.
Many have found that the practical advice in the Bible
helps them manage their stress.
Here’s one example.
It’s found at Matthew 6:34.
Much better!
Instead of dwelling on the problems,
the publisher directed the householder
to something positive.
The best way to be upbuilding and positive
is to base our words on the Bible.
So use the Bible when replying to questions.
And when giving a talk, teach from the Scriptures.
In our teaching, we should focus on things
that will improve a situation and that inspire confidence.
In this way, we’ll be upbuilding and positive.

在这个演讲我们会谈谈以下的问题
首先，为什么守时很重要？
然后，我们也会谈谈
有哪些方法让我们更加守时
这位讲者先称赞了会众
他相信所有的弟兄姐妹都很想守时
让耶和华高兴
所以他把演讲集中在积极的方面
就是怎样守时，而不是怎样避免迟到
这让他的演讲更激励人心
我们在传道的时候
对住户有积极的看法也非常重要
如果我们把每一个传道对象
看作是未来的弟兄姐妹
我们传道时就会更热心
我们要想使演讲激励人心
就要尽量少用消极的资料
这个世界确实有很多的难题
我们不能对此视而不见
不过要记得，我们在教导时
只有在必要的时候才会选择一些消极的信息
例如一个演讲的引言
可能提到人类政府统治带来的难题
有罪行、有暴力
以及随处可见的不道德的事
要是我们花很多时间讨论消极的事
就会让听众感到很沮丧
整体而言，我们的演讲应该是积极的
我们在传道的时候
通常会以地区里的人关心的问题展开交谈
不过，我们传道的目的
是向人宣扬上帝王国的好消息
所以我们展开交谈后
要尽早把住户的注意力引到圣经真理之上
接着，我们来看看这位传道员做得怎么样
我们想跟你谈谈，怎样减轻压力
你有没有觉得，现在的人的压力越来越大？
现在的人的压力真的很大
是啊，你看社会治安越来越差
赚钱养家也很不容易
而且国际局势这么紧张
不知道哪天核战就爆发了
我不想听！
对话进行不下去了
因为传道员没有谈积极的信息
反而说了一大堆消极的事
让我们再给她一次机会吧
我们想跟您谈谈，怎样减轻压力
你有没有觉得，现在的人的压力越来越大？
现在的人的压力真的很大
我这里有一些减轻压力的好方法
给你看一下圣经马太福音6:34
这就好多了！
传道员让住户留意积极的信息
而没有一直谈论消极的事情
我们想言谈积极
最好的方法就是让我们说话的内容
围绕着圣经的信息
传道时要用圣经来回答问题
弟兄在演讲时也要运用经文
我们施行教导时要着重谈谈
情况会怎样改善，让人对未来充满希望
这样，我们就做到言谈积极了

titles.cn: 第16课：言谈积极

title: 로버트 P. 존슨: 어릴 때부터 여호와께 헌신한 삶

ko.text: 오늘 제 가까운 벗인 로버트 존슨 형제와 함께하게 되어 정말 기쁩니다.
존슨 형제를 이 자리에 모신 것은
형제가 여호와를 섬기면서 삶에서 많은 축복을 누린 훌륭한 본이 되시기 때문입니다.
형제 가족은 여러 세대에 걸쳐 진리 안에 있으셨죠.
제가 알기론, 증조할아버지께서 러셀 형제 시대에, 1914년 이전에 진리를 받으셨다죠.
그럼 우리 프로그램을 시청하고 있는 많은 청소년들처럼,
존슨 형제도 한때는 여호와의 회중에서 성장하던 어린 소년이었네요.
그런데 어떻게 여호와를 섬기기 위해 헌신하기로 결정하시고 침례를 받으셨나요?
제 삶에 좋은 영향을 준 요인이 적어도 두 가지가 있었습니다.
진리 안에서 받은 유산이 도움이 되었죠.
하지만 부모님은 제 마음에 여호와를 기쁘시게 하고
그렇게 하는 데 내 삶을 바치려는 열망을 심어 주셨습니다.
부모님은 제가 목표를 갖게 해 주시고 진리를 가르쳐 주셨어요.
여호와 하느님께 헌신하고 그분과 가까운 관계를 누릴 수 있었습니다.
부모님께 말씀드렸더니 기뻐하셨지만, 침례는 좀 더 기다려 보면 좋겠다고 하셨습니다.
특히 십 대 청소년기를 잘 보낼 수 있는지 보자고 하셨어요.
그러면 기다리던 침례를 결국 언제 받으셨나요?
뉴욕 양키 스타디움에서 열린 1953년 국제 대회였는데,
그때가 바로 어제 일처럼 기억이 납니다.
형제에게 좋은 영향을 준 분이 또 한 분 계셨죠?
사람들을 진리 안에서 훈련시키는 특별한 프로그램이 있을 거라고 밝혔습니다.
우리 회중에 찰스 리처드슨이라는 기름부음받은 형제가 계셨는데,
아버지는 이 프로그램으로 절 훈련시켜 달라고 그분께 부탁하셨습니다.
그래서 리처드슨 형제는 5년 동안 저를 가르치고 훈련해 주셨죠.
여러 해 동안 그 형제는 봉사의 직무란
사람들이 여호와와 가까운 관계를 맺도록 돕는 일이란 걸 깨닫게 도와주셨죠.
교리를 알려 줄 뿐 아니라 여호와를 실재하시는 분으로 여기게 해 주라고 하셨어요.
그 조언 덕분에 지금까지 행복하게 여호와를 위해 봉사하고 있습니다.
방금 하신 말씀이나 전에 하셨던 말씀을 생각해 보면,
리처드슨 형제가 형제의 삶에 엄청난 영향을 주었다는 걸 알 수 있네요.
그래서 형제도 다른 사람들을 훈련시켜 주고 싶어 하신 거 같습니다.
제가 봉사부에 왔을 때 절 훈련시키도록 임명되셨잖아요.
사실, 일평생 다른 사람들을 훈련시켜 오셨으니까요.
사실, 저도 훈련을 받고 도움을 받았습니다.
여호와께서 보잘것없는 저에게 과분한 친절을 베풀어 주시고
모든 것이 가능해지게 해 주신 겁니다.
당연히 저도 제가 받은 걸 다른 사람에게 베풀어야죠.
그들도 다른 사람에게 훈련을 베푸는 걸 보면 행복합니다.
그럼 다시 열다섯 살이셨을 때로 돌아가 보죠.
그 나이에 침례를 받으신 것이 어떻게 유익했다고 느끼시나요?
자신이 무엇을 하고 싶은지 알고 그것에 초점을 맞추면
나중에 어려움을 헤쳐 나가기가 더 쉽다는 것입니다.
저는 어린 나이에 헌신을 하고 침례를 받았기 때문에
그 후로도 계속해서 진리에 초점을 맞출 수 있었습니다.
그래서 다른 사람들도 되도록 일찍 헌신하도록 도우려고 노력합니다.
그러면 그들도 저처럼 여호와의 축복을 맛보게 될 겁니다.
그럼 열다섯 살에 어떤 문이 열리기 시작했나요?
침례받은 형제가 되니까 어떤 기회가 생겼죠?
열여덟 살에는 고등학교를 졸업하자마자 파이오니아를 시작했죠.
그 후 도움이 더 필요한 곳에서 봉사할 때
스물한 살에 회중의 종, 즉 지금의 장로로 섬기게 되었습니다.
그러던 중, 조직에서는 여행하는 봉사를 할 수 있는 형제가 필요해서 찾고 있었죠.
그래서 스물다섯 살에 여행하는 감독자로 일하는 특권을 받게 되었습니다.
스물한 살에 장로가 되고, 스물다섯 살에 순회 감독자가 되셨는데,
그렇게 젊은 나이에 좀 버겁지 않으셨나요?
진리에 대한 확신은 있었지만 저 스스로에 대한 자신감이 부족했습니다.
하지만 여호와께서 도우실 건 알고 있었죠.
젊은 나이에 순회 감독자로 일하며 많은 걸 배웠어요.
제가 방문하던 3년 동안 순회구 형제 자매들이 잘 참아 주신 데 대해 여호와께 감사하죠.
그래도 젊은 순회 감독자가 방문하면 어떤 유익이 있다고 보십니까?
회중을 위해서는, 야외 봉사를 더 오래할 수 있는 형제가 방문하면 좋죠.
그리고 또 회중의 청소년들과 젊은 사람들의 경우,
젊은 순회 감독자가 그들을 더 잘 이해할 수 있다는 점이 있습니다.
그리고 제가 젊을 때 섬기던 순회구에 있던 여러 사람이
지금도 찾아와 어떤 유익을 얻었는지 얘기해 주기도 해요.
예를 들어, 야외 봉사와 회중 집회를 잘 즐긴 다음에는
아이들과 함께 여가 시간을 가지곤 했습니다.
우리는 밖에 나가서 달리기를 하기도 하고,
또 보드 게임을 하거나 또 소프트볼이나 농구를 하기도 했죠.
배우자를 고를 시간은 나중에 많을 테니까
어떻게 봉사를 첫째 자리에 둘 수 있는지 얘기하며
전 두 가지 생활을 모두 즐겼어요.
독신 생활을 하면서 여호와께서 주신 축복을 누렸습니다.
그땐 제가 이미 순회 활동에 적응하고 두 번째 순회구에서 봉사할 때였죠.
여호와께 감사하게도, 그레이시와 저는 결혼을 하고 지금까지 52년 동안
계속 전 시간 봉사를 할 수 있었습니다.
처음에는 순회 활동을 하시다가 나중에 지역 감독자로 일하셨죠?
그리고 현재는 자매와 함께 특별 파이오니아를 하고 계십니다.
그럼 벌써 60년이 넘게 전 시간 봉사를 하셨네요.
그 행복했던 60년을, 아니 60년이 넘는 그 기간을 되돌아보면서,
형제가 어린 시절에 내린 결정을 생각해 볼 때,
비슷한 결정을 앞둔 청소년들에게 어떤 말씀을 해 주시겠어요?
여호와께선 보잘것없는 제 노력을 축복해 주셨죠.
요즘 젊은 사람들에게는 기회가 더 많습니다.
예수 그리스도의 인도 아래 확장되고 있고 빠르게 움직이기 때문이죠.
조직에서는 우리가 일할 자리를 찾아 우리를 사용할 거라고요.
젊은 사람들이 바톤을 이어받아 달리는 걸 보는 게 제 큰 기쁨입니다.
지금까지 어려움을 견디기 너무 힘들어서 제 결정을 후회한 적은 없습니다.
물론 어려움이 많았지만 여호와의 도움으로 여기까지 왔습니다.
따라서, 젊을 때 기회를 붙잡기 바랍니다.
여호와께서 어릴 때부터 그분을 섬겨 온 사람들에게 주시는 축복을 경험해 보시기 바랍니다.
존슨 형제, 오늘 이렇게 나와 주셔서 정말 즐거웠습니다.
기쁨과 축복으로 가득 찬 형제의 삶에 대해 말씀해 주셔서 유익했습니다.
어렸을 때 여호와께 헌신하고 침례받기로 결정한 덕분이라는 걸 알게 되었습니다.

en.text: I’m so happy to welcome today
a very dear friend of mine,
Brother Robert P. Johnson.
R. P., welcome to the program.
Thank you, Mark.
I appreciate being here.
Now, you’re here, R.P.,
because you are a wonderful example
of someone who’s had a life
filled with blessings in Jehovah’s service.
OK.
So I know that your family goes way back in the truth.
Yes.
In fact, I understand that your great grandfather
learned the truth in Brother Russell’s time, even before 1914.
That’s right!
So that means you’re a fourth-generation Witness.
Mm-hm.
But now, like so many who are watching our program,
you were a little boy growing up in a congregation of Jehovah’s people.
So how did you come to the decision that you wanted
to dedicate your life to serve Jehovah and then get baptized?
Well, Mark, thinking back, I can identify
at least two outstanding influences in my life.
And the first was my parents.
Having that heritage in the truth helped me.
I was just an average kid in my early years.
But the parents instilled in me a desire
to please Jehovah and make it my life to do that.
They set goals before me.
They taught me the truth.
I learned enough from them to be able
to make a dedication to Jehovah God
and to have a close relationship with him.
And so early on, that’s what I did.
I remember that evening after supper
in my bedroom
praying to Jehovah to accept my dedication.
The date was May 25, 1949.
I was 11 years old at the time.
I told my parents, and they were happy,
but they just wanted me to wait longer to make sure
especially how I would handle the teenage years
and so on, so I waited.
And so then when did the moment come for you to finally get baptized?
It was at the 1953 international convention
in Yankee Stadium in New York
on July 22, 1953, when I was baptized.
And again, I remember that like it was yesterday.
When I came up out of the water,
I thanked Jehovah that finally,
“I am one of Jehovah’s Witnesses!”
and I also, like a child, added,
“You can bring the end anytime now.”
So you mentioned your parents, the good influence they had on you,
but was there another influence on you that helped you?
Yes.
At the 1953 convention, Brother Knorr had identified
that there would be a special program
for training people in the truth.
And from the congregation, there was a brother
of the anointed named Charles Richardson,
and my father asked Brother Richardson
to train me in this training program.
And Brother Richardson
was a mentor to me for the next five years of my life.
Over the years, he helped me
view the ministry as an opportunity
to help people develop a relationship with Jehovah
and, therefore, to reach out to them
in teaching them the truth —the doctrinal truth—
but to help them to see that Jehovah is a real person.
And he helped me to enjoy the ministry.
That is what has kept me happy
in Jehovah’s service down to this day.
Now, just from your expressions and what you talked about with me before,
I could see that this Brother Richardson
had a tremendous impact on your life.
And I think, R.P., it really made you
want to be a trainer of other people
because that’s how I first met you, right?
Right. Right.
You were the brother assigned to be my trainer
when I came to the Service Department.
I remember that fondly.
And I know that I’m not the only one.
I mean, you’ve really spent your whole life training other people.
Well, it’s been a privilege.
And I was trained; I was helped along the way.
I was nobody special, but Jehovah
has extended undeserved kindness to me
and made all these things possible.
So there’s no excuse for me not passing along the baton.
And it’s a delight for me to see others carry it.
So now, let’s come back.
You’re 15 years old.
You get baptized at Yankee Stadium,
and now as a result of being baptized at this age,
how do you feel you benefited?
For one thing,
if you know what you want to do and you stay focused on it,
it makes it easier to deal with whatever challenges come later.
And so being dedicated
and baptized early in life
helped me to stay focused on the truth.
I still remember that dedication.
It means something to me,
and I tried to make it mean something to others
(for as young as they can possibly make it).
And they’ll find the same thing I found:
Jehovah’s blessing will be with them.
So now, at 15,
what doors start to open up?
What opportunities come to you because you are a baptized brother?
At age 17, I was appointed as a ministerial servant.
I started pioneering right out of high school at age 18.
And serving where the need was greater,
I got a chance to work at starting a new congregation.
And so at 21,
I was congregation servant, or an elder, at that point.
Then there was a need:
The organization was looking for brothers who could do traveling work.
So at age 25, I had the privilege
of being a traveling overseer.
So now, how did you feel being an elder at 21?
being a circuit overseer at 25?
Was it a little bit overwhelming at such a young age?
I was scared.
I knew the truth,
but I was uncertain about myself,
but then I also knew Jehovah would help me.
I learned a lot as a young traveling overseer, and I thank Jehovah
that the people in the circuits that I served
endured those three years that I was with them.
But now, those were the challenges,
but what do you see as being the benefits of being a young traveling overseer?
For the congregation, they had somebody
who could stay out in field service long hours.
And also
the younger traveling overseer could relate
to the young people
and the younger adults in the congregation.
There were other benefits that even today different ones
that I served in earlier circuits bring forth to me.
For example, after having a good time in field service
and then the meetings, I would do recreational things with the kids.
And we ran track
out in the streets,
and we played board games,
softball, basketball,
and then we had good times just talking about the truth
and also talking
about how you can put your ministry first,
and there’s plenty of time for seeking a mate later.
So now, for a time, you were serving as a single brother,
but at some point, that changed.
When did that happen?
I have enjoyed the best of two worlds.
I enjoyed singleness and the blessings Jehovah gave me.
But when I was 28 years old,
I married a beautiful pioneer sister,
and I had already gotten adjusted in my circuit work.
This was my second circuit.
So, thanks to Jehovah,
we were able to be married, and to this day
Gracie and I continue in full-time service
after 52 years of marriage.
So R.P.,
you started with circuit work, and then later you went on to district work.
Right.
And then you were teaching the Kingdom Ministry School.
Mm-hm.
And then you got invited to Bethel.
Right.
And 31 years at Bethel, right?
Oh, yes.
And now you and Gracie are doing special pioneer work.
Right, in Orlando, Florida.
So you have more than 60 years of full-time service to Jehovah.
It’s because of Jehovah’s blessing,
and it’s made me happy.
So the question I want to ask you is:
When you’re looking back now to these 60 wonderful years
—more than 60 wonderful years—
what would you say to young people who are facing the same decision
that you faced when you were a little boy growing up in the truth?
It’s the best thing I could’ve done with my life,
and I had many opportunities.
Jehovah blessed my humble efforts
as he has blessed you and others too.
The young people today
have even more opportunities
because Jehovah’s organization under the leadership of Jesus Christ
is expanding and moving fast.
And, like Brother Richardson taught me,
if you just make yourself available,
then the organization
will find a place for you and use you,
and that’s so true today.
One of my greatest joys is to see the young people
take the baton and run with it,
and I have no regrets.
There’s been no challenge
that has overwhelmed me and made me regret things.
There were challenges, of course,
but with Jehovah’s help, well, I’m here today.
And that can be true of our young people.
So seize the opportunity while you’re young
and experience the blessing
that Jehovah gives those who serve him from youth onward.
R.P., it has been such a wonderful joy
to have you here on this program
and to hear about your life filled with joy,
your life filled with blessings,
all because of the decision you made just as a little boy
to dedicate your life to Jehovah and get baptized.
Thank you so much.
Thank you. I appreciate talking about it.

ko.text: 성서 연구를 처음 시작했을 때, 이것저것 방해되는 게 많았어요.

제 생활을 변화시키려면 직업을 바꿔야 한다는 걸 깨닫게 되었습니다.
하지만 침례를 받으려면 담배도 끊어야 했습니다.
담배를 하루에 두세 개비 정도로 줄였어요.
그러다 어느 날 담배를 딱 한 개비만 샀습니다.
불을 붙였는데, 여호와께 기도하면서 도와 달라고 간청했습니다.

성서 연구를 시작한 지 10년 만에 침례를 받았습니다.

en.text: When I started studying the Bible,
there were various factors that hindered my study.
I was a truck driver, and I was on the road a lot.
I had the worst kind of friendships,
and I smoked.
I smoked, on average, 60 cigarettes a day.
I realized that if I was going to make the needed adjustments,
I had to change my profession.
So I changed my job.
But if I wanted to get baptized, I had to stop smoking.
I cut down to two or three cigarettes a day.
One day, I bought a single cigarette.
I lit it, and I prayed to Jehovah.
I begged him to help me,
and he did help me
—so much so that I never smoked again.
And to this day, I don’t even have the urge to smoke.
Ten years after my first Bible study, I was baptized.
I’ve been serving Jehovah for 20 years now,
along with my wife and all my children.

ko.text: 저는 퀸즐랜드주 돌비에서 다섯 자녀 중 막내로 태어났습니다.
부모님은 작은 돼지 농장을 운영하고 계셨고
우린 시내에서 10분 거리에 있는 그 농장에 살았죠.
부모님은 제가 여덟 살 때 별거하셨고, 전 큰 충격을 받았습니다.
너무나 힘들었는데, 그로 인한 후유증이 수십 년은 간 것 같아요.
방학이면 농장에 가서 아버지와 같이 지냈습니다.
아버지는 매일같이 술을 마시고 담배를 피고 욕을 했습니다.
그러다 보니 저도 청소년이 됐을 무렵엔
십 대 후반에는 날마다 마리화나를 피웠고,
일주일에 많게는 4일 밤을 술집과 클럽에서 보냈습니다.
저는 술과 담배, 마리화나, 음란물에 중독되었는데,
얼마 지나지 않아 몸이 망가지기 시작했습니다.
어느 날 오후에 여호와의 증인 두 명이 찾아왔는데,
뭔가 답을 찾아 뉴 에이지 사상을 알아보던 중이었죠.
우연이라고 하기에는 참 절묘한 때에 두 사람이 찾아온 겁니다.
하느님이 제게 책을 받으라고 하시는 것 같은 느낌이 들었어요.
뉴 에이지 사상을 알아보는 건 그만두고,
제가 필요한 변화를 하는 데 결정적인 역할을 한 것은
마침내 그 단계를 밟았을 때, 이제 올바른 길에 들어섰다는 생각이 들었습니다.
여호와께서 저를 찾아내 이끌어 주셔서 너무나 감사했습니다.
내가 당신의 하늘을, 손가락으로 하신 일들을,
너무나 보잘것없는 저를 여호와께서 알아 주신 겁니다.
또 영원한 생명을 바라볼 수 있다는 것과
여호와께서 제 잘못을 다 용서해 주시고
새로 시작할 수 있게 해 주셔서 정말 감사드립니다.
순회 활동을 하도록 초대를 받았을 때,
제가 그럴 자격이 있나 하는 강한 의구심이 들었어요.
제가 이 일에 적합한 사람이 아니라는 생각이 머릿속을 떠나지 않았습니다.
그런데 전 시간 순회 활동을 하도록 임명을 받은 바로 다음날 아침이었어요.
모세가 여호와께 자기가 말을 잘하는 사람이 아니고
그분은 모세에게 누가 사람의 입을 만들었냐고 물으셨어요.
여호와 덕분에 인생을 바꿀 수 있었죠.
진리를 알기 전에는 길을 잃은 것처럼 어디로 가야 할지 몰랐어요.
사람답게 살고 싶었지만 어떻게 해야 할지 몰랐어요.
여호와께서 제가 새사람이 되게 해 주셨습니다.

en.text: I was born in Dalby, Queensland.
I’m the youngest of five children,
and my mother and father owned their own piggery.
So we lived on a little farm about ten minutes out of town.
When I was eight years old, my parents separated,
which came as a huge shock to me.
It was devastating, and the consequences just seemed to roll on for decades.
I would go and stay at the farm with my father for school holidays,
but my dad abused alcohol
and smoked cigarettes and used bad language.
So by the time I was a teenager,
I was doing exactly the same thing.
In my late teens, I was smoking marijuana every day
and I was spending up to four nights a week
at pubs and clubs and parties.
I was addicted to alcohol, cigarettes, marijuana,
and pornography, and I had no power to stop.
Obviously, it was only a matter of time
before that lifestyle affected my health.
I lost my social skills, and I became depressed.
The turning point in my life
came one afternoon when two
of Jehovah’s Witnesses knocked on my door.
Because of feeling so lost and so unhappy,
I had started to search for answers and I’d begun looking
at New Age teachings.
The timing felt too remarkable to be just coincidence.
I really felt like God wanted me to take the book.
I never looked at New Age teachings again.
I started to read the Greatest Man  book instead.
A major key for me to be able to make the necessary changes
was to cut off bad association.
I was baptized in March 1994.
When I finally took that step,
I felt like I’d started on the right path.
I was so grateful that Jehovah
had found me and that he’d drawn me.
I really fell in love with the thoughts of Psalm 8:1, 3, 4:
“O Jehovah . . . ,
“when I see your heavens,
“the works of your fingers,
“the moon and the stars that you have prepared,
“what is mortal man that you keep him in mind,
and the son of earthling man that you take care of him?”
I felt so insignificant,
and yet Jehovah knew me.
The hope of everlasting life also really touched my heart,
and so did Jehovah’s forgiveness.
I felt so grateful that Jehovah could forgive me
for all of my wrongdoing and that I could have a fresh start.
When we were invited to start circuit work,
I had serious doubts about my inadequacies.
I was not fast at preparing talks.
For me, it always felt like trying to fit
a square peg into a round hole.
But the very morning
after receiving our assignment to go in the circuit work full-time,
my Bible reading was Exodus chapters 3 and 4,
where Moses cited his inadequacies to Jehovah
—that he was not a fluent speaker.
Well, of course, Jehovah asked him,
‘Who is it that assigns a mouth?’
It was like Jehovah was saying to me:
‘Don’t worry. I will help you.’
To make the changes that I did in life,
I’m just so grateful to Jehovah.
Before I learned the truth, I was lost.
I didn’t know who I was.
I was just a mess.
I wanted to be a man,
but I didn’t really ever know how to do it.
Jehovah has rebuilt me from the ground up.
Jehovah has given me everything.

我完全没有办法控制自己
这种生活方式迟早会影响我的健康
渐渐地
我不知道怎样跟别人正常地交流
我变得非常地沮丧
一天下午
两个耶和华见证人敲我的门
这是我人生当中的转折点
我不知道人生的意义，一直感觉到不开心
所以我开始寻找人生许多问题的答案
我开始对各种宗教和通灵术产生了兴趣
不过，耶和华见证人来得正是时候
我真的感觉是耶和华让我留下那本书的
我不再对其他宗教感兴趣
我开始认真阅读《最伟大人物》这本书
为了作出必要的调整
我必须跟以前的那些坏朋友彻底断绝来往
我在1994年3月受浸
直到受浸后
我才觉得，自己开始了一个全新的人生
耶和华找到了我
然后帮助我亲近他
我真的非常感谢耶和华！
我非常喜欢诗篇8:1,3,4
经文说
“耶和华我们的主啊……
我看见你指头所造的天
目睹你设置的月亮星辰， 就想
凡人算什么，你竟惦记他？
世人算什么，你竟眷顾他？”
我这么渺小，但耶和华竟然认识我
耶和华乐意宽恕人
他也赐给人永生的希望
这让我非常感动
我做了那么多的坏事
耶和华竟宽恕我，给我全新的人生
我真的很感谢他！
后来我们夫妻受到邀请
从事分区探访的工作
但我却觉得自己无法胜任这个工作
我准备演讲非常慢
每次都需要花很多时间来准备
我总是觉得自己不适合这个工作
在我收到委派信的那个早上
我正在读出埃及记的第三、第四章
这里面提到摩西对耶和华说
他不是一个口齿伶俐的人
他一定做不好耶和华交托给他的工作
接着，耶和华问摩西
是谁造了人的口呢？
这就好像耶和华在对我说
“不用担心，我会帮助你。”
我真的很感谢耶和华
他帮助了我，彻底改变我的人生
在学习圣经前
我很绝望，我很迷茫
我的生活一团糟
我想做个有用的人，但我不知道怎么做
但耶和华重新塑造了我
我需要的一切他都赐给了我

titles.ko: 앤드루 헌터: 여호와께서는 제가 새사람이 되게 해 주셨습니다
titles.en: Andrew Hunter: Jehovah Has Rebuilt Me From the Ground Up
titles.cn: 安德鲁·亨特: 耶和华重新塑造了我

ko.text: 생활을 완전히 바꿔야 한다는 걸 알았지만 직업 때문에 그러질 못했습니다.
전 인생을 어떻게 사는 게 좋을지 생각해 봤어요.
그 형제 부부와 성서 연구를 시작하고 한 달 이후부터 계속 집회에 참석하게 되었습니다.
부모님이 연구를 중단하셨기 때문에, 저희 셋만 집회에 나갔습니다.
여호와께선 인생에 대한 우리의 생각을 완전히 바꾸실 수 있죠.
배운 대로 살기만 하면 여호와께서 버리지 않으신다는 걸 깨달았습니다.
여호와와 더 친밀한 관계를 가지려고, 성경을 날마다 읽고 기도합니다.
지금은 기도할 때, 가까운 친구한테 말하는 것 같은 느낌이 들어요.
제가 여호와께 가까이 가고 왕국을 실제적으로 느끼는 데 큰 도움이 된 거 같아요.
그래서 침례를 받고 싶은 마음이 생겼죠.
그리고 4개월 뒤에 여호와께 헌신하고 침례를 받았을 때
그 기쁨은 이루 말할 수가 없었죠.
오늘 이곳에서 우리 아이들 셋이 침례를 받았어요.
어둠 속에서 절 끌어내 주신 여호와께 매일매일 감사를 드립니다.
여호와께 충성하겠다는 결심으로 용기를 내서 순결을 지키면
절 돌봐 주시는 하늘의 아버지께서 계시다는 걸 아는 것만큼
제가 정말 이 모든 축복을 받을 자격이 되나요?’ 하고요.
제가 정말 만족스럽고 행복한 삶을 살고 있다는 생각이 듭니다.
여호와께서 제게 가르쳐 주신 중요한 특성은 사랑입니다.
가족에게서, 여호와에게서, 친구들에게서 그 사랑을 느꼈죠.
전 사람들을 사랑할 수 있고 또 사랑해야 한다는 걸 배웠어요.
여호와와 가까이 일하니까, 정말 그분의 가족이란 느낌이 들죠.
여호와께 충성을 바친다는 건, 내 삶을 바치는 거죠.
여호와께서 내게 이 모든 일이 일어나게 허용하신 건 사실이지만
여호와께서 언니와 저에게 해 주신 일을 묵상해 보니까, 두려워할 필요가 없어요.
정말이지, 여호와를 섬기기로 선택한 건 제 인생 최고의 결정입니다.

en.text: I enjoyed associating
with Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Later, I also started to study the Bible.
I knew that I had to make
drastic changes in my life,
but my job prevented me from doing so.
So I asked myself,
‘What would I like to do with my life?’
I began studying the Bible again with the couple
and one month later
started attending meetings regularly.
Since our parents had stopped studying,
only three of us went to the meetings.
Jehovah can do a lot with you.
Jehovah could, you know,
your whole perspective can change.
I knew if I applied what I learned,
Jehovah would not let me down.
To strengthen my relationship with Jehovah,
I read the Bible daily and I pray.
My relationship with Jehovah
has gotten stronger.
When I pray now,
it feels like I’m talking to my close Friend.
Going out in service more—
I think it really helped me
to draw closer to Jehovah
and make the Kingdom feel real to me.
And so that’s why I wanted to get baptized.
What a great pleasure it was for me
when four months later
I could dedicate myself to Jehovah
and get baptized!
That made me so happy.
Today is a very, very special day for me,
because today I’m getting baptized.
At the regional convention, August 9, 2014,
it was a beautiful day.
Now, when I think about my three children
who got baptized today,
I feel my heart is full of joy,
and I really thank Jehovah!
Yeah, it’s not a day I don’t go thank Jehovah
for taking me out of the darkness.
If we are determined to be loyal to Jehovah
and we have the courage to remain chaste,
well, we won’t have any regrets.
To know that you have a heavenly Father
that cares about you
—that was the best feeling on earth.
I often think: ‘God, is it true? Is it real?
Do I really deserve to have all these blessings?’
All these blessings have helped me to see
that this life provides true satisfaction and true happiness.
The important quality
that Jehovah has taught me is love.
I felt that love from my family,
from Jehovah, and from my friends.
I learned that it’s OK to love people,
and that’s what you are supposed to do.
Working closely with Jehovah,
I really feel part of his family.
When you give your faith to Jehovah,
you’re giving your life to him.
He’s permitted these things to come upon me;
I knew that.
But he protected me.
When I meditate and think
about what Jehovah has done for me and Lei Lei,
I don’t have to be afraid.
Jehovah is my “secure refuge,”
because life may change, but Jehovah does not change.
Choosing to serve Jehovah
was the best decision I have made in my life.

我和耶和华的关系更牢固了
现在向他祷告
就好像和一个好朋友说话一样
经常出去传道

这推动我决定受浸

我决心献身受浸给耶和华

2014年8月9日的区域大会

我每一天都感谢耶和华
把我从黑暗中拉出来

就会有勇气保持贞洁
而且不会做出让自己后悔的事
知道有一位天父关心我

这是真的吗？
我真的配得到这些福分吗？

这样的生活才能得到真正的满足
和真正的快乐
耶和华帮助我明白
爱是最重要的特质
我从家人、朋友
从耶和华那里都能感受到这种爱
我学到我也应该爱别人

与耶和华亲密合作
让我在他的大家庭里有归属感
当你全心信赖耶和华
就是把你的一生都献给他了
我知道我经历的种种遭遇
都是他允许的
但他也保护了我
每当回想耶和华为我和蕾蕾做的事情
我就确信我不需要害怕
因为耶和华是我的避难所
生活可能会改变

选择事奉耶和华
