titles.cn: 受浸之路

ko.text: 모잠비크 특별 지역 대회는 여러모로 뜻깊은 행사였습니다.
이 대회가 특별했던 이유 한 가지는
믿음 때문에 수감된 경험이 있는 많은 용기 있는 형제들이 참석했기 때문입니다.
유럽의 몇몇 나라에서 온 이 형제들은 충절을 증명해 왔고 우리에게 훌륭한 본이 됩니다.
용감한 모잠비크 형제 자매들이 이 형제들과 한 자리에 모여
이 대회에 참석하니까 참 격려를 받습니다.
우리는 말라위 형제들과 함께 “재교육 수용소”에서 10년을 보냈어요.
저희 둘은 같은 수용소에 있었는데, 오늘은 이 대회에 같이 참석해 있네요.
우리는 조롱과 박해를 받았지만 여호와 덕분에 용기를 낼 수 있었어요.
오늘 이 아름다운 대회에 참석하니 용기가 훨씬 더 생깁니다.
금지령 시절에 저는 몇몇 형제들과 함께
자전거를 타고 먼 거리를 달려 출판물을 배달하는 일을 했습니다.
경찰이 우리를 찾으러 다녔기 때문에 참 힘들었죠.
여호와께서 용기를 주셔서 두려움을 극복할 수 있었습니다.
모두 합해 4년 가까운 시간을 감옥에서 보내야만 했습니다.
여호와께서 주시는 용기로 잘 이겨 낼 수 있었습니다.
그리고 이곳에서 다시 형제들을 만날 수 있었습니다.
어려움이 많이 있었지만 오늘 저는 너무 행복합니다.
이 대회에서 츠와어와 세나어로 「그리스어 성경」을 발표했습니다.
여호와여, 이 놀라운 선물을 주셔서 감사합니다.
츠와어로 여호와의 이름을 알려 줄 때, 꼭 이 성경을 사용할 거예요.
읽기도 쉽고, 가족 숭배에서 얻는 유익도 더 커질 것 같아요.
이 두 언어로 모잠비크에서 그리스어 「신세계역」이 처음 번역된 것입니다.
이 특별 지역 대회는 모잠비크의 18곳을 연결하여 진행되었고,
마푸토에서 열린 이 대회에서 침례를 받은 981명 중에
청소년들이 많이 있었다는 점이 화제가 되었습니다.
청소년들이 여호와를 알고 사랑하고 진정한 용기를 나타내도록
열심히 돕고 있다는 걸 알 수 있었습니다.
아프리카에서 특별 지역 대회를 조직하려면, 많은 노력이 들고 잘 계획해야 합니다.
하지만 분명 여호와께서는 이 특별 지역 대회를 축복하셨습니다.
대회는 모든 면에서 성공적이었고 대표자들은 매우 행복해했습니다!
여호와의 영이 함께한다는 걸 확실히 느낄 수 있었습니다.
모잠비크에서 금지령이 있기 전에 우리는 함께 왕국 노래를 불렀습니다.
그리고 이 대회에서도 대표단에게 왕국 노래를 불러 주고 있지요.
현지 형제 자매들과 함께 야외 봉사에 참여한 것을 꼽았습니다.
모잠비크 형제 자매들은 형편이 넉넉하지 않은데도
극진한 후대를 나타냈고 대표자들은 큰 감동을 받았습니다.
삶을 완전히 바꾸어 놓을 만한 경험을 했다고 말했습니다.
모잠비크 형제 자매들에게 중앙장로회가 그들을 사랑한다는 걸 알려 드리고 싶습니다.
더 중요한 것으로 여호와께서 그들을 알고 사랑하고 도와주십니다.

en.text: The Mozambique special convention
is truly outstanding
for so many different reasons.
One thing that has made this convention unique
is that we have so many courageous brothers
who have been in prison for their faith
from Angola, Korea, Malawi, Zimbabwe,
and from some of the countries in Europe
and who had to really stand up and set an example.
And to have them all here
with our courageous
Mozambican brothers
has made this
convention so special.
It is very encouraging
to be at this special convention.
We have spent ten years
in the “reeducation camps”
along with our brothers from Malawi, and we were at the same camp.
And today we are together at this special convention.
It’s very encouraging.
In 1990, I was judged and condemned
to 15 months of prison in Paris.
We were about 100 brothers in prison.
They tried to shame us,
but thanks to Jehovah, we had courage.
And today this beautiful convention
fills us with even more courage.
I was one of the brothers serving
as a bicycle courier during the ban,
delivering literature long distances.
It was difficult work because the police were searching for us.
Jehovah blessed us with courage, giving us a heart without fear.
Because of our Christian neutrality,
we were in prison.
Although it was a difficult time,
Jehovah gave us courage to endure,
and now we are here together.
We really thank Jehovah for that.
I was arrested and sentenced
to six years in prison.
Despite all these difficulties,
today I feel very happy.
I feel very encouraged.
At this convention, we released
the Greek Scriptures  in Tshwa and Sena.
Thank you very much, Jehovah,
for this wonderful provision.
I will surely use it
while speaking about
Jehovah’s name in Tshwa.
We are so happy to have
this Bible in the Tshwa language.
It’s easy to read, and it will improve our family worship.
Those were the first two local languages
in Mozambique to receive any part of the New World Translation.
So it was a very exciting day!
This convention was tied
in to 18 locations in Mozambique.
A total of 1,685 were baptized.
I have faith in Jehovah
and want to have
a close relationship with him.
Many have commented on the fact that among the 981
who were baptized in Maputo, there were many young ones.
And it just shows that the families here in Mozambique
are working very hard with their young ones
to help them to know Jehovah and love Jehovah
and to know what it means to be courageous.
To organize
a special convention
in Africa
requires a lot of work and a lot of planning.
But you can truly see the blessing of Jehovah here
because everything has gone so beautifully
and the delegates are so happy!
You can really feel that Jehovah’s spirit is with us.
Before the work
was banned in Mozambique,
we used to sing to Jehovah.
At the camps, we continued to sing joyfully.
Now with the special convention,
we continue to sing to our delegates.
Many of the delegates commented that their favorite part
of the convention was going out in the ministry with the local brothers.
Even though the brothers may have very limited resources,
they showed them tremendous hospitality;
it made a huge impression.
Some of the delegates even said that when they go back,
this is going to have a life-changing effect on them.
We want to assure
these dear brothers and sisters
that the Governing Body loves them.
But greater than that, Jehovah God knows about them;
he loves them; he’s supporting them.

在同一个改造营里被关了10年

茨瓦语和塞纳语的《希腊语经卷》
今天发行了
谢谢耶和华，给我们这么好的礼物
我一定会用这本茨瓦语的圣经
跟人谈论上帝的名字
我们非常高兴能有茨瓦语的圣经

这对我们的家庭崇拜肯定更有帮助
茨瓦语和塞纳语

title: 마크 샌더슨: ‘사람들을 제자로 삼아 침례를 주십시오’

ko.text: 차를 타고 여행할 계획을 한다고 상상해 보십시오.
필요한 게 다 있는데, 지도도 있고, 차도 준비됐고, 연료도 충분하죠.
하지만 출발하기 전에 꼭 알아야 할 것 있는데,
네, 목적지를 모른다면 어떤 길로 가야 할지 알 수 없을 겁니다.
우리가 하는 봉사도 그런 여행과 비슷하다고 말할 수 있습니다.
우린 “영원한 생명을 얻기에 합당한 성향을 가진 사람들”을
우린 봉사 도구함의 모든 도구를 포함해서
이 여행에 필요한 걸 다 갖고 있습니다.
우리가 봉사에서 달성하고자 하는 가장 중요한 목표는 무엇입니까?
아니면 사람들을 예수 그리스도의 제자로 삼아
각각의 목표가 중요하지만 그중 어떤 목표가 가장 중요할까요?
예수께서는 마태복음 28:19, 20에서 그 점을 이렇게 알려 주셨습니다.
“그러므로 가서 모든 민족의 사람들을 제자로 삼아,
아버지와 아들과 성령의 이름으로 그들에게 침례를 주고
내가 여러분에게 명령한 모든 것을 지키도록 가르치십시오.”
네, 우리의 목적지는 침례받은 제자를 만드는 것입니다.
우리의 웹사이트를 알려 주든, 재방문을 하든, 성서 연구를 사회하든,
우리는 침례받은 제자를 만드는 것을 최종 목표로 삼아야 합니다.
간단히 말해, 구원받으려면 침례가 꼭 필요하기 때문입니다.
성경 베드로 전서 3:21에서는 이렇게 알려 줍니다.
예수 그리스도의 부활을 통해 지금 여러분을 구원하고 있습니다.”
따라서 관심 있는 사람을 처음 만날 때부터
그를 침례받은 제자로 만드는 것을 계속 우리의 목표로 삼아야 합니다.
우리와 성서 연구를 하는 사람에 관해
그리하여 장차 믿음 안에서 형제 또는 자매가 될 사람으로서
그 연구생에게 진정한 개인적 관심을 반영해야 한다.”
우리가 침례받은 제자를 만드는 최종 목표를 확고히 염두에 두지 않는다면,
다음 동영상에 나오는 형제가 어떤 문제를 겪고 있는지 보시기 바랍니다.
이 형제의 상황에 공감이 되지 않으십니까?
단지 우릴 좋아해서 반기는 사람을 재방문한 경우가 있으신가요?
아마 수개월, 심지어 수년 동안 출판물을 전했지만
영적으로 발전하는 데는 진지한 관심을 나타내지 않았을지 모릅니다.
그 사람이 그리스도 예수의 제자가 되는 데 관심이 없는 사람일 수 있기 때문입니다.
그러므로 “영원한 생명을 얻기에 합당한 성향을 가진” 사람들을 찾는 데
우리의 시간을 사용하는 것이 더 나을 것입니다.
물론, 우리 웹사이트로 주의를 이끄는 JW.ORG 카드나
출판물을 전하는 것이 중요하지 않다는 말이 아닙니다.
우리의 봉사 도구함에 있는 이런 도구들은 다 목적을 갖고 있죠.
“합당한 성향을 가진” 사람들의 마음에 이르는 데
따라서 여호와의 조직이 제공하는 이런 도구들을
관심 있는 사람과 성서 연구를 시작하는 목표를 결코 잊지 마십시오.
여러 해 동안 성서 연구를 해 왔지만, 발전하지 않는 연구생의 경우는 어떨까요?
그리스도인 집회에 참석하는 데는 진실한 관심이 없습니다.
어떤 사람들은 단지 성경을 배우는 것을 좋아하기 때문에,
물론 우린 사람들에게 성경을 가르치는 걸 좋아하죠.
단지 성경을 가르치는 것 자체가 우리의 주된 목표는 아니라는 점입니다.
이것도 샛길로 빠지는 게 될 수 있죠.
사실, 성경을 높이 평가하고 성경에 대해 배우는 것을 좋아하지만
예수의 침례받은 제자가 되는 데는 관심이 없는 사람들이 있습니다.
세상에는 성경에 관한 교육은 많이 받았지만
그리스도 예수의 제자는 되려고 하지 않는 성서 학자들이 아주 많습니다.
예를 들어, 한 성서 학자는 총 세 군데의 신학교를 거치면서
성서와 종교에 관해 많은 교육을 받았습니다.
성경에 쓰인 그리스어에 대한 지식도 해박합니다.
따라서 단지 성경을 가르치는 것이 우리의 주된 목표는 아닙니다.
우리는 사람들이 하느님에 대한 믿음을 기르고,
헌신과 침례라는 목적지를 향해 나아가도록 돕기를 바랍니다.
따라서 성서 연구생이 잘 발전하고 있는지
배운 내용에 따라 자신의 생활을 변화시키고 있습니까?
그리스도인 모임에 참석해서 유익을 얻고 있습니까?
「왕국 봉사」 1988년 10월호에 나온 다음과 같은 조언을 따를 수 있습니다.
“만일 합리적인 기간이 지나도록 참을성 있게 도와 왔는데도
연구생이 의미 있는 발전을 하지 않는다면,
합당한 사람을 찾는 일에 더 유용하게 시간을 사용하는 것이
연구를 중단하는 것이 현명할 수도 있다.”
그런데 누구와 성서 연구를 할지 선택하는 것이 왜 그렇게 중요합니까?
아무도 없는 집이나 관심이 없는 사람을 찾아가는 것보다는
비생산적인 연구라도 하는 게 더 낫지 않을까요?
마태복음 10:11-13에 나온 예수의 말씀을 읽어 보겠습니다.
그곳에서 합당한 사람을 찾아내고, 떠날 때까지 거기에 머무르십시오.
그 집이 합당하면 여러분이 비는 평화가 그 집에 이를 것이고,
합당하지 않으면 그 평화가 여러분에게 돌아올 것입니다.”
이 말씀과 일치하게, 우리는 예수께서 가르쳐 주신 대로,
합당한 사람, 즉 “영원한 생명을 얻기에 합당한 성향을 가진” 사람에게
우린 재방문하거나 연구하는 사람에게 참을성을 보여야 하는데,
모든 사람이 같은 속도로 발전하지는 않죠.
‘사람들을 제자로 삼아 침례를 주는 것’임을 잊지 말아야 합니다.
우리가 목적지를 향해 잘 가고 있는지,
아니면 샛길로 빠지고 있는지 알게 될 겁니다.
그 비행기는 여러분이 방문하는 사람과 같은데,
성경의 소식에 진실한 관심을 나타내는 것 같습니다.
활주로에서 이륙해서 성서 연구를 시작하는 것입니다.
연구가 시작되면, 비행기는 날기 시작한 것이죠.
하지만 일단 비행기가 이륙하면 목적지에 눈을 고정해야 합니다.
그냥 계속 공중에 떠 있기만 할 수는 없죠.
우리의 목표는 침례받은 제자를 만드는 것입니다.
만약 합리적인 시간이 지났는데도 연구생이 발전하지 않는다면,
그런 연구를 계속하는 것은 그냥 공중을 빙빙 도는 것과 같습니다.
계속 공중에 떠 있기만 할 뿐 아무 곳으로도 가지 못하는 비행기와 같죠.
어느 한 곳이든 착륙을 해야 하는데,
침례받은 제자라는 목적지에 도착하든지, 아니면 연구를 중단하든지 해야 합니다.
그런데, 연구생이 침례라는 목적지에 도착하지 못하게
세상 축일을 지키는 일이나 흡연과 같은 불결한 습관에 빠져 있다면요?
이 형제가 흡연 습관을 극복하기 위해
기도로 여호와께 도움을 청했다는 점에 유의하셨나요?
이 형제는 담배를 끊는 데 필요한 믿음을 기르기 위해서
여호와 하느님과의 개인적인 관계를 발전시켜야 했습니다.
우리는 연구생들이 여호와와 개인적인 관계를 발전시키도록 도울 필요가 있습니다.
그래야 연구생들이 침례로 나아가는 데 방해가 되는 장애물들을
그런데, 현재 성서 연구를 사회하고 있지 않다면 어떨까요?
성서 연구생이 침례받게 돕는 훌륭한 경험을 해 본 적이 없다면 어떨까요?
그럼 여호와께 드리는 여러분의 봉사는 가치가 없는 걸까요?
우리는 봉사의 직무에서 각자의 몫을 하고 있는 것입니다.
고린도 전서 3:6, 7에서 사도 바울이 한 이 말을 기억하십니까?
“나는 심었고 아볼로는 물을 주었지만, 자라게 하신 분은 하느님이십니다.
그러므로 심는 사람이나 물을 주는 사람은 아무것도 아닙니다.
따라서 여러분이 하는 역할을 절대 과소평가하지 마십시오.
바울이 말했듯이, 봉사에서 거두는 성과는 모두 함께 이룬 것이죠.
연구 사회자의 노력만으로 그렇게 된 것이 아닙니다.
아마도 다른 누군가가 출판물을 전했거나 어떤 식으로든 증거한 것이
연구생이 처음에 흥미를 갖게 된 계기가 되었을 수 있습니다.

en.text: Imagine for a moment
that you’re planning a road trip.
You have everything you need:
a map, a car, and plenty of fuel.
Before you start the engine, though,
you need to know your destination —wouldn’t you agree?
If you don’t know where you are trying to go,
you won’t know which road to take.
The same is true of our ministry,
which is, in a sense, like that road trip.
As Acts 13:48 shows, we’re always searching
for “those who [are] rightly disposed for everlasting life.”
We have everything we need for the journey,
including all the tools in our Teaching Toolbox.
But what would you say is our destination?
What’s the most important goal
that we are trying to accomplish in our ministry?
Is it placing literature?
directing people to jw.org®?
making return visits?
starting Bible studies?
educating people about the Bible?
or making disciples of Christ Jesus and baptizing them?
Each of those goals has value.
But which one is our primary goal?
What’s the destination that we want to reach?
Jesus identified it
at Matthew 28:19, 20.
There he said:
“Go, therefore, and make disciples
“of people of all the nations, baptizing them in the name
“of the Father and of the Son and of the holy spirit,
“teaching them to observe all the things
I have commanded you.”
Our destination, then, is a baptized disciple.
Each person we meet,
each piece of literature that we place,
each time we direct attention to the website,
each return visit we make,
each Bible study we conduct
—we should have the final goal
of making a baptized disciple.
Why is baptism essential?
Put simply, it’s because baptism
is necessary for salvation.
That’s what the Bible tells us
at 1 Peter 3:21:
“Baptism . . . is also now saving you
“(not by the removing of the filth of the flesh,
“but by the request to God for a good conscience),
through the resurrection of Jesus Christ.”
So from the time we meet an interested person,
we want to have our eyes on that goal
of making a baptized disciple.
In fact, the November 1977 Kingdom Ministry
made this statement regarding those we study with:
“Our discussions should reflect
“a genuine personal  interest in the student
“as a potential disciple and therefore
a potential brother or sister in the faith.”
If we don’t have that end-point
of a baptized disciple fixed firmly in mind,
we could end up stuck on side roads.
For example, watch this video,
and see if you can identify the problem that our brother has.
Are you going out in field service after lunch?
Yes, I’m going to be there, but I’ve got one return visit that I’ve got to make.
All right, see you.
See you.
My neighbor lost his job after 20 years,
and as a result, he’s got to move out of his house,
got to move into an apartment.
So I decided to go help him out a little bit
to pack up to make it a little easier for him to make that move.
You know, won’t it be nice at a time period
where we don’t have to worry about economic troubles like that?
Yeah, it will.
Uhm, you know, that’s why I’m so happy
that my grandchildren chose to go for higher education.
They both landed good jobs.
You know that bridge you cross when you come here.
You’ve noticed that they’re starting to do some work on it.
And that’s pretty extensive work.
They’re going to replace that whole bridge.
So according to the newspaper article,
it’s going to be like a six to eight month project.
Wow! That is a long time.
Uhm, you know, Chris,
the reason why I came by is I wanted to show you this magazine.
I love these. These are so well written.
Isaiah 48:17 is a key scripture here.
Notice what it says:
“I, Jehovah, am your God,
the One teaching you to benefit yourself.”
That’s familiar.
I think your dad read that to me once or twice.
How’s your dad doing anyway?
Doing good.
Ah, you know, they said they’ve got more Bible studies
than they can even cover in one week.
Well, well, you know, I can remember when you and your dad came here.
You were a little kid about this high,
and you just stayed right by his side.
And your dad was so proud.
You know, Chris, I know my dad had offered
to study the Bible with you in the past.
John, to be honest,
I’m too old to change;
I’m set in my ways now.
I think that God is just going to have to take me the way I am.
More chocolate?
Uhm, yeah. I don’t mind.
Could you identify with the brother in that video?
Have you ever had a return visit with someone
who just loves your company?
Perhaps you’ve been leaving literature with that person for months
—even years— and yet the person
has no genuine interest in progressing.
Why is that a problem?
Apparently, the person isn’t interested
in becoming a disciple of Christ Jesus.
Our time would be better spent searching for other people
who are “rightly disposed for everlasting life.”
Of course, that doesn’t mean that there’s no value
in placing literature or leaving contact cards
that direct people to jw.org.
These provisions are part of our Teaching Toolbox for a reason.
They can play a vital role in reaching the hearts
of those who are “rightly disposed.”
So continue to make good use of these tools
that Jehovah’s organization provides.
At the same time, never lose sight of your goal
to start Bible studies with interested ones
—and then the ultimate goal:
to “make disciples . . . , baptizing them.”
What about a person you’ve been studying with for years,
but the person isn’t making changes,
hasn’t stopped going to church,
and shows no real interest in attending Christian meetings?
Some people are glad to study the Bible with us
simply for the fact that they value Bible education.
And we love to teach people about the Bible.
But we have to remember that providing Bible education
for its own sake is not our primary goal.
In fact, it could be a side road.
The fact is,
some people who value Bible education
are not interested in becoming
baptized disciples of Jesus.
The world is full of Bible scholars
who are highly educated in the Bible
but who do not become disciples of Christ Jesus.
For example, one Bible scholar was educated
at a Bible institute, a religious college,
and a theological seminary.
He holds a doctorate in religious studies.
He has a thorough knowledge of Biblical Greek,
and he’s written 30 books about the Bible.
Yet, he describes himself
as an “agnostic atheist.”
So just providing Bible education
is not our primary goal.
We want people to build faith in God
and to have their own relationship with Jehovah
that will move them toward the destination
of dedication and baptism.
That’s why it’s important to honestly analyze
the progress of our Bible students.
Are they simply taking in knowledge?
Do they prepare in advance for the study?
Do they answer in their own words and from their heart?
Are they making changes in their life
to conform to what they’ve learned?
Are they attending and benefiting from Christian meetings?
If not, we may need to follow the advice
of the Kingdom Ministry of October 1988, which stated:
“If a student is not making meaningful progress
“after you have patiently aided him
“over a reasonable period of time,
“it may be best to use the time
“to better advantage searching for deserving ones.
“Depending on the circumstances,
it may be wise to discontinue the study.”
But why is it so important to be selective
about who we spend our time with?
Isn’t conducting an unproductive study
better than knocking on doors where no one is home
or where no one shows interest?
To answer that, let’s read Jesus’ words
at Matthew 10:11-13.
Now, when instructing his disciples
about how to conduct their ministry, Jesus said:
“Into whatever city or village you enter,
“search out who in it is deserving,
“and stay there until you leave.
“When you enter the house, greet the household.
“If the house is deserving,
“let the peace you wish it come upon it;
“but if it is not deserving,
let the peace from you return upon you.”
In harmony with those verses,
we want to focus our attention on deserving ones
as Jesus instructed,
people who are “rightly disposed for everlasting life.”
Obviously, there is a balance.
We need to be patient with those we call on and study with,
and not everyone progresses at the same rate.
But as we call on people and study with them,
we should never lose sight of our goal —our destination—
to “make disciples . . . , baptizing them.”
If we have that goal clearly in mind,
we’ll know when we are moving toward it,
and we’ll know when we are getting sidetracked.
We could illustrate it like this:
Think of a plane on a runway.
That plane is like a person you’ve visited
and you believe shows sincere interest in the Bible’s message.
Your short-term goal at this point
is to get them off the runway and into a Bible study.
If you do, that means the plane has taken off.
But once your study is airborne,
you have to keep your sights on your destination.
You can’t just stay in the air indefinitely.
Your goal is to make a baptized disciple.
If, in a reasonable amount of time,
the student isn’t progressing, what will you do?
To keep the study going would be like flying in circles.
In the same way, a Bible study
that’s simply suspended in the air goes nowhere.
We have to land the plane
—either at the destination of a baptized disciple
or at the termination of the study.
But what if something is holding your Bible student back
from the destination of baptism
—maybe an attachment to holiday celebrations
or an unclean habit, like smoking?
Notice how this issue arises in the following brief video.
When I started studying the Bible,
there were various factors that hindered my study.
I was a truck driver, and I was on the road a lot.
I had the worst kind of friendships,
and I smoked.
I smoked, on average, 60 cigarettes a day.
I realized that if I was going to make the needed adjustments,
I had to change my profession.
So I changed my job.
But if I wanted to get baptized, I had to stop smoking.
I cut down to two or three cigarettes a day.
One day, I bought a single cigarette.
I lit it, and I prayed to Jehovah.
I begged him to help me,
and he did help me
—so much so that I never smoked again.
And to this day, I don’t even have the urge to smoke.
Ten years after my first Bible study, I was baptized.
I’ve been serving Jehovah for 20 years now,
along with my wife and all my children.
Did you notice this man had to pray to Jehovah
to get the help he needed to overcome smoking?
In other words, he had to cultivate
his own relationship with Jehovah
in order to build the faith he needed to stop smoking.
In the same way, we need to help our students
to build their own relationship with Jehovah
so that they’ll also overcome any obstacles
that might hold them back from progressing to baptism.
But what if you’re not presently conducting a Bible study?
What if you’ve never had the privilege
of having one of your Bible students get baptized?
Does that mean your service to Jehovah is not valuable?
Not at all.
Remember, we each do our part in the ministry.
Do you remember what the apostle Paul said
at 1 Corinthians 3:6, 7:
“I planted, Apollos watered,
“but God kept making it grow,
“so that neither is the one who plants anything
“nor is the one who waters,
but God who makes it grow.”
So never feel that your efforts are unimportant.
Just as Paul said,
what’s accomplished in the ministry is a group effort.
When a person reaches baptism,
it isn’t just because of the effort
of the person who conducted the study.
The efforts of others played a role.
Perhaps someone else initiated that person’s interest
by placing literature or in some other way
giving a witness.
But remember what Paul said.
Jehovah is the one “who makes it grow.”
He is the one that is drawing to himself
those who are “rightly disposed for everlasting life.”
What a privilege we have
to be fellow workers with Jehovah
as we help people become disciples of Christ Jesus!
If we keep that goal clearly in mind,
how will it help us?
We won’t be content just to place literature
or just to direct interest to jw.org.
We won’t be satisfied
just making return visits or starting Bible studies.
We’ll always have in mind our primary destination
—making disciples of Christ
and baptizing them.
We of the Governing Body
wish you Jehovah’s rich blessing
as you work shoulder to shoulder with us
in helping “rightly disposed” ones
become baptized disciples of Jesus.

ko.text: 당국이 여호와의 증인의 집들을 대대적으로 수색했습니다.
대문 앞에 복면을 쓴 두 남자가 서 있더라고요.
그래서 대문을 열었더니 더 많은 사람들이 있었어요.
그들은 우리 둘을 마당에 서 있게 했는데, 비도 내리고 있었어요.
그래서 아이가 신발을 신을 수 있게 해 달라고 했더니
증인 신도인 로만 마흐네프에게 수갑이 채워졌습니다.
그가 조금도 반항하거나 저항하지 않았는데 말이죠.
바로 그 시간에 또 다른 특수 대원들이
전 그때 바로 이 방에서 화분에 물을 주고 있었어요.
그래서 방에서 나와 봤더니 사람들이 있더라고요.
몸이 안 좋아서 일어날 수 없다고 했죠.
극단주의 서적으로 분류된 책들을 그들의 집에 몰래 숨겨 놓았으며
“아깐 없었는데 왜 이 책이 내 방에 있는 거지?”
아무도 신원을 밝히지 않았고, 영장도 보여 주지 않았어요.
나처럼 힘없는 노인의 집에 쳐들어온 겁니다.
정말 말도 안 되는 일이 벌어진 거죠.
무슨 기계실 같은 데에 있는 라디에이터에
다음날 아침에 신문을 받을 때까지 그렇게 있었죠.
남편이 갑자기 아프기 시작했고 딸이 소릴 질렀죠.
남편은 약을 받아 먹고 좀 좋아졌어요.
남편은 26일에 체포됐는데 당국은 29일까지 아무 음식도 주지 않았죠.
로만 마흐네프와 드미트리 쿠진이 체포되고 이틀 후인 6월 28일에,
칼루시스키 지방 법원은 그들을 교도소로 보냈습니다.
우리 아빠가 범죄자가 아니라는 걸 사람들이 빨리 알게 됐으면 좋겠어요.
아빠가 얼른 집으로 돌아와서 다시 함께했으면 좋겠어요.
체포된 두 여호와의 증인은 자신들이 무죄라고 생각하며,
포기하지 않고 남편 편에 끝까지 서서 싸울 거예요.
이러한 명백한 사실을 하루빨리 인정해 줬으면 좋겠어요.
우리 여호와의 증인이 사회에 해가 되지 않고
정부에 조금도 위협이 되지 않는다는 사실을 말이에요.

en.text: On June 26, 2019, in Kaluga, Russia,
mass searches were carried out in the homes of peaceful believers.
Two of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
Roman Makhnev and Dmitriy Kuzin,
were arrested simply because of their religion.
I heard a commotion on the street.
When I went out, I saw two masked men in the courtyard.
I took the keys for the gate and opened the door.
Several more men were there.
My daughter came out.
She was barefoot,
and they made her stand next to me on the courtyard flagstone.
It was drizzling.
I asked to let the child put shoes on.
He said, “Later.”
The believer, Roman Makhnev,
was handcuffed, even though in no way
was he ever aggressive or disorderly.
At the same time, another group of security forces burst
into Dmitriy and Svetlana Kuzin’s apartment.
I was here in this room at home,
watering my plants.
I heard my husband unlocking the door.
I went out of the room and saw a bunch of people.
My husband had obviously been knocked down
face-first to the tile floor as he came in.
His hands were handcuffed behind his back.
Yet another group of armed law-enforcement officers
raided the home of 87-year-old Olga Verevkina.
There was a full SWAT team in camouflage.
No warrant was shown.
They demanded, “Get up!”
I said: “I can’t.
I’m infirm.”
My blood pressure went up to 200/115.
According to the believers, during the searches,
publications from the Federal List of Extremist Materials were planted
in their homes and their rights were violated.
I heard Dasha scream: “This was not in my room!
Explain to me how it got here!”
And I heard my husband’s voice, saying, “This was planted.”
Just that afternoon,
I was vacuuming under the bed,
and there was nothing there.
No one identified himself.
No documents were shown.
The search began at 9:00 in the evening
and lasted until about 4:30 in the morning.
But for camouflaged security forces
to burst in on old, infirm people
—that’s unbelievable!
It’s quite interesting.
In order to deal with an elderly woman,
our law-enforcement officers come en masse,
wearing masks, and carrying weapons.
What cowards!
And these people claim that they are actually fighting extremism.
After the searches, Roman Makhnev and Dmitriy Kuzin
were taken to the FSB building.
When Papa was taken away, the only thing I managed to whisper to him
was that I was proud of his integrity.
And then they took him away, and I felt sad.
I was scared.
When they brought Roman to the FSB building,
he was handcuffed to a radiator
in some sort of utility room
and was kept like this until he was called
for questioning in the morning.
It is noteworthy that several hours earlier, during the searches,
an ambulance was called for Roman Makhnev.
Roman became very ill.
Dasha started to scream.
The FSB called an ambulance, and it came quickly enough.
He was given medication, and then he felt better.
Roman was arrested on the 26th, and they didn’t feed him until the 29th.
Roman Makhnev was given no food for three days.
They said,
“Well, he could eat whatever he brought with him.”
Interesting.
I have filed complaints with various agencies.
On June 28, two days after their arrest,
the Kaluzhskiy District Court sent
Roman Makhnev and Dmitriy Kuzin to a detention center.
I hope that people will realize
that my dad is not guilty of anything,
and he is not a criminal.
Therefore, I hope that soon he’ll be back,
and we will be together again.
The believers do not agree with the charges,
and they intend to seek justice.
I don’t know if we’ll be able to, but I’m determined to fight
to the end to help my husband
and to support him.
I very much hope that common sense will prevail
and that the authorities will finally realize
that we do not present a threat to society,
much less to the State.

cn.text: 在俄罗斯的卡户加
当局大规模搜查耶和华见证人的家
两名耶和华见证人
罗曼·马赫涅夫和德米特里·库津
因信仰被逮捕
我听到外面很吵闹
我往外走
看到两个蒙面的男子站在我家院子里
我拿钥匙开了门，发现院子里有不止两个人
我的女儿也出来了，她没有穿鞋
那些人命令她光着脚站在我旁边
站在石板地上
当时天下着雨，我请求让孩子先穿上鞋
一个人说：“等会儿”
罗曼·马赫涅夫虽然没有做出任何反抗
也没有任何攻击行为，却被当局铐了起来
与此同时，另一队执法人员闯入了
德米特里·库津和妻子斯韦特兰娜的家
我当时就在家里的这个房间给植物浇水
我听见丈夫开门进来
我就走出去，看到一群人
我也看见我丈夫趴在地上
他们肯定是趁我丈夫进门的时候
把他按倒在地的
他的双手也被铐在背后
另有一队武装警察
闯进了87岁的奥莉加·韦廖夫金的家
他们全都是穿着迷彩服的特种部队
也没有出示任何证件
他们说：“站起来！”
我说：“我站不起来，我身体不好。”
我的血压一下子升到了200/115
被搜查的人表示
那些书刊是执法人员偷偷放在他们家
要栽赃给他们的
他们的权利受到了侵犯
我听女儿喊道
“这些是从哪来的？我房间里根本没有这个！”
我听到丈夫说：“我们被栽赃了。”
那天下午，我刚刚打扫过床底下
那里什么都没有
他们没说自己是谁，也没有出示搜查令
他们从晚上9点钟就开始搜查
一直到了第二天凌晨4点半
这些武装警察竟然闯入
像我这样年老体弱的人的家
简直太过分了！
这些武装人员全体出动
带着面具，拿着武器
就为了对付一个年老体弱的老太太
真的很荒谬
这些人是有多害怕啊！
他们还声称自己是在对付一个极端主义分子
搜查结束后
马赫涅夫和库津被带到了联邦安全局
爸爸被带走的时候
我唯一能做的就是悄悄地对他说
我以你的忠贞榜样为荣
然后他们把他带走了
我很难过，我很害怕
罗曼被带到联邦安全局后
一直被他们铐在机房的暖气片上
铐了一夜
直到第二天早上，他被带去问话
就在几个小时前执法人员搜查的时候
马赫涅夫的身体出了状况
他们叫了救护车
罗曼的情况很危险，女儿开始大叫
联邦安全局叫的救护车很快就到了
他吃了药以后，才缓过来一些
罗曼26号被逮捕
一直到29号他们都没给他吃东西
他们三天都没有给罗曼·马赫涅夫吃东西
他们说：“他自己不会带吃的进来吗？”
这种说法真的很可笑
我已经为他的遭遇向很多机构提出申诉
6月28日，马赫涅夫和库津被逮捕两天后
卡卢斯基地方法院将他们送到拘留所
我希望人们能知道我爸爸不是坏人
他没有犯罪
我希望他很快就能回来
这样我们一家就能团聚了
耶和华见证人认为这些指控不符合事实
他们希望得到公正的裁决
不论最后的结果怎样
我们都会争取公正的裁决
我也会一直支持我的丈夫
我十分希望公众能够看清一个事实
也希望当局能够尽快意识到这个事实
也就是我们对社会没有危害
更不可能威胁政府

ko.text: 도저히 그 자매를 용서할 수 없다는 생각이 들었어요.
그리스도인이라면 어떻게 하는 게 옳은지 알고 있죠.
하지만 정말 그렇게 하는 건 쉽지 않아요.
그 기사는 어떻게 용서해야 하는지 알려 줬죠.
이 사람 저 사람에게 말하면 안 되었어요.
그리고 자매의 말도 잘 들어 줘야 했어요.

en.text: She said she had forgotten about our invitation.
This wasn’t the first time.
Why does she do this again and again?
I said in my heart that I could
never forgive her.
Will you forgive her?
Hm.
Of course I will.
A Christian usually knows the right thing to do.
But doing the right thing —that’s different.
I found what I needed.
I knew I would forgive my sister,
but the article reminded me how to handle it.
The three points were:
(1) Act promptly.
I couldn’t wait.
I needed to talk with her as soon as I could.
(2) I shouldn’t talk to others about it.
I must do it privately.
And (3) act peacefully.
Rather than accusing her,
I should simply express how I feel,
and I also need to listen patiently to my sister.
I needed to act right away.

cn.text: 她竟然说她忘了要来
这已经不是第一次了
她怎么老是这样？
我觉得
我永远都不会原谅她
没关系
我们原谅她吧
好吧
基督徒通常知道应该要怎么做
但要做到却很不容易
我找到了相关的资料
我知道我需要原谅我的姐妹
这篇文章提醒我该怎么做
有三点
一、尽快处理，不要拖延
我应该赶快找她谈
二、要跟她私下解决
我不应该跟其他人讲这件事
三、心平气和地跟对方谈
不是跟对方争论谁对谁错
而是应该把我心中的感觉说出来
也要耐心地听她说话
我现在知道该怎么做了！

titles.cn: “要穿上爱”

ko.text: 어릴 때부터 영적 목표를 갖게 되었습니다.
십 대 때 침례를 받고 정규 파이오니아를 시작했어요.
하지만 회중에서 나쁜 친구들을 사귀기 시작했고,
전 그런 부모님과 계속 살 수 없었죠.
전 집을 떠나 완전히 세상으로 나가 인생을 즐기기로 했습니다.
흥청거리고 술을 많이 마시면서 마음대로 살았어요.
마약에도 손을 댔고 부도덕한 생활을 했죠.
평일엔 일만 하다가 주말에 노는 게 제 삶의 전부였어요.
이건 내가 원했던 행복한 삶이 아니었습니다.
바로 여호와를 전 시간 섬길 때였어요.
반드시 의사한테 가야 한다는 걸 전 잘 알고 있었습니다.
뼈가 잘 붙도록 맞춰 주는 건 의사만 할 수 있는 일이죠.
저도 훈련받은 영적 의사인 장로들에게 가야 했어요.
장로들은 성경을 사용해 영적으로 치료해 주죠.
전 여호와께 돌아가기 위해 장로들을 찾아갔습니다.
집회에 입고 갈 만한 옷이 하나도 없어서,
부모님도 제가 올 줄 전혀 모르고 계셨어요.
절 정말 따뜻하고 친절하게 대해 줬습니다.
전 여호와의 징계가 최상의 유익을 준다는 걸 직접 경험했죠.
여호와께서는 제가 간절히 바라던 행복을 누리게 해 주셨고,
제가 상상도 못 했던 봉사의 특권도 주셨어요.
그분의 가장 중요한 특성인 사랑을 경험했죠.

en.text: I was raised in the truth
and had good spiritual examples in my family
that helped me to set goals at a young age.
I progressed to baptism in my teen years
and also started regular pioneering as a teenager.
But I started hanging around the wrong crowd
(inside the congregation first
and then bad association outside)
partying, drinking heavily,
living a double life.
I knew I couldn’t continue that and stay at home
because my parents were still serving Jehovah faithfully,
so I decided to move out
and go into the world 100 percent because I just wanted to have fun.
Well, with nothing holding me back,
the partying and the heavy drinking
led to experimenting with drugs and living an immoral lifestyle.
The lifestyle in the world was pretty much to work all week
and to party on the weekend, and that’s what we did.
But I eventually saw that that was just a vicious cycle.
Eventually, things got to the point where
I started having money problems—losing work.
I lost my license at one point, lost my apartment, couldn’t pay the rent.
And so I knew this was not the way to true happiness,
and I was miserable.
I thought back to the time when I was the happiest,
and that’s when I was serving Jehovah full-time.
And I wanted that back.
So I poured my heart out to Jehovah in prayer,
and I let him know that I wanted to return to him.
I knew from personal experience that if you break a bone,
such as your arm, you need help; you need to see a doctor.
Only they are qualified to fix it —set the bone right so it can heal.
I knew I had to seek out the elders
because they’re trained, spiritual doctors.
They know how to use the Scriptures to help you heal.
So I went to them because I wanted to return to Jehovah.
I didn’t even have dress clothes anymore; I had lost all that.
I just went back in jeans and a T-shirt.
My parents didn’t even know I was coming, but I showed up at the meeting anyway.
The elders, when I met with them, were so loving and kind and patient.
I’ve learned firsthand that Jehovah’s discipline is for the best.
Yeah, it’s true; it may hurt; it may sting initially.
But if we allow ourselves to be molded and trained by it,
it’ll always work out for the best.
I’m so glad that I made the decision to return to Jehovah.
Jehovah blessed me
with the happiness that I longed for and a lot more:
privileges of service I never would have imagined.
And I’ve experienced through Jehovah’s discipline
his greatest quality—love.
And I’ve never been happier.

cn.text: 我在耶和华见证人的家庭中长大
在我小的时候，父母就帮助我立下目标
我十几岁的时候就受浸，也开始做正规先驱
但是，我开始和会众里那些
不是那么爱上帝的人来往
之后也在外面交了坏朋友
我到处参加派对、喝得烂醉
过着表里不一的生活
我知道，如果我想继续过这样的生活
就不能住在家里
因为我父母都热心崇拜上帝
于是我决定搬出去
这样就可以随心所欲地生活
终于没有人管我了
我就成天酗酒、在外面混
最后开始吸毒，过不道德的生活
大部分人都是一到五拼命工作
周末拼命玩，我们也不例外
不过后来我发现
这样周复一周的循环真的让人感到空虚
后来，我的状况越来越糟
我丢了工作，经济出现问题
有一次驾照还被吊销
又因为付不起房租被赶走
我开始意识到这样的生活并不能给人快乐
我感到很痛苦
我想起过去做先驱的时候真的很快乐
很想再回到那样的生活
我向上帝祷告，告诉他所有的想法和感受
也跟他说我真的很想回到他身边
我曾经骨折，知道要恢复就一定要找医生
因为只有他们才能帮助你，让你的骨头复位
现在我需要长老的帮助
他们受过专门的训练
知道怎样用圣经帮助我修复与耶和华的关系
我想回到耶和华身边就一定要去找他们
我连一件适合聚会的衣服也没有
只好穿着T恤和牛仔裤去聚会
我去的那天，我的父母完全不知道我会去
长老们都很有爱心，也耐心、仁慈地待我
我真的感受到，耶和华的管教才是最好的
当然一开始，管教确实让人很难过
但如果我们接受来自上帝的管教
也愿意改变，就一定会有好结果
我很高兴我做了对的决定
回到耶和华身边
耶和华赐福给我
让我得到我最想要的快乐
甚至还给我从没想过的服务机会
耶和华的管教让我体会到他最伟大的特质
就是爱
我从来没有这么快乐过

titles.cn: 耶和华所爱的，他必管教

ko.text: 성서 연구생이 어떻게 침례받은 그리스도인으로 발전할 수 있습니까?
그 과정을 성공적으로 밟은 많은 분들의 이야기를 들어볼 것입니다.
때때로 성서 연구생들은 성경을 배워 가면서
삶에서 큰 변화를 해야 할 필요성을 깨닫는데,
여호와께 헌신하는 사람들이 느끼는 기쁨을 감동적으로 보여 줍니다.
차를 타고 여행할 계획을 한다고 상상해 보십시오.
필요한 게 다 있는데, 지도도 있고, 차도 준비됐고, 연료도 충분하죠.

여호와께서 용기를 주셔서 두려움을 극복할 수 있었습니다.
모두 합해 4년 가까운 시간을 감옥에서 보내야만 했습니다.
여호와께서 주시는 용기로 잘 이겨 낼 수 있었습니다.
그리고 이곳에서 다시 형제들을 만날 수 있었습니다.
어려움이 많이 있었지만 오늘 저는 너무 행복합니다.
이 대회에서 츠와어와 세나어로 「그리스어 성경」을 발표했습니다.
여호와여, 이 놀라운 선물을 주셔서 감사합니다.
츠와어로 여호와의 이름을 알려 줄 때, 꼭 이 성경을 사용할 거예요.
읽기도 쉽고, 가족 숭배에서 얻는 유익도 더 커질 것 같아요.
이 두 언어로 모잠비크에서 그리스어 「신세계역」이 처음 번역된 것입니다.
이 특별 지역 대회는 모잠비크의 18곳을 연결하여 진행되었고,
마푸토에서 열린 이 대회에서 침례를 받은 981명 중에
청소년들이 많이 있었다는 점이 화제가 되었습니다.
청소년들이 여호와를 알고 사랑하고 진정한 용기를 나타내도록
열심히 돕고 있다는 걸 알 수 있었습니다.
아프리카에서 특별 지역 대회를 조직하려면, 많은 노력이 들고 잘 계획해야 합니다.
하지만 분명 여호와께서는 이 특별 지역 대회를 축복하셨습니다.
대회는 모든 면에서 성공적이었고 대표자들은 매우 행복해했습니다!
여호와의 영이 함께한다는 걸 확실히 느낄 수 있었습니다.
모잠비크에서 금지령이 있기 전에 우리는 함께 왕국 노래를 불렀습니다.
그리고 이 대회에서도 대표단에게 왕국 노래를 불러 주고 있지요.
현지 형제 자매들과 함께 야외 봉사에 참여한 것을 꼽았습니다.
모잠비크 형제 자매들은 형편이 넉넉하지 않은데도
극진한 후대를 나타냈고 대표자들은 큰 감동을 받았습니다.
삶을 완전히 바꾸어 놓을 만한 경험을 했다고 말했습니다.
모잠비크 형제 자매들에게 중앙장로회가 그들을 사랑한다는 걸 알려 드리고 싶습니다.
더 중요한 것으로 여호와께서 그들을 알고 사랑하고 도와주십니다.
그 대회에서 침례를 받은 1685명의 형제 자매들 역시
침례받는 날만큼 특별한 날도 없을 텐데요,
이번 뮤직비디오에 그 감동이 고스란히 담겨 있습니다.
우리 각자가 여호와께 헌신할 때 갖게 되는
생각과 감정을 잘 표현한 아름다운 오리지널송이네요!
오늘 우리는 봉사에서 우리의 주된 목표가
그분께 헌신하고 침례를 받도록 돕는 것임을 배울 수 있었습니다.
침례를 받는 데 방해가 되는 것도 극복할 수 있다는 걸 배웠습니다.
침례가 인생의 전환점이 될 수 있다는 것을 보여 주었습니다.
또 어려움을 극복하고 침례를 받은 많은 사람들의 얘기를 들을 수 있었고,
그 특별한 날의 기쁨과 행복도 볼 수 있었습니다.
그리고 어릴 때 여호와께 헌신하기로 결정하면
기쁨과 여호와의 풍성한 축복을 평생토록 누릴 수 있다는 걸 알게 되었습니다.
마치기 전에 앙골라의 우리 형제 자매들을 만나 보겠습니다.
아름다운 이 나라는 매우 다양한 지형을 갖고 있습니다.
숨막히게 아름다운 칼란둘라 폭포가 이곳에 있습니다.
우리 형제들은 며칠이면 구역을 다 도는 루안다시에서부터
길이 험해서 걸어서만 갈 수 있는 외딴 지역에 이르기까지
이런 어려운 상황 속에서도 많은 사람이 진리를 받아들이고 있습니다.
앙골라에는 16만 명이 넘는 여호와의 증인이 있습니다.
그들은 72만 건이 넘는 성서 연구를 사회하고 있습니다.
따라서 숭배 장소가 정말 많이 필요합니다.
현재, 300개 이상의 왕국회관과 13개의 새로운 대회회관이 필요합니다.
앙골라에 있는 사랑하는 우리 형제 자매들이
여호와의 증인 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다!

en.text: Welcome to our program.
Our focus this month is baptism.
How does a person progress from Bible student
to baptized Christian?
We’ll hear from many
who successfully completed the journey.
Sometimes as students gain Bible knowledge,
they realize they need to make a major change in their life.
That was the case with this brother.
We’ll see how he met the challenge.
And our new music video beautifully shows the joy experienced
by those who dedicate their life to Jehovah.
This is the March 2020 edition of JW Broadcasting®.
Imagine for a moment
that you’re planning a road trip.
You have everything you need:
a map, a car, and plenty of fuel.
Before you start the engine, though,
you need to know your destination —wouldn’t you agree?
If you don’t know where you are trying to go,
you won’t know which road to take.
The same is true of our ministry,
which is, in a sense, like that road trip.
As Acts 13:48 shows, we’re always searching
for “those who [are] rightly disposed for everlasting life.”
We have everything we need for the journey,
including all the tools in our Teaching Toolbox.
But what would you say is our destination?
What’s the most important goal
that we are trying to accomplish in our ministry?
Is it placing literature?
directing people to jw.org®?
making return visits?
starting Bible studies?
educating people about the Bible?
or making disciples of Christ Jesus and baptizing them?
Each of those goals has value.
But which one is our primary goal?
What’s the destination that we want to reach?
Jesus identified it
at Matthew 28:19, 20.
There he said:
“Go, therefore, and make disciples
“of people of all the nations, baptizing them in the name
“of the Father and of the Son and of the holy spirit,
“teaching them to observe all the things
I have commanded you.”
Our destination, then, is a baptized disciple.
Each person we meet,
each piece of literature that we place,
each time we direct attention to the website,
each return visit we make,
each Bible study we conduct
—we should have the final goal
of making a baptized disciple.
Why is baptism essential?
Put simply, it’s because baptism
is necessary for salvation.
That’s what the Bible tells us
at 1 Peter 3:21:
“Baptism . . . is also now saving you
“(not by the removing of the filth of the flesh,
“but by the request to God for a good conscience),
through the resurrection of Jesus Christ.”
So from the time we meet an interested person,
we want to have our eyes on that goal
of making a baptized disciple.
In fact, the November 1977 Kingdom Ministry
made this statement regarding those we study with:
“Our discussions should reflect
“a genuine personal  interest in the student
“as a potential disciple and therefore
a potential brother or sister in the faith.”
If we don’t have that end-point
of a baptized disciple fixed firmly in mind,
we could end up stuck on side roads.
For example, watch this video,
and see if you can identify the problem that our brother has.
Are you going out in field service after lunch?
Yes, I’m going to be there, but I’ve got one return visit that I’ve got to make.
All right, see you.
See you.
My neighbor lost his job after 20 years,
and as a result, he’s got to move out of his house,
got to move into an apartment.
So I decided to go help him out a little bit
to pack up to make it a little easier for him to make that move.
You know, won’t it be nice at a time period
where we don’t have to worry about economic troubles like that?
Yeah, it will.
Uhm, you know, that’s why I’m so happy
that my grandchildren chose to go for higher education.
They both landed good jobs.
You know that bridge you cross when you come here.
You’ve noticed that they’re starting to do some work on it.
And that’s pretty extensive work.
They’re going to replace that whole bridge.
So according to the newspaper article,
it’s going to be like a six to eight month project.
Wow! That is a long time.
Uhm, you know, Chris,
the reason why I came by is I wanted to show you this magazine.
I love these. These are so well written.
Isaiah 48:17 is a key scripture here.
Notice what it says:
“I, Jehovah, am your God,
the One teaching you to benefit yourself.”
That’s familiar.
I think your dad read that to me once or twice.
How’s your dad doing anyway?
Doing good.
Ah, you know, they said they’ve got more Bible studies
than they can even cover in one week.
Well, well, you know, I can remember when you and your dad came here.
You were a little kid about this high,
and you just stayed right by his side.
And your dad was so proud.
You know, Chris, I know my dad had offered
to study the Bible with you in the past.
John, to be honest,
I’m too old to change;
I’m set in my ways now.
I think that God is just going to have to take me the way I am.
More chocolate?
Uhm, yeah. I don’t mind.
Could you identify with the brother in that video?
Have you ever had a return visit with someone
who just loves your company?
Perhaps you’ve been leaving literature with that person for months
—even years— and yet the person
has no genuine interest in progressing.
Why is that a problem?
Apparently, the person isn’t interested
in becoming a disciple of Christ Jesus.
Our time would be better spent searching for other people
who are “rightly disposed for everlasting life.”
Of course, that doesn’t mean that there’s no value
in placing literature or leaving contact cards
that direct people to jw.org.
These provisions are part of our Teaching Toolbox for a reason.
They can play a vital role in reaching the hearts
of those who are “rightly disposed.”
So continue to make good use of these tools
that Jehovah’s organization provides.
At the same time, never lose sight of your goal
to start Bible studies with interested ones
—and then the ultimate goal:
to “make disciples . . . , baptizing them.”
What about a person you’ve been studying with for years,
but the person isn’t making changes,
hasn’t stopped going to church,
and shows no real interest in attending Christian meetings?
Some people are glad to study the Bible with us
simply for the fact that they value Bible education.
And we love to teach people about the Bible.
But we have to remember that providing Bible education
for its own sake is not our primary goal.
In fact, it could be a side road.
The fact is,
some people who value Bible education
are not interested in becoming
baptized disciples of Jesus.
The world is full of Bible scholars
who are highly educated in the Bible
but who do not become disciples of Christ Jesus.
For example, one Bible scholar was educated
at a Bible institute, a religious college,
and a theological seminary.
He holds a doctorate in religious studies.
He has a thorough knowledge of Biblical Greek,
and he’s written 30 books about the Bible.
Yet, he describes himself
as an “agnostic atheist.”
So just providing Bible education
is not our primary goal.
We want people to build faith in God
and to have their own relationship with Jehovah
that will move them toward the destination
of dedication and baptism.
That’s why it’s important to honestly analyze
the progress of our Bible students.
Are they simply taking in knowledge?
Do they prepare in advance for the study?
Do they answer in their own words and from their heart?
Are they making changes in their life
to conform to what they’ve learned?
Are they attending and benefiting from Christian meetings?
If not, we may need to follow the advice
of the Kingdom Ministry of October 1988, which stated:
“If a student is not making meaningful progress
“after you have patiently aided him
“over a reasonable period of time,
“it may be best to use the time
“to better advantage searching for deserving ones.
“Depending on the circumstances,
it may be wise to discontinue the study.”
But why is it so important to be selective
about who we spend our time with?
Isn’t conducting an unproductive study
better than knocking on doors where no one is home
or where no one shows interest?
To answer that, let’s read Jesus’ words
at Matthew 10:11-13.
Now, when instructing his disciples
about how to conduct their ministry, Jesus said:
“Into whatever city or village you enter,
“search out who in it is deserving,
“and stay there until you leave.
“When you enter the house, greet the household.
“If the house is deserving,
“let the peace you wish it come upon it;
“but if it is not deserving,
let the peace from you return upon you.”
In harmony with those verses,
we want to focus our attention on deserving ones
as Jesus instructed,
people who are “rightly disposed for everlasting life.”
Obviously, there is a balance.
We need to be patient with those we call on and study with,
and not everyone progresses at the same rate.
But as we call on people and study with them,
we should never lose sight of our goal —our destination—
to “make disciples . . . , baptizing them.”
If we have that goal clearly in mind,
we’ll know when we are moving toward it,
and we’ll know when we are getting sidetracked.
We could illustrate it like this:
Think of a plane on a runway.
That plane is like a person you’ve visited
and you believe shows sincere interest in the Bible’s message.
Your short-term goal at this point
is to get them off the runway and into a Bible study.
If you do, that means the plane has taken off.
But once your study is airborne,
you have to keep your sights on your destination.
You can’t just stay in the air indefinitely.
Your goal is to make a baptized disciple.
If, in a reasonable amount of time,
the student isn’t progressing, what will you do?
To keep the study going would be like flying in circles.
In the same way, a Bible study
that’s simply suspended in the air goes nowhere.
We have to land the plane
—either at the destination of a baptized disciple
or at the termination of the study.
But what if something is holding your Bible student back
from the destination of baptism
—maybe an attachment to holiday celebrations
or an unclean habit, like smoking?
Notice how this issue arises in the following brief video.
When I started studying the Bible,
there were various factors that hindered my study.
I was a truck driver, and I was on the road a lot.
I had the worst kind of friendships,
and I smoked.
I smoked, on average, 60 cigarettes a day.
I realized that if I was going to make the needed adjustments,
I had to change my profession.
So I changed my job.
But if I wanted to get baptized, I had to stop smoking.
I cut down to two or three cigarettes a day.
One day, I bought a single cigarette.
I lit it, and I prayed to Jehovah.
I begged him to help me,
and he did help me
—so much so that I never smoked again.
And to this day, I don’t even have the urge to smoke.
Ten years after my first Bible study, I was baptized.
I’ve been serving Jehovah for 20 years now,
along with my wife and all my children.
Did you notice this man had to pray to Jehovah
to get the help he needed to overcome smoking?
In other words, he had to cultivate
his own relationship with Jehovah
in order to build the faith he needed to stop smoking.
In the same way, we need to help our students
to build their own relationship with Jehovah
so that they’ll also overcome any obstacles
that might hold them back from progressing to baptism.
But what if you’re not presently conducting a Bible study?
What if you’ve never had the privilege
of having one of your Bible students get baptized?
Does that mean your service to Jehovah is not valuable?
Not at all.
Remember, we each do our part in the ministry.
Do you remember what the apostle Paul said
at 1 Corinthians 3:6, 7:
“I planted, Apollos watered,
“but God kept making it grow,
“so that neither is the one who plants anything
“nor is the one who waters,
but God who makes it grow.”
So never feel that your efforts are unimportant.
Just as Paul said,
what’s accomplished in the ministry is a group effort.
When a person reaches baptism,
it isn’t just because of the effort
of the person who conducted the study.
The efforts of others played a role.
Perhaps someone else initiated that person’s interest
by placing literature or in some other way
giving a witness.
But remember what Paul said.
Jehovah is the one “who makes it grow.”
He is the one that is drawing to himself
those who are “rightly disposed for everlasting life.”
What a privilege we have
to be fellow workers with Jehovah
as we help people become disciples of Christ Jesus!
If we keep that goal clearly in mind,
how will it help us?
We won’t be content just to place literature
or just to direct interest to jw.org.
We won’t be satisfied
just making return visits or starting Bible studies.
We’ll always have in mind our primary destination
—making disciples of Christ
and baptizing them.
We of the Governing Body
wish you Jehovah’s rich blessing
as you work shoulder to shoulder with us
in helping “rightly disposed” ones
become baptized disciples of Jesus.
In our first video, we’ll hear from several brothers and sisters
about how they progressed to baptism.
We’ll learn answers to questions commonly asked about baptism:
What does it take to qualify?
What does one need to work on?
What’s the actual day of baptism like?
And what blessings can you expect after baptism?
I enjoyed associating
with Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Later, I also started to study the Bible.
I knew that I had to make
drastic changes in my life,
but my job prevented me from doing so.
So I asked myself,
‘What would I like to do with my life?’
I began studying the Bible again with the couple
and one month later
started attending meetings regularly.
Since our parents had stopped studying,
only three of us went to the meetings.
Jehovah can do a lot with you.
Jehovah could, you know,
your whole perspective can change.
I knew if I applied what I learned,
Jehovah would not let me down.
To strengthen my relationship with Jehovah,
I read the Bible daily and I pray.
My relationship with Jehovah
has gotten stronger.
When I pray now,
it feels like I’m talking to my close Friend.
Going out in service more—
I think it really helped me
to draw closer to Jehovah
and make the Kingdom feel real to me.
And so that’s why I wanted to get baptized.
What a great pleasure it was for me
when four months later
I could dedicate myself to Jehovah
and get baptized!
That made me so happy.
Today is a very, very special day for me,
because today I’m getting baptized.
At the regional convention, August 9, 2014,
it was a beautiful day.
Now, when I think about my three children
who got baptized today,
I feel my heart is full of joy,
and I really thank Jehovah!
Yeah, it’s not a day I don’t go thank Jehovah
for taking me out of the darkness.
If we are determined to be loyal to Jehovah
and we have the courage to remain chaste,
well, we won’t have any regrets.
To know that you have a heavenly Father
that cares about you
—that was the best feeling on earth.
I often think: ‘God, is it true? Is it real?
Do I really deserve to have all these blessings?’
All these blessings have helped me to see
that this life provides true satisfaction and true happiness.
The important quality
that Jehovah has taught me is love.
I felt that love from my family,
from Jehovah, and from my friends.
I learned that it’s OK to love people,
and that’s what you are supposed to do.
Working closely with Jehovah,
I really feel part of his family.
When you give your faith to Jehovah,
you’re giving your life to him.
He’s permitted these things to come upon me;
I knew that.
But he protected me.
When I meditate and think
about what Jehovah has done for me and Lei Lei,
I don’t have to be afraid.
Jehovah is my “secure refuge,”
because life may change, but Jehovah does not change.
Choosing to serve Jehovah
was the best decision I have made in my life.
What beautiful expressions!
Did you notice what helps a person qualify for baptism?
It’s studying the Bible, attending meetings,
having a share in the ministry, and praying.
It was obvious that these brothers and sisters
were so happy they had made the decision to get baptized.
For some, the road to baptism takes much effort.
But when that day comes,
it marks a turning point in their life.
We’ll see that in our next video.
I was born in Dalby, Queensland.
I’m the youngest of five children,
and my mother and father owned their own piggery.
So we lived on a little farm about ten minutes out of town.
When I was eight years old, my parents separated,
which came as a huge shock to me.
It was devastating, and the consequences just seemed to roll on for decades.
I would go and stay at the farm with my father for school holidays,
but my dad abused alcohol
and smoked cigarettes and used bad language.
So by the time I was a teenager,
I was doing exactly the same thing.
In my late teens, I was smoking marijuana every day
and I was spending up to four nights a week
at pubs and clubs and parties.
I was addicted to alcohol, cigarettes, marijuana,
and pornography, and I had no power to stop.
Obviously, it was only a matter of time
before that lifestyle affected my health.
I lost my social skills, and I became depressed.
The turning point in my life
came one afternoon when two
of Jehovah’s Witnesses knocked on my door.
Because of feeling so lost and so unhappy,
I had started to search for answers and I’d begun looking
at New Age teachings.
The timing felt too remarkable to be just coincidence.
I really felt like God wanted me to take the book.
I never looked at New Age teachings again.
I started to read the Greatest Man  book instead.
A major key for me to be able to make the necessary changes
was to cut off bad association.
I was baptized in March 1994.
When I finally took that step,
I felt like I’d started on the right path.
I was so grateful that Jehovah
had found me and that he’d drawn me.
I really fell in love with the thoughts of Psalm 8:1, 3, 4:
“O Jehovah . . . ,
“when I see your heavens,
“the works of your fingers,
“the moon and the stars that you have prepared,
“what is mortal man that you keep him in mind,
and the son of earthling man that you take care of him?”
I felt so insignificant,
and yet Jehovah knew me.
The hope of everlasting life also really touched my heart,
and so did Jehovah’s forgiveness.
I felt so grateful that Jehovah could forgive me
for all of my wrongdoing and that I could have a fresh start.
When we were invited to start circuit work,
I had serious doubts about my inadequacies.
I was not fast at preparing talks.
For me, it always felt like trying to fit
a square peg into a round hole.
But the very morning
after receiving our assignment to go in the circuit work full-time,
my Bible reading was Exodus chapters 3 and 4,
where Moses cited his inadequacies to Jehovah
—that he was not a fluent speaker.
Well, of course, Jehovah asked him,
‘Who is it that assigns a mouth?’
It was like Jehovah was saying to me:
‘Don’t worry. I will help you.’
To make the changes that I did in life,
I’m just so grateful to Jehovah.
Before I learned the truth, I was lost.
I didn’t know who I was.
I was just a mess.
I wanted to be a man,
but I didn’t really ever know how to do it.
Jehovah has rebuilt me from the ground up.
Jehovah has given me everything.
We can learn a lot from this experience.
Some people, like Andrew,
have lives filled with challenging problems.
Yet, by developing a relationship with God,
Andrew said,
“Jehovah has rebuilt me from the ground up.”
We saw that major changes
may be needed to make spiritual progress.
In Andrew’s case, he cut off bad association.
Finally, Andrew’s experience shows
that baptism isn’t the end of the journey.
He continued to grow spiritually.
But what if you’ve been raised as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses?
Are you thinking about getting baptized?
Have you made baptism your personal goal?
Getting baptized when you’re young
can lead to a life filled with rich blessings.
With that in mind,
I’m so happy to welcome today
a very dear friend of mine,
Brother Robert P. Johnson.
R. P., welcome to the program.
Thank you, Mark.
I appreciate being here.
Now, you’re here, R.P.,
because you are a wonderful example
of someone who’s had a life
filled with blessings in Jehovah’s service.
OK.
So I know that your family goes way back in the truth.
Yes.
In fact, I understand that your great grandfather
learned the truth in Brother Russell’s time,
even before 1914.
That’s right!
So that means you’re a fourth-generation Witness.
Mm-hm.
But now, like so many who are watching our program,
you were a little boy growing up in a congregation of Jehovah’s people.
So how did you come to the decision that you wanted
to dedicate your life to serve Jehovah and then get baptized?
Well, Mark, thinking back, I can identify
at least two outstanding influences in my life.
And the first was my parents.
Having that heritage in the truth helped me.
I was just an average kid in my early years.
But the parents instilled in me a desire
to please Jehovah and make it my life to do that.
They set goals before me.
They taught me the truth.
I learned enough from them to be able
to make a dedication to Jehovah God
and to have a close relationship with him.
And so early on, that’s what I did.
I remember that evening after supper
in my bedroom
praying to Jehovah to accept my dedication.
The date was May 25, 1949.
I was 11 years old at the time.
I told my parents, and they were happy,
but they just wanted me to wait longer to make sure
especially how I would handle the teenage years
and so on, so I waited.
And so then when did the moment come for you to finally get baptized?
It was at the 1953 international convention
in Yankee Stadium in New York
on July 22, 1953, when I was baptized.
And again, I remember that like it was yesterday.
When I came up out of the water,
I thanked Jehovah that finally,
“I am one of Jehovah’s Witnesses!”
and I also, like a child, added,
“You can bring the end anytime now.”
So you mentioned your parents, the good influence they had on you,
but was there another influence on you that helped you?
Yes.
At the 1953 convention, Brother Knorr had identified
that there would be a special program
for training people in the truth.
And from the congregation, there was a brother
of the anointed named Charles Richardson,
and my father asked Brother Richardson
to train me in this training program.
And Brother Richardson
was a mentor to me for the next five years of my life.
Over the years, he helped me
view the ministry as an opportunity
to help people develop a relationship with Jehovah
and, therefore, to reach out to them
in teaching them the truth —the doctrinal truth—
but to help them to see that Jehovah is a real person.
And he helped me to enjoy the ministry.
That is what has kept me happy
in Jehovah’s service down to this day.
Now, just from your expressions and what you talked about with me before,
I could see that this Brother Richardson
had a tremendous impact on your life.
And I think, R.P., it really made you
want to be a trainer of other people
because that’s how I first met you, right?
Right. Right.
You were the brother assigned to be my trainer
when I came to the Service Department.
I remember that fondly.
And I know that I’m not the only one.
I mean, you’ve really spent your whole life training other people.
Well, it’s been a privilege.
And I was trained; I was helped along the way.
I was nobody special, but Jehovah
has extended undeserved kindness to me
and made all these things possible.
So there’s no excuse for me not passing along the baton.
And it’s a delight for me to see others carry it.
So now, let’s come back.
You’re 15 years old.
You get baptized at Yankee Stadium,
and now as a result of being baptized at this age,
how do you feel you benefited?
For one thing,
if you know what you want to do and you stay focused on it,
it makes it easier to deal with whatever challenges come later.
And so being dedicated
and baptized early in life
helped me to stay focused on the truth.
I still remember that dedication.
It means something to me,
and I tried to make it mean something to others
(for as young as they can possibly make it).
And they’ll find the same thing I found:
Jehovah’s blessing will be with them.
So now, at 15,
what doors start to open up?
What opportunities come to you because you are a baptized brother?
At age 17, I was appointed as a ministerial servant.
I started pioneering right out of high school at age 18.
And serving where the need was greater,
I got a chance to work at starting a new congregation.
And so at 21,
I was congregation servant, or an elder, at that point.
Then there was a need:
The organization was looking for brothers who could do traveling work.
So at age 25, I had the privilege
of being a traveling overseer.
So now, how did you feel being an elder at 21?
being a circuit overseer at 25?
Was it a little bit overwhelming at such a young age?
I was scared.
I knew the truth,
but I was uncertain about myself,
but then I also knew Jehovah would help me.
I learned a lot as a young traveling overseer, and I thank Jehovah
that the people in the circuits that I served
endured those three years that I was with them.
But now, those were the challenges,
but what do you see as being the benefits of being a young traveling overseer?
For the congregation, they had somebody
who could stay out in field service long hours.
And also
the younger traveling overseer could relate
to the young people
and the younger adults in the congregation.
There were other benefits that even today different ones
that I served in earlier circuits bring forth to me.
For example, after having a good time in field service
and then the meetings, I would do recreational things with the kids.
And we ran track
out in the streets,
and we played board games,
softball, basketball,
and then we had good times just talking about the truth
and also talking
about how you can put your ministry first,
and there’s plenty of time for seeking a mate later.
So now, for a time, you were serving as a single brother,
but at some point, that changed.
When did that happen?
I have enjoyed the best of two worlds.
I enjoyed singleness and the blessings Jehovah gave me.
But when I was 28 years old,
I married a beautiful pioneer sister,
and I had already gotten adjusted in my circuit work.
This was my second circuit.
So, thanks to Jehovah,
we were able to be married, and to this day
Gracie and I continue in full-time service
after 52 years of marriage.
So R.P.,
you started with circuit work, and then later you went on to district work.
Right.
And then you were teaching the Kingdom Ministry School.
Mm-hm.
And then you got invited to Bethel.
Right.
And 31 years at Bethel, right?
Oh, yes.
And now you and Gracie are doing special pioneer work.
Right, in Orlando, Florida.
So you have more than 60 years of full-time service to Jehovah.
It’s because of Jehovah’s blessing,
and it’s made me happy.
So the question I want to ask you is:
When you’re looking back now to these 60 wonderful years
—more than 60 wonderful years—
what would you say to young people who are facing the same decision
that you faced when you were a little boy growing up in the truth?
It’s the best thing I could’ve done with my life,
and I had many opportunities.
Jehovah blessed my humble efforts
as he has blessed you and others too.
The young people today
have even more opportunities
because Jehovah’s organization under the leadership of Jesus Christ
is expanding and moving fast.
And, like Brother Richardson taught me,
if you just make yourself available,
then the organization
will find a place for you and use you,
and that’s so true today.
One of my greatest joys is to see the young people
take the baton and run with it,
and I have no regrets.
There’s been no challenge
that has overwhelmed me and made me regret things.
There were challenges, of course,
but with Jehovah’s help, well, I’m here today.
And that can be true of our young people.
So seize the opportunity while you’re young
and experience the blessing
that Jehovah gives those who serve him from youth onward.
R.P., it has been such a wonderful joy
to have you here on this program
and to hear about your life filled with joy,
your life filled with blessings,
all because of the decision you made just as a little boy
to dedicate your life to Jehovah and get baptized.
Thank you so much.
Thank you. I appreciate talking about it.
Baptism is always a special feature
of our conventions and assemblies.
We’ll see that in the following report on the special convention
held in Mozambique in 2018.
The Mozambique special convention
is truly outstanding
for so many different reasons.
One thing that has made this convention unique
is that we have so many courageous brothers
who have been in prison for their faith
from Angola, Korea, Malawi, Zimbabwe,
and from some of the countries in Europe
and who had to really stand up and set an example.
And to have them all here
with our courageous
Mozambican brothers
has made this
convention so special.
It is very encouraging
to be at this special convention.
We have spent ten years
in the “reeducation camps”
along with our brothers from Malawi, and we were at the same camp.
And today we are together at this special convention.
It’s very encouraging.
In 1990, I was judged and condemned
to 15 months of prison in Paris.
We were about 100 brothers in prison.
They tried to shame us,
but thanks to Jehovah, we had courage.
And today this beautiful convention
fills us with even more courage.
I was one of the brothers serving
as a bicycle courier during the ban,
delivering literature long distances.
It was difficult work because the police were searching for us.
Jehovah blessed us with courage, giving us a heart without fear.
Because of our Christian neutrality,
we were in prison.
Although it was a difficult time,
Jehovah gave us courage to endure,
and now we are here together.
We really thank Jehovah for that.
I was arrested and sentenced
to six years in prison.
Despite all these difficulties,
today I feel very happy.
I feel very encouraged.
At this convention, we released
the Greek Scriptures  in Tshwa and Sena.
Thank you very much, Jehovah,
for this wonderful provision.
I will surely use it
while speaking about Jehovah’s name
in Tshwa.
We are so happy to have
this Bible in the Tshwa language.
It’s easy to read, and it will improve our family worship.
Those were the first two local languages
in Mozambique to receive any part of the New World Translation.
So it was a very exciting day!
This convention was tied
in to 18 locations in Mozambique.
A total of 1,685 were baptized.
I have faith in Jehovah
and want to have
a close relationship with him.
Many have commented on the fact that among the 981
who were baptized in Maputo, there were many young ones.
And it just shows that the families here in Mozambique
are working very hard with their young ones
to help them to know Jehovah and love Jehovah
and to know what it means to be courageous.
To organize
a special convention
in Africa
requires a lot of work and a lot of planning.
But you can truly see the blessing of Jehovah here
because everything has gone so beautifully
and the delegates are so happy!
You can really feel that Jehovah’s spirit is with us.
Before the work was banned in Mozambique,
we used to sing to Jehovah.
At the camps, we continued to sing joyfully.
Now with the special convention,
we continue to sing to our delegates.
Many of the delegates commented that their favorite part
of the convention was going out in the ministry with the local brothers.
Even though the brothers may have very limited resources,
they showed them tremendous hospitality;
it made a huge impression.
Some of the delegates even said that when they go back,
this is going to have a life-changing effect on them.
We want to assure
these dear brothers and sisters
that the Governing Body loves them.
But greater than that, Jehovah God knows about them;
he loves them; he’s supporting them.
What a joyous occasion!
I’ll never forget it and, I trust, neither will
the 1,685 brothers and sisters
who were baptized at that convention.
There’s nothing like the day you’re baptized.
Our new music video
captures this in word and song.
In the quiet of the night, With a million stars above,
When I think of you and of all you do, It fills my heart with love.
If I give my life to you, You will always be my guide.
As the days go by, you will see that I Am forever on your side.
Because you gave me hope That changed my life
And strength to help me through,
Because you gave your Son To die for me,
I give my life to you; I give my life to you.
As the sun lights up the sky, Melting warm upon my skin,
How your endless days and your tender ways Stir these feelings deep within!
Because you gave me hope That changed my life
And strength to help me through,
Because you gave your Son To die for me,
I give my life to you; I give my life to you.
Because you gave me hope That changed my life
And strength to help me through,
Because you gave your Son To die for me,
I give my life to you; I give my life to you.
What a beautiful original song
about the thoughts and feelings we each have
when we dedicate our life to Jehovah!
Our program has focused on baptism.
We learned that our primary goal in the ministry
is to help people establish their own relationship
with Jehovah that moves them
to dedicate their life to him and be baptized.
We saw that with Jehovah’s help,
obstacles in the way of baptism can be removed.
Andrew’s experience showed us
that baptism can be
a turning point in one’s life.
We saw that making the decision
to dedicate your life to Jehovah when you’re young
can lead to a lifetime of joy
and rich blessings from Jehovah.
We heard from many who successfully made the journey to baptism
and saw the joy and happiness of that special day.
Before we close,
let’s visit our brothers and sisters in Angola.
The Republic of Angola is on the west coast of Africa.
This is a beautiful and geographically diverse land.
It’s home to the breathtaking Kalandula Falls.
The ministry here ranges from the city of Luanda,
where the territory is worked every few days,
to rugged and remote areas accessible
only by walking.
Angola’s population
of some 30 million people
includes many indigenous tribes and language groups.
About 45 percent of the population
is under the age of 15.
Angola has been recovering
from a civil war that lasted 27 years.
Despite the challenges, many are embracing the truth.
Angola is home
to more than 160,000 Jehovah’s Witnesses.
They’re conducting
over 720,000 Bible studies.
An average of 25 people
are baptized every day,
13 congregations are formed every month,
and an average
of 15 new circuits every year.
This has created a tremendous need for places of worship.
Currently, more than 300 new Kingdom Halls
and 13 new Assembly Halls are needed.
This is the Malueca Congregation in Luanda.
This beautiful Kingdom Hall was recently completed
and is already used by five congregations.
Our dear brothers and sisters in Angola
send you their love and greetings.
And, brothers and sisters,
we love you all very much.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting!
