is to feed us and to keep us awake spiritually and keep us alert.
And thinking about it, when that day comes
when Jesus brings destruction on this wicked system of things,
where do you want to be?
on a beach drinking a martini?
climbing a symbolic tree to get the last bit of fruit from this world?
Or do you want to be busy in Jehovah’s service,
whether it’s building and preaching and all the things we need to do?
We know the answer.
Yes, but to do that, we have to remain sober spiritually.
And one final point, if we look in the Insight  volume
under the heading “Soberness,”
there’s a very interesting point,
because Peter and Paul
used this expression in Greek.
And the Insight  volume makes this very interesting comment.
It says: “In keeping his senses,
“Timothy was to realize that Paul
would not be on the scene much longer.”
Then it says about Peter:
‘Peter likewise knew that he and his fellow apostles
would not be on hand much longer.’
Then it goes on to say:
“Knowing the seriousness of the times,
“with growing persecution from the world,
“they should be sound in mind, watchful, vigilant,
“and should not neglect serious prayer,
to obtain the strength they would need for endurance.”
Yes, the faithful slave has been serving us
with spiritual food for 100 years.
But, friends, remember,
the faithful slave will not always be here.
Soon will come the time when the remaining ones of the anointed
will be taken to have their reward.
Of course, Jehovah will continue to care for us.
He always has a provision in place to care for us.
But what is the important thing?
What is it that the faithful slave wants to convey to us?
Just the same as Paul and Peter
wanted to convey to those to whom they wrote,
we want to convey to you the importance of each one of us
being moderate in habits,
vigilant with regard to prayers,
keeping our senses, not being distracted by false stories,
and being alert to the time in which we’re living.
So we leave you with that question,
Are you sober?
Are you completely  sober?
Well, we certainly appreciate this sobering talk.
You will now be interested to hear what Brother Kenneth Cook
has to say on the topic
“Will You Care for It?”
Brother Cook, please.
We care for the things that are important to us, don’t we?
And there are many of such things.
For example, we care for our families,
we care for our friends, we care for our ministry,
and above all, we care for our worship of Jehovah.
And we do this faithfully to the very end.
When others need us, we’re there for them, as we’ve seen today.
During times of natural disasters, civil unrest,
and severe opposition to our work, we are there for one another.
In addition to all of that, our love must also, though,
be great enough to care for those
whom we try to reach in our public ministry.
In this, Jesus set the example for us.
We can feel his caring attitude in what he said
at Matthew 9:36-38.
So please follow along at Matthew 9:36.
It says: “On seeing the crowds,
“he felt pity for them,
“because they were skinned and thrown about
“like sheep without a shepherd.
“Then he said to his disciples:
“‘Yes, the harvest is great, but the workers are few.
“‘Therefore, beg the Master of the harvest
to send out workers into his harvest.’”
Jesus felt pity for the people, didn’t he?
What does pity mean in this case?
The pity mentioned here stems from heartfelt love.
He loved the people. We love people.
It’s a tender feeling toward persons
in a state of need or suffering.
Like Jesus, our love for others
must include genuine care for them —even pity for them—
so that we’re moved to help them,
hoping that they respond to God’s Word
and will desire to do Jehovah’s will.
And we must do this because caring for others
is an important part of following the Christ, right?
In a few minutes, we will look at how we can remain focused
on compassionately carrying out our ministry
and helping people to dedicate their lives to God.
And this will include revealing what our yeartext is for 2020.
So as Brother Lett said earlier, “Stay tuned.”
Before we get to that, though,
we’ll draw out some Bible principles from long ago
that will help us today in caring for the people
that we must yet reach in this important ministry, or work.
Since ancient times,
Jehovah has taught his people how to care for others.
In fact, the Israelites were told to show consideration
even for the animals under their care.
For instance, when they were about to leave Egypt,
Jehovah gave them this command
at Exodus 12:5, 6.
Please follow along.
Now, here is the setting:
Jehovah gives instructions about selecting the Passover sacrifice.
Verse 3 tells us that the Israelites
were to select the sheep on the tenth of the month.
With this in mind, notice what verse 5 states:
“Your sheep should be a sound, one-year-old male.
“You may choose from the young rams or from the goats.
“You must care for it
“until the 14th day of this month,
“and the whole congregation of the assembly of Israel
must slaughter it at twilight.”
Why was it important for them
to not only select the sheep
but to “care for it until the 14th”?
To answer that question, let’s draw out two principles
that we will then apply to our ministry
—and they do apply.
First, we know that the sacrificial sheep
needed to remain unblemished
to be acceptable to Jehovah.
Verse 5 said: “Your sheep should be a sound, one-year-old male.”
If an Israelite selected a sound sheep
but then neglected it and the sheep was injured in some way,
that sheep would no longer be
acceptable to Jehovah for sacrifice.
The principle:
Keep the sacrifice acceptable.
Don’t neglect it just because the end is close,
and we can apply that principle to our ministry.
Now, principle number two:
We can also be certain that a measure of compassion
was involved in what Jehovah told them there.
In this case, the sacrificial sheep was no less important
just because its time, so to speak, was short.
See, as we’ll see in this discussion,
this too can apply to our ministry.
And we’re wise to remember these principles.
Fittingly, it is Jehovah who sets the example for us
in showing compassion
and caring for what is important to the very end.
Foremost in this is how Jehovah cared for Jesus
right up to the end of his earthly ministry.
For instance, Jehovah showed his support for Jesus
by answering Jesus’ prayers.
At one point, Jesus even said:
“Father, I thank you that you have heard me.”
Also, Jehovah voiced his support for Jesus.
At his baptism, Jesus heard Jehovah speak from heaven,
stating: “This is my Son, the beloved,
whom I have approved.”
Imagine how that encouraged him!
And then later, as Jesus was in agony
during the hours before his death,
an angel of God comforted Jesus,
and no doubt that angel was a friend whom Jesus knew well.
Yes, from the beginning to the very end,
Jehovah cared for Jesus, the sacrificial “Lamb of God.”
We benefit when we apply such principles
to what we have been given to do today.
For instance, the time is short, yes.
Yet, our public ministry is no less important now
just because the end is close.
In fact, it’s even more important
that we continue caring for this ministry
as the end approaches.
We must care for this “sacrifice of praise”
to our heavenly Father right up to the end
—that is, right up to the time when Jehovah makes it clear
that this part of our service to him has come to an end.
Until that time,
what should be the focus of our public ministry?
Jesus stated what it should be
at Matthew 28:18-20,
so please go to those verses.
Now, starting at Matthew 28:18,
it says:
“Jesus approached and spoke to them, saying:
“‘All authority has been given me in heaven and on the earth.
“‘Go, therefore, and make disciples of people of all the nations,
“‘baptizing them in the name of the Father
“‘and of the Son and of the holy spirit,
“‘teaching them to observe all the things I have commanded you.
“‘And look! I am with you all the days
until the conclusion of the system of things.’”
So now, with these words of Jesus in mind,
what should be the focus of our public ministry?
Well, the focus must be to ‘make disciples of Christ
‘among people of all the nations,
teaching them and baptizing them,’ as Jesus stated.
Notice that Jesus’ statement was more than just a command.
He didn’t start off saying: “I command you! Go!”—right?
Rather, Jesus said:
“All authority has been given me . . . Go, therefore.”
Jesus’ true disciples would see beyond the command
embedded in those words and go forth with conviction.
Why?
Because they would know that Jesus was empowered, authorized,
to oversee this great work
that they were now commissioned to do.
He would be with them, and he is with us today.
We’re absolutely confident of that fact.
In view of that, how can we help our Bible students
so that even more of them become baptized disciples,
as Jesus there directed?
This is important to consider because,
while many get baptized each year,
our yearly baptism figures have remained
at about the same level for some time.
Now, are these good figures?
Yes, they are.
Absolutely!
But what can we do to help even more people
take this vital step before the end comes?
To answer that question,
let’s briefly consider four ways to reach the heart.
There’s much that we can do, but we’ll just consider four ways here.
We do it through what we emphasize about Jehovah,
what we teach our students about prayer,
how we help them get to meetings,
and how we help them handle problems.
Let’s consider that first way:
We reach the heart through what we emphasize about Jehovah.
Our goal is to help our students see
that Jehovah cares for them.
He cares about them. He loves them deeply.
As we use our publications
(such as the Teach Us  book) with our students,
we should prepare well
and highlight the Scriptural answers to questions such as:
Does God care about us?
How does God feel when people suffer?
Is it possible to be Jehovah’s friend?
Discuss the answers,
draw out the meaning that brings us joy
and identify the principles that improve our life,
and help the student to grow ever closer to Jehovah.
Now the second way:
We reach the heart through what we teach our students about prayer.
Show him or her how to pray properly,
with meaning and from the heart,
as we pray with them at each study session.
Explain that in our private prayers
we can really open up to Jehovah
and express feelings that we might not share with other humans.
We can also ask for God’s help
to love only what he loves.
Why can we do this with confidence?
Because Jehovah cares for us,
and we should make that very clear as we teach our Bible students.
Next, the third way:
We reach the heart through how we help our students get to meetings.
Invite your Bible student to attend meetings as soon as possible.
What a student sees at our meetings
may touch his heart and help him to progress.
Very early on, show the video
What Happens at a Kingdom Hall?
Then warmly invite him to attend with you; appeal to him.
Also, offer transportation if it is needed.
I really appreciated getting a ride to the first meeting that I attended,
and I still remember it.
Finally, the fourth way:
We reach the heart through how we help our students handle problems,
including problems that may develop
if someone offends him or her.
This is all part of reaching the heart
and preparing and helping them.
Our Bible students need to experience Jehovah’s love
as they benefit from applying Bible principles.
See, this helps them to know Jehovah better.
To help them, show your students how to use tools
such as the JW Library® app,
the Research Guide for Jehovah’s Witnesses,
and jw.org®.
When our students are trained to search for answers before baptism,
they will be better prepared to handle problems
and get along with others.
When we do these things for our Bible students,
we show that we are really caring
for what Jehovah has entrusted to us.
Both Jehovah and his Son desire
that we help as many people to the point of dedication and baptism
while there’s still time.
To succeed,
don’t spend time conducting an unproductive study.
Rather, focus on “those who [are] rightly disposed for everlasting life,”
and care for them with Jehovah’s blessing on your efforts.
So, then, with all of this in mind, what is our yeartext for 2020?
It is taken from Matthew 28:19:
“Go, therefore, and make disciples . . . , baptizing them.”
Now, for those of you who listened to Alexa earlier in the program
or read your daily text for today,
you know that this is also the Scripture text for today,
October 5, 2019.
That’s just a coincidence.
Don’t expect it next year.
Now, with that text in mind,
keep putting your heart into your ministry
and into helping people,
and be certain to take care of this ministry
with those principles we considered
to the very end.
Thank you very much, Brother Cook, for your presentation.
Looking back on the program that we were able to enjoy,
we certainly felt encouraged by being reminded
that we have no human leader
but that it is Jesus who is our Leader.
Remember what it says at Matthew 23:10:
“Neither be called leaders,
for your Leader is one, the Christ.”
We enjoyed also listening to Brother Stephen Lett,
who emphasized that our relief ministry
is overseen and directed by Jehovah.
I’m sure that you also enjoyed the four videos.
The first one was entitled
‘The Good Hand of Our God Is Upon Us . . . Let Us Get Up and Build.’
The next video provided a historical look
at property acquisitions,
followed by another video related
to the new construction project that is being planned.
The fourth video was about the new application
for processing applications,
followed by a presentation
on a new way to access
jw.org® audio files.
After that, we enjoyed the Scriptural discussion,
“An Attack Coming From the North,”
presented by Brother David Splane of the Governing Body.
And Brother Samuel Herd next encouraged us
to study the Bible with a Study Bible.
And how we appreciate the Study Bible!
After singing a song together and listening to greetings
from brothers in other places and countries,
Brother Anthony Morris reminded us
that we have work to do.
As indicated in the news media, there are increasing problems in the world.
In certain areas, we can also see
increasing hostility against God’s people.
Brother Mark Sanderson of the Governing Body
showed that we do not have to be fearful
because the Almighty is on our side.
Next, we heard the talk
by Brother Geoffrey Jackson,
“Are You Completely Sober?”
We are if we keep our senses.
And finally, Brother Kenneth Cook
of the Governing Body raised the question
“Will You Care for It?”
Brother Cook reviewed how Jehovah cared for Jesus,
the sacrificial Lamb of God,
until the very end of his life on earth.
Likewise, in harmony with the 2020 yeartext
that’s taken from Matthew 28:19,
he highlighted how we must care for our ministry
and our “sacrifice of praise” until the very end.
This includes our efforts to help ‘those who are rightly disposed’
to dedicate their life to Jehovah and to get baptized.
Well, we have had an encouraging time together, haven’t we?
Well, we enjoyed the various videos and also the video presentations,
and we all benefited from the Scriptural talks
delivered by members of the Governing Body.
And then we also appreciate the discussion
on the yeartext for the coming year:
“Go, therefore, and make disciples . . . , baptizing them.”

有正确态度的人献身给耶和华
受浸成为基督徒
我们都从这些节目受到很大的鼓励，对吗？
年会播放的所有短片，我们都非常喜欢
我们也从中央长老团的弟兄
发表的演讲学到很多
最后，很高兴知道
2020年的全年经文就是
所以你们要去
使所有国族的人做我的门徒
为他们施浸

titles.cn: 2019年年会——演讲和2020年全年经文

ko.text: 여러분이 좋아하는 과일을 먹고 있다고 상상해 보시죠.
아삭한 배와 사과가 식탁에 놓여 있습니다.
맛도 좋고 향도 좋고 몸에도 좋습니다.
사실 그 씨는 창조주에 관해 많은 것을 밝혀 줍니다.
고린도 후서 9장을 보면 그 점을 잘 알 수 있는데
함께 성경을 펴서 고린도 후서 9:8-15을 살펴보도록 하시죠.
오늘은 특히 여호와의 놀라운 성품 한 가지를 살펴볼 것입니다.
여호와께서는 우리가 맛있고 몸에 좋은 음식을 즐기기를 원하십니다.
단지 오늘만이 아니라 앞으로도 계속 즐기기를 원하시죠.
또 우리의 후손들도 그러한 좋은 것들을 계속
만약 우리가 과일 하나에 들어 있는 모든 씨앗을 심는다면
혼자선 다 먹지도 못할 만큼 많은 과일을 얻게 될 것입니다.
하나의 수박에는 적게 잡아도 200개의 씨앗이 있고
각 덩굴에는 적게 잡아도 2통의 수박이 열립니다.
혼자서 한 철 내내 아무리 먹어도 다 먹을 수 없는 양입니다.
이제 고린도 후서 9장을 함께 살펴보도록 하겠습니다.
여기서 우리는 이 중요한 표현이 무엇을 가리키는지
여호와의 과분한 친절의 의미와 목적에 대해 살펴보도록 하시죠.
또 씨에 대해 좀 더 생각해 보고
이 모든 것이 우리의 숭배와 어떻게 관련이 있는지 알아볼 것입니다.
자신의 모든 과분한 친절이 여러분에게 넘치게 하실 수 있습니다.
그리하여 여러분은 항상 모든 면에서 부족한 것이 없고,
모든 선한 일을 하는 데 필요한 것을 넉넉히 갖게 됩니다.”
네, 우선 과분한 친절이라는 표현을 생각해 보시죠.
그 뜻을 정확하게 번역하는 것은 정말 어렵습니다.
이 단어는 “당신은 이것을 받을 만한 자격이 전혀 없지만
내가 어쨌든 베풀어 주는 겁니다” 라는 식으로
받는 사람이 얼마나 부족한지를 설명하는 단어가 아닙니다.
오히려 주는 분이 얼마나 훌륭한지에 초점을 맞추는 말이죠.
우리가 먼저 그분께 뭔가를 드렸기 때문이 아닙니다.
그분이 우리에게 주셔야 할 의무가 있는 것도 아니죠.
우리가 보답해 드릴 수 있는 것보다 훨씬 더 기꺼이 주시는 분입니다.
그것이 바로 과분한 친절이라는 단어의 핵심이며,
“성경 용어 설명”을 보면 그 점을 확인할 수 있습니다.
사람들에게 기적을 통해 선한 것을 풍부히 주실 수 있습니다.
하지만 훨씬 더 좋은 방법을 택하셨죠.
그분은 자신의 관대함을 나타내는 데 우리를 사용하십니다.
우리가 불완전하지만 그 일에 최대한 참여할 수 있게 해 주시죠.
그렇게 할 때 우리가 행복해진다는 걸 아시기 때문입니다.
우리가 여호와와 사람들에 대해 어떻게 생각하는지를 보여 줄 기회가 되며
그처럼 사랑을 나타낼 때 우리는 여호와와 더 가까워지고
그 모든 점이 8절에 어떻게 잘 설명되어 있는지 유의해 보시죠.
항상 모든 면에서 부족한 것이 없고,
모든 선한 일을 하는 데 필요한 것을 넉넉히 갖게 됩니다.”
널리 나누어 주고 가난한 사람들에게 주었으니,
그 의는 영원히 계속된다’라고 [시편 112:9에] 기록된 것과 같습니다.”
이 성구에서 무엇을 알 수 있습니까?
그분의 종들은 다른 사람에게 의로운 행동으로 나누어 줄 수 있을 만큼
필요한 것을 언제나 넉넉히 갖게 될 것임을 알 수 있지 않습니까?
그 점이 이 성구에서 알려 주는 교훈입니다!
따라서 우리 모두는 이렇게 자문해 보아야 합니다.
즉 여호와께서 관대한 사람이 의로운 행동을 하게 도와주시기 때문에
그에게 아무것도 부족하지 않을 것임을 믿고 있는가?
여호와께서 그의 의로운 행동이 영원히 계속되도록
과분한 친절로 넘치게 보상해 주실 것임을 믿고 있는가?’
우리가 먹는 과일에 하느님의 관대함이 어떻게 나타나 있는지
만약 우리가 과일 하나에 담긴 씨앗을 모두 심는다면
혼자서는 다 먹을 수 없을 만큼 많은 과일을 얻을 수 있습니다.
여러분에게 뿌릴 씨를 주시고 불어나게 하시며
여러분의 의의 소출을 늘려 주실 것입니다.)
여러분은 모든 면에서 부유해져서 온갖 관대함을 나타내게 될 것이며,
우리를 통해 그 관대함이 전해질 때
그러면 여호와께서는 왜 그토록 풍부하게 베풀어 주십니까?
우리도 관대하게 베풀 수 있도록 하시려는 것입니다.
관대함을 나타내는 건 믿음과 사랑의 행동이죠.
우리의 숭배의 일부라고 할 수 있는 이유는 무엇입니까?
사람들이 하느님께 감사를 드리게 될 것”이라고 알려 줍니다.
우리가 관대함을 나타내면 사람들은 기도를 하게 되죠.
“이 봉사 활동은 거룩한 자들의 필요를 채워 줄 뿐 아니라,
하느님께 드리는 많은 감사가 풍성해지게 하기 때문입니다.”
연례 총회 때 우리는 조직이 지난 두 봉사 연도에 걸쳐
구호 활동에 거의 5000만 달러를 사용했다는 것을 알게 되었습니다.
또한 형제들의 집이 복구되기 전과 후의 모습을 사진으로 보았습니다.
형제들이 잘 보살핌을 받고 있다는 사실을 알고 정말 기뻤죠.
그 봉사를 통해 많은 사람이 여호와께 감사를 드리게 됩니다.
“이 구호 봉사 활동이 제시하는 증거로 인해
그들과 모든 사람에게 관대하게 기부하기 때문입니다.
하느님께서 여러분에게 베푸신 탁월한 과분한 친절 때문에
이루 말할 수 없는 선물을 주시는 하느님께 감사합니다.”
이 선물 즉 그분의 과분한 친절은
우리가 상상하거나 보답해 드릴 수 있는 것 이상으로 관대하게 베푸시는
그 선물 덕분에 우리는 계속해서 주는 사람이 될 수 있습니다.
여러분이 나타내는 관대함 덕분에 매일같이 수많은 사람들이
그 덕분에 형제 사랑이 더욱 강해집니다.
그럼 우리가 관대하게 줄 수 있는 이유는 무엇입니까?
다른 사람을 위해 사용할 시간, 활력, 자원, 아이디어, 의욕, 사랑,
여호와의 과분한 친절 덕분에 갖게 된 것이죠.
또한 그것은 오늘의 성구에서 알려 주는 것처럼
우리가 주의 손에서 받은 것을 드렸을 뿐입니다.”
기꺼이 베푸시는 그분의 성품에 관해 중요한 점을 배웠습니다.
우리는 그분의 약속을 신뢰했고 그분의 선한 특성을 본받았으며
이것이 바로 여호와의 조직이 운영되는 방식입니다.
그분이 계속해서 풍부히 축복해 주시기를 바랍니다.

en.text: Imagine that you’re eating
your favorite fruit
—a cool, crisp watermelon;
a fragrant peach;
a juicy pear; or that apple
in front of you at the breakfast table—
refreshing, distinctive, nutritious.
And then you get to the seed.
Most people consider that to be a waste product,
and yet that seed tells us
much about our Creator.
It’s revealed for us
in 2 Corinthians chapter 9.
Please turn there, and we’re going to consider together verses 8-15.
Jehovah has a remarkable quality
that we want to discuss today.
Jehovah wants us to enjoy
good, delicious food today.
But not only that, he wants us to enjoy it again and again and again.
And he wants all of our offspring
to enjoy these good things again and again.
And if you were to plant all of the seeds
in one piece of fruit,
you would yield more than you could possibly eat by yourself.
By conservative estimates, one watermelon contains 200 seeds
and each seed produces a vine
and each vine produces,
by conservative estimates, two fruits.
So you would have
with just the seeds of one melon
400 more watermelons,
far more than you could eat by yourself in one season.
And there’s a good reason for that.
Now as we look at 2 Corinthians chapter 9,
we want to examine this passage carefully.
Verse 8 begins with an important expression
that we need to understand clearly:
God’s “undeserved kindness.”
So let’s read verse 8, then we’ll define the term,
then we’ll discuss the purpose of Jehovah’s undeserved kindness
(and eventually, we’ll get around to watermelons),
and we’ll come to understand what all of this has to do with our worship.
Second Corinthians 9:8:
“Moreover, God is able to cause
“all his undeserved kindness
“to abound toward you
“so that you are always completely
“self-sufficient in everything,
“as well as having plenty
for every good work.”
Now, first, that expression “undeserved kindness”
—do you have a clear understanding of that term?
It’s difficult to translate perfectly in English.
It’s not an expression of judgment, as if to say,
“You are nowhere close to deserving this, but I’m going to provide it anyway.”
No. That’s not the concept at all.
The term is describing not the recipient
but the giver.
Jehovah is ready to give.
That is his disposition.
You didn’t pay him first.
He is disposed to share himself
—his generous, good, loving, kind qualities—
not because you earned it and obligated him,
but because that is who he is.
He is great, and yet he is humble and willing
to give in ways grander
than we could ever imagine or repay.
That is what undeserved kindness means.
And you’ll find the essence of that definition
in your “Glossary of Bible Terms.”
Now, Jehovah could just miraculously endow
people with an abundance of good things,
as he did in the garden of Eden or as he did with the manna provision,
but he does something even better.
He allows his friends to participate
in showing this quality of his to the extent
that we can within the limitations of our human imperfection,
and he does that because he knows it makes us happy.
“There is more happiness in giving than there is in receiving”
because it gives us the opportunity to show
how we feel about Jehovah and about people
and because our showing love
draws us closer to Jehovah
and strengthens the bonds of our worldwide brotherhood.
Now notice how all of this is borne out in that verse:
“God is able to cause
“all of his undeserved kindness to abound
“toward you so that you are
“always completely self-sufficient in everything,
as well as having plenty for every good work.”
And verse 9 says: “(Just as it is written
“[at Psalm 112:9]:
“‘He [that is, the generous person who fears Jehovah]
“‘has distributed widely; he has given to the poor.
His righteousness continues forever.’)”
So are these verses suggesting
that Jehovah’s undeserved kindness is so great
that his servants will always have enough for themselves
and plenty to share with others
as acts of righteousness?
Yes, that is exactly
what these verses are teaching us!
The question I need to ask myself is:
‘Do I thoroughly believe that?
‘Do I believe that a generous person
‘suffers no loss
‘because Jehovah enables him to do righteous deeds?
‘because Jehovah more than makes up for it
‘with his undeserved kindness so that those acts of righteousness
may continue forever?’
Remember the evidence
in every fruit
and vegetable that you eat.
God puts a seed in each one.
And if you were to plant all the seeds found in one fruit,
you would have more than you could possibly eat by yourself.
Verses 10 and 11 use this exact illustration:
“(Now the One who abundantly supplies seed to the sower
“and bread for eating will supply and multiply
“the seed for you to sow and will increase the harvest
“of your righteousness.)
“In everything you are being enriched
“for every sort of generosity,
“which produces through us
an expression of thanks to God.”
Beautiful verses.
So why does Jehovah provide so bountifully?
So that (the words of verse 8) you and I can be generous.
Clearly, generosity is an act of faith and love.
But why can it be said that generosity
is also an expression of worship?
Well, look at how verse 11 continues:
“Generosity . . . produces through us
an expression of thanks to God.”
Think of it.
Your generosity causes prayer,
which is worship.
And not only that, verse 12 continues:
“Because the ministry of this public service is not only to provide well
“for the needs of the holy ones but also to be rich
in many expressions of thanks to God.”
At the annual meeting, we learned about the almost $50 million (U.S.)
that our organization just spent on disaster relief
during the last two service years.
And we saw before and after photos
of the homes of some of our brothers.
We were pleased to note that our brothers
are well cared for.
And verse 12 calls that work a “ministry.”
It is sacred service, and, as such,
it results in many expressions of thanks to Jehovah.
And verse 13 continues: “Through the proof
“that this relief ministry gives,
“they glorify God because you
are submissive to the good news about the Christ.”
Yes, you are real Christians.
You live what you believe “as you publicly declared,
“and because you are generous in your contribution to them and to all.
“And with supplication for you, they express affection for you
“because of the surpassing undeserved kindness of God upon you.
“Thanks be to God
for his indescribable free gift”
—that is to say, his undeserved kindness,
his disposition
to be generous beyond our imagination or ability to repay.
That is the gift that enables us
to keep giving.
Each day, millions of prayers of gratitude
ascend to Jehovah for your generosity.
That strengthens the bonds of our brotherhood.
Now, how are you able to be generous?
Where did you get the time, the energy,
the resources, the idea, the motivation,
the love, the opportunity to give of yourself in this way?
Jehovah gave us these things through his undeserved kindness.
And when you support Kingdom work, you help those in need.
And Jehovah is worshipped,
as the words of our day’s text say at 1 Chronicles 29:14:
‘Everything is from Jehovah, and we have given
to him what comes from his own hand.’
You have drawn the right conclusion
from Jehovah’s undeserved kindness,
from his disposition to give freely.
You have trusted in his promise;
you have imitated his goodness;
you are participating in his happiness.
This is how Jehovah’s organization functions.
May Jehovah continue to bless you richly
for your participation in that.

cn.text: 想象一下，你正在吃你最喜欢的水果
可能是冰凉爽口的西瓜
香甜的水蜜桃
多汁的梨或是摆在你眼前的苹果
很好吃又有营养
吃了会让你神清气爽
吃完后你会看到种子
很多人都觉得种子是要丢掉的
但其实这个种子
透露了很多关于创造主的事
我们可以从哥林多后书第9章
知道种子透露了什么事
请打开圣经，我们看看8-15节
我们今天会讨论耶和华的一个杰出特质
耶和华希望我们可以享受美味又健康的食物
而且不只享受一次
他还希望我们总是能吃到这样的食物
他也希望我们的子孙后代
都可以享用这些美食
如果你把一个水果里的种子都拿去种的话
你收获的水果会比你能吃掉的还多
保守估计，一颗西瓜有200粒种子
每粒种子会长出一条西瓜藤
每条西瓜藤最少会长两颗西瓜
所以如果你把一颗西瓜的种子都拿去种
最少就会结出400颗西瓜
这比你在一个夏天所吃的西瓜还多很多
从这件事我们可以看出什么呢？
现在来看看哥林多后书第9章
我们会仔细地讨论这里的经文
先从第8节开始
这里有一个很重要的词语
我们要清楚了解
就是上帝的“分外恩典”
我们先念第8节，然后解释这个词语
再讨论耶和华为什么赐给我们分外恩典
接着我们再回来讨论西瓜
最后我们就会知道这些事
跟我们的崇拜有什么关系
哥林多后书9:8说
“此外，上帝能把一切分外恩典
厚赐给你们
使你们样样充足，时刻一无所缺
能做各种善事。”
经文谈到“分外恩典”
那么“分外恩典”到底是什么意思呢？
英语其实很难把这个词的意思完全翻译出来
这个词并没有评判一个人的意思
并不是说
“你根本就不配得到这个福分
但我还是会给你”
事实上，“分外恩典”完全没有这样的意思
“分外恩典”说的不是接受而是施与
耶和华很乐意向人施与
他就是这样的上帝
你不用先为他付出什么
他也会很乐意向你表现
慷慨、良善、爱心、仁慈
这不是因为你做了什么所以上帝要奖赏你
而是因为他就是这样一位伟大的上帝
但他又很谦卑，也愿意施与
他的慷慨远远超过我们的想象
也是我们报答不了的
这就是分外恩典的意思了
你可以在圣经后面的词语解释找到它的定义
其实耶和华
只要行个奇迹就能给人很多好东西
像他以前在伊甸园和旷野所做的一样
不过，他希望我们得到更好的东西
他让我们跟他一起表现慷慨
虽然我们不完美，但他让我们跟他一起工作
尽己所能对人慷慨
因为他知道慷慨会让我们快乐
“施与比接受更快乐”
向人施与让我们有机会
表现对上帝和对别人的爱
我们对人表现爱心
可以使我们跟耶和华更亲近
也跟全球的弟兄姐妹更团结
现在，我们再回来看看哥林多后书第9章
第8节说
“上帝能把一切分外恩典厚赐给你们
使你们样样充足，时刻一无所缺
能做各种善事。”
第9节说
“圣经上写着［就是指诗篇112:9］
他［也就是敬畏耶和华的人］慷慨施与
救济穷人。他的正义永远长存。”
这两节经文是不是说
耶和华的分外恩典一定会使你们一无所缺
样样充足，让你们有足够的东西可以
对人表现慷慨，显出正义呢？
没错！
这两节经文说的就是这个意思！
不过，我们需要问问自己
我真的相信吗？
我真的相信慷慨的人会一无所缺吗？
我相信耶和华会使人有能力表现慷慨吗？
我相信一个人表现慷慨
耶和华就会给他更多
让他可以继续表现这种特质吗？
别忘了你吃的水果和蔬菜就是一个证据
上帝在水果里面放了种子
如果你把某个水果里的种子都拿来种
你后来收获的水果会多到连你自己都吃不完
第10节和11节就是这么说的
“他是厚赐种子给人撒种
也厚赐食物给人享用的上帝
他会格外多赐种子给你们撒种
让你们的正义行为有更丰富的收获
你们现在样样富足
因此能在各方面慷慨施与
通过我们所做的使人感谢上帝。”
经文说得很对！
为什么耶和华要这么慷慨呢？
是为了使我们都可以对人表现慷慨
很明显地，慷慨是信心和爱心的表现
但为什么对人慷慨
也是我们崇拜上帝的一种方式呢？
11节说，我们慷慨施与能使人感谢上帝
想一想，别人会因为你的慷慨
而祷告感谢上帝
而祷告就是一种崇拜
不只这样，第12节也说
“因为这个救济众人的职务
不但是要充分满足圣民的需要
也是要让人多多感谢上帝。”
从年会我们知道
组织光是在过去两个工作年度
就用了差不多5000万美元在救灾上
我们也看到一些弟兄姐妹的家
在修复前和修复后的照片
我们很高兴弟兄姐妹都被照顾得很好
12节的经文说救灾工作
也是一种“职务”
是神圣的服务
而这样的服务让很多人感谢耶和华
第13节还说
“他们从这个救济职务看到证据
知道你们顺从基督的好消息”
没错，救灾工作可以表明我们就是真基督徒
经文接着说
你们做的，跟你们“公开声明的一样
也知道你们对他们和所有人都慷慨捐献
就把荣耀归于上帝
他们也因为上帝赐给你们
无与伦比的分外恩典
就为你们恳切祈求
借此表达对你们的温情
愿感谢归于上帝
他无偿给人的恩赐实在难以言喻。”
所以，上帝的分外恩典，也就是他的慷慨
远远超过我们的想象
是我们无法回报的
这让我们能够一直对人慷慨
因为你的慷慨
耶和华每天都收到上千万个感谢的祷告
这让弟兄姐妹更团结了
那为什么我们能表现慷慨？
我们怎么有时间、精力、资源、动力
爱心、机会和点子去表现慷慨呢？
都是因为我们有耶和华的分外恩典
你支持王国的工作
不仅是在帮助需要的人，也是在崇拜耶和华
像历代志上29:14说的
“万物都从你而来
我们献给你的，都是从你手里得来的。”
你已经从上帝的慷慨和分外恩典
学到宝贵的一课
由于你相信上帝的保证
也效法他的良善
所以你现在就能体验来自上帝的喜乐
这就是耶和华的组织
愿耶和华继续因你们表现慷慨
而大大赐福给你们

titles.en: David Schafer: Imitate Jehovah’s Generosity (1 Chron. 29:14)
titles.cn: 戴维·谢弗：效法耶和华表现慷慨（代上29:14）

ko.text: 대규모 프로젝트에는 여러 해에 걸쳐 많은 자원봉사자가 필요합니다.
재해 구호 활동과 지부 개축 공사에 관해 살펴봤습니다.
이런 점을 생각하면서 다음 동영상을 시청해 보시기 바랍니다.
종이로 된 여러 가지 지원서를 사용해 왔습니다.
많은 충실한 형제 자매들이 그런 지원서로
그렇게 자원하는 것은 예수께서 마태 9:37에서 하신 말씀처럼
현재 그 어느 때보다 자원봉사자들이 더 많이 필요합니다.
더 많은 형제 자매들이 자원할 수 있을까요?
다양한 형태의 봉사에 간편하게 지원할 수 있는 방법이 있습니까?
이제 jw.org를 통해 온라인 지원서를 이용할 수 있게 되었음을
장로들은 온라인으로 지원서를 검토하고 승인할 것입니다.
여러분이 신권 봉사를 확장하는 데 기꺼이 자원한다면,
일꾼이 더 필요한 다양한 분야에 도움이 될 것입니다.
“당신의 백성이 자신을 기꺼이 바칠” 것이라고 기록했습니다.
여호와의 백성은 언제나 마음을 다해 자원해 왔습니다.
여러분이 다양한 형태의 봉사로 왕국을 지원하고
이 새로운 방법이 도움이 되기를 바랍니다.
다양한 봉사에 지원하려는 분들을 위한 이 새로운 마련은
그런 발전을 여호와의 백성을 위해 활용할 수 있는 방법이 있습니까?
워릭에 있는 멥스 부서 감독자인 클라이브 마틴 형제가
jw.org의 음성 파일을 들을 수 있는 새로운 방법을 소개할 것입니다.
우린 웹사이트와 앱에서 영적 양식을 풍부히 얻고 있습니다.
그런데 오디오 출판물과 프로그램을 쉽게 찾아서 들을 방법이 없는지
그런 방법이 있다면 시력에 제약이 있어서
오디오 프로그램이 꼭 필요한 형제 자매들에게
이제 기쁘게도, 아마존 알렉사와 구글 보이스 어시스턴트를 통해
jw.org의 내용을 들을 수 있게 되었습니다. (현재 이 기능은 영어로만 이용할 수 있습니다.)
여러분은 음악을 듣고, 뉴스나 날씨를 확인하고,
이런 음성 인식 서비스를 사용해 보셨을지 모릅니다.
이제 그런 기능을 영적 양식을 들을 때도 사용할 수 있게 되었습니다.
“알렉사, jw.org에서 이번 주 성경 읽기 범위 재생해 줘.”
특정한 장을 읽어 달라고 해 볼까요?
“알렉사, jw.org에서 러시아어 연구용 파수대 재생해 줘.”
이 새로운 친구들이 못하는 것도 있다는 겁니다.
“알렉사, 파수대에서 새로 배운 내용에 대해 어떻게 생각해?”
JW 월간 방송 프로그램을 오디오로 듣고 싶으신가요?
이번 달 방송에 오신 여러분을 모두 환영합니다.
구체적인 연도와 달을 지정해서 재생해 달라고 할 수도 있습니다.
비슷한 방법으로 왕국 노래를 듣는 것도 가능합니다.
또 집회 때 부를 노래를 연습해 보고 싶으면 이렇게 해 보세요.
며칠 내에 이러한 기능들을 사용할 수 있을 것입니다.
알렉사나 구글 기기로 이런 기능을 사용하시려면
다음 주에 jw.org에 게시될 설명을 살펴보시기 바랍니다.
우리가 풍부한 영적 자료들에서 유익을 얻도록
이처럼 간편한 방법을 마련해 주신 여호와 하느님과
그럼 이제부터는 성경적인 연설을 기대해 보겠습니다.
중앙장로회 여러 성원이 수고하실 텐데, 먼저,
북쪽에서 오는 메뚜기들의 공격을 말하는 것입니다.
요엘 2장에서 그 공격에 관해 읽어볼 수 있는데요,
이 예언에 관해 몇 구절 살펴볼 것이기 때문에,
요엘서를 계속 펴 두시면 좋을 것 같습니다.
메뚜기 떼의 재앙 같은 공격을 묘사하는데요.
저마다 자기 진로로 나아가고 자기 길에서 벗어나지 않는다.
서로 밀치지 않고 제각기 자기 진로로 나아간다.
무기에 맞아 쓰러지는 자가 있다 해도 대열이 흐트러지지 않는다.
도시 안으로 달려 들어가고 성벽 위를 달린다.
문자적인 곤충에 관해 말하는 게 아니라는 걸 분명히 볼 수 있는데,
‘각 남자가 자기 진로로 나아간다’ 고 되어 있죠.
따라서 메뚜기와 같은 특성을 지닌 사람들을
그렇게 비유한 것임을 알 수 있습니다.
우린 여러 해 동안 이 메뚜기 떼가 좋은 사람들이라고,
왕국의 좋은 소식을 전파하는 여호와의 증인들이라고 말이죠.
그들이 메뚜기 떼와 같다고 생각한 이유는 우선,
누구도 그들이 전파하는 걸 막을 수 없기 때문입니다.
또 그들은 좋은 소식을 계속 전하기 위해 무슨 일이든 하는데,
뭐 그게 아니라면 어떤 일이든 할 것입니다.
좋은 소식을 전하기 위해서 그들은 어떤 반대의 벽에 부딪히든,
이러한 설명이 타당해 보일 수 있습니다.
하지만 어떤 예언을 가장 잘 이해하려면 문맥을 살펴보아야 합니다.
다른 결론을 내릴 수 밖에 없게 됩니다.
이제, 왜 그런지 몇 가지 이유를 생각해 보죠.
문맥을 살펴보겠다고 했으니까, 같은 장의 20절을 찾아 보실까요?
“내가 북쪽에서 온 자들을 너희에게서 멀리 쫓아내어
후위대는 서쪽 바다 쪽으로 흩어 버리겠다.”
이들이 좋은 소식을 전하는 왕국 선포자라면,
따라서 이 메뚜기들은 좋은 사람들이 아닌 것 같습니다.
“떼 지어 다니는 메뚜기, 날개 없는 메뚜기,
게걸스러운 메뚜기, 마구 먹어 치우는 메뚜기,
곧 내가 너희 가운데 보낸 큰 군대가 먹은 햇수대로
왕국 봉사자들은 사람들의 생명을 구하는 일을 하는 데 말입니다.
왜 그걸 피해를 입히는 것으로 보시겠습니까?
왜 그것을 보상해 주어야 한다고 말씀하시겠습니까?
생각해 볼 점이 하나 더 있는데,
28절을 볼 텐데, 첫 부분만 읽어볼 것입니다.
이때는 이미 여호와께서 메뚜기들을 쫓아내신 이후라는 점입니다.
땅을 황폐시켰고, 땅의 모든 식물을 먹어 치웠습니다.
그리고 여호와께서는 북쪽에서 온 그 메뚜기들을
내가 모든 부류의 육체에게 나의 영을 부어 주리니.”
만약 메뚜기들이 정말 전파 활동을 수행한 것이라면,
왜 그 활동이 끝나고 나서야 성령을 받았을까요?
우리가 여호와의 강력한 성령의 도움 없이
여러분 모두 우리가 강력한 여호와의 성령의 도움 없이는 결코
계속 전파할 수 없다는 사실에 동의하실 것입니다.
따라서 이 예언에 대한 우리의 이해를 조정할 필요가 있습니다.
그런데, 어떤 분들은 계시록 9장이 생각나실지 모릅니다.
거기 보면, 사람의 얼굴을 한 메뚜기들이 나오는데,
사실, 계시록 9장과 요엘 2장 사이에 비슷한 점이 있긴 하지만,
그 두 예언 사이에는 중요한 차이점이 있습니다.
예를 들어 요엘의 예언에서는 메뚜기들이 북쪽에서 옵니다.
비슷한 점이 있지만 분명 차이점이 있습니다.
성경에서 한 가지 사물이 상황에 따라 다양한 의미를 전달하는 것은
여호와께선 자신의 큰 군대라고 부르신 메뚜기들과 같은
자신의 백성이 포로가 되게 하실 것이었습니다.
그 군대는 북쪽에서 온 자들이라고 불리는데,
북쪽에서 나와서 이스라엘을 침공할 것이었기 때문입니다.
“서로 밀치지 않고 제각기 자기 진로로 나아간다.
무기에 맞아 쓰러지는 자가 있다 해도
도시 안으로 달려 들어가고 성벽 위를 달린다.
그 누구도 바빌로니아 군대의 칼을 피할 수 없습니다.
이사야의 기록은 이 기록과 조화를 이룹니다.
그 공격과 그로 인한 결과를 예언했습니다.
물고기를 잡듯 그들을 잡게 할 것이다.’
모든 산과 모든 언덕과 바위틈에서 그들을 사냥하게 할 것이다.”
올바른 마음을 가진 사람을 사냥하고 잡는 것으로 이해했죠.
그들을 찾아 일종의 표하는 일을 하는 것으로 생각한 것 같습니다.
이 내용을 올바로 이해할 수 있습니다.
16절 끝에선 “그들을 사냥하게 할 것” 이라고 했는데,
사냥 당하는 건 올바른 마음을 가진 사람이 아니라 악한 자들입니다.
“내 눈이 그들이 하는 모든 일을 보고 있다.
자기들의 잘못을 내 눈앞에서 숨기지 못한다.”
18절에서도 하느님께선 ‘그들의 잘못을 다 갚아 주겠다’고 하십니다.
따라서 그들은 올바른 마음을 가진 사람들이 아닙니다.
그들은 숲속에 숨으려 해도 사냥을 당할 것이고,
바다로 가서 숨으려 해도 잡히고 말 것입니다.
그들은 바빌로니아 군인들에게서 벗어나지 못할 것입니다.
이젠 좋은 소식을 좀 듣고 싶으시죠?
요엘은 어느 시점이 되면 많은 사람에게
영적 양식이 풍부히 공급될 것이라고 말합니다.
이제 요엘서로 돌아가서 이번엔 28, 29절 전체를 읽어 보겠습니다.
[바빌로니아 군인들이 할 일을 다 한 후에]
내가 모든 부류의 육체에게 나의 영을 부어 주리니,
노인은 꿈을 꾸며 젊은이는 환상을 볼 것이다.
그날에 나의 남종과 여종에게도 나의 영을 부어 줄 것이다.”
사도 베드로는 기원 33년 오순절에 여호와께서 성령을 부어 주셨을 때
우리가 아는 사실은 그 수가 1세기 말까지도
1세기 중에 시작된 왕국 상속자들을 찾는 일이
하지만 그 3000명은 좋은 소식을 열심히 전파하기 시작했고
여호와께서는 그들의 열심 있는 활동을 축복하셨습니다.
그 결과 수만 명이 말씀에 순종하게 된 것이죠.
오늘날에도 비슷한 점을 볼 수 있을까요?
그분이 그 노력을 축복하셨음이 분명히 드러났습니다.
14만 4000명이 넘는 사람들이 침례를 받고 있다는 사실을 아십니까?
따라서 이것은 여호와께서 이 마지막 때에
자신의 성령을 넘치도록 부어 주고 계시다는 걸 보여 줍니다.

최선을 다해 하느님의 아들을 알아 가도록 하십시다.
하늘에 계신 사랑 많은 우리 아버지 여호와도
더 잘 알아 가게 될 것입니다.
자신의 언어로 연구용 성경을 보실 수 있는 분들은
그 축복이 얼마나 큰지 이미 아실 겁니다.

en.text: Big projects require thousands of volunteers
over a period of several years.
On our program thus far, we have also considered disaster relief work
and branch renovation projects.
All of these initiatives require
that volunteers fill out an application
to be used in these capacities.
And there are so many avenues of service
that require the submittal of an application.
With that thought in mind,
please carefully watch the next video entitled
A New Application for Processing Applications.
Have you ever submitted an application to expand your ministry?
Since the early 1900’s,
our organization has used paper applications
for many forms of service
and faithful workers have responded.
This growth is in fulfillment of Jesus’ words at Matthew 9:37:
“The harvest is great.”
And the needs are greater than ever before.
Can more workers make themselves available?
Can applying for different avenues of service be simplified?
We are pleased to announce
online applications on jw.org®!
Publishers will be able to apply online to expand their ministry!
Elders will review and approve applications online.
When needed, circuit overseers will review
and approve applications online.
Your willing spirit to expand your theocratic service
supports the need for more workers in many ways.
Jehovah inspired King David to write:
“Your people will offer themselves willingly.”
And Jehovah’s people have always wholeheartedly responded.
We hope this new online tool
will help you support the Kingdom
in whatever way you can, all to Jehovah’s praise.
As you noted, this provision will be available
for those applying for various privileges of service
beginning January 2020.
Technology continues to make advancements.
Is there a way to harness such advances
for the benefit of Jehovah’s people?
Brother Clive Martin,
who oversees the MEPS Department at Warwick,
will discuss a new way
to access jw.org® audio files.
Please, Brother Martin.
We just love the rich supply of spiritual food on our website and app.
However, some have asked if there’s an easier way to find
and listen to the audio publications and programs.
This would be particularly helpful
for many of our dear publishers who have limited vision
and who depend on these audio programs.
With this in mind, we’re happy to introduce
jw.org® for Amazon Alexa
and the Google Voice Assistant.
You may have bought
one of these voice assistants
to listen to music,
check the news and the weather,
or perhaps to control your home appliances.
Now you can use it to listen
to the content that we need
for our regular spiritual routine.
Let’s try it out.
“Alexa, read the daily text from jw.org.”
Reading the daily text.
Saturday, October 5:
“Make disciples of people of all the nations, baptizing them.”
“Alexa, play the Bible reading for this week from jw.org.”
Playing this week’s Bible reading.
The letter of James.
Chapter 1.
For Google devices, the command is just a little different.
Let’s ask for a specific chapter.
“Hey, Google,
ask jw.org to play Matthew 24.”
Playing the Bible starting at Matthew chapter 24.
Chapter 24:
“Now as Jesus was departing from . . . ”
Are you learning another language?
Here’s a feature that can help.
“Alexa,
play the Watchtower  study in Russian from jw.org.”
Playing this week’s Watchtower  study article in Russian.
Just remember, though,
that your newfound friend does have some limitations.
“Alexa, what do you think of that new point in The Watchtower?”
I don’t have an opinion on that.
And that’s probably just as well.
Would you like to listen to the audio track of the monthly broadcast?
“Hey, Google, ask jw.org to play the broadcast.”
Playing JW Broadcasting®, September 2019.
Hello, everyone.
We’re so happy to have you with us for this month’s broadcast.
You can also ask for the broadcast for a specific month or year.
Now, how about some theocratic music?
“Alexa, play original songs from jw.org.”
Playing original songs.
You can also listen to our collection of Kingdom songs in the same way.
Or if you want to practice a specific song for the meeting,
“Hey, Google, ask jw.org to play song 57.”
Playing 57, “Preaching to All Sorts of People.”
These features will be available within the next few days.
So look on jw.org this coming week for instructions
on how to enable these features for your Alexa or Google device.
We thank Jehovah and his organization
that they make it ever easier for us to benefit
from our rich library of spiritual content.
We now look forward to Scriptural talks to be presented
by various members of the Governing Body.
First, please give your attention to Brother David Splane.
His subject is intriguing:
“An Attack Coming From the North.”
Alexa!
Where are you when I need you?
Well, an attack coming from the north—
What are we talking about?
Are we talking about the attack of Gog of Magog?
No.
We’re talking about an attack
by a plague of locusts
coming from the north.
And we can read about that plague in Joel chapter 2.
I’d like you to follow and leave your Bibles open, please,
at Joel because we’re going to be considering
a few verses in this prophecy.
This is Joel 2:7-9
—an attack by a plague,
a swarm, of locusts.
Joel 2:7:
“They charge like warriors,
“they scale a wall like soldiers,
“each keeps to his own course,
“and they do not swerve from their paths.
“They do not shove one another;
“each man advances in his course.
“If the weapons cause some to fall, the others do not break ranks.
“Into the city they rush, on the wall they run.
“Onto the houses they climb,
through the windows they enter like a thief.”
Now, I think you can see that we’re not talking about insects here.
Notice in verse 8:
“Each man  advances in his course.”
So we’re talking about people
who are likened to locusts,
who have the characteristics of locusts.
And the question is,
Are these good people, or are they bad people?
Well, for many years,
including in the April 15, 2009, Watchtower,
our understanding was that these were good people.
In fact, these were Jehovah’s people.
These were Jehovah’s Witnesses
who were preaching the good news of the Kingdom.
And the idea was that they were just like locusts because,
first of all, you couldn’t stop them from preaching
and they would go to any length to keep preaching the good news
—probably not go into people’s windows like thieves,
but otherwise, they’d stop short of that.
But they would do other things.
Preaching the good news
—it didn’t matter what wall of opposition was erected against them;
they would scale that wall and keep preaching.
And if we were to confine ourselves to a reading of just these three verses,
we could make a case for that explanation.
But now, prophecy is best understood
when we consider it in context.
And if you look at the context of Joel chapter 2,
you are forced to come to a different conclusion.
Now let’s consider a couple of reasons why this is so.
Now, we talk about context,
so let’s look at verse 20 in the same chapter,
Joel chapter 2.
And here in verse 20,
we’re talking about the locusts that come from the north,
and we’re going to see how Jehovah views these locusts.
Are these good people, or are they bad people?
Verse 20:
“I will drive the northerner far away from you;
“I will disperse him to a dry and desolate wasteland,
with his vanguard toward the eastern sea.”
Well, Jehovah is talking about the locusts here,
and he says he’s going to drive them away.
If these were Kingdom publishers who are declaring the good news,
why would Jehovah want to drive them away?
And then how does Jehovah view these locusts?
Look at the last part of verse 20:
“The foul smell from him will ascend,
the stench from him will keep ascending.”
That’s not good.
So it’s looking like these locusts are not good people.
What is Jehovah talking about here?
Pest control.
He doesn’t like the locusts.
Now look at verse 25.
Jehovah says:
“And I will make compensation to you for the years
“that the swarming locust, the unwinged locust,
“the voracious locust, and the devouring locust have eaten,
my great army that I sent among you.”
Well, now, if the locusts were ministers of the Kingdom,
why would Jehovah say that he had to “make compensation”
for the damage that the locusts have done?
The locusts, if they were Kingdom publishers,
would just be helping people to save their lives.
So why would Jehovah call that damage?
Why would he say they would have to “make compensation”?
Now, that’s one aspect of this that we considered.
But there’s another one, and that is the sequence of events.
Look at verse 28,
and we’ll read just the first part of verse 28.
And keep in mind, at this point,
Jehovah has driven the locusts away.
They have done all the damage they could.
They have devastated the land.
They have destroyed all of the vegetation,
and now Jehovah God has driven
“the northerner,” the locust, away.
And so, what does he say in verse 28?
“After that
“[after the locusts have been driven away]
I will pour out my spirit on every sort of flesh.”
Now let’s think about that.
If the locusts were really carrying out the preaching work
and they don’t get the holy spirit until after they finish the preaching work,
does that mean that we’ve been preaching all this time
without the help of Jehovah’s powerful holy spirit?
I’m sure you’ll all agree, we couldn’t possibly keep preaching
without the help of Jehovah’s powerful holy spirit.
So it’s obvious that we have some thinking to do about this prophecy.
Now, someone might bring up Revelation chapter 9,
because in Revelation chapter 9,
we read of locusts with “human faces”
and what “seemed to be crowns of gold” on their heads,
and they torment the wicked.
And someone will say,
“Well, don’t those locusts represent
Jehovah’s anointed servants and their preaching work?”
And the answer is yes.
And it’s true that there are some similarities
between Revelation chapter 9 and Joel chapter 2,
but there are significant differences as well.
For example, in Joel’s prophecy,
the locusts come from the north,
they devastate the vegetation, and they’re driven away.
But what about Revelation?
Well, those locusts come out of an abyss,
and “they [are] told not to harm the vegetation,”
and they stay on until their work is done.
So there are similarities, but there are also differences.
What are we saying?
We are saying that the locusts in Revelation
are not the same as the locusts in Joel.
Now, it’s not unusual for a symbol to mean one thing in one Bible book
and something quite different in another
—Revelation 5:5, Jesus, “the Lion of the tribe of Judah”;
1 Peter 5:8, Satan the Devil, “a roaring lion”
—same symbol but quite different meanings.
Well, now,
if the locusts are bad people,
if they are not Jehovah’s faithful servants,
we have to look for a different explanation.
What could it be?
It’s a simple one.
Joel is predicting a military attack.
Jehovah will use Babylonian soldiers who are just like locusts
—“my great army,” he calls them—
to bring his people into captivity.
And the army is called “the northerner”
because the Babylonians will come up and invade Israel from the north.
And when we read Joel 2:8, 9
with the idea of Babylonian soldiers, it all makes sense.
Let’s just read those verses again, verse 8 and verse 9:
“They do not shove one another;
“each man advances in his course.
“If the weapons cause some to fall, the others do not break ranks.
“Into the city they rush, on the wall they run.
Onto the houses they climb, through the windows they enter like a thief.”
Can you picture the scene?
There are soldiers everywhere.
No one can escape the sword of the Babylonians.
And this concords with what the prophet Isaiah wrote.
He was looking into the future,
and he was looking at this event and the outcome of this event.
And he says: “All who were found were taken prisoner,
even though they had fled far away.”
Now, the prophet Jeremiah foretold something similar
at Jeremiah 16:16.
Let’s read that; then we’ll go back to Joel.
Jeremiah 16:16:
“‘Here I am sending for many fishermen,’
“declares Jehovah, ‘and they will fish for them.
“‘After that I will send for many hunters,
“‘and they will hunt them down
“‘on every mountain and every hill
and out of the clefts of the crags.’”
Now, we used to think that the hunters and fishers
were hunting and fishing for righthearted ones
in sort of a marking work, I guess,
where they were looking for righthearted ones.
But now, the revised New World Translation
helps us to get the right understanding of this.
Did you notice what it says?
“They will hunt them down.”
It’s the wicked who are being hunted, not the righthearted ones.
And just to confirm that, look at verse 17:
“For my eyes are on everything they do.
“They have not been hidden from before me,
nor has their error been hidden from my eyes.”
And then in verse 18, he says he is going
to ‘repay the full amount of their error.’
So these are not righthearted ones.
These are people who might try to hide in the forest.
They’ll be hunted down.
If they go out and try to hide in the sea, they’ll be fished out of the water.
They will not get away from the Babylonian soldiers.
But now Joel has some good news for us,
and we want some good news after this, don’t we?
And the news is restoration.
And Joel is saying that at some point an ample supply of spiritual food
is going to become available for the people.
Let’s go back to Joel
and this time read entirely verses 28 and 29.
Joel 2 —Joel 2:28, 29:
“After that
“[so the Babylonians have done what they were going to do]
“I will pour out my spirit on every sort of flesh,
“and your sons and your daughters will prophesy,
“your old men will dream dreams, and your young men will see visions.
“And even on my male slaves and female slaves
I will pour out my spirit in those days.”
Well, when was the prophecy fulfilled?
After that, certainly.
The apostle Peter tells us
that it was first fulfilled at Pentecost 33 C.E.
Jehovah poured out his spirit, and at the end of that day,
there were 3,000 publishers of the Kingdom.
And did Jehovah bless their zealous activity?
He certainly did, because by the end of the century,
thousands had become obedient to the word.
How many thousands?
We don’t know.
The Bible doesn’t say.
But we do know that it would have to be
a lot less than 144,000
because the search for Kingdom heirs was going on in the first century,
and it wasn’t nearly complete by the end of the first century.
Yet, the zealous activity of those 3,000
who began preaching the good news,
that zealous activity, was blessed by Jehovah God,
and thousands became obedient to the word.
Well, now, can we see a little bit of a parallel here?
The year 1919.
In 1919, according to official records,
there were fewer than 6,000 publishers
of the good news.
But has Jehovah blessed the efforts
of those 6,000 publishers?
By the end of the century,
he certainly had shown that he’d blessed the efforts of the brothers.
Do you know that every year
since 1983,
more than 144,000
have been baptized each year?
And our brothers today don’t have the gifts of the spirit.
So, what does this indicate?
It indicates that Jehovah has made
a mighty outpouring of his spirit
in these last days.
It’s a marvelous thing to behold.
Now, when you think of it,
we sort of had our explanation backward in the past.
Because in the past, the idea was that the spirit
was poured out in 1919 and then the locusts went to work,
because the locusts were Jehovah’s people.
But that’s not what the Bible says, is it?
The Bible says that the locusts finish their work,
and after that, the spirit is poured out.
Well, today, thousands upon thousands are getting baptized,
and we can expect that more are going to get baptized in the future,
with the new instructions we’ve received:
Concentrate more on conversations;
concentrate more on starting Bible studies.
And with those instructions in mind,
no doubt we’re going to have a tremendous increase in baptisms.
But now, here’s a little word of caution:
By all means, have conversations;
by all means, read the Bible to people;
by all means, offer Bible studies.
But don’t forget to offer literature.
If you say,
“I deliberately didn’t offer one piece of literature all month,”
you’re not bragging.
What do we print it for?
And, brothers, let’s be realistic about it:
You have a lovely conversation with someone,
and then you don’t find the person for another three weeks.
Leave the person some literature
that he can read so that he can further his interest.
Well, we might think of this explanation and say:
“Well, that’s obvious. This explanation is obvious.
Why didn’t we see it before?”
And the answer is, yes, it’s obvious
when Jehovah’s time for us to understand it comes along.
But before Jehovah’s time for us to understand it comes along,
it isn’t always so obvious.
So we always look to Jehovah God for clarification in matters.
Now, what has changed?
It’s true that in a few lands (but not many)
Jehovah’s people do seem to be everywhere,
as numerous as locusts,
and it’s true that in every land we won’t allow
any wall of opposition to prevent us from doing our work;
but we’re just not doing it
in fulfillment of Joel chapter 2 and Jeremiah chapter 16.
So let’s continue having a zealous share
in proclaiming the life-giving message that God has given us,
confident that he won’t drive us away.
He will sustain us until the work is done.
Well, it was certainly very encouraging and interesting.
Thank you, Brother Splane.
Now Brother Herd has something to share with us.
His title is “Study the Bible With the Study Bible.”
Who is the most important person that you know?
Well, as dedicated Witnesses of Jehovah, I’m sure you would say, “Jehovah.”
Well, who is the second most important person that you know?
I asked my wife that once, and she said, “You.”
And then she said, “I’m just joking.”
No, it’s Jesus Christ, and we all know that.
But, now, how important is it for us to know
not just Jehovah but also his Son?
Well, let’s look at something in the Bible.
Open your Bibles, if you please,
to John 17:3,
one of the most familiar scriptures that we learn when we come into the truth,
John 17:3:
“This means everlasting life, their coming to know you,
the only true God, and the one whom you sent, Jesus Christ.”
Well, now, let’s think about it.
It means our salvation —doesn’t it?—
to come to know Jehovah God and his Son, Jesus.
Come to know them —it means everlasting life.
Our salvation rests on our knowledge
of Jehovah God and his Son, Jesus.
It means our life.
But “coming to know,” what does this mean?
Could it be what the study note on this verse says?
“The verb is used in the present tense to express continuous action.”
Absolutely! That’s the correct answer.
So coming to know Jehovah
or someone else is an ongoing process.
We have to become acquainted with that person.
Now, if I should ask you, How many of you know me?
Raise your hands, please.
Get them down because you don’t really know me.
Oh, in a sense, you were right in raising your hand.
You know who I am; you know the position I have.
You’ve got my name, you’ve heard me give some talks, and so forth.
So you have some knowledge of me, but there are so many things
about me that you don’t know.
And if you did know these things,
it wouldn’t help you.
But, now, coming to know Jehovah is altogether different.
Coming to know Jesus is altogether different.
The more we know about them, why, then
the better we have a relationship with them.
And we’re going to benefit from that knowledge in ever so many ways.
So we want to come to know Jehovah.
No matter how long we’ve been in the truth
(and some of you have been there for decades),
we must keep working at coming to know Jehovah God
and his Son, Jesus.
But the question is,
How can we come to know Jehovah better and better?
Well, we can learn much through creation.
We look around us, and it draws us ever closer to Jehovah.
When we see the animal creation, as we have earlier today
(the zebra and various birds and other animals),
we think of Jehovah and his great wisdom
and the blessings that he has showered upon us
as a result of the creation around us.
And how many of us enjoy going to the beautiful parks a certain time of year
and enjoying all the creation —the greenery, the flowers, the trees?
My, there’s just no end to it!
And whenever we see fish that we’ve never seen before
(and there are so many fish that are so new to us),
their beauty—
It all speaks of Jehovah as the Creator, does it not?
And we marvel at these wonderful things.
But here’s another way that we benefit:
It’s through his Word.
It’s through the Bible that we’re able
to know the name of our God—Jehovah.
We’re able to appreciate what that name stands for,
and we’re drawn ever closer
to him as a result of that knowledge.
We’re able to have the knowledge of his purpose.
We know that he’s not responsible
for all the wickedness that goes on in the earth around us.
That’s not of his making, but yet people in the world feel that it is.
If someone dies, they blame God: “Why did he take that beautiful little girl?
“She was only two years old.
Why did he do a thing like that?”
Well, they have no knowledge, but you have knowledge.
When a person dies whom they love,
people in the world have no idea
about the resurrection.
They feel that two things can happen.
Many of them feel this way (not all),
that two things can happen —either they go to heaven
and become a flower in His garden up there in some kind of a way
or else they go somewhere else
where they are tormented
day and night forever and ever.
Now, what about God’s Son?
How can we come to know him better and better.
Well, let’s watch the following video,
How Can We Come to Know the Son of God Better and Better?,
seven minutes.
He was neither rich nor powerful from the world’s point of view.
He did not even have a home that he could call his own.
Yet, his teachings have changed the course of history.
They have helped millions to gain
something more important than material wealth.
The man is Jesus Christ, the Son of God.
Jehovah wants us to know his Son,
to love his Son, to be like his Son.
To help us know his Son, Jehovah lovingly reserved
a portion of his Word, the four Gospels
—Matthew, Mark, Luke, and John— and the book of Acts.
These Bible books have helped true Christians to find
the happiest, most meaningful life possible.
The Gospels portray a man of tender and deep feelings.
They show the wide range of Jesus’ personality:
compassion for a leper,
indignation at self-righteous religious leaders,
deep sadness over the nation that rejected him.
In the Gospels,
we learn of the many miracles Jesus performed,
from healing the sick to raising the dead.
Those miracles changed people’s lives,
yet Jesus was not known as Healer or a miracle worker.
Instead, he was called the Teacher.
And what a teacher he was!
Think of the wise sayings of Jesus that have become
part of everyday speech
thousands of years after he uttered them.
The Gospels give a fourfold historical account
of the life and ministry of Jesus.
Matthew, an apostle, evidently wrote
his Gospel for the Jews.
Over 40 percent of its content is unique.
Matthew gives us a far more extensive account of the Sermon on the Mount.
In this profound sermon,
Jesus does not just tell us the course of wisdom.
He does much more.
He shows us by explaining, reasoning, and offering proof.
How we marvel at the simplicity, clarity,
and unparalleled wisdom in the teachings of Jesus!
Mark’s vigorous, fast-moving account
was seemingly written for non-Jewish readers.
It mentions 19 miracles of Jesus,
including the only account of the deaf man whose hearing Jesus restored.
Considerately, Jesus takes the man away from the crowd
and heals him in a private place.
How reassuring to learn that Jesus uses his power
in such a considerate and thoughtful way!
Luke, the beloved physician,
wrote for both Jews and non-Jews.
Some 60 percent of this Gospel is unique,
including the account of the resurrection
of the only child of the widow of Nain.
Jesus is “moved with pity” for this widow.
After resurrecting her son,
Jesus gives him to his mother.
Death has torn the family apart,
but Jesus makes them a family again.
How beautifully this account reveals a very tender side of the Son of God!
John, the apostle who was especially close to Jesus,
wrote his Gospel last.
Some 90 percent contains information
not found in the other three Gospels.
Only John mentions the resurrection of Lazarus.
In this touching account,
Jesus openly sheds tears.
How comforting it is to know that Jesus
has such deep empathy!
Together, the four Gospels paint a detailed portrait of Jesus.
The Bible book of Acts
also helps us to come to know Jesus.
Written by the physician Luke, Acts is a continuation
of the Gospel of Luke.
In the opening chapter, we learn of Jesus’ final words
to his disciples before ascending to heaven.
The resurrected Jesus leaves no doubt as to what he expects his disciples,
including us, to do.
They are to be witnesses of him
“to the most distant part of the earth.”
The Bible book of Acts helps us to understand
what being a follower of Jesus is all about.
How can we benefit fully from the four Gospels and the book of Acts?
We must do more than just read them.
We must slow down and take the time
to study them carefully and meditate on them deeply.
We need to bring the accounts to life by doing research,
observing details,
comparing parallel accounts,
and using our imagination
to see, hear, and feel the action.
Over the years, our organization has published a number of books
designed to help us to dig deeply.
At the annual meeting in 2015,
the Governing Body announced
that a new online Study Bible  would be released.
How can the Study Bible help us come to know Jesus better?
Within the four Gospels alone, there are about 2,300 study notes.
Added to that, the image gallery, maps, and introduction videos
bring the Bible accounts to life.
There’s no question about it.
Our organization has given us the help we need
to dig deeper into the Gospels and the book of Acts
and to reflect appreciatively on them.
As a result, we come to know the Son of God better and better.
We agree with the sentiment of the apostle Peter,
who said of Jesus:
“Though you never saw him, you love him.”
Have you benefited from using the online Study Bible?
I’m sure you will agree that it is a great tool to help us
come to know God’s Son better and better.
But what if accessing the information online
is not easy for you as an individual?
Let’s face it, not everyone has easy access
to the Internet or finds it easy to navigate online.
Well, the Governing Body
is pleased to announce the release of a printed version
of the Study Bible
containing the five Bible books we just discussed in the video
—Matthew through Acts.
Why are we releasing a printed version of the Study Bible?
Well, many prefer a printed medium such as a book,
especially for doing deeper reading and making notes.
It’s easier to slow down
and absorb the information at hand.
And many of us find it easier when we use a printed and bound book
for our study periods.
Have you ever gone back and found something you read in a book
because you recall that it was either at the top
or bottom of a page
or on the left- or on the right-hand side of a two-page spread?
Would you like to see what this new publication looks like?
Well, let’s watch the next video.
What are some of the features of the printed Study Bible
that make it an effective tool for studying the four Gospels and the book of Acts?
Let’s see.
Each Bible book has an introduction with noteworthy facts,
study notes about the title,
and an overview of the book.
Subheadings within the sacred text help you
to locate specific accounts more easily.
Wide margins offer ample space for note-taking.
Study notes are found below the scriptures.
The image gallery contains 153 illustrations and photographs
from the books of Matthew through Acts.
The map gallery helps you to combine
specific events with locations.
The glossary gives definitions of Biblical and non-Biblical words
that are used in the main text or in the study notes.
Would you like to read the entire Bible in one year?
Then use the Bible reading schedule to keep track of your progress.
This Study Bible  is designed to help you study more deeply
and bring Bible accounts to life.
Take, for instance, the account of the widow in the temple.
Verse 41 says that
Jesus “sat down
with the treasury chests in view.”
Hmm.
What does the study note say about treasury chests?
That’s interesting: ‘According to rabbinical sources,
there were 13 treasury chests’ for collecting
the contributions of those entering the temple.
And these chests were “apparently located in the area
called the Court of the Women.”
I wonder where that was in the temple.
Hmm.
The study note directs us to Appendix B11.
Wow, look at those four giant golden lampstands!
‘The facade surrounding the front doors
may have been plated with gold.’
Impressive!
The “light from the rising sun
would have been reflected with dazzling brilliance.”
Let me go back to the account.
Verse 42 says: “Now a poor widow came
and dropped in two small coins of very little value.”
What does the parallel account say?
Luke’s account calls her “a needy widow.”
The study note says:
“Needy . . . may denote a person
“who lacks the basic necessities of life
or someone for whom life is a great struggle.”
Might the widow have felt that her small gift
was too insignificant to matter?
I’ve felt that way before.
Jesus showed that the widow and her contribution
were valuable to Jehovah.
“This poor widow put in more than all the others . . .
She . . . put in everything she had.”
She gave her best.
When I give Jehovah my best,
no matter how much it is, it is precious to him.
Clearly, the Study Bible is designed to help us study
the Bible more deeply.
May this printed edition of Matthew through Acts
help you to come to know Jesus Christ,
the Son of God, better and better.
Remember that Jehovah set aside
a significant portion of his Word
for us to become acquainted with his Son, Jesus
—our Ransomer, our Leader and, of course, our King.
Jehovah wants us to know his Son.
He wants us to love his Son
and to put faith in his Son.
So by all means,
let’s—each and every one of us—use this new Bible
to make progress in coming to know the Son of God.
And as you do,
you will also be coming to know better
the One whom Jesus perfectly imitated,
our loving heavenly Father, Jehovah.
Thank you very much, Brother Herd.
We appreciate what we heard from you.
And what a blessing the Study Bible  has proven to be
for those who have it available in their language.

en.text: At Hebrews 8:1, the apostle Paul wrote:
“Now this is the main point of what we are saying.”
When we teach, we want our main points to stand out.
Why?
Well, which is easier to listen to?
A rambling discourse that outlines seemingly unrelated facts
or an organized presentation
with main points that relate to the theme?
When we make our main points stand out,
we help our audience to pay attention,
understand, and remember what we say.
So how can you make the main points stand out?
First, decide on the objective of your talk.
Aim to accomplish something.
If you don’t know your objective, neither will your audience.
Do you want to inform, convince,
encourage, motivate, or something else?
For example, let’s say that you’re discussing the resurrection.
If you’re speaking to a grieving family made up of fellow Christians,
your objective may be to give encouragement and comfort.
On the other hand, if you’re speaking about the resurrection
to unbelieving relatives who have questioned your beliefs,
your objective might be to convince them.
In each instance, the main points you choose will be different
because the objective is different.
So when preparing,
select only main points that help you achieve your objective
and that you can teach effectively in the allotted time.
Then develop the points in a logical order.
Ask yourself:
‘What questions or objections might my audience have about this topic?
In what logical order would they raise those questions or objections?’
Often, however, we are given an outline to develop,
and the main points have already been selected and put in a certain order.
In such a case,
analyze the outline to have clearly in mind
the objective of the talk
and how the main points will help you to reach that objective.
As you give the talk,
you don’t want the audience to lose sight of your theme.
So at various times during your discourse,
repeat key words in the theme or use synonyms.
Your audience will remember only a few main points,
so don’t develop too many.
Even if you’re giving a longer talk,
focus on developing a few points well.
As you develop secondary points,
explain their connection to the main point.
Don’t add ideas just because they’re interesting.
To make your main points stand out,
you might repeat in a sentence or two
each main point before going on to the next.
Or you might state the main points in the introduction
and then restate them in the conclusion.
When you finish,
the audience should be able to remember the main points.
Let’s watch a brother who’s in the middle of giving a talk.
See if you can discern the main point he’s developing and his theme.
Let’s turn to Proverbs 28:1.
Here the righteous are compared to a very impressive animal.
“The wicked flee when no one pursues them,
but the righteous are as confident as a lion.”
You and I can be like a lion.
Imagine that!
Bible writers were familiar with lions
because they were once plentiful in Israel,
although they are now extinct there.
A lion’s thunderous roar can be heard for miles.
They can move at a speed of 40 miles per hour.
They are so powerful
that a single blow from a lion’s paw
is enough to break the neck of a small antelope.
According to Insight on the Scriptures,
the lion serves as a fitting symbol of courageous justice.
And so Jesus is called
“the Lion that is of the tribe of Judah.”
Could you tell from that talk what the theme is?
Is it something about lions?
Jesus? the righteous?
Actually, the theme of this talk is
“Jehovah Makes Us Bold.”
What’s the main point that the speaker is trying to develop?
Jehovah is the Source of true boldness.
Let’s watch the speaker try again.
This time, notice how he emphasizes
the theme and main point.
Let’s turn to Proverbs 28:1.
As we read this verse, look for the answer to this question:
What sort of people can be truly confident?
“The wicked flee when no one pursues them,
but the righteous are as confident as a lion.”
So who can be confident?
The righteous.
And who are the righteous?
Those who have faith in the ransom
and who strive to adhere to Jehovah’s requirements.
Here’s the point:
Confidence comes not from natural ability,
education, or riches;
the source of true boldness
is our relationship with Jehovah.
So when we go in the ministry, we don’t need to be afraid.
We’re doing what Jehovah requires, and Jehovah is supporting us.
Remembering this will help us to preach with boldness.
This time, the speaker introduced the scripture in a way
that called attention to the main point.
He avoided cluttering his talk with details that didn’t support his point.
And to make sure the audience got the main point,
he told them, “Here’s the point.”
Then, he connected the point to the theme.
Whether from the platform or in the ministry,
our teaching should be simple and clear.
If we group our thoughts under just a few main points
that relate to our objective and theme,
our presentation will be easy to follow
and hard to forget.

cn.text: 我们施行教导时
要突出主要论点

你喜欢听哪一种演讲？

还是井井有条

也能帮他们理解和记住我们说的话
有什么方法能让主要论点更突出呢？
首先要确定你的演讲想要达到什么目的
我们的目标要非常明确
如果你自己都不知道你演讲的目的是什么
听众就更不知道你的演讲的目的是为了
传达信息
跟对方推理
还是鼓励他们采取行动
假设你今天要跟别人谈论复活这件事情
如果你说话的对象是弟兄姐妹
他最近刚刚失去亲人
那么你的目的就是要安慰和鼓励他
如果你的说话对象是未信主的家人
