늪에 빠져 허우적대고 있다고 느낄 때,
성경의 이 놀라운 교훈들을 생활에 적용하십시오.
스랍들을 본받아, 얼굴을 가리고 겸손을 유지하십시오.
여호와의 웅대한 영적 성전에서 현재 맡은 소중한 역할을 수행하고,
앞으로 영원히 여호와 곁에 머무시기 바랍니다.
누매어 형제, 훌륭한 연설을 해 주셔서 감사합니다.
정말 믿음을 강하게 해 주는 길르앗 프로그램이었습니다.
JW 방송을 통해 보실 수 있습니다.
이곳에는 화산 모래로 이루어진 아름다운 해변,
폭포, 깊은 계곡, 뾰족한 봉우리들이 있으며,
지상에서 가장 활발한 화산 중 하나인
첫 왕국 전도인이 레위니옹에 도착한 것은 1955년입니다.
지금은 3000명이 넘는 형제 자매들이 이곳에서 봉사하는데,
이곳에서 통용되는 레위니옹 크레올어 회중이 13개 있습니다.
따뜻하고 사랑 넘치는 이 형제 자매들은
우리가 사랑하는 레위니옹의 형제들에게 안부를 전합니다.

en.text: We extend a warm welcome to all of you
to the December 2019 edition
of JW Broadcasting®.
The Watchtower Bible School of Gilead
began on February 1, 1943.
Since then,
thousands of students have benefited
from the school’s in-depth course
of Bible study.
After months of intense study,
graduation day is a highlight for the class.
In this month’s program,
you’ll enjoy Part 1 of the graduation
of the 147th class of Gilead.
Pay close attention
to these encouraging Scriptural talks
delivered to the graduates
on Saturday, September 14, 2019.
Well, this is a very happy day
for those who are very soon to graduate
from this 147th class of Gilead.
I wanted to begin by asking them a question,
and that is, How far will you go?
Well now, when people ask that question,
How far will you go?
(normally in connection with secular education)
the meaning of the question is,
Are you going to get your bachelor’s degree
or are you going to go for your master’s
or are you going to go for a PhD and get your doctorate?
And so, in that sense, often going far in secular education
is solely a means of self-fulfillment
and not necessarily to help others.
Some study what’s called pure science,
meant just to advance mankind’s understanding of science
but with no practical benefit;
some study dead languages;
some study bacteria or insects,
which is wonderful if you like insects.
It may increase knowledge,
but it doesn’t necessarily help anyone.
Well, divine education is so different.
You see, it motivates us to ask the question,
‘How far can I go,
‘not to further myself,
but to help others?’
Now, Jehovah God and Christ Jesus
really set the example for us here.
Would you join me?
Let’s read together Psalm 113,
and let’s look here at verse 6.
Speaking of our wonderful God, Jehovah,
it says: “He stoops down
to look on heaven and earth.”
Well, now, how high do you imagine Jehovah to be?
Well, no matter how high you imagine it,
you know it’s still higher.
Jehovah is so high as the Almighty God.
But what does it say here in verse 6?
“He stoops down.”
Well, just think.
You might think of an illustration of a man who is perhaps very, very tall,
and he’s talking to a very, very small child.
What does he do?
Well, oftentimes he might crouch down,
get down on one knee,
and get right down onto the level of the child to speak to him.
And as a result, how does the little child feel?
Well, not so afraid,
not so intimidated by that large man.
The child becomes calm.
Well, think about Jehovah.
How far has Jehovah gone to “stoop down”
so that we feel loved?
so that we feel valued?
so that we feel appreciated?
What a beautiful example Jehovah sets
in going far to make us feel
so comfortable with him!
Now, what about our Lord Jesus?
Well, think how far he went to help each one of us.
Just look at the scripture here in Philippians chapter 2.
Philippians chapter 2
says that Jesus, of course, came from heaven, didn’t he?
Can you imagine how far that is?
It says in verse 5: “Keep this mental attitude in you
“that was also in Christ Jesus,
“who, although he was existing in God’s form,
“gave no consideration to a seizure,
“namely, that he should be equal to God.
No, but he emptied himself.”
And what did he do?
He “took a slave’s form and became human.”
Well, that was pretty far to go.
And while you and I think the earth
is pretty amazing and pretty wonderful,
have you ever seen heaven?
And that’s where Jesus left —willingly—
to come down to be among us, to serve us.
And then in the end, how far did he go?
Well, what does verse 8 say?
“More than that, when he came as a man,
“he humbled himself and became obedient [to what?]
“to the point of death,
yes, death on a torture stake.”
Jesus was willing to go very, very far
to help people.
Well, now, you have all come to Gilead.
Why did you come to Gilead?
What was the purpose of it?
You see, was it to increase your Bible knowledge?
Was it to give you some grand knowledge of Bible history
or to give you some comprehensive knowledge
of Biblical Greek or Hebrew?
No.
The purpose of your coming to Gilead
was to help you so that you could strengthen
and stabilize the field and branch territory.
That’s the purpose of Gilead.
But now, what is the field and the branch territory?
What is that?
It’s people —it’s people that need to be loved;
it’s people that need to be organized;
it’s people that need to be trained and helped.
And at Gilead, you have learned
that Colossians 4:11
says to be “a source of great comfort” or,
as the footnote says,
to be “a strengthening aid” to other people.
Well, now, the question that sits before you now is,
How far will you go?
How far will you go to be fathers and mothers?
to be brothers and sisters to all of these ones?
There has never been a need,
such a great need, for this type of help.
We have now in the world
more of our brothers facing persecution than we have ever seen,
and we expect that that is going to increase.
In some lands, we have lawlessness
on a level previously unheard of,
where kidnapping and rampant violence occur on a daily basis.
And many of our brothers are facing anxieties and pressures
that they have never ever had to experience before.
They need your help;
they need to be strengthened and comforted by you.
Well, sometimes you’re going to feel overwhelmed.
Sometimes you’re going to wonder, ‘What should I do?’
And you won’t know exactly what to do.
Sometimes even your best efforts of working very, very hard
won’t work out the way that you want them to.
But remember that the brothers and sisters
that you’re working with, the people that you’re trying to help,
are wonderful people,
and they will work with you,
and they will support you.
But most of all,
our wonderful and amazing God, Jehovah,
will be there to support you.
Here’s an experience that I just heard
that really brought this to my mind and strengthened it.
It comes from Abaco in the Bahamas.
Now, you remember that just about a week ago,
we had this terrible Hurricane Dorian that struck this part of the world.
The Disaster Relief Committee in the Bahamas
was working very hard to evacuate
our brothers from Abaco Island to Nassau.
Now, they had an airplane.
They worked very hard to have an airplane ready to go in the evening.
And although almost all communication had been cut off with Abaco Island,
they sent a message on all possible channels
for the brothers in Abaco to make their way to the airstrip.
Now, as they were loading the plane with all the necessary materials,
they were told that the government
would not grant permission for the plane to land that day.
Now, the brothers tried everything.
They persisted,
but the government authorities would not budge.
Can you imagine how they felt?
But an hour or so later, much to their surprise,
they heard reports that 14 brothers and sisters
from Abaco would be landing soon in Nassau.
And they wondered, ‘How could this be possible?’
Well, they made preparations immediately
at the Nassau Assembly Hall,
and 14 exhausted, hungry brothers and sisters
arrived who had just been evacuated.
There was a congregation meeting just ending at the Assembly Hall.
The brothers all went out greeting them
and singing our new song “Unfailing Love.”
Can you imagine what the scene must have been there at Nassau?
But, of course, the question was, How could this have happened?
Well, the brothers explained:
“We heard the message to go to the airstrip,
“so we made our journey there.
“A plane arrived, and we thought it was the brothers,
“but it was a company who had a plane circling the island.
“When they saw a group of people at the airstrip,
they landed and evacuated us.”
Everyone was in tears.
Fourteen of the brothers got the message.
They followed the direction.
They assembled to be rescued,
and the Disaster Relief Committee said,
“Jehovah made sure that his people were evacuated to safety.”
Isn’t that wonderful?
So even when your best doesn’t seem to be good enough,
Jehovah will make up for it.
Do your best, and Jehovah will do the rest.
If you have love for God
and you have love for your brothers in your heart,
how far will you go?
You will go very, very far.
Well, we’re looking forward now to our first talk
from a member of the Governing Body, our dear Brother Samuel Herd,
and he is going to give us a very fine warning.
His talk is entitled
“Be Careful! ‘Knowledge Puffs Up.’”
I’m looking at you.
I’m looking at you too.
But you have something that I can’t see.
It’s in your head and in your heart.
It’s knowledge.
You’ve been cramming now for five months,
stuffing things into that brain
and allowing it through meditation
to trickle down into your heart.
So you may feel that you have enough.
“I can’t get any more into the brain.”
But we know better.
There’s still room for you
to put a little more knowledge into the brain.
And you’re going to do that,
but you may feel right now that you are ready to explode.
Don’t you do it.
But here’s something to think about:
“Knowledge puffs up,
but love builds up.”
Now, that’s a scripture found at 1 Corinthians 8:1.
Now, it doesn’t have to be this way,
especially with divine knowledge,
the knowledge that you receive from Jehovah.
It’s not designed to puff you up
and to make you feel better than your neighbors
—your brothers and your sisters—
who may not have the amount of knowledge and education
that you have and what you have just now received.
No, that’s not the purpose of the knowledge that you have acquired
here in Gilead School.
But there is something we have to think about.
What is that?
Well, let’s open our Bibles.
Let’s open our Bibles to 2 Peter,
and let’s take a look
at what is stated here at 2 Peter
the first chapter, verses 5 and 6.
It says: “For this very reason,
“put forth all earnest effort to supply to your faith virtue,
“to your virtue knowledge, to your knowledge self-control,
“to your self-control endurance,
to your endurance godly devotion.”
You see what you must apply to your knowledge?
Self-control.
We can’t allow our mouths to just run wild
with the information that we’ve received
—just spreading it everywhere.
It doesn’t matter who may receive it,
but you have to control
how much knowledge you permit
to flow out of your mouth at a given time.
Self-control is needed.
So that means we should not boast over our accomplishments.
All glory must go to Jehovah God
and not to ourselves.
And it’s easy for others
to feel that we are putting them down a little bit
because of the vast knowledge that we have.
So we have to be careful and control it and not boast.
It reminded me of a story, a fable, I heard years ago
about a little flea by the name of Herman.
Herman the Flea got on the back of a giant elephant.
And he rode on that elephant across the rickety bridge,
and the bridge just shook as if it was going to explode and fall apart.
But they made it to the other side.
And when they made it to the other side and the flea left the elephant
and found his friends,
he bragged about what he was able to do,
along with the elephant,
in making that bridge shake as they crossed it.
Now, how much do you feel that that flea contributed
to the shaking of that bridge?
Now what we’re going to do, though—
We’re going to leave the fable, and we’re going to go to the Bible.
Let’s go to the Bible,
and we’re going to trade that flea in for a grasshopper.
Now, here it is—Isaiah 40:22.
Take a look at it:
“There is One who dwells above the circle of the earth,
“and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers.
“He is stretching out the heavens like a fine gauze,
and he spreads them out like a tent to dwell in.”
Now, what we can do is we can apply this to ourselves.
Now, of course, in this scripture’s context,
Jehovah is really not talking about his people as grasshoppers
but of people with worldly knowledge
that they’ve acquired.
They are like grasshoppers as far as Jehovah is concerned.
You see the whole context of what he’s talking about.
But we’re going to apply it to ourselves
because we are so small in the eyes of Jehovah
that we can be just like a grasshopper
on the back of a giant elephant.
And our accomplishments that we make
are not of our own abilities,
but it’s because of the help that we have
coming from heaven—Jehovah.
And we find that the apostle Paul
set a fine example of not being a braggart.
What did he have?
Well, he had so much knowledge.
In fact, when known as the man Saul of Tarsus,
he was highly educated and was a Pharisee,
and that was viewed as an impeccable Jewish pedigree
that this man had.
But when he wrote letters, he didn’t glorify himself.
For instance, take a look at 1 Corinthians chapter 2,
and read along with me verses 1 through 5.
And you’ll find that he did not allow knowledge to puff him up.
This is how it reads:
“So when I came to you, brothers, I did not come with extravagant speech
“or wisdom declaring the sacred secret of God to you.
“For I decided not to know anything among you except Jesus Christ,
“and him executed on the stake.
“And I came to you in weakness and in fear and with much trembling;
“and my speech and what I preached were
“not with persuasive words of wisdom
“but with a demonstration of spirit and power,
“so that your faith might be,
“not in men’s wisdom,
but in God’s power.”
There’s the example.
Let’s try our best to follow that example
and not be like men and women of the world
who attend these great universities.
And they come out, and they’re able to get doctorate degrees
in science or this or that, and they kind of show all that off.
But we’re not like that.
But we could be if we’re not careful.
Now, the Bible shows
what worldly wisdom can accomplish and what it cannot accomplish.
For instance, in Ecclesiastes 1:16-18,
the account starts off this way.
It says: “Then I said in my heart: ‘Look!
“‘I have acquired great wisdom,
“‘more than anyone who was before me in Jerusalem,
and my heart gained a great deal of wisdom and knowledge.’”
It goes on: “I applied my heart to knowing wisdom
“and to knowing madness and to knowing folly,
“and this too is a chasing after the wind.
“For an abundance of wisdom brings an abundance of frustration,
so that whoever increases knowledge increases pain.”
Now, if you’ve got a little whiff of that,
Know-it-all,
then blow it away.
Move away from it.
You don’t want to think that way.
Let’s never try to be a know-it-all.
Jesus doesn’t know everything that he has been learning
from Jehovah for aeons of time.
Now, how long is an aeon?
An aeon is a really, really, superlong,
impossible-to-measure length of time.
That’s an aeon.
Only Jehovah knows everything.
Keep that in mind.
There is nothing beyond his understanding.
How do we know that?
Well, the Bible tells us.
That same chapter where he mentions a grasshopper
—Isaiah chapter 40—
but this time verses 13 and 14 say:
“Who has taken the measurements of the spirit of Jehovah,
“and who can instruct him as [an] adviser?
“With whom did he consult to gain understanding,
“or who teaches him in the path of justice, or teaches him knowledge,
or shows him the way of true understanding?”
Think about it.
We can know what we need to know
at the time we need to know it.
Now, that’s a mouthful!
Or should we say, “a headful”?
Yes, all of you graduates of Gilead School,
please share with others what you’ve learned here at Gilead School.
Don’t walk away from this talk thinking you should keep your mouths closed.
We’re not saying that.
But control what you say and when you say it
and to whom you tell it to.
So we know that you’ve learned so much at this school,
but share it discreetly.
Keep in mind these words of King Solomon.
He says: “There is an appointed time for everything, . . .
a time to be silent and a time to speak.”
Don’t point to yourselves; point heavenward.
Always glorify Jehovah; point to Jehovah.
Now, Governing Body members —all of us—
we have to be very careful ourselves
because we get credit for things that we are not responsible for.
Brothers will come and hug you:
“Oh, thank you, brother, you Governing Body member
—you really, wow, whoo, how, wah!”
Now, we know we didn’t do anything.
You could have done what we did if you’d been in our seat.
It’s Jehovah’s spirit that causes these things to happen.
Now, it’s true that we’re tools that he uses,
but he’s the One.
Now, we’re not saying that you can’t say,
“Thank you, brother, for what you’re doing, the work that you do.”
No, we’re not saying that.
It’s just—
Be careful that you’re not glorifying men,
but glorify God.
The Governing Body gets credit that we don’t deserve.
It belongs to Jehovah and Jesus,
and we haven’t been able to close the mouths
of over eight million bleating sheep.
But we will keep trying.
So in conclusion,
be like the grasshopper that rode on the back of the elephant.
Stay close to Jehovah, and enjoy the ride;
but always give Him the credit
for your accomplishments.
Well, we thank you so much, Brother Herd,
for that excellent warning for us.
Of course, the one day I mention insects in my introduction,
Brother Herd uses insects in his talk.
I guess we do need to know about insects.
Well, now we’re looking forward to hearing
from a helper to the Service Committee of the Governing Body,
Brother Christopher Mavor,
and Brother Mavor is going to speak to us on the topic
“‘Count Your Days.’”
Isn’t it true that we often “count our days” when we anticipate an exciting event?
And no doubt you Gilead students
were counting your days in anticipation of this day.
And then, if you were, you know that today is
the 138th day of your Gilead School experience.
But after today, will you continue to ‘count your days’?
Should you?
To answer that question, please open your Bibles to the 90th Psalm,
and it’s a prayer that Moses said to Jehovah.
And notice what Moses asked him in verse 12:
“Teach us how to count our days
so that we may acquire a heart of wisdom.”
So the answer to this question is, Yes, we should continue to count our days.
But what does that mean—count your days?
And why will we need God’s help to do it?
The answer is this:
because we are dedicated servants of Jehovah God.
Each and every day, we need to make sure that we are using it
in his service to bring him glory.
Now, we’re imperfect, so this is not always easy to do.
In fact, if we look at verse 10 of the 90th Psalm,
we notice that Moses said that our days are few
and they are filled with a lot of difficulties.
So we need God’s help to fulfill our dedication.
Yes, we need to count our days, and Jehovah promises
that he will be there to help us.
Notice this promise at Isaiah 30:21.
Jehovah says: “And your own ears will hear a word behind you saying,
“‘This is the way.
“Walk in it,’
in case you should go to the right or in case you should go to the left.”
So the reality is that we need Jehovah
to help us to live a dedicated life to him.
Thankfully, we don’t need to figure it out on our own.
He’s there to guide and direct us.
But did you note what he expects of us?
Looking back at that scripture, he says that when he tells you something,
“walk in it.”
That’s an emphatic statement, isn’t it?
It doesn’t leave any doubt.
We need to do it and make it happen in our life.
We cannot be passive about our dedication.
You know, as Christians, we live a very busy life.
We have various events to go to.
And especially if you’re in full-time service,
well, you are given an assignment
and oftentimes that assignment is spelled out for you,
and even the schedule in which to accomplish that work is set for us.
We don’t really need to think too much about it.
Now, if we’re not careful,
we could just get carried along with the flow of time
and the flow of the work and not remember
why we are doing it and who we are doing it for.
In fact, we could become like this fine young brother on a raft.
He is enjoying himself; he’s going with the flow of the time.
But is he really mindful of where he is going and why?
He’s sitting down; he’s looking all around.
The oar is not in his hand.
He’s not actively steering his life; he’s passive.
Now, being passive in our dedication to Jehovah
is a very dangerous situation
because as Ecclesiastes 9:11 tells us:
‘Time and unexpected events overtake us.’
Now this fine brother is about to get a rude awakening.
An unexpected rock has popped up.
A sudden storm of difficulties has overtaken him.
Because he was passive, he was caught off guard.
He lost his balance.
Now he’s suffering spiritual shipwreck.
He did not count his days.
He forgot to listen to Jehovah God
and to pay attention to his dedication in his life.
He wasn’t listening.
Jesus emphasized that it’s so important for us
not to be passive about our dedication to God.
At Luke 13:24, Jesus made it clear
that we are to ‘exert ourselves vigorously,’
not just at a work assignment,
but in our life as a Christian
—being personally involved in what we are doing in our Christian dedication.
The apostle Paul also gave good counsel to the young man Timothy
that we benefit from today.
At 1 Timothy 4:7, you’ll recall that Paul said:
“Train yourself
with godly devotion as your aim.”
Now, when we’re training ourselves, that means we’re not finished yet;
we’re still in the competition; we’re still in training.
Godly devotion must be something that we personally do
for ourselves and work at it.
It just doesn’t happen on its own.
But thankfully, Jehovah helps us.
He’s given us his Word, the Bible.
He’s given us his organization, which helps us apply Bible principles in our life
and gives us warnings on the things to look out for.
It’s up to us to do it.
It’s as if Jehovah gives us the oar,
and he says, ‘Now pick it up, and use it in your stream of time.’
And when we do, then we’re like this young brother now.
He’s taking a firm hold on the oar.
He’s using it even during peaceful times in his life,
making sure that his life is continuing on in a faithful Christian course.
Then, when he encounters temptations or trials,
well, he’s got his oar in his hand.
Jehovah is there to help him and to guide and direct him,
to navigate through the difficult times.
It takes effort; it can be distressing,
but Jehovah has given us the means
to navigate through these difficult times and to continue on in pursuing
our dedicated Christian life.
Jesus set the perfect example in this.
Every day, Jesus relied heavily on Jehovah’s direction.
He did not take it for granted.
But Jesus knew that when he was sent to the earth, he had an assignment;
he was on a very strict time budget.
It was humanly impossible, really,
for a man, even a perfect man,
to accomplish what Jesus did.
He relied on Jehovah.
He did not take a casual viewpoint of it,
but every day he looked to Jehovah
to help him to apply the principles that he learned through His Word
—the direction that he received from Jehovah God
in going through this difficult assignment.
And Jesus knew at the end of the day
—after the things he preached and the things he did—
He knew that that was a miracle.
He said so at John 14:10.
He said: “The Father who remains in union with me is doing his works.”
He knew that Jehovah was backing him up,
and Jesus worked with Jehovah.
He didn’t take a casual view of it.
Now, we can have the same kind of confidence in Jehovah.
He is there for us, even when we are encountering something
that we feel is humanly impossible.
We have a good example of that.
There was a couple who graduated in the 24th class of Gilead.
Their names are Malcolm and Grace Allen.
Now, their life story is in the October 15, 2013, Watchtower,
and it’s really worthwhile reading.
We will find that in their early life they both pioneered;
they got married; they pioneered together;
they were in the circuit work for a number of years;
they were invited to Gilead;
and after Gilead, they were assigned to Brooklyn Bethel.
And there Brother Allen served in some very responsible positions,
and his wife was a housekeeper.
They loved their Bethel service.
But 25 years into their Bethel career,
their course in life took a sudden change —a detour.
Unexpectedly,
both sets of parents became very ill and needy,
and it became apparent that they would have to relinquish their Bethel service
and full-time service in order to care for them.
Now, mind you, at this point in their life, they’re both in their late 50’s.
They used their youth in service to God, so Brother Allen did not really have
a secular career or a skill on which to go back to.
He needed to start in his late 50’s
to be the breadwinner of the family.
Sister Allen now needed to take care of both sets of parents.
This was a sharp change in events for them,
but they held firm to their oar
that Jehovah God had given them.
They learned to rely on Jehovah God and to lean on him
every inch of the way, and they were successful.
Brother Allen found a job as an insurance salesman,
which provided for the family.
And they kept going, even though it was stressful times.
They were successful.
Now, eventually, their parents died, and they thought,
‘Well, maybe we can return to Bethel service.’
But unfortunately, at this point in their life,
their own health and age overtook them.
And now they had to be content with being
good, local, congregation publishers.
How did they view this?
Was this a view of failure on their part?
Did they think, ‘I failed’ or ‘I’m bitter because of things that happened’?
Well, Brother Allen makes this very profound statement
about life in Jehovah’s service.
This is what he says:
“Life is unpredictable at times, uncertain,
“and even hard to deal with.
“But Jehovah blesses those who lean on him, not on their own understanding.
“This is what my wife and I have experienced
over our long and rewarding life.”
They rejoiced in their life as dedicated servants of God
by taking advantage of every opportunity to express
their dedication to him
and pursuing and practicing godly devotion in their life.
And they saw Jehovah’s hand
in their life in truly miraculous ways.
Now, they will experience another miracle of God,
because both of them are now sleeping in the grave.
But we know that Jehovah has already calculated the days
when he will resurrect Malcolm and Grace
and bring them back to life so that they can continue serving him
in a dedicated way for an eternity of days to come.
This is certainly a good lesson for all of us:
to count our days and to be fully invested in our journey
as a dedicated Christian to Jehovah.
Therefore, you Gilead students and really all of us,
let us continue to lean on Jehovah
and to work vigorously at doing what Jehovah directs us to do
during these difficult last days —living up to our dedication to God!
And by doing so, we can be assured
that we too will be blessed by Jehovah.
He will give us an eternity of days to enjoy
in his glorious new world soon to come.
Well, we thank you very much, Brother Mavor,
for that very good reminder.
Well, now we have the privilege to hear
from one of our more recently appointed helpers to the Governing Body
—Brother Leonard Myers— a helper to the Writing Committee.
He’s going to speak to us on the topic
“‘You Trusted in Me.’”
“You trusted in me.”
Now, you may be saying: “Brother Myers, I don’t even know you.
How can I trust in you?”
And it’s true that we need to have a relationship
with an individual to truly trust him.
But the “me” in our talk title isn’t referring to any human;
it’s referring to our trustworthy God, Jehovah.
And that phrase “you trusted in me” was stated
by Jehovah to the faithful man Ebed-melech.
Why could Jehovah tell him that?
And how can his example help you students?
Well, turn with me, please, to Jeremiah chapter 38.
And as we review his example, look for ways
that Ebed-melech trusted in Jehovah.
Now, as you know, Ebed-melech was an Ethiopian eunuch
employed in the house of King Zedekiah,
and he was a friend of the prophet Jeremiah.
At the time, Jerusalem was under siege by the Babylonians,
and Jeremiah had repeatedly declared that this city was doomed.
He had encouraged the people to save themselves by surrendering.
Now, that enraged certain princes who were Zedekiah’s advisers.
They were determined to defend the city at all costs,
and Jeremiah was an obstacle to that defense.
Well, if you look in verse 4 of Jeremiah chapter 38,
the princes went to Zedekiah, and they accused Jeremiah of weakening
the morale of the soldiers and all the people.
Weak king that he was, Zedekiah stated in verse 5:
“Look! He is in your hands,
for the king cannot do anything to stop you.”
Well, we know what that resulted in.
Those princes had Jeremiah lowered into a miry, muddy cistern.
With the food supply being virtually exhausted in Jerusalem,
there was no hope of Jeremiah receiving food from anyone.
His death was just a matter of time.
Well, in stepped Ebed-melech.
He heard what those princes had done, and trusting in Jehovah,
he approached the king, not privately and not secretly,
but in public at one of the city gates.
And notice what he stated in verse 9:
“O my lord the king,
“what these men have done to Jeremiah the prophet is evil!
“They have thrown him into the cistern,
“and he will die there because of the famine,
for there is no bread left in the city.”
And what was the result of his bold action and trust in Jehovah?
The king stated in verse 10:
“Take 30 men with you from here,
and pull Jeremiah the prophet up out of the cistern before he dies.”
Now, 30 men certainly would have served as a protection.
Yet, Ebed-melech may still have feared what those princes would do to him.
But his concern was outweighed by his friendship
and respect for Jehovah’s prophet
and by his trust in Jehovah.
And as we know, verses 11-13 outline his successful rescue mission.
But why could Ebed-melech be so courageous
when he approached the king and rescued Jeremiah?
It was because he trusted in Jehovah.
And because of that trust, notice how Jehovah would reward him.
In chapter 39, we’ll start reading in the B  portion of verse 16.
Notice Jehovah’s words through Jeremiah to Ebed-melech:
“‘Here I am fulfilling my words on this city for calamity and not for good,
“‘and in that day you will see it happen.
“But I will rescue you in that day,’ declares Jehovah,
“‘and you will not be handed over to the men you fear.
“‘For I will surely provide you with escape, and you will not fall by the sword.
“‘You will have your life as a spoil,
because you trusted in me.’”
Ebed-melech didn’t need to fear.
As he had viewed Jeremiah’s life as precious,
so Jehovah viewed his life as precious
and would preserve him alive
—all because, as verse 18 says, ‘he trusted in Jehovah.’
Now, whether he was deported to Babylon and died a natural death
or was left back in the land of Judah, the Bible doesn’t say,
but his life would be spared,
and he could continue to worship the God in whom he trusted.
At this point, Ebed-melech vanishes from Bible history
but not his name nor the example that he set for you and me
to trust in Jehovah.
Now, this thought of trusting in Jehovah isn’t new to you students.
Trusting in Jehovah got you to Gilead.
In your assignments at Bethel or the field,
you proved your trust in God.
Trust helped you through your studies at Gilead.
Do you remember the times when you prayed for Jehovah’s help
with an assignment or a test
or, as one recent graduate said, “when your brain was full and you needed
a full week off to digest all the material”?
Remember those times?
See, that took trust that Jehovah would help you.
And as you look to the future, trusting in Jehovah
will help you to be successful in your assignments.
Notice these comments from graduates of the last class of Gilead.
One brother wrote: “We have placed our lives in Jehovah’s hands.
“We pray to Jehovah with an intensity and trust
that never existed before.”
Another brother wrote:
“At times I have felt like, ‘What do we do?’
“Then I’m reminded that we confidently leave the matter in Jehovah’s hands,
trusting that he will handle it or make clear to us the course to take.”
And finally another brother wrote:
“At times we have felt quite overwhelmed
“with the new language, responsibilities, culture, and so forth.
“However, our trust in Jehovah
“reminds us that this is his organization
“—his work— and they are his sheep.
“If we do our part and work hard, there is no doubt that he’ll help us.
We never have to rely on ourselves.”
Like Ebed-melech, trusting in Jehovah
will help you to be successful in your assignments.
Here are two ways that you can add to your trust.
(1) Trusting in Jehovah
involves trusting in the power of holy spirit.
For example, trusting in that spirit will help you
to deal with your brothers and sisters.
Now, your assignments will involve close contact with them.
Will there be challenges at times?
Very likely. We’re all imperfect.
Trust that holy spirit can help you to cultivate the love,
peace, patience, mildness, and self-control
that you’ll need to deal with those situations.
(2) Trusting in Jehovah means
trusting those whom he trusts.
Jehovah has arranged for “the faithful and discreet slave”
to care for earthly Kingdom interests.
Trust in the appointment of the slave,
trust in Jehovah’s arrangement,
follow any direction that the slave provides.
Those are two ways that you can add to your trust in Jehovah.
We encourage you to trust in Jehovah,
especially when you face challenging situations.
During those times, remember scriptures such as these:
Proverbs 3:5:
“Trust in Jehovah with all your heart,
and do not rely on your own understanding”;
Psalm 56:3, 4:
“When I am afraid, I put my trust in you.
“In God —whose word I praise—
in God I put my trust”;
and Isaiah 26:3, 4:
“You will safeguard those who fully lean on you;
“you will give them continuous peace,
“because it is in you that they trust.
Trust in Jehovah forever.”
Scriptures like those can really help you during challenging times.
Trust got you here to Gilead,
trust helped you through your studies,
and trust in Jehovah will help you in your assignments.
Like Ebed-melech, continue to trust in Jehovah.
You know, one day I hope to get to know all of you students.
Then we can truly say that we trust one another.
Until then, continue to trust in Jehovah
so that he can say of you dear Gilead students:
“You trusted in me.”
Well, we thank you for that excellent advice, Brother Myers.
And now we’re looking forward to hearing from one of the Gilead instructors,
and I’m sure all the students are going to be interested to hear what he has to say.
Brother James Cauthon is going to speak to us on the subject
“Shaken but Not Forsaken.”
Congratulations.
Today, you become a graduate of the 147th class of Gilead.
It’s a day to be celebrated; it’s a day to be enjoyed.
And you deserve it; you worked hard.
And even when you thought you had reached your limit,
you didn’t give up.
You kept coming in; you kept trusting in Jehovah.
As your instructors, we’re very pleased
to see your happy, smiling faces.
And if we could, we’d wish that for you
every day for the rest of your lives.
However, as much as we try,
we can’t control what happens to us in life, isn’t that true?
A change comes for everyone.
Sooner or later, it’s inevitable.
Some changes are small.
Other changes, however, can rock our world
and leave us shaken to the core.
And when that happens, we may suddenly find
that we’re no longer the person we thought we were.
It can seem as if our very identity
has been ripped away from us.
Consider Moses.
Moses grew up in one of the most luxuriant places on earth at the time,
that is, the Egyptian royal court.
Members of the royal household resided in opulent mansions
that were dotted along the Nile.
These homes were decorated in precious stones,
incorporated with pools and gardens.
They housed a large staff that prepared lavish meals.
Moses likely had a knowledge and understanding of some
of the most amazing structures the world has ever seen, and why?
Likely, it’s because he was schooled from a young age
in subjects such as writing,
math, science, and architecture.
In addition,
Moses may have witnessed Egypt’s rise to become a mighty empire
and a powerful military force.
Moses enjoyed a privileged and extravagant upbringing,
and no doubt he became a man of confidence and influence.
Acts 7:22 says:
“So Moses was instructed in all the wisdom of the Egyptians.
In fact, he was powerful in his words and deeds.”
So when he killed an Egyptian on behalf of his fellow Hebrew brother,
he saw himself as a deliverer.
He was confident,
he was ready, but he was wrong.
We know what happened.
He fled to Midian.
He was no longer the favorite prince and no longer in charge of anyone
except some sheep.
The confidence he knew back in Egypt
had been replaced with confusion, loss, and fear.
Moses must have been shaken.
So often, disappointments in life bring on feelings of sadness,
self-doubt, and worthlessness.
And those things, in effect, strip us of our cherished identity.
And we’re especially vulnerable
if we define ourselves by our natural skills and qualities
or by what others think of us
or even by our assignment or position.
In effect, when we do that, we’re saying:
“I am what I do” or “I am what others think of me.”
These are deceptive filters
that cause us to lose sight of who we really are
and, then, when change comes, we’re shaken.
But are we forsaken?
Let’s consider Moses again.
Moses was the chosen one to—
Was Moses the chosen one to deliver the Hebrews?
Well, the answer is yes.
Was it Jehovah’s time?
The answer is no,
and neither was he fully qualified for the appointment
or the assignment.
You see, he needed divine training,
and that was something that he could not get in Egypt.
It’s true that he had worldly education; he had confidence; he had poise,
but he needed the qualities of patience, meekness,
humility, and self-control to be developed to a greater degree.
Jehovah saw that,
and he knew just how to accomplish it.
That would be the lowly occupation of being a shepherd in Midian.
Now, after 40 years,
Moses sees the flaming thorn bush,
and to his surprise and shock,
Jehovah commissions him 40 years later.
Now think about how Moses must have felt at that moment
—the realization that he wasn’t worthless
and that Jehovah still valued him.
His daily pain of heart over the suffering of his fellow Hebrews
was now being replaced with a keen anticipation
for what Jehovah was going to do,
and no doubt in a marvelous way.
So, you see, Moses was never really forsaken by God.
No.
Rather, Jehovah had been with him every step of the way
during those 40 years,
molding him and preparing him for an incredible future assignment
that he could never have possibly imagined.
Jehovah will do the same for you.
You see, he takes a long-range view.
He sees your potential.
He knows how to accomplish it.
And remember that Jehovah will do it at the right time
and at his time
and that his view must be our view.
So when a change comes, whatever it may be,
it’s just the scene;
it’s not the entire movie;
it’s a chapter; it’s not the book.
You may not know what’s coming next, but don’t worry,
Jehovah does.
Decades later, after leading Jehovah’s people out of Egypt
and navigating through the wilderness,
it was now time for Joshua to step up.
At Deuteronomy 31:8
Moses said to Joshua:
“Jehovah . . . will neither desert you nor abandon you.”
Those must have been very encouraging words.
You see, Moses never forgot the lesson he learned all those years ago.
He had been shaken, yes,
but he was not forsaken.
And perhaps that was his motivation for writing another passage in the Bible.
See if you remember this:
“Anyone dwelling in the secret place of the Most High
“will lodge under the shadow of the Almighty.
“I will say to Jehovah:
“‘You are my refuge and my stronghold,
my God in whom I trust.’”
Does that sound familiar?—Psalm 91.
Moses had become absolutely convinced
that Jehovah was always with him
through the good times and through the hard times.
So like Moses,
you’ll experience joys
and some disappointments
and, sooner or later, change
—perhaps a change away from a cherished assignment.
It may feel devastating.
You can either roll with it or you can be rolled over by it.
How will you roll with it?
You can roll with it if you remember
that you’re not your career;
you’re not your assignment; you’re not your privilege.
You are, however, loved by God,
you have a spiritual heritage,
and you have a wonderful, bright future.
And when you remember that,
you can gracefully accept the changes that come.
And there’s something else you can do:
You can use your experience to help others.
In fact, your willingness to help others even when you’re shaken
by a personal experience,
will reveal your loyalty and your maturity.
Do little things as if they were great things.
Small tasks reveal a big heart.
It’s all a part of our training now and for life in the new world.
And remember this too:
A change of circumstances is rarely as important
as a change of attitude.
So it’s not your position,
but it will be your disposition
that will bring Jehovah’s blessing.
So in conclusion: Yes, change will come.
The world changes;
circumstances change; we change.
However, Jehovah does not change,
his Word does not change,
and his love for you will never change.
So while you may be shaken at times,
rest assured, you will never ever be forsaken.
Well, I don’t know about you, but I marked down,
“It’s not your position; it’s your disposition.”
I’ll be using that one in the future.
Thank you very, very much, Brother Cauthon,
for those excellent thoughts.
Well, now we have the privilege to hear
from another of the Gilead instructors, Brother Mark Noumair.
He’s going to speak to us on the topic
“Remember the Vision.”
One of the rarest privileges
a human has ever had
is to see a vision of Jehovah’s throne.
And it’s good for us now
to look on with a man
who had this privilege
and how the vision changed his life.
What were the circumstances around this event?
And more importantly for you, how does it affect you?
And what lessons do we want you to take to heart?
So please open your Bibles
or listen closely to these words
recorded at Isaiah 6:1.
Isaiah 6:1:
“In the year that King Uzziah died,
“I saw Jehovah sitting
“on a lofty and elevated throne,
and the skirts of his robe filled the temple.”
The skirts of Jehovah’s magnificent garment
filling the temple
—this is what Isaiah saw.
What does it show?
It shows that Jehovah was figuratively present in the temple
and that he was keenly aware of everything
that was going on there,
including what had happened with King Uzziah.
Now, recall that Uzziah
was not content with his role as king.
What did he do?
He forced his way into the holy compartment of the temple.
Why?
To burn incense like a priest.
And for that, he was struck with leprosy.
But it is of interest
that Jehovah inspired Isaiah to write,
not in the year
that Jotham (Uzziah’s son) became king,
but, rather, “in the year that King Uzziah died.”
By directing Isaiah to pen those words
in the year that Uzziah died,
it could be said that Jehovah was setting the stage
for teaching Isaiah what qualities he loves
and what qualities he hates.
So you see, this vision is going to be
life-changing for Isaiah,
and we want it to be life-changing for you.
So, what happens next?
Well, verse 2 shows that Jehovah reveals something
perhaps no other human has seen in vision
—seraphs.
Isaiah is the only Bible writer that mentions them.
Now, the privileges these seraphs enjoy
—their high rank and serving close to the Universal Sovereign—
move them to humbly cover their faces
with their wings
and sing Jehovah’s praises with such power
that the temple foundation shakes.
What lesson in contrast
could Jehovah have been impressing on Isaiah?
Well, consider this:
Uzziah became king at only 16 years old
and showed tremendous potential at the outset.
When Isaiah became a prophet,
he too was a young man, most likely in his twenties.
He was married to a supportive wife; she’s called a prophetess.
So by showing Isaiah the example of these humble seraphs
in the same year Uzziah died,
it was as if Jehovah was saying:
‘You know, Isaiah, you’re a fine young man.
‘You have a bright future.
‘You have a good wife.
But don’t become presumptuous like Uzziah.’
What a powerful contrast for Isaiah to meditate on!
No doubt this affected him deeply.
And this is your first lesson:
Like Isaiah, you have a bright future.
Don’t miss the purpose of why you’ve been called to Gilead.
Your assignment is to honor Jehovah God.
You’ve been trained to support his organization.
We are investing in you for the future.
So remember the vision.
Imitate the seraphs.
Cover your face,
and don’t spoil your humility
by drawing undue attention to yourself.
You see, even the most subtle boasting
invites others to take a peek at you and look in.
‘Who are you? What are you doing?’
No, that detracts from Jehovah’s glory.
So when tempted to blow your own horn,
remember the mighty song of the seraphs.
Sing Jehovah’s praises, not your own.
Any privilege you receive
should make you more humble like the seraphs,
not puff you up like Uzziah.
And by remaining humble, Jehovah can use you to a greater extent.
Why?
Because he can trust you to give him the glory.
Seraphs —they don’t aspire to be kings;
they don’t aspire to be priests.
But they’re content with their role as workers.
So be like the seraphs by doing your part
to advance pure worship.
What else could Isaiah learn from this song?
Well, chapter 6, verse 3b says:
“The whole earth is filled with his glory.”
Now, that’s an interesting statement.
Why may Jehovah have included those words as part of the vision?
Well, consider this:
Isaiah was faced with extreme apathy in his assignment.
The land of Judah was full of false worship.
The rebellious ten-tribe kingdom of Samaria had rejected Jehovah.
To Isaiah, it could have felt like no one was glorifying Jehovah.
‘Where’s the glory for Jehovah?’
If he focused on those trials,
it could have been so easy for him to get discouraged, to give up.
‘What’s the use? Why should I put up with this?
No one is listening.’
So, what would help him not to give up?
He would need to go back to the vision
and imagine a future time
of the whole earth being filled with Jehovah’s glory.
And with eyes of faith, Isaiah would focus on what Jehovah
was yet to accomplish as part of His purpose.
Jehovah strengthened Isaiah with prophecies about the future
when the whole earth would be filled with His glory
—prophecies about the Messiah and the restoration of true worship.
Isaiah himself even witnessed
the prophecy being fulfilled in his own lifetime
—the fall of the ten-tribe kingdom to the Assyrians.
Then more than 40 years later after his hard work,
imagine, he was honored to record
one of the most spectacular demonstrations
of God’s executional power in all Scripture
—the destruction of 185,000 soldiers in one night.
An outstanding reminder:
‘Isaiah, my glory is indeed filling the whole earth.’
It was as if Jehovah was saying:
‘Isaiah, listen;
‘I know you see badness among people,
‘but keep your focus.
‘Focus on the good things that I’m accomplishing right now
and will accomplish in the future.’
And this is lesson number two for you:
When you find yourself becoming consumed with trials
—the imperfections of others
(maybe some you work with two, three, four, five here and there),
the frustrations of the work,
being passed over again for a privilege,
and you start thinking: ‘What’s the use of working hard?
‘Why am I trying so hard to apply the good training I’ve received at Gilead?
No one here cares’
—take a deep breath.
Back away;
return to the vision;
shift the focus off yourself and onto the big picture,
which is the whole earth being filled with Jehovah’s glory.
Put your focus on the 8.5 million people earth wide
who are glorifying Jehovah God in his great spiritual temple.
Each one is playing a small but valuable role
in accomplishing Jehovah’s purpose.
If you do that, it will help you to cherish
your place in God’s global arrangement.
Next comes the invitation.
The invitation —here it comes.
And that invitation in verse 8
is so real, so vivid, to Isaiah that he’s moved to declare:
“Here I am! [Here I am!] Send me!”
No hesitation —he didn’t ask what he would gain.
He didn’t ask what other assignments his contemporary prophets got.
‘What about that one? What about this one?
What’s Micah going to do? Hosea and what—?’
No.
He just said: “Here I am! Send me!”
Isn’t that amazing?
And the fact is he didn’t know everything he was signing up for.
Those details would come later,
and they did
—about 17 years later.
Now Isaiah is told to take his small son Shear-jashub
and go meet King Ahaz —wicked King Ahaz—
and offer him help.
I mean, can you imagine?
Isaiah —what was he thinking?
‘Now, wait a minute, wait a minute, Jehovah.
‘Ahaz murders his own children,
‘and now you want me to take my son along?
I said: “Here I am! Send me—not us.”’
And what about his wife?
What about his wife?
‘Isaiah, you’re not taking my little boy.
Shear-jashub, get back here.’
I mean, you don’t know, but it just helps you to think about this.
So both Isaiah and his wife
would need to return to the vision for reassurance
that Jehovah’s skirts, his attention, was indeed filling Judah.
He was aware of everything.
They would need to trust in Jehovah —follow his direction.
Isaiah, in effect, said: ‘I’ll go; I’ll go.
I’ll be faithful even if the king is not.’
Isaiah did not let the tests of others make him fail his.
Lesson number three:
Assignments to support the Kingdom work
are not always easy,
and you wives feel it too.
When your husband receives an assignment perhaps no one else wants,
you play a crucial role.
How will you respond when he tells you of the assignment?
‘Why did they pick you?
‘Can’t you tell them to find someone else?
You did it last time.’
Or will you be proud of your husband
—proud of him for being Isaiah-like,
accepting the assignments faithfully,
even volunteering for them?
You wives, your support is priceless in God’s eyes,
and it can make all the difference.
How do you think Isaiah remembered the vision?
No doubt he recalled not only the images but the sounds
of Jehovah’s skirts stretching,
filling the temple;
the seraphs’ powerful wings beating through the air;
the melodious words echoing in song.
They would no doubt be permanently etched in his mind.
We can only imagine that Isaiah and his wife
replayed that vision over and over again in their minds.
And how it must have helped them to hold on to Jehovah
and never let go for those 40 plus years.
And the vision can do the same for you.
That’s the point.
This inspired vision, this holy scripture,
can help you to stick to Jehovah and never let go,
especially when times are hard.
When you are struggling to keep afloat spiritually,
you have a challenge you have to overcome,
you might even feel at times like you’re swimming in mud,
don’t give up.
Make the vision come alive in your mind.
See the images; hear the sounds;
feel the awe Isaiah must have felt.
And then —and then apply the lessons in your life.
Apply these wonderful Scriptural lessons in your life.
Imitate the seraphs: Cover your face; stay humble.
See God’s glory filling the whole earth.
Focus on the big picture.
Keep ablaze the “Here I am! Send me!” fire.
Yes, remember the vision
and let it motivate you to keep your cherished place
in God’s great spiritual temple now
and in Jehovah’s heart for all eternity.
Well, we thank you so much, Brother Noumair, for those excellent thoughts.
It truly was a spiritually enriching Gilead program.
And in the coming weeks,
Parts 2 and 3 of the graduation
will be released on JW Broadcasting,
so keep on the lookout.
We’ll conclude this month’s program by traveling to the island of Réunion,
located in the Indian Ocean
between Madagascar
and Mauritius.
It’s decorated with beautiful volcanic sand beaches,
waterfalls,
deep valleys, rugged peaks,
and one of the most active volcanoes on earth,
Piton de la Fournaise.
The first Kingdom publisher arrived to Réunion in 1955.
Now more than 3,000
of our brothers and sisters are serving there;
over 400 of them are regular pioneers.
While French is the official language of the island,
there are 3 congregations in Malagasy
and 13 in the common tongue of Creole of Réunion.
Because of the brothers’ evangelizing spirit,
over 6,500 people on Réunion attended the Memorial
This is the Grand Bois Congregation.
They have more than 130 publishers,
with 13 regular pioneers.
And as of May 2019,
they were conducting 61 Bible studies.
And here is the Salazie Creole Congregation,
with just 21 publishers.
But they conduct 13 Bible studies!
These warm and hospitable brothers and sisters
in both Grand Bois and Salazie Creole
are working hard to proclaim the Kingdom message.
We love our brothers in Réunion and send them our greetings.
And we love all of you faithful ones
who are viewing this program.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting!

JW电视节目
自从守望台基列圣经学校
在1943年2月1日开办以来
有数千位弟兄姐妹
在这个学校对圣经进行了深入的学习
他们都获益不浅
经过几个月高强度的学习
大家终于迎来了毕业的这一天
在这个月

en.text: The whole obligation
and privilege of mankind
is to develop a relationship
with our God and Maker, Jehovah.
But the question is,
How do we develop that relationship?
And then, How do we keep it?
Well, let’s start with, How do we develop it?
If you open to Ecclesiastes 12:13,
note the two components mentioned in this verse
—Ecclesiastes 12:13.
It says: “The conclusion of the matter,
“everything having been heard, is:
“Fear the true God and keep his commandments,
for this is the whole obligation of man.”
So the obligation begins with fearing the true God
and then keeping his commandments.
So, what does it mean to fear?
What kind of fear are we talking about?
The Insight book says this:
“The fear of God is healthful;
“it is an awe
“and a profound reverence for the Creator
“and a wholesome dread of displeasing him.
“This fear of incurring his displeasure
“is a result of appreciation
“of his loving-kindness and goodness
“together with the realization that he is the Supreme Judge
and the Almighty.”
So how does one come to have this awe of God?
Well, as the text says today that we’ve already read,
‘we first hear about his fame
and about all he has done.’
Now, it’s of interest that just simply hearing
and knowing what he does
does not necessarily lead to awe
or to the kind of awe
that will help us develop a relationship with him.
The Scriptures explain this if you go to Joshua chapter 9,
where we read about a group of Canaanite kings.
In Joshua chapter 9
and in verse 1, it says:
“When all the kings who were on the west side of the Jordan
heard what had happened.”
Well, what did they hear that had happened?
Well, of course, the stories of the Exodus of Israel out of Egypt
was one thing they heard
and also the mighty acts of Jehovah God in connection with his people.
And then when Israel first penetrated Canaan
after crossing the Jordan,
they set up a camp at Gilgal,
which was not far from the walled city of Jericho.
And these Canaanite kings
had heard about what Jehovah did at Jericho
—the great destruction there in behalf of his people.
And remember, Rahab was spared, and her family was spared,
because when she heard about the mighty acts of Jehovah God,
it moved her to put faith in him.
Now, if you just glance through Joshua chapter 8,
we find that following that great destruction,
they went to Ai —the city of Ai.
And Jehovah God had instructed them how to ambush that city,
which led to the destruction there.
So after hearing those acts of Jehovah and then many other acts of Jehovah,
what did it do to the Canaanite kings?
Were they moved with awe?
Well, let’s read chapter 9, verse 2.
It says: “They formed an alliance
to fight against Joshua and Israel.”
So it had the opposite effect upon them, didn’t it?
But now, notice the different reaction it had upon the Gibeonites.
Now, they heard the very same reports,
and in chapter 9 and verse 9, it says:
“At this they said to him:
“‘Your servants have come from a very distant land
“‘out of regard for the name of Jehovah your God,
“‘because we have heard about his fame
“‘and about all he did in Egypt
and about all he did to the two kings of the Amorites.’”
So in this case,
they heard it and it led to their awe,
which led to their developing a relationship with Jehovah God.
Well, today, the same thing is true
that the mighty acts of Jehovah God
are all around us.
And those that are “rightly disposed”
recognize them and are moved to this awe
that leads to a good relationship with Jehovah God.
We have a number of experiences in this regard
that are related to the relief efforts going on right now.
I’d like to share one of them with you.
It was in the middle of the night, Monday, October 9, 2017,
and the wildfires began to engulf areas
around the city of Santa Rosa, California.
The elders began to call, text,
and even personally alert those in the congregation
that they needed to evacuate immediately.
And in time, hundreds of friends made their way to the Kingdom Hall,
and from there arrangements were made
for these displaced publishers to be housed
with their brothers and sisters
in unaffected areas, especially to the south.
Well, there was one Spanish family that hesitated to accept the hospitality
that was being extended to them, and they did not want to be relocated.
And upon the loving inquiries of the elders,
it was learned that the father was a non-Witness
and he felt uncomfortable staying in another Witness home.
And he was embarrassed at the way he looked,
the way he was dressed,
and how dirty he was because of the circumstances.
So he requested to stay overnight at the Kingdom Hall with his family.
Well, temporary beds were set up at the Kingdom Hall.
And during the night, the circuit overseer
had children singing Kingdom songs on the platform
which really encouraged all.
The next morning,
after experiencing the loving atmosphere in the Kingdom Hall
and seeing how well Jehovah took care of this man’s family,
as well as the other publishers,
the man stated that he was going to call the brother back
who studied with him many years ago
and he would resume his Bible study
and he would never ever miss a meeting again.
Yes, those “rightly disposed” become in awe of Jehovah God,
and that moves them to have a good relationship with him.
Remember, ‘the whole obligation of man is to fear God.’
So the question is, Now that we have developed
this relationship with Jehovah God,
how do we keep it?
Well, for sure, we must continue to be observant
of Jehovah’s mighty acts
in connection not only with ourselves
but in connection with his people worldwide.
Never should we allow the wonderful experiences that we hear
—the outstanding World Service Report
or the support and comfort that Jehovah God is giving those in need—
to become commonplace to us.
We must stay in awe of our God and Father.
Now, you remember the first scripture we read in Ecclesiastes
where it says that in addition to fearing the true God,
we’re told to keep his commandments.
So it would be good to ask ourselves this question:
‘What commandment of Jehovah God do I have difficulty keeping?
‘Is it a commandment that involves my self-control,
‘my zeal,
‘my humility,
or perhaps my honesty?’
If so, then we should give immediate attention
to improving the spiritual person that we are
so that keeping God’s commandments
will become as easy as being in awe
of what Jehovah is doing in behalf of his people.
Brothers and sisters,
we stand at the threshold of the promised new world,
and may we heed the words here at Hebrews 12:28
(by not only developing
but by keeping a relationship with Jehovah God),
where it says
—Hebrews 12:28:
“Therefore, seeing that we are to receive
“a Kingdom that cannot be shaken,
“let us continue to receive undeserved kindness,
“through which we may acceptably offer God
sacred service with godly fear and awe.”

cn.text: 认识造物主是人的义务
跟他做朋友也是我们人能享有的殊荣
但问题是
怎样才能跟耶和华培养深厚的友谊呢？
还有，我们怎样巩固这份友谊呢？
首先，我们谈谈
怎样培养跟耶和华的深厚友谊
请打开传道书12:13
这节经文谈到两件值得我们留意的事情
传道书12:13，经文说
“这一切你都听到了
结论就是
要敬畏上帝，遵守他的诫命
人的义务全在于这一点。”
所以这两件事就是
要敬畏上帝和遵守他的诫命
那么，“敬畏”是什么意思呢？
这个词跟一般人说的“畏惧”是不一样的
《洞悉》书解释说
“敬畏”上帝对人有百利而无一害
一个人深深尊敬上帝
害怕令他不悦
就是对上帝有敬畏之心
他之所以害怕令上帝不悦
是因为感激上帝
对他显出忠贞之爱和良善
也因为承认上帝是全能的
是至高的审判官
一个人怎样才能培养
对上帝的敬畏之心呢？
约书亚记9:9说
基遍人听到耶和华的名声和他所做的一切
就敬畏上帝
但通常，一个人不会只是
因为听到或看到耶和华所做的事
就马上产生敬畏之心
也不会很快就跟上帝有深厚的友谊
约书亚记第9章就说明了这一点
我们一起看看一些迦南国王的例子
请打开约书亚记9:1，经文说
“约旦河西的所有国王听说了这些事”
他们听说了什么事呢？
他们一定听说了以色列人离开埃及的事
也听到耶和华为他的子民
所施行的许多奇迹
以色列人穿过约旦河
进入迦南地的时候
他们在耶利哥城附近的吉甲扎营
后来，耶和华为了他的子民
毁灭了耶利哥城
这些迦南国王肯定也听说了这件事
但请留意
喇合和她的家人却在这次毁灭中得救了
因为喇合听到了耶和华曾经施行的奇迹
就显出信心、采取行动
约书亚记第八章提到
耶利哥城被毁灭之后
以色列人开始攻打艾城
耶和华指引以色列人埋伏并攻下艾城
迦南的列王听到艾城战败
听说了耶和华所做的这些事情后
他们有什么反应呢？
他们对上帝产生敬畏之心了吗？
我们一起读一下约书亚记9:2
经文说
他们“就结盟要攻打约书亚和以色列人。”
显然，他们完全没有敬畏之心
但是请留意，听到同样的事情后
基遍人却有完全不同的反应
他们有什么反应呢？
我们从9:9开始看
他们说
“仆人仰慕耶和华你上帝的圣名
所以从很远的地方来
我们听到他的名声和他在埃及做的一切
也听说了他怎么处置
约旦河东亚摩利人的两个国王”
我们看出
基遍人听到耶和华所做的事情后
就产生了敬畏之心
想要投奔耶和华、崇拜他
在我们的日子
耶和华也为他的子民
做了很多伟大的事情
那些有“正确态度”的人看到之后
就产生了敬畏之心
想要成为耶和华的朋友
最近的救灾报告里
就提到很多这样的经历
我想跟你们分享其中一个
2017年10月9日星期一的半夜
在加利福尼亚州
一场大火开始向圣罗莎及周边蔓延
会众的长老开始打电话
发短信给会众成员
甚至亲自上门告诉他们要迅速撤离
很快就有几百个弟兄姐妹赶往王国聚会所
弟兄们作出安排
让他们住在没有受火灾影响的弟兄姐妹家
这些家庭大多都在加州南部
有一个讲西班牙语的家庭
不想住在弟兄姐妹的家里
他们不太愿意接受这个安排
会众的长老们非常关心他们
后来得知
原来这个家庭的家主
不是耶和华见证人
他觉得住在弟兄姐妹家有点尴尬
因为他的衣服、身上都很脏
这让他觉得很不好意思
所以他想跟家人一起
在王国聚会所过夜
弟兄们就临时在王国聚会所
准备了床铺
那天晚上
分区监督邀请孩子们
到讲台上唱王国诗歌
这真的鼓励了所有人
那位家主看到弟兄姐妹充满爱心
也看到耶和华怎样照顾他的一家和其他人
第二天早上
这位家主就说
他要打电话给以前的圣经老师
他想要再次学习圣经
还说以后再也不会错过任何聚会了
没错，那些有“正确态度”的人
会敬畏上帝
也会想要和耶和华建立深厚的友谊
圣经说
要敬畏上帝
人的义务全在于这一点
我们已经讨论了
怎么才能跟耶和华培养深厚的友谊
那么接下来我们谈谈
怎样才能保持这种友谊呢？
我们要继续留意耶和华为我们所做的事
也要留意他为世界各地的弟兄姐妹所做的事
当我们看到年度全球总报告的精彩数据时
听到耶和华上帝怎样安慰
并扶持遭遇患难的弟兄姐妹时
千万不要把这些事情看作理所当然
我们要有敬畏之心
要保持跟天父耶和华的亲密关系
你还记得演讲开头提到的传道书的经文吗？
经文谈到
我们不仅要敬畏上帝
还要遵守他的诫命
因此，我们最好问问自己
耶和华说的哪条诫命是我不容易服从的呢？
服从这条诫命需要什么特质呢？
是自制
热心
谦卑
还是诚实呢？
当我们意识到自己缺乏这些特质时
就要马上开始培养
这些特质会帮助我们想要服从耶和华
也会帮助我们对耶和华产生敬畏之心
弟兄姐妹们
我们很快就要进入新世界了
我们需要培养
并巩固跟耶和华的深厚友谊
愿我们所有人
都能够听从希伯来书12:28的话
希伯来书12:28说
“我们既然会得到一个不能被震动的王国
就该继续接受分外恩典
这样，我们就能怀着虔诚
而敬畏的心敬奉上帝
得到他的接纳。”

ko.text: 우리가 안전에 유의해야 할 중요한 이유가
집에서든, 길에서든, 신권 건축 현장에서든 말이죠.
안전에 대한 우리의 태도는 자신의 영성은 물론
여호와와 형제 자매들에 대한 사랑의 깊이를 보여 줍니다.
이제 세계 여러 곳에서 제작한 다음 영상을 통해
우리가 어떻게 안전에 더 유의할 수 있는지 보시겠습니다.
다른 사람이 다칠 수도 있었단 걸 깨달았어요.
전 한 번도 교통사고를 낸 적이 없었고,
하지만 운전할 때는 잠시만 한눈을 팔아도
다른 사람의 목숨을 빼앗게 될 수 있죠.
당신의 빛으로 우리가 빛을 볼 수 있습니다.”
다른 활동을 할 때에도 조심하려고 합니다.
하지만 큰 부상을 당하기 쉬운 운동은 더 이상 하지 않죠.
제가 아직 살아 있다는 것에 대해 여호와께 매일 감사드립니다.
전 몇 백 번도 더 다녔던 도로를 건너고 있었어요.
거기서 다친 사람이 아무도 없었기 때문에,
게다가 그날 해야 할 일을 생각하는 데
자동차 브레이크 소리를 듣고 나서야 차가 오는 걸 눈치챘어요.
안전에 더 신경을 썼으면 얼마나 좋았을까
무언가 하기 전에 먼저 멈춰서, 생각하고,
우리가 생명을 정말 소중하게 여긴다는 걸

cn.text: 耶和华的子民必须重视安全
使徒行传17:28说
生命是来自上帝的宝贵恩赐
所以我们必须留意安全
以行动表明自己尊重生命
无论是在建筑工地还是其他地方
组织的目标都是“零事故”
我们每个人也一样
不管是在家还是在外面
使用交通工具或参与组织的建筑工程
都必须时刻留意安全
事实上，我们的安全意识
能反映出自己对耶和华
和弟兄姐妹的爱有多深
接下来，让我们看看世界各地的例子
想想自己可以怎样更加注意安全
那天发生的事改变了我的人生
那一刻，我意识到自己的行为
可能对人造成多大的伤害
甚至让自己欠下血债
那个时候，我真的过度自信
因为从没有出过车祸
所以我以为这种事情绝不会发生在自己身上
但没想到我差点因瞬间的分心
而酿成大祸，让人丧命
后来我沉思了诗篇36:9
现在，对“生命的源头”耶和华的爱
让我在开车、或做其他事的时候
都格外留意安全
我很喜欢运动，但我不再玩那些危险的运动
即便有些运动通常不会导致受伤
我还是会保持警惕，留意安全
我每天都感谢耶和华让我还活着
之前，我差点发生严重的意外
当时我正走在一条我经常走的路上
那里从来没有发生过交通事故
所以我觉得很安全
再加上当时我满脑子想的都是
那天要做的事
结果直到听见紧急刹车声
我才看到有车子过来
真希望我能早一点明白安全的重要性
现在我和丈夫经常教孩子
哪怕是在熟悉的环境里
做任何事之前都要停下来想想
会不会有危险
我们注意安全
就是向耶和华表明自己有多珍惜生命
不论在家还是外面
留意安全已成为我们的习惯
我们会众的长老团
特别留意箴言22:3的提醒
如果我们只顾赶进度
对潜在的危险睁一只眼闭一只眼
万一出现问题，我们就要承担责任
我们深爱耶和华和弟兄姐妹
所以绝不能容许自己疏忽大意
LDC保养维修培训小组给我们良好的指引
让我们学会运用箴言22:3的原则
每次
我们都会先想想有哪些安全隐患
以及如何避免
然后再开始工作，以确保安全
我们也会根据弟兄姐妹的知识、能力和限度
为每个人安排最合适的工作
我们很高兴看到孩子们也积极参与
但我们会确保他们的身边总是有成年人
不管是父母还是其他人
好能时刻留意他们的安全
大会前，大家都很想帮忙布置会场
而时间通常也比较紧迫
不过我们从不会为了赶工而忽略安全
因此，事先好好安排真的很重要
就算我们从没受过伤，这次也平安无事
但如果我们心存侥幸，不遵守安全规范
还算得上是好榜样吗？
我们一步一步来、事先好好计划
工作时集中注意力
就是听从箴言3:21,23的提醒
这个原则不但在筹备大会时适用
在大会期间也适用
我们见到朋友自然很开心
但有时会忘记，走路时也要注意安全
特别是在人多的地方
楼梯或电梯上
停车场、住宿地点
或其他容易摔倒的地方，就更要小心
连我们的鞋子也有可能造成危险
每年都有不少姐妹
因高跟鞋而发生严重的意外
研读让我们明白
如果我们能清楚看出
什么会危害自己跟上帝的关系
也就能清楚看出什么会危害自己
和他人的安全
我们想要把最好的献给耶和华
就会在开始工作前，停下来思考
并分析情况
我也学到，在评估潜在的风险时
要记得我们做这件事
是出于对耶和华和弟兄姐妹的爱
就算按照最安全的方式工作
得花更多时间和金钱
我们也在所不惜
我们的培训课程强调的一句话是
“一看到危险，就要马上说出来。”
这和腓立比书2:4的原则一致
把我们留意到的危险告诉别人
就能避免意外发生
生命是来自耶和华的礼物
所以我希望帮助孩子明白生命多么宝贵
有时候
一个小小的举动也能拯救人的生命
我现在良心清白
也明白了一个重要的道理
我留意安全
就是向耶和华和弟兄姐妹表达我的爱
这让我很开心
有时，我们的举动是不是显示出
我们不够重视生命呢？
就像前面谈到的
爱上帝的人也一定会重视安全
所以我们会努力养成注重安全的习惯
有了良好的安全意识
我们就会认真评估风险
并做出所需的调整
这样我们就能降低
甚至消除可能出现的危险
这个世界崇尚效率，轻视安全
上帝的子民却截然不同
无论是与崇拜有关的事
还是每天的生活
我们都时刻注重安全
以此表明我们爱耶和华
尊重他所赐的宝贵生命！

ko.text: 전 차 밭에서 찻잎 따는 일을 하고 있어요.
한 번은 하느님께 간절히 이렇게 기도했어요.
근데 여호와의 증인들이 이틀도 못 돼서 우리 집 문을 두드렸고
바로 그 전날, 성경을 배우게 도와달라고 기도했으니까요.
그래서 수요일 저녁에 미리 가방을 싸 놓습니다.
커다란 가방 두 개를 어깨에 메고
그래서 저희 가족은 집회에 항상 일찍 갑니다.
파이오니아 봉사를 한 지 이제 1년 반이 됐네요.
파이오니아 봉사보다 더 행복한 게 없어요.
이 전파 활동은 지금 아니면 기회가 없을 거예요.
그래서 할 수 있는 한 최선을 다해 여호와를 섬기기로 결정했죠.
그분을 이렇게 섬길 수 있어서 정말 행복해요.
한번은 임금을 전혀 받지 못한 적이 있어요.
수중에 남아 있는 돈이 한 푼도 없었죠.
그래도 그날은 아이들과 함께 잘 먹었어요.
다음 날을 어떻게 살아갈지 무척 걱정이 됐죠.
그래서 전 여호와께서 어떻게든 필요한 것을 주실 거라고 믿었어요.
보통 이 시간엔 전화가 안 와요.
그래서 ‘이 늦은 시간에 누가 전화를 한 걸까?’하고 생각했죠.
책꽂이에 가서 「위대한 인물」 책을 꺼내 보세요”라고 했죠.
어느 페이지를 펴 보라고 해서 거기를 펴보니까,
그 액수는 딱 그달 우리 생활비였거든요.
며칠 전 그 형제 부부가 저희 집에 왔을 때
우리에게 필요한 걸 이미 정확히 알고 계셨죠.
저는 매일 밤이 되면 문을 열고 집 밖으로 나가서,
그분이 얼마나 놀라운 일을 하실 수 있는지에 대해 묵상합니다.
이 지구와 이 우주를 놀랍도록 잘 돌보는 분이에요!
아주 작은 일들까지도 다 돌봐 주시죠.
우리를 도와주실 수 있다는 사실을 늘 잊지 않으려고 해요.
항상 우리 손을 꼭 붙잡고 계셔서,
우리에 대한 애정이 참 많으신 분이세요.
그 누구도 우리에 대한 여호와의 사랑을 막지 못할 거예요.

en.text: My name is Reeta.
My son is Jackson, and my daughter is Sherina.
It’s just the three of us.
I have been working on a tea estate as a tea picker.
One day, I prayed to God very hard.
I said,
“Please help me to learn about the Bible.”
Within two days, Jehovah’s Witnesses came
and knocked on my door, and I agreed to study the Bible.
I couldn’t believe it.
I only prayed yesterday, asking God to help me to study the Bible.
Our meetings begin at 4:45 p.m.,
but we have to get ready by 12 o’clock
to attend the meetings.
So we prepare our bags on Wednesday night.
I carry two big bags on my shoulders
and walk for three and a half kilometers (2 mi) to get to the meetings on time.
We love seeing our brothers.
That’s why we always go to the meetings early.
I have been pioneering now for a year and six months.
There is no greater happiness than what comes from pioneering.
This is a onetime opportunity.
That is why we decided that we should give the best that we can to Jehovah.
Now I am so happy to be serving this way.
One time, I was not paid at all.
I didn’t even have a rupee.
On that day, my children and I ate well.
But after eating, we were very worried
about what we were going to do the following day.
So that night, I said a prayer with the kids
and we read the Bible.
Jesus said,
‘Don’t worry about tomorrow.’
So I trusted that somehow
Jehovah would give us what we needed.
It was 10:30 at night.
I was fast asleep, and the phone rang.
Usually no one calls this late,
so I wondered, ‘Who could be calling me this late?’
I picked up the phone, and it was a brother on the line.
He said, “Sister, go to your bookshelf
and take the Greatest Man book.”
Then he asked me to turn to a page.
When I turned to that page,
there were 10,000 rupees (about $55, U.S.) between those pages.
We could not believe our eyes.
It was exactly what we needed for that month’s expenses.
A few days earlier, he and his wife had visited us
and secretly left the money in the book before leaving.
So I thanked Jehovah in prayer with the kids.
Jehovah already knew exactly what we needed
even before we realized it.
Honestly, every night I open the doors,
go outside, and look up at the night sky.
When I look up, I see many stars.
I daily meditate about his wisdom,
his power, what amazing things he is able to do.
This earth, this universe
—how amazingly well he cares for them!
He takes care of the smallest thing.
I completely rely on Jehovah,
and then I remember that Jehovah has the ability
to help us with his holy spirit.
He’s such a loving Father.
He’s always holding our hand tight,
and no one can separate us from him.
If anyone tries, they will fail.
He’s so generous with his love.
He’s so affectionate with us.
No one can take away the love Jehovah has for us.

cn.text: 我是蕾塔
我的儿子叫杰克逊，女儿叫雪莉娜
我们一家就三口人
我是一个采茶工人，一直在茶园工作
有一天，我非常恳切地向上帝祷告，说
“求你帮助我了解圣经。”
第二天，耶和华见证人就来敲我的门了
我同意跟他们学习圣经
真不敢相信
我前一天才向上帝祷告，第二天就有人来了
我们的聚会是在下午4:45开始
但我们中午12点就会出发
所以
我们会在前一天晚上准备好要带的东西
我要带两个很大的背包
走大约3.5公里才能到聚会所
我们很喜欢跟弟兄姐妹在一起
所以我们到得很早
我做先驱已经一年半了
没有什么事比做先驱更让我快乐的了
现在的传道机会非常宝贵
所以我们决定把自己最好的献给耶和华
我很高兴自己能够做先驱
有一次，老板没有给我那个月的工资
我身上连一块钱都没有了
那天，我和孩子们吃得很饱

不知道第二天该怎么办
当天晚上
我和孩子们一起祷告、一起看圣经
耶稣说“不要为明天忧虑”
这句话给我很大的安慰
这让我完全相信
不管怎样
耶和华一定会帮助我们的
那天晚上十点半
我已经上床睡觉了
突然电话响了
通常没有人会这么晚打电话过来
我心想，“这么晚，是谁打来的啊？”
我接了电话
原来是一个弟兄打来的
他说
“姐妹，现在到你的书架那里
把《最伟大人物》那本书拿下来。”
然后他要我翻到其中一页
翻开书后，我就看到有1万卢比夹在那里
我真的不敢相信自己的眼睛！
这正好是我们一个月的生活费
原来几天前，这位弟兄和太太来看我们时
就偷偷把钱放在书里了
我们就祷告感谢耶和华
是的，在我们还不知道自己需要什么的时候
耶和华就已经知道了
每到晚上，我都会走到外面
抬头看看夜空，看看满天的星星
每天我都会沉思上帝的智慧
上帝的力量
还有上帝奇妙的作为
这个地球，这个宇宙
上帝把它们照顾得这么好！
连最不起眼的小东西
上帝也把他们照料得非常好！
现在，我完全倚靠耶和华
也深信耶和华会用神圣力量来帮助我们
上帝是一位很有爱心的父亲
他总是紧紧拉着我们的手
没有人可以把我们分开
要是有人想这么做，他一定会失败的
耶和华非常有爱心，也很爱我们
任何人都不能夺走耶和华对我们的爱！
