성경 원칙들을 일상생활에 적용하는 일에 관한
우린 여호와의 원칙과 표준을 적용할 때,
또 그분을 기쁘시게 하는 방법으로 살 수 있다는 걸 배웠습니다.
하느님의 원칙을 적용하면 놀라운 희망도 갖게 됩니다.
믿음을 키울 수 있다는 사실을 보여 줍니다.
침례를 받은 건 제 삶에서 가장 중요한 결정이었습니다.
하지만 그건 그리스도인 생활의 시작일 뿐이었죠.
자기들 나라를 위해 뭔가 해 볼 생각은 전혀 안 하나?
아녜요. 전 여호와의 증인이라 생일 축하를 안 해요.
그래서 루카스의 생일 카드에 제 이름을 쓰고 싶었죠.
하지만 아빠는 여호와께서 어떻게 느끼실지 알게 도와주셨어요.
루카스를 위해 뭔가 딴 걸 하려고 해요.
부모님은 항상 제게 훌륭한 본을 보이셨어요.
하지만 제가 도움이 필요한 곳으로 이주한 후로
두 분이 점점 멀어지는 것 같았죠.
여호와에 대한 사랑이 도움이 됐다고 말씀해 주셨어요.
두 분은 아브라함과 사라의 본을 묵상하셨대요.
그들은 서로 잘 들어 주고 관심을 가짐으로, 서로를 존중했죠.
그 본은 부모님께 큰 도움이 됐어요.
모든 관계에 도움이 된다는 걸 알게 됐습니다.
심각한 장애를 갖게 되거나 죽을 수도 있다고 말했을 때,
또 남편이 여호와의 증인이 아니었기 때문에,
제가 마음을 가라앉히고 낙태를 왜 할 수 없는지 설명하려면
그 어느 때보다 하느님의 도움이 절실히 필요했습니다.
전 성서 연구를 받아들이기까지 수년이 걸렸고,
침례받을 자격을 갖출 수 있을 만큼 변화를 하는 데는
그렇지만 지금은 아내와 함께 여호와를 섬기고 있는데,
우리 둘 다 이보다 행복할 수가 없어요.
진정한 행복은 여호와를 섬기는 데서 옵니다.
하지만 그분을 충실히 섬기는 데는 용기가 꼭 필요하죠.
학교에서 미경이의 관심을 거절하는 게 아주 힘들었어요.
그 애와 너무 가까워지면서 죄책감이 들었습니다.
삼촌은 성경을 사용해서 제가 올바른 시각을 갖도록 도와주셨고,
중요한 사실 두 가지를 일깨워 주셨어요.
여호와께서 절 자랑스러워 하시고 전 혼자가 아니라는 사실이죠.
여러분이 여러 가지 시련을 만날 때에
그처럼 시험받은 믿음이 인내를 낳는다는 것을
저는 군 복무를 거부하기 때문에 곧 법정에 서게 될 수 있거든요.
제게 지금 필요한 믿음과 용기를 기르는 데 도움이 됐습니다.
한동안 제한된 상황에서 지내야 할지 모르지만,
가끔 외로움을 느낄 때가 있지만, 괜찮아요.
임지에서 봉사하기 위해 당분간은 이렇게 지내기로 했어요.
낙원을 구경시켜 주고 여호와에 관해 더 가르쳐 줄 거예요.
실제로 보면 훨씬 더 좋을 거예요.
그땐 우리 딸을 다시 품에 안을 수 있을 거예요.
이 달의 초점은 여호와께서 다양한 방법으로
그분은 우리가 헌신과 침례를 향해서 노력할 때
회중 집회에서 그리고 우리가 영적 가족과 함께 있을 때도
그분은 우리가 박해와 어려움들을 잘 이겨낼 때도 함께 계시죠.
왕국의 좋은 소식을 전할 때도 함께 계십니다.
이번 달 진행을 함께 해 주셔서 정말 감사드립니다.
테네리페섬에 사는 우리 형제 자매들을 만나 보겠습니다.
테네리페섬은 아프리카의 북서 연안에 위치한 섬들인
이곳 날씨는 연중 내내 온화하고 화창합니다.
이곳에 살고 있는 사람은 백만 명 정도이지만,
매년 천만 명이 넘는 관광객들이 찾아와서
해변과 울창한 자연 경관과 음식을 즐깁니다.
우리 형제 자매들은 15개가 넘는 언어로 전파합니다.
여러분에게 따뜻한 그리스도인 사랑과 안부를 전합니다.

en.text: Welcome to JW Broadcasting®.
This is my friend and cohost, Izak Marais.
Izak, what’s in store for this month’s program?
Thank you, Brother Lösch.
This month we’ll examine the many ways
Jehovah assures us that he is with us.
Our music video for this month shows how,
from the moment that we start to take steps
toward dedication and baptism,
Jehovah draws close to us.
Jehovah is also with us in the ministry.
In this report, we’ll see how he blessed
a special preaching effort in Europe.
And Jehovah is with us as we meet challenges of daily life,
as our Sister Reeta and her children learned.
That sounds exciting!
Let’s get started.
This is the November 2019 edition of JW Broadcasting.
Millions have benefited
from the animated series
Become Jehovah’s Friend
and many other Bible-based videos.
Have you enjoyed getting to know Caleb and Sophia?
When you’ve watched a video,
perhaps you’ve wondered:
‘How does the Governing Body know that the video will turn out exactly right?
How can they see and hear the video before it exists?’
Let’s go behind the scenes and see how this works.
Animated videos,
like those in the series Become Jehovah’s Friend,
have been helping young ones draw closer to their heavenly Father
for several years now.
Look, Mom, I’m rejoicing in the hope!
Wee!
But did you know
that what you see on the screen
might last just a few short minutes
but it may involve weeks of work
by a virtual army of volunteers?
With so much time and expense involved in making an animated video,
a lot of careful planning is required to avoid waste
and to keep the process running smoothly.
Let’s take a look at how the effective use
of preproduction tools help all of these brothers and sisters
work together to take a video
from initial concept to final production.
Under the direction of the Teaching Committee of the Governing Body,
the work begins long before the artists even get started.
They provide direction on the theme that needs to be taught.
Members of the animation team collaborate
to develop the featured characters as well as plot structure,
and they work closely with writers and storyboard artists
to develop the approved idea into a story line.
Once a complete script is ready,
the whole team gathers together for a table read.
This is the first time the team hears the whole script being read aloud.
Dialogue is meant to be heard.
So when we read it aloud at the table read,
we pick up on things
we didn’t see in the written script.
We’re able to tighten the story
and make it as clear as possible.
The script is reviewed by the research team for accuracy.
Then it’s revised, polished, and submitted
to the Teaching Committee for approval.
With an approved script in hand,
the director then works with an artist
to start turning words into pictures
—visualizing each scene on a storyboard.
First come the rough boards,
showing what will be included in each shot.
When it comes to the animation world, really,
everything you see on screen
has to be designed and created
—the characters,
the furniture,
the props, the environment
are all created by a designer.
The storyboard really helps us
figure out exactly what we need to create
so that we’re not creating too much or too little.
Once approved by the director,
the storyboard artist cleans up each of the boards.
Preliminary recordings of dialogue, music,
and sound effects are added.
These are then used by the director
and compositor to create an animatic.
An animatic is a rough draft of the entire video.
The animatic is very important for us.
That way the director
and, more importantly, the Teaching Committee
can see the entire video before we are actually making it.
And with that they can review it and give us the proper direction.
The finished animatic is submitted
to the Teaching Committee for review.
Based on direction from the committee,
the team makes sure that the teaching points come across clearly
and that the finished product is true to the spirit
and intent of the approved concept for the video.
Finally, using the approved animatic as a blueprint,
full production begins.
Really, everything in animation can be very time-consuming.
An animator working full-time here at Bethel
may be able to produce four to six seconds of animation in one week,
and that doesn’t even include other aspects
that are very important, such as modeling,
rigging, lighting, compositing, and many others.
From the examples shown here,
you can see just how closely the final version
of the video Make Jehovah Happy  follows the animatic.
Preproduction tools such as storyboards and animatics
do more than save the organization time and money.
They enable the Teaching Committee
to carefully evaluate every project along the way
from the initial approved concept
to the final product
in order to keep providing videos
that help all of us honor our Friend, Jehovah.
Isn’t it amazing to see all the work
that goes into our videos?
Jehovah provides for his people
just what they need at the right time.
Truly, he is with his people.
Brother Lösch,
I know you have some thoughts on this.
I’d like to talk
about a very common expression
in the Bible.
The expression is:
“I am with you.”
Thirteen times it’s attributed to a statement from Jehovah.
Three times it’s something that Jesus said
to one or more of his disciples.
Of course, there are dozens of other times
that the same sentiment is expressed using similar wording.
Few things in the world equal the joy humans experience
than the birth of a child.
As children grow up,
they are sometimes exposed to situations
that tend to cause nervousness
or even fear.
So a parent may occasionally feel compelled
to reassure a child:
“Have no fear; I am with you.”
Jehovah loves his servants as if they were his children.
Likewise, at John 13:1,
Jesus’ feelings for his disciples are well expressed.
There it says:
“Jesus, having loved his own who were in the world,
loved them to the end.”
So when we face fears,
trials, or causes for anxiety,
both our heavenly Father and his Son, Jesus,
reassuringly say, “I am with you.”
Think of the righteous man Noah.
Genesis 6:9 says
that “Noah walked with the true God.”
There’s no doubt that Jehovah was with Noah.
He preserved him and his family through the Flood.
Afterward, Jehovah further proved he was with Noah.
In Genesis chapter 9, Jehovah said:
‘I am now establishing my covenant with you:
‘Never again will all flesh be destroyed
by the waters of a flood.’
Jehovah could have made that determination
and promised himself that he wouldn’t do that again,
but instead, he reached out to Noah
and reassured him that he was with him
by making the rainbow covenant with Noah and his offspring.
Using similar terminology,
Jehovah indicated that he was with Abraham,
Isaac, Jacob, Joseph,
Moses, Joshua, and Gideon.
They were all individuals whom Jehovah was pleased with,
so he reassured them that he was with them.
How about for a group of people?
Is Jehovah moved to feel the same way
toward a large crowd of his servants collectively?
Please find with me Exodus 6:6, 7.
The whole nation of Israel
was experiencing severe trials
and suffering as slaves in Egypt.
Notice Jehovah’s reassurance to the vast number of people.
Verses 6 and 7 state:
“Therefore, say to the Israelites:
“‘I am Jehovah,
“‘and I will bring you out from under the burdens of the Egyptians
“‘and rescue you from their slavery,
“‘and I will reclaim you with an outstretched arm
“‘and with great judgments.
“‘And I will take you in as my people, and I will be your God,
“‘and you will certainly know that I am Jehovah your God
who is bringing you out from under the burdens of Egypt.’”
If that great, mixed group of people would follow his leadings,
he said he’d ‘take them in’ and he ‘would be their God.’
What was he saying?
He was reassuring them:
“I will be with you,”
and he was.
For forty years in the wilderness, he was with them
—feeding them, providing water for them,
ensuring that their clothes and sandals would not wear out,
protecting them from poisonous snakes, and so forth.
And later, when entering the land of promise,
he protected them during enemy warfare.
Jehovah promised to be with and to support
the kings of Israel
as long as they heeded his commandments and direction.
King Solomon was told:
“Jehovah [your] God . . . will not desert you or abandon you,
but he will be with you.”
King Asa was informed:
“Jehovah is with you as long as you remain with him.”
When faced with overwhelming enemy forces,
King Jehoshaphat was told:
“Tomorrow go out against them, and Jehovah will be with you.”
Jehovah also proved to be with the many prophets
that he sent out in his name.
Just one example is Jeremiah.
Imagine if you had Jeremiah’s assignment.
Suppose you had been directed to deliver
a scathing denunciation and judgment
against wicked kings, corrupt priests, and false prophets.
How would you feel?
underqualified?
Would you feel like a little child
challenging a whole group of evil grown-ups?
Notice how Jeremiah felt as he expressed himself
at Jeremiah 1:6:
“But I said: ‘Alas, O Sovereign Lord Jehovah!
I do not know how to speak, for I am just a boy.’”
What were Jehovah’s reassuring words in reply?
Jeremiah 1:8, 9:
“‘Do not be afraid
“‘because of their appearance, for “I am with you to save you,”
“declares Jehovah.’
“Then Jehovah stretched out his hand and touched my mouth.
“And Jehovah said to me: ‘I have put my words in your mouth.’”
If Jehovah put the words that you were to say “in your mouth,”
you’d no longer feel like a little child, would you?
We don’t think of Jeremiah as being an incredible superman;
he was a human like us.
It’s of interest that though Jeremiah lived in another time and place,
he faced situations similar to those we face.
We interact with different types of people
in our daily life, at work, and at school.
Some of them can be intimidating.
And like Jeremiah,
Jehovah has commissioned us to go to strangers and preach.
We share the good news of the Kingdom.
Some are interested; others are just plain apathetic.
But at times, we may come across someone who is angry
and may even be threatening.
This is the time to remember Jeremiah.
Though initially timid,
he courageously faced
the challenge of an intimidating response.
How did he rally to the occasion?
It was because Jehovah had reassured him:
“I am with you.”
He said: “I have put my words in your mouth.”
Does Jehovah do something similar for us?
Yes.
Long after Jeremiah and the other faithful ones
who are recorded in the Hebrew Scriptures came and went,
Jehovah has proved to be with true Christians,
both past and present.
Find with me John chapter 8.
Think of Jesus.
It’s true he was a perfect man,
but did Jehovah leave him all alone?
At John 8:16, what did Jesus himself say?
“And yet even if I do judge, my judgment is truthful,
“because I am not alone,
but the Father who sent me is with me.”
We might be thinking of that intimidating person in the ministry.
Even if you are facing the person without a fellow Witness standing beside you,
are you really all alone?
Jesus knew that at the most stressful
and emotionally draining time
during his human life,
his disciples would leave him all alone.
But was he really alone?
Let’s read the inspired account
at John 16:32.
Again, these are Jesus’ own words:
“Look! The hour is coming, indeed, it has come,
“when each one of you will be scattered to his own house
“and you will leave me alone.
“But I am not alone,
because the Father is with me.”
Jesus was not alone during his most anxious moments.
Jehovah was with him.
If you think you are alone
standing at the door of an irritated householder,
think again.
Jehovah is with you.
You have more with you
than if you had your whole congregation
standing in the person’s front yard.
Well, why did Jesus share
this precious insight with us?
Look at the next verse.
Jesus explains his reason for saying what he did.
John 16:33:
“I have said these things to you
“so that by means of me you may have peace.
“In the world you will have tribulation,
“but take courage!
I have conquered the world.”
We thank Jesus for addressing
our fears and concerns when giving a witness.
Instead of trembling with fear,
he shared his confidence in Jehovah’s support
so that we “may have peace.”
He acknowledged that we would face tribulation,
but he said that we could look at his example
and have courage to deal with the tribulation.
Why?
Jesus said in verse 32
that it was because ‘the Father was with him.’
Do you recall that Jehovah told Jeremiah:
“I have put my words in your mouth?”
Can Jehovah do the same for us
when we are opposed by unbelievers?
The Christian Greek Scriptures answer with a resounding yes!
Please follow along with the reading
of the book of Mark chapter 13,
and please notice that the setting Jesus describes
is in the ministry, preaching the good news.
Maybe you’ve had a good morning in service,
but then you take one more door.
The person is irate and even calls the police.
What should you do?
What will you say when the police arrive?
You don’t have to be overly concerned.
Why not?
Because similar to Jeremiah,
Jehovah will, in effect, put His words in your mouth.
Mark 13:10, 11 says:
“Also, in all the nations, the good news has to be preached first.
“And when they are taking you to hand you over,
“do not be anxious beforehand about what to say;
“but whatever is given you in that hour, say this,
“for you are not the ones speaking,
but the holy spirit is.”
By this, do we mean that Jehovah
will miraculously put words in your mouth for you to say?
Not necessarily.
Did you notice verse 11 said
that “the holy spirit” is the one speaking?
You’ve been taught the basis for your faith from the Scriptures,
and you know the reason that you teach the Bible’s message.
That’s all stored in your mind.
So, what’s the holy spirit’s role
when we are in an intimidating situation
when sharing the good news?
Jehovah is with you.
He uses his holy spirit to bring to the surface
some of those precious gems that might be buried in your mind.
You may be amazed at what you remember
when put under pressure by the authorities
or even by outright opposers.
In this way, Jehovah is with you.
Add to the fact that Jesus is with you in the disciple-making work.
Let’s be reminded of this very encouraging thought
at Matthew 28:19, 20.
Jesus was discussing our commission
to preach, teach, and make disciples.
And how does he conclude the Bible book of Matthew?
Let’s read Matthew 28:19, 20:
“Go, therefore, and make disciples of people of all the nations,
“baptizing them in the name of the Father
“and of the Son and of the holy spirit,
“teaching them to observe all the things I have commanded you.
“And look! I am with you all the days
until the conclusion of the system of things.”
Jesus said that he is with us now
when we are making disciples and teaching people the truth.
And he promises he’ll support us in this important work
until the end of this wicked system of things.
As prophesied, during this time of the conclusion of the system,
we are being persecuted in different areas of the world.
As the Scriptures show, Satan and his angels
are “misleading the entire inhabited earth.”
Recently, Jehovah’s people have been persecuted in Russia.
But will the persecution
succeed in eliminating
true worship in that area of the world?
No!
Why not?
It’s because Jehovah is with them.
He and Jesus promised: “I am with you.”
Russia did not learn from the past.
It will prove to be the same for them
as it was for Nazi Germany under Hitler.
Hitler thought his regime
could eradicate true worship and God’s people
from areas under their control.
But they made a big mistake.
While it is true that they murdered some 2,000 brothers,
in the end, their scheme ended up in failure.
Why?
Because God was with us, not with them.
“God with us”
—those words have decorated national emblems
and even the uniforms of soldiers of Prussia
and the Czarist Russian Empire.
These words were also on the belts of German troops
when they marched into Belgium in the year 1914 of our Common Era.
But they had it wrong!
The Sovereign Lord Jehovah was with us, not with them.
He’s with all of us now.
He’ll be with us during Armageddon.
He’ll be with us after Armageddon.
He’ll be with us at the end of the Thousand Year Reign of Christ.
He’ll be with mankind at the end of 100,000 years.
He’ll be with humans at the end of 100 million years
and at the end of 100 million years times 100 million years.
Jehovah will be with mankind forever,
and so will Jesus!
They are both on record as saying:
“I am with you”!
Thank you very much, Brother Lösch.
Today, Jehovah is with his people everywhere.
We’re going to see examples of this next.
First is the experience of Adam and Nancy Solomon.
When they came into the truth,
they faced bitter opposition from their families.
Notice how Jehovah was with them during this stressful time.
My family are Hungarian Jews.
Most of them were killed in concentration camps.
That’s something that the Holocaust took from me
—it took the concept of family.
I needed explanations.
I needed to know why my family was murdered.
It made me really search at a very young age to see
if there was a real religion out there.
It was just a secular thing to be Jewish;
it was a cultural thing.
A friend of mine came up to me and said:
“I have to tell you something.
“I got this book from one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
It is the most beautiful book I have ever read.”
I said, “Oh, I’ll read it.”
And it couldn’t have been a week later
that I got a knock on my door, and there were
two young women at the door who started to talk to me about the Bible.
Once I started having a study on a regular basis with Carolyn,
I enjoyed it more and more.
One day my father was home.
He just screamed at them
and basically threw them out of the house.
It just progressed after that.
There was just no peace at any time
and a lot of tears.
And I just couldn’t understand
why they weren’t even asking me:
“Well, what is it that you like about this religion?
“Who are these people?
Let us talk to—” No, nothing.
It was very, very hard.
Shortly after my baptism,
my mother came up to me, and she said:
“Your father and I are going out for the day.
You better not be here when we get home.”
I was 17 years old.
I didn’t know where I was going to go.
I didn’t know what I was going to do.
But I trusted in Jehovah.
And I picked up the phone, and I called my Carolyn.
In what seemed like minutes, there were brothers and sisters at the house.
They were putting my things into this truck and bringing it over to Carolyn’s house.
And she said, “You can live with me.”
Before I was baptized, I would drive back and forth
to school with a friend of mine.
Little by little, I was telling him what I was learning.
He said: “You know, I want to meet these people.
I have some questions.”
I had questions.
I asked them: “Why do we die?,
Why do we grow old?,” and so forth and so on.
And they went right to the Bible,
and when I left the house after that,
I said, “This is the truth!”
Growing up in my house, going to church every Sunday
was something that you had to do.
But when I became a teenager, then religion became less in my life,
and basketball became more.
Being a young man, you’d watch sports
and you’d see that sports players made a lot of money.
My teachers would tell my parents:
“He’s going to be a good basketball player.
“Take care of him.
“He could be worth, you know,
several hundred thousand dollars by the time he graduates.”
I received over 125 scholarships.
Now you’re talking about a free education
just because you can play basketball.
So I realized, you know, at an early age that playing
professional basketball could mean a lot,
not only for me but for my family.
So as far as God was concerned, I had a little interest in God
(like I would ask my mom questions),
but it wasn’t until Nancy brought me to the Witnesses
that really something just kicked in.
I was studying,
and my mom was downstairs in the basement.
I heard her crying, and I said, “What’s wrong?”
And she said, “I know you’re going to become one of those Jehovah’s Witnesses.”
So realizing in my mind
that I’m not going to become a basketball player
but that I’m going to become one of Jehovah’s Witnesses
because that’s more important
—that affected me many, many times.
When others found out
that I was going to become one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
people shied away.
People try to use you when they think
you can give them something or you’re going to be somebody big.
By going the direction of serving Jehovah completely,
you lost all the worldly people that you thought were your friends.
And so that was
in one summer that I started the study with Brother Crespo,
and in six months, I was baptized.
And then we decided to get married.
The scripture that says
that ‘even if my own father and my mother would abandon me,’
that even ‘Jehovah would take me in,’
—it proved to be true in so many ways.
Once you become one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
you’re part of a family that will do anything for you.
We’ve had adversity over the years,
but Jehovah never said everything was going to be perfect.
What he says is that when you face these problems,
you will not face them alone.
And Jehovah has never let us down when it comes to that.
When their families and friends abandoned them,
did you notice how Jehovah continued to be with Adam and Nancy?
Their spiritual family immediately stepped in to support them.
I appreciated what Nancy said:
‘Jehovah never said everything will be perfect.
‘He said that when you face problems,
you will not face them alone.’
She and Adam never felt alone.
Often, we ask Jehovah to be with us when we need something
—a spiritual need or a material need.
But as we’ll see in this next experience,
even before we know that we have a need,
Jehovah already knows what we need.
My name is Reeta.
My son is Jackson, and my daughter is Sherina.
It’s just the three of us.
I have been working on a tea estate as a tea picker.
One day, I prayed to God very hard.
I said,
“Please help me to learn about the Bible.”
Within two days, Jehovah’s Witnesses came
and knocked on my door, and I agreed to study the Bible.
I couldn’t believe it.
I only prayed yesterday, asking God to help me to study the Bible.
Our meetings begin at 4:45 p.m.,
but we have to get ready by 12 o’clock
to attend the meetings.
So we prepare our bags on Wednesday night.
I carry two big bags on my shoulders
and walk for three and a half kilometers (2 mi)
to get to the meetings on time.
We love seeing our brothers.
That’s why we always go to the meetings early.
I have been pioneering now for a year and six months.
There is no greater happiness than what comes from pioneering.
This is a onetime opportunity.
That is why we decided that we should give the best that we can to Jehovah.
Now I am so happy to be serving this way.
One time, I was not paid at all.
I didn’t even have a rupee.
On that day, my children and I ate well.
But after eating, we were very worried
about what we were going to do the following day.
So that night, I said a prayer with the kids
and we read the Bible.
Jesus said,
‘Don’t worry about tomorrow.’
So I trusted that somehow
Jehovah would give us what we needed.
It was 10:30 at night.
I was fast asleep, and the phone rang.
Usually no one calls this late,
so I wondered, ‘Who could be calling me this late?’
I picked up the phone, and it was a brother on the line.
He said, “Sister, go to your bookshelf
and take the Greatest Man book.”
Then he asked me to turn to a page.
When I turned to that page,
there were 10,000 rupees (about $55, U.S.) between those pages.
We could not believe our eyes.
It was exactly what we needed for that month’s expenses.
A few days earlier, he and his wife had visited us
and secretly left the money in the book before leaving.
So I thanked Jehovah in prayer with the kids.
Jehovah already knew exactly what we needed
even before we realized it.
Honestly, every night I open the doors,
go outside, and look up at the night sky.
When I look up, I see many stars.
I daily meditate about his wisdom,
his power, what amazing things he is able to do.
This earth, this universe
—how amazingly well he cares for them!
He takes care of the smallest thing.
I completely rely on Jehovah,
and then I remember that Jehovah has the ability
to help us with his holy spirit.
He’s such a loving Father.
He’s always holding our hand tight,
and no one can separate us from him.
If anyone tries, they will fail.
He’s so generous with his love.
He’s so affectionate with us.
No one can take away the love Jehovah has for us.
Did you notice from Reeta’s experience
that Jehovah is with us in several ways?
Reeta really appreciates congregation meetings.
They love being with their brothers.
How about you?
Do you value the meetings
and the encouraging association you find there?
Reeta takes time to meditate on the wonders of creation,
and she does more than marvel at what she sees.
She notices how Jehovah’s love and care for her
is evident in all his works.
She knows that Jehovah has the power to create anything,
and he wants to use his power in her behalf.
It’s no surprise that Reeta is keenly aware
of Jehovah’s constant support in her pioneer ministry.
Jehovah proves to be with us in the ministry,
whether we’re preaching in our local community
or sharing in a special campaign.
Let’s go to Europe
and watch a report about a special campaign.
As with Reeta’s experience,
see if you can identify
how Jehovah was with the many thousands
who volunteered for this campaign.
In the Central Europe branch territory,
a special campaign was organized.
Actually, the School
for Branch Committee Members and Their Wives
triggered an evaluation of how much territory
in the countries we oversee is not really covered thoroughly.
So we asked our circuit overseers
to recommend to us which sections
of the congregation’s territory
could be listed as so-called “unassigned territory.”
All in all, we received over 11,000 territories
from the congregations, with approximately 3 million inhabitants.
So because of this grand scale, there was suddenly the idea,
‘Why not organize a special preaching campaign
‘to cover all these territories
on one single weekend?’
This was really exciting.
And after getting the Branch Committee’s approval,
the Service Department started to organize it.
To be honest, at first, we were not really sure
how the publishers would react to such a campaign.
But we fully trusted in Jehovah,
and the response was stunning.
Over 20,000 publishers participated
and were assigned to all these territories throughout Germany.
The campaign took place on one weekend in May 2017
and was especially successful in metropolitan areas,
as in Berlin, Hamburg, and Düsseldorf.
At one door, a man just arrived.
He wanted to open his shop where he sells Arabian specialties.
We were able to show him a video in Arabic.
Then he gave us his address and phone number.
He also agreed to have someone visit him again.
Yes, it’s really a privilege to join in such a campaign
and to see that every human is precious to Jehovah,
no matter where they live or where they come from.
Because of the need and the fantastic response in 2017,
it was decided to repeat such a campaign in May 2018.
And this time it was expanded to Switzerland,
Austria, Luxembourg, and Liechtenstein.
And now imagine,
over 32,000 publishers participated,
which is actually over 60 percent more
than in May 2017.
This was really faith-strengthening.
And, again, a lot of wonderful experiences were reported.
It’s incredible.
No matter where you are in Berlin,
you can see small groups of brothers everywhere.
That was really great.
In the ministry we met a woman, and she told us
that she had just prayed for a Bible study.
We are now more than ever convinced
that Jehovah leads all this work
through his angels.
Today, Sunday, we had a nice experience.
A woman called us from behind.
She had actually already passed us,
but she had the feeling she had to go back again
—she told us later.
After she had invited us to her home,
we exchanged our contact information
and we also filled in the online contact form.
Had we been in the territory just one minute later,
we would never have made the contact.
This must have been guided by the angels.
Yesterday morning while in the ministry,
a young man ran after us and asked us what we were doing.
We explained it to him.
He asked us why there is still so much evil in the world, then.
In the afternoon, we were able to call on him again.
We could start a Bible study right away
and arrange a return visit, which we will make today.
Being together with the friends is just so great.
You’re out and about with a large group.
You meet up again regularly
to change partners and to relate experiences.
It’s just great.
Thousands of videos were shown,
and a lot of Bible studies were started.
And what is very interesting is that a lot of publishers
felt motivated to expand their ministry after the campaign.
For sure, these preaching campaigns truly prove
that Jehovah and Jesus are directing the preaching work.
And the angels are helping us in reaching out to all people.
Yes, we really have a lot of reasons to be Jehovah’s happy people.
Jehovah truly proved to be
with all who volunteered to share in this campaign.
How else could the good news reach three million people
in such a well-organized way?
We’d like to thank the more than 32,000 brothers and sisters
who shared in this special work.
As Brother Lösch noted in his talk,
Jehovah is with us in the ministry.
There’s no doubt he is directing the global preaching work
through Jesus and his angels.
Did you notice how many people were contacted
soon after they prayed for a Bible study
or for a question to be answered?
Isn’t that interesting?
When we’re together with a large group of Jehovah’s people
in the ministry and at our meetings and assemblies,
we really feel Jehovah’s blessing, don’t we?
But what if we’re isolated?
What if we’re facing persecution?
This is what Alphonse Takla experienced some years ago in Egypt.
Let’s see how Jehovah proved to be with him.
All was dark;
everything was pitch-black dark.
Egypt was at war with Israel,
and they were arresting the brothers,
charging us of practicing illegal activities
as a banned organization.
On that night, we were being transferred
to the concentration camp.
We couldn’t see much.
“What’s going on there? What’s this place look like? Where is it?”
The officer got two soldiers to escort us
to our cell where the brothers were.
We knew that when people are taken to the concentration camp,
they spend years
and some of them never return back.
When I was, you know, a teenager,
I liked the characters in the Bible,
like Abraham,
Daniel,
Moses.
I thought that they were champions of true worship.
At some stage, I felt jealous of them.
They had this huge relationship with God,
so I’d like to be part of that.
I continued to read the Bible
to get closer to God.
I knew that Jehovah would look after me;
he would not abandon his servant.
So we tried to encourage them:
“Brothers, keep in mind
that we’re here because we worship Jehovah.”
We sat together to discuss, you know,
what we were going to do
to keep spiritually strong.
So we thought that we needed to pray.
We picked out a scripture every day, like a daily text,
and then after that, recited scriptures.
One would handle a talk from the memory of heart
and then an open discussion of Bible questions.
At that stage, we didn’t have a Bible with us.
The officers wanted us to renounce our faith,
so they told me to lay on the ground,
and there they started to beat me.
The whole camp was around,
and one of the prisoners fainted.
I started to pray to Jehovah:
“Jehovah, help me to be able to endure that!”
It was very severe pain.
And I felt his help because after a few beatings,
my body felt numb.
I didn’t feel much more pain.
One of the prisoners said to me,
“If I get out of here alive,
“I’ll tell my children that in the concentration camp,
“I saw the Christians that reminded me of the first-century Christians
—that they were happy even to die without renouncing their faith.”
One of the officers
—this nasty one that used to beat us very, very severely—
came one day and said,
“We need two of you to come out
and write a report about what you believe.”
So we thought about it: ‘Is it wise to do that?
Or maybe they will use it against us.’
You know, we prayed to Jehovah for help to make a decision here,
to guide us on what to do.
So in the end, we reached a point that,
well, we may get out; we may not.
So we might as well give them a witness.
I told the officer, “We need a Bible.”
And he said, “What for?”
I said to him, “Because we need to quote from the Bible in this report.”
So he said, “OK, do you have a Bible in the storeroom?”
I said, “Yes, I have a Bible.”
He said, “OK, go and get your Bible.”
I went to my bag and picked up the Bible.
So he picked up the Bible from my hand, opened it randomly, and started to read.
“Numbers.”
He looked at me. “Who wrote this book?”
I said to him, “Moses.”
“You’re a liar!” at the top of his voice.
So I kept quiet,
and he closed the book again
and opened it again.
“You’re a liar!” again at the top of his voice.
I was racing in my mind where it is written in the Bible
that Jehovah told Moses to write any of this.
He shut the book again, and for a third time,
opened it again, and he started to read in a loud voice.
So the officer looked at me with a big surprise on his face.
After we wrote the report,
I asked him, “Can we keep the Bible, please?”
He said, “OK, keep the Bible.”
For three months, nearly every day,
the officers came in and beat us
and expected us to compromise.
We never did that.
All I can say is that it was Jehovah’s hand.
Jehovah was helping us to endure
—to continue to do his will
by not compromising because we belong to him
and we rely on him.
God will not abandon his servant.
Why was Alphonse thrown into prison?
It wasn’t because he refused to say
a simple greeting to the president of his country.
No, that phrase was a political slogan.
Like many Jehovah’s Witnesses,
Alphonse was persecuted for his neutrality.
What helped Alphonse to be loyal?
He prayed.
He prayed to maintain a strong spiritual routine,
he prayed when he had to make a decision,
and he prayed for help to endure brutal treatment.
Like Alphonse, do you depend on the power of prayer?
Alphonse and, earlier, Reeta
likened their relationship with Jehovah to holding His hand.
Reeta said, ‘Jehovah holds our hand tight.’
Alphonse said, “All I can say is that it was Jehovah’s hand.”
What a beautiful image!
That’s how close we can be to Jehovah.
This month’s music video reminds us of that.
Jehovah is always willing to hold our hand.
It’s entitled Jehovah’s Always by Our Side.
At times, I felt scared inside, Only looking for a place to hide.
The world made me feel different. Now I hold my head up high.
He said he’d be my confidence, That he’d come to my defense.
His love I can’t deny,
’Cause he gave me Courage when I was feeling weak,
Courage when I could not speak, Courage in my darkest night,
Courage to stand up tall, Courage to face it all,
Courage to trust him with my life. Jehovah’s always by my side.
He walks with me To help me see
His ways are always right. He’ll take my hand,
Help me understand It’s worth the sacrifice.
You are not alone. Even far away from home,
He’ll be your guide. He will pick you up
Even when you think you’ve had enough And make you strong and wise,
’Cause he’ll give you Courage when you are feeling weak,
Courage when you cannot speak, Courage in your darkest nights,
Courage to stand up tall, Courage to face it all,
Courage to trust him with your life. Jehovah’s always by our side—
Always, always. Jehovah’s always by our side.
He walks with you and me To help us see
His ways are always right. Jehovah’s always by our side.
He’ll take our hand, Help us understand
It’s worth the sacrifice.
He gave me Courage when I was feeling weak,
Courage when I could not speak, Courage in my darkest night,
Courage to stand up tall, Courage to face it all,
Courage to trust him with my life. Jehovah’s always by our side—
Always, always. Jehovah’s always by our side—
Always, always. Jehovah’s always by our side.
What a beautiful song!
For many months on JW Broadcasting,
we’ve enjoyed a series of video dramatizations
about applying Bible principles in our lives.
We have learned that we can enjoy happier lives today
and live in a way that pleases God
when we apply Jehovah’s principles and standards.
Applying God’s principles also gives us a wonderful hope.
As our concluding video in this series shows,
focusing on our future hope
helps us to build the faith
to withstand trials we face today.
See if you remember these scenes.
Getting baptized
was the most important decision I ever made.
But it took some time to realize that
that was just the start of my Christian life.
Sometimes it was hard to show courage.
Why don’t you people get involved and make a real difference for once?
And it was hard for my son too.
No thanks.
I’m a Jehovah’s Witness, and I don’t celebrate birthdays.
What?
Hum?
That’s rude.
Come on, sign it!
I really liked Lucas,
and he was very sick.
I really wanted to sign his birthday card,
but Dad helped me to see how Jehovah felt about it,
and that helped me be brave.
I still didn’t sign the card,
but I’m going to do something else for Lucas.
My parents had always set a good example for me.
But after I moved to serve where the need was greater,
it seemed like my parents were growing apart.
Are you both doing OK?
Because you don’t look OK.
Of course, we’re OK.
OK? We’re doing wonderful, right?
Yeah, we’re doing good.
Everything is good.
I was really worried.
Later, they told me that what helped them
was their love for Jehovah.
They meditated on the example of Abraham and Sarah,
who showed honor to each other by listening and by caring.
That example really helped my parents.
And since then,
I’ve seen how it can help in any relationship.
I’m a long way from home, but showing love to others
—it helps me to stay happy in my assignment.
When our doctor told us that our baby
would likely be born with severe problems
and could even die,
it was more than I could bear.
And because my husband was not one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
I needed God’s help more than ever
to calm my heart and help me explain why I could never have an abortion.
And even though it took me years
before I would agree to a Bible study
and even more years before I made enough changes to qualify for baptism,
the life we have now
—serving Jehovah together—
nothing could make me happier.
Nothing could make us happier.
Happiness really does come from serving Jehovah,
but serving him faithfully definitely takes courage.
It was so hard for me to turn down that girl at school.
And I felt so guilty for how involved I’d gotten with her.
My uncle used the Bible to help me get back on track
and to remind me of two other very important things:
that Jehovah was proud of me and that I was not alone.
James 1:2, 3 says:
“Consider it all joy, my brothers,
“when you meet with various trials,
“knowing as you do
“that this tested quality of your faith
produces endurance.”
I think about that scripture a lot
because soon I’ll probably be sent
to prison for refusing military service.
Being courageous with that classmate
helped me build the faith and courage that I need now.
I can give up anything for Jehovah.
I might live in a small cell for now,
but in Paradise, I’m going to travel everywhere.
Sometimes I get lonely, but that’s OK.
It’s a choice that I’ve made to stay in my assignment right now.
In the future, if I choose to get married,
I hope to have a marriage like my parents.
I really hope that Lucas is resurrected so I can show him around Paradise
and teach him more about Jehovah.
I showed him pictures,
but the real thing will be so much better.
Then I can hold my baby girl again.
Our program has focused on the many ways
that Jehovah is with us.
He’s with us as we work toward dedication
and baptism.
He’s with us at our congregation meetings
and when we are with our spiritual family.
He’s with us as we successfully face
persecution and hardship.
And Jehovah is with us
when we share the good news of his Kingdom
with everyone we meet.
And, Brother Marais,
I appreciate that you were here with me
for this month’s program.
Thank you, Brother Lösch.
We end this month’s program
with a visit to our brothers and sisters in Tenerife.
Tenerife is the largest of the Canary Islands,
an archipelago off the northwest coast of Africa.
These islands were formed by volcanic eruptions.
The highest point
is the dormant Teide volcano on Tenerife.
Here the weather is mild and sunny throughout the year.
This has made the Canary Islands famous for their extensive banana plantations.
Tenerife is a popular tourist destination.
It’s home to nearly a million people,
but more than ten million visitors
come every year to enjoy the beaches,
the lush terrain,
and the food.
The island of Tenerife has 33 congregations
and more than 3,000 publishers,
492 of whom are regular pioneers.
Because of the influx of visitors from all over the world,
our brothers and sisters preach in over 15 languages,
including Russian,
German,
French,
Hindi,
and Romanian.
They preach everywhere
—in the cities as well as the rural and mountainous regions.
Our brothers and sisters in Tenerife
send you their warm Christian love and greetings.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting.

천사장 미가엘이 모세의 시체를 놓고 마귀와 논쟁했다는 점은
악한 자들에게 심판을 집행하실 것이라는 에녹의 예언도
하느님께서 심판을 집행하신 여러 예들에 유의해 보고,
유다가 사용한 생생한 비유들을 묵상해 보고,
하느님의 왕국을 상속받을 희망을 가진 사람들이
순결함과 영성을 지키기를 유다가 얼마나 간절히 바랐는지

en.text: An introduction to the book of Jude.
The Jude, or Judas, who wrote this inspired letter
was evidently the same Judas named as a half brother of Jesus Christ.
Jude wrote his letter about 65 C.E.,
likely from his Jewish homeland.
At the time, a threatening situation had developed:
immoral, animalistic men
had begun to slip into the congregation.
So Jude stressed the need for Christians
to put up a hard fight for the faith.
The letter of Jude has 25 verses.
In verse 5, Jude reminds us
that Jehovah, after delivering his people from Egypt,
destroyed the Israelites who showed a gross lack of faith.
Likewise, verse 7 says
that “Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them”
are “a warning example
by undergoing the judicial punishment of everlasting fire.”
Using powerful metaphors,
verses 12 and 13 describe the wicked intruders
who enter into the Christian congregation
as “rocks hidden below water,”
as “waterless clouds carried here and there by the wind,”
as “fruitless trees” that have been uprooted,
and as “wild waves of the sea that cast up the foam.”
Did you know?
Jude’s letter has information not found elsewhere in the Bible.
Jude alone mentions
the archangel Michael’s dispute with the Devil
over Moses’ body.
And only Jude mentions Enoch’s prophecy
that God, using myriads of angels,
would execute judgment against the wicked.
Jude concludes his letter
by urging his brothers to keep themselves “in God’s love,”
to “continue showing mercy to some who have doubts,”
and to “save them by snatching them out of the fire.”
As you read Jude’s letter,
note his many references to examples of God’s judgments,
meditate on his vivid illustrations,
and observe how concerned he was about the purity and spirituality
of those who hope to inherit God’s Kingdom.

title: 우연의 산물인가? 색이 결코 바래지 않는 새의 깃털

ko.text: 하지만 많은 종의 새들은 그렇지 않습니다.
주로 깃털 구조의 미세한 차이 때문에
깃털 표면의 모양에 따라 빛이 분산되어
우리 눈에 보이는 여러 색을 내는 것입니다.
깃털의 구조는 시간이 지나도 변하지 않기 때문에
이러한 발견은 새로운 가능성의 장을 열어 주었습니다.
우리도 같은 방식으로 제품에 색을 낼 수 있다.”
연구가들은 새의 깃털을 모방한 물질을 개발 중입니다.
여러 번 빨아도 새것처럼 색이 선명한 천을 만들 수도 있을 것입니다.
색이 결코 바래지 않는 새의 깃털은 진화된 것입니까?

en.text: Colors fade on man-made materials
—for example, paint and clothing.
Yet, for many species of birds this isn’t the case.
Their feathers remain permanently bright and vivid.
What’s their secret?
Researchers
examining the feathers of the Eurasian jay
discovered that their colors are generated
primarily by small changes in feather structure,
as opposed to pigment.
Surface variations scatter the reflected light,
which produces the hues we see.
And since this structure doesn’t change with age,
the colors never fade.
This discovery opens a whole new world
of possibilities.
Dr. Andrew Parnell states:
“If nature can assemble this material ‘on the wing,’
then we should be able to do it synthetically.”
Researchers are now working to produce
materials that mimic this.
This could lead to paints that never fade,
and perhaps even fabrics that look new
and vibrant wash after wash.
What do you think?
Did the unfading color of bird feathers
come about by evolution?
Or was it designed?

cn.text: 人造的很多东西都会褪色
例如颜料和衣服
可是很多种鸟的羽毛色彩鲜艳
永远不会褪色
为什么会这样呢？
研究员发现
松鸦身上的羽毛呈现不同的颜色
主要是因为结构上的差异而非色素
光线照在不同结构的羽毛上
就会产生不同的颜色
羽毛的结构不会随着时间而改变
所以鸟儿身上的颜色永远都不会褪色
这项发现给研究员很多新的灵感
安德鲁·帕尔内尔博士说
研究员想模仿这样的结构，研发出新的材料
例如不会褪色的颜料
甚至做出无论洗多少次都色泽鲜艳的布料
你觉得怎样？
鸟不会褪色的羽毛
是进化而来的？还是经过设计的呢？

ko.text: 하지만 아주 작은 불이 얼마나 큰 숲을 태워 버리는지
하지만 혀는 작아도 엄청난 힘이 있습니다.
사실 이 작은 혀로 수만 킬로그램을 들어 올릴 수 있는데요,
예를 들어 대회 사회자가 이렇게 말할 때죠.
좋게 쓰일 수도 있고, 나쁘게도 쓰입니다.
조심하지 않으면 혀는 큰 해를 초래할 수 있죠.
아주 작은 성냥불이라도 아무렇게나 던져 버리면,
넓은 아름다운 숲 전체를 완전히 태워 버릴 수 있는 것처럼요.
그럼, 파괴적인 산불과도 같은 말에는 어떤 게 있을까요?
거짓말, 중상, 험담, 해로운 소문 이야기,
하지만 오늘 살펴볼 말은 종류가 좀 다른 건데요,
더 교묘하고 은밀하면서도 아주 해로운 말입니다.
“희미하고 지속적인 낮은 소리나 소리의 연속”이란 뜻도 있죠.
물론, 자연에는 아주 듣기 좋은 그런 소리가 참 많습니다.
예를 들어, 산들바람에 나뭇잎이 바스락거리는 소리를 들으면
시냇물이 졸졸 흐르는 소리를 들어도 마음이 즐겁죠.
하지만 사람의 혀에서 나는 투덜거리는 소리는 다릅니다.
이 히브리어 단어가 가진 또 다른 의미는
물론 사탄의 세상에선 투덜거리는 게 보통이죠.
온갖 나쁜 일에 대해 그분을 탓합니다.
여기에 나오는 흥미로운 기록에서 여호와의 견해를 엿볼 수 있습니다.
[아마도 한두 번 말한 게 아닐 겁니다].
여호와께서는 그 많은 질병 중에서 왜 하필
특히 성경 시대에 나병에 걸린 사람의 모습은
투덜거리고 있던 미리암의 영적인 모습이 흉측했을 겁니다.
여호와께선 미리암에게서 이미 보신 모습이 어떠한지
두 장 뒤엔 또 다른 기록이 있는데요.
정탐꾼 열 명의 부정적인 보고를 듣고 나서
그의 마음속에선 불만이 점점 더 쌓이게 됩니다.
게다가 투덜거리는 사람은 불평을 늘어놓기 때문에
자기 처지에 불만을 품도록 최초로 부추긴 자는 누구입니까?
그는 하와의 마음속에 불만이 싹트게 했습니다.
따라서 투덜거리는 사람은 마귀의 방식을 따르는 것이고,
여호와께서는 그런 사람을 보면서 대적 사탄을 떠올리실 겁니다.
“만족할 줄 안다면 경건한 정성은 큰 이득이 됩니다.”
우리가 여호와께 받은 축복들에 대해 생각해 본다면,
두 번째 이유로, 투덜거리면 미움이 생깁니다.
우리 자신과 다른 사람들의 마음 모두에요.
문제를 계속 이야기하는 자는 친한 친구들을 갈라놓는 것이다.”
보셨듯이, 우린 사랑으로 다른 사람의 잘못을 덮고 용서해야 합니다.
그의 잘못에 대해 계속 이야기하면서 투덜거린다면,
우리 마음에 그에 대한 미움이 자랄 겁니다.
“왜 원망하지 말아야 하는가?”란 기사에 이런 예가 나옵니다.
임명된 장로에 관하여 당신에게 불평을 한다고 가정해 보자.
만일 당신이 그 불평을 들어 준다면
당신도 그와 같이 생각하게 될 수 있다.
다음에 그 장로를 볼 때, 당신은 속으로
‘이제 보니 친구가 이 장로에 관하여 말한 것이 맞아,
전에는 전혀 그렇다고 생각지는 않았는데’ 하고 말하게 될 수 있다.”
네, 전엔 괜찮던 것이 이제는 못마땅해 보이고,
결국 그 장로의 행동 하나하나가 눈에 거슬리게 될 수 있습니다.
세 번째 이유로, 투덜거림은 교만을 드러냅니다.
온 회중이 다 거룩하고 여호와께서 그들 가운데 계시오.
여호와의 회중 위에 자신을 높이는 거요?”
그들의 마음속 상태를, 즉 교만을 드러냈습니다.
우리의 말로 다른 사람을 깎아내려 자신을 높이려고 해서는 안 됩니다.
투덜거리는 사람이 되지 않기 위한 해결책은
만족하는 태도와 사랑과 겸손을 기르는 것입니다.
여호와께 우리가 그분의 조직의 자산임을 증명할 수 있죠.
앞으로 신세계에서도 우리를 반겨 주실 것입니다.

en.text: James 3:5, 6 tells us in part:
“The tongue is a small part of the body,
“and yet . . . see how small a fire it takes
“to set a great forest ablaze!
The tongue is also a fire.”
Well, just how small is the tongue?
An average adult’s tongue weighs
only about two and a half ounces (70 g).
That’s a small part of the body weight of a 200-pound (90 kg) man.
But that little two-ounce tongue has great power.
If you think about it, it can actually lift thousands of pounds of weight
—for example, when a chairman at a convention says, “Please stand.”
Of course, that power
can be used for good or for bad.
And the warning in today’s scripture text:
If we’re not careful, it can cause great damage,
just like a tiny lighted match flipped carelessly aside
can burn thousands of acres
of beautiful trees to the ground.
Well, what are types of speech that can be like a destructive fire?
Lying, slander, backbiting, harmful gossip,
and false teaching —a few examples.
But during our discussion, let’s talk
about a type of speech that may be more subtle, more insidious,
but nevertheless is very harmful.
What is it? Murmuring.
Let’s discuss: “Avoid Murmuring.”
Now, what is murmuring?
According to the dictionary, to murmur
means “to make a low, continuous,
indistinct sound or succession of sounds.”
Of course, in nature,
there are many very pleasant murmuring sounds.
For example, it’s pleasant to listen
to gentle breezes murmur through the leaves of trees.
It’s soothing to listen
to a small stream murmuring its way
through a forest or down a mountain slope.
But the same cannot be said about murmuring by the human tongue.
It is far from pleasant.
One dictionary said that “murmuring by humans
“means complaining
in low mumbling tones, grumbling.”
The Watchtower said
that “the Hebrew term meaning ‘to murmur’ can also mean ‘to growl.’”
When we’re out in service and if a dog growls at us,
it’s not a pleasant sound that draws us.
We want to distance ourselves.
Of course, murmuring permeates Satan’s world.
Children murmur against their parents;
wives murmur against their husbands;
employees murmur against their employers;
multitudes murmur against God,
blaming him for bad things that happen.
But, now, here’s an important question, How does Jehovah view murmuring?
Well, open up to Numbers chapter 12, please,
and here’s an interesting account
that gives us some insight into Jehovah’s viewpoint
—Numbers 12:1:
“Now Miriam and Aaron
“began to speak against Moses
because of the Cushite wife he had married.”
Verse 2: “They were saying
“[and apparently on an ongoing basis]:
“‘Is it only by Moses
“‘that Jehovah has spoken?
Has he not also spoken through us?’”
Now notice the next thought:
“And Jehovah was listening.”
And Jehovah didn’t like what he heard, did he?
If you look at verse 9, his “anger burned,”
and he struck Miriam with leprosy.
Now think about this: Of all the diseases
Jehovah could have struck Miriam with,
why did he choose leprosy?
Well, Jehovah doesn’t tell us.
But think about this: A person struck with leprosy,
especially in Bible times, was made physically repulsive,
or (you could say) physically ugly.
Well, by talking the way she was talking already,
she was spiritually repulsive in Jehovah’s eyes.
So by striking her with leprosy,
Jehovah allowed everyone to see
what Jehovah already saw in Miriam.
There’s another account two chapters later.
It talks about how the Israelites began to murmur
after hearing the negative report
from the ten spies.
How did Jehovah react?
He decreed that all the murmurers 20 years of age and over
would never make it to the Promised Land.
They would die in the wilderness.
So, obviously, Jehovah hates murmuring.
You could say that he abominates it.
But now the question is, Why?
Well, let’s briefly discuss three reasons.
One: It breeds discontent
both in ourselves and in others.
Jude 16 speaks of ‘murmurers
complaining about their lot in life.’
And it’s true that the more
a person complains about his lot in life,
then the deeper the discontent becomes in his own heart.
And since murmurers never keep their complaints to themselves,
it sows discontent in others.
And if you think about this:
Who was the original promoter of discontent with one’s lot in life?
Satan the Devil.
He succeeded in sowing discontent in Eve’s heart.
So a murmurer is actually imitating the methods of the Devil,
and apparently a murmurer
reminds Jehovah of his archenemy, Satan.
And that’s certainly something no wise person wants to do
—to remind Jehovah of Satan.
Well, what is the antidote?
Cultivating contentment.
First Timothy 6:6:
“There is great gain in godly devotion along with contentment.”
And several scriptures talk about contentment.
And when we count our blessings that we have from Jehovah,
we can be content —can’t we?—
no matter what our circumstances now.
A second reason Jehovah hates it:
It incites hatred,
again, both in our own heart and in others.
Open up to Proverbs chapter 17, please.
And here’s an interesting scripture on this,
Proverbs 17:9:
“Whoever forgives a transgression seeks love,
“but the one who keeps harping on a matter
separates close friends.”
So notice, love should move us to cover over, forgive, the transgressions of others.
But if we don’t do that and we keep harping
about their transgressions,
murmuring about them,
then hatred for that one grows in our own heart.
And how does it affect others?
Well, again, it sows hatred in their heart.
The Watchtower some years ago had a little article
“Why Keep Free from Murmuring?”
And it gave an example.
It says: “Suppose . . . a Christian starts to complain to you
“about a certain appointed elder
“[about how he performs his duties, how he] . . .
handles his parts on the platform.”
And it says: “If you listen to the complainer,
“you can begin to think as he does.
“Then, as you observe the elder, you could be saying to yourself:
“‘Now that I think [about] it,
“‘what my friend says about this elder is true.
I never thought of it that way before.’”
Before it didn’t bother you; now it bothers you.
Eventually, everything the elder does
can be improper in your eyes.
But, now, what is the antidote?
Well, like it said in Proverbs:
“Whoever forgives a transgression seeks love”
—so cultivating love, making allowances for others,
forgiving them, not harping about their transgressions,
but forgiving as we pray and hope Jehovah will do for us.
But, now, the third reason Jehovah hates it: It manifests pride.
Korah, Dathan, Abiram
—remember they murmured against Moses.
“We have had enough of you!
“The whole assembly is holy, all of them,
“and Jehovah is in their midst.
“Why, then, should you exalt yourselves
above the congregation of Jehovah?”
Their murmuring was an outward expression
of an inward condition—pride.
And we know how Jehovah reacted in that case.
But, now, what’s the antidote?
Humility, lowliness of mind
—not trying to tear others down
with our talking to elevate ourselves.
But lowliness of mind will protect us.
So we’ve discussed that murmuring
breeds discontent, incites hatred, manifests pride.
No wonder Jehovah hates it.
But as we said, if we cultivate contentment,
love, and we cultivate humility,
these will serve as antidotes to our ever becoming murmurers.
And we’ll be successful in applying Philippians 2:14,
which says: “Keep doing all things
free from murmuring.”
And it didn’t say most things.
“Keep doing all things free from murmuring,”
and we’ll prove to Jehovah that we’re assets in his organization.
He’ll want us in his organization now;
he’ll want us in his new world in the future.

cn.text: 雅各书3:5,6说
“舌头在身体中虽然很小......看
一点小火苗就能使一大片森林烧起来！
舌头就是火。”
你们知道舌头有多重吗？
成年人的舌头重量只有70克左右
对于一个70公斤的人来说
舌头的重量也许不算什么
舌头虽小，但力量可不小
你知道吗？
一个小小的舌头
可以举起几千甚至几万公斤的重物
例如:大会主席对全场说
“请站起来。”
舌头发挥的力量可以带来益处
也可以造成伤害
今天的经文提醒我们
如果我们不小心运用舌头
就可能造成巨大的伤害
打个比方，一根小小的火柴
点着后，如果随意乱丢
就可能使数千公顷的森林化为灰烬
那么什么样的言谈
有这么大的杀伤力呢？
比如:谎言、诽谤、中伤
害人的闲话、错误的道理等等
现在我们来谈谈另外一种言谈
这种言谈不易察觉，但杀伤力极强
这是什么呢？
就是埋怨
我们今天要谈的主题是
“不要埋怨”
“埋怨”这个词的英语是“murmur”
一部英语辞典对这个词的解释是
发出连续而轻微的声音
当然，这个词也可以描述
自然界里美妙的声音
比如:微风吹过树叶时的沙沙声
小溪穿过山林时的潺潺声
这些声音让我们感到身心愉悦
但当这个词用来描述舌头发出的声音时
就一点也不美妙了
一部英语辞典对murmur的另一个解释是
低声埋怨或抱怨
我们的出版物也谈到murmur的希伯来语
含有“低声吼叫”的意思
我们在外面传道时
如果有一只狗对我们低声吼叫
听到这样的声音我们肯定不想靠近
甚至想躲得越远越好
撒但的世界就弥漫着埋怨的精神
孩子埋怨父母
妻子批评丈夫
员工抱怨老板
还有很多人也指责上帝
觉得他应该为世上的坏事负责
接下来我们要思考一个重要的问题
耶和华怎么看待埋怨呢？
请打开民数记第12章
这个记载可以帮助我们
看出上帝的观点是什么
民数记12:1,2谈到
米利暗和亚伦因为摩西娶了古实人做妻子
就批评他
他们说
“难道耶和华只通过摩西一个人说话吗？
他不也通过我们说话吗？”
接下来请留意经文说
“这些话耶和华都听见了。”
耶和华很不喜欢这些话
我们怎么知道呢？
9节说:“耶和华向他们发怒”
他就使米利暗长了麻风
其实，耶和华可以用其他疾病来打击米利暗
但为什么偏偏选择用麻风病呢？
他没告诉我们
但请想想，一个人如果患了麻风病
尤其在圣经时代，没有人想接近他
因为他看起来很可怕、很丑
当米利暗对摩西发怨言的时候
她在上帝眼中就已经变得非常丑陋了
所以，耶和华打击米利暗
使她长了麻风
这样别人就能看出
在耶和华眼中米利暗是怎样的人
另外一个例子是在民数记的第14章
听到10个探子带回来的坏消息后
以色列人就开始大发怨言
耶和华作出判决
所有发怨言的人，只要年满20岁
都不可进入应许之地，全都会死在旷野
所以我们看出
耶和华不喜欢人发怨言
也可以说他憎恨怨言
那么耶和华为什么憎恨人发怨言呢？
我们会简单谈谈三个原因
第一个原因是
发怨言会激起自己和别人的不满
犹大书16节说
常常抱怨的人总是对境遇诸多不满
换句话说，一个人越是常常抱怨
他心里就会越来越不满
如果我们常常向人抱怨
就会影响别人
把不满的种子撒在别人心里
想一想
最初是谁把不满的种子撒在别人心里呢？
就是魔鬼撒但
他成功地把不满的种子撒在夏娃的心里
所以，一个人如果发怨言
就是在效法魔鬼
这会让耶和华联想到他的大仇敌——撒但
明智的人肯定不会这样做
有什么方法可以帮助我们不发怨言呢？
就是要培养知足的态度
提摩太前书6:6说
“虔诚而又知足，就会得到许多益处。”
圣经也有其他经文谈到知足
所以，不管我们的情况怎样
只要我们数算耶和华赐给我们的福分
我们就都会感到知足
耶和华不喜欢人发怨言的第二个原因是
发怨言会激起自己和别人的恨意
我们一起看看箴言第17章
有一节经文很有意思
箴言17:9说
“原谅别人过错的，追求爱心
反复谈论过失的，离间密友。”
经文说
爱会推动我们遮盖、原谅别人的过错
可是如果我们反复谈论别人的过失
常常抱怨，我们就会越来越讨厌那个人
那么听我们抱怨的人又会受到什么影响呢？
他们也可能开始讨厌我们埋怨的对象
多年前有一篇《守望台》文章
标题是《为什么要避免发怨言？》
里面有一个例子
假设一位基督徒开始跟你埋怨某位长老
他批评长老处理问题的方式
还有在聚会里的教导方式
如果你听这个人抱怨
你可能就开始跟他有同样的想法了
当你再次留意这位长老的时候
你就可能想:“我朋友说的没错
他真的是这样的人
我以前从来没有留意到。”
在这之前
你没发现那位长老有什么问题
但现在你受到影响了
到后来，不管这位长老怎么做
你都觉得有问题
那么，我们可以怎么做呢？
就像箴言说的
“原谅别人过错的，追求爱心”
也就是要培养爱心，包容别人
原谅别人的过错
就好像我们求耶和华
希望他原谅我们一样
第三个原因是什么呢？
发怨言是骄傲的表现
可拉、大坦、亚比兰对摩西大发怨言说
“我们受够了！民众都是圣洁的
所有人都是，耶和华也在他们当中
你们为什么抬高自己
凌驾于耶和华的会众之上？”
他们说的话反映了他们的内心情况
就是骄傲
我们都知道耶和华对这件事有什么反应
那么我们可以怎么做呢？
就是要培养谦卑，看别人比自己优越
谦卑的人不会贬低别人、抬高自己
谦卑可以为我们带来保护
我们刚才讨论了
发怨言不但会引起不满、恨意
还是骄傲的表现
但如果我们培养知足、爱心和谦卑
我们就不会成为爱发怨言的人
腓立比书2:14说
“你们无论做什么，都不要埋怨”
经文没说有些事可以埋怨
而是说在任何情况下
我们都不该埋怨
我们这样做就表明
自己是耶和华组织中宝贵的一员
耶和华不但希望我们现在留在他的组织中
也希望将来我们可以
在新世界里过美好的生活

titles.cn: 斯蒂芬·莱特：不要埋怨（雅3:5）

ko.text: 귀여운 재롱을 부린 일에 관해 이야기할 때인가요?
열정을 보이는 부면은 사람마다 다 다릅니다.
하지만 여호와를 사랑하고 자신의 말에 확신을 가지고 있더라도
연설할 때 열정이 부족할 수 있습니다.
무슨 말을 할지 준비하는 것만으론 부족합니다.
듣는 사람에 대해 생각하고, 생기 있게 말하는 것이 필요하죠.
회중에서 연설할 때든 야외 봉사를 할 때든 마찬가지입니다.
이제 한 자매가 봉사하는 모습을 보며,
이 자매가 말할 때 열정이 더 필요한지
이 땅은 아름다운 낙원이 될 거예요.
여러 가지 축복 중 하나를 보여 드릴게요.
포도원을 만들어 그 열매를 먹을 것이다.
그들이 지은 집에 다른 사람이 살지 않고,
하느님의 왕국이 이 땅에 가져올 축복에 대해 이야기할 때
이 땅은 아름다운 낙원이 될 거예요!
성경에서 하느님이 약속하신 여러 가지 축복 중
포도원을 만들어 그 열매를 먹을 것이다.
그들이 지은 집에 다른 사람이 살지 않고,
그들이 심은 것을 다른 사람이 먹지 않을 것이다.
내 백성의 날은 나무의 날과 같고,
그 손으로 일한 것을 한껏 누릴 것이다.”
어조와 표정에 그 점이 아주 잘 나타났죠.
처음부터 끝까지 계속 강한 열정을 나타내면
어떻게 그러한지 한 형제가 연설하는 모습을 통해 생각해 보시죠.
성경 예언에 따르면 곧 어떤 일들이 일어날까요?
그 후에 나라들이 거짓 종교 세계 제국인 큰 바빌론을 공격하면서
그 공격은 “선택된 자들 때문에” 단축될 것입니다.
나라들의 연합체인 마곡의 곡이 하느님의 백성을 공격할 것입니다.
연사가 앞으로 있을 일들에 대해 말하면서
다소 과한 열정을 나타낸 것 같지 않았나요?
또한 똑같은 몸짓을 반복적으로 계속 사용하면
따라서 의미 있는 몸짓을 사용해야 하고,
요점을 다룰 때나 듣는 사람에게 행동하도록 동기를 불어넣을 때
성경 예언에 따르면 곧 어떤 일들이 일어날까요?
그 후에 나라들이 거짓 종교 세계 제국인 큰 바빌론을 공격하면서
그 공격은 “선택된 자들 때문에” 단축될 것입니다.
하지만 여호와께서는 “하느님의 큰 날의 전쟁”인 아마겟돈 때
듣는 사람에게 힘을 주고 행동하도록 동기를 부여할 수 있습니다.

en.text: What fills you with enthusiasm?
Do you enjoy talking about tasty food?
Or do you speak with enthusiasm about the playful antics
of your little niece or nephew?
Reasons for enthusiasm vary from person to person.
But why might a speaker who loves Jehovah
and who believes what he’s saying lack enthusiasm when speaking?
It’s not enough just to prepare what to say.
We must get our heart involved,
think about our listeners,
and breathe life into our delivery.
This is important both in the congregation and in the ministry.
As you watch the following example, consider the question,
‘Does this sister need more enthusiasm for her subject or less?’
The coming Paradise will be wonderful.
Notice just one of the prophecies in the Bible
regarding the abundant blessings God has promised.
It’s here at Isaiah 65:21, 22:
“They will build houses and live in them,
“and they will plant vineyards and eat their fruitage.
“They will not build for someone else to inhabit,
nor will they plant for others to eat.”
So how did she do?
When we speak about the blessings of the new earth under God’s Kingdom,
we should brim with enthusiasm.
Enthusiasm is contagious.
Let’s watch another example.
The coming Paradise will be wonderful!
Notice just one of the prophecies in the Bible
regarding the abundant blessings God has promised.
It’s here at Isaiah 65:21, 22:
“They will build houses and live in them,
“and they will plant vineyards and eat their fruitage.
“They will not build for someone else to inhabit,
“nor will they plant for others to eat.
“For the days of my people will be like the days of a tree,
and the work of their hands my chosen ones will enjoy to the full.”
Well done!
Our sister spoke from the heart and breathed life into her material.
It was evident in her tone of voice and facial expression.
Of course, we need to be balanced.
We could tire our listeners if we
project a high level of enthusiasm throughout our presentation.
To illustrate this, watch this brother giving a talk at the Kingdom Hall.
What prophetic events can we expect in the near future?
First, there will be a pronouncement of “peace and security.”
Then, the great tribulation will begin when the nations turn on Babylon the Great,
the world empire of false religion.
However, in harmony with the words of Matthew 24:22,
the attack will be cut short “on account of the chosen ones.”
What will happen next?
Gog of Magog, a coalition of nations, will attack God’s people.
Also, . . .
What do you think?
The speaker was clearly enthusiastic
—a bit too enthusiastic about the devastating events to come.
Also, our listeners will be distracted
if we use the same gesture repeatedly.
So we should try to make our gestures meaningful
and show enthusiasm primarily
when teaching main points
and when motivating our listeners to action.
Let’s give our brother another chance.
What prophetic events can we expect in the near future?
First, there will be a pronouncement of “peace and security.”
Then, the great tribulation will begin when the nations turn on Babylon the Great,
the world empire of false religion.
However, in harmony with the words of Matthew 24:22,
the attack will be cut short “on account of the chosen ones.”
What will happen next?
Gog of Magog, a coalition of nations, will attack God’s people.
But Jehovah will rescue his servants during Armageddon,
“the war of the great day of God the Almighty.”
So, what must we do now?
Romans 12:11 commands us to “be aglow with the spirit.”
By putting enthusiasm into our delivery,
we’ll stimulate and motivate our listeners to action.

cn.text: 你谈到什么会感到兴奋呢？
每个人热衷的话题都不一样
你喜欢谈论美食吗？
还是谈到小孩子调皮可爱的事呢？
我们都很爱耶和华上帝
但有些弟兄姐妹在表达自己的信念时
可能会缺乏热诚
为什么呢？
因为只准备要说的内容是不够的
我们需要先打动自己的心
考虑听者的需求
以及说话生动
无论是演讲还是传道
都要留意这些要点
让我们来看看以下的例子
想一想
这位姐妹在表现热诚方面做得怎么样呢?
将来的乐园会是很美好的
关于上帝承诺的种种福分
请看圣经的以赛亚书65:21,22
“他们要建造房屋，自己居住
栽种葡萄园，吃园中的果子
他们建造的，不会被人占据
他们栽种的，不会被人吃掉。”
她做得怎样？
当我们谈及上帝王国将会带来的福分时
我们应该充满热诚
热诚是有感染力的
我们再给她一次机会吧
将来的乐园会是很美好的
关于上帝承诺的种种福分
请看圣经怎么说
“他们要建造房屋，自己居住
栽种葡萄园，吃园中的果子
他们建造的，不会被人占据
他们栽种的，不会被人吃掉
我子民的寿命，要像树木的寿命
我挑选的人会充分享受自己劳碌的成果。”
做得很好！
我们从姐妹的语气和面部表情可以看出
她的话是发自内心的
她说的话听起来就更生动了
但是
我们也要注意
不要每句话都那么慷慨激昂
这会使听者感到疲惫
我们来看看一个弟兄在聚会所发表的演讲
圣经的预言会怎样应验呢？
首先，列国会宣告“和平安全了”
然后，政治势力会攻击大巴比伦
也就是世上的所有错误宗教
这时大患难就会爆发
不过，耶稣在马太福音24:22说
“为了被选上的人
那段时期是会被缩短的。”
接着呢？
“玛歌革地的歌革”，也就是联合起来的列国
会对上帝的子民发动攻击
另外……
你觉得他讲得怎样？
毫无疑问
讲者对未来将要发生的灾难很兴奋
但未免有点太兴奋了
另外，讲者不断做同样的手势
会让听众分心
所以手势需要配合内容
我们的热诚应该用在强调重点
或促请听者采取行动的时候
让我们再给他一次机会吧
圣经的预言会怎样应验呢？
首先，列国会宣告“和平安全了”
然后，政治势力会攻击大巴比伦
也就是世上的所有错误宗教
这时大患难就会爆发
不过，马太福音24:22说
“为了被选上的人
那段时期是会被缩短的。”
接着呢？
“玛歌革地的歌革”，也就是联合起来的列国
会对上帝的子民发动攻击
不过，上帝会拯救他的子民
让他们渡过哈米吉多顿大战
那我们现在需要采取什么行动呢？
罗马书12:11说
“要靠着神圣力量满腔热诚”
我们的热诚能激发听众的兴趣
促请他们采取行动

cn.text: 嗨，小詹！ Xiǎozhān!

ko.text: 여호와께서 뱀, 즉 사탄에게 하신 말입니다.
창세기 3:15의 예언을 이해한 하느님을 두려워하는 사람들은
이 예언의 성취를 오랫동안 고대해 왔습니다.
사탄과 악귀들이 다 사라지고 난 세상은 어떨지
그들은 현재 우리와 우리의 생각에 어떤 영향을 미치고 있습니까?
“인간에게 영향을 끼치는 방법” 이라는 소제목이 나옵니다.
감정, 도덕, 영성을 공격하기 위해 사용하는
또는 현재 어려움을 겪고 있는 문제들도 있을지 모릅니다.
위협, 사람들 사이의 불화, 조롱, 유혹과 같은 것들이죠.
각각의 항목에 대해 우리 출판물이 참조되어 있는데,
우린 그 내용을 통해 현재 어떤 문제와 싸우고 있든,
격려를 얻고 필요한 성경 원칙을 찾을 수 있습니다.
사탄이 쓰는 두 가지 방법을 살펴볼 텐데요,
사랑받을 수 없다고 생각하게 만드는 것입니다.
용서받을 수도 없다고 믿게 만들려 하죠.
과거의 잘못 때문에 염려하고 스스로를 지나치게 비판하고
실제 하느님께 사랑받고 용서받을 수 없는 존재는
낙담시키는 사탄의 전략에 어떻게 맞설 수 있을까요?
“하느님은 거짓말하실 수 없다”는 사실을 기억하는 겁니다.
우리를 위해 탄원해 주시는 분이 바로 그리스도 예수이십니다.”
이 말은 영으로 기름부음받은 그리스도인들에게 한 말이지만,
하느님의 벗으로서 의롭다고 인정된 다른 양들에게도 적용됩니다.
우리에게 가장 소중한 사랑하는 아들을 주신 분이
이젠 우릴 사랑하지 않으신다는 게 말이 되겠습니까?
또 그 아들은 현재도 우릴 위해 하느님께 탄원하고 계십니다.
현재 있는 것도 오게 될 것도 권세도 높음도 깊음도
우리 주 그리스도 예수 안에 있는 하느님의 사랑에서
하느님이 충실한 종들을 사랑하지 않는다고 주장할 근거가 없습니다.
이제 사탄의 전략에 맞서는 두 번째 방법은
그의 거짓말을 결코 믿어선 안 됩니다.
한 순회 감독자가 낙심한 사람을 돕는 방법을 설명하는데,
사탄의 거짓말인 걸 아니까, 당연히 안 믿는다고 대답합니다.
그럼 형제는 사탄의 또 다른 거짓말이 있는데,
바로 여호와께서 우리 각자를 사랑하지 않는다는
자신은 하느님께 사랑받을 수 없고 무가치하다고 생각하는 사람들이
사탄의 거짓말을 물리치도록 도울 수 있습니다.
우린 여호와께서 하신 말씀을 믿어야 합니다.
우리 개개인이 그분의 사랑을 확신하길 바라십니다.
색인에 나온, 사탄이 사람들을 속이는 또 다른 방법을 살펴볼 텐데요,
선전과 관련해서 색인에 참조되어 있는 한 「파수대」 기사의 제목은
사탄이 아주 위험한 무기로 당신을 해치려 하고 있습니다.
당신의 몸이 아니라 정신을 공격하기 위해
특별히 고안된 그 무기는 바로 선전입니다!’
사탄은 자신의 악한 세상 제도를 총동원해서 거짓말을 퍼뜨립니다.
그의 목적은 우리의 믿음과 도덕 표준을 약화시키고,
하느님이 베푸시는 인도에 대한 확신을 잃게 만들려는 것이죠.
‘진리를 알게 되면 진리가 여러분을 자유롭게 할 것입니다.’”
우린 사탄의 선전과 싸우는 데 필요한
모든 걸 성경에서 찾을 수 있는데,
마귀의 선전을 물리치기 위한 또 한 가지 방법은
사탄은 우리가 명료하게 생각하지 못하게 만들려고 한다는 점을
생각 없이 그대로 믿어선 안 됩니다.
다른 사람에게 속아 조종당하는 것을 본 적이 있습니까?
그때 속으로 ‘그 말을 믿으면 안 돼! 거짓말이야!’
결코 사탄의 선전에 귀를 기울이지 마십시오.
여호와의 말씀을 잘 듣고 그분을 신뢰하십시오.”
앞으로 사탄이 천년 동안 무저갱에 갇히면
그런 세상에서 살 때가 온다고 생각하면 정말 안심이 됩니다.
하지만 사탄은 최종 시험 때 무저갱에서 잠시 풀려날 것입니다.
아까 나온 56가지 방법 중 하나를 사용하거나
아니면 새로운 속임수를 생각해 낼 것입니까?
여호와께서는 거짓말하실 수 없다는 사실을 기억한다면
성경에 담긴 첫 예언을 인용한 부분인데요,
사탄을 여러분의 발 아래 짓밟히게 하실 것입니다.”
무저갱에 갇히는 정도가 아니라 사탄은 완전히 멸망될 것입니다.
짓밟는 것, 부서뜨림으로써 철저히 멸망시키는 것을 의미합니다.’
그때까지 우리는 부정적이거나 잘못된 생각이 떠오를 때마다

en.text: “He will crush your head.”
That was Jehovah speaking to the serpent
—really, to Satan.
And God-fearing people who have understood
the prophecy of Genesis 3:15
have been hanging on to those words
for a long time
because we long to see the complete elimination of Satan
and his influence from our lives.
Can we fully imagine what life will be like
once Satan and the demons are out of the picture?
How much influence do they have on us
and our thinking right now?
If you open Watchtower Library
and go to the Watchtower Publications Index 1986-2016
under the subject “Satan,”
you will find a subheading entitled
“methods of operation on humans.”
It lists 56 devices that he uses
to trip us up mentally, emotionally,
morally, and spiritually.
Likely you see things in the list that you have had to contend with
or are contending with even now:
discouragement, entertainment, family opposition,
intimidation, personal differences,
ridicule, temptations.
With each of these, the Index  provides
references to our publications where we can find helpful encouragement
and Scriptural principles to deal with whatever is threatening us.
Well, let’s talk about two of Satan’s methods that were on the list,
starting with one that was near the top of the list:
convincing people of being unloved or worthless.
The Devil would have us believe
that from God’s standpoint we are unlovable and unforgivable.
He wants us to worry about our past mistakes,
become overly self-critical,
and underestimate Jehovah’s compassion and forgiveness.
But Satan is just taking the spotlight off of himself
because he is the one who is unlovable in God’s eyes
and who is really unforgivable.
Now, how do we combat this method of Satan’s to dishearten us?
Well, one thing is that we can remember:
“It is impossible for God to lie.”
So take to heart what Jehovah has written truthfully
in the Bible about his love for us.
As an example, please turn to Romans chapter 8,
and keep your Bibles open there, if you will.
It’s Romans chapter 8.
We’re going to read verses 33 and 34:
“Who will file accusation against God’s chosen ones?
“God is the One who declares them righteous.
“Who will condemn them?
“Christ Jesus is the one who died,
“yes, more than that, the one who was raised up,
who is at the right hand of God and who also pleads for us.”
Now, those words were addressed to spirit-anointed Christians,
but, in principle, they also apply to those of the other sheep
who are declared righteous as God’s friends.
So do Satan’s false accusations really matter?
No.
It is Jehovah who declares true Christians righteous
based on their faith in the sacrifice of Christ.
And, really, why would Jehovah stop loving his worshippers
after he has given them the most precious gift he possibly could
—his own beloved son who even now “pleads for us” with God?
Well, let’s keep reading in Romans chapter 8,
continuing with verses 38 and 39:
“For I am convinced that neither death nor life nor angels
“nor governments nor things now here
“nor things to come nor powers
“nor height nor depth nor any other creation
“will be able to separate us from God’s love
that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.”
No one, including Satan, can successfully challenge
God’s favorable judgment of his devoted servants.
Now, a second thing we can do
to combat this method of the Devil’s to dishearten us
is to remember that Satan is a malicious liar.
The truth is not in him,
so we have to reject his lying accusations.
A reference listed in the Index
tells of how a traveling overseer addresses this issue.
He asks downhearted ones, “Do you believe in the Trinity?”
And the discouraged one would say, “Of course not,”
realizing that’s one of Satan’s lies.
Then the brother would ask, “Do you believe in hellfire?”
Again comes the answer, “Of course not.”
So the brother tells them that there is another satanic lie
that’s usually not recognized as such
—the lie that Jehovah does not love us as individuals.
And that approach often gets positive results
in helping the person to recognize and reject Satan’s lie
that we are unloved or worthless in God’s eyes.
So we need to take Jehovah at his word.
He is the one who tells the truth,
and he wants us to believe that he loves us individually.
Another method that was in that list in the Index
that Satan uses to deceive people is propaganda.
That is false, biased, or deceptive information
used to manipulate the way we think.
The first reference shown in the Index  for propaganda
is an article in The Watchtower  that we are currently studying
—an article entitled “Winning the Battle for Your Mind.”
And it begins: “You are under attack!
“And your chief enemy, Satan, is using a very dangerous weapon against you.
“What is it?
“Propaganda!
A weapon specially designed to attack, not your body, but your mind.”
Satan can use any part of his wicked system of things
to disseminate his lies.
And his objective is to weaken our faith and morals,
to stir up contentions between us,
and to undermine our confidence in the leadership that God is providing us.
How can we resist?
The article says: “Jesus gave this simple rule
“for combating propaganda:
‘Know the truth, and the truth will set you free.’”
In the Bible, we can find all we need
to combat Satan’s propaganda,
provided we’re diligent in “carefully examining the Scriptures daily”
and we use our God-given abilities
and power of reason to make the truth our own.
Now, the second thing we can do to combat this method of the Devil’s
is to keep in mind that Satan does not want us
to think clearly or reason things out well.
So never be content passively
to blindly accept what you hear from politicians,
the news media, the Internet,
because Satan is the master of fake news.
And the article concludes:
“Have you ever watched a film in which,
“from your vantage point in the audience,
“you can clearly see that someone is being deceived and manipulated?
“Did you find yourself thinking:
“‘Do not believe it! They are lying to you!’
“Imagine, then, the angels shouting the same message to you:
“‘Do not be fooled by Satan’s lies!’
“Shut your ears, then, to Satan’s propaganda.
Listen to Jehovah and trust in him.”
Now, all satanic influence will be gone when Satan is bound
and hurled into the abyss for a thousand years.
And what a relief it will be
to live in a world totally free from his wicked influence.
But then he’ll be released from the abyss
for a short while for a final test.
What method will he use then to deceive us
—one of the 56 devices we saw earlier in the list
or some new diabolical trick that he has thought of?
Well, we don’t know.
But we do know that if we remember that he is the liar
and Jehovah is the truth-teller,
we should fare just fine.
Let’s go back to Paul’s letter to the Romans,
where he echoes the first Bible prophecy
at Romans 16:20
—Romans 16:20:
“For his part, the God who gives peace
will crush Satan under your feet shortly.”
Rather than being merely abyssed,
Satan will actually be completely annihilated.
The Revelation Climax  book says:
“This is more than a superficial bruising.
“. . . Paul here used a Greek word,
“. . . that means to bruise into a jellylike state,
to trample down, to destroy utterly by crushing.”
And the “God’s Love”  book says:
“With Satan . . . out of the way,
you will feel relief that may be hard to fathom now.”
Meanwhile, whenever wrong or negative thoughts
creep into our mind,
we need to reject Satan’s lies

cn.text: “他会打碎你的头”
这句话是耶和华对蛇
也就是对撒但说的话
对于已经了解创世记3:15预言的弟兄姐妹来说
大家都很期待这个预言可以应验
我们都希望有一天看到撒但被彻底消灭
你能想象要是没有撒但和邪灵
我们的生活会是怎样的呢？
那么现在撒但和邪灵用什么手段
影响我们的思想呢？
如果你打开书库的《守望台出版物索引》
在“撒但”这个条目下
你会看到一个小标题叫“迷惑人的方法”
里面列举了50多种撒但使用的手段
撒但用这些手段影响我们的思想、感情、行为
使我们和上帝的关系疏远
这里列出的种种手段
也许是你以前或现在正在努力应付的
例如:个人纠纷、灰心、讥诮、迫害
威吓、引诱、娱乐
针对撒但的每一种手段
《出版物索引》都提供了一些参考资料
让我们可以找到实用的建议和原则
帮助我们应付撒但的诡计
在刚才列举出的手段当中
我们先来谈谈其中两个
第一个是
“使人以为自己没有人爱或一无是处”
魔鬼想让我们觉得
上帝根本不爱我们
也不会原谅我们
他希望我们为自己的过错内疚、自责
让我们以为上帝不愿意了解我们的感受
也不会宽恕我们
其实撒但这样做是为了掩人耳目
因为在上帝眼中
最不值得爱、最不值得原谅的就是撒但自己
我们要怎样抵抗撒但的诡计
不让自己灰心呢？
首先，要记得
耶和华是不可能说谎的
他也通过圣经告诉我们
他有多爱我们
现在我们来看看一个例子
请大家翻到罗马书第8章，请不要合上
罗马书第8章，我们先来看看33,34节
“谁能指控上帝挑选的人呢？
上帝已经把他们称为正义的人了
谁能定他们的罪呢？
基督耶稣已经死了，而且死而复生
在上帝的右边为我们祈求。”
这段话是对小群羊说的
但这个原则也同样适用于另外的绵羊
撒但的不实指控，对我们有影响吗？
没有，因为是耶和华把真基督徒定为义人的
他们被定为义人
是因为对耶稣的牺牲有信心
如果上帝不爱他的子民
又怎么会献出他最宝贵的儿子
让他在上帝面前为我们祈求呢？
让我们接着看看罗马书8:38,39
“我深信，无论是死，是生
是天使，是政府
是现在的事，是将来的事，是有力量的
是高处，是深处，是任何别的受造物
都不能隔绝上帝对我们的爱
这爱是通过我们的主基督耶稣表现出来的。”
如果有谁包括撒但
声称耶和华不爱他的忠贞子民
那肯定就是个谎言
为了抵抗撒但的诡计
我们要记住的第二点就是
撒但是一个邪恶的骗子
真理不在他里面
所以我们千万不要相信他说的任何话
《出版物索引》的参考资料提到
一位分区监督怎样帮助灰心的人
看穿撒但的谎言
他往往会问:“你相信三位一体吗？”
对方可能会说:“当然不相信！”
因为他们知道三位一体是撒但的谎言
接着监督会问:“那你相信地狱永火吗？”
对方同样会说:“当然不相信！”
这时，监督会说
撒但还有一个不容易被发现的谎言
就是他会让人以为我们不配得到上帝的爱
上帝也根本不在乎我们的感受
这样的推理往往可以帮助人看穿撒但的谎言
不致被他骗倒
撒但用来骗人的第二个手段就是“宣传”
撒但往往通过虚假、片面
或者欺骗性的信息来左右我们的思想
在索引中
“宣传”小标题下有一篇《守望台》文章
标题是《在思想的战争中获胜》
文章的开头说
你的头号敌人撒但正用致命的武器攻击你
他瞄准的不是你的身体，而是你的思想
那么，撒但用的武器究竟是什么呢？
就是宣传
没错，撒但就是通过他的邪恶制度来散播谎言
他的目的是削弱我们的信心
降低我们的道德标准
在基督徒之间挑起纷争
让我们怀疑在组织中带头的弟兄
怎样才不会被这些“宣传”骗倒呢？
耶稣告诉我们一个简单的原则
你们会认识真理，真理会使你们自由
没错，只要我们“天天用心查考圣经”
就不会被撒但的“宣传”骗倒
当然，我们也要运用上帝赐给我们的思考能力
把学到的真理实践出来
我们要记住的另一件事情就是
撒但不想要我们仔细思考或好好推理
撒但是新闻媒体幕后的推手
他很擅长通过政治人物
新闻媒体或网络来宣传虚假的信息
千万不要轻易相信或盲目接受！
《守望台》文章这样总结
你曾经在看影片时
发觉剧中的人被骗或被利用吗？
当时你是不是很想大喊
“不要相信那些人，他们在骗你！”
天使也很想对我们说
“不要被撒但骗了！”
千万不要听信撒但的宣传
要听耶和华的话，全心信赖他
过不了多久，撒但就会被摔到无底深渊
长达一千年的时间
这期间，他对人类造成的影响也会随之消失
想到我们的生活不再受撒但影响
这会是多大的纾解啊！
但一千年以后
撒但会从无底深渊被释放一会儿
那时他会用什么手段欺骗我们呢？
是用刚刚索引中列出的那些手段吗？
还是新的诡计呢？
我们不知道
但我们知道的是，撒但是谎话之父
而耶和华是信守真理的父亲
谨记这点我们就不会受骗了
让我们再回到罗马书
保罗在罗马书16:20说的话
让我们想起圣经的第一个预言
罗马书16:20说
“赐人安宁的上帝
不久就要把撒但压碎在你们脚下了。”
撒但不仅会被摔到无底深渊
他最终还会被彻底毁灭
《启示录高潮》这本书提到
撒但不是受轻伤
保罗在这里用了一个希腊语动词
意思是践踏、捣成糊状、彻底摧毁压碎
《上帝的爱》这本书也说，撒但将不复存在
到时你会享有无法想象的安舒
在等候预言应验的同时
一旦我们开始有消极或错误的想法
就要集中精神，用心思考耶和华所教的真理
这样就不会被撒但的谎言骗倒了
