title: 안드리 네스마치니: 축구는 제 삶의 전부였습니다

ko.text: 여섯 살 때 부모님이 저를 축구팀에 등록해 주셨어요.
열두 살 때 어머니에게 여호와에 대해 배웠습니다.
어릴 때부터 디나모 클럽에서 뛰는 걸 꿈꿨거든요.
그 순간부터 제 모든 힘과 시간을 선수 생활에 바쳤습니다.
영적인 일을 할 시간은 하나도 없었어요.
선수들에 둘러싸여 있다 보니 저도 자연스레 그들처럼 됐죠.
엄청난 돈이 생겨서 원하는 대로 쓸 수 있었거든요.
다들 친해지려 하고 절 만나고 싶어 했어요.
또 저는 부동산에 아주 큰 돈을 투자했습니다.
구단 경영진과 어떤 문제로 이야기하는 중이었는데
마치 다 쓰면 구겨서 버리는 일회용 컵처럼요.
거기다 젊은 선수들로 세대 교체가 이루어지고 있었고,
그러다 인생의 의미에 대해 생각하게 됐습니다.
직업도 아니고, 돈도 아니면, 도대체 뭘까?’
그러곤 청소년 때 여호와에 관해 배운 것들이 떠올랐어요.
저는 아내와 함께 다시 성서 연구를 시작했습니다.
제 삶에 크나큰 기쁨과 만족이 찾아왔습니다.
그 어떤 메달이나 우승컵과도 비교할 수 없죠.
두 주인을 섬길 수 없다는 걸 깨달았지만,
아직 디나모 키예프와의 계약이 2년 더 남아 있었습니다.
그분의 이름에 대해 좋은 증거를 할 수 있었습니다.
그럼 전 진심을 담아 아니라고 말하죠.
이 세상이 제공하는 건 다 잠시뿐입니다.
사람들은 명성이나 돈과 같은 한쪽 면만 보고,
부상이나 실망과 같은 또 다른 면은 보지 않아요.
또 정신적으로나 감정적으로 굉장히 힘들고 자유도 전혀 없죠.
그러니까 우리의 노력을 가치 있게 여기시는 분께
언제나 행복과 기쁨과 만족을 가져다 줍니다.

en.text: Soccer was my reason for living.
I always dreamed of becoming a professional soccer player.
I thought that happiness came from fame,
a good career,
money.
When I was six, my parents signed me up for soccer.
I really loved playing soccer.
I spent all my time at the stadium, even late into the night.
When I was 12, I learned about Jehovah from my mom.
At that time,
she started studying the Bible.
And after about a year,
I began to preach from door to door.
When I was 17 years old, I finished school
and I received an invitation from the Dynamo Soccer Club in Kiev.
Oh, that was unforgettable!
Yes, my emotions were running high
because since childhood I had always dreamed of playing for Dynamo.
From that moment on, all my energy and all my time
were devoted to my career.
Every day we either trained or there was a game.
There was no time left for spiritual things.
Of course, being around people like that, I became just like them.
I led an immoral lifestyle
because huge amounts of money opened up many opportunities.
Going to nightclubs, the nightlife
—it was so immoral.
Everyone wants to be your friend and to meet you.
And, of course, this was tempting.
I also invested huge sums of money in real estate.
I wanted to create a foundation for the future and wealth for myself,
my family, and my relatives so that no one would be in need.
Yes, I was sure that this really was happiness.
This continued for nine years.
The turning point
was a conversation with management when an issue came up,
and they hurled insults at me.
At that moment, I felt worthless,
like a disposable cup
that you use and then crush
and throw away.
Besides, a new generation of soccer players was arriving
—many young guys.
I stopped being included in the starting lineup.
Also, the financial crisis began,
and real estate prices fell drastically.
I panicked; I didn’t know what to do.
And I started to think about the meaning of life:
‘What really is the meaning of life?
‘If it’s not a career, not money
—then what is it?’
And then I remembered everything that I learned
about Jehovah when I was a teenager.
I began to study the Bible again along with my wife.
After a year, I started preaching again, and in 2009,
I was baptized as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
And this brought me so much joy and satisfaction.
These feelings can’t be compared to winning any medal or cup.
I realized that I couldn’t slave for two masters,
but I still had to play two more years for Dynamo Kyiv.
Although it was a difficult time,
I took advantage of this opportunity,
and I am thankful to Jehovah that a good witness
was given about his name.
There were some soccer players
who showed interest in the truth.
In 2011 when my contract ended,
I finished my professional career.
First Timothy chapter 6
encourages us “to place [our] hope, not on uncertain riches,
but on God,” and “to be rich in fine works.”
People ask me: “Do you regret it?”
“Maybe you’d like to come back; do you miss soccer?”
And I honestly and sincerely say no.
I don’t miss it, and I don’t want to go back
because my relationship with Jehovah—
Well, it can’t be compared to anything.
Everything that this world offers is all short-lived,
and it’s only an illusion.
People see only one side of the picture —the fame and the money.
The other side are the injuries and disappointments.
It’s very hard psychologically and emotionally;
you have no freedom.
That’s why it’s better to give the very best to the One
who appreciates it.
What you do for Jehovah will always bring you happiness,
joy, and satisfaction.

cn.text: 足球曾经是我生活的全部
我从小就梦想成为一名职业足球运动员
我以为快乐就是来自名誉
成功的事业、金钱
我6岁时
爸妈送我去一个足球队接受训练
我真的很喜欢足球
整天都在球场踢球
一直到晚上很晚
在我12岁的时候
妈妈开始学习圣经
她也帮助我认识耶和华
大约一年后，我开始挨家挨户传道
17岁的时候，我从学校毕业
那时我收到了基辅迪纳摩足球俱乐部的邀请
哦，真是太不可思议了！
我永远都忘不了！
当时我很兴奋
因为我从小就梦想为迪纳摩效力
从那时起，我就把我所有的精力和时间
都用在足球事业上
我们每天不是训练就是比赛
我根本没有时间崇拜耶和华
每天都跟队友们在一起
我的生活也变得跟他们一样了
我有很多钱，所以我想做什么就做什么
我也过着不道德的生活
我的夜生活就是去夜店
这种生活真的很放荡
每个人都想认识你，都想跟你做朋友
当然，这是个很大的诱惑
我也把大量的金钱投资到房地产
我想为未来积累财富
让我自己、我的家人、我的亲戚
想要什么就有什么
我当时觉得这就是真正的快乐
这样的生活持续了9年
后来我的生活出现了转折
当时球队出现了一个问题
管理层找我谈话
他们不停地辱骂我
我觉得自己毫无价值
就像一个用完的杯子
被人捏扁，然后扔掉一样
另外，年轻一代的球员不断加入
越来越多的年轻球员成为主力
我甚至不能进入首发名单
当时，经济危机也开始了
房地产的价格急剧下降
我陷入了恐慌，我不知道该怎么办
我开始思考
人生的意义究竟是什么呢？
如果不是为了事业、金钱
那又是为了什么呢？
后来，我想起十几岁时从圣经学到的内容
我就再次开始学习圣经
我的妻子也开始学习
一年后，我又开始传道了
2009年，我受浸成为耶和华见证人
这给我的生活带来很多的喜乐和满足
这些感觉是赢得任何奖牌或奖杯都不会有的
我知道我不能做两个主人的奴隶
但我跟基辅迪纳摩还有两年的合约
还要再踢两年的球
这样的生活真的很不容易
但感谢耶和华让我可以善用这两年时间
向队友作见证
有些队友对真理很感兴趣
2011年，我跟俱乐部的合约到期了
我的职业球员生涯终于结束了
提摩太前书第6章鼓励我们
“不要寄望于无定的财富而要寄望于上帝”
也要“在善事上富足”
别人问我：“你后悔吗？”
“说不定你还想回到球队
你会舍不得吗？”
我会坚定地说“不”
我不会后悔，我也不想回去球队
因为我跟耶和华的关系比任何事都重要
这个世界给你的都是短暂的，很快会消失
你只能看到它诱人的一面
比如名誉和金钱
但这个世界的另一面却是伤害和失望
你的内心和感情会遭受很大的伤害
结果你就成了奴隶，没有自由
要把你最好的献给耶和华
这样做非常明智
耶和华非常珍视你的付出
你也一定会收获幸福、喜乐和满足！

ko.text: 독특한 상황이 생겼으니 도와달라는 요청을 받았습니다.
당시에 그곳에서 봉사하던 한 특별 파이오니아는 말하기를,
천 명 정도의 같은 교회 신자들이
여호와의 증인과 성서 연구를 하고 싶어 한다는 것이었습니다.
이 모든 일은 한 번의 비공식 증거로 시작됐습니다.
어느 날 회중의 한 형제가 저한테
자기 직장 동료와 있었던 일을 얘기해 줬습니다.
그 동료는 한 교회를 책임 맡고 있었는데,
형제가 그에게 비공식 증거를 했던 거죠.
그런데 그가 여호와의 증인과 성서 연구를 하고 싶다면서,
자기 교회 신자들도 같이 성서 연구를 하도록
사실 그는 교회에서 영향력이 큰 사람이었습니다.
그래서 자신이 형제한테 들은 내용을 교회 신자들에게 전해 주면서,
우리가 성경을 더 잘 이해할 필요가 있다는 점을 확신시켜 줬습니다.
많이들 그 얘길 들었는데, 보기 드문 사건이었거든요.
제가 듣기로는, 그때 거의 천 명이
그 성서 연구를 한 건씩 다 사회할 수가 없었죠.
일주일에 한두 번씩 왕국회관에서 성서 연구를 사회했습니다.
하지만 이 모든 질문에 대한 논리적인 답이
한 성구가 다른 성구를 설명하곤 했죠.
성경으로 어떤 주제든 다 설명할 수가 있더군요.
처음엔 두 세 가족씩 그룹이 되어 함께 연구했습니다.
그분들이 성경으로 대답하는 걸 보고 놀랐어요.
‘성경에서는 이렇게 말하는구나, 저렇게 말하는구나’ 하면서 들었죠.
모두 다 집에서부터 훈련이 잘 돼 있었죠.
자녀들은 자기 「진리」 책과 성경을 앞에 놓고
그래서 이 가족들이 집회에 왔을 때도
아이들은 부모 곁에 앉아 움직이지 않고,
그들이 오기 시작했을 때, 전 어렸는데 기억이 생생해요.
제가 처음 집회에 참석한 곳은 여기
진리와 일치하게 사는 데 필수적인 역할을 했습니다.
전 어렸을 때, 죽음이 정말 두려웠어요.
근데 죽고 나면 아무 고통도 없다는 걸 알고 나니 안심이 됐어요.
원하면 이룰 수도 있었을 목표들이 중요하지 않게 되었죠.
그때부턴 단순하게 살고, 조직과 함께 걷고,
자녀를 진리 안에서 기르는 게 목표가 되었어요.
지금 이 형제들은 조직에서 많은 일을 하고 있죠.
여러 지역에서 봉사하고, 중요한 책임들을 맡고 있습니다.
아버지는 자녀들에게 좋은 본을 보이려 노력하셨고
현재 저와 아내는 여기 캐나다 지부에서 봉사하고 있습니다.
저희 가족이 집회에 나가기 시작했을 때
당시에 회중에서 저희를 정말 잘 돌봐 줬던 게
15살 땐 매일 성경을 읽고 연구하기 시작했습니다.
정말 여호와께서는 우리 내면에 무엇이 있는지를 보셨어요.
저희 혼자 힘으론 결코 교회를 나와 진리를 찾지 못했을 거예요.
그 많은 사람이 성서 연구를 하고 인생이 바뀐 겁니다.

en.text: In the mid-1970’s, several brothers from the Montréal area
were approached to help with a unique situation that was unfolding.
A special pioneer, who was taking the lead at the time,
said that about a thousand people —all from the same church—
wanted to study the Bible with Jehovah’s Witnesses.
And it was all because of an informal witness.
The story began this way:
A brother in the local congregation
approached me one day
to tell me about an experience
he had with one of his workmates.
This man was responsible for a small local church,
and the brother had been able to give him an informal witness.
The man indicated
that he would like a Bible study,
and he wanted to convince the other members of his church
to also study the Bible with Jehovah’s Witnesses.
The fact was that this person
had a certain influence in the church.
So he talked to the church members
about the message he had heard from the brother,
and he convinced them that what they were missing
was a better understanding of the Bible.
Many people heard about it
because it was an exceptional event.
From what I heard, there were around a thousand people
who wanted to study the Bible at that time.
We didn’t have the brothers and sisters
that were needed to conduct all these Bible studies.
So they formed groups of 10, 12, 15 people.
And once or twice a week in Kingdom Halls, they conducted Bible studies.
It was questions, questions.
Everyone was asking questions.
But the Bible could always answer all these questions in a logical way
—one verse would explain another.
And we came to see
that the Bible in its entirety could explain every subject.
At the beginning,
groups of two or three families studied together.
And, yeah, they answered with the Bible.
That amazed me because
I didn’t know the Bible at all.
But I thought, ‘The Bible talks about this;
the Bible talks about that.’
It was like a discovery for me.
That was the parents.
The children weren’t there.
So when we accepted it, then we’d teach it to our children.
Everyone was disciplined while sitting at the table.
The children were very quiet
with their Truth book in front of them and their Bible.
When these families came to the Kingdom Hall,
the children were sitting beside their parents,
not moving, paying attention to what was being said.
I was young when they started coming.
I remember it very well.
A lot of them were my age.
I saw them like future potential friends.
It was really touching.
The first meeting I attended was here in Laval.
It really contributed to me one day taking a stand
and Jehovah becoming my God
and the truth becoming my way of life.
When I was young,
I was very afraid of death.
It was such a relief to learn that we don’t suffer when we die.
It’s like a sleep.
The ambitions I had before,
that may have been attainable,
became second place.
Now it was to have a simple life,
to walk with the organization,
and to raise my children in the truth.
Today, these brothers are really doing a lot in the organization,
helping in different areas, shouldering great responsibilities.
My father always strived
to set the example for all his children,
and it made an impression on me.
Now my wife and I have the privilege of serving here at the Canada branch.
I was eight years old
when my family started attending meetings.
I have really good memories of how
the local congregation at the time
took care of us and looked after us.
At the age of 15,
I started reading my Bible every day and studying it too.
From that point on,
I knew what I wanted to do with my life
—serve Jehovah full-time.
I really think Jehovah could see us on the inside.
Jehovah helped us a lot.
You can’t have anything better than that.
On our own, we never would have got out of that situation.
But Jehovah found a way to find “rightly disposed” ones.
A simple informal witness led to Bible studies that touched so many.

cn.text: 40多年前
蒙特利尔的几个弟兄受到邀请
去处理一个非常罕见的情况
当时，有一位特别先驱负责处理这件事
他说有大约一千人
想跟耶和华见证人学习圣经
他们都来自同一个教会
这么美好的成果
只因为一次非正式见证
这件事是怎么开始的呢？
有一天，当地的一位弟兄找到我
告诉我他向同事传道的经历
这位同事是当地一个小教会的负责人
弟兄向他作非正式见证时
他说他想学习圣经
也想说服他们教会的其他成员
跟耶和华见证人学习圣经
这个人在教会有一定的影响力
所以，他从弟兄听到真理以后
就去告诉教会的其他成员
让他们也学习圣经
这样他们就能对圣经有更好的理解
这样的事真的很少见
所以，很多人都听说了
我听到的是
当时大概有一千人想学习圣经
那时要学习的人很多
无法做到让每个人都有自己的圣经课程
所以，他们就被分成10人
12人和15人的小组
一周一次或两次
在王国聚会所里学习圣经
我们有很多很多问题要问
每个人都在问问题
但是
圣经总是能够合乎逻辑地解答所有问题
一节经文能够解释另一节经文
我们渐渐看出每一个问题
都能在圣经里找到答案
刚开始
每两三个家庭组成一个小组
一起学习圣经
他们总是用圣经回答问题
我太惊讶了
因为我完全不了解圣经
我心想
圣经这个问题也能回答
那个问题也能回答
我好像发现了新大陆一样
当时，父母们先开始学习圣经
孩子们没有在场
我们接受真理以后
就教导自己的孩子
每个孩子都乖乖地坐在桌子旁边
学习摆在他们面前的《真理》书和圣经
他们跟着父母来参加聚会的时候
都坐在父母身边不会乱动
专心聆听聚会的内容
他们来聚会的时候，我还很小
我记得很清楚
很多孩子跟我差不多大
我把他们看成我未来的好朋友
当时的情景真的很感人
我参加的第一个聚会是在拉瓦勒
那次的聚会对我来说是个里程碑
从那时起
我就开始崇拜耶和华，维护真理
也开始按真理生活
我小时候特别害怕死亡
知道人死去以后不会受苦
而是像睡着了一样
这带给我很大的安慰
我曾经很想追求世界的东西
但认识真理后，它们就不那么重要了
我学会了过简单的生活
跟耶和华的组织同行
也努力按照真理养育孩子
今天，这些弟兄们分别在不同的地区
担负重要的职责

title: 우리의 조직이 이루고 있는 일들—워릭 박물관을 위해 수고하는 형제 자매들

ko.text: 우리의 활동이 어떻게 조직되는지 더 잘 이해하게 됩니다.
여러분이 즐겁고 유익한 견학을 할 수 있도록
세계 본부가 뉴욕주 워릭으로 이전할 것임을 발표했을 때
이곳을 방문하는 전 세계 형제들을 맞이할 때가
깜짝 놀랄 만한 것들이 기다리고 있으니까요.
영적 보물들도 보실 수 있을 겁니다.
현재 미국 세계 본부를 찾는 방문객들은
워릭 베델에 있는 세 개의 전시관을 견학할 수 있습니다.
모든 방문객을 환영하고 그들이 유익을 얻도록 도우려면
전시물과 오디오 기기를 관리하는 일이 포함됩니다.
원격 봉사자들이 이 모든 일을 지원합니다.
견학자들의 언어에 따라 언어를 맞추어 놓죠.
형제 자매들을 만나고 섬길 수 있어서 정말 기쁩니다.
보이지 않는 곳에서 수고하는 분들도 많은데,
직접 체험할 수 있는 전시물의 내용과
그러면 팀에서는 그 지침에 따라 전시물의 디자인 초안을 만들죠.
견학자들이 직접 체험할 수 있는 프로그램을 제작합니다.
교육적인 면과 미적인 면에서 균형을 잘 잡아야 해요.
사람들이 뭔가 배울 수 있도록 교훈점이 잘 부각되게 하면서,
사람들이 뭔가 느낄 수 있게 해 줘야죠.
진귀한 성경과 귀중한 유물들을 기증하고 있습니다.
전문 기술자가 그러한 성경과 유물들을 관리합니다.
그리고 다른 사람들을 훈련하는 일도 하죠.
거기엔 그분의 약속과 그분의 이름이 들어 있죠.
그분의 이름이 어떻게 보존되었는지 알려 줍니다.
아주 많은 분들이 유물과 성경을 기증해 주시기 때문에,
다른 지부들이 빌려 가서 전시하기도 하죠.
오늘날에도 여호와께서는 전시관을 짓고 관리하는 데
이 정도 규모와 수준의 박물관을 건축하고 운영하려면
하지만 가능한 한 많은 출퇴근 봉사자와
비용을 아주 많이 절감할 수 있었습니다.
이러한 특별 전시관을 다른 지부들로도 옮겨 설치하는데,
그러면 지부들이 전시품과 진귀한 성경을 공유하고
이러한 전시를 계획하는 데도 여러 달이 걸립니다.
러시아에 관한 특별 전시를 준비하도록 마련했는데,
러시아 형제 자매들이 나타내 온 훌륭한 본을 알려 주는 것이었습니다.
특히 최근에 극심한 반대를 받으면서 말이죠.
10월에 있을 연례 총회와 봉헌식 때까지 완성하는 게 목표였습니다.
“용기”라는 주제의 전시를 열기 위한 조사와 설계가 시작됐습니다.
다른 지부에서 전시할 내용은 최종 승인을 받기 전에
조정자 위원회에서 전시관을 만드는 데 동의하면,
전시관을 마련하기 위한 공간과 비용을 사용할 허락을
흔히 우리의 전시관은 네 가지로 나눌 수 있는데,
각각의 전시관은 해당 지부의 현지 느낌을 반영하도록 조정됩니다.
젤터스 베델의 전시실은 워릭과 구조가 다릅니다.
그래서 전시관을 그에 맞게 조절해야 했죠.
워릭과 동일한 스타일로 전시관을 설치할 수 있었습니다.
형제들이 전시관을 위해 아주 열심히 일했습니다.
러시아 형제들을 더욱 사랑하게 해 주죠.
새로운 전시관 설계와 관련하여 도움을 받았습니다.
이러한 지부들에는 매년 50만 명 이상이 방문합니다.
전시관의 수준을 더욱 높이기 위해 어떤 일들을 합니까?
전 세계에 있는 유물들을 검색할 수 있게
유물의 사진과 세부 정보를 볼 수 있습니다.
그러면 그러한 유물을 빌려서 전시관에 사용할 수 있습니다.
유물을 잘 보존하도록 지부들에 도움을 주기도 합니다.
또한 전시물 설치나 영상과 관련해서 지원하고,
터치스크린이나 음향 장치에 대해서도 도움을 주죠.
그런 시설 덕분에 직접 체험하는 견학이 가능합니다.
전 세계에 있는 형제 자매들이나 회중이나
증인이 아닌 분들에게서 받은 것도 있습니다.
특별 전시관을 위해 빌려준 것도 있죠.
하지만 모든 유물을 워릭 전시관에서 쓸 수 있는 건 아닙니다.
유물의 희귀성, 중요성, 언어 등을 고려합니다.
또 방문객이 보고 받게 될 느낌까지 생각하죠.
워릭이나 다른 지부의 전시관들에 그 유물을 전시할지 정합니다.
전 세계의 전시관 중 하나에 그 물품이 전시될 수도 있습니다.
가능하다면 미국 세계 본부를 방문해 보실 것을
그렇게 하면 많은 것을 배우게 되고,
여호와께서 이 마지막 날에 그분의 백성을 인도하고 계시다는 믿음이

把这些概念实际呈现出来

我们就会开始构思怎样布置展览
等我们收到展品后，就会围绕展品进行设计
设计时，最重要的
就是兼顾展览的教育意义和艺术感
我们的目标是让参观的人明白

耶和华送给我们圣经这份宝贵的礼物

做好标记后运到中欧分部
预备在那里展出

世界总部会为不同分部的展览提供相关指引

申请办展览所需要的预算和场地

我们很开心

截至2018年年底
有超过35个分部

ko.text: 고대 이스라엘 사람이 성전을 후원하기 위해 마음에서 우러나와 예물을 바쳤을 때,
오늘날 세계 전역에 있는 여호와의 증인의 왕국회관에는
자진적인 헌금을 할 수 있도록 마련된 작은 헌금함이 있습니다.
그러면 우리가 한 헌금은 실제로 어디에 쓰입니까?
매년 수십만 명이 우리의 새로운 형제 자매가 됩니다.
이렇게 점점 늘어나는 형제 자매들을 위해,
전 세계에 새로운 숭배 장소와 지부 시설을 건축하는 데 자금이 사용됩니다.
한 집안의 가장, 아버지, 남편인 분들이
휴가를 내고 이곳에서 일하는 모습을 볼 때마다 감명을 받아요.
이 일을 지원하고 또 저희가 여기서 일할 수 있게 도와주는
수백만 명의 형제 자매들의 아낌없는 물질적 지원으로
건축 활동이 계속될 수 있다는 건 감동적인 일입니다.
더 많은 일을 할 수 있는 큰 문이 신권 학교들을 통해 열리고 있습니다.
복음 전파 활동을 열심히 인도하도록 훈련을 베풉니다.
조직과 조직이 베푸는 하느님의 교육에 대해 생각해 보면,
국민을 교육시키는 면에서 왕국을 따라올 정부는
세계 어디에도 없다는 걸 알게 됩니다.
생각지 못한 방법으로 여호와와의 관계를 강하게 해 주었지요.
자진적인 헌금은 전 세계의 수많은 특별 전 시간 종들을 지원하는 일에도 쓰이는데,
여호와께서 형제 자매들이 하는 헌금을 통해 이 일을 지원하신다는 걸 분명히 알게 되죠.
야외에서 수고하는 형제 자매들의 희생이 있기에
제가 하는 봉사가 가능하다는 걸 깊이 깨닫고 있습니다.
특별 전 시간 종들에는 선교인, 여행하는 감독자,
형제 자매들의 그 모든 지원 덕분에 이 봉사를 할 수 있어요.
왕국의 좋은 소식을 전하는 데 매주, 매달, 매년,
전 시간을 바쳐 일할 수 있다는 건 큰 특권이자 정말 즐거운 일이에요.
가능한 많은 사람이 여호와를 알도록 도울 수 있는 거죠.
영적 보석과 같은 것들을 받게 될 일을 손꼽아 기다립니다.
일들이 원활히 진행되게 하는 데 쓰입니다.
올해는 연합을 증진하는 데 과학 기술이 사용되는 걸 보면서 감동을 받았어요.
여러 도시에서 통치체 성원과 보조자들의 연설이
동영상으로 중계되었을 때 청중의 반응이 정말 뜨거웠습니다.
프로그램 중에 자리를 떠나지 않는 사람들이 더 많아졌어요.
이 특별한 내용을 한 순간이라도 놓치고 싶지 않은 거죠.
여러분의 헌금은 재난이 닥쳤을 때 도움이 필요한 형제 자매들에게
음식, 옷, 건축 자재, 그 밖의 많은 물품을 가능한 신속히 보냅니다.
여호와의 조직에 깊이 감사하는 마음이 생겼어요.
이렇게 사랑으로 지원을 베푸는 조직은 세상 어디에도 없습니다.
확실히 알았어요. 여호와께서 우릴 돌보신다는 걸.
뭐라 감사를 드려야 할지, 기도가 절로 나와요.
우리가 하는 모든 헌금은 전 세계 왕국 권익을 지원하는 데 가치 있게 쓰입니다.
각각의 헌금은 ‘하늘에 계신 우리 아버지 여호와께 드리는 예물’과 같습니다.
마음에서 우러나와 드림으로 우리는 여호와에 대한 사랑을 표현하며,
이것이야말로 그분께 드릴 수 있는 최상의 예물입니다.

en.text: In ancient times, when an Israelite
made a heartfelt offering to support the temple,
that offering was referred to as ‘a gift in hand to Jehovah.’
Today, in Kingdom Halls of Jehovah’s Witnesses
around the world, there are small boxes
marked for voluntary contributions.
When we give our valuable things, where does it actually go?
Each year, hundreds of thousands become our new brothers and sisters.
To accommodate our growing numbers,
funds are provided to help construct new places of worship,
as well as branch facilities all over the world.
One thing that I really appreciate about being here
is to see family heads, fathers and husbands,
choose to use their vacation time.
So thank you to the families and the congregations
that support all of this and us to be here.
But what’s just as impressive is seeing millions of brothers and sisters
voluntarily give of their funds so that we can keep building.
Just that in itself is an amazing act of Jehovah’s holy spirit.
Large doors leading to greater activity
are being opened by means of theocratic schools.
Training is provided to help those enrolled to develop spiritually
and take a zealous lead in the evangelizing work.
When you think of the organization and the education,
the divine education that it provides,
there is no government on earth today
that educates its citizens like the Kingdom.
It has strengthened my relationship with Jehovah
in ways I never considered before.
The training is wonderful; it motivates spiritual growth.
Voluntary contributions help support
the thousands of special full-time servants worldwide.
These include Bethelites.
While working in the printery, it’s abundantly clear
that none of this could happen without Jehovah’s support,
shown by what the friends can give.
I love my assignment, and serve with the knowledge
that my sacrifice wouldn’t be possible
without the sacrifice of brothers and sisters in the field.
Also included are missionaries,
traveling overseers,
international servants, and special pioneers.
All the support makes it possible
and makes our assignment a great joy and a privilege,
something that we look forward to each and every week,
each and every month,
each and every year that we’re able to devote
our full-time efforts in preaching the good news of the Kingdom.
It allows us to be here so that we can help as many people as possible
who do want to learn about Jehovah.
Every year, we look forward to receiving
rich spiritual gems at our conventions.
Funds are provided for equipment and other needs
to help everything run as smoothly as possible.
It was a delight this year to see
how technology was used to promote the unity.
Having the different cities involved
where video streaming to them for the key talks
by Governing Body members and their helpers
received tremendous response from those cities.
We’ve seen more people in their seats during the program
because they were afraid to get up even for a moment
cause they might miss something that was special.
When disaster strikes,
your donations help give immediate relief
for our brothers and sisters in need.
Food, clothing, building materials,
and much more are shipped over as quickly as possible.
I have come to really appreciate Jehovah’s organization.
No other organization can compare
in how it provides support in such a loving way.
I know now that Jehovah does look after his people.
So I’m really grateful for that,
and I’ve been praying and giving thanks.
Yes, all our contributions have a meaningful share
in supporting Kingdom interests worldwide.
Each donation is like ‘a gift in hand to our heavenly Father Jehovah.’
When we give from our heart,
we are expressing our love for him,
and that is the best gift we can give him.

cn.text: 在古代
以色列人甘心乐意捐献支持圣殿
所奉献的会视为给耶和华的礼物
今天在世界各地的耶和华见证人王国聚会所
都有捐款箱用来收集自愿捐款
我们的捐款会用来做什么呢？
每年有数十万人成为我们的弟兄姐妹
由于人数不断增加
捐款会用来在世界各地
建造崇拜场所和分部设施
这里最令我欣赏的
就是看到家主、做父亲的、做丈夫的
运用假期来服务
我要向他们的家人和会众说谢谢
有了你们的支持
这一切工作才得以展开
令我感动的是
数百万弟兄姐妹自愿捐款
让建筑工程一项接着一项进行
单单这点就显示神圣力量的作用多么奇妙
各种训练班促进传道工作的扩展
为神圣服务打开了大门
许多接受培训的人在崇拜方面更加进步
他们热心带头做传道工作
谈到上帝的组织和组织提供的神圣教育
现在世上没有任何政府
对国民所提供的教育
能跟上帝的王国相比
训练班强化了我跟耶和华的关系
远远超出了我的想象
这个培训课程真好
大大促进了我的成长
自愿捐款
也用来资助全球众多参与特别全时服务的人
例如伯特利成员
我在印刷厂工作
清楚看出只有耶和华支持这一切才有可能
收到的捐款就是明显的证据
我很喜欢在这里服务
我知道没有弟兄姐妹的捐献
我也不可能在这里献出自己
捐款还会用来资助特派传道员
分区监督
国际仆人
和特别先驱
这些资源让我们能够参与全时服务
喜乐地献出自己
也让我们可以时时刻刻、全心全意
投入宣扬王国好消息的工作
全凭这些支持，我们才能到这里
帮助更多想认识耶和华的人
每年我们都很期待从大会获得滋养信心的食物
捐款会用来资助大会的设备和其他开销
好让大会顺利进行
今年很高兴看到科技怎样有助于促进团结
通过即时影音传输技术
中央长老团成员和他们的助手的演讲
可以传送到不同城市，观众都十分兴奋
我们发现节目进行时离场的人少了
大家一刻也不愿意走开
以免错过任何精彩之处
灾难发生时
捐款能让受灾的弟兄姐妹很快得到帮助
食物、衣服、建筑材料
还有其他物品也得以尽快送到灾区
我真的很感激耶和华的组织
因为世上没有其他团体能像耶和华的组织
这样充满爱心地提供援助
我现在体会到耶和华真的会照顾他的子民
我充满感激一直祷告不断感谢他
所有的捐款都会用来支持上帝王国
在世界各地的事务
每一笔捐款
都是从我们手中献出给天父耶和华的礼物
我们甘心乐意地捐献
就是表明我们爱耶和华
这份爱就是送给耶和华最好的礼物！

titles.cn: “奉献给耶和华的礼物”

ko.text: 여호와께서는 우리의 잠재력을 알려 주고 계시죠.
여호와께서는 우리가 자신의 능력 이상의 일을 할 것을
자신의 힘으로는 더는 버틸 수 없다고 느낄 때에도,
여러분이 마지막으로 마귀를 대적한 때는 언제입니까?
우리는 예수께서 마귀에게 세 번 유혹받으셨을 때처럼
하지만 마귀는 자신의 목적을 이루기 위해
많은 분들이 이런저런 건강상의 문제를 겪고 있습니다.
심각한 병이나 장애를 겪는 분들도 있죠.
건강 문제가 마귀를 대적하는 것과 어떤 관련이 있습니까?
마귀가 사용하는 교묘한 방법 중 하나는
건강에 대한 우리의 합당한 염려를 이용해
우리가 영적인 것에 초점을 맞추지 못하게 하는 겁니다.
우리가 지나치게 건강에 몰두하게 만들려고 하죠.
그는 우리가 건강 문제에 정신이 쏠려서
그걸 우리의 삶에서 가장 중요한 위치에 두기를 바랍니다.
또는 우리가 건강 관리에 너무 몰두한 나머지
예수께서 이런 의미 있는 말씀을 하셨습니다.
자기의 수명을 조금이라도 늘릴 수 있겠습니까?”
우리는 자신이 어떻게 할 수 없는 문제에 대해
한번은 대회에서 안내인으로 일하는 30대 형제를 만났습니다.
얘길 하다 보니 그 형제가 실은
자기가 지금 병원에 있어야 한다고 말하는 거였습니다.
의사들한테 자기가 5개월밖에 못 살 거라는 말을 들었다고 했죠.
그 형제는 치료법을 찾는 데 너무 몰두한 나머지
그리고 안내인으로 일하면서 다른 사람들을 돕고자 했죠.
형제는 대회를 통해 크게 힘을 얻고
우리는 결코 영성을 희생해서는 안 됩니다.
영적 균형을 유지하면서 다른 사람들을 도와야 합니다.
매일매일 그렇게 하고 있는 분들도 계십니다.
이제 두 번째 부면을 생각해 보죠.
우리는 자신의 태도와 관련해서도 마귀를 대적해야 합니다.
정말 중요하다는 걸 우린 잘 압니다.
남들이 우리에게 보이는 반응이 달라질 수 있죠.
감사하는 태도를 보이느냐 하는 것도 마찬가집니다.
불평하는 사람은 모든 상황을 암울하게 봅니다.
객관적으로 보면 실제로는 상황이 좋은데도 말이죠.
그건 마치 방에 있는 아름다운 장식품을
이게 마귀를 대적하는 것과 무슨 관련이 있죠?
부정적인 태도를 사탄이 이용할 수 있습니다.
그런 태도가 마음에서 자라 우리 정신을 사로잡으면
나쁜 행동을 하지 않겠다는 결심이 약해질 수 있습니다.
마귀가 어떻게 우리의 태도를 이용하는지 알 수 있지 않나요?
부정적인 태도와 불평하는 태도를 피해야 하는데,
많은 일을 하지 못해서 낙심하게 될 수 있죠.
그걸 이루지 못해서 실망한 적이 있습니까?
어쩌면 더 많은 시간 봉사하려는 목표를 세웠을지 모릅니다.
그런데 생각한 대로 상황이 흘러가지 않았을 수 있죠.
다른 형제들이 봉사하면서 한 좋은 경험을 듣게 됩니다.
사탄이 어떻게 우리의 부정적인 태도를 이용하는지
우리는 기운이 빠지고 힘을 잃게 될 수 있습니다.
그런데 사탄은 우리가 가진 그러한 감정을 교묘히 이용해
따라서 우리는 자신에 대해 균형 잡힌 견해를 가져야 합니다.
이런 균형 잡힌 시각을 가질 때
마귀의 계략에 넘어가지 않을 수 있습니다.
여러분이 마지막으로 마귀를 대적한 때는 언제입니까?
지금까지 마귀의 교묘한 책략 두 가지를 살펴봤습니다.
아마 우리 모두는 매일 마귀를 대적하고 있을 것입니다.
우리는 건강 문제에 대해 지나치게 염려하지 않으며
좋은 태도를 유지하기 위해 힘써 노력합니다.
여러분이 이 자리에 함께하신 것 자체가

en.text: James 4:7:
“Oppose the Devil, and he will flee from you”
is indeed powerful encouragement.
By these reassuring words,
Jehovah reminds us of the potential we have.
Why can we say so?
Because Jehovah would never expect us to do something
that is beyond our abilities.
And even if we ourselves in certain situations might feel
we do not have the strength anymore,
we know Jehovah will empower us.
Now,
when was the last time that you opposed the Devil?
We all understand the general concept of James 4:7,
and yet it might be a challenge
to get specific when it comes to applying it on a personal level.
We are not having conversations directly with the Devil
as Jesus did when he was tempted three times.
And we know that the Devil
might not cause all of our problems,
but we also know
that he is sure to use them for his purpose.
Therefore, let us try
to analyze two examples, two areas,
where we oppose the Devil and experience that he flees from us.
First of all, let’s talk about our health.
Now, health problems are something
most of us have to deal with in one way or another.
Sadly, some of us even have to deal with serious issues or disabilities.
So, now, what does this have to do with opposing the Devil?
One of the subtle attacks of the Devil
is that he tries to use our proper concern for our health
in order to shift our focus away from spiritual things.
He wants to make use of us being overly distracted.
He would like us
to become consumed with matters of health to the extent
that they take first place in our life,
or he would like us to go to extremes
in striving to maintain our health.
But he has no success.
One of the reasons for this we find in Luke chapter 12.
I’d like to invite you to open with me to Luke chapter 12,
and we would like to read verse 25.
Here Jesus asked a good question.
He says:
“Who of you by being anxious
can add a cubit to his life span?”
So while we take good care of our health
in line with Jesus’ words found at Luke 5:31,
we are not becoming unduly anxious
over things we cannot control.
At the convention, I talked to one of the attendants,
a brother in his 30’s.
At first, it was just normal small talk till later in the conversation
he revealed to me that he was actually supposed to be at the hospital.
The doctors had told him
that he would not survive the next five months.
Would he now be fully absorbed in finding some treatment
and forgetting all of his spiritual routine?
No.
Our brother persisted in getting some medicine
to be able to attend the convention.
He wanted to serve as an attendant.
He wanted to care for others.
And so strengthened by the program,
he was ready to go back to the hospital the next day.
We are not sacrificing our spirituality.
We maintain our spiritual balance,
and despite our challenges, we are caring for others.
In this way, we oppose the Devil
—and some of us on a daily basis.
Now let’s look at this second example.
Another area where we successfully oppose the Devil is our attitude.
We all know that attitude makes a big difference in life.
For example, a positive or a negative attitude
can influence how we deal with certain situations
and how other people react to us.
The same is true with a complaining
or a grateful attitude.
If we had a bad attitude, nothing would seem right,
even when from an objective point of view,
life is just good.
It would be like
putting a dirty towel on a nice piece of decoration in our room.
So, what does this have to do with opposing the Devil?
A negative attitude can be used by Satan.
It can accumulate in our heart
and overpower our ability to decide wisely.
We might lose our joy in Jehovah’s service.
It also can weaken our resolve to resist wrongdoing.
So do we see how the Devil
would be able to benefit from it?
Of course, as Christ’s followers,
we avoid a negative or a complaining attitude,
although this is not always easy.
And maybe we feel down
because we are sometimes not content with what we’re able to accomplish.
Are we, for example, disappointed at times
that we did not reach a goal that we set for ourselves?
Maybe we were encouraged to spend more time in the ministry,
and then things just did not turn out the way we planned them.
And then we are sitting in a congregation meeting,
and we are listening to the nice experiences of others.
How do we feel?
Are we discouraged?
That can be dangerous.
Let’s turn to Proverbs chapter 24 together.
Let’s read together Proverbs 24:10
because here this danger
that can be utilized by Satan is identified.
Here we read at Proverbs 24:10:
“If you become discouraged in the day of distress
“[that’s what we’re talking about],
your strength will be meager.”
Prolonged negative feelings can rob us of our strength,
making us feel weak and vulnerable.
Satan knows this well.
It is difficult enough if our heart is plagued
with such feelings of unworthiness or worthlessness.
However, when Satan attempts to exploit such feelings,
it makes this situation even more burdensome.
So as we maintain a balanced view of ourselves
or, as the apostle Paul calls it at Romans 12:3,
as we maintain “a sound mind,”
we oppose the Devil.
As we remind ourselves that Jehovah just expects 100 percent
—our personal 100 percent, today’s 100 percent,
not the 100 percent of somebody else,
not the 100 percent of what we were able to do years ago
—and as we keep this balanced view of ourselves,
we are not doing the Devil’s work.
So when was the last time that you opposed the Devil?
We just discussed two subtle forms of his attacks.
Probably we are all opposing the Devil on a daily basis.
We do not allow ourselves to be unduly anxious about health matters,
and we work hard in maintaining a good attitude.
The fact
that we are here together today
is proof that we all oppose the Devil
and that we experience that he flees from us.

cn.text: 雅各书4:7说
“反抗魔鬼，魔鬼就会离开你们逃跑了。”
耶和华通过这句非常有力的话提醒我们
我们是有能力反抗魔鬼的
为什么可以这么说呢？
因为耶和华从不会要求我们
做超出我们能力限度的事
就算我们有时因为面对的情况非常严峻
而感到无力应付
我们知道耶和华一定会加力量给我们
你上一次反抗魔鬼是什么时候？
我们都知道雅各书4:7的意思
但是实际运用到个人生活上就是另一回事了
耶稣曾三次面对魔鬼的引诱
但我们不会像耶稣那样直接与撒但正面交锋
另外
我们知道,我们的难题并不都是魔鬼造成的
但他确实利用我们的难题攻击我们
现在让我们从两个方面分析一下
看看我们可以怎样反抗魔鬼
魔鬼就会离开我们逃跑了
首先，我们来谈谈健康的问题
现在，大多数人或多或少
都会有一些健康的问题
令人难过的是
有些人要面对严重的健康难题或者身体残疾
这跟反抗魔鬼有什么关系呢？
魔鬼知道人人都关心自己的健康
所以他狡猾地利用这个正常的愿望攻击我们
他希望我们过度关注健康
不再把崇拜上帝放在生活的第一位
魔鬼撒但希望我们把所有心思
都集中在健康难题上
甚至希望我们为了保持健康不惜一切代价
但魔鬼是不会得逞的
其中一个理由在路加福音12章
请大家一起翻到路加福音12:25
这里耶稣说了一句发人深省的话
他说
“你们谁能靠忧虑叫寿命延长一点呢？”
所以，一方面我们要
听从耶稣在路加福音5:31的忠告
好好照顾自己的身体
另一方面我们也不需要过度担心
自己无法控制的情况
我在参加大会时
跟一个30多岁的招待员弟兄聊天
刚开始我们只是简单聊聊
后来他告诉我，他现在本来应该在医院里
因为医生说他的病非常严重，活不过5个月
这位弟兄并没有只想着找治疗的方法
而忽略更重要的事
他坚持先吃一些药控制一下
确保他可以来参加大会
他很想做大会的招待员，为别人服务
大会让他受到很大的鼓励
使他有力量第二天回到医院面对健康难题
我们非常重视自己跟耶和华的关系
把崇拜他当作生活中最重要的事
尽管面对逆境，我们也会考虑别人的需要
这样做就是反抗魔鬼了
有些人可能每天都在这样做
现在让我们看看第二方面，就是我们的态度
我们能否成功反抗魔鬼取决于我们的态度
你的态度会决定你过怎样的生活
例如，在面对同样的情况时
一个人态度积极，有感恩之心
跟一个人态度消极、爱抱怨
结果可能完全不一样
而且会影响别人对我们的看法
如果我们爱挑剔
就可能看什么事都不顺眼
即使我们过得其实还不错
这就好像把一块很脏的抹布
盖在一件漂亮的装饰品上
这和我们反抗魔鬼有什么关系呢？
魔鬼可能会利用我们消极的态度攻击我们
因为消极的思想会不断累积
使我们不能作出明智的决定
不能快乐地为耶和华服务
还会削弱我们做对的事的决心
魔鬼看到我们思想消极
他会多么高兴呢！
虽然有时不容易
基督徒还是要竭力避免消极或抱怨的态度
有时我们灰心是因为觉得自己总是做得不够好
例如，有时我们因为
没有达到自己的目标而感到灰心
也许我们定下目标要多花点时间传道
但突然有别的事情发生
使我们不能达到原定的目标
结果在聚会的时候
我们只能听别人分享他们的美好经历
遇到这样的情况时，我们会感到灰心吗？
如果会
那就危险了
让我们一起翻到箴言24章
我们一起读24:10
就能明白撒但会怎么利用这一点攻击我们
“如果你在苦难的日子气馁”
我们现在说的就是这种情况
经文继续说
“你的力量就会微弱”
如果我们长时间感到灰心
我们就会变得软弱，失去力量
撒但深知这个方法非常有效
我们在忍受难题的同时
如果感到自己没有价值
那就更是雪上加霜了
撒但会利用这样的感觉来攻击你
因此，我们要用耶和华的观点看待自己
就像使徒保罗在罗马书12:3中提到
“要思想健全”
这样就是反抗魔鬼了
我们要经常提醒自己
耶和华希望我们把自己最好的献给他
把今天最好的献给他
而不是把别人最好的献给他
也不是把多年前我们最好的献给他
我们有这样平衡的观点
就不会让撒但破坏我们和耶和华的关系
上一次你反抗魔鬼是什么时候？
我们刚才谈到
撒但攻击我们的两个狡猾的方法
很可能我们天天都要反抗魔鬼的攻击
所以，我们学到
第一，不要让自己过度担心健康问题
第二，要努力让自己保持积极的态度
事实上
我们今天在这里就表明我们反抗魔鬼
也让魔鬼离开我们逃跑了

titles.cn: 盖乌斯·格洛肯汀：要反抗魔鬼（雅4:7）

ko.text: 우리 가족은 늘 함께 여호와를 섬겨 왔지만,
얼마 안 있어 모든 집회를 빠지기 시작했습니다.
저 혼자 이 모든 걸 하고 있다는 게
그이는 가정을 영적으로 이끄는 일도 중단했습니다.
마땅히 해야 할 일을 하도록 일깨워 주려고 했죠.
하지만 제가 말을 하면 할수록 상황은 악화됐고,
그동안 전 제가 힘든 점만 생각하느라
말이 아니라 아내의 행실을 통해 믿게 될 것입니다.”
상황을 개선할 다른 방법이 있었던 거예요.
제 태도와 행동은 남편에게 큰 영향을 줄 수 있죠.
공감해 주고 동정심을 보이면 효과가 있어요.
성경에 나온 아비가일의 본을 생각해 봤습니다.
제 남편은 나발과는 전혀 다른 사람이죠.
그날 밤 우린 진솔한 대화를 나눴습니다.
아무 말 없이 잘 들어 주었어요.
남편이 그렇게 많은 압박감에 시달리고 있는 줄은
저와 아이들 모두 아빠를 무척 사랑한다고 안심시켜 줬죠.
제 태도를 바꾸고 남편을 지원한 것이
제가 할 수 있는 어떤 말보다도 좋은 결과를 가져왔죠.
때로는 생각지 못한 축복을 얻게 됩니다.

cn.text: 我们一家人经常一起参加崇拜活动
但最近我丈夫变得有点不太对劲
他说他很累
然后就什么聚会都不参加了
我居然要自己一个人带孩子们去聚会
长老们来鼓励他
但还是没什么用
他也不再帮助家人亲近上帝
我越来越受不了他了
我一直提醒他
帮助家人亲近上帝是他的责任
也是他应该要做的
可是我说得越多，他就越不想理我
情况也变得越来越糟
我不知道该怎么办
我只看到自己的痛苦
却不知道其实他也很痛苦
聚会结束后，长老们来鼓励我
跟我一起看彼得前书3:1，经文说
我发现原来事情还有别的解决方法
我的态度和行为会对丈夫有很大的影响
对丈夫表现爱和体贴，胜过千言万语
我想到圣经里亚比该的例子
她的丈夫拿八是个很差劲的人
但亚比该一直对他很有耐心
我的丈夫不像拿八
他比拿八好太多了
那天晚上，我们聊了很多
我丈夫说出他内心的感受
我没有打断他，只是一直在听
我才知道原来他承受了那么大的压力！
我跟他说
我不会再给你压力了
等你准备好了再去聚会吧！
我跟丈夫说我和孩子们一直都很爱他
情况渐渐开始好转了
家里每个人都感觉好多了
我们知道要像以前那样还需要一些时间
我全力支持丈夫
也改变对他的态度
这胜过千言万语
虽然不知道结果怎么样
但只要我们运用圣经原则
上帝就一定会赐福给我们
真的非常感谢耶和华！
感谢他赐给我们这么宝贵的圣经原则！

titles.cn: 好品行胜过千言万语

ko.text: 이번 달 방송에 오신 여러분을 모두 환영합니다.
보시는 것처럼 제 친구와 함께 진행할 텐데요,
다양한 경험을 한 형제인데요, 네덜란드에서 태어났고,
저와 아내 케이는 세 나라에서 봉사했죠.
저희 삶을 돌아보면 세 단어가 떠오릅니다.
증인이 한 명도 없는 외딴 우림 지역이었어요.
‘여호와를 섬기려는 사람을 대체 어디서부터 어떻게 찾지?’
자전거를 타고 마을 사람들을 전부 찾아다녔어요.
얼마 후 25건의 성서 연구를 사회할 수 있었습니다.
예를 들어, 한 여자는 자녀들과 힘을 합해
“여호와를 위한 거예요”라고 하는데 우린 그만 눈물을 흘렸죠.
하루는 용기 있는 여러 성서 연구생들이
교회에서 탈퇴하려고 쓴 편지를 우리에게 보여 주더군요.
그 주에 그 작은 마을에 있는 교회의 목사는
그 작은 집단이 회중으로 발전하게 하시는 걸 직접 보면서
사실 이런 일을 어디서나 볼 수 있는데요,
여호와께서 소중히 여기고 돌보시는 걸 보면
그러면 이번 달 방송 내용을 소개해 주실까요?
이달에는 은퇴한 축구 선수인 안드리 네스마치니를 만나 볼 텐데요,
우리가 삶의 우선순위를 검토하는 데 도움이 될 것입니다.
영적인 일 사이의 균형을 잡는 법을 배웠는지 볼 것입니다.
우리 모두가 한가족이라는 걸 생각나게 해 줄 겁니다.
이번 달에는 두 가지 주제로 말씀드리겠습니다.
우리 출판물 번역에 대해 이야기해 볼 텐데요,
번역과 관련해 특히 언급하고 싶은 점이 있습니다.
언어가 다른 나라로 이주하신 분들이 많이 계실 겁니다.
번역이 다른 경우를 보게 될 수 있습니다.
그럴 때 그 이유가 궁금할 수 있죠.
하지만 그렇다고 해서 번역자들이 일을 대충 하고 있다거나
조직의 인도를 무시하고 있다고 생각해서는 안 됩니다.
번역이 다른 데에는 합리적인 이유가 분명히 있을 겁니다.
따라서 이번 시간에는 그러한 이유들 중
먼저 번역자들이 따르는 한 가지 원칙을 생각해 보겠습니다.
번역자들은 영어 원문에 있는 사상을 정확하게 전달하면서도,
사람들이 실제 말하는 방식을 염두에 둬야 합니다.
따라서 정확하고, 명료하고, 자연스럽게 번역해야 하죠.
그러면 그렇게 번역하려면 어떻게 해야 할까요?
번역자들은 히브리어 성경을 베껴 쓴 유대인 필사자들과는 다릅니다.
그 필사자들은 토씨 하나 안 틀리고 정확히 베껴 쓰기 위해,
그들이 원문에서 베껴 쓴 단어 수뿐만 아니라
번역문에도 일곱 단어가 있어야 하는 건 아닙니다.
원문의 모든 단어를 번역하는 게 아니라
원문의 온전한 사상이 들어 있어야 하죠.
영어에서는 앞 문장에 이미 나온 사상을 단어들만 조금 바꿔서
우리 출판물에 대한 인식도 나빠질 수 있죠.
그런 경우에는 번역자들이 영문에 나오는 두 문장을
영어의 긴 문장을 두 문장으로 나눌 수도 있습니다.
번역된 문단의 길이와 다른 것을 보게 되더라도
외국어를 배운 형제들이 이렇게 말할 때가 있습니다.
“왜 번역자들이 영어를 단어 그대로 번역하지 않았지?
그렇게 번역을 해도 말이 되는데 말이야.”
물론 단어 대 단어로 번역을 해도 “말은” 될 수 있죠.
하지만 그 언어가 모국어인 사람들은 어색해할 수 있습니다.
흔히 어떤 표현이 자연스러운지 가장 잘 판단할 수 있는 사람들은
우리가 겸허하다면 그 점을 인정할 것입니다.
또 우리가 생각해 보아야 할 점이 한 가지 더 있습니다.
번역된 어떤 표현에 대해 비평적으로 말한다면,
그 번역물을 영적 양식으로 삼고 의존해야 하는 모국어 사용자들이
번역자들은 아주 진지한 태도로 일하고 있습니다.
이제 여러 해 동안 번역 작업을 해 오신
그러한 어려움 몇 가지에 대해 이야기해 보겠습니다.
번역자들이 번역할 때 무엇을 고려하는지 알아보시죠.
그 세 가지는 성경 표현, 비유, 어휘입니다.
매우 어려울 수 있는 이유를 말씀해 주시겠습니까?
거짓 종교의 가르침과 그걸 반영하는 용어들이 들어 있죠.
그런 용어들이 우리의 번역에 영향을 주지 않도록
잘못된 방식으로 번역한 어떤 표현이 있는지
그에 해당하는 표현은 하늘에 있는 영적 존재를 가리키며
독자들에게 큰 혼동을 줄 수 있겠네요.
번역자들은 그 부분을 어떻게 처리할 수 있나요?
많은 언어권에선 성령에 가장 근접하는 의미를 전달하는
“성스러운 능력”이나 “성스러운 힘”과 같은 번역 표현을 찾아냈죠.
좀 다르게 들릴 수 있지만 같은 사상을 전달합니다.
다른 영어 번역판들엔 “하느님의 성령”으로 돼 있죠.
네, 그렇게 하면 형제들이 봉사하거나 연설할 때
사람들이 이해할 수 있는 적절한 표현을 사용할 수 있겠네요.
하지만 형제들은 새로운 표현에 익숙해질 필요가 있죠.
형제들은 이전 성경의 옛날 표현을 사용해
여러 해 동안 사람들에게 진리를 가르쳐 왔습니다.
그러한 용어들이 유익하다는 걸 알게 되고,
이제 두 번째 부면을 생각해 보죠.
비유를 번역하기가 특별히 어려운 이유는 무엇입니까?
특정 비유가 어떤 문화권에선 통하지 않을 수 있습니다.
비유는 읽는 사람이 공감할 수 있을 때 효과가 있죠.
그래서 예수께서는 사람들에게 익숙한 일상적인 것들로
우리 출판물도 사람들이 공감할 수 있는 비유를 사용하죠.
참을성을 보일 필요를 다룬 적이 있는데,
꽉 막힌 도로에 갇힌 운전자의 비유를 들었습니다.
그런데 한 번역 팀에서 문의를 해 왔어요.
많은 사람들이 교통 체증에 익숙하지 않다는 거였죠.
그래서 번역 팀은 비유를 바꾸길 원했습니다.
줄을 길게 서서 기다리는 광경을 흔히 볼 수 있었고,
참을성을 보여야 한다는 요점을 이해하는 데
이 두 비유는 완전히 다른 비유지만
영어에서 사용된 비유와 다른 것을 보게 되더라도,
본부의 승인을 받아 그러한 변경을 한 것임을 확신할 수 있습니다.
이제 세 번째 부면으로 넘어가 보죠.
각 나라 언어에서 쓰이는 단어들을 말합니다.
흔히, 모국어에 있는 중요한 단어 하나하나에 대해
정확히 일치하는 외국어 단어가 있을 거라고 생각할 수 있는데,
사실, 번역은 그보다 훨씬 더 복잡합니다.
하느님의 평화를 주제로 한 대회가 있었는데요,
번역하기에 그리 어려워 보이지 않을 수 있죠.
하지만 그 대회에서 이 단어가 약 350번 정도 사용되었는데,
때로는 하느님과 사람 사이의 평화를 가리켰고,
또 다른 경우엔 가족이나 이웃과의 평화를 가리켰죠.
한 단어만으론 그 모든 의미를 전달할 수가 없었습니다.
그 언어들에서는 제각기 다른 단어를 사용해서

성경엔 안 나와 있다고 하면서 넘어갈 수도 있죠.
하지만 계산해 보면 알아낼 수 있습니다.
「통찰」 책의 “연대 계산” 항목을 찾아 볼 수 있습니다.
노아와 아브람이 과연 서로 아는 사이였는가 하는 거였습니다.
필요한 게 다 나와 있을 겁니다.
아브람이 기원전 2018년에 태어났단 걸 알게 됩니다.
적어도 서른 살은 많았을 거라는 말이 자주 나옵니다.
그런데 뭐든 그냥 넘어가지 않는 여러분의 연구생이
다윗은 왕이 됐을 때 몇 살이었을까요?
사울은 이미 이스라엘을 10년 동안 다스리고 있었습니다.
하지만 사울이 왕이 됐을 때 요나단은 성인이었습니다.
근데 군 복무를 하려면 적어도 20세는 돼야 했죠.
그러니까 요나단은 사울이 왕이 됐을 때 적어도 20세였고,
그러면 요나단과 다윗은 나이 차이가 얼마나 됩니까?
이제 다음 건 조금 더 복잡합니다.
모세와 욥이 같은 시기에 살았다고 알려 줍니다.
근데 그걸 어떻게 알 수 있을까요?
욥이 시험받은 때는 요셉이 죽은 후 어느 때였을 겁니다.
‘욥과 같은 사람이 땅에 없다’고 하시기 때문입니다.
여호와께선 요셉과 욥과 같은 사람이 없다고 하셨을 겁니다.
시험이 더 일찍 있었다면 이렇게 말씀하셨겠죠.
또는 아브라함과 욥 같은 사람은 없다고요.
또 노아의 생애도 아브라함과 2년밖에 차이가 나지 않지요.
그러니까 욥은 요셉이 죽은 후에 시험을 받았을 것입니다.
하지만 「통찰」 책과 성경에 그 연도를 직접 계산하는 데 필요한
이스라엘 백성이 모세의 인도 아래 이집트에서 나왔는데,
그 144년 기간의 어느 시점에 있었을 겁니다.
욥은 시험을 받은 후로 140년을 더 살았습니다.
욥은 여전히 우스 땅에 살고 있었을 겁니다.
같은 시기에 살았다는 결론을 내릴 수 있죠.
계산을 해 보니 무엇을 알게 되나요?
일단 우리는 아브라함이 노아가 죽고 2년 뒤에 태어났다는 것,
요나단이 다윗보다 30세 이상 나이가 많았다는 것,
모세와 욥이 분명 같은 시대에 살았다는 걸 배웠죠.
그런 질문들의 답을 얻게 된 것입니다.
그런 답이 여러분이 늘 알고 싶었던 점은 아닐 수 있지만,
여기엔 더 많은 의미가 들어 있죠.
때때로 숫자는 단순한 숫자에 불과한 게 아니란 점입니다.
다른 방법으론 결코 알 수 없는 정보를 줄 수 있죠.
계산하느라 많이 힘드셨으니까, 이제 음악을 들어 볼까요?
이번 달 뮤직비디오는 국제 대회를 위해 여행하고
전 세계 영적 가족을 만나는 큰 기쁨을 상상해 볼 수 있게 해 줄 것입니다.
내 가족 있는 건 멋진 일이죠.
우리와 한가족인 새로운 형제 자매들을 만나는 기쁨이
마음이 올바른 사람들이 진리를 받아들이는 데
우리의 행실이 도움이 된다는 걸 봤죠.
또 번역 작업이 어떻게 이루어지는지도 살짝 봤고요.
판 셀름 형제, 함께 집필부에서 일해서 참 좋고요,
이번 달 방송도 함께 할 수 있어 좋았습니다.
이번 달에 다음 지역 대회 날짜를 알게 되신다고 들었는데요.
제가 목소리를 낮출 테니까, 잘 들으세요.
우린 여러 기회에 이 대회 주제를 알리게 될 것입니다.
대회 가슴표를 단 모습을 상상해 보세요.
이제 방송을 마치기 전에 판 셀름 형제가
보츠와나에는 자연 경관이 아름다운 곳이 많습니다.
보츠와나는 세계에서 코끼리가 가장 많이 사는 나라이기도 하죠.
면적이 아주 넓은 이 나라에 널리 퍼져 삽니다.
그래서 이곳 전도인들은 더 필요한 곳에서 봉사하기 위해
여러 날 또는 여러 주에 걸쳐 가장 먼 마을까지 전파합니다.
현재 이 나라엔 회중 45개와 격지 집단 2개가 있습니다.
지금 보시는 에차 회중은 오카방고 모레미 지역에 있는데,
집회에 오는 데만도 먼 거리를 흔히 걸어서 여행해야 하죠.
하지만 이 여행이 어려운 건 단지 멀어서만이 아니라
형제 자매들은 함께 모여 여호와를 섬기고
전파 활동에 참여하는 것을 정말 좋아합니다.
수많은 충실한 형제 자매들이 아주 외딴 지역에까지
이곳 형제 자매들이 여러분 모두에게 사랑과 인사를 전합니다.
보츠와나에 있는 형제 자매 모두에게 우리의 사랑을 전합니다.

en.text: Hello, everyone.
We’re so happy to have you with us for this month’s broadcast.
As you can see, I have a friend with me as cohost.
We are friends, aren’t we?
Yes, we are, David.
Oh, that’s so good to hear.
This is Herman van Selm.
He’s a helper to the Writing Committee,
and we work together every day in the Writing Department.
Herman has quite a background.
He was born in the Netherlands
and spent a number of years as a missionary in South America.
What was that like, Herman?
Thank you, David, for asking.
My wife, Kay, and I served in three different lands.
Now, to sum up that part of our life,
three words come to mind: challenging,
amazing, rewarding.
In one challenging assignment,
we lived in a remote area in the rain forest
where there were no other Witnesses.
We wondered: ‘Will we be able
‘to find people who want to serve Jehovah?
Where do we start?’
We got on our bikes and visited all the villagers.
In time, we conducted about 25 Bible studies.
Wow!
Now, despite fierce opposition from neighbors,
the Bible students made amazing progress.
For example, one woman, with her children,
worked hard to build this beautiful hut,
and it brought us to tears when she told us:
“This hut, we made it for our meetings.
It is for Jehovah.”
Amazing!
One day, a group of courageous Bible students
showed us the letters they had written
to resign as members of their church.
Now, that week, the church’s pastor
in that tiny village received
a lot of mail!
I guess, mail he didn’t want to receive.
It was no fan mail.
It was such a rewarding experience for Kay and me
to see close up how Jehovah made that little group
grow into a congregation.
In fact, it strengthens the faith
of all of us, wherever we may live,
to see how Jehovah cares for people
who are often viewed as insignificant by the world
but who are precious in God’s eyes.
Great pictures—I love it!
Now, what can the friends look forward to this month?
Well, David, this month
we’ll meet Andrey Nesmachniy, a retired professional
soccer player whose story
may help us to analyze our own priorities in life.
Later, we’ll see how Thomas learns to balance
his secular work with his spiritual needs.
And we’ll enjoy an upbeat music video
that reminds us all of the wonderful “family”
we enjoy in Jehovah’s organization.
Sounds exciting, let’s get started!
This is the September 2019 program
of JW Broadcasting.
This month,  I’m going to talk about two different subjects.
First, I’d like to talk about the translation
of our publications,
and there’s a particular aspect
of translation I’d like to comment on.
Now, I know that quite a number of you have moved
to a country where your mother tongue isn’t spoken
—either to find work or to serve where the need is greater.
And others are serving right at home
but in foreign-language congregations.
At times, you may have compared an article in your mother tongue
with the same article in your second language
and found differences in the translation,
and you might wonder why that is.
Well, we’d never conclude that the translators
had been unfaithful or careless
or that they were running ahead of the organization.
No.
We trust our hardworking brothers and sisters.
So we know there must be good reasons for the differences,
and the purpose of this brief discussion
is to suggest what some of those reasons might be.
First, a word about one of the principles our translators follow.
They’re expected not only to render the thought in the English text accurately
but also to keep in mind the way people speak.
So accuracy, clarity,
and naturalness are needed
while maintaining the dignity of our message.
Now, what’s involved in preparing a translation
that’s both accurate and natural?
It’s not as if the translators are like the Jewish scribes
who made copies of the Hebrew Scriptures.
To make sure that the copies they made
were accurate in every detail,
they would count not only every word
but also every letter they copied from the source text.
Translation is not like that.
It’s not as if there must be seven words in the target language
if there are seven words in English.
Every word in English may not be translated,
but the complete thought of the English has to be there.
English makes effective use of repetition.
What do we mean by that?
Well, you can write one sentence in English and then repeat the same thought
in slightly different words in the next sentence,
and it sounds fine.
But in some languages,
to repeat a thought would be viewed as poor writing,
and that wouldn’t reflect well on our publications.
So in such cases,
the translators are allowed to combine
two sentences into just one sentence
as long as the thought is completely conveyed.
Or they might make two sentences out of one long English sentence
if that’s more natural in the language.
So you can’t always compare the length of an English paragraph
with the length of the paragraph
in the target language and say,
“Hey, this paragraph is shorter than that paragraph.”
Sometimes we hear brothers who have learned a second language say:
“I don’t see why the translators didn’t follow the English word for word.
After all, you can say that in the language.”
Well, you may have the words.
It may be possible to “say” that,
but would a literal translation sound strange to native speakers?
No matter how well a foreigner has learned a language,
native speakers who speak the language well
are usually the best judge of what is natural.
Modesty will help foreign speakers to recognize that.
There’s another thing that foreign speakers need to be aware of.
If they’re vocal in their criticism of a certain translation,
how would that affect the confidence of native speakers
who have to rely on the translation for their spiritual food?
Of course, nobody is perfect,
and as long as translation is done by imperfect people,
it won’t be perfect.
But rest assured that our translators
take their work very seriously.
The subject of translation is complex.
And I’m surely no expert.
Let’s hear from some brothers who have worked in the field for many years
and see what we can learn.
Meet Nick Ahladis,
Nick Exarcheas,
and Saki Marais.
As we have just heard,
the goal of translators is to convey ideas
accurately, naturally, and clearly.
This isn’t an easy thing to do.
Let’s discuss a few of the challenges of translation.
We will focus on three areas
and see why translators make the choices they do:
Bible expressions,
illustrations,
and vocabulary.
So our first point is Bible expressions.
Nick, could you please tell us
why translating some expressions in the Bible
can be very challenging?
Well, before our brothers and sisters
receive the New World Translation in their language,
they have to use Bibles produced by Christendom.
Often, these Bibles contain false religious ideas
and terms that reflect those ideas.
So when we produce the New World Translation,
great care has to be taken
not to allow such terms to distort our translation.
Can you give us an example of an expression
that was translated the wrong way
in the Bibles produced by Christendom?
Well, one example is the term “holy spirit.”
In many Bibles produced by Christendom,
the term gives the idea of a spirit creature in heaven,
even a “holy ghost,” sometimes even a “holy demon.”
That must be very confusing to the readers.
But what can the translators do about that?
In many languages, our translators have found
that the closest way to translate “holy spirit”
is to say “holy power” or “holy force.”
This may sound very different,
but it conveys the same idea.
And even the English New World Translation
describes the term “holy spirit”
as “God’s active force” at Genesis 1:2,
while other English translations say “God’s holy spirit.”
Good.
So now the brothers can use an expression
that is understood by the field and the audience.
But it must be a wonderful thing to have the New World Translation.
Yes, it’s a wonderful thing.
But still, the brothers have to get used to the new terms.
Remember that they’ve been using
the original terms in their local Bibles for years
to teach people the truth.
But as they get used to the new terminology
in their personal study, at meetings, and in the ministry,
they begin to see the benefits of the new terms,
and afterward they really embrace the New World Translation.
Thank you.
Now let us go to the second challenge,
illustrations.
Why are illustrations
particularly difficult to translate?
An illustration that works in one culture might not work in another.
Illustrations are only effective if the reader can relate to them.
And that’s why Jesus used illustrations
based on everyday things that his audience was familiar with,
such as farming, building, fishing.
And today, our publications
also use illustrations that people can relate to.
I remember an article that discussed the need
for us to be patient in difficult situations.
And it used the illustration of a driver who is stuck in traffic.
Now, one translation team wrote to the Translator Help Desk,
and they explained that most of their readers
were not familiar with traffic jams.
For someone who lives in a big city,
that sounds unbelievable, but it’s true.
So the team wanted to use a different illustration.
They are familiar with the idea of people standing in long lines,
waiting for their maize, or corn, to be ground at the milling machine.
And this illustration was approved
because it would help their readers to get the point:
They need to be patient.
Now, these are completely different illustrations,
but the point —or the message—
is the same, for example, then, about being patient.
Now, when we read in our language edition
of The Watchtower or other publication
a different illustration than the one we read in English,
we can be confident that the translators received approval
to make this adjustment so that the right message is conveyed.
Well, that was very helpful. Thank you.
Now let us go to our third challenge
—that of vocabulary,
that is, the words that are used in a language.
Now, we might assume that for every important word
in our language
there will be an exact equivalent
in another language.
Well, translation is much more complicated than that.
Take, for example, the word “peace.”
Some years back,
we had a convention about godly peace.
And one might think, ‘Well, that’s an easy word to translate.’
But that word was used about 350 times
in talks on the convention
—sometimes referring to peace between God and man,
sometimes referring to peace in family or with our neighbors,
and other times referring to peace of mind.
Now, in some languages, there’s simply no way
to use just one word to convey all those aspects of peace
because they have one word for the kind of peace that God gives,
a different word for when there’s no war in a country (that kind of peace),
and a different word to indicate that people
are getting along with one another.
So those translators need to understand the point
of each usage in the context
and then convey the right translation accordingly.
Now it opens our minds to how wonderfully Jehovah made us,
with the capacity to think and feel
and have many concepts and ideas
and to have the ability to express them in our language
—in words— to use words for that.
But we express them in so many different ways.
Yes, it’s so true.
Every language has its own vocabulary and way of expressing things.
What I find very interesting is how other languages
render standard expressions that we use as Jehovah’s Witnesses.
For example, “field service,” “circuit overseer,”
“Kingdom Hall,” “special pioneer”
—those expressions were first used in English,
and then translators had to come up with equivalents
in their languages so that it would make sense.
But that wouldn’t be difficult —would it?—
because for the word “kingdom”
surely we have another word in another language,
and for the word “hall” we have an equivalent word.
And all you have to do is put the two words together
to translate “Kingdom Hall.”
They may have the words,
but a literal translation of “Kingdom Hall”
could mean something totally different.
Now, some countries still have a king.
In those places, this “Kingdom Hall” could mean
“government office,” or it could mean
“hall belonging to the kingdom of Jehovah’s Witnesses.”
So that would be totally misleading.
And that’s why the Governing Body has given approval to say
the “Meeting Place of Jehovah’s Witnesses”
or the “Hall of Jehovah’s Witnesses.”
Even though the expressions sound a little bit different,
the basic intent is the same, and people get the right idea.
So it is obvious that the challenges of translation are huge.
But now the question is,
How can a newly formed translation team
or one in a very remote location
have the confidence and have the assurance
that they produce the highest standard possible?
Well, all translation teams, regardless of size or location,
benefit from regular communication
with the Writing Committee of the Governing Body.
Well, we understand that the Governing Body
directs matters from headquarters,
but do they really know what the translators are doing?
Well, the Writing Committee trusts the translators,
but at the same time, they don’t try to micromanage their work.
What they have done is set in place training programs
to teach translators basic translation principles
to help them to understand how to apply those principles
when translating the publications.
And this ensures that the same message
is being conveyed regardless of language.
And when they’re not sure that their solution
is exactly right on target,
they can write to the Writing Committee
and ask for direction to inquire whether this solution
conveys the right idea in the context.
Also, the Writing Committee answers
hundreds of translation questions every week
as part of the ongoing training of the teams.
All of the translators have access to these answers
so that they can learn from one another
how to solve problems that are delicate and difficult.
This effective communication system
really helps to unify the thinking of all the translators
and to make sure that they all produce the same message.
And that unifies the thinking of the worldwide field.
Well, thank you very much for explaining those factors
affecting translation,
and it is impressive
that Jehovah has an arrangement in place
that reverses the effect of Babel.
And it is also so wonderful that by means of his holy spirit,
Jehovah unifies his people around the earth
regardless of what language they use.
Thanks, brothers.
You’ve given us an even deeper appreciation
for all of the work involved in making a quality translation.
I learned a lot.
I’m sure our audience did too.
Now, the following video
relates an experience that is very dear to my heart.
You see, in the 1970’s,
my wife and I were in the circuit work in Montreal, Canada.
Now, one Tuesday evening after the meeting,
I was approached by a ministerial servant.
He was very excited!
He said: “David, I work with a man who is the head of a small church.
He has invited me to his home!”
“That’s nice,” I said.
He said: “No, no, no, you don’t understand!
“They never invite anyone to their home unless they are members of the church.
I think this is going to be big.”
“Well,” I said, “if he’s interested,
“invite him to come to the meeting this weekend.
I’d love to meet him.”
Well, that weekend I was on the lookout for the man,
but he didn’t show up.
But neither did the ministerial servant.
Soon after, on a Monday morning
—fairly early—
I received a phone call from Brother Laurier Saumur,
who was well-known in Montreal and was a special pioneer at the time.
Laurier said: “We have a problem.
“A thousand people want Bible studies,
and many of them are going to be attending our meetings this week.”
They were the members of that church.
I asked Brother Saumur to take the lead in organizing the studies.
Now, here’s what happened:
The ministerial servant had been to the man’s home
and he’d given a good witness.
Then,
the brother met with the other responsible men of the church.
They were interested in what the Bible says,
and they wanted other members of the church to learn about the Bible too.
So about half the members of the church,
around 1,000 people,
accepted the invitation to have a Bible study.
But what moved the leader of the church
to invite the brother to his home in the first place?
Watch the following video, and I’ll answer that question at the end.
In the mid-1970’s, several brothers from the Montréal area
were approached to help with a unique situation that was unfolding.
A special pioneer, who was taking the lead at the time,
said that about a thousand people —all from the same church—
wanted to study the Bible with Jehovah’s Witnesses.
And it was all because of an informal witness.
The story began this way:
A brother in the local congregation
approached me one day
to tell me about an experience
he had with one of his workmates.
This man was responsible for a small local church,
and the brother had been able to give him an informal witness.
The man indicated
that he would like a Bible study,
and he wanted to convince the other members of his church
to also study the Bible with Jehovah’s Witnesses.
The fact was that this person
had a certain influence in the church.
So he talked to the church members
about the message he had heard from the brother,
and he convinced them that what they were missing
was a better understanding of the Bible.
Many people heard about it
because it was an exceptional event.
From what I heard, there were around a thousand people
who wanted to study the Bible at that time.
We didn’t have the brothers and sisters
that were needed to conduct all these Bible studies.
So they formed groups of 10, 12, 15 people.
And once or twice a week in Kingdom Halls, they conducted Bible studies.
It was questions, questions.
Everyone was asking questions.
But the Bible could always answer all these questions in a logical way
—one verse would explain another.
And we came to see
that the Bible in its entirety could explain every subject.
At the beginning,
groups of two or three families studied together.
And, yeah, they answered with the Bible.
That amazed me because
I didn’t know the Bible at all.
But I thought, ‘The Bible talks about this;
the Bible talks about that.’
It was like a discovery for me.
That was the parents.
The children weren’t there.
So when we accepted it, then we’d teach it to our children.
Everyone was disciplined while sitting at the table.
The children were very quiet
with their Truth book in front of them and their Bible.
When these families came to the Kingdom Hall,
the children were sitting beside their parents,
not moving, paying attention to what was being said.
I was young when they started coming.
I remember it very well.
A lot of them were my age.
I saw them like future potential friends.
It was really touching.
The first meeting I attended was here in Laval.
It really contributed to me one day taking a stand
and Jehovah becoming my God
and the truth becoming my way of life.
When I was young,
I was very afraid of death.
It was such a relief to learn that we don’t suffer when we die.
It’s like a sleep.
The ambitions I had before,
that may have been attainable,
became second place.
Now it was to have a simple life,
to walk with the organization,
and to raise my children in the truth.
Today, these brothers are really doing a lot in the organization,
helping in different areas, shouldering great responsibilities.
My father always strived
to set the example for all his children,
and it made an impression on me.
Now my wife and I have the privilege of serving here at the Canada branch.
I was eight years old
when my family started attending meetings.
I have really good memories of how
the local congregation at the time
took care of us and looked after us.
At the age of 15,
I started reading my Bible every day and studying it too.
From that point on,
I knew what I wanted to do with my life
—serve Jehovah full-time.
I really think Jehovah could see us on the inside.
Jehovah helped us a lot.
You can’t have anything better than that.
On our own, we never would have got out of that situation.
But Jehovah found a way to find “rightly disposed” ones.
A simple informal witness led to Bible studies that touched so many.
The brother was able to give a good witness,
but what motivated the church leader to listen to him in the first place?
It was the brother’s conduct.
He was a very loving brother,
and the way he dealt with others in the workplace really impressed the man.
The poet said: “I’d rather see a sermon than hear one any day.”
Those words certainly proved true in this exciting experience!
That’s an excellent transition into the next part of our program.
In this dramatization,
we’ll see for ourselves how a Christian’s conduct, even at work,
can have a powerful effect on those around them.
Sometimes I really hate my job.
I don’t know how Jason stays so positive.
I asked Jason why he refused the money,
and I found out that he’s one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
My wife is too,
so I know a lot about them.
But what Jason did really surprised me.
I wondered why he didn’t feel like
he was entitled to the extra money.
He’s such a hard worker,
and most of our supervisors accept bribes.
Jason showed me a Bible verse:
“Whatever you are doing, work at it whole-souled
as for Jehovah, and not for men.”
Jason’s relationship with God influences
every aspect of his life,
even his attitude toward work.
He couldn’t participate
in something dishonest, even if others did.
I could see that Jason really lived by his beliefs.
Jason invited me to see the construction project
he’s been volunteering at.
I felt like I had entered another world.
People of different races
worked alongside each other
without prejudice, and they were all volunteers.
Jason offered to study the Bible with me.
Emma has asked me to study in the past,
and I’ve always refused.
But this time, I accepted.
I liked my study
and even enjoyed going to the Kingdom Hall occasionally.
But I had to work overtime
to support my family.
I couldn’t go to meetings every week.
Hey, Jason,
how do you do it all
—work, family, meetings, even volunteer work?
I try to keep in mind Jesus’ words at Matthew 6:22.
Jesus compared our eyes to a lamp.
He said that if ‘our eye was focused, our whole body would be bright.’
It’s impossible
to focus on more than one thing at a time.
Jesus wanted his followers to focus on a single purpose:
that of doing God’s will.
Rather than being distracted by material things,
my wife and I lead a simple life,
avoiding unnecessary debt
or acquiring possessions that consume a lot of time and attention.
This way of life allows us to have time for what’s truly important.
If you asked Emma, which do you think she would prefer:
that you made more money or spent more time with her at the Kingdom Hall?
Jason’s example really impressed me.
He was an honest and diligent worker,
but he also kept secular work in its proper place.
It made me think about the choices I make,
and I decided that I too
wanted to ‘work whole-souled for Jehovah.’
James 2:17, 18, in part, states:
“Faith by itself, without works, is dead. . . .
“Show me your faith without the works,
and I will show you my faith by my works.”
Now, the faith that Jason displayed “by works” at his secular job
motivated Thomas to accept a Bible study and to continue to make spiritual progress
despite setbacks.
Seeing this and hearing of real-life examples,
such as in our previous video,
are excellent reminders of what a powerful witness
our actions can be.
But what if we’re in a situation where displaying faith
calls for us to give up something we previously loved or enjoyed?
The story of soccer player Andrey Nesmachniy
may help us to see what action to take.
Soccer was my reason for living.
I always dreamed of becoming a professional soccer player.
I thought that happiness came from fame,
a good career,
money.
When I was six, my parents signed me up for soccer.
I really loved playing soccer.
I spent all my time at the stadium, even late into the night.
When I was 12, I learned about Jehovah from my mom.
At that time,
she started studying the Bible.
And after about a year,
I began to preach from door to door.
When I was 17 years old, I finished school
and I received an invitation from the Dynamo Soccer Club in Kiev.
Oh, that was unforgettable!
Yes, my emotions were running high
because since childhood I had always dreamed of playing for Dynamo.
From that moment on, all my energy and all my time
were devoted to my career.
Every day we either trained or there was a game.
There was no time left for spiritual things.
Of course, being around people like that, I became just like them.
I led an immoral lifestyle
because huge amounts of money opened up many opportunities.
Going to nightclubs, the nightlife
—it was so immoral.
Everyone wants to be your friend and to meet you.
And, of course, this was tempting.
I also invested huge sums of money in real estate.
I wanted to create a foundation for the future and wealth for myself,
my family, and my relatives so that no one would be in need.
Yes, I was sure that this really was happiness.
This continued for nine years.
The turning point
was a conversation with management when an issue came up,
and they hurled insults at me.
At that moment, I felt worthless,
like a disposable cup
that you use and then crush
and throw away.
Besides, a new generation of soccer players was arriving
—many young guys.
I stopped being included in the starting lineup.
Also, the financial crisis began,
and real estate prices fell drastically.
I panicked; I didn’t know what to do.
And I started to think about the meaning of life:
‘What really is the meaning of life?
‘If it’s not a career, not money
—then what is it?’
And then I remembered everything that I learned
about Jehovah when I was a teenager.
I began to study the Bible again along with my wife.
After a year, I started preaching again, and in 2009,
I was baptized as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
And this brought me so much joy and satisfaction.
These feelings can’t be compared to winning any medal or cup.
I realized that I couldn’t slave for two masters,
but I still had to play two more years for Dynamo Kyiv.
Although it was a difficult time,
I took advantage of this opportunity,
and I am thankful to Jehovah that a good witness
was given about his name.
There were some soccer players
who showed interest in the truth.
In 2011 when my contract ended,
I finished my professional career.
First Timothy chapter 6
encourages us “to place [our] hope, not on uncertain riches,
but on God,” and “to be rich in fine works.”
People ask me: “Do you regret it?”
“Maybe you’d like to come back; do you miss soccer?”
And I honestly and sincerely say no.
I don’t miss it, and I don’t want to go back
because my relationship with Jehovah—
Well, it can’t be compared to anything.
Everything that this world offers is all short-lived,
and it’s only an illusion.
People see only one side of the picture —the fame and the money.
The other side are the injuries and disappointments.
It’s very hard psychologically and emotionally;
you have no freedom.
That’s why it’s better to give the very best to the One
who appreciates it.
What you do for Jehovah will always bring you happiness,
joy, and satisfaction.
Did you notice how Andrey mentioned that he couldn’t “slave for two masters,”
and this led him to eventually abandon the world of professional sports?
Yes, often our faith moves us to leave behind
careers and activities we once loved.
But to quote Paul’s words at Philippians 3:8:
“I have taken the loss of all things
“and I consider them as a lot of refuse
“[or as the footnote states, “garbage; rubbish.”],
that I may gain Christ.”
We can have confidence that anything we throw away
for the sake of our spirituality
has no real value when we compare it to the blessings
we enjoy as Jehovah’s friends.
Back to you, David.
Thanks, Herman. That was great.
For my second discussion on this broadcast,
I’d like to talk to you on the theme “Do the Math.”
Yes, you heard right: “Do the Math.”
Now, math may not be your favorite subject,
but as we’re going to see, someone has to do it.
Sometimes doing the math is the only way we can make a time line
or get interesting background information
that makes our Bible reading more enjoyable.
And you do want to make your Bible reading more enjoyable, don’t you?
Of course you do!
Well, let’s start with a number
we might quickly skip over in our Bible reading.
Let’s turn to Matthew 19:28,
and let’s see how a number
can sometimes tell us more than what’s written on the page.
Matthew 19:28:
“Jesus said to them: ‘Truly I say to you,
“‘in the re-creation,
“‘when the Son of man sits down on his glorious throne,
“‘you who have followed me will sit on 12 thrones,
judging the 12 tribes of Israel.’”
Did you see anything interesting there?
I’ll give you a hint:
These words were spoken near the end
of Jesus’ earthly ministry.
Does that give you a hint?
I’ll give you another hint: the number 12.
At this point, Jesus knew
that only 11 of his apostles were going to be faithful.
Yet, he said there would be 12 thrones in the Kingdom, not 11.
What did it mean?
It meant that Judas would have to be replaced as an apostle.
And sure enough, he was.
Well, that was easy, wasn’t it?
There was no math involved.
It was just a number.
But, let’s see how doing the math can help us to answer a few questions.
During family worship, one of the kids asks
whether Noah and Abraham knew each other.
How are you going to handle that?
Do you know?
You might just say,
“The Bible doesn’t say” and leave it at that.
But you could figure it out
if you did the math.
Now, here’s what we know:
The Flood occurred in 2370 B.C.E.
Now, that date is absolutely solid.
And if you’d like to figure it out for yourself,
you can look it up under “Chronology”
in the Insight book—2370 B.C.E.
That’s the Flood.
And Noah lived for 350 years after the Flood.
So by subtracting 350 from 2370,
we learn that Noah died in 2020 B.C.E.
But remember the question?
The question is, Did Noah and Abram know each other?
Abram entered the land of Canaan
in 1943 B.C.E.
Now, once again, if you want to prove that to yourself,
look in Insight under “Chronology.”
You’ll find everything you need to prove it to yourself.
So in 1943 B.C.E., Abraham
(Abram in that case)
enters the land of Canaan
and he’s 75 years old at the time.
So Abram must have been born
75 years before 1943 B.C.E.
Add 75 to 1943,
and you find that Abram was born
in 2018 B.C.E.
So Noah died in 2020 B.C.E.,
and Abram was born two years later, in 2018 B.C.E.
They never knew each other, but it was close.
Our publications have often said
that Jonathan was at least 30 years older than David.
But the Bible doesn’t say that.
Your progressive Bible student
(you know, the one who makes you prove everything)
asks you about that.
Can you prove it?
Can you?
You can if you do the math.
King Saul ruled Israel for 40 years.
Then David became king.
Now, how old was David when he became king?
The Bible says that he “was 30 years old.”
That means that when David was born,
Saul had already been ruling Israel for ten years.
But when Saul became king, Jonathan was a grown man.
He was probably already in the army.
You had to be at least 20 years old to be in the army.
So if Jonathan was at least 20
when Saul began to rule and David was born 10 years after that,
what difference in age would there have been
between Jonathan and David?
About a 30-year difference
—20 plus 10 equals 30.
Now, the next one
is a bit more complicated; it’s the last one.
And we can do this.
Insight on the Scriptures says
that Moses and Job lived at the same time.
But the Bible doesn’t say that.
How can we be so sure?
Once again, what do we do?
Do I hear it?
You’re right; we do the math.
Job’s test must have occurred
sometime after the death of Joseph.
We know that because in Job chapter 1,
Jehovah told Satan:
“There is no one like [Job] on the earth.”
“No one.”
Now, if Joseph had still been alive,
Jehovah would have said that there was no one like Joseph and Job on the earth.
And if the test had occurred earlier,
Jehovah would have said that there was no one like Jacob and Job,
Isaac and Job, Abraham and Job.
And remember, there were only two years between Noah and Abraham,
so we can conclude that the test of Job
occurred after the death of Joseph.
When did Joseph die?
The date is solid.
It’s 1657 B.C.E.
How do we figure that?
If you don’t like math, trust me, you don’t want to know!
But Insight and the Bible will give you
all the information you need to figure it out for yourself.
But let’s keep it simple.
Let’s go with 1657 B.C.E.
That’s 144 years before Israel left Egypt
under the direction of Moses in 1513 B.C.E.
So Job’s test must have occurred
sometime within that 144-year period.
Now this is a big hint:
144 years before Israel left Egypt.
Are you beginning to put it together?
Here is the clincher:
Job lived for 140 years
after he passed the test,
so he was probably still alive in the land of Uz
when Israel left Egypt.
Conclusion: Job and Moses
definitely lived at the same time.
So, what have we learned by doing the math?
Superficially, we might say:
“Well, we’ve learned that Abraham was born two years after Noah.
“And we’ve proved that Jonathan was at least 30 years older than David
and that Moses and Job definitely lived at the same time.”
Superficially, we got the answers to those questions, yes.
But the fact is
that probably none of those questions ever kept you up at night.
There’s a broader picture here.
What we’d like you to take away
is the fact that sometimes a number is more than just a number.
It can provide information that we couldn’t get any other way,
and if we can understand that,
this discussion will have been well worth having.
So when you see a number in the Bible,
don’t run the other way.
Embrace it; stop and think about it.
You may be glad you did.
Well, after all that math, how about a little music?
This month’s music video will let us experience some of the joy
of traveling to an international convention
and meeting our spiritual family members from around the globe.
Touching down in a foreign land With a thousand miles behind us—
Since we left our home,
It’s Jehovah’s hand That is blessing ev’ry move.
And the work that we do isn’t easy, But it’s all for Jehovah.
And the love that we feel for this fam’ly is real,
So this we say to you:
“We’re all Jehovah’s people; United, we are family.
“And though your land is far away, We love you.
We’re your family.”
Waiting there as our plane came in, You were reaching out to greet us.
Then the music starts, and the day begins, And our love grows even more.
But we know that it’s only Jehovah Who can cause this to happen.
So we’ll praise him together and love him forever
On ev’ry distant shore.
“We’re all Jehovah’s people; United, we are family.
“And though your land is far away, We love you.
We’re your family.”
Silver wings fly across the sea To a land so unfamiliar.
But we bring good news, and the ones we meet Are so gentle, kind, and good.
And the love we receive from our brothers Makes us feel we belong here.
So wherever we are and no matter how far, We love our brotherhood!
It’s good to know That we have family ev’rywhere we go—
From Mali to Mexico, From Japan to Jamaica.
“We’re all Jehovah’s people; United, we are family.
“And though your land is far away, We love you.
“We’re your family.
“From ev’ry tribe and nation— United, we are family.
“These bonds of love are plain to see Because we’re Jehovah’s family!
“Fiji, Tahiti, and New Caledonia— Navajo, Blackfoot, and Cherokee—
“Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, and Estonia— We love you.
We’re your family.”
That song really captures the excitement that we feel
when we meet new members of our family.
I certainly agree. It was great.
Well, this month we saw how our actions
can help motivate right-hearted ones to accept the truth.
We peeked behind the scenes to learn how translation work is done.
And we even did a little math.
Herman, I love working with you in the Writing Department,
and I loved working with you on this project this month.
Thank you, David.
Well, thank you.
I really appreciate your help.
Now, I’ve been informed that many of you will be notified
of the dates for your regional convention this month.
Would you like to know the theme for the 2020 convention program?
I’ll lower my voice, and I’ll let you in on it.
The program is based on Philippians 4:4
and the theme “Always Rejoice”!
Isn’t that a great theme?
We’re going to have a great time advertising this convention theme.
Can you imagine having that on your convention badge?
And people will look at that badge and they’ll say,
“What do you have to be so happy about?”
And then we’ll tell them.
But before we end the program,
let’s join Herman
on a short visit to the country of Botswana in the southern part of Africa.
Botswana is home to many natural wonders.
Among them is the Okavango Delta,
a natural haven for wildlife.
This country is also the home of the highest concentration
of elephants in the world.
However, when it comes to people,
there are only about two and a half million residents
spread out over this very large country.
And with only 2,316 publishers,
the ratio of Witnesses to residents
is about 1 to 1,000.
So they always enjoy it
when need-greaters offer to come
and assist them as they cover hundreds
of kilometers of unassigned territory on preaching trips that can
last for days or even for weeks
in order to reach the most remote villages.
Currently, there are 45 congregations and 2 isolated groups.
The Etsha Congregation, located in the Okavango Moremi area,
is small with only seven publishers and no elders.
But the zeal of these publishers
is amazing as they travel long distances,
often on foot, just to attend meetings.
This travel isn’t only difficult because of the distance
but also because wild animals roam freely in the area.
Regardless of the challenges,
the brothers and sisters enjoy coming together
to serve Jehovah and to share in the ministry.
This congregation is just
one of many examples of the faithful brothers and sisters
throughout Botswana
who are spreading the truth into even the most remote locations.
And they want to share their love and greetings with all of you.
We send our love to all of our brothers and sisters in Botswana
and to all of you wherever you might be.
We love you all very much.
Until next time,
this is JW Broadcasting
from the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

en.text: How can you make important points of instruction
more vivid as you teach?
Use a visual aid.
That’s what Jehovah did when speaking with Abraham
as recorded at Genesis 15:5.
Jehovah brought Abraham outside and said:
“Look up, please, to the heavens and count the stars.”
Imagine Abraham looking up to the heavens on a clear night
and seeing thousands of stars twinkling like diamonds.
Jehovah then made the point of instruction clear when he said:
“So your offspring will become.”
Abraham understood,
and he remembered Jehovah’s promise for the rest of his life.
Well, how might we use visual aids in our teaching?
We can choose pictures, diagrams, maps, time lines,
or other items to highlight
not minor details but important concepts.
And whether we’re teaching in the field ministry or in the congregation,
we need to make sure that our listeners can “see” the visual aid.
As we watch the following example,
consider whether this use of a visual aid
is appropriate or inappropriate.
Rumors are like this balloon:
full of hot air,
floating through the room.
What should we do with rumors?
Deflate them
before they travel any further.
Was that an appropriate use of a visual aid?
Oh, it’ll be remembered but for all the wrong reasons.
Our objective in using visual aids
is not to shock or entertain the audience.
Let’s give the speaker another chance to make
appropriate use of a visual aid.
Why should we spend time getting to know our brothers and sisters?
Well, we could compare them to this beautiful rock
called a geode.
If we look past the surface imperfections
and take the time to get to know our brothers and sisters,
we may come to know their beautiful inner qualities,
“the secret person of the heart.”
Simple and clear.
Our publications also use visual aids.
How can we make good use of them in the ministry?
Let’s watch a brother conducting a Bible study.
Does he make good use of the artwork?
What will life be like in the coming Paradise?
In order to visualize what we just considered in paragraphs 17-23,
notice the artwork on page 37.
Nice, right?
Let’s move on to paragraph 24.
The publisher briefly called attention to the illustration.
But he could have made better use of it.
While we don’t need to focus on minor details in a picture,
we should try to highlight key aspects of the artwork.
Let’s watch him try again.
What will life be like in the coming Paradise?
In order to visualize what we’ll consider in paragraphs 17-23,
notice the artwork on page 37.
What aspects of this scene are different from life in today’s world?
Everybody is happy.
That’s right.
The whole earth will be a paradise.
What else?
Does anyone in this scene have glasses or a cane?
No.
Sickness and death will be gone too.
What about war and violence?
What do you see in the picture?
Everybody is getting along,
even people of different races.
Exactly!
There will even be peace between humans and the animals.
But you might be thinking,
‘That’s just too good to be true.’
Well, let’s now consider the verses from the Bible
that provide the basis for this picture.
Would you please read paragraph 17?
In this case,
the publisher used the artwork to preview information to follow.
We can also use the artwork to review key points.
The important thing is for our listeners to remember the point of the visual aid.
Brothers who conduct the Watchtower Study
and the Congregation Bible Study
should make good use of the visual aids that appear in the lesson.
When we select visual aids that enhance our teaching
rather than detract from it, we’ll honor Jehovah
and make important points of instruction memorable to our audience.
