많은 원주민과 부족민들이 터를 잡고 살아가고 있습니다.
많은 부족들이 자신들의 문화와 언어를 유지해 왔습니다.
현재 미국 지부는 여러 원주민 언어들로 번역을 하고 있는데,
그 가운데는 체로키어, 호피어, 라코타어, 나바호어가 있습니다.
이 일을 위해, 2015년에 친리에 현지 번역 사무실이 지어졌는데,
친리는 나바호족이 사는 지역의 중심부에 위치해 있습니다.
이 사무실에는 13명의 전 시간 봉사자들을 포함해
이곳에서 번역된 출판물, 동영상, 오디오 출판물이
지난 5년 동안 매년 나바호어로 3일간의 지역 대회가 열렸습니다.
전 세계 여러분 모두에게 따뜻한 그리스도인 사랑을 전합니다.

en.text: Welcome to JW Broadcasting.
Here are some highlights from this month’s program.
What should we do if we encounter spiritism
in some form?
And how can we help
others break free from it?
This dramatization will provide some valuable principles.
We’ve all beheld the wonders of creation.
This month’s beautiful music video
will move us to pause,
think, and thank Jehovah
for his magnificent works.
And we go to world headquarters to visit another museum.
We’ll see how, in our time, Jehovah is
blessing “a people for his name.”
This is the August 2019 edition
of JW Broadcasting.
Our broadcast this month has the theme
“Cherish Your Privilege of Prayer.”
Do you think it’s appropriate
to label prayer as a miracle?
Miracles are described
in our New World Translation
“Glossary of Bible Terms”
as “actions or phenomena
“that surpass all powers
“known to humans and are attributed
to a supernatural agency.”
Does prayer fit that description?
The moment you say a prayer,
your innermost thoughts and feelings
are communicated instantly to the Creator
from wherever you are
—even if you pray silently.
That’s certainly beyond any power that humans know.
Therefore, the fact that a human
can call out to God in prayer
and be heard by him
is truly a miracle.
It’s only by the undeserved kindness of Jehovah
that we can approach his heavenly throne in prayer.
Today our lives are very complicated
and, in some cases, very troubled.
Whether young or old, there are times
we may feel overwhelmed with our problems.
At other times, we may simply feel alone and helpless.
What can we do?
The apostle Paul says that prayer will help.
Please open your Bible to Philippians 4:6
and listen to his spirit-inspired recommendations:
“Do not be anxious over anything,
“but in everything by prayer and supplication
“along with thanksgiving,
let your petitions be made known to God.”
So Paul is saying that in all circumstances of life,
prayer is essential.
While no one around us
can see the inner struggles we may be having,
Jehovah sees them.
What will he do?
Let’s read verse 7:
“And the peace of God that surpasses all understanding
“will guard your hearts and your mental powers
by means of Christ Jesus.”
This incomparable “peace of God”
is an unusual tranquillity
enjoyed by Jehovah’s dedicated servants,
even in the most trying circumstances.
Have you felt that inner peace
that results from intimate communication with Jehovah?
How much we benefit from prayer
is closely related to the strength
of our personal relationship with Jehovah.
A key factor in that relationship
is found at Psalm 37:3:
“Trust in Jehovah and do what is good;
reside in the earth, and act with faithfulness.”
Likely you’d agree that when we need to talk to someone about our worries,
we go to a trusted friend.
Why?
It’s because we’ve developed a relationship with him.
He knows us and our situation,
and we know we can count on him.
More than ever,
we need a close personal relationship with Jehovah.
For that to be possible, we must be convinced
that Jehovah knows who we are and that he understands us
—our situation, our worries,
our concerns, and our needs.
Notice what Jehovah promises
in verses 4 and 5:
“Find exquisite delight in Jehovah,
“and he will grant you the desires of your heart.
“Commit your way to Jehovah;
rely on him, and he will act in your behalf.”
Jehovah does know who we are.
He understands us better than anyone else,
even better than we understand ourselves.
He invites us to trust him,
and he promises to act in our behalf.
The miracle of prayer lets us experience
Jehovah’s love in a truly intimate way.
Our Father personally takes the time to listen to us;
he has not delegated that to anyone else.
However, you might be wondering,
‛Why would the Creator of the universe want to listen to me?’
The inspired answer at 1 Peter 5:7 says:
“Because he cares for you.”
Your determination to keep doing
the best you can to serve him
in spite of all the problems you face
endears you to him.
He feels for you and is eager to help.
How does that make you feel?
At Psalm 116:1, it says:
“I love Jehovah
“because he hears my voice,
my pleas for help.”
Even though we can’t see him listening to us,
it’s as if we feel
Jehovah’s loving arms around us when we pray.
As a result, the more we pray,
the more our love and trust in him grows.
What else will help us
to build our love and trust in our God, Jehovah?
It’s more than recognizing that he hears our prayers.
We must be convinced
that he answers our prayers.
What evidence do we have that Jehovah answers prayers?
Let’s look at some specific answers to prayers,
both past and present.
Open your Bible to 2 Chronicles chapter 20.
When Judah was threatened by the combined forces
of Ammon and Moab and the mountainous region of Seir,
King Jehoshaphat humbly prayed for Jehovah’s help.
In verse 12, he prayed:
“O our God, will you not execute judgment on them?
“For we are powerless
“before this large crowd that is coming against us;
“and we do not know what we should do,
but our eyes are toward you.”
What was Jehovah’s answer?
There was no voice from heaven.
Jehovah caused a prophet to speak up.
Verse 15 says:
“Here is what Jehovah says to you,
“‘Do not be afraid or be terrified because of this large crowd,
for the battle is not yours but God’s.’”
Then verse 17 continues:
“You will not need to fight this battle.
“Take your position, stand still,
and see the salvation of Jehovah in your behalf.”
Did you note the formula?
Jehovah’s dedicated servant is facing a serious problem.
He prays specifically,
and then he remains attentive to the answer.
The answer may have seemed strange to Jehoshaphat.
Jehovah didn’t provide a battle plan.
As strategies go, just walking out
to meet the enemy doesn’t sound like a very good one.
But Jehoshaphat discerned
that this was the answer from Jehovah,
and he let it direct his actions.
What happened?
Jehovah fought for Judah
by striking confusion into the ranks of the enemy
so that they slaughtered one another.
Jehoshaphat’s prayer was answered
in a mighty way.
We have examples in the first century
of collective prayers being answered.
One occasion was when King Herod
was out to gain the favor of the Jews,
so he had the apostle Peter imprisoned
and placed under heavy guard.
What would the congregation do?
Acts 12:5 gives us the answer:
“So Peter was being kept in the prison,
but the congregation was intensely praying to God for him.”
Did Jehovah answer their prayers in behalf of Peter?
The account in verses 7-11 tells us
that an angel of Jehovah led Peter out of jail
and delivered him to safety.
Imagine how these events must have drawn
the Christians in Jerusalem closer to Jehovah
when they saw that he had answered their prayers.
What about today?
Consider the example of our brothers in South Korea.
Over the years, more than 19,000 of our brothers
have been imprisoned as conscientious objectors
to military service.
Did you personally pray in behalf of these brothers
that they might endure in their faith
or that they might be released from prison
if it was Jehovah’s will?
We’re sure that you did.
In fact, many of you prayed for these brothers by name,
just as the congregation in the first century
prayed in behalf of Peter.
With what result?
In 2018, a series of court rulings in South Korea
finally recognized conscientious objection
to military service for religious reasons
as a fundamental human right,
and our brothers were gradually released
from their prison bonds.
What do you think?
Did Jehovah hear our prayers
in behalf of these dear brothers?
As a worldwide brotherhood,
there can be no doubt
that our incessant prayers to Jehovah
were a major factor in these marvelous developments,
and we praise and thank Jehovah
that he’s heard our prayers.
What does this review of how Jehovah answered the prayers
of his servants in the past and present do for us?
Doesn’t it build confidence that Jehovah
is listening to and acting on the prayers of his people?
The apostle John had that confidence.
He wrote at 1 John 5:14:
“And this is the confidence that we have toward him,
“that no matter what we ask according to his will,
he hears us.”
But now the question is:
When was the last time that Jehovah answered
one of your personal prayers?
We spend much time on learning
how to pray and what to pray for,
but do we put forth enough effort
in identifying the answers to our prayers?
For us to have the closeness to Jehovah,
we must be certain that he’s listening
and responding to our personal prayers.
It may not always be readily discernible
just how some prayers are answered.
So, what can we do?
Take time to meditate on Jehovah’s response
to your prayerful requests.
If you’re married,
freely discuss matters that you have prayed for in common
and how Jehovah may be answering those prayers.
Be observant and alert to things that are happening around you,
and learn to connect these things
with the answers to your prayers.
Make your prayers more specific,
and you’ll become more keenly aware of Jehovah’s answers
—even though they may be subtle.
Identifying your answered prayers
will make Jehovah more real to you.
This process of identifying answers to our prayers
should be learned early on in one’s spiritual development.
We cannot take it for granted that our children
or our Bible students will connect the answers
they receive to the prayers they’ve offered.
One Witness said,
“I find that people feel closer to God
“if I help them to recognize
answers to their prayers.”
What if we can’t identify
the answer to one of our prayers?
Does that mean it wasn’t according to Jehovah’s will?
Not necessarily.
There are two important factors that might be involved.
One is that Jehovah knows
the best time and way
to answer our prayers.
He takes all matters into consideration.
The answer may not come
according to our timetable, but it will come.
So we must be patient
and keep looking for the answer.
The second factor that Jehovah considers
is the issue raised by Satan
regarding man’s integrity.
Listen again to the challenge Satan makes
as recorded at Job 1:10, 11:
“Have you not put up a protective hedge
“around him and his house and everything he has?
“You have blessed the work of his hands,
“and his livestock has spread out in the land.
“But, for a change, stretch out your hand
“and strike everything he has,
and he will surely curse you to your very face.”
Jehovah permitted this issue
to be raised out of love for his intelligent creatures.
He permitted Job to undergo a test
by Satan before the entire universe.
Jehovah gives his creatures the privilege
of proving the Devil a liar and of removing the slander
not only from God’s name
but also from their own.
So Jehovah, seeing the entire issue,
may allow his servants to endure trials.
But that doesn’t mean
he’s not answering the prayer of the afflicted.
When we are under trial, we may have prayed for relief,
but we may have also prayed:
“Let your name be sanctified.”
We must remain convinced that Jehovah
will not simply answer a prayer;
he will provide the best answer.
Isn’t it true that when we maintain our integrity,
even through serious illness,
it can be a tremendous witness to others?
That was the case with Jerod Septer.
God’s Word says:
“Remember, then, your Grand Creator
“in the days of your youth,
before the days of distress come.”
And “the days of distress”
—they arrived early on Jerod at 11.
Jerod was diagnosed with lymphoma cancer in the middle of 1991.
We started trying to figure out how we could get him
the treatment that he needed, of course, but in no way would we accept
a blood transfusion, and neither would Jerod.
When Jerod was in the hospital, Child Protective Services
did investigate us.
They were concerned there was negligence.
It was just adding to the pain.
The way it turned out, they backed completely away from that.
They realized that we hadn’t been negligent.
So as we faced different situations, we’d pray at the time,
not to have miraculous answers,
but for Jehovah to open our eyes and to be able to find things.
And it seemed as though he was really directing us,
so that we could take care of ourselves spiritually
through this situation as well as take care of Jerod’s medical needs.
I remember
many times falling on my knees
and praying and thinking: ‘This is it.
I’m tested beyond what I can bear.’
And Jehovah would strengthen me.
And someone would come,
or they would say something.
And they fed us.
The brother made a schedule, and he said,
“You’re going to feed these friends.”
And the brother’s instructions were:
“You don’t bring it and just drop off the food.
You stay with those friends.”
It made me cry
—the love and the care that we experienced.
One time, I remember
the hallways of this hospital
—1,500 miles (2,400 km) away from our home—
started filling up with people.
To me, that was answering prayers too.
It was hard for us to get out of the hospital,
so they recorded talks.
They would look us in the eye, and they’d say:
“Now, you need to listen to this.
It will keep you strong.”
Jerod was worried about us, and he made it clear
that he was going to be fine.
He just didn’t know if we were going to be.
He died
in June of 1992.
He was at home.
And the last thing he said to us was,
“Work hard so we can all be together again.”
It’s numbing
because it’s almost like you’re living a nightmare
because you never think that those things will happen to you,
but it did.
I didn’t want people to see me cry.
I didn’t want pity, and I didn’t—
Because of that
—those negative feelings— my imagination ran wild.
What helped me, I know,
was Gary putting into my heart and mind
that this is a fight.
It’s been a challenge for all mankind.
‘If you make it hard on them, they won’t love you’
—Satan said that about Jehovah and individuals.
So I would be giving in to that.
The strong feelings I had
and my sorrow almost made me stop.
I prayed a lot to go back to the Kingdom Hall.
The congregation cried; they lost a little boy.
It wasn’t just Gary and Beth.
They lost a little boy.
They cried,
and I didn’t feel alone.
And then we hugged; we cried together.
It really benefited us to get right back
into spiritual focus and to get our minds off ourselves.
And I could’ve given in to my pain and thought,
‘Well, I’m too heartbroken.’
It made me have more joy
because I realized that now they have a hope.
People around us were vital
—the support system Jehovah has—
and his Word, his spirit.
Jehovah answered those prayers.
Our goal was really to stay
in the full-time ministry (maybe doing something else),
but we never, ever thought we would be in the circuit work.
But to have our daughter working with her husband in the circuit work
—it’s almost hard to believe that it’s happening.
We look forward to seeing Jerod again, having him back with us.
So I’m waiting, and I know I’m not going to be disappointed.
How encouraging to know that Gary and Beth
are able to take vacation time to travel occasionally
to see their daughter and her husband,
who are also serving in the traveling work.
And did you notice how Gary, Beth, and Jerod
felt Jehovah’s loving support as they prayed
throughout this heart-wrenching trial?
They asked for wisdom
when seeking medical treatment for Jerod.
Jehovah put his arms around them and listened
when they felt overwhelmed with grief and negative feelings.
He strengthened Jerod’s hope in the resurrection
and helped Brother and Sister Septer
stay spiritually strong.
Can there be any doubt
that Jehovah was answering their prayers?
Doesn’t that strengthen our conviction
that Jehovah will also answer Jerod’s prayer
that they all will be together again?
No, Jehovah didn’t miraculously cure Jerod.
But through his endurance and strong faith,
Jerod gave a witness to the universe
that even a child that trusts in Jehovah
can prove his loyalty to death.
Now, other situations
may turn out differently and not end up in death.
If an individual feels that relief
was because of Jehovah’s intervention,
he should certainly give thanks.
However, we must recognize that Jehovah knows
the best way to handle matters
so that it results in honor to his name
and to the lasting good of his servants.
Finally, it’s worth mentioning that the Bible
often connects our remaining spiritually alert
with our need to pray.
At Matthew 26:41,
Jesus said:
“Keep on the watch and pray continually.”
At 1 Peter 4:7,
Peter wrote:
“But the end of all things has drawn close.
“Therefore, be sound in mind,
and be vigilant with a view to prayers.”
Indeed, our prayers are so important.
Our personal prayers will help us
to remain spiritually alert and active in God’s service
as we await the great tribulation
that lies just ahead of us.
So in summary, our prayers to Jehovah
reveal the closeness of our relationship with him
and the degree of our dependence upon him.
They show the trueness of our faith,
the depth of our devotion,
and the genuineness of our appreciation.
Our prayers also help us to remain spiritually alert
as we endure these last days
before the great tribulation.
We’ll be drawn even closer to Jehovah
when we learn to recognize his answers to our prayers.
Yes, we can be assured that Jehovah
will not fail in giving us the desires of our heart
as we continue rendering him sacred service.
May we all cherish our marvelous,
miraculous privilege of prayer.
Let’s look at one practical example
of when prayer is of utmost importance
—when confronted with the powers of wicked spirits.
Spiritism is very real and dangerous.
Yet, with Jehovah’s help,
people can break free from its hold.
In this dramatization,
notice how one sister helped her Bible student to do that.
Emma and I were so worried
about her Bible study, Palesa.
She had spent another sleepless night
after again hearing her dead grandmother’s voice,
plus the sound of slamming doors and items crashing in the house.
Palesa had put an amulet on her baby’s wrist for protection,
but the terror continued all night long.
Of course, it wasn’t really her grandmother,
and nothing in the house was broken;
but the attack was real.
Stories about the spirit world weren’t new to me.
Our neighbors, the people I work with,
the people in our territory
—almost everyone believes in spirits, whether they admit it or not.
No—more than believe—they fear them!
I had only been studying the Bible about six months longer than Palesa.
But my study had proved to me that wicked spirits are here on earth,
that they try to interact with people,
and that they are dangerous enemies.
Emma called the elders for help.
She didn’t want us to handle the situation on our own.
As Emma told the story,
I had to speak up and tell the elders that she was leaving things out.
But I was surprised when the elders said they didn’t need all the details.
They explained that while we are aware of the danger the demons pose,
we do not spend time talking about their activities.
Even Jesus, when he was on earth,
could have told his disciples many stories
about the doings of wicked spirits,
but instead, he focused on Jehovah and His activities.
We should do the same
instead of telling stories about what the demons
may or may not have done.
The elders skillfully used the Bible, shepherding everyone.
We read Ephesians 6:11:
“Put on the complete suit of armor from God
“so that you may be able to stand firm
against the crafty acts of the Devil.”
Those instructions were so important.
A soldier would be vulnerable if he only wore part of his armor
or if he didn’t keep it in good repair.
Then we read Ephesians 4:27:
“Do not give the Devil an opportunity.”
The elders explained to Palesa
that the string around her daughter’s wrist
is not part of the armor from God.
Instead, it is giving Satan an opportunity to continue to harass the family.
The brothers reminded us that anyone who wants Jehovah’s protection
must completely break free
from anything associated with superstition,
spiritism, and demon worship.
Who would ever choose to side with wicked spirits instead of with Jehovah?
Emma reminded Palesa of how urgent the situation was.
But only Palesa could decide what she would do.
I want to be a loyal servant of Jehovah.
That’s why I’m getting baptized.
I’ve decided not to listen to or tell
any more stories about the demons.
But more than that,
I need to look at other parts of my life.
Am I doing anything that would “give the Devil an opportunity”?
Clearly, there are still changes I need to make.
Did you notice how they prayed
for Jehovah’s direction?
They followed the principle of Psalm 37:5:
“Commit your way to Jehovah;
rely on him, and he will act in your behalf.”
And as you noticed,
as he’s committing his life course to Jehovah,
Thomas’ Christian conscience has now started to guide him.
And he likely realizes
that he has to safeguard his heart from things that may tempt him.
In this Bethel Morning Worship,
Brother Morris of the Governing Body helps us to see why it requires
effort to protect our relationship with Jehovah.
This morning, I thought we’d talk about accepting
the facts about our figurative heart
and how that safeguards
our relationship with Jehovah.
Let’s read the day’s text
in its entirety
in Jeremiah chapter 17.
And what a sobering inspired thought
from our heavenly Father!
Jeremiah chapter 17
and we’ll read verse 9:
“The heart is more treacherous
than anything else and is desperate.”
So there we have it.
That’s the truth.
That’s what Jehovah makes very clear to us
—that each and every one of us has to deal with a treacherous,
or deceitful, figurative heart.
And how encompassing
the expression here
“more treacherous than anything else.”
And what complicates it even more is that it’s desperate.
It always wants its way
—so a lot to meditate on.
And now, Jehovah put it here for the very reason
that we have to accept this fact.
And to safeguard our relationship with him,
we have to accept that this is the case.
And you could be a fine Christian for many years
—mature, nice outlook, nice attitude.
But if you ever find yourself forgetting Jehovah’s estimation
of what we have within us, in our figurative heart,
then we’re in danger because the Devil will always exploit
the fact that our imperfect figurative hearts
are treacherous and deceitful
more than anything else and are desperate.
So accept that fact.
It’s not that we want to dwell on it, and you start feeling,
‘Well, what a miserable person I am!’
Even though that is something the apostle Paul acknowledged,
it’s just accepting the fact.
And then we’re cautious about allowing
the treacherous heart to lead us astray.
Now, perhaps you haven’t thought about this in a while,
but notice what Jesus said
—a fundamental truth for all of us—
here in Matthew chapter 6
and what we sometimes refer to as the model prayer.
Matthew chapter 6
(and a lot of spiritual food for thought,
of course, anything Jesus said is spiritual food for thought)
and verse 13 of Matthew chapter 6:
“And do not bring us into temptation,
but deliver us from the wicked one.”
So it’s been there for all these years.
We could personally reflect on,
‘When was the last time we mentioned that in a prayer to our Father, Jehovah:
‘“Do not bring us into temptation
but deliver us from the wicked one,” or “rescue us from the wicked one”?’
What are we really saying there?
Well, we’re asking our heavenly Father to guide and help us
so that we’re not “overreached by Satan” —very simple.
But the closer we get to the end,
make no mistake, it’s even more urgent
to keep in mind the need to beg Jehovah not to bring us into temptation
and to guide us so that we’ll be delivered
from this wicked one who wants to exploit the fact that we have
a treacherous, traitorous figurative heart
that can ruin our relationship with Jehovah personally.
Now, the apostle Paul recognized this,
and it’s quite interesting what he wrote
to his beloved brothers in Thessalonians, that first letter.
So if you’d find 1 Thessalonians,
in chapter 3,
I found this quite revealing.
And tying in with the thought
of accepting the facts about how our figurative heart
safeguards our relationship with our God and Father, Jehovah,
at 1 Thessalonians 3:5,
Paul writes: “That is why, when I could bear it no longer,
“I sent to learn of your faithfulness,
“[now notice] in case somehow
“the Tempter might have tempted you,
and our labor might have turned out to be in vain.”
So he didn’t get into any specific detail.
But it helps us to appreciate that there’s this danger that somehow
the Tempter, Satan the Devil, might tempt us,
and this is connected with the need to beg
Jehovah to deliver us, or rescue us, from the wicked one
in his effort to tempt us to break our integrity
and have our cherished relationship with Jehovah be damaged.
So he knows the heart is treacherous.
And whoever we are and however long we’ve been in the truth,
remember what Paul wrote to the Thessalonians
—“somehow”— because he’s always looking
to somehow lead us
into breaking our integrity to Jehovah God.
Now, if you think of Revelation chapter 12
and where we are in this stream of time,
(this occurred to me when preparing these thoughts here)
Revelation chapter 12 has very familiar thoughts here.
The Devil is expelled from the heavens,
he and the demons, and notice
the familiar verse 12 of Revelation chapter 12:
‘On this account be glad, you heavens
and [boy, they’re rejoicing] those that reside in them!’
And that’s an exclamation.
Notice, though: “Woe for the earth and for the sea,
“because the Devil has come down to you, having great anger,
knowing that he has a short period of time.”
Well, if that was true after he was ousted from the heavens,
what do you think about now?
So it’s sobering.
We want to safeguard our relationship with Jehovah
because notice verse 17 of the same chapter:
“So the dragon became enraged.”
Great anger—he’s enraged,
and he’s waging war with the remnant, as it brings out here.
And those that observe the commandments of God
—anyone supporting the remnant— this is a war.
And the war is that he’s out to somehow
cause us to break our integrity to our precious
heavenly Father, so this helps us to appreciate that,
even though it was long before
the thoughts here in Revelation and what Jesus taught us.
In Proverbs chapter 4, it still helps us:
“More than all else that is to be guarded, safeguard your heart,
for out of it are the sources of life.”
So even back then, there was the recognition
that we have to safeguard our heart and accept the fact that our heart,
our figurative heart, is treacherous
—that’ll safeguard our precious relationship with Jehovah God.
Now, to help us with that, notice what Paul wrote
—very familiar verses in 2 Timothy chapter 3.
And we’ve used this in the ministry many times,
and yet think about it as it connects
with safeguarding our hearts
and accepting the fact that it’s treacherous
—that we won’t break our integrity
or allow the Devil to somehow cause us to break our integrity.
Second Timothy chapter 3 and you’ll notice what we’re emphasizing here.
The fact is in verse 16: “All Scripture is inspired of God.”
But notice the benefits.
So it’s “for teaching,” it’s “for reproving,” “setting things straight”
—see the point here, though?—
“for disciplining in righteousness.”
So you think of that maybe on your Bible study.
‘I use the Bible to discipline my Bible study to get God’s thinking.’
And it’s appropriate that elders use the Scriptures to discipline.
However, we want to emphasize here for you
that when you’re doing your personal Bible reading (many of us),
let the Scriptures discipline that treacherous heart.
It’s a mirror.
When something hits you because maybe you’ve had wrong thinking
(could be all sorts of things, anything that could lead us astray
and cause us to break our integrity), just face the fact.
It’s just between you and Jehovah.
You’re reading it, and let it discipline you in righteousness.
And that’s what’s going to enable us to protect
our precious relationship with Jehovah God.
So we all have to face that fact, as we mentioned,
our figurative heart is treacherous; it’s a traitor.
What’s wonderful is we’re confident that Jehovah loves us.
So when he made that estimation in Jeremiah,
it’s motivated by his love.
So that helps us to protect our relationship with him
—facing that fact.
That’s the way it is.
So indeed, we accept the fact about our figurative heart,
but we’re determined to protect and safeguard
our precious relationship with Jehovah God.
Yes, praying for Jehovah’s help
is an important tool in safeguarding our heart.
And having a desire to protect our relationship with Jehovah
is closely linked to how much we appreciate what he’s done for us.
Our appreciation moves us to action
and strengthens our faith in him.
Such appreciation is highlighted in this month’s
music video which is entitled Thankful.
Dandelions growing on top of the hill,
Mountains in the distance, wind blowing through the field,
Warmth of the sun casting down from the sky,
Birds fly up above, Clouds rolling by—
What did I do To see such beauty?
And what do I do To show how much I care?
I’ve got to be thankful, Tell Jehovah in prayer
That I’m thankful For the love that he shares.
Stop, look around,
Take a moment, and let it sink down in my heart.
Never take for granted all he’s done.
I’ve got to be thankful. I’ve got to be thankful.
So many colors now painted in the sky,
What a beautiful canvas you’ve laid before my eyes!
The sound of the river running into the night,
The stars are dancing in the moon’s spotlight—
What did I do To see such beauty?
But I know what to do To show how much I care.
I’ve got to be thankful, Tell Jehovah in prayer
That I’m thankful For the love that he shares.
Stop, look around,
Take a moment, and let it sink down in my heart.
Never take for granted all he’s done.
I’ve got to be thankful.
I see your wisdom and your strength,
Your goodness in ev’rything, And how much you love.
And I’m so thankful; I’ve got to be thankful.
I’ve got to be thankful, Tell Jehovah in prayer
That I’m thankful For the love that he shares.
Stop, look around,
Take a moment, and let it sink down in my heart.
Never take for granted all he’s done.
I’ve got to be thankful. I’ve got to be thankful.
We’ve got to be thankful.
Did you notice one way of expressing our gratitude to Jehovah?
Yes, by means of prayer.
Having that channel to the Sovereign of the universe
is a benefit of being his people.
And speaking of being Jehovah’s people,
in last month’s program,
we had an opportunity to visit one of the museums
at world headquarters in Warwick, New York.
But there’s more to see.
Let’s join Brother John Ekrann, a helper to the Coordinators’ Committee,
on another visit, and this time,
we’ll stop by a museum called “A People for Jehovah’s Name.”
Do you enjoy a good story?
If so, you’re in for a special treat.
“A People for Jehovah’s Name”
at world headquarters in Warwick is more than a history museum.
It’s the modern-day story of a people seeking to know the true God
and to do his will.
But this isn’t just any story
—it’s our story.
So let’s take a thrilling journey back in time.
The story unfolds on the narrative wall
and in several galleries along the way.
We begin in the 1870’s,
when a small group in Allegheny, Pennsylvania,
decided to reexamine the Bible.
As C. T. Russell reasoned:
All the creeds of Christendom
claim to be founded on the Bible;
and these are conflicting.
Is it possible that the Bible has been misrepresented?
The more they learned, the more they wanted to share.
So in 1879,
they began publishing Zion’s Watch Tower.
Readers were soon taking a stand for the truths that they were learning.
Listen.
What I want to tell you is this,
I am free!
The truth has made me free!
To-day I was excluded from the Baptist church . . .
So I am all alone in the ‘flesh,’ but not in the ‘spirit.’
They became known as the Bible Students,
and they soon realized that people everywhere should hear the good news.
But how could this small group preach the Bible’s message earthwide?
Transcontinental and international tours
helped them to see how they could expand
their preaching work even further.
In just one tour
beginning in December 1911,
C. T. Russell and his associates
traveled completely around the world.
Let’s imagine what it was like to live in those exciting times.
In this gallery, you can experience what life was like
for a pilgrim, or what we today call a circuit overseer.
Here’s a pilgrim’s formal jacket that he’d wear when giving a public talk.
The Bible Students offered the Studies in the Scriptures series in the ministry.
And they carried lists to locate
and visit Watch Tower subscribers.
Then in 1914,
they presented the exciting “Photo-Drama of Creation.”
Its purpose was to build faith in the Bible
as God’s inspired Word.
It was an innovative combination
of moving pictures,
sound recordings,
and beautiful, hand-colored glass slides.
Hundreds of people reenacted Bible scenes,
some with live animals!
Was this enormous work worth all the effort?
DEAR BROTHER RUSSELL, I want to thank you;
oh, . . . so much, for the privilege
of seeing the PHOTO-DRAMA OF CREATION!
I had never thought to live to see
the everlasting Gospel preached to those who dwell on the earth . . . !
Yet so it is.
Words cannot tell you how my heart rejoices!
—Your sister, F. E. Riley.
By the end of 1914, over nine million had viewed it.
But with such success,
the Bible Students didn’t realize what tests lay ahead.
The Gentile Times have ended;
their kings have had their day!
So we know not what awaits us.
World War I broke out in 1914.
Then in 1916,
the death of C. T. Russell left the Bible Students in shock.
It was a unique time of testing.
Inside the organization,
some struggled over who should take the lead.
Outside,
governments tried to force them to take sides in the war.
Then in 1918,
J. F. Rutherford and seven of his close associates
were imprisoned.
Was this the end for the Bible Students?
Or would they prove to be
a people for Jehovah’s name?
The joy that came with the release of our brothers
from the Atlanta Federal Prison on Tuesday,
March 25, 1919, knew no bounds.
Their further devotion to Jehovah was shown in the fact
that they immediately set to work to herald
forth to the people of God everywhere
the knowledge of Jehovah’s deliverance.
—Thomas Sullivan.
The Bible Students moved forward with renewed zeal.
But the opposition didn’t end there.
In this gallery, you will see how our brothers and sisters
have stood firm for their faith.
In Russia, a father imprisoned for ten years
encouraged his young daughters
with hand-drawn postcards.
In Greece,
a son used the same blanket in prison
that his father used when imprisoned before him.
It was an encouraging reminder of his father’s integrity.
In Korea,
Witnesses were locked in tiny cells
for up to 30 days at a time.
When you stand in the lighted outline, you get a sense of what it was like.
All of these brothers and sisters looked beyond the prison bars
to their firm hope for the future.
As light from God’s Word increased,
the Bible Students humbly let go
of cherished but unscriptural traditions.
Songs used in worship were examined in the light of what the Bible taught.
The people for Jehovah’s name were becoming even more evident.
So in 1931,
they were thrilled to take on their new name
—Jehovah’s Witnesses.
Then in 1935,
Brother Rutherford identified the great multitude of other sheep,
who served alongside the anointed.
At the climax of his talk, he asked:
Will all those who have the hope of living forever on the earth please stand?
With this new understanding,
they saw the true scope of Jesus’ commission to make disciples.
New and innovative methods were needed.
Our third gallery shows the preaching methods used in the 1930’s and 1940’s.
Radio was a powerful way to spread the Kingdom message
to large audiences.
They also used large phonographs,
called portable transcription machines,
with loudspeakers mounted on sound cars.
Brothers played recorded talks wherever people gathered.
Lighter phonographs were also designed and produced so publishers
could take the recorded message directly to people at home.
These methods helped bring unity to the message,
but the time had come to train each one
of Jehovah’s people to be an effective Witness.
Schools were started.
The Course in Theocratic Ministry
trained publishers in the congregation.
And the Bible School of Gilead
began training missionaries for global expansion.
We had entered into a new era of divine education.
And we were about to receive an amazing tool.
we received the New World Translation of the Christian Greek Scriptures.
And by 1961, the complete Bible was released.
Since then, we’ve seen our tools continue to improve
with the wise use of modern technology.
From high-speed printing to the Internet and video,
these methods help us to stay unified,
to reach millions with the good news,
and to glorify God.
Yes, this museum’s story is about people,
but not just any people.
We are “a people for Jehovah’s name.”
Only one question remains:
What will you contribute to this wonderful story?
This month, after discussing the theme
“Cherish Your Privilege of Prayer,”
we saw how we should act
when we encounter spiritism.
When counteracting wicked spirits,
praying for Jehovah’s guidance is very important.
Next, Brother Morris showed us the importance of praying
to protect our heart.
And the music video
reminded us of not forgetting to thank Jehovah
for everything he’s given us.
The provision of communicating with Jehovah
is a privilege we have of being his people.
A visit to Warwick Bethel showed us how Jehovah
has guided his people in modern times.
Before we conclude,
we’ll visit the remote translation office
in Chinle, Arizona, in the United States.
Located in the southwestern part of the country,
the region is home
to many native peoples and tribes.
European settlers arrived in the 1500’s.
Throughout the many years since then,
many of the tribes were able
to retain their culture and language.
Currently, the United States branch translates
into several indigenous languages, including
Cherokee, Hopi, Lakota, and Navajo.
To help with that work,
in 2015, a remote translation office, or RTO,
was built in Chinle,
which is in the heart of the Navajo nation.
Over 100 volunteers,
of which 13 are full-time servants,
work at the RTO.
The Navajo field has over 430 publishers,
including approximately 130 regular pioneers
and some 20 special pioneers.
The literature, videos,
and audio publications translated
at the RTO
are distributed to 8 Navajo congregations,
11 groups, and 5 pregroups.
For the past five years, three-day regional conventions
have been held in the Navajo language.
In 2018, they had a peak attendance of 471,
with one baptized.
The volunteers at the RTO in Chinle
send their warm Christian love to all of us around the world.
And we love them dearly.
This is JW Broadcasting
from the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

不断留意他会怎样回应我们
耶和华考虑的第二个因素
与撒但的质疑有关
撒但质疑人崇拜上帝是出于自私的动机
我们一起看看撒但怎样质疑人类的动机
耶和华允许撒但提出这个质疑
因为他深爱人类
耶和华允许撒但在宇宙众生面前考验约伯

耶和华有时允许他的仆人经历考验

但这并不是说
上帝不会垂听那些身受患难的人所做的祷告
我们身受患难的时候
也许曾祷告求上帝减轻我们的痛苦

“愿你的名彰显为圣”
我们必须确信
耶和华不但会回应我们的祷告
也会以最好的方式回应我们
我们对上帝保持忠贞
即使有严重的疾病
仍然可以向别人作美好的见证
在这方面
杰罗德·塞普特立下了很好的榜样
圣经说

这个日子却提早来了

为了给孩子治病
我们尝试了各种方法

杰罗德也不接受
在治疗过程中
儿童保护组织来调查我们

这就好像是在我们的伤口上撒盐！
不过最后他们停止了调查
因为他们发现我们是很好的父母
在那段艰难的时期
我们不断恳求耶和华
我们没有求他施行奇迹
只是求他给我们智慧
让我们作出明智的决定
耶和华的确给我们智慧
也帮助我们作出明智的决定
所以在尽力照顾孩子的同时
我们也能继续亲近耶和华、崇拜他
记得有好多次，我跪下来跟耶和华说

ko.text: 여호와께서 자신의 백성을 가르치시는 주된 수단은
집회나 크고 작은 대회와 같은 그리스도인 모임입니다.
베델 성원들에게는 아침 숭배와 월요일 저녁 프로그램도 있습니다.
일깨워 주는 성구를 하나만 고르라고 한다면
“서로 생각해 주어 사랑과 훌륭한 일을 고무하며,
일부 사람들의 습관처럼 함께 모이는 일을 그만두지 마십시오.”
이 성구가 고리타분하고 진부한 얘기로 들릴 겁니다.
하도 많이 접하다 보니 이 권고가 크게 와닿지 않을 수 있죠.
여호와께서 가르치고 의의 길로 인도하시는 모임에
반드시 참석해야겠다는 매우 강력한 동기가 생길 수 있습니다.
아직 집회에 참석하지 않고 있는 성서 연구생이나
집회를 자주 빠지는 무활동자에게 알려 줄 수 있습니다.
먼저 히브리서의 배경을 좀 생각해 보겠습니다.
바울은 이 편지를 유대교에서 개종한 그리스도인들에게 썼는데,
그리스도인 숭배 방식이 그들이 한때 따르던 유대교 방식보다
더 우월하단 점을 일깨우기 위해 쓴 것입니다.
함께 성경을 펴서 히브리서 1장의 소개말을 한두 구절 읽어 보겠습니다.
여러 경우에 여러 방법으로 우리의 조상들에게 말씀하셨습니다.
그러나 지금 이 시대의 끝에 와서는
하느님께서는 그를 모든 것의 상속자로 삼으셨으며.”
그런 다음에 바울은 모세 율법과 그리스도교의 여러 부분을 대조합니다.
계약, 중개자, 숭배의 천막, 제사직, 희생, 피 등을요.
그러면서 그리스도의 제자로 하느님을 숭배하는 것이
모든 면에서 훨씬 낫다는 걸 알려 줍니다.
사실 바울은 숭배를 위한 유대 제도의 여러 특징이
앞으로 있을 휠씬 더 큰 것을 가리키는
율법을 성취시키실 때 있을 일의 모형인 것이죠.
바울은 특히 예수께서 하늘의 대제사장으로서 수행하는
예수의 제사직이 레위 지파를 통한 제사직보다
훨씬 더 우월하다는 점을 보여 주었죠.
예수의 제사직은 아론에게 물려받은 것이 아닙니다.
우릴 위해 인간 제사장은 절대 할 수 없는 일을 하실 수 있습니다.
그에 대해 공개적으로 선언하는 일을 굳게 잡읍시다.
우리의 대제사장은 우리의 약함을 동정하지 못하는 분이 아닙니다.
그는 우리와 마찬가지로 모든 면에서 시험을 받으셨지만
그러므로 말의 자유를 가지고 과분한 친절의 왕좌로 나아갑시다.
그리하여 자비를 얻고 과분한 친절을 받아,
피와 살을 가진 인간으로 온갖 박해를 겪으셨기 때문에
우리의 약함을 동정하고 도와주실 수 있습니다.
우린 제때에, 개인적으로 가장 필요할 때,
예수께서 자비와 친절을 보이실 것을 확신할 수 있습니다.
“따라서 그는 자기를 통해 하느님께 가까이 가는 사람들을
그는 하늘에 계신 ‘존엄하신 분’의 왕좌 오른편에 앉아 계시며.”
아담의 자손으로 죄를 갖고 태어난 우린
그분의 귀에 대고 우릴 위해 중재하고
우리에게 자비를 베풀어 주실 것을 탄원할 수 있습니다.
“그리스도께서는 실체의 모형인 사람의 손으로 만든 거룩한 곳이 아니라
지금은 우리를 위해 하느님 앞에 나타나 계십니다.”
자기 자신의 피를 가지고 단 한 번 거룩한 곳에 들어가
살아 계신 하느님께 신성한 봉사를 드릴 수 있게’ 하신다고 말합니다.
예수의 희생은 아론계 제사장이 바치던 희생과는 달리
그분의 희생이 실제로 우리의 죄를 없애 주기 때문입니다.
우린 참으로 용서받고 양심이 깨끗해지게 되죠.
그에 더해 바울은 이 대제사장이 하늘 자체에 들어가
우리를 위해 하느님 앞에 나타나셨다고 말합니다.
네, 제사장께서 우릴 위해 하시는 모든 일을 생각해 보십시오.
예수께선 우리의 약함을 동정하시고 우릴 위해 하느님께 탄원하시죠.
우린 제때에 필요한 도움과 자비를 얻습니다.
또 우린 현재 깨끗한 양심을 누리며 결국 영원한 구출을 얻을 겁니다.
우리의 대제사장께서 하시는 모든 일에 대해
거룩한 곳에 들어가는 길로 나아갈 담대함을 가지고 있습니다.
그가 휘장 곧 자신의 육체를 통과하여,
생명으로 인도하는 새로운 길을 우리에게 열어 주신 것입니다.
그리고 우리에게는 하느님의 집을 맡은 위대한 제사장이 계십니다.
“그러므로 진실한 마음과 온전한 믿음을 가지고 하느님께 나아갑시다.
우리의 마음은 피가 뿌려져서 악한 양심에서 벗어나 깨끗해졌고
따라서 우린 예수의 이름에 대한 굳은 믿음을 가지고
겸손히 여호와께 우리의 죄를 용서해 달라고 기도해야 합니다.
이게 바로 여호와께서 해 주신 마련이죠.
우리의 희망을 공개적으로 선언하는 일을 흔들림 없이 굳게 잡읍시다.”
흔들림 없이 이 구원의 수단에 대한 우리의 희망을 선포하는 것입니다.
또한 전파 활동에서 사람들에게 진리를 가르침으로
“그리고 서로 생각해 주어 사랑과 훌륭한 일을 고무하며,
일부 사람들의 습관처럼 함께 모이는 일을 그만두지 말고,
그날이 다가오는 것을 볼수록 더욱더 그렇게 합시다.”
네, 우리는 그리스도인 집회와 크고 작은 대회, 아침 숭배,
월요일 저녁 프로그램 같은 모임에 참석합니다.
우리의 대제사장의 봉사에 감사를 나타내는 방법이죠.
따라서 하느님의 영이 머무는 모임에 참석하려고
또 우린 여호와께서 우릴 위한 예수의 탄원을 들어주시길 바라죠.
따라서 예수께서 회중과 “충실하고 슬기로운 종”을 통해
베푸시는 지침을 들을 수 있는 모임에 참석하려고

不要放弃聚会，别像有些人常常缺席”
对常常错过聚会的人来说
经文可能有点老生常谈
因为听了太多遍
就失去了应有的提醒作用
但如果我们仔细沉思这段经文的上下文
就肯定能激励我们参加聚会
我们参加聚会，就能受耶和华教导
让他带领我们走在正直的路途上
就像今天的经文，大卫说的一样
接下来我要谈的事
你们可以跟还没有参加聚会的圣经学生
或是经常错过聚会的弟兄姐妹分享
希伯来书是保罗写给那些原本属于犹太教
后来成为基督徒的弟兄姐妹
写作的目的是要帮助他们清楚看出
按照基督的教导崇拜上帝
远比过去他们按照
犹太教的传统崇拜上帝优越得多
请翻开你的圣经到希伯来书的第一章
让我们读读开头的几节经文
保罗说

多次通过先知对我们的祖先说话

保罗接着比较了摩西法典
和基督法律的一些特色
誓约、居间人
圣幕、祭司
献祭的安排和祭物的血
他的说明显示
从任何角度来看
基督徒崇拜上帝的方式都优越得多
事实上，保罗指出
犹太教的崇拜方式只是个象征和影子
指向未来要发生的更伟大的事
也就是基督献上自己的生命作为祭物
保罗特别强调，身为天上的大祭司
耶稣所做的
远比利未部族的祭司所做的更加优越
根据家谱，耶稣不是亚伦的后代
因此耶稣的祭司职分并不是根据血统
耶稣是上帝直接任命的大祭司
不像以色列的祭司
耶稣会永远做大祭司
因为他不会死，不需要有人接替他
耶稣作为大祭司
他为我们做的事
地上没有任何人做得到
例如，让我们看看希伯来书4:14
保罗说
“我们有一位伟大的、穿越了高天的大祭司
他就是上帝的儿子耶稣
既然如此，我们就该坚定不移地宣扬他
我们这位大祭司能够体恤我们的软弱
因为他在各方面都受过考验，像我们一样
只是他没有犯罪
所以我们应该到施恩的宝座前
放心向上帝倾诉
这样，我们正需要帮助的时候

耶稣被委任成为大祭司
是再恰当不过的事
因为他曾经来到地上成为血肉之躯
经历各种迫害
所以他能体恤我们的软弱
同情我们的遭遇
正如保罗说

让我们继续看7:25，保罗说

“这里所谈的重点是

保罗为什么说这里谈的是重点呢？
我们都是亚当的后代，生来就有罪
真的需要这位能体恤我们的大祭司
另外，耶稣坐在上帝的右边

而耶稣也会向上帝替我们说情
为我们求恩
现在让我们读9:24

“他不是带着山羊和牛犊的血

14节的后半部分提到
耶稣也能“使我们良心清白
摆脱死的行为

亚伦家族的祭司必须重复献上祭物
但耶稣只一次献上自己的生命作为祭物
就已经除去我们的罪了
耶和华已经宽恕了我们
使我们的良心变得清白
而这是摩西法典永远做不到的事
想象一下
这位大祭司来到上帝面前时
会做什么呢？
这位大祭司体恤我们的弱点
为我们向上帝求恩
在我们最需要的时候
上帝就会怜悯、帮助我们
现在我们享有清白的良心
而且最终能得到拯救

我们从10:19开始读
“弟兄们，我们凭着耶稣的血

经文接着就提到我们首先可以做的事
在第22节
“我们应该诚心诚意

祷告

怀着坚定的信心向上帝祷告
谦卑地求上帝宽恕我们的罪
我们要做的第二件事在23节
“要坚定不移地宣讲我们的希望

“坚定不移地宣讲我们的希望”呢？
就是在聚会时衷心地发表评论
另外，教导别人圣经真理

第三件事，10:24说
“要互相关心
以求激发爱心，促进善行

就更要这样做。”
经文鼓励我们要参加聚会、大会
以及为伯特利成员准备的各种聚会
我们这样做，就是感激大祭司耶稣了
我们的确需要耶稣为我们求恩
我们必须参加聚会
因为上帝的神圣力量
会在这些场合发挥作用
我们需要，也希望上帝会仔细留意
耶稣为我们向上帝祈求的恩典
我们要尽力参加聚会
这样我们就可以接受耶稣通过会众
和忠信睿智的奴隶给我们的教导了

ko.text: 사도 바울은 이 편지를 로마에서 기원 65년경에 기록했습니다.
바울은 로마에서 두 번째로 투옥되어 있었습니다.
첫 번째로 투옥되었을 때는 가택 연금을 당했습니다.
하지만 이번에는 상황이 매우 좋지 않았습니다.
바울은 쇠사슬에 매여 있었고 죽음이 임박한 상황이었습니다.
바울이 디모데에게 이 애정 어린 편지를 쓴 것은
계속 하느님의 승인을 받기 위해 최선을 다하고,
바울은 편지 서두에서 디모데를 따뜻하게 격려합니다.
그때 디모데는 아직 에베소에 있었을 것입니다.
바울은 아시아에 있는 일부 형제들이 자신을 떠났다고 말합니다.
하지만 그는 오네시보로가 용기 있게 자신을 찾았으며
바울이 디모데에게 쓴 두 번째 편지는
그가 약 15년의 기간 동안 영감을 받아 기록한
사람들이 일반적으로 어떤 특성을 나타낼 것인지 예언합니다.
그런 다음, 디모데에게 “하느님의 영감을 받은” 성경이
그를 “지혜롭게 하여 구원을 얻게 해 줄 수 있다”고 일깨워 줍니다.
경건한 정성으로 살고자 하는 모든 사람은
긴박감을 가지고 말씀을 전파하라고 엄숙히 명령합니다.
거짓 이야기로 자기 귀를 즐겁게 해 주기를
또한 바울은 자신의 죽음이 임박했다고 말하면서
바울이 자신의 죽음이 임박한 상황에서도 다른 사람들,
특히 그가 사랑하는 디모데에게 깊은 관심을 나타냈다는 점,
경건한 정성으로 살고자 하는 모든 사람이 박해를 받을 것이라는 점,
바울과 디모데처럼 우리도 하느님의 왕국에 계속 초점을 맞추면서
봉사의 직무를 완수해야 한다는 점에 유의해 보시기 바랍니다.

en.text: An introduction to 2 Timothy.
This letter was written by the apostle Paul
in Rome about 65 C.E.
Emperor Nero
had begun persecuting Christians,
and Paul was again a prisoner in Rome.
During his first imprisonment,
he was under house arrest.
This time his situation was far more serious.
He was not only in chains
but he was also facing imminent death.
Paul wrote this warm letter to Timothy to encourage him
to “stir up like a fire the gift of God” that he received,
to do his utmost to remain approved by God,
and to flee from the improper desires of youth.
Second Timothy has four chapters.
Paul opens his letter with warm encouragement for Timothy,
who may still be in Ephesus.
Paul mentions that some brothers in Asia have turned away from him.
But he commends Onesiphorus,
who courageously searched for Paul to minister to him.
In chapter 2,
Paul tells Timothy to teach other faithful men
the many things he learned from Paul.
The apostle urges Timothy
to “reject foolish and ignorant debates,
knowing that they produce fights.”
Did you know?
Paul’s second letter to Timothy
is the last of 14 books
that the apostle was inspired to write
over a period of about 15 years.
He wrote at least five of those books
while he was in confinement in Rome,
the book of Hebrews being written
either shortly before
or shortly after his release.
In chapter 3, Paul foretells
what people in general will be like
during the last days of Satan’s world.
Paul then reminds Timothy
that the Scriptures, which are “inspired of God,”
are able to make him “wise for salvation.”
Paul also says that ‘all those desiring to live
with godly devotion in association with Christ Jesus
will be persecuted.’
In chapter 4,
Paul solemnly charges Timothy
to preach the word urgently
because the time is coming when some will reject the truth,
preferring to have their ears tickled with false stories.
Paul then indicates that his death is near,
so he asks Timothy to come to him quickly and to bring Mark along.
As you read Paul’s second letter to Timothy,
note how Paul, despite facing imminent death,
was primarily concerned about others,
especially his beloved Timothy;
how all those desiring to live with godly devotion
will be persecuted;
and how, like Paul and Timothy,
we should fully accomplish our ministry
as we keep our focus on God’s Kingdom.

cn.text: 提摩太后书简介
保罗在罗马写下提摩太后书
当时大约是公元65年
罗马皇帝尼禄已经开始迫害基督徒
保罗再次被囚禁在罗马
他前一次只是被软禁
但这次他要面对更严峻的情势
保罗不仅被关在牢房，而且即将被处死
保罗写了这封充满温情的信给提摩太
鼓励提摩太要善用上帝给他的恩赐
“就像把火堆挑旺一样”
也要全力成为“上帝认可的人”
保罗还提醒提摩太
要“远避年轻人的欲望”
提摩太后书一共有4章
保罗写信时，提摩太可能还在以弗所
保罗在信的开头说了些话鼓励提摩太
然后他提到亚细亚行省的弟兄
离弃了自己
但奥尼色弗勇敢地寻找并帮助他
让保罗感到很欣慰
第2章，保罗吩咐提摩太
把从他身上学到的事
教给忠信的弟兄
保罗告诉提摩太
要“弃绝愚蠢无知的辩论”
因为“这种行为会引起争吵”
你知道吗？
提摩太后书
是保罗写的14封信中的最后一封
保罗在大约15年内
写下这些受上帝启示的经卷
其中至少有5封
是他在罗马被囚禁时写的
而希伯来书可能是保罗获释前
或获释后不久写下的
第3章
保罗预告撒但的世界快要结束时
人们普遍会有哪些态度和行为
保罗提醒提摩太
经卷里的话都是上帝指引人写下的
让提摩太“有智慧可以得救”
保罗也说
“所有想要追随基督耶稣
过虔诚生活的人都会受到迫害”
第4章，保罗郑重吩咐提摩太
要急切地传讲上帝的话语
因为“将来会有一段时期
人们容不下健全的教导”
只想听顺耳的话
保罗的话显示他知道自己将被处死
因此他促请提摩太和马可尽快来见自己
你读提摩太后书时，请留意
保罗虽然知道自己即将被处死
还是非常关心别人
特别是他所疼爱的提摩太
所有想过虔诚生活的人
都会受到迫害
我们可以向保罗和提摩太学习
将目光专注在上帝的王国之上
彻底完成传道工作

title: 더 필요한 곳에서 섬기다—꿈이 현실이 되기까지

ko.text: 형제 자매들이 여호와를 위해 큰 희생을 하고
더 필요한 곳으로 이주하는 걸 보면 늘 부러웠죠.
우리도 그런 경험을 하는 게 항상 꿈이었어요.
우리가 삶에서 그런 변화를 하는 건 불가능할 것 같았어요.
그런 일은 특별한 사람들이나 할 수 있는 거라고 생각했죠.
윌리엄스 형제 가족이 에콰도르로 이주한 동영상을 보고
사실 우리도 주저할 이유가 없다는 생각이 들었죠.
우리라고 못 할 게 뭐 있겠어요?
아시아의 여러 나라에 도움이 많이 필요하다는 걸 알고,
우리는 생활을 더 단순하게 하고 싶어서
태국에 살고 있는 한 부부를 만났는데,
우리에게 많은 조언과 격려를 해 줬습니다.
우린 우리를 간략히 소개하는 편지를 써서
봉사 위원회는 태국 지부에 그 편지를 보냈죠.
얼마 동안 시부모님 댁에서 지낼 수 있었죠.
우리는 새로운 회중에서 도움을 엄청나게 많이 받았습니다.
살 곳과 차가 필요했고 알아야 할 것도 많았죠.
이를테면 어디에서 장을 봐야 하는지 같은 거요.
형제들의 사랑과 격려는 정말 큰 도움이 되었습니다.
태국 지부에서 보내 준 답장도 많은 도움이 되었죠.
그 편지에서는 이곳의 생활비와 태국 문화나 음식에 대한 정보,
영성을 유지하는 방법에 대해 알려 주었습니다.
마음이 한결 편안해지고 더 열심히 하고 싶어졌어요.
우리는 형제 자매들이 여호와를 위해 희생하고
축복을 받은 경험에 대해 읽을 때마다
하지만 그걸 직접 경험하는 건 정말 놀라운 일입니다.

en.text: We always admired friends who had sacrificed a lot for Jehovah
and moved to a place
where the need is greater.
And it’s always been our dream
to experience it ourselves.
But at the same time,
we felt that we wouldn’t be able to do something like that.
Even though we had the desire,
we felt that only superhumans
could make that kind of change in their lives.
On JW Broadcasting® of August 2015,
we saw a very encouraging video about the Williams family
and how they moved to Ecuador.
And we thought
that in reality there wasn’t anything standing in our way,
so why couldn’t we do the same?
So we discussed it and decided on a date
—late November 2017—
and then we prayed to Jehovah.
I read the 2016 Yearbook,
and the story about Indonesia
really touched me.
We saw that there is a great need in many Asian countries,
and we thought maybe Thailand.
We wanted to simplify our lives even more, so we moved to a smaller apartment.
At the special convention in Helsinki,
we met a couple who lives in Thailand,
and they gave us a lot of advice
and encouragement.
We wrote a letter where we told a bit
about ourselves and then gave it
to the service committee in our congregation.
They then sent the letter
to the branch in Thailand.
We sold our car, and we also had the opportunity
to move in with Benjamin’s parents.
We received tremendous help from all
in the congregation.
For instance, we needed to find
a place to live,
a car, and to know where to shop for food.
And their love and encouragement has been invaluable.
We received a letter from the Thailand branch
in response to the letter we wrote earlier.
They gave us information
about the living expenses
and some pointers about the culture,
the food, and our spirituality in the new environment.
And we have felt more comfortable
and motivated by knowing
that we have followed the directions from Jehovah.
We have always felt encouraged
by reading experiences about brothers and sisters
who have made sacrifices for Jehovah
and how they have been blessed.
But to experience it for yourself is amazing.
When a problem or an obstacle arose,
Jehovah was there
and ready to help us.
And now we are happy to enjoy the privilege
of serving Jehovah here.

title: 우연의 산물인가? 교통 체증을 피하는 개미의 능력

ko.text: 하지만 교통 체증은 찾아볼 수 없습니다.
군대개미는 집을 나서는데 먹이를 들고 오는 동료를 마주치면
먹이를 든 동료는 민첩하게 길을 바꿀 수 없기 때문입니다.
가위개미는 뭔가를 운반하느라 느리게 가는 동료들이 앞에 보이면
짐을 든 무리에게 우선 통행권이 있어서
집에서 나오는 개미와 정면으로 충돌하는 일을
또 개미는 더듬이를 접촉해 소통을 할 수 있습니다.
그래서 훨씬 복잡한 상황에서도 서로 뒤엉키는 일이 없습니다.
반면에 사람들은 교통 체증으로 엄청난 시간을 낭비합니다.
따라서 과학자들은 도로 상황이 변할 때도
차량 흐름을 최적화할 수 있는 교통 시스템을 연구 중입니다.
그렇게 하는 데 개미가 정체를 피하기 위해
정체를 일으키지 않고 이동하는 개미의 능력은 진화된 것입니까?

en.text: Daily, millions of ants
travel from their nest to their hunting grounds
with nearly no congestion.
How?
When army ants leave their nests,
they navigate around those returning with food,
instinctively adjusting to the returning ants’ limited maneuverability.
When leaf-cutter ants encounter slow-moving,
load-carrying members, they adapt
by reducing speed, forming clusters,
and moving as a collective group.
Researchers say that this actually
helps ants reach their destination quicker,
as they will have the right-of-way
and avoid head-on collisions
with ants coming out of the nest.
Additionally, ants can communicate
by touching antennae, enabling them to overcome
even more complex navigational problems.
In contrast, billions of hours each year are wasted
when individuals find themselves locked in traffic.
Scientists hope to mimic the ant’s instinctive adaptability
by designing traffic systems
that optimize vehicle flow
through changing road conditions.
What do you think?
Did the ant’s ability to avoid congestion
come about by evolution?
Or was it designed?

cn.text: 每天，成千上万的蚂蚁
在蚁窝和觅食的地方之间往返
但几乎没有过“堵车”的问题
它们是怎样做到的呢？
背着食物回来的行军蚁速度较慢
为了避免与它们相撞
离开蚁窝的蚂蚁会出于本能给它们让路
当切叶蚁前方出现背着东西
行动缓慢的蚂蚁时
它就会配合前方的蚂蚁降低速度
跟它们一起行走
此外，这些回来的蚂蚁也拥用先行权
避免跟出蚁窝的蚂蚁相撞
研究员发现
蚂蚁这样做就可以更快到达目的地
另外，蚂蚁也会用它们的触角互相沟通
这样就可以应付更复杂的“交通问题”
然而，每年人们花在堵车上的时间
加起来就有数亿小时
科学家希望从研究蚂蚁的本能
学到怎样设计优良的交通系统
可以随着路况的改变作出调整
让交通更顺畅
你认为怎样？
蚂蚁避免“堵车”的本能是进化来的
还是经过设计的呢？

그럼 어떻게 비유를 사용해야 요점을 잘 가르칠 수 있을까요?
“세상은 지나가고 있으며 세상의 욕망도 지나가고 있습니다.
우리는 시간과 활력을 올바로 사용해야 합니다.
예를 들어 다른 지역에 사는 친척 집에
며칠 가 있게 됐다고 생각해 보시죠.
침대가 집에서 쓰던 것보다 좀 불편한 것 같습니다.
벽에는 그림도 안 걸려 있고 창문도 없습니다.
며칠 쓰겠다고 큰 침대를 사고 그림을 사다 거시겠습니까?
편의를 위해 의자나 테이블 같은 물건의 위치를 바꿀지는 몰라도
방 전체를 새로 꾸미진 않을 겁니다.
우리도 지나가 버릴 이 세상에 잠시 머무는 동안
단순하게 생활하면서 왕국에 초점을 맞추어야 합니다.
어떤 여자가 그것을 가져다가 밀가루 서 말에 섞었더니,
청중에게 익숙한 빵 만드는 일이 소재였고
알맞은 예를 어떻게 찾을 수 있을까요?
주변을 주의 깊이 살펴보고, 우리 출판물을 연구하고,
나중에 사용할 만한 비유를 모아 둡니다.
호소력이 있는 간단한 비유를 사용하도록 하십시오.

en.text: Illustrations are powerful teaching tools.
They help to explain complex ideas.
They also stimulate thinking and can break down prejudice.
Illustrations stir emotions and appeal to the heart.
They’re also memory aids.
It’s no wonder, then, that Jesus made good use of them.
Here are three things that will make your illustrations effective:
Select simple illustrations,
choose them with your listeners in mind,
and use them to teach the points that are truly important.
Listen to the following illustration, and see if it’s effective.
“Furthermore, the world is passing away and so is its desire,
but the one who does the will of God remains forever.”
If the world is passing away
and life in this system of things is temporary,
shouldn’t that affect how we use our time and energy?
For example, imagine you’re going on a seven-day, European cruise.
The ports of call are Lisbon, Gibraltar,
Barcelona, Monte Carlo, Florence, and Rome.
Because the ship will have many activities, you’ve chosen an inside cabin.
Although the room is nicely decorated,
it’s not exactly your taste.
For example, you don’t like the brightly colored carpet and walls
that are common on many cruise ships.
Also, the bedspread and curtains are not what you would’ve chosen.
You have a refrigerator in the room, but it’s small.
Would you spend time redecorating the room
—maybe put down a new carpet,
paint the room a different color,
hang new curtains, or purchase a larger refrigerator?
Of course not!
Your stay is only temporary.
Similarly, our stay in this system of things is only temporary.
Does it make sense that we would spend time and energy
to make our life as comfortable as possible?
Although this illustration made a good point,
was it as effective as it could have been?
Was it simple?
Well, was it necessary for the audience to know the reason for the trip,
how long the cruise was, or the cities where the ship was stopping?
No.
These details actually complicated the illustration.
Here’s something else:
Did the speaker have his listeners in mind?
Probably few in his audience have taken a cruise,
so it would be hard for them to identify with the situation.
Therefore, the point of the illustration could be lost,
or their minds might be diverted to the speaker
rather than his message.
How might the speaker have illustrated the same point more effectively?
Let’s watch him try again.
“Furthermore, the world is passing away and so is its desire,
but the one who does the will of God remains forever.”
If the world is passing away
and our life in this system of things is temporary,
shouldn’t that affect how we use our time and energy?
For example, imagine that you’re visiting relatives
in another village for a few days.
They kindly give you a room.
However, the bed is not as comfortable as yours.
The walls could use a few more pictures, and there’s no window.
Would you purchase a larger bed for your stay
and some pictures for the walls?
Or would you take time to install a window?
Of course not!
You’re only staying a few days.
We might relocate the chairs and tables and a few simple things
to make our surroundings more comfortable during our temporary stay,
but we would not go to great effort or expense
to redecorate the entire room.
In like manner,
we keep matters simple during our temporary residency in this old system,
giving our main focus to Kingdom interests.
Jesus’ illustrations were simple.
For example:
“The Kingdom of the heavens is like leaven that a woman took
“and mixed with three large measures of flour
until the whole mass was fermented.”
It’s just one sentence about baking bread,
a situation familiar to his audience.
This simplicity made Jesus’ illustrations appeal to the heart.
Jesus also used illustrations
to teach main points, not minor details.
So use illustrations selectively.
If you were to use an illustration to teach a minor detail,
your audience may remember the illustration
but not the point of instruction.
How can you find appropriate illustrations?
Be observant.
Look at the world around you,
study our Christian publications,
and listen to skilled teachers.
Some experienced teachers save illustrations in a file to use later.
If you want to teach like Jesus,
enhance your teaching with simple illustrations that appeal to your listeners
and that teach main points.

cn.text: 比喻是十分有力的教导工具
比喻可以把复杂的道理变简单
激发思考
让人放下偏见看问题
也可以打动人心、引起共鸣
比喻也能帮助人记住要点
难怪耶稣会在教导时经常使用比喻
在运用比喻施行教导时
你需要留意以下三点
要用简单的比喻
取材时要考虑到听者
比喻要用来解释主要论点
不是细节
请看一位弟兄运用比喻演讲时效果如何
“这个世界和世界的欲望正在消逝
遵从上帝旨意的人却永远长存”
既然这个世界正在消逝
我们在这个制度里的生活只是暂时的
那么
应该怎样运用自己的时间和精力呢？
请想象一下
假如你报名了欧洲游轮七日游
你会去好多地方
比如里斯本、直布罗陀
巴塞罗那、蒙特卡洛
佛罗伦萨和罗马
船上有很多活动
你为了省点钱
就决定住在没有窗户的房间
虽然那个房间也装饰得不错
但那不是你喜欢的风格
比如
你不喜欢颜色太鲜艳的地毯
墙壁颜色也太俗气
床单和窗帘也不合你的胃口
那里有个冰箱
不过非常小
你会花很多时间去重新布置这里吗？
买张新地毯？
把墙壁刷成另一个颜色？
挂上新窗帘？
再搬一个大冰箱进来？
当然不会！
你只在这里住几天而已
同样
我们在这个制度的生活
也只是暂时的
我们花太多时间和精力
去提高物质生活水平是明智的吗？
虽然这个弟兄的比喻能带出要点
但它达到了理想的效果吗？
比喻够简单吗？
其实，旅行有多少天
都要去哪些城市
为什么要选那个房间等等这些细节
听众都不需要知道
说这些反而让比喻变得很复杂
另外
讲者有没有考虑听众的情况呢？
也许只有少数人坐过游轮
大部分人不清楚那是什么样的
结果他们不能理解比喻的要点
听众也可能开始分心
忘记讲者想讲的道理
这个弟兄可以怎样让比喻
达到更好的效果呢？
我们再来看看
“这个世界和世界的欲望正在消逝
遵从上帝旨意的人却永远长存”
既然这个世界正在消逝
我们在这个制度里的生活只是暂时的
那么
应该怎样运用自己的时间和精力呢？
请想象一下
假如你在远方的亲戚那里住几天
他们特意为你准备了一个房间
不过，那张床不如你自己的舒服
墙上也没有什么装饰
屋子也没有窗户
你会为了这几天去买一张床
再买一些画装饰墙壁吗？
你会凿出一个窗户出来吗？
当然不会！
你只在这里住几天而已
也许你可以简单调整一下
桌子椅子的位置
让自己住得舒适些、方便些
但不该花很多时间
花很多钱去重新布置这个房间
同样
我们在这个旧制度里的生活
也是暂时的
要尽量过简单的生活
把焦点集中在上帝的王国
耶稣用的比喻都很简单
例如
“天上的王国好像酵
有女人拿去跟三大份面粉混合在一起
直到整个面团都发了酵”
这个比喻很简短
当时人们都很熟悉发酵的过程
耶稣的比喻简明扼要
所以能打动人心
此外，耶稣只用比喻说明主要的论点
而不是次要的细节
我们也要在恰当的地方使用比喻
如果一些不重要的细节
都用比喻来说明
那么听众可能只记住比喻
而忽略了你想要他们明白的重点
怎样才能找到合适的比喻呢？
要留心观察
要观察周围的事物
也可以从我们的出版物借鉴
或者向有经验的讲者学习
有些讲者把比喻搜集起来备用
如果你想要像耶稣那样
有效地施行教导
就要记得，比喻要简单
适合听众并用来解释重要的道理

titles.cn: 第8课：比喻有教导作用

title: 케네스 쿡 2세: 겸허—“선한 것”의 중요한 특성

ko.text: 자신을 알리라고, 자기 맘대로 해도 된다고,
자기가 원하는 건 뭐든 될 수 있다고 말합니다.
살펴보겠지만, 이런 사고방식은 완전히 잘못된 것인데,
사실 겸허는 모든 선한 것의 한 가지 중요한 특성입니다.
“선한 것이 무엇인지를 그분이 네게 알려 주셨다.
단지 공의를 행하고 충성을 소중히 여기며
겸허하게 네 하느님과 함께 걷는 것이 아니냐!”
겸허가 “선한 것”의 한 가지 주요 부면이란 점에 유의하십시오.
왜 그런지 이해하기 위해, 세 가지 점을 살펴보죠.
간단히 말해, 자신의 한계를 아는 것입니다.
흔히 겸허를 정숙한 옷차림이나 몸단장과 관련짓지만,
겸허와 대조되는 부정적인 특성이 주제넘음이라는 걸 알 수 있습니다.
그런 사람은 정해진 경계나 한계를 무시합니다.
그런 태도는 종종 어리석은 실수를 하거나
주변 사람에게 나쁜 평판을 얻게 만들죠.
또, 무엇보다 하느님의 호의를 잃게 만들 수 있습니다.
그 예로 사울왕을 생각할 수 있죠.
시간이 지나며 주제넘은 태도를 갖게 됐습니다.
그 결과 사울은 여호와의 은혜를 잃고
그는 주제넘게 행동했기 때문에 불명예를 피할 수 없었습니다.
반면에, 지혜롭고 겸허한 사람은 자신의 한계를 잘 알고,
오늘의 두 번째 요점과 관련이 있죠.
그분은 스스로 정하신 한계를 지키면서 일하십니다.
우리에게 본을 보여 겸허를 나타내는 법을 가르쳐 주시죠.
왜 여호와께서 자기 자신에게 한계를 정하신다고 할 수 있을까요?
그분은 우리에게 선물한 자유 의지를 결코 뺏지 않으십니다.
우리가 그분을 억지로 섬기게 하지 않으시죠.
그렇게 하실 수 있는 힘이 있으시지만요.
사랑에서 우러나와 그분을 섬기기로 선택할 수 있다는 데
여호와께선 다른 면으로도 겸허를 나타내는 법을 알려 주십니다.
여호와께서는 소돔과 고모라를 멸망시키고자 하셨을 때,
아브라함이 그에 대해 우려하는 걸 참을성 있게 들어 주셨습니다.
또한 천사들에게 아합을 꾀어 낼 방법을 제안하도록 하셨고,
한 천사에게 그의 제안을 실행할 권한을 주셨죠.
조직에서 책임 있는 직책을 맡고 계십니까?
그렇다면 다른 사람을 너무 일일이 감독하지 않음으로
여호와를 본받아 그들을 품위 있게 대하고
겸허한 사람이 돼야 할 이유가 또 있습니다.
다른 사람의 도움을 감사하고 기쁘게 받아들일 것입니다.
병을 고쳐 준 예수께 돌아와 감사를 표현했죠.
예수께서 해 주신 일이 자기 힘으론 결코 할 수 없단 걸 알았기에
겸허를 길러야 하는 또 다른 이유는
다른 사람들과 좋은 관계를 누릴 수 있기 때문입니다.
보통 이렇게 생각하는 사람에게 이끌리긴 어렵죠.
‘역시 일을 제대로 하려면 내가 직접 해야 해.’
반대로 우리가 사람들을 신뢰한다는 걸 보여 줄 때
또 겸허하면 자신을 다른 사람과 비교하지 않게 되니까
자연히 사람들과 좋은 관계를 누리게 됩니다.
누가 더 큰지를 놓고 여러 차례 논쟁했던
얼마나 나쁜 일을 저질렀는지도 생각해 보십시오.
자신이 어떤 위치에 있는지에 집착하지 않습니다.
이 면에서 모세가 남긴 좋은 본을 생각해 볼 수 있죠.
자신만이 그런 특별한 임무를 수행해야 한다고 생각하지 않았죠.
겸허하면 좋은 관계를 누리게 되는 또 한 가지 이유는
겸허한 사람은 자신이 이룬 일을 자랑하거나
자신에게 필요 이상으로 주의를 끌지 않기 때문인데,
그런 행동은 남에게 불쾌감을 줄 뿐이죠.
겸허란 무엇이며 왜 겸허해야 하는지 알아봤습니다.
‘어떻게 이 훌륭한 특성을 기를 수 있는가?’ 하는 것이죠.
한 가지 방법은 앞서 살펴본 것처럼
성경의 본들, 좋은 본과 나쁜 본 모두를,
성경의 본 중엔 다니엘도 있는데, 겸허하게도,
느부갓네살왕의 꿈을 해석한 공을 자신에게 돌리지 않았죠.
배울 수 있는 점은, 우리가 가르치는 임명을 받았거나,
봉사에서 어느 정도 좋은 결과를 거둘 때,
그 모든 영광을 여호와께 돌려야 합니다.
그분의 도움 없인 할 수 없는 일이란 걸
또 예수의 본도 연구해 볼 수 있는데,
더 많은 권위를 차지할 생각조차 하지 않으셨죠.
제자 야고보와 요한이 어머니와 함께 와서
예수께서 주실 권한이 없는 특권을 달라고 요청했을 때,
왕국에서 누가 그분의 오른편과 왼편에 앉을지는
오직 여호와께서 결정하실 일임을 겸허히 인정하셨죠.
겸허를 기르는 또 어떤 방법이 있을까요?
고린도 전서 4:6에 나오는 성경의 조언을 적용하는 것입니다.
이건 일차적으로 하느님의 말씀에 ‘기록된 것들’을 뜻하지만,
더 크게 보면 우리 출판물에 나오는
누가 우리에게 조언을 구할 때 결코
자신의 견해를 강요하거나 그저 떠오르는 대로 말해선 안 됩니다.
성경과 성경에 근거한 출판물에 나오는 조언으로
자신이 겸허한 사람이라는 평판을 받고 있는지
이 점과 관련해 기억나는 성경 원칙이 있죠.
“철이 철을 날카롭게 하듯, 사람도 친구를 예리하게 한다.”
누군가가 우리에게서 개선할 점을 보고 친절히 알려 준다면,
우린 그 말에 기분 나빠 하지 않을 겁니다.
물론 그런 솔직한 말에 자존심이 상할 수도 있죠.
하지만 우리 모두 그런 조언이 필요할 때가 있지 않나요?
다른 사람이 우릴 보듯 자신을 보기는 어렵습니다.
개선이 필요한 부면이 무엇인지 알아야만 한다는 것입니다.
모르는 걸 고칠 순 없기 때문이죠.
주의할 점으로, 거짓 겸허를 조심해야 합니다.
단지 겸허한 사람처럼 보이는 게 아니라
다음과 같은 질문을 묵상해 볼 수 있습니다.
조언이나 충고를 받을 때, 나는 실제로 어떻게 느끼는가?
경험이나 권위가 더 많은지 적은지에 따라,
나는 누가 한 제안이든 기꺼이 받아들이는가?
“모든 좋은 선물과 모든 완전한 선물은 위에서,
겸허 역시 여호와에게서 오는 좋은 선물이므로,
이 특성을 기르게 도와 달라고 여호와께 진실하게 기도하고 청하면
그분이 응답하실 것을 확신할 수 있습니다.
성경에 있는 좋은 본과 나쁜 본 모두를 묵상하고
또 ‘기록된 것들에서 벗어나지 말라’ 는 조언을 따르고,
사람들에게 내가 겸허한지 솔직히 말해 달라고 부탁할 수 있습니다.
더 겸허한 사람이 되게 도와 달라고 여호와께 기도로 청하십시오.
우리 자신과 다른 사람에게 가져오는 모든 유익을 생각할 때,

en.text: One of the most underrated qualities
in today’s world is modesty.
In fact, the world encourages
the exact opposite of modesty.
The world says that you are the most important person;
you should promote yourself; you have no limits;
you have the right to be anything you want to be.
As we’ll see, the world’s thinking is completely backward
—and for several reasons.
Really, modesty is a quality
that stems from everything that is good.
Our theme scripture for this discussion is Micah 6:8:
“He has told you . . . what is good.
“And what is Jehovah requiring of you?
“Only to exercise justice, to cherish loyalty,
and to walk in modesty with your God!”
Notice that modesty is one
of the key aspects of “what is good.”
To help us understand why,
let’s discuss three questions:
What is modesty?
Why do we want to have this quality?
How can we cultivate it?
First, what is modesty?
Basically, it’s an awareness of our limitations.
Of course, we often link modesty
with appropriate dress and grooming,
but much more is involved.
How do we know?
Consider what we read at Proverbs 11:2:
“When presumptuousness comes,
“dishonor will follow,
but wisdom is with the modest ones.”
Notice that modesty is contrasted
with a negative quality—presumptuousness.
A presumptuous person runs ahead without the authority to do so.
He or she ignores proper boundaries and limitations.
That kind of attitude often leads to foolish mistakes
and a bad reputation with fellow humans.
And above all, it can cause a person to lose God’s favor.
For example, we might think of King Saul.
Although he started out as a modest young man,
in time he became presumptuous.
He even went so far as to offer up
a burnt sacrifice even though he was not authorized to do so.
As a result,
Saul lost Jehovah’s favor
and eventually the kingship.
In Saul’s case, presumptuousness definitely
led to dishonor.
On the other hand,
a wise and modest person
recognizes his limitations and works within them.
Why is modesty the course of wisdom?
This brings us to our second main point,
Why do we want to have this quality?
The foremost reason
is that modesty is essential
to pleasing our heavenly Father, Jehovah.
Although we don’t speak of Jehovah as being modest,
even he works within certain limitations
that he’s imposed on himself.
He teaches us by example how to demonstrate this quality,
even though it’s not one that he needs to display.
Why can we say that Jehovah imposes limitations on himself?
Consider just one example:
He’ll never violate the gift of free will that he’s granted us.
Jehovah will never force us to serve him
—even though, of course, he has the power to do so.
Aren’t we grateful that he allows us to serve him
because we choose to out of love
and not because we are forced to?
Jehovah teaches us to display modesty in other ways as well.
For example, we might think of how he listened patiently
as Abraham voiced his concerns about Jehovah’s purpose
to destroy Sodom and Gomorrah
or how Jehovah invited the angels to suggest ways to fool Ahab
and then authorized one of their suggestions to be carried out.
What’s the lesson for us?
If Jehovah, who doesn’t need input or help from anyone,
patiently listens and delegates,
how much more should we do so
—especially since we’re all so imperfect and limited!
Are you a family head or an elder in the congregation,
or do you have another responsible position in the organization?
If so, you can imitate Jehovah
by not micromanaging others.
Be willing to delegate tasks to them
and listen to their suggestions.
Imitate Jehovah’s example of dignifying others
and wanting to help them succeed.
Besides pleasing Jehovah,
we have other good reasons to be modest.
Modesty helps us to be joyful.
How so?
By going hand in hand with a related quality—gratitude.
A faithful brother who worked in the Writing Department
for some 50 years was fond of saying,
“Only a grateful person can be happy.”
If we’re modestly aware of our limitations,
we’ll be grateful and happy
for the help that we receive from others.
For example,
think of the leper who returned
to thank Jesus for healing him.
This man realized his limitations.
He was very thankful that Jesus had done something for him
that he could never have done on his own.
Another reason to cultivate modesty
is that it promotes good relationships with others.
Let’s face it:
People aren’t usually drawn to those who think,
‘If I want something done right,
I have to do it myself.’
But they usually appreciate it when they’re shown
that we have confidence in them.
This, in turn, draws them to us.
Another way that modesty promotes good relationships
is that it helps us to avoid comparing ourselves to others.
Comparing ourselves to others
is always a dangerous road to navigate.
Just think, for example, of Jesus’ apostles
who argued many times over who was the greatest
or of Joseph’s brothers and the terrible things they did
because of being jealous of Joseph.
A modest person doesn’t obsess
over his perceived rank in comparison with others.
In this regard,
we can remember the good example of Moses.
How did he react when Jehovah
enabled some of his fellow Israelites
to begin acting as prophets alongside him?
Moses rejoiced,
saying that he wished all of Jehovah’s people were prophets.
Moses didn’t feel that he was the only one who should have such a privilege.
Finally, modesty promotes good relationships with others
because it prevents us from bragging about our accomplishments
or drawing undue attention to ourselves,
which could stir up resentment in others.
So now we know what modesty is and why we want to have it.
This brings us to our third main point,
How can we cultivate this beautiful quality?
One thing we can do
is to read and meditate on Bible examples
—both good and bad— such as those we just discussed.
Other Bible examples include Daniel,
who modestly didn’t take credit
for the interpretation of King Nebuchadnezzar’s dream.
The lesson for us?
If we’re privileged to have a teaching assignment
or we enjoy a measure of success in the ministry,
we want to give all the glory to Jehovah.
We should modestly recognize
that we couldn’t do these things without his help.
We can also study the example of Jesus,
who didn’t even think of trying to grasp
for more authority than Jehovah had granted him.
Philippians 2:6 tells us:
“He . . . gave no consideration to a seizure,
namely, that he should be equal to God.”
Consider how Jesus responded
when his disciples James and John approached him
with their mother and asked for a privilege
that was beyond his authority to grant them.
Jesus modestly acknowledged
that only Jehovah could decide
who would sit at his right and left hand in the Kingdom.
Jesus respected his limitations.
What are some other ways we can cultivate modesty?
One is to apply the Bible’s counsel
found at 1 Corinthians 4:6:
“Do not go beyond the things that are written.”
This refers primarily to ‘the things written’ in God’s Word.
By extension, the principle also applies to the Scriptural direction
that we receive from our publications.
When asked for advice,
we would never want to impose our own opinion
or simply give an answer off the top of our head.
Rather, we want to direct attention
to the counsel found in the Bible
and Bible-based publications.
Another way we can cultivate modesty
is by asking for frank comments
from a trusted friend
as to whether or not we have a reputation for being modest.
In this regard, we remember the Bible principle:
“As iron sharpens iron,
so one man sharpens his friend.”
If someone is willing to offer
kind observations about how we can improve,
we wouldn’t want to bristle at the comments.
Granted, it may sting our pride to hear such honest feedback,
but don’t we all need to hear these things from time to time?
As imperfect humans,
each one of us has blind spots, as it were.
It’s hard to see ourselves the way others see us.
Remember, we can work to improve our Christian personality
—but only if we know the areas that could use some improvement.
We can’t change what we don’t see.
A word of caution:
We want to beware of false modesty.
Remember that it’s not about simply appearing modest
but actually being modest at heart.
To help us examine ourselves,
we might meditate on questions like these:
When I receive advice or counsel,
how do I really feel about it at heart?
Does my internal reaction depend on whether the person giving it
has less or more experience or authority than I do?
Am I willing to accept valid suggestions regardless of who offers them?
A final way we can develop true modesty
is to ask Jehovah to help us.
We know what James 1:17 says:
“Every good gift and every perfect present is from above,
coming down from the Father of the celestial lights.”
Since modesty is one of Jehovah’s good gifts to us,
we can be sure that if we pray to Jehovah and ask him
to help us cultivate this quality,
he’ll answer our sincere prayers.
In review, what is modesty?
It’s a proper recognition of our limitations.
Why do we want to have this quality?
Because it pleases Jehovah,
it promotes good relationships with others,
and it adds to our joy.
How can we cultivate modesty?
There are many ways:
We can meditate on Bible examples, both good and bad,
and then apply the lessons in our own life.
We should apply the counsel to ‘not go beyond the things written.’
We can ask others for honest feedback
on how we’re doing in showing this quality.
And above all, we can pray to Jehovah
and ask him to help us develop it more fully.
When we think of all the positive ways
that modesty benefits ourselves and others,
wouldn’t you agree that it truly is a quality
that comes from “what is good”?

cn.text: 现在，很多人不再重视谦虚这个特质了
这个世界根本不鼓励人谦虚
让人觉得只有自己才是最重要的
这个世界鼓励人抬高自己
随心所欲
想做什么就做什么
让人觉得这是自己的权利
我们会谈谈
为什么说这个世界的思想
与耶和华眼中的“善”是完全相反的呢？
其实，耶和华眼中的“善”
也包括谦虚这个特质
我们今天讨论的主题经文就是弥迦书6:8
经文说
请留意谦虚是“善”的最重要的一部分
为了了解这一点
我们会讨论3个问题
一般来说
谦虚就是知道自己的能力限度
清楚知道自己哪些事情能做、哪些事不能做
关于谦虚
箴言11:2有这样的描述
我们一起来看一下
经文说
在这里越权妄为
也就是骄傲
与谦虚形成了鲜明的对比
越权妄为的人通常会做自己无权做的事
他们不愿意承认
有些事是自己不能做也不该做的
这样的态度通常会让他们犯下愚蠢的错误
破坏自己的名声
更糟的是
可能会失去上帝的喜悦
我们可能会想到扫罗王
他原本是个非常谦虚的年轻人
后来却变得越来越骄傲
他甚至越权行事，擅自献上祭牲
没有听从耶和华的安排等候撒母耳
结果，他失去了与上帝的友谊
最终失去了王位
扫罗的例子让我们看出
人如果越权行事
一定会自招羞辱
相反
一个明智谦虚的人
清楚知道自己的限度在哪里
不会做自己不该做的事情
为什么说谦虚是智慧的表现呢？
这就涉及到第二个要点
最重要的理由是
我们只有保持谦虚才会让天父耶和华开心
虽然我们不会用谦虚这个词来形容上帝
但是耶和华还是刻意限制自己不做某些事
虽然他不需要表现谦虚
但还是亲自向我们示范什么是谦虚
为什么说
耶和华会限制自己不做某些事呢？
比如说，虽然他赐给我们自由选择的权利
但是他从不会剥夺这个权利
虽然他可以强迫我们为他服务
但是他从不这样做
耶和华希望我们因为爱他而崇拜他
而不是被迫这样做
知道这一点我们不是很感激他吗？
耶和华也用其他方式教导我们表现谦虚
一个例子是
耶和华要毁灭所多玛和蛾摩拉的时候
他耐心听亚伯拉罕的忧虑
另一个例子是
耶和华问天使们怎样欺骗亚哈
后来耶和华让一个天使用他自己的方法去做
我们学到什么呢？
耶和华根本不需要别人的建议和帮助
但他却耐心听
也愿意把工作交给别人
我们是不完美的人
不是更应该这样做吗？
你是家主或者长老吗？
你在组织中担任某个职责吗？
如果是这样的话
你可以效法耶和华
不用对别人所做的每一件小事都一一过问
要愿意把工作交给其他人去做
愿意听别人的建议
要效法耶和华尊重别人
愿意帮助他们完成工作
除了让耶和华开心以外
我们还有什么理由要保持谦虚呢？
谦虚可以让我们更加喜乐
因为谦虚的人往往怀有感激之心
很容易保持喜乐
有位弟兄在写作部忠贞地服务了将近50年
他常常说
“只有心存感激的人才会快乐。”
如果我们谦虚地承认
有些事情是自己无法做到的
我们就会心存感激地接受别人的帮助
圣经提到有个麻风病人被耶稣治好后
特意回来感谢耶稣
他知道自己的能力限度
他无法医好自己
所以他被治好后
非常感激耶稣
我们培养谦虚的另外一个理由就是
这可以拉近我们和别人的关系
有些人会这样想
“只有我亲自去做才能把事情做好”
我们都承认自己不想和这样的人走得太近
可是如果我们信任别人
他们就会很高兴
这也会拉近我们彼此之间的距离
另外，谦虚可以帮助我们
避免拿自己跟别人比较
这可以拉近我们和别人的关系
跟别人比较会让我们陷入险境
为什么这么说呢？
也许大家还记得
耶稣的使徒们多次争论谁最大
约瑟的哥哥们因为嫉妒约瑟而陷害他
一个人如果谦虚的话
就不会老想着自己的地位
比别人高还是比别人低
在这方面摩西树立了很好的榜样
当耶和华让其他以色列人也做先知时
摩西有什么反应呢？
摩西非常高兴
他说他希望耶和华的所有子民都是先知
他没有觉得自己是唯一一个
能被耶和华任用的人
最后，谦虚的人不会吹嘘自己所做的事
也不会把注意力引到自己身上
这可以拉近我们跟别人的关系
否则，就会引起别人的反感
刚才我们谈过了什么是谦虚
为什么要有谦虚这个特质
现在来谈谈第三点
其中一个方法就是
阅读并沉思圣经中的好榜样和坏榜样
我们刚才已经谈过几个了
另一个好榜样是但以理
他成功地为尼布甲尼撒王解梦
却没有把功劳归给自己
如果我们有机会在台上演讲
或者在传道上取得很多成果
就要把所有荣耀都归给耶和华
我们应该承认
没有耶和华的帮助
我们就无法做好这些事
想想耶稣的榜样
他对耶和华赐给他的权力感到满足
从来没有想过要得到更多的权力
腓立比书2:6说
当耶稣的使徒雅各和约翰
跟他们的妈妈请求耶稣
赐给他们俩显要的地位时
耶稣怎样回答呢？
耶稣谦虚地承认
只有耶和华才有权决定
将来谁会坐在他的左边和右边
耶稣知道自己没有权力这样做
我们还有什么方法
可以培养谦虚这个特质呢？
其中一个是
实践圣经在哥林多前书4:6的劝告
经文说
虽然这里主要是指上帝的话语圣经
但这个原则也同样适用于圣经刊物的指引
向人提出劝告时
我们不该把自己的看法强加于人
或是没有仔细考虑就随便提出劝告
相反，我们提出的劝告
都应该以圣经和上帝组织的出版物为依据
另一个方法是
问问一位会跟你说实话
而且是你信赖的朋友
看看你在别人眼中是不是一个谦虚的人
关于这一点
有些人可能会仁慈地跟你说
哪些地方可以做得更好
听到这些话不要觉得自己被冒犯了
当然听到别人的“实话”可能有点伤自尊
但其实我们都需要常常听到这样的“实话”
我们都是不完美的人
都有自己的盲点
正所谓
当局者迷，旁观者清
不过，我们可以改善自己的品格
但前提是
我们要知道自己在哪些方面需要改善
如果我们不知道自己有哪些缺点
就很难改善
在这里我想提醒大家
我们要小心，不要假装谦虚
真正的谦虚不是表面的
而是发自内心的
我们可以沉思这些问题来察验自己
我是个愿意接受劝告的人吗？
我会看劝告是“谁”提出的吗？
比我们更有经验的人
或负有更多职责的人给我们劝告时
我们也许会听
但是如果给我们劝告的人
经验职责都不如我们
我们的反应又怎样呢？
培养真正谦虚的最后一个方法
就是向耶和华寻求帮助
雅各书1:17告诉我们
耶和华愿意赐给我们谦虚这个宝贵的礼物
我们就可以确信
只要我们诚恳地祷告
求他帮助我们培养谦虚
他一定会回应我们
什么是谦虚呢？
就是承认有些事只靠自己是无法做到的
为什么我们想要有这个特质呢？
因为这不但可以让耶和华开心
拉近我们和别人的关系
还可以使我们更加快乐
怎样培养谦虚这个特质呢？
沉思圣经中的好榜样和坏榜样
并把学到的在生活中实践出来
向人提出劝告时
不该越出圣经上的话
问问别人
自己是不是一个谦虚的人
最后，向耶和华祷告
请他帮助我们成为更谦虚的人
我们可以看出谦虚的确是“善”的一部分
因为谦虚不但能使自己获益
也能使别人受益不浅

en.text: Mom has been working hard lately,
but I wish she worked harder for Jehovah.
I try to help out where I can.
Oh, by the way, I’m Jin.
Every day starts the same.
I grab a drink of water;
I say hi to Jun (he’s in my congregation);
and then there’s Mee-Kyong.
OK. Here we go.
I say hello,
she says something clever,
and I try to leave.
So this is different.
She’s having trouble in math and needs my help.
I don’t want to be rude,
but
if I help her with her homework,
how far could the relationship develop?
How do you say no to a girl like her?
Why can’t I get her out of my head?
Things are always better
when Uncle and Auntie are around.
Even Mom makes sure she’s home for “dinner and broadcast” night.
Uncle wants to work together in service this weekend;
maybe that will help clear my head.
Jehovah must be disappointed in me.
I couldn’t take it anymore.
It was difficult,
but I told Uncle everything.
I felt guilty that I knew I shouldn’t,
but I liked the attention.
We read Genesis 39:7-12.
I knew the account about Potiphar’s wife,
but he mentioned something I hadn’t thought of before.
He told Potiphar’s wife:
“How could I commit this great badness
and actually sin against God?”
But why did Joseph have to flee?
Joseph fought her every day,
but she wasn’t going to give up.
In her mind, it wasn’t a question of if but when.
There came a point when he had to flee.
I explained why I was ending the relationship,
but she would not give up.
You know the last thing she said to me?
That I was a coward.
But she’s wrong.
You’re never a coward if you run to Jehovah.
