ko.text: 여러 해 동안 충실하게 추구해 오신
그리고 이 마지막 때에 살다 보면
세상에 겁나는 일이 수도 없이 많을 겁니다.
만약 새로운 문화에 적응 못하면 어쩌지?
내가 기대하지 않은 새로운 일을 맡게 되면 어쩌지?’
또 JW 방송을 통해 시청하실 많은 분들의 경우엔
이건 전 세계 우리 형제 자매들이
하지만 이 사실만큼 확실한 게 또 있는데요,
왜 의로운 자를 공격해서는 안 될까요?
한 참고 문헌에서는 이렇게 알려 줍니다.
방금 읽은 잠언과 비슷한 사상을 말하지만,
네, 여호와께서 의로운 자가 일어나게 도우십니다.
하지만 여호와께선 의로운 자들에게 재난이 닥칠 때
무슨 일이 닥쳐도 기도하는 걸 중단하지 않고,
40에서 하나를 뺀 매를 다섯 번 맞았고,
거짓 형제들 사이에서 겪는 위험을 당했고,
많은 사람은 이런 일 중 한 가지만 당해도
빠져나갈 길이 전혀 없는 것은 아닙니다.
어떤 고난이 닥쳐도 바울은 중단하지 않았습니다.
그런데 바울의 경우만 그런 게 아니라,
충실한 하느님의 종들 한 사람 한 사람,
이번엔 아들이 허우적대며 부르짖는 소리가 들렸습니다.
어떻게 해서든 가족을 구하지 못한 자신이
그가 할 수 있는 일이 아무것도 없는 상황이었다고
태풍은 사람의 힘으로 막을 수 없다고요.
그곳 형제들의 집을 다시 짓는 일을 도왔습니다.
그 지역에서 왕국회관을 건축하는 일을 수행했습니다.
꽤 멀리 떨어진 곳에 있는 회중을 돕겠다고 자원했습니다.
가는 데만 오토바이로 한 시간 반이 걸리는 곳이었지만,
그 회중에 장로의 도움이 필요했기 때문에
체포된 후에는 치료를 받을 수가 없어
비로소 다른 도시에서 치료를 받는 것이
형제가 수술을 받고 침대에 누워 있는데요,
그 시점에 형제는 이런 말을 들었죠.
그동안 자신의 신앙에 대해 말하고 다닌 것은 잘못이었으며,
다시 일어날 수 있었던 이유는 뭘까요?
하느님의 원칙을 지킬 것인지 무시할 것인지
이 작은 캐나다 베델 가족의 성원이 되었습니다.
지부의 종과 긴밀히 일했던 한 자매와
배교한 지부의 종이 베델에서 해임될 때
그와 함께 해임된 베델 봉사자 일곱 명 중에
물론 처음엔 마음에 상처를 입었다고 합니다.
짝 자매와 텐트 생활을 하면서 봉사했는데,
두 사람은 여호와의 증인 회중이 없는
프렌치 자매는 잠시 휴가를 하러 토론토에 갔는데,
그땐 갑자기 여호와의 증인에게 금지령이 내려진 때였습니다.
자매는 자신이 베델에서 나가게 됐을 때
프렌치 자매는 다른 사람들에게 오해를 받았을 때에도
우린 정말 쓰러졌다고 느낄 수 있습니다.
하지만 우리가 무엇을 해야 할진 늘 알고 있죠.
언제나 기도하고, 빠지지 않고 집회에 참석하고,
항상 여호와께서 기뻐하실 결정을 내리는 것입니다.
우리가 다시 일어날 수 있는 방법을 알려 주실 것입니다.
먼저 아가르발 형제 부부는 인도로 돌아갑니다.
드라부셰프스키 형제 부부는 핀란드로 돌아갈 것입니다.
로키아우 형제 부부는 필리핀으로 갈 것입니다.
모건 형제 부부는 케냐에서 봉사할 것입니다.
페롱 형제 부부는 세네갈에서 봉사할 것입니다.
산도발 형제 부부는 스페인으로 갈 것입니다.
센달 형제 부부는 트리니다드 토바고로 돌아갑니다.
제노노스 형제 부부는 그리스로 갈 것입니다.
그 어느 때보다도 잘 볼 수 있었습니다.
하느님의 말씀을 깊이 연구하며 얻은 유익과
과거에 여호와께서 다른 사람을 훈련하기 위해
전 세계의 연합된 형제들 전체에 대해
아직 듣지 못한 양 같은 사람들에 대해
또한 여러분 한 사람 한 사람이
우리는 우주에서 가장 강력한 하느님의 성령에 의지해,
졸업, 듣기만 해도 참 좋은 말이죠?
전 세계의 지부 또는 전국 위원회에
길르앗 교육 중이나 교육을 받은 지 얼마 후에
전 세계 밭과 소중한 우리 형제들에게
여러분이 임지에 자리를 잡게 될 때
영적 목표를 다 이루었다고 생각할 때
예를 들어, 우리가 예수를 따르는 것의
성서 시대 군인들은 전투가 없을 때
그들은 보호해 주는 이 전투 장비를
물질적인 부를 추구하는 사람들을 예로 들어
강하게 하고 있음을 나타낼 수 있습니다.
영적 일과를 소홀히 하는 일이 없게 하십시오.
자기 만족에 빠지는 일이 있어선 안 됩니다.
승리를 거둔 군인과 같이 될 것입니다.
훌륭한 싸움을 싸울” 준비가 돼 있을 것이며,
여호와와 그분의 아들의 축복을 받을 겁니다.

en.text: We’ve now come to the point where we can enjoy
the principal talk of our Gilead graduation program.
It is entitled “The Righteous One Will Get Up,”
and we have Brother Mark Sanderson
of the Governing Body to deliver that for us.
Well, for those of you who are graduating today,
this is indeed one of the happiest days of your entire life.
And rightly so,
because today represents a wonderful milestone
after years of faithfully pursuing a spiritual career.
But I have to be realistic.
I hate to be a downer at this moment,
but realistically,
we have to say that not every day
of your life ahead is going to be as happy as this one.
Now, why do we say that?
Well, of course, we know that Satan rules this world.
And living in these last days that we live in brings us anxiety,
sometimes even fear.
Life is full of what-ifs.
In fact, those two words “what if”
can send us down all kinds of roads that can be quite terrifying.
For you who are graduating today,
maybe it’s something like: ‘What if I can’t learn the new language?
‘Or what if I can’t adapt to a new culture?
‘Or what if I get home and the brothers
have a new assignment for me that I’m not expecting?’
Well, that’s for you.
But for all of us who are here in this audience
and perhaps even for our larger audience via JW Broadcasting®,
maybe it’s questions like:
‘What if I face persecution,
‘even violent persecution?
‘What if there’s a natural disaster?
‘What if I become seriously ill?
What if I lose a loved one in death?’
Well, those questions can seem hypothetical,
but many of our brothers and sisters around the world
are facing those situations right now.
For them, it’s not a matter of what if;
it’s what is.
Well, now, brothers, while it is absolutely certain
that we are going to experience calamities
because we live in the last days
where we expect “critical times hard to deal with,”
there is something that is equally certain
—that is no “what if.”
It’s a fundamental principle that applies
to every single righteous and faithful servant of Jehovah.
And that principle can fill us
with confidence and courage.
Now, what is this principle?
Well, open your Bibles; let’s look at Proverbs chapter 24.
And as you’re turning your Bibles there,
I’ll just remind you that in the Proverbs,
many of these proverbial thoughts
actually are made up of two verses,
and so this one begins in verse 15.
It actually begins with a warning,
and this is what it says:
“Do not wickedly lie in ambush
“near the home of the righteous one;
do not destroy his place of rest.”
Now, why?
Why is it that you should not attack the righteous one?
Well, now, notice the reason, and here’s this fundamental truth:
“For the righteous one may fall seven times,
“and he will get up again,
but the wicked will be made to stumble by calamity.”
Well, now, let’s take this verse apart.
What is it really trying to tell us?
For example, what does it mean to fall?
The March 15, 2013, Watchtower,
commenting on Proverbs 24:16,
defined fall as “an adversity or a setback.”
One reference work says:
“‘Falls’ is the word that can simply mean
“‘falls over or falls down.’
“But it also has a figurative meaning of [now notice this]
‘experiences disaster or ruin.’”
And that is the sense here.
Well, what does it mean, then, to get up?
That same reference work goes on to say:
“Likewise, ‘rises again’
“can simply mean ‘gets up after falling down.’
“But here, it has the figurative sense
“of ‘overcomes adversity
or becomes prosperous again.’”
Well, now, why seven times?
The same reference work says:
“Most translations render ‘seven times’ literally,
“but the figure seven
“probably has its Hebrew symbolic meaning in this context,
“namely, ‘completeness.’
“For that reason, some translations read:
“‘Even if a righteous person falls down many times,
he will always get up.’”
The Contemporary English Version says:
“Even if good people fall seven times, they will get back up.
But when trouble strikes the wicked, that’s the end of them.”
So, what is Proverbs 24:15, 16 trying to tell us?
Well, basically, that when a wicked person experiences calamity,
he’s conquered; he will not get up.
But that is not the case for a righteous one.
A righteous person will get up;
he will not give up.
He will overcome calamity,
and he will become prosperous again.
In fact, verse 15, in effect, says:
‘Don’t even try to set a trap for the righteous one
‘because no matter how hard you knock him down,
he’s going to get up again.’
Now, why?
Why is it that the righteous one gets up?
Is it because he’s just so strong and he’s just so personally resilient?
No.
I want you to look at the cross reference
for Proverbs 24:16.
Do you see the scripture?
It’s Psalm 34:19.
Now, here the psalmist David expresses a similar thought
to what we just read here in Proverbs,
but he adds an important detail.
That verse says: “Many are the hardships
“[or if you look at the footnote, “calamities”]
“of the righteous one,
but Jehovah rescues him from them all.”
So Jehovah helps the righteous one to get up.
In fact, if we go back to that March 15, 2013, Watchtower,
where it commented on Proverbs 24:16, it said:
“Jehovah will not allow those trusting in him
“to stumble or to experience a fall
“—[that is] an adversity or a setback in their worship—
from which they cannot recover.”
Well, now, brothers, what does that mean?
Does it mean that somehow Jehovah is going to intervene miraculously
every time one of his servants experiences calamity?
No.
But Jehovah has taught his righteous ones
what they need to do in times of calamity.
They know that they must ‘keep on seeking first God’s Kingdom
and God’s righteousness,’
as Matthew 6:33 says.
And so, what does the righteous one do when calamity comes?
You see, it doesn’t stop the righteous one from praying;
it doesn’t stop him from attending meetings
or talking to others about his faith.
No, he keeps on doing what pleases Jehovah,
even in the face of calamity.
And doing what is right
is what helps him to recover
from whatever calamity may come upon him.
Now, the apostle Paul
is a wonderful example of the truth of this principle.
Let’s look in 2 Corinthians chapter 11,
and let’s just remind ourselves
of some of the calamities that came upon the apostle Paul.
Second Corinthians chapter 11
—let’s begin reading in verse 23.
Paul says: “Are they ministers of Christ?
“I reply like a madman, I am more outstandingly one:
“I have done more work, been imprisoned more often,
“suffered countless beatings, and experienced many near-deaths.
“Five times I received 40 strokes less one from the Jews,
“three times I was beaten with rods,
“once I was stoned,
“three times I experienced shipwreck,
“a night and a day I have spent in the open sea;
“in journeys often, in dangers from rivers,
“in dangers from robbers, in dangers from my own people,
“in dangers from the nations, in dangers in the city,
“in dangers in the wilderness, in dangers at sea,
“in dangers among false brothers,
“in labor and toil, in sleepless nights often,
“in hunger and thirst, frequently without food,
in cold and lacking clothing.”
Well, now, brothers, honestly,
many people would’ve been conquered
by just one of those things, isn’t it true?
But Paul kept getting up; he kept getting up and going on.
And what was his conclusion?
Well, just read it in 2 Corinthians chapter 4,
and look here at verse 8.
Paul says: “We are hard-pressed in every way,
“but not cramped beyond movement;
“we are perplexed, but not absolutely with no way out;
we are persecuted but not abandoned.”
And now notice this one:
“We are knocked down, but not destroyed.
“Always we endure in our body
“the death-dealing treatment that Jesus suffered,
“that the life of Jesus may also be made manifest
in our body.”
Did you see that?
“Knocked down [knocked down],
but not destroyed.”
Righteous Paul was not destroyed
by the adverse experiences that came to him.
He didn’t allow calamity to stop him
from giving that next witness,
from offering that next prayer to Jehovah,
from taking advantage of the next opportunity
to meet with his brothers.
You see, that’s what a righteous person does.
He keeps on seeking Jehovah
and seeking to please him.
And because Paul did that,
he was always able to get up
with the help of Jehovah.
But now, brothers, that’s true for Paul,
but it’s also true for every one
of God’s faithful and righteous servants
all around this earth.
I’d like to introduce to you
three different faithful servants of Jehovah
who have also experienced the truth
of Proverbs 24:16.
This is Brother Michael Legaspi
from the Philippines.
When Typhoon Haiyan struck in 2013,
Michael went with his wife and his young son
to the Kingdom Hall in Tacloban City to seek shelter.
There had been many typhoons before.
This was not an unusual event in the Philippines,
but this time, there was something different.
This was the first time in recent memory
that there was a storm surge
—a wall of water 15 feet high,
or four and a half meters high,
that struck the Kingdom Hall.
The walls and the roof collapsed.
Michael worked very, very hard
to try to rescue his wife
and the other brothers and sisters
who were trapped under the debris.
But sadly, his wife had already perished.
Then, in the water by this time,
he heard his son cry out to him:
“Papa! Papa!”
He reached out, and he grabbed him in the water.
But because of his exhaustion
from already helping the brothers to escape
from under the debris
and because of the cold temperature of the water,
he became unconscious.
And when he woke up, his son was gone;
he too had perished in this storm.
Well, at first,
Michael was inconsolable.
He blamed himself.
He felt that there was something more
that he could have done to save them.
But the elders shepherded him.
They helped him to see that there was nothing that he could have done.
The storm was beyond the power of any man.
But even in those difficult times,
Michael continued with his spiritual program.
He continued to serve as an elder
and as a regular pioneer.
The brothers encouraged him,
“Why don’t you begin to volunteer at the disaster relief center?”
The whole area was completely devastated;
all the homes had been destroyed.
Michael got busy
and worked to help rebuild
the homes of the local brothers.
And when that work was finished, he enrolled as a construction volunteer,
working with a group of brothers
building Kingdom Halls within the region.
And then when that work was complete,
he volunteered to help a congregation
that was quite a distance away.
It required him to travel one and a half hours
each way by motorcycle.
But he was willing to do it
because the congregation needed the help of an elder.
Well, now, here is Michael today
—busy and active in Jehovah’s service.
Just like all righteous ones,
Michael kept doing Jehovah’s will
despite the terrible calamity that he experienced.
Now, what do you think, brothers?
Do you think Michael got up?
This is Teymur Akhmedov
who lives in Kazakhstan.
In 2017, Teymur was arrested
on a false charge of inciting religious hatred.
After being in pretrial detention for three months,
Teymur was sentenced to a five-year prison term.
Before his arrest,
Teymur was being treated for cancer.
When he was arrested, his treatment stopped,
and the disease began to progress.
Now, you talk about calamity.
Not only was he in prison because of his faith
but he also had to deal with life-threatening cancer at the same time.
After being held for 13 months,
Teymur was finally allowed to go to another city for medical care.
Now, here you see Teymur after surgery in his hospital bed,
but you notice he’s chained,
both at the arm and at the leg.
After the courts had rejected multiple appeals to have Teymur released,
it appeared that it was impossible.
All options had been exhausted.
Yet Teymur was told at this point,
“You can be released if you’re willing to sign a confession.”
The authorities told him to write out
that he had made a mistake in speaking to other people about his beliefs
and that he was now sorry for his actions.
Teymur absolutely refused.
He told the authorities that he would rather sit in prison
with a clear conscience
than be released with a guilty one.
Well, by Jehovah’s undeserved kindness,
after fourteen and a half months in prison,
the president of Kazakhstan gave Teymur
a full pardon without any admission of guilt,
and he was released.
Here you see Teymur in a recent photo taken with his dear wife.
What was it that helped Teymur to get up
despite imprisonment
and dealing with a life-threatening illness?
This is what he said:
“We each have a choice
“—whether to stand by God’s principles or to ignore them.
“If we stand by God’s principles,
then we can get through any test successfully.”
Teymur overcame the adversity, would you agree?
He truly got up.
This is Sister Laura French.
She began Bethel service
on May 1, 1926.
She was part of this small Bethel family
in Canada,
made up of less than 20 persons.
About 1936,
it became apparent that the branch servant in Canada
was an apostate.
In time, the matter was investigated.
And although Sister French was not involved with the apostasy,
she had been a roommate with one of the sisters
who was working closely with the branch servant.
Thus, she was wrongly viewed
as one of his supporters.
And so on May 1, 1936,
she was among a group of seven Bethelites
who were dismissed from Bethel, along with the branch servant.
What did Sister French do?
She never complained.
She did not say that it was unfair, or unjust,
although she said that initially she was hurt.
She decided that the best remedy
would be to go on serving Jehovah.
She said, “After leaving Bethel,
“I had four marvelous years
in the pioneer service.”
The first two years,
she and another sister lived in a tent
while preaching in a large area
where there were no congregations
of Jehovah’s people.
Later, she and her pioneer partner
worked from a house car.
These faithful sisters
truly worked hard for Jehovah.
Well, in 1940, Sister French came to Toronto
for a short vacation
when suddenly the ban on Jehovah’s Witnesses struck.
To her surprise and delight,
she was invited to come and work at the underground branch office.
And with the approval of Brother Rutherford,
Sister French returned to Bethel service
and continued to serve there
until she finished her earthly course
on December 23, 1990.
At the end of her earthly life,
she said she was so happy
that she had decided to go pioneering
when she was dismissed from Bethel.
Of that group who were dismissed,
she was the only one
who continued to serve Jehovah faithfully.
Sister French kept doing the right thing,
even when she was misjudged by others.
She overcame an unjust situation;
she overcame that adversity; she truly got up.
Do you agree?
Well, brothers, what have we learned
from considering this principle
at Proverbs 24:16?
When calamity strikes,
you truly may feel knocked down.
You may not know the details
of exactly how everything is going to work out,
but you will always know what to do next.
You will know how to pray;
you’ll know to go to that next meeting;
you’ll know to go out in the ministry;
you’ll know to always make decisions
that will please Jehovah.
And as you do so,
Jehovah will show you the way to move on
and to get up from any calamity that you might face.
That was true of the apostle Paul.
That was true of Michael Legaspi.
It was true of Teymur Akhmedov.
It was true of Laura French.
And it will be true for all of you.
Remember this:
When calamity knocks you down,
seek Jehovah, and you’ll rebound.
What does the principle say?
‘For though the righteous one
‘may fall seven times,
he will get up again.’
And with that confidence in your hearts,
may you go to your assignments
with all of our love
and with the rich blessing
of our marvelous and amazing God, Jehovah.
Well, that brings us now to the point in our program
for the presentation of the diplomas,
and I will be assisted in this by our dear Brother Kenneth Flodin.
The first couple is Brother and Sister Aggarwal.
They’ll be returning to India.
And we have Brother Batsaikhan, who will go back to Mongolia.
Brother and Sister Chiposa will return to Zambia.
Brother and Sister Cicio are going back to Romania.
Brother and Sister Dhillon are returning to India.
And now we have Brother and Sister Drabysheuski,
who are going back to Finland.
Brother and Sister Dredge will be returning to Thailand.
And this is Brother and Sister Habiyaremye.
They’re going back to Rwanda.
Brother Horváth is going back to Hungary.
And Brother Jerczyński is going to Poland.
And this is Brother and Sister LaFrancois,
and they will now be serving in Korea.
Brother and Sister Locquiao are going to the Philippines.
Brother and Sister Ludlow are going to be returning to Myanmar.
And Brother and Sister Mkulichi will be returning to Malawi.
And Brother and Sister Morgan will now be serving in Kenya.
And we have Sister Palma.
She’ll be returning to the Philippines.
Brother and Sister Perron will now be serving in Senegal.
Brother and Sister Purnomo will be going to India—no, Indonesia.
I was influenced by the video.
And Brother and Sister Sandoval will now be going to Spain.
Brother Sasaki will be returning to Japan.
And Brother and Sister Sendall will be going back to Trinidad and Tobago.
Brother and Sister Sivakumaran will be returning to Sri Lanka.
And now we have Brother and Sister Wilson,
and they’re going to be assigned to Congo (Kinshasa).
Brother and Sister Woosley —they’ll now be assigned to Asia.
And now we have our final couple —Brother and Sister Zenonos.
They’ll be going to Greece.
We want to thank Brother Flodin
for caring for all those names for me.
It’s such a big help.
Well, now it’s a pleasure to present to you
the graduates of the 146th class of Gilead.
And the class has a letter that will now be read,
and Brother Philip Morgan will do that for us.
“To the Governing Body and the United States Bethel family.
“Over the course of the past five months,
“more than ever before,
“we have been tuned to the evidence of Jehovah’s powerful holy spirit
“all around us.
“From the day we entered the main lobby here at the Watchtower Educational Center,
“the fruitage of that spirit enveloped us
“with love and kindness
“through the hospitality of the United States Bethel family.
“Without your daily help and encouragement,
“we would not have been able to give such concentrated focus to our studies.
“We thank you all from the bottom of our hearts!
“We also have sensed how our instructors
“have striven to allow the holy spirit to shape and mold them,
“even as they shared the benefits of their own deep study of God’s Word
“and experience with us each day in the classroom.
“Just like those Jehovah used to train others in the past,
“they imparted to us not only the finer points of the truth
“but ‘[their] very souls.’
“They ‘became . . . beloved to us,’ even as we know we are to them.
“Perhaps most touching has been the personal attention
“shown to us by you dear brothers of the Governing Body.
“The evidence of Jehovah’s spirit working through you
“is something we will cherish for the rest of our lives.
“We realize how much concern you carry with you
“for the entire association of our brothers worldwide,
“as well as for the many sheeplike ones
“yet to be reached with the Kingdom good news.
“We especially appreciated the fact
“that you each took time to spend with our class
“and spoke to us as a father to children to reassure us,
“to protect us with reminders,
“and to build confidence that Jehovah will be with us in the days ahead.
“And you sent many of your helpers to do just the same,
“which we deeply appreciated.
“The apostle Paul reminded his anointed brothers
“that ‘where the spirit of Jehovah is, there is freedom.’
“Now more than ever, we see evidence of how true that is.
“By means of his faithful slave, the Gilead arrangement,
“and this beautiful Bethel family,
“Jehovah has used his spirit
“to free us from any inhibitions,
“fears, or hesitations.
“We feel more prepared to accomplish whatever work he assigns
“by relying on that most powerful force in the universe
“—God’s holy spirit.
“Along with the rest of God’s family of servants,
“heavenly and earthly,
“we are ready to follow the leading of that spirit
“wherever it will send us in the days ahead!
“With heartfelt love,
“we are your brothers and sisters
of the 146th class of Gilead.”
Graduates —that has a nice sound to it, doesn’t it?
It came quickly.
Well, I’ve been asked to give a few comments here at the end
and to include this point, so I’ll begin with it:
Back in 2011,
the Governing Body adjusted the objective of Gilead training
in order to help further strengthen and stabilize
the field and branch organization.
And as a result,
we have seen Jehovah’s rich blessing on this adjustment
as it relates to branch and country committees worldwide.
Since the time of the graduation of the 132nd class,
182 graduates have been appointed to a committee,
either during or sometime after their training at Gilead.
That’s a wonderful fact, isn’t it?
And it’s something that is really proving to be a blessing
to the worldwide field and to our dear brotherhood and, above all,
in upholding and honoring Jehovah’s name.
So this is a marvelous arrangement.
Now with this in mind, just for a couple of minutes,
I want to give concluding comments on this topic:
“Maintain Your ‘Shield of Faith.’”
You see, when you are settled into your assignments
—perhaps with new responsibilities—
remember to remain watchful
so that you stay focused on what is most important,
namely, the doing of Jehovah’s will.
The danger can come when we feel that we’ve achieved most
or even all of our spiritual goals.
If we allow that to happen,
our interests could turn to other things.
For example, if we lose sight of the point
and the purpose behind what it means to follow Jesus,
we could start to center our thoughts on other goals (it could happen),
perhaps even material things.
But don’t let this happen to you.
Keep your shield of faith strong.
In Bible times,
soldiers repaired and secured their shields between battles.
They treasured those protective pieces of armor.
Because their shields were often covered with leather,
the soldiers would rub oil on to the shield to help preserve it
and to keep the metal parts free from rust.
If a soldier found damage or weakness, what did he do?
He immediately made the needed repairs to his shield.
In this way, he was always ready for the next battle.
We need to keep this up in a spiritual way.
Over time, a brother or sister
might lay down his or her shield of faith
and go after things that have no lasting value.
The Devil wants nothing more than for us to neglect our faith
and open up our heart to his attacks.
And for this reason,
Paul, the apostle Paul, was inspired to say
that those who go after material riches, for instance,
would cultivate “many senseless and harmful desires.”
He added: “Flee from these things.”
You see, ultimately, we are each responsible for how large
and how strong our shield of faith proves to be.
Now, we show that we are strengthening
our faith in Jehovah and his Son
when we take time to continue caring for our spiritual needs.
So don’t take liberties with your spiritual routine
just because you’ve graduated from this wonderful school.
Don’t become self-satisfied
because of resting on a privilege you may come to enjoy.
That’s not the point of it, is it?
Keep growing as a spiritual person
by giving attention to your faith day by day.
Oil and preserve your shield
by regularly attending Christian meetings
and speaking about Jehovah’s name and his Kingdom to others.
Also, maintain strong faith by reading God’s Word every day
—as you’ve been encouraged to and have been doing—
and applying its counsel in all that you do.
Imitate the Christ every step of the way.
In this way, you’ll be like the victorious soldier who worked hard
to care for his shield and other valuable pieces of armor.
Hold your shield firmly in front of you.
Use it to protect your figurative heart
and to defend Jehovah’s pure worship.
Keep it well maintained,
and you will always be ready to “fight the fine fight of the faith.”
Jehovah and his Son will bless you for it.

cn.text: 现在，到了发表毕业典礼主旨演讲的时候了
讲题是《正义的人一定会重新站起来》
这个演讲会由中央长老团成员
马克·桑德森弟兄发表
各位亲爱的毕业生
今天也许是你们一生中最快乐的一天
你们的确有理由开心
因为你们多年来忠心耿耿
以敬奉耶和华为一生的事业
今天是个重要的里程碑
但现在我不得不泼点冷水
我想说几句现实的话
你们前头的日子
不可能每一天都像今天这么开心
为什么这么说呢？
因为这个世界是受撒但统治的
而且我们生活在最后的日子里
难免会有忧虑甚至恐惧
生活中有许许多多的“万一”
“万一”这个词
会让我们想到各种各样的可能性
也许令人担忧害怕
对各位毕业生来说
你们担心的可能是
万一我学不会新的语言怎么办？
万一我适应不了新的文化呢？
万一我回到原来的地方
换到意想不到的岗位，怎么办？
这可能是毕业生的忧虑
至于在场的听众
以及在JW电视网观看这个节目的观众
你们担心的可能是
万一我受到反对
甚至遭遇严峻的迫害，怎么办？
万一发生天灾呢？
万一我得了重病呢？
万一死亡夺去亲人或朋友的生命呢？
这一切听起来只是假设
但其实世界各地的很多弟兄姐妹
正在面对这样的情况
对他们来说
这些事不是万一发生
而是正在发生
弟兄姐妹，我们正生活在最后的日子
一个“难以应付的非常时期”
所以我们会经历患难
这是毫无疑问的
但有另一点同样是毫无疑问的
是不变的真理
而且没有万一
这个真理适用于每一个正义的人
每一个忠心敬奉耶和华的人
谨记这个真理
会让我们充满信心和勇气
什么真理呢？
请大家打开圣经
我们一起来看一下箴言24章
请大家留意
箴言中的很多道理
其实都是用两节连续的经文来说明的
现在我们从15节看起
经文警告说
“不可作恶伏击义人的居所
也不要抢掠他安歇的地方。”
为什么呢？
为什么不要攻击正义的人呢？
我们来看看理由
理由就是以下这个不变的真理
“义人跌倒七次，也必起来
恶人却要遭灾，一蹶不振。”
现在我们来分析一下这节经文
经文想说明什么呢？
首先看看“跌倒”是什么意思
《守望台》2013年3月15日刊
对箴言24:16作了解释
文章谈到
“跌倒”有遭遇挫折的意思
有一份参考资料说
“跌倒”也可以指实际摔倒或者绊倒
但请注意
“跌倒”也可以比喻遭遇灾难或重创
而经文说的就是这个意思
那么“起来”是什么意思呢？
同一份参考资料说
“‘起来’可以指摔倒后爬起来
但在这节经文里
‘起来’是比喻克服困难
振作起来，苦尽甘来。”
为什么是七次呢？
这份参考资料说
“很多译本都按字面意思译作‘七次’
但在这里
‘七’表达的很可能是
希伯来语词的象征意义
也就是‘完全’。”
因此，有一个译本把这节经文译作
“正直的人无论跌倒多少次
总能重新站起来”。
《圣经当代译本》这样翻译
“不要像恶人一样暗算义人
破坏他的家
因为义人跌倒七次也必起来
恶人却被灾祸击垮。”
就彻底完了
想要告诉我们什么呢？
就是灾祸降临在恶人身上
他就会被打垮，再也站不起来
正义的人却不一样
正义的人一定会重新站起来
不会放弃
他会克服逆境
重新振作，苦尽甘来
其实15节就等于在说
“你设圈套陷害正义的人是没有用的
因为不管你想出什么方法要把他打垮
他还是会重新站起来。”
为什么呢？
正义的人为什么能重新站起来呢？
是因为他特别坚强，个性特别坚韧吗？
不是
请大家看看箴言24:16的参考经文
看到了吗？
就是诗篇34:19
执笔者大卫表达了跟箴言类似的意思
但补充了一个很重要的细节
经文说
“义人多灾多难
［也就是遭遇打击或重创］
但耶和华救他脱离这一切。”
所以，是耶和华帮助正义的人重新振作的
如果我们回到《守望台》
2013年3月15日刊的文章
就会看到箴言24:16的解释
文章说
“信赖耶和华的人就算跌倒了
在信仰上遭遇挫折
耶和华也不会让他们一蹶不振
不能复原。”
这句话是什么意思呢？
是不是说，每当上帝的仆人遭遇患难
耶和华就会施行奇迹，出手相救呢？
不是的
不过，耶和华已经告诉正义的人
在遭遇患难的时候，他们应该怎么做
他们知道必须要先追求
上帝的王国和他的正义
就像马太福音6:33说的一样
那么，当灾祸来到的时候
正义的人会怎么做呢？
正义的人会继续祷告
继续参加聚会
继续跟别人谈论自己的信仰
患难阻挠不了正义的人
患难阻挠不了他们
他会继续做耶和华喜欢的事
不会被困难吓倒
帮助他重新站起来的关键是
无论陷入什么困境
他都继续做对的事
使徒保罗的经历
充分印证了这个不变的真理
那我们一起打开圣经
我们看看哥林多后书第11章
看看使徒保罗遭遇过的一些患难
请大家打开哥林多后书第11章
我们先来看看第23节
看看在这里保罗经历了哪些患难呢？
保罗说:“他们是基督的仆人吗？
我要狂妄地说，我更是
我比他们劳苦更多，下狱更多
被人拷打过多
时常险死还生
我被犹太人打过五次
每次四十减一下
我被杖打过三次
被石头打过一次
遭遇海难三次
一日一夜在深海漂浮
我时常远行
历经江河的危险
强盗的危险
同族的危险
外邦的危险
城里的危险
旷野的危险
海上的危险
假弟兄的危险
劳苦艰辛，不眠不寐
又饥又渴，多次缺粮
赤身挨冷。”
各位弟兄姐妹，坦白地说
很多人就算遭遇其中一种患难
也可能被打垮了
不是吗？
但保罗每一次都重新站起来
不但站起来，还继续向前
保罗的结论是什么呢？
让我们看看哥林多后书第4章
从第8节看起
“我们四面受压
却不致陷于绝境
心里迷惘，却不致走投无路
受迫害，却没有被弃。”
请留意下一句
“倒下来
却没有灭亡
我们随时随地身受死亡的威胁
就像耶稣所遭遇的一样
这样
耶稣的一生也就体现在我们身上了。”
经文怎么说呢？
“倒下来[倒下来]，却没有灭亡。”
正义的保罗没有被这些患难打垮
他没有因为这些患难就不再向人传道
不再向耶和华祷告
不再抓紧机会跟弟兄姐妹聚在一起
请看，正义的人就是这样的
他继续寻求耶和华
继续做耶和华喜欢的事
正因为保罗这样做
他每一次都能靠着耶和华的帮助
重新站起来
亲爱的弟兄姐妹们
保罗站起来了
同样，世界各地
每个忠心敬奉耶和华的正义的人
也都重新站起来了
我想给大家介绍三个
忠贞敬奉耶和华的弟兄姐妹
他们的经历也印证了箴言24:16的话
首先，我们来看看第一个经历
这位弟兄来自菲律宾
他的名字叫迈克尔·莱加斯皮

ko.text: 외국 임지에서 일하는 특별 전 시간 종들이
그들의 여행을 지원하는 업무가 광범위하게 진행되고 있습니다.
이 업무에서 세계 본부에 있는 여행 지원부는 어떤 역할을 합니까?
과거에는 여행 지원 업무가 어떻게 진행되었습니까?
과거 신권 조직에서 형제들이 어떤 방식으로 여행했는지 살펴보고,
올해 국제 대회에 참석할 특별 전 시간 종들에게 도움을 주기 위해
보이지 않는 곳에서 어떤 일들이 수행되는지 함께 보시죠.
여행은 우리 조직의 신권 활동에서 늘 중요한 자리를 차지해 왔습니다.
땅의 가장 먼 곳까지 이르러 나의 증인이 될 것입니다.”
러셀 형제는 먼저 미국 북동부 지역을 다녔고,
중국, 인도, 일본, 필리핀 등 여러 나라를 여행했죠.
1914년에는 300여 명의 형제들이 당시 그들의 표현을 빌리자면
세계 모든 도시와 지역으로 파견되어 성서 강연을 했습니다.
러더퍼드 형제와 노어 형제도 광범위한 지역을 여행하면서
조직은 매년 수백 명의 형제 자매들을 학교로 초대하고
어느 날 전화를 한 통 받았는데
10층으로 가서 노어 형제를 만나 보라고 하더군요.
그런 얘기를 들으면 보통 긴장이 되게 마련이지만
저는 크게 잘못한 게 없다고 생각했어요.
노어 형제는 제게 사무실로 와서 일해 주면 좋겠다고 하면서
선교인들의 비자 업무를 처리하는 데스크 일을 맡아 달라고 했죠.
호화로운 여객선이 아니라 화물선을 타고 임지로 떠났죠.
그런 배를 타고 가면 시간이 많이 걸렸지만
대부분의 형제들은 비행기를 타고 임지로 갈 수 있게 되었습니다.
지부들의 수가 점점 늘어나자 노어 형제는
해외의 지부들을 방문해야겠다는 생각을 하게 되었죠.
그래서 그 데스크가 항공편 업무를 담당하는
여행 안내 데스크 역할을 하게 되었어요.
세계 본부의 여행 지원부에서 맡게 되었습니다.
특별 전 시간 종들이 다른 나라로 가는 여행,
즉 치료를 받거나 길르앗을 비롯한 신권 학교에 참석하거나
그 밖의 많은 이유로 해외로 가는 여행을 지원합니다.
지금까지 약 80개 지부에 그런 도움을 줄 수 있었죠.
여행 지원부는 소중한 헌금을 절약하기 위해
싸게 잘 샀다는 생각에 기분이 좋습니다.
왼쪽에 앉은 사람과 이야기를 나눠 보니
여행 지원부는 컴퓨터 예약 프로그램을 활용해서,
일단 중간 가격대의 표를 예매해 둔 뒤
저렴한 표를 찾으려고 몇 주 동안 검색하기도 해요.
여러 달 동안 노력해서 결국 표를 찾아낸 적도 있죠.
형제 자매들이 기부한 항공사 마일리지로 표를 사기도 해요.
세계 곳곳의 형제 자매들을 위해 표를 많이 예약하다 보니
항공사나 협력 업체들이 할인을 해 주기도 해요.
그 덕분에 더 저렴한 가격에 표를 사거나,
수화물 혜택을 받거나, 수수료 없이 탑승 일자를 변경할 수 있죠.
더 저렴한 가격을 계속 확인해 주는 프로그램 덕분에
출발하는 날까지도 더 싼 표를 찾아 볼 수 있죠.
리워드 포인트 기부라는 이 마련 덕분에
여행 관련 비용을 절감할 수 있습니다.
그냥 사라져 버릴 수 있었던 마일리지 덕분에
그 덕분에 조직에서는 헌금을 약 800만 원이나 절약할 수 있었죠.
호텔 포인트도 잘 활용하여 헌금을 절약하고 있습니다.
대회에 참석하거나 베델을 방문할 계획을 하는 형제 자매들은
객실을 제공하는 호텔 목록을 받게 되죠.
그 포인트를 활용하면 여행에 드는 비용을 줄일 수 있죠.
하느님의 종들은 여러 신권 대회들을 통해
그렇게 해서 큰 축복을 주는 연례 대회 마련이 시작되었습니다.
50여 년이 흐른 지금도 대회의 규모는 계속 커지고 있습니다.
대표자들은 할인된 가격으로 호텔과 항공권을 예약할 수 있죠.
현지 형제 자매들과 함께하는 야외 봉사와 환영 행사에 더해,
현지 지부 사무실에서 제안하는 다양한 활동도 선택할 수 있는데요.
관광 명소 방문 등을 신청할 수 있습니다.
베델에서 마련한 웹사이트에 들어가서 항공편을 검색하고
세계 본부의 여행 지원부에 제출하면 그에 따라 처리가 됩니다.
이제 선교인들은 가족과 친구들을 만나 행복한 시간을 보내고
대회를 통해 영적으로 새 힘을 얻는 데 온전히 집중할 수 있죠.
먼 곳에서 오는 선교인들을 만날 날을 손꼽아 기다리고 있습니다.
올해 국제 대회가 정말 기대되지 않으십니까?
분명 하느님의 조직은 끝이 오기 전에
땅의 가장 먼 곳까지 계속 여행하면서

cn.text: 许多人都知道
为了协助在外国服务的特別全时仆人
参加2019年举行的国际大会
有很多的工作要做
在这些安排中
世界总部的差旅部扮演了什么角色？
他们怎样节省花费？
以往的旅程是怎样安排的？
以下的报告
不仅能帮助我们明白过去弟兄们
为了上帝的组织怎样安排旅程
还能让我们一窥今年国际大会幕后的筹备工作
为了完成上帝组织的工作
耶和华的子民经常需要旅行
耶稣在使徒行传1:8说
他的门徒会做他的见证人，直到地极
1880年，罗素弟兄跟随耶稣的榜样
展开了传道旅行
一开始，罗素弟兄先拜访美国东北的各州
然后展开了国际旅行
1911年，他前往中国、印度
日本和菲律宾等地，旅程长达5万6000公里
1914年，有超过300位弟兄
被派到当时他们认识的世界的每个角落
发表圣经演讲
卢述福弟兄与诺尔弟兄也同样到处旅行
鼓励各地的信徒
后来，1943年基列学校成立
每年都会邀请上百位学生接受培训
然后派他们到世界各地做特派传道员
有一天，我接到一通电话
要我去十楼见诺尔弟兄
这通常会让人感到有点不安
但我知道自己并没有犯什么严重的错
结果，诺尔弟兄告诉我
我们想派你来楼上的办公室工作
负责照料特派传道员的签证事宜
协助他们抵达获派的地区
在1950年代，飞机票相当昂贵
所以大多数特派传道员都是搭船
而且不是搭豪华邮轮，而是货船
他们都不介意搭乘较慢的船前往获派的地方
后来飞机票变便宜了
大部分的弟兄可以搭飞机到获派的地方
当各地分部纷纷成立后
诺尔弟兄看出他必须探访这些分部
所以当时我工作的事务处
就成了差旅事务处，负责安排机票
我们为弟兄安排旅行的工作
就是这样开始的
当然后来工作也变得更多
从2013年起，这项不断扩展的任务
由世界总部差旅部继续执行
要安排哪些旅程呢？
比如特別全时仆人的跨国任务、到国外就医
参加基列学校和其他训练班
还有很多其他的事
目前我们已经协助了
来自约80个分部的弟兄姐妹
世界总部差旅部是怎样节省大量捐款的呢？
想象你在飞机上
很高兴自己只花了500美元买机票
在跟左边的人聊天后
你发现他花了800美元，所以更沾沾自喜了
接著，你却发现右边的人只花了300美元
这正是旅行的现实情况
世界总部差旅部使用全球订票系统
努力避免购买较贵的机票
我们会先预订中间价格的机票
然后再搜索最便宜的
有时候要花好几个星期才能等到机票降价
我曾经花了几个月的时间找便宜的票
最后终于找到了！
我们也会用捐赠的飞行里程和积分来购买机票
我们为世界各地的弟兄姐妹预订了大量机票
所以能取得航空公司和供应商提供的折扣
这样我们就能买到优惠的机票
和额外的托运行李额度，还能免费更改日期
我们也使用许多自动系统
比如说，即使在买好机票后
我们也有一个程序
可以在出发前继续搜寻较低的票价
从2016年开始
美国的弟兄姐妹可以通过jw.org网站
捐赠饭店点数
飞行里程和积分
以及礼券
这个捐赠安排帮助我们节省了旅行的花费
一对夫妻决心简化生活，捐出了许多飞行里程
这让我们省下了好几千美元
而他们的点数也不会白白浪费掉
伯特利的一对夫妻
捐出超过20万的个人飞行里程
结果帮组织省下了7000美元
除了机票，组织也善用饭店的积分点数
省下了不少捐款
弟兄姐妹计划参加大会或参观伯特利时
弟兄们经常会提供协商好房价的饭店名单
正如经常搭飞机的人能累积里程数
组织也能得到饭店的积分点数
然后再依照旅行需求在世界各地运用
有超过100年的时间
区域大会都为上帝的仆人
带来了鼓励、欢欣和喜乐
1886年《守望台》邀请读者
在耶稣受难纪念聚会之后参加为期三天的大会
这为以后每年大会的美好安排开了先河
1922年，俄亥俄州杉树角举行了划时代的大会
有美国和来自欧洲的人参加
截至1950年，有67个国家地区的代表参加大会
到了1958年，大会代表来自123个国家地区
50多年后，这个数字仍在持续增长
2018年8月，各地会众收到通知
2019年国际大会将分別在24个地点举行
这次大会代表的数目是有史以来最多的
我们要协助他们安排旅程
弟兄姐妹获选为大会代表后
就可以登入jw2019.org
这个网站是在教导委员会督导下设立的
大会代表能以优惠价预订饭店和机票
除了当中一天参加传道
一个晚上跟当地的弟兄姐妹一起聚餐
分部也安排了一些活动让大会代表报名参加
例如参观分部办事处，或是游览当地景点
我们也为上千个特派传道员
和其他全时仆人作了类似的安排
他们可以使用一个特別的网站
搜寻机票、挑选行程
并将选择提交给世界总部差旅部处理
然后，这些特派传道员
就能快乐地和家人、朋友
一起专注于振奋人心的大会了
我们所有人都期待
见到这些远道而来的特派传道员
有了国际大会，这一年更令人兴奋！
毫无疑问，上帝的组织会继续走遍地极
达成上帝的旨意，直到终结来到

ko.text: 그때 바울은 로마에서 첫 번째로 감금되어
바울이 골로새에 간 적이 없었다는 것을 알 수 있습니다.
그곳 회중은 에바브라가 열심히 활동한 결과로 세워진 것 같습니다.
하지만 바울은 그 회중의 몇몇 성원들을 알고 있었습니다.
회중 성원들을 잘못된 길로 인도하려고 했습니다.
하느님에 관한 정확한 지식을 계속 늘려 나가기를 바란다고 말합니다.
그분을 통해 ‘다른 모든 것이 창조’되었다고 말합니다.
모세 율법을 지켜야 한다고 주장하는 자들에 대해 경고합니다.
그는 하느님께서 모세 율법을 지워 버리셨음을 강조합니다.
그분은 그것을 그리스도의 형주에 못 박아 없애셨습니다.
바울과 바나바의 1차 선교 여행 때 한동안 그들과 동행했습니다.
하지만 마가는 그들을 떠나 예루살렘으로 돌아갔습니다.
둘 사이에 어떤 좋지 않은 감정이 있었든,
거기에는 그리스도께서 하느님의 오른편에 앉아 계십니다.”
‘옛 인간성을 벗어’ 버리고 “새 인간성”을 입으라고 권고합니다.
그러면 각 사람에게 어떻게 대답해야 할지 알게 될 것입니다.”
계속 늘려 나가는 것이 얼마나 중요한지,
어떻게 그리스도와 같은 인간성을 발전시킬 수 있는지,
은혜롭게 말하는 것, 특히 왕국의 좋은 소식을 선포할 때

en.text: An introduction to the book of Colossians.
The apostle Paul wrote this inspired letter
in Rome around 60 or 61 C.E.
This was during his first imprisonment there,
while he was under house arrest.
Paul’s letter to the Colossians indicates
that he had not visited Colossae.
Evidently, the congregation there
was the fruitage of the work of Epaphras.
Still, Paul knew several members of the congregation,
including Apphia, Archippus, and Philemon,
to whom he also wrote an inspired letter.
Some time after the congregation was founded,
false teachers tried to mislead the Colossian Christians
with deceptive philosophies.
Epaphras traveled many hundreds of miles
from Colossae to Rome
to give a report on the congregation to Paul.
The letter to the Colossians has four chapters.
In chapter 1, Paul expresses his desire
that the Colossians continue to grow in accurate knowledge of God.
Paul then describes God’s Son
as “the image of the invisible God,
the firstborn of all creation,”
and the one through whom “all other things were created.”
Christ is also the head of the congregation.
In chapter 2, the apostle warns the Colossians
about those who are promoting philosophies
and the observance of the Mosaic Law.
Paul stresses that the Mosaic Law
has been erased and taken out of the way.
God had figuratively nailed it to Christ’s torture stake.
Did you know?
At Colossians 4:10,
Paul mentions “Mark, the cousin of Barnabas.”
For a short time, Mark, also called John,
accompanied Paul and Barnabas on their first missionary tour.
But Mark left them and may have returned home to Jerusalem,
which disappointed Paul.
About 12 years later, however,
Mark was in Rome as Paul’s coworker.
Clearly, any breach between the two had been healed.
In chapter 3, Paul encourages the congregation
to “go on seeking the things above,
where the Christ is seated at the right hand of God.”
The apostle also exhorts the Colossians
to “strip off the old personality,”
to clothe themselves “with the new personality,”
and to continue “forgiving one another freely.”
In chapter 4, Paul tells the Colossians
to “persevere in prayer,” along with thanksgiving.
He also writes: “Let your words always be gracious,
“seasoned with salt,
so that you will know how you should answer each person.”
As you read the inspired letter to the Colossians,
note how we should continue to grow in accurate knowledge of God,
how we can cultivate a Christlike personality,
and how our speech should always be gracious,
especially as we proclaim the good news of God’s Kingdom.

cn.text: 使徒保罗在罗马时写下歌罗西书
时间大约是公元60至61年
保罗当时在罗马第一次被囚，软禁在家中
歌罗西书的内容显示
保罗写信时还没有去过歌罗西
歌罗西会众是在以巴弗的协助下成立的
不过，保罗认识那里的一些基督徒
例如亚菲亚、亚基布和腓利门
保罗曾受上帝启示，写信给腓利门
会众成立后不久
就有假导师提倡错误的道理
企图误导会众里的人
于是以巴弗不远千里
从歌罗西启程去罗马
向保罗报告歌罗西会众的情况
歌罗西书一共有4章
第1章，使徒保罗勉励歌罗西的基督徒
要继续吸收知识，确切认识上帝
保罗接着谈到
耶稣基督“是人看不见的上帝的形象”
是受造物中的“头生子”
上帝通过耶稣创造了万物
另外，耶稣也是会众的元首
第2章，保罗告诫歌罗西会众
要小心那些鼓吹哲学思想
或强求别人遵守摩西法典的人
保罗说明上帝已借着基督
把摩西法典废除了
仿佛把法典钉在苦刑柱上
你知道吗？
在歌罗西书4:10
保罗提到“巴拿巴的表弟马可”
马可又叫约翰
在第一次传道旅程时
马可曾陪伴保罗和巴拿巴一小段时间
但令保罗失望的是
马可突然离开他们，回耶路撒冷去了
大约12年后，马可在罗马陪伴保罗
显然，他们已经化解矛盾，再度并肩工作
第3章，保罗鼓励歌罗西的基督徒
要“继续追求天上的事
那里有基督坐在上帝的右边”
此外，使徒保罗也劝他们要“脱去旧品格”
并且“穿上新品格”
也要继续“彼此甘心宽恕”
第4章，保罗勉励他们“祷告要坚持不懈”
也要常常怀有感恩之心
保罗告诉歌罗西的基督徒
说话“应该总是仁慈体贴，仿佛用盐调味，
这样你们就知道应该怎样回应各人”
你读歌罗西书时，请留意
我们要不断吸收知识，确切认识上帝
基督徒要培养良好的品格
我们说话应该亲切有礼
尤其在分享上帝王国的信息时
更要留意这点

titles.cn: 歌罗西书简介

ko.text: 우리가 수년 전부터 무척 즐기고 있는 건데요.
루마니아에서 온 부부를 만나서 알아 보죠.
인도 지부에서 온 학생 네 분의 이야기를 듣고 나면
루마니아에서 온 이오누츠 치치오와 델리아 치치오 부부입니다.
루마니아에서 우리 활동이 어떻게 시작됐는지 설명해 주실까요?
네, 1949년에 공산 정권이 우리 활동을 금지했고,
두 분 다 가족이 진리를 받아들인 때가
사실, 할머닌 금지령 하에서 오랫동안 파이오니아를 하신 분이에요.
나중에 언니와 저와 여동생도 진리 안에서 컸습니다.
그래서 여동생과 저도 진리 안에서 자랐습니다.
두 분은 금지령 아래서 아이들로서 충실을 유지하셨네요.
금지령 하에서 집회에 참석했던 기억이 나시나요?
대문이랑 현관문을 잠그고 모든 창문의 커튼을 쳤죠.
우린 함께 모일 기회를 놓치고 싶지 않았어요.
다 같이 모였을 때 가장 안전하다고 느꼈죠.
그럼 두 분 가족이 집회에서 만나기도 했겠네요?
제 가족과 아내 가족은 서로 다른 그룹에 속해 있었거든요.
그 결과 증인들은 두 개의 큰 그룹으로 갈라졌습니다.
한쪽은 브루클린 세계 본부와 계속 연락을 취했는데,
하지만 두 그룹 다 계속 여호와를 섬겼습니다.
그러니까 두 분 다 여호와의 증인이었지만
그럼 한쪽이 다른 쪽을 배교자로 여기진 않았나요?
어느 날 밤 어머니가 주무시지 않고 연구를 하셨어요.
조직의 본부와 연결된 그룹으로 옮기기로 결정하셨어요.
그래서 제가 조직의 본부와 연합해 있는 그룹에서
한번은 우리 정원에 벌집을 놔 둔 적이 있어요.
우리도 벌처럼 부지런할 수 있다고 가르치셨어요.
금지령 아래서도 여호와를 바쁘게 섬길 수 있다고요.
집회 때 출판물이 금지됐는데 뭘로 공부하셨죠?
집회 때 집중을 잘하지 않으면 안됐겠군요.
혹시 더 큰 규모로 같이 모일 기회는 없었나요?
당시에 우리는 대회를 열 수는 없었지만,
장례식, 결혼식, 야유회는 가질 수 있었죠.
어릴 때 함께 모여 노래를 외우던 기억이 납니다.
여호와의 증인이라는 우리의 신분을 숨기지는 않았거든요.
이를테면 집회나, 전도 봉사, 출판물 등이요.
두 분은 학교에서 꿋꿋하게 충실을 유지하셨군요.
그럼 갈라진 두 그룹은 어떻게 됐죠?
금지령 없이 영적 일과를 즐길 수 있으니까요.
하지만 절대 잊지 못할 교훈도 얻었습니다.
우린 늘 사탄의 공격을 받는단 거죠.
어떤 형제들은 금지령 때는 충실을 유지했는데
사탄도 우리를 공격할 새로운 전략을 모색하는 거죠.
지금 루마니아에는 4만 명이 넘는 증인이 있습니다.
루마니아의 활동을 보여 주는 동영상이 있는데,
그들은 양의 탈을 쓰고 여러분에게 오지만,
얼마나 위장을 잘 했던지 일부는 장로가 되어
많은 수의 형제들이 누구를 신뢰해야 할지 몰라,
하느님의 왕국의 좋은 소식을 전하는 일을
그 일은 영적 수확을 하기에 무르익은,
이안 플로리안 형제와 테투 빈두 형제는
본부와 연합된 주 조직에 속한 회중에
현재 그들은 한 회중에서 함께 장로로 섬기고 있죠.
세계적인 가족에 속한 사람만이 느낄 수 있는 감정이죠.
현재 두 사람은 함께 연합하여 섬기며,
그들의 풍부한 경험은 젊은 사람들에게 유익이 되죠.
전도인 수가 거의 두 배로 늘었습니다.
좋은 소식을 전하는 일을 하고 있습니다.
사용한 교활한 계략은 모두 수포로 돌아갔습니다.
현재 루마니아의 형제 자매들은 여호와의 축복으로
금지령 아래서 큰 용기와 믿음으로 충절을 지켰군요.
치치오 형제와 자매, 두 분의 경험 감사합니다.
인도에서 무려 네 분의 학생을 모셨습니다.
네, 인도엔 영어 회중이 여러 개 있어요.
우선, 인도에서 전파 활동이 어떻게 시작됐는지
이름이 에이 제이 조셉이란 남자가 있었는데,
그런데 누가 러셀 형제가 쓴 책들을 주었고,
인도에서 활동을 정착시키는 데 큰 역할을 했습니다.
네, 사실 1912년에 러셀 형제가 인도를 방문했죠.
한 마을에선 사람들이 실제로 마을 이름을
사실, 인도에 관해 오해가 참 많습니다.
남동쪽이나 남서쪽엔 기나긴 해변이 뻗어 있고요,
인도에서 수천만 명이 기독교인이라고 하는 거네요.
그럼 인도에 여호와의 증인은 얼마나 될까요?
증인 수는 5만 명이 조금 못 됩니다.
실제로 많은 사람과 진리에 관해 쉽게 대화할 수 있어요.
또 전파되지 않은 구역에 형제들을 보냈는데,
네, 제가 예전에 회중에서 파이오니아를 했을 때,
하루에 성서 연구 두세 건은 쉽게 생겼어요.
나중엔 호별 방문할 시간이 없을 정도였는데,
이 사람들이 왜 그렇게 열심히 듣는 거죠?
그리고 흔히들 억압받고 무시당한다고 느끼기 때문에,
형제들이 보이는 사랑과 존중심에 이끌리게 되는 거에요.
특히 나를 정말 사랑하고 아껴 주는 창조주가 계시다는 걸 알면,
나 자신을 보는 시각도 바뀌게 되죠.
사실 우리는 해마다 특별 활동을 조직해서
전파되지 않은 구역의 일부를 돌고 있는데요,
다른 나라들에서 형제 자매들이 지원하러 오십니다.
도움이 더 필요한 인도로 오신 거죠?
그리고 인도의 수화 밭도 확장되고 있어요.
지금은 회중 13개에 예비 집단과 집단이 46개나 돼요.
그리고 이번엔 과일을 먹는 걸 해 볼게요.
그럼 제가 수화를 해 볼 테니까
저도 인도 수화에 소질이 있나 봐요.
회중에서 관심을 보여 줄 때 정말 마음이 끌립니다.
약속한 날 형제들이 그의 마을에 도착해 보니,
관심자인 그 청각 장애인 남자와 함께,
친구가 한 명만 와 있는 게 아니고
거기 교실 몇 개로 사람들을 나눴죠.
정말 인도에 할 일이 엄청나게 많다는 걸
여러 가지 질문이 생길 수 있죠.
예를 들면, 정말 인도에 도움이 많이 필요할까요?
우리 형제 자매가 될 가능성을 가진 사람들이
많은 수의 발전하는 성서 연구를 사회합니다.
조금만 조사해 보면 뜻밖의 답을 얻을지 몰라요.
“영원한 생명을 얻기에 합당한 성향을 가진 사람들”을 찾고 있죠.
혹시 이 일에 더 많이 참여하고 싶어서 기도하고 있다면,
인도에서 활동이 저렇게 빨리 진척되는 걸 보고
끝이 가까웠다는 건 의심할 여지가 없죠.
지금이 인도의 활동에 중요한 때라고 느껴요.
우릴 위해 그곳에서 무슨 일을 하실지 기대됩니다.
‘주인에게 수확할 일꾼을 더 보내 달라고 청하십시오.’

en.text: The next part of our program is one
that we’ve come to enjoy so much in the past few years.
It’s the prerecorded video The Inside Story.
This installment of The Inside Story will be hosted
by Brother Kenneth Stovall, with our Theocratic Schools Department.
So let’s give attention to and enjoy this video.
Welcome to this edition of The Inside Story.
Imagine yourself as a child
growing up in a country where our work is under ban.
What would that be like?
You’re going to find out as we talk to a couple from Romania.
Are you familiar with the progress of our work in India?
I think you’re in for a few surprises as we talk to four students
who come to us from the India branch.
But let’s get started by introducing our first guests.
From Romania —please welcome Ionuţ and Delia Cicio.
Nice to see you.
Good to see you, Brother Stovall.
Welcome to The Inside Story.
It’s a privilege to be here.
Yes, it is—but a nervous privilege.
Well, I hope you’re not too nervous.
Well, to start with, could you just help us
to understand how the work got started in Romania?
The work started in 1911.
By 1919, there were over 1,700 publishers
and 150 groups or congregations in Romania.
My goodness, that was very fast growth!
But there was some opposition to the work.
Yes, in 1949, the Communist government banned our work,
and sadly, it lasted until 1990.
That’s amazing! So that’s 40 years under ban.
But now, as I understand it,
that’s when both of your families got the truth —when the ban was going on.
Is that correct?
Yes, my mother was a baby
when my grandparents got baptized,
so she grew up in the truth.
In fact, my grandmother was a pioneer under the ban for many years.
Later, my two sisters and I
were raised in the truth.
Very interesting.
And, Ionuţ, what about you?
My parents were contacted by the Witnesses
ten years before the ban was lifted,
so my sister and I were also raised in the truth.
So this is very interesting.
Often, we have talked about brothers who were faithful under ban who were adults,
but you were children while the ban was going on, and you stayed faithful.
So, Delia, do you remember what it was like
going to meetings under ban?
Yes, we met secretly in small groups.
The friends would arrive at different times,
but once everyone was inside the home,
we would lock the gate and the door
and pull down all of the shades.
The meetings were moved to a different location each week.
Very interesting.
Now, it must have been, though,
that you probably had to miss a lot of meetings under ban.
No, no—we didn’t want to miss any opportunity to meet together.
But weren’t you frightened in these meetings
(where you’d pulled down all the shades)
that you might be discovered or arrested?
You might think so, but the opposite was true.
I felt the most safe when we were all together.
You could feel Jehovah’s protection.
That’s very touching.
So, Ionuţ, did you and Delia know each other growing up?
Yes, we grew up in the same town, Negreşti-Oaş,
so our families knew each other.
So did your families, then, occasionally attend the same meetings?
No, we didn’t.
You see, my family was
in a separate group from Delia’s family.
In a separate group?
Now, explain what you mean.
You might remember Brother Lösch’s video
from the 2018 annual meeting.
He explained how government spies
infiltrated the Witnesses in Romania,
and this made it difficult to know who to trust.
This caused the Witnesses to separate
into two large groups
—one group stayed in contact
with world headquarters in Brooklyn,
and the other did not.
But both groups continued to worship Jehovah.
Amazing!
So you grew up —both of you as Jehovah’s Witnesses
but associating with different groups.
Now, did one group view the other group as apostates?
Generally, no.
We didn’t see the other group as apostates.
Our beliefs were essentially the same.
Yes, I should mention that when I was small,
I remember my mother stayed up one night studying.
After all night of study, meditation, and prayer,
she decided to switch to the group connected to the main organization.
So that’s why I grew up as a part of the group associated with the main organization.
My, it sounds like your mother was very conscientious
and set a really good example for you.
I deeply appreciate her and my grandparents
for being faithful examples and good teachers.
OK, when you say good teachers, what do you mean?
For example, we kept beehives in our garden;
my mother helped us to see how Jehovah made them to be industrious.
Then she drew the lesson that we could be industrious like the bees,
and in spite of the ban, we could stay busy serving Jehovah.
Those must be some cherished memories, those lessons like that.
Now, I wonder.
At meetings, since the literature was banned, what did you study?
At meetings, usually there was one copy of The Watchtower for the whole group.
When the paragraph was read,
we would listen and answer the question from memory.
My goodness, you had to pay really close attention at the meetings.
Were there ever times when you could get together in larger groups?
We couldn’t have assemblies and conventions,
but we could have funerals,
weddings, picnics.
These became our assemblies and conventions.
Sometimes, a funeral could have
as many as 1,000 people,
and it could last up to four hours.
Wow!
Now, what about songs?
The songbook would have been part of the banned literature.
Could you sing songs at your meetings?
I remember being a child
and getting together to memorize the songs.
We enjoyed that; it was entertainment for us.
So you memorized the songs?
So if someone called out a song number,
you could sing the song from memory?
Yes.
What was going to school like under ban?
Our classmates and our neighbors
all knew we were Jehovah’s Witnesses
because when under ban,
we didn’t hide our identity as Witnesses.
We just hid the things
that the government outlawed, such as meetings,
preaching, literature.
So you must have been very determined
to stay faithful in school.
So whatever happened to the two groups?
I’m happy to say they reunited
as one organization in 1988;
then the ban was lifted in 1990.
The brothers were overjoyed.
I can imagine.
They must have felt a great deal of relief
when they could go about their spiritual routine without the ban.
True.
But I learned a lesson I never want to forget:
Ban or no ban, we are always under attack by Satan.
I saw brothers that stayed faithful during the ban
but fell away once the ban was lifted.
As circumstances change,
Satan will always look for new ways to attack us.
So ban or no ban,
we must stay close to Jehovah.
Those are profound thoughts, Ionuţ.
Well, how is Jehovah blessing the work in Romania today?
Today, there are more than 40,000 Witnesses in Romania.
Actually, we brought a video that shows what’s being done in Romania today.
Would you like to see it?
Yes, that would be wonderful!
Jesus said: “Be on the watch for the false prophets
“who come to you in sheep’s covering,
but inside they are ravenous wolves.”
During the mid-20th century,
government agents in Romania used techniques
to infiltrate the congregation
—feigning interest and posing as spiritual brothers.
They were so convincing that some were even appointed as elders
and given very responsible positions.
Not knowing who could be trusted,
a large group of brothers separated from the organization
that was being used by headquarters.
Still, they were really brothers in their heart;
they loved the truth.
So in 1988,
a reunification of about 5,000 was accomplished.
And now that our Romanian brothers and sisters were reunited,
they could fully work “shoulder to shoulder”
in sharing the good news of God’s Kingdom.
This was beautiful timing
because conditions in Romania were ripe
for accelerated spiritual growth.
In 1990, the ban that they had endured
for more than 40 years was finally lifted.
Brothers Ian Florian and Tetu Bindu
remember the period of fiery test.
At one time, Brother Florian was part of the separated group.
Brother Bindu was always with a congregation
that remained with the main organization
associated with headquarters.
They now serve together as elders in the congregation.
When I returned to Jehovah’s organization,
I had experienced the most profound and noble feelings
that only someone who belongs to Jehovah’s worldwide family can have.
Today, they serve in unity
and enjoy many spiritual blessings.
Like so many other mature ones with a similar background,
their rich history and experience benefit younger ones.
In just six years after the ban was lifted,
the number of publishers nearly doubled.
Regular pioneers increased by nearly 3,000 percent.
There are now more than 40,000 publishers.
Looking forward, the Romanian branch has begun working
with the Central European branch to form foreign-language circuits
for Hungarian- and Romany-speaking people.
Recently, a seminar was organized
for language instructors.
The unity of our Romanian brothers and sisters
is making it possible to reach
people of all languages with the good news.
The cold, insidious tactics of Satan’s agents
failed to separate our brothers from Jehovah
and each other,
and even now,
Jehovah is blessing them
with a spiritual paradise.
What a wonderful video!
Obviously, the brothers in Romania,
both the adults and the children,
had a lot of courage and faith
to keep their integrity under the ban.
Thank you, Ionuţ and Delia, for sharing your story with us.
Now let’s introduce our next guests.
From India, we have not two, but four students.
Please welcome Sarb and Geeta Dhillon
and Puneet and Ritu Aggarwal.
Ritu.
Hello.
Hello, Brother Stovall.
Thank you, good to see you.
Well, thank you so much for joining us.
Thank you!
Now, you all serve at the India branch,
and as I understand,
you are in English congregations.
Yes, there are several English congregations in India.
Very interesting.
So could we start by having you just explain
a little bit about the background of the work in India?
Sure!
The work got started around 1905.
There was a man called A. J. Joseph.
He had questions about the Bible,
and somebody gave him books by Brother Russell.
He read those books
and came into the truth,
and for around 60 years,
he proved to be instrumental in establishing the work in India.
It is amazing how Jehovah used Brother Russell
to spread the good news so far!
Yes.
And in fact, Brother Russell went to India in 1912, and in one village,
the villagers actually changed the name of the village to Russelpuram,
which means “The Place of Russell.”
Amazing! So is it still there today?
Yes, it’s in the beautiful state of Kerala, which is in the south of India.
Now, there are a lot of misconceptions about India.
Uh-huh.
Often, when you see pictures,
you see what appear to be tremendously overcrowded cities,
but there must be more to India than that.
Yes, brother, actually India is a very, very diverse country,
and it’s a very beautiful country.
If you go to the north of India,
you will have the world famous Himalayan Mountains;
if you go to the northwest, you will find the Great Indian Desert;
and if you go to the southwest and southeast, you will have miles of beaches;
and then in the southern tip of it,
we have another national beauty that’s called backwaters.
These are actually lagoons or lakes.
What a beautiful country!
Yes.
And what diversity!
And, you know, the peoples and the cultures are as diverse as the country.
In fact, we have over 700 languages.
Seven hundred languages!
That’s amazing!
What about religion? Is it diverse also?
Yes, the majority of people are Hindus,
but there are also Buddhists and Muslims.
In fact, there are several states in the northeast,
known as the Seven Sisters, where people profess to be Christians.
How many people are we talking about?
Millions of people.
So there are millions of people in India that profess to be Christian.
Yes.
I did not know that.
So, what’s the situation with Jehovah’s Witnesses in India?
Well, we have just under 50,000 Witnesses in the whole of India.
Now, that’s a ratio of 1 publisher
to every 27,000 people.
Now, what that means is that some 90 percent
of our territory is actually unworked,
so the need over there is very, very great!
Well, I can see there’s an amazing need.
You see, in those states where the people are,
or profess to be, Christian, there are actually millions of people
that you can speak to about the truth very easily.
But there’s also been an amazing response
to the truth in other parts of India too.
Amazing response?
Now, what do you mean by amazing response?
Well, there have been reports of congregations where there are 50 publishers,
but over 850 people have attended the Memorial,
for example, in places like Kaushambi and Allahabad.
And brothers have been sent into untouched territories,
into villages where villagers just come out,
sit on the ground, and listen to the brothers for hours.
Those are such interesting reports.
What about you personally?
I mean, what have you personally experienced as far as response to the truth?
Brother, when I was a pioneer back in my congregation,
I found people were very, very nice.
They were always ready to listen.
It wasn’t difficult to start two or three Bible studies in a day.
And eventually, I came to the point that I couldn’t continue
the house-to-house ministry because I had so many Bible studies.
That’s fantastic!
What makes the people so eager to listen?
Well, the Indian people in general are spiritually-minded,
and the majority do believe
in the existence of a God, or even many gods.
And many people feel downtrodden and overlooked,
and so they are drawn to the love and respect
that they experience among the brothers.
And especially when they learn about a Creator
who actually loves them and cares for them,
it changes their viewpoint toward themselves,
and that also helps them to come into the truth.
Well, given the need and the response that you’re getting,
can you get help from other places,
like from brothers or publishers from other countries?
Absolutely!
In fact, every year we organize special campaigns
to try to cover some of our unworked territory,
and we have friends come from other countries who support these campaigns.
And how does that work out?
Well, the friends who come really enjoy themselves.
They enjoy themselves so much that they often come back again
for longer periods of time.
So you have need-greaters in India?
We do!
Could you use more?
Oh, yes, please!
And there is also a growing sign-language field in India.
The deaf field is one of the fastest growing fields in India.
For example, a few years ago, there were no congregations for the deaf,
but today, we have 13 congregations
and over 46 pregroups and groups.
Wow! Again, that’s amazing response.
What kind of sign language do you use in India?
Is it similar to American Sign Language?
No. We have Indian Sign Language,
which is very natural and very easy to learn.
Actually, I can help you to learn some.
You can try!
Yes, OK.
So the sign for women is like this
because they wear nose rings,
and the sign for men is like this
because they have mustaches —not all, of course.
And then I just act like I’m eating a fruit.
So now I’m going to do a sign, and let’s see if you can understand.
You can guess.
You’re giving me a test.
Yes, it’s from the Bible; it’s very easy.
So if I do like this, which Bible character is it?
Eve.
Oh! Very good!
And if I do like that?
Adam.
Wow! Very good!
I’m on my way to learning Indian Sign Language.
Yes, yes!
Excellent!
And Brother Stovall, the deaf people
are really drawn to the attention
they receive in the congregation
because, unfortunately, in the Indian society, they are neglected.
For example, there was a brother who was trying

en.text: An introduction to the book of Philippians.
The apostle Paul wrote this inspired letter from Rome,
where he was under house arrest.
He wrote the letter about 60 or 61 C.E.
Some years earlier,
during his second missionary tour,
Paul had received a vision
while he was in Troas.
A Macedonian man entreated him:
“Step over into Macedonia and help us.”
So in about 50 C.E.,
Paul and his companions
began to preach the good news
in the Macedonian city of Philippi.
Paul established a congregation there,
but not without opposition.
He and Silas were beaten with rods and thrown into prison,
where their feet were fastened in stocks.
Paul returned to Philippi
during his third missionary tour.
His letter to the congregation
reveals the special bond of love
that he and the Philippian brothers
had for each other.
The letter to the Philippians has four chapters.
In chapter 1,
Paul writes that his current imprisonment in Rome
has led to “the advancement of the good news.”
The apostle’s courage in the face of opposition
has strengthened the brothers to keep speaking the word of God fearlessly.
In chapter 2,
Paul encourages the Philippians
to keep imitating the mental attitude of Christ.
The Philippians are then commended
for “shining as illuminators in the world.”
Did you know?
Sometime earlier,
the Philippians had sent Epaphroditus to Rome
with a gift for Paul.
Paul later sent Epaphroditus back to Philippi,
entrusting him with his inspired letter to the congregation.
In chapter 3,
Paul warns against those who have “confidence in the flesh,”
evidently because of their Jewish background.
Paul considers any advantages that he once enjoyed as a Pharisee
to be refuse compared with the privilege of knowing Christ
and being in union with him.
In chapter 4,
the Philippians are reminded, not to be “anxious over anything,”
but to find “the peace of God”
through prayer, supplication, and thanksgiving.
Paul also thanks the congregation
for its generosity in providing for his material needs.
As you read the letter to the Philippians,
note how our being steadfast under trial
can encourage others to stand firm,
how God’s Word and spirit can help us
to keep imitating the mental attitude of Christ,
and how true peace comes to those
who turn to God in heartfelt prayer
as they await his Kingdom rule.

cn.text: 使徒保罗被软禁在罗马
在这期间他写下腓立比书
这卷书是在公元60或61年左右写成的
多年前
保罗在第二次传道旅程期间来到特洛阿斯
他在那里看到一个异象
一个马其顿人在异象里恳求保罗说
请到马其顿来帮助我们吧
于是，大约在公元50年
保罗和同伴
开始在马其顿地区的腓立比城
传讲好消息
他在当地建立了一群会众，但也受到迫害
民政官下令用杖痛打保罗和西拉
又把他们关进监牢
用枷锁把他们的脚锁住
保罗在第三次传道旅程期间回到腓立比
他写给腓立比会众的信
充分表达了自己
跟当地基督徒之间的深厚感情
腓立比书一共有4章
第1章，保罗表示
他被监禁在罗马反而有利于传讲好消息
使徒保罗在迫害下勇敢坚定
这让其他弟兄受到鼓励
放胆宣扬上帝的话语
第2章，保罗勉励腓立比的基督徒
要不断培养基督的思想态度
保罗称赞他们
说他们“在世人当中如同明光照耀”
你知道吗？
保罗被囚在罗马期间
腓立比会众派以巴弗提送礼物给保罗
之后，保罗差以巴弗提回腓立比
请他把信带给腓立比会众
第3章，保罗提醒会众
当心倚仗外在的条件的人
这些人因为自己是犹太人而感到优越
保罗以前属于法利赛派
他把当时享有的名誉地位视作废物
对保罗而言
认识基督并与他联合更有价值
第4章
保罗劝勉弟兄姐妹
只要向上帝祷告
恳切祈求，并表达感谢
就可以感到内心安宁
保罗也感谢会众表现慷慨
为他提供物质援助
你读腓立比书的时候，请留意
我们在考验下勇敢坚定可以鼓励其他人
上帝的话语和他的神圣力量
可以帮助我们培养基督的思想态度
我们真诚地向上帝祷告
并耐心等候他的王国
就会有真正的内心安宁

ko.text: 사도 바울은 데살로니가 회당에서 유대인들을 가르칠 때
그리스도가 고난을 당하고 부활되어야 했다는 것을 설명하고
그 결과 몇몇 유대인이 그리스도인이 되었죠.
우리도 바울처럼 가르치려면 어떻게 해야 할까요?
자료 내용에 대해 함께 추리해야 합니다.
여러분이 마지막 날에 관한 공개 강연을 한다고 해 보시죠.
“매년 1억 명이 넘는 사람이 말라리아에 감염되는 것으로 추산된다.
어떤 곳에서는 그 지역의 거의 모든 사람이 감염되기도 한다.”
과학적 사실이나 뉴스 기사나 경험담과 같은 자료를 언급하려면
그 자료가 믿을 만하고 최신 정보인지 확인해야 합니다.
성구를 설명할 때는 성구의 문맥, 성경 전체의 내용,
“충실하고 슬기로운 종”이 마련한 출판물과 일치하게 설명해야 합니다.
이제 한 형제의 연설 내용에 주의를 기울여 보시죠.
여호와의 백성은 계속 평화로운 상태에 있을 것입니다.
“마곡 땅의 곡”에 대한 흥미진진한 예언이 나옵니다.
평온하고 안전하게 살고 있는 자들을 치러 가리니,
그들은 모두 성벽이나 빗장이나 성문도 없이
다시 말해, 사탄 마귀는 우리를 공격할 것입니다.
마곡의 곡에 대한 설명이 가장 최신 이해와 일치한 것이었나요?
그들은 모두 성벽이나 빗장이나 성문도 없이
다시 말해, 나라들의 연합체는 우리를 공격할 것입니다.
그 내용에 대해 함께 추리하는 게 꼭 필요합니다.
내 생각엔 하느님이 단순한 생명체를 창조하셨고
진화나 창조 둘 중 하난데, 창조가 더 논리적이야.
내 생각엔 하느님이 단순한 생명체를 창조하셨고
근데 난 생명체가 굉장히 정교하다는 걸 생각하면
그런데 모든 것을 지으신 분은 하느님이십니다.”
이 핸드폰이 저절로 생겨난 거라고 하면 그 말을 믿겠어?
그럼 훨씬 더 정교한 생명체는 두말할 필요도 없겠지.
물론 어떤 질문을 받았는데 그에 대한 답을 모르겠다면
조사를 해 본 다음 다시 오겠다고 말할 수 있습니다.
그들을 생명의 길로 인도할 수 있을 것입니다.

en.text: When the apostle Paul was teaching Jews
in the synagogue in Thessalonica,
he was accurate and convincing.

As a result of Paul’s teaching,

What will help us to be accurate
and convincing when we teach?
We must consult reliable sources,
use those sources properly,
and reason on the evidence with our audience.
Let’s say you’re giving a public talk about the last days,
and you read the following quote regarding pestilence
from the 1996 edition
of The Encyclopedia Americana:
“It is estimated that more
“than 100 million cases
“of malaria occur each year.
“In some places,
“nearly the entire population
is infected.”
Is The Encyclopedia Americana
a reliable source?
Yes.
Is the source up-to-date?
No.
When referring to a scientific discovery,
a news report, a person’s experience,
or other information as evidence,
make sure that your sources are trustworthy
and up-to-date.
Additionally, be sure to use sources properly.
Don’t overstate or exaggerate facts and figures.
Also, we must apply scriptures in harmony
with their context, the Bible’s overall message,

“I will come against those living in security,

“all of them living in settlements
unprotected by walls, bars, or gates.”
Yes, Gog of Magog,
which represents a coalition of nations,
will attack Jehovah’s people.
This, in turn, will provoke a reaction
from the Sovereign Lord Jehovah himself.
Now, how can we reason with people on the facts
so that we’re not only accurate but also convincing?
Let’s look in on an informal setting.
So based on that,

We can’t force our view on others,

Both.

By using trustworthy evidence to help

cn.text: 保罗在帖撒罗尼迦的会堂教导犹太人时

有关最后日子的演讲

是

title: 앨리스 톰슨: 여호와께선 우리를 돌봐 주십니다

ko.text: 어머니는 아주 어릴 때 진리를 받아들이셨는데,
제가 봉사와 영적인 일들을 열심히 했기 때문에,
그래서 남편이 제게 마음이 끌렸던 것 같아요.
전혀 마음의 준비가 되어 있지 않았거든요.
이 아이를 여호와께서 주신 선물로 보게 해 달라고요.
지부에 특별한 일이 있을 때마다 형제들은 우릴 초대해 줬어요.
우린 딸과 함께 자주 봉사를 했어요.
저는 ‘우리 딸이 선교인이 다 됐네’ 하고 말하곤 했어요.
여러 해 동안 그곳에서 섬기면서 아주 행복했습니다.
우린 여행하는 일을 하라는 임명을 받았어요.
남편 톰슨 형제와 함께 6년 동안 순회 활동을 했죠.
여호와께서 우리의 필요를 돌보신다는 걸 느꼈습니다.
남편이 죽고 나선 딸아이가 제 버팀목이 되어 주었죠.
그 아일 생각하면 아직도 가슴이 미어져요.
하느님의 평화가 제 마음과 정신력을 지켜 주고’ 있습니다.
성경을 읽고 또 읽으면서 계속 배우게 되죠.
조직의 최근 소식에 깨어 있으려고 노력하죠.
전 시간 봉사와 같이 훌륭한 선택을 할 수 있도록
형제 자매들은 제가 집회에 나오는 것만 봐도
정말 격려가 된다고 늘 말해 줍니다.
집회에 갈 때마다, 아이들이 와서 절 안아 줘요.
정말 여호와께서는 우리를 잘 돌보아 주십니다.

我们12月就结婚了
在接着的1月
我们就搬到伯利兹服务了
我们才做了两年的特派传道员
我就发现自己怀孕了
我丈夫刚开始很难接受，他还没准备好
之后，我们就从特派传道员之家搬了出来
不过我们就在那附近找到了房子
我跟耶和华祷告说
我希望这个孩子可以像撒母耳一样被他任用
我求耶和华帮助我教导女儿
也帮助我把女儿看作是耶和华赐给我的礼物
不管分部有什么活动
弟兄们常常会邀请我们参加
他们总是会说
带你女儿一起来吧！
那段时间真的很快乐！
我们常常带女儿去传道
伯利兹的弟兄姐妹也会带她去传道
我觉得女儿就好像是一个“小特派传道员”
我在伯利兹有很多圣经学生
在伯利兹服务的那几年我真的很快乐
后来回到了牙买加
圣经学生还会经常打电话、寄卡片给我
也会告诉我她们自己和孩子的情况
后来我们被委派做探访工作
我们做了六年的分区探访工作
我能体会到耶和华一直关心照顾我们
这大大强化了我的信心
我丈夫快去世时，我对他说
他真的是个很好的爸爸
很好的长老、很好的丈夫
丈夫去世后，女儿一直在我身边支持我
后来女儿也去世了
我觉得天都塌了
到现在我的心还是感觉很痛
我女儿去世后
上帝赐给我超越人所能理解的平安
这大大守护了我的内心和头脑
我经常做个人研读，也常常看圣经
我一遍又一遍地看圣经
不断地学习、吸收
我也会定期收看电视网节目
还会留意组织有哪些改变和调整
我能做多少就做多少
我会尽力鼓励年轻人做明智的决定
包括鼓励他们参与全时服务
弟兄姐妹一直说
只要我来聚会，只要能看到我
他们就已经受到很大的鼓励了
每次去聚会，小朋友都会来抱抱我
我常跟他们说
没有你们的抱抱，我还真活不下去了
耶和华一定会照顾我们的
我的一生就是一个很好的证明！

titles.ko: 앨리스 톰슨: 여호와께선 우리를 돌봐 주십니다
titles.en: Alice Thompson: Jehovah Takes Care of Us
titles.cn: 艾丽斯·汤普森：耶和华一定会照顾我们

ko.text: 이번 봉사 연도 초에 학생 56명이 전 세계에서 모여
워치타워 길르앗 성서 학교 교육을 받았습니다.
길르앗 교육의 목적은 학생들 각자의 믿음을 강화하여
그들로 하여금 자신의 임지에 있는 형제들을 강화하게 하는 것입니다.
뉴욕주 패터슨에 있는 워치타워 교육 센터에서 열렸습니다.
이제 믿음을 강화해 주는 연설들이 들어 있는
길르앗 졸업식의 첫 번째 부분을 즐기시기 바랍니다.
길르앗 제146기 졸업식에 참석하신 여러분을 뵙게 되어 기쁩니다.
또 미국과 캐나다와 푸에르토리코의 베델 시설,
무엇보다도, 곧 이 훌륭한 학교를 졸업하게 될
그리고 이처럼 특별한 날 함께해 주신
여러 가지 성경 기록에서 원칙을 끌어내는 훈련을 받으셨을 겁니다.
예수의 제자 몇 사람이 모든 것을 뒤로하고 예수를 따르는데요,
예수께선 이들의 마음을 움직여 자신을 온전히 따르게 할 생각이셨죠.
“한번은 예수께서 게네사렛 호숫가에 서 계실 때에
무리가 그분에게 몰려들어 하느님의 말씀을 듣고 있었다.
그분은 호숫가에 대어 놓은 배 두 척을 보셨다.
어부들이 배에서 내려 그물을 씻고 있었다.
그분은 그 배들 중 하나에 타셨는데, 그것은 시몬의 배였다.
그분은 그에게 배를 육지에서 조금 떼어 놓으라고 하셨다.
그리고 배에 앉아 무리를 가르치기 시작하셨다.
그분은 말씀을 마치시고 시몬에게 ‘깊은 데로 가십시오.
그리고 그물을 내려 고기를 잡으십시오’ 하고 말씀하셨다.
‘선생님, 우리가 밤새도록 애썼지만 한 마리도 잡지 못했습니다.
그러나 말씀하신 대로 제가 그물을 내리겠습니다.’
그들이 그렇게 하자 물고기가 매우 많이 잡혀서
다른 배에 있는 동료들에게 손짓하여 와서 도와 달라고 했다.
그들이 와서 고기를 두 배에 가득 채우자
이것을 보고 시몬 베드로가 예수의 무릎 앞에 엎드려
저는 죄 많은 사람입니다’ 하고 말했다.
그와 함께 있던 사람들도 몹시 놀랐던 것이다.
이제부터 당신은 사람을 낚는 어부가 될 것입니다.’
그러면, 이 기록에 나온 기적의 취지는 무엇이었습니까?
물론 그러려면 예수를 믿고 말씀을 잘 들어야 했습니다.
그들은 많은 물고기가 잡히는 걸 똑똑히 보고,
분명 예수께서 자신들의 필요도 채워 주실 거란 걸 알 수 있었습니다.
모든 것을 버리고 예수를 따랐다고 알려 줍니다.
고기잡이 사업과 관련된 모든 것을 다 포기하고
이 순간의 경험으로 예수를 더 믿고 신뢰하게 되었던 겁니다.
여러분이 여호와에 대한 믿음과 신뢰심을 길러서
그러면 여러분은 계속 여호와와 가까워지게 되어,
그분이 어떤 일이나 어떤 책임을 맡기시더라도
겸손히 기적의 취지에 따라 행동한 제자들을 본받으십시오.
그들은 모든 걸 버리고 예수를 따랐습니다.
그럼, 처음에 드린 질문의 두 번째 부분을 보면,
제자들에게 어떤 깊은 뜻을 지니고 있었을까요?
호수 깊은 곳으로 가서 그물을 내리자
두 배에 가득 채우자 배가 가라앉을 정도였습니다.
그들이 물고기를 어떻게 했는지는 성구에 없지만,
물 위를 걸을 수 있는 분이 제자들이 가라앉게 두셨겠습니까?
이제 예수께서 기적을 행하신 더 큰 목적을 생각해 보시죠.
제자들이 그것을 보고 놀라움에 휩싸였을 때 뭐라고 하셨습니까?
사람을 낚는 어부가 될 것입니다”라고 하셨죠.
예수께서는 제자들에게 더 큰 목적을 보여 주신 것입니다.
물질적 필요가 채워질 뿐 아니라 (이 취지는 이해했죠),
앞으로 있을 훨씬 더 큰 기적을 지적한 겁니다.
제자들이 얼마나 성공적으로 사람을 낚을지를 보여 준 것일 텐데요,
물고기로 가득 찼던 그 배들을 떠올려 보면서
아직도 해야 할 일이 많다는 걸 생각할 수 있었을 겁니다.
그건 사람들이 예수의 제자가 되도록 돕는 일이었죠.
여러분이 이 중요하고 다시 반복되지 않을 일을
계속 지원하는 데 도움이 될 것인데
그게 이 교육의 더 큰 목적이죠.
그러므로 이제 여러분이 어떤 임지에서 무슨 일을 하게 되든,
여러분이 이 학교에 있는 동안 받은 축복의 취지와 목적을
여호와와 그분의 아들이 항상 여러분을 도와줄 것을 믿고,
길르앗에서 배운 대로 여러분이 가서 섬기게 될 지부와 구역에서
이 점을 좀 더 애기해 보겠습니다.
그럼 이제 격려적인 연설들을 즐기실 차례입니다.
듣고 있는 우리 모두의 믿음과 신뢰심을 강하게 하고
우리 하느님의 놀라운 목적을 강조할 것입니다.
중앙장로회 성원인 데이비드 스플레인 형제가 하실 텐데요,
우리 모두 그래야 한다는 걸 알지만,
우린 때때로 다른 사람을 비판적으로 보는 경향과 싸워야 합니다.
다른 사람의 동기를 의심할 때도 있죠.
어쩌면 좀 샘이 나서 그럴 수도 있습니다.
회중에 연설을 정말 잘하는 형제가 있다고 가정해 보겠습니다.
그 형제가 연설하는 날이면 회관이 꽉 찹니다.
남편 연설은 잘 칭찬 안 하면서.
절대 늦지 않고, 일을 못하는 날도 없고,
하루에 엄청난 양의 일을 해내는 데다,
이렇게 그 사람의 동기를 의심하게 될 수 있죠.
그 형제에게서 좋은 점을 찾을 수 있을까요?
형제에게 유리한 쪽으로 생각해 줄 수 있을까요?
아마도 그 형젠 여호와께 가장 좋은 걸 드리도록
그가 더 많은 일을 하는 이유는 그렇게 훈련받았고,
여호와께 드릴 수 있는 가장 좋은 걸 드리길 원하기 때문입니다.
그러고 보니 그 형젠 결코 여러분의 봉사를 비판한 적이 없죠.
단지 가능한 한 가장 좋은 걸 드리려 했을 뿐입니다.
바로 그런 태도로 그는 파이오니아를 했고,
만약 형제가 그렇게 한다면 그는 가장 좋은 걸 원하시고
연설을 잘하는 아까 그 형제에겐 뭐라고 할까요?
”여호와께서 형제에게 주신 훌륭한 재능을 잘 활용하시네요.”
그럴 때 우린 형제들의 단점을 모르지 않지만
주로 긍정적인 면에 초점을 맞추려 합니다.
물론 부족한 점을 얘기해야 할 때도 있죠.
하지만 우리가 얘기하는 단점은 한 번 있었던 일입니까,
형제들의 긍정적인 면을 보는 걸 습관으로 삼으면,
때때로 실망하는 일도 생길 수 있죠.
큰 화를 불러올 수도 있다는 걸 보여 주는 성경의 예를 보겠습니다.
이새가 막내 아들인 다윗을 전장에 있는 세 형들에게 보냅니다.
이스라엘에서 누구든 나와서 겨루어 보자고 외치는 걸 듣습니다.
‘저 할례받지 않은 블레셋 사람이 도대체 누구이기에
이때 듣고 있던 맏형 엘리압이 말합니다.
“다윗이 사람들과 말하는 것을 맏형 엘리압이 듣고
광야에 있는 몇 마리 안 되는 양들은 누구에게 맡겨 두었느냐?
너의 주제넘음과 마음의 악한 의도를 내가 잘 알고 있다.
엘리압의 성품에 대해 무엇을 배울 수 있습니까?
이 질문에 함정이 있단 걸 아시겠죠.
우린 엘리압에 대해 아는 게 별로 없으며,
단 한 번 있었던 일을 근거로
엘리압은 단 한 번 그런 겁니까, 아니면 늘 그랬습니까?
이 상황을 분석할 때 자문해 보십시오.
나중에 사과해야 했던 적이 한 번도 없었는가?”
그런 일이 일회성인지, 반복적인지 하는 거죠.
형제 자매들과의 관계에서도 이 점을 꼭 적용할 필요가 있습니다.
한 번의 사건을 근거로 어떤 사람이라고 단정하지 마십시오.
물론 이 경우 엘리압이 잘못한 것이라고 할 수 있죠.
그는 다윗의 동기를 의심하며, 나쁘게 봤습니다.
다윗이 엘리압의 이런 말을 받아들였다고 생각해 보세요.
내가 대체 뭐라고 저런 전사와 맞서 싸울 수 있겠어.’
일시적으로라도, 이스라엘은 큰 화를 겪었을 것입니다.
최선의 것을 여호와께 드리고 있는 사람을 낙담시키지 마십시오.
이제 엘리압의 생애 중 있었던 다른 한 사건을 보면서
그에 대해 긍정적인 얘기를 해 보죠.
그의 아버지의 온 집이 그 소식을 듣고
따라서, 다윗이 필요로 할 때 엘리압은 그의 곁에 있었습니다.
후에 다윗의 아들 하나는 엘리압의 딸과 결혼했습니다.
분명 여호와의 영이 다윗에게 언제 맞서 싸우고,
언제 도망해 숨을지 알려 주었을 겁니다.
아무튼, 부정적으로 받아들일 수 있는 상황도
긍정적으로 생각하는 법을 배우면 화날 일이 줄어들 겁니다.
복도에서 누군가의 뒤를 바짝 따라 걷고 있는데,
그 사람이 여러분의 코앞에서 문을 쾅 닫고 가 버리는 겁니다.
아니면 어쩌다 이번 연설을 좀 지나치게 열정적으로 한 것입니까?
차갑고 도도한 사람입니까, 수줍음이 많은 겁니까?
여러분 형제들 중 어떤 분들은 책임 있는 위치에서,
늘 다른 사람의 실수를 찾는 사람은
격려적인 연설을 해 준 스플레인 형제께 진심으로 감사합니다.
이제 미국 지부 위원이신 트로이 스나이더 형제가
그것도 우리가 큰 환난의 문턱에 와 있는 이 때에 말이죠.
여호와께선 이스라엘 백성이 이집트에서 구출되기 바로 전에
이 말을 듣고 이스라엘은 힘을 얻었습니다.
그 말씀이 ‘나는 내 뜻을 이루는 데 필요한 무엇이든 되겠다’
(즉, 저와 여러분)이 무엇이든 되게 하신다”를 의미하기도 합니다.
이 진리는 우리를 여호와께서 기꺼이 주시는 그 무엇과 연결해 줍니다.
여기서 여호와의 이름의 한 부면을 살펴보면,
그분의 성품과 그분이 기꺼이 나눠 주시는 것이 뭔지 알게 되는데,
네, 여호와의 이름은 그분의 능력과 연관되죠.
그 이름은 여호와의 능력을 밝혀 줍니다.
그분은 기꺼이 그 능력을 사용해 우릴 강화하십니다.
여호수아가 싸울 때 태양이 멈추어 서게 한 것도
피곤하고 지친 예언자가 병거보다 빠르게 달려갔습니다.
우린 기진맥진해져서 힘이 다 빠졌다고 느낄 때가 많죠.
내 뜻을 완수하는 데 필요한 능력을 주겠다’고 하십니다.
사탄과 여호와의 적들은 왜 그분의 이름을 숨기려고 해 왔을까요?
그 이름이 지닌 능력과 그 이름이 중요하고
그 이름은 또 어떤 일을 합니까?
여호와의 종 하나가 어떻게 그런 경험을 했는지,
예레미야는 여호와를 대표하는 매우 어려운 임무를 받았습니다.
