왕이 될 뻔한 사람 정도로 여기지 않으셨습니다.
그 훌륭한 본이 자신의 영감받은 말씀에 기록되게 하셨습니다.
또는 몇몇 사람에게만 주어진 어떤 특권입니까?
인도하는 역할을 맡게 될 때가 올 것입니다.
여러분은 그를 지지하고 그의 지침에 따라 일하며
아내 여러분, 여러분도 마련을 지지하실 겁니까?
‘나는 요나단처럼 내 활을 기꺼이 내줄 것인가?
하느님의 조직에서 책임을 맡도록 선택된 사람이 누구든
여러분에게 상상을 뛰어넘는 상을 주실 겁니다.
여호와의 은혜와 승인보다 더 좋은 것이 무엇입니까?
활을 내주도록 여러분을 감동시킨 그 사람을
오늘 오전에 이렇게 훌륭한 연설을 많이 들을 수 있어서 기뻤습니다.
미크로네시아의 열대 섬인 코스라에로 여행해 보겠습니다.
울창한 정글과 열대 숲과 그림 같은 해변이 있고,
많은 주민이 관광업과 어업과 농업에 종사하고 있습니다.
형제 한 명과 자매 네 명이
정규 파이오니아 2명을 포함해 총 15명의 전도인이 있습니다.
이들은 6천명이 넘는 섬 주민들에게 열심히 전파하고 있는데요,
코스라에의 형제 자매들이 따뜻한 사랑의 인사를 전합니다.
우리 모두도 이 프로그램을 통해 그들에게 사랑과 격려를 보냅니다.

en.text: Welcome to the June 2019 program of JW Broadcasting.
Earlier this year,
56 students from all over the world
gathered to attend
the Watchtower Bible School of Gilead.
They enjoyed a 20-week course that gifted them
with an in-depth study of the Bible.
The aim of Gilead schooling
is to help strengthen the faith of each of the students
so that they in turn can strengthen the brothers in their respective assignments.
On March 9 of this year,
the graduation program for the 146th class
was held at the Watchtower Educational Center
in Patterson, New York.
You’ll now enjoy faith-strengthening talks
that were delivered during the first part
of the Gilead graduation program.
Well, we’re happy to be here today
for this graduation of the 146th class of Gilead,
and we welcome all who are tied in with us
at our Bethel complexes in the United States,
in Canada, in Puerto Rico,
and in a number of remote translation offices.
We especially welcome our Gilead students
who are about to graduate from this marvelous school.
And we welcome your dear family members
and friends who are joining you on this very, very special day.
You seem excited, and you should be.
We’re happy. We’re very, very happy for you.
Now, throughout your schooling, you’ve been asked to draw out principles
from many different Bible accounts, haven’t you?
With that in mind, here’s the theme of our introductory comments:
“Do You See the Point and Remember the Purpose?”
We’re going to illustrate what we mean
by looking at Luke 5:1-11.
This is the account where some of Jesus’ disciples
chose to leave everything behind and follow him.
Here’s the setting:
Some of Jesus’ disciples were fishermen
who had followed Jesus for a time,
but then they went back to their fishing business.
Jesus sought to reach their hearts
and move them to follow him fully.
So, what did he do?
He used a powerful object lesson
that provided a point and a purpose.
Let’s read it at Luke 5:1-11,
and look for the point, first of all, behind what Jesus did here.
It says: “On one occasion when the crowd was pressing in on him
“and listening to the word of God,
“he was standing by the lake of Gennesaret.
“And he saw two boats docked at the lakeside,
“but the fishermen had got out of them and were washing off their nets.
“Going aboard one of the boats, which was Simon’s,
“he asked him to pull away a bit from land.
“Then he sat down, and he began teaching the crowds from the boat.
“When he stopped speaking, he said to Simon:
“‘Pull out to where it is deep, and let down your nets for a catch.’
“But in reply Simon said:
“‘Instructor, we toiled all night and caught nothing,
“but at your word I will lower the nets.’
“Well, when they did this, they caught a great number of fish.
“In fact, their nets began ripping apart.
“So they motioned to their partners in the other boat to come and assist them,
“and they came and filled both boats, so that these began to sink.
“Seeing this, Simon Peter fell down at the knees of Jesus,
“saying: ‘Depart from me, Lord, because I am a sinful man.’
“For both he and those with him were overwhelmed with astonishment
“at the catch of fish they had taken,
“and the same was true of both James and John, Zebedee’s sons,
“who were partners with Simon.
“But Jesus said to Simon:
“‘Stop being afraid.
“From now on you will be catching men alive.’
“So they brought the boats back to land
and abandoned everything and followed him.”
So, what was the point
behind this miracle here?
What was this?
Their needs would be cared for
if they trusted in Jesus and followed him.
Of course, to do this, they had to believe Jesus, didn’t they?
They had to listen to him.
This was not a trick.
With their own eyes, they could see that catch of fish
and then deduce that their needs would, in fact, be cared for by Jesus.
That was the point.
Did they get it?
Yes, they did.
With what result?
Well, it says that they were moved to abandon everything
and follow Jesus
—that is, everything related to the fishing business.
They gave it all up and followed him.
Almost instantly, their faith and trust in Jesus grew, didn’t it?
Now, let’s bring the point up to our day.
Soon you will go to your assignments.
Will you remember the point of your Gilead training?
Well, what is the point?
The point has been to build up your faith
and your trust in Jehovah
and thereby strengthen your relationship with him.
In turn, as you draw steadily closer to Jehovah,
you will be ready for whatever work
and whatever responsibility he chooses to place on you.
Jehovah, by means of his Son, will care for you.
He will help you to faithfully fulfill your assignments,
and you will add to his glory.
And in all that you do,
remember those disciples who were humble enough to get the point
—abandon everything and follow Jesus.
Now, for the second part of the question we mentioned at the beginning,
What was the purpose behind what Jesus did?
In other words, Jesus’ miracle on that day
carried what deeper meaning for them?
Well, looking back at Luke chapter 5,
what happened when the disciples listened to Jesus,
went out to where the water was deep,
and lowered their nets?
The catch was so great that it says
they filled two boats to the point of sinking.
The account doesn’t say what the disciples did with the fish,
but they made it to shore.
A man who could walk on water was not going to let them sink.
Now, we get, though, to the greater purpose behind Jesus’ miracle.
Do you recall what Jesus said to the disciples
after that catch of fish
and after the disciples became filled with astonishment?
He told them: “Stop being afraid.
From now on you will be catching men alive.”
You see, by means of that miracle,
Jesus illustrated something greater for them, didn’t he?
They would not only be cared for materially
(they got that point)
but, more importantly, they would also become
very successful fishers of men.
In other words, the first miracle
pointed to an even greater one yet to come.
If their large catch was meant to illustrate
how successful they would be as fishers of men,
then they could look back on that catch years later
and visualize those boats filled with fish
and be reminded that they had much work yet to do
in being fishers of men
—“catching men alive,” so to speak, and helping them to become disciples of Christ.
Your Gilead training will help you to continue supporting
this vital and never-to-be-repeated work,
which is the greater purpose behind your training.
So, then, whatever you’re given to do and wherever your training may take you,
never forget the point and the purpose behind the blessing
that you just experienced in being part of this class.
Trust in Jehovah and in his Son to help you at all times,
and use your Gilead training to support this important work
in the branches and the territories where you will serve.
Well, we’ll say a little bit more about this
at the conclusion of our program today.
Now we’re going to enjoy a series of very encouraging talks
that will strengthen your faith, build up your trust,
(in fact, for all of us listening in)
and highlight God’s wonderful purpose
that we support.
To begin, we’re very happy to have with us
a member of the Governing Body, Brother David Splane,
who is going to present the talk
“If You Look for It, You Will Find It.”
If you look for it,
you will find it.
Look for what?
Look for the good in your brothers.
And when you find it,
don’t be afraid to acknowledge it.
Now, we all know that we should do that,
but we do have to fight the tendency
to view others a bit critically at times.
Sometimes we question their motives,
maybe because we’re just a little bit jealous.
Now, think about that brother in your congregation
who is just an excellent public speaker.
When he is scheduled to give a talk, the hall is full.
And everybody raves about his talks,
even your wife
—yours, not so much.
‘The show-off; he doesn’t impress me.’
Or what about this:
You’re working in a department with one of those annoying people
who is very efficient.
He’s never late,
he never misses a day’s work,
he gets a tremendous amount done in a day,
and he almost never makes a mistake.
‘That doesn’t impress me either.
Mr. Perfect, he’s trying to make the rest of us look bad.’
Well, there we go questioning someone’s motives.
Now, can we look for the good in Mr. Perfect?
Can we, see, give him the benefit of the doubt?
Maybe his parents trained him
to offer the very best gift he could to Jehovah.
In other words, if he could do more,
he was expected to do more,
because he wanted his gift
to be the very best gift that he could possibly give.
Now, come to think of it, he never criticizes your gift to Jehovah.
He just wants to give his very best gift to Jehovah.
That’s the way he approached the pioneer ministry,
and that’s the way he approaches his Bethel service.
So, now, what do you do with Mr. Perfect?
Do you tell him to slow down?
“You’re making the rest of us look bad.”
Well, if he did that, he’d be giving a substandard gift to Jehovah,
and Jehovah expects and deserves the very best.
So, what do you do?
You acknowledge his gift.
“You really get a lot done in a day;
I wish I had your stamina.”
And what about Mr. Show-off, the outstanding speaker?
“Jehovah has given you a wonderful gift.
You use it well.”
Now, was that hard?
Elders occasionally have to evaluate brothers for privileges of service.
And while we’re not blind to the shortcomings of our brothers,
we try to keep the discussion mainly positive.
Now, sometimes we have to discuss a shortcoming—a negative.
But are we talking about one isolated incident,
or is it a pattern?
It’s true that if we make it a habit to look on the positive side,
we’ll be disappointed sometimes.
But it’s better to be disappointed occasionally
than to develop a cynical or resentful attitude
toward our brothers.
Let’s consider a Scriptural example
where questioning the motives of a brother
could have led to disaster.
It’s in 1 Samuel chapter 17
—and a little bit of background, a little bit of the setting—
Jesse has sent his youngest son, David,
to visit his three oldest brothers in the army,
and Israel is having a face-off with the Philistines.
And when he arrives, David hears Goliath
challenge any man of the house of Israel
to a battle to the death.
There are no volunteers.
David is a man of faith, and he can’t believe it.
He says: “Who is this uncircumcised Philistine
that he should taunt the battle line[s] of the living [true] God?”
Now, his oldest brother, Eliab, is listening,
and we pick up the account in verse 28.
So that’s 1 Samuel chapter 17,
and we’ll read verse 28:
“When his oldest brother Eliab heard him speak to the men,
“he became [very] angry with David and said:
“‘Why have you come down?
“‘And with whom did you leave those few sheep in the wilderness?
“‘I well know your presumptuousness
“‘and the bad intentions of your heart;
you came down just to see the battle.’”
Now, what did we learn about Eliab’s personality from this verse?
Not much.
You recognize that as a trick question.
We just met the man, we don’t know very much about him,
and we certainly aren’t going to pass judgment on somebody
over one isolated incident, are we?
Now the question is this:
Was this a one-off for Eliab, or was he always like that?
Was this an isolated incident, or was it a pattern?
When analyzing the situation, ask yourself this,
‘Was there ever an occasion
‘when I got so frustrated with my fleshly brother
‘that I said something awful,
something that I had to apologize for later?’
Well, did that make you a terrible person?
So the question is: Is this a one-off?
Is it isolated, or is it a pattern?
These are things that we really need to apply
when it comes to our relations with our brothers and sisters.
Don’t write somebody off on the basis of one incident.
Well, we can say that on this occasion, Eliab was wrong.
He questioned David’s motives, and he wasn’t nice about it.
But that’s not the worst of it.
Suppose that David had listened to Eliab saying,
‘Slow down, you’re making the rest of us look bad.’
What might have happened?
Suppose David had said: ‘You’re right, Eliab.
‘I am a bit arrogant.
Who do I think I am that I could fight this mighty man of war?’
Well, that could have had disastrous consequences for Israel,
at least temporarily.
So, what’s the lesson?
Don’t discourage anyone from giving their best to Jehovah,
even if their best is better than your best.
Now, let’s take another isolated incident from the life of Eliab
and say something positive about the man.
Let’s look for the good in Eliab.
First Samuel 22
—1 Samuel 22:1,
it says: “So David went from there,
“escaping to the cave of Adullam.
“[So David is running away from Saul.]
“When his brothers
“and his father’s entire house heard of it,
“they went down there to him
[his brothers, including Eliab].”
So, what’s the point?
Well, when he was needed, Eliab was there for him.
He could be counted on.
And later, one of David’s sons married one of Eliab’s daughters.
Oh, wait a minute, say that again.
David ran away from Saul?
He didn’t run away from Goliath, did he?
But he ran away from Saul.
Jehovah’s spirit must have indicated
when David should stand and fight
and when he should run and hide.
Sounds like material for another talk.
Well, it’ll help our blood pressure
if we can learn to give a positive spin
to potentially negative situations.
Maybe you’ve run into this.
You’re walking down the hallway following closely behind someone.
He goes through the door and lets the door slam right in your face.
Is he self-centered or just lost in thought?
How do you choose to characterize that incident?
Is the public speaker a show-off,
or on this occasion is he simply trying a bit too hard to be enthusiastic?
Is the brother being picky, or is he trying to be thorough?
standoffish and proud or just shy?
Now, one day, some of you brothers are going to have positions of responsibility,
and you’re going to be dealing with people.
And when that happens, remember this:
Many joys are denied those who keep looking for mistakes,
but the one who sees the good in others
will have “a feast constantly.”
Remember that!
And may Jehovah bless you richly.
We love you.
Well, we thank you very, very much for that encouraging talk, Brother Splane.
Now we have a member of the U.S. Branch Committee
with us to deliver the talk
“He Causes to Become.”
Brother Troy Snyder will do this for us.
Well, as Gilead graduates, you’re being sent out
to strengthen and stabilize Jehovah’s precious sheep.
And you’re being sent out
on the threshold of the great tribulation.
Now, what one scripture will strengthen
and stabilize you so you can help others?
Well, here’s a clue:
What truth did Jehovah reveal to fortify the Israelites
right before they were to be delivered from Egypt?
Let’s turn our Bibles to Exodus chapter 3,
and let’s notice what truth Jehovah revealed.
You remember the account?
Moses was asking Jehovah,
‘What can I tell the Israelites
so that they will have confidence in your deliverance?’
In essence, that’s what he was asking Jehovah.
Notice what Jehovah said to fortify them in verse 14:
“So God said to Moses:
“‘I Will Become What I Choose to Become.’
“And he added: ‘This is what you are to say to the Israelites,
“I Will Become has sent me to you.”’”
That fortified the Israelites.
They understood that Jehovah was saying,
‘I’ll be whatever is necessary to carry out my will.’
And according to Appendix A in our New World Translation,
it appears that the name also means
“He Causes to Become”
or “He Causes His Creation (you and me) to Become”
whatever is needed to carry out his will.
And doesn’t that harmonize with who Jehovah is?
We know him as the Creator, don’t we?
He’s created us.
He brought about this universe.
He is the God who causes to become.
You see, this truth —this extraordinary truth—
can strengthen and stabilize you
because it links you
to something that Jehovah is willing to give you.
Let’s look at what that is.
Let’s go to Jeremiah chapter 10.
You see, this aspect of Jehovah’s name
reveals something about his personality
and something that he’s willing to share with you.
Notice what it is in verse 6, Jeremiah 10:6.
It says: “No one is like you, O Jehovah.
“You are great,
“and your name
is great and mighty.”
Yes, Jehovah’s name is linked to his power.
That’s what it reveals about Jehovah.
And Jehovah is willing to use his power to strengthen us.
See, it was Jehovah’s power that caused the Red Sea to part.
It was Jehovah’s power that made the sun stand still when Joshua was in battle.
It was Jehovah’s power that caused a bird to feed Elijah.
It was Jehovah’s power
that took a tired prophet who was exhausted
and made him run faster than a racing chariot.
Isn’t that reassuring —to know that Jehovah is saying,
‘I’m going to give you my power’?
Because oftentimes we’re exhausted
and we may feel like we’re unraveling.
But Jehovah is saying, ‘I love you so much
that I’m going to give you the power you need to accomplish my will.’
You can see why Satan and Jehovah’s enemies
have tried to hide Jehovah’s name
—not just because it identified Him,
but because they wanted to obscure the power that that name has
and what it means to us and how it strengthens us.
But you know what else it also does?
It comforts us.
It can reassure our hearts.
It can allay our fears.
Notice how it did this with one of Jehovah’s servants.
Let’s go back over to Jeremiah chapter 1.
Remember Jeremiah?
He was commissioned with a very difficult assignment,
representing Jehovah.
And what did Jeremiah express to Jehovah?
He said: “I am but a boy.”
It was like he was saying: ‘Jehovah, I’m inexperienced.
‘I know I have a spiritual foundation you’ve given me; you’ve trained me.
But I don’t know if I can handle this; I’m afraid.’
What did Jehovah say to him to fortify him?
What did Jehovah cause him to become?
Notice verse 18, Jeremiah 1:18.
It says: “For today I have made you a fortified city,
“an iron pillar,
“and copper walls against all the land,
“toward the kings of Judah and her princes,
toward her priests and the people of the land.”
“A fortified city”
—see, Jehovah says: ‘I will strengthen you.
‘I’ll make you like that iron pillar.
I’ll give you that inner strength you need to carry out your assignment.’
But “copper walls”
—what was significant about copper walls?
Well, it might be how Jehovah created copper.
What can copper do?
Copper at very high temperature will not buckle,
will not warp, will not lose its strength.
See, it’s as if Jehovah is saying,
‘Jeremiah, I will make it so you can take the heat.’
And that’s what Jehovah is doing for you.
He will make it
—make you— possible to handle any situation.
And you notice those were copper walls —they fortified him.
They surrounded the city.
It’s as if mentally, emotionally, spiritually,
and physically Jehovah would give him
whatever was needed to carry out his assignment.
Now, that fortified Jeremiah!
Could you imagine how Jeremiah may have drawn upon this
as he dealt with challenges?
For example, when he was persecuted,
he was put in stocks.
Now, that’s torture; that’s a form of torture.
Could you imagine Jeremiah’s prayer,
‘Jehovah, cause me to become what I need to become
to stay faithful to you’?
Now, did Jehovah block the pain?
We don’t know.
But what we do know is
that Jeremiah stayed faithful.
This experience did not break his will,
did not break his spirit, nor did it break his integrity.
Or how about the time when Jeremiah
had to go in front of the temple
and in front of the priests and the leaders
and had to tell them that their precious temple
was going to be destroyed?
And he had to illustrate it
by slamming that clay vessel on the ground
and watching it shatter.
Could you imagine Jeremiah’s prayer?
‘Jehovah, help me become
‘what I need to to deliver this message.
‘Give me the poise.
‘Give me the courage.
Help me have that inner strength to do so.’
And Jehovah did.
Jehovah was with Jeremiah time and time again.
Yes, the very name of Jehovah
makes it clear that you will succeed.
You will be able to carry out his will.
And you’ve been doing that.
In your introductions to the family,
we heard how Jehovah was causing you to become.
For example, one of you talked about how as a young girl
you and your sister were asked to leave the family home
because of your relationship with Jehovah.
What happened?
Jehovah caused you and others around you
—your brothers and sisters—
to become what was necessary to keep you close to Jehovah.
One of you related how you were on a theocratic construction expansion project
and you were assigned to cut brick in the heat with all your gear on.
You said you maintained your joy.
Why?
Because Jehovah caused you to become.
One of you dear ones related to us
how you had thought your service to Jehovah had no value to him.
You had lost your joy.
But what happened?
Jehovah caused someone to encourage you,
to strengthen you.
And one of you related how Jehovah
helped you serve beyond the capacity of your heart.
Yes, Jehovah has caused all of you
to become what is necessary to carry out his will.
So whenever you feel discouraged, whenever you feel afraid,
whenever you feel unqualified,
pray to Jehovah.
Ask him to help you become what is necessary to carry out his will.
Ask him to help you do whatever you need
so you can glorify his name.
Consider: When did Jehovah reveal
this truth to the Israelites?
It was right before they were about to face challenges.
When did Jehovah reveal this truth to us?
It was really with the revision of the New World Translation.
It really helped bring it into focus —the power of his name—
really, right before we are to be ushered
into Jehovah’s new world.
So, what trials will you face?
What challenges will you experience?
What will the great tribulation bring?
It doesn’t matter
because you worship Jehovah.
That’s his name —the God who causes to become.
Well, we deeply appreciate that very fine talk, Brother Snyder.
Now we have Brother Donald Gordon,
who serves as a helper to the Publishing Committee,
with us to deliver the talk
“Live in Sync With Jehovah.”
Well, for the last five months you dear students
have been downloading a lot of wonderful information about Jehovah.
Now that the class has finished, the download is complete
—all synced up.
Well, it may seem that way for the moment.
Of course,  Jehovah did not create us like simple computers
where we just store away information in our memories.
We were created “in his image.”
So as we take in knowledge from Jehovah,
we have the ability to absorb it and then to reflect his image
—to think like him, to feel like him.
We begin to act like him.
So he has given us what we have here in his Word,
and he as well created us
in our human capacity to assimilate his Word
into the beautiful facets of his image,
and then we can truly be in sync with Jehovah.
But how does our being in sync with Jehovah
bring honor to him and joy to him?
Well, when we think of the various ones who are in sync with Jehovah,
no doubt the foremost example is Jesus Christ.
Everything he did, everything he said,
every thought he had was in full harmony with his Father.
Jesus said: “I cannot do a single thing of my own initiative.”
Sometimes it’s like a husband and wife
who’ve been married a number of years.
With just a glance, without a word, they know what the other one is thinking.
They’re in sync.
Or perhaps you’re thinking of two ice skaters
flowing across the ice as one, in unison.
Well, one example of Jehovah and Jesus
working in unison, in sync,
is when the woman with the flow of blood was cured
by just touching the fringe of Jesus’ garment
—one of our favorite miracles.
Recall that scene again, recorded here
at Mark 5:29, 30
—Mark 5:29.
The woman has made her way through the crowd;
she touches the garment, and then in verse 29:
“Immediately her flow of blood dried up,
“and she sensed in her body that she had been healed
“of the grievous sickness.
“Immediately Jesus realized in himself
“that power had gone out of him,
“and he turned around in the crowd and asked:
‘Who touched my outer garments?’”
Well, that moment when that woman sensed that she was cured,
Jehovah and Jesus were working in complete harmony.
Actually, until that moment, Jesus may have been unaware
that Jehovah was watching this woman with a desire to heal her.
I suppose that Jehovah could have just cured the woman on his own,
as it were, without Jesus even knowing.
But no, he chose to work through his Son,
who he knew was working in harmony with him.
So when Jesus felt the power go out from him,
he naturally wanted to know who was cured
—‘Who did my Father see that I did not see?’—
because they were working together in harmony.
And then seeing this woman, realizing that actually she was unclean
and where she did not belong,
Jesus was still in complete agreement with his Father.
He was in sync with Jehovah’s view of this woman
and very happy to have been involved in the cure of her
—leaving us, of course, with one of our favorite accounts of Jesus’ life.
Well, what’s a lesson for us?
Whether we are at our work assignments,
in our congregations, or out in the ministry,
we want to be in sync with how Jehovah views other people.
We often tend to view others through our own eyes.
This can be clouded by our own human concerns and viewpoints,
perhaps tainted by some misunderstandings
or misconceptions or wrong information
or perhaps our need to be a little more forgiving.
You see, if any of those feelings are tainting our judgment
or relationships even in a small way,
to that degree we are out of sync with Jehovah.
Jesus and Jehovah were focused on this woman’s faith:
“Your faith has made you well.
Go in peace.”
Well, let us in every situation
strive to see others as Jehovah sees them.
This brings honor to Jehovah
and allows him to use us in harmony with his will.
Now, there was another situation where being in sync with his Father
took more time and effort.
When Jesus chose his 12 apostles, he, of course,
wanted to be in harmony with his Father,
but this did not happen with just a glance.
Of course, Jesus had a very deep, intimate knowledge of Jehovah.
And these men that he was considering —he knew them well.
Still, this decision took hours of prayer
to arrive at the 12 apostles selected.
So it will be in performing your work
and making decisions in your assignments
—you cannot simply rely on your knowledge of the Scriptures,
as deep as it may be.
To make decisions, we must implore Jehovah in our prayers
—maybe many prayers—
and our meditations.
Don’t hold back from beseeching Jehovah
as you struggle for a decision.
But certainly, always relying, of course, on his Word, the Bible
—knowledge from his Word—
prayers to our Father, and then meditation on his will.
Of course, you’ve learned in your class
that the knowledge of Jehovah is such a multifaceted gem.
There is an intriguing scripture that sheds further light on this thought
here at Ephesians 3:19,
Ephesians 3:19.
It says “and to know the love of the Christ,
which surpasses knowledge.”
Well, now, how can knowing something
be more than the knowledge?
Well, you’ve learned here that the Greek term rendered “to know” means
to know “practically, through experience.”
Now, of course, the Gospel accounts teach us much about Christ’s love.
We come to know his patience, his humility, his willingness to forgive, etc.
We read and we study that with delight.
But to really know it,
it’s like, well, a skill that we might learn
only after we actually do it.
For example,
a doctor goes to school to learn to be a doctor.
There’s lots of learning and years of study involved,
but then when the studies are complete, they begin their internship.
They begin making the rounds at the hospital.
They now begin taking part in this education
—what they learned from the books—
and applying it to real-life situations.
The knowledge learned from this experience
surpasses the knowledge learned in the books.
So we have studied the Christ; we do the bookwork; we have learned.
Now, you Gilead students have had the amazing opportunity these last five months
to read and study about his patience, his love,
his forgiveness, humility, compassion.
You cherish that knowledge; you’re in sync
—not quite yet.
You see, now we must do the internship;
now we must take that knowledge and make the rounds, as it were.
We go around the congregation; we interact with our workmates;
we go out in the field ministry.
You deal with a sticky, difficult situation
and put into practice what you’ve learned from the Christ.
This is the way to get the full impact.
You’ve read and studied what he was thinking,
but now you know how he was feeling
—how it feels to unselfishly give of oneself in behalf of others.
How does it really feel to act with humility as Jesus did?
Or you come to know how it really feels
to forgive from the heart as Jesus did.
In this way, by experience
you come “to know the love of the Christ,”
and that ‘surpasses the knowledge.’
Now not only is what you know about God and is treasured in your heart in sync
but now your actions, your life,
and who you are is in sync with Jehovah.
Indeed, like King David, who expressed in the 139th Psalm,
you dear students have found in God’s Word
the precious thoughts of Jehovah.
Continue to search them out,
bring them to mind, cherish them, and do them.
And then you will be living your life in sync with Jehovah.
Well, we are very grateful for that heartfelt talk, Brother Gordon.
Now we go to one of our Gilead instructors for the next talk;
it’s Brother Mark Noumair.
And he will speak on the subject
“Offer Your Bow.”
At the age of 20, he was a natural leader,
commanding a thousand men.
His tribe was legendary
for their military prowess.
He was known as a skilled archer.
His bow never turned back from its target.
He was the firstborn, favored prince
—courageous, loyal, loved by the people.
Everything was lining up perfectly
for Jonathan to become Israel’s next king
—everything except
that he was not Jehovah’s choice.
So how would he react when he saw David
receive Jehovah’s special favor?
How would he react when David
was now transferred permanently
to the king’s house?
Would he be filled with envy, jealousy?
Would he feel threatened?
Would he work to assassinate David’s character?
After all,
David was 30 years younger than Jonathan
and came from a rather insignificant family.
So, what would Jonathan do?
This is what he did.
He did something remarkable.
And it’s found at 1 Samuel 18:3, 4.
And this is what we want you to think about: what he did do and the application,
because this is so valuable for you.
First Samuel 18:3, 4:
“And Jonathan and David made a covenant,
because he loved him as himself.”
Now, note verse 4:
“Jonathan took off the sleeveless coat
“that he wore and gave it to David,
“along with his gear, his sword,
his bow, and his belt.”
Now, this dramatic act of deep symbolism
indicated that Jonathan would submit
his will to Jehovah’s will.
He was going to humbly support David.
But think about it.
By offering his bow to David,
Jonathan was giving up a major part of his identity.
The Bible describes Jonathan as a manly warrior
—‘swifter than an eagle,’ ‘mightier than a lion.’
He was winning battles against the Philistines
before David was even born.
But was he worried about losing the respect of others?
Did he say: ‘What will people think of me?
Will I lose my credibility if I support this younger David?’
No.
Nor did he feel that Jehovah rejected him
because of the special favor upon David.
Jonathan’s bow and his other war equipment
were his trademark,
and that symbolized his military power.
But the bow did not make the man.
Love made the man
—love for Jehovah, love for Jehovah’s choices.
This is what we’re highlighting.
And once Jonathan offered his bow,
he never retracted it,
even when he knew
that David would be the next king.
He respected the divine arrangement,
and repeatedly Jonathan would support David.
He would reassure David, ‘You are Jehovah’s choice.’
Jonathan was not insecure.
He was not afraid to appear insignificant.
He was not threatened to see David rise;
nor did he view David as a rival to be eliminated.
Now, in human terms, this cost Jonathan.
He lost the prospect of being king;
he lost his close relationship with his father;
he might have lost some stature in the eyes of men.
But in spiritual terms, he gained.
His unselfish devotion to David
received honorable mention in God’s Word,
which never would have happened had he resisted Jehovah’s choice.
We wouldn’t even be talking about this right now
if he took a fleshly view
of Jehovah’s divine arrangement.
So this is your first big lesson:
Don’t measure your worth by your job title.
It’s your love of Jehovah
—that’s what makes you so valuable.
A spiritual person is a most powerful tool
in the hands of God, and this is what you are.
So how can you imitate Jonathan?
Offer your bow
by showing your support of Jehovah’s organizational decisions,
even if it means giving up something you love
or want to cling to.
For example,
some of you have been given new country assignments,
and yet you might not have planned
on moving to another country.
You were content where you were; you were happy doing what you were doing.
Thank you.
Thank you for your unselfish support of the decisions made
to advance Kingdom interests globally.
Thank you.
Or perhaps you’ve been trained in some capacity
—something you really enjoy.
And yet now someone else is assigned to do that job.
Will you, like Jonathan,
put your heart into supporting and reassuring
the new person that took your job?
And how about you as a sister?
What about if a new sister comes and gets
the job assignment you love, you cherish?
You wake up every day ‘I love my job!’
and now you’re asked to train her.
What will you do?
Will you offer your bow?
Or the sister gets the office that you dreamed of
—the one with the window.
There it is. You had your eyes set on it.
You might have seniority.
She could be younger than you, but perhaps oversight
took other factors into consideration
that you were not aware of.
What will you do?
What will all of you do in these situations?
Will you accept the fact that supporting decisions
by the organization at times
involves sacrifices on your part?
Well, let your love for Jehovah
mean more than your cherished work assignment.
And this is a very, very big lesson —lesson number one—
and very important for you to think about,
offering your bow in this way.
You’ve already shown this spirit.
We’re just reinforcing something
that you need to hear prior to your departure.
Now, I want you to think about this for a moment.
Compare Jonathan’s good example
with that of his brother Ish-bosheth.
When Saul died,
2 Samuel 2:8 says
that his general, Abner,
made Ish-bosheth king
—no loyalty to Jehovah’s choice.
And Ish-bosheth agreed, ‘I want that.’
Ish-bosheth craved position,
which led to a civil war, which led to problems.
Now, instead of Ish-bosheth offering his bow
and his war equipment to David,
2 Samuel chapter 2
describes how he provoked war with David,
which resulted in bloodshed
and the death of 380 men in Israel.
Ish-bosheth’s heart wasn’t with David.
That was Jehovah’s choice.
He was unlike his brother Jonathan.
But now imagine if Jonathan was still alive
when Saul died and Abner now comes to Jonathan and says:
‘Jonathan, I want you to be king.
You’d make a great king.’
Would Jonathan have agreed?
Would he have then said, ‘Give me my bow back’ and retract it
and take it back and tell David: ‘No, I feigned loyalty to you.
This is what I really wanted. I want to be king’?
No. No.
Jonathan wouldn’t have done that.
Why?
Because he gave not just his bow to David,
he gave not just his war equipment to David (no),
he gave his very heart to Jehovah’s choice.
And that’s the beautiful thing about him.
The difference between Jonathan,
who sees an opportunity to support Jehovah’s cause,
and Ish-bosheth, who never thought for a moment
about how Jehovah God was directing David, is striking.
And the results speak for themselves.
Jonathan was loved and honored.
Ish-bosheth was hated and murdered.
When Jonathan died,
David was so deeply grieved
by the loss of his dear friend
that he was moved to do something.
And what he did is recorded
at 2 Samuel 1:17, 18.
I’d like to read this to you.
Second Samuel 1:17, 18:
“Then David chanted this dirge [or this song]
“over Saul and his son Jonathan and said
“that the people of Judah should be taught
the dirge [the song] called ‘The Bow.’”
“The Bow.”
Could David have had in mind the bow
that Jonathan gave him at the beginning of their friendship?
Jonathan supported the nation without demanding
that he receive high rank, or position.
Jonathan was so loyal.
It was a powerful lesson that David never forgot,
and neither did he want the sons of Judah to forget,
because he instructed that they all learn this song by heart.
Offering your bow
is a powerful word picture.
When you continue to work in the background
(work quietly in the background),
in loyal support of Jehovah’s choices
despite the cost, despite the human imperfections,
despite the disappointments, despite the perceived injustices,
you don’t worry about all of that.
That’s simply the ebb and flow of life.
Pick yourself up; keep on moving; grow mighty;
become a living example to the brotherhood in loyalty.
That’s what you’ve been trained to do.
And you will receive
Jehovah’s attention and favor
just as Jonathan did.
Jehovah did not merely dismiss Jonathan as a would-have-been king.
No.
Rather, he took note of Jonathan’s loyal support
and had his wonderful example embedded,
etched, into his inspired Word.
So as you go to your assignment,
what is your bow?
Everyone has one.
Is it your cherished work assignment?
Is it that privilege that you have been given that few others enjoy?
Is it the responsibility
that requires many to consult you for direction?
Well, think about this:
The time will come
when someone is put in a leading role,
and you will be asked to support that person,
work under that person, help that person.
And when that time comes, ask yourself,
‘What will I do?’
And not just you brothers, you sisters too,
I mean, you wives, will you support?
will the wife support as well?
Single sisters, will you support the arrangement?
That’s the point.
Ask yourself: ‘Will I offer my bow like Jonathan?
‘Will I offer it freely?
‘Will I offer it generously to anyone chosen
for a role of responsibility within God’s organization?’
And be assured that Jehovah in turn will offer you
—offer you an unimaginable treasure.
And that treasure is his favor and approval.
Jehovah’s favor and approval
—what is better than that?—
now and life in the new world.
And when you get to the new world,
be sure to look for the one
who inspired you to offer your bow.
Well, we thank you, Brother Noumair, very much for that encouraging talk.
In fact, we’ve enjoyed a series of wonderful talks this morning, haven’t we?
What an encouraging program thus far!
And in the upcoming weeks,
look for Parts 2 and 3 of the graduation program.
They’ll be found under Latest Videos
or under the Video on Demand segment of JW Broadcasting.
We’ll conclude this month’s program
by traveling to the tropical island of Kosrae in Micronesia.
Located in the Pacific Ocean,
Kosrae is filled with dense jungles, mangroves,
picturesque beaches, and is surrounded by beautiful coral.
Many on the island work in the tourism,
fishing, or agricultural industries.
Although the official language of Kosrae is English,
there’s a remote translation office here.
One brother and four sisters assist with translating literature
into Kosraean.
There’s one congregation on Kosrae
with 2 field missionaries, 2 special pioneers,
and 2 regular pioneers, and a total of about 15 publishers.
They preach to the over 6,000 inhabitants of the island.
And their hard work is bearing fruit.
For example, in 2018,
there were 82 in attendance at the Memorial celebration
and a peak of 65 attended the regional convention.
And in 2018,
the congregation reported some 60 Bible studies.
The brothers and sisters in Kosrae
send you their warm love and greetings.
And by means of this program,
we all send our love and encouragement back to them.
This is JW Broadcasting
from the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

공사 방식이 제가 알던 것과 약간 달라서,
여기선 상황이 다르다 보니까 일도 다르게 하는 거죠.
처음엔 같은 언어를 쓰니까 다 비슷할 줄 알았습니다.
하지만 같은 언어라도 차이가 있다는 걸 알게 됐어요.
처음 와서 특이했던 점 하나는 인사였는데,
내가 오늘 좀 아파 보이나 하는 생각이 들어요.
제가 살던 곳에선 뭘 지시할 때
무례해서가 아니라 그냥 그 지역 문화가 그렇죠.
하고 물어 본 다음에 본론을 꺼내더라고요.
이 방법이 참 좋은 게, 같이 일하는 형제들을 잘 알게 되요.
큰 차이가 아니어도 그렇게 부른다는 걸 모르면
익숙한 방식일 수 있지만, 여기 방식은 다른 것이죠.
처음엔 왜 다르게 하는지 의문이 들 수 있지만
같은 일을 하는 다른 방법을 배우게 됩니다.
제가 현지 언어를 배우려고 노력할 때
시간을 내서 현지 문화를 공부해 보니까
왜 다른지 이유를 알고 나니 거슬리지가 않아요.
형제 자매들을 이해하면 그들을 사랑하고 긍정적으로 보기가 더 쉽죠.
마감일도 맞춰야 하고 제약이 되는 점도 있지만
감독자들께서 세 가지는 결코 희생해선 안 된다고 했는데,
집회 참석과 야외 봉사와 가족 숭배죠.
영성이 있어야만 문제를 극복할 수 있어요.
영적인 시각이 없으면 어려움을 겪게 됩니다.
분명한 건 우리가 영성을 잘 돌보면
나머진 여호와께서 돌보셔서, 일이 다 잘된다는 겁니다.
참을성과 친절, 사랑, 오래 참음이 필요해요.
다들 평화를 이루는 이런 특성들을 나타내니까
무엇을 하든 여호와의 영을 분명히 볼 수 있어요.
다른 문화를 가진 다양한 형제 자매들과 함께 일하는 건
전에 일하던 곳에선 이런 차이가 문제가 됐어요.
하지만 이곳에선 그런 게 문제가 되지 않아서 정말 좋습니다.
모든 나라와 종족과 언어에서 나온 사람들에 관한
이걸 글로만이 아니라 직접 경험하고 있어요.
여호와께선 언어를 혼란시켜 공사가 중단되게 하셨습니다.
다양한 언어와 문화에서 나온 형제들을 연합시키셔서
자신의 공사가 성공적으로 수행되게 하고 계십니다.

en.text: Theocratic projects are largely built by volunteers from all over the world,
speaking different languages, from different cultural backgrounds,
with different work practices
—things that could divide and create barriers.
One of the biggest challenges for me has been the language
—above all, the accents and the way people speak.
The ways of construction are a bit different than what I’m used to.
That can create a challenge.
You might be used to doing something one way.
But then here we do it differently because of different circumstances.
Initially, we thought that with a similar language,
things would be the same.
But even with a similar language, we learned that there are differences
in how we speak and the things that we say.
Are you OK?
One of the things that I think probably got us when we first arrived was the greeting.
We’re used to just saying “hello,”
but a lot of times we would be greeted with . . .
All right?
Hey, are you OK?
After being asked that several times in the same day,
you begin to question whether or not you actually are all right.
That’s just how they say “hello” here.
Oh, OK.
In the culture where I’m from, people are a bit more straightforward
and to the point when they’re giving instructions,
which is not being rude.
It’s just the way we do it there.
Here I learned that it’s nice to ask:
“How are you? How’s your day?
How was your weekend?”
—and then get to the point.
It’s something I got used to, and I really like it
because you get to know the brothers that you work with.
There are different ways of saying the same thing.
Lauren, can I have the spanner, please?
Sure!
And the differences aren’t really all that big.
Since you don’t know it, it becomes a challenge to understand at first.
But it makes it a little more exciting
—a little fun!
Oh, it’s that one.
This one?
Oh, thank you. A wrench.
It might be a way of doing things at home
that I’m used to or that I’ve been learning in school.
But then here we do it differently.
It’s just a matter of obedience,
and you do as you are instructed.
At first, you might question,
“Why are we doing it differently?”
But if you’re patient and you wait,
then you realize that you’ve just learned another way of doing something.
Hey, give me some guanti, please.
Something that is really nice to see is that when I try to learn the language,
the brothers help me —and that’s a real blessing!
Taking our time to learn
about the culture has really helped us to understand why things are different.
And then, when you understand why they’re different,
it doesn’t really bother you.
You understand your brothers and sisters,
and it makes it easier for you to love them and to be positive.
We realized that we are the ones
that have to adapt to the new culture
—the new nation.
We have to have Christ’s mentality.
He came to serve, not to be served.
Spiritual things keep us united
—to not see the negatives in other cultures, accents, and work practices.
Although there may be deadlines and constraints,
keeping our spirituality up is of the utmost importance.
Our overseers reminded us of three nonnegotiable things:
our meeting attendance, the field ministry, and our family worship.
Spirituality is everything
when it comes to overcoming challenges
because if you don’t have a spiritual view of things, then you will struggle.
What continues to be more evident is that if we take care of our spirituality,
then Jehovah will take care of the rest.
The work will get done.
The key to unity here on site is that everyone is working on “the fruitage of the spirit.”
We need to be patient, kind, loving, long-suffering.
They exhibit these qualities that really pursue peace,
and it makes it easy; it makes it fun.
And you realize: ‘You know what? We are just working with family.’
And of course, Jehovah’s spirit is clearly shown
in everything that we do.
Having all the different brothers and sisters and the different cultures is special,
and it really does help you grow.
Where I worked before, differences were an issue.
It’s beautiful to see, however,
that here it doesn’t matter where you are from or what job you are doing.
We are all on the same level; we are all equal.
It makes you think of Revelation 7:9
where the scripture talks about people of every tribe and nation and tongue
—and we’re one family.
And instead of just reading about it, when we’re here we experience it.
When Nimrod was building the tower of Babel,
Jehovah used language to halt the project.
Yet, today, working on a project
with so many different languages and cultures,
Jehovah is unifying them to make his project successful!

title: 우리의 조직이 이루고 있는 일들—오리지널송 제작 과정

ko.text: 2014년 10월에 조직은 첫 JW 방송 프로그램을 방영하면서
그 후 거의 5년 동안 영적 목표를 갖도록 격려하는 오리지널송이
지금도 계속 새로운 노래가 나오고 있습니다.
집안일을 하면서 계속 틀어 놓을지 모릅니다.
이 노래들은 전 세계에 있는 우리의 형제 자매들에게
많은 기쁨과 위로와 영적인 격려를 주고 있습니다.
교습 위원회가 오리지널송을 만드는 모든 과정에 관여합니다.
어떤 느낌을 전달할지를 정하는 것까지 말이죠.
음악이 마음을 움직이는 힘이 있다는 걸 알기 때문에
음악 팀은 승인된 주제와 지침을 검토하고
하나의 노래에 두 사람을 배정하기도 하죠.
예를 들어, 가사 작업은 영국에서 하고
그걸 합치면 다양한 문화권의 사람이 좋아할 만한
그걸 녹음해서 교습 위원회가 검토하도록 보냅니다.
위원회는 기도로 인도를 구하며 오리지널송을 검토한 뒤,
음악 팀과 스토리 팀에 가사, 음악, 영상에 관한 지침을 전달합니다.
그러면 팀들은 그 지침에 맞춰 제작에 들어가죠.
필요한 부분을 수정하고 최종 녹음을 합니다.
전 세계 여러 나라의 음악가들이 사용되죠.
다른 지부의 녹음 엔지니어를 사용하기도 합니다.
그러면 엔지니어가 노래와 반주를 합쳐서 노래를 완성합니다.
이제 다음 단계로 넘어갈 수 있습니다.
11개의 국제 비디오 팀 중 한 곳에 작업을 배정합니다.
영상의 초안을 그리는 사람이 배정된 팀과 밀접히 협력하는데,
영상의 초안을 그리는 사람이 영상 감독과 팀과 함께 일하면
해당 지역의 문화와 풍경을 초안에 포함시킬 수 있죠.
이렇게 초안이 만들어지면 뮤직비디오의 초벌 영상을 제작하는데,
위원회가 이 초벌 영상을 검토하고 승인하면,
팀에서는 실제 촬영과 제작에 들어갈 수 있습니다.
성서 시대 영상이나 현대 영상의 정확성을 확인합니다.
그 후 필요한 부분을 수정하면 위원회가 최종 승인을 합니다.
인터뷰나 재연 영상을 번역하는 것과 아주 다르죠.
노래를 할 때는 실제 단어가 아닌 소리를 내기도 합니다.
사람들이 헷갈리지 않도록 허락을 받아 다른 말로 바꿨습니다.
또 가사가 나오는 단순한 악보도 만드는데요,
이걸 보면서 형제들은 직접 연주하며 노래를 부를 수 있죠.
전 세계 형제들이 보낸 편지들을 보며 큰 격려를 받습니다.
이 노래들이 많은 사람에게 감동을 준다는 걸 알게 되니까요.
저는 요리를 하거나 빨래를 갤 때 오리지널송을 듣죠.
가족 숭배 때 같이 노래하며 춤도 춰요.
전 매달 나오는 이 노래들을 정말 좋아합니다.
저희 딸도 노래 덕분에 사랑을 나타내는 법을 배웠어요.
친구들에게 편지도 쓰고 가진 걸 나눠 줍니다.
전 출근길에 차에서 이 노래들을 듣습니다.
그러면 정말 행복해지고 하루를 보낼 힘이 나죠.
같이 일하는 사람들이 절 짜증 나게 하거나 화나게 할 때가 있거든요.
상사가 제게 거친 말을 할 때도 있죠.
그럴 때면 점심시간에 차로 가서 오리지널송을 듣습니다.
그러면 마음이 차분해지고 다시 기분이 좋아져요.
남은 하루를 행복하게 보낼 수 있죠.
이 노래들은 형제 자매들에게 큰 축복이 되고 있습니다.
오리지널송은 우리의 믿음을 강하게 해 주고,
영적 목표를 세우려는 동기를 불어넣어 주고,
여호와를 계속 충성스럽게 섬기려는 굳은 결심을 하게 해 줍니다.

en.text: An introduction to the book of Ephesians.
The apostle Paul first came to the port city of Ephesus
on his second missionary tour,
probably in 52 C.E.,
accompanied by Aquila and Priscilla.
After a short visit, Paul departed,
leaving Aquila and Priscilla behind
to continue preaching and teaching.
But on his third missionary tour,
Paul stayed for about three years,
zealously carrying out his ministry
and forming a close bond
with the Ephesian brothers.
Later, about 60 or 61 C.E.,
the apostle Paul wrote the letter
to the Ephesian congregation.
He wrote it from Rome,
where he was under guard awaiting trial.
The letter to the Ephesians has six chapters.
Chapter 1 highlights
that God purposed an administration
(or a way of managing his household).
By this means,
those chosen to live in heaven
and those who would live on earth
would be united with Jehovah through Christ.
In chapter 2,
the apostle likens the Mosaic Law to a wall
that had long separated Jews and Gentiles.
The sacrificial death of Jesus abolished the Law covenant
and thus “destroyed the wall in between” the two groups.
In chapter 3,
Paul mentions “the sacred secret of the Christ”
and explains that it is God’s will to include non-Jews
among the relatively small number of humans
who are called to reign with Christ in heaven.
Did you know?
The city of Ephesus was famous
for a huge temple dedicated to the goddess Artemis.
As related in Acts chapter 19,
silversmiths of Ephesus had a lucrative business
selling small “silver shrines of Artemis.”
During his roughly three-year stay in Ephesus,
Paul had exposed as wrong the use of images in worship.
As a result, a number of people in Ephesus
abandoned their idolatry and became believers.
Because of that,
those making and selling such idols
became infuriated and caused a riot.
In chapter 4,
the Ephesians are counseled to “put away the old personality,”
according to their former conduct,
and to “put on the new personality”
in harmony with Jehovah’s will.
In chapter 5,
Paul encourages the Ephesians to “go on walking in love.”
That love should be reflected in the family.
Wives are counseled to “be in subjection to their husbands.”
Husbands are counseled to “continue loving” their wives,
“just as the Christ also loved the congregation.”
In chapter 6,
Paul uses an illustration about armor
and urges the Ephesians to put on
the complete suit of spiritual armor.
Doing so will help them
to remain faithful despite all difficulties.
As you read the inspired letter to the Ephesians,
note how we must put on the new personality
according to Jehovah’s will,
how we should put on the complete suit of spiritual armor,
and how Jehovah purposed to unite Jews and non-Jews
as heirs with Christ in the Kingdom.

en.text: Our audience needs to see the connection
between the scriptures that we read and the point we’re making.
We can accomplish this when we introduce a scripture
in a way that draws attention to the main point
and then emphasize key words as we read the text.
But that’s not always enough
for the audience to grasp the application of the scripture.
Therefore, after reading the text,
it’s important to offer an explanation,
even if the scripture is familiar to the audience.
We can make the application clear by
isolating key words,
by explaining how those words
relate to our reason for reading the text,
and by not complicating the application with irrelevant details.
To illustrate, see if you can discern
where the following speaker succeeds
and where he fails in making scripture application clear.
Today, many churches baptize people
by sprinkling water on them.
Is this how baptisms should be done?
Let’s read how Jesus was baptized
according to Mark 1:9, 10.
Look for the answer to this question:
When Jesus was baptized, was he sprinkled with water?
“In the course of those days,
“Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee and was baptized in the Jordan by John.
“And immediately on coming up out of the water,
“he saw the heavens being parted
and, like a dove, the spirit coming down upon him.”
Another popular practice in Christendom is infant baptism.
Wait!
The speaker just moved on to the next point.
He had a good introduction, and he read with proper emphasis,
but he took no time to make the application.
He didn’t give the audience time to reflect
on the meaning of what they just read.
Let’s give him another chance.
“And immediately on coming up out of the water,
“he saw the heavens being parted
and, like a dove, the spirit coming down upon him.”
Notice that verse 10 says that Jesus
came “up out of the water.”
That means that he had been
completely immersed in the river.
So Jesus was not merely sprinkled with water, was he?
Because Christians try to follow Jesus’ steps closely,
wouldn’t it be reasonable that Christian baptism
would entail complete immersion and not mere sprinkling?
Another popular practice in Christendom is infant baptism.
Notice that the speaker did not comment
on unrelated details of the verses he read.
For example, he didn’t elaborate on the end of verse 10
because it didn’t contribute to the main point.
Whether you’re teaching from the platform or in the ministry,
help your listeners to see clearly the connection between the scripture you read
and the point you’re making.

ko.text: 특히 우리 형제들에게 사랑을 나타내라고 격려합니다.
오늘 생각해 볼 주제는 “사랑의 길을 추구하십시오”입니다.
‘쫓다, 잡으려고 꾸준히 따라가다’ 라는 뜻이 있습니다.
어린아이가 나비를 쫓아가는 장면을 떠올려 볼 수 있겠는데요,
나비를 잡기 위해 애쓰면서 쫓아가고 있습니다.
생각해 보면 사랑도 우리를 벗어나려고 합니다.
주된 이유는 우리의 타고난 불완전성 때문입니다.
원래 아담이 여호와의 형상대로 만들어졌다고 알려 줍니다.
아담은 여호와와 그분의 특성을 완벽히 반영하고 있었고,
하지만 그는 죄를 지었고, 불완전성이 시작됐습니다.
서커스 같은 곳에서 볼 수 있는
왜곡된 거울을 떠올려 볼 수 있는데요.
이런 거울로 보면 우리가 실제보다 훨씬 더 커 보이거나
작아 보이거나 뚱뚱해 보이거나 날씬해 보이죠.
네, 우린 여호와와 그분의 특성을 왜곡된 모습으로 반영하게 되었고,
자, 그럼, 여호와께서도 사랑의 길을 추구하신다고 할 수 있을까요?
그분은 애쓰지 않고도 자연스럽게 사랑을 나타내십니다.
성경 전체가 사랑을 추구하는 법을 알려 주지만,
사랑을 추구하는 방법을 구체적으로 알려 줍니다.
사랑에 관한 이 16가지 표현을 자세히 조사해 본다면
우리는 사랑을 추구하는 올바른 방법을 알 수 있습니다.
방법을 몰라 헤매거나 잘못된 방법으로 표현하지 않게 되죠.
사랑을 나타내는 것이 아닌 행동 몇 가지를 함께 살펴보겠습니다.
성경에서 질투는 좋은 의미도 있고, 나쁜 의미도 있죠.
좋은 의미로 질투는 열심과 밀접한 관련이 있습니다.
하지만 여기 언급된 질투는 물론 나쁜 의미고,
성경에선 질투가 나쁜 뜻으로 쓰인 경우가 대부분이죠.
다른 사람에게 생긴 좋은 일을 시기한다는 의미입니다.
화가 나더라도 금세 풀릴 수 있지만,
질투는 깊이 품고 있을 수 있죠.
뼛속까지 영향을 줄 수 있다고 말합니다.
우리는 어떻게 질투하지 않고, 사랑을 추구할 수 있을까요?
로마서 12장에 나와 있는 대로 해야 합니다.
둘 중 뭐가 더 힘들다고 생각하십니까?
보통, 우는 사람과 함께 우는 건 그리 어려운 일이 아니죠.
누가 암에 걸렸거나 가족을 사별했을 때,
하지만 기뻐하는 사람과 함께 기뻐하는 건 더 어려운 경우가 많죠.
누가 좋은 걸 받았거나 좋은 일이 생겼는데,
지역 대회 연설 임명을 받고 아주 기뻐하고 있다고 합시다.
우리도 늘 그런 특권을 원했지만 받지 못했다면 어떨까요?
우리는 기뻐하는 형제와 함께 기뻐할 것입니까?
그냥 겉으로만 형제와 함께 기뻐하는 척 하면서,
우리는 기뻐하는 형제와 함께 진심으로 기뻐할 수 있습니다.
우린 사랑으로 질투를 무너뜨릴 수 있습니다.
사랑의 길을 추구한다면, 기도로 도움을 청하며,
말할 때 자신을 높이지 않기 위해 노력할 겁니다.
또한 자기 자신에게 주의를 이끌게 만드는
“나는”, “내가”와 같은 표현을 너무 자주 쓰지 않을 겁니다.
다른 사람들과 특히 우리 하느님 여호와께 주의를 이끌 겁니다.
우쭐대는 건 뽐내는 것과 관련이 깊은데,
그런데 뽐내진 않지만 우쭐댈 수 있을까요?
사실 우리도 그럴 수 있는데, 겉으로 드러내진 않지만,
자기 자신을 너무 중요하게 생각할 수 있습니다.
우쭐대는 게 왜 사랑이 없는 태도일까요?
그렇게 되면 결국 사람들을 세워 주는 게 아니라
여호와께서는 우리 마음의 그런 태도를 보시고
우리의 생각과 관련해 이렇게 하라고 하시죠.
마땅히 생각해야 하는 것 이상으로 생각하지 마십시오.”
네, 여호와께선 우리가 자신에 대해 그런 식으로
반면에 예의가 부족한 정도의 무례함도 있죠.
우린 조금이라도 무례하게 행동하고 싶지 않을 겁니다.
특히 베델 봉사자로서 예의 있게 행동하길 원하죠.
예를 들어, 고맙다는 말과 공손한 표현을 자주 사용하고,
다른 사람을 위해 문을 잡아 주고,
다른 사람이 먼저 자신이 좋아하는 것을 선택할 수 있도록
형제들을 복도에서 마주칠 때 따뜻한 인사를 건넬 겁니다.
마주친 그 형제보다 전자 기기에 더 관심을 갖지 않을 겁니다.
사랑에 대한 다음 표현으로, 사랑은 “성내지 않습니다.”
초록불로 바뀌자마자 뒤에 있던 차가 경적을 울립니다.
우린 화가 나서 일부러 느리게 출발할 것입니까?
또한 사랑은 “해를 입은 것을 기억해 두지 않습니다.”
이 말은 해를 입은 기억을 정신에서 완전히
이것은 빌려 준 돈에 대한 장부를 기록하듯,
해를 입은 것을 유념해 두지 않는 것을 가리킵니다.
해를 입은 기억은 있을지 몰라도 마음 속에서 용서한 것이죠.
사랑에 관한 여섯 가지 표현을 알아 봤습니다.
직접 조사해 보시도록 숙제로 내 드리겠습니다.
오늘 우리가 배운 건 사랑을 추구해야 한다는 것인데,
살펴본 것 중에 노력 없이 되는 건 하나도 없습니다.
하지만 여호와의 도움으로 사랑을 추구할 수 있죠.
그땐 더 이상 사랑을 추구할 필요가 없을 겁니다.
하지만 그 멋진 때가 오기 전까지,

en.text: Today’s scripture text and Watchtower comments
encourage us to exert ourselves
to show love to others,
especially our brothers.
So let’s discuss the theme
“Pursue the Way of Love.”
And interestingly, that expression,
“pursue love,” is found three times in the Bible.
The verb “pursue” is very appropriate.
Why?
Well, it means to chase,
to persistently follow in an effort
to overtake or capture.
Now, we could illustrate with
a small child chasing a butterfly
—pursuing it, chasing,
pursuing in an effort to overtake or capture.
Now, what is the butterfly trying to do?
Get away, escape, evade.
If we think about it, that’s what love tries to do to us.
But, now, why?
The question is, Why does love try to get away from us,
thus requiring that we pursue it?
Well, the main reason
is because of the imperfection that we’ve inherited.
Genesis 1:27 tells us
that originally Adam was made
in Jehovah’s image,
perfectly reflecting Jehovah and his qualities.
He did that just perfectly.
But then when he sinned,
imperfection entered.
And we could say that Adam became
a distorted reflection of Jehovah and his qualities.
Now, we can illustrate this
with a distorted mirror,
perhaps at the fair or circus.
It can make you look a lot taller,
a lot shorter, a lot fatter,
a lot thinner than you really are
and distort you in other ways.
Well, in effect, Adam became a distorted reflection
of Jehovah and his qualities,
and we’ve inherited that condition.
We are distorted reflections
of Jehovah and his qualities,
so we have to pursue love.
But now let me ask this,
Would you say that Jehovah is pursuing the way of love?
Well, that could be a trick question.
But is Jehovah chasing, trying to catch love?
No.
First John 4:8: “God is love.”
He just naturally displays it, see.
He doesn’t have to work at it.
He, you can say, radiates it.
It emanates from Jehovah God.
But with us it’s different, see.
In our imperfection,
love is not our natural inclination;
we have to pursue it.
But now the question is, How do we do it?
Well, the entire Bible tells us how to pursue love,
but specifically the five verses
at 1 Corinthians 13:4-8
tell us how to pursue love.
Now, there we have 16 expressions of love:
nine ways that love does not behave
and seven ways that it does behave.
And if we closely examine those 16 expressions of love,
we’ll have direction in our pursuit of love.
We won’t wander aimlessly;
we won’t travel erroneously.
Now, as time permits,
let’s discuss some of the ways that love
does not act and ways it doesn’t behave.
One: “Love is not jealous.”
Now, in the Bible, jealousy can have a good connotation or a bad connotation.
In the good connotation, it’s closely related to zealous.
But, of course, here Jehovah is using it in the bad sense,
and by far the majority of times in the Bible that’s the way the word is  used.
Now, what does it mean?
Well, it means envious
of good things coming to others.
It can be worse than anger.
Anger can come and pass quickly,
but jealousy can be harbored deep.
In fact, Proverbs 14:30
talks about it being deep down in the bones.
Well, how can we avoid jealousy
and pursue love even though it’s not easy?
We have to prayerfully, with Jehovah’s help,
do what is mentioned in Romans chapter 12.
Please turn there.
In Romans chapter 12,
here’s what Jehovah tells us to do,
verse number 15:
“Rejoice with those who rejoice;
weep with those who weep.”
Now think about it.
Which of the two is the hardest?
Well, generally, it’s not so hard to weep with someone who is weeping.
They found out they have cancer; they lose a loved one in death.
We can be very sorry with them.
But, now, often it’s harder
to rejoice with someone who rejoices.
They may receive some good thing
or something good has happened to them,
and it didn’t happen to us.
Now, here’s just one little illustration:
Let’s say an elder is so happy that he received
an assignment for the regional convention.
Now, we’ve always wanted to get an assignment,
but we didn’t get an assignment.
Are we going to rejoice
with our brother who is rejoicing
—not just on the outside,
outwardly appearing that we’re happy for him—
but inside we have jealousy?
Truly in our heart being happy,
rejoicing with our brother who is rejoicing
—with Jehovah’s help— we can do that.
We can work on our attitude.
And if you think about it, about the only emotion
that is stronger than jealousy is love.
With love we can smash jealousy.
Now, another expression of love: Love “does not brag.”
If we’re pursuing the way of love,
we will prayerfully work hard
not to elevate ourselves in our speech.
We’ll strive not to so often use the pronouns
“I” and “me,”
thus directing attention to ourselves.
Rather, we’ll play our role down.
We’ll direct attention to others
and especially to our God, Jehovah.
Another expression of love:
Love “does not get puffed up.”
Now, puffed up is closely related to bragging
because normally a person who is puffed up brags, doesn’t he?
But do you think it would be possible to be puffed up and not brag?
Yes.
We could actually have this attitude, thinking too much of ourselves
even though we didn’t make an outward expression of that attitude.
Well, why would that be unloving
if we were puffed up but we didn’t brag?
Well, others would sense it
—see, that attitude would come across.
It would project and, in effect,
it would put others down rather than build them up.
And most important, Jehovah would read that attitude in our heart,
and he wouldn’t bless us.
So here’s what he tells us to do regarding our thinking.
Romans 12 again,
and this time take a look at verse 3,
and right in the middle there Jehovah says:
“I tell everyone there among you
“not to think more of himself
than it is necessary to think.”
So you notice, Jehovah is saying that we
shouldn’t even think that way about ourselves.
We should have a humble attitude.
Another expression of love:
Love “does not behave indecently.”
Now, there are varying degrees of indecency
—shocking indecency, immorality.
But on the other end of the spectrum,
perhaps a lack of good manners.
Well, we don’t even want to be slightly indecent, do we?
Especially as Bethelites, we want to have good manners
by generously using the expressions
“thank you” and “please,”
by holding the door for others,
by allowing them
to have their preferences
—the first place, and so forth.
When we pass them in the hall,
warmly greeting our brothers
and not being more interested in our electronic device
than we are that brother that we’re passing.
See, show good manners
as we interact with our brothers.
Another expression of love: Love “does not become provoked.”
Now, here’s one example, just quickly.
Let’s say we’re driving our car;
we’re parked at a red light;
the light turns green,
and immediately the person behind us blows the horn,
indicating we should move on quicker.
Now, does that get to us?
Do we start off very slow?
We’re going to make them pay for that.
Well, we’re getting provoked.
Remember, love does not get provoked.
One more example: Love “does not keep account of the injury.”
Does that mean we have to totally blot out of our mind
any recollection of the injury?
No.
As the scripture says, we don’t “keep account of the injury,”
which would indicate maintaining a ledger
—a debt being owed.
Now, we may remember the injury,
but we have forgiven in our heart.
We have cancelled the debt.
Well, there we have six expressions of love.
And I’m going to assign you the other ten
to do the research there in those verses that we were talking about.
But from our discussion, it’s obvious that we have to pursue love.
It doesn’t come easy;
it doesn’t come effortlessly
—none of these expressions.
Like that butterfly we talked about  in the beginning
trying to get away from the child,
love tries to get away from us.
But with Jehovah’s help, we can pursue it.
And we’re going to have to keep doing this.
How long?
Well, until the marvelous time
when we’re perfect,
and then we’ll no longer have to pursue love.
Like Jehovah and Jesus,
we will simply be able to display love.
But until that marvelous time,
may 1 Corinthians 13:4-8
give direction to our pursuit of love.

cn.text: 今天的每日经文和守望台评论
都鼓励我们要尽力对别人表现爱心
特别是爱我们的弟兄姐妹
所以我们今天要讨论的主题是
《追求爱这至善之道》
有趣的是
“追求爱心”这个词组在圣经中出现了三次
“追求”这个动词用得非常贴切
为什么这么说呢？
因为它有追逐、坚持不懈地追的意思
这就好像，一个小男孩在追一只蝴蝶
追啊，追啊，坚持不懈地追
那只蝴蝶会等着被抓吗？
当然不会
它会马上逃走
仔细想想，就会发现爱也是一样
向人表现爱心就像小孩子追蝴蝶一样难
为什么呢？
为什么爱会逃走
我们甚至要去追它呢？
主要原因是
因为我们都不完美
创世记1:27提到
亚当是按照上帝的形象创造的
能够完美地反映出上帝的本质
和他的各种特质
但亚当犯罪，变成不完美的人之后
就没办法反映耶和华的特质了
这种情况就好像是你在游乐场
或是在马戏团看到的哈哈镜
镜子中的你可能看起来
比实际的你更高或更矮、更瘦或更胖
事实上，亚当的情况正是这样
他像哈哈镜一样
无法完美地反映出上帝的特质
而这种情况也遗传给我们
我们现在也无法完美地效法耶和华
无法完全反映他的特质
所以我们都需要“追求”爱心这个特质
你觉得耶和华也需要努力追求爱心吗？
你可能觉得他也需要
但其实他完全不需要
约翰一书4:8说
“上帝就是爱。”
他自然而然就可以表现出爱
不需要付出什么努力
也可以说
上帝散发出爱的光芒
他是爱的源头
但我们就不同了
因为我们不完美
不会自然而然就有爱心这种特质
所以必须努力去培养
问题来了
我们可以怎样培养呢？
其实整本圣经都在教导我们
怎样追求爱心这个特质
特别是在哥林多前书13:4-8
里面提到16种表现爱心的方法
其中有些是我们该做的
有些是我们不该做的
如果我们仔细探讨这16种方法
就会知道怎样去爱别人
不会用错误的方法或是
不知道该怎么去表现爱
接下来
我们讨论几个有爱心的人不会做的事
第一个是
“爱不嫉妒”
这里翻译成“嫉妒”的希腊语词
有时指正面的特质
有时指负面的情绪
正面的特质跟热心有关
当然，耶和华在这里用的是负面的意思
在圣经里这个词大多数时候都是负面的
那么，嫉妒是什么意思呢？
嫉妒的人会眼红别人有好的际遇
嫉妒比愤怒更糟
愤怒的情绪可能来得快去得也快
但嫉妒却会一直深藏在心里
事实上
嫉妒甚至能使人的骨头腐烂
虽然不容易
但我们怎样做才能对别人表现爱心
不嫉妒别人呢？
我们需要祷告
求上帝帮助我们做到
罗马书12章里面所说的事
我们来看看
在罗马书12章里上帝要我们做什么
15节说
“要和欢乐的人一同欢乐
和哭泣的人一同哭泣。”
想想看，这两件事
哪件事比较不容易做到呢？
通常，和哭泣的人一同哭泣并不困难
可能有人得了癌症
或者失去了亲人
看到这种情况
我们也会为他们伤心难过
但和欢乐的人一同欢乐就没那么容易了
我们不一定会因为别人得到了很好的东西
或是有很好的际遇就为他们开心
我们现在来考虑一种情况
有一位长老收到区域大会的委派
非常高兴
我们自己也一直很想有这样的机会
但始终没收到委派
我们会跟这个弟兄一起“欢乐”吗？
还是只是表面上为他高兴
心里却在嫉妒呢？
在耶和华的帮助下
我们是可以做到
发自内心跟弟兄一起“欢乐”的
我们可以努力改变自己的态度
要记住
虽然嫉妒是一种很强烈的感情
但爱更有力量
只有爱才能帮助我们战胜嫉妒
另外一点就是“不吹嘘”
如果我们努力追求爱这种特质
就会祷告求上帝帮助我们
不在说话时抬高自己
我们会尽量避免常常使用“我”这个代词
不要让人觉得我们把自己看得很重要
不要把注意力放在自己身上
要放在其他人身上
特别是耶和华上帝身上
还有一种表达爱的方式就是“不自大”
自大跟吹嘘是息息相关的
因为通常一个自大的人会自我吹嘘
你觉得一个人有没有可能自大但不吹嘘呢？
有可能
我们可能表面上没说什么也没做什么
但可能心里却把自己看得很重要
为什么说我们虽然没有吹嘘
但在心里自大也是没有爱心的表现呢？
因为其他人还是可以感觉得到我们的态度
这种态度还是会不经意地表现出来
让别人灰心
最重要的是
耶和华清楚了解我们内心的真实情况
他会因此不再赐福给我们
在罗马书12章耶和华告诉我们
我们的心里应该有怎样的想法
我们看看12:3的前半部分
“我凭着所得的分外恩典吩咐你们
不要自视过高。”
注意到了吗？
耶和华不要我们把自己看得很重要
我们应该保持谦卑
另一个表现爱心的方式是
“不罔顾规矩”
“罔顾规矩”有分很多种
有的是非常下流的行为
比如不道德的性行为
轻的呢
例如没有礼貌
我们不想做没有规矩的人
就连没有礼貌这样的行为我们也不想做
尤其是在伯特利
我们应该对人表现礼貌
我们会常常对人说“请”、“谢谢”
也会帮别人开门
尊重别人的喜好等等
我们在走廊上跟弟兄姐妹擦肩而过时
要亲切地跟他们打招呼
不要一直盯着手机或平板
跟弟兄姐妹相处时一定要有礼貌
另一个表现爱心的方式是“不轻易动怒”
我们来想象一种情况
例如你在开车
正在等红灯的时候
绿灯突然亮了
后面有人马上就按喇叭催你快点开
你会不会很生气呢？
你会故意慢慢开来气死他吗？
如果你这样做的话
就像经文说的那样
“轻易动怒”了
别忘了，爱是“不轻易动怒”
还有一种表现爱的方式
就是“不计较别人所加的伤害”
这是不是说
我们必须完全忘记别人对我们的伤害呢？
不是
经文说
我们“不计较别人所加的伤害”
意思是我们不会把别人对我们的伤害
一笔一笔记下来
我们可能还没忘记那些伤害
但我们选择从心里宽恕对方
把对方的错一笔勾销
我们刚刚讨论了六种表现爱的方式
另外十种就是你们的作业了
大家可以自己做一下个人研读
从刚才的讨论可以清楚看出
我们必须追求爱这种特质
爱的每一方面都不容易表现出来
需要我们刻意培养
就像刚才提到的蝴蝶一样
爱也会离开我们
可是，在耶和华的帮助下
我们是可以追到爱的
我们会不断追求爱心
追多久呢？
在我们变完美之前
都不会停止
我们变完美的那一刻
就不用再追着爱跑了
就可以像耶和华和耶稣一样
自然地表现爱心了
在那一刻来到之前

帮助我们表现爱这至善之道

title: 외딴 지역을 방문하는 순회 감독자의 일주일

ko.text: 화요일 오전 9시에 브라질 북부의 도시 벨렝에서
여행하는 감독자 부부가 이 배에 올라,
그들이 일주일간 머물 평화로운 외딴 섬으로 향합니다.
코티주바섬에 가는 중인데요, 한 시간쯤 걸리죠.
항구에 닿으면, 형제 자매들이 기다리고 있을 거예요.
우린 말이나 오토바이가 끄는 마차에 짐을 싣고 올라타서,
한 주 동안 지낼 숙소로 가죠.
할 수 있는 건 다 해 주려고 하죠.
아무거나 주는 게 아니라 가장 좋은 걸 줘요.
형제들이 경제적으로 넉넉하지 않다는 게 자주 보여요.
하지만 우리에게는 좋은 음식과 머물 곳을 마련해 주는데,
어떤 건 자신들은 평소에 누리지 못하는 것들이에요.
우린 주는 것보다 받는 게 훨씬 더 많아요.
순회 감독자는 장로들과 함께 회중 기록을 검토합니다.
형제 자매들은 이 시간을 손꼽아 기다렸죠.
형제 자매들은 이 세상에서 이미 어려움을 많이 겪죠.
저하고 있을 땐 최대한 마음 편하게 해 주려고 노력해요.
매일 오전과 오후에 회중과 함께 전도 활동을 합니다.
섬이 커서 넓은 지역을 다녀야 합니다.
한 곳에서 점심을 먹고, 섬 저 끝에서 성서 연구를 한 후,
또 이곳 교통수단은 시간이 이랬다저랬다 해서,
필요할 때 늘 이용할 수 있는 게 아닙니다.
사랑 많은 한 가족의 집에서 점심을 먹습니다.
점심 먹으러 와 보니, 맛 좋은 음식이 정말 많네요.
새우와 오크라로 만든 요린데, 풍미가 좋아요.
이 부부는 한 주 내내 아침부터 바쁜 일정을 소화하면서도,
남편이 장로 및 봉사의 종 모임에 가면,
전 그 시간을 활용해서 개인 연구도 하고, 방도 치우죠.
순회 감독자의 방문을 여러 달 전부터 기대합니다.
그래서 순회 방문은 회중 성원 모두에게,
우리가 어떤 점을 바꾸고 개선하면 더 좋을지 배웁니다.
그리고 6개월 후 다시 모일 때, 자신이 얼마나 발전했는지 알게 되죠.
여러분의 훌륭한 본과 열심과 인내를 보면서요.
매일 식사도 마련해 주시고 저희를 잘 돌봐 주셨습니다.
또 방문 내내 모든 마련을 지지해 주시는 걸 느꼈습니다.
오전 봉사, 오후 봉사, 성서 연구 마련도요.
저희를 후대하시고 이 방문 동안 적극 지지해 주신 여러분께
이제 이 모든 게 다시 시작됩니다.
하지만 이번엔 다른 지역에 있는 또 다른 회중에서죠.

en.text: It’s 9:00 a.m.
on a Tuesday morning.
A boat leaves the harbor in Belém, a city in the north of Brazil.
A traveling overseer and his wife are on the boat,
heading for a peaceful, rural island where they will spend the week.
We’re going to the island of Cotijuba.
It’s about an hour away.
There are no cars on the island.
We’ll arrive at the harbor, and there’ll probably
be some friends already waiting for us there.
We’ll get a horse-drawn or a motorcycle-drawn carriage,
load up our luggage, and go to where we’ll be staying for the week.
The generosity of the friends is incredible.
They can’t do enough for us.
They’ve been preparing to receive us for the last six months
—we can really feel that.
They don’t give us just anything; they give us their best.
You notice that often the friends don’t have
very much financially—they really don’t.
But they prepare things for us to eat or give us somewhere to stay
—things that sometimes they don’t have for themselves during their day-to-day life.
You just have to love them.
Everything we do doesn’t compare to what they do for us.
On Tuesday, after lunch, the circuit overseer
starts analyzing the congregation records with the elders.
Also, that evening,
he delivers his first talk.
The friends really look forward to this.
They go through so much in life
and this makes them feel looked after.
One of the things that I always make
an effort to do is encourage the friends.
That’s the key.
I think the friends already suffer a lot in this world.
I try to help the sisters
and the brothers feel as comfortable as possible around me.
After that, every morning  and every afternoon
the couple goes out with the congregation
in the preaching work, on return visits, and Bible studies.
You have to cover a large area because it’s a big island.
So you have lunch in one area,
then you go to one end of the island for a Bible study,
then to the other end for a shepherding call.
And don’t forget that the transportation available here
is quite precarious and it isn’t always available when you need it.
After a busy morning in the ministry,
lunch is at a loving family’s home.
And of course, local dishes are a must!
We’ve arrived for lunch.
Look at how many delicious things there are —all traditional food.
This is maniçoba,
a delicious local dish.
And these are white beans—really tasty.
What else do we have here?
Caruru—a dish made
from okra and shrimp—full of flavor too.
The couple’s week is full of activities with an early start every morning,
but they never forget to feed themselves spiritually too.
While my husband is at the meeting with the ministerial servants and elders,
I make the most of my time by doing my personal study.
And then I tidy up a bit before he arrives.
Months before the visit,
we start looking forward to the circuit overseer’s arrival
because we need guidance and encouragement.
That’s why the visit is really good for us,
for all the members of the congregation,
and for the circuit overseer.
When we have the pioneer meeting, we get a better idea of what we need to adjust
and where we need to improve.
And when we have the meeting again six months later,
you realize how much you’ve changed and that makes you
really happy and motivates you.
Brothers, it was a pleasure for my wife and I to visit you this week.
We were really pleased and encouraged by your good example,
by your zeal, and by your endurance.
Your generosity made us very happy
—the meals,
the care you showed us every day.
We felt your support throughout the visit
—in the mornings,
the afternoons,
on Bible studies—
for all the arrangements that were made.
We thank you from our hearts
for all of your care
and excellent support during our visit.
And so it all begins again.
But this time, in another congregation in another place.
