베델 봉사에 대해 자녀와 늘 이야기를 나누고,
자녀가 전 시간 봉사에 관심을 갖게 도우십시오.
베델을 견학하기 위해 미국 뉴욕주에 있는 세계 본부나
자녀와 함께 방문하도록 마련해 보시기 바랍니다.
그러면 자녀는 베델에서 왕국 권익을 증진하기 위해
어떤 일을 수행하는지 직접 볼 수 있을 것입니다.
여호와께 드리는 봉사를 확장할 잠재력이 있는 회중 청소년들이
여호와께선 봉사를 확장하라는 자신의 초대에 기꺼이 응할 사람들을
“내가 누구를 보낼까? 누가 우리를 위하여 갈까?”
다른 흥미진진한 신권 봉사를 할 자격을 갖추게 되어,
그분이 주신 건강과 활력을 더 온전히 사용할 수 있게 될 것입니다.
많은 분이 래프랜카 형제가 알려 준 내용에 격려를 받아,
여호와께선 우리가 영적으로 바쁘게 일하는 데
도움이 되는 많은 마련을 해 주시죠.
우린 그중 하나인 지역 대회를 기대하고 있는데요.
준비된 대회 소개 동영상을 함께 보실까요?
진정한 사랑이란 무엇이며, 어디서 찾을 수 있는지,
어떻게 진정한 사랑을 주고받을 수 있는지
우리가 사랑을 찾을 수 있다고 알려 주십니다.
그 사랑은 결코 없어지지 않을 것입니다.
우리의 형제 관계는 큰 힘을 발휘합니다.
수백 명 혹은 수천, 수만 명이 모이는 우리의 대회는
서로를 격려할 수 있는 최상의 기회입니다.
24개의 국제 대회가 세계 전역에서 열리기 때문이죠.
여러분이 지역 대회나 국제 대회에 참석하는 이 좋은 기회에
형제 자매들을 더 많이 알게 되시기 바랍니다.
성경에 나온 많은 일이 그 지역에서 일어났습니다.
바로 터키에서 가장 높은 아라라트 산 부근이었죠.
골로새, 갈라디아 회중도 이 지역에 있었습니다.
거의 550만 명에 달하는 사람들에게 열심히 봉사하고 있습니다.
터키의 회중들은 주로 공개 증거를 하는데,
고대 시리아의 도시 안티오크 근처에 있는
바울은 안티오크를 선교 여행의 본거지로 삼았죠.
오늘날 터키의 이 지역은 음식으로도 유명한데,
그중엔 향신료와 허브와 과일과 단 음식이 있죠.
최근 이 지역은 전쟁과 소요 사태를 겪었습니다.
분쟁이 일어난 곳 근처에 사는 형제 자매들은
총성과 폭탄이 터지는 소리를 듣기도 했습니다.
회중엔 11명의 정규 파이오니아와 2명의 특별 파이오니아를 포함해
전 세계의 형제들에게 사랑과 안부를 전합니다.
열심과 굳건한 믿음을 보이는 그들에게 우리도 사랑을 전합니다.
지금까지 여호와의 증인 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다.

en.text: Welcome, brothers and sisters, to JW Broadcasting.
In this month’s program,
we’ll learn ways to deal with worry and anxiety.
Here are some highlights.
From childhood, this brother found it a challenge
to attend meetings, go to school, hold a job,
and even leave his home each morning.
What can we learn from his experience
to help us cope with our anxieties
one day at a time?
These two sisters have worked shoulder to shoulder in full-time service
for more than 60 years.
We’ll learn what has helped them to remain joyful
despite everyday struggles and unexpected trials.
Have you ever wondered what motivates
our brothers and sisters to make themselves available for Bethel service?
We’ll hear from ones who are serving at Bethel,
and we’ll learn how to prepare and qualify
for this special form of full-time service.
There’s much to enjoy in this May 2019 edition
of JW Broadcasting.
Do you sometimes feel completely overwhelmed
when life’s problems cause you anxiety?
Just trying to provide the necessities
for one’s family can lead to anxiety.
At the same time,
you might be dealing with a chronic or life-threatening illness,
caring for a sick or elderly relative,
grieving the death of a loved one,
loneliness, a natural disaster,
or maybe you’re struggling with the devastating effects
of past or present abuse.
Now, you firmly believe that God’s Kingdom will fix these problems,
but that’s in the future.
What about today?
Perhaps you feel like David,
who prayed at Psalm 13:2:
“How long will I have anxious concern,
with grief in my heart each day?”
A sister who has struggled with anxiety for many years wrote this:
“Anxiety robs me of sleep, impacts my health,
affects the way I treat others, and makes me want to give up.”
She added: “Anxiety is like a monster
“that lives in my body somewhere between my heart and my belly.
“I cannot wait for Jehovah to kill that monster in the new world.
“But until then, the monster snarls and tears at my insides
and tries to take over my life.”
Can you identify with her feelings?
We often hear a person say concerning anxiety:
“I’m just trying to take it one day at a time.”
But one brother put it this way:
“I try to take it one day at a time,
but sometimes several days attack me at once.”
For so many of us, anxiety is a daily struggle.
If you battle with anxiety,
please know this: You are not alone.
Do not give up the fight.
Jehovah and Jesus are aware of the anxieties
that weigh on your mind and that are deep in your heart.
The Governing Body knows that living in this system of things
is especially “hard to deal with.”
So the theme chosen for this program is
“Deal With Anxiety One Day at a Time.”
First, what is anxiety?
In the Christian Greek Scriptures,
the word “anxious” occurs 19 times.
The first occurrence is in Jesus’ Sermon on the Mount.
Now, Jesus knew that people worried about how to provide for their family.
So at Matthew 6:25,
he gave this wise counsel:
“On this account I say to you:
“Stop being anxious about your lives
“as to what you will eat or what you will drink,
“or about your bodies as to what you will wear.
“Does not life mean more than food
and the body than clothing?”
The Study Bible note for verse 25
says that “the Greek term for ‘anxious’
“can refer to worry that divides a person’s mind
and distracts him, robbing him of joy.”
At Luke 12:29,
Jesus says to “stop being in anxious suspense”
or to “stop worrying.”
The study note here says
that the Greek word for “anxious suspense” was used
to refer “to ships being tossed at sea.”
It says that Jesus used it “figuratively
“for being anxious or unsettled,
“as if tossed about or wavering
because of doubt and anxiety.”
By saying “stop being anxious,”
Jesus recognizes that anxiety is already in progress.
He is very aware of our imperfect nature.
He knows that we tend to bring our worries from yesterday
(the would-haves, could-haves, and should-haves)
and our imagined worries about tomorrow
(the what-ifs) to today.
But ask yourself,
‘How often have I worried myself sick about what might happen tomorrow,
only to find that tomorrow wasn’t nearly as bad as I feared it would be?’
Jesus also knows that anxiety can have real,
sometimes painful, consequences.
It can stop us from making spiritual progress.
Overthinking and overanalyzing our problems
can literally shut us down.
How, though, can we “stop being anxious”?
What’s the antidote?
Let’s consider four practical things we can do.
First, rely on Jehovah
and take one day at a time.
This is exactly what Jesus prescribed for us
at Matthew 6:33, 34:
“Keep on, then, seeking first the Kingdom
“and his righteousness,
“and all these other things will be added to you.
“So never be anxious about the next day,
“for the next day will have its own anxieties.
Each day has enough of its own troubles.”
Verse 34 has a study note
telling us that “undue anxiety about what may happen in the future
“can adversely affect a person’s relationship with God,
causing him to rely on his own wisdom rather than on God’s.”
So, what’s the lesson?
Instead of relying on ourselves,
rely on Jehovah, and take one day at a time.
A cross-reference to Matthew 6:34
takes us to Exodus 16:4.
In this account,
Jehovah provided the Israelites with enough manna
for every day of their 40-year trek.
Could Jehovah have provided
a week’s worth of manna? a month’s worth? a year’s worth?
Of course.
So why did he only provide enough for each day?
Well, think about it.
When they stepped out of their tents each morning,
there was no question whether there would be manna on the ground or not,
and there was no question where it came from.
Jehovah never failed to provide for their needs,
not even for one day.
They also knew from the past that Jehovah
always provided for those who were loyal to him.
We too can look back at how Jehovah provided for his servants.
We can have complete confidence that Jehovah knows exactly
what we need when we need it
—for today, tomorrow, and for all eternity.
Even if we have such confidence,
why do we sometimes continue to feel anxious?
The simple answer:
We’re imperfect people trying our best
to serve Jehovah in Satan’s wicked world.
Daily challenges cause anxiety that can make us forget to rely on Jehovah
and take one day at a time.
So we need to add our second way to deal with anxiety:
Pour your heart out
to Jehovah in earnest prayer.
Read with me the reassuring words
at Philippians 4:6, 7:
“Do not be anxious over anything,
“but in everything by prayer
“and supplication along with thanksgiving,
“let your petitions be made known to God;
“and the peace of God that surpasses
“all understanding will guard your hearts
and your mental powers by means of Christ Jesus.”
Paul doesn’t simply tell us not to be anxious,
but he tells us how.
He said “by prayer and supplication,”
which is earnest and specific prayer.
With what benefit?
The “peace of God . . . will guard your hearts.”
“Guard” was a military expression referring to troops
assigned to protect a city.
The inhabitants could sleep soundly
knowing that soldiers were guarding them at night.
In a similar way, when we have “the peace of God,”
our hearts and minds can rest.
This can prevent us from being overwhelmed by anxiety or discouragement.
How reassuring are the words of the psalmist
at Psalm 4:8:
“I will lie down and sleep in peace,
“for you alone, O Jehovah,
make me dwell in security.”
So when we feel trapped, like there’s no way out of our worries,
the peace from God gives us hope
that there’s light at the end of the tunnel.
What, though, must you do?
Turn your worries into deep, heartfelt prayers.
In fact, at 1 Peter 5:7,
Jehovah invites you to “throw all your anxiety on him,
“[and leave it with him]
because he cares for you.”
Jehovah is the one person who truly understands how you feel.
He knows every moment of your life
—why you feel or react a certain way.
He loves and values you personally
despite your imperfections, your anxieties,
your cares and worries.
He not only has the power to help you, he wants to.
Knowing this should move you to pray specifically,
expressing your deepest emotions
and pleading that he grant you peace of mind and heart.
To the extent you do so,
1 Peter 5:10 promises
that “he will make you firm,
“he will make you strong,
he will firmly ground you.”
Never underestimate the power of prayer!
Jehovah is always ready to help you
—one day at a time.
Our third way to deal with anxiety
is to read and meditate on God’s Word.
Let Jehovah speak to you.
Allow Jehovah’s thoughts to become your thoughts.
At Psalm 94:19,
notice how the psalmist admitted his own anxiety:
“When anxieties overwhelmed me,
you comforted and soothed me.”
Yes, even servants of God can feel overwhelmed by anxieties
or, as one translation says, “burdened with worries.”
That in itself is comforting
that an inspired Bible writer struggled with anxieties.
But Jehovah “comforted and soothed” him,
calming his troubled heart.
God can do the same for us
through his inspired Word, the Bible.
Remember, the Bible is how Jehovah speaks to us.
Rather than allowing our emotions to run wild,
we can learn to focus our mind on upbuilding things,
such as what the apostle Paul listed at Philippians 4:8:
“Finally, brothers, whatever things are true,
“whatever things are of serious concern,
“whatever things are righteous,
“whatever things are chaste,
“whatever things are lovable,
“whatever things are well-spoken-of,
“whatever things are virtuous,
“and whatever things are praiseworthy,
continue considering these things.”
The footnote to verse 8 shows that “considering”
involves “thinking about” or “meditating on.”
We can and should meditate on positive things from the Bible,
replacing negative things that may enter our mind and cause anxiety.
Ask Jehovah to help you to find passages
in his Word that will soothe your heart.
Ask others what scriptures have calmed their heart during anxious moments.
Make your own personal list.
Then set aside time to read
and meditate on those passages.
Meditation is the doorway to your heart.
Meditation lets God’s thoughts affect you
on the deepest possible level.
Imagine that Jehovah is speaking directly to you,
because he is.
Never underestimate the power of God’s Word
—of letting Jehovah speak to you.
Our fourth way to deal with anxiety
is to share your feelings with a trusted friend.
Proverbs 12:25 says:
“Anxiety in a man’s heart weighs it down
“[or, as the footnote says, ‘depresses him’],
but a good word cheers it up.”
“A good word” can come from a fellow believer
who is motivated by God’s spirit and guided by his Word.
When the apostle Paul was alone in prison,
he prayed for encouragement
and Jehovah provided what he needed to cheer him up.
With a heart full of appreciation,
he said at Colossians 4:11
that “my fellow workers  . . . have become
a source of great comfort to me,”
or “a strengthening aid.”
What can you do if you feel weighed down or imprisoned by anxiety?
Like Paul, pray for encouragement.
Pray for someone you can talk to,
someone you can trust with your feelings.
The answer to your prayer may be an elder
or a mature Christian brother or sister.
But what if it’s difficult for you
to open up to others and confide in them?
Try the advice in the March 1, 1997, Watchtower article
“Are You Afraid to Trust Others?”
When confiding in someone
it says: “Reveal your concerns gradually.
“If he [or she] responds in an appropriate,
“sympathetic, and discreet way,
you might then try disclosing more.”
Even if it takes some effort,
never underestimate the power of our brotherhood.
Jehovah can use a fellow worshipper
to ease your mind of “anxious concern.”
Even at times when there’s no one to talk to,
we can let the experiences,
upbuilding music,
and talks on JW Broadcasting® be like
an encouraging hug from a trusted friend.
Yes, when we make the effort, we give Jehovah something to bless.
Jehovah can help us conquer the seemingly unconquerable.
That may not mean that we’ll completely eliminate anxiety,
but we can learn to take control.
How?
Remember our four ways:
First, rely on Jehovah
and take one day at time;
second, pour out your heart
to Jehovah in earnest, specific prayer;
third, read and meditate on God’s Word
—let Jehovah speak to you;
and fourth, share your feelings with a trusted friend.
With Jehovah’s help,
you can deal with anxiety one day at a time.
Earlier, I read a quote from the sister who described
anxiety as a monster living inside her.
I’m so pleased to say that the sister who wrote that letter about her anxieties
is actually here with us in the studio to tell us more about her experience.
This is Jordan Williams and her husband, Robert.
Thank you so much
for coming here to share with us your battle with anxiety.
Can you elaborate on that, please?
I feel ashamed of my anxiety.
I feel like there’s something wrong with me, and I feel guilty about that.
I feel like I’m letting Jehovah down by feeling anxious
and that I’m even being disobedient to Jesus,
when he says: “Stop being anxious.”
But I just can’t.
Thank you for sharing that.
Robert, what do you do to help Jordan battle this anxiety?
It’s a monster —sometimes a very stubborn monster—
that won’t go away.
Remembering that it’s not her fault
helps me be more compassionate
and caring—listening when she’s explaining these anxieties
that I may not completely understand.
Jordan, are there other practical things that help you battle anxiety?
The single biggest help is walking with Jehovah every day.
I mean that literally.
I’ll wake up in the morning super anxious.
And I can’t breathe; and my chest is tight.
And I’ll get up, and I’ll read the chapter
of the Bible that the daily text comes from.
And then I’ll go on a walk and talk to Jehovah for an hour,
and I try to use the model prayer as an outline.
So I’ll talk to Jehovah about his name
and how I feel so privileged to have that name on me.
And I’ll talk to him about his Kingdom
that’s going to solve all of these problems, including anxiety.
And I’ll talk to him about his will
and specifically what his will is for me that day.
And most of the time,
those three things cover the things that were worrying me.
But if there is another thing, I’ll talk to him specifically about that.
What a nice walk you have with Jehovah.
Are there other things that help you deal and battle anxiety?
Personal study projects help a lot,
especially if they don’t have anything to do with anxiety.
If I do a study project on the spiritual suit of armor or the ransom,
it kind of distracts the “anxiety monster” so that my heart can calm down,
and then these pearls of wisdom will come from Jehovah, and they can get in.
And some of those pearls are actually just what I need to deal with my anxiety.
Are there specific things that help you?
Yes, I made an Anxiety tab in the Personal Study section
of my Study Bible on my tablet,
and I collect scriptures and comments
that really help with my anxiety.
For example, in 2014, there was a regional convention talk
about Matthew chapter 6 and six specific things that combat anxiety.
And it made me think of the twelve-step program  to overcoming addiction.
These are the six steps to overcome anxiety.
What are those six steps?
The first one is to help those in need,
and then pray a lot, to be forgiving,
not to be hypocritical, to store up treasures in heaven,
and then to focus on spiritual matters.
So when we got back from the convention,
she took those items and she wrote them down
and put them on magnets and put them on our refrigerator.
I try to do each one of those six things every day.
And when I accomplish one, I’ll turn the magnet
so that I can see what I still need to work on.
So when I come to the refrigerator in the morning,
if the magnets are turned, we know where she’s at.
If they’re not turned, we know we’re in trouble.
It’s a bad day.
It’s time to do something else.
Very good—nice barometer.
So, what can others do or say
that would be helpful to those going through anxiety?
For the friends, it’s really nice when they’re understanding
and nonjudgmental
and respect my privacy (that’s really helpful)
and when they don’t freeze me in time
or decide that ‘Oh, she’s anxious, and this is how she’s going to be all the time.’
That’s really helpful.
I even forget that Jehovah approves of me.
So reminding me of that
—reminding me that the things that I do to please him are successful
and maybe even reminding me of things that I have accomplished for Jehovah
in the past.
You know, you should tell Ron about your broken dish.
Oh, yeah.
Yes. I’d like to know about that.
So I just found out about this Japanese art called Kintsukuroi.
And it’s basically taking
a broken piece of pottery and fixing it by putting it back together
with gold or silver lacquer,
and the concept is that the piece is more beautiful for having been broken.
And that really resonates with me because I do feel broken by anxiety.
But Jehovah gave Jesus as a ransom,
and that ransom is just pure gold;
and He can take all the broken anxious little bits of me
and put me back together.
And maybe I’ll even be more useful to Jehovah for having been broken.
That’s very precious.
Thank you for sharing that.
Are there other things that help you deal with anxiety?
I’ve learned to recognize when anxiety is clouding my thinking,
and I’ll ask him, “Can I borrow your brain for a minute, please?”
So, what we did is we went and purchased a whiteboard and put it in my office.
And sometimes we’ll go to the whiteboard
and write out all the anxieties that she’s dealing with.
As we are writing them out,
sometimes we realize that those are yesterday’s anxieties
and that they’ve been cared for, so we can erase those from the board.
Some of them are for tomorrow,
and so we don’t want to borrow those and bring them to today.
They’re tomorrow’s anxieties.
And some anxieties can be grouped in little clusters,
and you can realize, ‘The root is here; let’s focus on that.’
I fight anxiety every single day.
And anxiety is constantly changing its tactics, so I have to be adaptable.
But Jehovah never leaves me to fight anxiety alone—ever.
I don’t understand what I’ve done to merit all of his attention,
but I do realize that I don’t need to understand why he loves me.
I trust him, and he never lies,
so I just need to accept it when he shows me that love.
We appreciate you sharing those personal feelings.
And again, we know that Jehovah and Jesus are so proud of you.
And we know that those who are listening in to this interview
will benefit so much from listening to your personal expressions.
Thank you very much.
Anxieties can surface at any time in our lives,
even when we’re very young.
Imagine, though, if the stress of growing up in this system
was made worse by a chronic disorder,
one that made anxiety feel impossible to overcome.
We’ll be encouraged by the experience of Brother Steing Dott,
who never gave up on Jehovah.
See if you can identify what has helped him cope
one day at a time.
My name is Steing Dott.
I was born in 1988 in Darwin, Northern Territory.
When I was eight years old,
I realized that life was getting very difficult for me.
I was diagnosed with ADHD,
obsessive-compulsive disorder, Tourette syndrome.
And on top of all of that, I was diagnosed with severe anxiety as well.
My mum said this affected the entire family
because I would repeatedly yell out “Good night!”
to each individual person in the family.
And on top of that, I used to constantly go
around the house, checking the locks and the windows.
My school life was the hardest thing I’ve ever had to deal with.
My school was approximately 500 meters from my home.
It would take me at least two hours to get to school
because one of my obsessions was that if there were cracks on the footpath
and if I stepped on one,
I’d have to go all the way back home and start again.
Well, I found life to be a constant struggle,
and as I got older, it only got worse.
Even at ten years old, I decided that I wanted to end my life
so that it would make everyone in the family’s life a lot easier.
But then we decided to use some medication,
which eased my problems a little bit.
Despite having medication,
life was still completely unbearable for me.
I had a constant struggle every day within myself.
I used to wash my hands hundreds of times a day.
I couldn’t leave the home;
I couldn’t get a driver’s license; I couldn’t even get a job.
A major turning point in my life
was my mum’s unwavering faith in Jehovah.
She used to iron my clothes for the meeting
and hang them on the doorknob,
even though I wasn’t ready to attend the meeting.
But what she didn’t know was that when my mum
went to the meeting with my sister, I’d get a Bible,
and I’d try and start to read it.
I also began to pray to Jehovah.
And then one day, I thought, ‘I’m going to give this a shot.’
So I put my suit on, I got ready,
and I went to the meeting.
When I went to the Kingdom Hall, I was absolutely terrified.
I was so nervous.
But when I got there, I saw an elder
who used to come and visit me, and he made me feel very relaxed.
And then the amazing welcome by the brothers and sisters
—it made me feel like I was part of Jehovah’s organization again.
The scripture that really helped me
was 1 Peter 5:7 because it says:
“While you throw all your anxiety on him, because he cares for you.”
So this made me feel like I had a very powerful Friend,
and Jehovah wanted me to throw my anxieties on him because he loved me.
On September 4, 2010,
it was my most important day of my life.
I got baptized as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses
at Adelaide Entertainment Centre.
I now serve as a ministerial servant.
I’ve had the privilege of giving public talks,
which is something I never thought I’d ever be able to do.
I completed pioneer school after three attempts
because the pioneer school environment made me feel
like I was back at school and made me have anxiety again.
So the third time I completed it.
And none of this would ever have been possible without Jehovah’s help.
On the 6th of August 2016,
I married my beautiful wife, Laura,
who helps me serve Jehovah,
and we can serve Jehovah every day together.
I, like the apostle Paul,
still feel like I have a war inside me sometimes.
But definitely, Jehovah has never let me down.
Never give up on serving Jehovah
because Jehovah will never give up on you.
Did you notice what Steing considered the turning point in his life?
It was the unwavering faith of his Mum,
the warmth of the congregation
and, most of all, help from Jehovah.
He called Jehovah “a very powerful Friend.”
That’s so true!
Brother Dott overcame monumental challenges,
but is his struggle with anxiety over?
No.
He said that like the apostle Paul,
he sometimes still feels a war within himself.
Do you ever feel that way?
This month’s music video reminds us
that we can find peace and joy despite our burdens.
It’s entitled Each Day Has Its Own Anxieties.
I know about the Paradise under God’s Kingdom,
And I believe with all my heart that better days will come.
But sometimes in this life, for me, It’s hard to see the things unseen,
To feel the love I know is there when my heart is in despair.
But I know Jehovah’s near.
So I say a prayer from the heart. When worries overtake my mind,
On his strength I can rely. I’m not alone; I know he’s there.
I have his words of comfort And true friends who really care.
Yes, each day has its own anxieties. So I take one day at a time;
Leave tomorrow until tomorrow; Peace is what I find
One day at a time.
So take these words I’ve said, my friend, And know that I care.
Focus on the joys in life, Not the burdens that we bear.
Think about what God has done. To show his love, he gave his Son.
So never doubt; keep trusting him. He gave his best so we could live.
So don’t give in to fear.
Say a prayer from the heart. When worries overtake our mind,
On his strength we can rely. We’re not alone, for he is there.
We have his words of comfort And true friends who really care.
Yes, each day has its own anxieties. So take one day at a time;
Leave tomorrow until tomorrow; Peace is what we’ll find
One day at a time.
Say a prayer from the heart. When worries overtake our mind,
On his strength we can rely. We’re not alone, for he is there.
We have his words of comfort And true friends who really care.
Yes, each day has its own anxieties. So take one day at a time;
Leave tomorrow until tomorrow; Peace is what we’ll find
One day at a time— One day at a time.
“We’re not alone, for he is there.
“We have his words of comfort and true friends
who really care.”
What an encouraging thought from that song!
Yes, true friends who share our love for Jehovah are invaluable.
We’ll see that in this story from Japan.
Sisters Takako Sato and Hisako Wakui
have worked together as pioneers since 1957.
Let’s learn how their friendship
has helped them serve Jehovah with joy.
We are pioneer partners.
We’ve been working together
for over 60 years.
I was the only Jehovah’s Witness in Nagano prefecture.
It was lonesome,
but I applied for regular pioneer service.
Surprisingly,
I was appointed as a special pioneer.
I was so happy that I found myself
rolling around on the tatami-mat floor
with the appointment letter in my hand.
That was the way I expressed my joy and appreciation.
When I was invited to serve
as a special pioneer, I was sent to Nagano,
and that’s where I met Hisako.
Takako and I focused on our ministry.
When an isolated group was established,
since there were no brothers,
I would wear a head covering and conduct the meetings.
Sometimes the outlines were in English.
We didn’t understand anything.
But people were delighted to hear
even just the scriptures and went home satisfied,
and that strongly impressed on me the power of God’s Word.
We were assigned to a territory in the city after that.
We found so many not-at-homes,
but we were determined to meet people.
So we changed the times we preached,
and we talked to people on the street
who were going to work.
We cherished even small opportunities.
When we had a chance to meet a householder,
we always tried to have a conversation
that we could link to the next visit.
Before long, I had ten Bible studies.
Takako acts like she’s cheerful,
but she’s been fighting various illnesses.
At times, it was so bad
that I could not even go out in service.
I had a serious skin condition.
I could not bear
to look at the illustration of Job in the magazine,
and I covered it up with paper.
But Jehovah helped me to look to Job’s example.
I learned
that our endurance under trial
would become praise to God.
I have often had health problems.
Just at one of those times,
I received a letter from the branch.
It said:
“What you can accomplish now may be limited.
“However, think about all that you have done up to now
“to give praise to Jehovah
“and about the people you were able to help learn the truth,
and be joyful knowing that you have been used by Jehovah fully.”
I couldn’t stop crying
because I really felt the care and concern
from the organization and from Jehovah.
Hisako also took really good care of me
and prayed with me.
Our thinking and personalities are different,
but we made efforts to talk things out.
Our heartfelt desire to want to serve Jehovah full-time
has always been the same.
For 60 years, we’ve enjoyed
a truly wonderful life of service to Jehovah.
Jehovah has supported us in difficult times
through the Bible, the organization, and friends.
I have tasted the truthfulness of the words:
“When I am weak, then I am powerful.”
‘When I said: “My foot is slipping,”
your kindness, O Jehovah, has supported me.’
I can say that too.
Although we don’t have energy or ability,
we’ve been able to enjoy full-time service together up until now.
I’m really content now.
It’s all thanks to Jehovah.
Like the apostle Paul, our sisters cultivated singleness
and focused on full-time service to Jehovah
for more than 60 years.
Yes, they face everyday challenges
and the extra ones that come with age,
but their heartfelt desire to serve Jehovah whole-souled
brings Takako and Hisako real joy and contentment.
Whole-souled service for nearly 20,000 brothers and sisters
is a full-time assignment at Bethel.
What motivates them to reach out for this special privilege?
What blessings do they experience?
And what’s the best way to prepare and qualify for Bethel service?
I’d like to invite my friend Patrick LaFranca
to discuss these and other questions.
Welcome, Pat.
Thank you, Ron.
How heartwarming it’s been
to see millions take their stand for true worship!
Thousands more are joining us every week.
Jehovah is speeding up the ingathering work,
and this makes us very happy.
But who will work to provide the Bibles, Bible literature,
and the audio and video publications
that sustain us spiritually
and help us to accomplish our Kingdom preaching and teaching work?
Bethel is a unique place.
It’s where mature Christians
render sacred service to Jehovah
in close association with Christ’s brothers.
They minister to the needs of our worldwide brotherhood
and support the preaching work.
The Bethel family is a group of dedicated,
baptized servants of Jehovah
who live and work together closely.
So they experience in a special way
what Psalm 133:1 says:
“Look! How good
“and how pleasant it is for brothers
to dwell together in unity!”
We’re very pleased to see that many have expanded their service
to Jehovah by making themselves available
for the special privilege of Bethel service.
Have you considered this as a goal?
Making yourself available
for Bethel service is like knocking on a door that leads
to many other privileges of service.
Of course, to serve at Bethel requires
a self-sacrificing spirit
and a willingness to serve
wherever there is a need, in harmony with the attitude displayed
by the prophet Isaiah at Isaiah 6:8:
“Then I heard the voice of Jehovah saying:
“‘Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?’
And I said: ‘Here I am! Send me!’”
When Isaiah learned about an opportunity
to do more in Jehovah’s service,
he responded eagerly,
even though he did not know exactly
what he was going to be assigned to do.
It was enough for him to know that Jehovah
was extending an invitation to serve in a special way,
and Isaiah wanted to volunteer.
The same spirit is shown by Bethel family members worldwide.
What especially motivates so many to serve at Bethel?
Love for Jehovah moves us
to put Kingdom interests ahead of self-interest.
As stated in the Proclaimers book, page 295:
“This is not work in which they gain
“personal prominence or material possessions.
“Their desire is to honor Jehovah, and they are satisfied
“with the provisions made for them
“in the way of food, lodging,
and a modest [allowance] for personal expenses.”
Are there any rewards that come from serving in this unique way?
Those who have offered themselves willingly
for Bethel service have truly been blessed.
The love and unity we feel here is incomparable.
It’s not like in a company out in the world
because here you can work with your friends every day.
Like-minded people
have the same goals and support each other.
That is what you can feel here.
Maybe you’re assigned a task
that you’ve never performed before,
but there are many experienced brothers and sisters
who can help —professionally as well as personally.
Whether it is the consideration of the daily text
or the Watchtower Study with the Bethel family,
listening to the practical, valuable comments
of our brothers and sisters is really refreshing.
You really feel that they love Jehovah,
and their comments help you to feel the same.
Here in Bethel, you have the best Employer
that there is—Jehovah.
No other employer is as grateful and considerate as he is,
so out of love for Jehovah, you’re simply happy to give him your best.
Whenever I think about what
is being done at Bethel
—publications are being
produced and shipped,
videos for our conventions are being made,
and translation is being done
into so many different languages—
I keep getting goose bumps.
No matter what I can do here,
knowing that by doing it
I am supporting Christ’s brothers makes me feel very, very good.
So how does a young person
qualify for Bethel service?
My parents raised me to have
a spiritual focus.
So during the school holidays
and growing up, our life revolved around the ministry
—doing spiritual activities.
And it really helped us
keep focused spiritually as a family
and helped me stay focused on the goals that I wanted to achieve.
I really enjoy reading,
and one day my Dad just said to me,
“Why don’t you read the Bible?”
And I know it sounds obvious, but at that point, I had never read it
from Genesis to Revelation.
So when I finished reading the Bible,
it really changed my thinking,
and it really proved the truth to myself.
And this helped me to keep
a spiritual focus, and it really was the first step
in reaching out and achieving
the spiritual goals that I wanted to achieve.
In the congregation, I was able to help out
with doing the magazines and the sound and the platform.
And these privileges really helped me to build
a good work ethic and give in ways
that I could give more to Jehovah.
So the elders used to work with me a lot in the ministry.
So when I felt
that ‘I can’t do this’
or ‘This is too much’ or ‘It’s too overwhelming’
or ‘I’ll never be able to reach this goal,’ an elder showed me
a scripture in the Bible where Jehovah
was encouraging Joshua to be courageous.
And that really impacted me,
so that I was able to be courageous, too, and to reach my goal of Bethel.
So when I visited Bethel,
I saw that they were normal people,
and they had so many good qualities
that I wanted to imitate
—very hospitable, very warm,
very inviting.
That helped me to want to reach my goal, so that I could be like them.
To serve at Bethel
there are qualifications that need to be met.
You should have a deep love for Jehovah
and the organization, which is demonstrated
by living in harmony with Bible standards.
You must have a fine reputation
as a spiritual person.
You should have respect
for Jehovah’s moral standards,
avoiding uncleanness and sexual immorality.
You should have a clean conscience
before Jehovah and be at peace with yourself
and with Jehovah’s organization.
Your dress and grooming should be exemplary,
befitting a Christian minister
even during leisure time.
Styles that are faddish
or extreme or that identify us
with undesirable elements of the world
are not acceptable at Bethel.
The applicant should not read, listen to,
or view any type of material
that is inappropriate for a Christian.
Such unwholesome material
certainly would include pornography,
debasing music, or any kind of entertainment
that features sexual immorality,
spiritism, or violence.
Bethel applicants should be
from 19 to 35 years of age.
Occasionally, there is an opening
for someone over 35 years of age
who may have specialized skills
that are needed at Bethel,
such as those with certain technical
or medical experience, translation skills,
or building trades such as plumbing, electrical,
heavy equipment mechanics, or carpentry.
Those with such capabilities and training
are welcome to apply.
In view of the unique demands
of a full-time assignment at Bethel,
you should be mentally and emotionally sound,
physically strong, and able to work long hours.
You should be able to read, write,
and speak the primary language
of the branch territory.
This will enable you to communicate well
with others serving at Bethel,
to receive needed training, and to work safely
in the Bethel environment.
Bethel applicants agree to serve
for a minimum of one year,
during which time you will receive training
for continued Bethel service.
With regard to secular skills, we do not encourage individuals
to obtain university education
or training with the thought that this will improve
their chances of being called into Bethel.
The best way to prepare for Bethel service
is to first serve in the full-time pioneer ministry.
The greatest need is for single brothers.
However, all who meet the qualifications, including sisters,
are encouraged to apply for temporary volunteer service.
Serving as a temporary volunteer at Bethel may open
the way to other opportunities
to expand your service to Jehovah.
If you are interested in applying for Bethel service,
which application should you request
from a member of your Congregation Service Committee?
Since there are two types
of applications available, first give careful
and prayerful consideration
to your circumstances.
Thereafter, decide whether you will request from the elders
the Application for Volunteer Program (A-19),
which is available for those interested
in serving on a temporary basis
for as brief as one week or as long
as several consecutive months.
Or you may decide to request
the Application to Become a Member of the Worldwide Order
of Special Full-Time Servants of Jehovah’s Witnesses (A-8).
This application is for those interested
in serving on a long-term basis
for one full year or longer.
If the Branch Committee determines that there is a need
for your services, they will decide
where you can best be used, whether at Bethel
or perhaps on a theocratic construction assignment.
Submitting your application may open
a door of opportunity to serve Jehovah
and his organization in a variety of ways.
Of course, not all of us
who have such a self-sacrificing spirit
have the circumstances in life to serve at Bethel.
But we can encourage others who do.
Parents, follow the example
of God-fearing parents
such as Hannah and Elkanah,
who willingly made their son available
for expanded theocratic privileges.
Continue to place the goal of Bethel service before your young ones,
and stimulate their interest in the full-time ministry
by your example and your positive expressions.
If possible,
bring them on tour of world headquarters in New York, U.S.A.,
or make arrangements to bring them on a tour of the Bethel
in the branch territory in which you live.
Such visits can help young ones to witness firsthand
the work that’s being done at Bethel to promote Kingdom interests.
Elders, help young ones in your congregation
who have the potential to expand their service
to Jehovah to meet the qualifications.
Jehovah continues to look for those willing to respond
to his invitation to expand their service to him.
As in Isaiah’s day, He asks:
“Whom shall I send, and who will go for us?”
Will you answer as did the prophet:
“Here I am! Send me!”
We encourage you to progress to spiritual maturity
and serve Jehovah whole-souled.
In due time, you may qualify to serve at Bethel
or in another form of exciting theocratic service
that permits you to use the health and strength
that Jehovah has granted you in an expanded way,
all to his praise.
Please be assured that we love you
for the willing spirit you show
as you continue to reach out in Jehovah’s service.
Thank you, Pat.
We hope that the information Brother LaFranca shared
motivates many more to have
the prophet Isaiah’s willing and self-sacrificing spirit.
So much of what Jehovah provides encourages us
to keep busy with spiritual things.
For one, we’re looking forward to our upcoming conventions.
The theme for this year is “‘Love Never Fails’!”
Would you like a preview of the program?
Let’s take a look.
Love
—is it gone?
Have we lost it?
Is it the possession of the wealthy?
the strong?
Or is it somewhere else?
At the 2019 convention of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
you will learn what real love is,
where to find it,
and how to show it
and have it shown in return.
God cares deeply about you.
And he wants you to know
that in this hate-filled world,
love can be found.
It is not lost.
And that love will never fail.
As we’ve discussed, we should never underestimate the power
of our brotherhood to help us overcome worries and anxiety.
Our conventions are wonderful opportunities for us to encourage one another
by the hundreds, thousands, and tens of thousands.
And this year, we’re especially excited
that 24 international conventions
will be held throughout the world.
Use the opportunity to get to know more of your brothers and sisters
at the regional or international convention you attend.
To conclude this month’s program,
let’s visit our brothers in Turkey.
Turkey is a nation of more than 80 million people
and a land rich in Bible history.
Turkey occupies a unique geographic position, bridging Europe and Asia.
It’s here that Noah’s ark came to rest near Mount Ararat,
Turkey’s highest mountain.
This is the land of the congregations in Colossae and Galatia,
as well as all seven congregations
mentioned in Revelation.
The territory is diverse and vast,
with a publisher-to-population ratio
of 1 to more than 26,000.
In the capital city of Ankara,
a single congregation is working hard
to reach almost 5.5 million people.
Many congregations in Turkey focus on public witnessing, with encouraging results.
Let’s visit the Hatay Congregation,
near the ancient city of Syrian Antioch.
Paul used Antioch as his home base for his missionary tours.
And it was here that the disciples were first called Christians.
Today,
this part of Turkey is known for its food
—such as spices, herbs, fruits, and sweets.
In recent times,
unrest and war have disrupted the region.
Some of our brothers and sisters have been so near to the conflict
that they could hear explosions from bombs and gunfire.
Despite these threats and anxieties,
the 56 publishers, including 11 regular pioneers
and 2 special pioneers, attend the meetings
and preach without letup.
Our brothers and sisters in Turkey send their love and greetings
to the worldwide brotherhood.
Our love goes back to them for their zeal and steadfast faith.
From the World Headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting.

예를 들어, 마태복음 6:28에는 “들의 백합”이란 표현이 있죠.
전 지금까지 마태복음 6장을 이해할 수가 없었어요.
“왕국을 첫째로 구하는” 것하고 무슨 상관이 있는지 늘 궁금했죠.
번역자들은 번역할 내용을 온전히 이해하기 위해
그런 다음 팀이 모여 원문을 검토하고
번역이 끝나면 임명된 형제가 번역된 내용의 영상을 준비합니다.
그리고 스튜디오에서 그 영상을 보며 최종 촬영을 하게 되죠.
그런 다음 녹화한 영상을 정밀 편집하고
청각 장애인이 볼 수 있게 준비합니다.
이 장면에서 수화자는 자신을 꽃으로 묘사하면서,
옷감을 짜듯 꽃잎을 하나하나 짠 다음
여호와께서 자상하게 이렇게 말씀하고 계신 거죠.
‘왕국을 첫째로 구하면, 필요한 걸 내가 다 줄게.
열차를 타고 출근하면서 봤는데, 혼자 생각했죠.
보다가 너무 빠져들어서 내릴 역을 지나쳐 버렸어요.
보다가 그만 또 내릴 역을 지나쳐 버린 거에요!
자연히 하느님께 가까이 가려는 마음을 갖고 있습니다.
사람들에게 보여 주거나 우리가 직접 읽을 때,
하느님께 가까이 가려는 그런 내재된 마음이 되살아나게 되죠.
하느님의 말씀에 확실히 그런 힘이 있다는 걸 느끼고 있습니다.
저도 아버지 여호와께서 제 모국어인 수화로 말씀하시는 걸 보면서
수화 성경이 그들의 마음에 이르렀다는 걸 알 수 있습니다.
자신의 얼굴을 그들에게 비추시는 모습을 상상해 봐요.
그래서 우리 형제들의 얼굴도 빛나고 있죠.
이제 그들의 모국어로 하느님의 말씀을 갖게 되어,
여호와께서 그들에게 자신의 얼굴을 비추고 계심을 보고 있습니다.

en.text: January 21, 2017, became a special day
for deaf people in Japan.
Jehovah’s Witnesses released the book of Matthew
in Japanese Sign Language.
What, though, was behind these smiles?
When I used to read the Japanese Bible,
I really didn’t understand it,
so I forced myself to read—not much of a joy.
Right, it was hard to understand and explain to people.
The Bible, written in a language we do not know, will not move our heart.
Having no sign-language Bible
was a huge disadvantage when it came to cultivating a longing for God.
When making shepherding calls, reasoning on a scripture
with a deaf person was difficult if that scripture
wasn’t translated into sign language.
There is a Bible in American Sign Language,
so I was envious and wanted to see the Bible
in Japanese Sign Language so much.
At last, approval was given for Bible translation
into Japanese Sign Language.
I noticed that the translation team
offered a prayer before they started each day’s work.
Also, when faced with difficult translation problems,
they relied on Jehovah’s holy spirit through prayers
so that they could exercise good judgment.
It was impressive.
There are various processes needed for God’s Word
to jump off the page and reach the heart of deaf people.
They considered carefully how to express scriptures
so that deaf people would understand.
Let’s take an example: “the lilies of the field” at Matthew 6:28.
I wasn’t able to understand Matthew chapter 6 until now.
I always thought, ‘“Birds of heaven” and “lilies of the field,”
What do they have to do with “seeking first the Kingdom”?’
The translators individually read and research
the source text to fully understand what they’ll translate.
Then the team meets to discuss the text
and explore ideas for translating certain concepts.
After the translation is complete,
the assigned brother signs the translation to prepare the prompt video.
Then studio recording takes place,
referencing the prompt video.
The recorded movie is carefully edited
and prepared for delivery.
In this case,
the signer pretends to be a flower
and weaves his own petals
and sews them on his face.
Then he asks,
“Flowers don’t do that, do they?”
God’s Word coming off the pages
has reached the heart of deaf people.
I understood for the first time that Jehovah is kindly teaching us,
‘If you seek the Kingdom first, I’ll give you everything you need.
Don’t worry.’
I was watching it on the train on my way to work.
I thought, ‘Wow, this is so good!’
I was absorbed in the video, and I missed my train station.
So I changed trains, but again,
I was watching the video and missed my station again!
The book of Matthew is that interesting.
Humans have beneficial feelings
because we are created in God’s image.
But because of Satan’s system of things, these feelings are driven away.
However, when you show God’s Word to people or read it yourself,
innate beneficial feelings well up in our hearts.
I strongly feel that God’s Word has the power to do that.
Just like a child grows up listening to what their father says,
I can be closer to my Father, Jehovah, by watching him
speak to me in my native tongue, sign language.
Comments from deaf brothers show
that the sign-language Bible talks to their heart directly.
I imagine that Jehovah loves our brothers,
and his face is shining.
And the faces of our brothers are also shining.
Now by means of having God’s living Word
in the language of their heart,
our deaf brothers and sisters
are seeing Jehovah’s face shining.

cn.text: 对日本的听障人士来说是个特别的日子
因为耶和华见证人
发行了日本手语《马太福音》经卷
为什么他们会这么开心呢？
以前读日语圣经的时候
我真的不知道是什么意思
我只是强迫自己要读圣经
但找不到乐趣
没错，要读懂并解释给别人听
真的很难
圣经如果是用我们读不懂的语言写成的
就很难打动内心
没有手语圣经
听障人士想要亲近上帝真的很不容易
做牧养探访时
要用经文跟有听力障碍的弟兄姐妹推理
但没有手语圣经
真的不容易！
我知道有美国手语圣经的时候
非常羡慕他们
心想
要是我们有日本手语圣经该有多好啊！
后来
总部批准要翻译日本手语圣经
翻译小组每天开始工作前都会先祷告
当他们遇到翻译难题时
也会祷告求上帝帮助他们
做出正确的决定
这让我印象深刻
为了打动听障人士的内心
让经文更有画面感
手语翻译过程会有很多步骤
翻译员会仔细考虑
如何把经文翻译得清楚易懂
我们来看看马太福音6:28说的
“野地里的百合花”是怎么翻译的
以前，我一直不明白马太福音第6章的意思
经文提到“天上的飞鸟”
和“野地里的百合花”
这跟先追求上帝的王国有什么关系呢？
为了透彻理解要翻译的内容
翻译员会各自研读并查找资料
接着
翻译小组会一起开会讨论要翻译的内容
看看怎么翻译比较好
翻译完成后
一位受委派的弟兄
会用手语把翻译好的内容录制成参考影片
然后，录制工作就开始了
手语演员会看着参考影片打手语
录制好的影片会再仔细编辑
然后就可以上传了
现在，看一个例子
一个手语演员把自己当作花朵
他辛苦编织花瓣
再把一片片的花瓣都“缝”在脸上
之后他又问
“花朵不会自己这样做，对吗？”
上帝的话语活现在眼前
所以能打动听障人士的内心
我终于明白了
耶和华在仁慈地教导我们说
“如果你先追求上帝的王国
你需要的一切东西我都会赐给你
你不用担心！”
有一次坐火车去上班
我在车上看手语圣经
不禁感叹说
哇，这太棒了！
影片的内容深深吸引了我
结果就坐过站了
我就换火车往回坐
我继续看圣经
没想到又坐过站了
手语的马太福音
真的太精彩了！
我们都会想要亲近上帝
因为我们是按照他的形象造的
但受到撒但世界的影响
我们想要亲近上帝的愿望变得越来越弱了
可是当你读圣经或向人传道时
就会再次想要亲近上帝
我深信上帝的话语大有力量
能够帮助我们亲近他
孩子一般会听爸爸说话
我也很想听天父说话
他用我的母语跟我说话
手语圣经让我跟他的关系更亲密了
从这些弟兄姐妹的话可以看出
手语圣经深深地打动了他们
看到这些弟兄姐妹绽放的笑容
我可以想象到
耶和华在天上也一定会很开心
耶和华赐给有听力障碍的弟兄姐妹手语圣经
这深深打动他们的内心
耶和华好像在用慈颜光照他们

titles.en: God’s Word Makes Their Faces Shine
titles.cn: 上帝的话语让他们绽放笑容

cn.text: 上次我说要和你讨论一个问题
就是复活的人会过怎样的生活
嗯，我记得
圣经说到时会有许多美好的事
我想跟你分享其中一个
请留意以赛亚书32:18怎么说
淑华，你可以帮忙读出这节经文吗？
好的
这里说的是人复活后的情况
经文说
到时人会过怎样的生活呢？
他们会有安稳的住处
不受骚扰吗？
对呀
圣经的意思是他们不用再过苦日子了！
你希望这一天来到吗？
当然希望
但我觉得很难相信
我们一开始也觉得这么好的事只是个梦想
不过我们夫妻俩学习圣经后
就发觉有充分的证据证明
这些事都是可以相信的
这样啊
当然，如果没有上帝
这些都不可能发生了
我们怎么知道上帝真的存在呢？
下次我们再过来跟你聊聊好吗？
可以啊！

titles.cn: 2019年5月 第二次续访（赛32:18）

cn.text: 很高兴再次见到你
这是我丈夫，志豪
你好，你好！
你好，很高兴认识你
昨天我们聊到
人死了就毫无希望了吗？
这个问题你有什么想法呢？
你昨天走了以后我想了一下
但不知道答案
其实，圣经很明确地告诉我们
死去的人有一个美好的希望
请你看看使徒行传24:15怎么说
淑华可以请你读出来吗？
好
谢谢
你留意到经文说
死去的人有什么希望呢？
复活吗？
没错，复活就是死去的人再次活过来
是上天堂吗？
昨天我们准备这个续访的时候
讨论怎样解释使徒行传24:15
看来现在强调在地上复活的希望
会比讨论人能不能上天堂更合适
很多人有这种想法
可是这节经文的意思是说
死去的人有希望在地上活过来
如果我们有机会再见到去世的亲人或朋友
你觉得好吗？
好是好啊
但怎么可能！
现在世界这么乱
大家压力这么大
如果活过来还要过这样的日子吗？
你说的有道理
不过圣经说复活的时候
世界的情况会跟现在很不一样
我们下次再来跟你谈谈
圣经说复活的人会过怎样的生活

titles.cn: 2019年5月 第一次续访（徒24:15）

cn.text: 你好！
很高兴见到你
我们今天在附近跟人聊聊
关心一下这边的邻居
我是杨太太
不知道怎么称呼你？
我姓张
张先生，现在人们都很努力赚钱
希望以后可以享福
但现实是我们的一生很短
所以很多人都想知道
我们过完这一生之后
难道就这样结束了吗？
还是可能还有其他的希望呢？
不知道你有没有想过类似的事呢？
嗯，我也不太清楚耶
就过一天算一天吧
很多人有一样的想法
我们的确要认真地去过每一天
因为我们的一生实在太短了
这让我想到圣经里的一句话
怡君
可以请你帮我读传道书9:5吗？
嗯，好
经文说
谢谢
像这段话说的
人死了就毫无知觉
当然也就不会有痛苦了
可是，我们那时候也不能做任何事了
所以真的要趁活着就尽力做好每一件事
对啊
不过，圣经说死亡并不是人的最终结局
人其实还有一个美好的希望
你是说死后上天堂？
很多人都这样认为
我很想告诉你圣经怎么说
我下次跟我的丈夫一起过来
再跟你聊聊这个未来的希望，好吗？
好

titles.cn: 2019年5月 初次交谈（传9:5上）

ko.text: 우리가 특별히 관심을 기울인 일에 대해 얘기해 보시죠.
케빈 형제는 이번이 첫 장로 모임이니까
앞으로 있을 일들에 용기 있게 맞설 수 있도록 격려해 주기로 했죠.
그리고 현재 용기를 나타내는 것을 칭찬하면서,
지금 기르는 용기가 미래에 용기를 내는 데
꼭 필요하다는 걸 기억하도록 돕기로 했어요.
결과가 어땠는지 이야기 좀 해 주시겠어요?
마크 형제가 겪은 일을 간단히 말씀드리고 싶은데요.
직장에서 중립 입장을 타협하라는 심한 압력을 받았어요.
마크, 정치에 관여 안 하는 거 알아.
근데, 이 법안이 통과되면 회사가 어려워진다니까?
그냥 여기에다가 시위를 지지한다는 서명만 해.
이건 투표도 아니고 정당에 가입하는 것도 아니잖아.
너만 빼고 회사 사람들 다 했어.
사장이 우리 부서에서 몇 명 내보낼 거라고 했는데,
서명 안 하면 너도 리스트에 오를 거야.
어떻게 했냐면, 그 순간에 바로 기도를 했대요.
그러니까 중립을 지킬 용기가 생겼다고 했어요.
지금 용기 있게 행동한 게 앞으로 도움이 될 거라고 말해 줬어요.
아, 그게, 전 다른 사람의 선택을 존중해요.
누구나 자신이 어떻게 살지 선택할 수 있지만
그리고 우리 교회는 이 행사 공식 스폰서라고요!
지금 용기를 나타내야 미래에도 용기를 나타낼 수 있어.
성경은 결혼한 남녀만 성관계를 가질 수 있다고 알려 줘요.
또 거짓 종교가 정치 세력에 멸망될 때를 생각해 보라고 했어요.
우리가 그때 여호와의 증인이라는 걸 밝히려면
분명히 샐리 자매처럼 용기를 내야 할 거예요.
와, 어렸을 때 봉사 따라 나와서 전도지 전하던 게
전도지 얘기하시니까 말인데, 저도 하나 말씀드릴까요?
「거짓 종교의 끝은 가까웠다!」라는 「왕국 소식」 전도지를 배부했었죠.
이번에 셰리 자매 양치는 방문을 했는데,
전 세계적으로 배부되는 이런 전도지를 전해 드리고 있어요.
당신네는 진짜고 우리는 거짓 종교란 말이야?
우리 개가 확 물어 버릴 테니까.
그때 일로 충격을 많이 받으셨나 봐요.
지금까지도 봉사에 참여하는 게 쉽지 않으시대요.
앞으로 더 어려운 시기가 오면 아마 전 못 할 것 같아요.
낯선 사람들을 만나서 이야기하려면 누구나 다 긴장이 돼요.
용기가 있다고 두려움이 없는 건 아니에요.
두려움을 이겨 내고 행동하는 것도 용기라고 할 수 있죠.
혹시 다음에 봉사 중에나 다른 때 용기가 필요한 상황이 생기면
이 성구에서 알려 주는 대로 해 보시는 거예요.
지금 말씀드리는 세 가지를 기억해 보세요.
나중에 우리가 심판의 소식을 전할 때도
전도인들이 북부 회중과 남부 회중으로 가게 될 거라고 광고했을 때,
우리 집단 다 북부 회중으로 가는데,
우리 둘만 남부 회중으로 가게 됐어.
하긴 뭐, 저건 그냥 제안일 뿐이라고 했으니까.
그래? 그런 뜻은 아닌 것 같은데.
“특별한 사정이 있을 때만” 바꿀 수 있다고 했잖아.
그러니까 가고 싶은 데로 가면 돼.
-근데, 다 그렇게 가고 싶은 데로 가면 .... -어, 테일러 자매.
근데 자매 손자들이랑 가족들은 북부로 가시던데.
어, 북부로 가실 거예요, 남부로 가실 거예요?
자매, 내 이름을 남부 회중 명단에서 봤다고 하지 않았어?
같은 회중 다니시는 게 맞는 거 아니에요?
형제들이 이 조정을 광고할 때 특별한 사정이 없는 사람이라면
내가 남부로 가는 이유는 다 몰라도,
아, 그리고 우리 남부 회중에서도 잘 지내 봅시다.
지금 용기를 나타내는 한 가지 방법이라는 생각이 들었어요.
특히 왜 그런 지시를 하는지 온전히 이해하기 어려울 때도 말이죠.
출판물에선 마곡의 곡이 여호와의 백성을 공격할 때
잘 이해가 안 되는 지시를 받게 될 수 있다고 했어요.
저희 집단에서 있었던 일도 하나 말씀드릴까요?
하루는 먼로 형제 가족이 저를 가족 숭배에 초대했어요.
“앞으로 있을 사건들에 어떻게 대비할 수 있습니까?”
마음으로 순종하는 태도를 길러 나가야 해요.
그렇게 하면 아마겟돈 때 살아남을 수 있어요.
브래드, 아까 그 그림 정말 열심히 보고 있더라.
그때 형제들이 우리가 어떻게 싸워야 되는지도 알려 줄까요?
그냥 가만히 서 있기만 하면 되는데.
브래드, 아마겟돈 때 우린 아무 걱정 안 해도 돼.
여호와께서 과거에 하신 일을 보면 알 수 있지.
이스라엘 사람들도 너처럼 아주 무서워했을 거야.
여호사밧은 백성을 성전에 모은 다음에 여호와께 기도했어.
모든 사람에게 용기를 주는 말씀을 해 주셨지.
“너희는 이 큰 무리 때문에 두려워하거나 겁내지 마라.
이 싸움은 너희의 것이 아니라 하느님의 것이다.
이 전쟁에서 너희는 싸울 필요가 없다.
이스라엘 사람들이 왔을 땐 전부 다 죽어 있었지.
그 성경 기록을 읽고 브래드가 용기를 많이 얻은 것 같더라고요.
미래에 큰 도움이 될 거라는 걸 일깨워 줄 수 있었어요.
뜻밖에도 필립 형제를 격려해 줘야 했어요.
필립 형제가 LDC 자원봉사자로 초대받은 거 기억나시죠?
근데 그 초대를 받고 좀 당혹스러웠나 봐요.
전 LDC가 아니라 베델이 더 잘 맞을 거라고 생각했는데.
전 건축은 하나도 모르고, 또 어디로 갈지도 모르잖아요.
한 번도 안 해 본 일인데 할 수 있을까요?
그래, 그런 생각이 들 수 있지.
전 정말 못 할 것 같아요.
와, 제 말에 동의하는 분도 계시네요.
나도 전파자 학교 졸업하고 이 회중에 왔을 때 겁이 났어.
여호와의 명령에 따라 성전을 건축하게 된 솔로몬에게
여호와 하느님, 나의 하느님께서 너와 함께 계시기 때문이다.
그분은 너를 버리거나 떠나지 않으실 것이며,
여호와의 집에서 섬기는 데 필요한 모든 일이 끝날 때까지
이 성구를 읽고 너무 걱정할 필요가 없다는 걸 알게 됐어.
여호와께서 도와주시니까 용기를 내서 한번 해 봐!
여러분과 함께 일할 수 있어서 정말 즐거웠습니다.
나도 북부 회중으로 가면 좋았을 텐데.
그리고 나이도 어린 재러드 형제가 북부 회중 조정자로 간다고?
내가 왜 이 문제로 힘들어하고 있지?
난 특별한 이유가 없으니까 당연히 남부 회중으로 가야지.
마음으로부터 여호와의 주권을 지지한다는 걸 나타내려면
지금이 바로 그런 용기가 필요한 때가 아닐까?
이기심 때문에 내 마음대로 행동하려는 경향을
여호와의 조직에서 우리를 위해 어떤 마련을 하면
양치는 방문 하길 정말 잘한 것 같아요.
이제 형제 자매들이 앞으로 있을 일들에
피터 형제, 마치는 기도를 해 주시겠어요?

en.text: Well, brothers, the next item on our agenda
is what we’ve been working on for the past three months.
And, Kevin, since this is your first elders’ meeting with us,
maybe we can fill you in on the background.
Thanks, that would be great.
We noted that some in the congregation were anxious
because of unstable world conditions,
and we decided to focus on strengthening the friends when shepherding
so that they’d be able to face future events with courage.
And we also wanted to commend them where they’re already showing courage
and to help them to see that the courage they develop now
will help them to display courage in the future.
Luther, how did things go in your group?
Maybe you can share an experience
that gives an idea of the overall results.
Sure.
I think the experience that best illustrates it is Mark O’Brien’s.
He was facing some serious pressure at work
to compromise his neutrality.
Look, Mark, I understand you don’t like to get involved in politics.
I don’t either.
But if we don’t protest this new bill,
our company is going to get hit with cutbacks and layoffs.
Joel, don’t get me wrong.
I’m concerned too,
but I won’t join the protest.
OK.
So you won’t stand in line and protest,
but at least sign the sheet to show you support the protest.
It’s not like you’re voting or joining a political party.
Your name won’t even be noticed.
We just need signatures.
So far, everyone in the company has signed it.
Mark, I’m going to be straight with you.
The boss told me
he’s going to have to let some people go,
and your name is under serious consideration
depending on the outcome of this discussion.
Just sign the paper, Mark!
Did he sign the paper?
No.
And do you know why?
At that moment, he said a silent prayer
that gave him the courage needed to remain neutral.
I commended him, and I reminded him
that displaying courage now is going to help him in the future.
Thanks, Luther.
That’s very encouraging to hear.
Matthew, how did things go with your group?
Matthew, how did things go with your group?
Very good.
In fact, Sally’s experience is one that stands out for me.
Hi.
Would you like to make a donation to the marathon?
Um, no thank you.
Oh.
Shall I put it in the bag, or do you want to wear it now?
Oh, no thank you.
What’s wrong, Honey?
You got something against them?
Well, no I— I don’t have anything against them personally.
So, what’s the problem?
I respect that they have a right to choose their lifestyle,
but as a Bible reader, I choose—
Excuse me!
I’m a Bible reader too!
I go to church,
and our church is one of the biggest supporters of this marathon!
So, what are you trying to say?
Displaying courage now
will help me display courage in the future.
Well, I’m one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
and we believe the Bible teaches that sex is for a man
and a woman who are married.
Intolerant people.
Wow, that sure took courage.
That’s what I told her.
And I asked her to think about when the political powers
destroy false religion.
At that time, people won’t want to admit that they’re religious.
And so for us to admit that we’re Jehovah’s Witnesses then,
well, that’s going to require the same type of courage
that she displayed at that market.
Wow, I remember
when Sally was just a little girl handing out tracts,
and now look how well she’s done.
Speaking of tracts,
may I share an experience with you brothers?
Sure.
Do you recall a little over ten years ago?
We had the Kingdom News campaign
“The End of False Religion Is Near!”
During our shepherding visit with Sherry Spencer,
she admitted that something happened to her during that campaign.
As a public service,
I’m sharing in an earth-wide distribution of this important message.
That’s your free copy.
Hey! What’s this about?
Are you trying to tell me that my religion is false and yours is true?
Get off my property!
If you come back again, I’m going to set my dog on you!
Nobody wants you here!
Sister Spencer said that that experience stayed with her.
To this day, she finds it very difficult to be in the ministry.
Brothers,
I feel that after all these years,
if I can’t get over this fear,
I may not make it when times get harder.
Sister Spencer, you may be surprised to know
that most of us get nervous when talking at the doors.
I know that I do.
You’re just trying to make me feel better.
No.
I’m saying it because it’s true.
Being courageous doesn’t mean we won’t get nervous.
Sometimes being courageous means taking action even though we are nervous.
Thanks. That is encouraging.
Here’s a suggestion that may help.
We’ve discussed Psalm 27:14.
Based on that scripture,
the next time you’re about to face a situation that calls for courage,
whether it be in the ministry or otherwise,
tell yourself you just need to do these three things:
pray,
hope in Jehovah,
and act.
You got it?
Pray,
hope in Jehovah,
and act.
Wait. I’m going to write that down.
Excellent!
Helping the friends address their fears
is really going to help
when our message changes from good news to judgment.
So, Peter, let’s hear from you next.
So, Peter, let’s hear from you next.
Well, when we informed everyone
that the publishers were going to be redistributed
to the North or South Congregation,
let’s just say some struggled with the idea.
Paula!
Did you see?
They have us going to the South Congregation,
and everybody else from our group is going to North.
Yeah, I saw that.
My aunt and cousins will be going there too.
Well, that doesn’t make any sense.
They should keep you together.
Well, at least the brothers said that the list was just a recommendation.
Well, they didn’t say it exactly like that.
They said, “if we had extenuating circumstances.”
So you don’t have to go if you don’t want to go.
But, Kim, if everyone did that, don’t you think—
Oh, hi, Sister Taylor.
Oh, hello, girls.
I saw your name on the list for the South Congregation,
but your grandkids and their families —they’re going to North.
So, what are you going to do?
What do you mean?
Well, are you going to North, or are you going to South?
Now, Sweetie, didn’t you say you saw
my name listed under the South Congregation?
Yeah, but . . .
So I’ll be going to the South Congregation.
Well, don’t you think it would make more sense
if you were in the same congregation as your grandkids and their families?
Does it make more sense?
Well, that’s a whole different question.
The brothers outlined an arrangement.
They said they hoped we could support that arrangement
unless we had extenuating circumstances,
and I don’t have any right now.
So for me, it’s simple.
Whether I know all of the reasons or not,
I’m going to support that arrangement.
Oh, look, girls, I’ve got to go.
Oh, and by the way,
I hope to see you both in the South Congregation.
Peter, you got a sec?
I think this experience well illustrates
one way to show courage now,
and that’s by following the direction of the brothers taking the lead
—even if we don’t fully understand the reasons why this direction is being given.
Exactly.
We’ve been told
that when Gog of Magog attacks Jehovah’s people,
we may receive direction
that may not seem practical.
So, courageously following directions now
will help us to do so then.
So, brothers, we’re almost done.
So, brothers, we’re almost done.
And if you don’t mind, I’d like to share what happened with my group.
The Monroes asked if I would join them on one of their Family Worship evenings.
So let’s ask our final review question:
“How can we prepare ourselves for the events that are to come?”
Sarah.
We want to develop heartfelt obedience
to the guidance that we receive now,
so that we’ll obey any future instructions Jehovah may give us.
So, doing this will help us survive Armageddon.
Well said.
Very nice, Dear.
May I ask Brad a question?
Sure, go ahead.
Brad, I noticed you’ve really been focused on that picture.
Do you mind if I ask what you’re thinking about?
Well, will the brothers tell us how to fight the people who will be attacking us?
We won’t need to do any fighting.
Then what will we need the instructions for?
Are we just going to stand there and do nothing?
We don’t know what those instructions will be, Son.
Brad, when Armageddon comes,
we’ll have nothing to worry about
and we won’t have to fight.
We know that because of what Jehovah has done for his people in the past.
I’d like to show you an account
in 2 Chronicles chapter 20.
It was a time when Moabites and Ammonites
started to war against the land of Judah,
which was being ruled by King Jehoshaphat.
Some of those Israelites were likely anxious, just like you.
Jehoshaphat gathered Judah at the temple
and began to inquire of Jehovah.
And Jehovah caused a Levite named Jahaziel to give an answer
that gave everyone courage.
What did he say?
“Do not be afraid
“or be terrified because of this large crowd,
“for the battle is not yours
“but God’s. . . .
“You will not need to fight this battle.
“Take your position, stand still,
and see the salvation of Jehovah in your behalf.”
Jehovah had turned the enemies against each other.
By the time the Israelites arrived,
not one soldier was left.
It was obvious that Brad’s courage was strengthened
after reviewing this Bible account.
And I’m happy to say that after our discussions,
the friends in our group are more aware of how their own acts of courage now
will help them be courageous in the future.
Enough from me.
It’s your turn, Albert.
Enough from me.
It’s your turn, Albert.
How did things go with your group?
All responded nicely,
but there was one discussion about courage that I didn’t anticipate.
Remember when Philip got accepted
to work with LDC as a construction volunteer?
Yeah.
Well, getting accepted to LDC wasn’t quite what he expected.
Wow, Philip! This is great!
Yeah, that’s what everybody keeps saying.
It’s just overwhelming.
I thought I was more cut out for Bethel.
But construction volunteer
—I don’t even know what that is.
Who knows where they’ll send me?
And what if I get asked to do stuff I’ve never done before?
Philip, your concerns are understandable.
I just don’t think I can handle all of this.
I don’t think you can either.
Wow, I’m glad someone finally agrees with me.
I say I don’t think you can handle this assignment
because it requires more than you to get it done.
I know what you’re saying.
Of course, Jehovah will help me.
But do you really believe that?
I do, but . . .
But what?
I guess what I’m saying is I’m afraid.
That’s OK.
When I first arrived in this congregation as my SKE assignment,
I was afraid.
But, you know, one verse that really helped me is 1 Chronicles 28:20.
These are David’s words to his son Solomon,
whom Jehovah assigned to build the temple.
“Then David said to his son Solomon:
“‘Be courageous and strong and go to work.
“‘Do not be afraid or be terrified,
“‘for Jehovah God, my God, is with you.
“‘He will not desert you or abandon you,
“‘but he will be with you
until all the work for the service of Jehovah’s house is finished.’”
This verse reminded me not to overthink all that needs to be done.
Just get started.
With Jehovah’s help, you can “be courageous”
—“go to work”!
There’s Philip, happy as can be.
He’s really doing well.
Thanks, Albert, for sharing that with us.
Well, brothers, it’s clear that Jehovah has blessed
the hard work of the body of elders.
Now there’s something I wanted to say
before we conclude our meeting.
And that’s—that’s, ah . . .
We know, David; we know.
We’re feeling it too.
Yeah, but I just have to say it.
I’ve really appreciated serving with you brothers.
When I saw that our congregation was going to be merged,
it wasn’t easy for me.
Well, we sure couldn’t tell.
I’m glad.
But it really hit me hard
the night we posted the list
recommending where the publishers should go.
It seems like it would have made more sense
for me to be assigned to the North Congregation,
where the majority of my friends will be going.
I’ve known those friends longer than any of the other brothers.
And now they’re sending that younger elder over to North
to be the coordinator of their body of elders.
I just don’t get it.
Why am I having such a hard time with this?
Of course, I’m going to go to the South Congregation.
There’s no reason not to.
But the problem is my attitude.
I’ve told others for years that there are times
when we have to put aside our personal preferences
to show our wholehearted support of Jehovah’s sovereignty.
This is one of those times.
I need to be courageous
and stand up to selfishness and independent thinking,
even if it’s my own.
I was reminded.
It’s simple.
When Jehovah’s organization outlines an arrangement,
we support it,
not just because we’re supposed to;
we do it with the right attitude.
Amen to that.
That’s a lesson we’re all learning.
But I’m glad we’ve been able to shepherd the congregation
before the changes take place.
Now our brothers and sisters are better equipped
to face the challenges ahead with courage.
It’s been a real pleasure to serve with you all.
Peter, would you please conclude our meeting with prayer?
Sure.
Our Father, Jehovah . . .

ko.text: 자신이 아프다는 걸 받아들였고 늘 긍정적이었어요.
여호와께서 부활시켜 주실 거라는 걸 믿고
2016년 2월 JW 방송을 촬영했을 때 정말 좋아했어요.

아내 품 안에서 아이가 눈을 감을 때
그 고통은 정말 이루 말할 수 없어요.
하다못해 식사 준비를 할 때도 용기가 필요하더라고요.
그냥 접시 하나, 의자 하나 덜 놓는 것뿐인데도요.
야이로의 딸에 대한 기록이 위로가 많이 됐어요.
야이로가 딸이 죽었다는 소식을 들었을 때
그의 딸은 죽은 게 아니라 자고 있었으니까요.
딸아이가 죽고 우린 바로 다음 집회에 참석했어요.
형제 자매들은 뭐라고 위로를 해야 할지 모르겠다고 했지만,
우릴 꼭 안아 준 것만으로도 큰 위로가 됐죠.
회중 성원들은 마치 가족처럼 우릴 도와주고 위로해 줬죠.
부활 희망에 대해 살펴보는 게 정말 힘들었어요.
하지만 그 시간은 우리 애들한테 도움이 됐어요.
애들이 밤에 혼자 기도하는 걸 들은 적이 있었는데,
펠리시티가 안전하게 여호와의 기억 속에 있으니까
아픈 걸 잊을 수 있어서 제일 좋다고 했어요.
이제 그 말이 무슨 뜻인지 알 수 있을 것 같아요.
딸아이를 잃고 나서 다른 사람들을 더 잘 위로할 수 있게 됐어요.
봉사할 때 사랑하는 가족을 잃은 사람들을 만나면,
감정 이입을 해서 더 잘 도와줄 수 있죠.
우리 가족은 봉사에 더 열심히 참여하고 있어요.
우리의 희망을 더 실재적으로 느끼게 되죠.
하지만 그렇다고 슬픔에만 빠져 있진 않을 거예요.

en.text: Phelicity was a bright, vibrant little girl.
She was a beautiful kid —she really was.
She embraced the fact that she was ill.
She was confident and courageous,
knowing that Jehovah would resurrect her.
Phelicity really enjoyed the privilege
of being invited to share in the February broadcast of 2016.
But sadly, just a few weeks later, Phelicity passed away.
When you watch a child die in her mother’s arms,
it’s the most saddening thing you’ll ever see.
The pain and the sting of death is so strong.
But after some time, as time goes by,
the sting starts to fade a little bit into,
‘I just really miss that person.’
Simple things like setting the table
—that’s when you need courage.
There’s one less plate, one less fork, one less knife,
one less seat.
On the day that Phelicity died,
the account of Jairus’ daughter actually helped Ben and I as parents.
At that moment,
when he was told that his daughter had died,
I know how he felt.
And yet Jesus said: ‘Do not fear.’
His daughter wasn’t dead.
She was just asleep.
After Phelicity died, we went to the very next meeting.
Many of our friends —they didn’t know what to say.
But they did the most important thing ever —they offered a warm embrace.
The friends in our Kingdom Hall are like family to us.
They really protected us; they comforted us.
Sometimes, there would be cards.
The hardest thing for us to do after Phelicity died
was to look at the resurrection hope during our family worship.
Our children lost their sister and their friend.
We were able to see the benefit,
especially when we heard their private prayers at nighttime.
They would make expressions about the resurrection hope,
and how they knew that Phelicity was safe in Jehovah’s memory.
Phelicity often said that she felt the best when she was in the ministry
because she didn’t focus on her own illness.
And since she’s died, we can truly understand what she meant by that.
Our experience with losing Phelicity
has actually given us the ability to comfort other people.
So when we’re in the field and we meet people who have lost someone they love,
we feel better equipped emotionally and spiritually
to be able to strengthen others.
The expansion of our ministry has been something that we’ve really enjoyed.
It keeps our minds occupied and keeps the hope more real to us.
Of course, there’s always a pain
that won’t go away until we get Phelicity back.
But we put it in its place.
We allow it to energize our family to do the things that Jehovah wants us to do.
The resurrection hope is real; it’s going to happen.
We just have to be patient.

en.text: The persecution spread throughout Malawi
soon after the announcement was made
that the Witnesses were banned in the country.
Their houses were burned,
and their maize crops were confiscated
because they refused to participate in the country’s politics.
The regular visits that Brother Johansson
was doing as a branch representative at that time
really encouraged the brothers from various parts of the country
who were affected by the persecution.
His wife, Linda,
suggested that he should ask someone to accompany him
so that he did not have to do the work alone.
And she suggested that I accompany him.
This was because of the fear of what might happen.
When we got to the ferry crossing,
the soldiers told Brother Johansson to get out and stand in front of the jeep.
They said to me, “You can pass,
but we first have to shoot the white man.”
Because the Scriptures say:
“No one has greater love than this,
that someone should surrender his life in behalf of his friends,”
I said:
“Shoot me instead!
What did this man do?”
Yes, it happened without me giving it a second thought.
It just happened spontaneously.
I stood between him and the soldiers.
Prayer helped very much
because the people that we thought were going to harm us
had a complete change of heart.
On the way back, Brother Johansson also saved my life.
We were stopped by a youth mob at a roadblock.
They asked for the political cards.
They would have killed me.
So Brother Johansson just sped off with his vehicle.
Yes, it was very exciting to see
that Jehovah God has many ways of saving his people.
Elisha said:
“For there are more who are with us
than those who are with them.”
In the end, Jehovah will rescue his people.
So in countries where our brothers are banned,
I encourage them to stand firm,
trusting in God —the God who never fails, Jehovah.

분명히 보여 주는 것이라고 할 수 있죠.
정말 아름다운 일이 아닐 수 없습니다.

en.text: Well, I have the privilege of being part
of a delegation of brothers from 18 countries
who’ve been assigned by the Governing Body to attend
the Supreme Court hearing in Moscow on July 17.
The principal objective is to just show unity and support for our brothers.
I’m going to Russia in order to be of encouragement
to the local Russian brothers and sisters there.
I will encourage them to continue
to ‘obey Jehovah as ruler rather than men.’
Our intent is to try and visit many of the embassies
and speak to a variety of different high officials
about what’s happening right now
with our brothers in Russia.
And, really, when you think of it,
this is almost a way of saying that our international brotherhood
is all coming to the defense,
or to the aid, of our brothers in Russia.
And actually, when you think about it or when you meditate on it,
it really is a very, very beautiful thing.
Jehovah has everything under control.
And whatever the outcome may be,
there is no doubt that Jehovah
will continue to strengthen our brothers.

在莫斯科最高法院举行的听证会

展现我们的团结
