ko.text: 다른 하나는 우주에서 가장 나이 많은,
사탄의 목적은 경험이 없는 하와를 속여
어떻게 그렇게 했나요? 아시다시피 뱀을 사용했죠.
그가 한 말에서 많은 걸 알 수 있는데요,
오늘의 성구가 나오는 창세기 3장을 함께 보시죠.
여기 그가 한 질문을 읽어 보겠습니다.
사탄은 무슨 의도로 이런 질문을 했습니까?
사탄은 하와의 마음에 의심의 씨앗을 심으려고 했습니다.
여호와께서 뭔가 좋은 걸 감추고 계시다는 암시를 줬습니다.
「신권 전도 학교 교육에서 얻는 유익」 책 66면을 보면,
질문에 대한 이런 흥미로운 설명이 있습니다.
가장 본질적인 부분이 표면 밑에 숨어 있는 것입니다.
흔히 밑에 있는 쟁점이 질문 자체보다 더 중요합니다.”
이 경우에 하와는 질문을 받았을 때
질문 이면에 담긴 의도를 파악하지 못했습니다.
2, 3절에 나오는 하와의 대답을 보면 알 수 있는데, 이렇게 말했죠.
“우리는 동산에 있는 나무들의 열매를 먹을 수 있다.
그러나 동산 가운데 있는 나무의 열매에 관해서는
하느님께서 ‘너희는 그것을 먹어서도 안 되고 만져서도 안 된다.
그렇게 하면 너희가 죽을 것이다’ 라고 말씀하셨다.”
하지만 사탄은 하와를 쉽게 속일 수 있음을 알아챘죠.
네, 사탄은 바로 하와의 이기심에 호소했습니다.
자신이 가진 모든 걸 주신 분인 하느님에 대한 사랑보다 말이죠.
너희가 그것을 먹는 날에 너희 눈이 열리고 하느님처럼 되어
선악을 알게 될 줄을 하느님께서도 알고 계시기 때문이다.”
하와는 여호와 하느님에 대해 마땅히 가져야 할
사랑과 감사하는 마음을 기르지 못했던 것입니다.
완전한 인간도 이런 비합리적인 생각에 속아 넘어갈 수 있다면,
우리 모두도 그럴 수 있다는 겁니다.
여호와께선 우릴 도덕적 자유 행위자로 창조하셨죠.
하와도요. 그분은 우리가 로봇처럼 행동하는 게 아니라,
옳은 것과 그른 것 중에서 선택을 내리길 원하십니다.
사탄은 우리가 잘못된 선택을 하길 바라죠.
그런 사탄의 공격을 어떻게 막을 수 있습니까?
우리는 자신의 마음에 무엇이 있는지 알아야 합니다.
“하느님의 과분한 친절을 얻지 못하는 사람이 없도록 주의하십시오.
그리하여 유독한 뿌리가 나서 문제를 일으키고
그것 때문에 많은 사람이 더럽혀지는 일이 없게 하십시오.
그리고 여러분 가운데 성적 부도덕을 저지르는 자나...
신성한 것의 가치를 인식하지 못하는 자가 없도록 주의하십시오.”
바울이 여기 15절에서 말했듯이, 우린 “주의”할 필요가 있습니다.
‘유독한 뿌리가 나서 회중을 더럽히는 일이 없게 주의해야 합니다.’
“유독한 뿌리”라는 표현은 회중에 있을 수 있는
일부 사람들을 가리키는데, 회중이 일하는 방식에 흠을 잡거나,
물론 우리 중 아무도 그런 사람이 되고 싶진 않죠.
하지만 생각해 볼 점은, 뿌리가 나려면
씨앗이 땅에 심겨서 싹이 나야 뿌리가 자라나겠죠.
말하자면, 우리는 부적절한 씨앗을 찾아내는 법을 배워야 합니다.
남이 대신해 줄 순 없죠. 마음을 읽을 수 없으니까요.
그 씨앗이 무엇인지 우리가 말로 드러내지 않더라도,
우리 생각과 마음 속에 있을 수 있죠.
이런 내면의 약점에 대해 조처를 취해야 합니다.
사탄은 그러한 상황을 교묘히 이용할 것이고
우리의 그 특정한 약점이 이제 두드러지게 나타날 수 있습니다.
야고보서 1:14, 15에 이 과정이 잘 나와 있습니다.
우리도 겪어 보지 않았나요? 욕망은 강력할 수 있죠.
하와도 이기심으로 인해 그런 일을 겪었습니다.
비슷한 것이죠. 따라서 어떻게 해야 할까요?
앞서 언급했듯이, 우리 안에 있을 수 있는
씨앗이 싹을 틔우고 자라게 두지 마십시오.
그러려면 도움을 받아야 할 수도 있는데,
자기 힘만으로 “유독한 뿌리”를 제거하지 못할 수 있기 때문이죠.
이제 사탄이 우주에서 가장 나이 많은 지성 있는 창조물,
이 경우에 사탄은 자신을 숨기지 않았는데,
아시는 것처럼, 마태 4장을 보면, 이렇게 말했죠.
‘내게 엎드려 숭배 행위를 한 번만 해 보시오.’
사탄에 대해 무엇을 알 수 있습니까?
오랫동안 시기해 왔다는 걸 알 수 있습니다.
사탄은 우리가 여호와를 숭배하는 걸 막기 위해서라면
할 수 있는 한 무엇이든 할 것입니다.
그는 여호와께 드리는 우리의 숭배를 변질시키고 싶어 하죠.
사탄이 예수 그리스도에게 다가가 그분을 속이려 할 만큼
대담했던 걸 볼 때, 그는 분명
우리 한 사람 한 사람도 속이려 할 겁니다.
우리가 영적으로 얼마나 강해 보이든 상관없이
그는 우리의 충절을 꺾으려 할 겁니다.
치명적인 책략을 사용한다는 걸 분명히 알려 줍니다.
하지만 다행히 우린 하와처럼 속지 않을 수 있죠.
예수께서 여호와 하느님에 대해 가지셨던 그 사랑을
우리 각자도 길러서, 충절을 굳게 지키도록 합시다.

en.text: This morning we’re talking
about the clever strategy of Satan,
designed to lure people away from Jehovah God.
And so we’re going to examine two approaches:
One he used
with the youngest intelligent creature in the universe,
and the other he used
on the oldest intelligent creature in the universe.
Let’s take the youngest first.
Of course, that was Eve.
So taking advantage of her inexperience,
his purpose was to trick this woman
and to seduce her.
Now, how would he do it?
Well, as we know, he was behind a serpent.
He didn’t want to show her who he really was
—what his aim really was.
His choice of words also reveal a lot.
And our text is Genesis chapter 3.
Let’s go there if you would.
I’d like to just read his question again,
Genesis 3:1:
“Did God really say
that you must not eat from every tree of the garden?”
Now, what was his motive in asking this question?
Well, as was stated by one of the commenters,
what he was trying to do
was to seed a doubt in her mind,
implying that Jehovah God was holding something back from her.
‘He was too restrictive on you.’
Well, it’s interesting concerning questions.
The be book, Benefit From Theocratic Ministry School Education,
on page 66 says:
“Some questions are like icebergs.
“The most substantial part lies hidden beneath the surface.
An underlying issue is often more important than the question itself.”
And in the case of Eve,
when the question was asked,
she didn’t see the underlying purpose of the question.
Her answer in verses 2 and 3 indicate this.
She said: “We may eat of the fruit of the trees of the garden.
“But God has said about the fruit of the tree that is in the middle of the garden:
‘You must not eat from it, no, you must not touch it; otherwise you will die.’”
Her answer was truthful,
and it was an honest, innocent answer.
But Satan had her exactly where he wanted her.
You see, he was banking
on her self-interest,
that she would be more interested in herself
—her own needs—
than the love she had
for the God that gave her everything that she had.
Read his words again in verses 4 and 5.
Satan said: “You certainly will not die.
“For God knows that in the very day you eat from it,
“your eyes will be opened and you will be like God,
knowing good and bad.”
Tragically, his gamble worked.
She had not cultivated
the kind of love and appreciation for Jehovah God
that she should have.
So, what can we learn from this example?
Well, if a perfect human can succumb
to this kind of reasoning —irrational reasoning, really—
it can happen to any one of us.
Jehovah God created us as free moral agents.
That’s the way he made Eve.
He doesn’t want robots.
He wants us to be able to think things through,
make the right choices,
decide between right and wrong.
Satan is counting on us to make the wrong choices.
Now, what can we do to counter that attack from Satan?
Well, we have to know what is in our hearts.
If you go to Hebrews 12:15, 16,
the apostle Paul gives a warning to his fellow Christians
against becoming people who do not appreciate sacred things.
And that’s sort of the context
of verses 15 and 16.
He says: “Carefully watch that no one
“fails to obtain the undeserved kindness of God,
“so that no poisonous root springs up
“to cause trouble and many are defiled by it;
“and watch that among you there is no one who is sexually immoral
nor anyone who does not appreciate sacred things.”
So there is a need, as he said here in verse 15,
to: “Carefully watch.”
‘Carefully watch that no poisonous root will spring up and contaminate the congregation.’
The expression “poisonous root” refers to a few that may be in a congregation
who may find fault with the way things are done,
maybe even find fault
with the direction Jehovah has given on matters
—maybe the sacredness of marriage or the need for moral cleanness.
So we don’t want to be those kind of people —obviously.
But tell me, what’s necessary before a root can appear?
Well, a seed has to be planted,
and then it germinates, and then it grows into a root.
So it’s at the seed level
that we have to give special attention.
We have to learn to identify
these improper seeds, as it were.
No one can do that for us because they can’t read our heart.
The seed may even—
We’ve never even voiced what the seed is,
but it could be in our thinking and in our heart.
And these internal weaknesses have to be addressed
for fear we find ourselves in a circumstance
maneuvered by Satan
to accentuate that particular weakness.
Now, James 1:14, 15 really describes the process well.
James 1:14, 15, where he says:
“Each one is tried by being drawn out and enticed
“by his own desire [own desire].
“Then the desire [the seed],
“when it has become fertile [starts to grow],
“gives birth to sin; in turn sin,
when it has been carried out, brings forth death.”
So, being “enticed by his own desire.”
Does that sound familiar?
It’s a powerful force.
It’s one that happened to Eve,
the self-interests —they’re similar.
So, what do we need to do?
Well, as we said earlier, identify the seed or seeds
if that may be the case.
Don’t let them germinate; don’t let them start to grow.
Rid ourselves of that thinking.
And if a “poisonous root”
may happen to be in us
or starting to grow, then we need to rip it out.
And you may need to have help to do it.
It may be impossible to remove a “poisonous root” by yourself.
Now, let’s spend a few moments on the approach Satan used
for the oldest intelligent creature in the universe,
of course, Christ Jesus.
Now, in this case, he didn’t try to hide himself.
He realized there was no need to do that.
Jesus knew exactly who he was.
He understood the motive.
And so he just went overtly right to Jesus.
And as you know, in the account of Matthew 4,
he said, ‘Look, just fall down and do an act of worship to me.’
Now, what does this tell us about Satan?
Well, he has long been driven by jealousy
over the worship that goes to Jehovah God.
And he’s going to go to any length possible
to try to violate our worship to Jehovah God.
He wants to pervert our worship to Jehovah God.
And so if he has enough boldness
to approach Jesus Christ,
then we know he will approach any one of us.
And it makes no difference how spiritually strong we look on the outside;
he will try to break our integrity.
Clearly, the Bible reveals that Satan
is a deadly strategist in seeking his aims.
Happily, though, we don’t have to be like Eve,
because we know the designs of Satan the Devil.
May each of us cultivate the kind of love Jesus had for Jehovah God,
so we too can stand firm in our integrity.

cn.text: 今天早上我们会谈谈撒但阴险狡猾的计谋
他一心想要诱惑人离开耶和华上帝
现在，我们来看看撒但用过的两个手段
他曾用在上帝创造的两个受造物身上
一个是当时宇宙中最年轻的
另一个是宇宙中最年长的
最年轻的是谁呢？
就是夏娃
撒但知道夏娃年轻、没有经验
就想要欺骗、引诱这个女人
那撒但怎么引诱她呢？
我们都知道，撒但躲在一条蛇的后面
不让夏娃知道是谁在跟她说话
也不让夏娃知道他有什么目的
我们从撒但说的话就可以知道他的手段了
方便的话请打开圣经到创世记第3章
我们再来看看撒但提出的问题
创世记3:1说
“上帝真的说你们不可吃
园子里各样树上的果子吗？”
撒但为什么要这样问呢？
刚刚有人已经解释过这一点了
就是撒但想要在夏娃心里
埋下一颗怀疑的种子
他想让夏娃以为耶和华没有把好东西给她
让她觉得上帝管得太严了！
关于该怎样回答问题
《传道训练班课本》第66页
提出了一个要点
有些人提出的问题好比疾病表面的症状
真正的病因往往不容易看到
因此，了解病因比看表面的症状更重要
所以，我们需要弄清楚
别人提出的问题有什么真正目的
然而，撒但提出问题时
夏娃没有听出他真正的目的
从2、3节我们就可以知道
夏娃说:“园子里树上的果子
我们都可以吃
只是园子中间那棵树上的果子
上帝曾经说:‘你们不可吃
也不可摸，免得死亡。’”
夏娃说得没错，她说的是实话
她只是单纯地回答问题而已
但这也让撒但看出夏娃很容易上钩
撒但就把赌注押在夏娃身上
如果夏娃只考虑自己的需要
爱自己超过给了她一切的上帝
那么撒但就赢了
撒但是怎样引诱夏娃的呢？
在4、5节，撒但对夏娃说
“你们一定不会死
只是上帝知道你们吃了
那一天你们的心眼就必打开
你们必像上帝一样，能辨识善恶。”
可悲的是，撒但赌赢了！
夏娃对上帝的爱的确还不够深
对上帝也没有感恩之心
我们从这件事学到什么呢？
要是一个完美的人
都会被这种荒谬的推理所骗
那不完美的我们呢？
不是更容易受骗吗？
耶和华创造人类时给了我们自由意志
所以夏娃也有自由意志
上帝不希望我们像机器人一样
他希望我们考虑事情的后果
能分辨是非善恶，作出正确的选择
但是，撒但却希望我们作出错误的决定
那么，我们怎么做
才不会让撒但的诡计得逞呢？
我们必须先了解自己内心深处的想法
保罗警告当时的基督徒要小心
不要变得“不重视圣物”
这就是当时的背景
知道这一点，可以帮助我们
更好地理解15、16节的经文
这里说
“你们要提高警觉
免得有人失去上帝的分外恩典
免得有毒根长起来危害你们，玷污许多人
也免得有人淫乱，不重视圣物。”
保罗在第15节劝勉我们“要提高警觉”
要警觉什么呢?
就是要小心有毒根长起来玷污会众
保罗提到的“毒根”，是指会众里的一些人
他们可能会挑剔会众处理事情的方式
甚至不接受耶和华在某些事上的观点
比如不认为婚姻是神圣的
或不同意保持道德洁净是必须的
我们一定不想成为这样的人！
但你想想，扎根之前需要先有什么呢？
需要先埋下一颗种子
种子发芽生长才会长出根来
所以在种子发芽前
我们就要特别留意
看看心里有没有埋下不好的种子
就是不好的念头
这件事没有任何人可以替我们做
因为别人看不到我们心里的想法
即使我们从没跟人说起过
自己内心也不愿意承认
但这种不好的念头可能就埋在我们内心深处
我们一定要铲除它，克服这些弱点
否则撒但就会利用这些弱点来攻击我们
雅各书1:14,15描述了这个过程
“各人受考验
是被自己的私欲所勾引诱惑的
［是自己的私欲］
私欲［也就是种子］
怀了胎［就是开始生长］
就生下罪来
罪既得逞，就生出死来。”
这里说“被自己的私欲所勾引诱惑”
听起来是不是很熟悉呢？
有时这种欲望会非常强烈
夏娃就是一个例子
她有了自私的欲望
结果就被勾引诱惑
那我们该怎么做呢？
刚刚谈到，我们要找出自己的弱点
有时可能不只一个
千万不要让它发芽，不要任由它生长
要除去这些不好的想法
要是我们心里已经长出“毒根”
就要立刻把它除掉
你可能需要别人帮助，因为只靠自己
我们可能没办法除掉“毒根”
现在来看看撒但用的另一个手段
他曾用在宇宙中最年长的那位身上
这就是耶稣
撒但引诱耶稣时完全不遮掩
他知道那只是多此一举
耶稣清楚知道撒但的真面目
知道他打的什么坏主意
所以撒但没有拐弯抹角
而是单刀直入！
在马太福音4章
撒但直接对耶稣说
“你拜我一下就可以了。”
从这件事我们看出什么呢？
撒但一直嫉妒上帝
渴望自己能像上帝那样受人崇拜
他用尽一切手段想要阻止我们崇拜上帝
想要破坏我们跟上帝的关系
既然撒但有这么大的胆子去试探耶稣
那他一定也有胆量来试探我们每一个人
不管我们跟上帝的关系看起来有多牢固
他都会设法引诱我们
想要我们不再忠于上帝
圣经清楚指出，撒但诡计多端
为达目的不择手段
但我们不用像夏娃那样被撒但蒙骗
因为我们已经知道撒但骗人的伎俩
希望我们每一个人
都像耶稣那样深爱耶和华！
这样，我们就可以对上帝忠贞到底

title: 용기를 나타내는 세계 전역의 우리 형제들 —남아메리카

ko.text: 어느 날 오후 집회에 가려던 참이었는데,
젊은 남자 몇 명이 다가오더니 우리 차를 빼앗아 갔어요.
어쨌든 집회에 가는 게 좋겠다고 생각했죠.
부정적인 생각에 사로잡혀 있는 건 아무 도움이 안 되니까요.
살면서 안 좋은 일을 겪을 때도
그곳에 가면 괴로운 마음이 싹 사라집니다.
강도당한 차는 제가 택시 기사로 일하면서 몰았던 세 번째 차였어요.
생계 수단을 잃은 거라 경제적으로 타격이 컸죠.
제가 일을 찾는 동안 우리 가족에게 많은 도움을 베풀어 주었습니다.
하루는 아들이 같은 회중 형제와 함께 성서 연구를 하러 나갔어요.
그런데 30분도 채 안 됐을 때 그 형제한테 전화가 왔습니다.
전활 받았더니 아들이 차에 치였다고 하는 거예요.
곧장 병원으로 달려갔는데, 이미 형제들이 많이 와 있었습니다.
그렇게 빨리 올 수 있었는지 모르겠어요.
하지만 그럴 때면 여호와께서 제 마음을 어루만지시면서
지금 많이 힘들겠지만 이 어려운 상황을 이겨 낼 수 있게
그분의 돌보심을 경험한 건 의미 있는 일이었죠.
강도를 만나고 아들이 교통사고를 당한 건
불과 1년도 안 되는 사이에 생긴 일입니다.
그 기간 내내 형제들은 늘 제 곁에 있어 줬어요.
또 악수를 하면서 돈을 건네줄 때도 있었는데,
마침 돈이 꼭 필요했을 때 그런 일이 자주 있었어요.
여호와의 도움 덕분에 우리 가족은 정말 행복합니다.
하루하루 그분은 저와 아내와 제 아들을 잘 돌봐 주시죠.
이겨 낼 수 있게 도와 달라고 매일 기도드리죠.
제 곁에 형제들이 있어서 절대 혼자가 아니라는 겁니다.
전 석유 관련 회사에서 책임자로 20년간 일했죠.
우리 가족은 저와 아내와 세 딸, 이렇게 다섯 명인데
먹을 거 걱정은 해 본 적이 없었습니다.
우리 회사의 경영진이 새로 바뀌었다는 걸 알게 됐습니다.
제가 20년 동안 업무를 보던 자리에 새로운 책임자가 앉아 있었습니다.
그는 손에 제 이력서를 들고 있었는데,
제가 정직하고 업무 성과가 좋다고 하면서
그런데 한 가지 빠진 게 있다고 하더군요.
정치 문제에서 중립을 지킨다는 걸 최대한 잘 설명했습니다.
그는 안색이 변하더니 목소리를 높이면서 막 화를 냈습니다.
오늘이 마지막 출근이 될 거라고 협박했죠.
하지만 전 정당에 가입하겠다고 서명하지 않았습니다.
그건 성적 부도덕을 저지르고 숨기는 것이나 마찬가지고
그냥 서명을 하고 계속 직장에 다닐 수도 있었겠지만,
그렇게 했으면 평생 양심의 가책을 느꼈을 겁니다.
집회에 나가고 회중에서 장로로 섬길 수는 없었죠.
20년간 다닌 직장을 잃었고 퇴직금도 받지 못했습니다.
집에 와 보니 아내와 딸들이 절 기다리고 있었어요.
또 우리가 견딜 수 있는 것 이상으로 유혹받지 않게 해 달라고
큰 시련이기는 했지만 여호와께 순종했기 때문에
이겨 낼 수 있을 거라고 확신했습니다.
직장을 잃은 뒤 여러 가지 일을 했습니다.
두 딸은 자주 보조 파이오니아를 하고 있고,
여호와께서는 항상 우리 가족을 잘 돌봐 주셨습니다.

en.text: One afternoon as we were going to our meeting,
I was robbed by a couple of thieves
—young men.
But right away, there at home,
we realized that the best thing to do was to go to the meeting anyway.
We just had to go to the meeting.
It didn’t make any sense to stay at home crying
and feeling all negative and frustrated.
At the Kingdom Hall you feel refreshed.
It’s a safe place and you feel at peace.
Your thoughts calm down,
and those terrible feelings caused by being a victim
of the bad things that happen in this system dissipate.
This was the third vehicle I’d had as a taxi driver.
It was a really big blow financially.
The brothers found out that I had lost my means of living.
I no longer had an income.
And while I was wondering what to do,
they began to attend to each of our needs.
David, my son —he left to go on a Bible study
with another brother from the congregation.
But less than half an hour later,
I got a call from the brother who was with him.
He gave me the terrible news that my son had been run over.
Well, when we got to where he was being treated,
there were many brothers there already —many brothers.
To this day, I can’t figure out how they got there so quickly.
Who called them?
How did they find out?
Our son’s accident was so distressing.
Our hearts took a beating.
As my heart was aching,
it was as if Jehovah took my heart in his hand
and caressed it:
‘Don’t you worry. Calm down.
‘Everything will be all right.
‘Just keep calm.
‘You’ve suffered a test, but now you will see my hand in this.
‘I won’t be coming down to be with you personally,
but look at all that’s happening.’
And we saw Jehovah’s power.
I’m not saying that it was good that it happened,
but it is important to see how Jehovah takes care of things.
Not a year passed by between the theft of my car
and my son’s accident.
The brothers were always there for us
—a greeting, a hearty handshake, a meaningful, “We’re right here, brother.”
And often there was something in that handshake
—money for things we needed at that moment.
Thanks to Jehovah,
my wife, my son, and I feel very happy
and amazed by all the good things
Jehovah does for us each day.
I want to take hold of Jehovah’s hand.
I concentrate on that and pray every day
to be able to cope with whatever problems arise.
And another important thing: I know that I can count on my friends.
I don’t have to face things alone.
I had a comfortable economic situation.
For 20 years I worked as the supervisor of a firm
contracted by the oil industry.
My family of five
—made up of my wife, my three daughters, and myself—
never had to worry about food.
One afternoon, as I watched the news on television,
I learned that the company I worked for
had come under new management.
That Monday, when I went to work,
I arrived at my office and found the new supervisor sitting in my chair
that I had occupied for 20 years.
I saw my résumé in his hand.
He congratulated me for being a hard worker
who was honest and productive,
but he said there was just one thing missing:
I needed to join a political party.
I replied as tactfully as I could
that my wife and I were Jehovah’s Witnesses
and that we were neutral in political matters.
The mood quickly deteriorated.
Visibly angered,
the supervisor’s facial expression and tone of voice changed,
and he threatened me, saying that if I did not join the political party,
then that would be my last day at work.
I did not sign it or join the political party,
because that would be like committing adultery
and keeping quiet about it.
I would feel as if I had betrayed Jehovah.
I could have signed it and kept my old job,
but I knew my conscience would bother me for the rest of my life.
I would never be able to go to the congregation
and serve as an elder knowing that I had let Jehovah down.
Suddenly, I was unemployed.
I lost 20 years of work and the severance and seniority pay I was due.
My wife and my daughters were waiting for me.
And right then and there,
we prayed together and asked Jehovah to please provide for us,
to please not let us be tempted beyond what we could bear.
We knew that we were facing a huge test,
but that we would prevail
because we had been obedient to Jehovah.
Since losing my job, I’ve done several different odd jobs
like gardening and painting houses,
and at present, I work with public transportation.
My daughter, Genesaret, the second oldest,
paints pictures, and we sell them.
My wife makes food and homemade sweets,
and we have learned other skills as well.
We have greatly simplified our life.
My wife and I were even invited to pioneer school in 2014.
Our two older daughters auxiliary pioneer from time to time,
and our youngest daughter, who is 13, was baptized.
Jehovah has never let us down.

title: 용기를 나타내는 세계 전역의 우리 형제들—오세아니아

ko.text: 우리 섬에선 전통을 지키는 게 정말 중요해요.
예를 들면, 가장이 정한 종교를 믿어야 하고
가장이 정해 준 사람과 결혼해야 하죠.
아버지는 제가 한 남자랑 결혼하기를 바라셨어요.
하루는 그 남자 가족들이 결혼 승낙을 받으려고 우리 집을 찾아왔어요.
전 그 사람과 결혼할 수 없는 이유를
막대기로 처음에 한 대 맞았을 땐 정말 아팠어요.
어머니가 아버지 대신 절 때릴 것처럼 하시더니
아버지는 저를 6개월 동안이나 집 안에 가둬 놓고
형제 자매들과 함께 여호와를 섬길 수 없었던 거예요.
그때 기도가 정말 큰 힘을 줬어요.
그리고 일요일에 가족들이 다 교회에 가고 나면,
혼자서 기도를 하고 노래를 부르고 항을 낭독하고
손을 들고 질문에 대한 답을 했죠.
형제 자매들과 함께 실제로 집회를 보는 것처럼 말이에요.
사촌 동생들이 우리 집 앞을 지나갈 때만 기다렸어요.
제 성서 연구와 재방문을 대신 해 줬거든요.
부엌 창문 앞에 가서 계속 기다렸어요.
그 애들은 절 못 봤지만, 저는 볼 수 있었어요.
사촌들이 제 성서 연구생들 집으로 가는 모습이 보일 때면
그런 시련들을 겪으면서 정말 무섭고 두려울 때도 있었죠.
그래서 여호와께 용기를 달라고 간절히 기도했고
그러면 그분은 즉시 제가 용기를 내서
마음이 편안해졌고 인내할 힘을 얻을 수 있었어요.
그 어려운 시간들을 이겨 낼 수 있게
여호와께서 도와주신 덕분에 지금 큰 축복을 누리고 있어요.
지금 전 그 어느 때보다도 행복합니다!
우리 부부는 2013년에 미국에서 마셜 제도로 이주했습니다.
우린 경제적으로 여유로웠고 부족한 게 없었습니다.
편안하게 살던 곳을 떠나 이주한다는 건 정말 큰 변화였습니다.
여긴 대부분의 집에 주방이나 실내 화장실이 없어요.
우리가 얻은 집에는 가스레인지와 냉장고도 없었죠.
늦은 나이에 새로운 언어를 배운다는 게 쉬운 일이 아니잖아요.
장로로서 어떻게 회중 성원들을 도울 수 있을지 걱정이 됐어요.
저랑 연구하던 분 집에 개가 한 마리 있었는데,
너무 사나워서 그 집엔 정말 가고 싶지 않았어요.
그래도 어쨌든 연구를 하러 갔는데, 개가 없는 거예요.
여러분이 한 일에 보상이 있을 것입니다”라고 했죠.
연구가 많다 보니까 1장만 한 열 번은 사회하게 됐죠.
사람들을 가르치고 여호와에 관해 알도록 도울 수 있었습니다.
근데 여긴 섬이니까 물에 둘러싸여 사는 셈이죠.
그런데 최근에 외딴 섬 구역에 가서 전파하는 특별 활동이 있었어요.
그곳 사람들은 하느님에 대해 배우고 싶어 하고
호별 방문을 하면 만나는 사람마다 하던 일을 멈추고
이곳 사람들은 여호와에 대해 알고 싶어 하고
그런 모습을 보면 힘이 나고 격려를 받죠.

en.text: Culture on my island is very strong.
For example, the head of the family can choose the family’s religion
and also who they will marry.
One day, many family members of a boy
that my father wanted me to marry
came to visit my father.
Their purpose was that they could request
that we would be married.
I respectfully explained that I could not do that.
So my father started beating me.
The first blow with the rod was very painful.
But Jehovah helped me by moving Mama to act
as if she would help him to beat me,
but instead, she didn’t actually beat me.
For six months, he imprisoned me in the house,
and he assigned me various hard jobs to do.
The thing that was the most difficult for me
was not being with the brothers and sisters
doing spiritual activities for Jehovah.
But what really strengthened me
was the gift of prayer.
I would pray constantly
and talk to Jehovah through prayer.
When I would do the meetings by myself,
I would make a schedule on Saturday night.
Then, on Sunday when all my family went to church,
I would start by praying,
singing, reading the paragraphs,
raising my hand,
and I would answer the questions myself.
It was as if I was with my brothers and sisters at the meeting.
Also, I would wait to see my younger cousins
every Sunday as they walked by
because I knew they would visit my studies and return visits.
I just went to the kitchen to wait.
I waited for them and watched them go by,
looking forward to being able to see them,
even though they didn’t see me.
Only I saw them.
And when they passed by,
I saw that they went to preach where the Bible students were.
I really felt strengthened, happy.
During those trials that I had to endure,
there were times that I was very scared, frightened.
I really needed the courage that Jehovah supplies.
That is why I begged Jehovah for courage,
and immediately Jehovah gave me courage
so that I didn’t have to be afraid anymore.
I had peace, and I was able to endure those trials.
By helping me to endure that test,
Jehovah helped me to experience the blessings that I’m having today.
Now, I am really happy!
In 2013, we decided to make a move
from the United States to the Marshall Islands.
We have a combined family
of 9 children and 24 grandchildren.
We had a middle income family,
and, you know, you have everything at your disposal.
It was a big adjustment
to move where we knew that we wouldn’t have those conveniences.
Life here is very different from the United States.
Many of the houses don’t have kitchens or indoor bathrooms,
and even in the house that we rented,
there was no stove or refrigerator.
I was very apprehensive about making the move.
It’s a little bit harder for older ones to learn a new language.
And so how would I be able to conduct Bible studies?
How would I be able to, as an elder, help out within the congregation?
I had one study who had a really fierce dog,
and I really didn’t want to go back to that house.
But I went back to have the Bible study,
and I didn’t see the dog.
So I asked her, “Where is the dog?”
And she said,
“My uncle ate him.”
At 2 Chronicles 15:7,
it says ‘do not be discouraged, there exists a reward for your activity.’
And so we busied and asserted ourselves in the work.
And so immediately we had, like, ten Bible studies in two weeks.
But the benefit of that is we would go over chapter one,
maybe ten times.
And so through repetition and through due diligence,
it really facilitated us
learning the language and being able to use it
to study with people and help them come to know Jehovah.
I am a bit afraid of water.
You know, we are on an island,
and here I’m surrounded by water, and I cannot swim.
We had a campaign recently to preach to the outer islands,
so I had to think about the people.
When I think about their desire to learn
more about God, their love for God,
their love and respect for the Bible,
it really motivates me to keep going in spite of my fears.
And when you think about going from door to door,
every person will stop —stop what they’re doing—
to talk to you about God.
They’ll accept the literature; they want Bible studies.
It’s really a pioneer’s dream.
Their desire,
their love for the truth and wanting to know about Jehovah,
well, that’s an additional blessing that is encouraging and strengthening us.
She says, “It’s a pioneer’s dream.”
I say, “It’s a pioneer’s paradise.”

ko.text: 지부 사무실에서 제일 좋은 구역을 주셨네요.”
그래서 우리는 기도를 하면서 성경에 나오는 조언도 찾아보고
알래스카에서 봉사했던 두 부부와도 이야기를 해 봤죠.
임지로 가기 위한 계획을 하기 시작했어요.
익숙한 환경을 떠나 임지로 가려면 용기가 필요하죠.
그런데 다른 형제들이 나타낸 용기를 보고 깊은 감명을 받았죠.
그중에 6명은 겨울을 한 번도 안 겪어 본 사람들이었는데
세계에서 가장 추운 곳 중 하나인 알래스카 북부로 임명받아 온 거예요.
이 젊은 형제 자매들이 주저 없이 익숙한 곳을 떠나
이렇게 독특한 지역으로 온 걸 보고 우리도 용기가 났죠.
거긴 그냥 춥기만 한 게 아니라, 해도 짧고 회중도 없고
형제들은 택시를 타고 그 날 봉사 구역의 가장 먼 곳으로 간 다음,
다시 걸어 돌아오면서 봉사를 하곤 했죠.
그곳에서 봉사하면서 정말 즐거웠던 일 하나는
유피크어 집단이 생기는 걸 본 거였습니다.
유피크어로 된 최초의 전도지를 번역하게 하셨죠.
유피크어를 읽고 쓸 줄 몰라서 걱정을 많이 했어요.
하지만 노아의 본을 통해 용기를 얻었고
노아처럼 “꼭 그대로” 한 결과 잘 해낼 수 있었죠.
성경은 “여호와의 축복은 사람을 부유하게 해 준다”고 말하죠.
하지만 삶을 정말로 의미 있게 하는 건
우린 정말 우리가 드린 것보다 훨씬 더 많이 받았습니다.
여호와께서 열어 주신 문으로 들어갈지 고민하고 계시다면,
분명 큰 축복을 받게 될 겁니다.
평일 집회 때 총을 든 남자 세 명이 왕국회관에 왔습니다.
큰돈을 요구하면서 돈을 안 주면 모두 해치겠다고 위협했어요.
그 사람은 절 한적한 곳으로 데려가서 내려놓고는
멕시코시티에는 총을 든 강도가 많아서 봉사하는 게 위험해요.
사람이 총에 맞는 걸 본 적도 있죠.
집회 때마다 스무 명의 안내인이 왕국회관 입구를 지킵니다.
누가 오면 위협이 되는 사람인지 먼저 확인한 뒤 들여보냅니다.
호별 방문을 할 때는 함께 그룹을 지어 봉사합니다.
혹시나 모를 위험에 대비해 항상 주변을 잘 살피죠.
잡지나 성경 같은 출판물을 늘 손에 들고 다녀요.
사람들이 우리가 여호와의 증인인 걸 알아볼 수 있게요.
또 핸드폰이나 반지 같은 귀중품은 집에 두고 나가죠.
위험한 구역이긴 해도 사람들이 정말 잘 듣죠.
많은 사람이 여호와에 대해 배우고 있습니다.
저를 납치한 남자는 차를 타고 가는 동안,
여호와의 증인과 다른 교회의 차이점이 뭐냐고 물어봤어요.
그런 상황에서도 증거할 수 있을 거라곤 생각도 못 했죠.
최악의 상황도 기회가 될 수 있죠.
중단하지 않고 전파하는 모습이 정말 격려가 돼요.
하지만 우리는 상황이 어떻든 여호와를 섬길 겁니다.
우리는 육체밖에 죽일 수 없는 사람을 두려워하지 않습니다.
또 그런 일이 생긴다 해도 우리 모두는 계속 전파할 겁니다.
또 이웃들도 범죄로 고통받고 있다는 걸 잘 알기 때문에
희망의 소식을 전해 주려고 최선을 다하고 있습니다.
전파 활동을 절대 그만두지 않을 겁니다.
범죄가 있든 없든 계속 해야 하는 일이기 때문이죠.

en.text: They said, “You’ve got to go to Alaska
—one of the greatest assignments that you can be provided from the branch.”
And then he popped up with the question,
he said, “Have you ever thought of going to Alaska?”
And we said, “Well, should we?”
No!
We definitely had to pray about it
and, Scripturally, look up some things.
And we talked to two couples that we knew that had served in Alaska.
You’re assigned to the people, and if you focus on that,
then you’ll find joy in your assignment no matter where it is.
I also like the spirit of Isaiah
where Jehovah asks: “Whom shall I send?”
And without a hesitation,
Isaiah pipes up: “Here I am! Send me!”
He was just willing to be sent.
And then there were the logistics of figuring out
how to simplify and how to actually get up there.
It definitely takes courage to take an assignment
where you’re out of your comfort zone.
We might have needed some courage for the assignment that we took,
but we were so impressed with the courage that the other brothers demonstrated.
There were a total of 16 different special pioneers
that were assigned,
and 6 of them had never experienced a winter,
and they’re being sent into the harshest of climates
—the harshest of winters in northern Alaska.
When we saw these young men, without hesitation,
going to very unique places out of their comfort zone
—it inspired us.
And it wasn’t just a harsh climate,
but it was darkness, no congregation—
—isolation—
—none of their friends, none of their family there.
They would get a taxi cab to drive them
to the farthest part of their territory for that particular day,
drop them off, and then they would work from that location
back to their hotel.
I would say that one of the blessings that we enjoyed
was seeing how Jehovah opened up the language group.
Jehovah chose the right ones
to get the first tract translated into the Yupik language.
One of the sisters who was asked to translate
was intimidated because she did not know how to read or write the language.
Contemplating Noah gave her the courage
to fulfill her assignment because she, like Noah, “did just so.”
You know the scripture that says ‘the blessings of Jehovah,
that is what makes rich.’
That is so true.
We could have stayed in Jersey in our little apartment,
maybe even by now have a comfortable living.
But what really makes life worth living is the people and friends you have.
As it was once said, “You can’t outgive Jehovah.”
If anyone is considering going through a door
that Jehovah has opened up for them,
don’t hesitate.
You’ve got the support of Jehovah,
unseen angels, His spirit, and the brotherhood.
And the blessings are just waiting for you.
On one occasion, my son called me on the phone and said:
“Dad, come quickly!
They kidnapped John!”
During a midweek meeting,
three armed men showed up at the Kingdom Hall.
They threatened to harm the brothers,
their families, or the congregation
unless they received a considerable sum of money.
I got to the Kingdom Hall,
and when I opened the car door, a kidnapper was there waiting for me.
They took me to an abandoned lot and left me there,
but they took my car.
It’s dangerous to preach in many parts of Mexico City,
since we’re in danger of being robbed at gunpoint.
For instance, I once witnessed a shooting.
My husband has been mugged.
These kinds of things don’t happen just in Mexico;
they happen all over the world.
At the meetings, we had as many as 20 attendants
at the doors of the Kingdom Hall so that the congregation would feel safe.
When the meeting starts, the doors are closed.
But we keep on the lookout, and if somebody wants to come in,
we make sure that they will not pose a threat to the congregation.
When we’re preaching from house to house,
we try to stay together as a group.
And we’re aware of our surroundings,
watching out for any dangers.
We’re always holding publications,
like a magazine or a Bible.
It helps us because people identify us as Jehovah’s Witnesses.
I try not to have any valuables on me, like a cell phone or jewelry.
It’s a very productive territory even though it is such a dangerous area.
A lot of people are coming to know Jehovah.
While I was in the car with the kidnapper,
he asked me what the difference is between Jehovah’s Witnesses and Christians.
I didn’t know I would have the opportunity to preach, but I did.
When life gives you lemons, you make lemonade.
I greatly admire the sisters that go out in service
—the courage they show—
because even though their territories are difficult, dangerous,
they will not give up in this important work.
For them, giving up is not an option.
And I will never give up either.
Crime happens and will continue to happen.
But we’re determined to serve Jehovah, no matter what.
We should not be afraid of those who kill the body.
If we were to face this situation again,
the congregation would not stop preaching.
They love Jehovah so much.
And they truly understand that their neighbors
are also suffering from crime,
so they put forth much effort to share a message of hope.
No, I will not stop preaching.
This work must go on
whether there’s violence or not.

就有一个人把我绑架了
他们带我来到一片荒地后就把我扔下
开着我的车走了
墨西哥城很多地方常有持枪抢劫的事
在那些地方传道很危险
我有一次就看到有人开枪
我丈夫也被抢过
这样的事不是只有墨西哥才有
全世界都有
聚会的时候
我们有20个弟兄在聚会所的各个门口站岗
这样会众里的弟兄姐妹能感到安全
聚会开始以后
所有的大门都会锁上
我们会继续看着大门
如果有人想要进来
我们会先确定他们不会威胁会众成员的安全
我们挨家挨户传道时
会一群人一起传道
我们会留意周围的情况
小心提防危险
我们手上总是拿着圣经或者圣经书刊
这样人们就能认出我们是耶和华见证人
我尽量不带任何贵重物品
比如手机或者珠宝
这个地区虽然很危险
但人们的反应却非常好
很多人都开始认识耶和华
当我和绑匪坐在车里的时候
他问我耶和华见证人和其他基督徒有什么区别
真没想到这时候还能作见证
于是我就作了见证
有坏事发生的时候
你也可以把它变成好事
我很佩服这些姐妹们
佩服她们那么有勇气
虽然在那里传道很难、很危险
但她们却从没想过要放弃这项重要的工作
她们不会放弃
我也绝不会放弃
犯罪活动仍在继续
但我们无论如何也不会放弃事奉耶和华
我们不会害怕那些杀身体却不能杀生命的
就算我们再遇到这样的情况
会众也不会停止传道

也知道地区里的人同样是犯罪活动的受害者
所以他们尽全力跟人分享未来的希望
我不会停止传道
绝对不会
就算有罪行
传道工作也必须进行下去

공기의 흐름을 흩어지게 해서 소음을 줄인다고 말합니다.
날개를 타고 흐르는 공기를 더욱 잘게 나눕니다.
올빼미 날개의 구조를 모방한 장치를 개발하고 있습니다.
이 장치를 풍력 발전기 날개에 부착해 사용했을 때

en.text: The wings of an owl enable it to fly in virtual silence.
How?
The feathers on the leading edge are serrated.
One theory suggests that this helps break up the flow of air,
reducing noise.
Meanwhile, the trailing edge of the wing
has a flexible fringe,
further dispersing airflow.
Nearly all remaining sound
is then absorbed
by the velvetlike feathers on the owl’s wings.
Scientists from Cambridge University
are developing a coating
mimicking this wing structure
for use on wind turbines.
Early tests show that the coating
significantly increases
blade speed and efficiency,
while drastically reducing noise.
In the future, scientists hope similar coatings
can be applied to a wide range of applications.
So, what do you think?
Did the owl’s wing evolve?
Or was it designed?

cn.text: 猫头鹰在飞翔时
几乎不会发出任何声音
这要归功于它的翅膀
猫头鹰翅膀前缘的羽毛结构呈锯齿状
有些科学家认为这能分散空气湍流
降低翅膀拍动时发出的声音
而后端的羽毛非常柔韧
可以进一步分散湍流
猫头鹰翅膀上还有大量松软的羽毛
可以吸音降噪
剑桥大学的科学家
仿照猫头鹰翅膀的构造
研发出一种涂层
覆盖在风力发电机的叶片上
初步实验显示
这不仅能大大提高转速和发电效率
也能有效地降低噪音
科学家期待
这类涂层在未来会有更广泛的用途
你认为怎样？
猫头鹰的翅膀是进化而来的
还是经过设计的呢？

ko.text: 하지만 어느 날 예기치 못한 일이
디트로이트 시의 한 고등학교에서 침례를 받았습니다.
그해 12월 28일, 제 생일 날짜에 베델에 들어왔어요.
전 출판물을 생산하는 일을 열심히 했어요.
생명을 얻을 수 있다는 걸 알았거든요.
한창 힘 있고 일을 많이 할 수 있는 젊은 나이에
여호와께 저의 모든 것을 드릴 수 있었으니까요.
차에 있던 나머지 사람들은 크게 다치지 않았지만,
그곳은 거의 전파되지 않은 구역과도 같았죠.
“절 살려 주셨으니, 저도 선생님을 살리고 싶어요.”
그냥 봐줘서 베델에 남아 있는 게 아니라,
제가 정말 유용하게 쓰일 수 있을까 하고요.
전 세계 지부에서 인쇄된 출판물들을 다루는 일입니다.
저는 시간이 지나면 몸이 회복되고 건강해져서
다시 할 수 있을 줄 알았는데,
더 많이 할 수 있다면 좋겠지만 제겐 그럴 능력이 없죠.
그래서 전 여호와와 평화로운 관계를 누립니다.
제 상황을 아시고 제가 할 수 있는
신세계에 가서 건강이 좋아지는 걸 체험하는 거죠.

cn.text: 约翰·福斯特弟兄
在美国伯特利服务已经50多年了
有一天他发生了一场意外
这彻底改变了他的一生
我在底特律的一所学校里受了浸
传道工作对我来说非常重要
它也是我生活的重心
因为这牵涉到拯救别人的生命
1962年，我参加区域大会时
提交了伯特利服务申请表
那年的12月28日
我就到伯特利报到
那天正好是我的生日
从那时起，我就决心
尽己所能全力为上帝服务
我负责印制书刊
我很努力地工作
因为我知道
这些书刊可以帮助人得到真正的生命
我在自己年轻力壮的时候
能够竭尽全力为上帝服务
那段时间我真的非常快乐
一场可怕的车祸彻底改变了我的生活
那一天，我们正在去聚会的路上
我们的车子撞上了一棵树
结果我的脖子和腿都受了重伤
很不幸，司机也去世了
车子里的人都受了伤
不过我伤得最重
我昏迷了3个星期
我醒来后，全身疼痛难忍
我努力向别人传道
这帮助我转移注意力
我在医院里分发圣经书刊
这里有很多人
好像都还没有听过圣经的好消息
我给了我的外科医生一本《圣经真理》书
我跟他说
“你救了我一命，我也要救你一命！”
事故发生后
我很担心自己还能不能继续在伯特利工作
也不知道弟兄们会不会仅仅因为同情我
才让我留在伯特利
现在，我的工作
是把组织印制的各种语言的书刊都保留一本
用来存档
我还有另一个工作
就是有时会去别的部门发表演讲
鼓励弟兄姐妹
我本来以为自己会完全康复
可以回去做原来的工作
但后来才发现这根本不可能
现在，我就按自己的能力
能做多少就做多少
我希望可以多做一点
但心有余而力不足
我知道耶和华不会对我有过高的要求
这让我感觉踏实多了
上帝肯定了解我的情况
知道我会尽力为他服务
我也知道只有到了新世界
我才能彻底康复
所以，我期待的是
我能在新世界里生活
到时我就会完全康复
我很期待拥有完美的健康！

ko.text: 사람들에게 성경 진리를 올바로 전해 주려면
성경과 그리스도인 출판물을 정확히 읽어야 하죠.
이제 한 형제가 성구 낭독하는 걸 들으면서
우리가 흔히 어떤 실수를 저지르는지 살펴보시죠.
그 답이 여기 성경 마태복음 24:43, 44절에 나오는데요.
“도둑이 몇 시에 올지 집주인이 알았다면, 깨어 있으면서
도둑이 집에 침입하지 모다게 했을 것입니다.
낭독을 들으면서 집주인이 잘 집중할 수 있었을까요?
읽는 내용이 중요하지 않다는 인상을 받게 되고
그 답이 여기 성경 마태복음 24:43, 44절에 나오는데요.
밤 몇 시에 올지 집주인이 알았더라면,
깨어 있으면서 집에 도둑이 침입하지 못하게 했을 것입니다.
혼자 읽을 때도 올바른 습관을 기르려고 해야 합니다.
“선생님, 모세의 기록에 따르면” 으로 읽어야 하죠.
쉼표를 무시하고 죽 읽으면 전혀 다른 의미가 되는 겁니다.
그러면 그분이 여러분에게 가까이 오실 것입니다.
하느님이 우리에게 가까이 오길 원하신다는 요점이
그러면 그분이 여러분에게 가까이 오실 것입니다.
이번엔 올바른 단어를 강조해서 요점을 잘 전달했습니다.
그리고 조사나 접속사와 같은 기능어를 불필요하게 강조하지 않도록
예를 들어 요한복음 3:36절을 낭독할 때 조사를 강조해서
“아들에게 믿음을 나타내는 사람에게는 ...” 이라고 읽지 말고,
중요한 의미가 있는 동사 부분을 강조하는 건 어떨까요?
“아들에게 믿음을 나타내는 사람에게는 영원한 생명이 있다.”
단어를 틀리지 않게 발음하는 것만을 의미하지 않습니다.
물론 정확한 발음도 쉬운 건 아니죠.
단어를 정확히 발음하려면 어디서 도움을 받을 수 있을까요?
우리가 정확하게 낭독하면 우리의 소식의 품위가 올라갑니다.
또 듣는 사람이 내용에 집중하게 되고
실수 때문에 주의가 흐트러지는 일이 없을 겁니다.

en.text: To convey Bible truth correctly,
we must read from the Bible
and our Christian publications accurately.
To do this, we must prepare well,
pronounce each word correctly,
and speak clearly.
As our brother reads Matthew 24:43, 44,
try to identify some common mistakes made in reading.
To answer that question, notice what the Bible says at Matthew 24:43, 44:
“But know one more thing: If the housekeeper had known when the thief was comin,’
“he woulda kept awake and not allowed his house to be broken in two.
“On this account, you two prove yourselves ready,
because the Son of God is comin’ at an hour that you do not think it to be.”
Do you think that the householder
might have been distracted by the reading?
Likely.
Making any of these errors could convey
a lack of respect for the material
or change the meaning of the verse.
Let’s watch a better example.
To answer that question, notice what the Bible says at Matthew 24:43, 44:
“But know one thing:
“If the householder had known in what watch the thief was coming,
“he would have kept awake
“and not allowed his house to be broken into.
“On this account, you too prove yourselves ready,
because the Son of man is coming at an hour that you do not think to be it.”
Much better!
To become effective at reading aloud,
we should work to develop good habits in our personal reading.
Strive to understand the meaning
and to observe all punctuation marks.
For instance, at Matthew 8:3,
Jesus did not say to the leper:
“I want to be made clean,”
but rather: “I want to! Be made clean.”
Running through the exclamation point
completely changes the meaning.
In other verses, we have to emphasize the right words
in order to convey the intended meaning.
For instance, how would you read 1 John 2:1?
Let’s watch.
“My little children, I am writing you these things
“so that you may not commit a sin.
“And yet, if anyone does commit a sin,
we have a helper with the Father, Jesus Christ, a righteous one.”
Because the brother stressed the word “father,”
he gave the impression that Jesus Christ is the Father,
which was clearly not the writer’s intent.
Let’s give our brother another chance.
“My little children, I am writing you these things
“so that you may not commit a sin.
“And yet, if anyone does commit a sin,
“we have a helper with the Father,
Jesus Christ, a righteous one.”
This time, the speaker made it clear
that the helper is Jesus Christ.
We should also be careful not to place undue emphasis on function words,
such as prepositions and conjunctions.
For instance, at 1 Timothy 4:16, instead of reading
“you will save both yourself and those who listen to you,”
why not emphasize the verb to convey the full meaning of the text?
“You will save both yourself and those who listen to you.”
Clearly, there is more to accurate reading
than simply pronouncing words correctly,
yet even that can be a challenge at times.
Where can you find help to pronounce a word or name correctly
—even Bible names?
You can look them up in a dictionary,
listen to an audio recording of the publication,
or ask a good reader for help.
Accurate reading adds to the dignity of the message we preach.
It allows our listener to focus on the message
rather than be sidetracked by any mistakes.
Most important, it honors Jehovah God.

cn.text: 想要让对方正确地理解圣经信息
我们在朗读圣经和圣经出版物时
就要正确无误
该怎么做呢？
朗读前要做好准备
确认读音
朗读时发音要清晰
让我们看看一个弟兄在读
犯了哪些常见错误
我们看一下马太福音24:43,44
经文说
住户看着圣经
听到弟兄读错很多地方
可能有些分心
这些错误可能让对方觉得
你不够重视你读的内容
甚至可能改变了经文的意思
让我们看看正确示范
我们看一下马太福音24:43,44
经文说
“有一件事你们要知道
家主如果知道几更天有贼来
就会保持警醒
不容贼挖洞进家里来
所以你们也要预备妥当
因为在你们认为不大可能的时刻
人子就来了。”
这就好多了！
我们平时养成良好的朗读习惯
读给别人听的时候
才能做到正确无误
我们要正确理解朗读的内容
也要留意标点符号
比如在马太福音12:38
有人对耶稣说
“老师，希望你行一件奇事......”
而不是
“老师希望你行一件奇事......”
如果在逗号的地方没有停顿
意思就变了
另外，为了避免让人误解经文的意思
我们要留意自己强调什么字眼
请看看这个讲者
怎么读启示录18:20
“天啊，你要因她而欢欣！
圣民、使徒、先知啊
你们也要欢欣！
因为上帝已经为你们惩罚她了！”
这个弟兄过度强调了
“天啊”这两个字
这会让人误以为他在感慨“我的天哪！”
误解经文的意思
我们再给他一次机会
“天啊，你要因她而欢欣！
圣民、使徒、先知啊
你们也要欢欣！
因为上帝已经为你们惩罚她了！”
这次弟兄强调了正确的字眼
听众就不会分心了
我们也要留意在朗读时
不要过度强调虚词
例如连词或介词
比如在罗马书12:2
与其读成
“不要被这个制度同化
倒要更新思想而改变自己”
不如强调动词
“不要被这个制度同化
倒要更新思想而改变自己”
这样意思更突出
可见“朗读正确无误”
不仅仅是把每个字都读对而已
如果不确定某些字词
比如人名地名该怎么读
可以怎么做呢？
你可以查字典或词典
听出版物的录音
或请教擅长朗读的人
我们读得正确
就可以帮助对方
把注意力集中在
我们传讲的重要信息之上
而避免不必要的分心
最重要的是
这能为耶和华上帝带来荣耀

titles.cn: 第5课：朗读正确无误

title: 데이비드 H. 스플레인: 모든 사람을 기념식에 초대하십시오 (시 118:22)

ko.text: 우리가 주 예수 그리스도의 죽음을 기념하는 이 특별한 날에
여러분 모두에게 이렇게 말씀드리게 되어 정말 기쁩니다.
예수께서 죄인들의 손에 불공정한 취급을 당하신 게 생각나죠.
“건축자들이 버린 그 돌이 주된 모퉁잇돌이 되었다.”
예수께선 유대 민족의 지도자들에겐 버림을 받았지만,
전 사도 베드로의 말이 참 좋은데요,
베드로 전서 2:4에서 그 점을 이렇게 말했죠.
혹시 집주인이 문 앞에서 거절할 때, 면전에서 문을 쾅 닫아 버릴 때
기분이 좀 상하는 분이라면, 이 말을 생각하시기 바랍니다.
이 말을 생각하면, 도움이 될 겁니다.
오늘 우리 모두가 해야 할 중요한 활동에 초점을 맞춰 보죠.
기념식에 최대한 많은 사람을 초대하는 일입니다.
오늘 일을 쉬시는 분이라면, 분명 봉사에 참여하실 텐데요.
오늘은 베델 봉사자들도 세계 전역에서 야외 봉사를 할 겁니다.
오늘 저녁에 가능한 많은 사람이 참석하도록
여러분이 하실 수 있는 일들이 있죠.
직장 동료나 학교 친구에게 얘기해 보면 어떻겠습니까?
또한 성서 연구생들과 재방문하는 분들도 잊지 마세요.
성서 연구생들과 재방문하는 분들도 잊지 말고 오늘 연락하십시오.
초대장을 찾지 못해 기념식 날짜를 잊었을지 모릅니다.
가끔 어떤 성서 연구생이 당연히 참석할 줄 알았는데,
나중에 알고 보니 사소한 일 때문에 참석하지 않은 것입니다.
한 번 더 권한다고 해서 나쁠 게 없죠.
우리와 연합했다가 무활동이 된 분들은 어떤가요?
제가 볼 땐 두 부류가 있는데요.
한 부류는 기념식에 빠지지 않는 분들입니다.
1년 내내 집회에 나가지 않다가 기념식에만 참석하는 게
또 믿지 않는 남편들도 잊지 마세요.
어쩌면 아내보다는 다른 사람의 초대에 더 잘 응할지 모릅니다.
기념식 날, 한 방문 연사와 장로의 회 조정자가
당시 그 형제는 15년째 집회에 참석하지 않고 있었죠.
하지만 그 이전엔 진리 안에서 활동적으로 일했고,
그 형제가 전에 활동하던 시절의 즐거운 추억을 떠올리며 얘기할 때,
그러다 대화를 마칠 즈음 이 말만 했습니다.
회중 성원 대부분은 그 형제가 누군지 몰랐지만
그런데 직장에서 오늘 저녁에 일을 해 달라고 했다면 어떻게 할까요?
직장 상사가 융통성 없기로 소문난 사람일 수 있습니다.
‘절대 일을 안 빼 줄 거야’라는 생각이 든다면 어떻게 하죠?
상사의 마음을 움직여 달라고 그분께 기도하면서,
호소력 있고 존중심 있게 말할 수 있도록 도와달라고 하세요.
생각보다 일이 잘 해결될 수 있습니다.
여호와의 종들은 늘 기념식을 매우 중요하게 여겼죠.
우리 형제 자매들은 강제 수용소나 노동 수용소에서도
최근에도 수감된 한국의 젊은 형제들이 그 본을 따랐죠.
교도소의 철창도 형제들이 기념식을 지키는 걸 막을 수 없었습니다.
관심자들이 기념식이 열리는 마을이나 도시에 가려면
먼 거리를 여행해야 하는 경우가 있습니다.
탄자니아에서 한 연구생은 외딴 지역으로 이사했는데,
가장 가까운 회중은 100킬로미터 정도 떨어져 있었죠.
서양의 나라들에선 그리 먼 거리가 아니겠지만,
버스를 타고 힘들게 여덟 시간이나 가야 했습니다.
둘째로, 버스가 여러 곳에 정차했기 때문이죠.
끝난 후에 형제들에게 한 달에 한 번이라도 찾아와
성서 연구를 계속하게 해 달라고 간청했습니다.
연구생이 많은 노력 끝에 기념식에 참석했으니,
몇 주 후, 특별 파이오니아 부부가 그 연구생을 방문했습니다.
그는 이미 17명이나 되는 마을 주민과 성서 연구를 하고 있었습니다.
기념식을 지키려는 굳은 결심을 보여 주었죠.
이 부부는 매우 험한 길을 여행해서
길이 어찌나 험한지 타고 가던 오토바이가 고장 나고 말았습니다.
안타깝게도 갈아 끼울 부품을 구할 수가 없었죠.
그 부부는 발이 묶여 버렸기 때문에,
바로 그곳에서, 그 낯선 마을에서 기념식을 지키기로 했습니다.
기념식이 얼마나 중요한지 설명하여 촌장의 협조를 얻었습니다.
촌장은 자기 소유지에서 기념식을 열도록 허락하면서,
젊은 남자들을 시켜 그곳을 청소하고 연단까지 만들어 주었습니다.
마침 부부에게 초대장이 있어서, 그걸 마을 주민들에게 전했죠.
그 결과, 기념식에 마을 사람이 80명이나 참석했습니다.
또 기념식에는 노래가 빠질 수 없죠?
그런데 마을 사람들은 증인이 아니라 우리 노래를 몰랐습니다.
하지만 여행하는 감독자의 아내가 노래를 잘했기 때문에,
청중을 도와 기념식 노래 두 곡을 함께 불렀습니다.
한 회중은 전도인 130명 모두가 기념식에 많은 사람을 초대하기 위해
아프리카 여러 지역에선 성원이 백여 명 정도인 회중의 기념식에
우리 회중엔 천 명은 어림도 없어.’
하지만 여러분도 아프리카 형제들처럼 열심히 봉사한다면,
여호와께서는 여러분도 그들만큼 축복해 주실 겁니다.
기념식을 준비하기 위해 우리 모두가 할 일이 또 있죠.
우리 모두는 여호와를 기쁘시게 하기 위해
더 할 일이 있는지 지금 자신을 살펴야 하죠.
지금이 그 감정을 풀 좋은 기회죠.
나쁜 습관 때문에 영적으로 발전하는 데
바로 지금이 그 습관을 버리기 위해 단호한 행동을 취할 때입니다.
이 명령을 여호와의 증인은 매우 중요하게 여깁니다.
여러분이 사람들을 초대하려고 열심히 노력할 때
그분을 그리스도로 받아들이기를 거부하기만 한 것이 아니었습니다.
그들은 예수를 죽이는 일에 가담한 것입니다.
그분이 부활되어야만 그렇게 되실 수 있었습니다.
사도 베드로는 ‘나사렛 사람 예수 그리스도’를 가리켜
하느님께서 죽은 사람들 가운데서 일으키신 분’이라고 말했습니다.
‘사람들에게 주어진 이름 가운데 우리를 구원할 수 있는’
이제 녹음된 낭독을 들으면서 오늘의 성서 읽기 범위를 읽어 보죠.
무교절 첫날에, 제자들이 예수께 와서 물었다.
내가 당신의 집에서 제자들과 함께 유월절을 지키겠습니다.”’”
제자들은 예수께서 시키신 대로 하여 유월절을 준비했다.
유월절 제물을 바쳐야 하는 무교절 날이 되자
“도시로 들어가면 물동이를 메고 가는 남자를 만날 것입니다.
그 사람이 들어가는 집으로 따라 들어가십시오.
유월절 식사를 할 방이 어디입니까?” 라고 말씀하십니다.’
그러면 그 사람이 잘 갖추어진 큰 위층 방을 보여 줄 것입니다.
그래서 그들이 가서 보니 그분이 말씀하신 대로였다.
그분이 열두 제자와 함께 식탁에 앉으셨다.
그들이 먹고 있을 때에 그분이 말씀하셨다.
여러분 중 한 사람이 나를 배반할 것입니다.”
이 말을 듣고 제자들은 몹시 근심하며
“나와 함께 그릇에 손을 넣는 사람이 나를 배반할 것입니다.
사실, ‘사람의 아들’은 자신에 관해 기록된 대로 떠나갑니다.
그러나 ‘사람의 아들’을 배반하는 그 사람에게는 화가 있습니다!
차라리 태어나지 않았더라면 자신에게 더 좋았을 것입니다.”
그러자 그분을 배반하려 하는 유다가 물었다.
예수께서 빵을 들고 축복의 말씀을 하신 뒤에
또 잔을 들고 감사를 드리신 다음 그들에게 주며 말씀하셨다.
이것은 죄를 용서해 주려고 많은 사람을 위해 쏟는
나는 내 아버지의 왕국에서 여러분과 함께 새것을 마시는 그날까지,
포도나무에서 난 이것을 결코 다시 마시지 않겠습니다.”
끝으로 그들은 찬양의 노래를 부른 다음 올리브 산으로 갔다.
“이 밤에 여러분은 모두 나와 관련해 걸려 넘어질 것입니다.
양 떼가 흩어질 것이다’라고 기록되어 있습니다.
“다른 사람들이 모두 주와 관련해 걸려 넘어질지라도,
저는 결코 걸려 넘어지지 않을 것입니다!”
이 밤에 닭이 울기 전에 당신은 나를 세 번 부인할 것입니다.”
“주와 함께 죽는 한이 있더라도, 저는 결코 주를 부인하지 않겠습니다.”
그때에 예수께서 제자들과 함께 겟세마네라는 곳으로 가서
“내가 저기 가서 기도하는 동안 여기 앉아 있으십시오”
그리고 베드로와 세베대의 두 아들을 데리고 가셨다.
여기에 머물러 나와 함께 깨어 있으십시오.”
그리고 조금 앞으로 나아가 얼굴을 숙이고 엎드려 기도하셨다.
이 잔을 제게서 지나가게 해 주십시오.
그러나 제 뜻이 아니라 아버지의 뜻대로 하십시오.”
그들이 자고 있는 것을 보시고 베드로에게 말씀하셨다.
“여러분은 나와 함께 한 시간도 깨어 있을 수 없었습니까?
유혹에 빠지지 않도록 깨어 살피고 계속 기도하십시오.
그분은 다시 두 번째로 가서 기도하셨다.
제가 마시지 않고는 이 잔이 지나갈 수 없다면,
그리고 다시 와서 보시니 그들이 자고 있었다.
다시 가서 세 번째로 기도하며 한 번 더 같은 말씀을 하셨다.
열두 제자 중 하나인 유다가 왔다.
그리고 수제사장들과 백성의 장로들이 보낸 많은 무리가
칼과 몽둥이를 들고 그와 함께 왔다.
“내가 입을 맞추는 사람이 바로 그 사람이니, 그를 붙잡으시오”
그때에 그들이 나아와 예수를 붙잡아 체포했다.
그런데 예수와 함께 있던 사람들 중 하나가
칼을 뽑아 대제사장의 종을 쳐서 그의 귀를 잘라 버렸다.
칼을 잡는 사람은 모두 칼로 망할 것입니다.
당장에 열두 군단이 넘는 천사들을 보내 달라고 할 수 없는 줄 압니까?
그러면 일이 이렇게 되어야 한다는 성경 말씀이
“여러분은 강도를 잡듯이 칼과 몽둥이를 들고 나를 잡으러 왔습니까?
그러나 이 모든 일이 일어난 것은
그때에 제자들은 모두 그분을 버리고 달아났다.
여러분이 오늘 봉사에서 좋은 결과를 거두고,

en.text: Good morning, everyone.
This Morning Worship program is originating
from world headquarters at Warwick, New York.
And, brothers and sisters,
it’s a real privilege and pleasure
to speak to all of you on this special day
when we observe the Memorial
of the death of our Lord Jesus Christ.
Today’s text will remind us
of the unjust treatment that he suffered at the hands of sinners.
And we have Brother William Malenfant here;
Bill is a helper to the Teaching Committee.
Bill, will you read the text for us, please?
Friday, April the 19th
—the Memorial date after sundown.
The text is taken from Psalm 118:22:
“The stone that the builders rejected
has become the chief cornerstone.”
Thank you, Bill.
Although Jesus was rejected by the leaders of the Jewish nation,
what got into him was having Jehovah’s approval.
You know, I love the way the apostle Peter put it
according to 1 Peter 2:4.
Peter said that Jesus was ‘rejected by men
but precious to God.’
Isn’t that nice?
Now, if you’re the type of person who gets a little bit upset
when you’re rejected at the doors (maybe someone slams a door in your face),
why not just think about this phrase
—‘rejected by men but precious to God’?
Memorize it: ‘rejected by men but precious to God.’
And then think about it; it’ll help.
Now, speaking of the ministry, I thought I’d focus the rest of my comments
on the important work we all have to do today
—to invite as many as possible to the Memorial.
If you have time off from work today,
no doubt you’ll be sharing in the ministry.
And that’s what Bethel family members
all over the world are going to be doing today.
But whether you have time off or not,
there are things you can do to make sure
that as many as possible are in attendance tonight.
If you have to go to work or to school,
why not talk to a workmate or a schoolmate
who you think would be willing
to attend the Memorial?
You might be happy at the outcome.
And don’t forget to get in touch
with your Bible students and return visits today.
I’m going to repeat that.
Don’t forget to get in touch
with your Bible students and return visits today,
even if you’ve already invited them to the Memorial.
Why?
Well, your return visits might have misplaced the invitation,
and perhaps they’ve forgotten what day it is.
All right, those are the return visits,
but what about our Bible students?
Sometimes we take it for granted
that such and such a Bible student is going to be there, and he doesn’t show up.
And later, we learn that he allowed
some trivial matter to interfere with his attendance.
A little extra encouragement won’t hurt.
Now, what about those who used to associate with us but who are inactive?
It seems to me that they fall into two categories.
You have some who would never miss the Memorial;
they appreciate what Christ has done, and they’re there.
And we love them, and we’re so glad to see them.
And then there’s a second group
who may feel that it’s hypocritical on their part
to attend the Memorial because they’ve missed every other meeting during the year.
Well, they have to start somewhere, don’t they?
So we want to give them
loving reassurance and a warm invitation to come.
And don’t forget unbelieving husbands
who might respond better to an invitation from an outsider than from their wife.
Friends, don’t underestimate the value
of a brief visit or a phone call to an inactive person.
Some time ago, on the day of the Memorial,
the visiting speaker and the coordinator of the body of elders
paid a visit to a brother who was inactive.
Now, that brother hadn’t attended a meeting
for 15 years, and yet before that,
he had been very active in the truth.
In fact, he’d enjoyed many privileges in the organization.
What did the brothers do?
They simply listened as the brother relived
the experiences he’d enjoyed when he was active,
and at the end of the conversation,
they simply said: “We’d love to see you at the Memorial.
Won’t you come?”
The brother came.
Now, most in the congregation didn’t know who he was,
but they gave him a warm welcome.
And you know what?
That was all it took.
That brother never looked back.
He was faithful to Jehovah for the rest of his life.
But now what about some of you dear ones
who have been asked to work secularly tonight?
You may be new on the job,
and maybe your boss has the reputation for being a bit inflexible.
You might say, ‘He’d never give me the time off.’
What to do?
Why not approach Jehovah in earnest prayer?
Tell him how you feel.
Ask him to touch the heart of your boss,
and ask him to help you to present your request respectfully
and in an appealing way.
You might be surprised at the outcome.
Jehovah’s servants have always taken the Memorial seriously.
Our brothers and sisters even observed it in concentration camps
and labor camps, such as this one in Mordoviya.
Following that pattern,
in our day, our young brothers who were imprisoned in Korea
didn’t allow prison bars to prevent them from keeping the festival.
In parts of Africa, interested ones may have to travel long distances
to get to the village or the city where the Memorial is going to be observed.
In Tanzania, a Bible student moved
to a remote area where there was no congregation.
The nearest congregation was more than 60 miles (97 km) away.
Now, to those in Western lands, that may not seem like much,
but in the area where he lived,
that was going to require a grueling eight-hour bus trip.
Why?
Number one: The roads were bad.
Number two: The bus made a lot of stops.
But he was there.
And after the meeting,
the man pleaded with the brothers to visit him
at least once a month so he could continue his studies.
Well, that man had put forth an effort to attend the Memorial,
so the congregation had to reciprocate.
And a few weeks later, a special pioneer couple visited him.
To their surprise, they found that the student
was already studying with 17 other people in the village.
How important is it to attend the Memorial?
In Congo, a traveling overseer and his wife
showed great determination to observe it.
They had to travel on a very bad road
to a congregation where the Memorial was going to be observed,
and the road was so bad that the motorcycle they were riding on broke down.
There was a defective part and no replacement available.
So the traveling overseer and his wife were stuck.
They were going to have to observe the Memorial right there,
at an unfamiliar village.
But there was a problem —no congregation and no brothers.
Undeterred, the brother went to the village chief
and explained the importance of the occasion,
and the chief responded.
He allowed the brother to observe the Memorial on his property,
and he even commissioned some young men to clean the place up
and build a platform for the speaker.
So now the location was ready, but you have to have an audience.
Well, the couple had invitations, and these were distributed in the village.
And as a result, 80 villagers attended the Memorial.
Now, of course, what’s a Memorial without music, without songs?
These people were not Witnesses; they didn’t know our songs.
But the traveling overseer’s wife was a good singer,
and so she helped the audience to sing the two Memorial songs.
Speaking of Africa, in Liberia, a congregation of 130
decided that they were going to do everything in their power
to invite many, many people to the Memorial.
So in the days leading up to the Memorial,
eight publishers worked from nine o’clock in the morning
till six o’clock at night distributing invitations.
Now, the Memorial was held in an open field.
And do you know how many attended? a congregation of 130?
Three thousand four hundred and ten.
In many places in Africa, it’s common
for a congregation of a hundred or more
to have an attendance into the thousands.
Well, you might say, ‘All right, that’s Africa,
but in our congregation, we’re not going to have a thousand people.’
But you are going to work just as hard
as our African brothers do,
and Jehovah is going to bless you just the same as he has blessed them.
In addition to inviting interested ones,
there is another thing all of us can do to get ready for the Memorial.
At 1 Corinthians 5:8, Paul wrote in part:
‘So, then, let us keep the festival
with sincerity and truth.’
Now, whether we’re of the anointed or of the great crowd,
all of us should examine ourselves now
to see if we can do more to be pleasing to Jehovah.
Are we holding a grudge against a brother or a sister?
Now would be a good time to let it go.
Are we allowing some bad habit
to hold us back from making spiritual progress?
Now would be an excellent time to take decisive action against it.
“Keep doing this in remembrance of me.”
That’s a command Jehovah’s Witnesses take very seriously.
So our prayer is
that Jehovah will bless your zealous efforts
to invite others to join us.
Now, Bill, will you please read today’s comment
from Examining the Scriptures?
“‘The builders,’ the Jewish leaders, rejected the Messiah.
“Their rejection was far more than just turning their backs on Jesus
“or refusing to accept him as the Christ.
“Many Jews rejected him to the point of clamoring for his death.
“Yes, they contributed to Jesus’ being killed.
“If Jesus was rejected and killed,
“how could he become ‘the chief cornerstone’?
“That could come about only
“by his being resurrected to life again.
“The apostle Peter spoke of ‘Jesus Christ the Nazarene,
“‘whom you executed on a stake
“but whom God raised up from the dead.’
“This resurrected Son thus became the only one
“whose name was ‘given among men
by which we must get saved.’”
Now please follow along as we enjoy today’s recorded Bible reading.
“On the first day of the Unleavened Bread,
“the disciples came to Jesus, saying:
“‘Where do you want us to prepare for you to eat the Passover?’
“He said: ‘Go into the city to So-and-so
“‘and say to him, “The Teacher says:
“‘“My appointed time is near;
“I will celebrate the Passover with my disciples at your home.”’
So the disciples did as Jesus instructed them and prepared for the Passover.”
“The day of the Unleavened Bread now arrived,
“on which the Passover sacrifice must be offered;
“so Jesus sent Peter and John, saying:
“‘Go and get the Passover ready for us to eat.’
“They said to him: ‘Where do you want us to get it ready?’
“He said to them: ‘Look! When you enter into the city,
“‘a man carrying an earthenware water jar will meet you.
“‘Follow him into the house that he enters.
“‘And say to the landlord of the house,
“‘“The Teacher says to you: ‘Where is the guest room
“‘where I may eat the Passover with my disciples?’”
“‘And that man will show you a large, furnished upper room.
“Get it ready there.’
“So they left and found it just as he had told them,
and they prepared for the Passover.”
“When evening came,
“he was reclining at the table with the 12 disciples.
“While they were eating, he said:
“‘Truly I say to you, one of you will betray me.’
“Being very much grieved at this,
“each and every one began to say to him:
“‘Lord, it is not I, is it?’
“In reply he said:
“‘The one who dips his hand with me into the bowl
“‘is the one who will betray me.
“‘True, the Son of man is going away,
“‘just as it is written about him,
“‘but woe to that man through whom the Son of man is betrayed!
“It would have been better for that man if he had not been born.’
“Judas, who was about to betray him, replied:
“‘It is not I, is it, Rabbi?’
“Jesus said to him: ‘You yourself said it.’
“As they continued eating, Jesus took a loaf,
“and after saying a blessing, he broke it,
“and giving it to the disciples, he said:
“‘Take, eat. This means my body.’
“And taking a cup, he offered thanks and gave it to them, saying:
“‘Drink out of it, all of you,
“‘for this means my “blood of the covenant,”
“‘which is to be poured out in behalf of many for forgiveness of sins.
“‘But I say to you: I will by no means drink again
“‘any of this product of the vine until that day
“when I drink it new with you in the Kingdom of my Father.’
“Finally, after singing praises, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
“Then Jesus said to them: ‘All of you will be stumbled
“‘in connection with me on this night, for it is written:
“‘“I will strike the shepherd,
“‘and the sheep of the flock will be scattered about.”
“‘But after I have been raised up,
“I will go ahead of you into Galilee.’
“But Peter, in response, said to him:
“‘Although all the others are stumbled in connection with you, I will never be stumbled!’
“Jesus said to him: ‘Truly I say to you,
“‘on this night, before a rooster crows,
“you will disown me three times.’
“Peter said to him: ‘Even if I should have to die with you,
“I will by no means disown you.’
“All the other disciples also said the same thing.
“Then Jesus came with them to the spot called Gethsemane,
“and he said to the disciples:
“‘Sit down here while I go over there and pray.’
“And taking along Peter and the two sons of Zebʹe·dee,
“he began to feel grieved and to be greatly troubled.
“Then he said to them:
“‘I am deeply grieved, even to death.
“Stay here and keep on the watch with me.’
“And going a little way forward, he fell facedown, praying:
“‘My Father, if it is possible,
“‘let this cup pass away from me.
“Yet, not as I will, but as you will.’
“He returned to the disciples and found them sleeping,
“and he said to Peter:
“‘Could you not so much as keep on the watch for one hour with me?
“‘Keep on the watch and pray continually,
“‘so that you may not enter into temptation.
“The spirit, of course, is eager, but the flesh is weak.’
“Again, a second time, he went off and prayed:
“‘My Father, if it is not possible
“‘for this to pass away unless I drink it,
“let your will take place.’
“And he came again and found them sleeping,
“for their eyes were heavy.
“So leaving them, he again went off and prayed for a third time,
“saying once more the same thing.
“Then he returned to the disciples and said to them:
“‘At such a time as this, you are sleeping and resting!
“‘Look! The hour has drawn near for the Son of man
“‘to be betrayed into the hands of sinners.
“‘Get up, let us go.
“Look! My betrayer has drawn near.’
“While he was still speaking, look! Judas, one of the Twelve, came
“and with him a large crowd with swords and clubs,
“sent from the chief priests and the elders of the people.
“Now his betrayer had given them a sign, saying:
“‘Whoever it is I kiss, he is the one;
“take him into custody.’
“And going straight up to Jesus, he said:
“‘Greetings, Rabbi!’
“and gave him a tender kiss.
“But Jesus said to him:
“‘Fellow, for what purpose are you present?’
“Then they came forward and seized Jesus and took him into custody.
“But look! one of those with Jesus reached out his hand
“and drew his sword and struck the slave
“of the high priest, taking off his ear.
“Then Jesus said to him:
“‘Return your sword to its place,
“‘for all those who take up the sword will perish by the sword.
“‘Or do you think that I cannot appeal to my Father
“‘to supply me at this moment more than 12 legions of angels?
“‘In that case, how would the Scriptures be fulfilled
“that say it must take place this way?’
“In that hour Jesus said to the crowds:
“‘Did you come out to arrest me with swords and clubs as against a robber?
“‘Day after day I used to sit in the temple teaching,
“‘and yet you did not take me into custody.
“‘But all of this has taken place
“for the writings of the prophets to be fulfilled.’
Then all the disciples abandoned him and fled.”
It’s a joy to be associated with you.
And on behalf of the Governing Body,
I’d like to wish all of you a successful day
in Jehovah’s service and a blessed Memorial observance tonight.
Be assured that we love you all very much.
Now, let’s all get busy and see what we can do
to invite as many as possible to the Memorial.

他还在说话
那十二人之一的犹大忽然来了
有一大群人跟着他
是从祭司长和民众的长老那里来的
带着刀剑棍棒
出卖耶稣的人事先给了他们一个暗号，说
“我吻谁，谁就是你们所要的人
你们要拘捕他。”
犹大随即上前来对耶稣说
“老师，你好！”
然后非常亲切地吻他
耶稣对他说
“你这个人来这里做什么？”
于是他们上前，下手拿住耶稣
拘捕了他
不料，跟耶稣同行的人当中
有一个伸手拔剑
向大祭司的奴隶砍去
削掉了他一只耳朵
于是耶稣对那个门徒说
“把剑收回原处！
凡拿剑的，都会死在剑下
难道你以为我不能求我的父亲
立刻给我派十二个军团以上的天使来吗？
要是这样
圣经说事情必然这样发生
又怎能实现呢？”
当时，耶稣对群众说
“你们带着刀剑棍棒出来捉拿我
像捉拿强盗一样吗？
我天天坐在圣殿里教导人
你们却没有拘捕我
可是这一切事发生
是要应验众先知所写的经文。”
那时门徒全都撇下他逃跑了
很开心能够跟大家分享这些经历
中央长老团希望你们今天的传道工作
有很多收获
也希望今晚的纪念聚会能够顺利地举行
我们很想让你们知道
我们非常非常地爱你们
现在
让我们出发
去邀请更多人参加
今晚的耶稣受难纪念聚会吧！
