en.text: Jehovah, the God of love, hates.
That’s quite a statement, isn’t it?
How can that be?
Well, look at the first part of today’s text
at Psalm 97:10:
“O you who love Jehovah, hate what is bad.”
Our God expects us to “hate what is bad” because he does that.
And the reason for this is explained in the first two verses of Psalm 97.
Verse 1 begins: “Jehovah has become King!”
Verse 2 concludes: “Righteousness and justice
are the foundation of his throne.”
And in the Scriptures, righteousness refers to what is right
according to God’s standard of right and wrong.
And here are just a few examples in the Bible
of the things that Jehovah says are wrong and that he hates.
At Psalm 11:5 it says:
“[Jehovah] hates anyone who loves violence.”
At Isaiah 61:8 it says:
“I, Jehovah, . . . hate robbery and unrighteousness.”
At Malachi 2:16 it states:
“‘I hate divorce,’ says Jehovah.”
The context is talking about treacherous, unscriptural divorce.
And then there’s Proverbs chapter 6,
let’s turn in our Bibles to that.
Proverbs the 6th chapter starting with verse 16:
“There are six things that Jehovah hates;
“yes, seven things that he detests:
“Haughty eyes, a lying tongue,
“and hands that shed innocent blood,
“a heart plotting wicked schemes,
“and feet that run quickly to evil,
“a false witness who lies with every breath,
and anyone sowing contentions among brothers.”
So, yes, the God of love hates,
and so does Jesus.
Look at what was said of God’s Son
at Hebrews 1:9.
Hebrews 1:9:
“You loved righteousness, and you hated lawlessness.
“That is why God, your God,
“anointed you with the oil of exultation
more than your companions.”
Well, if we desire Jehovah’s blessing,
then we also must hate what is bad
—that is, have an intense aversion,
a strong abhorrence for what God hates.
And having that godly hate serves as a powerful protection for us
not to get involved in any bad practices.
But exactly what do these include?
Well, we just read in Proverbs
seven categories of hateful things.
They’re basic, but they cover virtually all types of wrongs.
Haughty eyes and wicked schemes are sins committed in thought.
A lying tongue and a false witness are sinful words.
Hands that shed blood and feet that run to evil
and someone who produces contentions among brothers
—why, those are all wicked deeds.
And interestingly, the writer,
when he increased the number of things Jehovah hates from six to seven
—that suggests that this list is not intended to be complete,
because humans keep thinking up bad things.
And as an example, consider the escalating trend toward the use
of more and more explicit sex and graphic violence
that appear today in advertising and entertainment
—from clothing ads to movies.
Now how much of that can we be exposed to
before it affects us mentally and morally?
It makes me think of the five-second rule.
Have you ever heard of that?
It’s the so-called rule that some people say applies
to food that’s dropped on the floor.
That it’s OK to eat it if you pick it up in five seconds or less
because bacteria won’t have time to contaminate it.
But is that really true?
Not according to research done last year at Rutgers University.
It was concluded that no matter how fast you pick up food that falls on the floor,
you will pick up bacteria with it
—sometimes in less than one second.
Of course, the longer the food sits on the floor,
the more bacteria it collects.
So if you eat food dropped on the floor,
you’re taking a chance no matter how long it sat there.
And you should know that a clean-looking floor
is not necessarily clean.
So if food falls on the floor, when in doubt, throw it out.
But how does this relate to our discussion of hating the things that Jehovah hates?
Well, how long does it take for an immoral, violent, or satanic image
to burn a thought into our mind?
Something we see on a billboard, in a magazine,
on television, at a movie, on the Internet
—Is there a five-second rule for this sort of thing?
Should we think that as long as we look at it only briefly,
it will not contaminate us?
Well, let’s use five seconds as an example
and see how long that is, and you can judge for yourselves.
Don’t take your eyes off the screen.
Now, do you think at lunch today you’ll be able to remember that picture,
a delicious looking chocolate ice-cream sundae
with syrup and a cherry on top?
Well, don’t expect to see it on the lunch line.
Now, let’s try four seconds.
What about this image?
Will this cute baby’s face come back to your mind tomorrow? next week?
Now, watch the screen for three seconds.
Will this image stick in your mind?
Next month, next year,
do you think you will be able to remember Jesus on a white horse,
riding off to the battle of Armageddon?
Now, you saw each picture for only a few seconds,
and yet scientists say the human brain
can process images in even less time
—in a split second, in the blink of an eye.
So think how much processing our brain can do
in several seconds or minutes or longer.
Now, the pictures we just looked at were all wholesome images.
But what if there had been a pornographic picture from the Internet?
a sexually explicit or graphically violent scene from a movie?
or some spiritistic gore in a video game?
If we gaze at something that Jehovah hates,
we’re taking a chance —no matter how long we look at it—
and that graphic image can come back to mind
again and again to haunt us.
Now, we may not be able to avoid all of this 100 percent
because of the wicked world that surrounds us,
but we certainly don’t have to linger in looking at these things,
and we do not want to seek them out.
And we need to realize that what we might think is a clean movie
is not necessarily clean.
So like food that has fallen on the floor,
when in doubt, we throw it out.
So we need to detest the immorality, the violence,
the spiritistic practices of Satan’s world.
In other words, hate every practice
that violates Jehovah’s righteous standards.
Now, even if we hate what is bad,
we may struggle because we live in a world that caters to the flesh,
and we have our own sinful nature to control.
So how do we develop the needed hatred for what is bad?
First, we strengthen our desire
to please Jehovah in everything we do.
Then, we meditate on what it is that he loves
and what it is that he hates.
And finally, we convince ourselves of the badness of the things that he hates
by considering how disgusting the results are
for those who practice them.
And one more thing, if we struggle with this,
then we pray earnestly to Jehovah
to help us strengthen our powers of self-control.
Well, you can be sure that as our day’s text, Psalm 97:10,
says of those who imitate Jehovah and hate what is bad:
“He is guarding the lives of his loyal ones,
[and] he rescues them from the hand of the wicked.”

cn.text: 上帝就是爱
但是他却憎恨某些事
这听起来是不是有点矛盾呢？
我们来看看诗篇97:10的前半部分
“爱耶和华的人啊，你们要憎恨恶事。”
上帝希望我们像他一样“憎恨恶事”
为什么呢？
诗篇97:1,2告诉了我们原因
1节说:“耶和华作王了！”
2节说:“正义和公正是他宝座的基础。”
经文说的正义指的就是
按照上帝制定的是非标准做对的事
在圣经中，有哪些事情耶和华说是错的
是他憎恨的呢？
我们看几个例子
诗篇11:5说
“凡喜爱暴力的人，〔耶和华〕必恨恶。”
以赛亚书61:8说
“我耶和华......恨恶抢劫和不义。”
玛拉基书2:16说
“上帝憎恨离婚。”
这节经文的上下文主要谈论的是
有些人因为诡诈背信
没有圣经认可的理由就离婚
箴言6章，请大家翻到第6章
我们从16节读到19节
“耶和华恨恶的有六项
他视为可憎的有七样
就是高傲的眼、说谎的舌
使无辜人丧命流血的手
图谋恶计的心、飞跑作恶的脚
吐谎言的假见证
以及在弟兄中散播纷争的人。”
没错，充满爱心的上帝憎恨恶事
耶稣也一样
谈到上帝的儿子
希伯来书1:9怎么说呢？
希伯来书1:9说
“你喜爱正义，恨恶不法
所以上帝，就是你的上帝，膏立了你
让你领受欢欣的膏油
胜过膏立与你位分相同的人。”
因此，想要得到上帝的赐福
我们就必须憎恨恶事，也就是恨上帝所恨
这是一种强烈的情感
我们恨上帝所恨就不会做上帝恨恶的事
这也会保护我们
这里说的恶事具体包括什么呢？
我们之前读的经文
箴言第6章提到了七种可憎的事
看上去可能不多
却包含了几乎各种方面的恶事
比如:高傲的眼和图谋恶计跟思想有关
说谎的舌和假见证与言谈有关
使无辜人丧命流血的手、飞跑做恶的脚
在弟兄中散播纷争的人
这些都与行为有关
箴言第6章的执笔者把耶和华憎恨的恶事
从六项增加到七样
这可能表明人所行的恶事不只这些
还会增加，因为人总能找到别的恶事去做
举例来说，今天有越来越多的色情画面
以及逼真的暴力镜头
出现在广告和娱乐当中
时尚广告或者电影里就有这样的画面
不难想象
这对我们的思想和道德
造成多么大的影响
大家听说过“5秒钟原则”的说法吗？
有人认为如果食物掉在地上
不超过5秒钟,就还能吃
因为他们觉得食物还没有被污染
但事实真的是这样吗？
罗格斯大学去年做的研究
却显示了不同的结果
研究结果显示
不管你捡起来的速度有多快
食物一旦接触到地面就有细菌了
哪怕不到1秒钟
当然，食物留在地面的时间越长
细菌就会越多
所以，只要你吃了掉在地上的食物
不管掉在地上多久
都可能会对你的健康有害
要知道地面看起来干净不一定就真的干净
因此，如果你不确定掉在地上的食物
该不该吃
最好别吃
这个例子与耶和华憎恨恶事
又有什么关系呢？
要让色情、暴力
通灵术的画面印在我们脑海里
你觉得需要花多长时间呢？
现在，我们很容易在广告牌
杂志、电视、电影
网络接触到这样的画面
那么5秒钟原则在这方面也适用吗？
我们该不该认为只是稍微看一眼
也不会受到什么不良的影响呢？
接下来，我们用5秒钟原则来做个实验
然后自己判断一下
请看屏幕，不要转移视线
你觉得今天中午吃饭的时候
还能记得这个画面吗？
美味可口的巧克力冰淇淋上点缀着一个樱桃
大家别想太多，我们今天中午可吃不到这个
我们用4秒钟来看看下面这个图片
这个小朋友可爱的脸
你明天还能记得吗？
下周呢？
我们再来看看这个画面3秒钟
这个画面又会在你的脑海里多久呢？
到下个月，明年，你还能记得这个画面吗？
耶稣骑着白马投入到哈米吉多顿大战中
我们只用了几秒钟就记住了这些图片
但科学家说人脑处理画面的速度其实更快
可以在瞬间储存画面
如果花更长时间注视某个画面
我们的大脑又会受到多大的影响呢？
刚才看的都是比较健康的图片
但是如果我们浏览的是网上的色情图片呢？
或者观看的是电影里露骨、血腥的镜头呢？
又或者玩的是魔法题材的电子游戏呢？
如果我们观看耶和华憎恨的内容
就是在冒险
不管看多久，那个画面都会
一直留在我们的脑海里，反复出现
我们不可能完全避开这些资讯
毕竟我们生活在撒但的世界里
但我们可以选择转移视线
不要盯着这些东西看
也不该主动找这些东西看
要记得，我们认为没有问题的电影
不一定就真的没有问题
如果我们不确定某部电影该不该看
就最好不要看
好像我们不吃掉在地上的食物一样
我们要憎恨撒但世界的所有恶事
比如性不道德、暴力、通灵术等等
换句话说，我们要憎恨
所有违反上帝正义标准的事
虽然我们知道要憎恨恶事
但还需要付出一番努力才行，为什么呢？
因为这个世界要我们一心满足自己的欲望
此外，我们还要跟不完美的身心搏斗
我们怎样才能真正做到憎恨恶事呢？
首先，无论做任何事
我们要下定决心让耶和华高兴
第二，我们要沉思哪些是上帝所爱
哪些是上帝所恨的
第三，我们要清楚明白
为什么耶和华憎恨这些恶事
也要想想做这些恶事会带来哪些后果
最后，我们还要衷心地向耶和华祷告
求他赐我们力量，帮助我们保持自制
如果我们这样做
就是在效法耶和华恨他所恨
他通过诗篇97:10提出保证说
“上帝守护他忠贞子民的性命
解救他们脱离恶人的毒手。”

ko.text: 둘째 딸 벨렌이 한 3살쯤 됐을 때
병원에서 검사를 받다가 뇌에 종양이 있다는 걸 알게 됐어요.
아이 상태가 점점 더 나빠져 갔기 때문에,
전 아버지로서 어떤 치료를 받는 게 아이에게 가장 좋을지
마치 제 앞에 골리앗이 서 있는 것 같았어요.
속으로 여호와께 얼마나 간절히 애원했는지 몰라요.
우리 힘만으로는 이겨 낼 수 없다는 걸 깨달았어요.
그 어느 때보다도 여호와의 도움이 절실히 필요했죠.
우리 가족은 영적인 활동을 꾸준히 해 나갔어요.
그런 상황에서도 두려움에 압도되지 않을 수 있었던 건
아내와 전 우리 딸들을 사랑에 찬 방식으로 가르치고,
벨렌은 정말 힘든 상황에서도 저한테 이렇게 말하곤 했죠.
우리 딸이 여호와를 실재하는 분으로 믿는다는 걸
그렇게 저를 격려해 줬던 때가 한두 번이 아니었어요.
전 우리 딸이 승리한 거라고 생각해요.
신세계에서 다시 눈을 뜨게 될 거고
우리 가족은 다시 함께하게 될 거니까요.

en.text: When our little daughter, Belen, was nearly three years old,
the doctors discovered that she had a brain tumor.
When her physical condition worsened,
as a father, I had to make decisions
on what kind of treatment she would receive to best take care of her.
And that completely terrified me.
It was like having Goliath
in front of me, and I felt desperate for a moment.
I remember that inside
I shouted to Jehovah to help me.
Through that situation,
I learned how to pray to Jehovah,
and Jehovah never left me.
Jehovah guided me.
Jehovah helped me make good decisions.
Only through prayer
did I understand
that what we were facing was too much for us to handle alone.
We needed Jehovah
more than ever.
As a family, we focused on our spiritual routine.
The key to not being afraid of these problems
is to trust in the resurrection hope.
My wife and I were determined to educate our girls with love
and also in a way that they would truly
get to know Jehovah as they grew up.
It was evident that we were leaning on Jehovah,
and they did the same.
Belen, when she was going through difficult circumstances,
she would say to me: “Don’t worry, Mom.
I prayed to Jehovah already!”
It made me see that, OK,
my daughter is seeing Jehovah as so real.
There were many moments where she strengthened me.
And even though it’s true that Belen fell asleep in death,
for me she came out victorious
because I know she’s going
to open her eyes in the new world,
and the four of us will be together again.

cn.text: 我们的小女儿贝伦
快要三岁的时候
医生诊断出她的脑部长了肿瘤
看到女儿的情况越来越糟
我是她的爸爸
我得做决定
到底怎样的疗法对她来说才是最好的
老实说，我自己也很害怕
难题就好像巨大的歌利亚一样在我面前
那时候我真的很绝望、很无助
我在心里大叫
耶和华啊！
求你帮帮我
那段时间
我体会到怎么祷告倚靠耶和华
而耶和华也从没离开我
他一直指引我
帮助我做正确的决定
祷告让我清楚知道
我们面对的情况
不是凭自己的能力可以应付的
现在我们比以前更需要耶和华
我们一家人更专注于属灵的活动
我们可以勇敢面对这些难题的关键是
坚信复活的希望一定会实现
我跟妻子都下定决心
要怀着爱心教导女儿
帮助她们在成长的过程
跟耶和华成为好朋友
我发现，只要我们信赖上帝
孩子也会照样做
有时候贝伦的身体很不舒服
但是她会说
“妈咪，别担心
我已经跟耶和华祷告了”
这让我很放心
我告诉自己
女儿把上帝看得多么真实啊！
很多时候其实是女儿鼓励了我呢！
虽然贝伦已经在死亡中沉睡了
但我相信
她一定会得到奖赏
在新世界
她会再次张开双眼活过来
到时，我们一家四口就能重聚了

titles.cn: 做一个勇敢的家长

ko.text: 이런 곳에서 내가 정말 잘 지낼 수 있을까 걱정이 됐어요.
얼마 안 지나서 작은 방을 하나 구했어요.
또 청소하는 일을 구했는데, 생활비를 벌기엔 좀 부족했죠.
제가 일하는 곳은 멀리 떨어져 있었어요.
몸이 항상 피곤했고 그러면서 봉사에 집중하기도 어려워졌어요.
여기 오기 전에 모아 둔 돈이 좀 있었는데,
그러다 우연히 구인 광고를 보게 됐어요.
한 시간 반 만에 전화가 와서 면접을 보기로 했어요.
제가 살 만한 아파트를 찾았다고 알려 줬어요.
아담하고 아늑한 제 집이 갑자기 생긴 거예요.
이렇게 해서 모든 게 잘 해결됐어요.
이젠 봉사와 회중 활동에 더 집중할 수 있게 됐죠.
우리가 그분을 시험해 본다면 우리의 노력을 축복하실 거예요.
여호와의 손에 제 삶을 맡기니까 마음이 편안해요.

en.text: After attending the School for Kingdom Evangelizers, I received an assignment
in another part of the country.
It is an area where it is costly to live, and the living expenses are high.
I was worried about how it would turn out
and if I could manage.
Not too long thereafter, I found a small room I could rent.
The housing conditions were not ideal, but it was OK.
I also received a small cleaning job,
but it was not quite enough for me to make ends meet.
I had to travel a long distance to get to work.
I was tired constantly,
so it was difficult to keep my focus on the ministry.
I had some savings when I moved, but it started to shrink.
My funds slowly dwindled.
By coincidence, I saw a job advertisement.
I handed in an application,
and one and a half hours later, they called me in for an interview.
They felt bad because they could only offer me a part-time position.
To compensate, they offered me a higher salary, which I didn’t object to.
At the same time that I found a job, a couple came to me in the Kingdom Hall
and said that they had found an apartment for me.
So in a city where it is very difficult to find a place to live,
I suddenly had a small and cozy apartment.
Now everything has come together.
This means that I can focus on my ministry
and the congregation.
Jehovah knows just what we need.
And when we test him out,
he will bless our efforts.
I really feel safe leaving my life in his hands.

cn.text: 我从王国传福音者训练班毕业后
被委派到国内的另一个城市
那个地方物价比较高
生活费也很贵
我很担心之后会怎么样
不知道能不能应付那里的生活
不久，我就租到一个小房间
房子的情况不是很好
但还过得去
我找到一份打扫的工作
但薪水不多，没办法应付整个月的开销
而且我工作的地方距离很远
这让我常常很累
所以很难专注在传道工作上
我搬来时还有点存款
但现在要动用这笔钱了
我的存款越来越少
后来，我突然看到一个招聘广告
我亲自把履历表交给他们
一个半小时后
公司就打电话说要面试
公司很不好意思地说
他们只能给我兼职的工作
为了补偿我
他们会给我高一点的薪水
我当然不会反对啦！
就在我找到工作的时候
有对夫妻在聚会所告诉我
他们找到一个很适合我的公寓
结果，在这么难找房子的城市里
我突然有了一个温暖的小天地
现在我需要的都有了
我可以专注在会众和传道工作上了！
我们的需要耶和华都知道
我们试试他
他就会赐福给我们
我把一生交给耶和华
真的很有安全感！

titles.cn: 做一个勇敢的先驱

ko.text: 우리 가족에게 이런 일이 생길 줄은 몰랐습니다.
어느 날 퇴근하고 돌아온 아들이 자기가 죄를 지었다고 말하더군요.
우리 애가 그럴 거라고는 정말 생각도 못했거든요.
여호와를 더 사랑해야 한다는 걸 잘 알고 있었습니다.
그래서 영적인 도움을 받아야 한다고 말해 줄 수 있었죠.
다 털어놓고 여호와의 도움을 받으라고 했습니다.
이 일로 우리 가족이 큰 상처를 받을 걸 알았으니까요.
시간이 지나 저는 다시 장로로 일하게 되었습니다.
마음을 다해 여호와를 섬기고 있어서 정말 기쁩니다.
여호와의 마음을 기쁘게 해 드리는 거죠.
우리 가족이 받은 많은 축복을 생각해 보면
어려움을 이겨 낸 보람이 있다는 생각이 듭니다.
우리 가족은 행복하게 여호와를 섬기고 있습니다.
이렇게 그분을 섬길 수 있다는 건 정말 큰 축복이죠.
옳은 일을 하기 위해 용기를 내야 합니다.
여호와께선 그런 상황을 잘 알고 계시고 모든 걸 보고 계시죠.
우리는 여호와의 이름을 반드시 옹호해야 합니다.
사탄이 그 이름에 도전을 제기하고 있으니까요.

en.text: As a father, I never expected this to happen to my family.
One day, my son came home from work and told me that he had committed a sin.
I asked him if it was serious, and he said that it was.
When my son confessed,
I felt incredibly sad —this deep pain—
because I really wasn’t expecting this from him.
I was very aware that the greatest love we should have should be for Jehovah,
and that gave me the strength to encourage him to seek spiritual assistance.
I said that the wise thing for him to do
would be to seek Jehovah’s help through the elders, to talk to them about it.
Regardless of what would happen to my privileges,
I knew there would be other consequences.
I knew that no matter what, this was going to hurt my family.
Later, I regained my privileges.
As a father,
I am extremely happy to see my son serving Jehovah
wholeheartedly alongside his wife, who’s a pioneer.
What matters most for us as humans
is to make Jehovah’s heart rejoice.
And we’ve been richly blessed,
and that means that all that we went through was worth the effort.
We’re happy.
We’re glad to be serving Jehovah,
and he has blessed us with wonderful privileges of service.
As elders, we need to be courageous
to stand up to difficult situations, knowing what is right.
We know that Jehovah is aware and that he sees everything.
We need to protect Jehovah’s name,
which is so important because of Satan’s challenge against it.

en.text: I first learned about the Bible
from a friend in my second year of high school.
I became convinced that the Bible’s record
of Jehovah God’s existence was the truth.
So I decided I wanted to serve him
for the rest of my life and decided not to go to college.
My family was very angry with my decision,
especially my uncle who was a doctor.
He burned my clothes and my identification card,
and then he beat me for many hours.
I had no choice but to run away.
I ended up in a city far away,
where I was able to find a Kingdom Hall.
The brothers and sisters there showed me warm hospitality.
I got baptized that year when I was 19.
In January of 1971, my wife and I were assigned to the circuit work
—and we were enjoying it—
when unexpectedly my wife became seriously ill.
She had to receive immediate medical attention.
Eventually, because of her condition,
we had to discontinue our service for a time.
We are so grateful to Jehovah, who supported us in ways
beyond our imagination during that difficult time.
In March 2015,
because of low blood pressure,
I fell and hit my head in the parking lot of our apartment.
Since we have no children, some might wonder who came to our aid.
But when we arrived at the emergency room,
brothers from many congregations were already there waiting for us
even before our ambulance arrived.
We are still truly grateful for their support.
We are convinced that Jehovah
has always been with us these past decades.
And we are certain
that no matter what the situation, he will always protect us
and guide us through any tribulation,
any hardship, or any difficulty that may arise.

en.text: Kind and patient, perfect in love,
Was Christ, who came down from above.
He took care of our needs With words and by deeds;
He gave of his time and his love.
He would keep the lowly in mind
By healing the sick, deaf, and blind.
To his royal commission he proved true
And willingly said: “I want to.”
We now try to follow his way
In all of our dealings each day.
We are loving and kind To all whom we find;
We help them to learn and obey.
We respond to friends when in need;
We love them in word and in deed.
So if widows and orphans should ask you,
Then readily say: “I want to.”

title: 큰 골프 대회가 열린 곳에서 공개 증거를 하다

ko.text: 이 도시에서 골프 선수권 대회가 있어요.
전 세계에서 온 사람들에게 증거하게 되어 가슴이 설렙니다.
샬럿에서 이렇게 큰 스포츠 경기가 열린 건 처음이었죠.
총 예상 방문객 수는 약 20만 명이었습니다.
특별 공개 증거 마련이 있을 거란 소식을 들었는데,
우린 가능한 한 많은 사람에게 전파하기 위해 최선을 다하고 싶었죠.
목표는 jw.org와 여호와와 왕국을 광고하는 것이었죠.
전시대를 볼 수 있는 장소들을 물색했습니다.
또 큰 스포츠 경기 때 공개 증거를 조직한
그 형제들은 경험을 통해 얻은 유용한 정보들을
한 프로젝트를 위해 이렇게 함께 일한 건 처음이었습니다.
조직과 계획이 중요했는데, 다들 정말 멋지게 해냈어요.
공개 증거를 할 때, 사람들이 우리의 미소 띤 얼굴을 보고
한 자매는 미소를 지으니까 사람들이 다가왔다고 했는데,
증인들의 미소가 행복하고 즐거운 삶을 바라는 사람들을
정말 그 답을 찾기를 원하는 사람은 다가오죠.
차들이 지나가면서 우릴 보는 경우가 있는데,
금방 지나가더라도, 전시대와 jw.org 표시는 볼 겁니다.
우크라이나 남부에서 왔는데 이게 다 뭔지 알고 싶어 했죠.
어떻게 읽을 수 있는지 알려 줬어요.
전시대와 우리 활동에 대해 러시아어로 설명해 줬습니다.
이 활동은 우리에게도 큰 격려가 됐어요.
한 자매는 “이젠 단지 출판물을 전한 수가 아니라,
우리에게 미소를 지었는지를 중요하게 보게” 됐다고 했죠.
이 활동으로 더 많은 형제 자매들이 공개 증거를 좋아하게 됐습니다.
그동안 달리 만날 수가 없던 사람들을
공개 증거를 통해 만날 기회를 얻었습니다.
우리 웹사이트를 전혀 모르는 많은 분들과 얘길 나눴어요.
많은 사람이 공개 증거 전시대를 보고
처음으로 생명을 구하는 소식을 들을 기회를 얻게 되죠.
활동이 끝나고 놀라운 성과를 거두었단 걸 알게 됐습니다.
이 공개 증거 활동은 지역 사회에도 좋은 증거가 되었습니다.
이 특별 활동을 통해 세계 각지의 방문객들에게

en.text: The city is hosting a golf championship,
and we are so excited to reach out to all of these international visitors.
This was the first time in Charlotte
that we had such a major sporting event.
People would be coming from some 60 countries.
A total of some 200,000 were expected.
And so when the branch contacted us
and said this was a special public witnessing initiative,
we knew that we wanted to do our very best to reach as many of those people as possible.
It was about advertising jw.org®, Jehovah, and the Kingdom.
And so we were looking at what would give the greatest visibility
to the cart and our effort.
The branch office was very, very supportive.
They gave us good direction, they put us in touch with brothers
that had been involved in organizing a public witnessing initiative
for another large sports event, and they provided us
with so much insight from their experience.
This was the first time that some 5 circuits,
75 congregations, and multiple language groups
got a chance to work on one project together.
We ended up with 48 locations
and some 1,400 publishers trained to man these locations.
We were running shifts from six o’clock in the morning until eight o’clock at night.
Organization and scheduling was the key, and they did it beautifully.
With public witnessing,
individuals often come to us
because they see our smiling faces.
We try to maintain a friendly disposition —a happy one.
We always try to make eye contact, and if it’s morning,
we greet them with a “Good morning.”
One sister said that she “smiled” people over to the cart,
and that’s really what a smile can do.
They’re looking for something to make them happy
—to enjoy life— and you represent that just by smiling.
When they see a topic that catches their attention,
internally, they’re asking themselves these questions.
If they really want to find the answers, they’ll come over.
You can see as cars pass by
that they’re taking note of our presence,
and it’s a witness in itself.
We’ve had individuals stop their cars
and wave us over to bring the literature to them.
They might just turn briefly, but they’ll see the cart; they’ll see jw.org®.
We talked to people from all over the world.
A man came by; he was from the southern part of Ukraine.
He wanted to know, “What is this all about?”
So I explained the Bible educational work.
I explained how, at the website, he can read literature online in his language.
He was quite impressed.
And then he brought his friend over, who was visiting from Kazakhstan,
and in Russian explained what the cart was all about and what we were doing there.
This work has had a really invigorating effect.
One sister said, “Now I no longer think simply in terms of literature placement;
I think in terms of looks and smiles.”
It’s identified brothers and sisters who are now excited
about doing public witnessing.
We are getting an opportunity through public witnessing to reach people
who we hadn’t reached any other way.
We got to talk to so many people about our website
who otherwise would have never known about it.
It’s really that life-saving message
that they’re getting the opportunity to see,
perhaps for the first time, when they see these public witnessing carts.
When it was all said and done,
this was an outstanding success.
This public witnessing campaign
had such a positive effect upon the community.
Through this special effort, we were able to show
true hospitality to these visitors from all over the world.
After the excitement and seeing the productivity of this work,
many were commenting, “Hey, when are we going to do this again?”
The final result was a witness beyond anything
we could have imagined at the very outset.

en.text: In 1998, I started dating a girl, and we dated for two years.
During that time, I also started studying the Bible.
Our relationship was going well.
We didn’t have any big issues; we got along well; we rarely argued.
So, then, how do you go to someone when you’re dating
and everything is going well and say:
“Listen, I can see you don’t feel the same as I do.
“I don’t want to date you anymore because now I’m studying the Bible.
I want to be one of Jehovah’s Witnesses”?
I really had to muster up a lot of courage
to tell her that.
But there are moments when you start to ask yourself,
‘Did I really make the right decision?’
And up to around the time when I got baptized,
I was still hoping that she would learn the truth.
But, unfortunately, that didn’t happen.
I was also involved in something else that I really loved, which was sports.
When I was younger, I was part of the track and field team,
and I participated in many local 5K and 10K competitions.
Some who trained with me at the time went on to become professional athletes.
Some even competed in the Olympics.
I knew I had a decision to make.
It wouldn’t be possible for me to keep training for track and field
while trying to serve Jehovah.
So I had to have enough courage to speak to my coach.
And after that, I gave up being an athlete.
Looking back now, it wasn’t easy to leave those things behind,
but what Jehovah has given me today
is much more valuable than anything I gave up.
I have the privilege of serving
in Bethel together with my wife, who also gives her all in Jehovah’s service.
I can honestly say that I am
truly happy serving Jehovah with all my heart.

cn.text: 我跟一个女生开始约会
我们交往两年
那时候我也开始学习圣经
我们的感情还不错
没有什么大问题，相处地很好
我们也很少吵架
唉，感情这么顺利的时候
你要怎么跟你女朋友说
“你知道吗？
我们的想法不一样
但我想学习圣经，做一个耶和华见证人
我们分手吧！”
我真的鼓起了很大的勇气才跟她分手
分手后，我常常想
“跟她分手是对的吗？”
一直到我受浸时
我都希望她会学习圣经
但很可惜，她还是没有接受！
还有一件我很热爱的事就是运动
我年轻时是个田径选手
常常参加5公里、10公里的国内长跑比赛
当时有些跟我一起受训的人
后来都成为职业选手
有的还参加奥运比赛
但我不可能一边接受田径训练
一边事奉耶和华
所以我必须做一个选择
我终于鼓起勇气跟教练说
最后我放弃了做运动员的梦想
现在回想
当时要放弃这些东西真的不容易
但耶和华现在给我的
比我当时放弃的更好！
我和妻子一起在伯特利服务
她也努力把最好的献给耶和华
能全心事奉耶和华真的非常快乐！

titles.cn: 做一个勇敢的圣经学生

ko.text: 성경 지식이나 경험이 많은 분들만 하시는 거라고 생각했었어요.
전 아직 어려서 못 할 거란 생각이 들었죠.
한 달도 안 돼서 승인 편지가 온 거예요.
막상 편지를 받으니까 겁이 나고 불안했어요.
“여호와 하느님, 전 못 할 것 같아요” 하고 기도했죠.
이런 마음을 가지고는 대도시 공개 증거를 못 할 것 같아서
기도를 하고 도움이 될 만한 자료를 찾아봤죠.
거기서는 우리가 어떤 임명을 수행할 자신이 없을 때에도
여호와의 능력에 의지하면 해낼 수 있다고 했어요.
‘자신이 보기엔 할 수 없을 것 같은 일도
여호와께서 능력을 주시면 해낼 수 있다’고 했죠.
처음엔 할 수 없다고 생각한 일을 해내게 도와주셨어요.
여호와께서 성경을 진심으로 알아보고 싶어 하는 사람들을
성경 공부를 신청하는 걸 알려 줄 때도 종종 있고요.
이 봉사를 하면서 영적으로 많이 발전한 걸 느껴요.
여호와께서 상상도 못한 큰 기쁨을 주셨어요.

en.text: I thought that only those with an abundance
of mature knowledge and experience did special metropolitan public witnessing.
I thought: ‘I can’t do it; I’m too young.’
Still, I decided to send in the application.
I received the invitation in the mail within a month.
I suddenly felt really insecure and afraid.
So I prayed to Jehovah, “I can’t do this yet.”
I thought I wouldn’t be able to participate in this type of service feeling that way,
so I prayerfully did research to find some material that would help me.
I found an article about Moses.
It was an article that stressed
that even if we think we aren’t able to carry out an assignment,
with Jehovah’s power we can.
I also heard a talk that used Jeremiah 20:7.
I was encouraged when he said,
“Even though you might feel you can’t do something,
if Jehovah gives you the power to do it,
then you can do it.”
Actually, Jehovah saw my potential
and gave me the courage to perform this service,
even though I thought it was beyond my ability.
I am being shown time and time again that Jehovah draws people
who are sincerely interested in the Bible to the carts.
I’ve even experienced helping people
make a request for a Bible study by using my smartphone.
I’m really able to grow, thanks to this ministry,
and gain more joy from Jehovah than I ever thought possible.

cn.text: 我原本以为能做都市公众场所特别见证的人
一定要有很多圣经知识和经验
我想
“我没办法做，我太年轻了！”
不过……我还是交了申请表
不到一个月
我就收到邀请函了
我突然感到很害怕
不知如何是好
只好跟上帝祷告说
“我现在能力还不够！”
我觉得自己真的没有能力参与这种传道
所以我祷告，也找了一些相关的资料
我找到一篇跟摩西有关的文章
文章说如果我们收到某个委派
觉得自己无法胜任
耶和华也会让我们有能力去完成这项委派
我还听到一个演讲提到耶利米书20:7
我受到很大的鼓励
讲者说
“就算你觉得自己没办法做某件事
只要耶和华给你力量，你就能够做到。”
虽然我觉得自己的能力不够
但耶和华看到了我的潜力
也给我勇气做都市见证
后来好多次的经历都让我看出
耶和华真的会把对圣经感兴趣的人吸引过来
我甚至曾经用手机
教人在网站上报名学习圣经呢
我越来越感激耶和华
感谢他让我从这样的见证工作获得喜乐
这真是我原本想象不到的

titles.cn: 做一个勇敢的传道员

ko.text: 학교는 우리가 좋은 일이든 나쁜 일이든
앞으로 겪을 일들에 대비하는 데 도움이 됐죠.
그러다 얼마 후에 LDC 봉사에 초대를 받았습니다.
그러다 나중엔 왕국회관과 관련된 일을 주로 하게 됐죠.
각 주마다 현장 대표자 부부가 임명됐는데,
어느 일요일 저녁에 식사 초대에 갔다 와서 잠자리에 들었어요.
남편을 보니까 뭔가 이상한 거 같아서
우린 잘 적응했고 임명을 계속 수행할 수 있었어요.
나중엔 보행기를 썼고 그 후엔 지팡이를 사용했어요.
아내는 그 누구보다도 정신력이 강한 사람이에요.
그 상황이 얼마나 큰 어려움을 주든,
그 어려움을 헤쳐 나갈 줄 아는 사람이죠.

en.text: My husband did not recognize me for three days.
It was a very dark time.
We went to BSCC, Bible School for Christian Couples,
in January of 2014.
It definitely helped prepare us
for everything that would come our way
—the good and the bad.
We were assigned to Jackson, Alabama.
It was a great assignment.
Within a very short time, we were asked to apply for LDC.
We traveled quite a bit, looking at different Assembly Halls,
and then the focus went more toward Kingdom Halls.
Each field rep couple was assigned a state,
and we were assigned the state of Louisiana.
On a Sunday night, we had been invited to a dinner party.
Just a normal— We went to bed at night.
We basically woke up to a stroke.
I walked over to him,
and I could see that something was wrong, and so I called 911.
Once they assessed him, they brought me in.
They told me that they needed to Life Flight him
to a larger hospital in New Orleans.
Thankfully, though, they said that if you’re going to have a stroke,
this was the kind you’d want to have
because it is fully recoverable.
We made adjustments.
We adapted so that we could continue in the assignment.
Well, he went from being in a wheelchair
to using a walker.
And then later, he started using a cane,
and now he walks without assistance.
It’s not a pretty walk, but we’re working on that.
She really has a durability
that I think excels all.
Just the way that she
—no matter what the situation, how stressful the circumstance may be—
she understands it’s necessary for her to continue forward.

cn.text: 我丈夫有整整三天都认不出我是谁
这打击真的很大！
我们参加了基督徒夫妇圣经研习班
研习班装备我们应付之后发生的事
不论是好事还是坏事
后来我们被派到阿拉巴马的杰克逊
我们很喜欢这个委派
不久，我们也受邀申请LDC
我们去了很多地方检查大会堂
之后重心就转向检查王国聚会所
在美国
每一州都会派一对夫妻做地区建筑代表
我们就被派到路易斯安那州
一个星期天晚上
有人邀请我们去吃晚餐
一切都跟平常一样
我们回家然后睡觉
半夜我丈夫很不对劲
我醒来发现他中风了
我就赶快打电话给911
医生检查后跟我说
现在他们必须叫直升机
送他到新奥尔良市的大医院才行
还好，医生说他中风的情况是可以复原的
真是不幸中的大幸
我们做了一些调整
这样就可以继续为上帝工作
我丈夫刚开始需要坐轮椅
后来就改用助行器
慢慢地，他可以拿着拐杖走
现在他走路不用拿任何东西了
当然，还不是走得很帅
但我们还在努力
她真的表现了很大的耐心
她就是这样的人
不管在什么情况下
也不管压力有多大
她都会表现勇气忍耐下去
绝对不会放弃

titles.cn: 做一个勇敢的配偶

ko.text: 조금만 기다려요. 근데, 좋은 게 생겼어.
직장에서 주말에 열리는 경기 티켓을 줬는데,
우리 부부도 안 가 본 지 오래고,
애들은 한 번도 안 가 봤을 거에요.
국가 부를 때는 우리 어떻게 해요?
딸아이 선생님들과 갖는 모임이 그 다음 주라,
음, 내일 저녁이 가족 숭배 날이니까,
공공 행사에서 어떻게 그리스도인 중립을 지킬지
중립에 대한 그리스도인 원칙을 조사하게 했어요.
압력 가운데서도 충성을 지킨 사람들의 예를 찾아봤죠.
그리고 전 엘리자베스의 새 학교에 전화해서
국기 경례를 하거나 국가를 부르는지 알아봤습니다.
아이들이 어렸을 때 이 주제를 연구했지만,
새로운 상황에 맞춰 다시 살펴볼 필요가 있었죠.
사람이나 사물을 숭배하는 일에 참여하는 것이죠.
어떻게 할지 결정하는 데 도움이 된 게 있어요.
엘리자베스가 본이 되는 좋은 예들을 찾았는데,
사드락, 메삭, 아벳느고에 관한 기록이 인상 깊었죠.
느부갓네살 왕이 금 형상을 숭배하라고 명령했을 때
그들은 다른 사람들을 따라 절하지 않고
전쟁 중에 정부가 애국 의식에 참여하라고 강요했지만,
애국심이 한껏 고취돼 있던 그 시기에도
우린 상황에 따라 대처 방법이 다를 수 있다는 걸 배웠어요.
무엇을 애국 의식에 참여하는 걸로 보는지에 따라 다르죠.
그들이 존중심을 갖지만 참여하진 않는다는 걸
우리 가족은 존중심을 보이면서도 중립을 지키고
우리가 오직 여호와만 섬긴다는 걸 나타내기로 결정해서

en.text: Collette, I’m home.
In the kitchen, Curtis.
How was your day?
Oh, it was a long day, but it’s nice being home.
That smells amazing! I can’t wait.
Oh, well, it will be ready in a few minutes.
But I have a surprise;
my job gave us tickets to the game this weekend
—enough for all of us to go.
So it’s downtown at the . . .
That sounded like fun.
It was a sport we could enjoy watching.
Collette and I hadn’t been in years,
and I don’t think the kids had ever gone.
We were all looking forward to a family night out.
But, Dad, what exactly do we do during the national anthem?
Honestly, I wasn’t sure.
Ladies and gentlemen,
would you please stand for the singing
of our national anthem?
Dad, I have a question too.
Will they salute the flag at my new school?
That’s right.
The conference with her teachers was next week,
and we didn’t know what they’d do there.
OK, class. Now that everyone is here,
let’s all stand for the pledge of allegiance.
Elizabeth, is everything all right?
What do you think, Honey?
Well, tomorrow night is our Family Worship evening.
So why don’t we do a study project as a family
on Christian neutrality at public events?
That sounds like a good idea.
Yeah.
I think this will be great. We’ll all get a chance to do our research.
I asked Daniel to research Christian principles on neutrality.
Collette and Elizabeth would find examples
of ones who proved loyal under pressure.
And for me,
my job was to call Elizabeth’s new school
to find out if they saluted the flag or sang the anthem.
Hello.
Hi, Mr. Johnson? This is Curtis, Elizabeth’s dad.
We’d studied this topic when the kids were younger,
but we needed reminders for these new challenges.
The kids found some great information.
Several Bible principles applied.
But what Jesus said at Matthew 4:10
was an essential foundation:
“It is Jehovah your God you must worship,
and it is to him alone you must render sacred service.”
If we participate in a nationalistic ceremony,
we’re sharing in worship
of something or someone other than Jehovah God.
But what would help us know what to do?
Elizabeth found some good examples to imitate.
The account of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego
was one of our favorites.
When King Nebuchadnezzar ordered them to worship the gold image,
they bravely stood while others bowed down.
They were determined to worship only Jehovah,
and He rescued them from the furnace.
And there are modern-day examples
of courage like the three Hebrews.
Some children have had to take a stand
when governments tried to force them
to take part in patriotic events during wartime,
when feelings of national pride ran strong.
And despite legal victories in some countries,
young ones today are still put to the test.
We learned there was no one answer on what to do.
Situations are different depending on where we live
or what a person does to show he’s participating.
But in every case,
Christians in some way make it evident
that they are respectful observers, not participants.
We felt good because we had decided
what we would do to be respectful but neutral
and show Jehovah that our family worships him alone.

cn.text: 珂莱特，我回来了！
我在厨房呢
今天过得怎么样？
太忙了！回到家真好！
做什么好吃的呢？
还有几分钟就好了
对了，有个好消息
公司给了我几张门票
周末我们可以去看比赛了
就在市中心......
听起来很有意思！
这项运动还不错
我们可以好好放松一下
我跟妻子已经好几年没有看这样的比赛了
孩子们也一样
我们一直期待能有个晚上
整家人一起出去玩
可是，爸爸
唱国歌的时候我们怎么办？
说实话，我还没想过
女士们，先生们
请大家站起来一起唱国歌
爸，我也有个问题
新学校会不会要求我向国旗敬礼？
对啊！下周才会跟新老师见面
新学校的情况怎么样
我们还不知道
同学们都到了
大家起立，向国旗敬礼
伊丽莎白，你怎么了？
你怎么想，柯帝斯？
刚好，明天晚上我们有家庭崇拜
要不我们讨论一下保持中立的问题
我们先各自查资料，怎么样？
-好主意！ -好啊！
我也觉得不错！
而且我们都可以查资料
我让丹尼尔查一查
跟保持中立有关的圣经原则
珂莱特和伊丽莎白找一找
在压力下保持忠贞的圣经人物
我呢，就负责
给伊丽莎白新学校的老师打电话
问问他们会不会向国旗敬礼或者唱国歌
你好
你好，是约翰逊先生吗？
我是伊丽莎白的爸爸
孩子们还小的时候
我们就讨论过怎么保持中立
但为了应付新的挑战
我们需要再次学习
孩子们找到的资料非常好
有几个圣经原则很适合我们的情况
最重要的原则就是
耶稣在马太福音4:10说过的话
如果我们参与带有爱国主义色彩的仪式
就是在崇拜某个东西或者某个人
而不是崇拜耶和华上帝
我们到底该怎么做呢？
伊丽莎白找到了一些圣经中的好榜样
我们非常喜欢沙得拉、米煞
亚伯尼哥的记载
尼布甲尼撒王命令他们向金像下拜时
他们勇敢地站着，没有像其他人那样跪下来
他们决心只崇拜耶和华
结果，耶和华把他们从火炉里救了出来
现代也有一些好榜样
像三个希伯来青年一样勇敢
在战争时期，爱国主义精神非常强烈
那时政府强迫孩子们参与爱国活动
所以，孩子们需要在重大压力下保持中立
在有些国家
虽然我们曾经获得法律方面的胜诉
但今天的年轻人还是面对不少考验
当然，不同情况有不同的应对方法
具体怎样做要看我们住在哪里
也要考虑周围人的良心
不管怎样，基督徒要清楚表明
他们尊重这个场合
但只是旁观者，不是参与者
现在我们心里踏实多了
因为我们知道怎么做
才能既尊重别人又保持中立
最重要的是可以向耶和华表明
我们只崇拜他

titles.cn: 在公众活动中保持中立

title: 「파수대」에서 배운 교훈—분열된 세상 가운데서 중립을 유지하십시오

ko.text: 저는 재무학 교수라 알아야 할 게 많아요.
또 그리스도인이라 알아야 할 게 많죠.
정치 문제에서 편을 들지 않기가 힘들어요.
정말 힘들죠, 그 문제에 대해 알고 있으니까요.
한 기자의 보도가 좋아서 즐겨 봤어요.
이 기자는 모든 정당의 장단점을 잘 짚어 줬거든요.
근데 언젠가 그 기자가 자기 의견을 말하면서
한 정당의 단점만 지적하니까 그게 싫더라고요.
정치 시위를 가장 크게 하는 곳이죠.
이 지역 사람들은 정치에 관심이 아주 많고, 견해가 뚜렷해요.
전 우리가 중립을 유지해야 한다는 걸 늘 알았지만,
제가 겉으론, 열띤 응원을 하지 않았지만,
또 우리 팀이 거둔 성적에 대한 자부심 때문이었죠.
제가 정치 문제에 쏠린 건 그 공의감 때문이죠.
중립은 행동으로 나타나지 감정은 관계 없다고 생각했죠.
다른 사람보다 자기가 낫다고 여기지 않는 거죠.
그 기사를 공부하니까 제가 중립을 유지하지 못했고
여호와께서 그 기사를 통해 제게 말씀해 주신 것 같다고 기도했어요.
잡지를 읽고 정말 깊은 감동을 받았습니다.
그날 저녁에 기사를 최소한 세 번은 읽은 것 같아요.
너무나 동떨어진 생각을 제가 하고 있더라고요.
기사에서 두 번째로 언급한 상황은 뉴스와 대중 매체에 관한 거였어요.
기사에는 심지어 정치에 관한 뉴스를 보는
양을 제한해야 한다는 취지의 제안도 있었죠.
정말 인상 깊었던 문장이 또 있어요.
그 기사의 여러 문장이 꼭 저에게 하는 말 같았어요.
그랬더니 직장에서 대화할 때 자제하기가 쉽더라고요.
직장 동료가 뉴스에 나온 얘기를 꺼낼 때도,
저는 보질 않았으니까 할 말이 하나도 없었죠.
“아무개가 이렇게 얘기하고, 누가 저렇게 대답하는 거 봤어?”
하고 물으면, 전 “아니, 못 봤어”라고 해요.
제가 사는 나라가 대여섯 번 우승을 하든,
월드컵에서 이기든 지든 여호와께는 중요하지 않아요.
저는 종이 한 장을 (그냥 아무 종이나) 가져다가,
기사에 나온 네 가지 요점을 거기에 적었습니다.
중립을 유지하는 데 도움이 되는 네 가지 방법이죠.
가방에 넣어 두니까 직장에서 언제나 읽을 수가 있어요.
조금씩 노력한 끝에 이젠 축구를 합당한 자리에 두게 됐어요.
그렇게 하니까 우월감이나 국가주의에 빠지지 않는 데 도움이 됩니다.
개인 의견을 말하지 않아야 한다는 걸 배웠어요.
그에 비길 만한 정부가 없다는 걸 확신하면,
제가 성경을 거울 삼아 어디를 개선할지 보게 해 주죠.
기사에 나온 대로 조언을 따르고 변화를 하니까,
이젠 왕국만이 인류의 문제를 해결할 수 있다는 걸

en.text: As a professor of finance, I need to be well-informed.
As a Christian, I also need to be well-informed,
as do all Christians.
It’s difficult not to take sides in politics.
It’s very difficult because we are aware of the issues.
I always really liked soccer ever since I was little.
I lived in a poor area, and soccer was what we used to do for fun.
There was a journalist that I liked to keep up with.
He would point out both the good and the bad on all sides of politics.
But when he spoke up and pointed out only the bad side of a political party,
I did not like that.
I live in the downtown area of the city.
That is where the largest political demonstrations take place.
People from this area are really into politics.
They have definite opinions.
And even though I always knew that we must remain neutral,
I secretly approved of the demonstrations.
On the outside, I wasn’t jumping up and down or cheering,
but on the inside, I was saying: ‘Come on! Let’s win!’
It was all about the desire, the crowd,
and the pride of your team having the most victories or the most trophies.
I used to rationalize saying:
“I was created in Jehovah’s image, and Jehovah is a just God.”
What was speaking was my sense of justice.
I thought neutrality was shown through actions
and not through what I felt.
The April 2016 Watchtower
has interesting information regarding neutrality.
Being neutral means that you do not consider yourself better than others
because “in God’s sight, all people are equal.”
After studying the article, I realized that I needed to make changes;
I was not being neutral.
So I read the article again.
I prayed to Jehovah;
I said to him that I knew it was as if he were speaking to me.
The magazine really touched me deeply.
I remember reading the article at least three times that evening.
I was really surprised.
I realized how far off I was
from what God wanted me to be on the inside.
The second situation mentioned in the article
had to do with news reports and the media.
The article even suggested that we limit
our intake of news that we watch related to politics.
There was another phrase that really moved me.
It said: ‘Even if we don’t march with protesters,
might we be with them in spirit?’
Yes! I was with them. Yes!
There were several phrases in that article
that were written just for me.
When I cut back watching so many news reports
—and I had to—
this helped me to have self-control when I spoke to others at work.
When workmates mentioned something that was in the news,
I didn’t have anything to say since I hadn’t seen it.
I didn’t know about it.
A workmate would say: “Did you see that so-and-so said this
and that someone else made a statement?”
I would say: “No, I didn’t see it,”
and that was the end of the conversation.
The article mentions Romans 10:12
which says that Jehovah is “Lord over all” of us,
that ‘there is no difference between Jew and Greek.’
To Jehovah, it’s not important if my country
has five or six titles or if it won or lost the World Cup.
To Jehovah, all people are equal.
I took a piece of paper, just a simple piece of paper,
and I wrote on it the four key points that the article talks about
—four key points that will help us to remain neutral.
I keep it in my purse; that way I can always read it at work.
I like watching soccer; it’s fun.
I still watch it on TV.
I still play soccer with my friends at Bethel,
but I’ve made an effort to change.
Little by little, I’ve managed to put soccer in its proper place.
This helps me to keep pride and nationalism from getting the best of me.
I learned from this article not to express opinions about politics.
That has to come from deep inside.
If I’m convinced that God’s Kingdom is the best solution
and that there’s nothing that comes even close,
remaining neutral will come naturally.
But I can’t let my guard down.
I really enjoy studying articles from The Watchtower,
especially those dealing with practical matters.
They help me see the Bible as if it were a mirror that shows me where I can improve.
Following counsel
and making the changes suggested in the article
has helped me to speak with the conviction
that only the Kingdom can solve mankind’s problems.

cn.text: 作为金融学教授，我要了解时事动态

希望自己支持的球队能赢

你不会觉得自己比别人优越

后来我又看了一遍
也向耶和华祷告
我觉得耶和华好像用这篇文章跟我说话
这篇文章对我的影响真的很大
记得那天晚上，这篇文章我至少看了3遍
我真不敢相信
原来我的想法跟上帝要我做的差这么远！
这篇文章提到的第二种情况
跟新闻报道和传播媒体有关
文章提醒我们要留意自己
花了多少时间来看政治新闻
还有一句话也打动了我
这句话说，虽然我们不会参加示威游行
但我们是不是在心里认同他们呢？
没错，这里说的不就是我吗？
文章里还有好几句话好像是对我说的
后来我就不常看新闻报道了
这帮助我跟同事说话时能够保持自制
同事们在谈某个新闻时
我因为没看过，不了解他们在谈的内容
所以插不上什么话
要是有同事问
“你看过这个人这样说吗？
还有那个人那样说吗？”
我会说:“没啊，我没看过。”
然后就聊不下去了
这篇文章提到罗马书10:12说
耶和华是我们所有人的主
不论犹太人还是希腊人都没什么分别
对耶和华来说
我的国家得世界杯冠军
得几个奖杯根本不重要
对耶和华来说，所有人都是平等的！
我随手拿了一张纸
写下文章里的4个重要方法
这4个方法可以帮助我保持中立
我把这张纸放在钱包里
这样工作时，我就可以随时拿出来看看
我还是很喜欢看足球赛
电视上有球赛的话我还是会看
在伯特利，我也会和朋友一起踢足球
不过我一直努力作出改变
慢慢地，我对足球赛的看法就越来越平衡了
这样我就不会有优越感
也不会被国家主义精神影响了
我从这篇文章学到
不要对政治发表个人看法
要保持中立，而且要从心里这样做
如果我打从心里相信
只有上帝的王国才能解决人类的所有问题
那么保持中立就容易多了
但我还是不能放松警惕
我很喜欢研读《守望台》文章
特别是跟生活有关的
这些文章帮我看出圣经好像镜子
让我知道哪里可以做得更好
我按照文章的建议作出调整后
传道时就可以坚定地告诉别人
只有上帝的王国才能解决人类的所有问题

John 17:14:

title: 데이비드 셰이퍼: 그리스도인 중립이란 무엇이며, 어떻게, 왜 지켜야 하는가?

ko.text: “그리스도인 중립이란 무엇이며, 어떻게, 왜 지켜야 하는가?”
어느 한 사람이 불공정한 일들을 끝낼 수 있을까요?
처음엔 나랑 전혀 관련 없는 얘기라고 느끼다가도,
가족이나 벗이 불공정을 겪으면 관심이 쏠릴 수 있죠.
우린 사람들이 정치적인 견해 때문에 분열될 것으로 예상합니다.
정부가 사람들 사이에서 뜨거운 논쟁거리가 되고
모두가 어느 한쪽 편을 들라는 압력을 받을 것이 예언되어 있죠.
따라서 우리 각자는 이렇게 자문해 봐야 합니다.
그리스도인인 우리는 무엇보다 그리스도의 본에 관심이 있습니다.
불공정을 끝낼 수 있는 사람이 있었다면
배고픈 사람을 먹이고 아픈 사람을 고치고
죽은 사람을 살리고 설득력 있는 말로
정치계에서 큰 영향력을 행사하실 수도 있었습니다.
한번은 사탄이 자기한테 숭배 행위를 하면
“사람이 거주하는 땅의 모든 왕국”을 주겠다고 제의했습니다.
사탄이 그런 제의를 할 권한이 없다고 주장하지도 않으셨고요.
동족인 유대인들이 그분을 왕으로 삼으려 했을 때도,
로마 정부에 세금을 바쳐도 되는지 질문한 적이 있었죠.
세상 통치자나 국가 지도자나 정치 운동가가 되길 거절하셨습니다.
사람들에게 무관심하거나 아무 견해가 없으셨기 때문일까요?
공의가 실제로 어떤 것인지 보여 주셨죠.
불공정을 영원히 없앨 하느님의 왕국에 대해 가르치는 것이었습니다.
로마 정부에 세금을 내는 것에 관한 질문을 받고
“‘데나리온 한 닢을 가져와서 보여 주십시오’ 하고 말씀하셨다.
그리고 예수께선 ‘카이사르의 것을 돌려주라’는 말씀도 하셨습니다.
당시 최고 권력자인 카이사르는 가치를 지닌 것들을 발행했는데,
따라서 카이사르는 그 일부를 돌려받을 권리가 있었습니다.
그렇게 해서 국가는 필요한 봉사를 계속할 수 있었죠.
한편 우리가 가진 가장 가치 있는 것들은 하느님께 받은 선물이죠.
우리의 마음, 생명, 정신, 힘 같은 것들요.
이런 건 애초부터 카이사르가 준 게 아니니까
따라서 하느님께 우리가 돌려드릴 사랑은 전적인 것,
우리의 몸, 능력, 활력, 감정이 모두 관련되는 것이죠.
그분이 왕으로 임명하신 분인 예수의 편에 섭니다.
그러면 예수의 제자들은 사람들이 왕국을 반대할 때
예수께서 지상에서 보낸 마지막 밤에 일어난 일을 통해
“많은 무리가 칼과 몽둥이를 들고” 예수를 잡으러 왔을 때
요한은 그 종의 이름이 말고라고 알려 주죠.
누가복음을 보면 예수께선 말고의 귀를 만져 고쳐 주십니다.
칼을 잡는 사람은 모두 칼로 망할 것입니다.”
왜 그분은 베드로의 용감한 행동을 승인하지 않으셨을까요?
그분이 정치 문제에 일절 관여하지 않으신 것과 같은 이유죠.
같은 날 밤 예수께선 본디오 빌라도 앞에서
“내 왕국은 이 세상에 속해 있지 않습니다.”
맞습니다. 예수의 왕국은 인간 정부가 아니기 때문에
이 말씀이 그런 의미라는 걸 어떻게 알 수 있나요?
내 종들이 싸워서 내가 유대인들에게 넘겨지지 않게 했을 것입니다.
그러나 내 왕국은 이 세상에서 나온 것이 아닙니다.”
어떤 사람은 우리가 특정 인간 정부를 지지하지 않으니까
1950년대에 현재 콩고로 알려진 나라의 정부 당국은
새로운 정부는 증인들이 공산주의자가 아니라며 비난했죠!
하지만 현재 여호와의 증인은 거의 30년 전부터
사람들은 우리의 중립 입장을 철저한 무관심이라고 생각하기도 하고,
국가에 위협이 되는 요소로 생각하기도 합니다.
우선, 둘 사이엔 큰 차이가 있습니다.
우린 결코 사람들에게 무관심하거나 그들의 감정에 무감각하지 않죠.
예수를 본받아 사람들의 고통을 덜어 주려 노력하는데,
불공정을 없앨 하느님의 왕국에 대해 가르쳐 주는 일을 합니다.
정치 제도가 아니라 사람들의 마음을 바꾸려고 노력합니다.
그게 더 현실적으로 도움이 된다고 생각하죠.
인류의 주된 문제는 정치가 아닌 도덕 문제니까요.
도움이 된다고 할 수 있는 이유는 무엇일까요?
우린, 특정 정당이나 후보를 위해 투표하지 않지만,
선거를 방해하거나 투표하려는 사람을 방해하지도 않죠.
로비 활동과 캠페인을 벌이거나 공직에 출마하지 않지만,
정치 개혁을 위한 시위에 참여하지도 않습니다.
우리가 부르지 않는 걸 널리 알리지도 않습니다.
같은 나라 사람들에게 폭력을 휘두르지도 않죠.
우린 어떤 정치적 견해도 지지하지 않으며,
국가가 예수의 명령과 어긋나는 걸 요구한다면 어떨까요?
국가가 하느님이 하지 말라고 하신 걸 하라고 하거나
하느님이 하라고 하신 걸 하지 말라고 할 경우,
하느님께서는 그걸 부당한 요구로 여기실 것입니다.
곤란한 상황을 불러올 수도 있다는 걸 우린 알고 있습니다.
예수께선 마태복음 24:9에서 그런 일이 있을 걸 예언하셨죠.
일부 제자들이 감옥에 갇힐 거라고 하셨습니다.
따라서 우린 감옥에 갇히든, 그렇지 않든
여러 해 동안 수많은 형제 자매들이 그리스도인 중립 입장 때문에
징역형을 선고받고 수감 생활을 해 왔습니다.
그들의 인내는 우리 모두에게 승리를 의미합니다.
“부디 여러분을 위해 내가 환난을 겪는다고 해서
바울은 로마에서 가택 연금되어 있을 때 이 편지를 썼죠.
바울은 시련 속에서도 끈기 있게 봉사함으로
에베소 회중 성원들에게 그들이 그리스도인으로서 누리는 특권이
별로 가치가 없다는 인상을 받았을 겁니다.
충실을 유지하는 게 얼마나 소중한 것인지 보여 주었죠.
마찬가지로, 수감된 우리 형제 자매들의 인내는
그들은 어느 인간 정부가 아니라 하늘 왕국의 공사들입니다.
전쟁이 없는 세상에서 누리는 영원한 생명을 상으로 줄 것입니다.

en.text: Our theme this month is
“Christian Neutrality
“—What It Means, What It Takes,
and Why We Choose It.”
What is your opinion?
Where do you stand?
Can one person make a difference in countering injustice?
When we hear people discussing political topics,
we might at first think their conversation is purely philosophical;
but when injustice threatens our loved ones,
it can seem personal.
We expect that people will be divided over political ideology.
Revelation chapters 8-13 foretold that in the last days,
government would be the burning issue among mankind
and that people would feel pressured to take sides.
The question each of us needs to ask himself is,
How do I respond when people debate solutions to serious injustices?
As Christians, we’re most interested
in the example of Christ.
If ever there was a person who could make a difference in countering injustice,
it was Jesus.
He felt deep compassion for people.
And with his abilities to feed the hungry,
heal the sick, raise the dead, and reach hearts with his winsome words,
Jesus could have exerted invincible influence in the realm of politics.
He certainly had the opportunity to do so.
Satan was pleased to offer him
“all the kingdoms of the inhabited earth”
in an exchange for one act of worship.
But Jesus wouldn’t accept it.
Neither did he assert that Satan had no authority to make such an offer.
Later, Jesus’ own countrymen tried to make him king,
but he rejected that too.
Later still, someone asked him
whether it was lawful to pay taxes to the Roman government.
Again, Jesus didn’t take sides.
He refused to become a world ruler,
a national leader, or a political activist.
Did that mean that Jesus didn’t care? that he had no opinion?
To the contrary!
Jesus cared more deeply than we can fathom.
And by treating people fairly,
Jesus promoted justice at the most fundamental level.
Still, his principal focus
was on teaching people about the Kingdom of God,
which would eliminate injustice for all time.
So, what did Jesus indicate should be our position
regarding human governments?
We learn from Jesus’ response to the question about Roman taxation
as recorded at Mark 12:15-17:
“‘Bring me a denarius to look at.’
“They brought one, and he said to them:
“‘Whose image and inscription is this?’
“They said to him: ‘Caesar’s.’
“Jesus then said:
“‘Pay back Caesar’s things to Caesar,
but God’s things to God.’”
What are Caesar’s things?
At Romans 13:1-7,
the apostle Paul lists tax, tribute,
fear, and honor.
Notice, too, that Jesus said to “pay back Caesar’s things.”
What does that imply?
That Caesar, the ruling authority of the day,
had issued valuable things —coins, for example.
Thus, Caesar had the right to ask for some of those coins back.
This enabled the State to continue rendering necessary services.
Jesus acknowledged that.
On the other hand,
our most valuable possessions are grants from God himself
—such gifts as our heart, our life, our mind, and our strength.
We can’t give those things back to Caesar
because Caesar didn’t grant them to us in the first place.
We rightly give those things back to God
in the form of our dedication and our love.
Regarding our love for God, Jesus said at Mark 12:30:
“You must love Jehovah your God
“with your whole heart and with your whole soul
“and with your whole mind
and with your whole strength.”
So the love we give back to God is total
—no bodily part, function,
capacity, or desire being left out.
Those who love God take the side of Jesus,
whom Jehovah has appointed as King.
But how would Jesus’ disciples defend his Kingdom when people opposed it?
We gain insight from events that occurred
on the last night of Jesus’ life on earth.
Recall from Matthew chapter 26
that when “a large crowd with swords and clubs” came to arrest Jesus,
Peter “drew his sword and struck the slave of the high priest, taking off his ear.”
John reports that the slave’s name was Malchus.
Luke adds that Jesus touched the man’s ear and healed him.
Imagine that!
Jesus bore no ill will toward the men taking him into custody.
Further, according to Matthew 26:52,
Jesus told Peter:
“Return your sword to its place,
“for all those who take up the sword
will perish by the sword.”
Why did Jesus disapprove of Peter’s brave act?
For the same reason that he had avoided the political process all the way up to that point.
Jesus explained this when he appeared before Pontius Pilate later that night.
At John 18:36, we read:
“My Kingdom is no part of this world.”
Yes, because Jesus’ Kingdom is not of human origin,
it doesn’t need human defenses.
How can we be sure that this is what Jesus meant?
Look closely at the rest of John 18:36:
“If my Kingdom were part of this world,
“my attendants would have fought
“that I should not be handed over to the Jews.
“But as it is,
my Kingdom is not from this source.”
So as Christians,
what is our position where political matters are concerned?
We are neutral.
Sometimes people misunderstand this viewpoint.
Some have concluded that because we don’t promote one human government,
that we must be promoting another human government.
In the 1950’s, in what is now the Republic of Congo,
authorities falsely accused Jehovah’s Witnesses of being Communists.
But during the 1970’s,
when Congo adopted a Communist form of government,
the new authorities found fault with us for not being Communists!
Today, however, and for nearly three decades,
Jehovah’s Witnesses have enjoyed legal status in the Republic of Congo.
And whereas some have perceived
our Christian neutrality as sheer apathy,
others construe our position as a threat.
Let’s address both of these viewpoints.
First, there is a big difference
between Christian neutrality and apathy.
Apathy is defined
as “a lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern.”
We certainly don’t lack interest in people,
nor are we insensitive to their feelings.
Like Jesus, we strive to alleviate people’s suffering
by helping them in practical ways
while teaching them about the only Kingdom
that can eliminate injustice.
By teaching people from God’s Word,
we endeavor to change hearts,
not political institutions.
We feel this approach is realistic
because mankind’s main problems are not political
but moral.
But why can it be said that Jehovah’s Witnesses are not a threat
but, rather, an asset?
We conscientiously obey the laws,
we support our communities through volunteer service
or compulsory civilian service where that exists,
and we pay our taxes.
It’s true, we don’t vote for political parties or candidates,
but neither do we disrupt elections
or interfere with those who choose to vote.
It’s true, we don’t lobby, campaign, or run for government office,
but neither do we criticize those in power,
undermine their policies, or demonstrate for political change.
It’s true, we won’t salute a flag,
but neither will we burn a flag, spit on a flag,
or disparage the nation that a flag represents
—even in lands where these are considered
protected expressions of freedom.
It’s true, we don’t sing national anthems,
but neither do we discourage others from singing,
nor do we make a public spectacle of not singing;
we simply don’t participate.
It’s true, we wouldn’t kill people in war,
but neither would we attack people at home.
So while we don’t promote any political position,
neither do we condemn any political position —even in our heart.
That is what neutrality means.
We don’t take sides.
But what if the demands of the State
conflict with the commands of Jesus?
There’s a Bible principle for that.
Are you thinking of what it says at Acts 5:28, 29
—that “we must obey God as ruler rather than men”?
This is not disregard for the State,
but, rather, reverence for God.
If the State demands that we do what God forbids
or refrain from doing what God commands,
then we believe God would consider that an invalid request.
Now, one might say,
‘I can imagine some situations where that viewpoint could get you into trouble.’
Jesus foretold as much at Matthew 24:9,
where he said: “You will be hated by all the nations
on account of my name.”
More specifically, at Revelation 2:10,
Jesus said that some of his disciples would be thrown into prison
—not all of us but some.
So we’re not disappointed if we don’t get thrown into prison,
but neither are we discouraged if we do.
Our minds turn to the thousands of brothers and sisters
who have been sentenced to prison over the years
for their Christian neutrality.
We are proud of them.
We pray for them.
We know that Jehovah is pleased with them.
Their endurance under trial spells victory for all of us.
How so?
To the congregation in Ephesus, Paul wrote:
“I ask you not to give up on account of my tribulations in your behalf,
for these mean glory for you.”
Paul wrote these words while he himself was under house arrest in Rome.
In what sense did Paul’s tribulations
“mean glory” for the Ephesians?
In that his perseverance in ministering despite trials
showed the congregation that the privileges they enjoyed as Christians
were of the highest importance.
If Paul had just given up, what would that have implied?
That their faith, their ministry,
and their hope in God’s Kingdom were not so valuable after all.
Instead, Paul’s endurance exalted Christianity.
It demonstrated that remaining faithful is worth any sacrifice.
In like manner, the endurance of our dear brothers and sisters in prison
proves that their hope is alive
and that the Kingdom they represent is real.
They have an identity as envoys,
not of any human government,
but of the heavenly Kingdom
—a Kingdom that will reward them with everlasting life
in a world without war.

cn.text: 这个月的主题是，基督徒保持中立
保持中立是什么意思？
怎样保持中立？
为什么要这样做呢？
你怎么看呢？
你的立场是什么？
有没有任何一个人
可以阻止不公平的事发生呢？
听到有人谈论政治话题时
我们的第一反应可能是
这跟我有什么关系呢？
可是，当亲戚朋友遭遇不公时
我们的反应可能就不一样了
其实
人们对政治有不同的见解一点也不奇怪
启示录8-13章曾预告
在最后的日子
人们都会非常关注政治话题
发表观点
也会迫于压力去支持某一方
因此我们每个人都可以问问自己
别人争论要如何解决不公正的问题时
我们该有什么反应呢？
在这方面，耶稣的榜样
很值得我们每一个基督徒学习
耶稣在地上时
如果他想解决不公正的问题
根本就不是什么难事
耶稣有同情心
也有能力喂饱饥饿的人
医治病人、复活死去的人
他说的话也很打动人
耶稣本可以成为一个
非常有影响力的政治领袖
当然他也有这样的机会
撒但曾经对耶稣说
“只要你崇拜我，就这一次
天下万国就都是你的了！”
耶稣马上拒绝了！
耶稣也没有质疑天下万国不是撒但的
还有一次，有一些人要耶稣做王
他也拒绝了
在另一个场合，有人问耶稣
该不该向罗马政府纳税
这一次，耶稣再次保持中立
撒但想让耶稣统治万国
参与政治改革，他都拒绝了
但这是不是说
耶稣对周围的人和事漠不关心呢？
当然不是
耶稣非常关心别人的处境
他待人毫不偏心
用行动告诉我们什么是真正的公正
总之，耶稣专注于帮助人认识上帝的王国
因为只有上帝的王国才能彻底铲除不公
那么，身为基督徒
我们应该怎样看待世上的政府呢？
从耶稣说的话就可以知道了
有人问耶稣，该不该向罗马政府纳税
耶稣说
属于凯撒的是什么呢？
保罗在罗马书13:1-7提到了一些事
纳税、进贡、敬畏、尊重
请留意耶稣怎么说
属于凯撒的要给凯撒
这是什么意思呢？
凯撒是当时的统治者
为人民提供的服务
包括发行钱币
所以他自然有权征税
而征收上来的税款
就可以用来为人民提供所需的服务
耶稣也承认这点
另一方面
耶和华上帝赐给我们哪些宝贵的礼物呢？
他赐给我们生命
让我们可以思考
也给我们力量
我们不能把这些东西给凯撒
因为这些不是凯撒给我们的
那怎样把属于上帝的都给上帝呢？
就是献身给上帝并且爱他
那怎样才算是爱上帝呢？
在马可福音12:30
耶稣说
所以我们要毫无保留地爱上帝
用全部生命
所有力量和感情去爱上帝
我们爱上帝就会拥护耶稣
拥护耶和华上帝委任的君王
当有人反对上帝的王国时
耶稣的门徒怎么做呢？
从耶稣牺牲前的那个晚上发生的事
我们就可以知道答案了
马太福音26章记载
“有一大群人
带着刀剑棍棒”来抓耶稣
然后彼得“伸手拔剑，向大祭司的奴隶砍去
削掉了他一只耳朵。”
使徒约翰说那个人叫做马勒古
而路加福音告诉我们
耶稣后来摸了摸他的耳朵医好了他
请想想
耶稣居然没有对来抓他的人怀恨在心
不但这样，在马太福音26:52
耶稣对彼得说
为什么耶稣不赞同彼得的这种行为呢？
因为耶稣不想参与政治
他的态度一直没改变
耶稣见本丢·彼拉多时，就解释了这一点
在约翰福音18:36，耶稣说
耶稣的王国不是人类统治的政府
自然不需要人用武力来保护
我们怎么知道耶稣说的就是这个意思？
让我们仔细看看约翰福音18:36
经文说
身为基督徒
对于政治事务我们应该有怎样的看法呢？
我们要保持中立
有人可能会对我们的立场有些误解
他们认为既然我们不支持这个政府
那就一定拥护另一个政府的统治
比如，在50年代
刚果共和国的政府诬告我们是共产党员
但到了70年代，它成了共产主义国家
这个新政府
又因弟兄们不是共产党员而极度愤怒
但到今天我们已经在刚果共和国
合法注册将近30年了
有些人觉得我们保持中立
就是对世上的人和事漠不关心
也有些人认为我们在反对政府
我们想作出以下的解释
保持中立和冷漠是两种完全不同的概念
冷漠的定义是缺乏情感、兴趣及关切之心
我们不是对人漠不关心
相反我们会像耶稣一样
尽力给别人实际的帮助
来减轻他们的痛苦
我们也会教导人认识上帝的王国
因为只有这个王国才能彻底铲除不公
我们帮助人学习圣经是为了改变人的内心
而不是政治制度
我们认为这才是最有效的方法
因为人类的主要问题不是政治
而是道德
为什么耶和华见证人不会对政府构成威胁
反而会对政府有帮助呢？
我们奉公守法，诚实纳税
也愿意做志愿服务来帮助社区里的人
在有替代役的国家
我们也愿意参与替代役服务
我们不会投票支持某个政党或候选人
不会干涉选举活动或阻止别人投票
我们也不会进行政治游说，不会参与竞选
也不会批评当权者或他们提出的政策
更不会为了改变政府的政策而示威游行
当然，我们不会向国旗敬礼、焚烧国旗
也不会向国旗吐口水
或者贬低国旗所代表的国家
哪怕这些行为在这些国家里不是违法的
我们也不会这样做
我们不唱国歌，也不会阻止别人唱
当然
我们也不会刻意让别人看出我们不唱国歌
我们只是不唱国歌而已
我们不会参战杀害别人
也不会用暴力对待自己国家的人
在政治方面，我们不会支持
也不会谴责任何一方
这样的念头也不会在心里产生
这就是中立的意思
我们不会偏向任何一方！
如果政府的要求跟耶稣的诫命有所冲突
我们该怎么办呢？
有一个圣经原则，大家可能想到了
“我们必须服从上帝的统治
而不是服从人。”
我们这样做是敬畏上帝
但并不表示我们不尊重政府
如果政府要我们做上帝明令禁止的事
或不让我们按上帝的要求做事
我们要确信上帝不希望我们向政府妥协
有人可能会说
你们这样的态度可能会激起政府的不满
其实
这正好应验了马太福音24:9的预言
耶稣说
在启示录2:10，耶稣说
他的一些门徒会被关在监狱里
不是所有人
所以，如果我们没有被囚禁
不要感到失望
要是真的被囚禁了，也不要难过
多年以来
我们有数千位弟兄姐妹
因为保持中立而被关进监狱
我们真的因为他们而感到自豪
耶和华肯定也以他们为荣
我们要为还在监狱的弟兄祷告
他们在考验下保持忍耐
对我们所有人来说就是打了一场胜仗
为什么这么说呢？
以弗所书3:13说
保罗写这些话的时候正被软禁在罗马
为什么说保罗的患难能为以弗所会众
“带来荣耀”呢？
因为他在考验下依然坚持为上帝服务
会让会众看出
他们的基督徒身份是最宝贵的
如果保罗放弃了，会有什么影响呢？
弟兄姐妹就会觉得
他们的信心、希望以及他们为上帝做的服务
就没什么价值了
保罗保持忍耐
让弟兄姐妹看出基督徒身份是非常宝贵的
也看出，为了保持忠贞
任何牺牲都是值得的
今天，被囚禁的弟兄姐妹也显出忍耐
这表明他们把未来的希望
和上帝的王国看得很真实
他们虽然不是地上某个国家的大使
却有幸做上帝王国的大使
在这个王国里，他们会得到永生
享有和平，直到永远

en.text: Why give attention to the way you introduce a scripture?
Because the promises of God,
which we find in his written Word, have tremendous power.
Hebrews 4:12 says:
“The word of God is alive and exerts power
“and is sharper than any two-edged sword
“and pierces even to the dividing of soul and spirit,
“and of joints from the marrow,
and is able to discern thoughts and intentions of the heart.”
Yes, God’s Word has the power to reach a person’s heart,
so we should always use it as the basis for our teaching.
But first, we should ensure that our listeners
are properly focused on those inspired words.
How might you do that?
Indicate what the text will reveal,
cite the Bible as God’s Word,
and say something that will make the listeners want to read the verse.
In the following demonstration,
see if the speaker accomplishes any of those goals.
Please turn to Psalm 55:22.
Even though we have read this many times before,
let’s read it again:
“Throw your burden on Jehovah, and he will sustain you.
Never will he allow the righteous one to fall.”
Although a Kingdom Hall audience
will likely turn to a scripture because you invite them to,
this audience didn’t know why the scripture was being read,
nor did the speaker give them any reason to be especially interested in what it says.
How might the speaker properly introduce a Bible verse?
There are a few ways to do this.
First, he could ask a question that the scripture will answer.
Let’s watch an example of that.
When a problem is so severe
that it seems you can think of nothing else,
what can you do?
The answer is found at Psalm 55:22.
Or the speaker could pose a problem that the scripture will help to solve.
Imagine that your marriage mate or a fellow believer
has said or done something hurtful to you.
The Bible tells us how not to respond
at Romans 12:17, 18.
Notice what it says.
Another good way to introduce Bible accounts is
by stating a principle that the account will illustrate.
We can avoid many problems by following divine instructions.
Please turn to 2 Samuel 6:2-7
and notice what happened when David
didn’t follow the proper procedure
for transporting the ark of the covenant.
What else must we do to introduce scriptures properly,
especially when our audience includes unbelievers?
Cite God’s Word as the authority.
Watch the following demonstration,
and see if you can discern how the publisher might improve
in drawing attention to the scripture.
Will crime and wickedness always exist?
David gives us the answer here at Psalm 37:10, 11.
The publisher aroused interest in what she was about to read
by raising a question,
and she correctly identified David as the writer.
Although it’s not wrong to mention the name of the Bible writer,
in this case the householder might have wondered, ‘Who is David?’
And even if she knew who David was,
she might have viewed his words as an ancient human opinion.
Let’s see how the sister could introduce this scripture
in a way that inspires more confidence in its reliability.
Will crime and wickedness always exist?
God’s Word gives us the answer
here at Psalm 37:10, 11.
So before reading a scripture,
do more than simply tell your audience
where it can be found and invite them to follow along.
Indicate the key point it will make,
and say something to make your listeners want to read it.
Especially when speaking to unbelievers,
introduce the scripture in a way that indicates its authority.
By doing these things, you can prepare the minds of your listeners
for the important words that you’ll read.

连外表和内心

title: 로버트 루시오니: 겸손하게 평화를 이루는 사람이 되십시오 (빌립보 2:3)

ko.text: “겸손하게 남을 자기보다 더 나은 사람으로 여기십시오.”
이 구절은 사도 바울이 기록한 것이지만,
사실 이것은 예수께서 사도들에게 여러 차례
도리어 여러분 중에서 누구든지 크게 되고자 하는 사람은
겸손하게 남을 자기보다 더 나은 사람으로 여기라는 거죠.
왜 예수께서는 제자들에게 겸손을 가르치려고 애쓰셨을까요?
겸손의 부족이 여호와의 성품과 상충된다는 걸
겸손하지 않으면 여호와의 성령이 흐를 수가 없습니다.
하느님의 백성 사이의 평화가 깨지리라는 것도 아셨죠.
평화가 없으면 여호와의 성령이 흐르지 않습니다.
제자들이 서로 다투고 논쟁한 기록을 살펴보면
오늘의 성구에 나오는 원칙을 적용하지 않았기 때문이라는 걸
다 큰 성인인 제자들이 길에서 실제로 이렇게 말했을까요?
사람의 마음을 읽으실 수 있었기 때문에,
“그분은 앉으신 다음 열두 제자를 불러 말씀하셨다.
‘누구든지 첫째가 되고자 하면, 모든 사람의 마지막이 되어
사실 생각해 보면, 사소한 다툼이나 논쟁,
겸손의 부족이 원인인 경우가 많지 않나요?
방에서 무슨 일로 논쟁했나요?’ 하시진 않을까요?
혹은 회중 장로나 전도인들 사이의 관계에서
서로 긴장된 관계에 있거나 논쟁이 벌어지는 것 같을 때
우리는 먼저 자기 자신을 돌아보아야 합니다.
혹시 내가 더 크다고 논쟁하고 있진 않나요?
이 점을 생각하면 꼭 떠오르는 인물이 있는데요.
사래 즉 사라는 임신을 하지 못했습니다.
광야로 도망합니다. 이런 생각이 들 수 있죠.
가서 겸손하게 행동하면 좋아질 거란 거죠.
평화가 깨진 이유가 무엇 때문일 수 있죠?
하갈이 자기가 임신한 걸 알게 되자
하갈이 깔보니까 사라도 깔보았을 수 있죠.
하지만 여호와께선 가정의 평화를 깨뜨린 책임을
나의 어떤 행동 때문에 평화가 깨질 수 있습니다.
어쩌면 내 생각, 내가 일하는 방식이
더 낫다는 느낌을 주고 있을 수 있죠.
그럼 교만하고 겸손하지 않고 우월해지려고 하는
우리의 불완전한 경향과 맞서 싸우는 것이
앞서 언급한 것처럼 하느님의 백성 사이의
평화 없이는 여호와의 영이 흐를 수 없습니다.
그 말은 그분의 도움이 없다는 뜻이죠.
그렇게 되면 우린 실패하고 말 겁니다.
사실 이 말은 저희 사무실 보드에도 적혀져 있는데요.
“아무리 질서 있는 체계라도 평화에 기초해 있지 않으면
그와는 달리, 하느님의 평화가 조성하는 질서는
걱정이 될 만한 상황이 생길 수 있지만,
부서와 부서 사이에서 긴장감이 생길 수 있습니다.
평화가 있으면 일이 아무리 어렵고 힘들더라도
처리할 수 있죠. 우린 일하는 걸 좋아하니까요.
하지만 평화가 깨지는 건 심각한 문제죠.
우리가 남을 더 나은 사람으로 여기는 게
평화를 유지하는 게 그분께 얼마나 중요합니까?
기뻐 외치며 항상 말하게 해 주십시오,

en.text: Philippians 2:3:
“With humility consider others superior to you.”
These words, penned by the apostle Paul,
really reflect a message that Jesus
tried again and again
to get across to his apostles.
In fact, let’s look at one account at Mark 10:42, 43
It says: “But Jesus called them to him and said to them:
“‘You know that those who appear to be ruling the nations lord it over them
“‘and their great ones wield authority over them.
“‘This must not be the way among you;
“‘but whoever wants to be great among you
must be your minister.’”
“With humility consider others superior to you.”
Now, why was Jesus so concerned
that his disciples learn this lesson of humility?
Because Jesus knew that a lack of humility
is contrary to Jehovah’s personality.
If we don’t have humility, Jehovah’s holy spirit cannot flow.
Psalm 138:6 says that Jehovah
only knows the haughty “from a distance.”
But Jesus also knew that lack of humility
disrupts the peace of God’s people.
And without peace, Jehovah’s spirit cannot flow either.
We may think of 1 Corinthians 14:33
that says that Jehovah “is a God . . . of peace.”
Now, it’s of interest as we look at the accounts
that Jesus recognized that when his disciples lost their peace
—when they were arguing, when they were bickering among themselves—
it was because they were not applying the principle in today’s text.
Let’s look at another account.
If you look back a page to Mark 9:33,
it says: “And they came into Capernaum.
“Now when he was inside the house, he put the question to them:
‘What were you arguing about on the road?’”
“What were you arguing about?”
Well, if you look at verse 34, they were quiet
because they were arguing about who was greater.
Now, think about this: These were grown men.
Do you really think they were walking down the road saying,
‘Well, I’m greater than you are’; ‘no, I’m greater’; ‘no, I’m the greatest there is’?
Maybe, but maybe not. These were grown, mature men.
But Jesus, in his wisdom of human nature and being able to read hearts,
knew what they were arguing about —the root of it.
The topic didn’t matter.
The real issue was that it was a lack of humility.
And notice what he says in verse 35.
It says: “So he sat down and called the Twelve and said to them:
“‘If anyone wants to be first,
he must be last of all and minister of all.’”
Have humility.
Consider others superior to you.
At Luke 9:46, 47,
when there was a dispute, that account says
that “Jesus, knowing the reasoning of their hearts,”
counseled them on humility.
He saw right through the argument —right through the issue—
and isolated the real problem: lack of humility.
Now, when you think about it,
isn’t it true that that’s usually what is
behind petty arguments, disputes, or disagreements we may have?
See, if Jesus was among us, would he say:
‘Come over here. What were you arguing about in the office?
What were you arguing about in the room?’
See, whether it’s between marriage mates,
those of us working together here at Bethel,
bodies of elders, publishers in the congregation,
what’s the lesson for us?
Well, the lesson is that when there seems to be a lack of peace
or when there seems to be tension or arguing,
the first person we should look at is ourselves.
Am I really arguing over who is greater?
Now, an account that always comes to mind when I think about this
is that of Hagar, Sarah’s Egyptian maidservant.
And if you turn back to Genesis chapter 16,
(and we’re familiar with this account)
Sarah, or Sarai at the time, was not able to become pregnant.
Hagar became pregnant,
and as soon as Hagar became pregnant, peace went out of the family.
There was tension; there was bickering; there was arguing.
Things escalated to the point of Sarai humiliating Hagar
and chasing her away into the wilderness.
We may first read this and say: ‘Oh, poor Hagar, this young pregnant girl.
Sarai is just jealous. Sarai has got the problem.’
Was that the case?
Well, we don’t have all the facts of the matter,
but it is of interest to note what Jehovah,
through his angel, told Hagar when he met up with her in the wilderness.
Look at Genesis 16:9.
It says: “Jehovah’s angel then said to her:
“‘Return to your mistress
and humble yourself under her hand.’”
‘Go back, and be humble; and everything will be OK.’
Now, did you notice what may have been the obstacle to peace?
Back in verse 4— Chapter 16, verse 4 says
that Hagar “began to despise her mistress”
when she, Hagar, found out that she was pregnant.
The Byington translation says
that Hagar began to ‘look down on her mistress.’
Hagar began to feel that she was superior.
And what happened?
Yes, Sarah chased her away.
Hagar reacted, and perhaps Sarah reacted.
Perhaps Sarah did not react well either.
But do you notice who Jehovah held responsible for the lack of peace in the family?
Hagar.
‘You go back and humble yourself under her hand.’
And see, that’s a good account that reminds us that sometimes
the real underlying challenge to peace may be me.
See, peace may have gone away because of how people are reacting to me.
Perhaps I’m telegraphing that I think my ways, my ideas,
my way of doing things are superior to others.
Now, why is it so important that we fight this imperfect tendency
that we all have toward pride,
toward lacking humility, and feelings of superiority?
Well, not only is it distasteful to Jehovah but,
as we’ve talked about, lack of humility
disrupts the peace of God’s people.
And without peace, Jehovah’s spirit cannot flow.
Without Jehovah’s spirit, we’re on our own.
And if we’re on our own, we’re going to fail.
There’s a powerful quote in the Kingdom Rules! book
on page 120 in paragraph 9.
In fact, we have it written on one of the whiteboards in our office
just to remind us of this point.
It says this: “Any structure of order
“that does not have peace as its foundation
“will sooner or later collapse.
In contrast, godly peace promotes the kind of order that lasts.”
Powerful point, isn’t it?
“Any structure of order that does not have peace as its foundation
will sooner or later collapse.”
And see, that applies in the congregation,
in a family, in our department at Bethel,
on a construction site, wherever we are.
And I know in our work,
no matter how challenging or how complicated things get,
no matter what we’re dealing with, the only time we really start to worry
is when we find that peace has gone away.
Maybe there’s tension between ones in the office;
maybe there’s tension between our department and another department.
That’s when we worry, and we start working quickly
to see what we can do to restore peace.
Because when peace is present—
No matter how challenging or how hard the topic is, it’s just work.
And that’s why we’re here: We love to work.
But when peace is disturbed, that’s when we’re in trouble.
Now, how important is it to Jehovah that we consider others superior to us?
How important is it to Jehovah that we maintain peace?
How does he feel about that?
Well, let’s look at a scripture at Psalm 35:27.
Psalm 35:27 says:
“But let those who take pleasure in my righteousness shout joyfully;
“may they constantly say: ‘May Jehovah be magnified,
who takes pleasure in the peace of his servant.’”
Jehovah takes pleasure in the peace of his servants.
He takes pleasure when he sees us working together
in unity and in peace,
and that takes humility.
So may we work hard to always apply the principle in today’s text.
Consider others superior to us.
May we work hard to maintain the peace
of all of us all around us,
and may Jehovah never have to say of us,
‘What were you arguing about on the road?’

cn.text: 腓立比书2:3说
“要谦卑，看别人比自己优越。”
这句话虽然是保罗写的
但却说明了耶稣一再教导使徒的一个道理
我们来看一个记载
马可福音10:42说
“耶稣叫他们来
对他们说
你们知道
列国的人有被尊为统治者的辖制他们
也有大臣掌权管理他们
你们中间可不要这样
谁想在你们中间为大
就得做你们的仆人。”
刚才也说过
“要谦卑，看别人比自己优越。”
为什么耶稣非常希望门徒学会
谦卑这个特质呢？
因为耶稣知道耶和华不喜欢缺乏谦卑的人
所以如果我们不谦卑
就会妨碍圣灵的运行
“至于高傲的人
〔耶和华〕只从远处鉴辨。”
耶稣也知道如果我们不谦卑
就很难保持和睦
没有和睦的关系
上帝的圣灵就不会运行在我们当中
我们可以想一想
哥林多前书14:33的话
“上帝……要人和谐”
有意思的是
耶稣看得出来门徒之间不和睦的真正原因
知道他们争吵的真正原因其实是因为
他们没有把今天的经文用出来
我们来看另一个记载
请大家翻到马可福音9:33
这里说
“他们来到迦百农，进了房子
耶稣问他们说
你们在路上争论什么呢？”
“你们在吵什么呢？”
请看34节说什么
他们默不作声
因为他们刚刚在争论谁最大
想想看
他们是一群成年男子
你觉得他们会在路上边走边吵说
“我比较大！”
“不对，我比你大！”
“不是，我才是最大的！”
也许会，也许不会
他们都是成熟的大人
可是，耶稣了解人性
看得出来他们内心的想法
知道他们争吵的根本原因是
缺乏谦卑的态度
请留意35节怎么说
“耶稣坐下，叫那十二人来
对他们说
谁想为首
就要做众人最末的一个
做众人的仆人。”
要谦卑，看别人比自己优越
路加福音9:46,47记载，有一次
他们又彼此争论
经文说:“耶稣知道他们心里思量的事。”
耶稣能看到问题所在
他关心的不是他们吵什么
而是有没有保持谦卑
想想看
我们是不是常常为了一点小事
就吵架或闹情绪呢？
背后的原因可能是我们没有保持谦卑
如果耶稣在这里
他对你说
“你来一下好吗？
你们刚刚在办公室里吵什么呢？
你们在房间里吵什么呢？”
不管是夫妻
还是一起在伯特利工作的弟兄姐妹
长老团、会众的传道员
我们都可以从这件事学到
如果大家相处起来不和睦
吵架或者气氛紧张
我们应该要先反省一下自己
我是不是不够谦卑
也在争论谁最大呢？
我想起一个圣经人物
夏甲
她是撒拉的埃及女仆
请看创世记16章
大家都很熟悉这个故事
撒拉又叫撒莱
她无法生育
但夏甲却怀孕了
夏甲怀孕后
家里就不得安宁，气氛很紧张
可能常吵架
事情变得越来越严重
结果撒莱羞辱夏甲
把她赶到旷野去了
第一次读这个记载的时候
我们可能会觉得
“夏甲真可怜，年纪轻轻又怀孕
还被撒莱忌妒
撒莱真的很坏。”
事情真的是这样吗？
我们不知道全部的情况
但夏甲在旷野时
请看创世记16:9
这里说
“耶和华的天使对她说
你要回到你主母那里去
在她手下谦卑自抑。”
“回家去吧！
只要你谦卑
一切都会没事的。”
你发现他们为什么不和吗？
请看第4节
“夏甲见自己怀孕，就轻看主母。”
《现代中文译本修订版》说
夏甲“瞧不起”撒莱
觉得自己更优越
结果呢？
撒拉就把夏甲赶走了
虽然夏甲的态度不好
但撒拉可能也没给她好脸色看
这件事耶和华觉得是谁的责任呢？
夏甲
因为耶和华跟她说
“你要回到你主母那里去
在她手下谦卑自抑。”
这个记载是个很好的提醒
有时候不和睦的真正原因可能是自己的问题
也许是我们没有表现谦卑的态度
导致大家不和睦
或许我们给别人一种
“我的想法、做法比你们好”的感觉
我们不完美
可能会骄傲、不谦卑
觉得自己比别人好
为什么克服这些不完美的倾向很重要呢？
因为耶和华不喜欢这种态度
而且就像我们刚才提过的
不谦卑会破坏弟兄姐妹的关系，失去和平
没有和平，圣灵就没有办法作用在我们身上
没有圣灵，我们就失去上帝的帮助
没有上帝的帮助，我们就会失败
《上帝的王国统治了！》这本书里
有一句话说得很好
在120页第9段
我们办公室的白板上
就写着这句话来提醒大家
“任何有秩序的组织如果不是建基于和平
就迟早会垮台
要让秩序维持下去
就非得有上帝所赐的和平不可。”
说得很好，不是吗？
“任何有秩序的组织如果不是建基于和平
就迟早会垮台。”
在会众也好，在家里也好
在伯特利或在工地也好
不管在哪里
这句话都对我们很有用
我们工作时遇到的困难再大、再难解决
我们都不担心
唯一担心的是同工之间不和
如果一起工作的弟兄姐妹之间气氛紧张
或部门跟部门之间不和
这才是我们要担心的事
我们要赶快想办法
恢复和睦的关系
如果大家是和睦的
不管难题多大、多难解决
这都不是什么问题
工作都能顺利进行
我们很喜欢在这里工作
可是一旦没有了和平
我们的工作就不能顺利进行
我们看别人比自己优越
这对耶和华来说有多么重要呢？
我们努力跟别人保持和睦
耶和华怎么看这件事呢？
他有什么感觉呢？
我们一起看看一节经文
“喜见我正义得以伸张的人
愿他们欢呼欣喜
愿他们常说
要尊耶和华为大
他喜见他的仆人平安。”
耶和华希望他的仆人得享平安
看到他的仆人团结、和睦地一起工作
耶和华会很高兴
而我们想要团结、和睦
就一定要表现谦卑
愿我们每一个人
都努力将今天的经文运用出来
看别人比自己优越
愿我们努力跟所有人保持和睦
我们一定不希望
耶和华突然哪天问我们说
“你们在吵什么呢？”

ko.text: 고등학교 때 한 대학교에서 입학 제의를 받았어요.
그 기회를 놓치면 정말 후회할 거라고 했어요.
이웃집 아주머니들이 찾아와서 엄마한테 이렇게 말하곤 했어요.
전 인생을 어떻게 사는 게 좋을지 생각해 봤어요.
저희 회중에는 야외 봉사를 돕기 위해
그분들을 보면서 저도 영적인 목표를 갖게 됐고,
아빠는 항상 여호와를 실재하는 분으로 여기도록 도와주셨는데,
봉사하면서 있었던 일이나 봉사가 얼마나 즐거운지
그래서 고등학교를 졸업하자마자 저도 파이오니아를 시작했어요.
전 영적인 일을 우선순위에 두려고 노력해요.
이 일로 필요한 생활비를 벌 수 있죠.
하지만 봉사하러 나가서 성서 연구생들과 어린아이들이
성경의 말씀을 잘 듣고 반응을 나타내는 걸 보면
사람들이 성경을 진심으로 배우고 싶어 하는 걸 보면
여호와께서 저에게 멋진 미래와 또 행복한 희망을 주고 싶어 하신다는
그게 사람들의 압력을 이겨 내는 데 도움이 됐죠.
전 성서 연구 네 건을 사회하고 있습니다.
성서 연구를 하시면서 정기적으로 집회에 참석하고 계시죠.
제가 정말 만족스럽고 행복한 삶을 살고 있다는 생각이 듭니다.

en.text: I received an offer to enter a university to further my studies.
So my teachers and friends tried to persuade me
to just take the offer.
Don’t miss out on this golden opportunity.
After we returned home
from preaching or from meetings,
women from our neighborhood
used to come to our home and say things like:
“Why are you doing this to your child?
“She is such a good girl,
“and she studies so well.
“So why can’t you
send her to a good college?”
So I asked myself,
‘What would I like to do with my life?’
When I saw brothers and sisters
moving into my congregation
to assist in the field ministry,
this helped me to set and pursue
spiritual goals so that I could eventually
pioneer in my congregation.
In all things, my father always helped us
to view Jehovah as a real person.
Also, as for my mother,
she serves as a regular pioneer.
She shares the experiences she has had
and the joy she has felt in the ministry.
So soon after completing high school, I started pioneering.
To live a simple life, I work on a vegetable farm.
And this work provides me with income that is just sufficient.
Even though this work is difficult and tiring,
when I go out to preach
and when I meet with the Bible students as well as the young ones
who love and appreciate the Bible truth,
it refreshes my heart to see them—their desire
and their eagerness to learn about the Bible.
Jeremiah 29:11 helped me to overcome
pressures from others with the firm belief that Jehovah
is thinking of giving me a nice future
and a beautiful hope.
Now I have four Bible studies, and my father,
who is not a Witness,
also regularly attends meetings and studies the Bible.
All these blessings have helped me to see
that this life provides true satisfaction and true happiness.
Choosing to serve Jehovah was the best decision
I have made in my life.

cn.text: 我得到保送大学的资格
有机会可以继续升学
老师、同学都一直劝我
要把握这个机会
他们说
“这么好的机会，千万别错过！”
我们传道后、或聚会结束后
邻居阿姨常常来我们家跟我妈说
“你为什么让你女儿做这些事？
她那么乖，功课也很好
为什么不让她念大学呢？”
所以我就想
“我这一生到底要做什么？”
每次我看到有弟兄姐妹搬来我们会众传道
扩大服务，就让我更想追求属灵的目标
后来我也开始做正规先驱了
爸爸常常鼓励我
要把耶和华当做自己最好的朋友
还有我妈，她是正规先驱
她常常跟我说她传道时发生的事
而且传道让她很开心
所以，我高中毕业后不久
就开始做正规先驱了
为了让生活简单一点
我找到一个蔬菜农场的工作
这个工作让我有足够的收入可以生活
虽然工作很辛苦又很累
但每次我出去传道
或见到圣经学生和喜爱真理的年轻人
看到他们打从心里真的很想了解圣经
我就觉得一点都不辛苦了
耶利米书29:11
帮助我克服别人给的压力
也让我更相信耶和华说的美好未来
和希望一定会实现
现在我有四个圣经学生
我爸爸虽然还不是耶和华见证人
但他常常参加聚会
也开始学习圣经
这些福分让我看出
这样的生活才能得到真正的满足
和真正的快乐！
选择事奉耶和华
是我这一生做过最棒的决定！
