title: 용기를 약화시키는 것과 용기를 강화시켜 주는 것

ko.text: 리아, 이렇게 같이 살게 되니까 좋다.
얼마나 있을진 모르겠지만, 엄마 힘들게는 안 할게요.
머리 아프다고 했는데, 한번 가 볼게요.
우린 네가 정말 잘하고 있다고 생각해.
정말요? 애들 아빠랑 헤어지고 다 엉망인데요.
애들 앞에선 힘든 티 안 내려고 하는데요,
너한테 무슨 성구를 읽어 주면 힘이 좀 날까 생각해 봤는데,
이 구절이 도움이 될 것 같았어.
하지만 다시 용기를 낼 수 있어.
그 비결은 첫 문장에 나오는 것처럼
우리가 가지고 있는 희망에 대해 묵상하면
지금 우리에게 필요한 용기를 기르는 데 도움이 되지.
어떤 어려움도 이겨 낼 수 있어.
뭐, 아침에 봉사 나갔다가 그냥 집에서 책 읽으려고요.
아니, 왜 친구들하고 좀 만나서 놀지 않고?
우리 회중 사람들 리아랑 애들한테 너무 신경 안 써 주는 거 아니에요?
당신 말대로 두 달밖에 안 됐잖아.
아니에요, 여보. 내 말 좀 들어 봐요.
솔직히 우리 테이샤처럼 착한 애가 어디 있어요.
근데 테이샤가 지금 친구를 못 사귀고 있어요.
지금 우리 애들이 얼마나 힘든데, 정말 속상해요!
지금 우리 애들이 얼마나 힘든데, 정말 속상해요!
왜요. 내가 애들 할머니라서 과민 반응한다는 거예요?
근데 그런 생각이 들 때 우린
다들 최선을 다하고 있다는 걸 기억해야 돼.
옛날에 당신 아팠을 때 기억 안 나?
그때 정말 힘들었는데 우릴 많이 도와줬잖아.
우리가 의지할 분은 여호와지 사람이 아니야.
우리 예전에 감사한 일 매일 세 가지씩 말하기 했었잖아,
우리 그거 다시 한번 해 볼까?
난 벌써 오늘 여호와께 감사해야 할 일이 하나 떠올랐어.
두 사람 바쁠 텐데 초대해 줘서 정말 고마워요.
리아 자매랑 교제할 수 있어서 저희가 좋죠.
예전부터 초대하고 싶었는데, 이제야 기회가 됐네요.
저기, 조용히 좀 해 줄래? 영화 좀 보자.
저기, 조용히 좀 해 줄래? 영화 좀 보자.
손자랑 같이 이웃 분들을 만나 뵙고 있던 ....
당신들 책 몇 권 봤는데, 다 옛날 과학 내용만 있더만.
뭘 제대로 알고 책을 쓰는 거예요?
시간이 지나면 새로운 과학적 사실들이 밝혀지기 마련이죠.
근데, 불변의 진리가 들어 있는 책이 있는데,
더스틴, 이사야 40:22을 펴서 여기 교수님께 읽어 드릴래?
“그분은 둥근 땅 위에 거하시며, 땅에 사는 사람들은 메뚜기와 같다.
와. 전 집주인이 너무 세게 나와서 약간 겁이 났어요.
주의 종들이 아주 담대하게 주의 말씀을 계속 전하게 해 주십시오.”
그러니까 우린 절대 진리를 부끄러워할 필요가 없어.
누나 온다는 얘기 듣고 진짜 반가웠어.
주말 근무랑 야근도 가끔 있긴 하지만.
열심히 벌어야 누나도 빨리 집 사지.
내가 대신 결정해 줄 순 없어.
또 도와주고 싶어 하는 건 나도 알지.
그런데 잭슨은 여호와를 섬기고 있지 않잖아.
함께 더 많은 시간을 보내게 되겠지.
내 일자리 신경 써 줘서 고마워.
아빠 때문이 아니라 내가 결정한 거야.
난 일 때문에 영적인 것들을 희생할 순 없어.
근데 애들한테 돈 많이 벌란 얘긴 또 안 했으면 좋겠어.
난 우리 애들을 영적으로 키울 거니까.
“오 여호와여, 내게 당신의 길을 가르쳐 주십시오.
나의 원수들이 있으니, 나를 올바른 행로로 인도해 주십시오.”
사장님이 오늘 좀 일찍 나와 달래요.
근데 제가 할아버지 서재 써서 죄송해요.
이렇게 밖에 있으면 개인 연구도 더 잘되고 좋아.
괜찮아. 네 취향이 어떻든 우린 이해해.
괜찮아. 네 취향이 어떻든 우린 이해해.
하지만 여호와께서는 모세가 혼자가 아니라고 하셨습니다.
그분은 ‘내가 너와 함께 있을 것’ 이라고 약속하셨습니다.”
사람들한테 성경을 가르쳐 주는 일을 하고 있거든.
성경? 하, 야 그건 옛날 책이야.
성경은 미래에 대한 희망을 주는 책이야.
근데 애들 반응은 별로 안 좋았어요.
넌 여호와를 정말 기쁘게 해 드린 거야.
저번에 너 성경 가르치는 일 한다고 했지?
나도 엄마 돌아가시기 전에 엄마랑 같이 성경 읽었었거든.
그래서 말인데 나도 너한테 성경 좀 배울 수 있을까?
혹시 성경에서 부활에 대해 알려 준다는 거 알아?
하지만 용기를 나타내는 게 항상 쉽지만은 않습니다.
오래전에 아내가 많이 아파서 병원에 입원한 적이 있었습니다.
아내가 입원해 있는 몇 달 동안,
갓 태어난 아들과 어린 딸을 혼자 돌봐야 했죠.
간절히 기도했지만 아무 응답이 없는 것 같았습니다.
믿음이 약해지기 시작했고 이런저런 의심이 들었죠.
심지어 여호와의 약속에 대한 확신까지 약해졌습니다.
다윗이 쓴 시편 27편을 읽어 보라고 격려해 줬어요.
처음엔 별로 내키지 않았지만 나중에 읽어 봤죠.
그 말씀을 읽고 정말로 큰 감동을 받았습니다.
그래서 시편 27편에 있는 말씀을 계속 읽고 묵상했습니다.
왜 지금도 용기를 기르기 위해 노력하고 있다고 하신 거죠?
저도 살아오면서 다른 사람들을 많이 도와 왔죠.
못 보게 될 거라는 말을 들었어요.
앞으론 예전처럼 회중 일을 많이 할 수 없을 거라는 생각을 하니까,
다른 사람들한테 용기를 내라고 말하는 건
어떤 어려움도 이겨 낼 수 있어.
“여호와는 나의 빛, 나의 구원” 이라고 했잖아.
넌 여호와를 정말 기쁘게 해 드린 거야.
하지만 정작 자신이 용기를 내는 건 쉽지 않죠.
그럼 용기를 기르기 위해 어떻게 하고 계신지 말씀해 주실 수 있나요?
성경의 지침을 생활에 적용하고 집회에 빠지지 않고 참석하고
또 우리의 희망에 대해 열심히 전파하고 있습니다.
그럼 최근에 특히 마음에 와닿았던 성구가 있으신가요?
“믿음이 없이는 하느님을 기쁘시게 할 수 없습니다.
하느님께 가까이 가는 사람은 그분이 계시다는 것과
상 주시는 분이라는 것을 믿어야 합니다.”
전 제가 앞을 보지 못하게 되더라도
믿음의 눈으로 계속 여호와를 찾고 바라볼 겁니다.
벤저민 형제, 우리 모두의 용기를 강화시켜 주는 회견에 감사합니다!

en.text: We made it.
Come on, y’all.
It’ll be good. You’ll see.
Go out and meet her.
Thank you, Taysha.
Dustin?
OK, talk to me.
There’s nothing to talk about.
I know this whole move hasn’t been easy.
But it’s only temporary until we’re able to get back on our feet.
It’s not just the move.
It’s everything. It’s all upside down.
The good thing is, we’re not alone.
We have help, and it’s the best kind of help
because it comes from Jehovah, and he will never let you down.
But it’s up to you to give him a chance.
We’re in this together, OK?
Leah, we’re so happy that you are all here with us.
Thanks, Mom.
I don’t know how long we’ll be here, but we’ll try to help out as much as we can.
You stay with us as long as you need to.
Thanks, Dad.
I thought Taysha would be down by now.
She said she had a headache.
I’ll go check on her.
Leah.
Hey, Dad.
Is everything OK?
Oh, yeah. Everything is fine.
You’re doing a wonderful job, you know.
Am I?
Ever since Scott left us, nothing has been right.
Leah, it’s not your fault.
Scott left Jehovah.
And now losing my job—
I’m trying so hard to be strong for the kids,
but, Dad, inside I . . .
You know, Leah, the Scriptures are so encouraging
and helpful in situations like this.
Please read for me Psalm 27:14.
“Hope in Jehovah; be courageous and strong of heart.
Yes, hope in Jehovah.”
I don’t feel very courageous, Dad.
But you can be, Leah, dear.
The key is in the first sentence of that verse:
“Hope in Jehovah.”
You see, meditating on our hope
enables us to build courage right now.
And with courage like that,
you’ll be able to meet any challenge.
You’ll see.
Taysha,
come taste this for me, please.
Mmm. Smells good.
Mhm, that tastes good.
Thanks.
Maybe add just a little bit more cumin.
OK.
So any plans for this weekend?
Well, I’m going to get an early start out in service
and then come home and finish my book.
Don’t you want to go out with some friends and have some fun?
Yeah, that would be nice.
Well, what’s the matter?
Well, first you need friends.
Oh, this must be about my job interview.
I’ll be right back.
OK.
Ben?
Yes?
I need to talk to you.
Why hasn’t the congregation taken more of an interest
in Leah and the kids?
It’s been two months.
We’ve invited people over to our home.
But it’s as you said, it’s only been two months.
No, Ben, that’s not it.
When I was out in service this morning,
I heard that someone invited the Campbells over.
They just moved here!
I know I’m being biased,
but I can’t think of a sweeter girl than Taysha.
And the fact that she’s having a hard time finding friends?
They’ve all been through so much!
It just hurts!
I expected more.
They’ve all been through so much!
It just hurts!
I expected more.
Well, you know what I think?
What?
That I’m completely overreacting as a grandmother?
No, no.
You’re— you’re a wonderful grandmother,
and you’re probably right.
But although we may feel justified,
we have to remember that the congregation
is made up of imperfect people,
and they’re doing the best they can.
I know that.
They’re going to have their failing moments,
but they’ll have their shining ones also
—like when you were sick years ago.
We both needed them, and they were there for us.
It reminds me of what the psalmist said:
“Jehovah is my light and my salvation.”
And notice, he said: “Jehovah,” not people.
True.
OK, I’m going to try and leave it in Jehovah’s hands.
I do trust Jehovah.
Now, that’s my Abby.
Hey, remember when we used to recount
three things every day that we were thankful for?
Why don’t we start doing that again?
OK, that sound like a good idea.
And I can already think of one thing
I’m thankful for today, and that’s you.
Here you go. Here’s a plate for you.
Oh, thank you.
Thank you.
You’re welcome.
You know, we really appreciate the both of you inviting us over.
It’s our pleasure.
We really love having Leah and the kids with us.
Actually, we’ve been wanting to do this for quite a while.
But we just haven’t had the chance until now.
We appreciate it.
Come on.
Thanks again, Grandpa, for a fun service morning.
You have any plans for later?
Yeah, I’m meeting some friends later at the movie theater.
Ah, have a good time.
Thanks.
Jamin, pass the popcorn.
Trade. Give me that.
Hey, this looks kind of . . .
Doesn’t this bother you?
Don’t let it freak you out.
Look, I just think maybe we need to leave.
No way! I’m not losing my money.
I really think we need to leave.
Hey, what’s going on?
Dustin is all freaked out because of this scene.
It’s just this scene.
Yeah, dude, just chill.
Hey, I’m trying to watch a movie.
Let’s cut the chit-chat.
I’m sorry.
Yeah, dude, just chill.
Hey, I’m trying to watch a movie.
Let’s cut the chit-chat.
I’m sorry.
Good morning, Sir.
My grandson and I would like to share an encouraging . . .
Look, Jehovah’s Witnesses, right?
I’m going to save you some trouble.
I’m a professor.
And I’ve read some of your books, but the science in them is really out-of-date.
Why do you people insist on writing about things you don’t understand?
It is true, Sir,
that over time, scientific research can become out-of-date.
But you know, there’s a book that is never out-of-date,
the Bible.
Dustin, would you please read
Isaiah 40:22 for the gentleman?
“There is One who dwells above the circle of the earth,
“and its inhabitants are like grasshoppers.
He is stretching out the heavens like a fine gauze.”
Wow! That ended so much better than I expected.
He was so intimidating.
It’s normal to feel that way, Dustin.
I’ve even had those feelings.
Even the apostles have had their moments.
I’d like to show you something.
It’s in Acts chapter 4.
Would you find that and read Acts 4:29?
Let’s see what the apostles prayed for.
“And now, Jehovah, give attention to their threats,
and grant to your slaves to keep speaking your word with all boldness.”
You see the point, Dustin?
Jehovah helped the apostles, and he’s going to help us.
So we never ever have to feel ashamed of the truth.
I’m out of here.
Dustin?
I’m not going back, Jamin.
Yeah, I know. Me neither.
My mom’s going to come and pick me up.
You want a ride?
Yeah, sure.
All right.
Mom, dinner was very good, thank you.
You’re welcome.
You know, it really is good to see you all.
Five years is a long time.
It is.
When Dad told me you were coming, I couldn’t wait to see you.
I have gifts.
Oh, it’s beautiful!
Thank you.
You’re welcome.
What? This is the latest model!
Thanks, Uncle Jackson.
You’re welcome.
Wow, this is very . . .
. . . professional.
Professional.
I want you to come and work for me.
I don’t know what to say.
I just want to help.
So let me.
It’s entry-level, but with benefits and bonuses.
What are the hours? Anything like yours?
Not as intense, but full-time —weekends, evenings too.
But you’ll be able to save money,
buy a home.
Hmm.
I got a job for you too.
What?
You could even buy a car.
Wow.
And anytime you want to come to the agency, it’s open.
We’ll make it a family business.
Nice.
This is work. Excuse me.
Can you two help me with the dishes?
I could use the job, Dad.
Would it be so bad to work the extra hours?
I can’t make that decision for you.
Your brother loves you very much,
and he genuinely wants to help.
But as you know, he never made the truth his own.
I know.
So you’ve got to figure out
if his offer is worth the cost.
Remember, extra hours
means extra association.
And Proverbs 13:20 says:
“The one walking with the wise
will become wise.”
Oh, yeah, I got you. All right.
Hey look, I have to go. I’ll talk to you later.
Leah.
Jackson, I want to thank you for offering to give me a job.
You got it. I’ll set up an interview.
But I have to turn it down.
Dad talked to you, didn’t he?
This isn’t coming from Dad.
It’s coming from me.
I just can’t sacrifice spiritual things for material ones.
I hope you can understand.
Jackson, I love you. We all do.
And we want to see you come back and visit us.
But please, for my sake,
don’t promote different goals for the kids when you come.
I’m trying hard to help them set spiritual priorities. OK?
All right.
It’s been a while, but come on give me a hug.
You know I’m keeping the bag, right?
OK.
“Instruct me in your way, O Jehovah,
lead me in the path of uprightness because of my foes.”
Good morning.
“Do not hand me over to my adversaries.”
Taysha! You’re up early.
Yeah, they called and asked if I could do a double shift today.
I see.
Grandpa, I’m sorry you had to give up your office space for me.
Don’t be, Taysha.
Besides, this suits me better.
For me, being outside makes personal study more enjoyable.
Well, I hope you enjoy the rest of your day, and I’ll see you later.
Thanks, we’ll see you when you get back.
OK.
Oh, hey, I found you.
Oh, hey. Yeah, I decided to take my break outside.
OK, cool. Well, when you get back, Denise was looking for you.
OK, thanks.
I’m making this dressing, but I think that it’s just missing something.
Can you try it?
Yeah, of course.
Mmm, maybe a little bit more lemon.
More lemon, OK.
Yeah.
Do you want me to help you?
Sure. OK.
Sweet.
Hey, can I borrow some of your hot pepper flakes?
Yeah, sure.
Sorry.
It’s OK.
Sorry about that.
Coming out.
Coming in.
That’s my salad?
Yep.
All right, everybody. I think that was the last plate.
Really?
Mhm-mhm.
All right, let’s clean up and get out of here.
Sounds good to me.
Hey, are you going to come with us?
Oh, thanks, Denise. But, no, I don’t think so.
Come on.
Don’t say no again.
I’m sorry.
I have other plans.
Oh, you have other plans. Huh?
Oh, I get it.
You have a secret boyfriend or girlfriend.
Wait. What?
Come on.
Whatever you’re into, it’s all right with us.
Just let us in on it.
What’s the deal?
Whatever you’re into, it’s all right with us.
Just let us in on it.
What’s the deal?
“Moses must have felt inadequate
“and incapable.
“But God assured him that he would not be alone.
‘I will prove to be with you,’ said Jehovah.”
Look, I don’t have a boyfriend or a girlfriend.
I have a Bible study.
I’m one of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
and we volunteer our time to help people learn about the Bible.
The Bible?
Come on. That book is ancient.
It closes your mind to new ideas.
Actually, it doesn’t.
It gives people a wonderful hope for the future.
Well, I believe we make our own future.
I’m sorry you don’t feel the same.
Come on.
Let’s go.
Bye.
So I told them I was one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
I’m just glad they know now.
We’re so proud of you for standing up like that.
Yeah, I surprised myself.
I just wish it ended a little bit better.
No matter the response, you made Jehovah happy today.
Thanks, Grandpa.
Hey.
Hey.
Uh, the other day, you said something about
—that you do Bible studies.
And it reminded me of something
my mom and I used to do together before she died.
She would read the Bible to me before bed.
So I was wondering
if you would show me what you show other people?
Of course. I’m really sorry to hear that about your mom.
Did you know that the Bible actually gives us a hope for a resurrection?
It’s here.
Next, we have Brother Ben Matthews with us.
Brother Matthews,
you’ve been able to raise a family, serve as an elder,
and pioneer for many years.
What a good example of faith and courage!
Thank you, Brother Nicoletti.
But truthfully,
courage isn’t something that comes easy to me.
I have to keep working on it.
Why is that?
Well, I remember years ago
when my wife, Abby, became very ill.
She was in the hospital for months
while I cared for our newborn son and young daughter.
I didn’t know if she would ever recover.
I prayed and prayed,
and it appeared as if nothing changed.
I could feel my faith
beginning to crack and give way to doubt.
I even started doubting Jehovah’s promises for the future.
So, what changed that?
A friend stepped in at the right time.
He encouraged me when I was home alone to read David’s words
at Psalm 27.
At first, I didn’t want to.
But eventually I did,
and something about those words
touched my heart.
You see, like a plant deprived of water,
I was starving my faith.
So I kept reading and meditating
on those words in Psalm 27,
and eventually my doubts began to melt away.
But as you mentioned, Brother Matthews,
that was decades ago.
But you said courage is something that you’re continuing to work on.
Well, for much of my life I’ve had to help other people be courageous.
But recently,
I found out that soon I will go blind.
Between this and not being able to do
as much in the congregation as I used to,
well, I could feel those doubts creeping up again.
I think it’s easier to help others
be courageous.
You’ll be able to meet any challenge.
“Jehovah is my light and my salvation.”
Jehovah helped the apostles,
and he’s going to help us.
No matter the response,
you made Jehovah happy today.
It’s harder to be courageous for yourself.
We empathize with you, Brother Matthews.
Can you tell us what you’re doing right now to build courage?
Absolutely.
Here’s my prescription:
regular prayer and study,
application of the Bible’s guidance,
attending as many meetings as I can,
and, of course, preaching to others about our hope.
That’s a very good prescription.
Is there a particular scripture that has meaning for you right now?
Right now, it’s Hebrews 11:6.
It says: “Moreover,
“without faith it is impossible
“to please God well,
“for whoever approaches God
“must believe that he is
“and that he becomes the rewarder
of those earnestly seeking him.”
So even if I lose my eyesight,
Brother Nicoletti, I will continue to seek Jehovah
with my family
and my eyes of faith.
Thank you, Brother Matthews, for being such a good example of courage!

title: 우리의 조직이 이루고 있는 일들—우리의 봉사를 더 효과적으로 수행함

ko.text: 우리는 역사상 가장 큰 규모의 전파 활동에 참여하고 있습니다!
고린도 전서 9:26에는 이러한 의미 깊은 말이 나옵니다.
우리가 시간과 활력을 더 효과적으로 사용해
최대한 많은 사람에게 전파하도록 돕기 위해 노력해 왔습니다.
우리의 전파 활동에 대한 일부 조정이
중앙장로회는 야외 봉사의 초점을 조정하고자 합니다.
여러 해 동안, 우리는 잡지를 전하는 활동을 강조했습니다.
하지만 그건 우리가 하는 봉사의 초점이 아닙니다.
그리고 봉사에서 사용할 도구가 너무 많아서
봉사 도구함에 몇 가지 도구만 있으면 됩니다.
“가서 모든 민족의 사람들을 제자로 삼으라”고 명령하셨습니다.
우리가 초점을 맞춰야 할 일이 이겁니다.
“영원한 생명을 얻기에 합당한 성향을 가진” 사람들을 찾는 거죠.
사람들이 결정을 내려야 할 이 시기에
우린 배운 대로 행동할 사람들을 찾아야 합니다.
집주인의 주의를 성경으로 이끄는 데 더 노력을 들이게 됐어요.
그냥 출판물에 나오는 말을 전하는 게 아니라,
사람들이 자기 성경을 직접 보도록 도와주고 있죠.
어떤 사람은 종교심은 있지만 우리 출판물은 절대 받지 않아요.
그런데 이제는 성경에 주의를 이끄니까 더 잘 듣더라고요.
또 이 마련 덕분에 몇몇 새로운 전도인들은
그래서 전보다 봉사도 더 많이 하고 싶어 해요.
이러한 조정에 대해 중앙장로회에 정말 감사합니다.
그리고 준비한 서론을 자주 쓰다 보니까
그리고 예전에는 필요한 출판물이 있어서 가방을 한참 뒤지다가
결국 찾지 못할 때가 종종 있었는데,
봉사 도구함에 잘 정리돼 있으니까 정말 편리합니다.
화면을 한 번만 누르면 필요한 출판물을 금방 찾을 수 있죠.
서론을 준비하는 게 전보다 많이 쉬워졌어요.
성서 연구를 시작하는 데 도움이 되죠.
봉사 도구함에 있는 동영상과 출판물을 사용해
언제든지 어렵지 않게 대화를 시작할 수 있어요.
전에는 집주인의 필요에 딱 맞는 걸 찾기가 좀 어려웠는데요,
봉사 도구함에서 쉽게 찾을 수 있어서 너무 좋습니다.
그리고 봉사 때나 성서 연구 때 들고 다니는 가방이
봉사 도구함 덕분에 더 쉽고 효과적으로 봉사할 수 있게 됐죠.
더 많은 사람에게 진리를 전하기 위해
이 도구함을 계속 잘 사용하고 싶어요.
잘 발전하지 않는 몇몇 성서 연구들을 중단했습니다.
그래서 이제는 진심으로 관심을 보이는 사람들을 돕는 데
성서 연구를 잘 준비하고, 집회에 참석하거나
집회에 참석하려는 마음이 있는 사람들 말이죠.
마리아는 여러 해 동안 연구를 하다 안 하다 했는데,
성서 연구를 다시 하고 싶다고 얘기했어요.
그래서 새로운 마련에 대해 알려 주면서
이젠 정말로 여호와를 섬기고 싶어 하는 사람들을 돕는 데
이제는 가족과 이웃에게 비공식 증거도 해요.
이젠 우리의 초점이 하나로 맞춰져 있어요.
우리의 시간과 활력을 더 효과적으로 사용한다면
여호와의 지원과 축복을 받게 될 것입니다.

ko.text: 왜 그런지 뚜렷한 이유를 알 때도 있지만
그 이유를 잘 모를 때도 있을 거야.
뚜렷한 이유는 없어 보이는데 우울한 기분에 휩싸일 때
첫째로, 부모님이나 친구같이 가까운 사람한테 말할 수 있어.
심한 고통을 겪을 때 자기 심정을 솔직하게 말했어.
너가 우울한 감정에서 빠져나오게 도와줄 수 있을 거야.
둘째로, 너의 생각을 글로 한번 적어 봐.
“실용적인 지혜와 사고력을 잘 지키라”고 알려 줘.
감정을 글로 적어 보는 건 그렇게 하는 데 도움이 되지.
글로 적으면 왜 그런 감정이 드는지 분석해 볼 수 있고,
그러다 보면 문제가 작아 보일 수 있어.
셋째로, 성경에선 기도로 자신의 문제를 하느님께 이야기하면
우리의 마음과 정신력을 지켜 줄’ 거라고 말하지.
마지막으로, 성경을 읽는 게 정말 도움이 돼.
성경에 나오는 좋은 말씀으로 생각을 채우면
근데 그래도 우울한 기분이 사라지지 않으면 어떡하지?
내가 아무 쓸모도 없는 사람이란 생각이 드니?
병원에 한번 가 보고 싶다고 부모님께 말씀드려 봐.
병원에 가면 너가 혹시 우울증에 걸린 건 아닌지
만약 우울증에 걸렸다 해도 부끄러워할 필요 없어.
병원 치료를 받으면 우울한 감정이 줄어들 수 있고
다른 사람의 도움을 받으면서 열심히 노력하면
깊은 구덩이 같은 우울한 감정에서 빠져나올 수 있어.
우울한 감정도 결국 사라질 수 있단 걸 꼭 기억해.

어른이 돼서도 큰 도움이 될 거야.
부모님이나 믿을 만한 친구들의 도움을 받으면
우울한 감정을 이겨 낼 수 있어.

en.text: Everyone gets sad now and then.
Do you?
In some cases, you may know the cause;
in other cases, you may not.
Even if there doesn’t seem to be a cause,
what can you do when sadness
holds you in its grip?
First, find someone to talk to about it,
such as a parent or close friend.
In the midst of his turmoil,
Job, a faithful man in Bible times, said:
“I will speak out in my bitter distress!”
When someone knows what you’re going through,
he or she can lower the rope
and pull you out of the pit.
Here’s another idea:
Why not put your thoughts on paper?
At Proverbs 3:21, the Bible tells us
to “safeguard practical wisdom
and thinking ability.”
Writing about your feelings can help you do that.
Once they’re on paper,
you can sort them out,
and then the sadness can be less overpowering.
A third suggestion:
The Bible says that if you pray about your concerns,
‘the peace of God that surpasses all understanding
will guard your hearts and thoughts.’
So don’t forget prayer.
Last but certainly not least,
reading the Bible can help
—especially the book of Psalms.
Filling your mind with positive thoughts from the Bible
can have a positive effect on your feelings.
But what if your feelings just won’t go away?
What if you’ve lost interest in just about all activities
that you used to find exciting?
What if you seem to have no appetite,
have trouble sleeping,
and suffer from intense feelings of worthlessness?
If symptoms persist,
why not talk to your parents
about getting a checkup?
A physician can help determine
if your sadness has a medical cause,
such as clinical depression.
If you do suffer from clinical depression,
it is nothing to be ashamed of.
With treatment,
many sufferers have begun to feel better
—perhaps even the best they have felt in a long time.
So whether your sadness is caused by depression or not,
with assistance and effort,
you can get out of the deep pit of sadness.
Remember,
feelings are temporary; they will pass.
And if you can learn to deal with them now,
you’ll be prepared to handle them as an adult.
By taking things a day at a time
and relying on the support of your parents
and trustworthy friends,
you can go from sad
to glad.

cn.text: 每个人都会有心情低落的时候
你也是吗？
有时候你知道原因
但有时候你不知道
那你可以怎样摆脱情绪的束缚呢？
一个方法是找个人聊聊
例如家人或好朋友
圣经里有个好人名叫约伯
他在人生中最痛苦的时候
也把自己的烦恼和感受说出来
如果你让别人知道自己的感受
他们或许能伸出援手
把你从悲伤的深谷中拉上来
你也可以试着把自己的想法写下来
圣经在箴言3:21劝我们
要有智慧也要保护思考力
把自己心中的感受写下来
可以帮助你理清头绪
这样，难过的感觉就不会那么强烈了
另外圣经说
只要你向上帝祷告
把心中的忧虑告诉他
上帝就会赐给你超乎想象的平安
守护你的内心和头脑
所以，要记得祷告哦！
还有一个方法也很有效，就是读圣经
比如你可以读读看诗篇
阅读圣经中鼓舞人心的话
能改善你的心情
可是，如果难过的情绪
赶也赶不走怎么办呢？
你对一向喜欢的事提不起劲吗？
你没有胃口吗？
睡也睡不好吗？
或老是觉得自己一无是处吗？
如果这样的情况迟迟没有改善
不妨跟爸妈商量一下去看医生
医生可以判断
你的情况是不是因为疾病造成的
例如抑郁症
假如你被诊断出得了抑郁症
不要感到难为情
很多患者在接受治疗后
不仅心情好多了
还能重拾快乐
不论你是因为什么原因感到难过
只要你接受别人的帮助
加上自己的努力
就可以从情绪的低谷中爬出来
要记得
情绪的波动起伏是暂时的
一定会有雨过天晴的时候
现在学会处理这些情绪
会让你一生受用
处理难过的情绪需要时间
但你不用着急
有父母和好朋友的支持
你一定可以破涕为笑

ko.text: 용감한 형제 자매들이 보여 준 믿음.

형제들이 체포됐을 때 그들을 변호해 준
새로운 시설들을 봉헌하게 되어 무척 기뻐했습니다.
그 시설들은, 주로 그 지역의 한 건물의
여섯 개 층에 자리 잡은 지부 시설,

jw.org 표지판을 들고 뱃지를 달고 있었죠.

다양한 나라에서 온 많은 손님들을 만나고
여러 해 동안, 우리는 양심적 병역 거부자인
우리 형제들을 위해 법적 투쟁을 했습니다.
그리고 단지 왕국 회관 하나를 갖기 위해서도
그런데 갑자기 지부 시설과 대회 회관과 학교 시설을
그냥 갖게 되다니, 저한텐 정말 믿기지 않는 일이죠.
축복을 실제로 쏟아 부으시는’ 것을 목격했습니다.

en.text: The story of Armenia
is a story of faith
—the faith of courageous brothers and sisters
who endured mob violence,
protests, and threats
from those who do not know God;
the faith of young brothers who were imprisoned
because they refused to compromise their neutrality;
and the faith of lawyers
who defended them when they were arrested.
In the early part of this period,
the work operated out of an office in a local brother’s home.
Today, the story is much different.
our brothers in Armenia were delighted to dedicate a group
of new facilities to accommodate future growth
—a branch facility
(mainly located on six floors of a local building),
a new Assembly Hall,
and also a school facility.
The dedication week started off with a welcome night,
where many traveled long distances to attend,
and some had not seen each other for a long time.
Well, we’ve never been to Armenia before,
and meeting the brothers and sisters was such an experience.
They gave us a really warm welcome.
When I was 90,
I decided, “No more Armenia.”
And now I’m 96, and Jehovah said,
“You’re going to Armenia.”
What a blessing!
It was amazing to see so many brothers and sisters from different countries,
and we enjoyed a very, very nice time with them.
Thanks to Jehovah, we really enjoyed this.
But the spiritual gems that we all enjoyed the most
were during the dedication program held at the end of the week.
The program was filled with reports and interviews
that touched our hearts,
and Brother Splane of the Governing Body gave the dedication talk.
Is it your desire to dedicate
the branch facilities, the Assembly Hall,
and the school facility to Jehovah today?
We could never have imagined such a thing happening five years ago.
From the time that we arrived at the airport
and we saw the brothers boldly holding up
the jw.org sign with their badges,
we were just so overwhelmed —so moved.
And I could feel as if I’m in the Paradise today
because we have so many guests from different countries,
and I could see their happy faces.
For many years, to be in courts
—in legal battles for our brothers as conscientious objectors
or to go to the court
for fighting a case for just one Kingdom Hall—
and suddenly to have a branch
and Assembly Hall and school facilities right away,
that’s for me kind of unbelievable.
Today is a great day
for Jehovah’s people in Armenia.
Truly, Jehovah has seen
the faithful obedience of our brothers and sisters in Armenia.
We have witnessed Jehovah ‘open the floodgates of the heavens
‘and actually empty out a blessing
until there is no more want.’

제가 세상에 속해 있지 않은 것처럼 그들도 세상에 속해 있지 않습니다.
그리고 저는 그들을 위해 저 자신을 거룩하게 하고 있습니다.
그것은 그들도 진리로 거룩해지게 하려는 것입니다.”
예수처럼, 생각과 행동 모두 세상에 속해 있지 말아야 해.
네! 제가 그런 확신을 갖게 해 준 내용이 있어요.
“이와 같이 여러분도 이 모든 일을 보거든
그가 문 앞에 가까이 있다는 것을 아십시오.”
그날이 왔을 때 우린 반드시 여호와의 편에 서 있어야 하죠.
이어지는 아침 숭배에서 중앙장로회의 앤서니 모리스 형제는
앞으로 있을 일들에 대해 왜 걱정할 필요가 없는지 설명합니다.
“사람이 거주하는 땅에 닥칠 일들에 대한 두려움과 예상 때문에
그리고 ‘하늘이 흔들리고’ 또 ‘사람의 아들을 본다’는 말이 나온 다음,
네, 아시는 것처럼, 이 예언은 큰 환난 중에 성취됩니다.
여기에 머지않아 있을 일이 예언되어 있습니다.
열 뿔은 “짐승[즉, 국제 연합]과 함께 한 시간”을 보낸 뒤에,
대다수의 사람은 믿기 어려워할 일일 겁니다.
하지만 열 뿔은 이렇게 할 것입니다.
‘어린양’은 주들의 주이며 왕들의 왕이므로 그들을 이길 것이다.
곧 부르심을 받고 선택된 충실한 사람들도 이길 것이다.”
오디오비디오 부서 형제들 실력이 아무리 좋아도,
아무도 이 사건을 영화로 촬영하지는 못할 것 같습니다.
그리고 왕 예수의 지시를 따르는 거룩한 천사들이 등장해야 하니까요.
앞으로 있을 이 사건을 영화로 만들려면
우린 이 사건들이 정확히 어떤 순서로 일어날지 모릅니다.
「파수대」 설명처럼 어떤 사건들은 서로 겹쳐서 일어날 수 있죠.
앞으로 어떤 사건으로 큰 환난이 시작될 것인가 하는 점입니다.
‘네가 본 물, 곧 매춘부가 앉아 있는 물은
네가 본 열 뿔과 짐승은 매춘부를 미워하여
파멸시키고 벌거벗겨서 그 살을 먹어 버릴 것이며,
그 여자를 불로 완전히 태워 버릴 것이다.’”
이 일이 일어나는 이유가 이제 17절에 나옵니다.
그분의 생각을 실행할 마음을 넣어 주셨기 때문이다.
자기들이 품은 하나의 생각을 실행하게 하신 것이다.”
사람들이 우리가 전하는 이 좋은 소식을 믿든 안 믿든 말이죠.
큰 환난의 시작인 거짓 종교 세계 제국의 멸망을 말하는 거니까요.
하느님의 백성에겐 희소식이 아닐 수 없습니다.
사람들은 그 일이 실제 일어나기 전엔 믿지 않겠지만,
그때는 여호와에 대한 우리의 사랑을 증명할 때죠.
우리는 하느님이 보호하시는 유일한 조직일 겁니다.
또 한 가지 의미심장한 내용이 이 「파수대」 기사에 나오는데,
“그때는 ‘왕국의 좋은 소식’을 전할 때가 아닐 것입니다.”
좋은 소식을 전하지 않을 때가 온다고요?
하느님의 백성의 마음과 정신에 새겨져 있는
“이 왕국의 좋은 소식이 모든 민족에게 증거되기 위해
사람이 거주하는 온 땅에 전파될 것입니다.”
그러니까 큰 환난 중에는 좋은 소식이 없죠.
“그리고 하늘에서 무게가 각각 한 달란트쯤 되는
사람들은 우박의 재앙이 매우 컸기 때문에
이건 거대한 우박이라고 여기 묘사되어 있죠.
완전히 멸망된다는 것을 선언하는 소식일 겁니다.
저도 최근에 어떤 구역에서 봉사해서 알지만,
예수처럼 우리 모두 필요한데, 호별 봉사가 도움이 되죠.
여러분이 현재 모욕을 당하는 것 같다면
즉 심판을 선언하는 일을 대비한 훈련이니까요.
그리고 「파수대」에서 언급한 다음의 사건도 기억하시기 바랍니다.
분명히 이해하기 위해 한번 찾아 보시죠.
그는 큰 나팔 소리와 함께 자기 천사들을 보낼 것이며,
그들은 선택된 자들을 하늘 이 끝에서 저 끝까지
처음 인장이나 최종 인장을 찍는 일이 아니죠.
이것은 남은 자들이 큰 환난 기간 중에
이 일은 곡의 공격이 시작된 이후
바로 그때에 마태 13:43의 이 말씀이 성취되죠.
정신이 번쩍 들면서도 정말 격려적인 내용입니다.
따라서 형제 여러분, 확신을 갖고 여호와를 신뢰합시다.
영적 일과를 계속 유지하면서 준비하고 있으십시오.
여호와의 날이 왔을 때 우린 보호를 받게 될 겁니다.
우리가 그리스도인 중립을 지키기 때문에 누리는 축복 중 하나입니다.
그들이 ‘세상에 속하지 않는’ 것 사이에 어떤 관련이 있는지 보여 줍니다.
여호와의 그 품 안에서 우린 하나야.
여호와의 그 품 안에서 우린 하나야.
이 노래는 원래 링갈라어로 쓰여진 노래입니다.
링갈라어는 아프리카의 콩고 민주 공화국과 콩고에서
이 노래를 링갈라어로 들어 보고 싶으시면,
거기서 오리지널송을 다양한 언어로 들어 보실 수 있습니다.
화면 오른쪽 맨 위에 있는 웹사이트 언어를
박해에도 불구하고 중립을 지킨 예를 살펴봤죠.
공공 행사에서 중립을 유지하는 것이 중요하다는 점도 배웠습니다.
그리고 중립에 관한 「파수대」 연구 기사를 적용하고 있는
모리스 형제는 여호와께서 세상을 심판하실 때
그리스도인 중립을 지킴으로 연합이라는 축복을 누리도록
그런데 뮤직 비디오에서 형제 자매들이 방송을 같이 보고,
한국에 있는 우리 형제 자매들을 만나 보시죠.
왕국 선포자들이 처음 이곳에 온 건 1912년입니다.
한국의 여호와의 증인들은 그 어느 편도 들지 않으면서
1만 9000명이 넘는 형제들이 믿음 때문에 수감 생활을 했습니다.
이 충실한 형제들에게 호의적인 판결을 내렸습니다.
형제들의 고통을 더 줄여 주기를 고대합니다.
회중 구역에는 약 2만 3000명의 주민이 살고 있으며,
휴전선 주변의 비무장 지대도 일부 포함되어 있습니다.
이 회중 구역에 있는 많은 사람은 외떨어진 마을들에 살고 있습니다.
형제 자매들은 군 부대에서 일하는 사람들을 자주 만나죠.
회중 구역이 휴전선과 가까운 곳이기 때문에,
버스를 타고 이곳을 관광하러 오는 사람들이 끊이지 않습니다.
그래서 형제들은 여러 장소에 전시대를 설치해서
방문객들에게 좋은 소식을 전하기 위해 노력합니다.
우리는 간성 회중의 형제 자매들을 매우 사랑합니다.
그곳의 우리 가족들이 전 세계 형제 자매들에게 사랑을 전합니다.

en.text: Welcome!
Here are some highlights from the program:
How should we act when our Christian neutrality is put to the test?
Do you know where to draw the line between being
a respectful observer and an active participant?
Join this family as these questions come up.
We’re confronted by the neutrality issue in all aspects of life.
What Bible principle should guide our thinking?
This month’s music video focuses
on the unity among our brothers and sisters.
As the world becomes more divided,
we become more united!
This is the March 2019 program of JW Broadcasting!
We begin by traveling to the country of Armenia,
which is located in the Caucasus
—a region situated at the border of Europe and Asia.
Despite facing persecution for many years,
our brothers and sisters in Armenia
have remained loyal to Jehovah.
The story of Armenia
is a story of faith
—the faith of courageous brothers and sisters
who endured mob violence,
protests, and threats
from those who do not know God;
the faith of young brothers who were imprisoned
because they refused to compromise their neutrality;
and the faith of lawyers
who defended them when they were arrested.
In the early part of this period,
the work operated out of an office in a local brother’s home.
Today, the story is much different.
our brothers in Armenia were delighted to dedicate a group
of new facilities to accommodate future growth
—a branch facility
(mainly located on six floors of a local building),
a new Assembly Hall,
and also a school facility.
The dedication week started off with a welcome night,
where many traveled long distances to attend,
and some had not seen each other for a long time.
Well, we’ve never been to Armenia before,
and meeting the brothers and sisters was such an experience.
They gave us a really warm welcome.
When I was 90,
I decided, “No more Armenia.”
And now I’m 96, and Jehovah said,
“You’re going to Armenia.”
What a blessing!
It was amazing to see so many brothers and sisters from different countries,
and we enjoyed a very, very nice time with them.
Thanks to Jehovah, we really enjoyed this.
But the spiritual gems that we all enjoyed the most
were during the dedication program held at the end of the week.
The program was filled with reports and interviews
that touched our hearts,
and Brother Splane of the Governing Body gave the dedication talk.
Is it your desire to dedicate
the branch facilities, the Assembly Hall,
and the school facility to Jehovah today?
We could never have imagined such a thing happening five years ago.
From the time that we arrived at the airport
and we saw the brothers boldly holding up
the jw.org sign with their badges,
we were just so overwhelmed —so moved.
And I could feel as if I’m in the Paradise today
because we have so many guests from different countries,
and I could see their happy faces.
For many years, to be in courts
—in legal battles for our brothers as conscientious objectors
or to go to the court
for fighting a case for just one Kingdom Hall—
and suddenly to have a branch
and Assembly Hall and school facilities right away,
that’s for me kind of unbelievable.
Today is a great day
for Jehovah’s people in Armenia.
Truly, Jehovah has seen
the faithful obedience of our brothers and sisters in Armenia.
We have witnessed Jehovah ‘open the floodgates of the heavens
‘and actually empty out a blessing
until there is no more want.’
Our theme this month is
“Christian Neutrality
“—What It Means, What It Takes,
and Why We Choose It.”
What is your opinion?
Where do you stand?
Can one person make a difference in countering injustice?
When we hear people discussing political topics,
we might at first think their conversation is purely philosophical;
but when injustice threatens our loved ones,
it can seem personal.
We expect that people will be divided over political ideology.
Revelation chapters 8-13 foretold that in the last days,
government would be the burning issue among mankind
and that people would feel pressured to take sides.
The question each of us needs to ask himself is,
How do I respond when people debate solutions to serious injustices?
As Christians, we’re most interested
in the example of Christ.
If ever there was a person who could make a difference in countering injustice,
it was Jesus.
He felt deep compassion for people.
And with his abilities to feed the hungry,
heal the sick, raise the dead, and reach hearts with his winsome words,
Jesus could have exerted invincible influence in the realm of politics.
He certainly had the opportunity to do so.
Satan was pleased to offer him
“all the kingdoms of the inhabited earth”
in an exchange for one act of worship.
But Jesus wouldn’t accept it.
Neither did he assert that Satan had no authority to make such an offer.
Later, Jesus’ own countrymen tried to make him king,
but he rejected that too.
Later still, someone asked him
whether it was lawful to pay taxes to the Roman government.
Again, Jesus didn’t take sides.
He refused to become a world ruler,
a national leader, or a political activist.
Did that mean that Jesus didn’t care? that he had no opinion?
To the contrary!
Jesus cared more deeply than we can fathom.
And by treating people fairly,
Jesus promoted justice at the most fundamental level.
Still, his principal focus
was on teaching people about the Kingdom of God,
which would eliminate injustice for all time.
So, what did Jesus indicate should be our position
regarding human governments?
We learn from Jesus’ response to the question about Roman taxation
as recorded at Mark 12:15-17:
“‘Bring me a denarius to look at.’
“They brought one, and he said to them:
“‘Whose image and inscription is this?’
“They said to him: ‘Caesar’s.’
“Jesus then said:
“‘Pay back Caesar’s things to Caesar,
but God’s things to God.’”
What are Caesar’s things?
At Romans 13:1-7,
the apostle Paul lists tax, tribute,
fear, and honor.
Notice, too, that Jesus said to “pay back Caesar’s things.”
What does that imply?
That Caesar, the ruling authority of the day,
had issued valuable things —coins, for example.
Thus, Caesar had the right to ask for some of those coins back.
This enabled the State to continue rendering necessary services.
Jesus acknowledged that.
On the other hand,
our most valuable possessions are grants from God himself
—such gifts as our heart, our life, our mind, and our strength.
We can’t give those things back to Caesar
because Caesar didn’t grant them to us in the first place.
We rightly give those things back to God
in the form of our dedication and our love.
Regarding our love for God, Jesus said at Mark 12:30:
“You must love Jehovah your God
“with your whole heart and with your whole soul
“and with your whole mind
and with your whole strength.”
So the love we give back to God is total
—no bodily part, function,
capacity, or desire being left out.
Those who love God take the side of Jesus,
whom Jehovah has appointed as King.
But how would Jesus’ disciples defend his Kingdom when people opposed it?
We gain insight from events that occurred
on the last night of Jesus’ life on earth.
Recall from Matthew chapter 26
that when “a large crowd with swords and clubs” came to arrest Jesus,
Peter “drew his sword and struck the slave of the high priest, taking off his ear.”
John reports that the slave’s name was Malchus.
Luke adds that Jesus touched the man’s ear and healed him.
Imagine that!
Jesus bore no ill will toward the men taking him into custody.
Further, according to Matthew 26:52,
Jesus told Peter:
“Return your sword to its place,
“for all those who take up the sword
will perish by the sword.”
Why did Jesus disapprove of Peter’s brave act?
For the same reason that he had avoided the political process all the way up to that point.
Jesus explained this when he appeared before Pontius Pilate later that night.
At John 18:36, we read:
“My Kingdom is no part of this world.”
Yes, because Jesus’ Kingdom is not of human origin,
it doesn’t need human defenses.
How can we be sure that this is what Jesus meant?
Look closely at the rest of John 18:36:
“If my Kingdom were part of this world,
“my attendants would have fought
“that I should not be handed over to the Jews.
“But as it is, my Kingdom
is not from this source.”
So as Christians,
what is our position where political matters are concerned?
We are neutral.
Sometimes people misunderstand this viewpoint.
Some have concluded that because we don’t promote one human government,
that we must be promoting another human government.
In the 1950’s, in what is now the Republic of Congo,
authorities falsely accused Jehovah’s Witnesses of being Communists.
But during the 1970’s,
when Congo adopted a Communist form of government,
the new authorities found fault with us for not being Communists!
Today, however, and for nearly three decades,
Jehovah’s Witnesses have enjoyed legal status in the Republic of Congo.
And whereas some have perceived
our Christian neutrality as sheer apathy,
others construe our position as a threat.
Let’s address both of these viewpoints.
First, there is a big difference
between Christian neutrality and apathy.
Apathy is defined
as “a lack of interest, enthusiasm, or concern.”
We certainly don’t lack interest in people,
nor are we insensitive to their feelings.
Like Jesus, we strive to alleviate people’s suffering
by helping them in practical ways
while teaching them about the only Kingdom
that can eliminate injustice.
By teaching people from God’s Word,
we endeavor to change hearts,
not political institutions.
We feel this approach is realistic
because mankind’s main problems are not political
but moral.
But why can it be said that Jehovah’s Witnesses are not a threat
but, rather, an asset?
We conscientiously obey the laws,
we support our communities through volunteer service
or compulsory civilian service where that exists,
and we pay our taxes.
It’s true, we don’t vote for political parties or candidates,
but neither do we disrupt elections
or interfere with those who choose to vote.
It’s true, we don’t lobby, campaign, or run for government office,
but neither do we criticize those in power,
undermine their policies, or demonstrate for political change.
It’s true, we won’t salute a flag,
but neither will we burn a flag, spit on a flag,
or disparage the nation that a flag represents
—even in lands where these are considered
protected expressions of freedom.
It’s true, we don’t sing national anthems,
but neither do we discourage others from singing,
nor do we make a public spectacle of not singing;
we simply don’t participate.
It’s true, we wouldn’t kill people in war,
but neither would we attack people at home.
So while we don’t promote any political position,
neither do we condemn any political position —even in our heart.
That is what neutrality means.
We don’t take sides.
But what if the demands of the State
conflict with the commands of Jesus?
There’s a Bible principle for that.
Are you thinking of what it says at Acts 5:28, 29
—that “we must obey God as ruler rather than men”?
This is not disregard for the State,
but, rather, reverence for God.
If the State demands that we do what God forbids
or refrain from doing what God commands,
then we believe God would consider that an invalid request.
Now, one might say,
‘I can imagine some situations where that viewpoint could get you into trouble.’
Jesus foretold as much at Matthew 24:9,
where he said: “You will be hated by all the nations
on account of my name.”
More specifically, at Revelation 2:10,
Jesus said that some of his disciples would be thrown into prison
—not all of us but some.
So we’re not disappointed if we don’t get thrown into prison,
but neither are we discouraged if we do.
Our minds turn to the thousands of brothers and sisters
who have been sentenced to prison over the years
for their Christian neutrality.
We are proud of them. We pray for them.
We know that Jehovah is pleased with them.
Their endurance under trial spells victory for all of us.
How so?
To the congregation in Ephesus, Paul wrote:
“I ask you not to give up on account of my tribulations in your behalf,
for these mean glory for you.”
Paul wrote these words while he himself was under house arrest in Rome.
In what sense did Paul’s tribulations
“mean glory” for the Ephesians?
In that his perseverance in ministering despite trials
showed the congregation that the privileges they enjoyed as Christians
were of the highest importance.
If Paul had just given up, what would that have implied?
That their faith, their ministry,
and their hope in God’s Kingdom were not so valuable after all.
Instead, Paul’s endurance exalted Christianity.
It demonstrated that remaining faithful is worth any sacrifice.
In like manner, the endurance of our dear brothers and sisters in prison
proves that their hope is alive
and that the Kingdom they represent is real.
They have an identity as envoys,
not of any human government,
but of the heavenly Kingdom
—a Kingdom that will reward them with everlasting life
in a world without war.
Whether we face imprisonment or not,
how prepared are we to remain neutral in our day-to-day life?
In this dramatization, a Christian family discovers
that they need to spend more time studying about the subject of neutrality.
Collette, I’m home.
In the kitchen, Curtis.
How was your day?
Oh, it was a long day, but it’s nice being home.
That smells amazing! I can’t wait.
Oh, well, it will be ready in a few minutes.
But I have a surprise;
my job gave us tickets to the game this weekend
—enough for all of us to go.
So it’s downtown at the . . .
That sounded like fun.
It was a sport we could enjoy watching.
Collette and I hadn’t been in years,
and I don’t think the kids had ever gone.
We were all looking forward to a family night out.
But, Dad, what exactly do we do during the national anthem?
Honestly, I wasn’t sure.
Ladies and gentlemen,
would you please stand for the singing
of our national anthem?
Dad, I have a question too.
Will they salute the flag at my new school?
That’s right.
The conference with her teachers was next week,
and we didn’t know what they’d do there.
OK, class. Now that everyone is here,
let’s all stand for the pledge of allegiance.
Elizabeth, is everything all right?
What do you think, Honey?
Well, tomorrow night is our Family Worship evening.
So why don’t we do a study project as a family
on Christian neutrality at public events?
That sounds like a good idea.
Yeah.
I think this will be great. We’ll all get a chance to do our research.
I asked Daniel to research Christian principles on neutrality.
Collette and Elizabeth would find examples
of ones who proved loyal under pressure.
And for me,
my job was to call Elizabeth’s new school
to find out if they saluted the flag or sang the anthem.
Hello.
Hi, Mr. Johnson? This is Curtis, Elizabeth’s dad.
We’d studied this topic when the kids were younger,
but we needed reminders for these new challenges.
The kids found some great information.
Several Bible principles applied.
But what Jesus said at Matthew 4:10
was an essential foundation:
“It is Jehovah your God you must worship,
and it is to him alone you must render sacred service.”
If we participate in a nationalistic ceremony,
we’re sharing in worship
of something or someone other than Jehovah God.
But what would help us know what to do?
Elizabeth found some good examples to imitate.
The account of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego
was one of our favorites.
When King Nebuchadnezzar ordered them to worship the gold image,
they bravely stood while others bowed down.
They were determined to worship only Jehovah,
and He rescued them from the furnace.
And there are modern-day examples
of courage like the three Hebrews.
Some children have had to take a stand
when governments tried to force them
to take part in patriotic events during wartime,
when feelings of national pride ran strong.
And despite legal victories in some countries,
young ones today are still put to the test.
We learned there was no one answer on what to do.
Situations are different depending on where we live
or what a person does to show he’s participating.
But in every case,
Christians in some way make it evident
that they are respectful observers, not participants.
We felt good because we had decided
what we would do to be respectful but neutral
and show Jehovah that our family worships him alone.
Since the tests of our neutrality differ depending on where we live,
why not do what the family in the video did
—devote a Family Worship evening or personal study session to researching
how to avoid participating inadvertently
in any activity that would violate our Christian neutrality.
The subject of neutrality was highlighted in a Watchtower article that we studied
in the congregations in 2016.
In this first episode of a new video series
called Lessons From the Watchtower,
note how our brothers and sisters have applied
the admonition found in that very practical article.
As a professor of finance, I need to be well-informed.
As a Christian, I also need to be well-informed,
as do all Christians.
It’s difficult not to take sides in politics.
It’s very difficult because we are aware of the issues.
I always really liked soccer ever since I was little.
I lived in a poor area, and soccer was what we used to do for fun.
There was a journalist that I liked to keep up with.
He would point out both the good and the bad on all sides of politics.
But when he spoke up and pointed out only the bad side of a political party,
I did not like that.
I live in the downtown area of the city.
That is where the largest political demonstrations take place.
People from this area are really into politics.
They have definite opinions.
And even though I always knew that we must remain neutral,
I secretly approved of the demonstrations.
On the outside, I wasn’t jumping up and down or cheering,
but on the inside, I was saying: ‘Come on! Let’s win!’
It was all about the desire, the crowd,
and the pride of your team having the most victories or the most trophies.
I used to rationalize saying:
“I was created in Jehovah’s image, and Jehovah is a just God.”
What was speaking was my sense of justice.
I thought neutrality was shown through actions
and not through what I felt.
The April 2016 Watchtower
has interesting information regarding neutrality.
Being neutral means that you do not consider yourself better than others
because “in God’s sight, all people are equal.”
After studying the article, I realized that I needed to make changes;
I was not being neutral.
So I read the article again.
I prayed to Jehovah;
I said to him that I knew it was as if he were speaking to me.
The magazine really touched me deeply.
I remember reading the article at least three times that evening.
I was really surprised.
I realized how far off I was
from what God wanted me to be on the inside.
The second situation mentioned in the article
had to do with news reports and the media.
The article even suggested that we limit
our intake of news that we watch related to politics.
There was another phrase that really moved me.
It said: ‘Even if we don’t march with protesters,
might we be with them in spirit?’
Yes! I was with them. Yes!
There were several phrases in that article
that were written just for me.
When I cut back watching so many news reports
—and I had to—
this helped me to have self-control when I spoke to others at work.
When workmates mentioned something that was in the news,
I didn’t have anything to say since I hadn’t seen it.
I didn’t know about it.
A workmate would say: “Did you see that so-and-so said this
and that someone else made a statement?”
I would say: “No, I didn’t see it,”
and that was the end of the conversation.
The article mentions Romans 10:12
which says that Jehovah is “Lord over all” of us,
that ‘there is no difference between Jew and Greek.’
To Jehovah, it’s not important if my country
has five or six titles or if it won or lost the World Cup.
To Jehovah, all people are equal.
I took a piece of paper, just a simple piece of paper,
and I wrote on it the four key points that the article talks about
—four key points that will help us to remain neutral.
I keep it in my purse; that way I can always read it at work.
I like watching soccer; it’s fun.
I still watch it on TV.
I still play soccer with my friends at Bethel,
but I’ve made an effort to change.
Little by little, I’ve managed to put soccer in its proper place.
This helps me to keep pride and nationalism from getting the best of me.
I learned from this article not to express opinions about politics.
That has to come from deep inside.
If I’m convinced that God’s Kingdom is the best solution
and that there’s nothing that comes even close,
remaining neutral will come naturally.
But I can’t let my guard down.
I really enjoy studying articles from The Watchtower,
especially those dealing with practical matters.
They help me see the Bible as if it were a mirror that shows me where I can improve.
Following counsel
and making the changes suggested in the article
has helped me to speak with the conviction
that only the Kingdom can solve mankind’s problems.
Because our enemy Satan tries to break our integrity in many subtle ways,
it’s important to know ahead of time how we’ll act.
Actions are important, and yet they’re preceded by thoughts,
as one young brother discovered.
In this dramatization, note what Bible principle
helped him to stay neutral in his heart.
“They are no part of the world.” —John 17:16.
“We must remain neutral in order to be loyal subjects of God’s Kingdom.
“Otherwise, how could we have a clean conscience
“when we preach the good news
“that only God’s Kingdom can solve mankind’s problems?
“. . . As Satan’s system nears its end,
we can expect the issue of neutrality to become more prominent.”
OK, people, we’re ready to go.
Dawn, Jordan, can I get you to grab the blinds please?
In your work groups this week, you’ll outline the policies
you feel world governments should implement.
Remember, it’s young people like you,
each of you, who must take action to solve the problems that threaten our planet.
When war comes, they’ll look for you and me to do the fighting.
Will you speak up and tell them, ‘No, no, we won’t?’
But I’m more worried about the elections, especially for your generation.
I mean, who do you think is going to win?
Uhm, well, we believe that—
uhm . . .
That’s actually a very interesting question.
And as Jehovah’s Witnesses, we believe that it’s God’s Kingdom
that’s going to bring about all the solutions that we need for all of our problems.
For example, . . .
That’s £7.50, please.
Thank you.
Hello, how can I help you?
But you know, this new government policy
—I really think it’s going to work.
You’re crazy.
With their policies, we’ll be bankrupt within three years.
But if it works, though, it’s going to make people rich.
Those who are rich already.
No, I’m fed up. They say the same thing.
We’ve invited a panel of experts to explore these issues,
namely, can the opposition party win?
Will they keep their promises to lower-income people?
And what changes could we expect on required military service?
You’ll want to hear the answers.
Let’s begin by speaking to John McGarthy, the minister of education.
If put to the test,
I do want to take my stand for Jehovah.
But the outcome of all these things can affect me now
—my family, my goals.
How can I stay neutral, even in my heart?
John 17:14:
“I have given your word to them, but the world has hated them,
“because they are no part of the world,
“just as I am no part of the world.
“I do not request that you take them out of the world,
“but that you watch over them because of the wicked one.
“They are no part of the world, just as I am no part of the world.
“Sanctify them by means of the truth; your word is truth.
“Just as you sent me into the world,
“I also sent them into the world.
“And I am sanctifying myself in their behalf,
so that they also may be sanctified by means of truth.”
No part of the world,
like Jesus, both in thought and action.
Sure, but in our lifetime?
Yes! And I have found something that has helped me to be sure of this.
Can I share it with you?
It’s here at Matthew 24:33.
Jesus said: “Likewise also you, when you see all these things,
know that he is near at the doors.”
Our being neutral today is urgent
because Jehovah’s day is coming quickly.
On that day, we must be absolutely certain
that we are on Jehovah’s side.
In this Bethel morning worship,
Brother Anthony Morris of the Governing Body
explains why we don’t need to worry about the events to come.
Now, The Watchtower
from where the comments are taken
had the theme
“Your Deliverance Is Getting Near.”
Now, this was a sobering and yet
a very encouraging Watchtower study article,
and that theme was taken from Luke chapter 21.
So if you’d like to find that —Luke 21—
and in the context prior to verse 28,
we know verse 26: “People will become faint out of fear
“and expectation of the things
coming upon the inhabited earth.”
Then it mentions “the heavens . . . shaken,”
then, “see the Son of man.”
And here’s where we find the theme, verse 28:
“But as these things start to occur,
“stand up straight and lift up your heads,
because your deliverance is getting near.”
Now, as we know, this is fulfilled during the great tribulation.
That’s something to keep in mind,
that at that time when these events take place,
they’ll be able to stand up
and look forward to their deliverance.
Now, for a moment, just reflect back
on the Hezekiah video
that we enjoyed
during the convention season last year.
It was amazing!
And what a beautiful job the brothers did in Audio/Video
depicting one angel
that destroyed 185,000 men.
It was spectacular!
However, find Revelation chapter 17
—Revelation chapter 17—
and this is what
is foretold for the near future.
The context here at Revelation 17,
where verse 12 mentions “the ten horns,”
and then down into verse 13
—after this “one hour with the wild beast” (the United Nations)—
they give their “authority to the wild beast.”
Humans in general would find that hard to believe
when they look at what’s going on in the world today.
But here’s what they’re going to do,
verse 14:
“These will battle with the Lamb,
“but because he is Lord of lords and King of kings,
“the Lamb will conquer them.
“Also, those with him
who are called and chosen and faithful will do so.”
Now,
as good as our brothers are in Audio/Video,
I personally doubt that anyone
could do a videography and capture this event.
You’re talking about Christ Jesus,
anointed immortal spirit creatures,
and then Jesus has the holy angels
that are under his direction as King.
This is going to be spectacular!
Now, all things are possible with God,
but I think they’d have to have Him to be able to show a video
to capture what’s coming in the future.
Just spectacular!
Now, just keep in mind (and The Watchtower made this clear),
we don’t know the sure and exact sequence of events
—the time order— some of it (as The Watchtower says)
will likely overlap.
However, what we do know
—Jehovah has been kind about this—
is what’s going to take place
to start the great tribulation.
Now, we find here in verse 15,
and we’ll read through verse 17 of Revelation 17:
“He said to me: ‘The waters that you saw,
“‘where the prostitute is sitting,
“‘mean peoples and crowds and nations and tongues.
“‘And the ten horns that you saw and the wild beast,
“‘these will hate the prostitute
“‘and will make her devastated and naked,
“‘and they will eat up her flesh
and completely burn her with fire.’”
Now, here’s the fact
and verification for why this will happen,
verse 17: “For God put it into their hearts
“to carry out his thought,
“yes, to carry out their one thought
“by giving their kingdom to the wild beast,
until the words of God will have been accomplished.”
So it’s as good as done.
This is what’s going to happen
regardless of how people view us
when we preach this good news.
Because this is good news —the destruction
of the world empire of false religion,
the beginning of the great tribulation.
This is spectacular news for God’s people,
and until it takes place, they won’t believe it.
But it will happen because Jehovah says it’s going to happen.
So that’ll be a time for us to prove our love for Jehovah God.
We’ll be the only group protected by him.
Now, this was profound, too,
this article in The Watchtower made this—
I thought it was a profound statement when you think
about the organization we’re a part of.
It said in paragraph 9:
“This will not be the time to preach
the ‘good news of the Kingdom.’”
My, we’re a preaching organization.
So there’s a time we’ll not preach the good news?
Yes.
Remember one of our favorite verses?
It’s etched on the minds and hearts of God’s people:
“And this good news of the Kingdom will be preached
in all the inhabited earth for a witness to all the nations.”
Well, don’t forget the last part:
“And then the end will come.”
So during the great tribulation —no good news.
However, we do know there’ll be preaching.
And you think we’re unpopular now?
Oh, my!
Notice Revelation chapter 16,
and in the context Armageddon is being addressed,
and notice verse 21:
“Then great hailstones, each about the weight of a talent,
“fell from heaven on the people,
“and the people blasphemed God
“because of the plague of [the] hail,
for the plague was unusually great.”
Yes.
So the message and the preaching
are going to be like “hailstones.”
I don’t know if you’ve ever been in a hailstorm,
but this is a huge hailstorm
being depicted here.
It’s likely, possibly, a hard-hitting message
—maybe a declaration announcing that Satan’s world
is about to come to a complete end.
So let’s just stay tuned.
And don’t feel bad—I know.
I was out in the ministry
in one territory recently,
and it’s good to suffer reproach.
We all need that, like Jesus did.
The door-to-door ministry is good for us.
But see, if you think we’re suffering reproach now—
Well, get ready!
It’s just training for this future declaration
that we’ll have the privilege to share in.
Now, keep in mind
that there is this event that The Watchtower
did mention in Matthew chapter 24.
And if you’ll find that,
it’s nice to have this clear.
Matthew chapter 24,
and we’re going to read verse 31:
“And he will send out his angels
“with a great trumpet sound,
“and they will gather his chosen ones together
“from the four winds,
from one extremity of the heavens to their other extremity.”
So, what The Watchtower stated there was
that it’s not the initial gathering
of the anointed nor the final sealing;
this is when the remnant —the remaining ones—
receive their heavenly reward during the great tribulation.
And this event takes place at some point
after the beginning of the attack by Gog.
Now, at that time,
that’s when Matthew 13:43 is fulfilled:
“The righteous ones will shine as brightly as the sun
in the Kingdom of their Father.”
So as we mentioned —sobering, yes, but encouraging.
Oh, yes, so encouraging.
So, brothers, let’s be confident;
let’s trust in Jehovah.
There’s no need to be afraid.
Let’s keep up our spiritual routine
and prove ourselves ready,
because the great tribulation is near.
When Jehovah’s day comes,
our brotherhood will be safe because it’s united.
Our worldwide unity is but one of the blessings
that result from our Christian neutrality.
In this month’s music video, notice the connection
between the love we enjoy as God’s people
and our being “no part of this world.”
The song is entitled “We Are One.”
There’s trouble in the world, disunity. No matter where we live, no harmony.
There are people suffering, fighting for change.
But among God’s people, we trust in his name.
So we must stick close to his Word And remain no part of this world
With love in ev’ry little thing we do.
Show love as we spread the good news, And feel the love of the brotherhood.
Though we stand out as diff’rent, With Jehovah, we are one.
No matter where we go from sea to sea, With God’s people, we find true family.
Yes, there are anxieties, but hope is real— A paradise to come.
True peace is near.
So we keep trusting in his Word And remain no part of this world
With love in ev’ry little thing we do. Show love as we spread the good news,
And feel the love of the brotherhood.
Though we stand out as diff’rent, With Jehovah, we are one.
We are one.
So let’s stay faithful and endure And remain no part of this world
With love in ev’ry little thing we do. Show love as we spread the good news,
And feel the love of the brotherhood. Though we stand out as diff’rent,
With Jehovah, We love in ev’ry little thing we do.
Show love as we spread the good news, And feel the love of the brotherhood.
Though we stand out as diff’rent, With Jehovah, we are one.
The song was initially written in the Lingala language,
an African language spoken mainly
in the Democratic Republic of Congo and the Republic of Congo.
If you’d like to hear the song in the Lingala language,
you can now find it on Video on Demand under the heading “Music.”
While you’re at it, why not listen
to other original songs in different languages?
After you have navigated to the “Music” section,
change the language of the website
in the top right corner to a language of your choice.
Have you noticed the many examples of Christian neutrality
we’ve seen during this program?
First, we visited Armenia and learned
how they’ve remained neutral despite persecution.
After the talk, we learned the importance
of remaining neutral at public events.
Next, we met a number of brothers and sisters
who shared their experiences in applying
the Watchtower study article about neutrality.
Brother Morris reminded us of Jehovah’s protection
when Jehovah judges this world.
And our music video encouraged us
to enjoy the blessings of unity
that result from our Christian neutrality.
And speaking of the music video:
Did you notice how our friends watched the broadcast,
and when the postcard came up at the end of the program, they waved back?
Have you ever felt like doing that?
If so, here’s another opportunity.
Let’s visit our brothers and sisters in South Korea.
Kingdom proclaimers arrived in Korea in 1912.
Today, the Republic of Korea
has some 1,300 congregations
with over 100,000 publishers.
Although the peninsula was under colonial rule for some time
and has been involved in other military conflicts,
Jehovah’s Witnesses there have maintained their Christian neutrality
by not taking sides.
Over the last seven decades,
more than 19,000 brothers have been imprisoned for their faith.
In 2018, a favorable court decision
was handed down in behalf of these faithful brothers.
In the future, we look forward
to even further relief from fair-minded officials in this country.
This is the Ganseong Congregation.
Their territory has a population of approximately 23,000
and is partially located
in the demilitarized zone near the North Korean border.
It’s not uncommon for the almost 50 publishers
to conduct over 60 Bible studies each month.
In fact,
some 30 publishers —or 60 percent of the congregation—
serve as regular pioneers.
Because of its location, many of the residents
of the villages in this area are isolated from the rest of the country.
Our brothers and sisters
often meet people who work for the military.
Because of the congregation’s proximity to the border,
busloads of tourists come on a regular basis
to see the North Korean border.
To reach such visitors with the good news, our brothers have organized
public witnessing stands in a number of locations.
We love our brothers and sisters in the Ganseong Congregation very much.
And they send their love to all of us around the world.
This is JW Broadcasting
from the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

en.text: I was imprisoned for a year and three months
for upholding Christian neutrality.
I was in a cell with all types of hardened criminals.
I was sitting at home.
My whole family had been arrested.
They burned down the villages.
We had to go live in the bush.
That was difficult because we had a baby.
The police came in with guns,
pointed them at us and handcuffed us,
searched all our house, took everything away,
and took us to the detention center.
And that was the beginning of our imprisonment.
I was taken to prison
all alone and scared,
but I trusted in Jehovah
—that only he could protect me.
During that entire time, what helped me was the thought
that Jehovah God would strengthen me
and that he was by my side.
Every day, I would review all those scriptures
in my mind and go over them;
that was the first thing I did in the day.
So never at any time, although I didn’t have a Bible,
did I feel any spiritual loss or weakness.
During the difficult moments with the baby,
we always prayed to Jehovah.
I saw Jehovah as my Father, as a real Person.
It was like I was hearing Jehovah’s voice saying to me:
“My daughter, don’t worry. I am with you!”
So I never shrunk back.
I remained firm!
If I had valued myself, my freedom,
my health, or material gain
more than my relationship with Jehovah,
I might not have chosen to serve him.
But because I loved Jehovah more than all these things,
I was able to choose Jehovah
even if that meant that I had to serve time in prison.
Now I can freely serve God,
attend religious meetings,
and go in the ministry with my family.
I felt that Jehovah’s hand was with me
and that fear disappeared.
The one who gave me so much strength was Jehovah.
If you love Jehovah, love has no fear;
love banishes fear.
And I can only say that my life,
despite everything, has been pleasant,
and I’ve been so happy.
In fact, there have been so many occasions
when it’s been positive joy.
So I feel that that is because I’ve always kept Jehovah
right in front of my mind,
and I’m confident
that brothers and sisters who do the same
will find Jehovah will bless them
as he’s blessed me.
The fact that Jehovah
will never forget the loyalty that we show him
and the hope of Paradise that he has given us
help me to feel his love,
overcome my fear,
and become determined to serve him loyally forever.

cn.text: 我因为坚守基督徒的中立立场
被关在监狱里一年3个月
我跟那些重刑犯被关在同一个牢房里
当时我坐在家里
我全家人都被逮捕了
他们放火把村子全烧了
我们只能住在树林里
而且最困难的是我们还带着一个小宝宝
武装警察闯进来
拿枪指着我们
把我们铐上手铐
又搜查我们的房子
带走所有东西
把我们关在拘留所
后来我们就被关进监狱里了
我被单独监禁，觉得很害怕
但我信赖耶和华
只有他才能保护我！
那段时间
我知道耶和华上帝在我身边
给我力量
所以我才能撑过来
我每天起床后第一件事
就是沉思我想到的经文
虽然当时我没有圣经
但却不觉得跟耶和华疏远
或是对他失去信心
我们带着小宝宝逃难
实在很辛苦
我们一直跟耶和华祷告
我觉得耶和华非常真实
就像我的爸爸一样
我好像听到耶和华对我说
“女儿，我就在你身边，不要害怕！”
所以我从来都没有害怕退缩
我一直很坚定！
要是我在乎的是自己、自由
健康、金钱而不是跟耶和华的友谊
我可能就不会崇拜上帝了
但因为我爱的是耶和华而不是那些东西
所以我才会选择事奉耶和华
即使要坐牢我也在所不惜！
现在我可以自由地崇拜上帝
参加聚会
跟家人一起去传道
我觉得耶和华的手一直在帮助我
我一点都不害怕！
耶和华给我很大的力量
“爱里没有恐惧”
只要你爱耶和华
你什么都不用害怕！
我虽然经历过不少患难
但我可以说
我这一生是充满喜乐的
有很多事都让我感到非常地快乐
我把耶和华看得很真实
他就好像站在我面前一样
我相信只要弟兄姐妹对上帝忠贞
耶和华也会赐福给他们
就像他赐福给我一样
我们对耶和华忠贞
他绝对不会忘记
上帝给我们乐园的希望
让我感受到他的爱
帮助我克服恐惧
也使我决心永远都要忠贞地崇拜他！

en.text: Jacob was 77 years old.
He was unmarried and hated by his twin brother, Esau.
At the direction of his parents,
Jacob fled to the land of Abraham’s relatives.
When he stopped to rest for the night,
Jehovah gave Jacob full assurance of divine support.
In a dream, Jacob saw a ladder, or stairway,
leading from earth to heaven.
Angels were busily ascending and descending the stairway.
Then Jehovah spoke to Jacob, saying:
“I am with you,
and I will safeguard you wherever you go.”
Just as Jehovah proved to be with Jacob,
so He has been with His people throughout history.
From ancient times to our day,
this world has tried to disturb the peace that God’s people enjoy.
Jehovah cares for his people.
Guided by Jehovah’s holy spirit
and with the support of the angels,
we are able to stand by our brothers and sisters under attack.
As a result, we feel as though we are standing
as one person against Satan’s attacks.
Jehovah is truly on our side!

cn.text: 雅各77岁时还没有结婚
他的双胞胎哥哥以扫对他恨之入骨
所以雅各按照父母的指示
逃到亚伯拉罕的亲戚那里
有一天晚上，雅各休息时
耶和华在梦里向他保证会全力支持他
雅各看见一道通往天上的阶梯
上帝的天使纷纷顺着阶梯上下往来
然后，耶和华对雅各说
“我与你同在
无论你到哪里去
我都必保护你。”
从历史我们看出耶和华一直与他的子民同在
就像他保证与雅各同在一样
从古至今
世界的人想尽办法破坏上帝子民享有的和平
耶和华很关心他的子民
有耶和华圣灵的指引和天使的帮助
我们就能支持受迫害的弟兄姐妹
虽然我们受撒但攻击
但作为上帝的子民
我们会团结一心，抵抗撒但
我们知道
耶和华一定会与我们同在！

ko.text: 우리에게는 겸손을 길러야 할 이유가 많이 있습니다.
네, 우리가 겸손하지 않으면, 여호와께서 대적하십니다.
겸손하면, 과분한 친절을 베풀어 주실 겁니다.
바로 이게 우리가 겸손을 길러야 할 주된 이유입니다.
하지만 한 번 겸손하다고 해서 꼭 언제나 겸손한 건 아닙니다.
어떤 이유로인가 겸손을 잃은 예가 많습니다.
그리고 현대에 겸손을 잃은 사람들의 예도
하지만 대개의 경우는 교만 때문에 완전히 파멸하고 말았습니다.
어떤 사람이 겸손을 잃게 되는 일이 생길 때
그 사람은 살다가 어떤 상황에 놓이게 되고,
자신에게 있던 겸손을 잃게 되지 않습니까?
우리의 겸손을 시험하는 다섯 가지 상황을
이런 상황이 생길 때 조심하지 않으면
아마 가나안 땅에 큰 기근이 들었을 때일 것입니다.
하갈은 그런 상황에서 아주 고맙게 느끼고 겸손했겠죠.
그런데 이제 자기가 아브라함의 첩이 되었고,
임신한 걸 알게 되자 어떻게 됐죠?
“하갈은 임신한 것을 알게 되자 자기 여주인을 업신여기기 시작했다.”
적절하게도 여호와의 천사가 하갈에게 이렇게 조언했습니다.
네, 하갈을 보면 한때 선한 마음을 가졌던 사람도
특권이나 권한이 생기면, 존중받는 위치에 있게 되면
겸손을 잃을 수 있다는 걸 잘 알 수 있습니다.
이제 겸손을 시험하는 두 번째 상황은,
우리가 어떤 노력을 기울인 끝에 그 일에서 성공한 때입니다.
여호와께서 여러 해 동안 웃시야를 축복해 주셨죠.
아시다시피 그는 성전에 들어가 분향까지 하려고 합니다.
그러니까 웃시야는 이런 성공, 이런 업적으로 콧대가 높아져서
제사장의 의무를 수행할 수 있다고 생각한 모양인데,
여호와께서 승리를 주셨다는 걸 잊어버린 거죠.
우리가 어떤 노력 끝에 성공을 거두더라도,
우리를 성공하게 해 준 모든 특성과 능력을
이제, 겸손을 시험하는 세 번째 상황은,
왕께서 하시려는 일은 제사장만 할 수 있습니다.
웃시야가 더욱더 교만해지자, 여호와께서 나병으로 치십니다.
처음에 그가 주제넘게 성전에 들어갔을 때 치신 게 아니죠.
절대로 교만해지지 않게 아주 조심해야 합니다.
특히 조언해 주는 사람보다 우리가 더 권한이나 경험이나 나이가 많고
겸손이 시험을 받는 네 번째 상황은,
재산을 물려받거나, 어떤 식으로인가 부유해질 수 있죠.
“젖과 꿀이 흐르는 땅”에 들어갔을 때 어땠나요?
그런 상황 때문에 우리의 겸손을 잃는 일이 있어서는 안 될 것입니다.
그럼, 겸손을 시험하는 다섯 번째이자 마지막 상황은
해설자 한 분이 앞에서 언급하신 것처럼
재판석에 떡 앉아서 공개 연설을 하기 시작하니까
어떤 지도자가 예수께 와서 “선하신 선생님”이라고 부르자,
하느님 한 분 외에는 선한 이가 없습니다.”
정말, 이 두 경우에서 배울 점이 있지 않습니까?
칭찬을 들으면 두 가지 반응을 보일 수 있죠.
헤롯처럼 자기가 그 영예를 받을 수도 있고,
예수처럼 여호와께 영예를 돌릴 수도 있습니다.
적어도 마음으로 그렇게 하고 말로도 표현할 수 있습니다.
이렇게 시험받는 것 한 가지는 그의 겸손입니다.
지혜로운 자는 칭찬을 바라지도 칭찬에 우쭐하지도 않는다.
허영심 많은 자는 칭찬을 바라며 약한 자는 칭찬에 들뜬다.
사실 가진 모든 걸 여호와께 받았음을 기억한다면,
그 사람은 여호와의 눈에 매우 귀중할 것이다.”
네, 이렇게 겸손을 시험하는 다섯 가지 상황을 살펴봤습니다.
조심하지 않으면 겸손을 잃을 수 있죠.
첫 번째, 특권이나 부가적인 책임을 맡게 될 때,
두 번째, 어떤 노력 끝에 성공했을 때,
우리의 겸손을 시험하는 다른 상황도 생각해 볼 수 있겠죠.
이런 시험을 잘 이겨내고 겸손을 유지하면,
여호와께서 우릴 절대 대적하지 않으실 겁니다.

en.text: Now, there are many reasons
why all of us want to cultivate humility,
but what would you say is the foremost reason?
Well, let’s get the answer from James 4:6
—the “b” part.
It says: “God opposes the haughty ones,
“but he gives undeserved kindness
to the humble ones.”
So if we don’t have humility, Jehovah is going to oppose us.
If we do, he’s going to give us undeserved kindness.
Obviously, that’s the main reason,
even though there are many others,
we want to cultivate humility.
But as you know, once humble
does not necessarily mean always humble.
The Bible contains many examples of ones who started out humble,
but somewhere along the way, they lost their humility.
And you probably can think of modern-day examples
of ones who lost their humility.
Now, in some cases, perhaps they regained it.
But in other cases, pride proved to be
their ultimate downfall.
But now think about this:
In a case of one who loses his humility,
does it just happen automatically?
Well, isn’t it true that in most cases
some situation develops in that person’s life
that proves to be a catalyst
that causes that person to lose his humility?
So this being the case,
let us discuss five situations
that could develop in our lives
and test our humility,
and if we’re not careful, cause us to lose it.
Number one: when we receive privileges
or added responsibilities.
In this regard, let’s think for a moment about Hagar.
Now, the Insight book suggests
that she perhaps became the maidservant to Sarah
during a time of great famine in Egypt.
So in that circumstance,
she would’ve been very appreciative, very humble.
But now when she became the secondary wife of Abraham
and found out she was pregnant, then what happened?
Well, Genesis 16:4 says:
“When she realized that she was pregnant,
she began to despise her mistress.”
Yes, with her new honored status,
she lost her humility;
and appropriately, Jehovah’s angel gave her some counsel.
The angel said: “Return to your mistress
and humble yourself under her hand.”
Well, Hagar well illustrates
that a person who has had a good heart
can lose their humility
upon receiving privileges or authority
—an honored position.
But now let’s take the second humility-testing situation:
when we receive success,
or achieve success, in some endeavor.
Now, let’s think about Uzziah in this regard.
In 2 Chronicles 26,
if you just scan down through verses 3 to 5,
it shows that he started out very humble.
He “was 16 years old when he became king,”
and in verse 4, “continued to do what was right in Jehovah’s eyes.”
At the end of verse 5:
“During the time he was searching for Jehovah,
the true God made him prosper.”
So he started out well; he ruled well.
He was humble, and Jehovah blessed him for many years.
But now look over at verse 16,
and you’ll notice that it starts out with the word “however.”
And when the Bible uses that word “however,”
it means something changed.
“However, as soon as he was strong,
his heart became haughty to his own ruin.”
And then, as you know, he even tried to go into the temple
and offer incense.
Now, what does that mean, ‘he became strong’?
Well, the Insight book explains
that he “became famous for his military successes.”
So apparently these successes,
these achievements, went to his head
to the point that he thought he could go into the temple
and usurp the duties of a priest.
He forgot that Jehovah gave him those victories.
Now, that’s a lesson for us, isn’t it?
If we happen to achieve success in some endeavor,
may we never forget that the qualities and abilities
that enable us to achieve that success
came from Jehovah.
But now let’s get our third humility-testing situation:
when we’re given counsel.
Now, Uzziah also well illustrates this point.
If you still have your Bible open there, in verses 17 and 18,
when Uzziah went into the temple to offer the incense,
you notice that it describes how ‘Azariah the priest
‘and 80 other [and notice, it calls them] courageous priests
went in there after him.’
They confronted him.
They tried to give him counsel: ‘You’re out of order.
‘What you’re trying to do, only priests are to do.
You’d better go out of this sanctuary.’
Well, they tried to give him counsel, didn’t they?
But how did Uzziah react?
Well, verse 19 tells us
that he “became enraged” at them.
‘Who are you to tell me what to do?
I’m the king.’
His pride became even bigger,
and Jehovah struck him with leprosy.
Now think about this: Jehovah didn’t strike him
when he presumptuously first went into the temple.
But only when he pridefully rejected the counsel,
then Jehovah struck him.
Now, that’s a good lesson for us, isn’t it?
We have to be very careful that we never become prideful
when we receive counsel.
And especially do we have to be on guard
if we think we have more authority, perhaps more experience,
or more seniority than the one giving us the counsel.
Let’s get our fourth humility-testing situation:
if we happen to come into material prosperity.
Maybe we get an inheritance, or somehow we come into material prosperity.
Well, what happened to the Israelites
when they entered the “land flowing with milk and honey”?
Well, the Bible tells us, and Jehovah is speaking at Hosea 13:6.
Jehovah says: “They were satisfied with their pastures,
“they were satisfied
“and their heart became proud.
And so they forgot me.”
Well, that’s a sobering lesson, isn’t it?
If we happen to come into material prosperity,
we never want to allow that situation
to cause us to lose our humility
—no matter what our material situation.
Then we must always humbly depend upon Jehovah
and not material things.
Well, let’s get our fifth, our last one, humility-testing situation
(and it was talked about earlier by one of our commenters):
when we receive praise.
Do you recall the account in Acts chapter 12
when Herod put on his royal raiment,
he sat down on the judgment seat,
he began to give a public discourse,
and the people shouted:
“A god’s voice, and not a man’s [voice]”?
Well, what happened?
An angel struck him dead;
he died; worms ate him up.
Why?
Because he didn’t give glory to Jehovah.
In stark contrast, think about the account in Luke 18
when a ruler came up to Jesus and called him “Good Teacher,”
and Jesus said: “Why do you call me good?
Nobody is good except one, God.”
Well, we can learn from those examples, can’t we?
When we receive praise, there are two ways we can react:
Like Herod, try to take the credit for ourselves;
or like Jesus, we can give the credit to Jehovah.
We can do that in words or at least in our heart.
Now, Proverbs 27:21 says:
“A person is tested by the praise he receives.”
And one way he’s tested is when his humility is tested.
The Watchtower some years ago said this:
“Praise [will] show the quality of a man’s heart.
“Wise men do not seek praise
“nor are they puffed up by it.
“Vain men seek it and weak men are inflated by it.
“If one can bear praise without injury,
“remembering that anything and everything he has is actually from God,
that one is sterling in the eyes of Jehovah.”
Well, there we have five situations
that can test our humility
and, if we’re not careful, cause us to lose it.
Do you have them?
(1) When we receive privileges or added responsibility,
(2) when we achieve success in some endeavor,
(3) when we receive counsel,
(4) if we happen to come into material prosperity,
and (5) when we’re praised.
But you can probably think of other situations that can test our humility.
The point is, If we meet these tests successfully
and keep our humility, with Jehovah’s help,
then Jehovah will never oppose us.
Rather, we will continue to receive
undeserved kindness from his generous hand.

cn.text: 我们有很多理由要培养谦卑这个特质
但你认为最重要的理由是什么呢？
雅各书4:6可以帮助我们找到答案
经文下半节说
“上帝与高傲的人为敌
却赐分外恩典给谦卑的人。”
所以，我们不谦卑就会成为上帝的敌人
那如果我们谦卑自抑
耶和华就会赐分外恩典给我们
这才是主要的理由
当然还会有很多其他的理由
我们都知道
一时的谦卑不代表一直都会谦卑
圣经有很多例子表明
有的人刚开始谦卑
但渐渐地就失去了这个特质
也许大家还能想到一些身边的例子
有的人不再谦卑了
但是后来又变得谦卑了
有的人被自骄心所胜
结果失去了跟耶和华宝贵的关系
大家觉得怎么样？
一个人会不会突然变得不谦卑了呢？
其实大多数情况下
一个人可能会因为某些因素或者某些情况
渐渐变得不再谦卑了
有哪些情况可能会让我们变得不再谦卑呢？
接下来
我们会讨论五种在生活中可能遇到的情况
而这些情况可能会让我们的谦卑受到考验
最后变得不再谦卑
情况一
当我们获得某项服务机会或担任更多职责时
在这方面我们先来考虑一个圣经人物，夏甲
《洞悉圣经》说
夏甲可能就是在迦南地发生饥荒时
成了撒拉的女仆
在这种情况下
夏甲一定非常谦卑
内心充满感激
但后来她成为亚伯拉罕的妾
还怀了孕
这时她的态度怎样呢？
创世记16:4说
“夏甲见自己怀孕，就轻看主母。”
没错，她的身份一改变就不再谦卑了
后来耶和华的天使给她劝告，对她说
“你要回到你主母那里去
在她手下谦卑自抑。”
所以，夏甲的例子让我们看出
即使一个人有谦卑的特质
但当他得到更多的服务机会
或负起更多职责时
也有可能变得不谦卑
接下来
让我们看看考验谦卑的第二个情况
当我们取得成功时
现在我们会一起考虑乌西雅的例子
历代志下26章，我们看3-5节
这里提到他刚作王的时候很谦卑
乌西雅登基的时候16岁
4节说
“乌西雅行耶和华看为对的事。”
5节说
“在他寻求耶和华的那段日子
上帝叫他富强起来。”
乌西雅一开始做得很好
是个既谦卑又贤明的统治者
所以有很多年耶和华都赐福给他
现在看看第16节
经文一开始就用了“可是”
在圣经里一出现“可是”这个词
就表示事情可能有所转变了
经文说
“可是，他一强盛
就心高气傲，自招败亡。”
我们都知道他甚至闯进耶和华的殿
要在香坛上烧香
经文说他“一强盛”是什么意思呢？
《洞悉圣经》说
“乌西雅善打胜仗，威名远扬。”
所以很明显，这些成就让他自以为是
变得骄傲
他居然闯进圣所
自以为有权利做祭司的工作
他显然忘记了是耶和华帮助他打赢这些仗的
这是多么深刻的教训
我们如果在某方面做得很成功
千万不要忘记
是因为耶和华赐给我们这方面的能力和特质
否则我们就不会成功
现在我们来谈谈第三个考验我们谦卑的情况
当我们受到劝告时
我们可以接着考虑乌西雅的例子
乌西雅闯进圣所献香的时候
请留意，经文说
“祭司亚撒利雅
马上率领耶和华的八十个英勇祭司
跟着他进去。”
这些祭司阻挡乌西雅王
劝他说
“你无权献香给耶和华
只有祭司才有权这样做
你赶快离开圣所吧！”
那么，他听到劝告后有什么反应呢？
19节说，乌西雅“怒不可遏”
向祭司们发怒
也许他说
“你们胆敢命令我？我才是王！”
他变得越来越骄傲
所以耶和华打击他
使他长了麻风
请留意当乌西雅擅自闯进圣所的时候
耶和华并没有打击他
而是在他拒绝接受劝告
态度傲慢的时候才打击他
我们学到什么呢？
千万不要让自骄心胜过我们
不听劝告
特别是当我们觉得提出劝告的人的职责
经验、资历不如我们
我们就更需要加倍小心
考验我们谦卑的第四个情况是
当我们变得有钱时
这也许是因为你继承了一笔财产
或者是赚了一大笔钱
其实以色列人的情况也类似
当他们进入“流奶流蜜之地”时
他们的谦卑就受到了考验
为什么这么说呢？
何西阿书13:6，耶和华说
“他们有了牧场就得到饱足
一饱足就心高气傲，因而忘记了我。”
这句话多么发人深省！
我们学到什么呢？
人一旦有了钱
也许就会变得不谦卑
我们绝对不希望这样的事发生
所以不管我们的经济情况怎样
我们都要下定决心
谦卑地依靠耶和华
而不是物质财富
现在来谈谈第五个
也是最后一个考验谦卑的情况
当我们受到称赞时
大家也许还记得
使徒行传12章提到
希律穿上王服
坐在审判座上
向聚集的人公开讲话
群众呼喊说
“这是神的声音，不是人的声音！”
接着发生了什么呢？
耶和华的天使打击他
他就被虫子咬死了
为什么会有这样的下场呢？
因为希律没有把荣耀归给耶和华
可是，耶稣呢？
路加福音18章说
有一位长官称耶稣为“良善的老师”
耶稣却说
“你为什么称我为良善的呢？
除了上帝一位
没有谁配称为良善的。”
我们从这两个记载学到什么呢？
当我们受人称赞时
是像希律那样把荣耀归给自己
还是像耶稣那样把荣耀归给耶和华呢？
我们可以在心里把荣耀归给耶和华
也可以通过言语表达出来
“称赞也可以试炼各人。”
称赞可以看出一个人是否真的谦卑
《守望台》曾描述
“称赞可以显露出我们的内在为人
明智人不会寻求称赞
也不会因称赞而变得自高自大
但爱慕虚荣的人会寻求他人的称赞
软弱的人则会因称赞而变得趾高气扬
如果一个人受到称赞却不骄傲
并清楚记得他的一切成就都来自耶和华
那么这个人在上帝眼中就是宝贵的。”
这五种情况可以使我们的谦卑受到考验
如果不小心
我们就会失去这个特质
有哪些情况呢？
第一、当我们获得某项服务机会时
第二、当我们取得成功时
第三、当我们受到劝告时
第四、当我们变得有钱时
第五、当我们受到称赞时
或许你还会想到其他一些情况
但重点是，如果我们想要保持谦卑
不被这些情况影响
我们就必须依靠耶和华的帮助
这样，我们就不会沦为上帝的敌人
反而会继续享有上帝所赐的分外恩典
