ko.text: 지부에는 동유럽의 몇몇 국가를 돌보도록 임명된
영적 양식을 전달하고, 비밀리에 모임을 갖고,
금지령 때문에 박해받는 현지 조직을 강화하는 일들을 했습니다.
우린 성경 인쇄용 종이를 사용해 초소형 서적을 인쇄했습니다.
그래야 더 많은 출판물을 그 나라들로 들여갈 수 있었거든요.
운반 요원들은 출판물을 자기 차에 숨긴 다음
그렇게 해서 수많은 서적이 운반될 수 있었습니다.
운반하는 형제가 출판물을 가지고 가다 국경에서 발각되면
하지만 그 형제들은 이 일을 보호하고
보통은 하루 이틀 지나면 형제들은 풀려났고
차가 압수되어서 대중 교통을 이용해 돌아가야 했어요.
그래도 그 형제들은 희생적으로 기꺼이 위험을 감수하고자 했습니다.
실제로 매년 수천 권 이상의 서적이
따라서 이 일을 할 수 있었던 건 우리가 아주 영리하게,
책들을 감쪽같이 숨겨 전달했기 때문이 아니에요.
우린 여호와의 성령이 돕고 있다는 걸 늘 온전히 확신했고,
또 우리는 동유럽의 형제들이 등사기를 사용해
같은 자료를 자체적으로 재생산할 수 있도록
또 다른 방법은 등사기를 그 나라에서 직접 제작하는 것이었는데,
아주 실력 있는 기술자 형제가 있었던 기억이 납니다.
그렇게 해서, 오프셋 인쇄기를 직접 만든 거죠.
형제들은 자기 집터를 파서 지하 인쇄실을
많은 경우, 형제들은 밤중에 인쇄 작업을 했습니다.
왜냐하면 공산 국가에서는 주간에 공장이나 아니면
다른 곳 어디든 가서 세속 일을 하지 않으면 안 되었기 때문이죠.
이 형제들이 보여 준 희생 정신은 정말 대단한 것입니다.
가족과 함께할 수 있는 개인 시간의 대부분을 희생한 것이지요.
어떤 형제들은 잠도 몇 시간 못 잤습니다.
하지만 여호와와 동료 형제들을 너무 사랑하니까
형제들은 개인 집에서 비밀리에 집회를 보았죠.
한 집에 어떤 사람들이 계속 들어가는 걸 이웃 사람들이 보면
그리고 매주 형제들의 집을 바꿔 가며 집회를 보았습니다.
우리의 활동을 보호하고 보안을 유지하는 데 도움이 되었죠.
형제들은 몇 번 노래인지 들으면 곧바로 부를 수 있었습니다.
노래는 형제들의 마음과 감정에 영향을 주었고,
그래서 충실함을 유지하려는 결심을 강화시켜 주었죠.
루마니아 형제들이 많은 압력을 받고 있었어요.
공산당은 형제들 사이에 불신의 씨를 뿌리려고 했습니다.
형제들을 따로 만나서 이 형제들에겐 이 말을,
그리고 정부 관리가 관심자인 척 위장하는 경우도 있었습니다.
단지 침례를 받는 정도가 아니라 심지어 장로가 되기까지 했습니다.
하지만 실제론 우리 조직에 대해 속속들이 알아내려고 잠입한
그래서, 한번은, 그로 인해 일부 형제들이,
그 뒤로 이 형제들은 여호와께서 사용하시는 조직에서
상당수의 사람들이 수 년 정도가 아니라
수십 년 동안 그렇게 분리되어 있었습니다.
그들은 계속 함께 모였고, 전파 활동도 했으며,
하지만 새로운 연구 자료는 거의 얻지 못했죠.
그 형제들을 다시 조직으로 돌아오게 하려고
우리를 충분히 신뢰하지 못하는 것 같아 보였습니다.
그는 반가워하면서 어느 정도 신뢰심을 보였습니다.
그래서 분리된 그룹의 인도자였던 알부 형제
그리고 그 그룹에서 네 명의 장로가 참석했고,
우리 측에서는 재라스 형제와 통역자 형제
또 루마니아 전국 위원회에 속한 형제 몇 명도 함께 참석했죠.
첫 날 저녁에는 서로가 했거나 하지 않은 일들에 대해
그래도 모두들 한 번 더 모이는 데 동의했죠.
여호와께서 형제들이 다시 연합하길 바라신다는 게 분명해졌습니다.
형제들은 터놓고 얘길 나누었고, 몇 가지 오해를 풀 수 있었습니다.
분리된 그룹의 인도자인 알부 형제가 한 말이 기억납니다.
그때부터, 재결합을 위한 실질적인 일들이 진행되었습니다.
그 형제들에게 우리 회중들과 다시 합치도록 제안했죠.
그러려면 그들 입장에선 상당한 겸손이 요구되었지만,
루마니아 형제들의 경험을 곰곰이 생각해 보면,
사람들 사이에는 언제든 오해가 생길 수 있다는 점과
책임을 맡은 형제들의 잘못된 행동 때문에
불평할 만한 정당한 이유가 생길 수도 있다는 걸 알게 됩니다.
이 조직이 여호와의 조직이라는 확신을 절대 잃지 않는 것이죠.
그분이 이루길 원하시는 일이 이루어질 것입니다.
우린 성공을 거두어 그분께 찬양을 돌리게 될 겁니다.

en.text: ‎I was serving at the Austria branch
‎from about the mid-1970’s to 1990.
‎We had a small department
‎that was assigned ‎to help certain countries in Eastern Europe.
‎And that included ‎visiting the brothers under ban,
‎bringing them spiritual food,
‎having secret meetings with them,
‎and also strengthening ‎the local organization
‎that was exposed ‎to persecution and ban.
‎We would print books on Bible paper
‎in miniature size.
‎This way, more books or literature
‎could be taken to these countries.
‎The couriers transported literature
‎to these countries ‎in their own private cars.
‎This way, ‎hundreds of books could be transported.
‎At the border, if a courier
‎would be found transporting literature,
‎they would interrogate the driver.
‎But these brothers were trained;
‎they knew what to say ‎to protect the work
‎and to not give away any secrets.
‎Usually, after a day or two days,
‎the officials would let them go back home
‎to their home country ‎but not with their car;
‎they had to use public transportation
‎because their cars would be confiscated.
‎But the brothers had the spirit of sacrifice; ‎they were willing to risk that.
‎But the majority got through, ‎and actually every year,
‎thousands of miniature books
‎were transported secretly ‎to Eastern Europe.
‎So it was not just a matter
‎of us being so clever in hiding things
‎and getting it to the brothers,
‎but we were always fully convinced ‎and had evidence
‎that it was Jehovah’s holy spirit ‎that helped us.
‎Also, we transported stencils
‎for local production ‎so that in their countries
‎they could reproduce the same material
‎with mimeographing machines.
‎In most cases, ‎the mimeographing machines
‎were transported secretly ‎by the couriers.
‎The other method ‎was to build it within the country.
‎I remember that there was a brother
‎who was a very skilled engineer,
‎and under his direction, ‎they decided to build it themselves.
‎So there were self-made ‎offset printing presses.
‎The brothers had a number ‎of underground printeries
‎that they had dug out ‎under their own homes.
‎In many cases, the brothers had to do ‎what they did during the night
‎because in Communist countries,
‎they had to go during the day
‎to a factory or whatever else ‎and do some secular work.
‎But it testifies to the great spirit
‎of sacrifice that the brothers showed
‎—to forfeit so much ‎of their private life as a family
‎to do at night the printing ‎of the spiritual food.
‎Some had only a few hours of sleep,
‎but they loved Jehovah ‎and the brothers so much
‎that they did it.
‎There was no Kingdom Hall.
‎The brothers ‎had secret meetings in private homes,
‎and they would not all come ‎at the same time
‎because if the neighbors ‎would see certain persons
‎all the time going to a specific house, ‎there could be suspicions.
‎And every week, they had the meetings
‎in a different home of the brothers.
‎And this helped to protect the work
‎so that it could be kept secret.
‎Singing was very important ‎for the brothers,
‎and they didn’t have to have ‎a songbook in hand.
‎They knew the text of the song by heart,
‎and immediately after saying a number,
‎they could sing the song.
‎That affected the heart ‎—the emotions of the brothers—
‎so they were strengthened ‎in their determination to be faithful.
‎A lot of pressure ‎was on the brothers in Romania.
‎The Communist Party tried
‎to sow distrust among the brothers,
‎meeting with them separately
‎and telling some brothers one thing
‎and telling other brothers something else.
‎Sometimes it happened
‎that an official posed ‎as an interested person
‎and was clever enough to disguise that
‎and pretend ‎to make progress in the truth
‎—not only to the point ‎of getting baptized
‎but even to the point ‎of becoming an elder.
‎But he was in reality an agent ‎of the secret police
‎with an aim to find out everything ‎about the organization.
‎So it did lead to, in one case,
‎the brothers starting to distrust someone
‎that was actually appointed by headquarters.
‎And these brothers then separated
‎from the organization that Jehovah used,
‎and some of them were separated
‎for not just a few years but for decades.
‎And they were a large number,
‎up to 5,000 publishers.
‎They continued to meet together.
‎They were preaching and using material
‎that they had left over from earlier years,
‎but they hardly got ‎any new material to study
‎because they were not in touch ‎with the organization
‎that was used by headquarters.
‎Attempts to bring the brothers back ‎into the organization
‎were made from time to time,
‎but it seemed that the brothers
‎from the separated organization ‎did not have sufficient trust.
‎But when we presented
‎to the leader of the separated group
‎that one ‎from the Governing Body would come,
‎he was happy about that ‎and he had enough trust in that case
‎to agree that we should have a meeting
‎and seriously talk about reunification.
‎And so from the separated group,
‎there were Brother Albu, ‎who was the leader,
‎and four of his main elders.
‎And from our side, ‎there was Brother Jaracz,
‎our translator, ‎and I was part of that group.
‎Also, there were several
‎from the Country Committee of Romania.
‎I remember that the first night ‎there were a lot of accusations
‎about what the others ‎had done or not done,
‎which did not create the best spirit,
‎and we mainly listened.
‎But everybody agreed ‎to meet another night.
‎And the second night, ‎Jehovah obviously wanted
‎the brothers to unite again
‎because the whole spirit was different,
‎and the brothers talked the matters over
‎and clarified some misunderstandings.
‎And at the end of the second evening,
‎I remember that the leader ‎of the separated group,
‎Brother Albu, said, ‎‘Let’s do it because if we don’t do it now,
‎we may never have ‎another opportunity again.’
‎And so the decision was made.
‎That doesn’t happen every day ‎that 5,000 brothers
‎come back to the organization.
‎From then on, all the practical things
‎were put in place ‎to accomplish this reunification.
‎They were asked to merge ‎with our congregations.
‎And that also took a lot of humility
‎on their part, ‎but they were willing to do it.
‎So they were really brothers
‎in their heart and loved the truth.
‎And so the reunification was accomplished,
‎and that was a wonderful victory ‎for Jehovah and against Satan.
‎Reflecting on the experience ‎with the brothers in Romania,
‎we can see that there could always be
‎misunderstandings among humans
‎and there could always be ‎even legitimate complaints
‎about the misconduct ‎of some responsible brothers.
‎But the important thing ‎is never to lose trust
‎that this is Jehovah’s organization.
‎That’s where Jehovah’s blessing is.
‎Jehovah sees it all.
‎Jehovah uses his holy spirit ‎to keep the organization together,
‎and what he wants ‎to have accomplished will happen.
‎If we work with the holy spirit,
‎then Jehovah will bless our efforts
‎and it will be successful to his praise.

cn.text: 我在奥地利分部服务
当时有一个部门
负责督导东欧几个国家的属灵活动
这个部门负责探访受禁制国家的弟兄姐妹
把组织的出版物运送给他们
跟他们一起举行秘密聚会
在有些地区工作受到禁止
弟兄们受到迫害
所以我们也会尽力强化他们
我们会缩小书刊的尺寸
也会用非常薄的纸张进行印刷
这样，我们就能多运送一些书刊
到这些国家了
弟兄们会用自己的车
把书刊运到那些受禁制的国家
有许多书刊都是这样运过去的
经过边境的时候
如果官员发现他们在运送书刊
就会把他们拦下来审问
但弟兄已经受过训练
知道该怎样回答才不会泄密
通常过一两天
官员就会放他们走
让他们回自己的家
但车子会被没收
所以弟兄们只能搭乘公共交通工具回去
弟兄们真的很有牺牲精神
为了弟兄姐妹他们甘愿冒险
不过，大部分情况下
运送工作都进行得很顺利
每年有数以千计的微型书刊
被秘密运送到这些东欧国家
工作能够顺利进行
绝对不是因为我们很聪明
很擅长掩人耳目
很多经历表明
这全都是耶和华的圣灵在帮助我们
我们确信这一点
我们也会运送一些印刷模板到这些国家
这样，那里的弟兄们
就能用油印机自己印刷书刊了
大多数油印机都是悄悄运进去的
不过也有一些是弟兄们自己制造的
我记得当时有位弟兄很懂机器
在他的帮助下
弟兄们决定自己制造机器
后来，我们有了自制的平板印刷机
一些弟兄还在自家的房子下面
建了地下印刷室
很多时候，弟兄们只能在夜里印刷书刊
这是因为他们生活在共产国家
白天都必须工作，去工厂上班
或是做些别的工作
但这些弟兄表现了非常美好的自我牺牲精神
很多个晚上
他们都牺牲了和家人在一起的时间
用来印制圣经书刊
有些弟兄晚上只能睡几个小时
他们深爱耶和华
深爱弟兄姐妹
所以甘愿作出这样的牺牲
那时没有聚会所
聚会会在弟兄姐妹的家里秘密地进行
另外，大家不能在同一时间过来
要不然，邻居看到同一群人
总是进出同一户人家
就会起疑心
弟兄姐妹也不会每周
都在同一个人的家里举行聚会
这样，当地的属灵活动
就能顺利地秘密进行了
唱诗歌对弟兄姐妹来说非常重要
他们不用看诗歌本
因为大家都把歌词背下来了
只要一说诗歌编号
就可以一起唱诗了
这些诗歌非常打动人心
牵动了弟兄们的感情
推动他们决心忠贞到底
罗马尼亚弟兄们的情况尤其不容易
共产党想破坏弟兄之间的信任
他们会单独约见一些弟兄
跟这个人这样说
跟另外一个人又那样说
有些官员还假装对圣经感兴趣
他们装得很像
看起来学得也很认真
有的人不仅受了浸
甚至还符合资格做了长老
但他其实是秘密警察派来的卧底
是来探查组织的所有底细的
结果，弟兄们开始彼此猜疑
甚至总部任命的弟兄也遭到了怀疑
后来不少弟兄就不再与耶和华的组织联系了
当时人数多达5000
他们当中有些人
甚至几十年都没有跟组织联系过！
他们有自己的组织安排
会一起聚会
也会去传道
但很难得到新的圣经书刊
只能用早年保留下来的书刊
因为他们跟上帝的组织已经没有来往了
组织好多次都想要帮助他们和组织恢复联系
但并不成功
因为这些弟兄还不够信任我们
后来，我们告诉他们当中带头的弟兄
这次会有一位中央长老团成员过来一起商讨
他听到这个消息后就很高兴
对这个安排比较有信心
也愿意跟我们见面
好好谈谈一起团结事奉耶和华的事
他们那边来了五个人
包括主要负责人阿尔布弟兄
还有另外四位长老
我们这边有杰拉斯弟兄
一位传译员
我也跟他们一起去了
另外，还有几位罗马尼亚地区委员会成员
我还记得
第一次见面的时候
气氛并不好
那几位离开的弟兄一直在诉苦
说自己受到了多么不公正的对待
我们基本上只是在听
不过，结束前大家都同意改天再接着讨论
第二次见面的时候
我们明显看出
耶和华希望我们团结起来
因为他们的态度完全不一样了
我们也有机会说明情况、澄清误会
我记得，第二次商谈结束的时候
他们的负责人阿尔布弟兄说
“我们再次团结起来吧
要是我们现在不这样做
恐怕以后就再也没有机会了。”
他们就这样回来了
一下子有5000位弟兄回到上帝的组织
这样的事情可不是每天都会发生的
从那时起，为了帮助这些回来的弟兄
组织作出了很多安排
也包括安排他们加入本地的会众
这非常需要谦卑的精神
但这些弟兄都乐意这样做
可见他们真的渴望回到上帝的组织
也发自内心地喜爱真理
我们重新团结起来了
耶和华大获全胜
撒但却一败涂地
回顾罗马尼亚弟兄们的经历
我们看出
人和人之间产生误会是在所难免的
甚至有的时候
我们感到不满也是有理由的
因为负有职责的弟兄
也可能会犯错
但重要的是，要记得这就是耶和华的组织
是蒙他赐福的组织
千万不要怀疑！
耶和华什么都知道
他会用圣灵帮助这个组织团结在一起
而且他总是说到做到
只要我们努力接受圣灵的指引
耶和华就一定会赐福给我们
我们的成就也会大大赞美耶和华

ko.text: 펜실베이니아 워치 타워 성서 책자 협회의
영적으로 유익한 연설과 격려적인 보고가 있었습니다.
또한 믿음을 강하게 해 주는 인터뷰도 있었는데,
그중에는 중앙장로회 성원인 게리트 뢰시 형제와 한
이제부터 2018년 연례 총회의 첫 부분을 즐기시기 바랍니다.
제가 할 첫 번째 연설의 제목은
이런 특별한 행사에 아주 적합한 주제라고 할 수 있겠죠.
여호와의 백성이 큰 바빌론의 영적인 포로가 된 때는
최근에 우리는 그때가 기원 2세기 언제쯤이란 걸 알게 됐습니다.
“억제하는 역할을 하고 있던” 사도들이 다 사망한 뒤인데요,
그리스도교국이라는 아주 못생긴 아기가 태어난 때입니다.
포로 상태에서 풀려나 순결한 숭배가 회복된 해입니다.
그 백 년의 세월 동안 여호와의 백성의 영적인 상태는 어땠습니까?
네, 우리의 상태는 점점 더 낙원과 같이 바뀌어 왔습니다.
그래서 오늘날에는 더없이 아름다운 영적 낙원이 되었죠.
원래의 낙원과 영적 낙원의 몇 가지 유사점을 살펴보죠.
—우리가 정말 낙원에 살고 있다는 걸 알게 되실 것입니다.
큰 바빌론의 포로 상태에서 해방시키셨다”고 말한 뒤,
기름부음받은 자들이 새로 태어난 나라가 되었다고 말합니다.
그런 다음 땅이 무엇인지 묻는데, 답은 이러합니다.
그것은 새로 태어난 나라에게 주어진 활동 영역입니다.
네, 성경의 예언들을 현대에 영적으로 성취시키는 활동들이죠.
기름부음받은 자들이 성경 예언을 성취시키는 활동 영역입니다.
에덴동산과 같이 우리의 영적 낙원에도 아름다운 풀과 나무가 있습니다.
네, 아담과 하와가 살던 에덴동산이 그랬단 건 분명한데,
성경에서는 하느님의 백성을 풀과 나무에 비유합니다.
이 비유적인 풀과 나무들도 열매를 많이 맺습니다.
여기 청중석에도 크고 아름다운 나무와 같은 분들이 많이 계신데요,
그럼, 세 번째 유사점을 생각해 보죠.
에덴동산과 같이 영적인 낙원도 식품이 풍부합니다.
이사야 65:13에서 여호와께선 그 점을 이렇게 대조해서 예언하셨죠.
날이 갈수록 점점 더 분명해지고 있습니다.
우리가 “여호와의 식탁”에서 먹는 음식을 비교해 보세요.
세상엔 영양가 없는 불량 식품과 해로운 식품이 넘쳐나지만
우리는 영적인 진수성찬을 즐기고 있지 않습니까?
영양가만 높은 게 아니라 맛까지 좋은 식품들을
우리는 출판물, 집회, 크고 작은 대회, jw.org,
그리고 최근엔 JW 방송에서 먹고 있습니다.
“네, 지금까지 여호와의 증인의 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다.”

수십 년간 충성스럽게 여호와와 왕국 권익을 위해
오랜 시간 충실함을 보인 많은 형제들에 더해,
여러분이 봉사의 특권을 놓아야 하는데도 말이죠.
하지만 주의 일에서 여러분이 나타낸 열심과 힘과
바울이 고린도 전서 15:58에서 한 말을 여기 계신 네 분과,
또 비슷한 상황에 있는 모든 형제들께 해 드리고 싶습니다.
확고하고 흔들리지 말며 항상 주의 일을 많이 하십시오.
여러분은 주와 관련된 여러분의 수고가 헛되지 않음을 알고 있습니다.”
이삼 주 후면 2부와 3부도 보실 수 있습니다.
중앙장로회 성원 다섯 명의 연설도 포함돼 있습니다.
모든 중앙장로회 성원을 만나시게 될 겁니다.
이번 달 방송을 마치기 전에, 크로아티아로 가 보실까요?
크로아티아는 유럽 남동부에 있는 다섯 개 나라에 둘러싸여 있습니다.
아름다운 해안에서 높이 솟은 산들에 이르기까지
나라 전역에 그림같이 아름다운 곳들이 많죠.
많은 외국인 근로자들과 관광객들과 난민들에게 증거하고 있습니다.
이 회중은 크로아티아 서부에 있는 자다르 회중입니다.
많은 섬들이 포함된 아주 넓은 구역에서 봉사합니다.
그들은 2015년에 크로아티아에서 열린 특별 지역 대회에 참석했습니다.
이 나라에서 진행된 특별 전파 활동에 참여하면서,
회중 구역에서 형제 자매들은 공개 증거용 전시대를 잘 활용해서
자다르 회중에 있는 모든 형제 자매들이
지금까지 여호와의 증인 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다.

en.text: We welcome all of you to the January 2019 broadcast.
The 2018 annual meeting
of the Watchtower Bible
and Tract Society of Pennsylvania
was held on October 6, 2018.
The program consisted of spiritually upbuilding talks
and encouraging reports.
It also included faith-strengthening interviews,
such as one with a member of the Governing Body,
Brother Gerrit Lösch.
Please enjoy the first part
of the 2018 annual meeting.
The theme for my opening talk is
“Appreciating Our Spiritual Paradise.”
And such a subject is very appropriate
on a special occasion like this.
But now let me ask you this:
When were Jehovah’s people taken into spiritual captivity
by Babylon the Great?
Well, we know that we’ve learned recently
that it was sometime in the second century C.E.
—after the death of the last of the apostles,
who were “acting as a restraint,”
and imitation Christians
began to infiltrate the congregation,
and the ugly baby Christendom was born.
But now, when did that captivity end?
Well, we know —1919—
the year when true anointed Christians
came out of captivity
and pure worship was restored.
And that means that because this is the year 2018,
Jehovah’s people have been set free for 99 years
—almost a hundred years now.
Now, what has been the spiritual condition of Jehovah’s people
during these nearly 100 years?
Well, our condition
has become more and more paradisaic.
And today,
it is truly like an exquisite paradise,
just like the garden of Eden
was truly an exquisite physical paradise.
In fact, let’s compare—
Let’s discuss some similarities
between that original Paradise and our spiritual paradise,
and we’ll see it is paradisaic
—this condition that we’re in.
Now, here’s the first similarity:
The garden of Eden, of course, had a land.
Well, our spiritual paradise has a land.
What is the land?
The July 1, 1995, Watchtower said
how “in 1919, Jehovah brought the anointed remnant
out of captivity to Babylon the Great.”
And then it says that that anointed group
became a newborn nation.
But then it asks, What is the land, though?
Here’s the answer:
It is the realm of activity granted to the newborn nation,
a place where Bible prophecies
have a modern, spiritual fulfillment.
So did you get that?
The realm of activity where the anointed fulfill Bible prophecies.
Now here’s a second similarity:
Like the garden of Eden,
our spiritual paradise has beautiful plants and trees.
Now, we certainly know that was true of the garden of Eden
where Adam and Eve were, but what about in our spiritual paradise?
Who are the plants and trees?
Well, the Bible likens God’s people
to plants and trees.
Here’s what 1 Corinthians 3:9 says:
“You [God’s people]
are God’s field under cultivation.”
Or think of Isaiah 61:3:
“And they [talking about God’s people]
“will be called big trees of righteousness,
the planting of Jehovah.”
And just like those plants and trees in the garden of Eden,
these figurative plants and trees bear much fruit
—the fruitage of lips, the fruitage of the spirit.
And just looking in the audience, we see many big, beautiful plants and trees
sitting out there,
and we’re happy to have you.
But now here is a third similarity:
Like the garden Eden, our spiritual paradise has abundant food.
Jehovah foretold it would exist
and, as a contrast, he said at Isaiah 65:13:
“Look! My servants will eat,
but you will go hungry.”
And especially today,
that contrast is more and more evident —isn’t it?—
between what the people of the world
are being served on “the table of demons”
and what we’re being served on “the table of Jehovah.”
I mean, they’re served empty calories
—junk food, poison food—
but we have a smorgasbord of spiritual things, don’t we?
We have these not only nutritious but delicious things
served in our publications, meetings,
assemblies, conventions, jw.org,
and, more recently, JW Broadcasting.
“This is JW Broadcasting
“from the world headquarters
of Jehovah’s Witnesses.”
You can see, I’m still working on that.
Here’s a fourth similarity:
The Bible tells us that out of the garden of Eden a river flowed.
So it must have been a large river,
and it divided into four other rivers.
Well, there must have been abundant, refreshing water in the garden of Eden.
Well, likewise in our spiritual paradise,
we have abundant spiritual water.
And again, Jehovah foretold it and the contrast.
At Isaiah 65:13, Jehovah said:
“Look! My servants will drink,
but you will go thirsty.”
It makes me think of what one young man
who was learning the truth
—this is what he said, a young man in Africa in his life story in The Watchtower—
said: “It seemed that my church
“had been giving me ‘acid’ to drink,
but now I was freely receiving the water of life.”
And he was so thankful to be set free
from the Trinity, worship of ancestors, and so forth.
Jehovah gives the invitation at Revelation 22:17:
“‘Come!’ and let anyone thirsting come;
let anyone who wishes take life’s water free.”
And we know that water represents
all of Jehovah’s provisions for gaining everlasting life.
Now here’s a fifth similarity:
Like the garden of Eden, our spiritual paradise
is a place that has many harmless animals.
Now, what do we mean by this?
Well, here’s what The Watchtower
said about this,
or I should say Isaiah’s Prophecy,
concerning the scripture, and we should read this first
—Isaiah 65:25.
Here’s what Jehovah foretold about harmless animals
at Isaiah 65:25:
“‘The wolf and the lamb will feed together,
“‘the lion will eat straw just like the bull,
“‘and the serpent’s food will be dust.
“‘They will do no harm nor cause any ruin
in all my holy mountain,’ says Jehovah.”
Now, there’ll be a literal fulfillment of this in the new world,
but there’s a figurative
—a spiritual— fulfillment right now.
And here’s what Isaiah’s Prophecy said
concerning that scripture we just read:
“Those coming into this spiritual paradise
make remarkable changes in their lives.”
Ones that previously had beastlike personalities,
the book said that with the help of the holy spirit,
they make drastic changes
and they tame those undesirable traits.
So that was the explanation of that scripture we just read.
And what a pleasure it is to fellowship
with you dear former wolves,
lions, bears,
and serpents also —throw that in there.
Now, you notice I said former.
In your former condition,
I wouldn’t have wanted to meet many of you in a dark alley,
and you would definitely say that about me
if I hadn’t been raised in the truth.
But what a pleasure to have these figurative, harmless animals!
Now here’s a sixth comparison:
Like the garden of Eden, our spiritual paradise
is a garden that needs maintenance.
Now, would you say that Jehovah is doing maintenance in this spiritual paradise?
Well, here’s Jesus’ answer: Look in John chapter 15,
John 15:2, Jesus said:
“He [Jehovah] takes away
“every branch in me not bearing fruit,
“and he cleans every one bearing fruit,
so that it may bear more fruit.”
Now, if you think of taking away unproductive branches
and cleaning productive ones to make it more productive,
is that not garden maintenance?
Well, what about us?
Are we expected to do maintenance?
Well, here is what the Organized to Do Jehovah’s Will book said:
“Your faith has brought you into a spiritual paradise.
“Benefiting from that paradise,
you have the responsibility to help maintain it.”
And then the book went on to say that by applying Bible counsel,
we help maintain our spiritual paradise.
Here’s one more similarity, number seven:
Our spiritual paradise,
like the garden of Eden,
has boundaries.
Now, regarding the garden of Eden, here’s what the Insight book said:
“It seems to have been an enclosed area,
bounded, no doubt, by natural barriers.”
And then it went on to say that it had an entrance on the eastern side,
and that, of course, was where the cherubs were placed to block the entrance.
Well, what about our spiritual paradise?
What are the boundaries?
Well, here are a few examples: 1 Corinthians 5:11
—stop keeping company with anyone who gets disfellowshipped.
We’re separate —a boundary.
Revelation 18:4 —get out of Babylon the Great.
We’re separate —a boundary.
What about John 17:14?
We must be no part of the world as Jesus was no part of the world.
We’re separate —a boundary.
But interestingly, Satan the Devil was able to lure
Adam and Eve out of their beautiful paradise home,
and he’s trying very hard to lure every one of us here
out of the boundaries of our wonderful spiritual paradise.
But we’re determined that we’re not going to let that happen.
But there, we have seven similarities,
and I’m sure you can think of others.
But truly, the situation we’re in
—the condition as Jehovah’s people—
is paradisaic.
And it is proof,
the reality of this spiritual paradise,
is proof that a literal paradise
will likewise soon become reality.
But now moving ahead in our program,
we’re going to have a privilege to look at a video.
The title of it is
Courage to Stand Firm in a Time of Trial.
And our video will be narrated by Brother Rick Ford,
who serves as the overseer
of the headquarters Museum Department
at Warwick.
And you’re going to enjoy this.
Brother Ford is going to really tell you
about something you’re going to look forward to visiting.
So let’s look at the monitors, please.
Courage to stand firm in a time of trial
—that’s the story of the Bible Students
from 1914 to 1919
and the theme of a new exhibit at world headquarters.
The tests they faced in those few pivotal years
are part of our spiritual heritage
that can strengthen our courage now
and for what lies ahead.
In the years just before 1914,
anticipation was high.
Since 1876,
Charles Taze Russell had published that the Gentile Times
would end in October 1914.
Many believed it would mean the end of their preaching work
and their being taken to heaven to rule with Christ.
The Bible Students spread their message by every means possible:
tracts, pamphlets,
and then in 1886
with The Plan of the Ages
—the first book in the Millennial Dawn series
(later called Studies in the Scriptures).
In December 1911,
Brother Russell embarked on an around-the-world tour.
And he went on an 8,000-mile (12,900-km)
transcontinental train tour in 1913.
When 1914 came,
so did a new way to expand the work.
The “Photo-Drama of Creation.”
The Bible’s message was now reaching millions.
Would 1914 turn out as they had hoped?
On June 28,
Austria’s Archduke Ferdinand was assassinated,
triggering the start of the Great War.
The end of the Gentile Times
seemed to be fulfilling expectations.
We held a convention at Columbus, Ohio.
I recall how that on June the 28th
right in the midst of that convention,
why, there was a shot fired
that was heard around the world.
When we read the newspaper, we said: “Aha!
“There it is, there it is.
The Gentile Times are drawing to their close.”
But 1914 brought unexpected trials
that would test the Bible Students’ faith
as never before.
The year 1914 came, and it went.
Contrary to expectations,
the heavenly reward did not come.
As they wondered how much longer they would need to preach,
they confronted a devastating turn of events.
Brother Russell died suddenly
on October 31, 1916.
We did not know what to do.
It was so unexpected,
and yet Russell had tried to prepare us for it.
What would we do?
The first shock of our loss of C. T. Russell was the worst.
For those first few days, our future was a blank wall.
In time, some felt
that all that God saw fit to reveal
had come through Brother Russell,
and that the revelation of truth had now ended.
After Joseph F. Rutherford was selected as the new president,
dissent arose among the Society’s directors.
On July 17, 1917,
the tension exploded with the publication of The Finished Mystery
—the seventh volume of Studies in the Scriptures,
based largely on Brother Russell’s earlier writings.
On that morning, a lengthy debate erupted
right in the Bethel dining room.
Vicious charges were hurled against Rutherford and his oversight.
Although four Society directors were soon dismissed from Bethel,
they soon began spreading their opposition
by an extensive speaking and letter-writing campaign
that threatened to divide the organization.
To disorganize the congregation,
they tried to put Brother Rutherford out.
So my uncle, he said:
“Well, this didn’t happen in Brother Russell’s day.
“I’m going to quit the whole business
and just read Brother Russell’s books.”
I said, “Well, I’m not going to quit the Society!”
I was convinced that the Society was God’s arrangement.
Another threat soon emerged.
Distribution of The Finished Mystery sparked renewed opposition
from religious and political leaders.
The book was banned
—first in Canada and then in the United States.
How did the Bible Students respond?
They launched a courageous campaign
to distribute Kingdom News No. 1, No. 2, and No. 3.
These boldly exposed clergy abuses
and defended the Bible Students’ Scriptural position.
But with the war still raging,
the next challenge demanded attention.
In many countries,
brothers took a neutral stand as conscientious objectors.
We were put into cells
that were more like dungeons.
Due to our refusal to undergo military drill,
a number of us
were taken to a secluded part
of the prison yard.
Lined up there were
a number of men in uniform
with canes in their hands.
One by one,
we were ordered to run the length of the court.
If the pace was too slow, we were seized
and dragged the distance and subjected
to lashes on the back and legs.
Beyond those persecuted for refusing military service,
others endured physical abuse instigated
by the clergy because of their courageous preaching.
Any uncertainty that our brothers may have felt
was only intensified by what happened next.
On May 7, 1918,
federal arrest warrants were issued
for Joseph Rutherford and seven associates.
They were charged with causing insubordination,
disloyalty, and refusal of duty in the military
and naval forces of the United States.
A month later, they were pronounced guilty
and given concurrent sentences
ranging from ten to twenty years
in a federal penitentiary.
The Brooklyn Tabernacle was sold,
and remaining operations were transferred back
to Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania.
These were dark and confusing times,
but Jehovah would not abandon his courageous people.
On March 26, 1919,
Brother Rutherford and his associates were released.
Seeking Jehovah’s will,
Brother Rutherford scheduled a public meeting
in Los Angeles, California,
on May 4, 1919.
It was a test.
Were people still interested in the Bible’s message?
Within 20 minutes after the doors opened,
the auditorium was filled to capacity.
About 3,500 showed up,
and another 600 were turned away with the promise
that an overflow meeting would be held the following day.
An additional 1,500 showed up to hear the second talk.
There was clearly much more work to do.
Bethel operations were moved back to Brooklyn.
Plans were made immediately for the 1919 Cedar Point convention
which was held four months later
—a turning point that reignited the preaching work.
New tools, including The Golden Age magazine, were released.
A Service Department was established at Bethel.
Service directors were appointed
to organize preaching in each congregation.
And as we now understand, “the faithful and discreet slave”
was commissioned to feed God’s flock.
Isaiah 46:8 says:
“Remember this, and take courage.”
Remember how these faithful ones preached an unpopular message,
how they moved forward despite unrealized expectations,
how they stayed loyal to God’s organization when others did not,
how they suffered when staying neutral in the world’s wars.
Remember their courageous example,
and take courage now
and in the days ahead.
Thank you very much, Brother Ford,
for sharing that very interesting theocratic history
concerning our spiritual predecessors,
the Bible Students.
And you’ve made us very eager
to visit our new museum exhibit.
But now we’re going to get to enjoy another video treat.
Brother Gerrit Lösch of the Governing Body
is going to share with us
some fascinating experiences from Eastern Europe.
I was serving at the Austria branch
from about the mid-1970’s to 1990.
We had a small department
that was assigned to help certain countries in Eastern Europe.
And that included visiting the brothers under ban,
bringing them spiritual food,
having secret meetings with them,
and also strengthening the local organization
that was exposed to persecution and ban.
We would print books on Bible paper
in miniature size.
This way, more books or literature
could be taken to these countries.
The couriers transported literature
to these countries in their own private cars.
This way, hundreds of books could be transported.
At the border, if a courier
would be found transporting literature,
they would interrogate the driver.
But these brothers were trained;
they knew what to say to protect the work
and to not give away any secrets.
Usually, after a day or two days,
the officials would let them go back home
to their home country but not with their car;
they had to use public transportation
because their cars would be confiscated.
But the brothers had the spirit of sacrifice; they were willing to risk that.
But the majority got through, and actually every year,
thousands of miniature books
were transported secretly to Eastern Europe.
So it was not just a matter
of us being so clever in hiding things
and getting it to the brothers,
but we were always fully convinced and had evidence
that it was Jehovah’s holy spirit that helped us.
Also, we transported stencils
for local production so that in their countries
they could reproduce the same material
with mimeographing machines.
In most cases, the mimeographing machines
were transported secretly by the couriers.
The other method was to build it within the country.
I remember that there was a brother
who was a very skilled engineer,
and under his direction, they decided to build it themselves.
So there were self-made offset printing presses.
The brothers had a number of underground printeries
that they had dug out under their own homes.
In many cases, the brothers had to do what they did during the night
because in Communist countries,
they had to go during the day
to a factory or whatever else and do some secular work.
But it testifies to the great spirit
of sacrifice that the brothers showed
—to forfeit so much of their private life as a family
to do at night the printing of the spiritual food.
Some had only a few hours of sleep,
but they loved Jehovah and the brothers so much
that they did it.
There was no Kingdom Hall.
The brothers had secret meetings in private homes,
and they would not all come at the same time
because if the neighbors would see certain persons
all the time going to a specific house, there could be suspicions.
And every week, they had the meetings
in a different home of the brothers.
And this helped to protect the work
so that it could be kept secret.
Singing was very important for the brothers,
and they didn’t have to have a songbook in hand.
They knew the text of the song by heart,
and immediately after saying a number,
they could sing the song.
That affected the heart —the emotions of the brothers—
so they were strengthened in their determination to be faithful.
A lot of pressure was on the brothers in Romania.
The Communist Party tried
to sow distrust among the brothers,
meeting with them separately
and telling some brothers one thing
and telling other brothers something else.
Sometimes it happened
that an official posed as an interested person
and was clever enough to disguise that
and pretend to make progress in the truth
—not only to the point of getting baptized
but even to the point of becoming an elder.
But he was in reality an agent of the secret police
with an aim to find out everything about the organization.
So it did lead to, in one case,
the brothers starting to distrust someone
that was actually appointed by headquarters.
And these brothers then separated
from the organization that Jehovah used,
and some of them were separated
for not just a few years but for decades.
And they were a large number,
up to 5,000 publishers.
They continued to meet together.
They were preaching and using material
that they had left over from earlier years,
but they hardly got any new material to study
because they were not in touch with the organization
that was used by headquarters.
Attempts to bring the brothers back into the organization
were made from time to time,
but it seemed that the brothers
from the separated organization did not have sufficient trust.
But when we presented
to the leader of the separated group
that one from the Governing Body would come,
he was happy about that and he had enough trust in that case
to agree that we should have a meeting
and seriously talk about reunification.
And so from the separated group,
there were Brother Albu, who was the leader,
and four of his main elders.
And from our side, there was Brother Jaracz,
our translator, and I was part of that group.
Also, there were several
from the Country Committee of Romania.
I remember that the first night there were a lot of accusations
about what the others had done or not done,
which did not create the best spirit,
and we mainly listened.
But everybody agreed to meet another night.
And the second night, Jehovah obviously wanted
the brothers to unite again
because the whole spirit was different,
and the brothers talked the matters over
and clarified some misunderstandings.
And at the end of the second evening,
I remember that the leader of the separated group,
Brother Albu, said, ‘Let’s do it because if we don’t do it now,
we may never have another opportunity again.’
And so the decision was made.
That doesn’t happen every day that 5,000 brothers
come back to the organization.
From then on, all the practical things
were put in place to accomplish this reunification.
They were asked to merge with our congregations.
And that also took a lot of humility
on their part, but they were willing to do it.
So they were really brothers
in their heart and loved the truth.
And so the reunification was accomplished,
and that was a wonderful victory for Jehovah and against Satan.
Reflecting on the experience with the brothers in Romania,
we can see that there could always be
misunderstandings among humans
and there could always be even legitimate complaints
about the misconduct of some responsible brothers.
But the important thing is never to lose trust
that this is Jehovah’s organization.
That’s where Jehovah’s blessing is.
Jehovah sees it all.
Jehovah uses his holy spirit to keep the organization together,
and what he wants to have accomplished will happen.
If we work with the holy spirit,
then Jehovah will bless our efforts
and it will be successful to his praise.
Thank you so much, Brother Lösch,
for sharing those captivating experiences.
But now we’re going to get to show you
a one-minute video trailer
to whet your appetite for something that is coming.
Since the beginning,
people have been given a choice.
Some have chosen to do what is wrong.
Others chose to make Jehovah happy.
What you do every day
can make his heart rejoice.
I know you will make Jehovah happy.
We’re looking forward to this new video.
But the question is,
When will we and our children
get to enjoy this video?
Well, we are happy to inform you
that in less than six months,
you’re going to be able to have this video.
Now, you don’t look like you’re too happy about that.
Well, I was teasing you;
I was truthful, though.
In less than six months, much less than six months,
in fact, right now,
you’re going to get to enjoy
the nine-minute epic video
Make Jehovah Happy.
From the beginning, Jehovah has always cared about people.
Sadly, many of them have caused him great pain.
But some have made him very happy.
Jesus always made Jehovah happy.
Satan didn’t like this.
He tried everything to get Jesus to do what was wrong.
If you are a son of God,
tell these stones to become loaves of bread.
It is written: “Man must not live on bread alone.”
Grr!
Hmm.
If you are a son of God, throw yourself down,
for the angels will carry you on their hands,
so you may not strike your foot against a stone.
Prove it to them.
Again it is written: “You must not put Jehovah your God to the test.”
Grr. Hmm.
See all this glory;
it is mine.
And I give it to whomever I wish.
And all these things I will give to you
if you fall down and do an act of worship to me.
Hmm.
Go away, Satan!
For it is written: “It is Jehovah your God you must worship,
and it is to him alone you must render sacred service.”
Jesus was determined to make Jehovah happy.
But this story isn’t over.
This is your story too.
What do you mean, Dad?
Well, what you do can make Jehovah happy.
Our text this morning, Proverbs 27:11
—Do you remember what that says?
Oh, yeah!
It says: “Be wise, my son, and make my heart rejoice.”
Good memory, Sophia!
That scripture is talking about you.
What you do every day,
not only big things
but also small things you do,
can make His heart rejoice.
Remember today’s text, children.
I know you’ll make Jehovah happy.
Let’s pray.
OK, kids.
It’s a pop quiz today!
Oh, man!
Yes!
Now, Sophia, if you ace this test,
you’ll be number one in the whole class.
Oh, yeah! You’re at the next level.
Keep going! Keep going!
. . . number one in the whole class.
Hey! You got this one?
Yeah, here.
Hey, Sophia!
You want the answer?
Oh, man!
That stinks. You lost!
Hey, Caleb!
You want to play?
Come on; it’s fun!
Um.
Forget it.
He’s a loser!
Let me play with it!
Are you going to play or not?
Yay!
Yeah!
Nooooo!
Caleb! Caleb! Caleb! Caleb! Caleb!
Caleb? Caleb? Caleb?
You going to play?
Hey, Sophia!
You want the answer?
And you too can have success!
That’s OK.
No, thanks.
There are certainly a lot of powerful lessons in that video
for our young ones and even for us.
And we’re happy to inform you that in less than six months,
you’ll be able to download—
I don’t think you’re going to fall for that again.
Here’s the real announcement:
“Some of you with nephews, nieces, children,
“or grandchildren are wondering,
“‘When will these little ones be able to see this video?’
“You’ll be happy to know that the video Make Jehovah Happy
“will be posted in over 100 languages
“this coming Monday, October the 8th,
“on both JW Broadcasting
and on the jw.org website.”
In two days, you’ll have it.
But now we’re going to get to enjoy
an interview that will be conducted
by Brother Samuel Herd of the Governing Body.
And he’s going to interview four brothers who have a lot to tell us,
but he’s going to do his best to hold them down to 19 minutes.
Look at the monitors, please.
We have four brothers with us—
Brother Stephen Hardy is serving in the Britain branch;
Brother Lorence Shepp is serving in Peru;
Brother Reiner Thompson’s current assignment
is in the Dominican Republic;
and last, alphabetically, is Brother Leon Weaver
who is serving on the United States Branch Committee.
All four of these brothers have at least two things in common.
First, they’ve all served as the Branch Committee coordinator
of their respective branches for a number of years.
And second, all four have hit a milestone in life
according to Psalm 90:10.
There, these brothers are identified as being “especially strong.”
Why so?
Because their life span is cresting 80 years of age.
It takes extra vitality and stamina
to still be walking and talking at that age and to still be making sense.
Believe me, I know!
I asked to retire at 80.
The Governing Body said, “Not until you lose it.”
I said, “Well . . . ”
Brother Weaver, what did all four of you
find out on May 26, 2014?
All Branch Committees got a letter from the Governing Body,
and that letter told us about a new policy.
And that new policy was
that once a Branch Committee coordinator
reaches the age of 80,
he would not be able to serve
as Branch Committee coordinator anymore.
But the Branch Committee would look for a younger brother
who could qualify to do that
and then recommend the younger brother to be the Branch Committee coordinator.
Would any of you like to describe your first thoughts
when you read that new policy?
Well, Brother Herd, I remember some words of my dad.
He worked in the circuit work in his senior years
but would tell me,
“Now son, if you see that I’m starting to lose it,
you be sure to tell me and get me to stop.”
Oftentimes, we don’t realize
that age takes a toll on our effectiveness.
I remember as a younger man
looking how far would I be able to do this work.
I thought, ‘Well, maybe at 65
I should step off from being the coordinator.’
Everybody retires at 65.
When I was 65, I felt pretty good.
So I went on to 70.
When 70 was drifting by, I felt pretty good.
I went on to 75, and I know if that new policy hadn’t come out,
I would probably have been setting it up to 85 or who knows where.
But really, for the benefit of the work,
we need to have younger men.
Experienced?
Yes, but younger and vigorous for the benefit of the work
and for the benefit of those with whom we work with on the committee.
Much of the branch work,
especially with the work of the coordinator, recently,
has to do with modern technology.
So as a result of this,
when I was serving as coordinator,
I had to use a younger, spiritually-minded brother
to keep me up to speed, as it were, to what was required.
So besides the aging process,
when the changes came,
I had no doubt that it was Jehovah’s decision.
And so then for me,
I was very happy to accept the change
without any questions or any doubts.
And then there was an additional paragraph in that policy letter
that said that if a coordinator is not yet 80 years of age
but he feels that now would be the best time
for a younger brother to take on that responsibility,
then his request should be considered.
Well, I was just 75 at that time.
But I began to realize that in the coming years,
after a couple of years with the Britain branch construction
and relocation project,
I realized that the responsibilities would become even more intense.
And because of the major organizational adjustments that we’d have,
I realized that it would be good to request a younger brother to take over.
I was just 79 when that change took place.
That was a very modest thing to do.
Thank you, brothers, for your comments.
I can’t help myself; I have to ask this:
What were your wives’ reactions to the new policy?
Did they leap for joy?
Don’t answer that second question.
Well, Ruby thought
it was a loving arrangement for us.
And actually, she thought that it would be
the best for her and for me.
And I agreed with her.
In our case, Brother Herd, down through the years
we’ve been surprised by many reassignments.
And Jeanne has always been
100 percent cooperative with all theocratic assignments.
But as assignments would come, she would pack or unpack,
whatever was the order of the moment.
With the new policy, she accepted it wholeheartedly,
and she was happy that she didn’t have to pack or unpack on this one.
And Ann’s reaction first of all was, “What are you going to do?”
So she realized that I’m always involved with my work.
I like to have plenty to do.
But she was fully supportive of the arrangement.
You know that was the same with Olimpia.
Of course, she was surprised.
We were all surprised.
But from the very moment,
just a few seconds after I told her of the change,
she accepted it.
And she was willing to cooperate,
because as she said,
she knew that this was direction by the faithful slave.
Solomon asked: “Who can find a capable wife?”
All four of you just answered that question beautifully.
I’m sure you remember the account of Barzillai
in 2 Samuel chapter 19.
He was very helpful to King David.
David offered for him to be part of the royal court,
but Barzillai had now turned 80 years of age.
He declined because he knew
he would not be as useful in the days ahead.
Instead, the privilege went to Chimham, a younger man.
Did that account come to your mind with this policy change?
I was convinced that the Governing Body was probably using
that to consider their new changes or policy.
I was 80 years of age.
I was still strong; I was still vigorous.
But I do have to admit that it crossed my mind, many times,
‘There’s going to come a time, Shepp,
‘when you’re going to have to relinquish
your privileges to somebody younger.’
And so then when the change came,
I accepted it as coming from Jehovah
and I had no doubts that it was the direction of the faithful slave.
Yes, I did think of Barzillai.
But then my mind went to his replacement, Chimham.
And I realized that on our Branch Committee
we had several younger brothers who were like Chimhams.
So I was at peace with that arrangement.
I must admit, Brother Herd,
that I reviewed this case of Barzillai.
But there was one thing about what he said and did
that I didn’t agree with.
Well, he said that he’d like to go back to his hometown and die.
Rather, I thought,
‘I’ll use my energies as much as I can
in other activities connected with our assignment.’
I’m sure that is the spirit of all four of you.
At what age did you dedicate your life to Jehovah?
And describe some of the privileges you have enjoyed since then.
At 13, I was baptized.
By 17, I was in regular pioneer work.
At 21, my faithful wife, Jeanne, and I graduated from Gilead
and were assigned to Puerto Rico.
We went into the missionary work in Puerto Rico
for about a year and a half to learn the language,
and then we had the privilege of circuit work.
Later, the Governing Body invited us —invited me—
to take up the Branch Committee work in Belize
when it used to be called British Honduras.
And from there, we were transferred to Nicaragua
as Branch Committee members.
And from there, we were deported
in the revolutionary years to Costa Rica.
I had the privilege to work with Brother Shepp for six years
in Costa Rica on the Branch Committee,
and there was also a branch building going on at that time.
And then, we’ve been for the last 30 years privileged to serve
with the Dominican Republic Branch Committee.
Over the last eight years,
it’s been our privilege to serve as headquarters representatives
in branch visits
and getting to know so many faithful and hardworking Bethelites
in different parts of the world, it truly—
It’s a wonderful organization to be working with.
And with me, Brother Herd, I was 17 when I was baptized.
And in 1957, I started to regular pioneer.
And in 1965,
the Governing Body appointed me to be a traveling overseer,
and Ruby and I traveled for 12 years,
And in 1977, they called us in to Bethel.
So we’ve been at Bethel for the last 41 years,
and about 23 years ago,
they invited me to visit
other branches throughout the globe.
And we’ve had quite an interesting and encouraging time doing that.
And we’ve had the privilege of you being a helper to the Service Committee
of the Governing Body since 1992.
You’ve racked up quite a life of dedicated service.
I was baptized at the age of 19.
I took up the full-time service
In 1960, I was appointed to be a circuit overseer.
I served in parts of Ontario, Quebec.
And then while serving there,
I was assigned to northwest Canada,
which included part of Alaska.
And after getting there, only four months or so,
we were called to Brooklyn
to attend the newly formed Kingdom Ministry School.
During our visit at Brooklyn,
Brother Knorr talked to some of us Canadians and he asked us,
“Would you be willing to accept
a missionary assignment without going to Gilead?”
Well, this was a marvelous opportunity,
and I was accepted
and later assigned to Nicaragua.
So just after a couple of years, I wanted to get married.
I wrote.
And Brother Knorr had kind of softened
his opinion about getting married at that time.
So 55 years ago,
I married Olimpia,
and we’ve been serving together in several countries.
We were assigned to Costa Rica
where we served together for 27 years.
And on the second of October,
we just completed another 25 years
of serving under the Peru branch.
I also consider it a tremendous privilege
having been assigned the privilege of visiting other branches
and sharing encouragement with them,
and that we’ve been doing for a little bit more than 20 years.
I’m getting tired out just listening to the work
you brothers have done over the years.
Brother Hardy, your story, please.
Well, I dedicated my life to Jehovah when I was 11 years old.
And then I started pioneering at 18, then special pioneered.
And when I was just 22,
my wife and I were invited into the circuit work.
And then in 1963, we got a surprise.
We were invited to Gilead
and from Gilead we were assigned to Burundi in Africa.
Well, we never heard of Burundi.
So immediately we went to get our Yearbook
to find out how many publishers there were in Burundi.
We looked down the list, but Burundi wasn’t even on the list,
so we suddenly realized we were going into virgin territory.
But sadly, the authorities in Burundi were not happy about that,
and after just four months, we had to leave the country.
And we were reassigned to Uganda.
And then we served there for ten years,
and again, there were difficulties in Uganda.
And so we were reassigned this time to Côte d’Ivoire,
and we served there for another ten years.
But then, my wife had gotten some medical problems,
and we had to return to Britain in 1983.
And after some years, she died.
But then a little later,
there was a commuter Bethel sister in London Bethel,
and her desire was to become a regular Bethelite.
And she knew the only way to do that,
according to her, was to marry a Bethel brother.
Well, I found her personality very attractive,
and what’s more, she was a really spiritual person.
So I succumbed.
And so Ann and I—
We’ve been serving happily in London Bethel since 1989.
And like the other brothers, I’ve had the privilege of serving
as a headquarters representative.
And we’ve visited some 60 branches and have thoroughly enjoyed that.
Thank you for that brief overview of your lives.
According to my notes, all told,
Brother Hardy has served
as a Branch Committee member for 38 years.
For the last 19 years,
he has been the coordinator of the Britain branch.
Brother Shepp, according to my calculations,
has served as a member of a Branch Committee for 52 years
and 48 of those years as the coordinator to a Branch Committee.
Brother Thompson has been serving
as a Branch Committee member for some 50 years,
with 44 of those years
as the coordinator of a Branch Committee.
Some of you who are newer to the organization might not realize it,
but there was not an official Branch Committee
in the United States until April 1, 2001.
Brother Weaver was appointed
as a Branch Committee member from its inception.
So that is now 17 years as a member of that Branch Committee,
and he has served as the coordinator for the past 11 years.
Being the coordinator of a Branch Committee
is a full-time job —and then some.
So I’m sure everyone is wondering what your new assignments entail.
Brother Hardy?
Well, I work in the Branch Committee Office,
and I do some proofreading of letters to other branches
and to the different committees of the Governing Body.
I’m one of the three brothers assigned from the Branch Committee
assigned to work in the Service Department,
and one of my assignments is to include shepherding.
I’ve had the privilege of calling personally
the 97 traveling overseers
and talking to them and to many of their wives.
I’ve been able to call the 52 field missionaries,
and I’ve been able to visit personally every one of the Bethel family.
I have a goal.
We have 47 very faithful special pioneers
that are not able to do as much as they used to.
So I’m starting to call them, and my goal is,
by the end of this calendar year, to be able to talk to every one of them.
The Branch Committee has assigned me to the area of what we call BRED,
which is Branch Real Estate Desk.
They’ve also given me the privilege,
having participated in the construction of two branches,
to help the younger brothers take advantage of the training programs
that we have in place for them.
Well, Brother Herd, all of us are still on the Branch Committee,
and there’s still much work to do in connection to the Branch Committee.
We have shepherding to do
of traveling overseers and Bethel family members.
We also still give our convention assignments.
We will do circuit assemblies.
And myself, personally,
I’d like to increase my field service time
with my congregation and with my wife, Ruby.
Thank you, brothers, for your many decades
of loyal dedicated service to Jehovah and to Kingdom interests.
And along with so many longtime faithful ones,
it is heartwarming to hear that you fully embrace
the decision of the faithful slave,
even if it means relinquishing a privilege of service.
But that in no way has any bearing on your zeal, energy,
and enthusiasm for the Lord’s work.
The Governing Body applies Paul’s words at 1 Corinthians 15:58
to the four of you and all of the others
who find themselves in similar circumstances.
There it says:
“Therefore, my beloved brothers,
“be steadfast, immovable,
“always having plenty to do in the work of the Lord,
“knowing that your labor is not in vain
in connection with the Lord.”
Thank you for joining us,
and thank your wives for their unwavering support
of your many responsibilities.
Thank you very much, Brother Herd and company,
for that delightful interview.
We love you five brothers very much.
What an encouraging program!
Parts 2 and 3 will be released over the next couple of weeks.
They’ll include talks given by five members of the Governing Body.
So by the time you see all three parts,
you will have heard from each member of the Governing Body.
To bring to an end this month’s broadcast,
we’ll travel to Croatia.
Croatia is nestled between five other countries
in southeastern Europe.
It has many picturesque locations throughout,
ranging from a beautiful coastline
to towering mountaintops.
There are around 5,000 publishers in the country.
In May 2018, the first foreign-language group was formed.
The English group, located in the capital city, Zagreb,
reaches out to the many foreign workers,
tourists, and refugees.
Croatia is also experiencing growth
in the sign-language and Roma fields.
This is the Zadar Congregation in western Croatia.
The 120 publishers there
have been assigned a vast territory,
which includes many islands.
they were able to attend the special convention held in Croatia.
And in the fall of 2018,
they participated in and hosted delegates
for a special preaching campaign in their country.
In their local territory,
they make effective use of public witnessing carts
to reach out to tourists and other passersby.
There are ten publishers in the congregation
serving as regular pioneers,
seven as elders, and four as ministerial servants.
All our dear brothers and sisters in the Zadar Congregation
send you their warm greetings.
From the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting.

耶和华的子民从什么时候开始
在属灵上成为大巴比伦的俘虏呢？

假基督徒开始混进会众当中
邪恶丑陋的基督教婴儿就诞生了
那么上帝的子民

并且复兴了正确的崇拜

意味着耶和华的子民已经获得自由99年
将近100年了
在这期间
耶和华子民的属灵情况怎么样呢？

我们越来越快乐
越来越和睦
今天，我们仿佛置身于一个实际的乐园

看看实际的乐园

耶和华把受膏基督徒
从大巴比伦的奴役中拯救出来

应验圣经里的预言
大家明白了吗？

我们的属灵乐园跟伊甸园一样
在亚当和夏娃曾经住的伊甸园里
那里一定有很多漂亮的花草树木
我们的属灵乐园里也有

是上帝耕种的田地。”
以赛亚书61:3说

要称为正义的大树
是耶和华所栽种的。”
就像伊甸园的那些花草树木一样

也培养圣灵果实的特质
看看现场的弟兄姐妹们
这里有许多茁壮、漂亮的花草树木
我们非常高兴能跟你们一起崇拜上帝
第三个相似之处是
我们的属灵乐园跟伊甸园一样

在以赛亚书65:13
耶和华把我们跟世人做了个对比
预言说
“我的仆人必得吃，你们却饥饿。”
尤其在今天，这个对比越来越明显
世人在“邪灵的宴席”上吃喝

世人吃的食物没有营养

有毒的食品
我们吃的却是满汉全席
我们的食物不仅有营养
而且很美味
比如，我们的出版物、聚会、大会
jw.org网站
还有JW电视网
“这里是耶和华见证人
世界总部的JW电视网”
你看，我还在练习说这句话
第四个相似之处
圣经记载说
有一条河从伊甸园流出来
这肯定是一条大河
因为它又分成了四条河流
所以，伊甸园里河水充足又清澈
属灵乐园也是这样
有充足的生命之水
耶和华在以赛亚书65:13
做了另一个对比
预言说
“我的仆人必得喝，你们却干渴。”
这让我想起了一个刚认识真理的年轻人
他住在非洲
《守望台》有他的经历
这个年轻人说
“教会给我喝的水是有害的

他很高兴能摆脱三位一体
祖先崇拜等错误道理
耶和华在启示录22:17
发出邀请说
“‘来吧！’谁渴了都要来
谁愿意，都要白白取生命的水喝。”
水象征耶和华提供的属灵资源
喝生命之水会带给我们永生
现在看一下第五个相似点
跟伊甸园一样
我们的属灵乐园也有很多不伤人的动物
这是什么意思呢？
《守望台》曾经谈到这一点
《以赛亚的预言》这本书也谈到了
这跟哪节经文有关呢？
我们来看看以赛亚书65:25
在这里，耶和华预言说
“豺狼必与绵羊羔同吃
狮子像牛一样吃草
尘土要作蛇的食物
在我的整个圣山上
这一切都不伤人，不害物。”
我们知道
这个预言会在新世界得到真正的应验
不过，现在在属灵方面已经得到了应验
《以赛亚的预言》谈到这节经文时说
“加入属灵乐园的人
都在生活上改弦易辙。”
像刚才经文描述的那样
有些人在学习真理之前
性格非常凶残
后来在圣灵的帮助下
他们做出非常大的改变
除去了不良的品格
现在我们能和睦共处
多么开心啊！
你们以前好像狼
狮子
熊
还有的像蛇一样
别忘了
我是说以前的你们啊！
那时，我肯定不想在黑漆漆的夜晚里
碰到你们
当然
你们肯定也不想碰到
还没有学习真理的我
但是，让我们高兴的是
我们都做出了改变
现在看一下第六个相似点
跟伊甸园一样
我们的属灵乐园也需要维护
也许你会问
耶和华正在维护这个属灵乐园吗？
我们看看耶稣怎么回答
在约翰福音15:2，耶稣说
“我的枝子，凡不结果实的
他［也就是耶和华］就除掉
凡结果实的，他就修整干净
叫果实结得更多。”
除掉不结果实的枝子
把结果实的枝子修整干净
好多结果实
这不就是园林维护嘛！
我们呢？
我们也要做维护工作吗？
《组织》书说
“由于有信心
你得以生活在一个属灵的乐园里
可是，既然有权利享受属灵的乐园
自然有义务要尽力维护这个乐园。”
这本书接着说
我们实践圣经原则
就能让属灵乐园变得欣欣向荣
另一个相似点
第七点
跟伊甸园一样
属灵乐园也有边界
谈到伊甸园
《洞悉》书说
“这园子看来有固定的范围
也许四周有天然屏障围住。”
接着又说
园子的东边有一个入口

title: 제145기 길르앗 졸업식—결론 연설 및 임명

ko.text: 이제 졸업식의 결론 연설을 들을 시간입니다.
중앙장로회 성원인 스티븐 레트 형제가 해 주실
여러분이 제일 좋아하는 성경 인물은 누구입니까?
길르앗에서 여러분은 여러 성경 인물을 살펴보며
그들의 좋은 본이나 나쁜 본에서 교훈을 얻으셨죠.
이 연설을 통해서 매우 흥미로운 성경 인물인
베드로에게서 배울 수 있는 많은 교훈 중 몇 가지 점을 살펴보겠습니다.
여호와와 예수에 대해 무엇을 배울 수 있는지 알아보죠.
한 가지 분명한 교훈은, 여호와와 예수께서
자신의 종들의 다양한 성격을 인정하실 뿐 아니라
그 점을 이해하기 위해 베드로의 성격을
다른 몇몇 사도들의 성격과 비교해 보겠습니다.
서로 다른 두 성격을 잘 보여 주는 흥미로운 내용이 나옵니다.
“그러자 베드로와 그 다른 제자 [아마도 요한]이 무덤을 향해 떠났다.
다른 제자가 베드로보다 더 빨리 달려가 무덤에 먼저 도착했다.
그가 몸을 굽혀 안을 보니 아마포 천이 그곳에 놓여 있었다.
시몬 베드로가 뒤따라와서 무덤 안으로 들어가 보니,
요한은 안을 들여다봤고, 베드로는 안으로 들어갔죠.
무리가 예수를 붙잡으러 겟세마네에 왔을 때,
대제사장의 종을 쳐서 그의 오른쪽 귀를 잘랐다고 알려 줍니다.
과연 베드로가 노렸던 게 오른쪽 귀였을까요?
의도한 대로 정확히 오른쪽 귀를 잘랐으니까요.
하지만 베드로는 칼 쓰는 사람이 아니었죠.
네, 베드로의 성격이 얼마나 충동적이었는지 잘 보여 줍니다!
갈릴리 바닷가에 나타나셨을 때 제자들은 배 위에 있었습니다.
그러자 베드로는 겉옷을 입고 바로 바다에 뛰어들었습니다.
그러니까, 요한은 말을 했고, 베드론 뛰어들었죠.
다른 제자들은 배로 왔지만, 베드로는 헤엄쳐 왔죠.
여호와와 예수께서는 자신의 종들이 가진 다양한 개성을 좋아하십니다.
문화나 배경이 아주 다른 형제 자매들도 포함됩니다.
우린 그들과 함께 시간을 보내고, 그들을 집에 초대하고,
지난 5개월 동안 학생 여러분은 그렇게 잘해 오셨죠.
