여러분의 형제 자매들인 길르앗 제145기 학급.”
여러분에게 이제 마지막으로 몇 마디 말씀을 드리겠습니다.
오늘 졸업식에서 정말 훌륭한 교훈을 많이 들으셨죠?
우리 자신에게 영광을 돌리지 않아야 한다는 점을 살펴보았습니다.
먼저, 다른 사람들이 우리를 칭찬할 때
그러한 영광을 받고 싶은 마음이 들 수 있다고 말씀드렸습니다.
그리고 또 한편으로는, 다른 사람들로부터 비난을 받을 때,
뜻하지 않게 자기에게 영광을 돌릴 수도 있다고 했습니다.
우리 자신에게 영광을 돌릴 수 있는 또 다른 상황이 있습니다.
사도 바울의 본을 통해 그 점을 알아보시겠습니다.
성경을 가져오진 않으셨으니까 그냥 들으시면 됩니다.
사도 바울에게서 중요한 교훈을 배울 수 있는데,
여기서 바울은 고린도에 갔을 때에 대해 말하고 있죠.
뛰어난 말이나 지혜로 하느님의 신성한 비밀을 전하지 않았습니다.”
바울은 “뛰어난 말”을 사용해서 인상적으로 보이려고 하지 않았죠.
“예수 그리스도 ... 외에는 아무것도 생각하지 않기로 결심했습니다.”
하느님의 능력에 바탕을 두게 하려는 것이었습니다.”
자기 자신의 지혜나 능력에 주의를 이끌지 않는 면에서
바울은 정말 훌륭한 본이 되지 않습니까!
물론 이 때문에 고린도의 일부 형제들은
하지만 바울이 다양한 규모의 청중들 앞에서
좋은 소식을 훌륭히 변호한 기록을 보면,
그가 얼마나 유능한 연사였는지 우린 알 수 있죠.
바울은 능력이 있었지만, 그걸 드러내지 않기로 한 겁니다.
유대인들은 유명한 랍비의 말이나 학자들의 말을 즐겨 인용했죠.
여기서 우린 어떤 교훈을 배울 수 있을까요?
이렇게 말하고 싶은 마음이 들 수도 있죠.
하지만 사도 바울의 본을 따르려면 어떻게 해야 할까요?
형제 자매들에게 전달하고 싶은 좋은 내용이 있다면,
배우신 대로 그것을 하느님의 말씀에서 찾으십시오.
자신이 보통 사람은 모르는 특별한 지식이 있는 듯 행동해선 안 됩니다.
하느님의 말씀과 그분의 조직에서 제공하는 출판물에 근거를 둔다면,
자신이 아니라 여호와께 영광을 돌리게 될 것입니다.

en.text: Now we come to the principal talk
of the graduation.
It’s going to be delivered by a member
of the Governing Body, Brother Stephen Lett.
And the very interesting theme he has selected is
“We Can Learn Much From Peter!”
Dear Gilead students,
let me ask you, Who is your favorite Bible character?
Well, during Gilead,
you’ve examined many Bible characters;
you’ve learned positive and negative lessons from them.
And perhaps your favorite character changed,
remained the same,
or now you have several favorite Bible characters.
But no matter who your favorite character is,
during this talk, we’re going to learn
some of the many lessons to be learned
from the very interesting Bible character Peter.
Now first, let’s learn some things
we can learn about Jehovah and Jesus from Peter.
One thing we definitely learn
is that Jehovah and Jesus allow for
—in fact, apparently relish—
different personalities among their servants.
Now, to illustrate this,
let’s contrast the personality of Peter
with that of some of the other apostles.
Open up to John chapter 20,
and here’s a very interesting little scripture
highlighting two different personalities.
John 20:3:
“Then Peter and the other disciple [who would be John]
“set out for the tomb.
“The two of them began running together,
“but the other disciple ran faster than Peter and reached the tomb first.
“Stooping forward, he saw the linen cloths lying there,
“but he did not go in.
“Then Simon Peter also came, following him,
“and he went into the tomb.
And he saw the linen cloths lying there.”
So John looked inside; Peter rushed inside.
Now, here’s another example:
When the mob came to arrest Jesus in Gethsemane,
John 18:10
says that Peter drew his sword
and cut the right ear of the slave of the high priest off.
Now, let’s think about this.
Do you think that Peter was going for that right ear?
I mean, that would truly be impressive —wouldn’t it?—
to go for that right ear and precisely take it off.
But remember, Peter was not a swordsman;
he was a fisherman.
Obviously, he was going for the man’s head, wasn’t he?
But he missed and took the ear off.
But what an impetuous,
you could say, personality he had there!
Here’s one more example:
The resurrected Jesus
is on the shore of the Sea of Galilee;
and the disciples are in the boat;
and John says to Peter, “It is the Lord.”
Well, upon hearing this, Peter put his garment on
and plunged into the sea.
The other disciples came in the boat.
So notice,
John spoke; Peter plunged.
The other disciples came in the boat; Peter came swimming.
Very different personalities
—but, as we said, Jehovah and Jesus relish
these different personalities among their servants.
But now, what’s the lesson for us?
Well, in imitation of Jehovah and Jesus,
we’re obligated
to “have love for the whole association of [our] brothers.”
—1 Peter 2:17.
And “whole” means 100 percent.
And that certainly includes those with very different personalities from ourselves
—ones from different cultures and backgrounds.
We’re obligated to receive these ones
into our company, into our homes, into our hearts.
Now, you’ve done a lot of this in the last five months,
you Gilead students.
Well, you want to keep doing this
and, of course, all of us want to do this.
But now, here’s another thing we learn about Jehovah and Jesus from Peter.
Jehovah and Jesus are very forgiving.
Now, let’s think about Jesus’ words
at Matthew 10:33.
In plain words
—and our publications have said
probably plain Hebrew words, it would have been—
Jesus said:
“Whoever disowns me before men,
“I will also disown him
before my Father who is in the heavens.”
Not once, not twice, but three times Peter did it, didn’t he?
But yet Jehovah and Jesus completely forgave him
because he was truly repentant.
In fact, to somewhat counterbalance what Peter had done,
Jesus allowed Peter
to reaffirm his love for Jesus three times.
Well, what’s the lesson for us?
We must imitate Jehovah and Jesus
in being very forgiving.
In fact, Jehovah makes it clear that He will forgive us
in direct proportion to how we forgive others.
If we don’t forgive others, Jehovah won’t forgive us.
Where does that leave us?
Doomed.
But let’s say we do forgive,
but we’re pretty tight; we’re pretty stingy.
It’s kind of hard to squeeze a little forgiveness out of us.
Well, the indication is that Jehovah puts
that same ruler on us that we put on others.
On the other hand, if we’re very generous in forgiving,
now Jehovah can be very generous in forgiving us.
So if someone hurt you deeply
—has sinned against you—
don’t view this as a bad thing;
view this as a big opportunity.
You’ve got a big opportunity
to get a lot of forgiveness from Jehovah,
so cash in on that opportunity.
But now, in addition to what we can learn
about Jehovah and Jesus from Peter,
there are many lessons (positive and negative)
that we can learn from Peter himself.
So let’s do that.
Now, here’s a negative lesson:
At times, Peter spoke too quickly.
He had what has been called hoof-and-mouth disease.
What is that?
Open mouth; insert foot.
And some of us have the same problem, don’t we?
But here’s an example in Matthew chapter 16.
Jesus was explaining that he would have to go to Jerusalem,
suffer many things, and be killed.
Well, quickly Peter spoke up,
and he actually rebuked Jesus
—if you can imagine that.
“Be kind to yourself, Lord;
you will not have this happen to you at all.”
It was hoof-and-mouth disease —wasn’t it?—
followed by, as you could expect,
some correction, humiliation:
“Get behind me, Satan!”
But the indication is
that even though Peter had this problem, he overcame it.
He overcame this.
Several times he spoke too quickly.
But at 1 Peter 3:10,
he was able to write with freeness of speech,
we know, and he would have lived up to this:
“Whoever would love life and see good days
must guard his tongue.”
So he learned.
It took time.
He learned just like we’re all learning.
But now, what’s the lesson for us?
Well, it’s summed up nicely here in Proverbs chapter 18.
Please go there.
Proverbs 18:13:
“When anyone replies to a matter before he hears the facts,
it is foolish and humiliating.”
So none of us can perfectly bridle our tongues.
But we do well to try to restrain our lips,
at least until we’ve heard the facts.
Now, here’s another negative lesson:
At times, Peter was overconfident.
The most notorious example
—Matthew chapter 26:
“Although all the others are stumbled in connection with you,
“I will never be stumbled!
“Even if I should have to die with you,
I will by no means disown you.”
Well, that was overconfidence, wasn’t it?
And we know it was ‘pride before the crash.’
Well, what was his problem?
He was relying, at this point, on himself
rather than Jehovah.
But again, the indication is very strong
that he overcame that weakness.
And later, he was able to write at 1 Peter 5:6:
“Humble yourselves, therefore, under the mighty hand of God.”
So don’t rely on yourself.
Be humble under Jehovah’s hand.
Now, what’s the lesson for us?
Well, like we learned at our convention
—the last talk on Saturday—
that true courage is not self-reliance.
True courage must be based
on modest reliance on Jehovah.
When we lean on ourselves, or rely on ourselves,
it’s like leaning, you could say, on a rubber crutch.
Did you ever lean on a rubber crutch?
You’re going to fall, aren’t you?
But at Deuteronomy 32:4, Jehovah is “the Rock.”
If you lean on a rock, now you have something.
So we learn that from Peter:
Don’t rely on yourself; rely always on Jehovah.
Now, here’s one more negative lesson:
At times, Peter was ensnared
by fear of man
or, we could say, in his most infamous example,
fear of girl.
Interestingly, in Matthew 26:
‘Peter was sitting outside and a servant girl came up and said to him:
‘“You too were with Jesus the Galilean!”
‘But he denied it.
‘“I do not know what you’re talking about.”
‘He went out to the gatehouse; another girl noticed him.
‘“This man was with Jesus.”
Again he denied it, even with an oath.’
So his first two denials, you could say, were fear of girl.
But it is obviously clear
that he truly overcame that weakness, that problem,
and he became
an outspoken, bold Witness of Jehovah and Jesus.
Think, for example, in Acts chapter 5,
where Peter and the other apostles were in front of the Sanhedrin,
and the high priest said: ‘We ordered you
to quit teaching about this Jesus.’
Peter said: “We must obey God as ruler rather than men.”
‘And furthermore, this Jesus, God has raised him from the dead.
This one that you killed.’
Wow!
No fear of man there, was there?
He obviously overcame this problem.
Now, what’s the lesson for us?
We want to do our utmost to never be ensnared
by fear of men, women, or girls.
And, of course, always remembering
that it’s Jehovah’s rating of us that counts will help us.
Humans can’t add five seconds to their life, can they?
Jehovah can add or subtract eternity.
But now, we’re going to move
to some positive lessons we can learn from Peter.
And by far, his positive qualities
outweigh the negative qualities that he displayed at times.
Now here’s one: Peter waited on Jehovah.
And a wonderful example of this is in John chapter 6.
Jesus had stated that unless you eat my flesh
and drink my blood,
you will not have everlasting life.
And the Bible says that many of the disciples were shocked;
they were stumbled; they quit following Jesus.
And Jesus said to Peter, ‘Do you want to leave also, Peter?’
Do you remember those beautiful words coming out of Peter’s mouth?
“Lord, whom shall we go away to?
You have [the] sayings of everlasting life.”
Now, if you think about it, Peter didn’t understand Jesus’ words
at this point any more than the rest did,
but he was willing to wait on Jehovah for further enlightenment.
And in time, he learned that those words
have to be understood figuratively
—that we have to exercise faith
in Jesus’ flesh and blood.
Well, what’s the lesson for us?
Like Peter, we must show
a waiting attitude for the “God of [our] salvation.”
—Micah 7:7.
Now, here are just a few examples:
Are we willing to wait —and this was touched on earlier in our program—
willing to wait with the right attitude
for any theocratic appointment,
or privilege of service?
Here’s another example:
Are we willing to wait uncomplainingly on Jehovah to correct
—in his way, his time—
any injustice that we perceive in the congregation?
Or what about this?
Are we willing to wait patiently
—and this could apply to some of the single ones—
Are you willing to wait patiently on Jehovah
to provide you a suitable marriage mate,
even if you have to wait until the new world?
Yes, like Peter, let’s have a waiting attitude.
But now, here’s another positive lesson from Peter:
In order to make progress spiritually,
he was willing to move out of his comfort zones.
Now, let’s get some examples.
When invited, he promptly left a life of pursuing material things
for a life of storing up treasure in heaven.
And apparently, he was an older man when he did this.
But he did not put financial security ahead of following the Christ.
Or here’s another example:
He went from being an unlettered, ordinary fisherman,
probably talking primarily to hired men and fish merchants,
to being a bold Witness
of an unpopular message before thousands.
One more example:
He went from being very prejudiced
against Samaritans and Gentiles
to truly loving his Samaritan and Gentile brothers.
Well, what’s the lesson for us?
Are we willing to move out of our comfort zones
in order to make spiritual progress?
Now, all of you, you know where your comfort zones are.
But are you willing to move out in order to make spiritual progress?
What about, in some cases, especially if you’re given an assignment,
are you willing to go where the need is greater,
where Jehovah wants you to go?
Or what about reaching out for various forms of the ministry
that you may not right now feel so comfortable with
—maybe public witnessing or working business territory?
What about being more courageous in informal witnessing,
even though you may be a quiet and shy type of person?
Well, let’s get another positive lesson from Peter.
He allowed discipline
to mold rather than stumble him.
Of all the apostles, he was the most outspoken, wasn’t he?
But that was matched by his being the most frequently corrected,
reproved, rebuked.
But beautifully, he didn’t quit.
He never gave up, did he?
For example, we touched on this before, when Jesus said, “Get behind me, Satan!”
We don’t read that he pouted for weeks or months
because of that strong correction.
In fact, the Bible indicates that six days later,
Jesus took Peter, James, and John
up into a mountain to experience the transfiguration.
Or what about after Peter denied Jesus?
The Bible tells us that Jesus looked straight at Peter
—in effect, indirect discipline.
Peter recalled what Jesus said.
He went outside, and he wept bitterly.
But yet you don’t read that he kept beating himself
—he kept being depressed over his serious sin of denying Jesus.
He knew Jehovah and Jesus had forgiven him.
So he put it behind him —didn’t he?—
and he moved ahead.
Well, the lesson for us?
Jehovah disciplines those he loves.
But don’t ever let that discipline harden or embitter you.
Let it soften you into a better person.
If we’ve committed sins in the past,
even serious sins, like Peter,
let’s put them behind us and move ahead.
Well, one more positive lesson we’re going to talk about from Peter:
He gained and then he maintained
true humility.
Now, it’s true that he had to really work hard to gain it, didn’t he?
He had to work at it because he and the other apostles
had been taught from infancy
to strive to be the greatest —seek prominence.
It was really indoctrinated into their minds and hearts.
And up until the very last night of Jesus’ life on the earth,
Peter still had a problem —didn’t he?—
and the other apostles too.
He had a problem.
Jesus was washing the feet.
John chapter 13 —Peter had not volunteered to do this
even after Jesus started washing the feet.
Have you ever thought about that?
Sometimes you don’t think of something until someone else starts doing it,
and you think, ‘Oh, well, let me help you with that.’
Did Peter say: ‘Oh. Oh, Lord.
‘I see you’re washing these feet here.
Let me help you. Let me catch a couple of feet for you.’
No. Neither he nor any of the apostles volunteered.
They still had a problem at this point.
But with Jehovah’s help and effort on his part,
in time, he truly developed true humility.
He went from the one striving to be the greatest
to the humbled man who lifted up Cornelius
when Cornelius tried to bow down to him.
Remember that account in Acts chapter 10?
“Peter lifted him up, saying:
‘Rise; I too am just a man.’”
Or what about his genuine humility
when the apostle Paul corrected him publicly
in front of the whole congregation?
Now, if he would have still had pride—
‘Well, who are you, Paul, to give me correction?
‘I’ve been in the truth a lot longer than you have.
‘When you were persecuting the Christians,
‘I was an apostle.
‘And furthermore, you could have at least talked to me privately,
not in front of the whole congregation.’
But no, he knew he was clearly wrong.
He deserved the counsel no matter how it was given.
He made the correction,
and he harbored no grudge.
And the indication is very powerful
that he remained humble
despite his many privileges.
I mean, looking back over his life, he had had many, many privileges.
Isn’t that true?
He walked on water, at least for a few minutes;
he saw Jesus transfigured;
he performed many miracles, including personally resurrecting Dorcas;
he received and used “the keys of the Kingdom”;
he helped many people into the truth.
But yet he remained truly humble
and could write with freeness of speech
in his inspired letter,
at 1 Peter 5:5,
these beautiful words that we read very often.
He said: “But all of you clothe yourselves
“with humility toward one another,
“because God opposes the haughty ones,
but he gives undeserved kindness to the humble ones.”
And where is Peter right now?
An immortal spirit
serving as one of the “12 foundation stones”
of the Messianic Kingdom.
So, what is the lesson for us?
We must gain true humility like Peter did.
Otherwise, if you think about it, we’re absolutely unusable by Jehovah.
And then, we must remain humble
no matter what privileges we may or may not receive,
and then Jehovah will never oppose us.
Rather, we will continue to receive undeserved kindness from him.
Well, our discussion has highlighted
just a few of the many lessons to be learned from Peter.
I’m sure that if you Gilead students —soon-to-be graduates—
make Peter a study project,
you could learn many, many more valuable lessons
and, of course, that’s true of many other Bible characters.
But unquestionably, there is so much to learn
from the faithful, colorful, human apostle Peter.
So now we come to the point where we’re going to make
the presentation of the diplomas,
and Brother Ronald Curzan is with me here.
Let’s start, please, Brother Ron.
OK, so first of all we have Brother Abraha
will be returning to Ethiopia.
Brother and Sister Abras will be returning to the Middle East.
Sister Bloedorn will be returning to Timor-Leste.
Brother and Sister Bohnfeldt will be returning to Greenland.
Brother Dugas will be returning to Canada.
Brother Ekra will be returning to Côte d’Ivoire.
Brother and Sister Ephraim will be returning to Ethiopia.
Brother and Sister Farr will be serving in Malta.
Brother and Sister Gorems will be returning to Ethiopia.
Brother Kaljula will be serving in Asia.
Brother Kiszkowski will be serving in India.
Brother Koroinaqisia will be returning to Fiji.
Brother and Sister Kristiadi will be returning to Indonesia.
Brother and Sister Lett will be serving in Trinidad and Tobago.
Sister Minginfel will be returning to Yap.
Brother Myat will be returning to Myanmar.
Brother and Sister Naidoo will be returning to Angola.
Brother Nazombe will be returning to Malawi.
Brother and Sister Nteziryayo will be returning to Rwanda.
Brother Ovalle will be returning to Chile.
Brother and Sister Pacanins will be returning to Venezuela.
Brother and Sister Petrov will be returning to Croatia.
Brother and Sister Razafintsalama will be returning to Madagascar.
Brother and Sister Reungkittikul will be returning to Thailand.
Brother and Sister Robert will be serving in Turkey.
Brother and Sister Scholz will be returning to Germany.
Sister Shebrah will be returning to Ghana.
Brother Srzić will be returning to Croatia.
Brother Stevens will be returning to Asia.
Brother and Sister Valminos will be serving in France.
And Brother Yambao will be serving in India.
And lastly, Brother and Sister Yli-Huhtala will be returning to Finland.
Well, thank you very much, Brother Curzan.
You did very well with those names.
Although, you did have me worried.
I thought we were sending Brother Lett somewhere else, but,
anyway, I got over the shock.
Well, we’d like to introduce to you now
the graduates of the 145th class of Gilead.
So at this point, we’re going to have a class letter
read to us by Brother Krish Naidoo.
Wow, it’s amazing how your friends can take your breath away.
“September 8, 2018.
“To the Governing Body and the Bethel Family.
“Dear Brothers: Five months ago,
“we arrived with excitement from the four corners of the earth.
“We anxiously waited to be molded into the people
“that our Father, Jehovah, knew we could become.
“Despite denied visas, health issues, and insecurities,
“we were prepared to be taught by our Grand Instructor.
“Even after enrollment, further challenges presented themselves.
“As a class, we fought measles,
“endured quarantine, survived tornadoes,
“nursed broken bones,
“and comforted each other in the face of bereavement.
“However, these hurdles did not hamper us;
“they drew us closer together as siblings
“and to our Father, Jehovah.
“Isaiah gave us a glimpse into a heavenly school
“when he described the training Jesus was then receiving from Jehovah
“to prepare him for his earthly assignment.
“Isaiah 50:4 describes Jesus’ special education saying:
“‘He awakens me morning by morning;
“‘he awakens my ear to listen like the taught ones.’
“Jesus knew very well the purpose of his training:
“‘So that [he] may know how to answer the tired one with the right word.’
“Out of deep love and appreciation,
“he became the perfect reflection of his Father.
“We too know very well the purpose of the loving training
“we have received here at Gilead
“—to answer the tired one, not out of our own thoughts,
“but with the words taught to us through God’s Word.
“Many in the brotherhood are like a smoldering wick
“and at times feel crushed in spirit.
“Jesus loved and cared for such ones.
“We are determined to reflect the love Jesus developed
“through his schooling and bring true comfort
“and refreshment to our brothers.
“Words fail to express the depth of our gratitude
“for all that has been done for us.
“The Bethel family welcomed us into their home
“and showed hospitality to a degree that we never imagined.
“Our dear instructors became like fathers,
“teaching us with grace and dignity.
“They showed us how to honor one another through their example.
“They took the time to comfort us in the face of trials.
“The winsome words we received through the curriculum
“were as soothing oil on our souls,
“healing and strengthening us for the days ahead.
“For this, we wish to deeply thank our instructors
“as well as you dear brothers on the Governing Body.
“It is now clearer than ever to us that Jehovah is using you mightily
“in fulfilling your weighty assignment of overseeing the preaching work.
“Above all, we must thank
“our Father, Jehovah, from the bottom of our hearts
“for this precious and unforgettable gift.
“Jehovah truly has given us
“‘more than superabundantly beyond all the things we ask.’
“At the end of this life-defining experience,
“we know our molding is far from complete.
“Our learning will continue.
“Our gratitude compels us to do our utmost
“to support you in all that we do.
“Our hearts overflow with excitement to work harder than ever before.
“May Jehovah continue to richly bless the marvelous provision of Gilead
“to the benefit of the worldwide brotherhood
“and the praise and honor of our most wonderful God, Jehovah.
Your brothers and sisters, the 145th Class of Gilead.”
Well, this is my opportunity
to say just a few final words to you.
There have been so many wonderful points
mentioned on our program today.
Remember how we started with our discussion
about the need to always bring glory to Jehovah
and not to be concerned about our own glory.
You remember we started off by mentioning
that maybe it could be tempting
to accept glory from others if they praise us.
But then on the other hand, if we get criticized,
it may also be tempting for us to try and justify ourselves
and inadvertently bring glory to ourselves.
But there is another way too that we may have to be careful
about not bringing glory to ourselves.
And we can see this
from the example of the apostle Paul.
Now, I know you didn’t bring your Bibles up.
All you have to do is listen.
It’s one scripture, 1 Corinthians chapter 2
—1 Corinthians 2:1, 2.
It’s a vital lesson that we learn from the apostle Paul.
Here he’s speaking about when he went to Corinth.
And as we realize, Corinth was a seat of learning.
The Greeks loved learning.
And what did he say?
In verses 1 and 2:
“So when I came to you, brothers,
“I did not come with extravagant speech
or wisdom declaring the sacred secret of God to you.”
So Paul didn’t use
“extravagant speech” to impress people.
He says in verse 2: “For I decided.”
Yes, he made a decision.
What was it?
“I decided not to know anything
among you except Jesus Christ.”
And then if we look at verse 5,
he says: “So that your faith [may] be,
not in men’s wisdom, but in God’s power.”
What a wonderful example Paul set
with regard to not drawing attention
to his own wisdom and ability,
even though some in Corinth because of this
felt he wasn’t a very good speaker.
When we look at how Paul defended the good news
before audiences large and small,
he certainly was a very, very good orator.
He had that ability, but he decided
to tone it down
because he knew the brothers there had a weakness.
Now, what weaknesses were prevalent at that time?
Well, among the Jewish people
—and there were some Jewish people there in Corinth as well—
they loved to quote great rabbis
and scholars.
And, of course, the Greeks loved to quote the philosophers.
So, what lesson do you think we learn from this?
Well, now as you go to your assignments,
perhaps you might be tempted to say:
“Oh! The instructor
or a Governing Body member said this.”
But why should we follow
the example of the apostle Paul?
Well, you see, if we have something worthwhile
to convey to the brothers and sisters,
find it in God’s Word as you’ve been searching.
Look in the library—Watchtower Library.
Find something there, but don’t rely
upon the “rabbis,”
the “gurus,”
to show that you have some inside knowledge
that cannot be verified by other mere mortals.
Rather, rely upon God’s Word.
Yes, rely on his Word and the publications
that we have through his organization,
and in that way, you can be sure
you will bring glory to Jehovah
and not to yourselves.

cn.text: 到了发表主旨演讲的时候了
这个演讲由中央长老团成员
斯蒂芬·莱特弟兄发表
他的演讲题目很吸引人
《从彼得身上学到什么？》
亲爱的基列毕业生
请问你们最喜欢的圣经人物是谁呢？
在上学期间
你们已经分析过了许多圣经人物
也从这些人物受到鼓励或者学到教训
也许现在，你最喜欢的圣经人物已经改变了
或者还是同一个
又或者你现在最喜欢的人物不止一个
这个演讲会分析一个很有意思的圣经人物
看看我们能从他身上学到什么
这个人就是彼得
首先，通过彼得的事例
我们看看可以学到哪些
跟耶和华和耶稣有关的事
其中很显而易见的一点就是
耶和华和耶稣不仅允许
而且非常喜欢他们的仆人有不同的性格
为了说明这一点
我们看看彼得的性格跟其他使徒的不同之处
请翻到约翰福音20章
在这里我们会看到两种截然不同的性格
我们从约翰福音20:3开始看
“彼得和那个门徒[应该是约翰]就出来
到纪念墓去
两个人一齐跑起来
不过那个门徒比彼得跑得快，先到了纪念墓
他俯身探头
看见有绷带搁在那里，却没有进去
西门·彼得跟着也来到，进了纪念墓
他看到绷带搁在那里”
所以约翰只是站在外面往里看
彼得却直接冲了进去
我们看看另一个例子
当一群人来到客西马尼园抓耶稣时
约翰福音18:10说彼得拔出剑来
挥剑削掉了大祭司一个奴隶的右耳
想想看，你觉得彼得
真的是要砍掉那个人的右耳吗？
那就真的厉害了，是吧？
他能那么准地把那个人的右耳削掉，太厉害了
但彼得只是个渔夫，没学过怎么用剑
显然他是想砍那个人的头
但他砍偏了，结果把那个人的耳朵削掉了
看得出彼得的性格真的非常冲动
再看一个例子
复活了的耶稣站在加利利海边
当时门徒都在船上
约翰对彼得说：“是主！”
彼得一听见，就束上外衣跳进海里
其他门徒则坐着小船来到岸边
你看，约翰只是说话而已
彼得却跳下水了
其他门徒坐船回岸边，彼得却是游回来的
他们的性格真的很不一样
但耶和华和耶稣非常喜欢这些差异
我们从中学到什么呢？
为了效法耶和华和耶稣
我们必须听从彼得前书2:17的吩咐
“爱[我们的]整个弟兄团体”
“整个”指的是所有人
包括跟我们性格非常不一样的人
也包括不同文化和背景的人
我们必须接纳他们
愿意款待他们、发自内心地爱他们
在这方面，基列毕业生们
过去五个月你们已经做得很好
相信你们会继续这么做
当然，我们所有人都想这么做
从彼得我们还可以
学到耶和华和耶稣的什么特质呢？
他们非常乐于宽恕人
我们现在想一想
耶稣在马太福音10:33说的话
我们的出版物说，在希伯来语里
耶稣的话已经很清楚了
他说：“谁在人面前不认我
我在我的天父面前也要不认他。”
但彼得不是一次，不是两次
而是三次不认耶稣
可是彼得真心悔改之后
耶和华和耶稣就完全宽恕了他
不仅如此，为了让彼得有机会弥补自己的过失
耶稣还让彼得三次表达他对耶稣的爱
我们从中学到什么呢？
我们必须效法耶和华和耶稣，乐意宽恕人
耶和华清楚告诉我们
他有多乐意宽恕我们
取决于我们多乐意原谅别人
如果我们不宽恕别人
耶和华也不会宽恕我们
那我们就完全没有希望了
但如果我们原谅别人时有所保留
十分吝啬，十分小气
那么我们怎么对待别人
耶和华也会怎么对待我们
相反，如果我们大方宽恕别人
耶和华也会大方宽恕我们
所以，要是有人深深伤害了你，得罪了你
不要把这件事看成一件坏事
要看作一个宝贵的机会
因为如果你甘心宽恕了别人
耶和华也会甘心宽恕你
所以要好好利用这个机会
从彼得的经历
我们不仅可以学到很多关于耶和华和耶稣的事
也能从彼得本人得到很多鼓励，学到很多教训
我们来一起分析一下
其中一个教训是
有时候彼得说话太冲动，说话不经大脑
我们有些人也有这个问题
让我们来看一个例子
请翻到马太福音16章
当时耶稣正在对门徒解释他必须要去耶路撒冷
受很多苦，还会被人杀死
但彼得鲁莽地制止耶稣，甚至批评他说
“主啊，你该爱惜自己
你绝不会有这种下场的。”
这不就是说话不经大脑吗？
所以他当然受到了耶稣的纠正
也可能因此觉得很尴尬
耶稣说：“撒但，退到我后面去！”
不过，我们从圣经可以看出
彼得后来克服了这个问题，他做到了
虽然彼得曾多次说话冲动
但他后来能够良心无愧地
说出彼得前书3:10的话
可见他已经改变了
他说：“谁喜爱生命，想见美好的日子
就要抑制舌头”
所以，他肯定学到了教训
但这需要时间，就跟我们一样
大家都需要时间才能改变
我们学到什么呢？
箴言18章总结得非常好
请翻到箴言18:13
经文说：“未听先答，就是愚蠢羞辱。”
虽然我们都不能完美地控制自己的舌头
但我们可以努力约束自己
至少在听到事实之前，不要冲动地发言
现在我们看看另外一个教训
有时候彼得过度自信
其中一个最典型的例子
记载在马太福音26:33，35
经文说：“哪怕别人全都因你的事而失足
我也永不失足！
我即使必须与你同死，也决不会不认你。”
这就是过度自信，对吗？
我们知道“骄傲自大是失败的先声”
彼得的问题是什么呢？
那时候他依靠的是自己，而不是耶和华
但我们从圣经可以清楚看出
这个弱点他后来也克服了
因为彼得前书5:6说
“你们要在上帝大能的手下谦卑自抑。”
所以不要依靠自己
要在上帝大能的手下保持谦卑
我们学到什么呢？
就像我们在区域大会
星期六的最后一个演讲学到的
真正勇敢的人不会依靠自己
只有谦逊地依靠耶和华
才能表现出真正的勇气
当我们依靠自己的时候
我们就好像是拄着橡胶做的拐杖
这样的话，你一定会摔倒的
但申命记32:4说耶和华是“磐石”
如果你靠在磐石上
就有了实实在在的支撑
所以从彼得我们学到
不要依靠自己，要依靠耶和华
来看看另外一点
有时候，彼得会惧怕人
最不可思议的是他作为一个男人
竟然会害怕女孩子
根据马太福音 26:69
当时彼得坐在外面的院子里
有一个女仆上前对他说
“你也是跟那个加利利人耶稣一伙的！”
但彼得否认说：“我不知道你说什么。”
他走到门廊以后
又有一个女仆注意到他，说
“这个人是跟拿撒勒人耶稣一伙的。”
彼得再次否认，甚至还起誓
我们可以说彼得头两次不认耶稣
都是因为害怕女孩子
但我们可以肯定
彼得后来克服了这个弱点
成为一个勇敢发言的人
能为耶和华和耶稣放胆作见证
其中一个例子记载在使徒行传第5章
彼得和其他使徒站在公议会面前
大祭司说：“我们吩咐过你们
不可以再教人关于这个耶稣的事。”
但彼得说：“我们必须接受上帝的统治
服从上帝而不是服从人
而且，上帝已经使耶稣复活了
当初就是你们杀害了他。”
他在这里表现得十分勇敢，根本不畏惧人
显然他已经克服了这个问题
我们学到什么呢？
我们要竭尽全力，绝不落入惧怕人的陷阱
不论对方是男人、女人，还是女孩子
因为耶和华怎么看我们才真正重要
谨记这一点，我们就会有勇气
人不能让我们的寿命延长5秒钟
但耶和华可以让人得到或失去永远的生命
接下来，让我们看看彼得
在哪些方面给我们留下了好榜样
比起他有时表现出来的缺点
其实他的优点更多
其中一个就是，彼得耐心等候耶和华
一个很好的例子记载在约翰福音第6章
耶稣说除非你们吃我的肉喝我的血
否则你们就得不到永生
当时耶稣的许多门徒被这句话绊倒
不再跟随他了
那时耶稣问彼得：“你也想走吗？”
你还记得彼得说的话多么感人吗？
“主啊，我们还归附谁呢？
你有永生的话语啊。”
我们可以想一想
彼得当时跟其他人一样
也不明白耶稣的话
但他愿意等候耶和华提供进一步解释
后来，他明白了耶稣的话不能按字面理解
而是指我们必须
对他献出的生命和流出的血表现信心
我们学到什么呢？
跟彼得一样
我们要按照弥迦书7:7说的
“耐心等候上帝[我们]的救主。”
比如，之前的演讲也提到过
我们愿意等候上帝的组织
给我们的委派和服务的殊荣吗？
当我们觉得会众里有不公正的事
我们愿意耐心等候耶和华按照他的方法
他的时间来纠正事态吗？
再举个例子
对于单身的弟兄姐妹
你们愿意耐心等候耶和华
赐给你们一个合适的配偶吗？
即使是等到新世界，你们也愿意吗？
希望我们都跟彼得一样
愿意耐心等候耶和华
从彼得身上还能学到什么呢？
为了跟上帝有更亲密的关系
他愿意克服困难作出改变
我们可以看几个例子
当受到耶稣邀请时
彼得立刻改变了生活方式
不再追求物质
开始在天上积存财宝
看来，那时候彼得已经不年轻了
但他认为跟随耶稣
要比得到物质保障更重要
再看另一个例子
彼得以前是一个没有受过教育的渔夫
可能主要跟雇工和鱼贩子打交道
但谁能想到
他后来竟可以在数千人面前勇敢地作见证
而且传讲的是一个不受欢迎的信息
又比如，他以往非常轻视撒马利亚人和外邦人
但他后来学会
真心地爱这些撒马利亚和外族的弟兄姐妹
我们学到什么呢？
为了更加亲近上帝
我们也愿意克服困难作出调整吗？
我们大概都知道自己在什么状态下最舒服
但你愿意作出改变，做得更多吗？
特别当你接到一个新的委派时
你愿意到需求更大的地方吗？
愿意去耶和华想让你去的地方吗？
有些传道方式你可能觉得不容易
也许是公众场所见证
或者是在商业地区传道
你愿意克服困难参与这些形式的传道工作吗？
如果你是个安静害羞的人
你愿意鼓起勇气，参与非正式见证吗？
再来看看另一方面
彼得从管教得到训练
而不是变得一蹶不振
在所有使徒中，彼得最快人快语
正因为这样
他受到了最多的批评、责备和纠正
但他做得很好，他没有放弃
比如，我们之前提到过
耶稣对他说：“撒但，退到我后面去！”
虽然耶稣的话非常严厉
但彼得没有几个星期或几个月一直闷闷不乐
因为六天以后
耶稣就带着彼得、雅各和约翰上了一座山
在那里，耶稣让他们看到自己改变形貌
彼得三次不认耶稣之后发生了什么事呢？
那时耶稣看了彼得一眼
这就是一种间接的管教
这让彼得想起了耶稣曾说过的话
于是他就到外面痛哭起来
但彼得没有因为犯下严重的罪
而一直自责伤心难过
他知道耶和华和耶稣已经原谅了他
就放下了这件事，继续进步
我们学到什么呢？
耶和华会管教他所爱的人
所以不要拒绝管教
或者因此愤愤不平
要接受管教
让自己被塑造成更好的基督徒
如果你以前也犯过严重的罪
就要像彼得一样
放下以往的过犯继续前进
我们再来谈谈彼得的另外一个美好特质
就是他学会了真正的谦卑
而且一直保持谦卑
当然，他也是经过了很多年的努力
才变得谦卑的
因为他和其他使徒一样
从小就受到教导要出人头地
要高人一等
这种根深蒂固的思想深入他们的头脑和内心
就在耶稣快牺牲生命的那个晚上
彼得依然有这个问题
其他使徒也一样
约翰福音13章记载耶稣帮门徒洗脚
彼得看见了，也没有主动去帮忙
请想一想，有些时候
我们没有想到要做一件事
但如果有人开始做了
我们就会说：“让我来帮你吧。”
那时候，彼得有没有说
“主啊，我看见你在帮大家洗脚
让我来帮你吧，让我替你洗几只脚吧！”
他没有这么说，其他使徒也没有
这时候他们还是很骄傲
但彼得靠着耶和华的帮助
以及他自己的努力
最终培养了真正的谦卑
当哥尼流要向他下拜时
他阻止了哥尼流
我们看出以前一心要出人头地的彼得
现在变得非常谦卑
记得使徒行传第10章的记载吗？
10:26说：“彼得拉他起来，说
‘起来，我也不过是人。’”
另一次，当保罗在会众面前公开责备彼得
他有没有表现真正的谦卑呢？
如果那个时候他还很骄傲
他可能会说
“保罗，你算什么，你凭什么纠正我
我在真理中的时间比你长得多
你还在迫害基督徒的时候
我就已经是使徒了
再说你可以私下对我说这些话
而不是当着整群会众的面这么做啊！”
但彼得没有这么说
他清楚知道自己错了
他知道自己需要受到纠正
不管是怎么提出来的
后来他作出调整，而且没有心怀怨恨
我们从圣经可以清楚看出
彼得尽管享有许多殊荣
却一直保持谦卑
回顾彼得的一生
我们可以看出他真的拥有许多殊荣
他曾在水上行走，至少也走了几分钟
他看见耶稣改变形貌
他施行了许多奇迹
包括亲自复活多加
他得到并使用了“王国的钥匙”
他帮助许多人认识真理
尽管如此，他一直保持谦卑
而且在圣灵指引下
可以良心无愧地写下彼得前书5:5的话
我们也常常读到这句话
说得很有道理，经文说
“其实你们所有人都要以谦卑相待
好像束腰服事人一样
因为上帝与高傲的人为敌
却赐分外恩典给谦卑的人。”
彼得现在在哪里呢？
他现在在天上，是不死的灵体
也是弥赛亚王国的十二块基石之一
那么，我们学到什么呢？
就像彼得一样
我们也要学会真正的谦卑
否则我们在耶和华眼中就会变得一无是处
此外，不论我们有没有得到某些殊荣
我们都要继续保持谦卑
这样，耶和华就永远不会与我们为敌
而我们也能继续得到他赐给我们的分外恩典
从彼得身上我们可以学到很多
今天我们只讨论了其中几点而已
你们就要从基列学校毕业了
我希望你们继续研读彼得的经历
你们一定会从中挖掘出更多的宝石
当然，你们也能从其他圣经人物身上
学到很多东西
但毫无疑问，我们从使徒彼得
这个忠贞而且个性鲜明的人物身上
一定可以学到很多宝贵的经验
现在，颁发毕业证书的时刻到了
罗纳德·柯赞弟兄会和我一起
为大家颁发毕业证书
请，柯赞弟兄
好的

ko.text: 최근 졸업식에서 새로 생긴 프로 하나는
이제부터, 강사 중 한 분이신 트렌트 리폴드 형제가
첫 번째 손님은 중부 유럽 지부에서 오신 알렉스 숄츠 형제입니다.
숄츠 형제, 받으신 임명에 뭐랄까, 꽤 넓은 구역이 포함돼 있다죠?
네, 저희 팀은 외국어 순회구들을 지원해요.
중부 유럽 지부에 있는 저희 팀은 다른 22개 지부와 협력하여,
유럽 대륙 전체의 외국어 순회구들을 조직하고 돌봅니다.
그 순회구들의 언어는 중앙장로회의 봉사 위원회에서 지정해 주죠.
보통 순회구는 한 지부가 관할하는 구역 내에서
여러 개의 회중으로, 때로는 몇 개의 집단으로 구성되죠.
아시다시피, 현재 유럽에는 여러 나라와 여러 지부 구역이 있죠.
그 언어를 할 줄 모르는 현지 순회 감독자가
외국어 회중이나 집단을 방문해야 하는 일이 있었습니다.
단지 그 지부 구역 내에 그 언어를 할 수 있는 순회 감독자가 없거나,
자체 외국어 순회구를 만들 만큼 회중이 많지 않았기 때문이죠.
물론, 순회 감독자가 해당 외국어를 못하거나
그 언어의 구역에 대해 잘 모를 때는 어려움이 많습니다.
회중에 맞춰 구체적인 지침을 베풀기가 아주 힘들 겁니다.

순회 대회나 파이오니아 모임을 갖지 못할 때가 있었고요.
유럽에 있는 여러 지부의 구역에 걸쳐 있죠.
지도를 보면 좋은데, 혹시 유럽 지도가 있나요?

국경 없이 영적 낙원에 연합해 있는 게 보기 좋네요.
같은 언어를 쓰는 사람들끼리 한데 모으는 게
사실 사람들을 분리시키는 거라고 느낄 수 있는데,
물론 언어가 사람들을 분리시킬 수 있다는 건 분명하죠.
하지만 사실, 여호와의 조직은 언어를 사용해서
어떤 특정 문화나 특정 언어를 지지하기 위한 게 아닙니다.
이 프로젝트를 통해 우리는 사람이 만든 국경을 넘어서,
현지의 언어들을 사용해서 순결한 언어인 성경 진리를 가르칩니다.
이제 임지에 가시니까, 길르앗에서 배운 점 특히 한 가지,
임지에서 적용하실 점을 특히 한 가지만 꼽는다면 어떤 건가요?
학급에서 여러 번 나온 내용 하나는
더 높은 사람이 아니라 친구로서 함께하셨고
마음을 터놓고 대화할 수 있는 분이셨죠.
넓은 밭을 돌보는 순회 감독자들과 대화하는 임명을 수행할 때,
그 멋진 본을 조금이라도 따르고 싶습니다.
또 책임을 맡은 다른 지부의 형제들과 대화할 때도
동료 일꾼이자 친구로서 서로 마음을 터놓고 대화할 수 있길 바라죠.
전파 활동을 확장하는 거, 제 목표도 그겁니다.
여호와께서 숄츠 형제 부부를 풍부히 축복하시길 바랍니다.
다음 손님은 그린란드에서 오신 토마스 본펠트 형제입니다.
사실 이건 정장 차림의 전통 의상인데요,
그래서 대회에서 침례가 있는 날에도 많이들 입어요.
그런데 그린란드하면 이름처럼 푸른 땅이 아니라
그린란드는 거의 다 북극권에 위치해 있어요.
이 땅의 대부분을 차지하는 그린란드 빙상은
여기서 거대한 빙산들이 떨어져 나와 바다로 들어가죠.
그러면 이게 궁금한데, 그린란드 사람들은 어떤가요?
그린란드 사람들은 마음씨가 좋고 아주 친절해요.
그린란드가 덴마크에 속해 있어서 덴마크어를 쓰는 사람도 많지만,
그린란드어 하면 생각나는 게 있는데, 단어가 길다는 거죠.
네, 그린란드어에 대해선 다들 그 얘기부터 하시죠.
예를 들어, 「파수대」라는 명칭에 두 줄이 필요해요.
갑자기 궁금한데, 그린란드에도 맞춤법 대회가 있나요?
네, 조금 합니다. 아직 배우는 중이죠.
저희는 원래 덴마크에서 태어나 거기서 자랐어요.
그런데 재밌는 건, 실제로 제 부모님이 젊을 때
그린란드에서 특별 파이오니아를 하며 회중 세우는 걸 도우셨대요.
몇 년 전에 가족이 함께 그린란드에 갔는데, 이건 그때 사진이죠.
사실 그때 ‘언젠가 여기서 봉사해야지’ 라고 생각했는데...
네. 그 후 몇 년이 흘러 퍼니나와 교제를 시작했죠.
약혼을 하고서, 우리가 어디서 봉사할지 지부 사무실에 물었어요.
그린란드어를 배우라는 답변을 듣고 깜짝 놀랐죠.
그래서 코펜하겐으로 이사해 그린란드어 수업을 받았는데,
두 분도 부모님의 발자취를 따라 그린란드로 가신 셈이네요.
형제들이 지원해 준 덕분에 적응할 수 있었죠.
여러 해 봉사하시는 동안 임명이 좀 바뀐 것 같아요.
네, 지금은 누크의 그린란드어 현지 번역 사무실에서 일해요.
저희 전 시간 봉사자 4명과 10명이 넘는 출퇴근 봉사자가 있죠.
그럼 14명이 조금 넘는 건데, 규모가 좀 작네요.
번역 사무실을 위해 할 일이 정말 많겠어요.
하시는 일이 사람들에게 실제로 도움이 되나요?
그린란드어로는 발행되는 일반 출판물이 많지 않은데,
우리 출판물은 여러 해 동안 발행되고 있어서
사람들은 우리 서적을 보면 무척 좋아해요.
더 필요한 곳에 봉사하러 온 형제 자매들에게 큰 도움이 되죠.
봉사가 어떨지 궁금해서 그린란드에 대해 좀 찾아봤는데,
회중이 다섯 개 있고, 전도인은 170명쯤 되고,
그런데 멀리 떨어진 마을에 사는 사람이 많다면서요?
외딴 지역에 사는 사람들에게 어떻게 봉사하시나요?
그럼 동영상을 보면서 빙산에 가 보죠.
그린란드는 1년에 약 7개월 동안 이런 모습을 하고 있습니다.
이 회중은 그린란드에서 가장 북쪽에 있는 회중입니다.
형제 자매들은 그린란드어로 좋은 소식을 전하기 위해
오늘은 오카트수트라는 마을에서 봉사를 할 겁니다.
배를 타고 한참을 온 끝에 도착했지만,
전에도 이 마을들에서 좋은 결과가 있었습니다.
사라는 더 북쪽에 있는 마을에 살았는데,
연구를 하고 싶어도 정기적인 방문을 받기엔 너무 먼 곳이었습니다.
그래서 일룰리사트에 사는 자매와 전화로 연구를 했죠.
여러 달 동안 전화선을 연결해 집회를 보았습니다.
처음으로 참석한 집회에서 사라는 눈물을 흘렸죠.
마침내 영적인 가족과 함께하게 된 겁니다.
날씨와 먼 거리 때문에 쉽지는 않지만,
형제 자매들은 매년 이 마을들을 다시 방문합니다.
그들은 그린란드 북부에 펼쳐진 광활하고 외딴 지역에서
‘평화의 벗’을 더 찾기 위해 계속 노력하고 있습니다.
그린란드에 할 일이 진짜 많아 보이네요.
전화선으로 연결해 들을 수 있도록 마련해 왔어요.
헤드폰과 라디오로 동시 통역을 하기 때문에,
덴마크어를 쓰든 그린란드어를 쓰든 모두 참여해 유익을 얻을 수 있습니다.
여호와께서 수고하는 형제 부부를 축복하시길 바랍니다.
학생 몇 분이 바로 이 주제로 노래를 준비했다고 합니다.
같은 반 학생들을 위해 준비한 노래를 들어 보시죠.
이번 학급 학생들의 모국어 24개가 한데 어우러진 노래였습니다.
조니, 두 분은 앞의 분들과 임명이 좀 다른데, 어떤 임명인가요?
베델 봉사자가 아니고, 순회 활동을 하죠.
에티오피아 사람들은 대체로 친절하고 따뜻하고 후대를 잘 하죠.
이야기를 잘 나누고 대부분 종교심이 있어요.
영적인 문제에 관심이 많기 때문에 대화를 시작하기가 쉽습니다.
경험하신 일 중에서 특별히 기억나는 것 좀 말씀해 주실까요?
우리는 에티오피아 남부에 있는 한 순회구에 임명됐는데,
특별 파이오니아 두 분이 거기서 봉사하고 계셨죠.
그 중 한 형제가 재방문이 있다고 하면서
만나서 연구를 시작하고, 2년 만에 다시 방문한다는 건가요?
우리는 먼저 버스를 타고 어느 작은 도시로 갔어요.
가다가 길에서 하룻밤을 지낼 때도 있었어요.
그래서 버스 다음에 트럭을 탔고, 트럭 다음엔 걸으셨나요?
‘혹시 여기서 무슨 일이 생기면 이 정글에서 어떻게 나가지?’
사도들 같은 특권을 받았다는 생각이 들었습니다.
형제가 떠나고 3일이 지났을 때 어떤 생각이 드셨나요?
살아 있는지, 다치거나 길을 잃지는 않았는지 알 수 없었죠.
순회 방문 중이라 사람들 앞에선 강한 모습을 보여야 했죠.
말할 순 없었지만, 사실 기도하면서 많이 울었어요.
원래는 하루 이틀만 머물려고 했는데 그럴 수 없었어요.
하나는 사람들이 관심이 정말 많아서 머물러 있어야 했죠.
또 하나는 우리 다리가 나무토막 같았거든요.
그 관심자가 우리와 얘기하며 정말 즐거워했거든요.
거기 전화가 있어서 제가 아내에게 전화할 수 있었죠.
말했듯이, 그 전엔 너무 걱정돼서 울었죠.
그런데 남편이 전화해 제 이름을 부르니까,
최근에 한 순회 감독자와 특별 파이오니아가 그들을 방문했죠.
세 개의 월라이타어 회중이 잘 발전하고 있죠.
그래도 여전히 형제들은 관심 있는 사람을 찾아
긴 여행길이지만 형제들은 버스에 자리를 잡고
사울라라는 곳에 들렀다 가는데, 형제 자매들이 마중을 나왔군요.
누가 이렇게 태워 주지 않는다면 말이죠.
오늘 이 형제들은 계곡을 지나고 산을 넘고 강도 건넙니다.
폭이 좁은 곳도 있고, 꽤 넓은 곳도 있죠.
여기선 먼저 형제들이 강을 걸어서 건너면,
저도 처음 갈 때 이걸 탔으면 좋았을 텐데요.
가던 길을 또 한 번 멈추고
라이하에서 그곳 형제들과 맛있는 식사를 합니다.
갓 볶은 커피 향이 지금도 코 끝을 맴도네요.
저는 이 형제 자매들이 정말 그립습니다!
이 형제는 제가 여러 해 전에 처음 이곳에 갔을 때 만났었죠.
지금은 살라이시에 열 명의 전도인이 있습니다.
이 모든 게 단 한 명의 관심자에서 시작됐다는 게 놀랍죠.
형제들은 하느님의 조직에 속하게 되어 어떤 마음일까요?
여호와는 우릴 사랑하십니다. 사랑으로 우릴 이끄셨어요.
국제적인 형제 관계 안으로 초대해 주셨죠.
양들을 더 많이 찾도록 이 소중한 벗들을 주셨으니까요.
정글을 헤치며 걷던 그 모든 여정을 통해
힘든 여정 내내 여호와의 손길을 느꼈죠.
여호와의 손 안에 있다는 걸 느꼈습니다.
남편이 어떻게 됐는지 알 수 없는 상황에서
‘여호와께서 남편을 보호해 주실 거야.’ 라고 계속 말했죠.
여호와의 뜻을 행하는 남편을 보호해 주실 거다.
이렇게 인사이드 스토리에서 두 분의 경험을 들려 주셔서 감사합니다.
그 이야기들도 언젠가 들을 수 있으면 좋겠습니다.
오늘 몇 분의 이야기만 들어 봤는데요,
얼마나 애쓰는지 보면서 격려를 많이 받았죠.
얼마나 많은 일을 하시는지 들으며 감동도 받았습니다.
“인사이드 스토리” 제작에 참여하신 모든 분께 감사드립니다.

en.text: In the past few graduation programs,
we’ve had a new feature entitled
The Inside Story,
and we’re going to have another “inside story.”
One of the instructors, Brother Trent Lippold,
is now going to present that to us.
From far in the North Atlantic to the islands of the South Pacific,
you will meet some cool and colorful brothers
and sisters in this 145th class.
They serve on 5 continents, represent 31 countries,
and speak more than 45 individual, or different, languages.
So let’s meet our first guest,
and he’s from the Central European branch, Brother Alex Scholz.
Welcome, Alex. Good.
Alex, I understand in your assignment,
you have quite, how shall we say, quite an expansive assignment.
Well, I work with a team that helps foreign-language circuits.
OK, very nice.
So foreign-language circuits in Germany?
Not just Germany.
Farther.
Foreign-language circuits in the Central European branch.
Even a little farther, Trent.
OK. Alex, you’re going to have to help me out with this.
What exactly does your assignment involve?
Well, our team in the Central Europe branch
works with 22 other branch offices
to form and coordinate
foreign-language circuits that span the continent
in languages that are assigned to the project
by the Service Committee of the Governing Body.
Wow, that sounds huge.
There must be a good reason for it.
Yeah. Sure, there is.
I mean, as we know, normally a circuit
consists of a group of congregations
and perhaps a few groups within one branch territory.
Now, in Europe, we know we have quite a number of countries
and also a number of branch territories.
So, what happened in the past is that in some languages,
there were foreign-language congregations or groups that had to be visited
by a local circuit overseer who didn’t speak the language.
And that was simply because perhaps in this branch territory,
they didn’t have a circuit overseer who speaks the language
or they didn’t have enough congregations
to form their own foreign-language circuit
in that branch territory.
And that, of course, poses a challenge if the CO doesn’t speak that language
or he’s not so familiar with the territory or that language field.
Sure, I can see that.
Then it would be difficult for him to really give specific direction to the congregation.
That’s the thing.
And some publishers in these groups perhaps felt isolated.
Besides, they didn’t necessarily have circuit assemblies
or pioneer meetings in their language or in their vicinity.
Right. But I know the Governing Body made a change about that.
Yeah, and that was excellent.
I mean, it’s a beautiful project.
Since 2016, we now have what we call
foreign-language circuits that span branch territories in Europe.
OK. Well, how does this work now?
Well, imagine Europe, or perhaps it’s best we take a look at a map.
We have a map of Europe?
OK. We have a map.
Super. Very good.
So this is how we look at Europe in this project
—Europe without borders.
OK.
All we want to see is,
Where are the foreign-language congregations and groups?
And maybe it’s best we can see this in one example with the Chinese field.
Wow.
So we look at all the congregations and groups
(we see them depicted here),
and simply what we do is we group them together
by a number of parameters into circuits.
But this is regardless of any national borders.
And what results is all these groups and congregations are in actual circuits.
They have their circuit events,
they have their pioneer meetings,
they have their circuit overseer who speaks their language,
and they meet together for circuit assemblies.
More people come together from various countries.
It’s a wonderful atmosphere.
Very nice. That’s incredible.
So this is the Chinese circuit.
That’s Chinese.
We have Russian here with . . .
OK.
. . . the 20 circuits that we have right now that span Europe.
And here’s the Romany field with growing circuits in Europe.
Very interesting.
I mean, how many are we talking about, Alex?
Right now we have in the project 115 circuits
with more than 4,000 congregations and groups involved.
Wow.
And to date, 18 languages have been assigned to the project.
That is remarkable.
So, what would you say?
How have the brothers and sisters
in these foreign-language congregations and circuits been affected?
Well, we have very positive reflections from the field.
The publishers often appreciate the fact that they now receive
theocratic care by a circuit overseer
who speaks their language, and that’s a beautiful aspect.
Besides that, because of this now theocratically borderless Europe,
if we want to call it this way,
we as branch offices have more opportunity to work together
—to organize conventions in these languages,
circuit assemblies, schools, pioneer meetings.
And all of this furthers the preaching work, and that’s amazing to see.
Well, that’s the benefit, isn’t it? That’s tremendous.
You know, Alex, for us in Gilead,
most of the instructors of Gilead, we’ve been in the circuit work.
So circuit work is close to our hearts.
As I’m looking at these huge circuits,
I’m asking myself,
‘How do these circuit overseers care for such huge territories?’
What is it like?
You know, that’s a very good question
because these brothers and sisters work so hard in these fields.
Actually, we have a little video
that follows one traveling couple, Brother and Sister Dietrich.
They are traveling in one of the Albanian circuits
that span branch territories in Europe.
And if you’d like, we could take a look at the video and see how they’re doing.
Excellent. Let’s look at the video now then.
Today, many Albanian Witnesses are settled
in different countries,
but they are not isolated.
Edlira and I are serving
one of three Albanian circuits in Europe
that span branch territories.
Serving a multinational circuit
takes extra effort and planning.
But seeing Jehovah’s care for his people,
no matter the situation, is worth it.
We’re a small congregation in a foreign country.
Our circuit is now supported by Albanian-speaking brothers
from several European countries,
and we feel the unity in our brotherhood even more.
At this regional convention,
brothers and sisters are attending from Germany,
Austria, Belgium, Great Britain,
and Switzerland.
We have met many friends who speak our language.
We are learning a lot about them
and are encouraged by their examples of faith.
In the circuit, those in northern Italy
are together with others in Germany, Austria, and Slovenia.
They are united across national borders
with others who speak Albanian.
That’s beautiful, Alex
—united in the spiritual paradise— no borders.
Absolutely. That’s true.
I think about this, though, Alex.
You know, some say that language actually divides.
I mean, that goes back to the Tower of Babel.
And some might feel that, well, by grouping people into language groups,
you’re actually dividing people.
How would you answer that?
Well, you know language definitely has the potential to divide
—no question.
But, honestly, by the way the organization is using language,
I see the opposite effect taking place.
You know, this project is not about promoting
particular cultures or particular languages.
What this project allows us to do
is to reach across man-made borders
to unite our brothers and sisters by using their local language
to teach the true and pure language.
And that is unity, as we’ve seen in the video.
Well, we look forward to hearing about more of those details.
Thank you.
Just maybe in conclusion, Alex, one final thought.
Thinking about your assignment, is there one particular thought from Gilead
(I know there’s probably many), but is there one particular thought
that you would like to especially apply in your assignment?
Yeah, you’re right. There are many.
Maybe just one that was repeatedly mentioned in class
is how Jesus worked with others
—never as a superior, but as a friend, as a confidant—
open, trusted communication.
And that’s a beautiful example.
And I just hope that I can pick up a little bit of this wonderful example
when I have the privilege to talk to the circuit overseers
out there in this huge field.
Or when we talk to the other responsible brothers
in the other branch offices, that it is this open, trusted communication
as friends and as fellow workers.
We all have the same goal —furthering the preaching work.
That’s a goal I have.
Very nice. It’s a valuable point for all of us.
Well, Alex, may Jehovah richly bless you and your wife, Tabitha, in your assignment.
Thank you very much.
Thank you.
Let’s welcome our next guest,
and it’s Brother Thomas Bohnfeldt from Greenland.
Hi, Thomas.
Hi.
Hey, welcome Thomas.
Thank you.
You look very comfortable.
Oh, thank you. I am.
So, what do you call that?
This is an anorak.
You know, it’s all about staying warm in Greenland.
So, actually, this is traditional formal wear,
and it is used for special occasions.
So many brothers wear it at the conventions on the day of baptism.
This is very special.
Well, I like Greenland already; I can tell you that.
When I think of Greenland, though, I’m not thinking green land;
I’m thinking ice, snow.
Yeah, you are right. It is really a land of ice and snow.
Most of Greenland lies within the Arctic Circle.
The biggest part of the land is the Greenland Ice Sheet,
and it’s up to 3,000 meters thick in the center.
And from there, huge icebergs break off out to the sea.
Icebergs like this one.
Yes.
Yeah, that definitely sounds cool to me.
So, what I wonder though is,
What are the people like in Greenland?
Ah, that’s where the warmth is.
People in Greenland are very kind and warmhearted.
Greenland is part of the Kingdom of Denmark.
So many speak Danish,
but the majority —the native Inuit—
speak Greenlandic.
Greenlandic—when I think of Greenlandic, the only thing that comes to mind is long words.
Yes, that’s the first thing many people notice about Greenlandic.
For example, we have the title of The Watchtower on two lines.
Can you say it?
Ah, I don’t think I can, actually.
But you said it so well.
As I look at that, though, I wonder,
Do you have spelling contests in Greenland?
No, we don’t have time for that.
You and Peninna, do you speak Greenlandic?
Yes, we do now. But we are still learning.
Of course. How did you learn Greenlandic?
So we are originally from Denmark and brought up in Denmark.
But, interestingly,
my parents actually were special pioneers
when they were young in Greenland
and helped form a congregation.
Well, that’s very interesting. That’s a nice spiritual heritage to have.
And some years ago, we visited Greenland as a family,
and we see pictures here.
You still look relaxed, Thomas.
Actually, back then I remembered, ‘Perhaps I could serve in Greenland sometime.’
But that thought just—
Really?
I forgot that thought.
Really?
Yeah, but then years passed.
I began to court Peninna, and when we were engaged to marry,
we asked the branch where we could serve.
And to our surprise, they asked us to start learning Greenlandic.
So we moved to Copenhagen and took some language courses.
And after three years, we were sent to Greenland as special pioneers
and helped support the translation office.
That’s amazing.
So it’s almost like you were following in your parents’ footsteps, then, to Greenland.
Yes.
So was it an easy adjustment?
Denmark? Greenland?
No. Denmark and Greenland are very different.
But with the help from Jehovah
and also with support from brothers, we adapted.
Yeah, it looks like you’ve fully adapted, actually.
I understand that your assignment has changed a little bit over the years.
So now we are at the RTO in Nuuk, in the Greenlandic RTO.
There are four of us full-time, and we have more than ten part-time commuters.
OK, so that’s more than 14 in the RTO but still a small group.
That’s a lot of work for a translation office.
Are there benefits?
Have you seen the benefits from the work you’re doing?
Yes, definitely.
So in Greenlandic, there’s not much published secularly
but our publications have been published for many years.
And they are very well-known.
So people really love when they see our literature.
And besides that, our videos in Greenlandic are a great support
for many of the need-greaters coming to support the ministry in Greenlandic.
Right.
Now, I wondered what the ministry was like.
Now, we did a little homework on Greenland.
I know there are five congregations in Greenland,
about 170 publishers,
and around 56,000 people that live in Greenland.
But we also understand that a lot of them live in very remote villages.
So how do you reach those people in these isolated areas?
Yes, well, that’s all about timing.
Timing?
Yeah.
But to help you understand it, we have a video
from a congregation far north of Nuuk
in the village of Ilulissat, meaning “icebergs.”
Well, let’s have a look, and let’s visit the icebergs.
For about seven months of the year,
Greenland looks like this.
But when the ice melts,
signs of life begin to emerge
and the brothers and sisters get moving!
The Danish congregation in the town of Ilulissat also preaches
to Greenlandic-speaking people.
It’s the northernmost congregation
in Greenland.
They travel to many remote villages
to spread the good news
in Greenlandic.
Their territory spans hundreds of miles.
Today, they are preaching in the village of Oqaatsut.
It’s good to be out of the boat after their long journey,
but their work is just beginning.
They’ve had good results in these villages before.
This is Sara from a village farther north.
She wanted to study,
but she lived too far away for a regular visit.
So a sister in Ilulissat
studied with her over the phone.
She would tie in to the meetings during the long, cold months of winter,
but she felt that wasn’t enough.
So she moved some 300 miles to Ilulissat.
She remembers the tears at her first meeting.
Sara was now with her spiritual family.
In time, she was baptized.
The weather and distances make it difficult for the brothers and sisters,
but they return to these villages year after year,
searching for more ‘friends of peace’
in the vast and isolated regions
of northern Greenland.
That was fantastic, Thomas.
But it looks like there is a lot of work to do in Greenland.
Yes, there is.
And arrangements have been made so that Sarah and other native speakers
can tie in to the Greenlandic meetings in Nuuk for some parts of the meeting.
And besides that, at our meetings in Nuuk,
we also use simultaneous translation
using headphones and radio
so that whether you speak Danish or Greenlandic,
you can participate and benefit.
Wow!
That is absolutely amazing.
How do you say “wow” in Greenlandic?
I’ll leave that for you.
Thank you very much for being with us, Thomas.
And, again, for you and your wife Peninna as well,
we wish you Jehovah’s blessing in your assignment.
Well, so far we’ve been talking about unity and language.
And some of the students have prepared a song that addresses just those themes.
So let’s enjoy the song that they’ve prepared to sing to their classmates.
That was a beautiful song sung in the 24 languages
of the heart of their classmates but with one voice.
Let’s welcome our next guests,
Meraf and Yohannes Gorems from Ethiopia.
Welcome, Johnny.
Welcome, Meraf.
Thank you.
Please.
I understand they call you Johnny, actually.
Johnny, you and Meraf have a different assignment.
Could you explain what your assignment is?
We are not Bethelites.
We serve in the circuit work.
But you like Bethelites?
I like.
Good.
So, what is the circuit work like in Ethiopia?
What are the people in Ethiopia like?
Ethiopian people are generally kind, warm,
hospitable, open to talking,
and most are religious people.
It is easy to start conversations because they love spiritual matters.
OK.
Is there maybe one experience, one special experience,
that stands out to you?
We were assigned a circuit in the southern part of Ethiopia.
Two special pioneers served there.
One of them asked me if I would go with him.
He had a return visit.
Two years ago, he met this man
and now he wanted to go back again.
Wait, so this is after two years.
He had a nice call; he studied with people there;
and now two years later, he wants to go back.
So why did he wait so long?
Because it was too remote.
How remote was it?
It takes three days from a nearby city to get there.
We started by bus, and we arrived in one small city.
Then we took a truck, seven to nine hours.
Sometimes we spent all night on that road.
So sleeping on the road —OK, there is a picture.
Yeah, but I slept well.
So I presume you took a truck because there were no more buses.
So the buses end, and now you take the truck.
After the truck, you walked?
I walked the rest of the way.
Short walk?
Depends what you call short.
If 11 hours is short to you, then yes.
Eleven hours?
So, what was it like walking 11 hours to this village?
When we walked in the jungle, I got scared.
I think I was thinking,
‘If something happens here, how could I get out of this jungle?’
How could you get out?
Yeah, so I prayed.
Immediately, my thoughts changed from fear to boldness.
I was thinking that this is a privilege, like the apostles.
Interesting.
Now, Meraf, you were not with Yohannes.
So, what were you thinking while he was gone?
I mean, this is three days already he was gone.
That was the hardest part of my life
because there was no network to contact him.
I didn’t know whether he was alive, wounded, or lost.
I had no idea.
And we were in a circuit visit,
so I should look strong in front of others.
So I couldn’t say anything, but I was praying and crying a lot.
So you reached the village after your 11-hour walk.
You found the interested person?
Uh-huh. He had other Bible students.
The interested person had Bible students?
The interested person.
How long did you stay?
My plan was one or two days to spend there, but I couldn’t.
Because of the interest, you couldn’t leave?
Yeah, because of two things.
The first thing: They were very interested, so I had to stay there.
The other thing was our legs were like wood.
Like wood?
Yeah.
From 11 hours of walking?
Eleven hours, yeah.
But when we arrived there, we became strong.
Our tiredness was lifted
because the interested person really enjoyed that conversation.
When did you leave the village?
Sunday —Sunday morning.
Your legs were feeling better?
Yeah, we spent nine hours.
We got to one area
where we had a telephone,
so I could call her.
So you walked nine hours to get to a telephone.
What was that phone call like, Meraf?
As I told you, I wanted to cry because I was so worried.
And he called and said my name.
So I was so happy, and I started to cry.
What’s happened since then, after that visit?
Do you know what’s happened to them?
Most of them now have gotten baptized.
Recently, one circuit overseer
and one special pioneer visited them.
I have a video.
Maybe you would like to see them?
No maybe. Let’s have a look at the video, please.
Our journey begins here in Sodo.
Sodo has a thriving Amharic congregation
and three congregations in Wolaita.
And yet, the brothers travel to support the search,
even in villages far away.
Today, their destination is the small village of Salaysh.
The journey is long, but the brothers settle in
and enjoy the beautiful countryside.
The first stop is Sawla, where our brothers
and sisters are waiting for them.
This is the end of the line for the bus ride.
How nice it will be to have a good night’s rest.
It is time to start walking,
unless you can catch a ride on one of these.
Today, they cross valleys,
mountains,
and rivers —some small
and some not so small.
Here, the brothers have to wade through the river first;
then the drivers bring the motorbikes across.
I wish I had this option on my first trip.
One more stop;
time for a delicious meal in Layha with the local brothers.
I can still smell
the fresh roasted coffee.
Finally, they make it to Salaysh.
How I miss these brothers and sisters!
I met this brother years ago on my first visit.
There are ten publishers now in Salaysh.
They conduct 24 Bible studies,
and many are attending the meetings.
To think this all started with just one interested person.
How do our brothers feel to be part of God’s organization?
Jehovah loved us.
Because of his love, he drew us to him.
He made us a part of the international brotherhood.
We are very happy, and we thank Jehovah.
We thank him from our heart.
And I am thankful to Jehovah
that he included these dear friends
to join him in the search for more sheep.
You must be very happy to see those faces.
Yeah.
Just thinking about that trip,
when you were out there walking in the jungle,
going all of that way,
what did you learn from that?
I saw Jehovah’s hand
during that difficult trip.
Jehovah carried me.
We didn’t fear, because we saw Jehovah’s hand.
We felt we were in Jehovah’s hand.
Beautiful.
What about you, Meraf?
Waiting alone, not knowing what was happening to Yohannes,
what did you learn from that experience?
At that time, I was thinking,
‘I know that Jehovah can protect him.’
So I was telling myself this, and that kept me strong.
Doing Jehovah’s will, Jehovah can protect him.
Very nice.
Yohannes and Meraf, thank you so much
for your experiences and being with us on The Inside Story.
Thank you.
Thank you.
Every one of the students has a story.
You have a story, and maybe one day,
we’ll all get to hear them.
But for today, we’ve just scratched the surface.
It’s been so encouraging to see the lengths
that our brothers and sisters will go to find ‘friends of peace.’
And it has been very touching to hear the lengths
that Jehovah will go to find his “little sheep” to bring them back.
We look forward to seeing you again on another episode of The Inside Story.
And that’s all for this time from the 145th class.
Well, we’d like to thank all those involved with producing The Inside Story.
It truly was appreciated by each one of us.

나이가 좀 있는 어떤 훌륭한 형제에게 기도를 부탁했는데,

전사들로 이루어진 백만 대군이 쳐들어오고 있는데,
아사는 여호와께 가까이 갔고, 여호와께서도 가까이 오셨습니다.
에티오피아 사람들이 아사와 유다 앞에서 패하게 하셨고,
이 모든 게 아사가 여호와께 가까이 갔기 때문이죠.
우리 역시 여호와께 가까이 가길 원합니다.
여호와께 가까이 가는 또 다른 방법은 묵상하는 것입니다.
기도로 어떤 말을 할지 생각할 수 있죠.
양의 위장은 네 부분으로 되어 있다고 합니다.
따라서 소화하는 데 오래, 이틀 이상이 걸리기도 합니다.
가끔 다른 사람에게도 물어볼 수 있죠.
기도와 묵상, 바로 이 두 가지가
우리가 여호와께 가까이 가기 위해 노력해야 할 중요한 부면입니다.

en.text: ‎Have you ever heard
‎a brother pray to Jehovah
‎and it just sort of touches your heart
‎—the words he uses
‎and his mannerisms and so forth?
‎And you may say to yourself,
‎‘Well, I wish I could talk to Jehovah like that.’
‎Well, maybe the way you talk to Jehovah
‎is not like that.
‎You may not have ‎all those words to use, and so forth,
‎due to a lack of education
‎when it comes ‎to the English language, and so forth,
‎but what you do have is in your heart.
‎And when you pour your heart out to Jehovah,
‎he hears you and he blesses you
‎just like he would bless ‎the one who has all the words
‎and the good mannerisms, and so forth.
‎So don’t worry about it.
‎Just pray to Jehovah from your heart.
‎It’s not the words that he’s that interested in;
‎it’s what comes out of the heart.
‎So, no doubt, ‎you are just as close to Jehovah
‎as that one that you admire.
‎And there’s certainly nothing wrong
‎with admiring a brother ‎who has that ability, or a sister.
‎But don’t worry about it;
‎that is not the main thing that Jehovah looks at.
‎Your approach has to come from the heart,
‎and if it does, it pleases Jehovah.
‎Notice something ‎here in the Bible at 1 Samuel 16:7.
‎It says: ‎“But Jehovah said to Samuel:
‎“‘Do not pay attention ‎to his appearance and how tall he is,
‎“‘for I have rejected him.
‎“‘For the way man sees ‎  is not the way God sees,
‎“‘because mere man sees ‎   what appears to the eyes,
‎but Jehovah sees into the heart.’”
‎That’s a beautiful scripture,
‎and it is one that humbles us before Jehovah.
‎We’re glad that he looks at our heart,
‎and we certainly want him to do that.
‎I’d like to tell you about something.
‎It has to do with a brother, an older brother,
‎years ago in one of the circuits I had.
‎And we were at the dinner table.
‎His wife wasn’t in the truth, ‎but she prepared a fine meal for us.
‎He was a fine brother ‎—elder in the congregation.
‎And it got around to:
‎“What did you do before you got the truth?
‎What kind of work did you do?” ‎and so forth.
‎And he said,
‎“I was a professional brother who prayed.”
‎He said, “The preachers in our town hired me
‎to go to their churches on Sunday and pray.”
‎He said: ‎“I had the ability to use right words.
‎“And my deep voice and mannerism
‎“just caused them ‎to reach deep into their billfolds
‎“and pocketbooks and give money.
‎“So afterward, the preachers ‎would divvy it up and pay me off.
‎“So I made quite a bit of money that way
‎—‘professional prayer.’”
‎Well, of course, he got the truth,
‎and he learned that that business was no good,
‎but he still could pray and reach the heart.
‎And that’s what prayer is all about, isn’t it?
‎Our text today ‎deals with drawing close to Jehovah.
‎And one of the main ways that we ‎draw close to Jehovah is through prayer.
‎Whether we’re on our knees
‎or standing or lying down, it matters not.
‎Jehovah still hears.
‎Silent prayers he hears.
‎We can pray as we’re driving the automobile
‎or doing anything else,
‎and he hears our prayers
‎if they come out of the heart.
‎And, of course, ‎we have to pray in the right way.
‎Years ago, we had a program ‎out in the traveling work
‎called “New Things Learned.”
‎Now, we changed that later on ‎to “Continue in the Things That You Learned.”
‎But at this particular time, ‎it was “New Things Learned.”
‎And I was a circuit overseer,
‎so I had the program on a Saturday evening
‎—“New Things Learned.”
‎One of my questions was,
‎“When you pray to Jehovah,
‎“do you go through Jesus at the beginning
‎“or during your prayer or at the end,
‎or does it matter?”
‎Well, we got all kinds of answers.
‎I tell you the truth.
‎You wouldn’t believe it if you were there
‎—all kinds of answers!
‎So anyway, we finally gave them ‎the correct answer, and so forth.
‎At the end of the meeting,
‎I called on an older brother ‎(very fine brother in the truth) to pray.
‎And he prayed to Jesus.
‎I said, ‎“Brother, why did you pray to Jesus?”
‎He said: ‎“I didn’t know who to pray to.
‎I was so confused.”
‎So Gloria, my wife, said,
‎“Please, don’t use that ‎on the ‘New Things Learned’ anymore.”
‎But that was truly a new thing learned.
‎‘We just hope you unlearned it, congregation.’
‎Anyway, we feel that ‎that prayer was heard by Jehovah.
‎He takes into consideration who we are,
‎what we have to give, ‎and how we can do it, and so forth.
‎But we wouldn’t practice a thing like that.
‎We wouldn’t deliberately ignore him ‎and pray to Jesus; that’s for sure.
‎But prayer is necessary.
‎We’re really not qualified to judge
‎whether the prayers of our brothers
‎are received favorably by Jehovah or not.
‎Some words come ‎from the brain and out of the mouth,
‎while others come ‎from the heart and out of the mouth.
‎We ask ourselves, ‎‘Am I speaking to Jehovah from my heart
‎or only from my brain?’
‎When we speak to Jehovah, ‎we want to use truthful words
‎that come from the heart
‎—words “seasoned with salt,” ‎the Bible tells us,
‎“gracious,”
‎words that are in good taste,
‎respectful,
‎and wholesome.
‎Job’s short prayer came from the heart
‎at Job 1:21
‎—just a real short prayer—
‎but Jehovah heard it.
‎And, of course, ‎he was with Job all the way.
‎If he hadn’t been with Job,
‎Job would have had a hard time, ‎wouldn’t he, worse than he had?
‎But here’s his prayer.
‎He said: ‎“Naked I came out of my mother’s womb,
‎“and naked I will return.
‎“Jehovah has given, ‎and Jehovah has taken away.
‎“Let the name of Jehovah
‎continue to be praised.”
‎Beautiful, isn’t it?
‎Solomon also gave ‎a beautiful prayer at 1 Kings 3:6-10.
‎We won’t read that; it’s lengthy.
‎When we need help,
‎talk to Jehovah from your heart like Asa did.
‎And at the very end,
‎when Asa asked Jehovah to help him
‎because they had a million people against them
‎—they were warriors, ‎and he had a small group—
‎well, Jehovah blessed that prayer.
‎Asa drew close to Jehovah,
‎and Jehovah drew close to Asa
‎so much so that he defeated the Ethiopians
‎before Asa and before Judah, ‎and the Ethiopians fled.
‎They ran away.
‎Why?
‎Well, Asa drew close to Jehovah ‎—that’s why.
‎And, of course, ‎we want to draw close to Jehovah.
‎Another way that we draw close to Jehovah
‎is through meditation.
‎We want to think about what we pray.
‎They say a sheep ‎has four compartments in his stomach.
‎So it takes a long time, ‎sometimes two days or longer,
‎to digest his food.
‎Well, some things ‎that we take in, too, are hard to digest.
‎It takes awhile, ‎and we digest it basically through meditation.
‎We have to think about it over and over again.
‎Sometimes we even have to ask others:
‎“How do you feel about this? ‎ How did you understand it?
‎What did it do for you?” ‎and so forth.
‎And they’ll help us.
‎So prayer and meditation ‎—these are the two key things
‎that we will want to think about
‎as we endeavor to draw close to Jehovah.

cn.text: 你曾经听到一个弟兄的祷告
内心被深深打动吗？
也许是因为他说话得体
用词恰当
你可能会想
“要是我能像他那样祷告就好了！”
你有这样的想法
可能是因为你的教育程度不高
词汇量有限
祷告时言词有点匮乏
但耶和华最重视的
是你发自内心地向他祷告
当你向耶和华倾心吐意时
他一定会垂听你的祷告
就像他垂听那位善于表达
言词丰富的弟兄的祷告一样
所以，不用太在意祷告的形式
只要发自内心地祷告就好了
耶和华最看重的不是你所用的词汇
而是你内心的真实想法
要知道，在耶和华眼里
你和那位令你钦佩的弟兄
都是他的密友
当然
羡慕某位弟兄或姐妹善于表达没什么不对
但就算你不善于表达也不用担心
重要的是你发自内心地向耶和华祷告
这样就会令他喜悦
我们一起看看
撒母耳记上16:7的经文
这里说
耶和华对撒母耳说
“不要看他的样子和他高大的身材
我不拣选他
因为上帝看人不像人看人
人是看外貌
耶和华是看内心。”
可见，我们应该在耶和华面前保持谦卑
因为耶和华是看内心的上帝
知道这一点让我们多么欣慰
我想给你们讲一个经历
多年前我做分区监督的时候
分区里有位年长的弟兄请我去他的家吃饭
他的妻子不是我们的姐妹
但她为我们准备了丰盛的食物
那是一位很好的弟兄
也是会众的长老
聊天时我就问他
“你在认识真理前做什么工作？
从事什么行业？”
他回答说
“我是专业做祷告的
我们镇上的牧师们
会雇佣我周日去他们的教堂祷告。”
弟兄继续说
“因为我特别擅长做祷告
说话很有技巧
听到我低沉的声音和煽情的话
信徒们就会深受触动
心甘情愿地做出捐献
结束后
牧师就会把收到的捐款分给我
作为职业祷告师我真的赚到了不少钱。”
后来这位弟兄认识了真理
他也意识到这个工作有点问题
现在他的祷告还是很专业
还是能打动人心
只是现在他怀着正确的动机
今天的经文谈到亲近耶和华
亲近他的一个主要方法就是祷告
无论我们是跪着
站着还是躺下祷告
耶和华都会垂听
甚至默祷他也会听
就算我们在路上或在做别的事情
也可以祷告
只要是发自内心的祷告
耶和华都会垂听
当然，我们需要用正确的方式祷告
多年前
分区探访有一个问答讨论的环节
叫做“要继续持守你所学到的事”
这个环节最初叫“学到的新事”
我当分区监督的时候
要在星期六晚上
主持这个叫“学到的新事”的环节
有一次
演讲中我问了大家一个问题
“当你们向耶和华祷告时
你们应该把奉耶稣基督的名放在祷告开始
中间、结尾
还是在哪里都可以？”
当时回答什么的都有
说实话，如果你当时在场
你都不敢相信能听到那么多种不同的答案
不管怎样
他们通过这个节目知道了正确答案
聚会结束前
我邀请一个年长的弟兄做祷告
他一直忠贞事奉耶和华
但没想到他竟然向耶稣祷告
之后我问他
“你怎么会向耶稣祷告呢？”
他回答说
“我也不知道该向谁祷告了
我已经糊涂了。”
后来我的妻子对我说
“亲爱的
下次千万别在‘学到的新事’环节里
问那样的问题了。”
那个祷告可真是“学到的新事”
我真希望那群会众忘记这件事
不过，我们相信耶和华也会听那个祷告
因为他清楚了解我们的为人
也明白我们想说什么
但我们不会明知故犯
我们肯定不会故意向耶稣祷告
祷告是我们个人和耶和华之间的事
我们不需要也没有资格来判断
耶和华会不会垂听某个弟兄的祷告
有些话来自头脑
但也许言不由衷
有些话却发自内心
是真正的肺腑之言
我们可以问问自己
“我向耶和华祷告的时候
是发自内心还是只经过头脑呢？”
我们祷告的时候
都应该说出发自内心的
真诚的话
“带着恩慈，用盐调味”
这样的话既得体又表现尊重
在约伯记1:21
约伯说出了一个简短而衷心的祷告
尽管内容很短
但耶和华却垂听了
很显然，耶和华一直在困境中支持约伯
因为如果没有耶和华的支持
约伯一定不容易忍耐到底
那约伯当时是怎样祷告的呢？
约伯记1:21说
“我赤身出于母腹
也必赤身归回
赏赐的是耶和华
收回的也是耶和华
耶和华的名是应当称颂的。”
这个祷告多么感人！
在列王纪上3:6-10
所罗门也做了一个感人的祷告
我们可以回去自己读一读
另外，当需要帮助时
我们可以效法亚撒王的榜样
当时一百万强敌大军压境
而亚撒的军队明显处于逆势
情势危急
于是亚撒向耶和华真诚地祷告
耶和华回应了他的祷告
在亚撒和犹大人面前
击败了埃塞俄比亚大军
让他们落荒而逃
亚撒诚心寻求耶和华、亲近他
所以上帝为他征战
我们也可以像他一样亲近耶和华
另一个帮助我们亲近耶和华的方法
就是沉思
我们需要好好想想祷告里要说什么
科学家说绵羊的胃里
有四个胃室
因此绵羊需要比较长的时间
来消化食物
有时长达两天或更久
有些属灵食物也需要比较长时间来消化
沉思可以帮助我们好好消化
并吸收这些固体食物
有时我们也需要问问别人
“对于这件事你有什么感觉？
你是怎么理解的？
对你有什么影响呢？”等等
别人也一定乐于相助
愿我们不断改善祷告和沉思的素质
这样就可以与我们的天父耶和华更亲近

ko.text: 여러분이 이제 막 공개 강연을 하려고 합니다.
청중이 여러분의 말을 잘 들을 것입니까?
그건 상당 부분 여러분의 서론에 달려 있습니다.
그 내용이 듣는 사람들에게 왜 중요한지 알려 주어야 합니다.
이제 한 형제가 어떻게 서론을 하는지 유의해 보시기 바랍니다.
이제 사람이 죽으면 어떻게 되는지 함께 알아보도록 하시죠.
전도서 9:5을 펴서 한번 같이 읽어 보실까요?
죽음을 피할 수 있었던 사람은 아무도 없었습니다.
그러면 그처럼 큰 고통을 주는 죽음이 과연
사람이 왜 죽는지, 죽으면 어떻게 되는지,
죽음이 어떻게 사라질 것인지를 알 수 있죠.
어떤 연설을 하든 이 방법을 사용할 수 있습니다.
그러면 봉사에서는 어떻게 효과적인 서론을 할 수 있을까요?
집주인에게는 우리가 낯선 사람이라는 걸 기억해야 합니다.
그가 하고 있는 일과 주변 환경을 살펴보십시오.
질문을 해서 대화를 시작할 수 있죠.
전 오늘 땅에 대한 하느님의 목적을 말씀드리러 왔어요.
그걸 보니 서론이 흥미를 불러일으키는 데 실패한 거 같네요.
전도인이 어떻게 서론을 했더라면 더 좋았을까요?
근데, 수고한 보람이 있으신 거 같아요.
참, 전 리사라고 하고 여긴 쥬디예요.
아주머니께선 집에 만든 정원을 잘 가꾸려고 하시잖아요.
전도인은 집주인이 관심 있어 할 만한 점이 뭘지
덕분에 대화를 시작하고 왕국 소식을 전할 수 있었죠.
물론 도시에선 사람들이 곧바로 용건을 이야기하는 경향이 있습니다.
서론에서 흥미를 불러일으킬 만한 말이나 질문을 해 보십시오.
좋은 대화를 나누고 좋은 소식을 전할 기회가 더 많아질 것입니다.

en.text: You’re at the Kingdom Hall about to give a public talk.
Will the audience listen to what you have to say?
Much depends on how you introduce your subject.
An effective introduction arouses interest,
identifies your subject,
and shows why the subject is important to your listeners.
Let’s give our brother an opportunity to introduce his subject.
As the meeting chairman mentioned,
we’re going to talk about death
and what it means to you and me.
Let’s read a scripture
at Ecclesiastes 9:5.
So, what do you think?
Did the speaker identify his subject?
Yes.
Did he arouse interest?
Not so much.
Did he show why the subject is important?
No.
So how might he approach the subject differently?
Let’s watch.
Throughout all of human history,
not one person has escaped death.
The lives of some people are cut short suddenly
by unexpected events or illness.
Have you ever lost a loved one in death?
If so, you know how painful that is.
Yet how can something that causes so much pain
be a normal, natural part of life?
The Bible is the key
to understanding why we die,
where we go when we die,
and how death will be reversed.
Let’s consider each of those points.
You can apply this principle
to any subject when giving a talk.
But how can you effectively introduce
a subject in the ministry?
Remember, of course, that in most cases
you’re a complete stranger to the householder.
Try not to startle the person.
Identify yourself early in the conversation.
To determine what a person might be interested in,
observe his activities or surroundings.
You might begin by asking a question
or making a brief comment about those things.
Let’s consider one example.
Hi, my name is Jill.
I’m here to talk about God’s purpose for the future.
The Bible says here—
Sorry, but I don’t have time to talk.
Was the introduction effective?
The householder didn’t want to continue the conversation,
so apparently the introduction didn’t arouse interest.
How might the publisher have handled the situation better?
Good morning.
You have a beautiful garden.
It must take a lot of work.
It sure does!
Well, your work is certainly paying off.
Thank you.
By the way, my name is Jill, and this is Tammy.
I’m Emily.
Emily, you work so hard to care for the garden you planted.
Do you think that God cares the same way
about this planet that he created?
Because the publisher took into account
the interests of the householder,
she increased the chances of starting a conversation
and sharing the Kingdom message.
This can also be done in urban areas
where people expect you to get right to the point.
In such settings, try to include a thought-provoking statement
or question in your introduction.
Effective introductions are the first step
toward productive conversations
and presentations of the good news.

cn.text: 你来到王国聚会所，准备上台演讲
你的演讲能够引起听众的兴趣吗？
这就要看你的引言怎么说了
有效的引言应该要激发听者的兴趣
让听者知道演讲要谈什么
还有为什么这个话题很重要
请看看这个弟兄做得怎么样
主席刚刚介绍过了
我们今天要谈论的主题是死亡
以及这跟你我有什么关系
让我们看传道书9:5
你觉得怎么样
这个讲者有没有说演讲会谈什么？
说了

ko.text: 이젠 여러분이 전 시간 봉사를 하면서 겪은 어려움에 대해 들어 보죠.
