title: 제프리 W. 잭슨: 여호와를 시험하는 일 (말라기 3:10)

ko.text: 오늘의 성구를 보면 아주 흥미로운 질문이 떠오릅니다.
예수께선 여호와를 시험해선 안 된다고 하시지 않았나요?
“여호와를 시험하는 것에는 잘못된 방법과 올바른 방법이 있다.”
그럼 어떻게 올바른 방법과 잘못된 방법을 알 수 있을까요?
우리는 믿음과 미련함의 차이가 무엇인지를 이해할 수가 있는데요,
먼저, 여호와를 시험하는 올바른 방법은 어떤 것일까요?
우리가 여호와에 대한 믿음을 나타내고, 그분을 신뢰하고,
여호와께서 먼저 행동하길 기다리는 게 아니라,
우리가 우선 그분께 순종하고, 적극적으로 그분이 원하시는 걸 할 때,
또한 살면서 여호와께서 허용하신 일들을 겪을 때 불평하지 않고
실제론 순종하지 않으면서 겉으로만 순종하는 척
여호와를 신뢰하고, 그분에게 믿음을 두고, 그분께 순종하는 겁니다.
그러면 여호와를 시험하는 잘못된 방법은 뭘까요?
여호와께서 허용하신 일들에 대해 이기적인 동기로 불평한다면,
또는 미련한 일 즉 주의하지 않고 어떤 일을 해 놓고,
여호와께서 기적으로 우릴 구해 주시길 기대한다면,
또는 그분의 뜻과 사실상 일치하지 않는
어떤 일을 해 달라고 계속 여호와께 조른다면,
실제론 그분을 불쾌하게 하는 일을 해서 여호와를 속이려 한다면,
이 모두가 사실 미련한 행동에 속하는 일들이죠.
그럼, 이와 관련해 우리가 생각해 봐야 할 점은 무엇입니까?
예수께서 하신 말씀의 근거 성구를 찾아 볼까요?
예수의 말씀을 더 잘 이해하는 데 도움이 됩니다. 16절.
“여러분이 맛사에서 여러분의 하느님 여호와를 시험한 것처럼,
이스라엘 백성은 “시험” 또는 “시련” 이라는 뜻을 갖게 된 그 장소에서
그때 대체 어떤 행동을 한 것입니까?
그때 실제 어떤 일이 있었는지 힌트를 얻을 수 있습니다.
“그리하여 그가 그곳의 이름을 맛사와 므리바라고 했다.
‘여호와께서 우리 가운데 계시는가, 안 계시는가?’ 하고 말하며
네, 이스라엘 백성이 어떻게 한 거죠?
그분이 그들 모두를 광야에서 죽게 내버려 두지 않으실 것임을 깨닫지 못하고,
우리에게 아주 중요한 교훈을 주지 않습니까?
또한 이스라엘 사람들이 약속의 땅으로 가지 않겠다고 한 일도
두 명의 훌륭한 수장이 한 보고에 몹시 화가 나서
열 명의 정탐꾼이 한 부정적인 보고를 받아들입니다.
그들이 벌을 받게 될 것임을 말씀하시자 그들은 어떻게 하죠?
그분의 말씀을 무시하고 약속의 땅으로 들어가려 합니다.
그들은 독자적으로 가려 했고, 여호와께선 지원하지 않으셨습니다.
네, 우리를 위한 아주 흥미로운 사례입니다.
여호와를 시험하는 올바른 방법과 잘못된 방법의 차이를
더 중요한 점으로, 우리는 여호와를 잘못된 방법으로 시험할 때
그분이 느끼실 감정을 생각해 보아야 합니다.
시편에서 그분의 그런 감정을 읽을 수 있는데요,
그리고 여호와를 화나게 만들고 실망시키는 일들을 함으로
따라서 여호와를 시험하는 올바른 방법과 잘못된 방법의 차이를 아는 것은
이와 관련해 우리가 피해야 할 일들은 무엇일까요?
우리를 위해 어떤 특별한 일을 해 달라고
여호와께 강요하거나 요구하는 일이 있어선 안 됩니다.
또 우리가 기대하는 일에 관해 그분께 불평하는 일이 있어선 안 되죠.
또한 불필요하게 위험을 무릅쓰는 일을 피해야 합니다.
그런 이유에서 우리에겐 안전 의식을 일깨워 주는
믿음과 미련함의 차이를 구분하지 못하는 사람들은
‘내가 무슨 일을 하든 여호와께서 다 돌봐 주실 거야.’
하지만 과거 1953년 「깨어라!」 에선 이렇게 알려 주는데요,
기사 제목은 “하느님을 시험해서는 안 된다” 였습니다.
우리에게 아무 일도 닥치지 않을 것처럼 행동한다면,
그것은 사실상 우리 자신을 매우 중요시하는 것과 다름없다.
우리는 비이성적인 또는 부주의한 행동을 함으로
우리가 무엇을 하거나 또는 하지 않았는데도
하느님께서 천사를 보내 우리를 사고나 해로부터
보호해 주실 것으로 기대할 수는 없다.”
선교인이었을 때 이 교훈을 깨닫는 데 여러 해가 걸렸죠.
선교 임지에서 보낸 처음 몇 년을 되돌아 보니,
구명 조끼도 안 입고 배에서 바다 위 작은 보트로 뛰어내렸는데,
따라서 우린 자신의 행동을 주의 깊이 따져 보면서
예수께서는 이 면에서 매우 지혜롭게 행동하셨죠.
하지만 예수께선 여호와를 섬기며 그분의 뜻을 행하고 있었기에
때 이른 죽임을 당하지 않을 거라는 여호와에 대한 신뢰가 있었죠.
용기 있게 보란 듯이 뛰어 내려보라고 부추겼을 때,
예수께선 그렇게 하는 게 미련한 행동임을 아셨습니다.
오늘날 우리 역시 결정을 내릴 때,
‘왕국을 첫째로 구하고 나의 뜻을 행하면 너희를 축복하겠다’고 약속하십니다.
그분이 결국 우릴 축복하실 것임을 확신할 수 있습니다.
하지만 위험을 무릅쓰거나 조심성 없이 행동함으로
여호와를 시험하겠다는 생각은 결코 하지 않도록 해야겠습니다.
결정을 내릴 땐, 늘 멈추어 기도하면서
이것이 믿음의 행동인지 미련한 행동인지 생각하도록 합시다.

en.text: ‎The scripture that we’re considering this morning
‎raises a very interesting question,
‎and that is,
‎How is it that we can ‘test Jehovah out’?
‎Didn’t Jesus say that we shouldn’t test Jehovah?
‎Well, the simple answer to that question
‎was given ‎in The Watchtower back in 1957.
‎It simply stated: ‎“There is a wrong way
‎and a right way ‎to put Jehovah to the test.”
‎Now, how do we know ‎what is the right way
‎and what is the wrong way?
‎Well, again, put simply,
‎it means knowing the difference ‎between faith and stupidity.
‎When we consider ‎what the Scriptures tell us,
‎it helps us to see the line
‎that is the demarcation ‎between faith and stupidity.
‎Consider, first of all, the good way
‎that we can test out Jehovah.
‎When we think about ‎showing faith in Jehovah,
‎having trust in him, ‎and then obeying him
‎—not waiting for Jehovah ‎to make the first move
‎but rather for us, ‎first of all, to obey him,
‎to reach out ‎and do what he wants us to do
‎—that, in a figurative way, ‎is putting him to the test,
‎because he’s already promised to bless us.
‎By us obeying him, ‎it means that we are showing faith.
‎It also means that we ‎don’t complain about the things
‎that Jehovah ‎allows to occur in our life,
‎and we don’t take unnecessary risks.
‎We don’t try to fool him
‎by acting one way
‎but then pretending to be another way.
‎So put quite simply, again,
‎the right way for us to test out Jehovah
‎means to trust him,
‎to have faith in him,
‎to obey him
‎even if it may be difficult to do so.
‎Well, what about the wrong way ‎to test out Jehovah?
‎Well, if we were to selfishly complain
‎about the things ‎that Jehovah allows to occur in our life
‎or if we were to do
‎something stupid, ‎something careless,
‎and expect that Jehovah ‎is going to perform a miracle to save us
‎or perhaps ‎we keep pushing Jehovah
‎to do something ‎that really is not in harmony with his will
‎or if we try to fool him
‎by pretending to serve him
‎but actually are doing things ‎that displease him,
‎all of those things really would be ‎a stupid act on our part.
‎Now, what do we really need to consider ‎with regard to this?
‎Well, let’s think about when Jesus ‎made that answer to Satan
‎and said, ‎‘You shouldn’t put Jehovah to the test.’
‎Let’s have a look at the scripture ‎that he based that comment on.
‎It’s found at Deuteronomy 6:16,
‎and this gives us ‎a little context to the meaning.
‎In verse 16, it says:
‎“You must not ‎put Jehovah your God to the test
‎the way you put him ‎to the test at Massah.”
‎Now, really, what was it
‎that the Israelites did ‎at this particular time
‎where the name of the location
‎where they were ‎meant “Testing” or “Trial”?
‎Well, if we turn back to Exodus 17:7,
‎it gives us some idea ‎of what this really involved.
‎Exodus 17:7:
‎“So he named the place ‎Massah and Meribah
‎“because of the quarreling of the Israelites
‎“and because they put Jehovah to the test
‎by saying: ‎‘Is Jehovah in our midst or not?’”
‎So, what did the Israelites do here?
‎Obviously, they didn’t trust Jehovah enough.
‎They didn’t have enough ‎faith in Jehovah to realize
‎that he wasn’t going ‎to let them all die in the wilderness.
‎But they pushed him.
‎They wanted something immediately.
‎They wanted to satisfy their selfish desires.
‎Well, that’s a very good lesson for us ‎—isn’t it?—
‎because this shows a lack of faith.
‎We could consider ‎when the Israelites decided
‎that they didn’t want to go ‎into the Promised Land.
‎Remember, ‎they were so upset with the report
‎of the two good chieftains ‎who had spied out the land
‎that they wanted to kill them.
‎They accepted the report ‎of the ten who had a negative report.
‎And why did they do that?
‎Again, lack of faith in Jehovah.
‎But then when Jehovah told them ‎what was going to happen,
‎the punishment ‎that was going to come on them,
‎what did they do?
‎They went straight ahead ‎and decided to go into the Promised Land.
‎And what happened?
‎You see, it was an act of stupidity.
‎They were going on their own,
‎and Jehovah ‎wasn’t going to give them support,
‎and that’s exactly what happened.
‎They were defeated.
‎So we see ‎this is a very interesting example
‎for us to understand the difference
‎between the wrong way ‎and the right way
‎of putting Jehovah to the test.
‎And, more important, ‎we need to remember
‎how Jehovah feels
‎when we put him to the test in the wrong way.
‎We can see this ‎if we turn to the book of Psalms,
‎“How often they rebelled against him
‎“in the wilderness ‎and made him feel hurt in the desert!
‎“Again and again ‎they put God to the test,
‎and they grieved ‎the Holy One of Israel.”
‎Yes, by their lack of faith ‎and by doing things
‎that we could say ‎irritated or disappointed Jehovah,
‎they grieved Jehovah.
‎So this is ‎a very important matter for us:
‎to realize the difference ‎between the right and wrong way
‎of putting Jehovah to the test.
‎With regard to this,
‎what sort of things ‎do we need to avoid?
‎Well, we need to avoid dictating, ‎or demanding,
‎that Jehovah do ‎certain special things for us.
‎We need to avoid ‎complaining to him
‎about our expectations.
‎We need to avoid ‎taking unnecessary risks and chances.
‎And that’s why we have ‎a very important group of brothers
‎that help to remind us about safety.
‎We do need to remember ‎safety standards.
‎Now, some perhaps do not realize
‎the difference between faith and stupidity,
‎and they may have the viewpoint,
‎‘Well, Jehovah will look after me ‎if I’m doing whatever I’m doing.’
‎But notice what the Awake! magazine ‎said back in 1953.
‎It was in the article entitled ‎“You Must Not Put God to the Test.”
‎And this is what it says:
‎“It really amounts ‎to considering ourselves very important
‎“when we act as though ‎nothing could happen to us
‎“because we are serving Jehovah. . . .
‎“We dare not put God to the test
‎“with irrational actions and carelessness.
‎“We simply cannot expect God
‎“to furnish us angels ‎to keep us from harm and accident
‎in spite of what we may or may not do.”
‎Well, that’s a good reminder ‎for all of us, isn’t it?
‎I know, as a missionary,
‎this was a lesson ‎I had to learn over the years
‎—the difference ‎between faith and stupidity.
‎When I look back on the first few years
‎I was in my missionary assignment
‎and some of the scary things we did
‎—jumping off ships into little boats ‎in the open sea without life jackets—
‎at the time, ‎I thought it was an act of faith,
‎but now I view it a little differently.
‎So we do need to be careful ‎to measure what we’re doing
‎and see if it really is an act of faith
‎or if it’s just doing something stupid.
‎Jesus showed great wisdom ‎in this regard, didn’t he?
‎When he served Jehovah ‎here on earth,
‎no doubt many times ‎his life was endangered
‎because the Pharisees ‎and the Sadducees opposed him.
‎They were looking ‎for ways to kill him.
‎But because he was serving Jehovah ‎and doing what Jehovah wanted,
‎he had trust in Jehovah
‎that he wouldn’t be killed ‎before the due time.
‎But on the other hand, ‎when Satan tempted him
‎in a way to boldly show off
‎and jump off the temple,
‎what did Jesus say?
‎‘You mustn’t test Jehovah.’
‎You see, Jesus realized that ‎that would have been an act of stupidity.
‎So for us today, it’s likewise important
‎when we’re making decisions
‎to balance out very carefully
‎what Jehovah wants us to do.
‎Yes, when Jehovah ‎makes a promise and says,
‎‘If you put the Kingdom first
‎and you do ‎what I want you to do, I will bless you’
‎and then we reach out and we do that,
‎we can be confident ‎that Jehovah will ultimately bless us.
‎But never may we ever ‎take the viewpoint
‎that we will just put ‎Jehovah to the test
‎by taking chances ‎and doing rash things.
‎Yes, whenever we make a decision,
‎let’s stop and prayerfully consider,
‎Is this an act of faith or stupidity?

cn.text: 今天的经文
玛拉基书3:10鼓励我们要试试耶和华
这是在让我们试探耶和华吗？
耶稣不是说不可以试探耶和华吗？
1957年的一期《守望台》
简单地回答了这个问题
文章说
“试探耶和华
也分正确的方式和错误的方式”
那么，什么是正确的方式
什么又是错误的方式呢？
简单来说
我们需要明白表现信心
和行事愚蠢之间的区别
为了看出两者之间的区别
让我们来考查一下圣经的记载
首先
我们看看正确地试探耶和华是什么意思
耶和华已经承诺会赐福给服从他的人
因此，如果我们信赖上帝的承诺
甘心服从他
这就好像是在试探耶和华
换句话说
我们不会等耶和华先赐福才服从他
而是会采取主动
先努力按他的要求去做
相信这样做会蒙他赐福
另外
我们不会对耶和华容许发生的事诸多埋怨
或不必要地冒险
我们也不会欺骗耶和华
只做表面功夫，假装服从他
所以，试探耶和华的正确方式就是要信赖他
就算情况不容易
也仍然会对他表现信心和服从
那么，我们怎样试探耶和华算是错误的呢？
当耶和华容许一些难题发生时
我们不该抱怨
我们也不该自己做事粗心大意
却期待耶和华施行奇迹来拯救我们
又或是不断恳求耶和华
做违背他旨意的事情来帮助自己
我们也要避免假装事奉耶和华
实际上却做一些耶和华不喜欢的事
这些都是很愚蠢的做法
关于试探耶和华
关键要考虑什么呢？
请想想耶稣曾怎样回答撒但
他说：“不可试探耶和华”
耶稣的这个回答
引用了《希伯来语经卷》的经文
就是申命记6:16
这节经文可以帮助我们
理解耶稣的话是什么意思
16节说
“不可试探耶和华你们的上帝
像在玛萨试探他那样。”
“玛萨”的意思是“试验”、“考验”
当时以色列人究竟在这个地方做了什么呢？
如果你看看出埃及记17:7
就会知道以色列人曾怎样试探耶和华
经文说：“他给那地方起名叫玛萨
又叫米利巴
因为以色列人在那地方争吵
又试探耶和华
说：‘耶和华真的在我们当中吗？’”
以色列人做了什么？
显然，他们不够信任耶和华
以色列人信心不足
担心耶和华会让他们死在旷野
他们没有耐心
想要耶和华立马帮助他们
满足他们的自私欲望
这些人缺乏信心
我们要吸取他们的教训
请也想想之后发生的事
以色列人吵着说不想去应许之地了
记得吗？
虽然有两个前去侦察的探子带来了好消息
但民众根本听不进去
还想打死他们
他们宁愿接受十个探子的负面消息
为什么？
还是因为对耶和华缺乏信心
可是，当耶和华后来宣告惩罚以色列人
他们又有什么反应呢？
他们还是没听从耶和华
反倒试图进入应许之地
多么愚蠢！
以色列人选择信靠自己
耶和华当然不会支持他们
结果怎么样？
他们被打败了
这个典型的例子帮助我们明白
试探耶和华的正确方式
和错误方式有什么区别
还有更重要的一点
请记得，当我们以错误的方式试探耶和华时
他会有什么感觉
我们可以参考一下诗篇78:40,41
“他们多少次在旷野反叛他
在荒漠叫他伤心！
他们一再试探上帝
使以色列的圣者悲痛。”
是的，以色列人缺乏信心
他们的行为激怒了耶和华
让他失望悲痛
所以说，知道什么是试探耶和华的正确方式
什么是错误的方式
这非常重要
具体来说
我们需要避免做什么事呢？
不要命令或要求耶和华为我们做某件事
不要因为愿望迟迟没有实现就对他产生抱怨
也要避免不必要地冒险
这就是为什么伯特利有一个部门
负责提醒我们跟安全有关的事情
我们确实有必要把安全指引牢记在心
但是
有些人可能分不清
信心和愚蠢有什么区别
他们可能觉得
不管自己做什么都会得到耶和华的保护
不过
请留意1953年的一期《警醒！》怎么说
这篇题为《不可试探上帝》的文章
是这么说的
“要是我们仗着自己事奉耶和华
就以为做什么都不会有问题
这其实反映出我们把自己看得很重要
我们绝不该行事鲁莽
做一些不理智的事
来试探耶和华
我们不该以为
不管我们做什么
上帝都会派天使保护我们
免遭意外、免受伤害”
这是个很好的提醒，对吗？
我自己做特派传道员的时候
花了很多年才明白信心和愚蠢有什么区别
我做特派传道员的头几年
做过一些很吓人的事情
比如，在海上不穿救生衣就从大船跳上小船
当时我以为这是很有信心的行为
真是一件蠢事
所以
我们真的需要仔细想想
自己正在做的事情
是真的出于信心
还是在做蠢事
在这方面
耶稣显出极大的智慧
他在地上的时候
生命多次受到威胁
因为法利赛派和撒都该派都反对他
想找各种机会把他杀了
不过，由于耶稣一直事奉耶和华
遵行上帝的旨意
他相信耶和华会保护他
在指定的时刻来到前
自己不会被杀掉
但另一方面，当撒但引诱耶稣
想让他炫耀自己、从圣殿往下跳时
耶稣是怎么回答的？
“不可试探上帝。”
显然耶稣看出那样做是愚蠢的
我们在做决定时
也需要仔细想想耶和华希望我们做什么
耶和华保证说
“要是你把王国事物放在首位
按我的吩咐去做
我就会赐福给你”
我们切实这样做
就可以确信耶和华最终一定会赐福给我们
但绝不要想着做一些鲁莽、冒险的事
来试探耶和华
每次做决定时
都要先停下来，仔细想想
我是在凭信心行事
还是在愚蠢行事？

titles.ko: 제프리 W. 잭슨: 여호와를 시험하는 일 (말라기 3:10)
titles.en: Geoffrey W. Jackson: Testing Jehovah Out (Mal. 3:10)
titles.cn: 杰弗里·杰克逊：试试耶和华（玛3:10）

title: 우리의 조직이 이루고 있는 일들—기꺼이 자원하여 섬기는 파트타임 출퇴근 봉사자들

ko.text: 여호와께 순결한 숭배를 드리기 위해 몰려들고 있습니다!
“말일에 여호와의 집의 산이 산들의 꼭대기보다 높이 굳게 서고
그리로 모든 나라 사람들이 몰려들 것이다.”
전 세계 수많은 사람들이 순결한 숭배의 탁월함을 알아보고
여호와 하느님께 드리는 신성한 봉사에 기꺼이 참여하고 있습니다.
전 세계 형제들의 영적 필요를 돌보기 위해
중앙장로회는 89개 나라에 지부 사무실을 두고 있습니다.
이 시설들에서 일하는 정규 베델 가족 성원들은
여호와께 숭배를 드리는 사람이 점점 늘어나고 있으며,
베델이나 현지 번역 사무실과 같은 여러 시설에서
다양한 업무를 지원할 자원봉사자가 더 많이 필요하게 되었습니다.
하지만 지부 시설을 확장하여 더 많은 베델 봉사자를 수용하려면
그러면 어떻게 더 많은 봉사자를 구할 수 있습니까?
중앙장로회 인사 위원회는 정규 베델 가족들에 더해,
그 밖의 자원하는 사람들을 파트타임 출퇴근 봉사자로 초대합니다.
그들은 대부분 세속 일을 하며 생계를 돌보는데,
그중에는 베델을 방문하는 수많은 사람을 안내하는 일도 포함됩니다.
그들은 컴퓨터부, 식품 봉사부, 설계부, 조경부, 번역부,
건물 봉사부 등 다양한 부서들에서 일합니다.
전 세계에서 9500명이 파트타임 봉사자로 일하고 있습니다.
베델에서 봉사하기 위해 어떤 희생을 합니까?
새벽 네 시에 일어나서 버스를 세 번 타야 했어요.
출퇴근 봉사를 하려고 삶을 더 단순하게 했죠.
어려움이 있긴 하지만 이 봉사를 절대로 포기하고 싶지 않아요.
여호와께 계속 기도하고 그분을 신뢰하면서 봉사하고 있습니다.
여호와께서 저희 부부를 돌봐 주시는 걸 경험했어요.
그해에 방문한 30만 2401명의 방문객을 따뜻하게 환영하기 위해
이처럼 커다란 희생을 치르는 이유는 무엇입니까?
시편 110:3에는 다음과 같은 보증의 말씀이 나옵니다.
“[여호와]의 군대의 날에, 각주에 의하면, [여호와]의 군대가 집결하는 날에,
베델에서 파트타임으로라도 일할 수 있는 특권에 대해
그들은 이처럼 기꺼이 자원한 덕분에 어떤 축복을 받았다고 말합니까?
사랑 많은 형제 자매들과 함께 일해서 너무 좋아요.

저는 회중에서 계속 기쁘게 파이오니아 봉사를 하고 있어요.
베델에서 일한 시간을 고려받을 수 있거든요.
다양하게 여호와를 섬길 수 있어서 좋습니다.
제가 특히 소중하게 여기고 감사하게 생각하는 한 가지 축복은
저희 가족이 영적으로 발전하는 데 제가 도움이 될 수 있었다는 거예요.
저한테는 일곱 살 된 여동생이 있는데,

동생이 저처럼 되고 싶어 한다는 게 저한테는 가장 큰 축복이에요.
영감을 받아 시편 필자는 자신을 기꺼이 바치는 “군대”가
하느님의 백성에게 새 힘을 줄 거라고 예언했습니다.
‘이슬방울 같은 젊은 남녀들의 무리가 여호와께 나온다’고 말합니다.
이스라엘 백성은 북쪽의 높은 헤르몬산에서 내려온 수증기가
약속의 땅의 저지대에서 이슬이 되는 모습을 상상했을 것입니다.
이 표현은 여호와께 더 많은 봉사를 드리고자 하는
열심 있는 수많은 형제 자매들이 얼마나 새 힘을 주는지
그들은 “자신을 기꺼이 바”쳐 전 세계 형제 자매들에게 유익을 주고

en.text: Welcome to this special news update.
As reported
in the “Newsroom” section of jw.org,
on November 30, 2018,
the South Korean government released 57 of our brothers
who had been imprisoned for conscientious objection.
The Governing Body, together with our worldwide brotherhood,
rejoices with these brothers and their families.
The Ministry of Justice granted an early release for our brothers
who had already served at least 6 months
of their 18-month sentence.
We expect that the remaining eight brothers
will also be released sometime after they’ve served
six months of their sentence.
They will be the last
of the more than 19,000 Witnesses
who have been sent to prison in Korea since 1953.
But what led to this momentous event?
During 2018,
a series of historic court rulings in Korea
finally recognized conscientious objection
as a fundamental right.
This development now puts South Korea in line
with many other countries in the world
who say that refraining from military service
for religious reasons is not a crime.
As a result of these rulings,
the prison doors were opened for 57 brothers.
Recently, our branch received a report
from the elders appointed to assist
our imprisoned brothers.
They said that brothers who have served at least six months
of their sentence could be released early on parole.
It was such great news that I almost couldn’t believe it.
My son will be released two months earlier than expected.
I’ve heard that two months in prison feels very long.
Well, even a single day feels long.
Since our brothers in the past had been allowed parole
after serving at least 14 months,
this was a great surprise to our brothers,
and many were beside themselves with joy.
It’s been over a year since I’ve been able to hug my son.
When I meet him tomorrow, the first thing I want to do
is give him a warm hug
and tell him he did a good job staying strong in prison.
My son was a caregiver for ill inmates, which can be dangerous
because of bloodborne diseases.
So he’d always show me he had no open wounds
on his hands and feet.
Tomorrow, I’ll be able to hold those hands,
and I don’t plan on letting go.
Finally, 57 brothers
were released at the same time
from 16 different prisons throughout South Korea.
It’s an amazing development!
The Supreme Court’s not-guilty decision last month
was pivotal in our brothers’ early release.
It stated that those ‘who object to military service
‘based on a conviction that is deep, firm,
and genuine should be protected.’
Many developments in the past few years led up to this wonderful outcome.
For example, since 2007, the Governing Body provided assistance
and encouragement to our brothers to make a fine defense in court.
As a result, more than 120 not-guilty decisions
were rendered in the lower courts.
The Constitutional Court, which had deliberated
on this issue for many years, rendered a historic decision,
declaring that the absence of alternative service is unconstitutional.
Furthermore, international human rights organizations
recommended the releasing of conscientious objectors.
Also, our brothers worldwide
have prayed incessantly for our imprisoned brothers.
We believe these prayers
were an important factor that brought about this great change.
They also sent many letters of encouragement
for our brothers to the branch,
and every one of these were forwarded to them.
There is no doubt these letters helped our brothers to endure.
Now our brothers who were separated from their families
for many months have been reunited.
I’ve been looking forward to this day so much,
and I’m so happy to be with my family again.
Thanks to Jehovah’s protection,
we’re able to have our son back in our arms in good health.
We welcome this decision and are overjoyed
at the early release of our brothers.
We look forward to seeing our brothers using their freedom
to bring praise to Jehovah.
He has brought salvation and shown favor to our brothers
walking the path of integrity for the past 65 years.
We are grateful for Jehovah’s loving care.
First Peter 2:19 states:
“It is agreeable when someone endures hardship
and suffers unjustly because of conscience toward God.”
This strongly applies to you brothers in Korea.
Through your long legacy of faith and endurance,
you have set a sterling example of integrity
and given a powerful witness.
As a result, you have Jehovah’s smile of approval.
Our thanks go to your families and all those around the world
who have kept you in their prayers.
The words of Romans 10:11
echo a fundamental truth about Jehovah:
“No one who rests his faith on him will be disappointed.”
Yes, all praise and honor go to Jehovah!

韩国政府2018年11月30日
释放了57位因良心拒服兵役的弟兄
中央长老团和全球的弟兄姐妹

自1953年以来

因为韩国在2018年

以前弟兄们起码要被关14个月以上才能被假释

我已经一年多没抱过我儿子了
明天，我一定要给他一个大大的拥抱！
跟他说他在监狱里一直保持忠贞，做得很好！
我儿子在监狱里时负责照顾一些生病的犯人
有些疾病会透过血液传染，非常危险
我每次都要看他的手、脚，确定没有任何伤口
明天，我就可以握到他的手了
我再也不想放开了
终于，在16个不同监狱里的57位弟兄
在同一时间被释放了！
这个结果真是不可思议！
上个月，韩国大法院宣判弟兄们无罪
因此，弟兄们可以提前被释放
判决书说:“一个人如果出于坚定、深厚
真诚的信念而拒服兵役
这样的人应该受到法律保护”
这个好结果跟过去几年的努力是分不开的
例如，中央长老团从2007年起就协助韩国弟兄
鼓励他们在法庭努力辩护
结果，地方法院对弟兄们做出了120多个无罪判决
多年来，韩国宪法法院一直仔细讨论这个议题
之后他们做了一个历史性的判决
声明“国家没有替代役的安排是违反宪法的”
另外，国际人权组织也敦促韩国
释放依良心拒服兵役的人
还有全世界的弟兄姐妹
也不断地为监狱里的弟兄祷告
我们相信，这些祷告一定发挥了很重要的作用
使得韩国作出了这么大的改变
这些弟兄姐妹也寄了很多信给韩国分部
想要鼓励监狱里的弟兄
分部把这些信都转给了他们
弟兄能在监狱保持忍耐
这些信一定大有帮助
现在，跟家人分开好几个月的弟兄们
又可以跟家人团聚了
这一天，我已经期待很久了
很高兴又可以跟家人在一起了
多亏有耶和华的保护
我们的儿子健健康康地回到了我们身边
我们的弟兄可以提前释放
很高兴法官做了这样的判决
我们很期待弟兄们好好运用他们的自由
来赞美耶和华
过去65年来
耶和华一直拯救这些忠贞的弟兄们
也仁爱地照顾他们
我们很感激耶和华
彼得前书2:19说
“人为了叫良心对得住上帝
甘愿受苦受屈，这是可喜的。”
这节经文非常适合韩国的弟兄
这么长时间以来，你们一直怀着信心
保持忍耐，忠贞事奉耶和华
为我们立下了非常好的榜样
也作了很有力的见证
耶和华一定很高兴
我们很感谢你们的家人
以及世界各地为你们祷告的弟兄姐妹
罗马书10:11道出了一个永恒不变的真理
“凡信靠他的，必不失望。”
没错，所有的赞美和荣耀都归于耶和华！

ko.text: 많은 사람은 어느 종교를 믿든 문제 될 게 없다고 생각합니다.
길은 달라도 같은 목적지로 갈 수 있듯이,
어느 종교를 믿든 하느님이 축복해 주실 거라고 여기는 것입니다.
성경은 다양한 종교를 두 가지 길로 묘사합니다.
한 길은 널찍하고 많은 사람이 다닙니다.
다른 길은 비좁고 찾아내는 사람이 적습니다.
올바른 숭배는 그 비좁은 길과도 같습니다.
그 길로 가야 하느님의 축복을 받고 생명을 얻게 됩니다.
우리가 올바른 길로 가고 있는지 어떻게 알 수 있습니까?
또 다른 사람은 지도를 보여 주면서 북쪽이 맞다고 알려 줍니다.
하느님의 축복을 받을 수 있는 길을 알려 줍니다.
그러면 사람들의 신앙이 그토록 다양한 이유는 무엇입니까?
사람이 죽어도 영혼은 어딘가에서 영원히 산다고 가르칩니다.
또는 식물로 환생한다고 가르치는 종교들도 있습니다.
이 밖에도 종교들은 서로 모순되는 다양한 신앙들을 가르칩니다.
그 모든 종교들이 정말 진리를 가르치고 있는 것입니까?
지도와도 같은 성경은 죽은 자는 아무것도 모른다고 말합니다.
때가 되면 하느님께서는 사람들을 부활시키실 것이며
의로운 자들은 땅에서 영원히 살 것입니다.
그러면 성경은 우리의 행실에 대해서는 무엇이라고 가르칩니까?
종교를 믿고 있어도 하느님이 불쾌하게 여기시는 행동을 하면
우리의 숭배는 아무 의미가 없게 될 것입니다.
사납고, 선을 사랑하지 않을” 것이라고 말합니다.

en.text: Many people believe that it doesn’t matter
which religion you choose,
that religions are like different roads that lead
to the same destination
—lasting blessings from God.
But can that be true?
Does God accept all forms of worship?
The Bible itself describes worship as two roads:
One is spacious with many people on it.
The other is cramped
with only a few finding it.
Only the cramped road
represents acceptable worship,
leading to life and blessings from God.
How can we tell
if we are on the correct path?
Imagine that you’re lost.
You stop someone to ask for directions.
One person says to head east;
another says to go west.
Finally, someone with a map shows you
that the destination is actually north.
Which one would you believe?
The Bible is like that map,
leading us to blessings from God.
So why are there so many conflicting beliefs?
For example,
many religions teach that the human soul
lives eternally in a spiritual realm,
while others believe that they are reborn
in another body or form.
This is just one example
of the many religious beliefs in conflict with one another.
Could all religions really be teaching the truth?
According to the “map,”
the dead know nothing at all.
In due time, God will restore them to life
and righteous ones will live forever on earth.
If the Bible is clear on this teaching,
what about other matters, such as our personal conduct?
We may belong to a religion,
but if our conduct offends God,
our worship may be futile.
The Bible teaches that many people today
would be “without self-control,
“fierce,
without love of goodness.”
However, it also says
that true worshippers of God
would be peaceable,
controlling their speech
and actions.
Rather than saying
there are many religions that please God,
the Bible says
there is only one faith.
True worship leads a person
to a good relationship with God
and everlasting life.
You may wonder:
‘How can you find the true religion?
Must you belong to an organized religion to please God?’
To learn more about what the Bible says
on this and many other topics,
go to jw.org.

en.text: So you are excited to go out in service!

Before you go in the ministry,

The three P’s?

Preparation,
personal appearance,
and proper behavior.
First, preparation.
Preparation is the first pillar
of success in the ministry.
Every job requires the proper tools.
When it comes to tools for preaching,
the variety might seem intimidating.
But never fear!
We have the Teaching Toolbox.
Finding the right tools is easier than ever!
Once you have your tools,
make sure and practice your presentation
before you leave the house.
We wouldn’t want to be preparing on the doorstep.

it’s time to talk about personal appearance.
How we look is very important because we represent Jehovah.

our appearance is saying the right things.

What that means is that we look and smell clean;
our clothes fit well,
but not too well;
our hair is done;
and we aren’t drawing too much attention to ourselves.
Looking sharp, my son!
Now it’s time to talk about proper behavior.
Our conduct while in the ministry
is another way we can bring praise to Jehovah.
So make sure you are on your best behavior.
Avoid talking or laughing loudly,
playing around,
or intruding on anyone’s property or privacy.
Also, no eating at the door.
Remember, when we go door to door, people see us,
and good behavior gives a good witness.
We would never want to give anyone
a reason to find fault with our ministry.
Can I go out in service now?
Yes!
It looks like you are ready.
It’s time to put the three P’s to the test.
Hi! My name is Caleb. What’s your name?
Hi, Caleb!
My name is . . .

title: JW 방송—2018년 12월: 길르앗 제145기 졸업식 프로그램

ko.text: JW 방송 2018년 12월 프로그램에 함께하시는 여러분 모두를
성경에 근거한 훌륭한 연설들을 듣게 되실 겁니다.
이것이 1부이고요, 몇 주 안에 나머지 부분도
몇몇 학생들의 이야기도 듣게 되실 것입니다.
그럼 이제 길르앗 제145기 졸업식 프로그램 1부를 시청하시겠습니다.
길르앗 제145기 졸업식 프로그램에 이렇게 함께할 수 있어서
이 세상 전역에서 볼 수 있는 다양한 졸업식 프로그램들과
다들 잘 알고 계시겠지만 일반적으로 세상의 졸업식에서는
개인이 달성한 일에 대해 이야기하고 그 사람을 칭송합니다.
하지만 길르앗 프로그램과 학생들이 이곳에서 받는 훈련 과정은 모두
여호와를 영광스럽게 하는 데 중점을 두죠.
성경을 보면 그 점을 분명히 알 수 있죠.
“나에게 베풀어진 과분한 친절을 통해서 그곳에 있는 여러분 모두에게 말합니다.
자기 자신에 대해 마땅히 생각해야 하는 것 이상으로 생각하지 마십시오.
오히려 하느님께서 각자에게 주신 믿음의 분량에 따라
우리가 가진 건 모두 여호와께서 주신 것입니다.
그러니 자신에 대해 필요 이상으로 생각해서는 안 되죠.
높은 것에 마음을 두지 말고 낮은 것에 이끌리십시오.
여러분은 이 말씀의 의미를 온전히 이해하고 있을 겁니다.
길르앗 교육을 통해 여호와와 튼튼한 관계를 갖게 되셨으니까요.
여호와를 알면 그분께 영광을 돌릴 수 밖에 없는데,
자신이 가진 모든 좋은 게 그분이 주신 것임을 알기 때문이죠.
하지만 이제 졸업생 여러분이 이전에 있던 곳이나 새로운 임지로 가면,
자신이 아니라 늘 여호와를 영광스럽게 해야겠다는 결심에 시험이 되는
시험을 금방 알 수 있는 경우도 있죠.
이전 임지로 돌아갔는데 이렇게들 말하는 겁니다.
전에 잘 못했다는 뜻일 수 있으니까요.
비유나 가르치는 방식이 놀랍네요” 라고 하면 어떨까요?
네, 저와 우리 모두는 졸업생 여러분이 그런 상황에서
자신이 아니라 여호와께 영광을 돌릴 것임을 잘 알고 있습니다.
따라서 그런 상황은 알아 보기가 비교적
하지만 어떤 상황에서는 어느 정도 자존심을 지키면서
자신에게 영광을 돌리고 싶은 유혹을 느낄 수도 있습니다.
우리에게 합당한 존중심을 보이지 않는 경우에는 어떨까요?
우리가 바라던 특권을 받지 못하면 어떨까요?
바로 그럴 때 유혹을 느낄 수 있죠.
내가 길르앗 학교에서 특별한 교육을 받고 졸업했다는 걸
사실, 이와 비슷한 함정에 빠진 사람으로 욥이 있습니다.
아주 충실한 사람, 충절을 지킨 사람이 떠오릅니다.
하지만 아시다시피 욥도 강한 조언을 받은 적이 있었습니다.
그러한 조언이 필요할 만한 행동을 한 것일까요?
욥기 1장에서 욥은 모든 걸 다 잃게 되죠.
하지만 욥기 1:22을 보면 알 수 있듯이,
그 모든 끔찍한 일이 일어나서, 그 어려운 시험을 겪으면서도,
그 후 두 번째로 시험이 닥쳤을 땐 어떻게 됩니까?
그러니까 이때도 잘 이겨냈다고 할 수 있죠.
욥이 실수를 저지르기 시작해서 강한 조언을 받아야 했던 것일까요?
친구라는 세 사람이 욥을 이렇게 비난한 때였습니다.
자네가 이렇게, 저렇게 했으니까 그런 거겠지.’
이와 같은 거짓 비난은 욥을 벼랑 끝으로 내몰았으며,
욥은 자신을 정당화하는 데 너무나 급급한 나머지
여호와께서 자신을 올바르지 않게 대하신다는 식으로 말했습니다.
이 예를 보면, 사람들이 우리에 대해
안 좋게 말하거나 거짓 비난을 할 경우,
자기도 모르게 스스로를 정당화하게 될 수 있습니다.
자신을 정당화하는 건 어떻게 하는 거죠?
영광을 자신에게 돌리고, 여호와께 돌리지 않는 것입니다.
우리 주 예수 그리스도께서는 이 면에서 훌륭한 본을 보이셨죠.
예수에 대해 나쁘게 말하면서 거짓 비난을 합니다.
욥처럼 함정에 빠져 자신을 정당화하려고 하셨습니까?
“나는 악귀가 들린 것이 아니라 나의 아버지를 공경하는 것입니다.”
영광을 구해 주시고 또 판단해 주시는 분이 계십니다.”
예수께서는 어려운 상황에서도 정말 훌륭한 본을 남기셨습니다.
깊은 인상을 주어서 사람들의 존경을 받으려고 할 필요도 없습니다.
우리 모두 무엇을 목표로 하면 좋을까요?
예수의 말씀을 함께 읽어 보고 싶은데요.
“이와 같이 여러분의 빛을 사람들 앞에 비추어,
하늘에 계신 여러분의 아버지께 영광을 돌리게 하십시오.”
이 점을 기억하면서 이어지는 프로그램을 즐기도록 하시죠.
여러 형제들이 이제 곧 임지로 떠날 여러분에게 도움이 될만한 내용을
먼저 존 에크란 형제의 연설을 들어 보시죠.
“가뭄이 드는 해에 여러분은 어떻게 할 것입니까?”입니다.
학생 여러분은 길르앗이란 강을 따라 심긴
“그는 물가에 심긴 나무와 같이 되어, 그 뿌리를 물길까지 뻗는다.
무더위가 닥쳐도 끄떡없고, 그 잎이 언제나 무성할 것이다.
오늘 졸업해서 이제 임지로 가시게 되면,
여러분은 잎사귀가 무성해지고 열매를 맺을 겁니다.
그런데 8절을 보면 의로운 나무들이 어떤 어려움을 겪어야 하죠?
그러면 이 무더위와 가뭄이 드는 해란 무엇입니까?
우리가 견뎌야 할 무더위에는 여러 형태가 있는데
특히 한 가지 형태의 무더위에 초점을 맞춰 보죠.
여호와의 증인에 관한 언론의 부정적인 기사들은
종교 지도층과 반대자들은 우리의 중립 입장,
성과 결혼에 대한 성경의 견해를 옹호하는 우리의 분명한 입장,
제명 처분을 통한 징계 등을 문제 삼아 우리를 헐뜯습니다.
게다가, 우리 형제들 중 일부는 연행되어 투옥되었죠.
공포와 의심 때문에 가뭄에 시들어 말라죽고 말까요?
가뭄에도 시들지 않을 거라고 그분은 확신하십니까?
여호와에게 확신을 두는 사람은 축복을 받을 것이다.”
따라서 가뭄이 드는 해에 여러분은 어떻게 할 것입니까?
사탄은 여호와에 대한 우리의 신뢰를 무너뜨리고 싶어 합니다.
사탄의 체제는 온통 공포, 불확실성, 의심에 기반해 있습니다.
박해는 마치 우리가 타고 가던 비행기가
한번은 제가 탄 비행기에서 한 여자가 공포에 질려 비명을 질렀는데,
기체가 약간만 흔들려도 매번 큰 소리를 질렀습니다.
하지만 경험 많은 승객들은 음식도 먹고 책이나 영화도 보면서,
그 정도의 사소한 난기류는 비행기가 쉽게 대처할 수 있다는 걸
경험상 알기 때문에 걱정하지 않은 거죠.
네, 우린 경험 많은 승객과 같습니다.
우린 이 세상의 난기류 즉 박해 때문에

그럴 때 “아버지를 사랑한다”라는 말이 내 생각을 좌우합니까?
그런 경험을 한 자매는 이렇게 말했습니다.
“우리 부서에서 있었던 일로 큰 상처를 받았어요.
그 후로 계속 제가 부족하다는 생각에 시달렸어요.
너무 낙담해서 힘이 다 빠진 것 같았죠.
여호와께 끝까지 고착하고 포기하지 않을 거예요.
반드시 부정적인 감정을 극복하고 영적으로•정신적으로 더 강해질 거예요.”
이 자매는 “아버지를 사랑한다”고 말만 한 게 아니라
몇 단어로 된 이 말에 힘입어
올바른 시각과 균형을 유지할 수 있었죠.
그분과 맺어진 강한 사랑의 띠를 소중히 여기면,
인간적인 일들보다 중요하게 여기고 앞자리에 둔다면,
그 방식에 대한 사랑을 기르고, 하늘의 아버지를 본받아야 합니다.
여러분이 예수의 그 본을 따를 거라고 확신합니다.
이겨 낼 수 있다는 걸 이제 여러분이 세상에 보여 줄 차례입니다.
여러분은 지금 우주에서 가장 강한 사랑의 띠를 매고 있으며,
뭐든 할 수 있게 하는 이 말이 여러분의 삶을 인도하기 때문입니다.
누매어 형제의 연설을 들으면서 시험 걱정을 하신 분은 없겠지만,
분명히 여러분도 저처럼 이 말을 적어 놓으셨겠죠?
유익한 점을 정말 많이 배울 수 있었습니다.
이 프로그램이 앞으로 163개 언어로 JW 방송에 올라가게 될 테니까,
이달 안에 게시될 이 특별 행사의 2부와 3부도 놓치지 마십시오.
마지막으로 대만에서 들어온 인사를 전해 드리고 싶습니다.
인구 밀도가 높은데, 인구는 2300만 명이 넘죠.
그 이유를 쉽게 이해할 수 있는데,
우거진 숲으로 뒤덮인 웅장한 산들이 있죠.
대부분의 사람들이 좁은 해안 평야 지역에 있는
제조업과 수출이 대만 경제의 중요한 축을 이루고 있습니다.
하지만 그 밖에도 16개의 원주민 언어가 있는 것으로 알려져 있지요.
형제들이 전파 활동을 하는 언어 중 하나는 아미어입니다.
출판물을 아미어로 번역하고 녹음 작업도 진행하고 있죠.
형제들은 화롄시에서 아미어를 사용하는 사람들을 찾아가는데,
그들은 중국어나 민난어를 쓰는 사람들과 함께 모여 삽니다.
아미어 사용자들 중엔 외딴 산간 지대에 사는 사람들도 있기 때문에
형제들은 스쿠터를 타고 먼 거리를 여행해 좋은 소식을 전합니다.
지금까지 여호와의 증인 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다.

en.text: We extend a warm welcome to all and are happy that you have joined us
for the December 2018 program of JW Broadcasting.
During this program, you’ll enjoy
exciting and upbuilding Scriptural talks
delivered to the students and other attendees
during the Gilead graduation
held on September 8, 2018.
And this is just the opener!
Parts 2 and 3 of the Gilead graduation program
will be released in the upcoming weeks.
In addition to motivating Bible talks,
you’ll get to know some of the students later this month
when you watch another edition of The Inside Story.
But now, please enjoy Part 1 of the graduation
of the 145th class of Gilead.
Well, what an exciting time this is
to be here for the graduation
of the 145th class of Gilead!
But let’s start by asking a question:
What makes a graduation program of Gilead
different from the various graduation programs
that people engage in right throughout the earth?
Well, I’m sure all of us would agree,
usually with regard to worldly institutions,
graduation programs are all about the accomplishments
and praise of individuals.
But as you dear students realize,
the Gilead program and the training that you’ve received
is all about glorifying Jehovah,
and that’s why the theme of our introductory comments are
“Always Seek Jehovah’s Glory and Not Your Own Glory.”
And that’s in harmony with what the Scriptures tell us.
If you’d like to turn with me, please, to the book of Romans
—Romans chapter 12
and notice what verses 3 and 16 remind us.
Romans 12:3:
“For through the undeserved kindness given to me,
“I tell everyone there among you
“not to think more of himself than it is necessary to think,
“but to think so as to have a sound mind,
each one as God has given to him a measure of faith.”
Notice the point there:
Whatever we have has been given to us by Jehovah.
So we shouldn’t think more of ourselves than is necessary.
And then verse 16 reminds us:
“Have the same attitude toward others as toward yourselves;
“do not set your mind on lofty things,
“but be led along with the lowly things.
Do not become wise in your own eyes.”
Now, we trust that you fully understand that admonition
because your Gilead training has been helping you
to strengthen your relationship with Jehovah,
and when we know Jehovah, we can’t help but glorify him
because we know that any good things we have come from him.
But now, as you graduate
and you go either back to your former assignments
or to new assignments,
you may find various tests to this resolve
—that you have to always glorify Jehovah and not yourself.
Now, what might be some of those tests?
Well, one is perhaps an obvious test.
You go back maybe to your former assignment,
and the brothers say, “Oh, you’ve changed;
you’re so much better.”
Well, that’s humbling in itself, isn’t it?
You didn’t realize how bad you were before you left.
“And your knowledge, the illustrations,
the way you’re teaching seems so much better”
—so now what’s your reaction?
Well, I’m sure you’re not going to say: “You’re welcome.
I noticed that too.”
I know (and I’m sure all of us know)
that you’ll be determined in a situation like that
to bring glory to Jehovah and not to yourselves.
So perhaps that’s the easy time
because that’s obvious we have to be careful.
But when is the other occasion, or situation,
where we may be tempted
to show a measure of pride and glorify ourselves?
Well, it could be if people criticize us
or perhaps don’t show us the respect that we feel that we deserve.
Or maybe we don’t get the privileges that we hope to receive.
Now, that could be a temptation for us
—to remind everyone of the special training
and the fact that we graduated from that training.
You see, this is similar
to the trap that Job fell into.
Now, when we think of Job,
we think of a very faithful man —a man of integrity.
The two words go together: Job and integrity.
But we also realize that Job needed to have very strong counsel.
Now, at what point in his life
did he do something that warranted him getting counsel?
Well, let’s think about it.
We won’t read the verses because you know them well,
but in chapter 1, remember that Job lost everything
—his children and his possessions one after the other.
But when we look at Job 1:22,
it tells us there that “Job did not sin.”
He didn’t “accuse God of doing anything wrong.”
So all these horrific things happened to him.
He had these huge tests, and he came out looking pretty good.
He hadn’t sinned at that point.
So then what happened in the second round?
Well, you remember that he had this loathsome disease,
and then his wife said to him, “Curse God and die!”
So now, is that when he deserved some counsel?
No.
In chapter 2 of Job and verse 10,
it tells us that he “did not sin with his lips.”
So at that point, he was winning we might say.
He proved himself an integrity keeper.
So when was it that he started to make a few mistakes
that resulted in getting that strong counsel?
Well, The Watchtower, back in 1980, tells us.
It said that it was when these three so-called friends
started to criticize him and said:
‘Maybe you did this. Maybe you did that.
That’s the— There’s a reason.’
Then The Watchtower said
that because of these false accusations,
it’s as if it pushed Job over the edge
and he vigorously determined to justify himself
even though that inferred that maybe Jehovah
wasn’t treating him correctly.
So do we see that this is a situation
where if we are criticized or some false accusations are made about us,
then all of a sudden, the self-justification can come in?
And what is self-justification?
Glorifying ourselves rather than glorifying Jehovah.
Of course, our Lord Jesus Christ is an excellent example in that regard.
Let’s have a look at the record
recorded in John chapter 8
Now here, we have a group of Jewish persons
criticizing Jesus, falsely accusing him of something.
Notice there in verse 48:
“In answer the Jews said to him [that is, to Jesus]:
“‘Are we not right in saying, “You are a Samaritan
“‘“[now, you remember that’s not a compliment]
and have a demon”?’”
On another occasion, they said, ‘You’re out of your mind.’
But now, what did Jesus do?
Did he fall into the trap that Job fell into and try to justify himself?
No. He just made a simple comment in verse 49:
“I do not have a demon, but I honor my Father, and you dishonor me.”
Then he says: “But I am not seeking glory for myself;
there is One who is seeking and judging.”
We see the excellent example of our Lord Jesus
in that difficult situation, where he was falsely accused
yet still focused on glorifying Jehovah.
So, what’s the lesson there for each one of us
—not only yourselves but all of us?
Well, you don’t need to remind other people
that you graduated from Gilead,
you don’t need to try to impress others
to get their respect,
and you don’t need to praise yourself.
What should be the goal of all of us?
Well, our final scripture that we want to share with you
are the words of Jesus as recorded in Matthew
—Matthew 5:16:
“Likewise, let your light shine before men,
“so that they may see your fine works
and give glory to your Father who is in the heavens.”
What a beautiful goal!
Yes, the goal is that we don’t glorify ourselves,
but we give all the glory to Jehovah God.
So with that in mind,
we’re going to look forward to our wonderful program.
We’ve got a number of brothers who put a lot of effort
in thinking about what they would like to convey to you
before you go to your assignments.
And the first of these brothers is Brother John Ekrann.
The theme that he selected is
“What Will You Do in the Year of the Drought?”
You students are really like beautiful trees
planted along the river Gilead.
Jeremiah 17:8
describes such beautiful trees.
Let’s read that together, Jeremiah 17:8.
It says: “He will become like a tree planted by the waters,
“that sends out its roots to the stream.
“He will not notice when heat comes,
“but his leaves will always flourish.
“And in the year of drought he will not be anxious,
nor will he quit producing fruit.”
Well, you’ve enjoyed the spiritual waters
taught here at Gilead.
And as you graduate today and you go off to your assignments,
your leaves are flourishing
and you’re producing fruit, figuratively speaking.
Now, did you notice, though, in verse 8
what the righteous trees had to deal with?
It says “when [the] heat comes”
and “in the year of drought.”
Now, it doesn’t say if the heat comes but when the heat comes.
So, what is that heat and year of drought?
While there are many forms of heat we deal with
(and in addition to what you considered about this verse in class),
I’d like to focus on one particular form of heat,
and that is persecution.
Restrictions on our work and bans
are designed to create fear.
Negative articles in the media about Jehovah’s Witnesses
are designed to create doubt.
Religious leaders and opposers
—they attack our neutrality,
our clear support for the Bible’s view of sex and marriage,
or discipline by disfellowshipping, and other matters.
And add to that, some of our brothers
are being rounded up and thrown into prison.
We can say that Satan has truly “turned up the heat.”
What will happen to the trees?
Will fear and doubt cause them
to shrivel up and die during the drought?
No. If you notice there in verse 8,
Jehovah says that the righteous ‘will not notice the heat’
and ‘not be anxious in the drought.’
Well, why is Jehovah confident
that the righteous trees won’t notice the heat
and won’t wither up in the drought?
Look at verse 7 of Jeremiah 17.
It says: “Blessed is the man who puts his trust in Jehovah,
whose confidence is in Jehovah.”
So, what will you do in the year of drought?
Trust in Jehovah.
Satan wants to destroy our trust in Jehovah.
Right from the very first with Eve:
“Is it really so?”
His whole system is built on fear,
uncertainty, and doubt.
Persecution—we could liken it to when you’re in an airplane;
and it has some turbulence; and it begins to shake.
One flight I was on,
there was one woman that cried in terror.
She screamed out loud every time the plane shook even just a little.
She was genuinely terrified.
I felt sorry for her.
But the experienced flyers
—they were eating, reading, watching movies;
they didn’t even notice the turbulence.
Why? Well, from experience,
they knew that the plane could easily handle
such a small amount of turbulence, and they were not worried.
It was designed for that.
Well, we are like experienced flyers.
We don’t let the turbulence,
or persecution, of this system
cause us fear or doubt.
With Jehovah and Jesus as our pilots,
we don’t need to be anxious, do we?
Let’s consider two ways that we can show trust in Jehovah
as Jeremiah 17:7 says.
First, we’re going to talk about trusting “the faithful and discreet slave”
and trusting Bible principles.
Let’s talk first about trusting the faithful and discreet slave.
The faithful and discreet slave
has been selected and appointed by Jehovah,
and experience has shown that we can trust them.
Trust is built by repeated good experiences.
Think of all the good experiences we’ve had
with the faithful and discreet slave and following their direction.
Now, some might reason:
‘Well, you know, the direction from the faithful and discreet slave
‘is good for the United States, but they don’t understand here.
‘They don’t understand my assignment where I’ve been assigned.
We need to do things differently.’
Trust in the faithful and discreet slave is not geographical.
Jehovah’s direction through the faithful and discreet slave
applies to all of God’s people all over the earth.
Fear is really a loss of memory
of what Jehovah has done for us.
Satan wants us to forget
all the good experiences we’ve had with the faithful and discreet slave
and let one moment of fear get to us
and cause us to wither in the heat.
Second Thessalonians 2:2 says
“not to be quickly shaken from your reason nor to be alarmed,”
especially at rumors.
Now, your trust in the faithful and discreet slave
is going to be put to the test.
Satan will make sure of that.
It could be your own thoughts of ‘I know better,’
or maybe some twisted lies you read or hear.
Either way, it’s a trap.
Stay away from such ideas.
Trust what you know about the faithful and discreet slave.
As Isaiah 30:15 says:
“Your strength will be
in keeping calm and showing trust.”
Remember, the faithful and discreet slave
has been selected and appointed by Jehovah,
and our experience has shown that we can trust them.
Now let’s consider trusting Bible principles, our second point.
Bible principles
are timeless pearls of wisdom from Jehovah.
But many people today attack our decision
to live by Bible principles in this modern world.
They say, “That’s outdated.”
However, we trust Bible principles
because experience tells us they always work.
I asked one sister what helps her to be calm
in very difficult, or trying, situations.
And she said, “Give me a scripture.”
Jesus’ mother, Mary,
had that same “give-me-a-scripture” attitude.
Luke 2:51 says that Mary made it her habit
to keep “these sayings in her heart.”
Mary was really like a tree, soaking in all of these waters
of Jesus’ teachings and his amazing miracles.
Well, the heat for Mary came when the Pharisees and Sadducees,
maybe even her own family,
and her neighbors began to attack Jesus,
call him names, slander his reputation,
and attack his motives.
What helped Mary to deal with the heat?
Those waters that she had treasured up in her heart.
What Bible principles and experiences
are you keeping in your heart
to help you when you come under attack?
Be like Mary and keep in your heart
your good experiences in applying Bible principles.
Stick to what you know works —Bible principles.
They always work, and they never get out of date.
Not you or anyone else
can come up with better principles to live by.
Remember, we trust Bible principles
because they come from Jehovah
and our own experience tells us they always work.
Now, trusting the faithful and discreet slave
and trusting the Bible
are just two of many ways
that we can show that we trust Jehovah.
So, what will you do in the year of drought?
Trust in Jehovah.
Think of the birds.
When they’re flying high up there, are they worried?
‘Oh, I think I’m going to fall. I’m really worried.’
Well, no. Birds don’t worry about that, do they?
Why? Well, they rely on the wings and instincts Jehovah gave them.
They can fly.
Likewise, we don’t need to be anxious when faced with lies,
bans, or attacks on our Bible principles.
Jehovah has given us what we need to fly, so to speak
—the faithful and discreet slave, Bible principles,
prayer, holy spirit, and more.
As we head further into this system
and as the heat from this system intensifies, remember,
fear and doubt are reactions,
but our decision is trust and courage.
Well, thank you very much, Brother Ekrann.
We really appreciated that.
I neglected to mention that Brother Ekrann
is a helper to the Coordinators’ Committee.
As chairman, you’d probably appreciate that it’s hard for me to take notes.
There are a few other things that I’m worried about.
But I did jot down a few things here:
“Drought won’t make us doubt.
Trust is a must.”
So hopefully, I’ve got something I’ll remember from Brother Ekrann’s talk.
Well, now Brother William Turner, who is a helper to the Service Committee,
is giving us a challenging question.
The theme is “Have You Become a Different Person?”
Well, I think it’s safe to say
that with all of the training and instruction you’ve received,
you definitely are not the same individuals you were
when you first arrived at Patterson.
But how exactly have you changed,
and why is it important that you continue to do so?
Well, let’s consider this by looking at someone who,
just like you, received a special privilege.
His privilege was being the first divinely selected king of Israel.
So the man was Saul.
When Saul was anointed,
the prophet Samuel gave him three prophetic signs
in order to confirm that Jehovah was with him.
I invite you to turn with me in your Bibles,
please, to 1 Samuel chapter 10.
And as we read verse 6, note what was to happen after the last sign.
Chapter 10, verse 6, says:
“The spirit of Jehovah will empower you,
“and you will prophesy along with them
and be changed into a different person.”
Now, what did this change mean?
Would Saul all of a sudden become unrecognizable?
Or would there be a drastic change in his personality?
Well, let’s go back one chapter to chapter 9.
In verse 21, here we get a glimpse of Saul’s personality
before he was appointed as king.
Verse 21 says: “At this Saul answered:
“‘Am I not a Benjaminite of the smallest of the tribes of Israel,
“‘and my family the most insignificant
“‘of all the families of the tribe of Benjamin?
So why have you spoken to me in this way?’”
So Saul shows himself to be a very humble,
modest individual.
Well, how about after his appointment as king?
Let’s go back to chapter 10.
If you look in verse 22,
here we see Saul’s introduction as king to the people.
Verse 22 says: “So they inquired of Jehovah:
“‘Has the man come here yet?’
“Jehovah answered: ‘There he is
hiding himself among the luggage.’”
—so evidently still modest, still humble.
Interestingly, the Insight book mentions
that about a month after his appointment as king,
Saul gained a couple of great military victorie
against the Ammonites and later against the Philistines.
So now, you think about that.
How did Saul change, and rather quickly,
from bashfully hiding among luggage
to leading a nation to victory?
That is evidence
of the power of God’s spirit
and the impact that it can have
when one allows it to be operative in their lives.
So, what’s the lesson?
All of you have manifested qualities
that are very pleasing and useful to Jehovah.
It has allowed you to be productive in your assignment.
It’s allowed you to now have this privilege of Gilead training.
But as you now go to your assignments,
you’re going to continue to need
to have that spirit operative in your life.
And just as we’ve seen in the case of Saul,
that will not always mean a drastic change in your personality.
Perhaps when we think of that expression
of someone becoming a different person,
maybe that’s where our mind goes
—to someone who has come out of Satan’s world,
now into Jehovah’s organization, and they put on the new personality.
And that’s correct.
But the reality is that all Christians,
even those spiritually mature,
need to be adjusted from time to time,
and those adjustments can have a tremendous impact.
Perhaps your personality is such
that you are naturally shy and reserved.
Maybe you would be quite comfortable, no problem, staying with the luggage.
But now having God’s spirit
coupled with appreciation for what you’ve learned
will now perhaps move you to come out of your comfort zone
—to initiate ways to share things that you’ve learned with others.
Or maybe before you came to Gilead, you had very good leadership skills.
You had a take-charge personality —one who got things done.
But now you may see the need to adjust.
You recognize there is wisdom
in perhaps slowing down, or even waiting,
perhaps even seeking input from others.
With the help of God’s spirit,
it can help you to become a kinder overseer,
a better shepherd, one who is more tolerant,
empathetic of others.
It’s just tremendous benefits all the way around.
But the extent that you become different
depends upon you and your response to God’s spirit.
Now, obviously, we know Saul’s story; it does not end well.
Instead of maintaining his reliance on Jehovah,
he begins to trust his own judgment.
He focuses more on his position as king
than he does on his relationship with God.
And it’s quite interesting, if you are still in chapter 10,
if you look in verse 27, where Saul had God’s spirit
even when he encountered challenges
—in this particular case, some questioning his appointment—
you’ll notice that Saul didn’t feel the need
to prove himself or challenge the men.
He just stayed silent and focused on his assignment.
But you read a little later that when he lost God’s spirit
and when that bad spirit began to take over him,
well, now the negative comments —the comments of others:
“Saul has struck down his thousands and David his tens of thousands”
—oh, well, now it’s an issue.
It’s a problem.
It affected his judgment;
it affected his emotions
and caused him to make bad decisions.
So, what can help you to avoid that
and to keep your focus?
Well, let’s look at the example
of the other Saul that’s mentioned in the Bible
—the man who later became the apostle Paul.
Now, we know, obviously, Paul’s personality needed more than a refinement.
Paul needed a complete overhaul.
But he truly became a different person by way of God’s spirit.
And he was given a privilege to serve as “an apostle to the nations.”
But if you turn to 1 Corinthians chapter 15,
let’s just note the attitude that Paul showed.
At 1 Corinthians 15:9,
he says: “For I am the least of the apostles,
“and I’m not worthy of being called an apostle,
“because I persecuted the congregation of God.
“But by God’s undeserved kindness
I am what I am.”
Beautiful perspective, isn’t it?
Now, why do you think Paul was able
to maintain this humble attitude for the rest of his life,
whereas King Saul could not?
Well, both men knew
that it was only by means of Jehovah’s undeserved kindness
that they could enjoy their privilege of service.
But Paul never viewed his privilege of service
greater than his relationship with God.
That’s why he studied, he meditated,
he discerned God’s will for him,
and then he was alert to follow the leadings of God’s spirit.
And in his assignment, Paul had challenges.
You remember, early on for parts of three years,
some of the brothers didn’t even believe he was an apostle.
But yet he never asserted his authority.
He never distanced himself from his brothers;
he just loved them.
He let his example speak for him, and you can do the same.
See, let the brothers feel.
Let them see the love that you have for Jehovah
and the love that you have for them.
So in review, maintain those wonderful traits
that qualified you for Gilead, like your modesty and humility.
And then study, meditate,
continue to follow the leadings of God’s spirit.
And when it becomes apparent that changes need to be made
either for the sake of the work or peace with your brother,
well, please be willing to make them.
And if you do, you will show
that you have become a different person
—one who is refined, one who is useful,
one who is dearly loved by Jehovah.
And may Jehovah continue to bless you
and all of the hard work that you do
in behalf of his name.
Thank you very much, Brother Turner.
We really appreciated that.
So my quick notes:
“Don’t change the change.
Continue to make the right change.”
Good. Well, now we have the privilege of listening
to a member of the Governing Body, Brother Kenneth Cook.
And Brother Cook is going to talk to us on the theme
“Find Joy in Jehovah’s Gradual Blessing!”
As you know from your own life experience
and from your Gilead instruction,
Jehovah is a God of action.
And as such, he does some things quickly, doesn’t he?
And that’s true when it’s needed, or it’s warranted.
He makes sure it happens just at the right time.
For example,
when a sudden stiff breeze
rushed into the upper room at Pentecost,
those present were filled with holy spirit.
In another example,
the Bible tells us that when this world in some way says
that it has achieved “peace and security,”
what happens next?
First Thessalonians 5:3 says
that ‘sudden destruction will come instantly on them.’
But not all things that Jehovah
causes to happen occur so quickly.
In fact, he often does things gradually.
Let’s look at two examples
and see what we can learn from them.
First, we will look at the angels and creation,
and then resurrected ones and perfection.
Finally, we will look at how this applies to you
and how you can find great joy
in a gradual blessing.
We begin with the angels who were on hand
when Jehovah made the earth and all the things in it.
What did the angels see?
Did they see an instant burst
of unimaginable power
that suddenly formed the earth and all life on it?
Not at all.
Jehovah could have done that,
but instead he created things gradually.
speak of him as setting the earth’s “measurements,”
sinking “its pedestals,”
and laying “its cornerstone.”
And in Genesis chapters 1 and 2,
we also read about how he gradually brought forth
life on earth and ultimately humans.
Imagine the joy that his angelic sons experienced
as they watched what Jehovah was gradually doing.
For example, undoubtedly, the angels could see
that their heavenly Father received great satisfaction
from a job well done.
They would also learn about facets
of Jehovah’s marvelous personality
as they observed everything from the first whale
breaching the surface of an ocean
to a hummingbird hovering over a beautiful flower
or seeing lion cubs playing together.
So stupendous was Jehovah’s work
and so enriching this experience for his angelic sons,
that Job 38:7 tells us
that at some point,
on seeing all of this and seeing the earth formed,
they “began shouting in applause.”
That gradual blessing
is something that the faithful angels
will never forget.
In fact, God’s Word tells us that the angels
are still focused on what Jehovah is doing on the earth,
especially with regard to his people.
First Peter 1:12 says
that “into these very things,
angels are desiring to peer.”
So then, do the angels find pleasure
in Jehovah’s gradual work and blessing?
Yes, they do.
And aren’t we grateful
that they love Jehovah so much
as well as each one of us?
What do we learn from their response to Jehovah’s gradual work?
We learn to treasure every moment
in Jehovah’s service and to be grateful
for every opportunity we have
to learn more about him.
So be like the angels and, in effect,
shout in applause
at each new thing you learn about our heavenly Father.
Take time to meditate on his works,
on his Word of truth,
and on his indescribable mercy
toward us through his Son.
In our next example,
we look to the future but not too far into the future.
We’re talking about the resurrection
—specifically the resurrection
and perfection.
When Jehovah through his Son resurrects countless millions
to life again in the new world,
they will not all come back at the same time,
nor will they come back in perfection.
But Jehovah will bring them back in such a way
that they will know themselves;
they will recognize themselves.
Although their serious infirmities will be gone,
they will instantly know
their own familiar thoughts and feelings.
They will know who they are as a person.
Imagine the joy that such ones will have
as they apply what they learn
and then see the progress
that they are making day after day in serving Jehovah.
They will experience the words of Proverbs 10:22 coming true for them.
Please follow along, where it says in verse 22:
“It is the blessing of Jehovah that makes one rich,
and he adds no pain with it.”
So, what will God’s gradual blessing do
for such ones at that time?
His blessing will make them rich
in the most important way of all —and that is spiritually.
Things that they struggle to be able to overcome
in this old world under man’s control
and Satan’s influence,
they will be able to overcome
because they love Jehovah
and he will help them to do so.
But even more than this, in the new world,
millions and millions of people
will come to experience physical vitality
and strength that exceeds
anything imaginable today.
Jehovah’s gradual blessing will take hold,
and grateful ones will rejoice day after day.
Also important is the fact
that as each person grows
toward perfection,
they will keep hold of the empathy needed
to teach and help still others
who will come back in a gradual resurrection.
How can contemplating such future blessings benefit us?
benefit you right now?
We benefit when we patiently focus on Jehovah
and how he often fulfills his promises
in a gradual way.
Having this in mind keeps us grounded, you could say.
We do our best, but we do not expect
everything right now, do we,
especially perfection?
That is yet in the future.
However, when we develop strong faith,
we will find joy no matter what we will yet face.
Why?
Because we are absolutely certain
that Jehovah’s promises will come true, right on time.
Now we get to the part that especially involves you.
As one graduating from Gilead School,
you may look back on the past five months
and worry that you did not do everything perfectly.
I know that’s how I would feel,
but please don’t focus on that.
Instead, imagine the joy that you will find
as you patiently apply the things that you have learned
and then you see Jehovah’s gradual blessing on your efforts.
Remember, a head full of knowledge
is not what brings Jehovah’s blessing.
What matters is what we do with what we know.
Consider the example of King Solomon.
First Kings 4:32 says
that ‘he composed 3,000 proverbs
and 1,005 songs.’
But there was a disconnect
between what was in his mind
and what was really driving him from the heart.
And as a result,
Solomon drifted away from Jehovah, didn’t he?
The Bible tells us that his foreign wives
gradually inclined his heart
away from Jehovah.
So you could say that he, in effect, substituted one gradual thing
for another gradual thing.
In turn, he lost the opportunity
to find joy in Jehovah’s gradual blessing.
Now, in contrast to that example,
make it your heart’s desire to be like the faithful angels.
Although they undoubtedly know
far more than 3,000 proverbs and songs,
they savor every morsel that they learn
about our magnificent heavenly Father.
And again, as you look to the future
—to the real life—
take what you have learned in this beautiful schooling
and humbly work for the interests of others.
Jehovah will bless that effort, and the gradual blessing
that you will enjoy will serve as a taste
of what is yet ahead in God’s new world.
Keep in mind that those who find joy now
in a gradual blessing
will have no problem in patiently waiting for
and then enjoying the gradual blessings that are still to come.
Thank you very much, Brother Cook.
We truly appreciated those fine comments.
I just had a brief note here:
“Expect the unexpected gradually.”
Well, I’m sure we all got that point,
and we’ll enjoy looking forward to seeing that program, or that talk,
again and going through the main points.
Now, for you students,
you’re about to be addressed by one of your instructors from Gilead.
You’ve heard from Brother Cauthon a number of times,
and now he’s going to address you this final time
on this intriguing theme
“Shoulder to Shoulder.”
By the spring of 1945,
Allied and Russian armies were converging upon Germany.
The Nazis were losing the war.
The Germans gave the ominous order:
March all the concentration camp prisoners west,
and destroy all the evidence of the horrors
that had taken place in those camps.
On the 20th of April, the evacuation of Sachsenhausen began.
The plan was to march the prisoners to the Baltic Coast,
ship them out to sea, and drown them.
And if that wasn’t horrific enough,
the SS guards had explicit orders
to shoot any of the prisoners who couldn’t keep up.
Already in a weakened state,
hundreds were shot along the way,
while many thousands more died of exposure, starvation, and exhaustion.
Thus began what came to be known as a death march.
Interestingly, the Sachsenhausen evacuation
included 230 of our brothers.
And just like the other prisoners,
they were in no shape
to make this journey physically,
but they were more than up to the journey spiritually.
How so?
Well, open your Bibles, if you would, to a promise Jehovah made.
It’s found at Zephaniah 3:9.
And here, he promised to give to his people
a pure language.
And the point being so that they could do what?
The latter part of that verse says
“to serve him shoulder to shoulder”
or, as the footnote says, “in unity.”
And that was the key.
The secret weapon
was their shoulder-to-shoulder unity.
Even the weak become strong when they are united.
Now, today, you and I are on a march for life.
And never forget that we’re not marching alone.
We have our brothers and sisters from all backgrounds and all ages
along with us for the journey.
But the question is,
Are we marching shoulder to shoulder?
What can we learn from our brothers who went through this death march?
Well, first of all,
to reach the coast, the Sachsenhausen prisoners
were to march 155 miles
—that’s 250 kilometers.
And throughout that journey, the Witnesses pooled all their food supplies
into one small bundle that was used for the benefit of all.
Now, you can imagine that sharing food is not an easy thing to do
when you’ve already been starved and you’re very weak.
But our brothers knew Bible principles,
such as the one at Proverbs 11:25 that says:
“The generous person will prosper,
and whoever refreshes others will himself be refreshed.”
So, what’s the lesson for us today?
The lesson is this:
Unity to be real must withstand the severest test.
Being a true Christian is more than a commitment to God;
it is a commitment to other Christians as well.
So don’t hold back.
Show a generous disposition in your assignment.
And remember, one of the most important resources
that you can share with others is your time.
So learn the balance.
Take time with others who may need it,
and don’t be ruled by time.
Rather than rush, refresh.
Second point:
When the SS guards gave the Witnesses a cart to haul,
that easily could have seemed like just another burden to bear,
but instead our brothers were thrilled.
Why?
Because they saw it as an opportunity.
How so?
Well, during the journey, the sick and elderly ones
were able to sit on top of the cart and rest for a while,
and then when one would get his strength back,
another one would replace him.
And so in a very real way, they carried one another.
The lesson for us?
Where there is unity, there is victory.
And in the middle of difficulty, lies opportunity.
So look for opportunities to encourage one another.
The word “encourage” literally means “to make strong or to hearten.”
Being spiritual people, we may not lose our hope
but we could lose heart,
especially during times of extreme crisis or grief.
But something as simple as a reassuring word
or even a kind deed can work like a miracle.
It can restore the weary soul.
It can carry others through a hard time.
So the point is this:
You’re not responsible for everyone in the Christian congregation,
but you are responsible to them.
Jehovah expects us to do whatever we can to help our brothers.
We simply cannot allow ourselves
to be separated in interest
or divided in purpose.
And then one more point:
On their last night, the prisoners were stopped near a forest.
The SS guards encouraged everyone to walk across to freedom.
Imagine you were there.
It must have seemed very tempting.
But naturally, they were unsure of what to do,
so they prayed for guidance
and unitedly they decided to stay put
—not one of them left the group.
Later, it was learned that those who had accepted the offer
were shot down.
The lesson for us?
Don’t allow anything or anyone to cause division.
Satan is the master of divide and conquer.
We must stand together until forever.
When problems arise,
you can use your energy
for retaliation or resolution, but not both.
The Bible says: “Have intense love for one another.”
So don’t allow differences to develop into distance,
and don’t nurture past offenses.
The brotherhood is a place where mistakes are not rubbed in
but rubbed out.
To recap:
We serve God in part, brothers,
by serving others.
Willingly share your resources with one another,
especially your time.
It’s in times of deep crisis and grief and doubt
that we need each other the most.
When you see a brother’s or a sister’s shoulders
beginning to droop,
pull out your “cart” for them.
Do what is needed even if it’s difficult or inconvenient.
Remember, our actions reveal what’s in our heart,
whether we like it or not.
Have intense love for one another;
remain united in heart and mind;
continue committed to one another
as you are to Jehovah God and Jesus Christ.
And finally,
there is beauty and power in unity.
Jehovah is creating a new world, brothers and sisters, a new world.
One world, one people
—a new world society of unified worshippers.
Stay focused on that fact.
In conclusion,
over 10,700 lost their lives
on that infamous death march from Sachsenhausen,
but not one,
not one of our 230 brothers lost their life.
Why?
Well, let’s let them tell us in their own words.
Here’s a quotation from a resolution
made by our brothers in that forest
just before their freedom.
I quote:
‘A long, hard time of trial is behind us
‘and we have been brought forth from the fiery furnace
‘without a scent of the fire upon us.
‘On the contrary,
‘we are full of power and strength in Jehovah.
‘We have only one desire
‘after our stay in the “lions’ den.”
‘We will serve Jehovah throughout eternity.
This would be our most precious reward.’
It’s signed:
“YOUR CO-FIGHTERS FOR JEHOVAH’S HOLY NAME.”
You see, they didn’t pretend to be brothers;
they were brothers.
They functioned as one united family throughout the whole ordeal,
and they were victorious.
And so, as this world grows colder and colder, brothers,
let us be more determined than ever
to serve our God shoulder to shoulder.
Well, thank you so much, Brother Cauthon.
There were so many excellent points in that talk.
What did I write down to remind me?
“Shoulder to shoulder.”
I did also write down, though:
“Imperfections—don’t rub in, rub out.”
Well, there are a lot of good points
that you dear students, soon-to-be graduates,
are taking down, I’m sure.
Now you’re going to listen
to another brother who’s very familiar to you
—one of your instructors.
But the difference is that this time
you’re not going to be looking at him and thinking of written exercises.
But you’re going to be thinking,
‘Well, I can sit back and enjoy these comments.’
Brother Mark Noumair, a helper to the Teaching Committee
as well as an instructor of Gilead,
will now talk to you on the theme
“Four Words to Live By.”
Can there really be four words that you can base your life on?
And if so, what would they be?
Well, we look to our Exemplar, Christ Jesus, for the answer.
We focus on the night before his death.
The future of every human being rested upon his shoulders.
His words, his actions, his very thoughts in these critical moments
would be remembered for thousands of years.
What would he give the world to remember?
He left no room for guesswork.
In one verse, one verse,
Jesus reveals what governed his every action and his decision
—in one verse.
Four words —four words that he lived by—
and we encourage you to live by these four words.
We encourage you to take these four words to heart.
Take them seriously.
They’re found at John 14:31,
John 14:31,
the last night of Jesus life:
“But for the world to know that I love the Father.”
“I love the Father.”
In these four words,
we find the most powerful bond in the universe
—an unbreakable bond of love between Jesus and his Father.
And it is this unbreakable attachment
that enabled Jesus to unselfishly defend
his Father’s reputation to his dying breath,
trusting that Jehovah would protect and resurrect him.
“I love the Father.”
But how did this love develop?
How did this unbreakable bond, this attachment of love, develop?
Well, the only-begotten Son was created perfect.
True.
However, was he created with love already fully developed?
No.
He was created with free will;
Satan was created with free will
and with the capacity to extend, enlarge, and enrich this love.
The Son of God
was not created with an unselfish, self-sacrificing love
already fully in place.
What did he have to do?
He had to cultivate this deep attachment for his Father,
cultivate this deep love.
How did he do that?
By observing his Father’s personality.
In his prehuman existence, imagine how the Son would do this.
He would observe closely how his Father used his power,
how he used his authority, how he used his strength
in behalf of people
—‘those crushed, those lowly in spirit.’
He would observe how his Father used his power
to help those “crushed in spirit.”
He watched his Father deal with Ruth the Moabite girl
—a Moabite girl from a pagan nation.
Might he have thought: ‘Now, a Moabite girl?
‘Weren’t these the Moabite women—?
‘Weren’t these the very women that lured the Israelite men into immorality
right on the threshold of the Promised Land?’
True.
But his Father saw that this girl was different.
She was different.
What a lesson for the Son of God!
His Father did not put people in categories;
he did not stereotype individuals.
‘Oh, that’s the Moabite girl. I’m not going to deal with her.’
No.
Jehovah God looked at Ruth as an individual.
And the Son’s love must have grown as now He allows this girl—
He allows a Bible book to be named in behalf of her
—Ruth as opposed to Naomi or Boaz—
Ruth, a Moabite girl.
That’s right.
And the Son’s love would’ve continued to grow
when he observed how his Father then allowed this girl
to become an ancestress to the Messiah.
But watching and admiring his Father wasn’t enough.
He went further.
As the Son continued to develop appreciation
for his Father’s qualities,
this bond of love became more than just a feeling.
No.
His love for his Father began to shape his decisions and actions,
and Jesus demonstrated this when he was on earth.
He didn’t just say the words, “I love the Father.”
He didn’t just feel the words
—feel “I love the Father’s cozy, warm, little feeling.”
No, no, no.
He lived those words,
and that is why Jesus could say in the second half of John 14:31:
“I am doing just as the Father has commanded me to do.”
“I am doing”
—you see, his entire life course
proved that he loved the Father.
For example,
when a Syrophoenician woman
begged Jesus to cure her demonized daughter,
initially Jesus said:
‘No, I was sent forth not to the Gentiles
but to the Jews.’
But the woman would not give up,
and showing her faith, she kept asking and asking.
So in light of this exceptional circumstance,
Jesus could see that this was no time
to enforce a general rule or to stereotype people
or to become inflexible or to put her in a category.
‘Oh, no. You’re a Gentile. You’re Syrophoenician. No, no.’
No, Jesus saw this was a time to bend
in response to higher principles.
Did he remember
how his Father handled that situation with Ruth?
And this moved him to say: ‘My Father did that with Ruth.
‘Now we have a similar situation.
What would my Father want me to do?’
Jesus helped the Syrophoenician woman.
He was ready to act in imitation of his Father’s love.
Another example would be what Jesus learned
from his Father about forgiveness.
He watched his Father forgive —forgive people.
He watched his Father forgive David for adultery,
forgive David for the murder of Uriah.
How many others did the Son of God watch?
How many others did he watch his Father forgive?
The Hebrew Scriptures are replete with Jehovah forgiving people.
He’s a largehearted Forgiver.
He’s ready to forgive.
He’s on the lookout to forgive.
That’s what the Son of God learned.
So this no doubt helped him to deal with the frequency
of the imperfections of the apostles and others.
Jesus viewed forgiving others
as an opportunity to imitate his Father
—another opportunity to allow his actions
to declare loud and clear
“like Father, like Son.”
He didn’t just say, “I love the Father.”
He didn’t just feel it; he lived it.
Now we take this discussion out of the classroom
and apply it to your real-life situations.
Right after Jesus said,
“I love the Father,”
he said, “Get up, let us go from here.”
Well, soon you’re going to get up
and you’re going to go from here,
and you don’t know what tests of faith are going to come upon you.
You don’t know.
We can’t anticipate every test that’s going to come upon us of faith.
However,
if you know these four words,
you know enough.
Etch these four words “I love the Father”
on your minds and on your hearts.
Let these four words govern every decision and action of yours.
For example,
if you’re entrusted with authority,
how will you treat people?
How will you treat those under you?
Learn from Jesus on this last night.
His words could’ve been all about himself.
‘For the world to know
‘that I am the Son of God,
‘“the firstborn of all creation.”
I’m the second greatest personage in the universe.’
Or he could’ve said,
‘I plan to surrender my life for you
as the ransom sacrifice for you.’
Or, ‘I am the one —I’m the one who fulfills all prophecy.’
But none of his thoughts were about himself,
his authority, or his accomplishments.
So like Jesus, don’t focus on your position.
Show by your dealings with others
that your heartfelt desire and motives
are to please your heavenly Father.
That’s what you want to do.
So as you go from here,
who will be your “Ruth”?
Show that you don’t put people in categories.
Show it.
Instead of that department,
that nationality, that language group,
or those sisters,
who will be your “Syrophoenician woman”?
Seize opportunities to be more flexible and reasonable.
Discern when it will be a time to bend
in response to higher principles
rather than always being on the lookout to check and correct.
Work hard to acquire thinking ability
—thinking ability that will assist you
to respond to higher principles.
Developing thinking ability is not easy
because as you begin to think about a person,
often your emotional reactions
toward that person start interfering.
You begin registering likes, dislikes,
respect, disrespect,
trust, distrust
—reacting emotionally before beginning an intellectual appraisal.
But if you make decisions solely based on feelings
that have slipped in under the guise of thoughts,
this often leads to poor decisions.
So listen to what I’m going to tell you right now.
Ask yourself,
‘Will my decision-making process
‘—will it be in response to higher principles
or simply because I do or don’t like the person?’
When it’s a response to higher principles,
now you’re strengthening and stabilizing the organization.
Who will be your imperfect, disappointing “apostles”?
Be on the lookout for opportunities to be more forgiving,
more patient with the shortcomings of others.
Maybe you’re an overseer
and your imperfect, disappointing “apostles”
will be those working under you.
For others, it might be a fellow translator
or a workmate in your department that disappoints you.
If this happens,
will these four words govern your thinking?
They did for one sister.
This is what she says:
“Something that happened in my department hurt me deeply,
“and it shook me to my very core.
“And since then, I struggle with constant feelings of inadequacy.
“I felt completely discouraged and dried up.
“However, I’m not a quitter.
“I will cling to Jehovah and not let go.
“I love Jehovah above everything,
“and I’m sure that I will overcome my negative feelings
and will become stronger spiritually and mentally.”
She didn’t just say the words
“I love the Father”;
she lived those words
—four words that gave her a proper perspective
and balance in life.
So it comes down to this:
When you cherish Jehovah’s approval
and your unbreakable bond of love for him
and this spiritual relationship overrides,
or supersedes, our human sphere of activity,
not much else matters.
How do you reach that point?
By thinking deeply on Jehovah’s way of doing things,
then loving those ways,
and then imitating your heavenly Father.
At John 13:15, Jesus said:
“I set the pattern for you.”
And it’s a pattern that we are confident that you will follow.
Like Jesus, show the world.
It’s your opportunity now to show the world
that you too can meet any challenge
and test of faith that comes your way.
We know you can do it; we have confidence in you.
Why do we know you can do it?
Because you are clothed
with the most unbreakable bond in the universe
and empowered by the unfailing four words to live by,
“I love the Father.”
Well, even though you were able to listen to Brother Noumair
and not have a written exercise afterward,
I’m sure, like me, you wrote down those four words:
“I love the Father.”
Thank you very much, Brother Noumair.
We really appreciated that.
And truly, there’s been an abundance of good points
that we’ve learned from the program so far.
And then, all of a sudden, I realized
that this program is going to be broadcast
on JW Broadcasting in 163 languages,
so I don’t have to take notes after all.
What an exciting and upbuilding program!
And don’t forget to tune in later this month
for Parts 2 and 3 of this special event.
To conclude, we’d like to share greetings from Taiwan.
Taiwan is a Southeast Asian island
over 35,000 square kilometers,
or nearly 13,000 square miles, in size.
It’s densely populated with over 23 million inhabitants.
The first Westerner who saw this island
named it Ilha Formosa, or “Island Beautiful.”
And it’s not hard to see why.
Taiwan has a beautiful coastline, fertile land,
and majestic mountains covered in thick, luxuriant forests.
The majority of the population live on the narrow coastal plains,
where you’ll find large bustling cities.
Manufacturing and exporting various goods drives the economy in Taiwan.
The official language of Taiwan is Mandarin Chinese.
However, there are also 16 recognized indigenous language groups.
One of the languages that our brothers reach out to is Amis.
In January 2018,
the Amis remote translation office was opened in Hualien City.
They translate written publications
and produce audio publications in Amis.
In the Hualien Amis Congregation, there are 80 publishers.
Five serve as elders and 22 are regular pioneers.
They conduct over 70 Bible studies each month.
These brothers search out Amis-speaking people in Hualien City,
where they live alongside Chinese- and Min Nan-speaking people.
In the mountains, Amis-speaking people are more isolated,
so our brothers travel long distances,
using scooters, to share the good news with them.
The brothers and sisters in the Hualien Amis Congregation
send you their warm love.
From the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting.

你会听到一系列令人振奋的演讲

现在

第145届基列学校毕业典礼

能够出席这一届基列学校的毕业典礼
想必大家都心潮澎湃！
首先
我想问大家一个问题
在这个世界上有各种各样的毕业典礼

我想大家都同意
