title: 모든 일에서 정직하게 처신하십시오 (베델/건축 봉사 지원)

ko.text: 여러분이 여호와를 위해 더 많은 일을 하려는 열망이 있고
여호와의 증인 특별 전 시간 종들의 전 세계 성직자회의 회원 지원서를
제출하려고 하는 것을 따뜻이 칭찬해 드리고 싶습니다.
이 특별한 봉사에 참여하고자 하는 여러분은
다양한 방법으로 섬길 기회가 생길 것입니다.
물론 우리 모두는 다양한 방법으로 여호와를 섬길 수 있습니다.
회중에서 전도인으로 봉사하든 정규 파이오니아로 섬기든,
혹은 베델이나 신권 건축 현장에서 봉사하든,
우리가 여호와에 대한 깊은 사랑에서 우러나와 여호와를 섬길 때
여러분이 거룩한 자들을 섬겼고 지금도 섬기면서 행한 일과
그분의 이름을 위해 나타낸 사랑을 잊지 않으십니다.”
봉사를 확장하기 위한 지원서를 제출하기 전에,
기도하면서 검토해 보는 것은 정말 중요합니다.
따라서 지원서에 나오는 질문들에 정직하게 답해야 합니다.
특히 건강 상태와 영적 상태에 대한 질문들의 경우는 더더욱 그러하죠.
베델이나 신권 건축 현장에서 일하는 사람은
주기적으로 의사의 도움이나 약물 치료를 받아야 하는 분들이
그런 건강 문제로 활동에 심한 제약이 따르는 분이라면
회중과 연합하여 계속 야외에서 충실하게 봉사하는 편이
가능하다면 정규 파이오니아 봉사를 할 수도 있겠죠.
자신의 건강 상태 때문에 지원서를 써도 될지 확신이 서지 않는다면
회중 장로들에게 도움을 요청할 수 있습니다.
장로들은 지원서의 건강 상태와 관련된 질문들을
여러분이 지원서를 제출할지 여부를 결정할 수 있도록 도와줄 것입니다.
여호와의 축복이 있어야만 성공을 거둘 수 있습니다.
“여호와께서 집을 세우지 않으시면 건축자들이 열심히 일해도 헛되며,
여호와께서 도시를 지키지 않으시면 경비병이 깨어 있어도 헛되다.”
그런데 여호수아 7장을 보면 알 수 있듯이,
여호와께서 축복을 거두시는 상황이 생길 수도 있습니다.
아간이 여호와께 바쳐야 할 것을 도둑질했을 때
그분의 축복을 잃는 일이 결코 없어야 합니다.
높은 수준의 영적 자격에 달해야 합니다.
베델 봉사나 그 밖의 신권적인 임무를 수행하려는 모든 사람은
여호와께서 보시기에 깨끗한 양심을 가지고 있어야 하며,
불결한 습관이나 부도덕한 행동을 모두 중단한 상태여야 합니다.
지난 1년 사이에 음란물을 본 적이 있는 사람은 지원해서는 안 됩니다.
또한 이성이나 동성과 불결한 행실에 빠진 적이 있는 사람이라면
여호와의 친절한 권고를 따를 필요가 있습니다.
믿음의 기도는 병든 사람을 낫게 할 것이며,
또한 그가 죄를 지었다 해도 용서를 받을 것입니다.”
자신이 저지른 일 때문에 양심의 가책을 느낀다면
여호와와의 관계를 강화하기 위해 도움을 요청해야 합니다.
그렇게 해서 깨끗한 양심을 가진 뒤에 지원서를 제출한다면
따라서 주저하지 말고 회중의 장로에게 도움을 요청하시기 바랍니다.
특별한 봉사를 수행할 수 있기를 바랍니다.
여러분이 여호와께 드리는 봉사에서 성공하기를 바라기 때문입니다.
또 여러분의 지원이 절실히 필요하다는 점도
따라서 영적으로 신체적으로 건강한 상태에 있고
여호와의 증인 특별 전 시간 종들의 전 세계 성직자회의 회원 지원서를 달라고
여호와를 계속 최선을 다해 섬기려는 여러분을 위해
우리가 기도하고 있다는 것을 기억하시기 바랍니다.

en.text: On behalf of the Governing Body,
we warmly commend you for your desire
to expand your service to Jehovah
and your interest in submitting an application
to serve as a temporary volunteer
or as a member of the Worldwide Order
of Special Full-Time Servants
of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
By making yourself available to serve in this unique way,
you imitate the faithful prophet Isaiah,
who said at Isaiah 6:8:
“Here I am! Send me!”
Submitting your application may open a door of opportunity
to serve Jehovah and his organization
in a variety of ways.
Of course, there’s a place for everyone in Jehovah’s service.
Whether we’re working hard as a congregation publisher,
a regular pioneer, a Bethelite,
or on a theocratic construction project,
we have the satisfaction of knowing
that Jehovah treasures what we’re doing
because of our heartfelt love for him.
Hebrews 6:10 says:
“God is not unrighteous so as to forget your work
“and the love you showed for his name by ministering
and continuing to minister to the holy ones.”
Before submitting an application for expanded theocratic service,
it’s important to consider prayerfully
how you’ll respond to the questions on the application.
Hebrews 13:18 says:
“We wish to conduct ourselves
honestly in all things.”
So you should be honest
in answering the questions on the application,
especially those that have to do
with your physical health and spiritual health.
The work being done at Bethel
and on theocratic construction projects
requires good physical, emotional, and mental health.
However, you may have a chronic health problem
that requires the regular attention
of a physician or must be treated with medication.
If you have a significant limitation in this way,
it would be better for you to continue your faithful service
in the field with your local congregation
and, if possible, in the regular pioneer service.
If you’re not sure whether your health situation
would prevent you from submitting an application,
the elders in your congregation can help you.
They can review with you the specific application questions
that deal with health matters
so that you personally may determine
whether or not you should apply.
Regardless of where we’re serving,
we need Jehovah’s blessing to be successful.
Psalm 127:1 says:
“Unless Jehovah builds the house,
“it is in vain that its builders work hard on it.
“Unless Jehovah guards the city,
it is in vain that the guard stays awake.”
But as the account in Joshua chapter 7 vividly testifies,
it’s possible for Jehovah to withhold his blessing.
Do you remember what happened
when Achan stole from the things
that were supposed to be dedicated to Jehovah?
Israel lost God’s backing.
Our service to Jehovah is important.
We cannot afford to lose Jehovah’s blessing.
For this reason, the spiritual qualifications
for expanded service are high.
It’s expected that all of those offering themselves to serve at Bethel
or in other theocratic assignments
have a clean conscience before Jehovah,
having left behind all unclean practices
or immoral conduct.
For instance, those who have viewed pornography
in the past year should not apply.
Also, if you realize
that you may have become involved in unclean conduct
with someone of the opposite sex or the same sex,
Jehovah very considerately explains what we should do
in James 5:14, 15:
“Is there anyone [spiritually] sick among you?
“Let him call the elders of the congregation to him,
“and let them pray over him,
“applying oil to him in the name of Jehovah.
“And the prayer of faith will make the sick one well,
“and Jehovah will raise him up.
Also, if he has committed sins, he will be forgiven.”
How reassuring!
If you have a heavy conscience because of something you’ve done,
you should get help to strengthen your relationship with Jehovah.
You can later submit an application with a clean conscience,
confident that Jehovah will bless your efforts.
So don’t hesitate to speak
with one of the elders in your congregation if you need help.
They love you and want you to progress and qualify
for special privileges of service in Jehovah’s organization.
We’ve spoken frankly to you
because we want you to make a success
of your service to Jehovah.
We also want to reassure you
that your assistance is very much needed.
So if you enjoy good health, both spiritually and physically,
and want to apply for expanded theocratic service
on a temporary or full-time basis,
ask your elders for an application
to serve as a temporary volunteer
or as a member of the Worldwide Order
of Special Full-Time Servants
of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
After completing the application, return it to your elders.
Then continue to allow Jehovah
to direct your steps wherever you may serve.
We love you for the willing spirit you show.
Please be assured of our prayers in your behalf
as you continue to reach out in Jehovah’s service.

ko.text: 해마에게는 여느 물고기와는 다른 독특한 특징이 있습니다.
꼬리를 사용해서 다른 물체를 감아쥘 수 있다는 것입니다.
그 덕분에 해마는 바닷물에 휩쓸려 가지 않고
해마의 꼬리는 단면이 원형이 아닌 정사각형입니다.
물체와의 접촉 면적이 더 넓기 때문에
해마의 꼬리는 물체를 더 강하게 감아쥘 수 있습니다.
해마는 별로 힘을 들이지 않고도 꼬리를 감거나 펼 수 있습니다.
해마의 꼬리를 감싸고 있는 뼈들은 얇고 평평한데,
이러한 구조는 척추가 손상되는 것을 막아 줍니다.
과학자들은 수색 구조 로봇이나 수술 도구를 만드는 데
해마 꼬리의 구조를 응용하려고 하고 있습니다.
좁은 공간에서 구부리거나 물체를 잡을 수 있으면서도
“공학자들이 만들어 내는 것은 조작은 쉽지만 유연하지 않다.
튼튼해서 부서지지 않으면서도 다양한 일을 할 수 있을 만큼 유연하다.
로봇 공학은 눈부신 발전을 이룰 것이다.”

en.text: ‎The seahorse ‎has a very unusual feature for a fish:
‎a prehensile, or grasping, tail.
‎This tail can anchor ‎the seahorse to one spot,
‎resisting the ocean currents ‎that surround it.
‎How does it work?
‎The cross-section ‎of the seahorse’s tail is square,
‎not round like that ‎of most other animals with gripping tails.
‎In contrast with a round shape,
‎this square shape ‎allows the tail to contact a greater area
‎of the surface being gripped,
‎making it more difficult to dislodge.
‎It can also
‎twist and untwist with minimal energy.
‎In addition, the tail ‎of the seahorse is encased
‎in overlapping bony plates ‎with many joints.
‎When subjected ‎to a potentially harmful force,
‎the plates slide over one another,
‎absorbing the energy.
‎This can prevent damage ‎to the seahorse’s spinal column.
‎The design of the seahorse’s tail ‎could be applied to search-and-rescue robots,
‎which need to be strong ‎and capable of bending and twisting
‎in tight spaces.
‎The same properties could be useful
‎in some surgical equipment.
‎According to Professor Ross Hatton:
‎“Human engineers tend to build things
‎“that are stiff ‎so they can be controlled easily.
‎“But nature makes things ‎just strong enough not to break,
‎“and then flexible enough ‎to do a wide range of tasks.
‎“That’s why we can learn ‎a lot from animals
‎that will inspire ‎the next generations of robotics.”
‎What do you think?
‎Did the seahorse’s tail evolve?
‎Or was it designed?

title: 조엘 델링거: 여러분의 희망을 강하게 하십시오 (계시록 21:4)

ko.text: 행복한 기억이 나쁜 기억을 전부 몰아낼 겁니다.
나도 봉사를 하면서 수도 없이 이 성구를 사용했지.’
네, 이 성구를 자주 사용하다 보니
아마 많은 분이 그 내용을 다 외우고 계시겠지만,
우리가 생각해 보면 도움이 될 질문들이 있습니다.
“이 기본적인 성경 진리는 지금도 여전히 나에게 힘을 주고 있는가?
그것은 여전히 내 ‘영혼을 위한 닻’이 되고 있는가?” 하는 거죠.
이 점을 생각하며 세 가지 질문을 검토해 보십시다.
셋째, 어떻게 희망을 강하게 할 수 있습니까?
사실을 부인하는 어리석음에 지나지 않는 것이라고 생각하는 것 같다.”
희망을 낙관적인 태도나 말 그대로 희망 사항으로 생각하기도 합니다.
하지만 사실에 근거하지 않은 소원이나 바람은 어떻습니까?
여호와를 고려하지 않은 소원이나 바람은 무엇과 같을까요?
물론 참그리스도인은 아무도 꿈같은 환상에 빠져 살아가기를
희망이 강해지게 하라는 권고는 분명히 나옵니다.
“희망”으로 번역된 성경 원어에는 이런 의미가 있습니다.
성경에서 희망은 단지 좋은 것을 바라는 것만이 아니라
그 좋은 일이 일어날 것이라고 믿는 근거까지 포함합니다.
믿음처럼 희망도 증거 즉 확실한 사실에 기반을 두고 있습니다.
좋은 것에 대한 우리의 열망이 희망과 관련되긴 하지만,
우리가 원하고 바라는 것이 희망의 출발점은 아닙니다.
희망은 하느님이 그분의 목적과 관련해 원하시고,
우리 개개인에게 원하시는 것에 우선적으로 기초해 있습니다.
성경에서 말하는 희망이란, 여호와께서 알려주신 대로
앞으로 현실이 될 일들에 대한 간절한 기대라고 할 수 있습니다.
우리가 잘 아는 믿음의 정의를 읽으면서
희망과 믿음이 어떻게 연관되어 있는지 유의해 보시기 바랍니다.
“믿음은 바라는[즉 희망하는] 것들에 대한 보증된 기대이며
우리의 숭배가 헛되지 않으려면 믿음이 꼭 필요합니다.
믿음과 희망 사이의 관계를 더 잘 이해하기 위해
인간적인 관점에서 아브라함과 사라는 출산 연령이 한참 지난 상태였죠.
아브라함과 사라 모두 천사의 말을 듣고 웃었다고 나옵니다.
생각만 해도 놀랍고 웃음이 나올 일이었겠죠.
하지만 아브라함은 그 약속에 어떤 반응을 보였습니까?
이 말씀이 희망을 가져야 하는 이유와 어떤 관련이 있는지 유의해 보시기 바랍니다.
‘너의 자손이 그와 같이 될 것이다’라는 말씀대로
많은 민족의 아버지가 될 것이라는 믿음을 가졌습니다.”
아들을 갖게 될 거라는 그의 믿음의 굳건한 기초가 됐습니다.
그리고 그 믿음은 또 다시 그의 희망을 밝고 강하게 해 주었죠.
아브라함은 여호와의 약속을 마음속으로 믿기만 한 것이 아니라
그것이 실현되는 것을 보기를 간절히 기대했습니다.
우리에게 희망이 필요한 또 다른 이유는
앞으로 이 세상의 끝이 오기 전에 직면해야 할
“희망은 영혼을 위한 확실하고 굳건한 닻”과 같다고 했죠.
배가 폭풍 속에서 잘 견딜 수 있고
위험한 모래톱이나 해안가로 떠밀려가지 않게 됩니다.
흥미롭게도, 사도 바울이 기원 58년에 배를 타고 로마에 가는 중에
배가 암초에 걸릴 뻔 한 적이 있었죠.
성경을 보면, 그때 선원들이 고물에서 닻을 네 개나
하나도 아니고 네 개나 던졌다고 알려 줍니다.
덕분에 폭풍 속에서도 안전할 수 있었죠.
폭풍 속에 있는 오늘날 희망이 왜 필요한지 분명히 알 수 있죠?
정신을 여호와의 약속에 고정하고 간절히 기대한다면,
가족 문제, 경제 문제, 건강 문제 등 어떤 문제가 생겨도
감정적, 정신적, 영적 균형을 유지할 수 있습니다.
우리는 여호와께서 하신 약속을 간절히 기대하기에
거짓말하실 수 없는 하느님 여호와께서 하신 약속을
우리에게 더 안정감을 주는 것도 없을 것입니다.
어떻게 희망이 강해지게 할 수 있습니까?
네 명의 해설자가 잘 해설해 주신 것처럼
우린 여호와의 약속이 우리 각자에게 어떻게 적용되는지,
가까운 장래에 그 약속들이 나와 내 가족에게 어떤 의미를 갖게 될지
물론 우린 사랑에서 우러나와 여호와를 섬기고
여호와께선 우리가 그분이 성경에 약속해 놓으신 상에 대해
우리가 그 축복들을 그려보고 묵상하길 바라시죠.
한 자매는 우리 잡지에 나온 아름다운 삽화를 언급하면서 말했습니다.
낙원에 제가 있는 모습을 상상하려고 노력하죠.
진정으로 있고 싶은 곳이 바로 그곳이니까요.”
우리가 희망을 더 강하게 하도록 어떻게 격려하는지 유의해 보시죠.
아마겟돈에서 있을 것으로 기대하는 일과 관련된 표현이죠]
여러분이 어떠한 사람이 되어야 할지 생각해 보십시오!
구성 요소들이 심한 열기에 녹아 버릴 것입니다.”
어떻게 희망을 강하게 하는지 알 수 있죠?
네, 의미 있는 기도, 의미 있는 성경 연구, 의미 있는 묵상은
우리가 여호와의 날을 계속해서 가깝게 여기고
“희망 가운데 기뻐할” 수 있게 도와줄 것입니다.
마침내 우린 “거짓말하실 수 없는 하느님”의 모든 약속,
우리의 희망이 실현되는 것을 보게 될 겁니다.

en.text: ‎You know, our text today
‎and the comments that we just heard
‎center our attention on our Christian hope.
‎Very soon, our loving Father, Jehovah,
‎is going to eliminate pain, suffering, death,
‎and indeed, as has been commented on,
‎the happy memories ‎will just push out all the bad memories.
‎“The former things ‎[will indeed] have passed away.”
‎Now, when I thought about Revelation 21:3, 4,
‎I thought to myself, ‎‘I’ve heard those words hundreds of times,
‎‘and I’ve probably shared those words
‎hundreds of times in our ministry.’
‎And while most of us through repetition
‎have probably memorized ‎those sacred thoughts,
‎a good question I thought ‎would be helpful to think about is,
‎Are these basic Scriptural truths
‎still strengthening me now?
‎Are they, as Brother Cotton just mentioned,
‎still serving “as an anchor for [my] soul?”
‎With that thought in mind, ‎let’s consider three questions:
‎What is the hope ‎as described in the Scriptures?
‎Second, why do we need hope?
‎And third, how can we strengthen our hope?
‎First, how would you define hope?
‎Back in 1993, The Watchtower ‎quoted a writer who said this:
‎“Most people seem to think that hope
‎is just a dopy form of denying the truth.”
‎Others today would equate hope
‎with optimism or wishful thinking.
‎And, of course, ‎the Scriptures encourage positive thinking,
‎and there are benefits ‎—emotionally and perhaps even physically.
‎But what do we call a desire or a wish
‎that’s not based on truth?
‎What is a desire or a wish ‎that does not take Jehovah into account?
‎Well, that’s a dream; that’s an unreality.
‎And, of course, none of us as true Christians
‎want to live in La-La land, ‎or in a dreamworld, do we?
‎Of course, the Bible ‎does not use the word “optimism,”
‎but it does encourage us ‎to strengthen our hope.
‎What is hope according to the Scriptures?
‎The original language words ‎used in the Bible that are translated “hope”
‎mean “to wait eagerly” and “to expect good.”
‎In the Scriptures, hope involves ‎not only the desire for something good
‎but it includes the basis ‎for believing that good will come.
‎That’s much more meaningful than optimism.
‎Hope, like our faith, is based on evidence
‎—convincing facts.
‎And though hope involves ‎our eager desire for something good,
‎it does not start with our desires ‎—what we want or what we wish for.
‎It’s first rooted in what God wants
‎with regard to his purpose ‎and what God wants for us individually.
‎Romans 5:5 tells us
‎that such “hope does not lead ‎to disappointment.”
‎So in a brief definition, ‎we could say that Scriptural hope
‎is eager expectation based on future realities,
‎rooted in what Jehovah has taught us.
‎Our second question:
‎Why is hope essential for all Christians?
‎Please open your Bible ‎with me to Hebrews 11:1,
‎and notice our well-known definition of faith,
‎but then notice how hope is associated.
‎Hebrews 11:1 says:
‎“Faith is the assured expectation
‎“of what is hoped for,
‎“the evident demonstration
‎of realities that are not seen.”
‎So just as faith is a requirement
‎for us to serve Jehovah acceptably
‎and for our worship not to be in vain,
‎hope, as an essential element of faith,
‎is also necessary for all Christians.
‎To see the connection ‎between faith and hope a little better,
‎we might think about the example of Abraham.
‎Now, from a human standpoint,
‎Abraham and Sarah ‎were way past childbearing age
‎when Jehovah promised them a son.
‎It’s interesting that in the Scriptures
‎both Abraham and Sarah ‎laughed at the angelic announcement.
‎It was an amazing and tickling prospect to them
‎to think that they ‎would have a baby in their older years.
‎But how did Abraham respond to the promise?
‎Notice, please, in Romans 4:18
‎what the Bible says,
‎linked to this discussion of the need for hope.
‎Romans 4:18 says:
‎“Although beyond hope, yet based on hope,
‎“he had faith that he would become ‎the father of many nations
‎“according to what had been said:
‎‘So your offspring will be.’”
‎Faith “based on hope”
‎—we see the connection better, don’t we?
‎You see, Abraham’s God-given hope
‎gave his faith that he would have a son
‎a firm foundation.
‎His faith, in turn, ‎brightened and strengthened his hope.
‎So it was not only this conviction in his heart
‎but it was the eager anticipation of seeing
‎what Jehovah had promised come to fulfillment.
‎Another reason that we need hope
‎has to do with the storms ‎that you and I are undoubtedly facing now
‎or will face ‎before the end of the system comes.
‎In Paul’s letter to the Hebrews, ‎he illustrated hope
‎“as an anchor for the soul, ‎both sure and firm.”
‎So when confronting storms,
‎what do sailors, ‎both in ancient times and today, often do?
‎They lower the ship’s anchor.
‎Why?
‎Well, if the anchor ‎takes hold of the firm seabed,
‎it helps the ship ride out the storm.
‎It keeps that ship ‎away from dangerous reefs or the shoreline.
‎Interestingly, ‎when the apostle Paul was on that ship
‎en route to Rome in the year 58 C.E.,
‎the ship was in danger of running aground.
‎The Bible tells us ‎that the sailors cast out four anchors
‎—not just one, four— ‎from the stern,
‎and as a result, ‎the ship safely rode out the storm.
‎Well, it’s not hard to see the connection
‎with hope and our stormy times today, is it?
‎Our “sure and firm” hope,
‎our setting our mind with eager expectation ‎of what Jehovah has promised,
‎keeps us emotionally, mentally, ‎and spiritually balanced
‎no matter what ‎is raging around us in our life
‎—in full-time service, with our family,
‎with our finances, with our health.
‎We can weather the storms
‎because of our eager expectation ‎of what Jehovah has promised.
‎Really, few things ‎could be more stabilizing in our life
‎than this eager expectation of what Jehovah,
‎the God who does not lie, has promised to us.
‎Well, that leads to a third question:
‎How can we strengthen our hope?
‎Well, as has been commented on beautifully ‎by our four commenters,
‎we need to think specifically
‎about how Jehovah’s promises apply to us
‎and what they will mean for us and our family
‎in the near future.
‎Though we serve Jehovah out of love
‎—and that’s our principal motivation—
‎Jehovah wants us to think about the rewards
‎that he has outlined for us in the Scriptures.
‎He wants us to visualize
‎and meditate on such blessings.
‎One sister, in referring to the beautiful artwork
‎that’s in our magazines, said this:
‎“When I see pictures ‎of the coming Paradise . . . ,
‎“I examine them closely, ‎as one would a travel brochure.
‎“I endeavor to see myself there
‎“because this is where I truly hope to be
‎in God’s due time.”
‎Daydreaming?
‎No.
‎Meditation on truths
‎and on precious promises that will not lie?
‎Yes.
‎Notice, please, ‎with me at 2 Peter 3:11, 12
‎how the inspired counsel encourages us
‎to strengthen and build up ‎our hope in view of what’s coming.
‎Second Peter chapter 3, ‎let’s read together verses 11 and 12:
‎“Since all these things ‎are to be dissolved in this way
‎“[with regard to what ‎we’re expecting in the near future
‎“with the great tribulation ‎leading into Armageddon],
‎“consider what sort of people you ought to be
‎“in holy acts of conduct ‎and deeds of godly devotion,
‎“as you await and keep close in mind
‎“the presence of the day of Jehovah,
‎“through which the heavens ‎will be destroyed in flames
‎and the elements ‎will melt in the intense heat!”
‎Notice in verse 12 that expression, ‎“keep close in mind”
‎—“eagerly desire,” literally, “speed up.”
‎Do you see how our positive meditation,
‎our visualizing what’s to come, ‎will strengthen us?
‎Yes, meaningful prayer,
‎meaningful Bible study,
‎meaningful reflection
‎will help us to keep ‎Jehovah’s day close in mind.
‎It will help us to “rejoice in the hope,”
‎and then we will experience the realization
‎of all that we’ve hoped for ‎from the God “who cannot lie.”

cn.text: ‎‎‪今天的每日经文和大家的评论
‎‎‪都让我们把注意力
‎‎‪集中到未来的希望之上
‎‎‪我们仁爱的父亲耶和华上帝
‎‎‪很快就会消除哀恸、苦难和死亡
‎‎‪在新世界
‎‎‪快乐的记忆会取代痛苦的回忆
‎‎‪正如经文所说的那样
‎‎‪“从前的事已经过去了”
‎‎‪在读启示录21:3,4的时候
‎‎‪我心想
‎‎‪我已经听过这句话几百次了
‎‎‪而且传道时，我也给别人读过不知多少次了
‎‎‪的确，这两节常用的经文
‎‎‪我们差不多都能背下来了
‎‎‪但我还是想到一些值得思考的问题
‎‎‪这个基本的圣经真理
‎‎‪现在还能强化我们的信心吗？
‎‎‪仍然“像生命的锚一样”
‎‎‪让我们坚定不移吗？
‎‎‪为了解答这些问题
‎‎‪我们从三方面考虑一下
‎‎‪圣经所说的希望是什么意思？
‎‎‪我们为什么需要希望？
‎‎‪怎样强化我们的希望？
‎‎‪首先谈谈
‎‎‪你怎样给希望下定义呢？
‎‎‪1993年的守望台引用了一位作家的话
‎‎‪他说
‎‎‪“看来大多数人认为
‎‎‪抱着希望
‎‎‪就是拒绝相信现实的一种愚昧表现”
‎‎‪另一些则认为
‎‎‪希望等同于幻想或者盲目的乐观主义
‎‎‪当然，圣经鼓励人要有积极的想法
‎‎‪这对人的情绪甚至身体都有益处
‎‎‪不过，对于不切实际的愿望
‎‎‪以及忽视耶和华旨意的愿望
‎‎‪我们会用什么词来形容呢？
‎‎‪我们会称之为幻想，或者空想
‎‎‪当然，我们基督徒
‎‎‪都不想生活在一个虚幻的理想世界里
‎‎‪圣经也没有用“乐观主义”这样的词
‎‎‪而是鼓励我们强化自己的希望
‎‎‪圣经里面的希望是什么意思呢？
‎‎‪“希望”在圣经原文里的意思是
‎‎‪“热切的等待”
‎‎‪“期待美好的事”
‎‎‪在圣经里
‎‎‪“希望”不仅是期待美好的事情实现
‎‎‪而且有充分的理由相信它会实现
‎‎‪这远比乐观主义有实际意义
‎‎‪希望就像信心一样
‎‎‪是建立在可靠的证据之上的
‎‎‪虽然圣经里的希望
‎‎‪和我们的美好愿望有关
‎‎‪但并不是因为我们的愿望而有的
‎‎‪而是因为上帝的旨意
‎‎‪以及上帝对我们个人的期望而产生的
‎‎‪罗马书5:5告诉我们
‎‎‪“这个希望必不令人失望”
‎‎‪总之，我们可以说
‎‎‪圣经所说的希望指的是
‎‎‪对未来怀有的热切期待
‎‎‪而这期待是以圣经真理为依据
‎‎‪是真实可靠的
‎‎‪第二个问题
‎‎‪为什么希望对基督徒来说是至关重要的呢？
‎‎‪请打开希伯来书11:1
‎‎‪这里是对信心的定义
‎‎‪请留意希望和信心有怎样的关系
‎‎‪“信心是确知希望必然实现
‎‎‪是不见的事实的明证”
‎‎‪我们崇拜耶和华的时候
‎‎‪必须表现信心
‎‎‪这样才能得到他的认可
‎‎‪因为希望和信心息息相关
‎‎‪所以希望也是同样重要的
‎‎‪为了更好的理解希望和信心之间的关系
‎‎‪我们可以想想亚伯拉罕的例子
‎‎‪从人的角度看来
‎‎‪亚伯拉罕和撒拉年纪老迈
‎‎‪早已过了生育的年龄
‎‎‪但是耶和华仍然承诺要赐给他们一个儿子
‎‎‪他们听到后都笑了起来
‎‎‪他们想到年纪这么大了还能有孩子
‎‎‪就觉得不可思议，就笑了
‎‎‪不过，亚伯拉罕怎样回应这个承诺呢？
‎‎‪请留意罗马书4:18
‎‎‪看看这节经文
‎‎‪和我们讨论的希望有什么关系
‎‎‪“他虽然本已没有希望
‎‎‪却仍然本着希望怀具信心
‎‎‪结果成为多国之父
‎‎‪正如先前有话说
‎‎‪‘你的苗裔将来也是这样’”
‎‎‪所以，信心是以希望为根据的
‎‎‪上帝给亚伯拉罕这个承诺
‎‎‪给了他希望
‎‎‪成为他信心的基础
‎‎‪这让他确信会生一个儿子
‎‎‪他的信心也让他的希望
‎‎‪变得更殷切、更真实
‎‎‪所以，他不仅相信上帝的承诺
‎‎‪而且也热切期待看到这个承诺的实现
‎‎‪我们需要希望的另一个理由是
‎‎‪在这个制度终结之前
‎‎‪我们真基督徒
‎‎‪迟早都会遇到暴风般的考验
‎‎‪但是保罗在希伯来书中保证
‎‎‪希望“就像生命的锚一样
‎‎‪又确定又牢靠”
‎‎‪遇到暴风雨时
‎‎‪船员一般会怎么做呢？
‎‎‪他们会抛下船锚
‎‎‪一旦船锚牢牢地扎在海床上
‎‎‪船就能安全渡过风暴
‎‎‪避免触礁或者撞上海岸的岩石
‎‎‪公元58年，当保罗乘船被押往罗马的时候
‎‎‪就有撞上岩石的危险
‎‎‪圣经记载水手从船尾扔下4个船锚
‎‎‪不是1个而是4个
‎‎‪结果船安全地渡过了风暴
‎‎‪同样，希望也像船锚一样
‎‎‪会帮助我们渡过这个暴风雨般的时代
‎‎‪我们热切盼望耶和华的承诺实现
‎‎‪这个“确定又牢靠”的希望
‎‎‪可以帮助我们保持内心平静
‎‎‪目光清晰
‎‎‪巩固我们和耶和华的关系
‎‎‪不论在生活中
‎‎‪在全时服务中遇到什么难题
‎‎‪家庭难题、经济难题
‎‎‪健康问题等等
‎‎‪我们都能应付
‎‎‪因为我们有希望
‎‎‪的确，在生活中
‎‎‪没有任何事比耶和华的承诺更可靠
‎‎‪因为上帝从不说谎
‎‎‪下面我们讨论第3个问题
‎‎‪怎样强化我们的希望？
‎‎‪想要了解这个问题的答案
‎‎‪我们需要具体想想耶和华的承诺
‎‎‪和我们有什么关系
‎‎‪以及这个承诺对我们和家人的未来
‎‎‪有什么重要意义
‎‎‪虽然我们崇拜上帝的主要动机是因为爱他
‎‎‪但是耶和华还是希望我们仔细想想
‎‎‪他承诺要给我们的奖赏
‎‎‪他希望我们想象、沉思这些福分
‎‎‪一位姐妹提到我们杂志里的漂亮插图说
‎‎‪“每当看到乐园图画时
‎‎‪我都会很仔细地看
‎‎‪就像看旅游杂志一样
‎‎‪我想象自己身在其中
‎‎‪因为我真的渴望在上帝所定的时候
‎‎‪在地上的乐园里生活”
‎‎‪这绝不是在白日做梦
‎‎‪而是在沉思上帝承诺必然实现的美好未来
‎‎‪请留意彼得后书3:11,12
‎‎‪对于将要发生的事
‎‎‪这两节经文怎样强化我们的希望呢？
‎‎‪我们一起看一下
‎‎‪彼得后书3:11,12的内容
‎‎‪经文说
‎‎‪“既然这一切都要这样销毁”
‎‎‪ 这里说的是即将到来的大患难
‎‎‪和随即引发的哈米吉多顿大战
‎‎‪“你们该做怎么样的人呢！
‎‎‪你们该有圣洁的品行
‎‎‪有敬虔的行为
‎‎‪等待耶和华的日子临到
‎‎‪紧记日子迫近
‎‎‪在那日，天会着火而销毁
‎‎‪元素也因极热而熔化”
‎‎‪12节里的“紧记”这个词
‎‎‪也就是“热切盼望”
‎‎‪字面意思是“加速”
‎‎‪我们能看出
‎‎‪积极地沉思、想象即将发生的事
‎‎‪可以怎样强化我们呢？
‎‎‪真诚的祷告
‎‎‪深入的研读和沉思
‎‎‪能帮助我们紧记耶和华的日子临近了
‎‎‪也能帮助我们“在希望中欢喜”
‎‎‪到时候我们会亲眼看到盼望的事实现
‎‎‪因为这是“不可能说谎”的上帝所给的希望

titles.ko: 조엘 델링거: 여러분의 희망을 강하게 하십시오 (계시록 21:4)
titles.cn: 乔尔·德林格：强化我们的希望（启 21:4）

title: 베네수엘라—힘든 시기에 형제들이 사랑과 믿음을 나타내다

ko.text: 베네수엘라 형제들의 상황을 전해 드리는 특별 보도입니다.
지난 2017년 8월에 여호와의 증인 뉴스 섹션을 통해 소개된 것처럼,
안타깝게도 그곳의 상황은 갈수록 악화되고 있습니다.
식품과 의약품 같은 기본 필수품도 구하기가 쉽지 않고,
폭력과 범죄가 계속 증가하면서 매우 혼란스러운 상황입니다.
우리는 전 세계 형제 자매들을 사랑하기 때문에
“한 지체가 고통을 당하면 다른 모든 지체도 함께 고통을 당합니다.
그리고 한 지체가 영광스럽게 되면 다른 모든 지체도 함께 기뻐합니다.”
분명 여러분도 베네수엘라 형제들을 위해 자주 기도하실텐데요.
그처럼 힘든 상황에서 우리 형제들은 영적으로 어떻게 지내고 있습니까?
경각심이 들면서도 큰 격려를 받으실 겁니다.
어려운 상황에서 어떻게 사랑과 믿음을 나타내는지 유의해 보십시오.
베드로 전서 3:8에서 권하는 대로 계속 ‘일치된 생각을 갖고,
동료감과 형제 애정과 부드러운 동정심’을 길러 나가겠다는
많은 사람들이 심한 어려움을 겪고 있고,
또 의지하면서 기쁨을 잃지 않고 있습니다.
지부 사무실에서 두 달 전에 집계를 해 봤는데요.
놀랍게도 3년 동안 무려 전도인 7000명이 베네수엘라를 떠났습니다.
생명에 위협이 되는 상황에 처했던 사람도 있었고,
풀려난 뒤에는 이곳을 떠나 다른 나라로 갔죠.
그중 하나는 평일 집회 시간을 앞당긴 것입니다.
베델에서 일하는 장로들이 연합하고 있는 곳도 많죠.
그래야 형제들이 날이 밝을 때 집회에 왔다가
날이 너무 어둡지 않을 때 집회를 마치고 집에 돌아갈 수 있기 때문입니다.
또 일부 부유한 회중들에 가 보면,
아무도 핸드폰이나 태블릿 PC를 가져오지 않습니다.
잃어버릴까 봐 집에 두고 온 게 아니라
괴한들이 그런 걸 빼앗으러 왕국회관에 올까 봐 그런다고 하더군요.
회중 전체가 피해를 입을까 봐 걱정하는 거죠.
전도인들은 이처럼 조심스럽게 행동하는 법을 배우고 있습니다.
예전에도 그래야 했지만 이젠 더 조심스럽게 행동해야 하지요.
하지만 대부분의 형제 자매들은 불평하지 않습니다.
제가 다니는 회중에서도 관심을 많이 보이면서 물어보아야,
형제 자매들은 그제서야 자기들이 겪는 어려움을 이야기하죠.
어떤 집에서 문을 아주 조금만 열더군요.
안에 있던 젊은 남자가 날 보고 문을 열어 줬고
“성경 읽어 본 적 있으세요?” 하고 물었더니,
아마 내 반응을 떠 보려고 그랬던 거 같아요.
그 사람 뒤에 다른 젊은 남자가 손에 총을 들고 있는 게 보였죠.
난 총을 봤지만 그냥 차분히 대화를 나눴어요.
그는 총을 주머니에 넣었고, 우린 20분 정도 대화를 했습니다.
그 집을 나오면서 짝 형제가 긴장한 목소리로
사람들을 많이 살해한 갱단 두목이라고 하더군요.
그래서 “그래요? 내 눈엔 좋은 소식을 필요로 하는
우리와 똑같은 사람으로 보였어요” 라고 했죠.
전도인 수만 아니라 파이오니아 수가 증가했습니다.
파이오니아를 시작한 사람들 상당수가 자매들이긴 하지만
회사가 문을 닫고 외국으로 이전하면서 직장을 잃었지요.
제게 이렇게 말한 형제들이 많이 있어요.
“직장을 잃긴 했지만 대신 이제 파이오니아를 할 수 있죠.”
그들은 영적으로 계속 열심을 잃지 않고 있습니다.
전 세계의 형제 자매들이 우리에게 관심을 갖고 있다는 걸 알고
중앙장로회는 여기 상황을 주시하면서 우리를 위해 기도하고
이런 일을 통해 우리는 혼자가 아니라
세계적인 형제 관계에 속해 있다는 걸 느끼기 때문에
여호와께서 인도하시는 보이는 조직에 대한 확신과 믿음도 강해지죠.
우리는 일개 나라보다 훨씬 더 큰 조직에 속해 있는 것입니다.
성경 말씀에 대한 믿음에 시험이 되고 있는 건 사실입니다.
평소 우린 성경 말씀이 옳다고 생각하는데,
시험을 겪으면 그 점을 더 확신하게 됩니다.
이 어려운 시기를 헤쳐나갈 수 있다는 확신도 갖게 됩니다.
따라서 야고보의 말처럼, 우리 각자는 인내가 그 일을 이루게 해야 합니다.
그러한 견해를 갖는다면 우린 현재의 힘든 시기를 통해
더 나은 그리스도인이 될 수 있을 겁니다.
여호와의 기쁨이 여러분의 산성입니다” 라고 말합니다.
따라서 우리는 부정적인 것들에 초점을 맞추는 게 아니라
전도인 7000명이 베네수엘라를 떠나서 한때 여러 기록이 하락했지만
회중들은 좋은 보고를 보내 오고 있습니다.
새로운 사람들이 진리 안으로 계속 들어오고 있다고 보고하죠.
형제 자매들은 상황이 어렵다고 활동을 중단하는 게 아니라
계속 왕국과 왕이신 예수를 바라보며 전진하고 있습니다.
결국 걸음을 멈추게 될 수 있습니다.
경제적인 문제에 대해 염려하게 될 수 있지요.
우린 그럴 게 아니라 계속 왕국에 초점을 맞춰야 합니다.
우리는 어려운 상황에서도 영적인 일에 열심을 나타내고
보고에 따르면, 베네수엘라에는 전도인이 약 14만 명이 있는데,
또 전도인들도 봉사 시간으로 매달 평균 열다섯 시간을 보고합니다.
전체 성서 연구 건수도 20만 건이나 되죠.
베네수엘라 형제들의 훌륭한 태도를 보여 주는
순회 감독자들의 보고 두 개를 소개해 드리겠습니다.
“형제들은 극도로 가난하고 치안이 불안한 지역에서 살고 있습니다.
대부분이 회관에서 멀리 떨어진 곳에 살아서
집회에 오려면 한 시간 이상 걸어야 하는데도
또한 전도인들 모두가 봉사에 정기적으로 참여합니다.”
또 다른 순회 감독자의 보고는 이러합니다.
장로가 두 명밖에 없지만, 그들은 겸손하게 열심히 일하면서
양들을 돌보는 일과 봉사에서도 모범이 됩니다.”
또 다른 특별한 동영상이 준비 중에 있습니다.
2018년 11월 12일에 ‘골라 보기’ 섹션에 올라올 이 동영상의 제목은
지금까지 여호와의 증인의 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다.

en.text: Welcome to this special news update
regarding our brothers in Venezuela.
As reported in the JW News section
of jw.org in August 2017,
our brothers in Venezuela are enduring difficult economic conditions.
Sadly, the overall situation continues to worsen.
Basic needs, like food and medicine,
are hard to obtain.
Violence and crime is on the increase.
Things are chaotic.
Because we love our worldwide brotherhood,
this difficult situation affects all of us.
As Paul said at 1 Corinthians 12:26:
“If one member suffers,
“all the other members suffer with it;
“or if a member is glorified,
all the other members rejoice with it.”
No doubt you pray regularly for our brothers in Venezuela.
Despite these difficult times,
how are our brothers doing spiritually?
We’re sure you’ll find the following report
to be sobering and encouraging.
Notice how, despite these difficult times,
our brothers in Venezuela are showing love and faith.
May this report motivate all of us to continue having
“unity of mind, fellow feeling,
brotherly affection, [and] tender compassion,”
as 1 Peter 3:8 says.
It’s amazing to see how far the situation has gone,
and we are still at it.
So people in general have a lot of endurance,
and the brothers
—they endure.
They’re still cheerful.
They have to trust one another;
they have to rely on one another.
We gathered some statistics two months ago,
and we found out that in only three years,
7,000 publishers
—among them many elders, many pioneers—
have left the country because of the dangers.
They have felt threatened; some had been kidnapped,
let go, and then they left the country;
family members have been killed, and so on.
So one of the things we had to do with the local congregations
—which most of them have quite a few Bethelite elders—
is move their meeting time on the weekdays
to an earlier hour so that the brothers can go to the meeting with daylight,
and sometimes they can go home after the meeting with some daylight.
If you go to some congregations that are well-to-do
(I’ve been to the place), you don’t see anyone at the meeting
with their cell phones or tablets.
And I said, “Why is that?”
Well, it’s not because they are afraid to lose it,
but they just don’t want to attract criminals into the Kingdom Hall.
And so for one tablet, all might suffer.
So you see, they’re learning to be streetwise even more,
because in Venezuela, you had to be streetwise
for a long time in the past,
but now it’s getting worse.
But the brotherhood in general don’t complain.
At least in my congregation,
you have to ask and you have to show real interest
so that the brothers and sisters can tell you what they’re going through.
I knocked on the door,
and the door opened just a little crack.
And the young man, when he saw me, opened the door wide, and we talked.
I asked him, “Have you ever read the Bible?”
He said, “Oh, when I was in prison, I read it a lot.”
He probably said that to see my reaction.
Well, we just kept talking and talking.
Behind him was another young man; he had a pistol in his hand.
I saw that, and I didn’t react.
He put the gun in his pocket,
and we kept talking for about 15-20 minutes.
When we went away, the brother that was with me was quite upset.
He said, “Do you know who that was?”
I said, “No.”
“That was one of the gang leaders.
He has killed a lot of people.”
I said: “Well, what I noticed is that he’s a human being just like the rest.
He needs the message.”
We have noticed, too, in the last few years,
an increase not only in publishers
but pioneers.
And who are starting to pioneer?
Well, as usual, mostly sisters, but many brothers,
many elders.
They may have had a good job;
they lost their job because the company closed down and left the country.
So many brothers have mentioned to me:
“Well, I lost my job; I have no job. Now I can pioneer.”
So they start pioneering.
And I think that’s very good, and it helps them to keep going.
I’m sure the brothers are happy to see that everybody cares
—everybody in the brotherhood worldwide.
The Governing Body is informed
and is doing all they physically can to help us
with their prayers.
So when you feel part of the worldwide brotherhood
—then you are not alone— that has a calming effect on you.
Your confidence, or faith,
in Jehovah’s organization
as a physical, visible organization, grows.
So we know we’re part of something bigger than just a country.
But this is putting to the test
how strong we will have faith in Bible principles.
We think they work,
but when they’re put to the test, then you’re convinced that they work.
And then I’m convinced that I will come out of this stronger.
That’s what James said
—that endurance needs to go to work in each one of us.
So if you view it that way,
then that gives you hope
that this sad and hard and difficult time
will make us better.
Nehemiah 8:10 says:
“Do not feel sad,
for the joy of Jehovah is your stronghold.”
So where is our strength?
In “the joy of Jehovah.”
I think we should always be positive,
not negative —not concentrate on the negative.
Like I quoted before, Nehemiah 8:10,
“the joy of Jehovah” —that’s what we see among the brothers.
The numbers came down because of the 7,000 that have left,
but the congregations keep reporting.
And the circuit overseers, in their reports, keep showing us
that new people are still coming into the truth
—many new ones.
So that’s positive.
They’re not paralyzed because of that.
They keep focused on the Kingdom,
Jesus the King, and they keep going in that direction.
Anytime anyone looks to the side and looks at the storm,
he stops in his tracks;
he starts missing meetings;
he starts thinking about his wallet —his money, his bank account.
So that is not good.
Keep focused on the Kingdom.
We’re proud of you brothers in Venezuela
for keeping focused on spiritual things
and maintaining a positive spirit during these difficult times.
The reports show that of the 140,000 publishers in Venezuela,
over 30,000 are regular pioneers
and 9,000 are auxiliary pioneers.
On average, publishers spend 15 hours
in the ministry each month.
They’re conducting close to 200,000 Bible studies.
To illustrate the spirit of our brothers in Venezuela,
note these two comments from circuit overseers:
“Our brothers live in an area of extreme poverty and insecurity.
“Meeting attendance is excellent,
“although most of our brothers live far from the Kingdom Hall
“and have to walk for more than an hour.
The regularity in service is 100 percent.”
Another circuit overseer reported:
“Fifty percent of the publishers are regular pioneers.
“There are only two elders, but they are hardworking,
“humble, well-organized,
and a good example in the preaching and shepherding work.”
We’re encouraged by the love and faith that you brothers in Venezuela show.
Please know that we love you all very much.
We’re going to hear more about our brothers in Venezuela
in another special report that will be released
on Video on Demand on November 12, 2018.
The video is entitled Surviving Trials in Venezuela.
It’s an interview with a couple from Venezuela
who recently attended the 144th class of Gilead.
This is JW Broadcasting
from the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

cn.text: 以下是关于委内瑞拉
弟兄姐妹的特别新闻报道
jw.org网站上的JW新闻栏目曾经报道
我们在委内瑞拉的弟兄姐妹
正经历严重的经济危机
但现在情况还在日益恶化
一些基本物资
比如食物和药品都十分紧缺
暴行和犯罪日益猖獗
情况十分混乱
我们深爱全世界的弟兄姐妹
他们的遭遇也牵动我们的心
正如保罗在哥林多前书12:26说
“身体一处受苦，各处就一同受苦
一处得荣耀，各处就一同欢乐。”
我们相信你肯定
常常为委内瑞拉的弟兄姐妹们祷告
尽管情况艰难
那里的弟兄依然信心坚定
我们相信以下的报道一定发人深省
也会让你大受鼓励
请留意委内瑞拉的弟兄姐妹们
如何在逆境中表现爱心和信心
希望这个报道能激励我们所有人
像彼得前书3:8说的一样
我们人人都要“思想一致，体恤别人
怀有弟兄之情、怜恤之心”
情况虽然越来越不好
但我们仍然能够应对
大多数人都要忍耐
但我们的弟兄不仅在忍耐
而且还保持喜乐
他们必须彼此信任，彼此依赖
两个月前，我们搜集了一些数据
发现仅仅三年内
就有7000个传道员
为了躲避危险而离开了委内瑞拉
其中有很多是长老和先驱
他们有的是因为生命受到威胁
有的是因为被绑架，后来获得释放
有的是因为家人遭到杀害，等等
虽然大多数本地会众都有伯特利的长老
但我们要做的一件事
就是调整平日聚会的时间
让弟兄姐妹可以早一点聚会
这样，有些时候弟兄姐妹们
就可以在天黑之前回家
在一些经济状况还不错的会众
我去过这样的会众
你在聚会的时候不会看见
有人拿着手机或平板电脑
这是因为他们不想
把犯罪分子招惹进王国聚会所
他们不是害怕被抢东西
而是不想为了一台平板电脑
就连累参加聚会的人
在委内瑞拉，我们一直都要很小心
但现在情况更糟了
大家就要变得更谨慎
但大部分弟兄都没有抱怨
至少在我的会众是这样
除非你特意地去问弟兄姐妹
否则他们不会告诉你自己正在经历什么
有一次，我敲了一家门
门只开了一条缝，里面有个年轻人
他看见我就把门打开，我们开始交谈
我问他：“你读过圣经吗？”
他说：“圣经啊，我在监狱的时候常看。”
他这么说，可能是要看我的反应
但我跟他还是聊下去
他身后站着另一个年轻人
手里拿着枪，我看见了，但没什么反应
他就把枪收起来
我们又聊了大概15到20分钟
离开那家之后
跟我在一起的弟兄很不高兴
他说：“你不知道那个人是谁吗？”
我说：“不知道。”
“他是一个黑帮头目，杀了很多人。”
我说：“原来是这样
不过他跟其他人一样
都需要听到圣经的信息。”
我们也发现，过去几年间
不仅传道员增加了
连先驱的人数也增加了
哪些人开始做先驱呢？
当然，大部分还是姐妹
但当中也有很多是弟兄和长老
他们以前可能有很好的工作
但因为公司倒闭就都失业了
许多弟兄对我说：“我失业，没工作了
所以现在我能做先驱。”
于是他们就开始做先驱
我觉得这很好
因为这能让他们保持坚强
全球的弟兄姐妹都很关心我们
这让我们深受鼓舞
中央长老团很清楚我们的情况
不仅为我们祷告
还竭尽全力帮助我们
当你意识到你属于一个全球的弟兄团体
你就能享有平安，不再感到孤独
你会更确信耶和华的组织是真实的
而且这个组织没有国界
但现在的情况会考验我们对圣经原则的信心
我们当然相信这些原则有用
但只有在考验下把这些原则运用出来
你才能更加确信这一点
我相信我们一定会变得更加坚强
正如雅各所说的
我们需要让忍耐在自己身上完全发挥作用
我们如果对考验有这样的态度
就能怀着希望忍耐
而这些困境能够使我们成为更好的基督徒

en.text: ‎During the 2015 annual meeting,
‎an announcement ‎was given that would affect
‎Bethels around the world.
‎The Governing Body has directed
‎that a number of our branch
‎and Assembly Hall ‎construction projects worldwide
‎be delayed, reduced in scope,
‎or in some cases cancelled.
‎The Governing Body
‎had two clear objectives
‎in mind with these changes:
‎Firstly, that of making the best use
‎of dedicated funds
‎but ultimately ‎giving even greater emphasis
‎to the preaching ‎and the teaching work.
‎In fact, here in Britain,
‎we were on the brink
‎of starting construction
‎on a new branch office,
‎and we really wondered
‎how these simplifications
‎would affect ‎the construction project.
‎To understand ‎why these changes were important,
‎we first need to take a look ‎at how Bethels function.
‎The field ministry ‎is a fundamental part
‎of our worship to Jehovah.
‎Bethels are there to support that work.
‎Bethels’ key departments
‎provide tools and training needed
‎to carry out the preaching work
‎and support and defend ‎our rights to do so.
‎Some of these departments
‎are Service, Audio/Video,
‎Local/Design Construction,
‎Translation, and Legal,
‎to mention a few.
‎In turn, none of these could function
‎without the support of departments
‎such as Purchasing, Accounting,
‎Computers, ‎Maintenance, and Kitchen
‎and Home Departments, ‎which care for the welfare
‎of the many volunteers working at Bethel.
‎So any simplification made to Bethel
‎would ultimately benefit the activity in the field.
‎Branch Committees around the world
‎were asked to reduce the size
‎of their Bethel families.
‎Now, this required us to rethink
‎the way we work ‎and the way we live at Bethel.
‎Simplified meal arrangements ‎has meant that Bethelites
‎now prepare some of their own meals.
‎Likewise, in many branches ‎they are responsible
‎for caring for their own laundry.
‎They now ‎also look after their own housekeeping.
‎Many more commuters ‎and remote volunteers
‎are being used to carry out work
‎that previously would have required ‎a permanent Bethelite.
‎These and other changes
‎have resulted ‎in making better use of donated funds
‎but are ultimately benefiting ‎the preaching work.
‎The Bethel family ‎has really responded very well
‎to these changes,
‎and we can see ‎how the direction given to us
‎from the Governing Body
‎is really benefiting ‎our brothers and sisters in the field.
‎And those ‎who’ve been reassigned to the field
‎are doing really well ‎in their assignments.
‎So how did this announcement
‎affect the branch relocation project ‎underway in Britain?
‎When the announcement was made in 2015,
‎plans were very well advanced.
‎This meant that we needed
‎to put the project on hold
‎while new requirements ‎for Bethel were evaluated.
‎This effectively led to a redesign
‎and a reduction ‎in the scope of the project.
‎For example,
‎the Bethel kitchen and dining spaces
‎became more compact,
‎as they were now largely preparing food
‎for only one meal a day rather than three.
‎There was no need for a central laundry,
‎as this would be cared for by the individuals
‎in their own private accommodations.
‎Rather than a large dining room ‎that’s only used for one hour a day
‎or an auditorium ‎only used one hour a week,
‎now a large multipurpose event space
‎was planned ‎which could be flexibly reconfigured
‎for various uses.
‎Offices could also be reconfigured,
‎either as private offices
‎or as large open work spaces
‎with relatively little reconstruction required.
‎The Governing Body was very clear
‎that as adaptive needs ‎of the organization came about,
‎they wanted ‎to make these changes quickly.
‎We trust that the lessons learned
‎from our project may aid
‎in other branch projects to follow.
‎In summary, we can see ‎that Bethels around the world
‎support the preaching and teaching work,
‎and these changes are evidence of that.
‎Well, at Philippians 1:10, we’re told
‎to “make sure ‎of the more important things.”
‎We desire to give priority to those activities
‎that contribute the most
‎to the spiritual welfare of God’s people
‎and the advancement ‎of the global preaching work.

ko.text: ‎그런데 우리에게 특히 요구되는 것 ‎두 가지는 무엇일까요?
‎여기, ‘계속 서로 참으라’는 ‎첫 번째 표현을 생각해 보시죠.
‎들으셨듯이, 첫 번째 표현은 ‎심각한 죄를 참으라는 것이 아니라,

‎‘딱히 뭐가 잘못됐다는 건 아니지만, ‎그래도 짜증이 난단 말이지.’

‎여러 해 전에 제가 서사모아 지부에서 ‎봉사할 때 이야기인데요,
‎그중 한 형제는 매일 습관처럼 ‎아침 일찍 식사 전에 와서
‎‘이른 아침에 쾌활하게 큰 소리로 ‎하는 인사는 저주로 여겨진다.’
‎뒷받침해 주는 성구를 ‎늘 찾을 수 있는 건 아닙니다.
‎이 그리스어 단어가 “용서”를 가리키는 ‎일반적인 단어가 아니기 때문입니다.
‎여기에는 요구된 것을 뛰어넘는 ‎관대함이란 뜻이 들어 있습니다.
‎「신세계역」이 나오기 한참 전인, ‎1882년에도 사용한 적이 있습니다.
‎그럼 우리가 “계속 서로 참고”, ‎“기꺼이 용서”하는 이 두 가지 면에서
‎우린 그 이유를 ‎여러 차례 들어서 잘 알고 있죠.
‎그러고도 자기한테 아주 적은 ‎돈을 빌린 남자를 찾아갔습니다.
‎하지만 그 종에게 왜 그랬냐고 물으면, ‎이렇게 말할지 모르죠.
‎돈이 필요해서 그 종에게 제 ‎돈을 받으려고 한 것뿐입니다.”
‎여호와의 본을 따르지 않을 ‎경우에도 늘 핑계는 있습니다.
‎두 번째 이유는 우리도 다른 사람의 ‎용서가 필요하기 때문입니다.
‎그런 경우에는, 서로의 단점이나 ‎독특한 점들을 알게 되죠.
‎「파수대」에선 더 ‎큰 규모로 모일 수 있는 지금이
‎서로 참아주는 법을 훈련할 수 있는 ‎좋은 때라고 했습니다.
‎후에 소규모로 여호와를 숭배해야 ‎할 때가 올 수 있기 때문이죠.
‎따라서 회중에서 평화를 유지하면 ‎우리에게 좋은 훈련이 됩니다.

en.text: ‎Well, perhaps we could take our Bibles
‎and turn to Colossians 3:​13.
‎And let’s analyze this verse together
‎and see what it is that Jehovah expects of us.
‎So in Colossians 3:​13,
‎it says: “Continue putting up with one another
‎“and forgiving one another freely
‎“even if anyone has a cause for complaint against another.
‎“Just as Jehovah freely forgave you,
‎you must also do the same.”
‎Well, certainly this verse
‎gives us plenty of food for thought ​—doesn’t it?​—
‎areas in which, perhaps, we can work on and improve in.
‎But what two things stand out
‎as being required of us?
‎Well, looking back, you notice the first one,
‎“continue putting up with one another,”
‎and then the second point,
‎“forgiving one another freely.”
‎Well, let’s look at that first expression:
‎“Continue putting up with one another.”
‎Well, what’s the difference between these two expressions?
‎Well, we’re told that this first expression
‎doesn’t refer to serious sins but perhaps talks about things
‎that are irritating, annoying,
‎things that we may not necessarily
‎have a cause for complaint concerning,
‎but they still get us very upset anyway
‎​—these minor things.
‎What are some of the things that annoy you?
‎Let’s be honest.
‎Are you annoyed when someone is always late?
‎Are you annoyed when they’re always early?
‎Are you annoyed when someone is outspoken?
‎Does it annoy you when someone is too quiet?
‎It’s amazing​ —isn’t it?​—
‎what the things that annoy us are.
‎I remember back in the ’70’s, Brother Knorr gave an outstanding talk
‎where he alluded to the fact that maybe there’s a sister in the congregation,
‎and she’s hearing this other sister, new in the truth,
‎answering up time after time,
‎and in her heart, she’s thinking,
‎‘Why doesn’t she just keep quiet?’
‎Well, maybe we’ve all experienced those feelings.
‎And if we’re judged on them, perhaps we’ll agree:
‎‘Well, it’s not justified; I don’t really have a cause,
‎but it still irritates me.’
‎It’s true—isn’t it?​— the expression
‎“Sometimes it’s not the mountains ahead of us that cause problems,
‎it’s the pebble in the shoe.”
‎And it’s sometimes the small things
‎that irritate us the most.
‎I remember when I was serving
‎in Western Samoa many years ago at the branch,
‎we had quite a number of brothers from overseas working on construction.
‎And there was one brother who had the habit of first thing in the morning
‎as he arrived before breakfast,
‎saying, “Good morning!” to everyone.
‎Some found that annoying.
‎Maybe you can relate to that.
‎And, no doubt, you feel very happy when you read the scripture
‎at Proverbs 27:14, where it says in one translation:
‎‘A loud and cheerful greeting early in the morning
‎is taken as a curse.’
‎You may be thinking, ‘Amen to that.’
‎And that brother ceased his habit after he read that scripture​
‎—or at least it was read to him.
‎But we may not always be able to find a scripture
‎that backs up this irritation that we feel.
‎So, what do we do?
‎Well, what does it say?
‎“Continue putting up with one another.”
‎“Continue”​—it’s something that we just have to keep on doing.
‎Now, that brings us to the second part of our verse,
‎“forgiving one another freely.”
‎It’s interesting, when we look at other translations of this verse,
‎most follow the King James Version
‎and just say “forgive.”
‎The New World Translation says ‘forgive freely.’
‎The reason is that this isn’t your normal
‎Greek word for “forgiveness.”
‎It denotes generosity,
‎a willingness to go beyond what’s required.
‎It’s interesting that The Watchtower even back in 1882
‎was using that expression, to ‘forgive one another freely,’
‎well before the time of the New World Translation.
‎So this gives us something to think about
‎because it’s not just a matter of forgiving,
‎but we need to be generous about forgiving.
‎We have to be willing to, as it were, bestow a pardon
‎on someone who really doesn’t deserve that pardon.
‎Now, why should we be interested
‎in developing and working on these two aspects:
‎“putting up with one another” and ‘forgiving freely’?
‎Well, we’ve heard the reasons many times before, haven’t we?
‎The first one, of course, is that Jehovah has forgiven us.
‎If we turn back just one chapter,
‎chapter 2 of Colossians and verse 13,
‎this point is highlighted for us.
‎It says in chapter 2, verse 13:
‎“Furthermore, though you were dead in your trespasses
‎“and in the uncircumcised state of your flesh,
‎“God made you alive together with him.
‎“He kindly forgave us
‎all our trespasses.”
‎So this is the model that Jehovah has given us.
‎It’s true, we sometimes can find some reason
‎why we feel we don’t have to forgive someone else.
‎But remember the illustration Jesus gave
‎of the slave who had the huge debt.
‎If you calculated it in denarius,
‎there were 60 million denarii that he owed;
‎he was forgiven that.
‎Then he went after the other man
‎who owed him just a small amount.
‎But have you ever thought that if you asked that slave,
‎maybe he would say: “Well, it’s true.
‎“I really appreciate having everything forgiven, but I still don’t have any money.
‎“I need some money, so that’s why I wanted to get
‎the other slave to give me the money.”
‎Well, there’s always a reason ​—isn’t there?​—
‎⁠even if it’s a distorted reason
‎as to why we don’t follow Jehovah’s example.
‎But looking back at Colossians 3:​13, what does it say?
‎“If anyone has a cause for complaint against another.”
‎So that gives us a good idea, doesn’t it?
‎The second reason, of course, is that
‎we do need others to forgive us.
‎The very things that annoy us
‎and irritate us in others are sometimes
‎the same things that we do to others.
‎Have you ever noticed that?
‎And how annoying it is when someone points that out to you:
‎“You’re annoyed with that person?
‎Don’t you realize what you do?”
‎Well, that’s something good for us to remember​ —isn’t it?​—
‎the fact that we do need to have others forgive us.
‎And then another reason
‎is that it maintains the peace within the Christian congregation.
‎The Watchtower made a comment on this.
‎It said that in countries where our work is restricted or under ban,
‎many of our brothers have to meet together in smaller groups.
‎And when you do that, you get to know
‎everyone’s weaknesses and idiosyncrasies.
‎It’s so much easier to be annoyed by others
‎when you’re dealing with small groups of persons.
‎The Watchtower then made the comment
‎what good training it is for us now
‎to learn how to put up with one another
‎when we’re in larger groups,
‎because later we may need to worship Jehovah in smaller groups.
‎So it’s good training for us as we keep peace in the congregation.
‎And what can help us?
‎Well, there are many different things that can help us in this regard.
‎The one point in the marginal reference
‎you see there is at 1 Peter 4:​8,
‎and that’s where it tells us we need
‎to “have intense love for one another”​
‎—not just love but “intense love.”
‎And this word “intense” means “full strength.”
‎Literally, it means “to stretch out our love.”
‎So as we come across these things that irritate us, annoy us, in life
‎or if we come across persons who actually do sin against us,
‎what should we keep in mind?
‎“Continue putting up with one another.”
‎‘Continue freely forgiving one another.’

cn.text: ‎请打开圣经
‎翻到歌罗西书3:13
‎我们一起来分析一下这节经文
‎看看耶和华希望我们怎么做
‎歌罗西书3:13说
‎“无论谁有理由对人不满”
‎“都要继续彼此包容”
‎“彼此甘心宽恕”
‎“耶和华怎样甘心宽恕了你们”
‎“你们也要怎样甘心宽恕人”
‎这节经文有很多值得留意的地方
‎帮我们在许多方面做得更好
‎不过  这节经文对我们的要求
‎主要有两点  是什么呢?
‎第一  要“继续彼此包容”
‎第二  要“彼此甘心宽恕”
‎好  让我们先来看看第一点
‎“继续彼此包容”
‎这和第二点有什么不同呢?
‎我们都知道  这里提到的包容
‎不是指包容严重的罪
‎而是要我们包容一些小事
‎就是那些让我们感到生气
‎或心烦的小事
‎我们因为一点小事就开始抱怨
‎可能没什么道理
‎但就是会感到不高兴
‎什么样的小事会让你生气呢?
‎有人总是迟到  你会不高兴吗?
‎或者你不喜欢有人总是到得很早吗?
‎你看不惯有些人说话太直接吗?
‎或者你受不了不爱说话的人
‎很有意思对不对
‎我们竟然就是为这样的事情生气!
‎我记得上世纪70年代
‎诺尔弟兄做过一个精彩的演讲
‎他举了一个很现实的例子
‎在会众里  一个受浸不久的姐妹
‎聚会时总是发表评论
‎另一个姐妹心里可能会想
‎她就不能安静一会儿吗?
‎我们每个人或许都有过类似的经历
‎要是仔细想一下  我们就不得不承认
‎其实自己没有什么正当的理由
‎但就是会生气
‎就像有句话说
‎有时候  给我们带来麻烦的
‎不是眼前的大山
‎而是鞋里的小石子
‎没错  有时候  最容易让我们生气的
‎反而是那些小事儿
‎还记得很多年前
‎我在西萨摩亚的分部办事处工作
‎当时有很多弟兄从国外过来
‎协助那里的建筑工程
‎其中的一个弟兄有一个习惯
‎就是每天早上吃饭前
‎都会跟大家说
‎早上好!
‎一些人觉得他的做法很烦人
‎也许你也有同样的感受
‎那么你一定很喜欢箴言27:14
‎因为这节经文说
‎“在清早大声祝福同胞的”
‎“就等于咒诅他”
‎你也许在心里说  阿们!
‎那个弟兄读过这节经文后
‎就改掉了这个习惯
‎也可能是别人读给他听的
‎不过  我们生别人气的时候
‎不是总能找到支持自己的经文
‎那我们该怎么办呢?
‎经文怎么说呢?
‎要“继续彼此包容”
‎“继续”就意味着要不断这样做
‎我们接着来看看第二点
‎“彼此甘心宽恕”
‎有意思的是  大部分圣经译本
‎都按照《英王钦定本》的译法
‎译作“彼此宽恕”
‎而《圣经新世界译本》说的是
‎“彼此甘心宽恕”
‎理由是  这里被译作“宽恕”的希腊语词
‎不仅包含宽恕的意思
‎还包括“慷慨  乐意付出更多”的意思
‎值得一提的是
‎早在《新世界译本》出版前很久
‎1882年的《守望台》文章里就使用了
‎“彼此甘心宽恕”这个说法
‎我们的确需要仔细想想
‎因为这不是说只要原谅对方就够了
‎同时还要表现慷慨
‎也就是说  即使对方并不值得被原谅
‎我们还是要心甘情愿地原谅别人
‎我们一定要学会
‎“彼此包容”和“甘心宽恕”
‎并努力实践出来
‎为什么呢?
‎我们都知道有很多理由要这么做
‎首要的理由
‎毫无疑问就是耶和华宽恕了我们
‎如果我们把圣经往前翻一章
‎翻到歌罗西书2:13
‎就会看到这个要点
‎经文说
‎“再说  你们从前因为过犯”
‎“因为在肉身上没有受割礼”
‎“而陷于死亡”
‎“上帝却使你们跟基督一同活过来”
‎“他甘心宽恕了我们的一切过犯”
‎这就是耶和华为我们树立的榜样
‎有时  我们确实觉得自己
‎有正当的理由不原谅某个人
‎但是请想想耶稣基督讲过的一个比喻
‎有一个奴隶欠了一大笔债
‎按古罗马银元来计算的话
‎他欠了6000万银元
‎但是王免除了他的债务
‎可是之后他却
‎向一个只欠了他一点钱的人讨债
‎如果你去问那个奴隶
‎你为什么这样做?
‎他可能会回答
‎我确实很感谢王免了我的债
‎但我自己还是没钱啊  我需要钱
‎找欠我钱的人还钱有什么不对吗?
‎我们要是不想向耶和华学习
‎总能找到理由为自己开脱
‎即使是一些歪理
‎可是  歌罗西书3:13告诉我们
‎“无论谁有理由对人不满”
‎“都要继续彼此包容”
‎所以  这已经很清楚了  对吗?
‎要甘心宽恕的第二个理由是
‎我们也需要别人甘心宽恕我们
‎有时候
‎别人做的一些事情让我们受不了
‎但往往这些事情
‎我们自己也做过
‎要是别人向我们指出
‎你受不了那个人吗?
‎你知不知道你自己
‎也做过他那样的事呢?
‎这就更让人受不了了
‎因此  我们要记住
‎我们也需要别人的宽恕
‎此外  还有一个理由
‎就是甘心宽恕能使会众保持和睦
‎《守望台》文章里提到
‎在传道工作受禁止或受限制的国家
‎弟兄姐妹都以小组形式举行聚会
‎这样的话
‎弟兄姐妹会很容易了解
‎彼此的缺点和个性
‎一起聚会的人少
‎互相之间就更加容易产生摩擦
‎《守望台》文章也提到
‎趁着一起聚会的人数还比较多时
‎我们就要学会彼此包容
‎这会是很好的训练
‎因为将来我们都可能要
‎小规模地举行聚会
‎所以  现在就要学会在会众保持和睦
‎我们怎样才能学会呢?
‎当然  有很多方法
‎我们来看一节参考经文
‎彼得前书4:8
‎这里说
‎“要热切地彼此相爱”
‎这里说的不只是要“彼此相爱”
‎而是要“热切地彼此相爱”
‎“热切”这个词有“竭尽全力”的意思
‎字面意思是“扩大我们的爱”
‎所以  不论是让我们心烦的小事
‎还是真的有人做了错事得罪我们
‎我们都要记住
‎要“继续彼此包容”
‎继续“彼此甘心宽恕”

titles.en: Geoffrey W. Jackson: “Continue Putting Up With One Another” (Col. 3:13)

ko.text: ‎창살 틈으로 손을 내밀고 ‎그 형제도 손을 맞잡고
‎세 번의 수감 생활을 통해서 ‎제가 느낄 수 있었던 건
‎그리고 특히 ‘우리 형제들을 통해서 ‎지원을 해 주셨구나’ 하는 걸
‎그곳에서의 생활이 이제 ‎아침에 오전 밥을 먹고 나가서
‎그리고 점심 먹고 와서 또 ‎오후에 300장을 나르는 건데
‎저는 이제 빨리 일을 하기 때문에 ‎한 20분 정도 쉬었다 들어갑니다.
‎그런데 저보다도 힘이 좋고 건장한 ‎박병만 형제가 있었는데
‎이 형제가 대신 가서 ‎최 형제 몫을 해 주는 거예요.
‎진정한 사랑, 숨은 사랑, ‎그 사랑을 나타내는 것을 보고 제가
‎그 형제들이 눈빛으로 저를 ‎감싸 주고 또 말로도 감싸 주고
‎따뜻하게 격려해 주고 그러한 격려 속에서 ‎제가 큰 감동을 받고
‎이곳에서 구할 수 있는 약 가지고는 ‎치료가 잘 안 되었었어요.
‎즙을 만들어 가지고 몇 날 며칠 ‎저를 정성껏 그 즙으로

‎거기 들어가 보기도 하고 ‎또 앉아 보기도 하고

en.text: ‎When I was 21 years old,
‎I was sent to prison
‎in the Nonsan military training center
‎because I refused to serve in the military.
‎The soldier working in the military prison came
‎and started to beat me, and he beat me relentlessly.
‎It was late December 1975.
‎Four of the brothers were put
‎into standing solitary confinement cells
‎called dokgeochang.
‎It literally feels like you are in a coffin.
‎The outside temperature dropped
‎to minus 13 degrees Celsius (8°F),
‎and cold air seeped out from the wet walls.
‎The brothers couldn’t lay down to sleep, so they had to crouch,
‎and I could hear them groaning all night.
‎I extended my hand through the iron bars
‎to the brother in the cell next to mine, and he did the same.
‎We held hands
‎and encouraged each other to stay strong.
‎My health condition wasn’t really good
‎while serving my prison sentence.
‎I weighed about 47 kilograms (103 lbs),
‎and without my family’s support,
‎I was mentally and physically weak.
‎Under these extremely difficult circumstances,
‎there were times I wasn’t able to eat at all.
‎During those times, the brothers provided me
‎with porridge —which was easy to digest—
‎warm clothing, and a sleeping bag for the winter.
‎I could really feel their love.
‎Having been sent to prison three times,
‎I truly feel that Jehovah showed interest in me
‎and took care of me just as he promised at 1 Peter 5:7.
‎He especially supported me through my brothers
‎when I was facing difficulties.
‎A day in the prison started
‎with us eating breakfast
‎and then moving 300 bricks.
‎After lunch, we would have to carry another 300 bricks.
‎Because I usually finished my work early,
‎I had a 20-minute break before going back in.
‎However, this brother named Park Byung-Man
‎who was much stronger and bigger than I was
‎carried bricks all day long.
‎I found out later that Park Byung-Man
‎was carrying Choi Sung-Kyu’s share
‎of bricks because of his frail health.
‎This kind of brotherly love really moved me
‎to start studying the Bible.
‎I got baptized a year later
‎in April of 1977 in the Anyang Prison.
‎After getting baptized,
‎my mother passed away,
‎and two months before being released,
‎my father passed away as well.
‎So that time was especially difficult for me.
‎But the brothers encouraged me
‎with their warm words and kind gestures.
‎Their encouragement really touched me
‎and helped me to endure until I was released.
‎One time, I had a severe stomachache.
‎The symptoms were not getting any better
‎with the medication I was given,
‎so I was having a very difficult time.
‎One day, we were served some vegetables
‎as a side dish
‎and one brother crushed
‎and squeezed the vegetables to make juice for me.
‎He cared for me that way for several days.
‎I really would like to see that self-sacrificing
‎and loving brother once again.
‎At the time, none of our publications
‎other than the Bible were allowed into the prison.
‎Of course, that included our songbook.
‎The brothers memorized
‎the lyrics from the songbook,
‎and they would write them down.
‎Also, there were some songs
‎that were sung at the regional convention.
‎Songs like . . .
‎or
‎We sang them silently together even in this isolated place.
‎It was a great source of encouragement
‎to share the love among our fellow brothers.
‎I remember this encouraging scripture
‎from 1 Corinthians 10:13.
‎It says that Jehovah ‘does not let us be tempted
‎‘beyond what we can bear and will make the way out
‎so we may endure it.’
‎Although there were many challenges, I was convinced
‎that Jehovah would always
‎make a way out through our fellow brothers.
‎Even though 40 years have passed,
‎when we look back at those days, the memories are still fresh
‎and we are moved to tears at times.
‎So to make a meaningful trip
‎out of our 40 years of friendship,
‎all the friends who went through the same trials
‎decided to visit the headquarters in the United States together.
‎It’s really refreshing to be here with everyone again today.
‎It feels like I’m taking a field trip.
‎I was especially moved to tears
‎when I saw our old prison uniforms
‎there in the museum
‎at world headquarters displayed in the neutrality section.
‎While on the tour, the brothers sat
‎and lay down on the floor inside the dokgeochang
‎and we were able to reflect on the times
‎we spent together in prison.
‎Our gratitude to Jehovah
‎for giving us such loyal friends was renewed.

cn.text: ‎‎‪我21岁时  因为拒服兵役
‎‎‪被关进了论山军事训练中心的监狱
‎‎‪一个执勤的士兵走过来
‎‎‪二话不说就开始不停地打我
‎‎‪他狠狠地打了我一顿
‎‎‪4个弟兄被分别关进了禁闭室
‎‎‪那是一个叫做独居仓的狭小空间
‎‎‪人在里面就好像进了棺材一样
‎‎‪外面的气温只有零下13度
‎‎‪冷空气会从潮湿的墙壁里透进来
‎‎‪弟兄们不能躺下睡觉  只能蜷缩着
‎‎‪整个晚上
‎‎‪我都能听到弟兄们痛苦的呻吟声
‎‎‪我把手从铁窗伸出去
‎‎‪隔壁牢房的弟兄也把手伸过来
‎‎‪我们紧紧握住对方的手
‎‎‪鼓励彼此一定要坚持住
‎‎‪在监狱服刑期间  我的身体非常不好
‎‎‪体重大概只有47公斤
‎‎‪再加上没有家人在身边
‎‎‪我身体很虚弱  精神状态也非常不好
‎‎‪严重的时候  我甚至一点儿东西也吃不下
‎‎‪那些日子  弟兄们会特意为我准备一些粥
‎‎‪给我保暖的衣服
‎‎‪冬天还会给我睡袋御寒
‎‎‪他们的爱心让我特别感动
‎‎‪我先后三次入狱
‎‎‪那时  我真的感觉到
‎‎‪耶和华特别关心我  照顾我
‎‎‪就像他在彼得前书5:7里承诺的那样
‎‎‪在我遇到困难时
‎‎‪他总是通过弟兄们给我帮助
‎‎‪在监狱时
‎‎‪每天早饭过后  我们就要出去搬砖
‎‎‪每人要搬300块
‎‎‪午饭后  还得再搬300块
‎‎‪我一般可以提前搬完
‎‎‪所以每次有大概20分钟的休息时间
‎‎‪当时有个叫朴炳万的弟兄
‎‎‪他块头比我大  也比我强壮
‎‎‪可是他却整天都在搬砖  没有休息
‎‎‪后来我才知道
‎‎‪原来他在帮另一个名叫崔成圭的弟兄搬砖
‎‎‪因为那位弟兄身体很虚弱
‎‎‪他们之间的弟兄之爱深深打动了我
‎‎‪于是我就开始学习圣经了
‎‎‪一年后  也就是1977年4月
‎‎‪我在安养监狱受浸了
‎‎‪后来  我突然收到了母亲去世的消息
‎‎‪接着  在我还剩两个月就要出狱的时候
‎‎‪父亲也去世了
‎‎‪那段时间对我来说真的非常不容易
‎‎‪弟兄们陪在我身边
‎‎‪用温暖的话语和亲切的举动
‎‎‪鼓励我  扶持我
‎‎‪我从他们得到很大的力量
‎‎‪能够继续保持忍耐  直到出狱
‎‎‪有一次  我的胃痛得很厉害
‎‎‪虽然我吃了监狱提供的药
‎‎‪但还是不见任何好转
‎‎‪我真的特别难受
‎‎‪那时  监狱的伙食里会有些蔬菜
‎‎‪一位弟兄就把这些蔬菜捣碎
‎‎‪做成蔬菜汁给我喝
‎‎‪他这样照顾了我好几天
‎‎‪想到他自我牺牲的爱
‎‎‪还有真挚的弟兄之情
‎‎‪我真希望能再次见到这位弟兄
‎‎‪那时  除了圣经
‎‎‪别的出版物都不允许带进监狱
‎‎‪当然  这也包括诗歌本
‎‎‪弟兄们凭着记忆
‎‎‪把诗歌本里的一些歌词写了下来
‎‎‪我们还记得当时区域大会一起唱的歌
‎‎‪比如
‎‎‪还有
‎‎‪虽然被孤立起来
‎‎‪但我们还是能聚在一起  低声唱诗
‎‎‪我们感受到了彼此间的弟兄之爱
‎‎‪这带给我们很大的鼓励
‎‎‪我记得一节很鼓励我的经文
‎‎‪就是哥林多前书10:13
‎‎‪经文说
‎‎‪耶和华必不让我们受引诱
‎‎‪超过我们能忍受的
‎‎‪他一定会打开出路  让我们能忍耐得住
‎‎‪尽管当时处境艰难  但我一直深信
‎‎‪耶和华会通过弟兄们打开出路
‎‎‪40年过去了
‎‎‪狱中的经历仍旧历历在目
‎‎‪我时常还会感动得热泪盈眶
‎‎‪为了纪念我们40年的深厚友谊
‎‎‪曾经一起在狱中经历考验的弟兄们决定
‎‎‪踏上这次非常有意义的旅程
‎‎‪一起去参观美国世界总部
‎‎‪能够再次跟大家相聚
‎‎‪而且是一起参观总部  实在令人振奋
‎‎‪我真的特别开心！
‎‎‪在总部展览的中立区
‎‎‪展出了我们当年的囚服
‎‎‪看到那些囚服时  我不禁掉下泪来
‎‎‪参观总部时
‎‎‪弟兄们在展出的独居仓里坐了坐  躺了躺
‎‎‪曾在监狱里共渡患难的那段岁月
‎‎‪又浮现在我们眼前
‎‎‪想到耶和华赐给我们这些忠贞的朋友
‎‎‪我的心里再一次充满了感激

title: 빅토르 빈터: 선은 악보다 더 강합니다

ko.text: ‎수용소에 있는 우리 형제들에겐 ‎영적인 것이 최우선 순위였습니다.
‎한 주에 한 번이 아니라 ‎매일매일, 날마다 모였습니다.
‎그러다 보니, 세상적인 생각을 할 ‎틈이 전혀 없었습니다.
‎노래를 부를 때, 우리는 ‎당직 감독관들이 있는 건물 근처에서
‎그런 식으로 우린 누군가 다가오기 ‎전에 흩어질 수 있었죠.
‎아주 흥미로웠던 건 수용소 안에서 ‎우리가 노래를 불렀다는 겁니다.
‎우리의 청중은 바깥에 담 너머 ‎나무 위에 앉아 있었죠.
‎바로 감독관과 교도관의 자녀들이 ‎우리의 합창을 듣고 있었던 겁니다.
‎심문 책임자가 제가 있는 감방으로 ‎오더니 이렇게 말하더군요.
‎너한텐 아무것도 남지 않을 거야. ‎가족도 자녀도 말이지.”
‎현재, 제게는 가족도 있고 ‎아내도 있고 아이들도 있습니다.
‎여호와께 찬양의 노래를 부를 때 ‎저는 이루 말할 수 없이 기쁩니다.

en.text: ‎On July 24, 1958,
‎I got baptized; and on November 5, 1958,
‎I already got arrested for refusal to do military service.
‎The second time I was convicted was again
‎for refusal to do military service.
‎The next court trial took place in 1963.
‎I got seven years ​—⁠and five years exile.
‎They added three years
‎that I did not serve for refusal to go to the army.
‎I was taken to Mordovia.
‎This was the first camp where all believers were put,
‎amongst them 360 of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
‎The detentions were very strict
‎because around this time the governments
‎and party politics changed.
‎They decided that prisoners must suffer hunger.
‎The food rations were cut.
‎This was very difficult, very difficult, I must say.
‎And the winters can be cold.
‎Even in March, it could get as cold
‎as 35 degrees Celsius ​—⁠minus 35 (-31°F).
‎Spiritual things were for all of us
‎​—⁠the brothers in this camp​— ⁠top priority.
‎First of all, all 360 people
‎were divided into four congregations,
‎and every congregation was divided into groups.
‎Every congregation had responsible brothers as overseers
‎and so had every group.
‎We conducted the study not just once a week,
‎but we conducted the study every day,
‎every day.
‎And brothers took this very seriously.
‎We had no time for any worldly thoughts.
‎Every Saturday and Sunday,
‎we had a very powerful choir​ —⁠men’s voices.
‎When we were singing, we stationed guards
‎near the oversight house where supervisors were on duty.
‎And if one of them came out, it was signaled
‎from one brother to the next so that if he or they came closer,
‎we would already be gone.
‎But the most interesting thing
‎was that we were singing in the zone.
‎We were the prisoners,
‎but our listeners were outside.
‎They were sitting up in the trees
‎​—⁠the children of the supervisors,
‎officers, and guards.
‎And they were listening to our choir.
‎All together during that time,
‎I was in seven prison camps.
‎I spent about 13 years there
‎and another 5 years in exile in Siberia.
‎But when I was convicted the last time,
‎the head of the interrogation department came into my cell and said,
‎“Viktor, when you finish all your prison terms,
‎you will have nothing at all​ —⁠no family, no children.”
‎I smiled at him and asked:
‎“How do you know this, Citizen Lieutenant Colonel?
‎I don’t know it either, but I do trust in Jehovah.”
‎Today, I do have a family
‎and do have my wife and my children.
‎We continue to serve Jehovah.
‎And my greatest joy
‎is when my six-year-old granddaughter
‎stands next to me in the Kingdom Hall
‎and sings songs that praise Jehovah.
‎Well, to make it simple, I would put it this way:
‎Preserve your love for Jehovah and for your brothers.
‎Joy in Jehovah’s service ​—⁠never lose it!
‎We will not fear anything bad
‎​—⁠neither cold nor hunger​—⁠
‎nothing.

cn.text: ‎我在1958年7月24日受了浸
‎同年的11月5日
‎我就因为拒服兵役被逮捕了
‎后来  我又一次被判刑了
‎还是因为拒服兵役
‎1963年  我又经历了一次庭审
‎因为拒绝参军
‎我被判了7年监禁  5年流放
‎其实  他们还判了我3年
‎不过后来没有执行
‎我被押到了莫尔多瓦
‎这是第一次政府把所有有信仰的人
‎都关在一个集中营里
‎当中有360名是耶和华见证人
‎那时正赶上执政党的政策发生了改变
‎他们决定对囚犯采取饥饿政策
‎所以我们当时非常艰苦
‎食物供应大大减少了
‎我不得不说
‎那段时间真的非常非常不容易
‎而且那里冬天非常冷
‎甚至到了三月
‎气温还会低到35摄氏度
‎是零下35度啊!
‎对我们这些被囚的弟兄来说
‎崇拜耶和华是最重要的事
‎我们把360个人分成了4群会众
‎每群会众又分成了不同的小组
‎每群会众都有带头的弟兄担任监督
‎每个小组也是这样
‎我们不是每周一次举行聚会
‎而是每一天都聚会
‎每一天!
‎弟兄们都非常重视聚会
‎我们没有时间为其它事情忧虑
‎每周六日  弟兄们都一起唱诗歌
‎歌声嘹亮有力
‎当我们唱诗的时候
‎会有弟兄在警卫室附近把风
‎如果有警卫出来
‎弟兄就会发出暗号
‎一个一个往下传
‎这样  等那些警卫过来的时候
‎我们就已经离开了
‎我们是囚犯  在集中营里面唱歌
‎但有意思的是
‎在围墙外面  竟然有人听我们唱歌
‎就是那些军官和警卫的孩子们
‎他们会爬到高高的树上
‎坐在那儿听我们唱歌
‎那些年  我一共在7个集中营待过
‎我被关了大约13年
‎还被流放到西伯利亚5年
‎我最后一次被判刑时
‎审讯室的负责人到我的牢房来说
‎维克托  等服刑期满了
‎你一定会一无所有
‎你不会有家庭  也不会有孩子
‎我笑了笑  问他
‎你怎么知道呢  中校先生?
‎其实  我也不知道
‎但我信赖我的上帝耶和华
‎今天  我有了自己的家庭
‎我有妻子  也有孩子
‎我们一直事奉耶和华
‎我最快乐的事情
‎就是在王国聚会所里
‎看到我6岁的外孙女站在身边
‎和我一起唱诗赞美耶和华
‎回顾一生  我想说
‎要保护你跟耶和华的关系
‎也要爱弟兄姐妹!
‎要喜乐地事奉耶和华
‎千万不要失去喜乐!
‎寒冷也好  饥饿也好
‎无论是什么糟糕的情况
‎我们都不畏惧

title: 디미트리스와 아기스: 이제 우린 진정한 형제입니다!

ko.text: ‎이제 더 이상 ‎아버지를 볼 수 없다는 사실을
‎그곳에서 처음으로 가두 증거를 ‎하고 있는 형제를 만났는데,
‎그리고 이해가 안 되는 점이 있으면 ‎노트에 다 적었습니다.
‎해리는 제가 질문을 할 때마다 ‎성경에서 답을 찾아 보여 줬고,
‎몇 달이 흘러갔고, ‎그 동안 전 공장 일에 매여 있었어요.
‎전 당국의 요구를 다 거절했는데, ‎압력이 점점 더 심해졌습니다.
‎그런 일들을 겪고 있을 때, ‎디미트리스 형이 찾아왔습니다.
‎제가 일어나는 일들을 이해할 ‎수 있게 도와주려고 했습니다.
‎그분은 제가 진정한 삶의 목표와 ‎희망을 가질 수 있게 돕고 계셨습니다.
‎침례를 받던 날, 전 여호와와 ‎점점 가까워지고 있단 걸 느꼈죠.
‎이 일을 하면서, 여러 해 전에 ‎형과 연구하면서 느꼈던

en.text: ‎My father was a self-made factory owner.
‎He started a business working with rubber and plastics,
‎and we led a financially comfortable way of life.
‎But in the middle of the 1970’s,
‎things started going badly with his work.
‎For this reason,
‎he fell into a depression, and he committed suicide.
‎This was a great shock.
‎I went to the wall and wrote the words
‎“He lives.”
‎I didn’t want to believe that from that day on,
‎I wouldn’t see my father again.
‎At the age of about ten, I began to develop
‎strong antireligious tendencies.
‎And later, at the age of 17,
‎I also expressed them by participating
‎in the most important incident
‎of the student movement against the military junta
‎that was prevailing in Greece and ruling the country.
‎I became a member of the Communist Party.
‎I went to Santorini and started a business.
‎I opened a bar.
‎Of course, all this included unsavory things
‎like immorality, drugs,
‎and plenty of alcohol.
‎A few months later, I left to study in Germany.
‎It was the first time I met a brother engaging in street work.
‎People would approach him,
‎and some would swear; some even spat at him.
‎It impressed me immensely
‎how he stood calmly and accepted this treatment.
‎We had interesting conversations.
‎My studies ended, and I returned to Greece
‎to take on the responsibility of the factory.
‎When I finished my studies in Germany,
‎I left with a sense of deep respect
‎for Jehovah’s Witnesses.
‎The influence of my friends
‎led me to go into the military,
‎and there I saw a huge amount of corruption.
‎The hope I had that we humans
‎would be able to succeed without external help
‎—without God— began to collapse,
‎and then the things I had heard
‎from Jehovah’s Witnesses suddenly came to my mind.
‎The same afternoon, I sought out a family friend,
‎the mother of a childhood friend, named Lily.
‎I said to her, “Please give me a Bible
‎and some Bible study publications because I want to study them.”
‎I read everywhere,
‎and anything that I didn’t understand,
‎I wrote down in a notebook.
‎I got to the point, in just a few days,
‎where I had written down 80 to 90 questions.
‎Harry impressed me
‎because every time I asked him a question,
‎he gave me the answer from the Bible.
‎That convinced me that I’d found the truth.
‎So in that moment,
‎I decided to leave the military and to quit smoking.
‎A few months passed by,
‎where I was occupied mostly with the factory,
‎until I recognized
‎that for me to make progress in the truth,
‎I had to sell my shares in the factory.
‎And on July 7, 1984, I was baptized.
‎The authorities —the police, the mayor,
‎the health inspectors— began to demand money
‎so that I could keep the bar open.
‎I refused all the things they asked of me,
‎and so the war became harder
‎until one night when I went to open the door to enter my home;
‎I heard a tramping from behind,
‎I tried to turn and see, and as I turned,
‎I was hit in the face.
‎During that time,
‎when all of this was happening, my brother Dimitris arrived.
‎As brothers, we never really had a relationship.
‎When he came to Santorini and began to talk to me
‎and help me understand what was happening to me,
‎I realized that this was a different Dimitris.
‎I said to him, “I want us to start studying the Bible together.”
‎I had the Bible with me almost everywhere I went
‎so that I could read it.
‎I realized that Jehovah was helping me to understand what I was living for.
‎He was helping me to understand
‎that I could have a real goal, a purpose,
‎and a hope.
‎On the day of my baptism, I felt that I was drawing closer to Jehovah.
‎I felt like my smile went from ear to ear.
‎And now with Lydia,
‎I have the great joy of serving
‎in the Romany territory.
‎We enjoy very nice Bible studies.
‎It is truly something
‎that shows you Jehovah’s love,
‎interest, and affection
‎—things that I had felt
‎many years ago when I studied with my brother.
‎Today, my brother and I love each other very much.
‎It is a relationship characterized
‎by brotherly love
‎as it is expressed in the Bible.
‎We are very close to each other.
‎This is really a change.
‎Now we are truly brothers!

cn.text: ‎我父亲开了一家工厂
‎主要经营橡胶和塑料
‎生意做得还不错
‎那时我们的生活条件很好!
‎不过  到了一九七几年
‎生意越来越差
‎父亲因此变得消沉  抑郁
‎最后竟然自杀了
‎这对我来说简直是晴天霹雳
‎从那天起  我再也见不到他了
‎我无法接受这个事实
‎于是我在墙上写下四个大字
‎“他还活着”
‎从10岁起
‎我就对宗教特别反感
‎17岁  我又加入了一个反政府的学生组织
‎当时  希腊正处于军政府统治时期
‎很多学生组织起来反对他们的统治
‎我成了其中一员
‎后来我还加入了共产党
‎后来  我去了圣托里尼做生意
‎在那里开了一家酒吧
‎可以想象  这种地方总是少不了吸毒
‎酗酒和性不道德的事
‎几个月后  我去德国留学
‎有一天  我看见一个耶和华见证人
‎在做街头见证
‎路过的人  有的骂他
‎有的朝他吐唾沫
‎但他却保持忍耐
‎一直心平气和地站在那里
‎这给我留下了深刻的印象
‎于是  我上前去和他聊了起来
‎我们聊得不错
‎在德国留学的那段时间
‎我对耶和华见证人有很好的印象
‎也非常尊重他们
‎学业结束后  我就回到了希腊
‎开始接手父亲留下的生意
‎后来  受一些朋友的影响
‎我参军了
‎没想到部队里充满了贪污腐败的事情
‎我曾经以为
‎人类不需要依靠上帝也能成功
‎但是这样的想法大错特错
‎那时  我突然想起了
‎从耶和华见证人那里听到的圣经知识
‎当天下午  我就去找一个朋友的妈妈
‎她是耶和华见证人
‎我告诉她我想学习圣经
‎也向她要了一本圣经
‎和一些学习圣经的书刊
‎我很喜欢这些书
‎走到哪儿都在读
‎不明白的问题
‎我就记在笔记本上
‎短短几天时间
‎我就写下了八九十个问题
‎哈利是我的圣经老师
‎我提出的每一个问题
‎他都用圣经帮我找到答案
‎这一点让我确信
‎我学到的是真理
‎于是  我决定离开部队
‎也决心戒烟
‎后来的几个月
‎我又开始忙家里的生意
‎这占据了我大部分时间
‎我意识到
‎如果想要在属灵方面进步
‎我需要放弃这门生意
‎1984年7月7日  我受浸了
‎想要继续开酒吧
‎就得交很多费用
‎警察  市长  还有卫生检查部门
‎都来找我要钱
‎但是我拒绝了他们
‎他们就疯狂地向我施压
‎一天晚上  我正要开门进屋时
‎突然听见背后传来一阵脚步声
‎我转过身去看
‎结果脸被狠狠地打了一拳
‎那段时间  我的生活真的糟透了
‎也正是那段时间
‎哥哥季米特里斯过来看我
‎在那之前  我们兄弟俩没什么来往
‎但这一次季米特里斯特意过来看我
‎跟我一起聊聊
‎还帮助我看出
‎自己的生活出了什么问题
‎我感觉到  他和以前不一样了
‎我跟他说  我想跟你一起学习圣经
‎于是  不管去哪里
‎我都会带着圣经
‎好随时阅读
‎在耶和华的帮助下
‎我渐渐明白了
‎活着的意义到底是什么
‎也可以追求真正的人生目标
‎同时对未来充满希望
‎在我受浸的那一天
‎我感觉  自己跟耶和华的关系
‎变得更亲密了
‎我高兴得合不拢嘴
‎现在  我和妻子莉迪娅一起
‎非常喜乐地在罗姆语地区服务
‎也找到了很多对圣经感兴趣的人
‎这样的经历帮助我看出
‎上帝充满爱心  温情和关怀
‎这让我想起许多年前
‎哥哥教我学习圣经时的那种感受
‎现在  我们兄弟俩真的彼此相爱
‎这就是圣经所说的弟兄之爱
‎我们俩的关系和以前完全不一样了
‎现在我们是真正的好兄弟了
