en.text: Spain is a land of castles.
From the mountains of central Spain
to the Mediterranean coast, castles dominate the landscape.
But there is one castle —the Castle of Santa Catalina—
that played a unique part in the history of Jehovah’s Witnesses in Spain.
This castle that guards the entrance
to the harbor of Cádiz, in southern Spain,
became a military prison over two centuries ago.
And this fortress
tested the faith of around 300 Spanish Witnesses.
The battle began in the 1960’s when Spain was ruled
by General Franco, a military dictator.
Franco wanted all Spanish men to serve the fatherland,
and this meant military service.
But in Spain, there were Jehovah’s Witnesses
whose conscience said no.
So this castle became a battleground
where Franco’s military regime fought
to stamp out the Christian consciences of those young Witnesses.
But times have changed in Spain.
The city of Cádiz has organized an exhibition
to salute the sacrifice made by those valiant Witnesses.
Over 40 years after their release,
some of those conscientious objectors have returned to Cádiz
to attend this exhibition.
At the inauguration,
the mayor described them as citizens who spoke up
and who presented arguments against the injustice
—arguments based on peace, freedom,
and, above all, their conscience.
Those who spent years of their lives behind bars
have vivid memories
of the times when this castle was their prison.
I think one of the greatest challenges
was never knowing
if we would be granted our freedom.
Our first sentence
was for three years.
And since we still refused to enlist in the military,
we were then sentenced again for another lengthy period.
So it seemed as if we had a life sentence.
We organized daily activities
to keep us busy.
Mornings, we worked at our trades
to earn a little money.
Afternoons, we set aside for spiritual activities.
Our preaching was done mainly by writing letters.
And in this way, some of us could even pioneer.
A few people did reply to our letters,
and we were thrilled to hear that some of them accepted the truth.
Of course, we also preached to other prisoners,
and a few of them became baptized Witnesses.
We also studied the Bible thoroughly,
both individually and as a group,
which proved vital in building us up spiritually.
At first, we had to study our literature secretly,
but later the guards
allowed us to have the Bible and other publications.
As our numbers grew,
all the Witnesses were kept together
in the same place —in the same barracks—
so we could organize meetings.
We even held assemblies, including the Biblical dramas.
And we loved
singing Kingdom songs.
These songs really lifted up our spirits.
We really felt Jehovah’s loving care when the brothers came to visit us.
We even had a special visit from Brother Grant Suiter
of the Governing Body,
but there were also other visits that we really looked forward to.
Many of the brothers endured years of separation from their families
and fiancées.
This was a real test.
But these faithful sisters
wholeheartedly supported their neutral stand.
Those were years that molded me spiritually.
I studied the Bible as I had never done before.
I developed skills as a public speaker and as an overseer.
Above all, it was a time in my life
when I learned to rely totally on Jehovah.
Thanks to my fervent prayers, he became my closest friend
and he never let me down.
That was priceless.
The firm stand of those Witnesses
gave a powerful testimony in Cádiz and throughout Spain.
The run-down military prison
that once tested their faith
has been restored.
It is now a tourist attraction
and a cultural center.
But while the castle has changed,
the faith of those valiant Witnesses has not.
The castle certainly tested them,
but they fought a fine fight for the faith.
And with Jehovah’s help, they won the battle.
Forty years later,
their victory is still giving a witness
to Jehovah’s name.

他们为信仰打了美好的一仗
40年过去了
他们的胜利仍然为耶和华的圣名
做着美好的见证

title: M. 스티븐 레트: "사람들로 된 선물"을 감사히 여기십시오

ko.text: ‎특별히 고른 멋진 선물을 받고 기뻐하지 않을 사람이 누가 있을까요?
‎멋진 색깔의 품위 있는 100퍼센트 실크 넥타이를 받는다면
‎예쁘고 우아한 실크 스카프를 선물로 받으면 어떠시겠습니까?
‎선물을 준 사람은 자기가 준 선물을 그런 식으로 사용하는 걸 보면서
‎전파하고 제자 삼는 중요한 일에서 솔선하는 사람들로 주셨습니다.
‎결코 다시 반복되지 않을 이 일을 함께 합시다.”
‎양 떼에게 영양가 있는 영적 음식을 먹이죠.
‎열심히 일하는 “사람들로 된 선물”을 어떻게 여기라고 말씀하실까요?
‎네, 우린 그런 형제들을 “존경하라”는 권고를 받고 있죠.
‎깊은 존경과 감사를 어떻게 나타낼 수 있습니까?
‎첫 번째 방법은 마음을 다해 협조하는 것입니다.
‎이 성구는 우리가 어느 정도나 협조해야 하는지 알려주는데요,
‎네, 분명 우리는 그들이 하는 말에 따르고 순종해야 합니다.
‎하지만 여호와께선 두 가지가 다 필요하다고 하십니다.
‎어떤 일을 처리하는 가장 좋고 효율적인 방법이 아니더라도
‎사실상, 이 예는 다소 과장된 면이 있지만,
‎장로의 회가 왕국회관 외벽을 새로 페인트칠 하기로 결정하고,
‎모든 전도인에게 폭이 5센티인 작은 붓을 주어 칠을 하게 합니다.
‎전도인들이 모두 화를 내면서 장로들의 결정에 불만을 토로합니다.
‎그 결과, 몇 사람이 다른 사람들을 부추기면서
‎페이트 롤러를 써서, 칠을 해야 된다고 주장합니다.
‎그런가 하면, 또 다른 전도인들은 사람들을 설득하면서,
‎돈을 주고 페인트 스프레이를 빌려서 싹 뿌려야 한다고 말합니다.
‎아예 애초에 왕국회관에 페인트 칠을 할 필요조차 없다는 사람들까지 있습니다!
‎전도인들은 걸려 넘어져 진리를 떠날 수도 있죠.
‎반대로 모두 겸손히 장로들의 말에 따르면서 이렇게 생각하면 어떨까요?
‎‘성경에서 5센티짜리 붓을 쓰지 말라고 한 것도 아닌데 못 할게 뭐 있어.
‎전도인들은 좋은 교제를 오랫동안 마음껏 즐기게 될 것입니다.
‎다소 과장하기는 했지만, 이 예의 요점은 무엇일까요?
‎일을 어떻게 하는지 보다 훨씬 중요하다는 것입니다.
‎여호와께서는 바로 그런 태도를 크게 축복하실 것입니다!
‎두 번째로 이 소중한 형제들에게 깊은 감사를 나타내는 방법은
‎장로인 바울이 형제들에게 자신을 위해 무엇을 해 달라고 권고하는지
‎바울은 다른 사람이 자신을 위해 기도해 줄 때,
‎여러분도 개인적 기도를 드릴 때 정기적으로 여호와께
‎그것은 열심히 일하는 장로들에게 감사하고 있음을 잘 보여 주는 것입니다.
‎그럼 세 번째로 깊은 감사를 나타낼 수 있는 방법을 생각해 보죠.
‎여러분은 정기적으로 여러 장로를 찾아가 이런 식으로 말합니까?
‎고마움을 표현하지 않는 전도인들도 계신 것 같습니다.
‎그것은 그들의 수고를 당연히 여긴다는 표시가 될 수도 있지 않을까요?
‎안 하다가 처음으로 감사를 표현하면 장로들이 깜짝 놀랄진 모르지만,
‎“마땅히 받아야 할 자들에게 [이러한] 선을 베풀기를” 주저하지 마시기 바랍니다.
‎네가 선을 베풀어야 할 자들에게 선을 베풀기를 주저하지 마라.”
‎그들을 칭찬하고 싶은 마음이 더 많이 생길 것입니다.
‎많은 장로는 가장이기 때문에 가족을 부양하기 위해
‎자녀가 있다면, 아버지로서 시간을 내고 관심을 기울여야 하죠.
‎건전한 오락을 위해서도 시간을 계획할 필요가 있을 것입니다.
‎가장 중요한 점으로 가장은 가족을 영적으로 돌봅니다.
‎가족과 함께 야외 봉사를 하고, 집회에도 데려가죠.
‎우리 중 많은 사람도 이와 같은 일을 할 책임이 있긴 하지만,
‎장로들은 이 외에도 많은 부가적인 책임들을 맡고 있습니다.
‎그리고 그들이 회중을 위해 하는 많은 수고는 흔히
‎일례로, 장로가 집회 때 연설하는 걸 보셨죠.
‎그가 오랜 시간을 들여 연설을 준비한 것이죠.
‎여러분은 평일 집회의 학생 과제를 준비하는 데 시간이
‎어떤 장로는 연설을 매주, 하나 이상 하기도 하죠.
‎그렇게 연설 경험을 쌓는 건 분명 유익하지만,
‎변하지 않는 사실은 좋은 연설을 하는 덴 많은 노력이 든다는 겁니다.
‎양치는 방문도 해야 하고, 사법 문제를 다룰 때도 있습니다.
‎장로들은 왕국회관이나 지부 시설을 건축하는 일을 돕느라
‎이 밖에도 정말 셀 수 없이 많은 일들을 수행하고 있습니다.
‎우리가 보는 건 고작 해야 빙산의 일각일 뿐입니다.
‎사도 바울은 자신을 가리켜, “음료 제물처럼 부어지고 있다”고 했죠.
‎음료 제물을 제단에 부으면 완전히 증발해 버립니다.
‎이 모든 점을 기억한다면 우린 열심히 일하는 장로들에게
‎자주 진심 어린 칭찬을 하게 될 것입니다.
‎깊이 감사한다는 걸 나타낼 수 있는 방법들을 살펴보았습니다.
‎첫 번째는 마음을 다해 그들에게 협조하는 것이었고,
‎앞서 말한 실크 넥타이나 실크 스카프를 받고서
‎신발 닦는 데 사용하는 감사할 줄 모르는 사람과 우리가
‎“사람들로 된 선물”에 대한 우리의 사랑과 존경과 감사를,
‎여호와와 예수 앞에서 증명할 수 있을 것입니다!

en.text: The theme for this month’s program is
“Appreciating Our ‘Gifts in Men.’”
Who of us does not enjoy being given
a fine, well-chosen gift?
For example, you brothers,
do you not take pleasure in receiving
a colorful but tasteful,
100 percent silk tie?
Or, you sisters, do you not delight in being given
an exquisite, charming silk scarf?
But what if you took that silk tie
or silk scarf
and used it to polish your shoes?
How do you think the giver of your gift would feel
if he saw you using his gift in that way?
Obviously, it would be misuse
and disrespect for the gift and would insult the giver.
What is the point of our illustration?
Well, Jehovah and Jesus have given us
a fine, well-chosen gift in the form of the elders.
But as we will discuss,
all of us must make sure
that we always show appreciation and respect
for this divine provision.
Please turn to Ephesians 4:8,
and let’s read about this gift
that Jehovah and Jesus have given us.
It reads:
“For it says:
“‘When he ascended on high
“‘he carried away captives;
he gave gifts in men.’”
You notice, by means of Jesus’ perfect integrity,
Jesus conquered Satan and his world.
As a world conqueror,
figuratively He has plundered captives
and has given them as gifts to the congregations.
How useful are these “gifts in men”?
Well, please look at verses 11 and 12 for the answer:
“And he gave some as apostles,
“some as prophets,
“some as evangelizers,
“some as shepherds and teachers,
“with a view to the readjustment of the holy ones,
“for ministerial work,
to build up the body of the Christ.”
Notice, they would be “evangelizers”
—taking the lead
in the all-important preaching and disciple-making work.
They do not simply say to the publishers,
“Go in the preaching work.”
They say: “Come. Come with us.
Let’s work together in this never-to-be-repeated work.”
They’re also “shepherds”
—protecting the flock from Satan
the “murderer,” “serpent,” “dragon,” and “lion.”
Additionally, they are “teachers”
—feeding the flock with nourishing spiritual food.
But now we ask,
How does Jehovah tell us
that we should feel about these hardworking “gifts in men”?
Let’s go to 1 Thessalonians chapter 5,
and let’s get the answer.
At 1 Thessalonians chapter 5,
beginning in verse number 12,
notice what Jehovah says:
“Now we request you, brothers,
“to show respect
“for those who are working hard among you
“and presiding over you in the Lord
“and admonishing you;
“and to give them extraordinary consideration
“in love because of their work.
Be peaceable with one another.”
Notice, we’re told to “show respect”
for these dear brothers.
But now, let’s move to a vital question,
How can we show, demonstrate,
that we do deeply respect
and appreciate these dear brothers?
The first way:
by wholeheartedly cooperating with them.
Please turn to Hebrews 13:17,
and this scripture describes how deep
our cooperation should be, verse 17:
“Be obedient
“to those who are taking the lead among you
“and be submissive,
“for they are keeping watch over you
“as those who will render an account,
“so that they may do this with joy and not with sighing,
for this would be damaging to you.”
Notice, we are told to “be obedient.”
Clearly, this means that we’re supposed to comply with,
or obey, what they tell us.
Of course, that would be with the proviso:
unless they tell us to do something that is unscriptural.
And, of course, that would be extremely rare.
We’re also told to “be submissive.”
This includes the attitude
with which we’re to be obedient
—doing so with a yielding, positive attitude.
Would it be possible to be obedient
but not submissive?
Well, what if we said:
“OK. I’ll do what the elders suggest.
I don’t want to do it, but I’ll do it.”
We would be obedient but not submissive.
However, Jehovah tells us
to display both of these qualities.
We should be obedient and submissive
even if what the elders are asking us to do
is not the best, most efficient way to do something.
Permit me to illustrate this point.
Admittedly, the illustration is somewhat exaggerated,
but hopefully it will make the point.
Please imagine that the elders decide
that the outside of the Kingdom Hall
needs to be painted and that all the publishers
will be given a small two-inch (5 cm) paintbrush
with which to paint.
Now, what could happen?
The publishers could get all upset
concerning this request of the elders,
saying, “It is ridiculous that the elders want us
to paint with a small two-inch (5 cm) paintbrush!”
Consequently, some could start campaigning
for the right for everyone to use a six-inch (15 cm) paintbrush.
Others might campaign for using paint rollers
to roll the paint on the Kingdom Hall.
Still others might start trying to build support
for renting and using a paint sprayer
to spray the paint on the Kingdom Hall.
In another camp, ones might champion the idea
of hiring out to a contractor
the painting of the Kingdom Hall,
while another group is promoting the idea
that the Kingdom Hall doesn’t even need to be painted.
Now, what would be the outcome?
The congregation would be divided,
the Kingdom Hall would never get painted,
publishers could end up stumbled right out of the truth,
the elders would be very discouraged,
Jehovah would be sad,
and Satan would be made very happy.
On the other hand,
what if everyone humbly supported the elders, perhaps thinking:
‘There’s no scripture
‘that says we can’t paint with a two-inch (5 cm) paintbrush.
‘In fact, Hebrews 13:17 tells us
‘to “be obedient” and “submissive” to the elders.
So why don’t we go ahead and support the elders?’
Now what would be the outcome?
The Kingdom Hall would get painted,
the publishers would get to enjoy
a lot of good association
because they’d be working together for a long time,
the elders would be very encouraged,
Satan would be sad,
and Jehovah’s heart would be made glad.
Well, what is the point of this hyperbole illustration?
Being obedient and submissive to those taking the lead
is much more important than how something is done.
That is the attitude
that Jehovah will richly bless.
But, now, a second way we can demonstrate
that we deeply appreciate these dear brothers
is to pray for them.
Please note what the elder Paul urged
the brothers to do for him
at Romans 15:30.
Here Paul said:
“Now I urge you, brothers,
“through our Lord Jesus Christ
“and through the love of the spirit,
“that you exert yourselves with me
in prayers to God for me.”
Paul recognized
the power that he would derive
as a result of others praying for him,
and your local elders feel the same way.
But the question is,
In your personal, private prayers,
do you regularly thank Jehovah
for your “gifts in men” and entreat Jehovah
to richly supply them with his powerful holy spirit?
Our answer to that question can reveal much
about our appreciation for these hardworking elders.
Now let’s move to a third way
that we can demonstrate deep appreciation:
We can do so by commending the elders.
Here is a soul-searching question:
Do you periodically go up
to various elders and say something like,
“Brother Elder,
“we just want to thank you for your hard work.
Please be assured that we appreciate it”?
However, it seems
that some publishers never ever commend the elders
or express appreciation.
Might this not indicate that we are taking them
and their hard work for granted?
Of course, they will not quit if you do not give them commendation;
they primarily do their work for Jehovah.
But if you do express appreciation,
believe me, it will be most encouraging to them.
And even though it may really surprise the elder
the very first time you do this,
please do not hold back
this “good from those to whom it is owing.”
Appropriately,
Jehovah tells us at Proverbs 3:27:
“Do not withhold good from those to whom you should give it
if it is within your power to help.”
And one thing that will move us to be more aware
of commending the elders is to remember all the good work they are doing.
Many elders are family men
who must work secularly to provide for their families.
If he has children,
these young ones need time and attention from their father.
He may need to help them with their schoolwork
as well as schedule time for them
to enjoy wholesome recreation.
Most important, he cares for the spiritual needs of his family
—regularly conducting family worship,
working with them in the ministry,
and taking them to meetings.
But in addition to these numerous responsibilities
common to many of us,
they have voluminous additional responsibilities
as elders.
And much of the elders’ hard work
in our behalf is not seen by the congregation.
For example, you may see
an elder giving a part on the meeting.
What you didn’t see
are the hours he spent preparing that part.
How long does it take you
to prepare a student assignment
on the midweek meeting?
Some elders have a part every week,
sometimes more than one.
While gaining experience in speaking is certainly helpful,
the fact remains
that good talks require hard work.
But that is not all that the elders do.
They have shepherding calls to make
and judicial cases to handle.
Some elders are also busy helping to build Kingdom Halls
and branch facilities,
serving on Hospital Liaison Committees,
volunteering at assemblies and conventions
—and elders do many other things
that are too numerous to recount.
What we see is often only the tip of the iceberg
—90 percent of an iceberg
is unseen underwater.
At 2 Timothy 4:6,
the apostle Paul referred to himself
as “being poured out like a drink offering.”
A drink offering
was poured on the altar and went up in smoke.
That well describes how the elders likewise
expend themselves.
Remembering all of this should move us
to regularly offer sincere commendation
to our hardworking elders.
Now we have discussed ways
that we can demonstrate
that we deeply appreciate our “gifts in men.”
We should (1) wholeheartedly cooperate with them,
(2) pray for them,
and (3) commend them.
Thereby we will prove
that we are not even slightly like
an unappreciative recipient of a silk tie or a silk scarf,
who uses that gift to polish his shoes.
To the contrary,
we will prove to Jehovah and Jesus
that we love, respect,
and appreciate
the divine gifts —our “gifts in men”—
that they have so generously given to us!

cn.text: 本期节目的主题是
要感激“作为恩赐”的人
有谁收到用心挑选的精美礼物
会不开心呢?
比方说
弟兄们  如果你收到一条真丝领带
颜色很漂亮  又很有品位
会不会很高兴呢?
姐妹们
如果你收到一条漂亮又雅致的丝巾
感觉又如何呢?
但是
如果你用那条真丝领带或者丝巾
擦你的鞋子
你觉得这种行为怎么样呢?
如果送礼物的人看到你这样做
你觉得他会怎么想呢?
很明显
这样做是在滥用礼物
送礼物的人看见会有被羞辱的感觉
我想强调的要点是什么呢?
会众的长老
其实就是耶和华和耶稣送给我们的
宝贵礼物
是他们精心挑选出来的
我们总要记得
长老们是来自上帝的恩赐
我们要尊重他们
并显出感激之心
关于这一点  我们来具体谈一谈
请打开圣经到以弗所书4:8
我们来了解一下
耶和华和耶稣给我们的这个礼物
以弗所书4:8
你留意到了吗?
耶稣坚守忠义  毫无瑕疵
战胜了撒但和他的世界
作为战胜世界的君王
他仿佛从这个世界得了俘虏
把这些人作为礼物送给会众
这些“作为恩赐”的人
发挥什么作用呢?
请留意
他们是传福音者
会带头从事传道
和使人做门徒的重要工作
他们不是只对别人说
你们去传道吧!
相反  他们说
来  和我们一起吧
让我们来做这个永不重做的工作吧
他们也是牧人
保护羊群
免遭撒但这个“杀人凶手”的伤害
圣经也将他比作蛇  大龙或狮子
此外  他们也是导师
会根据圣经施行教导  滋养人心
这些“作为恩赐”的人都辛勤工作
现在我们考虑一下
耶和华希望我们怎么对待他们呢?
我们来看看
帖撒罗尼迦前书第5章的经文
看看经文怎么说
请翻到帖撒罗尼迦前书第5章
我们会从第12节开始读
请留意  耶和华说
经文告诉我们
要“敬重”
这些亲爱的弟兄们
那么  一个关键的问题是
我们怎么做就表示自己
深深敬重
和感激这些亲爱的弟兄呢?
首先
要全心跟长老合作
请翻到希伯来书13:17
这节经文告诉我们
怎样才算是全心跟长老合作
请留意  经文说“要服从”
意思很清楚
就是我们应该听长老的话
当然  这排除一种情况
就是他们说的话违反了圣经原则
其实  这种情况非常少见
经文也说“要顺从”
这强调了表现服从时的态度
就是要有积极
甘心乐意的态度
想想看
一个人有没有可能
只服从不顺从呢?
举个例子
假如我们说
好  我接受长老的建议
但我其实很不愿意
算了  我还是照着做吧
这显示什么呢?
我们是服从了  但是没有顺从
然而  耶和华告诉我们
既要服从  也要顺从
即使长老的安排不是最好的
不是最有效的

ko.text: ‎정확한 수치에 대해선 전문가마다 견해가 다르지만, 일반 건물에서,
‎그 건물이 수명이 다할 때까지 드는 운영 및 유지 보수 비용은
‎처음 건축비의 네 배에서 여섯 배에 달합니다.
‎예를 들어, 한 외부 에너지 컨설턴트의 최근 추산에 따르면,
‎우리는 이 공사에 에너지 절약 기술을 적용했기 때문에
‎비슷한 시설을 일반적인 방식으로 건축했을 때에 비해
‎매년 백만 달러 이상의 비용 절감을 기대할 수 있습니다.
‎그러면, 워릭 공사에 어떤 에너지 절약 및 환경 관련 기술이 적용되어,
‎또 비용을 절감할 수 있었는지 궁금하실 겁니다.
‎조경, 빗물 관리, 조명 관리, 에너지 효율, 물 사용입니다.
‎관리 시스템이 강수량과 지역 일기 예보를 확인해서
‎각 관개 구역에 얼마만큼의 물이 필요한지를 결정합니다.
‎또 내건성이 뛰어난 자생 식물과 나무들은 물 소비를 줄여 주죠.
‎유리창 주변의 빛 센서가 관리 시스템과 연결되어 있어서,
‎효율이 높은 공조 설비, 보일러, 냉각기가 설치되었습니다.
‎약 120개의 지열 우물로 구성된 지열 우물 단지는
‎재생 가능한 에너지를 활용해서 건물의 냉방과 난방을 돕습니다.
‎이제 살펴볼 다섯 번째 분야는 바로 물 사용인데,
‎바로 운영 및 유지 보수에 드는 비용입니다.
‎물과 조명과 에너지를 절약하는 일을 얼마나 실천하느냐에 따라,
‎새 시설들의 유익과 잠재력과 목적이 실현되는 데

ko.text: ‎미국 순회 강연 차 기차 여행을 하고 있었습니다.
‎러셀 형제는 여러 해 동안 여행을 하고 있었는데요,
‎물론, 그만큼 여행을 하신 분들이 이 중에도 계실 테지만
‎기타 다른 교통 수단을 이용해서 그만큼 여행한 거니까
‎야고보 4:13, 14의 말씀이 참되다는 것을 알 수 있는데
‎장사를 하여 이익을 내겠다’라고 말하는 사람들이 있습니다.
‎자기 생명이 내일 어떻게 될지 알지 못합니다.
‎“어떤 부자가 자기 땅에서 많은 소출을 거두었습니다.
‎‘수확물을 모아 둘 곳이 없으니 어떻게 할까?’ 하고 생각했습니다.
‎“네가 여러 해 동안 쓸 좋은 것을 많이 쌓아 두었으니,
‎오늘 밤 네게서 네 목숨을 요구할 것이다.
‎그러면 네가 쌓아 둔 것을 누가 갖게 되겠느냐?’
‎하느님에 대해 부유하지 못한 사람은 그와 같습니다.”
‎‘여러 해’ 동안 살 [수] 있을 것이라고 생각한 것입니다.”
‎이 사람은 소유물이 많은 것과 수명이 긴 것을 동일시한 것입니다.
‎그의 생명은 자기의 소유물로부터 오는 것이 아닙니다.’”
‎그 어떤 것도 절대 과신해서는 안 된다고 알려 줍니다.
‎이 점은 단지 우리의 삶에 대한 견해만이 아니라
‎우리가 하는 이런저런 일에 대해서도 말하고 있죠.
‎그러니까 사실 우리의 다양한 일상 활동 전부가 관련됩니다.
‎최근 들어, 우리는 러시아를 비롯한 여러 나라에서
‎우리가 누리는 숭배의 자유는 앞으로도 지속될 거라고,
‎우리의 모든 활동이 그 나라에서 금지되어 버렸죠.
‎네, 이 일에서 어떤 교훈을 얻게 됩니까?
‎우리의 활동이 앞으로 언제든지 금지될 수 있다는
‎그런 예상치 못한 일 때문에 형제들은 어떤 영향을 받았습니까?
‎우린 여호와로 인해 틀림없이 안전을 누릴 것입니다.

en.text: ‎Over 100 years ago,
‎on October 31, 1916,
‎Brother Charles Taze Russell
‎was traveling on a train
‎as part of a lecture tour
‎across the United States.
‎Quite unexpectedly,
‎and at the young age of 64,
‎Brother Russell died.
‎For years, he had been traveling continually.
‎You know, it’s been said that Brother Russell covered
‎more than a million miles.
‎Now, of course, some of you may have accomplished that feat,
‎but at that time, of course, we were not talking about air travel.
‎Brother Russell had to accomplish that by train and ship
‎and goodness knows what other means —quite an accomplishment!
‎In addition to that, he had delivered
‎more than 30,000 sermons, lectures, and talks.
‎He had written books and other material
‎totaling over 50,000 pages.
‎Yet, despite all of the privileges that he had enjoyed
‎​—his tremendous Bible knowledge
‎and the powerful way that Jehovah had used him​—
‎in just a moment he was gone.
‎It really illustrates the truth of what James says here
‎at James 4:​13, 14.
‎Let’s read this together,
‎James 4:​13.
‎It says: “Come, now, you who say:
‎“‘Today or tomorrow we will travel
‎“‘to this city and will spend a year there,
‎“and we will do business and make some profit,’
‎“whereas you do not know what your life will be like tomorrow.
‎“For you are a mist that appears for a little while
‎and then disappears.”
‎Well, that’s true.
‎You see, really, no matter what privileges we may enjoy​
‎—how skilled a teacher we may be, what knowledge we’ve accumulated​—
‎we are all just like
‎‘a mist appearing for a while and then disappearing.’
‎Well, this is an idea
‎that occurs over and over again in the Scriptures
‎and, really, with the purpose
‎of encouraging all of us
‎to take a close and sober and serious look
‎at the way that we use our lives.
‎And even more importantly,
‎how we use them to serve Jehovah.
‎In Luke chapter 12,
‎you’ll remember that Jesus taught an illustration regarding a rich man.
‎Do you remember this?
‎Let’s open our Bibles and read it together,
‎Now, just before we read it, you’ll remember that the purpose
‎of Jesus giving this illustration was to emphasize the importance
‎of being rich toward God.
‎Now, let’s read what he says here in verse 16:
‎“The land of a rich man produced well.
‎“So he began reasoning within himself,
‎“‘What should I do now that I have nowhere to gather my crops?’
‎“Then he said, ‘I will do this:
‎“‘I will tear down my storehouses and build bigger ones,
‎“‘and there I will gather all my grain and all my goods,
‎“‘and I will say to myself:
‎“‘“You have many good things stored up for many years;
‎take it easy, eat, drink, enjoy yourself.”’
‎“But God said to him, ‘Unreasonable one,
‎“‘this night they are demanding your life from you.
‎“Who, then, is to have the things you stored up?’
‎“So it goes with the man who stores up treasure for himself
‎but is not rich toward God.”
‎Well, what was the problem with this man?
‎In the 2007 Watchtower, August 1st issue,
‎this illustration was discussed.
‎And The Watchtower said that “the rich man’s plan
‎“provided [really] only a false sense of security.
‎“Practical as it might have seemed [to him],
‎“it left out one vital element​—God’s will.
‎“The man was only thinking about himself,
‎“how he would be able to take his ease
‎“and eat, drink, and enjoy himself.
‎“He thought that because [he had] ‘many good things,’
‎he would also have ‘many years.’”
‎Isn’t that an interesting point?
‎You see, he thought the abundance of things that he possessed
‎would somehow equate to the length of his life.
‎But The Watchtower went on to say:
‎“Too bad for him, things did not work out that way.
‎“Just as Jesus said earlier, ‘even when a person has an abundance
‎his life does not result from the things he possesses.’”
‎Well, that brings us back to James chapter 4.
‎Let’s go back there again,
‎and look at what verse 15 says.
‎See, after commenting on how a life is just like a mist appearing,
‎then verse 15 says:
‎“Instead, you should say: ‘If Jehovah wills,
‎we will live and do this or that.’”
‎You see, the Bible makes it clear that we should never ever develop
‎overconfidence —overconfidence in anything​—
‎in our position, our knowledge, our wisdom, our wealth.
‎But instead, you see, have complete confidence in Jehovah.
‎Really, our only hope,
‎our only confidence is with Jehovah.
‎Now, this applies not just to our view of life itself
‎but, really, also to our view of all of our activities.
‎You see, in that verse in James chapter 4,
‎it says that it’s not just about our life
‎but about whether we will do this or do that.
‎So it really applies to all
‎of the different things that we do every day.
‎Recently, we’ve been hearing reports
‎of increasing persecution in various lands, including Russia.
‎Now, when we hear those reports,
‎perhaps we begin to think right away
‎that this is something that could only happen in a faraway land.
‎You see, in countries like the United States and Canada
‎(those who are listening to this program),
‎perhaps we have the attitude that, well,
‎this freedom of worship that we enjoy
‎is always going to be here, and it will never change.
‎But it’s interesting to consider what happened in one case
‎in 1972 in the country of Singapore.
‎On January 12, 1972,
‎a missionary who was serving at the branch,
‎received a letter suddenly ​—hand delivered to him​—
‎saying that he was banished from the country
‎and must leave within two weeks.
‎Now, this brother had been serving there peacefully
‎for 23 years;
‎everything was going along very smoothly.
‎Two days later, the Kingdom Hall was padlocked,
‎all the literature was banned in the country,
‎the bank accounts that belonged to the branch
‎and to the congregation were all seized.
‎Well, suddenly and very unexpectedly our work
‎and all of our activities had been banned in that country.
‎Well, now, what do we learn from this?
‎Is it to teach us that we should live in some kind of morbid fear
‎that our work is going to be banned at any moment?
‎Well, what’s the real reality of what happened in Singapore?
‎How did those unexpected events
‎affect our brothers in that land?
‎Well, they were not broken.
‎Looking to Jehovah with complete confidence,
‎they continued to find ways to worship Jehovah.
‎And Jehovah has blessed their efforts
‎right up until this present day.
‎So, brothers, it’s true,
‎as James chapter 4 teaches us,
‎life in this system is really filled with uncertainty.
‎But if we have made Jehovah our confidence
‎and if we are truly rich toward God,
‎then, really, whatever may come,
‎whatever situation may befall us
‎​—even our untimely death​—
‎we are completely and totally safe with Jehovah.
‎And he is the One ​—because we’ve made him our confidence​—
‎who will care for us in every way.

ko.text: ‎수십 년 동안 다양한 형태의 전 시간 봉사를 해온
‎특별히 고른 멋진 선물을 받고 기뻐하지 않을 사람이 누가 있을까요?
‎멋진 색깔의 품위 있는 100퍼센트 실크 넥타이를 받는다면
‎예쁘고 우아한 실크 스카프를 선물로 받으면 어떠시겠습니까?
‎선물을 준 사람은 자기가 준 선물을 그런 식으로 사용하는 걸 보면서
‎전파하고 제자 삼는 중요한 일에서 솔선하는 사람들로 주셨습니다.
‎결코 다시 반복되지 않을 이 일을 함께 합시다.”
‎양 떼에게 영양가 있는 영적 음식을 먹이죠.
‎열심히 일하는 “사람들로 된 선물”을 어떻게 여기라고 말씀하실까요?
‎네, 우린 그런 형제들을 “존경하라”는 권고를 받고 있죠.
‎깊은 존경과 감사를 어떻게 나타낼 수 있습니까?
‎첫 번째 방법은 마음을 다해 협조하는 것입니다.
‎이 성구는 우리가 어느 정도나 협조해야 하는지 알려주는데요,
‎네, 분명 우리는 그들이 하는 말에 따르고 순종해야 합니다.
‎하지만 여호와께선 두 가지가 다 필요하다고 하십니다.
‎어떤 일을 처리하는 가장 좋고 효율적인 방법이 아니더라도
‎사실상, 이 예는 다소 과장된 면이 있지만,
‎장로의 회가 왕국회관 외벽을 새로 페인트칠 하기로 결정하고,
‎모든 전도인에게 폭이 5센티인 작은 붓을 주어 칠을 하게 합니다.
‎전도인들이 모두 화를 내면서 장로들의 결정에 불만을 토로합니다.
‎그 결과, 몇 사람이 다른 사람들을 부추기면서
‎페이트 롤러를 써서, 칠을 해야 된다고 주장합니다.
‎그런가 하면, 또 다른 전도인들은 사람들을 설득하면서,
‎돈을 주고 페인트 스프레이를 빌려서 싹 뿌려야 한다고 말합니다.
‎아예 애초에 왕국회관에 페인트 칠을 할 필요조차 없다는 사람들까지 있습니다!
‎전도인들은 걸려 넘어져 진리를 떠날 수도 있죠.
‎반대로 모두 겸손히 장로들의 말에 따르면서 이렇게 생각하면 어떨까요?
‎‘성경에서 5센티짜리 붓을 쓰지 말라고 한 것도 아닌데 못 할게 뭐 있어.
‎전도인들은 좋은 교제를 오랫동안 마음껏 즐기게 될 것입니다.
‎다소 과장하기는 했지만, 이 예의 요점은 무엇일까요?
‎일을 어떻게 하는지 보다 훨씬 중요하다는 것입니다.
‎여호와께서는 바로 그런 태도를 크게 축복하실 것입니다!
‎두 번째로 이 소중한 형제들에게 깊은 감사를 나타내는 방법은
‎장로인 바울이 형제들에게 자신을 위해 무엇을 해 달라고 권고하는지
‎바울은 다른 사람이 자신을 위해 기도해 줄 때,
‎여러분도 개인적 기도를 드릴 때 정기적으로 여호와께

‎그때 이후로 자매는 자녀들에게 진리를 부지런히 가르쳐
‎최근에는 또 다른 아들이 봉사의 종으로 임명되었고
‎지금은 모국어인 크레올어 성경을 읽으면서 큰 유익을 얻고 있습니다.
‎아이티에서 사용되는 미국 수화 밭에서도 좋은 성과가 나타나고 있는데요,
‎수화 회중에서 여호와께 찬양의 노래를 부르고 있네요.
‎얼마나 많은 준비가 필요한지 우리에게 보여 줬습니다.
‎토요일 아침 지부 부지 내에 있는 옥외 대회 회관에서 열렸습니다.
‎우리는 일부 형제들이 미국 수화로 프로그램을 즐기며
‎유익을 얻는 것을 보고 큰 격려를 받았습니다.
‎녹화된 프로그램이 그날 오후와 일요일에 전국의 왕국 회관으로 송출되었고,
‎두 번째 지부 방문을 위해 도미니카 공화국으로 갔는데,
‎우리는 반건조 지역을 통과해 두 나라 사이의 국경으로 향했습니다.
‎작은 산들과 비옥한 농업 지대와 카리브 해안을 지나며
‎국경 지대와 여러 검문소에서 일부 사람들에게 증거할 수 있었고
‎지부 사무실의 큰 JW.ORG 표지판을 얼른 알아보았습니다.
‎73명의 베델 가족 중 많은 분이 열정적으로 우릴 환영해 주었죠.
‎다른 많은 언어로도 봉사하기 위해 노력을 기울이고 있습니다.
‎지부 관할 구역에는 현재 아이티 크레올어 순회구가 5개,
‎그 밖에도 러시아어, 중국어, 이탈리아어, 프랑스어 회중 및 집단이 있습니다.
‎우리는 산토도밍고시의 차이나타운에서 형제 자매들과 함께 봉사했습니다.
‎우리 그룹은 스페인어와 중국어를 말하는 사람들에게 가두 증거를 했는데,
‎저는 도미니카 군대에서 복무하면서 의학 과정을 마쳤습니다.
‎그 책을 말도 없이 가져와 혼자 다 읽었습니다.
‎군대 대장들이 동굴 속에 몸을 숨기는 환상이 나와요.
‎전 그 환상에 깊은 인상을 받아 여호와를 섬기기로 결심했습니다.
‎그건 제가 군대를 떠나야 한단 걸 의미했죠.
‎전 서둘러 직속상관에게 제대할 수 있게 해 달라고 요청했습니다.
‎그래도 전 아랑곳하지 않고 인사 업무를 담당하는 대령에게 다시 요청했습니다.
‎눈을 떴는데, 한 장교가 다가와 제 이름을 부르며 인사했습니다.
‎여호와의 증인이 되기 위해 제대를 하고 싶다고 설명했죠.
‎“걱정 말고 서류를 주게. 나는 대령의 보좌관이네.”
‎얼마 안 있어 전 전도인이 됐고, 여호와의 증인으로 침례를 받았습니다.
‎분명 여호와께선 그분을 온전히 신뢰하는 사람들을 도와주십니다.
‎이곳의 베델 가족은 오랜 세월 선교인으로 봉사한 분들과
‎전 그중 연로한 성원 다섯 분을 만나 즐거운 시간을 보냈는데요,
‎윌리엄 딩먼 형제는 길르앗 제1기 졸업생이고, 아내인 에스텔 자매는 12기 졸업생이죠.
‎바버라 파커 자매는 42기, 헬렌 페라리 자매는 2기 졸업생입니다.
‎이분들이 얼마나 오래 전 시간 봉사를 해 왔는지 알 수 있는 예로,
‎큰 무리에 속한 사람으로 일어난 청중 가운데 있었습니다.
‎더 인상 깊은 건 이분들의 평균 전 시간 봉사 연수가 73년이라는 거죠.
‎이 충실한 분들은 노령과 건강 상의 제약에도
‎계속 활동적으로 봉사함으로 훌륭한 본이 되고 있습니다.
‎여호와의 이 충성스런 종들은 어디서든 영적인 보물과 같은 분들이죠.
‎눈이 너무 나빠서, 많이 할 순 없지만 노력하죠.
‎다리가 안 좋아 걸을 수가 없어서 사람들이 내 휠체어를 밀어줘요.
‎제 인생 전체에서, 선교인으로 일하고 도미니카 공화국에서
‎봉사한 시간들을 생각해 보면, 참 멋진 삶이었습니다.
‎그리고 왕국의 좋은 소식을 전파하는 것보다 더 행복한 삶도 없을 겁니다.
‎이 충실한 분들을 돌보는 일을 지원하는 것을 특권으로 여깁니다.
‎총 3050명이 영적 프로그램과 그리스도인 교제를 통해 유익을 얻었습니다.
‎참여한 모든 사람에게 격려를 주고 영적 축복이 된 시간이었습니다.
‎오랜 시간 여호와를 섬겨 온 그분의 종들에 관한
‎아내의 지원을 받아 수십 년간 전 시간 봉사를 하면서
‎저희 집에서 작은 집단이, 나중엔 작은 회중이
‎페기의 가족이 「파수대」 연구를 하러 저희 집에 왔죠.
‎전 아마 그 무렵 여덟아홉 살이었고, 페기는 한 살 어렸어요.
‎아직도 할 일이 많은 나라들에 가고 싶었습니다.
‎길르앗 과정을 마치고 임명을 받았는데, 정말 놀랐어요.
‎길게는 9년 동안이나 수감 생활을 한 형제들이 계시죠.
‎그 형제들에게 많은 것을 배울 수 있을 겁니다.”
‎식당에 줄을 서 있는데 바로 제 옆줄에 서 있었죠.
‎서로 연락하면서 둘이 함께 봉사하는 문제를 생각해 보기로 했죠.
‎전 이미 순회 활동을 하라는 임명을 받았고,
‎우리가 순회 활동을 시작할 때 전 스물넷이었어요.
‎순회 감독자로 일할 자격을 갖출 만한 훈련을 전혀 받지 못했거든요.
‎그래서 자매들이 대화를 이어받으면, 전 하나도 못 알아듣고 그냥 서 있었죠.
‎2년이 지나니까 신권 용어는 전부 이해할 수 있었어요.
‎9년 동안 순회 활동을 하고 끝 부분엔 지역 활동도 했습니다.
‎노어 형제가 제게 지부 감독자로 일하면 어떻겠냐고 하셨을 때였습니다.
‎1969년 뉘른베르크에서 열린 대회 때 있었던 일이죠.
‎약 40년 동안 지구 감독자로 일하는 놀라운 특권도 누렸습니다.
‎90개가 넘는 나라들을 방문하면서 정말 멋진 경험을 했습니다.
‎또 어디를 가든 형제들이 여호와께 정성을 다하고,
‎아주 어려운 상황에서도 그분을 충실히 섬기려고 하는 것을 보았습니다.
‎이렇게 지구 활동을 하는 임명을 받아 많은 지부들을 여행하다 보니,
‎우리는 여러 나라에서 야외 봉사에 참여할 기회를 가질 수 있었습니다.
‎만약 제가 그냥 선교 봉사를 했더라면 절대 경험하지 못했을 일이죠.
‎저는 1952년 1월 1일부터 계속해서 전 시간 봉사를 해 왔습니다.
‎그건 다른 무엇과도 바꿀 수 없는 소중한 일이었죠.
‎“전 시간 봉사를 하지 않았다면 지금 어떻게 되었을까?”
‎분명, 우리가 일평생 누린 많은 것들을 경험해 보지 못했겠죠.
‎열심히 일하며 도움을 주는 젊고 유능한 형제 자매들이 정말 많습니다.
‎우린 그들에게 여호와의 조직에서 전 시간 봉사를 하는 걸
‎전 시간 봉사를 목표로 할 수 있는
‎젊고 재능 있는 형제나 자매 중 한 명입니까?
‎여호와를 위해 최선을 다하는 그 밖의 사람들의 본을 생각할 때,
‎여호와와 예수께 우리의 사랑을 표현하는 한가지 방법은
‎카메라가 어떻게 촬영할 것인지 알 수 있도록
‎그런 다음 팀원들은 프로그램 사회자 대역과 함께
‎실제 사회자는 자신이 맡은 다른 일에 집중할 수 있습니다.
‎촬영을 시작하기 전에 방송팀은 모여 짧은 회의를 합니다.
‎기도를 한 뒤 각자 자기 위치로 갑니다.
‎그 달의 월간 프로그램 촬영이 끝나게 됩니다.
‎이곳 스튜디오에서 열심히 일하는 우리 형제 자매들이
‎기쁜 마음으로 여러분에게 따뜻한 사랑의 인사를 전합니다.

en.text: We warmly welcome all of you
to this month’s broadcast.
Here is just a taste
of what we can look forward to on the program.
A life spent in the full-time ministry
is both exciting and challenging.
We’ll meet a brother and his wife
who have spent decades in various forms of this service.
What lessons can we learn from their experiences?
Then we’ll hear the story of a woman
who struggled for years with severe drug addiction.
What would help her eventually break free?
And our new music video
will help us feel the brotherly love we enjoy
as a part of Jehovah’s organization.
There’s certainly plenty to enjoy
on this August 2018 edition
of JW Broadcasting.
The theme for this month’s program is
“Appreciating Our ‘Gifts in Men.’”
Who of us does not enjoy being given
a fine, well-chosen gift?
For example, you brothers,
do you not take pleasure in receiving
a colorful but tasteful,
100 percent silk tie?
Or, you sisters, do you not delight in being given
an exquisite, charming silk scarf?
But what if you took that silk tie
or silk scarf
and used it to polish your shoes?
How do you think the giver of your gift would feel
if he saw you using his gift in that way?
Obviously, it would be misuse
and disrespect for the gift and would insult the giver.
What is the point of our illustration?
Well, Jehovah and Jesus have given us
a fine, well-chosen gift in the form of the elders.
But as we will discuss,
all of us must make sure
that we always show appreciation and respect
for this divine provision.
Please turn to Ephesians 4:8,
and let’s read about this gift
that Jehovah and Jesus have given us.
It reads:
“For it says:
“‘When he ascended on high
“‘he carried away captives;
he gave gifts in men.’”
You notice, by means of Jesus’ perfect integrity,
Jesus conquered Satan and his world.
As a world conqueror,
figuratively He has plundered captives
and has given them as gifts to the congregations.
How useful are these “gifts in men”?
Well, please look at verses 11 and 12 for the answer:
“And he gave some as apostles,
“some as prophets,
“some as evangelizers,
“some as shepherds and teachers,
“with a view to the readjustment of the holy ones,
“for ministerial work,
to build up the body of the Christ.”
Notice, they would be “evangelizers”
—taking the lead
in the all-important preaching and disciple-making work.
They do not simply say to the publishers,
“Go in the preaching work.”
They say: “Come. Come with us.
Let’s work together in this never-to-be-repeated work.”
They’re also “shepherds”
—protecting the flock from Satan
the “murderer,” “serpent,” “dragon,” and “lion.”
Additionally, they are “teachers”
—feeding the flock with nourishing spiritual food.
But now we ask,
How does Jehovah tell us
that we should feel about these hardworking “gifts in men”?
Let’s go to 1 Thessalonians chapter 5,
and let’s get the answer.
At 1 Thessalonians chapter 5,
beginning in verse number 12,
notice what Jehovah says:
“Now we request you, brothers,
“to show respect
“for those who are working hard among you
“and presiding over you in the Lord
“and admonishing you;
“and to give them extraordinary consideration
“in love because of their work.
Be peaceable with one another.”
Notice, we’re told to “show respect”
for these dear brothers.
But now, let’s move to a vital question,
How can we show, demonstrate,
that we do deeply respect
and appreciate these dear brothers?
The first way:
by wholeheartedly cooperating with them.
Please turn to Hebrews 13:17,
and this scripture describes how deep
our cooperation should be, verse 17:
“Be obedient
“to those who are taking the lead among you
“and be submissive,
“for they are keeping watch over you
“as those who will render an account,
“so that they may do this with joy and not with sighing,
for this would be damaging to you.”
Notice, we are told to “be obedient.”
Clearly, this means that we’re supposed to comply with,
or obey, what they tell us.
Of course, that would be with the proviso:
unless they tell us to do something that is unscriptural.
And, of course, that would be extremely rare.
We’re also told to “be submissive.”
This includes the attitude
with which we’re to be obedient
—doing so with a yielding, positive attitude.
Would it be possible to be obedient
but not submissive?
Well, what if we said:
“OK. I’ll do what the elders suggest.
I don’t want to do it, but I’ll do it.”
We would be obedient but not submissive.
However, Jehovah tells us
to display both of these qualities.
We should be obedient and submissive
even if what the elders are asking us to do
is not the best, most efficient way to do something.
Permit me to illustrate this point.
Admittedly, the illustration is somewhat exaggerated,
but hopefully it will make the point.
Please imagine that the elders decide
that the outside of the Kingdom Hall
needs to be painted and that all the publishers
will be given a small two-inch (5 cm) paintbrush
with which to paint.
Now, what could happen?
The publishers could get all upset
concerning this request of the elders,
saying, “It is ridiculous that the elders want us
to paint with a small two-inch (5 cm) paintbrush!”
Consequently, some could start campaigning
for the right for everyone to use a six-inch (15 cm) paintbrush.
Others might campaign for using paint rollers
to roll the paint on the Kingdom Hall.
Still others might start trying to build support
for renting and using a paint sprayer
to spray the paint on the Kingdom Hall.
In another camp, ones might champion the idea
of hiring out to a contractor
the painting of the Kingdom Hall,
while another group is promoting the idea
that the Kingdom Hall doesn’t even need to be painted.
Now, what would be the outcome?
The congregation would be divided,
the Kingdom Hall would never get painted,
publishers could end up stumbled right out of the truth,
the elders would be very discouraged,
Jehovah would be sad,
and Satan would be made very happy.
On the other hand,
what if everyone humbly supported the elders, perhaps thinking:
‘There’s no scripture
‘that says we can’t paint with a two-inch (5 cm) paintbrush.
‘In fact, Hebrews 13:17 tells us
‘to “be obedient” and “submissive” to the elders.
So why don’t we go ahead and support the elders?’
Now what would be the outcome?
The Kingdom Hall would get painted,
the publishers would get to enjoy
a lot of good association
because they’d be working together for a long time,
the elders would be very encouraged,
Satan would be sad,
and Jehovah’s heart would be made glad.
Well, what is the point of this hyperbole illustration?
Being obedient and submissive to those taking the lead
is much more important than how something is done.
That is the attitude
that Jehovah will richly bless.
But, now, a second way we can demonstrate
that we deeply appreciate these dear brothers
is to pray for them.
Please note what the elder Paul urged
the brothers to do for him
at Romans 15:30.
Here Paul said:
“Now I urge you, brothers,
“through our Lord Jesus Christ
“and through the love of the spirit,
“that you exert yourselves with me
in prayers to God for me.”
Paul recognized
the power that he would derive
as a result of others praying for him,
and your local elders feel the same way.
But the question is,
In your personal, private prayers,
do you regularly thank Jehovah
for your “gifts in men” and entreat Jehovah
to richly supply them with his powerful holy spirit?
Our answer to that question can reveal much
about our appreciation for these hardworking elders.
Now let’s move to a third way
that we can demonstrate deep appreciation:
We can do so by commending the elders.
Here is a soul-searching question:
Do you periodically go up
to various elders and say something like,
“Brother Elder,
“we just want to thank you for your hard work.
Please be assured that we appreciate it”?
However, it seems
that some publishers never ever commend the elders
or express appreciation.
Might this not indicate that we are taking them
and their hard work for granted?
Of course, they will not quit if you do not give them commendation;
they primarily do their work for Jehovah.
But if you do express appreciation,
believe me, it will be most encouraging to them.
And even though it may really surprise the elder
the very first time you do this,
please do not hold back
this “good from those to whom it is owing.”
Appropriately,
Jehovah tells us at Proverbs 3:27:
“Do not withhold good from those to whom you should give it
if it is within your power to help.”
And one thing that will move us to be more aware
of commending the elders is to remember all the good work they are doing.
Many elders are family men
who must work secularly to provide for their families.
If he has children,
these young ones need time and attention from their father.
He may need to help them with their schoolwork
as well as schedule time for them
to enjoy wholesome recreation.
Most important, he cares for the spiritual needs of his family
—regularly conducting family worship,
working with them in the ministry,
and taking them to meetings.
But in addition to these numerous responsibilities
common to many of us,
they have voluminous additional responsibilities
as elders.
And much of the elders’ hard work
in our behalf is not seen by the congregation.
For example, you may see
an elder giving a part on the meeting.
What you didn’t see
are the hours he spent preparing that part.
How long does it take you
to prepare a student assignment
on the midweek meeting?
Some elders have a part every week,
sometimes more than one.
While gaining experience in speaking is certainly helpful,
the fact remains
that good talks require hard work.
But that is not all that the elders do.
They have shepherding calls to make
and judicial cases to handle.
Some elders are also busy helping to build Kingdom Halls
and branch facilities,
serving on Hospital Liaison Committees,
volunteering at assemblies and conventions
—and elders do many other things
that are too numerous to recount.
What we see is often only the tip of the iceberg
—90 percent of an iceberg
is unseen underwater.
At 2 Timothy 4:6,
the apostle Paul referred to himself
as “being poured out like a drink offering.”
A drink offering
was poured on the altar and went up in smoke.
That well describes how the elders likewise
expend themselves.
Remembering all of this should move us
to regularly offer sincere commendation
to our hardworking elders.
Now we have discussed ways
that we can demonstrate
that we deeply appreciate our “gifts in men.”
We should (1) wholeheartedly cooperate with them,
(2) pray for them,
and (3) commend them.
Thereby we will prove
that we are not even slightly like
an unappreciative recipient of a silk tie or a silk scarf,
who uses that gift to polish his shoes.
To the contrary,
we will prove to Jehovah and Jesus
that we love, respect,
and appreciate
the divine gifts —our “gifts in men”—
that they have so generously given to us!
But, now, what effect can these “gifts in men”
have on individuals who have strayed from Jehovah
and his organization?
What actions show that they are loving shepherds
who want to assist these ones to return to Jehovah
despite serious struggles or even addictions?
Let’s look for those answers in the following story.
‘Turn your life around,
‘so that seasons of refreshing
may come from Jehovah himself.’
Those words changed my life,
and they saved the life of my little girl.
I was raised in a Witness family.
But I chose
a dark underworld
of practically everything that Jehovah hates.
After about 15 years,
although financially secure,
I was confronted with the failure that my life had become.
I was trying to raise a child while addicted to drugs.
I just didn’t want to live like that anymore,
and I wanted to be a good mother.
So for the first time in years,
I prayed to Jehovah.
The knock came on my door the very next day.
I began studying with a vengeance.
I had 15 years to catch up on.
I had a lot of help.
I progressively changed my lifestyle,
I changed my associates,
and I conquered my addiction.
I slowly began to overcome
feelings of worthlessness.
So none of these changes were easy to make,
but it made me feel
clean and happy
knowing that Jehovah was pleased.
My burning desire at that point really was to begin sharing
with other people what I was learning,
but I didn’t qualify to engage in the public ministry
because I was still living with my boyfriend at the time.
And he didn’t understand some of the changes I was making.
I was determined
to turn my life around and overcome this last hurdle
that was preventing me from serving Jehovah fully.
Two weeks later,
I found out I was pregnant.
I was devastated.
I didn’t know what all those people who had helped me would think
and how Jehovah felt about what was happening.
I was so ashamed.
I actually blamed Jehovah for letting it happen.
I was so confused.
My first inclination
was just to get an abortion.
But deep down, I knew that was wrong.
I thought, ‘Now everyone will know
‘that I’m still the worthless person
that I always knew I was.’
At that point, I just felt like giving up.
I told my aunt and uncle,
who are Jehovah’s Witnesses, about my situation.
They didn’t judge me at all,
but they did offer a curious suggestion:
They invited me up to Bethel for a visit.
They introduced me to an elder who was very kind,
and I talked to him about my situation.
I was shocked
by how loving he was.
So he shared with me Acts 3:19.
“Repent, therefore, and turn around
“so as to get your sins blotted out,
“that seasons of refreshing
may come from the person of Jehovah.”
Well, he told me
I had already sinned, but why should I sin a second time?
Why should this innocent child pay
for what I had done wrong?
He suggested I teach my baby
about Jehovah and raise the child up
to know Him and have a friendship with Him.
I loved that he took something that was
sad and depressing for me
and turned it into something beautiful.
Well, I had a new plan now.
I was really determined to do everything I had to do
to turn my life around in order to please Jehovah.
So eventually I qualified to become an unbaptized publisher,
and later I was baptized in 2010.
I gave birth to a healthy baby girl.
I already dedicated my life to Jehovah.
So two of my goals are to get baptized and pioneer.
I’m as determined as ever to raise Jolie up to love Jehovah
and to avoid the traps that almost cost us our lives.
Describing our elders,
Isaiah 32:2 reads:
“And each one will be like a hiding place from the wind,
“a place of concealment from the rainstorm,
“like streams of water in a waterless land,
“like the shadow of a massive crag
in a parched land.”
Did you note two key ways our “gifts in men” did that?
One, the elder she met at Bethel
was kind and approachable.
He made her feel comfortable to express herself.
Two, he lovingly used the Bible
to help her make a wise decision and avoid further calamity.
This is an excellent example
of how elders can help ones who are struggling spiritually.
But in what other ways can elders be an example?
In their zeal for the ministry.
But what if weather conditions in our territory make this difficult?
When the elders take the lead,
the rest of the congregation responds in the same way.
The example of those preaching in the Faroe Islands
will offer some encouraging tips.
The Faroe Islands are also called the Land of Maybe.
The weather is very diverse and can rapidly change.
So when you begin in the ministry, the weather can be sunny.
And then ten minutes later, you find yourself
in a massive rain shower and everything gets wet.
Wind is another challenge.
We have some severe winter storms.
So you have to be careful that your service partner or the car door
doesn’t blow away while you’re getting out of the car.
We make sure to wear clothes appropriate for the weather.
And also to stay updated on the weather situation
and see where in our territory the weather is most suitable, and then adapt.
If the weather is nice, then we try to go from house to house.
And if the weather is bad,
then you can go on calls where you can go inside,
meaning where they will invite you in
or where the entrance is covered.
And you can plan your ministry so that if the weather gets bad,
you can make visits that you know will be at home that time of day.
When the weather is poor, it’s good to adjust.
Maybe you can do some telephone witnessing or letter writing.
At a meeting for pioneers,
an elder reminded us that when the weather is bad,
try not to think: ‘The weather is bad again,’
but instead, ‘Yay! Now people are actually at home.’
It is a good idea to have a plan for whom you’d like to visit
and what you’d like to talk to them about
because then when it rains or the weather isn’t ideal,
you focus on your plan
instead of thinking that now I have been out preaching
for five hours in stormy weather.
I think Ecclesiastes 11:4 applies quite well to our territory:
“The one who watches the wind will not sow seed,
and the one who looks at the clouds will not reap.”
If we have to wait for the perfect weather conditions to preach,
then we wouldn’t be out that often.
Something else that helps us to endure bad weather
is to think of the first publishers in the Faroe Islands.
They fought with seasickness, bad weather,
and they had to hike over the mountains to visit remote settlements.
They overcame these obstacles,
and it motivates me to overcome the challenges I am facing today.
I remember when we came to the Faroe Islands,
I looked out the window and thought,‘Is it even possible
to go out in the ministry in this kind of weather?’
And then we arrived at the meeting for field service,
and the friends with children and strollers were there
and were positive and ready for field service.
It made me think that if they can do it, then I can too.
So we are a team of publishers, and we have the weather as our challenge.
And especially when the weather is bad, we encourage one another.
We really like the song “The Life of a Pioneer.”
It’s an amazing song.
It says: “In the work we endure, whether sunshine or rain.”
It’s because we love Jehovah.
We really want people to get to know Jehovah.
They need to know the truth.
When Jesus said that we should preach,
I think that he also would have put on a raincoat
and gone out to preach the good news.
We experience how Jehovah blesses our efforts when we go in the ministry.
And you especially feel it when you persist in your efforts
to preach when the weather isn’t good.
It may be that one day you have a really nice conversation
with a person about the Bible.
I also feel it gives me great joy.
Paul said that the one who “sows bountifully will also reap bountifully.”
So if you want to sow bountifully in the Faroe Islands,
you need to preach also when the weather is bad.
And we feel that we have reaped bountifully
with nice return visits and Bible studies.
I feel it’s worth all the effort
because we see that people in the territory
really appreciate what they are learning.
All that we do in our ministry
is motivated by love for Jehovah
and the people in the territory, and it won’t be changed by bad weather.
It’s an opportunity to show that our worship is wholehearted.
You don’t just go in the ministry when everything is good
and the sun is shining.
I think we have become more enduring
and flexible in our ministry.
We saw that the publishers were fully supporting
the spirit that the elders showed
in sharing the good news
despite inclement weather.
Around the world,
many of our brothers face severe opposition
because of remaining loyal to Jehovah
and maintaining their Christian neutrality.
Let’s travel to Spain
and hear how some of our brothers
have dealt with these challenges firsthand.
Spain is a land of castles.
From the mountains of central Spain
to the Mediterranean coast, castles dominate the landscape.
But there is one castle —the Castle of Santa Catalina—
that played a unique part in the history of Jehovah’s Witnesses in Spain.
This castle that guards the entrance
to the harbor of Cádiz, in southern Spain,
became a military prison over two centuries ago.
And this fortress
tested the faith of around 300 Spanish Witnesses.
The battle began in the 1960’s when Spain was ruled
by General Franco, a military dictator.
Franco wanted all Spanish men to serve the fatherland,
and this meant military service.
But in Spain, there were Jehovah’s Witnesses
whose conscience said no.
So this castle became a battleground
where Franco’s military regime fought
to stamp out the Christian consciences of those young Witnesses.
But times have changed in Spain.
The city of Cádiz has organized an exhibition
to salute the sacrifice made by those valiant Witnesses.
Over 40 years after their release,
some of those conscientious objectors have returned to Cádiz
to attend this exhibition.
At the inauguration,
the mayor described them as citizens who spoke up
and who presented arguments against the injustice
—arguments based on peace, freedom,
and, above all, their conscience.
Those who spent years of their lives behind bars
have vivid memories
of the times when this castle was their prison.
I think one of the greatest challenges
was never knowing
if we would be granted our freedom.
Our first sentence
was for three years.
And since we still refused to enlist in the military,
we were then sentenced again for another lengthy period.
So it seemed as if we had a life sentence.
We organized daily activities
to keep us busy.
Mornings, we worked at our trades
to earn a little money.
Afternoons, we set aside for spiritual activities.
Our preaching was done mainly by writing letters.
And in this way, some of us could even pioneer.
A few people did reply to our letters,
and we were thrilled to hear that some of them accepted the truth.
Of course, we also preached to other prisoners,
and a few of them became baptized Witnesses.
We also studied the Bible thoroughly,
both individually and as a group,
which proved vital in building us up spiritually.
At first, we had to study our literature secretly,
but later the guards
allowed us to have the Bible and other publications.
As our numbers grew,
all the Witnesses were kept together
in the same place —in the same barracks—
so we could organize meetings.
We even held assemblies, including the Biblical dramas.
And we loved
singing Kingdom songs.
These songs really lifted up our spirits.
We really felt Jehovah’s loving care when the brothers came to visit us.
We even had a special visit from Brother Grant Suiter
of the Governing Body,
but there were also other visits that we really looked forward to.
Many of the brothers endured years of separation from their families
and fiancées.
This was a real test.
But these faithful sisters
wholeheartedly supported their neutral stand.
Those were years that molded me spiritually.
I studied the Bible as I had never done before.
I developed skills as a public speaker and as an overseer.
Above all, it was a time in my life
when I learned to rely totally on Jehovah.
Thanks to my fervent prayers, he became my closest friend
and he never let me down.
That was priceless.
The firm stand of those Witnesses
gave a powerful testimony in Cádiz and throughout Spain.
The run-down military prison
that once tested their faith
has been restored.
It is now a tourist attraction
and a cultural center.
But while the castle has changed,
the faith of those valiant Witnesses has not.
The castle certainly tested them,
but they fought a fine fight for the faith.
And with Jehovah’s help, they won the battle.
Forty years later,
their victory is still giving a witness
to Jehovah’s name.
As we noted earlier,
the apostle Paul said
that he was “being poured out like a drink offering.”
Similarly, by remaining neutral,
these brothers offered up a great sacrifice
of praise to Jehovah despite resistance.
And as we learned, by loyal endurance,
they went on to be “gifts in men”
to those in the congregations and circuits that they later served.
Other examples of “gifts in men”
are those who serve as headquarters representatives
visiting branch offices
and encouraging members of the Bethel families.
Brother Daniel Molchan had the privilege
to visit the countries of Haiti and the Dominican Republic.
They have had some exciting spiritual developments
in those lands.
On Sunday, February the 26th,
I traveled to Port-au-Prince for the branch visit
and was warmly welcomed by many of the Bethel family of 54 members.
The branch office supervises the preaching work
for more than 20,000 publishers.
Although Haiti has faced economic challenges
and suffered recent natural disasters,
our brothers are positive
and focus their attention on helping others to identify our Scriptural hope.
The Haitian people show a keen interest in the Word of God.
Our brothers average more than 42,000 Bible studies each month,
and Haiti enjoyed a Memorial attendance
of more than 86,000 in 2016.
This was four times more than the number of publishers in the branch territory.
The brothers love to use the videos in the ministry.
This is made possible by the Haiti audio/video team
translating the videos into their native language.
While many in Haiti speak French,
the common language of the people in general is Haitian Creole.
Creole is said to be
an expressive language that combines French words
with the grammar of West African languages.
The number of publishers in Haiti has quadrupled since the start
of Creole translation back in 1987.
The complete New World Translation Bible
was released in Creole in 2015.
We met with the translation team to commend them for the good work they do.
We reminded them of the many positive results
in the field ministry that have taken place
since translating the Bible and our literature into Creole.
As an example, Mirlène is a vendor of fruits and vegetables who was asked
if she would supply some of her produce to Bethel.
Although she was very impressed
the first time she arrived at the Bethel property,
she said she found the large steel gate to be intimidating.
So she prayed to God to protect her
while in the yard at Bethel.
The brothers dealt kindly with her when she made
her deliveries on Monday each week.
One of the brothers from the kitchen told her that maybe someday
she too would become one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
She accepted an invitation to the Memorial,
and despite some personal challenges, such as not being able to read well,
she began to attend some congregation meetings.
Mirlène could see the difference
between Jehovah’s loving people and those in her church.
A study was started with her,
and she progressed to the point of baptism in 2009.
Since then, she has worked diligently
to teach the truth to her children with good results.
Her oldest son graduated from the School for Kingdom Evangelizers
and serves as an elder and temporary special pioneer.
Recently, another of her sons was appointed a ministerial servant,
and the four other children are unbaptized publishers.
Having our literature in Creole
and with the help of her children, she has improved her reading.
She now benefits from reading the Bible in Creole,
the language of her heart.
Good results are beginning to be seen
in the field of American Sign Language, which is now used in Haiti.
There are now 87 deaf publishers
in 4 ASL congregations and 8 groups.
The congregation here is singing praises to Jehovah.
Even our little sister is learning to do this.
This brother showed us the effort he puts forth
to prepare for a Bible reading.
A special program for Haiti was held
on Saturday morning at the open-air Assembly Hall
on the branch property.
A total of 1,405 were in attendance.
We were very encouraged to see
the group of our brothers who benefited from the program
in American Sign Language.
The program was recorded and presented at Kingdom Halls throughout the country
later that same day and also on Sunday
to a combined audience of 34,812.
We felt a little sad to leave the brothers on Sunday morning
for a drive of about six hours or so
to the Dominican Republic
for the second branch visit.
En route, we traveled through some semiarid areas
to the border between the two countries.
The terrain varied greatly as we drove through small mountains,
rich agricultural regions, and along the Caribbean Sea.
We took the opportunity to witness to some individuals at the border
and at various checkpoints, leaving literature along the way.
Upon entering the city of Santo Domingo,
we quickly identified the large JW.ORG sign at the branch office.
We were enthusiastically greeted
by many of the 73 Bethel family members.
Although the preaching work is done primarily in Spanish,
our brothers are expanding their ministry
to reach the language of the hearts of many peoples and cultures.
There are now 5 Haitian Creole circuits in the branch territory,
26 American Sign Language congregations,
and other congregations or groups
in Russian, Chinese, Italian and French.
We joined a group of brothers and sisters in the field ministry
in the Chinatown district of Santo Domingo.
Our group gave a witness to both Spanish-
and Chinese-speaking people on the streets
—most of whom respectfully listened to our message.
A Bethel brother, Evan, told us of the challenge
he faced when learning the truth.
I was finishing medical school
while serving in the Dominican army.
By then I had been serving for six years.
At my aunt’s home, I found the Revelation book.
It made such an impact on me,
that I stole it and read it all on my own.
There’s a vision in chapter 6 of Revelation,
where the sixth seal is opened
and the skies darken and the army commanders hide in caves.
That vision impressed me so much
that I decided to serve Jehovah.
That meant that I would have to leave the army
because Witnesses are neutral.
I quickly decided to talk to my immediate commander
to ask him to please discharge me from the army.
However, he rejected my request and said:
“No, you have served in the army for six years.
You have to stay in the army.”
I was not concerned because I could still appeal
to the colonel in charge of personnel.
However, my request for resignation was rejected again.
I left and went into the hallway.
I prayed to Jehovah:
“I want to serve you.
“What should I do?
Help me find a way out of this!”
When I opened my eyes, another army officer approached
and greeted me using my name.
I still don’t know who he was.
He asked me, “What do you need?”
I explained that I wanted to resign in order to become a Jehovah’s Witness.
He said: “Don’t worry, give me your papers.
I’m the colonel’s assistant.”
Within 20 minutes, my discharge papers were ready and approved.
In a short period of time, I became a publisher
and I got baptized as one of Jehovah’s Witnesses.
At this time, I have been serving happily in Bethel
for over 11 years with my wife, Jael.
Without a doubt, Jehovah helps those who put their complete trust in him.
The branch is blessed to have as part of their Bethel family
some who had been longtime missionaries.
I enjoyed a very pleasant visit
with five of the senior members of this group
—three of whom are 98 years of age.
Brother William Dingman is of the first class of Gilead.
His wife, Estelle, attended the 12th class.
Thelma Critz is also of the 12th class.
Barbara Parker is of the 42nd class,
and Helen Ferrari attended the 2nd class of Gilead.
To illustrate the length of their full-time service
is the fact that Sister Ferrari
is among those who stood up to identify themselves
as part of the great multitude
at the 1935 convention in Washington, D.C.
The average age of this group is 94.
Even more impressive
is that their average years of full-time service is 73.
These faithful ones set a fine example
continuing to be active in the ministry
—taking into account their ages and health limitations.
Such loyal servants of Jehovah are considered
spiritual treasures wherever they may serve.
I still have one study so far,
although my eyesight doesn’t allow
me to do too much.
But I try.
My legs aren’t so good for walking,
so they wheel me around.
In all of my life, I would consider
the life that I have spent as a missionary
and in Dominican Republic as well
—it’s a wonderful life.
I couldn’t have chosen
a better companion
and also a better life
than to be preaching
the message of the good news of the Kingdom.
The Dominican Republic Bethel family
considers it a privilege to have a share in providing
care for such faithful ones.
On Sunday, March the 12th, a special program was held
at the open-air Assembly Hall adjacent to the branch office.
A total of 3,050 benefited
from the spiritual program and Christian association.
The visits to the Dominican Republic and Haiti branches
proved to be an encouragement and a spiritual blessing
to all who participated in them.
We thank Brother Molchan for that report
and for sharing those motivating experiences
of longtime servants of Jehovah.
Another example of this are Richard and Peggy Kelsey.
How has he, with the support of his dear wife,
proved to be one of the “gifts in men”
throughout his decades of full-time service?
I was born in a little town
called Adair, Iowa
—actually out on the farm​—
and that was in 1930.
I was born in 1931,
also in a small town in Iowa.
My father wanted to be a farmer.
So we moved to a farm, and I grew up on a farm.
And then the Watchtower Study of a little group,
and then a little congregation was in our home.
And happily, when Peggy’s father came into the truth,
the family came to our place to the Watchtower Study.
I was—I guess at that time— eight or nine,
and Peggy was one year younger.
But the thing was, they moved away just after about one year.
Well, I started pioneering in September 1948.
Gilead was what I wanted.
I didn’t apply for Bethel
because I liked the field service,
and I thought South America, Africa,
countries where there is still so much to do
—that’s what I wanted.
I was called to Gilead
in 1951, in February.
The assignment after attending Gilead
was a great surprise.
Brother Schroeder, one of the instructors,
he said: “You will have
“a very wonderful opportunity,
“being assigned to the German Bethel.
“There are brothers there
“who have been in concentration camps for up to nine years,
and you can learn very much from these brothers.”
And that was very true.
In 1953, at the convention in New York,
I saw a beautiful young sister
standing in the cafeteria line next to my cafeteria line.
And I looked twice,
and it was Peggy.
So we were together for the rest of the convention
and decided that we would correspond and think about serving together.
In 1955 we married.
I had received the assignment to circuit work.
We were assigned to northern Germany.
When we began circuit work, I was 24.
I felt completely inadequate
because I’d been serving in Bethel
and had no training
that would qualify me to serve as a circuit overseer
—that was my feeling.
In the first place, the sisters with me always got nervous
with me not being able to speak correctly.
So they would take over the conversation,
and I stood there and didn’t understand anything.
But with time, you pick it up.
After two years, I could understand everything
in the theocratic language,
but in the kitchen I was still lost.
It was nine years for circuit work and, at the conclusion, district work.
And then we were called back into Bethel.
The biggest shock for me
was when Brother Knorr asked me
if I would be branch overseer.
And that was at the convention
of 1969 in Nuremberg.
And despite different arguments that I presented,
I got a letter later saying that I’d have that assignment.
For about 40 years,
we had the wonderful privilege of doing zone work or,
as it’s now stated, being representative of headquarters.
So it was wonderful to visit
somewhat over 90 different countries.
We became acquainted with Jehovah’s lovely family
—the worldwide brotherhood, the unity,
and seeing how the brothers everywhere
are devoted to Jehovah
and want to serve him faithfully
under sometimes very difficult conditions.
I would say, sometimes we benefited more
from the visit than the brothers we were visiting
because it was so faith-strengthening.
When we got this privilege
of traveling to many branches in the zone work,
we were able to engage in the field ministry
in numerous countries,
which I never would have had, of course,
if I would have just gone into missionary service.
So I said to myself,
‘Accept every assignment Jehovah gives you
and you’ll find that you have the greatest blessings possible.’
Since the 1st of January 1952,
I’ve been able to keep full-time service as my career.
And it’s something I certainly wouldn’t have changed
for anything else.
We have often said,
“Where would we be today if we hadn’t taken up full-time service?”
Certainly, we would not have enjoyed
so many things as we have in our lifetime.
There are so many young, talented brothers and sisters
who are working and helping.
We encourage them to make full-time service
in Jehovah’s organization their goal in life.
Are you one of those young, talented brothers or sisters
who Brother Kelsey mentioned could make full-time service a goal?
If so, keep it in your prayers.
Yes, as we look back at our program
and the examples of various “gifts in men,”
their wives,
and numerous others doing all they can for Jehovah,
what is it that motivates them
to live such self-sacrificing lives?
Love.
And that’s the theme of this month’s music video
entitled Brotherly Love.
Wherever you go, you will have fam’ly near.
Because wherever you go, Jehovah’s people are there.
And you’ll feel love.
You’ll feel love, A brotherly love.
So feel the love.
Brothers and sisters all over the world Unite with Jehovah and follow his Son
To bring you love— A nation of,
Of brotherly love. So feel the love.
Our Father provides for us all— No one left over.
Deep in the jungle or on mountains high,
In big, modern cities or on islands afar,
You belong. You belong to the people of God.
So feel the love.
Our Father provides for us all— No, no one left over.
But in the world, it can be cold— A scary place, truth to be told.
So how wonderful it is to know The one true God and his people!
Jesus, he taught his disciples to love.
So millions of people, as a nation, they show
Jehovah’s love— And you belong among all of them.
So feel the love.
So feel the love.
What a beautiful song
and a good reminder that one way
we can show our love to Jehovah and Jesus
is by showing love, respect, and appreciation
for the “gifts in men” they have generously given us.
Now, before we end the program,
we have a special treat.
Our postcard this month comes from right here
at our JW Broadcasting studio.
Yes, you get a sneak peek behind the scenes
of how our broadcast is produced.
First, a group of brothers and sisters
set aside their regular Bethel work for parts of three days.
Early on the first day,
the director reviews the “shot list” with crew members.
The “shot list” is a series of photographs
showing how the cameras will record each scene.
In the control room, media is prepared for display
on the studio’s video screen.
The microphones and cameras are all properly adjusted.
Then the crew rehearses the entire program several times
while a stand-in substitutes for the program host.
This allows the real host to concentrate on his other work
during these technical rehearsals.
On the third day, the actual host reports
to the studio’s makeup room,
where wardrobe makes sure that he looks his best.
Before recording begins,
the crew assembles for a brief meeting.
The host often gives a few brief comments,
and the floor director gives any final instruction to the crew.
After a prayer, everyone takes their positions.
Within a few hours,
the entire recording for that month’s program is completed.
Yes, our hardworking brothers and sisters that work in the studio
happily send you their warm love and greetings.
This is JW Broadcasting
from the world headquarters
of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

cn.text: 非常欢迎大家收看本月的
电视网节目
这个月有什么让人期待的内容呢?
我们来看一下接下来的预告
能善用一生参与全时服务
既令人兴奋又充满挑战
我们会认识一对夫妇
过去几十年间
他们参与过不同形式的全时服务
从他们的经历
我们可以学到什么呢?
我们也会听到一位姐妹的故事

ko.text: 자신만의 연구용 성경을 만들어 보도록 격려하기로 결정했습니다.
이러한 결정에 따라 우리는 기존 성경보다
여백이 더 넓은 성경을 생산하는 것이 가능한지 검토해 보기로 했습니다.
연구 조사한 내용을 적을 충분한 공간을 만들기 위해서였죠.
「신세계역」의 본문을 개정해야 할 필요가 있다는 점을 알게 되었습니다.
그래서 본문 개정 작업이 끝날 때까지
새로운 온라인 「연구용 성경」이 나올 것이라는 발표가 있었는데,
마태복음을 시작으로 성경의 다른 책들이 차례로 나올 예정이었습니다.
그 이후로 2년간 마태복음, 마가복음, 누가복음, 요한복음이 나왔습니다.
그런데 「연구용 성경」이 나오는 데 왜 이렇게 시간이 오래 걸리는 걸까요?
간단히 말하자면 작업량이 아주 많기 때문입니다.
작업량이 얼마나 많은지 쉽게 이해할 수 있도록
사복음서에는 대략 2300개의 연구 노트가 달려 있습니다.
이것은 「파수대」 연구 기사 115개에 들어 있는 단어 수와 맞먹는 양이죠.
다시 말해 2년 치의 연구 기사 자료보다 많은 양이라는 뜻입니다.
복음서 한 권에 들어 있는 연구 노트를 다 합하면
연구 노트에 더해 미디어 갤러리도 있습니다.
그리고 성경의 각 책을 소개하는 동영상을 볼 수 있죠.
하느님의 이름을 복원시킨 이유와 뒷받침하는 자료를 알려 주죠.
이런 자세한 내용은 처음 보실 겁니다.
J라고 표시된 목록에서 그 자료를 보실 수 있는데요.
그러면 연구 노트를 위한 자료들은 어디서 수집할까요?
또한 자신만의 연구 노트를 만들어 온
그런 분들 중에는 길르앗 강사로 일하는 형제들도 있습니다.
참고 자료들에서 볼 수 있는 내용을 비롯한
여러 자료를 요약해 놓은 것이나 마찬가지이죠.
앞으로는 또 무엇이 나올지 기대되지 않나요?
“성경과 그리스도인 생활”이라는 새로운 항목이 추가될 것입니다.
「‘모든 사물을 확인하고 훌륭한 것을 굳게 잡으라’」라는
양 치는 방문을 할 때나 일상생활에 도움이 되는 성구들을 찾고 싶을 때
「연구용 성경」 작업에 왜 이렇게 시간이 많이 걸리는지
성경이 66권밖에 안 돼서 얼마나 다행인지 모르겠네요.
여러분에게 알려 드릴 기쁜 소식이 있습니다.
온라인 「연구용 성경」을 어떻게 잘 활용할 수 있는지 알려 주는
그 두 동영상을 지금부터 함께 시청해 보시죠.
jw.org에 있는 「신세계역」 연구용 성경을 어떻게 잘 활용할 수 있습니까?
성경 페이지에서 연구용 성경 표지나 제목을 클릭하십시오.
목록에는 연구용 성경이 나온 책들이 표시되어 있습니다.
부록을 포함한 다른 자료들도 사용할 수 있는데,
어떤 자료는 연구용 성경에서만 사용할 수 있습니다.
먼저 성경 책을 누르고, 읽고 싶은 장을 선택하십시오.
페이지 왼쪽의 읽기 창에서 성경 내용을 볼 수 있습니다.
해당 장의 첫 구절부터 녹음 파일이 재생됩니다.
특정한 구절을 누르면 재생 버튼이 나타나는데,
이 버튼을 누르면 그 구절부터 녹음 파일이 재생됩니다.
페이지 오른쪽의 연구 창에 있는 보물 탭에는
읽고 있는 장의 각 구절에 대한 연구 노트, 각주,
보물 탭의 맨 윗부분에는 해당 부분의 개요가 나옵니다.
개요를 펼치면 세부 사항을 볼 수 있습니다.
버튼을 다시 눌러 세부 사항을 숨길 수 있습니다.
단어나 어구 뒤에 있는 각주 표시를 누르면
대체 번역 표현이 나오는 각주를 볼 수 있습니다.
단어나 어구 뒤에 있는 상호 참조 성구 표시를 누르면
상호 참조 성구들에는 인용된 원래의 성구나
평행 기록 혹은 인물, 장소, 가르침,
예언에 관한 일반 참조 성구들이 나옵니다.
해당 장의 모든 상호 참조 성구가 항목별로 나옵니다.
평행 기록 성구가 맨 먼저 나오고
항목 옆의 모두 하이라이트 박스를 체크하면
해당 항목의 모든 상호 참조 성구가 읽기 창에 표시됩니다.
해당 구절을 여러 성경 번역판에서 어떻게 번역했는지 볼 수 있습니다.
오른편 하단의 화살표를 누르면 연구 창이 나옵니다.
화살표를 한 번 더 누르거나 읽기 창을 누르면
「신세계역」 연구용 성경에서 연구 노트와 미디어 갤러리를 사용해 보십시오.
연구 창에 있는 보물 탭에서 그 구절에 대한 연구 노트를 볼 수 있습니다.
그 구절에 나오는 단어나 표현이 굵은 글씨로 되어 있고
그 구절의 다른 주요 단어나 표현이 설명 가운데 나올 경우,
연구 노트에 있는 용어 설명 링크를 누르면
해당 단어나 표현에 대한 설명을 볼 수 있습니다.
연구 노트에 있는 부록 링크를 누르면
어떤 부록은 텍스트 형태로도 볼 수 있고
보기 변경 버튼을 클릭하여 선택할 수 있습니다.
관련 성구에 대한 연구 노트로 연결되는 링크도 있습니다.
링크를 클릭하면 관련 성구와 연구 노트를 볼 수 있습니다.
어떤 구절들에는 삽화나 동영상 같은 미디어 자료가 있습니다.
삽화나 제목을 클릭하면 미디어 갤러리 창이 열립니다.
미디어 갤러리에는 성경의 특정한 책들과 관련된
삽화나 동영상을 선택하면 해당 미디어 자료와 설명이 나옵니다.
이전 자료나 다음 자료를 볼 수 있습니다.
동영상 자료는 재생 버튼을 클릭하여 볼 수 있습니다.
소리가 함께 나오는 자료도 있고 영상만 나오는 자료도 있습니다.
원래 읽던 성경 부분으로 돌아갈 수 있습니다.
온라인 「연구용 성경」에서 많은 유익을 얻는 데
이 두 동영상이 도움이 될 것이라고 확신합니다.
여러분이 기뻐할 만한 소식을 한 가지 더 알려 드리죠.
어제 늦게 주무셨거나 오늘 아침에 정말 일찍 일어나신 분이라면
새로운 버전의 「JW 라이브러리」 앱을 사용할 수 있게 되었습니다.
아침 숭배가 끝난 뒤에 앱 스토어에서
「JW 라이브러리」 앱이 최신 버전인지 확인하시기 바랍니다.
그러면 그 연구 노트들과 「연구용 성경」의 연구 노트들을
우리가 개인적으로 성경을 계속 깊이 있게 연구한다면
여호와께서 우리의 노력을 축복해 주실 것입니다.
‘여호와의 생각나게 하는 것들에 고착하게’ 되기를 바랍니다.
