en.text: Well, if you’re like me,
you may need to review
some of these points sometimes.
We had the parable of the virgins explained
in The Watchtower some time ago.
But let’s try to review the parable
and see what we can remember.
Now, we know that there are ten virgins,
and all of them are waiting for a bridegroom to come.
Now, there are five wise virgins, or discreet virgins,
and then there are five foolish virgins.
And there’s a difference.
The wise are prepared for any contingency.
They not only have oil in their lamps
but they have extra oil as well.
And you can be sure that it’s virgin olive oil.
Now, the wise virgins, why do they have so much oil?
Because they’re willing to wait until the bridegroom comes.
They must love the bridegroom very much.
And they know that it’s all about him; it’s not about them.
They want somebody to be on hand when the bridegroom arrives.
The foolish virgins
—well, they’re willing to wait for a while.
But the bridegroom had better hurry up
because they only have a little bit of oil in their lamp,
and they have no extra oil at all.
They’re primarily concerned with themselves.
Well, the bridegroom doesn’t come right away,
and all of the virgins fall asleep.
But in the middle of the night, there is a cry,
apparently in the distance:
“Here is the bridegroom!”
But the bridegroom still doesn’t make an appearance.
Well, the virgins awaken, they dress their lamps,
they put their lamps in order, and they wait.
And still the bridegroom doesn’t come.
The lamps of the foolish virgins begin to flicker,
and they realize that they’re going to run out of oil.
So they ask the wise to share some of their oil with them,
and the wise refuse.
Why?
Because they’re selfish?
No.
Because they’re wise.
If they share some of their oil with the foolish virgins,
then the wise will run out and the foolish will run out
and then no one will be on hand to greet the bridegroom.
And really, it’s all about the bridegroom.
They want someone to be on hand
to hail the bridegroom when he arrives.
So, what do the foolish do?
They rush off to find an all-night 7-Eleven
or Walmart that might be selling oil
—like that’s going to happen in the first century.
And in the meantime, while they’re gone,
the bridegroom arrives
and the wise virgins are ushered into the wedding feast.
Well, now this is a parable for the last days.
How do we know that?
Because everything in Matthew 24 and 25
relates to the last days.
So we’re talking about something that occurs
during Jesus’ presence.
Whom do the virgins represent?
All of the anointed.
Not just “the faithful and discreet slave”
but all of the anointed.
Now, that’s quite a statement.
How would you prove that?
What scripture would you point to to prove
that the virgins represent all of the anointed and not just a small class
—small group— like “the faithful and discreet slave”?
Our go-to scripture is Luke chapter 12.
Let’s turn there.
And now, this is not a parallel scripture to Matthew 24.
This is Jesus talking about the same subject on another occasion,
but this will clarify matters for us.
Luke chapter 12,
and first we’ll read verse 32 to get the context.
He says: “Have no fear, little flock.”
Well, who constitute the “little flock”?
All of the anointed, right?
“Have no fear, little flock,
for your Father has approved of giving you the Kingdom.”
So he’s talking to all of the anointed.
And what does he say to them in verses 35 and 36?
See if you can see the similarity with what we just read.
“Be dressed and ready
“and have your lamps burning,
“and you should be like men waiting for their master to return from the marriage,
so when he comes and knocks, they may at once open to him.”
Do you see the similarity between Matthew 24 and Luke 12?
So now Jesus is addressing these words
to all of the anointed.
Now, in the parable there’s an interval
between the cry “Here is the bridegroom!”
and the coming of the bridegroom.
Now what about the fulfillment?
When do you think the cry went up,
“Here is the bridegroom”?
You’re right, 1914.
But the bridegroom didn’t come just then.
When does he come?
At the great tribulation.
How do we know?
We know because in Matthew 24 and 25,
there are eight references to the coming of the Master,
and each and every one of them refer to the great tribulation.
So we’re talking about the Master returning
—the bridegroom coming at the great tribulation.
And will he find the anointed with their lamps burning,
or will they have let their light go out?
That is the simple question there.
Now, is Jesus saying that many of the anointed would be found unfaithful
when the great tribulation breaks out?
No.
Remember what we said about the evil slave
referred to in Matthew 24?
He talks about a “faithful and discreet slave,”
and then he talks about an evil slave.
And we learn that Jesus is not saying
that there is a separate “faithful and discreet slave”
and then a separate and distinct evil slave.
But rather, he is saying, if the faithful slave becomes evil,
then he cannot expect the Master’s favor.
And it’s the same with the parable of the virgins.
He’s saying, if any of the anointed
did allow their light to go out,
they could not expect the favor of the bridegroom
and be allowed to enter into the wedding feast.
Well, that’s very interesting.
But that’s quite a statement, isn’t it?
And some have had questions about the evil slave
and whether the Bible really allows for the faithful slave becoming evil
or whether it’s a separate group.
And the reason why they’ve raised the question
is because of the way Jesus put it in Matthew chapter 24.
Let’s just check it
—Matthew 24.
Now, we know in verse 45,
Jesus said: “Who really is the faithful and discreet slave?”
Verse 46: “Happy is that slave
if his master on coming finds him doing so!”
But then, in verse 48, he says:
“But if ever that evil slave says
“in his heart, ‘My master is delaying,’”
and then, in verse 50: “The master . . . will come . . .
and he will punish him with the greatest severity.”
So they’ve looked at the expression
“if ever that evil slave” and they’ve said,
“Well, doesn’t that allow for a separate evil slave?”
And we say no.
But why do we say that?
Just look at the end of verse 48.
Do you see at the very end of verse 48 there’s a little “j”?
It’s a marginal reference.
Now, notice the marginal reference to “j.”
It returns us to our go-to scripture,
Luke chapter 12,
this time verses 45 and 46.
So let’s see if that will shed some light on this.
Let’s turn to Luke chapter 12,
and we’re going to start reading from verse 42.
And remember what we’re trying to discover:
Is Jesus talking about two different groups
—a faithful slave and an evil slave?
Or is he talking about the faithful slave becoming evil?
See if the way he puts it on this occasion clarifies it for you.
Starting with verse 42:
“Who really is the faithful steward,
“the discreet one, whom his master will appoint over his body of attendants
“to keep giving them their measure of food supplies at the proper time?
“Happy is that slave
“if his master on coming finds him doing so!
I tell you truthfully, he will appoint him over all his belongings.”
Well, we’re on track, aren’t we?
This is what Jesus was talking about in Matthew 24.
But now notice the way he puts it
according to verse 45:
“But if ever that slave,”
the same slave that’s mentioned in verse 43: “Happy is that slave.”
“If ever that slave should say in his heart,
“‘My master delays coming,’
“and starts to beat the male and female servants
“and to eat and drink and get drunk, the master of that slave
“will come on a day that he is not expecting him
“and at an hour that he does not know,
and he will punish him with the greatest severity.”
He’s talking about the same slave, isn’t he?
If that slave is faithful, he will be rewarded;
if that slave is unfaithful, he will be punished.
And it’s the same with the parable of the virgins.
If the virgins are faithful, they will be rewarded;
if not, they will be punished.
This parable does have relevance to the “great crowd.”
How do we know?
Mark 13:37, Jesus said:
“What I say to you, I say to all:
Keep on the watch.”
So just as the anointed have to be found faithful at the great tribulation,
those of the great crowd have to be found faithful as well.
So in very simple terms, how would you sum up
the lesson of the parable of the virgins?
Keep on the watch!

cn.text: 我们都一样
需要经常复习一些学过的要点
以前的《守望台》杂志
解释了关于十个处女的比喻
现在我们再次复习一下这个比喻
看看我们还记得什么
我们知道有10个处女
她们都正在等待新郎来到
其中5个处女是睿智的
另外5个处女是愚蠢的
为什么会有这么大的区别呢?
睿智的处女已经准备好
应付任何意外
她们不仅灯里装了油
还另外带了一些油
她们准备的应该是上等的橄榄油
那么  她们为什么会准备这么多油呢?
她们肯定对新郎有很深的感情
所以无论新郎什么时候到
她们都乐意等候
她们知道
当天的主角是新郎而不是她们自己
她们希望新郎到的时候
会有人在那里迎接他
愚蠢的处女也愿意等候
但她们不愿意一直等下去
希望新郎最好赶紧来
因为她们灯里的油不多
也没多准备一些
在她们心里
她们自己更重要
然而  新郎没能马上来到
所有的处女都睡着了
半夜时分  有人喊叫说
“新郎到啦!”
显然这是从远处传来的
新郎还没到
处女们都醒来了
她们马上起来整理自己的灯
做好准备  等候新郎
新郎还是没有出现
但这时
愚蠢处女的灯开始变得微弱起来
她们意识到灯很快就要熄灭了
于是她们央求睿智的处女分些油给她们
但被拒绝了
为什么?  是睿智的处女自私吗?
不是  她们很明智
如果她们把油分给愚蠢的处女
那么不仅她们自己的油不够
而且愚蠢处女的油也会很快用光
结果就没有人迎接新郎了
是的  新郎才是最重要的
她们希望新郎来到时
有人迎接他
那么  愚蠢的处女怎么办呢?
她们赶快出去
找一个可能卖油的24小时便利店
当然  在公元1世纪还没有这样的店
就在愚蠢的处女离开的时候
新郎到了
睿智的处女就跟着他
进去参加婚宴了
这个比喻跟最后的日子有关
我们怎么知道呢?
因为马太福音24,25章
都在讲最后的日子
所以我们刚才讨论的
是耶稣临在期间发生的事
处女代表谁呢?
所有受膏基督徒
不只是“忠信睿智的奴隶”
而是所有的受膏基督徒
为什么我们敢这么说呢?
有什么根据吗?
有什么经文可以证明
处女代表的是所有的受膏基督徒
而不只是“忠信睿智的奴隶”
这一小群人呢?
我们看看路加福音12章的经文
在这里  耶稣也谈到了这个话题
这会有助于我们理解马太福音的经文
请打开路加福音12章
我们先读一下32节
了解一下经文的背景
他说“小群羊啊  不要怕”
谁是“小群羊”呢?
所有的受膏基督徒  对吗?
“小群羊啊  不要怕”
“你们的父亲乐意把王国赐给你们”
这是耶稣对所有受膏基督徒说的
在35和36节
耶稣还对他们说了什么?
请想想
这跟马太福音的经文有什么相似之处
“你们要束腰点灯”
“像奴隶等候主人参加完婚礼回来一样”
“主人来到敲门”
“他们就马上给主人开门”
你看出马太福音和路加福音的经文
有什么相似之处了吗?
耶稣的这些话
是对所有受膏基督徒说的
在比喻中
有人喊叫说“新郎到啦!”
和新郎实际到达
中间有一段时间
这件事会怎样应验呢?
什么时候会听到有人喊叫
“新郎到啦”?
没错  就是1914年
不过  那时新郎还没到
他什么时候来到呢?
就是在大患难期间
我们怎么知道呢?
因为马太福音24,25章
有8节经文
提到了耶稣“来到”
每次提及“来到”
都是在说大患难
所以我们说  主人回来
或者说新郎来到
是在大患难期间
他来的时候
受膏基督徒的灯是一直燃烧着
还是已经熄灭了呢?
这是个关键的问题!
我们再想想
当大患难发生的时候
耶稣是不是说
很多受膏基督徒会变得不忠呢?
不是的
你还记得耶稣在马太福音24章
谈论的“邪恶的奴隶”吗?
他先谈到
一个“忠信睿智的奴隶”
然后又说了一个邪恶的奴隶
我们知道耶稣不是说有两个奴隶
一个是“忠信睿智”的
另一个是邪恶的
相反  耶稣的意思是
如果忠信的奴隶变得邪恶
他就得不到主人的喜爱
比喻中的处女也是这样
如果受膏基督徒让他们的灯灭了
他们就得不到新郎的喜爱
也不能进去参加婚宴
这一点非常重要
也值得我们留意  对吗?
有的人对于“邪恶的奴隶”指谁
有些疑问
圣经真的说
忠信的奴隶会变得邪恶吗?
还是在说另外一个奴隶呢?
他们提出这样的问题
是因为耶稣在马太福音24章的表达方式
那么  我们来看一下马太福音24章
在45节
耶稣问
“到底谁是忠信睿智的奴隶?”
46节说“他的主人来到”
“看见奴隶正这样做”
“奴隶就有福了!”
然后在48节耶稣说
“可是  邪恶的奴隶如果心里说”
“主人不会这么快回来的”
50节接着说
“给他最重的惩罚”
当他们看到“邪恶的奴隶”这个表达时
可能会问
难道这里不能理解成另一个奴隶吗?
是的  不能
为什么这样说呢?
如果你看51节
在“给他最重的惩罚”这里
有一节参考经文
就是路加福音12:46
请翻到这节经文
45节也一起看一下吧
看看我们能不能得到一些启发
请翻到路加福音12章
我们从42节开始读
请记得我们的问题是
耶稣是不是在说两个奴隶
一个忠信  一个邪恶
分别代表着两群人呢?
还是说忠信的奴隶会变得邪恶呢?
看看这里的表达方式
能不能帮我们解答这些问题
“谁是忠信睿智的管家”
“受主人委派管理全体侍役”
“在适当的时候”
“把食物分配给各人呢?”
“主人来到  看见奴隶这样做”
“奴隶就有福了!”
“我老实告诉你们”
“主人必委派他管理一切财物”
我们刚刚在马太福音24章
看过类似的话  对吗?
耶稣在谈论同一件事
但请留意这一次耶稣是怎么说的
45节说
“可是奴隶如果心里说”
这和43节“奴隶就有福了!”
说的是同一个奴隶
继续看45节
“奴隶如果心里说”
“主人不会这么快回来”
“就动手打其他仆婢”
“又吃喝醉酒”
“奴隶的主人必在他意料不到的日子”
“在他不知道的时刻  突然来到”
“给他最重的惩罚”
到这里  我们就能看出
耶稣说的是同一个奴隶了
如果这个奴隶保持忠信
他就会得到奖赏
如果不忠信  他就会受到惩罚
比喻中的处女也是这样
如果处女保持忠信
就会得到奖赏
不然  就会受到惩罚
这个比喻也值得“大群人”留意
马可福音13:37耶稣说
“我对你们说的话”
“也是对所有人说的”
“要时刻守望”
正如受膏基督徒需要保持忠信
一直到大患难
同样  大群人也需要
一直保持忠信
我们从十个处女的比喻
可以学到什么呢?
要时刻守望!

titles.ko: 데이비드 H. 스플레인: 나는 당신들을 알지 못하오(마태 25:12)
titles.en: David H. Splane: I Do Not Know You (Matt. 25:12)
titles.cn: 戴维 · 斯普莱恩：我不认识你们（太25:12）

ko.text: 자신이 가진 것을 기꺼이 주고 싶어 합니다.
그들은 고린도 후서 9:7에 나오는 이러한 태도를 나타냅니다.
우리가 그런 관대한 태도를 보이는 한 가지 방법은
돈을 넣어 기부를 하는 방식에 익숙합니다.
그런데 최근에는 기부 방법에 변화가 생겨
이 새로운 도구를 어떻게 활용할 수 있는지
기부 정보가 나오는 페이지로 들어갈 수 있습니다.
그 나라에서 이용할 수 있는 기부 방법을 볼 수 있습니다.
나라에 따라 이용 가능한 기부 방법이 다를 수 있습니다.
사람들은 이 새로운 도구를 어떻게 활용하고 있을까요?
신용 카드나 체크 카드를 사용해 기부할 수 있습니다.
온라인 기부를 하기 위해 새로 계정을 만들 수 있습니다.
많은 사람은 ‘자신의 형편에 따라 매주 얼마를 따로 모아 두라’는
성경 고린도 전서 16:2의 말씀을 이미 따르고 있습니다.
온라인 기부도 그렇게 할 수 있습니다.
정기 기부를 설정해 놓으면 매월 자동으로 기부할 수 있습니다.
저는 헌금함에 돈을 넣는 걸 자꾸 잊어버리는 게 문제였습니다.
온라인 기부를 할 수 있다는 걸 알게 되었어요.
더 놀라웠던 건 매달 같은 금액을
자동으로 기부하도록 설정할 수 있다는 거였죠.
지금은 제 기부금이 잘 전달되었다는 영수증을 매달 받아요.
여호와께 도움이 되는 일을 매달 할 수 있어서 정말 행복합니다.
또 다른 방법으로 자신의 은행 계좌에서
일부 나라들의 경우, 지부 사무실로 기부금을 바로 보낼 수 있도록
이 계좌로 기부금을 보낼 수 있습니다.
제 계좌에서 바로 온라인 기부를 할 수 있어요.
수표나 우편환을 보내 기부하는 사람들도 있습니다.
수표나 우편환을 받을 곳에 관한 자세한 정보 역시
전 세계에서 이루어지고 있는 일들을 알게 되죠.
그럴 때마다 형제들의 수고에 감사를 표하고 싶다는 생각이 들어요.
이제는 몸이 불편해서 할 수 있는 일이 그리 많지는 않지만,
감사 편지와 수표를 보내 제 마음을 표현합니다.
이용할 수 있는 또 다른 방법으로 계획 기부가 있습니다.
유언, 신탁, 생명 보험 증권, 퇴직 연금 등을 활용해
사망 시에 자산을 기부하기로 할 수 있습니다.
또한 살아 있는 동안이나 사망 시에 양도성 예금 증서,
주식과 채권, 매각 가능한 부동산을 기부하기로 할 수도 있습니다.
우리가 예기치 않은 일이 발생하는 시대에 살고 있는데,
그래서 저희가 가진 자산을 여호와와 그분의 조직을 위해서
활용하는 것이 좋겠다 생각하게 되어서 계획 기부를 결정하게 되었습니다.
저도 제가 가지고 있는 모든 것은 여호와로부터 온 것이며,
그것을 여호와께 다시 돌려드릴 수 있다는 그 기회가
바로 제가 생각할 때 여호와께서 주신 축복이라고 생각합니다.
자신이 사는 나라에서 이용할 수 있는 방법들이 나와 있습니다.
어떤 방법들은 잘 계획하거나 더 많은 정보를 알아보고 선택해야 합니다.
궁금한 점이 있다면 해당 지부 사무실로 문의할 수 있습니다.
더 많은 정보를 요청하는 양식을 제출하면,
지부 사무실에서 며칠 내로 이메일을 보낼 것입니다.
또는 지부로 직접 전화를 걸어 문의할 수도 있습니다.
자신이 해 오던 방식대로 계속 기부하고 싶거나
새로운 도구를 활용하는 방법이 잘 이해되지 않는다면
물론 처음에는 어렵게 느껴질 수 있습니다.
하지만 회중의 믿을 만한 형제나 자매에게 도움을 받는다면
새로운 도구를 잘 활용할 수 있습니다.
그때에 마음이 감동된 모든 사람과 영이 고무된 모든 사람이 와서 ...
자신들이 여호와께 무엇을 바칠 수 있는지 알고 있었습니다.
우리도 어떤 다양한 방법과 도구를 활용해
기부 정보 페이지에 나오는 내용을 시간을 내어 살펴보고,
자신에게 가장 적합한 방법과 도구를 활용해 보십시오.
우리가 하는 기부는 모세 시대와 마찬가지로
순결한 숭배를 지원하는 데 사용된다는 것을 확신할 수 있습니다.
그분이 “기쁘게 주는 사람을 사랑하신다”는 것을 확신합니다.

也乐意施与
他们听从圣经在

en.text: In 1946, the first missionaries arrived in Peru,
and the good news spread quickly in the Spanish field.
However, centuries of mistreatment caused many Quechua-speaking people
to regard outsiders with reservation and mistrust.
Over the decades,
interested ones had to study in Spanish in order to learn the truth,
even if it wasn’t their first language.
It’s true that many Quechua speakers also understand Spanish;
it’s the language commonly used in business and taught in school.
However, it was noted that although they understood the words we were teaching,
the Bible’s message didn’t easily reach the heart.
The good news still had to be preached
not only in every nation
but to all “tribes and peoples and tongues.”
In 1992, the branch office in Peru received permission
to translate literature into Quechua
and to start a preaching initiative to test the response in the field.
When Quechua speakers were approached
with a warm greeting and presentation
in their own language,
it made a remarkable difference.
People started responding favorably to the message,
and many Bible studies were started.
Gradually, translators realized that it was necessary
to translate into other Quechua languages.
Just as there are a variety of cultures within Peru,
there are also a variety of Quechua languages spoken.
Translation teams were established where three of these languages are spoken
—in Ayacucho, Cuzco, and Huaraz.
In 2013, permission was granted to build
two new remote translation offices
—one in Cuzco and another in Ayacucho.
Many local and international brothers
volunteered to help on the building projects.
Whether rain or shine,
they worked together with a joyful spirit.
By early 2016, the new offices were ready to operate.
On May 1, 2016,
Brother Geoffrey Jackson of the Governing Body
delivered the dedication talk of these new facilities
to a delighted audience
from around the country.
We promise to use these buildings exclusively
for Jehovah’s praise and glory.
Do you accept our resolution?
These facilities are like gifts from Jehovah.
Not only are the new offices clean and beautiful
but they are specifically designed for the translation work.
One of the most important features of the new offices, therefore,
is the audio recording studio,
equipped with a special soundproof room
where high-quality recordings are produced.
Children and older ones alike
are captivated by videos of Juancito and Anita,
the Quechua version of Caleb and Sophia.
Just as when a tree grows and flourishes
when provided with an ample supply of water,
congregations have been growing and being fortified
by an increasing flow of spiritual food
in their own language.
This great ingathering of the Quechua people
to Jehovah’s organization
truly contributes to the fulfillment of the prophecy at Revelation 7:9:
“Look! A great crowd, . . . out of all nations
“and tribes and peoples and tongues,
“standing before the throne
and before the Lamb.”

en.text: Imitation really is built into human nature.
It’s one of our most used
and powerful learning tools.
I mean, think of all the things
that you’ve learned by imitation.
Even just think
of the current work assignments you have
or your job.
How much of it did you learn by just watching someone else do that work?
Children imitate their parents when they learn how to speak,
think, eat, and even walk just like them.
Children even learn to imitate the very subtle accents of their parents,
and those accents get passed on from one generation to the next.
I’ve had people say to me, “John, you walk just like your father.”
I have no idea how that happened.
Sometimes we imitate others, and we don’t even know that we’re doing it.
Have you ever been listening to the radio,
and a few hours later you’re humming or singing a song,
and you realize that that was the very song
that was on the radio several hours ago?
Imitation is such a part
of the human learning experience that we’re doing it all the time.
We can’t turn it off.
Imitation is also used by animals
to learn their skills by watching their parents.
I saw the cutest example of this
when we were watching a herd of elephants in Zambia.
The mother elephant and the baby elephant were walking by,
and the baby elephant was trying to grab some grass
and tear it off and put it in his mouth like his mother was;
but every time he did it, he ended up with nothing.
But he was sure watching his mom —how she was doing it—
and seeing how he could imitate and get some of that for himself.
Well, since imitation is such a powerful learning tool
and has such an effect on the person we are
and the person that we are to become,
we need to be very careful about who we choose to imitate.
Who do you choose to imitate?
Well, see, who we choose to imitate determines who we want to become.
That’s why there’s so much caution in the Scriptures about our association,
because who we choose to imitate rubs off on us, so to speak,
in subtle ways that we might not even notice right away.
Notice the counsel given to the Israelites
about not imitating the nations around them.
If you look at Exodus 23:24,
notice the counsel that Jehovah gave to the Israelites.
He said: “You must not bow down to their gods
“or be persuaded to serve them,
and you must not imitate their practices.”
And he continues this thought at Deuteronomy 18:9.
Deuteronomy 18:9, it says:
“When you have entered into the land that Jehovah your God is giving you,
“you must not learn to imitate
the detestable practices of those nations.”
Well, what happened when the Israelites chose to imitate the nations around them,
to ignore the advice Jehovah had given them?
Well, let’s look at 2 Kings 17:15.
Second Kings 17:15:
“They continued rejecting his regulations and his covenant
“that he had made with their forefathers
“and his reminders that he had given to warn them,
“and they kept following worthless idols
“[And notice what happened to them when they did that.]
“and became worthless themselves,
“imitating the nations all around them
that Jehovah had commanded them not to imitate.”
So if we imitate worthless things, what’s going to happen to us?
We’re going to be worthless.
If we fast-forward to Christian times,
we can see that the same advice was given to us.
If we look at 3 John 11,
it’s very straightforward advice:
“Beloved one, do not imitate what is bad,
“but imitate what is good.
“The one who does good originates with God.
The one who does bad has not seen God.”
Well, the message is clear.
If we want to ‘see God,’ or have a good relationship with Jehovah,
then we need to imitate what is good.
And our text for today at Ephesians 5:1
really says it about as simply and clearly as we can:
“Become imitators of God.”
So Jehovah is telling us in our text for today: ‘Imitate me.’
So if someone asks us, “Who do you choose to imitate?”
we follow the advice of Ephesians 5:1;
we want to imitate Jehovah.
Well, how can we imitate Jehovah?
Well, first, one way is by reading the Bible.
We have learned love, hope, faith, loyalty,
and so many other fine qualities
by reading about how Jehovah wants us to conduct ourselves.
I mean, look at the Law that Jehovah gave to the nation of Israel.
We can learn so much about how Jehovah
feels about being honest, clean, fair, just.
Or in different Bible examples, we see Jehovah’s patience
in dealing with Jonah and His mercy in dealing with the Ninevites.
Reading the Bible gives us a very clear picture
of our perfect God, Jehovah, who we worship.
And he gives us the perfect role model to imitate.
When we read the Bible and continually ask ourselves,
‘What do I learn about Jehovah, and how can I learn to imitate him?’
that really is like us keeping our eye on Jehovah, with our mind’s eye,
and watching what he’s doing, and we’re imitating him.
Another way that we can imitate Jehovah
is by imitating others who are imitating him.
Jehovah has used the pages of the Bible
to give us real-life stories of people who we can imitate.
I mean, we’ve never met Abraham and Sarah,
but don’t you feel like you know them?
I’m sure there’s much more that we can learn
about these beautiful, spiritual people in the new world,
but what is laid out in the Scriptures is enough
for us to imitate the beautiful examples they set for us.
Or what about Jesus?
We’ve never met Jesus,
but by reading the Bible accounts,
don’t you feel like you know him
and you know how he would react and think about certain situations?
The apostle Paul simply explained this
at 1 Corinthians 11:1.
He said: “Become imitators of me, . . . as I am of Christ.”
So we have Jesus Christ as an example of imitating his Father.
The apostle Paul was imitating Christ.
Now, the apostle Paul, of course, wasn’t saying,
“Imitate the way I give my talks; imitate the way I move;
imitate the way I walk or say things.”
But at Hebrews 13:7,
he stressed what it was that we were to imitate about others,
Hebrews 13:7:
“Remember those who are taking the lead among you,
“who have spoken the word of God to you,
“and as you contemplate how their conduct turns out,
imitate their faith.”
So we are to imitate the faith
and example that others set in imitating Jesus and imitating Jehovah.
Now, to illustrate the choice that we have of who we’re going to imitate,
I’d like you to imagine in your mind
two big, huge machines with lots of parts.
Now, one machine is run by Jehovah and Jesus Christ,
and the other machine is run by Satan and the world.
And I want you to imagine that you’re a part on the mechanics bench.
When Jehovah goes to pick you up and look at you and see,
Do you fit as a part in his organization?
well, we can if we imitate him
and other spiritual people who are useful to Jehovah.
We can become a useful part of his beautiful organization.
If we imitate Jehovah, then if Satan goes over to that bench
and picks us up and tries to put us into his machine,
we’re not going to fit anywhere.
We are no part of his world or organization.
I mean, how sad it would be
if we shaped and imitated ourselves after the world
and when Satan picked us up we fit right in
with his machine and organization!
So who do you choose to imitate?
We choose to imitate Jehovah.
We want to be just like him when we grow up.
How can we imitate Jehovah?
By getting to know him personally through reading the Bible
and imitating others who are imitating him.

cn.text: 模仿是人的天性
这是我们最常用的一种学习方式
而且特别有效
请想想有哪些事情
是你通过模仿而学到的
比如说  你现在所做的工作
有多少技能是你通过观察别人
而学会的呢?
孩子会模仿父母说话
思考  吃饭的方式
甚至连走路姿势也会模仿他们
孩子也会模仿父母的口音
结果他们家的这种口音
就会一代代传下去
有人曾经对我说
约翰  你走路的样子很像你父亲
我也不知道是怎么学来的
有时候
我们不知不觉就在模仿别人了
你有过这样的经历吗?
有一天你听了收音机广播
几个小时后  你忽然发现
自己不知不觉在哼唱
之前收音机里播放的那首歌
可见  模仿是人类学习的一个重要方法
这是不可缺少的
我们总是在模仿
动物也会模仿它们的父母
通过观察学习一些技能
我曾在赞比亚看到一个非常可爱的画面
当时有一群大象从我们身旁经过
我们看到一头小象跟着它的妈妈
小象努力模仿妈妈的样子
用鼻子卷起一些草
想拔起来送到嘴里
但总是什么也吃不到
不过它显然是在留心观察它的妈妈
看她是怎样做的
并学着妈妈的样子自己拔草吃
所以说
模仿真的是个很有效的学习方法
会对我们有很大的影响
也会决定我们将来成为怎样的人
因此我们必须谨慎选择
自己要模仿的对象
你想要模仿谁呢?
从我们选择的模仿对象
可以看出我们想成为怎样的人
这就是为什么圣经多次提醒我们
要小心来往的对象
因为我们和谁来往
就会模仿对方
不知不觉就会受到影响
不会立刻察觉到
我们知道
古代以色列人也受到劝告
不要模仿周围的民族
请看出埃及记23:24
这是耶和华给以色列人的劝告
经文说
“你不可跪拜他们的神”
“也不可受引诱去事奉他们的神”
“不可仿造他们所造的任何偶像”
类似的劝告也记载在申命记18:9
我们看看这里说什么呢?
经文说
“你进了耶和华你上帝赐给你的地以后”
“不可学当地国民所做的可憎之事”
可是  以色列人
却选择漠视耶和华的劝告
模仿周围民族的行径
结果怎样呢?
我们看看列王纪下17:15
我们一起看看这里说了什么?
“他们弃绝了上帝的条例”
“背弃了上帝跟他们祖先所立的约”
“又不理会上帝所叮嘱的劝戒”
“转去跟随无用的偶像”
请留意结果怎样呢?
“自己也成为无用的人”
“他们还跟从周围的外族人”
“就是耶和华吩咐他们不可跟从的”
所以如果我们的模仿对象没有价值
我们也会变得一无是处
在早期基督徒生活的时代
也有相同的劝告
请看约翰三书11节
这里的建议很直接
“亲爱的弟兄”
“不要仿效邪恶”
“倒要仿效良善”
“行善的源于上帝”
“作恶的没有看见过上帝”
这里说得很清楚
如果我们想“看见”上帝
想跟耶和华有良好的关系
就需要“仿效良善”
今天的经文以弗所书5:1
简单明了地告诉我们
“要效法上帝”
耶和华通过这节经文对我们说
要向我学习
所以如果有人问
你想向谁学习呢?
我们会听从以弗所书5:1的建议
向耶和华学习
那么  我们要怎样向耶和华学习呢?
一个方法是阅读圣经
通过阅读圣经
我们学到耶和华希望我们怎样行事为人
我们学会表现爱心
希望  信心  忠贞
以及其他很多美好的特质
比如  从耶和华给以色列民族的律法
我们可以知道
耶和华对诚实  洁净
公平公正有什么看法
又比如  从耶和华对待约拿
和尼尼微的方式
我们可以看出他的耐心和仁慈
阅读圣经可以让我们更清楚地看出
我们崇拜的耶和华是完美的上帝
他为我们树立了完美的榜样
阅读的时候可以经常问问自己
关于耶和华  我们学到什么?
我该怎样向他学习呢?
这就好像我们在观察耶和华
用我们的心眼观察他怎样做
然后自己也照着做
效法耶和华的另一个方法就是
以那些效法上帝的人为榜样
圣经记载了一些人物的真实故事
我们可以向他们学习
比如说  虽然我们从来没见过
亚伯拉罕和撒拉
却感觉认识他们  不是吗?
相信未来在新世界里
我们可以更认识这些值得赞赏的忠仆
即使在现在
我们通过圣经记载的事迹
也能向这些好榜样学到很多
再比如说耶稣
虽然我们从来没见过他
但是通过圣经的记载
我们就能认识他
也知道他在面对某些情况时
会怎么想  怎么做
在哥林多前书11:1
使徒保罗清楚地解释道
“你们要效法我  像我效法基督一样”
所以  耶稣基督效法上帝
而使徒保罗又效法基督
当然  他并不是说
你们要学习我做演讲的方式
学习我走路的方式  说话的方式
在希伯来书13:7
保罗强调了我们该怎样效法别人
经文说
“要记住那些领导你们的人”
“就是素来向你们传讲上帝话语的人”
“你们要仔细留意”
“他们处世做人的成果”
“效法他们的信心”
所以  我们要效法的是别人的信心
学习他们在效法耶和华和耶稣方面
立下的好榜样
关于选择模仿的对象
我想打个比方
请想象一下
有两台需要很多零件的大型机器
一台是耶和华和耶稣的
另一台是撒但和这个世界的
想象一下你是一个机器零件
耶和华拿起你这个零件
仔细端详
看看你能不能用在他的机器上
你会是对他的组织有用的人吗?
如果我们效法耶和华和他的忠仆
就可以成为
他组织里的一个有用的零件
如果我们效法耶和华
当撒但拿起我们
想把我们安装到他的机器上
就会发现  装在哪儿都不合适
我们不属于世界
不是撒但组织的一部分
可是  如果我们刻意迎合模仿世人
结果会怎样呢?
当撒但把我们拿起来安装在他的机器上
放在他的组织里  会发现特别合适
那就太可悲了!
那么你要效法谁呢?
要效法耶和华
我们希望不断进步
越来越像我们的天父
我们怎样效法耶和华呢?
就是要经常阅读圣经
还要向那些效法上帝的人学习
真正认识耶和华

en.text: An introduction to the book of John.
When he was a much younger man,
John and his brother James were mending their fishing nets
alongside the Sea of Galilee
when Jesus invited them to be his followers.
After the Passover of 31 C.E.,
Jesus chose John as one of his 12 apostles.
John was among Jesus’ closest companions
and the disciple to whom he entrusted the care of his mother, Mary.
The Gospel of John
is the last of the four Gospels.
It was written about 98 C.E.,
in or around Ephesus
—nearly 65 years after Jesus’ death.
During those decades,
Jesus’ prophecy concerning
the destruction of Jerusalem was fulfilled.
It is said that 92 percent of this book
contains material not covered
in the other Gospels.
John writes about love more than any other Gospel writer.
The book of John contains 21 chapters.
Chapter 1 reveals Jesus’ role in the heavens before coming to earth.
He is described as the one through whom Jehovah created all other things.
Jesus is called “the Word,”
highlighting his assignment as Jehovah’s spokesman.
Chapters 2 to 6 cover about two years of Jesus’ ministry.
Chapter 2 describes Jesus’ first miracle at a wedding feast in Cana.
When the wine ran out, he miraculously turned
some 380 liters, or 100 gallons, of water
into “fine wine.”
Seeing this miracle strengthened the faith of Jesus’ disciples.
Chapter 6 reports how Jesus miraculously fed a crowd
of about 5,000 men, along with women and children.
Chapters 7 to 12 cover the events
following the Passover of 32 C.E.
Jesus travels to Bethany
and resurrects his friend Lazarus.
Although Lazarus had been dead for four days,
he comes back to life at Jesus’ command.
Chapter 12 contains a description
of Jesus’ triumphal entry into Jerusalem.
A large crowd greets him with the words:
“Save, we pray you!
“Blessed is the one who comes in Jehovah’s name,
the King of Israel!”
Chapters 13 to 19
relate the events of just one day,
Nisan 14, 33 C.E.
Jesus celebrates the Passover with his apostles
in an upper room in Jerusalem.
Did you know?
We can find evidence in the book of John
that supports the fact
that Jesus celebrated four Passovers
during his ministry.
This provides one of the lines of evidence
that his ministry was
three and a half years long.
Showing great humility at the final Passover,
Jesus performs the duty of a servant,
washing the feet of his apostles.
Later that evening, Jesus says:
“I am giving you a new commandment,
“that you love one another;
just as I have loved you.”
The commandment was new
because it required that Christ’s disciples
show love to a greater degree.
Chapter 17 contains Jesus’ last prayer
in the presence of his disciples.
Later in the garden of Gethsemane,
Jesus fearlessly identifies himself
to the soldiers who come to arrest him.
Shortly thereafter,
Jesus suffers death for all mankind.
Chapters 20 and 21
relate how the resurrected Jesus
appears to his disciples on various occasions.
As you read the Gospel of John,
note Jesus’ love for mankind,
his example of humility,
and his identity as the Messiah, the King of God’s Kingdom.

cn.text: 约翰年轻的时候
他和他的兄弟雅各
在加利利海的岸边修补鱼网
他们受到耶稣的邀请
成为他的门徒
公元31年逾越节后
约翰被耶稣选为使徒
约翰是耶稣的密友
耶稣在死前
将母亲马利亚托付给他
约翰福音是四福音中最后完成的
约翰可能在以弗所
或附近写成约翰福音
当时大约是公元98年
距离耶稣去世将近65年
在这之前
耶路撒冷已如耶稣所预告的
被毀灭了
约翰福音中的资料
有百分之92是其他福音书没有的
约翰比其他的福音书执笔者
更常提到爱
约翰福音一共有21章
第1章记载耶稣降世为人之前的身份
他在耶和华身边
协助耶和华创造一切
耶稣被称为“话语”
表示耶和华委任耶稣做他的代言人
第2至6章记录耶稣传道工作
头两年发生的事
第2章记录耶稣施行的第一个奇迹
他去迦拿参加婚宴
婚宴进行到一半
酒就没了
于是耶稣将380升的水
变成上等好酒
这个奇迹使门徒对耶稣更有信心
第6章记载耶稣施行奇迹
喂饱将近五千名男子
还有很多妇女和小孩
第7至12章记录
发生在公元32年逾越节之后的事
耶稣去伯大尼复活他的好友拉撒路
虽然拉撒路已经死了四天
但耶稣施行奇迹
将他从死里复活
第12章描述
耶稣进耶路撒冷城时
受到民众热情地欢迎
他们向耶稣欢呼说
上帝啊，愿你施行拯救！
奉耶和华的名而来的以色列王有福了！
第13至19章
讲述公元33年
尼散月14日发生的事
耶稣和门徒
在耶路撒冷一所房子的楼上
庆祝逾越节
你知道吗？
根据约翰的记载
耶稣传道期间
一共过了四次逾越节

title: 마크 누메어: "생명의 말씀을 계속 굳게 잡으십시오"

ko.text: ‎‪길르앗 학교에 가 보는 게 평생 소원인 분들이 많은데,‏
‎‪이 과정은 학생들이 ‘생명의 말씀을 굳게 잡게’ 도와주죠.‏
‎‪5개월간의 집중 학습이 부담스러운 분들도 계실 겁니다.‏
‎‪하느님의 말씀을 읽는 일에서 최대의 유익을 끌어내기가‏
‎‪그리고 연구 시간에 더 많은 유익을 얻는 방법입니다.‏
‎‪학교에 갈 수 없는 많은 분을 위해‏
‎‪연구하지 않고선 “생명의 말씀을 굳게 잡을” 수 없기 때문이죠.‏
‎‪수감된 사도 바울이 이 말을 기록했을 땐‏
‎‪활동으로 가득 찬 그의 삶도 저물고 있었습니다.‏
‎‪그는 세계 곳곳에 하느님의 말씀을 전하며 황금기를 보냈죠.‏
‎‪마케도니아에 있는 빌립보 회중 형제 자매들에게 편지를 썼습니다.‏
‎‪영감을 받아 바울은 동료 형제들이 영원한 생명의 상을 얻는 데‏
‎‪자신의 권고를 잘 들은 동료들과 재회했을 때‏
‎‪바울의 말은 우리가 영원한 생명을 얻는 데 도움이 됩니다.‏
‎‪우리가 마지막 날을 통과해 영원한 생명의 상을 얻게 해 줄‏
‎‪기본적인 조언을 정신과 마음에 새기게 해 주죠.‏
‎‪나무랄 데 없고 흠 없는’ 상태를 유지할 것입니까?‏
‎‪하느님의 충실한 종들과 함께 신세계에서 기뻐할 수 있을 것입니까?‏
‎‪“생명의 말씀을 계속 굳게 잡으라”는 바울의 조언을 마음에 새긴다면‏
‎‪우리는 반드시 그렇게 할 수 있을 것입니다.‏
‎‪‘계속 굳게 잡는다’는 말은 어떤 모습을 떠올리게 하나요?‏
‎‪그처럼, 생명의 말씀을 계속 굳게 잡는 건‏
‎‪하느님이 분명히 명하거나 금하신 걸 아는 것만으론 부족하죠.‏
‎‪성경에 담긴 원칙들 즉 중요한 교훈점들을 분별할 수 있어야 합니다.‏
‎‪이 값진 진리가 우리 삶의 특정한 상황들에‏
‎‪결정을 내릴 때 그리고 시련이나 유혹에 대처할 때‏
‎‪‘나는 생명의 말씀을 얼마나 굳게 잡고 있는가?’‏
‎‪우린 흔히 즉석에서 정보를 찾아 그 내용을 바로 언급할 수 있지만,‏
‎‪물론, 우린 제공된 모든 연구 도구에 감사합니다.‏
‎‪그로 인해 정신적 게으름에 빠지지 않도록 주의해야 합니다.‏
‎‪링크 기능을 사용해 성구를 읽을 수 있습니다.‏
‎‪터치 한 번만 하면 금방 성구를 찾아 볼 수 있습니다.‏
‎‪꾸준히 이렇게 하면 생명의 말씀을 잡을 수 있습니다.‏
‎‪그러려면 손가락으로 쓸어 넘기며 빨리 내용을 훑어보는 것보다‏
‎‪여러분의 마음과 정신에 분명하고 또렷하게 새겨질 것입니다.‏
‎‪그럼 연구할 때 어떻게 더 큰 유익을 얻을 수 있을까요?‏
‎‪보시게 될 시는 영국의 작가인 러디어드 키플링이 쓴 것인데‏
‎‪하느님의 말씀을 연구할 때 이 질문들을 자문해 본 뒤에,‏
‎‪야곱이 생을 마칠 즈음 이 말을 했다는 걸 알게 됩니다.‏
‎‪야곱의 가지 중에 요셉은 형제들보다 더 뛰어난,‏
‎‪요셉에게 인도하는 데 필요한 특성들이 있었기 때문이죠.‏
‎‪하지만 그런 능력보다 더 가치 있는 것으로‏
‎‪질문을 통해 연구를 영적인 방향으로 이끌어 보죠.‏
‎‪이 기록은 여호와에 관해 무엇을 가르쳐 줍니까?‏
‎‪여호와는 자신의 충실한 종들을 결코 버리지 않으십니다.‏
‎‪이제 여러분을 포함한 오늘날의 여호와의 백성과 연관 지어 보시죠.‏
‎‪영혼을 다해 자신을 섬기는 모두에게 충성스런 사랑을 보이시죠.‏
‎‪이 기록은 성경의 주제와 어떻게 연관되어 있습니까?‏
‎‪요셉은 고난을 겪었지만 그로 인해 아브라함의 후손이 생존할 수 있었고,‏
‎‪그들과 관계를 개선하기 위해 먼저 손을 내미셨습니다.‏
‎‪우리의 반응은 여호와의 영이 우리와 함께한다는 걸 드러낼 것입니까?‏
‎‪성경 기록이 우리의 것이 되게 해 줍니다.‏
‎‪우리의 사고 방식과 행동 방식의 일부가 되게 해 주죠.‏
‎‪흥미롭긴 하지만 금방 잊혀질 정보들의 모음이 아니라‏
‎‪우리의 결정에 영향을 미치고 우리의 삶을 인도할 수 있는‏
‎‪연구의 3단계를 수확, 체질, 빵 굽기에 비유할 수 있습니다.‏
‎‪뛰어다니며 그저 곡식을 한 움큼 움켜쥐는 게 아니라,‏
‎‪체질은 ‘누가, 언제, 어디서, 무엇을, 어떻게, 왜’ 질문을 사용해‏
‎‪어느 누가 대신 해 줄 수 없습니다.‏
‎‪질문들은 연구를 영적인 방향으로 이끌어 줄 수 있습니다.‏
‎‪그 내용이 여호와에 관해 무엇을 가르쳐 주는지,‏
‎‪사고력을 기를 수 있는 능력을 선물로 주셨습니다.‏
‎‪연구가 보람 있고 즐거운 일이 될 것입니다.‏
‎‪생명의 말씀을 계속 굳게 잡을 수 있죠.‏

en.text: How would you feel
if you received an invitation
to attend the next class of Gilead School?
For many, it has been a lifelong dream to attend Gilead.
The course helps students keep “a tight grip on the word of life.”
For others, the idea of five months of intense study seems intimidating.
We know we need to study,
but we may find it a challenge to get the most
out of the time we spend reading God’s Word.
In this program, we will discuss why study is so important,
what it means to study something,
and how you can get more from your study sessions.
Since most cannot attend Gilead,
we will demonstrate the method used in Gilead School.
First, why is study so important?
Only by study can we keep “a tight grip on the word of life.”
When the apostle Paul penned these words,
he was imprisoned and nearing the end of his action-packed life.
He had been the “apostle to the nations”
and had spent his best years
taking the Word of God to the then-known world.
As he reflected on the fruits of his labors,
he wrote a letter to his friends in the congregation in Philippi in Macedonia.
Inspired by holy spirit, he wrote words
that would aid his brothers to gain the prize of eternal life.
These words are found at Philippians 2:15, 16.
Let’s read them:
“So that you may come to be blameless and innocent,
“children of God without a blemish in the midst
“of a crooked and twisted generation,
“among whom you are shining as illuminators in the world,
keeping a tight grip on the word of life.”
Imagine the joy Paul felt
when he was reunited in the heavenly resurrection
with those who listened to his admonition
to keep “a tight grip on the word of life”!
Whether we have the heavenly or earthly hope,
Paul’s words can help us gain the prize of eternal life.
They imprint on our hearts and minds a basic exhortation
that will lead us through these last days and into our everlasting reward.
The question is, Will we remain ‘blameless and without blemish
in the midst of this crooked and twisted generation’ of our day?
Will we rejoice with other faithful servants of God in the new world?
We can and we will
if we take to heart Paul’s counsel
to keep “a tight grip on the word of life.”
Next, what does it mean to study?
Stop and contemplate this word picture
for keeping a tight grip.
Imagine a hiker who has slipped near a ledge.
But before falling over the cliff, he grabs hold of a tree branch.
How tight do you think his grip will be on that branch?
This is not a halfhearted effort.
Likewise, keeping a tight grip on the word of life
is not just a mechanical routine, nor is it a casual habit.
It requires strenuous effort.
It involves actively living by the truths in God’s Word.
To do this, we must understand
more than what God expressly commands and condemns.
We must be able to identify principles,
or life lessons, contained in the Bible.
Once identified, we must understand
how to match these valuable truths
to specific situations in our lives.
Then we must allow these principles to influence our decisions
and guide our reaction to trials and temptations.
Ask yourself,
‘How strong is my grip on the word of life?’
To answer that,
let’s consider the fundamentals of Bible study.
This is not about old methods or new methods,
nor is it about what device you are using.
This discussion transcends devices.
Study requires active thinking.
In a world of increasing distractions,
this is becoming an even greater challenge.
We’ve often received instant information
that enables us to quickly recite facts,
but this is not the same as active thinking.
Through active thinking,
we draw meaningful conclusions in our hearts.
We are certainly grateful for all the study tools we’ve been given.
We should use these to the full.
At the same time, we need to be careful
that these tools do not cause us to develop mental laziness.
Devices can help us to access information,
but they can’t think for us.
We must work hard if we are to develop new patterns of thinking.
For example, if we study The Watchtower on a device,
we can use the hyperlink feature to read the Scriptures.
With a simple touch, we quickly find and read the verse.
That is good!
If you regularly do this, you get a grip on the word of life.
But would you like to get a tight grip on the word of life?
To get a tight grip requires more effort
than a swipe of a finger and then swiftly moving on.
You need to slow down and analyze the material.
Only then will the information you study
become imprinted on your mind and heart,
leaving a clear and distinct impression.
How, then, can I get more out of my study?
Let’s demonstrate a method taught during Gilead School.
It involves the use of six questions.
The following poem, written by English journalist Rudyard Kipling,
can help guide better thinking:
“I keep six honest serving-men
“(They taught me all I knew);
“Their names are What and Why
“and When and How
and Where and Who.”
When studying God’s Word, ask yourself these questions
and then do research in our publications
to get the facts and discern the spiritual lessons.
To illustrate how to do this,
let’s open our Bibles to Genesis chapter 49
and look at verses 22 through 25.
First, we ask the when and where.
Now, with some research,
we learn that Jacob spoke these words near the end of his life.
He was in Egypt,
but what he described takes us back to Canaan some 40 years
when his son Joseph was a young man.
Now we have a clearer picture of these verses.
So now, let’s read and analyze verse 22:
“Joseph is the offshoot of a fruitful tree,
a fruitful tree by a spring, whose branches extend over the wall.”
“The offshoot of a fruitful tree.”
Who is the “fruitful tree”?
It is Joseph’s father, Jacob.
How was he fruitful?
He bore many children.
Joseph’s “branches extend over the wall.”
As Jacob’s offshoot, Joseph is singled out
for a special blessing superior to that of his brothers.
Why?
Joseph proved he had the qualities needed for leadership.
However, of even greater value than his abilities
was his being a spiritual man.
Let’s read verse 23:
“But the archers kept harassing him
and shot at him and kept harboring animosity against him.”
“The archers kept harassing him.”
Who are “the archers”?
Joseph’s half brothers.
How?
They shot figuratively at Joseph
—arrows of envy and hatred and jealousy were used to attack him.
Now, eventually, his brothers sold him into slavery.
Now let’s read verse 24:
“And yet his bow remained in place,
“and his hands stayed strong and agile.
“This was from the hands of the powerful one of Jacob,
from the shepherd, the stone of Israel.”
“His bow remained in place.”
How?
Despite the repeated attacks,
Joseph repaid animosity with kindness.
Joseph endured this ill-treatment
and did not weaken in his devotion to God.
Now we ask, How?
How is it that Joseph kept a spiritual outlook
despite the harassment and animosity?
Let’s read verse 25:
“He [Joseph] is from the God of your father,
“and he will help you, and he is with the Almighty,
“and he will bless you with the blessings of the heavens above,
“with the blessings of the deep below,
with the blessings of the breasts and womb.”
“He is with the Almighty.”
Joseph had Jehovah’s help.
The Almighty was by his side through it all.
We’ve used our questions to get the facts of the account,
but we’re not done.
Now let’s use them to take our study to a spiritual plane.
Next, let’s ask a what question.
What does this account teach us about Jehovah?
Jehovah never abandons his loyal servants.
Even in the depths of prison, Joseph was not alone.
Jehovah found ways to bless Joseph.
Now make the connection to Jehovah’s people today,
including yourself.
Jehovah will never abandon us.
Rather, he shows loyal love to all those who serve him whole-souled.
Would Jehovah let Joseph remain in prison indefinitely?
No.
At the appointed time, relief came.
Joseph was raised from a prisoner in chains
to the second most powerful man in Egypt
—from prison to palace in one day.
Make the connection to us.
Our trials are temporary.
Jehovah will soon bring relief,
even in unexpected or surprising ways.
Meanwhile, we are never alone;
Jehovah is with us.
Again, let’s ask the question, How?
How does the account contribute to the Bible’s theme?
Joseph suffered, but his suffering led
to the survival of Abraham’s offspring,
leading to the Messiah.
Joseph’s account is not just a riveting story.
It directly contributed
to the development of Jehovah’s purpose.
Think about this:
In spite of the poor conduct of his brothers,
Joseph forgave them and took the initiative
to improve their relationship with him.
Joseph’s attitude was a reflection of Jehovah’s attitude.
With their family reunited,
Jehovah also forgave Joseph’s brothers
and took the initiative in restoring their relationship with Himself.
In fact, Jehovah gave Joseph’s brother Judah
the honor of being an ancestor of the Messiah.
What are the lessons in this account?
Let’s highlight just one.
Genesis 49:23:
“But the archers kept harassing him
and shot at him and kept harboring animosity against him.”
Arrows of animosity were fired at Joseph.
Recall Joseph’s response in verse 24?
“And yet his bow remained in place,
and his hands stayed strong and agile.”
In other words, he did not return fire.
His bow remained in place.
Reflect on the last time you were wronged by someone.
How did we react to what we experienced?
Did we seek to vindicate ourselves or insist on our rights?
Did we fire arrows of animosity in return,
or did we show mercy and loyal love?
Did our reaction reveal that God’s spirit was operative on us?
Like Joseph, we know we will have Jehovah’s approval
even if we are wronged or experience trials
that make us feel like we are in prison.
Reflective questions like these
enable us to make the account our own.
It becomes part of us,
part of our way of thinking, our way of acting.
This nourishes our relationship with Jehovah.
This type of study rewards us not simply with a collection of facts
that impress us today and are forgotten tomorrow.
Rather, it leaves us with core principles that we remember,
that influence our decisions, and that guide our lives.
We tighten our grip on the word of life.
Let’s review the fundamentals of study.
Again, this is not about old methods or new methods
or about what device you are using.
This discussion transcends devices.
It’s about basic methods of Bible study.
We can liken these three phases of study
to gathering, sifting, and baking grain.
Gathering is when we read the Bible.
We don’t run through the field grabbing just handfuls of grain;
we systematically harvest the field.
Sifting is when we sort out what we gathered,
answering who, what, where, when, why, and how to get the facts.
Baking is when we think
—“turning up the heat” in our mind and heart—
something no one else can do for you.
The questions we ask can take our study to a spiritual plane.
Most importantly, what does this teach me about Jehovah?
How does it contribute to the Bible’s theme?
And the bottom line: What is the lesson for me?
Jehovah gave us a mind that is begging to learn.
It is a gift with the capacity to cultivate thinking ability.
When we make the effort to unearth gems from God’s Word,
we find that study is rewarding and delightful.
More importantly, our study skills enable us
to keep a tight grip on the word of life.
A tight grip on God’s Word will make our life better now
and give us the opportunity to continue learning
about our heavenly Father for all eternity.

cn.text: 假如你被邀请参加下一届基列学校
会有什么感觉呢?
这是很多人毕生的愿望
因为基列的课程能帮助学员
“紧握生命的话语”
不过  对另一些人来说
五个月的高强度课程
听起来有点可怕
我们知道我们需要研读圣经
但想要从研读获得最大的益处
这可能是个挑战
在这期节目中  我们会讨论一下
为什么研读十分重要
研读意味着什么
以及你可以怎样
从研读的安排获得更多益处
考虑到大部分人
都没有机会参加基列学校
所以  我们会先示范一下
基列学校的研读方法
首先  为什么说研读十分重要呢?
因为只有通过研读
我们才能“紧握生命的话语”
这是使徒保罗在被囚期间写的
那时候他的生命快到尽头了
保罗的一生忙碌而充实
他在外邦人当中做使徒
善用一生最宝贵的岁月
把上帝的话语传遍当时所知的世界
回想自己以往辛劳的成果时
保罗就给腓立比会众的朋友们
写了一封信
在圣灵的启示下
保罗向那里的弟兄姐妹们提出劝勉
帮助他们得到永生的奖赏
这些话记在腓立比书2:15,16
想象一下
那些弟兄们听从了保罗的劝勉
“紧握生命的话语”
当他们和保罗
都复活到天上重聚的时候
保罗该有多么开心啊!
不管我们的希望
是在天上还是在地上
保罗的话都能帮助我们
赢得永生的奖赏
如果我们把保罗的鼓励和劝勉
铭记在心
就可以在最后的日子忍耐到底
最终得到永生
问题是
我们会“无可指责”
“在这一代歪邪不正的人当中”
“毫无瑕疵”吗?
我们会进入新世界
和上帝的其他忠心仆人一同欢乐吗?
如果我们将保罗的劝告谨记在心
“紧握生命的话语”
就一定会!
接着我们谈谈  研读是什么意思
请想象一下
当你紧紧抓住某样东西的时候的感觉
假如一个登山的人
不小心从悬崖上滑了下去
就在这时  他抓住了一根树枝
你觉得他抓得有多紧呢?
他一定使出浑身的力气抓住那根树枝
同样  “紧握生命的话语”
不是一种机械性的常规
也不是一个漫不经心的习惯
相反  我们必须要竭尽全力
在生活的各个方面
努力实践圣经的真理
要做到这一点
只知道上帝的要求还不够
我们还要看出圣经中
包含的原则和教训
然后  仔细想一想
如何把这些原则
在生活中具体地运用出来
我们在做决定时必须考虑这些原则
也要用这些原则
帮助我们去面对考验和引诱
请问问自己
我对生命的话语握得有多紧呢?
为了回答这个问题
我们来考虑一下研读圣经的基本方法
我要说的不是该用印刷版
还是电子版圣经来研读
也不是说要用什么设备研读更好
我想强调的是
在研读中最重要的一点
那就是要深入思考
这个世界令人分心的事越来越多
想要深入思考真的不容易
我们随时能收到各种信息
可以知道很多事实
但知道和深入思考是不一样的
深入思考意味着我们会仔细分析
彻底想清楚自己该怎么做
当然
我们很感激组织提供的各种研读工具
也应该好好善用这些工具
但同时  我们也要当心
这些便利的工具
也许会让我们越来越懒得思考
电子产品可以帮助我们得到信息
但不能替我们思考
如果想养成新的思考习惯
我们就必须下苦功
比方说
用电子设备研读《守望台》时
我们可以用文章里的经文链接
来查看相关的经文
只要轻轻点一下  经文就出来了
这很方便
如果你经常用这个功能
就能握住生命的话语
不过  你想不想
紧紧握住生命的话语呢?
想要“紧握生命的话语”
就要付出更多努力
不只是用手指划两下
匆匆读过就算了
相反  要放慢速度
仔细分析研读的资料
只有这样
你所学习的內容
才会深印在你的头脑和內心
推动你采取相应的行动
那么  该如何从研读获得最大益处呢?
我想分享一下
基列学校所教的一个方法
这个方法就是通过六个问题来思考
下面这首诗提到了可以怎么思考
这是英国记者鲁德亚德·吉卜林写的
研读上帝的话语时
要问问自己这些问题
然后查考组织的出版物
深入挖掘相关的细节
看看可以学到什么
让我们一起试试这个方法
请翻开圣经
我们会看看创世记49:22-25
首先  考虑一下何时  何地
稍微查一些资料就会看出
这是雅各临终前说的话
当时他在埃及
不过他的话让我们想到
大约40年前
约瑟年轻时在迦南地所经历的事
了解完经文的背景之后
让我们再来分析一下22节
“果实累累的树上的枝子”
“果实累累的树”是谁呢?
就是约瑟的父亲雅各
他生了很多孩子  确实果实累累
经文也说
约瑟的“枝条向上伸延  越过墙头”
在雅各的孩子们中  约瑟与众不同
他得到了上帝特别的赐福
为什么呢?
约瑟的经历表明
他具备领导的才能
不过  比这些更宝贵的是
约瑟是个属灵的人
接着23节
经文说  “弓箭手扰害他”
“弓箭手”是谁?
约瑟同父异母的哥哥们
怎样对待约瑟呢?
他们嫉妒约瑟  仇视他
仿佛朝他射箭  不断攻击他
最后甚至把他卖为奴隶
接着24节
约瑟的弓怎样“坚定长存”呢?
尽管不断受到攻击
约瑟仍然表现仁慈  以善胜恶
虽然受到恶待
但他保持忍耐  继续忠于上帝
我们可以再问一个问题
在受扰害  被仇视的情况下
约瑟是怎样保持积极的态度
继续信赖耶和华的呢?
接着看25节
“他与全能者同在”
约瑟得到了耶和华的帮助
全能的上帝一直在他身边扶持他
我们运用问题
弄清楚了这个记载的来龙去脉
这还不够
现在我们要进一步想想
这些內容可以怎样强化
我们和耶和华的关系
接下来  我们可以问问自己
关于耶和华
我们从这个记载学到什么呢?
耶和华绝不会离弃他的忠仆
即使在监牢里
约瑟也绝不是孤立无援的
耶和华一直找机会赐福给他
这跟耶和华的现代子民
跟你  有什么关系呢?
耶和华绝不会离弃我们
相反  他对每个全心全意事奉他的人
都表现忠贞之爱
耶和华有没有让约瑟
一直关在监牢里呢?
没有
到了指定的时候
约瑟就被释放了
而且还成为全埃及
仅次于法老的重要人物
一天之內  他就从牢房搬进了皇宫!
同样  我们面对的考验也是暂时的
耶和华很快就会为我们带来纾解
甚至通过意想不到的方式
为我们打开出路
耶和华一直与我们同在
我们绝非孤立无援
再来问问自己
这个记载和圣经的主题
有什么关系呢?
约瑟在患难中忠于耶和华
这保全了亚伯拉罕子孙的性命
保全了弥赛亚的世系
约瑟的经历
不只是引人入胜的故事而已
在耶和华实现他旨意的过程中
约瑟扮演了重要的角色
想想看  尽管哥哥们行为恶劣
约瑟还是原谅了他们
并主动修复了彼此之间的关系
约瑟的这种态度
也反映了耶和华的态度
看到这个大家庭再次团聚
耶和华也宽恕了约瑟的哥哥们
并主动恢复了跟他们的关系
事实上
耶和华还使约瑟的哥哥犹大
有幸成为弥赛亚的祖先
从这个记载我们学到了什么呢?
我就强调其中一点
请看创世记49:23
哥哥们的恨意使约瑟成了众矢之的
约瑟有什么反应呢?
24节说
经文说他的弓坚定长存
换句话说  他没有还手
他的弓留在原处
回想一下  你上一次被人冒犯的经历
那个时候你有什么反应呢?
有没有只顾着为自己辩解
或坚持自己的权利呢?
是用怨恨的箭还击
还是表现了仁慈和忠贞之爱呢?
我们的反应有没有表明
上帝的圣灵在我们身上发挥作用呢?
像约瑟一样
即使我们受到考验或者不公正的对待
仿佛被囚禁一样
我们还是可以确信
我们是上帝喜欢的人
仔细思考这些问题
能够帮助我们从这些记载充分获益
这会影响我们的生活
影响我们的思考方式和行为模式
也会巩固我们和耶和华的关系
这样研读圣经
我们就不会走马观花地
了解一堆有趣的事实
但没过几天就忘记了
反而  这会帮助我们
将重要的圣经原则谨记在心
这些原则会影响我们的决定
指引我们的生活
这样我们就能“紧握生命的话语”了
让我们再回顾一下该如何做研读
再说一遍
我们不是在说
用什么工具  用什么设备
我们讨论的不是用什么设备研读
而是研读圣经的基本方法
研读可分为三个阶段
这就好比小麦的收集  筛选和烘焙
读圣经就好像是收集小麦
我们收割时
不会匆匆跑过麦田随便用手抓麦粒
而会有序地收割小麦
筛选
就是对收集到的材料进行分析整理
通过之前提到的六个问题
来弄清事情的来龙去脉
烘焙
就是要在头脑和內心“把火开大”
进行深入思考
这一步必须自己亲自完成
别人无法代劳
研读时善用这些问题
可以强化自己和耶和华的关系
最重要的是  要问问自己
关于耶和华  我从经文学到了什么?
这个记载和圣经的主题有什么关系?
还有  我从中学到什么教训?
我们拥有渴望学习的头脑
也能够培养思考力
这都是来自耶和华的宝贵礼物
如果我们付出努力
挖掘上帝话语中的宝石
就会从中得到益处和快乐
更重要的是
研读的能力会帮助我们
“紧握生命的话语”
我们紧握上帝的话语
就不但会改善目前的生活
还有机会不断加深对天父的认识
直到永远

title: 효과적인 개인 연구를 통해 말씀을 계속 “굳게 잡으십시오”

ko.text: 개인 연구를 할수록, 여호와를 더 알게 되고,
여호와께선 “내 생각은 너희 생각과 다르다”고 하시죠.
그분의 생각을 더 잘 이해하려면 연구를 깊이 있게 해야 돼요.
개인 연구는 계속 나아갈 힘을 주는 음식과 같아요.
하루 중 제가 지쳐 있을 만한 시간대를 피해서 연구를 해요.
그럼 나중엔 몰라도, 연구할 땐 피곤하지 않죠.
전 성경 연구를 하기 전에 매번 기도합니다.
이 내용이 절 위한 조언임을 깨닫게 해 주시고,
전 색깔을 사용해서 뭐가 뭘 나타내는지 표시해요.
어떤 색깔은 여호와께서 사람들을 어떻게 도와주셨는지 알려 주는 기록에,
또 어떤 색깔은 경고가 되는 본에 표시하죠.
본받을 만한 좋은 본에는 또 다른 색깔로 하고요.
묵상을 하면 그 지식을 실천할 힘이 생기죠.
어떤 상황이고, 몇 명이 나오는지 알아보면,
그 구절의 진짜 의미를 알게 되실 겁니다.
그때부터 아버지와 함께 하늘에 계셨던 거예요.
전 빌립보 4:6, 7을 여러 번 반복해서 읽어 봤어요.
여호와와 좋은 관계를 누릴 때 얻죠.
또 하느님의 평화는 어떻게 ‘마음을 지켜’ 줄까요?
그 덕분에 여호와와의 관계가 가능해진 거죠.
전 개인 연구를 할 때 원칙을 찾으려고 해요.
그러기 위해, 계명 속에 숨겨진 것을 찾죠.
전 이 계명에서 이웃 사랑이란 원칙을 발견했죠.
이 원칙은 제가 성별, 인종, 국적에 상관없이
모든 사람에게 전파하는 데 도움이 됐어요.
거기서 배운 연구 방법 한 가지는
성경 기록을 다양한 관점에서 분석하는 거였습니다.
한쪽에서만 보면 전체 그림을 못 보죠.
전 공부한 점을 연구생에게 말해 줘요.
그럼 연구생이 여호와를 더 잘 알고,
자신이 배우는 내용이 실용적이란 걸 깨닫는 데 도움이 되죠.
야곱에 대해 연구한 적이 있는데, 그는 천사와 밤새도록 씨름했죠.
전 공부한 점을 몇몇 친구들에게 말해 줬어요.
그런데 그 얘기를 할 때 주위에 앉아 있었던 한 형제가
“저는 전 시간 봉사를 그만두기로 결정을 다 해 놨었어요.
그런데 그 이야기를 듣고, 그만두지 않기로 했습니다.”
제게 아이가 생긴 걸 알고 기도했죠.
전 이 아이를 영원히 지킬 수 있을 거예요.”
전 배운 걸 아이에게 전부 가르쳐 줬어요.
강한 믿음을 유지하는 게 여기에 달렸죠.
우리가 매번 올바른 연구와 묵상을 할 때마다,
우리 믿음을 튼튼하게 해 주는 기둥이 하나씩 생기는 겁니다.
위층 방으로 달려가 모든 걸 차단하면
살면서 예상치 못한 일을 많이 겪지만,

en.text: The more you study,
the more you understand Jehovah.
The more you understand Jehovah,
the more you love him.
Jehovah clearly tells us:
“My thoughts are not your thoughts.”
So if we want to understand Jehovah’s thinking better,
we need to dig deep in our study,
and then we share those thoughts with others.
Personal study is like fuel
that keeps you going.
Personally, I’m not a good student,
but I really learned how to study the Bible.
The Bible came alive during Gilead.
Self-discipline is involved —very much.
I overcome the tiredness aspect
of Bible study by not doing it
at a time of day when I know I’m going to be tired.
I can be tired for other things later on —but not for that.
Each session of my Bible study begins with a prayer,
“Please help me recognize it is counsel for me,
and then give me the strength to work on it.”
I have a color-coded system,
so I know what certain things stand for.
I have a particular color
for Jehovah’s good hand in people’s lives;
I have another color for warning examples;
I have another for fine examples to imitate.
You have to get behind the information,
not just focus on one verse or one chapter.
See who’s involved, the time,
the conditions, how many people are there,
and then you’ll get the true meaning of the verse.
John 1:1,
who is “the Word”?
We can go to verse 18.
“Begotten” meant
he had a beginning, a time when he started
—when he began—
in heaven with his Father.
That’s where he was.
Philippians 4:6, 7 is a scripture that I’ve read many times over.
“The peace of God that excels all thought.”
OK, how do you get that?
It’s from having a good relationship with Jehovah.
How is it that God’s peace ‘guards your heart’?
“By means of Christ Jesus” our Lord.
And I said: “Why by Jesus?
“Because Jesus paid the ransom;
that ransom is what makes possible a relationship with Jehovah.”
So it almost goes full circle.
I attended a School for Congregation Elders
that had Gilead graduates as instructors.
One of the methods is to analyze
a certain Bible account from different perspectives.
We can’t see the whole picture from one angle.
I share my research results with Bible students,
and that helps them to know Jehovah better,
and it helps them to see that what they’re studying
is of practical value.
I had studied up on Jacob;
he wrestled all night
with an angel.
And I wanted to share it with some of my friends.
One of the brothers that happened to sit around
when this discussion was going on came back to me, and he said to me:
“I had concluded my arrangements
“to quit full-time service.
“But after listening to that discussion,
I’ve decided that I’m no longer stopping.”
And that was such a wonderful moment for me.
I thanked Jehovah.
When I learned that I was going to become a mom,
I said, “Jehovah, if this little one
could love you, then I’ll get to keep him forever.”
And I began to teach everything I was learning to him.
So it’s a matter
of keeping my faith strong,
and there’s no shortcut.
Every session of study that is properly done with good meditation
adds a new pillar
to the strength of our faith.
I look forward to those times when I can, you know,
run upstairs by myself and just shut everything off,
and it’s just me and Jehovah.
Life today is very unpredictable,
but I’ve come to see that as long as I keep a tight grip on God’s Word,
nothing can “separate [me] from God’s love.”

cn.text: 我们越研读  就越了解耶和华的想法
越了解他的想法  也就会越爱他
耶和华说
“我的思想跟你们的思想不同”
如果想清楚了解耶和华的想法
研读时就需要深入挖掘
然后把学到的和别人分享
研读可以加添力量
就像给汽车加油一样
我不算是个好学生
但在基列学校
我学到了该怎样研读圣经
也看出上帝的话语是活的
研读需要自律  这非常重要
我会在自己精力最充沛的时候研读
而不是在已经感觉累的时候才开始
要把精力充沛的时间留给研读
累的时候可以做点别的
我每次开始研读前都会做祷告
求耶和华帮我理解研读的内容
让我有力量实践出来
我会用不同的颜色做标记
提前想好每种颜色代表什么
我会用不同颜色做标记
一种颜色是耶和华怎样用他的手帮助人
另一种颜色是前车之鉴
还有一种是值得我们效法的好榜样
研读和沉思密不可分
研读帮助我们吸收知识
而沉思会让我们更有动力
把学到的实践出来
只是看某一章或某一节经文还不够
还要深入挖掘
考察一下经文背景
比如时间  地点  事件
有多少人  他们是谁等等
这样你就更明白这节经文了
约翰福音1:1
这里提到的“话语”是谁呢?
接着看第18节
这里说“独生的”
看来他是有开始的
那他最开始在哪里呢?
在天上  和他的父亲在一起
找到答案了!
腓立比书4:6,7
这段经文我读过很多遍
上帝会“赐下超越人能理解的安宁”
我怎样才能得到这种安宁呢?
就是要和耶和华有良好的关系
那这种安宁会怎样守护我的内心？
“通过基督耶稣”
我就继续问
为什么要通过耶稣？
因为耶稣付出了赎价
而赎价让我有机会亲近天父耶和华
这样，前后就全都联系起来了
我个人研读时
会努力找出律法和诫命背后有什么原则
比如  在马太福音28:19,20
耶稣吩咐我们
“要去  使所有国族的人做我的门徒”
背后的原则是什么呢?
就是“要爱人如己”
这个原则会让我
更愿意向各种各样的人传道
无论对方来自哪里  有什么背景
我参加会众长老训练班的时候
有一位导师是基列毕业生
他跟我们分享了一个研读方法
就是从不同的角度分析一个圣经记载

ko.text: ‎‪하지만 어떤 청소년들은 가족의 지원 없이 믿음을 길러야 했습니다.‏
‎‪미국에 사는 얼시 로이어 자매의 경험을 들어보겠습니다.‏
‎‪자매는 겨우 14살 때 어떤 영적 결정을 내려야 했을까요?‏
‎‪또 자매가 한 어떤 행동이 깊은 개인 연구의 중요성을 보여 줄까요?‏
‎‪온 식구가 회중에서 열심이야’라고 하는 그런 집이 아니었죠.‏
‎‪내가 왜 믿어야 하나 하는 생각이 들었죠.‏
‎‪뭔가 어색하고 혼자 고립된 느낌이 들 수 있어요.‏
‎‪제가 배운 모든 게 틀렸다는 걸 증명해 볼 거예요.”‏
‎‪결국 여호와께로 모두 연결된다는 걸 알 수 있었죠.‏
‎‪하나만 믿고 나머지는 안 믿을 수가 없는 거죠.‏
‎‪특히 시편에 ‘내가 태아일 때 당신의 눈이 나를 보셨다’라고 한 구절이‏
‎‪‘와, 부모님이 지금 진리 안에서 열심히 하지 않으시는데도‏
‎‪일주일이 안 돼서 회중에서 한 자매를 찾게 됐는데‏
‎‪지금도 그 자맨 제가 얼마나 고마워했는지 모를 거예요.‏
‎‪영적으로 발전해 가면서 가족의 지원을 받지 못했어요.‏
‎‪여호와께서 계속 절 도와주신다는 걸 신뢰해야 했어요.‏
‎‪집회에서 얻은 힘과 형제 자매들과 함께 한 기쁨은‏
‎‪그걸 보고 몹시 화가 난 부모님이 문 앞에 나오셨죠.‏
‎‪제가 왜 여호와를 더 전적으로 섬기려는 결정을 하는 건지‏
‎‪전 그 옷만 입은 채 집을 떠났어요.‏
‎‪단 몇 분 사이에 제 삶이 완전히 달라졌죠.‏
‎‪영적 이모 같은 한 자매가 집에서 같이 지내게 해 주시고‏
‎‪또 문자 그대로 먹여 주시고 입혀 주시고‏
‎‪여러 해 전에 한 자매가 해 주신 말씀이 기억나요.‏
‎‪“어렸을 때 너에게 필요했던 바로 그런 사람이 되렴.”‏
‎‪어린 친구들을 볼 때면 자신에게 이렇게 묻죠.‏
‎‪‘내가 저 나이였을 때 다른 사람이 시간을 내서‏
‎‪그리고 그들이 혼자가 아니라는 걸 알려 주려고 하죠.‏
‎‪이게 진리인지 아직 확신이 없는 청소년이 있다면‏
‎‪그들이 그분을 알 수 있는 방법을 찾고 계세요.‏
‎‪여호와는 실재하는 분이고 청소년들의 이름을 다 아시죠.‏
‎‪정말 여호와께서 자기를 알고 사랑하시는지 확인하다니 대단하죠?‏
‎‪한 번 길게 연구하고 만 게 아닙니다.‏
‎‪그 습관은 얼시가 인내하고, 자라고, 영적인 사람이 되게 해 줬죠.‏
‎‪언젠가 가족이 영적으로 다시 연합하기를 바란다고 말했습니다.‏

en.text: Young ones, it’s true that the more you understand Jehovah,
the more you love him.
And what a blessing you have if your family worships Jehovah with you
and teaches you how to draw close to him.
But some young ones have had to build their faith
without their family’s support.
Listen to the experience of Ersi Royer from the United States.
What spiritual decision did she face at just 14 years old?
And what did she do that illustrates the value
of deep personal study?
Growing up,
it wasn’t the typical,
“My mom is a pioneer, my dad is an elder,
and we’re doing great in the congregation.”
My family life wasn’t the best,
so why would I want to do this religion that nobody is happy
in our family with?
And I think that can make you feel
very alone or odd
or awkward or secluded.
And at that time, I was graduating eighth grade.
There were dances;
friends were hanging out, going to parties.
And I remember thinking: ‘Wow, these look like really nice kids.
Why aren’t I doing that?’
I hadn’t really delved into the Bible enough to answer questions
that I really needed to know.
I went in prayer to Jehovah and said: “I’m so sorry, but today I’m not a Witness.
I’m going to try to prove everything that I’ve been taught is wrong.”
I asked him that if he’s real,
to help me understand.
So I went in my room
and shut the door.
I got every book off the shelf.
I started off organized,
but by the end of the evening,
I had books all over the place with pages open.
The more I kept reading about Jehovah,
the more the next topic would take me to then connect the scriptures.
Jesus is linked to Jehovah;
the angels are linked to Jehovah; the resurrection is linked to Jehovah.
So you can’t believe in one thing and not everything else
if you really want to know the truth.
And so that’s what did it for me,
especially the scripture in Psalms
when it said that ‘you saw even the embryo of me.’
And it was an emotional scripture for me
because I thought: ‘Wow,
‘my parents aren’t doing great in the truth right now.
‘But Jehovah found a way to find me,
‘and he knew what I could be.
‘Now I have my answer. I don’t have an excuse.
‘Jehovah gave me enough knowledge that now I’m responsible.
I now need to act on that and show my love in return for him.’
Within a week, I found another sister
in the hall that was really helpful in me getting out
in service quite often.
I don’t think to this day she ever knew how much I appreciated that.
Although things were declining in our family spiritually,
I was able to get baptized.
As I progressed spiritually,
I could see that I did not have
the support of my family,
but I had to trust that Jehovah would help me through it.
And at least by the time I got home, if there was an issue,
I had the strength of the meeting and the brothers and sisters
and joy that they couldn’t take away from me.
I remember I came home one day with some friends.
It was a nice day
—encouraging, upbuilding.
We pulled into our driveway; they dropped me off
and said good-bye.
My parents were really upset
when they came and met me at the door.
They couldn’t fully understand
why I was making my decisions
the way I was to serve Jehovah more fully.
We just could not agree
on where my relationship with Jehovah was going.
And at that point, I left with the clothes on my back.
In a matter of a few minutes,
my life forever changed.
I had a spiritual aunt that took me in,
helped me gather myself together,
and literally fed me, clothed me,
helped me spiritually.
And so then, my support became Jehovah
and the congregation.
I remember that a sister told me years ago,
“Be who you needed when you were young.”
And so when I look at those little ones,
I look at myself and say,
‘How could I have benefited
from someone taking the time for me when I was that age?’
I’ve always tried remembering the young ones
—because that’s just part of who I am—
and making sure that they know that they’re not alone.
If there is a young one out there who isn’t sure
if this is the truth or not,
I would like them to know that Jehovah knows
who they are,
and he’s finding a way for them to know him.
Jehovah is real, he knows them by name,
he wants them to live, and he’s fighting for them.
How amazing that young Ersi chose to spend an entire day studying
—proving to herself that Jehovah knew her and loved her.
But this was no onetime study marathon.
From there, she worked to develop the study habits she needed
to endure, grow, and become a spiritual person.
She pioneered for several years,
and now serves at Bethel with her husband, Jeff.
In my conversation with Ersi, she expressed her love for her family
and the hope that someday in the future
she’ll be reunited with them spiritually.

“我们都在会众中堪作模范的家庭”
我的家庭没有从真理得到快乐
当时我想  既然这样
我为什么还要加入这个团体
做耶和华见证人呢?
我在会众里感到很孤单
不自在  很格格不入
那时中学快毕业了
同学们经常去跳舞  吃喝  玩乐
当时我心想  他们过得真开心
为什么我不能过那样的生活呢?
那时我还没好好读过圣经
很多基本道理都不知道
我跟耶和华祷告
我很抱歉  今天就当我是个不信的人
我想试试
证明我学到的一切都是错的
我请求上帝
如果你真的存在
就帮助我看出这一点!
于是  我回到房间  关上门
把书架上的书都搬了下来
一开始  我计划一本一本地看
但到了晚上  书已经摊了一地
都是翻开的
我读到越多关于耶和华的事
就越看出圣经內容相互联系
都和耶和华有关
耶稣和耶和华有关
天使和耶和华有关
复活也关系到耶和华
可见  如果我真的想认识真理
就不可能只相信一个而否定其他
这加强了我的信心
特别当我读到诗篇的一句话
“我还是胚胎的时候”
“你的眼睛就看见我了”
我很感动  心想
尽管我的父母在属灵方面
没能好好带头
但耶和华还是想方设法帮助我
相信我可以做得更好
现在我既然找到了答案
耶和华也给了我充足的知识
我应该负起责任  以爱还爱
就在那个星期
我在会众里找到一位姐妹
她经常约我去传道
对我帮助很大
我想她一定不知道我有多感激她
尽管我家人的属灵情况越来越糟
我最终还是符合资格受了浸
我逐渐看出
虽然家人不支持我
但耶和华一定会帮助我
他通过聚会和弟兄姐妹给我力量
每当聚会后回到家
无论有什么令人灰心的事
我都可以应付
也可以保持喜乐
有一天朋友们送我回家
那天我从他们那里
得到了不少鼓励和强化
到了家门口
我下了车
和他们很高兴地告别
但是  我的父母来给我开门时
却很不高兴
他们无法理解
为什么我这么看重这个信仰
他们也不希望我全心事奉耶和华
结果  我什么都没拿
就义无反顾  转身离开了家
短短的几分钟
我的人生就发生了剧变
会众里一位年长的姐妹
让我住在她家
她帮助我重新振作起来
她对待我就像对待自己的家人
为我提供吃的穿的
也在属灵方面帮助我
从那时起
耶和华和会众就成为我的一切了
很多年前  有位姐妹对我说
你年轻时需要怎样的帮助
那你现在就要怎样帮助那些年轻人
所以  每当我看到青少年
就对自己说
我像他们那么大的时候
如果有人愿意花时间帮我
我会得到什么益处呢?
我一直很关心会众里的年轻人
希望他们知道
他们不是孤立无援的
毕竟我也是从那个年纪过来的
如果有哪个年轻人
不确定这是不是真理
我希望他们知道
耶和华认识他们
而且正想方设法帮助他们
耶和华是真实的
他知道每个年轻人的名字
希望他们永远活下去
也会一直扶持他们

拨出一整天的时间来研读圣经
这让她看出耶和华了解她
也很爱她
真的值得称赞!
当然  她不是一下子读很多
以后就不读了
而是渐渐养成了研读的好习惯
这帮助她保持忍耐
在属灵方面不断进步
她做了几年先驱
现在和丈夫一起在伯特利服务
和艾尔西交谈时
她说她很爱自己的家人
她告诉我  希望有一天
能再次和家人一起事奉耶和华

title: 앨런 보일: 더 정확한 그림을 위해 깊이 연구하다

ko.text: 먼저 앨런 보일 형제와 과거에 했던 회견을 보죠.
우리가 읽는 내용을 그려 보고 묵상하게 도와주어
그런 삽화를 그리는 일은 참 즐겁지만,
그 일을 하는 사람은 영적 특성들이 필요합니다.
함께 협력하고 겸손하게 남의 의견을 잘 들어야 하죠.
또 영적 양식에 포함될 삽화를 준비하려면
“충실하고 슬기로운 종”의 지침에 꼭 따라야 합니다.
그 일을 하려면 열심히 성경을 연구해야 합니다.
그가 임무를 잘 수행하는 데 무엇이 필요했는지 알아보시죠.
하루는 어머니가 당시엔 부회의 종이라고 불렀던 형제를
그분이 저한테 앞으로 어떻게 살 거냐고 묻길래
3주 뒤 저는 런던에서 열린 대회에서 침례를 받았고
스물한 살 때 순회 활동을 시작했어요.
오토바이 뒤에다 가방이랑 타자기랑 옷 가방을 다 싣고 다녔는데,
그땐 제가 선교인이 되어 아일랜드에 가게 될 줄 몰랐어요.
제 친구가 삽화 작업을 하도록 런던 베델에 초대됐습니다.
실은 저도 늘 베델에 가고 싶었지요.
전화해서 축하해 줘야겠다 싶어 친구에게 전활 했더니,
다음 날 아침에 런던 베델에 전화했고,
일주일도 안 돼 전 런던 베델로 와서 잡지를 위한 삽화 작업을 하게 됐어요.
그 후에 배리 형제의 초대로 브루클린 베델로 오게 됐습니다.
유익을 주고 도움이 되는 일을 한다고 생각해 보세요.
사람들이 중요한 점을 기억하도록 도와주는 일입니다.
미술부에서 그림을 그리는 일을 할 때 가장 좋은 것 하나는
대홍수 전에 노아가 방주를 지을 때 상황은 어땠을까?
방수는 어떻게 했을까? 제일 중요한 건데.
이런 소소한 질문들을 다 생각해 봐야 되죠.
보통 갑판 밑에는 평형 유지를 위한 50kg짜리 모래 자루가 있었습니다.
분명 그분은 이 자루를 베고 주무셨을 겁니다.
사실 「왕국 행간역」을 보면 베개 앞에 정관사 “the”가 붙어 있어서
일반적인 베개가 아니었단 걸 알 수 있죠.
2000년 전 당시 그 지역 사람들은 그 “베개”가 뭔지 다 알았을 겁니다.
전에 시베리아에 가 본 적이 있는 형제를 만났었는데,
그 형제가 시베리아에 사는 어떤 분의 주방 사진을 보여 줬어요.
한쪽 벽에 여기 브루클린에서 생산한 출판물의 한 페이지가
그림을 그리는 데 필요한 다양한 보조 업무든,
전 세계 모든 곳에 있는 형제 자매들에게 영향을 준다는 사실이었습니다.
정말 시간을 가치 있게 보내는 거죠.
우리는 다른 사람들이 성경을 이해하고 유익을 얻도록 돕습니다.
여호와께 드리는 봉사는 정말 보람 있고 가슴 벅찬 일이죠.
앨런 보일 형제는 2016년에 지상 행로를 마쳤습니다.
열정이 넘치고 세부점까지 놓치지 않았던 보일 형제의 모습을 기억합니다.
그가 임무를 잘 수행할 수 있었던 건 개인 성서 연구 덕분이었죠.
성서 장면을 그리는 데 필요한 조사를 하며 보람을 느꼈습니다.
현재는 집필부에서 자료 조사 팀을 구성해 미술부 업무를 지원하죠.
형제는 연구 조사에 무엇이 도움이 됐다고 했나요?

en.text: We begin with an archived interview of Brother Allan Boyle.
Among his many assignments, Brother Boyle spent 37 years
in the Art Department at world headquarters.
The beautiful and accurate illustrations
produced there enhance our study,
helping us to visualize and meditate on what we are reading.
An assignment to create these pictures is exciting,
but it requires that a person have spiritual qualities.
Artists collaborate
and must humbly listen to each other’s comments.
They must apply direction from “the faithful and discreet slave”
to prepare artwork that we can take in as spiritual food.
As you’ll hear Brother Boyle describe,
a person must be an avid student of the Bible.
Listen to Brother Boyle’s story,
and note what he said was needed for him to do his assignment well.
I was born in 1933.
I got to the age of 18, and one suppertime
my mother had invited the company servant,
as they were called back then, to come for supper.
He asked me what I was going to do with my life.
I said to him, “Well, I’m going to pioneer.”
So three weeks later, at the convention in London,
I got baptized and then went pioneering six months after that.
I was 21 when I was in the circuit work,
and that was a wonderful experience.
And in those days, of course, you didn’t have a car.
I used to have a motorbike.
And I’d go around on the motorbike with my briefcase
and my typewriter and my clothes in the other case on the back.
Yeah, that was very exciting.
I was invited to go to Gilead, and that was wonderfully exciting.
We had 103 in the class.
Little did I know at the time
that I would be sent as a missionary to Ireland.
My friend had been invited to go down
to London Bethel to do the artwork there.
I’d always wanted to be in Bethel.
I thought, ‘Well, why don’t I just call him up and congratulate him?’
So that’s what I did, and he told me that he decided not to go.
So he said: “If you’re still interested, why don’t you go?
You know, call them up and let them know.”
So that’s what I did. The next morning, I called up London Bethel,
and within a week I was in London Bethel doing the graphics work
for the magazines, you know.
It was a wonderful, thrilling experience.
I was in London Bethel for a couple of years,
and then Brother Barry invited me to come over to Brooklyn Bethel.
You know that you’re doing something that’s going to be beneficial
and helpful to other people,
even to people in different languages, in different cultures.
A little painting that you do is going to help them
to get a memory of something significant.
One of the most beautiful things about working in the Art Department
and doing paintings is that it makes you do research.
You have to investigate. Is this the right time of the day?
Is it night? Is it day?
What did the sky look like?
What was it like before the Flood when Noah built the ark?
How did he paint underneath the ark?
How did he waterproof it?
Because that’s the most important part, isn’t it?
He used bitumen. OK, how did he get underneath the ark?
Maybe he put it on stilts.
You have to come up with all these little questions in your mind.
To do the research was very rewarding.
This is a little model of a boat,
and underneath the deck they used to keep
a ballast sack of 110 pounds (50 kg) of sand.
It says in the Scriptures that Jesus was asleep on “a pillow.”
Apparently, this was the ballast sack that he was asleep on.
And actually, in the Kingdom Interlinear translation,
it doesn’t say that he was asleep on “a pillow”;
it says he was asleep on “the pillow.”
So apparently, back 2,000 years ago in that area,
everybody knew what “the pillow” was.
I remember meeting a brother once who’d been to Siberia,
and he’d taken a snapshot of somebody’s kitchen in Siberia.
And to my amazement, on the wall
—pinned with drawing pins on the wall—
was one of the pages of the publications
that we produced here at Brooklyn.
And so, remarkably,
it’s wonderful to feel that whatever we do here
—if it’s support work, if it’s the painting,
and, of course, we need a lot of support work for the paintings—
all of what we do here
has an effect upon the brothers and sisters
out there in the world, wherever it might be.
And you really feel that your time is well spent.
You’re adorning the Word of truth.
You’re helping other people to be taught something from the Bible,
which is going to be to their benefit.
It’s been very rewarding and thrilling
to be in Jehovah’s service, and I’ve really enjoyed it.
Allan Boyle finished his earthly course in 2016.
Those in the Art Department who worked with him
remember his enthusiasm and his thorough attention to detail.
What Allan brought to his assignment
was rooted in his own personal study of the Bible.
He found it rewarding to do the research
needed to illustrate Bible scenes.
Today, the Writing Department supplies
a team of researchers to assist the artists.
But did you recall what Allan said helped his research?
He asked questions about the scenes he was painting!
These same kinds of questions are part of the study methods
Gilead students learn in class.

ko.text: 그런 결정은 여호와와의 관계에 영향을 미치죠.
올바른 결정을 하기가 쉬운 것 같아요.
우리가 현명한 결정을 하는 건지 어떻게 알 수 있을까요?
가도 괜찮을지 잘 모르겠다는 생각이 들었어요.
남편은 아직 성서 연구를 선뜻 받아들이진 않지만,
제가 진리에 들어온 뒤로 여러 해 동안 태도가 누그러졌어요.
제가 교회에 예배하러 가지 않는 건 그이가 이해하겠지만,
파이오니아 학교에 해 갈 점심 메뉴 짜는 걸 도와주려고요.
제 상황을 잘 이해하는 것 같지 않았죠.
절 판단하는 것 같은 기분이 들었어요.
다음 날, 샬럿 자매와 앨런 형제 부부를 찾아가 조언을 구하기로 했어요.
저처럼 자매도 남편보다 여러 해 먼저 진리에 들어오셨죠.
두 분은 제 상황을 잘 이해했어요.
샬럿 자매는, 성경에 구체적인 명령이 없다면
그건 양심 문제라는 걸 설명해 주셨어요.
그리고 어떤 사람의 양심엔 괜찮은 게
다른 사람에겐 아닐 수 있다는 것도요.
중요한 건, 선한 양심을 유지할 수 있는 결정을 내리는 거라고 하셨어요.
에마 자매, 그건 훈련에 달려 있어요.
“단단한 음식은 장성한 사람들 곧 분별력을 사용하여 훈련함으로
옳고 그른 것을 구별할 줄 아는 이들의 것입니다.”
바울은 그 말을 기록하기만 한 게 아니라,
하느님의 말씀에 담긴 원칙들을 주의 깊이 연구했죠.
그 결과, 바울은 선한 양심을 유지할 수 있는 결정을 내릴 줄 알게 되었어요.
그러니까, 어떤 문제에 대해 분명히 언급하는 법이 없을 때도,
하느님의 생각을 이해하게 해 주는 성경 원칙은 늘 찾을 수가 있는 거죠.
저도 이 문제에 대해 기도한 다음, 개인 연구를 해 봤어요.
「‘하느님의 사랑’」 책 2장에서 정말 좋은 내용을 찾았어요.
또, 비슷한 상황을 겪은 사람들에 대해 읽으면서,
그들에게 어떤 성경 원칙이 도움이 됐는지 알게 됐어요.
읽고 나서 그런 점들을 다 묵상했죠.
제 양심이 단지 제 마음을 따라가지 않고
여호와의 영의 인도를 따르게 할 수 있었어요.
모두가 항상 똑같이 생각하게 되는 건 아니라는 점을 알게 됐어요.
하지만 성경 원칙을 적용하면서 양심을 훈련한다면,
우리 각자가 하느님의 사랑 안에 머물 수 있게 될 거예요.

en.text: Every day we make choices
that can affect our relationship with Jehovah.
When there’s a clear Scriptural command,
the right choice may seem easy.
But what if there’s not?
How can we be sure we’re making a wise decision?
An invitation to our niece’s wedding arrived.
Thomas was excited about it.
I was excited too.
But the ceremony
was being held at a local church.
I wondered if it would still be OK for me to attend.
Even though Thomas wasn’t yet willing
to accept a Bible study, he gradually softened over the years
since I came into the truth.
I knew he understood why I would never enter a church for worship,
but what about attending a wedding?
Jehovah approves of weddings.
That afternoon,
I went to help Amy plan a menu
for the pioneer school lunch coming up.
She noticed I was a bit distracted,
so I told her my concerns about the wedding.
But you’re not thinking of going, are you?
Amy sure had a strong opinion on the matter,
but I didn’t feel she really understood my situation.
Although I appreciated her concern,
I felt like she was judging me.
The next day, I decided to visit Charlotte and Allan
and ask their advice.
Like me, Charlotte had come into the truth
many years before Allan, so they really understood my situation.
Is Amy right?
Would it be wrong to attend the wedding?
What would you do if you were me?
Charlotte explained that in situations
where there’s no specific Bible command,
it becomes a matter of conscience.
And what one person’s conscience allows
may be different from another.
The important thing
is that we make decisions that leave us with a good conscience.
But how do I do that?
Dear Emma, it’s really a matter of training.
Allan showed me the scripture at Hebrews 5:14,
where the apostle Paul wrote:
“Solid food belongs to mature people,
“to those who through use
“have their powers of discernment trained
to distinguish both right and wrong.”
But Paul didn’t just write those words;
he lived them.
He carefully studied the principles in God’s Word.
And as a result, he was able to make decisions
that left him with a good conscience.
So even when there’s no stated law on a matter,
we can always find a Bible principle
that can give us insight into God’s thinking.
So I made it a matter of prayer, and then I got to work.
I researched articles
in the Watch Tower Publications Index and the Research Guide.
I found a really good thought in chapter 2 of the “God’s Love” book.
I also read about others who faced similar situations
and what Bible principles they found helpful.
Then I meditated on all these.
As I kept studying, I was able to bring my conscience
in harmony with Jehovah’s spirit,
not just with my heart.
I realized that having a Bible-trained conscience
doesn’t mean everyone will always think exactly alike
—and that’s OK.
But if we train our conscience by applying Bible principles,
it will guide us along in life, so that each of us
can remain in God’s love.
