titles.cn: 83. 挨家挨户

ko.text: 여러분에게 교습 위원회가 하는 업무 두 가지에 대해 소개할 수 있어 기쁩니다.
먼저, 지역 대회를 준비하기 위해 교습 위원회는 어떤 일들을 할까요?
다음으로, 평일 집회에서 어떤 기대할 만한 변화가 있을 것입니까?
우선 교습 위원회는 베델의 모든 부서들에 대해 매우 고맙게 생각합니다.
대회와 평일 집회에서 즐기는 영적인 프로그램을 위해
베델에서 일하는 여러분 각자가 어떤 식으로든 기여하고 있기 때문입니다.
1889년 이래로 지역 대회는 많은 발전을 거듭해 왔습니다.
이제 살펴보겠지만, 여호와께서 그런 발전을 이루게 해 주셨죠.
이번 지역 대회는 아주 훌륭합니다. 정말 큰 감동을 주죠.
지역 대회 덕분에 우리 모두 영적으로 강해졌어요.
지난 100여년 동안 수많은 사람이 비슷하게 느꼈습니다.
오랜 세월 진리 안에 계셨던 분들이 지역 대회가 열릴 때마다
이번 대회가 가장 좋았다고 말씀하시는 이유는 무엇입니까?
그런 이야기를 들으면 대회 프로그램을 준비하는 형제들은 어떤 느낌이 들까요?
그 형제들은 2017 지역 대회 영상에 나왔던 준이처럼 느낄지 모릅니다.
하지만 이 일은 사람의 일이 아닙니다.
우리는 시기적절한 대회들에 대해 여호와께 찬양을 돌려야 하죠.
그분의 영은 기꺼이 자원하는 많은 사람들을 통해 작용하고 있습니다.
이제 지역 대회를 어떻게 준비하는지 간단히 살펴보겠습니다.
한 단어로 된 주제를 여러 해 전에 미리 선정하죠.
그 단어에 근거해서 대회 프로그램을 준비하게 됩니다.
교습 위원회는 대본을 만들기 위해 드라마를 검토하는 팀과 함께 작업하면서
경험 많은 집필자들이 대회 주제에 꼭 맞는 교훈이 담긴 성경에 근거한 이야기를 만듭니다.
그러고 나서 대본을 폭넓게 연구 조사한 뒤,
드라마 제작을 위해 오디오/비디오 봉사부로 보냅니다.
이 모든 작업은 여러 해 전에 시작해야 합니다.
그러면 나머지 대회 프로그램은 어떻게 준비합니까?
전 세계의 지부 위원회와 본부 대표자들이 보내온 보고를 주의 깊이 검토합니다.
그러한 보고들을 보면 대회에서 어떤 점을 다루면 좋을지 알게 되기도 하죠.
전 세계 형제들의 필요에 맞게 대회 주제를 더 구체적으로 정합니다.
그리고 그 주제를 중앙장로회의 모든 성원에게 보내서 승인을 받습니다.
그러고 나서 지역 대회의 각 날에 맞는 주제 성구를 정하게 됩니다.
금요일 프로그램은 대회 전체의 기초를 놓습니다.
그 점이 지금 왜 우리에게 중요한지를 다룹니다.
토요일에는 개인 행실, 야외 봉사, 가정생활과 관련된 교훈이 베풀어지죠.
일요일에는 성경이 미래에 관해 무엇이라고 알려 주고,
우리가 계속 희망을 갖도록 어떻게 도와주는지를 다룹니다.
이렇게 기본적인 구성을 마치면 각 날에 어떤 연설들을 할지,
연설에 어떤 사상과 내용을 포함시킬지 정합니다.
또한 사상을 잘 전달하기 위해 다양한 방법을 생각해 보는데요.
성경의 교훈이 마음에 더 잘 이를 수 있도록 인터뷰나 동영상을 활용하기도 합니다.
교습 위원회는 이러한 세부적인 작업을 다 마무리한 후
오디오/비디오 봉사부는 집필자들과 협력하여 짧은 동영상들을 제작합니다.
미술부는 대회를 소개하고 광고하기 위한 아이디어를 구상합니다.
편집자는 집필된 내용에 대한 조사, 사실 확인, 교정 등
그렇게 해서 모든 골자와 대본이 완성되면
이제 지역 대회가 열리는 343개 언어로 번역 작업이 진행됩니다.
번역 봉사부는 전 세계의 번역 팀들이 번역을 수월하게 할 수 있도록 도와주죠.
작곡가와 편곡자들은 대회 때 부를 18개의 노래와 6개의 음악 영상에 사용될 곡을 만듭니다.
그리고 영화와 음성 드라마, 또 연설에 포함되는
약 40개의 짧은 동영상에 사용될 음악을 제작하고 녹음하는 작업도 음악 팀에서 진행하죠.
교습 위원회가 주관하는 일은 이 밖에도 더 있습니다.
교습 위원회는 연사를 임명하고 음향 장비를 설치하고
숙박업소나 대회 시설을 계약하고 대회와 관련된 부서들을 운영하고
자원봉사자들을 훈련하는 일에 관한 지침을 제공하죠.
이처럼 대회를 준비하기 위해 많은 사람이 기꺼이 자원하여 일합니다.
모두 하느님의 영감 받은 말씀과 성령의 인도를 따르며 일하죠.
이런 협력이 가져오는 유익한 결과는 지역 대회에서만 볼 수 있는 게 아닙니다.
「그리스도인 생활과 봉사」 집회가 시작된 지도 2년이 됐는데요.
집회 때 더 열심히 참여하려고 하죠.
집회 때 동영상이 많아져서 좋아요. 전 세계의 형제 자매들이랑 더 친해진 것 같아요.
나이가 아주 어린 아이들까지도 실연에 참여하죠.
이젠 예습할 때 그냥 밑줄만 치지 않고 어떤 보물이 있는지 찾아봐요.
성경을 깊이 파 들어 가면서 정말 많은 걸 배우죠.
집회가 끝난 뒤에도 자신이 찾은 영적 보물에 대해 서로 이야기합니다.
집회 때마다 주말에 바로 실천할 수 있는 실용적인 점들을 배워요.
이제 우리 가족은 성경을 읽을 때 여호와의 특성에 더 많은 주의를 기울이죠.
청소년이나 새로운 전도인들이 호별 봉사에 더 자신감을 갖게 됐습니다.
집회 때 배운 걸 그대로 따라하면 되니까요.
평일 집회의 구성 방식도 생각해 볼 수 있는데요.
길르앗 학교에서 공부하는 방식을 집회에 도입했습니다.
길르앗 학교에서는 성구의 문맥, 설명, 적용에 초점을 맞춥니다.
문맥을 분석하려면 시대적 상황, 역사적 배경, 필자의 의도가 무엇인지를 알아야 합니다.
평일 집회 때 살펴보는 성경에 담긴 보물 부분이나
「성경 소개 동영상」을 만들 때 바로 그런 점들을 염두에 두죠.
성구에 대한 설명은 모두 “충실하고 슬기로운 종”이 발행한 출판물에 근거해 있기 때문에
성구를 정확하게 올바로 이해할 수 있습니다.
사실, 길르앗 학생들도 추측에 근거해 성구를 설명해서는 안 된다고 배우죠.
성구가 정확하게 설명되면 그 내용을 올바로 적용할 수 있습니다.
이런 식으로 문맥과 설명과 적용에 초점을 맞추면
성경을 의미 있게 연구할 수 있죠.
대화 방법과 그리스도인 생활 부분에 관해 제안합니다.
집필부는 봉사와 집회에서 출판물을 활용하는 방법에 관한 지침을 줍니다.
배부용 「파수대」가 1년에 여섯 개 호가 아니라 세 개 호만 발행될 것입니다.
또한 제공할 출판물을 미리 정해 놓는 마련도 중단되었습니다.
따라서 야외 봉사 때 사용할 대화 방법 제안에 변화가 생길 것입니다.
이제부터는 출판물을 전하는 것보다는 대화를 나누는 데 더 중점을 둘 것입니다.
분명, 평일 집회와 지역 대회를 준비하는 데는 엄청난 노력이 듭니다.
베델의 여러 부서에서 많은 사람들이 주의 깊이 계획하고 협력해야 하죠.
하지만 그 덕분에 전 세계 형제들이 유익을 얻습니다.
이런 집회를 보게 해 주셔서 여호와께 정말 감사해요.
베델에 보내 주신 편지들을 보면 때때로 이런 말이 나옵니다.
사실 이 모든 일을 하는 형제 자매들은 지칠 때가 분명히 있습니다.
하지만 그들은 결코 지치지 않는 분인 여호와를 늘 신뢰하며 그분과 협력해 일하고 있죠.
우리가 받는 모든 교육은 하느님이 베푸시는 것입니다.
오직 그분만이 구리를 금으로 바꾸실 수 있죠.
따라서 우리 앞에는 언제나 최상의 교육이 펼쳐질 것입니다.

en.text: It’s a pleasure to relate to you two aspects
of the Teaching Committee’s work.
First, what does it take
to put a regional convention together these days?
And second, what can we expect with regard to our midweek meetings?
The Teaching Committee is very grateful to every Bethel department.
Each of you has contributed in some way
to the spiritually festive events
that we enjoy at our conventions and our midweek meetings.
Our conventions have come a long way since 1889.
But as you’ll see, the improvements must be attributed to Jehovah.
This convention is so beautiful.
It moves you to the core.
It’s a very spiritually enriching experience for all of us.
We really see the Governing Body is caring for us.
It’s amazing!
This sentiment has been echoed for over a century.
How is it that year after year people who have been in the truth for decades
can say that the most recent convention
has surpassed all preceding ones?
And how do the brothers who prepare convention programs feel
when they hear comments like that?
If this were merely the work of humans,
they might feel like Caleb as depicted in the 2017 regional conventions.
Thankfully, this is not the work of one man.
All praise goes to Jehovah for the timely conventions we enjoy.
His spirit is working through many willing volunteers.
Let’s take a brief look at how our conventions are made.
It all begins with the theme.
As Brother Morris pointed out at the 2017 regional convention,
one-word themes are determined years in advance.
That one word will guide those preparing the program.
Dramas —the most labor-intensive part of a program—
are developed five years in advance.
To prepare scripts, the Teaching Committee cooperates closely
with the Writing Department in working with a team
known as the Drama Review Group.
These experienced writers
develop Scriptural plots that teach lessons in harmony
with the convention theme.
Scripts are extensively researched
and then sent to Audio/Video Services,
or AVS, for production.
All of this work has to begin early.
But how is the rest of a convention program developed?
Each year, the Teaching Committee carefully considers reports
from around the world from Branch Committees
and world headquarters representatives.
Often, such reports indicate topics that could be addressed on a convention.
The Teaching Committee then selects a more specific theme
that will serve as the basis for addressing the needs
of our worldwide brotherhood.
The theme is submitted to the entire Governing Body for approval.
Then, work begins on Scripture themes for each day of the convention.
The Friday program lays the foundation:
What is the central truth under discussion?
Why should we give attention to it now?
Saturday brings admonition on personal conduct,
field ministry, and family life.
Sunday often highlights what the Bible says
about our future and encourages us to maintain our hope.
Once this general framework is established,
talks are conceived
and additional lines of reasoning are chosen.
Attention is given to how to present ideas
in a variety of ways:
Could a Scriptural discussion reach the heart more effectively
by means of an interview or a video?
This detailed sketch is all worked out
before the Teaching Committee assigns teams of writers.
AVS collaborates with the writers in the development of brief videos.
The Art Department brainstorms ideas
for convention branding.
The compiler follows the written content through 70 steps
of research, fact-checking, and proofreading.
Then, all of these outlines and scripts have to be translated
into the 343 languages in which we hold regional conventions.
Translation Services helps teams around the world
to overcome challenges with the text.
Composers and arrangers
make music tracks for the 18 songs
that have been selected and the 6 music-video preludes.
Music services also produces and records
musical scores for the feature film, the audio drama,
and some 40 other brief videos that are used on the program.
But the Teaching Committee’s involvement
doesn’t end here.
It provides direction regarding the assigning of speakers,
the design of sound systems,
the securing of contracts for hotels and venues,
the operation of convention departments,
and the training of volunteers.
Thousands of willing workers are involved,
each submitting to the inspired direction
in God’s Word and the influence
of his holy spirit.
The benefits of such collaboration are felt
not only at our annual conventions
but also at our weekly meetings.
It’s been two years since the inception
of the Our Christian Life and Ministry midweek meeting.
How have things been going on that front?
Everything got better: how the brothers and sisters feel
about the meeting and how they participate.
There are more videos at the meetings,
so I feel closer to the worldwide brotherhood.
I really enjoy what it does for young ones,
especially the two-minute parts.
You see young ones, even very young children, do a demonstration.
Instead of just underlining to prepare,
now I get excited looking for gems.
We really dig into a Bible account.
I learn a whole lot more.
After the meeting,
we enjoy discussing the gems we discovered.
Every meeting gives you something practical
that you can apply the next weekend right away.
Now we don’t just read the Bible as a family,
but we pay more attention to Jehovah’s qualities.
Young ones and new publishers are now less hesitant
about sharing their beliefs at the door
because they simply do what they learned at the meetings.
Regarding production of the meeting,
methods of the Gilead School are employed
in the approach to study.
The Gilead approach to study
considers context, explanation,
and application.
Analyzing the context considers the time period,
the historical setting, and the writer’s intent.
These are built into the Treasures From God’s Word
and the Bible Book Introduction Videos
we see at the midweek meetings.
The explanations for the verses are all based on the publications
of “the faithful and discreet slave”
to ensure accuracy and correct understanding.
After all, at Gilead School, students aren’t allowed to guess.
Once a scripture is explained accurately,
then it can be applied properly.
This method of context and explanation
followed by application leads to meaningful Bible study.
The Service Committee Office
provides input on field service presentations and Living as Christians.
The Writing Department gives insight on how to feature our publications.
What will change after January?
As announced at the 2017 annual meeting,
the public edition of The Watchtower will be published
three times a year instead of six.
The same will be true for Awake!
Also, specific monthly literature offers have been discontinued.
Thus, we will enjoy some adjustments in our field service presentations.
As you will see, the new focus will be
not so much on publications
but on conversations.
Clearly, the production of our midweek meetings
and regional conventions takes a lot of planning
and the cooperation of many willing workers
in a variety of Bethel departments.
But the positive effects are felt around the world.
All I can say to Jehovah is, “Thank you, Jehovah, for letting me be here.”
I feel very grateful to Jehovah for the meetings.
Thank you, Jehovah.
Sometimes Bethel receives letters that go something like this:
“Thank you for your tireless efforts.”
Actually, the brothers and sisters working on all these projects are tired.
But they never tire
of trusting in and cooperating with the One who truly is tireless:
the Source of all divine instruction, Jehovah.
He alone can replace copper with gold,
so that each segment of divine education
truly is the best ever.

cn.text: 很高兴向大家介绍
教导委员会负责的两项工作
首先，我们会讲讲在现代
要怎样举办一场区域大会
然后，我们会看看周中聚会有哪些调整
教导委员会非常感谢伯特利的所有部门
你们都在某方面作出贡献
让大家可以享受大会和聚会
这些振奋人心的盛宴
从1889年以来
我们的区域大会在每一方面都进步很多
可是你会看出
这些进展全都要归功给耶和华
这个区域大会太美好了！
真的打动我们的内心
这个大会加强我们所有人对上帝的信心
我们确实看出中央长老团关心我们
太棒了！
一百多年来
许多人都有同样的感受
为什么在真理中好几十年的人都认为
区域大会一年比一年好呢？
筹备大会节目的弟兄听到这样的评论
有什么感觉呢？
如果这只是人的功劳
这些弟兄的感觉
就可能像2017年
区域大会影片中的志轩一样
还好，这不只是人的功劳
我们能从大会得到适时的鼓励
全靠耶和华
上帝的神圣力量
通过许多甘心乐意的志愿人员
发挥作用
我们看看区域大会是怎样筹备的
一切都从大会的主题开始
莫里斯弟兄在2017年区域大会说
大会开始之前好几年
就已经定好大会主题的关键词了
所有节目都会环绕这个词进行编排
戏剧是最需要大量人力的环节
五年前就要开始准备了
教导委员会和写作部
也会跟“戏剧审阅小组”密切合作
编写剧本
这些经验丰富的写作人员
会根据大会主题想要传达的真理
构思剧情
剧本经过广泛的考查之后
就会送到影音服务部AVS
准备制作影片
这些工作往往在好几年前就开始进行

ko.text: 길르앗 학교에서 사용하는 연구 방법을 살펴볼 텐데요.
잠시 우리가 길르앗 학생으로 하루를 시작한다고 상상해 보시죠.
오늘 아침 수업이 너무나 기대가 돼요.
배우는 내용이 마음에 정말 와 닿는 것 같아요.
더 영적인 사람이 된 것 같고,
학생들이 여호와와 더 가까운 관계를 맺는 데 도움이 되는 연구 방법이 뭘까요?
우리 개인 연구에 그 방법들을 어떻게 적용할 수 있을까요?
이 형제 자매들이 개인 성서 연구를 어떻게 하는지 이야기해 줄 겁니다.
이들은 성경을 읽고 묵상하면서 어떤 질문들을 해 볼까요?
기본 가르침보다 더 많은 걸 이해할까요?
청소년 여러분, 지금 성경을 깊이 파고 있습니까?
그게 진리를 자신의 것으로 만드는 데 어떻게 도움이 될까요?
가까운 사람들의 영적인 도움 없이도 잘 해낼 수 있을까요?
이 자매의 경험은 숨겨진 보물을 찾듯 성경을 조사하는 것이
양심 문제에서 지혜로운 선택을 위해 준비할 수 있습니까?
양심을 준비하고 훈련해 뜻밖의 상황에 대비하는 데
이 동영상에 나오는 자매가 어떤 답을 제시하는지 보실 겁니다.
먼저 앨런 보일 형제와 과거에 했던 회견을 보죠.
우리가 읽는 내용을 그려 보고 묵상하게 도와주어
그런 삽화를 그리는 일은 참 즐겁지만,
그 일을 하는 사람은 영적 특성들이 필요합니다.
함께 협력하고 겸손하게 남의 의견을 잘 들어야 하죠.
또 영적 양식에 포함될 삽화를 준비하려면
“충실하고 슬기로운 종”의 지침에 꼭 따라야 합니다.
그 일을 하려면 열심히 성경을 연구해야 합니다.
그가 임무를 잘 수행하는 데 무엇이 필요했는지 알아보시죠.
하루는 어머니가 당시엔 부회의 종이라고 불렀던 형제를
그분이 저한테 앞으로 어떻게 살 거냐고 묻길래
3주 뒤 저는 런던에서 열린 대회에서 침례를 받았고
스물한 살 때 순회 활동을 시작했어요.
오토바이 뒤에다 가방이랑 타자기랑 옷 가방을 다 싣고 다녔는데,
그땐 제가 선교인이 되어 아일랜드에 가게 될 줄 몰랐어요.
제 친구가 삽화 작업을 하도록 런던 베델에 초대됐습니다.
실은 저도 늘 베델에 가고 싶었지요.
전화해서 축하해 줘야겠다 싶어 친구에게 전활 했더니,
다음 날 아침에 런던 베델에 전화했고,
일주일도 안 돼 전 런던 베델로 와서 잡지를 위한 삽화 작업을 하게 됐어요.
그 후에 배리 형제의 초대로 브루클린 베델로 오게 됐습니다.
유익을 주고 도움이 되는 일을 한다고 생각해 보세요.
사람들이 중요한 점을 기억하도록 도와주는 일입니다.
미술부에서 그림을 그리는 일을 할 때 가장 좋은 것 하나는
대홍수 전에 노아가 방주를 지을 때 상황은 어땠을까?
방수는 어떻게 했을까? 제일 중요한 건데.
이런 소소한 질문들을 다 생각해 봐야 되죠.
보통 갑판 밑에는 평형 유지를 위한 50kg짜리 모래 자루가 있었습니다.
분명 그분은 이 자루를 베고 주무셨을 겁니다.
사실 「왕국 행간역」을 보면 베개 앞에 정관사 “the”가 붙어 있어서
일반적인 베개가 아니었단 걸 알 수 있죠.
2000년 전 당시 그 지역 사람들은 그 “베개”가 뭔지 다 알았을 겁니다.
전에 시베리아에 가 본 적이 있는 형제를 만났었는데,
그 형제가 시베리아에 사는 어떤 분의 주방 사진을 보여 줬어요.
한쪽 벽에 여기 브루클린에서 생산한 출판물의 한 페이지가
그림을 그리는 데 필요한 다양한 보조 업무든,
전 세계 모든 곳에 있는 형제 자매들에게 영향을 준다는 사실이었습니다.
정말 시간을 가치 있게 보내는 거죠.
우리는 다른 사람들이 성경을 이해하고 유익을 얻도록 돕습니다.
여호와께 드리는 봉사는 정말 보람 있고 가슴 벅찬 일이죠.
앨런 보일 형제는 2016년에 지상 행로를 마쳤습니다.
열정이 넘치고 세부점까지 놓치지 않았던 보일 형제의 모습을 기억합니다.
그가 임무를 잘 수행할 수 있었던 건 개인 성서 연구 덕분이었죠.
성서 장면을 그리는 데 필요한 조사를 하며 보람을 느꼈습니다.
현재는 집필부에서 자료 조사 팀을 구성해 미술부 업무를 지원하죠.
형제는 연구 조사에 무엇이 도움이 됐다고 했나요?
자신이 그리는 장면에 대해 여러 가지 질문을 해 보았죠!
길르앗 학생들이 익히는 연구 방법 중 하나입니다.

여러분이 다음 번 길르앗 학급에 초대된다면
길르앗 학교에 가 보는 게 평생 소원인 분들이 많은데,
이 과정은 학생들이 ‘생명의 말씀을 굳게 잡게’ 도와주죠.

그리고 연구 시간에 더 많은 유익을 얻는 방법입니다.
학교에 갈 수 없는 많은 분을 위해

마케도니아에 있는 빌립보 회중 형제 자매들에게 편지를 썼습니다.

하느님의 생각을 이해하게 해 주는 성경 원칙은 늘 찾을 수가 있는 거죠.
저도 이 문제에 대해 기도한 다음, 개인 연구를 해 봤어요.
「‘하느님의 사랑’」 책 2장에서 정말 좋은 내용을 찾았어요.
또, 비슷한 상황을 겪은 사람들에 대해 읽으면서,
그들에게 어떤 성경 원칙이 도움이 됐는지 알게 됐어요.
읽고 나서 그런 점들을 다 묵상했죠.
제 양심이 단지 제 마음을 따라가지 않고
여호와의 영의 인도를 따르게 할 수 있었어요.
모두가 항상 똑같이 생각하게 되는 건 아니라는 점을 알게 됐어요.
하지만 성경 원칙을 적용하면서 양심을 훈련한다면,
우리 각자가 하느님의 사랑 안에 머물 수 있게 될 거예요.
에마 자매의 어떤 점을 본받을 수 있을까요?
또 양심을 깨끗하게 유지할 결정을 내리기 위해 연구했습니다.
우리도 양심 문제가 생길 때 똑같이 할 수 있죠.
성경에 분명한 명령이 없는 문제들에 대해
양심이 따라야 할 표준을 알려 주는
성서로 훈련받은 양심과 일치하게 결정할 수 있습니다.
그것이 여호와께 고착하고 영원한 생명의 선물을 받는 데
왜 꼭 필요한지 우린 알게 됐습니다.
또한 효과가 증명된 개인 성서 연구 방법을 사용해
말씀을 굳게 잡는 실용적인 방법도 배웠죠.
그 밖의 신권 학교에 참석할 수 없을지 모르지만,
성경에서 유익을 얻는 법을 알려 주십니다.
저희는 뉴욕 주 패터슨의 세계 본부 시설에 있는
길르앗 학교는 1943년에 첫 학급이 시작된 이래로
영적인 것에 정신을 집중해 하느님의 말씀을 공부할
땅이 여호와에 관한 지식으로 가득 찰 것”이라고 알려 줍니다.
전 세계 우리 형제들은 이 예언과 일치된 노력을 하고 있죠.
수업 중에 성경의 모든 부분을 다루면서
그 내용을 잘 이해하는 데 도움이 되는
멍들고 상처 입은 바울이 말하는 겁니다.
학생들은 생활하고 임명을 수행하면서 적용할 수 있는 교훈들을
과거 회중의 방식을 그대로 따르고 있다는 점입니다.
하늘에 계신 아버지 여호와와의 관계를 자라게 하는
학교 강사들도 학생들의 유익을 위해 열심히 일합니다.
이곳과 야외에서 열리는 학교들의 교육 과정을 관리합니다.
그들의 부지런한 노력과 여호와의 축복 덕분에
신권 학교부 성원들은 형제들과 중앙장로회를 섬기는 이 일을
여러분께 따뜻한 그리스도인 사랑과 안부를 전합니다.

en.text: Welcome to JW Broadcasting.
In this month’s program,
we will feature the study methods that are used in Gilead School.
For a moment, let’s imagine ourselves starting our day as a Gilead student.
See you later.
See you, Nathan.
Morning.
Have a good day in class.
Thank you.
Welcome.
How are you?
Good morning.
Hello, Nathan.
Lyubomyr.
Nice to see you.
How are you?
Good.
I am good.
Good to see you.
How was your night?
It was good.
A long night of studying, but it was worth it.
I’m really looking forward to the lesson this morning.
You know, I agree with you. I feel the same.
The information we have been studying is really touching my heart.
I know what you mean.
I feel like I’ve become more of a spiritual person,
and my relationship with Jehovah has become so much stronger.
Good morning everyone. Very good to see you all here this morning.
What are the study methods that are helping the students grow
in their relationship with Jehovah?
And more importantly, how can we apply these methods
in our own personal study?
We’ll find the answers and more.
Here are some of the highlights of what’s ahead.
These brothers and sisters describe
how they approach their personal Bible study.
They’re from different parts of the world,
but they share many common study techniques.
What questions do they ask as they read and meditate on the Bible?
How does their deep study take them beyond the basics of Bible understanding?
Young ones, are you digging deep into God’s Word now?
How can this help you make the truth your own?
And can you succeed even without the support
of those spiritually close to you?
This sister’s experience will show us
the benefits of searching the Bible
as if for hidden treasures.
Can you be ready to make a wise choice in matters of conscience?
Do study habits affect how well-prepared and well-trained
your conscience is for an unexpected situation?
We’ll see how the sister in this dramatization
answers these questions.
This is JW Broadcasting for July 2018.
We begin with an archived interview of Brother Allan Boyle.
Among his many assignments, Brother Boyle spent 37 years
in the Art Department at world headquarters.
The beautiful and accurate illustrations
produced there enhance our study,
helping us to visualize and meditate on what we are reading.
An assignment to create these pictures is exciting,
but it requires that a person have spiritual qualities.
Artists collaborate
and must humbly listen to each other’s comments.
They must apply direction from “the faithful and discreet slave”
to prepare artwork that we can take in as spiritual food.
As you’ll hear Brother Boyle describe,
a person must be an avid student of the Bible.
Listen to Brother Boyle’s story,
and note what he said was needed for him to do his assignment well.
I was born in 1933.
I got to the age of 18, and one suppertime
my mother had invited the company servant,
as they were called back then, to come for supper.
He asked me what I was going to do with my life.
I said to him, “Well, I’m going to pioneer.”
So three weeks later, at the convention in London,
I got baptized and then went pioneering six months after that.
I was 21 when I was in the circuit work,
and that was a wonderful experience.
And in those days, of course, you didn’t have a car.
I used to have a motorbike.
And I’d go around on the motorbike with my briefcase
and my typewriter and my clothes in the other case on the back.
Yeah, that was very exciting.
I was invited to go to Gilead, and that was wonderfully exciting.
We had 103 in the class.
Little did I know at the time
that I would be sent as a missionary to Ireland.
My friend had been invited to go down
to London Bethel to do the artwork there.
I’d always wanted to be in Bethel.
I thought, ‘Well, why don’t I just call him up and congratulate him?’
So that’s what I did, and he told me that he decided not to go.
So he said: “If you’re still interested, why don’t you go?
You know, call them up and let them know.”
So that’s what I did. The next morning, I called up London Bethel,
and within a week I was in London Bethel doing the graphics work
for the magazines, you know.
It was a wonderful, thrilling experience.
I was in London Bethel for a couple of years,
and then Brother Barry invited me to come over to Brooklyn Bethel.
You know that you’re doing something that’s going to be beneficial
and helpful to other people,
even to people in different languages, in different cultures.
A little painting that you do is going to help them
to get a memory of something significant.
One of the most beautiful things about working in the Art Department
and doing paintings is that it makes you do research.
You have to investigate. Is this the right time of the day?
Is it night? Is it day?
What did the sky look like?
What was it like before the Flood when Noah built the ark?
How did he paint underneath the ark?
How did he waterproof it?
Because that’s the most important part, isn’t it?
He used bitumen. OK, how did he get underneath the ark?
Maybe he put it on stilts.
You have to come up with all these little questions in your mind.
To do the research was very rewarding.
This is a little model of a boat,
and underneath the deck they used to keep
a ballast sack of 110 pounds (50 kg) of sand.
It says in the Scriptures that Jesus was asleep on “a pillow.”
Apparently, this was the ballast sack that he was asleep on.
And actually, in the Kingdom Interlinear translation,
it doesn’t say that he was asleep on “a pillow”;
it says he was asleep on “the pillow.”
So apparently, back 2,000 years ago in that area,
everybody knew what “the pillow” was.
I remember meeting a brother once who’d been to Siberia,
and he’d taken a snapshot of somebody’s kitchen in Siberia.
And to my amazement, on the wall
—pinned with drawing pins on the wall—
was one of the pages of the publications
that we produced here at Brooklyn.
And so, remarkably,
it’s wonderful to feel that whatever we do here
—if it’s support work, if it’s the painting,
and, of course, we need a lot of support work for the paintings—
all of what we do here
has an effect upon the brothers and sisters
out there in the world, wherever it might be.
And you really feel that your time is well spent.
You’re adorning the Word of truth.
You’re helping other people to be taught something from the Bible,
which is going to be to their benefit.
It’s been very rewarding and thrilling
to be in Jehovah’s service, and I’ve really enjoyed it.
Allan Boyle finished his earthly course in 2016.
Those in the Art Department who worked with him
remember his enthusiasm and his thorough attention to detail.
What Allan brought to his assignment
was rooted in his own personal study of the Bible.
He found it rewarding to do the research
needed to illustrate Bible scenes.
Today, the Writing Department supplies
a team of researchers to assist the artists.
But did you recall what Allan said helped his research?
He asked questions about the scenes he was painting!
These same kinds of questions are part of the study methods
Gilead students learn in class.
And these are the same methods that we’ll learn about in this program.
How would you feel
if you received an invitation
to attend the next class of Gilead School?
For many, it has been a lifelong dream to attend Gilead.
The course helps students keep “a tight grip on the word of life.”
For others, the idea of five months of intense study seems intimidating.
We know we need to study,
but we may find it a challenge to get the most
out of the time we spend reading God’s Word.
In this program, we will discuss why study is so important,
what it means to study something,
and how you can get more from your study sessions.
Since most cannot attend Gilead,
we will demonstrate the method used in Gilead School.
First, why is study so important?
Only by study can we keep “a tight grip on the word of life.”
When the apostle Paul penned these words,
he was imprisoned and nearing the end of his action-packed life.
He had been the “apostle to the nations”
and had spent his best years
taking the Word of God to the then-known world.
As he reflected on the fruits of his labors,
he wrote a letter to his friends in the congregation in Philippi in Macedonia.
Inspired by holy spirit, he wrote words
that would aid his brothers to gain the prize of eternal life.
These words are found at Philippians 2:15, 16.
Let’s read them:
“So that you may come to be blameless and innocent,
“children of God without a blemish in the midst
“of a crooked and twisted generation,
“among whom you are shining as illuminators in the world,
keeping a tight grip on the word of life.”
Imagine the joy Paul felt
when he was reunited in the heavenly resurrection
with those who listened to his admonition
to keep “a tight grip on the word of life”!
Whether we have the heavenly or earthly hope,
Paul’s words can help us gain the prize of eternal life.
They imprint on our hearts and minds a basic exhortation
that will lead us through these last days and into our everlasting reward.
The question is, Will we remain ‘blameless and without blemish
in the midst of this crooked and twisted generation’ of our day?
Will we rejoice with other faithful servants of God in the new world?
We can and we will
if we take to heart Paul’s counsel
to keep “a tight grip on the word of life.”
Next, what does it mean to study?
Stop and contemplate this word picture
for keeping a tight grip.
Imagine a hiker who has slipped near a ledge.
But before falling over the cliff, he grabs hold of a tree branch.
How tight do you think his grip will be on that branch?
This is not a halfhearted effort.
Likewise, keeping a tight grip on the word of life
is not just a mechanical routine, nor is it a casual habit.
It requires strenuous effort.
It involves actively living by the truths in God’s Word.
To do this, we must understand
more than what God expressly commands and condemns.
We must be able to identify principles,
or life lessons, contained in the Bible.
Once identified, we must understand
how to match these valuable truths
to specific situations in our lives.
Then we must allow these principles to influence our decisions
and guide our reaction to trials and temptations.
Ask yourself,
‘How strong is my grip on the word of life?’
To answer that,
let’s consider the fundamentals of Bible study.
This is not about old methods or new methods,
nor is it about what device you are using.
This discussion transcends devices.
Study requires active thinking.
In a world of increasing distractions,
this is becoming an even greater challenge.
We’ve often received instant information
that enables us to quickly recite facts,
but this is not the same as active thinking.
Through active thinking,
we draw meaningful conclusions in our hearts.
We are certainly grateful for all the study tools we’ve been given.
We should use these to the full.
At the same time, we need to be careful
that these tools do not cause us to develop mental laziness.
Devices can help us to access information,
but they can’t think for us.
We must work hard if we are to develop new patterns of thinking.
For example, if we study The Watchtower on a device,
we can use the hyperlink feature to read the Scriptures.
With a simple touch, we quickly find and read the verse.
That is good!
If you regularly do this, you get a grip on the word of life.
But would you like to get a tight grip on the word of life?
To get a tight grip requires more effort
than a swipe of a finger and then swiftly moving on.
You need to slow down and analyze the material.
Only then will the information you study
become imprinted on your mind and heart,
leaving a clear and distinct impression.
How, then, can I get more out of my study?
Let’s demonstrate a method taught during Gilead School.
It involves the use of six questions.
The following poem, written by English journalist Rudyard Kipling,
can help guide better thinking:
“I keep six honest serving-men
“(They taught me all I knew);
“Their names are What and Why
“and When and How
and Where and Who.”
When studying God’s Word, ask yourself these questions
and then do research in our publications
to get the facts and discern the spiritual lessons.
To illustrate how to do this,
let’s open our Bibles to Genesis chapter 49
and look at verses 22 through 25.
First, we ask the when and where.
Now, with some research,
we learn that Jacob spoke these words near the end of his life.
He was in Egypt,
but what he described takes us back to Canaan some 40 years
when his son Joseph was a young man.
Now we have a clearer picture of these verses.
So now, let’s read and analyze verse 22:
“Joseph is the offshoot of a fruitful tree,
a fruitful tree by a spring, whose branches extend over the wall.”
“The offshoot of a fruitful tree.”
Who is the “fruitful tree”?
It is Joseph’s father, Jacob.
How was he fruitful?
He bore many children.
Joseph’s “branches extend over the wall.”
As Jacob’s offshoot, Joseph is singled out
for a special blessing superior to that of his brothers.
Why?
Joseph proved he had the qualities needed for leadership.
However, of even greater value than his abilities
was his being a spiritual man.
Let’s read verse 23:
“But the archers kept harassing him
and shot at him and kept harboring animosity against him.”
“The archers kept harassing him.”
Who are “the archers”?
Joseph’s half brothers.
How?
They shot figuratively at Joseph
—arrows of envy and hatred and jealousy were used to attack him.
Now, eventually, his brothers sold him into slavery.
Now let’s read verse 24:
“And yet his bow remained in place,
“and his hands stayed strong and agile.
“This was from the hands of the powerful one of Jacob,
from the shepherd, the stone of Israel.”
“His bow remained in place.”
How?
Despite the repeated attacks,
Joseph repaid animosity with kindness.
Joseph endured this ill-treatment
and did not weaken in his devotion to God.
Now we ask, How?
How is it that Joseph kept a spiritual outlook
despite the harassment and animosity?
Let’s read verse 25:
“He [Joseph] is from the God of your father,
“and he will help you, and he is with the Almighty,
“and he will bless you with the blessings of the heavens above,
“with the blessings of the deep below,
with the blessings of the breasts and womb.”
“He is with the Almighty.”
Joseph had Jehovah’s help.
The Almighty was by his side through it all.
We’ve used our questions to get the facts of the account,
but we’re not done.
Now let’s use them to take our study to a spiritual plane.
Next, let’s ask a what question.
What does this account teach us about Jehovah?
Jehovah never abandons his loyal servants.
Even in the depths of prison, Joseph was not alone.
Jehovah found ways to bless Joseph.
Now make the connection to Jehovah’s people today,
including yourself.
Jehovah will never abandon us.
Rather, he shows loyal love to all those who serve him whole-souled.
Would Jehovah let Joseph remain in prison indefinitely?
No.
At the appointed time, relief came.
Joseph was raised from a prisoner in chains
to the second most powerful man in Egypt
—from prison to palace in one day.
Make the connection to us.
Our trials are temporary.
Jehovah will soon bring relief,
even in unexpected or surprising ways.
Meanwhile, we are never alone;
Jehovah is with us.
Again, let’s ask the question, How?
How does the account contribute to the Bible’s theme?
Joseph suffered, but his suffering led
to the survival of Abraham’s offspring,
leading to the Messiah.
Joseph’s account is not just a riveting story.
It directly contributed
to the development of Jehovah’s purpose.
Think about this:
In spite of the poor conduct of his brothers,
Joseph forgave them and took the initiative
to improve their relationship with him.
Joseph’s attitude was a reflection of Jehovah’s attitude.
With their family reunited,
Jehovah also forgave Joseph’s brothers
and took the initiative in restoring their relationship with Himself.
In fact, Jehovah gave Joseph’s brother Judah
the honor of being an ancestor of the Messiah.
What are the lessons in this account?
Let’s highlight just one.
Genesis 49:23:
“But the archers kept harassing him
and shot at him and kept harboring animosity against him.”
Arrows of animosity were fired at Joseph.
Recall Joseph’s response in verse 24?
“And yet his bow remained in place,
and his hands stayed strong and agile.”
In other words, he did not return fire.
His bow remained in place.
Reflect on the last time you were wronged by someone.
How did we react to what we experienced?
Did we seek to vindicate ourselves or insist on our rights?
Did we fire arrows of animosity in return,
or did we show mercy and loyal love?
Did our reaction reveal that God’s spirit was operative on us?
Like Joseph, we know we will have Jehovah’s approval
even if we are wronged or experience trials
that make us feel like we are in prison.
Reflective questions like these
enable us to make the account our own.
It becomes part of us,
part of our way of thinking, our way of acting.
This nourishes our relationship with Jehovah.
This type of study rewards us not simply with a collection of facts
that impress us today and are forgotten tomorrow.
Rather, it leaves us with core principles that we remember,
that influence our decisions, and that guide our lives.
We tighten our grip on the word of life.
Let’s review the fundamentals of study.
Again, this is not about old methods or new methods
or about what device you are using.
This discussion transcends devices.
It’s about basic methods of Bible study.
We can liken these three phases of study
to gathering, sifting, and baking grain.
Gathering is when we read the Bible.
We don’t run through the field grabbing just handfuls of grain;
we systematically harvest the field.
Sifting is when we sort out what we gathered,
answering who, what, where, when, why, and how to get the facts.
Baking is when we think
—“turning up the heat” in our mind and heart—
something no one else can do for you.
The questions we ask can take our study to a spiritual plane.
Most importantly, what does this teach me about Jehovah?
How does it contribute to the Bible’s theme?
And the bottom line: What is the lesson for me?
Jehovah gave us a mind that is begging to learn.
It is a gift with the capacity to cultivate thinking ability.
When we make the effort to unearth gems from God’s Word,
we find that study is rewarding and delightful.
More importantly, our study skills enable us
to keep a tight grip on the word of life.
A tight grip on God’s Word will make our life better now
and give us the opportunity to continue learning
about our heavenly Father for all eternity.
Joseph’s account was an excellent example for us
to demonstrate the fundamentals of Bible study.
During our discussion,
we used pictures to help bring the account to life.
As we learned from Brother Boyle’s interview,
pictures and illustrations give us an accurate image
to use in our meditation.
And if there’s a video,
we have yet another way to imagine ourselves in the account.
So we’re excited to introduce this month’s music video
depicting the trials and blessings that Joseph experienced.
It reminds us that, like Joseph,
when we have Jehovah, we are never alone.
Abandoned and betrayed, Forsaken and alone,
Despair my one companion, My heart within me like a stone
With no one here for me, No kindly word of care,
Who’ll offer consolation? My heavy burden, who can share?
I’m not alone; I never was.
I’ll never be, And all because
Jehovah knows; Jehovah sees.
He hears my prayer; He’s here with me.
Whatever comes my way, I’m never alone.
Whatever I may lose By sticking close to you,
No matter who may fail me, I know you’ll never be untrue.
You’re close to me, O God, And never far away.
My faith, my hope, reliance​— I know you never will betray.
I’m not alone; I never was.
I’ll never be, And all because
Jehovah knows; Jehovah sees.
He hears my prayer; He’s here with me.
Whatever comes my way, I’m never alone.
I never was.
I’ll never be, And all because
Jehovah knows; Jehovah sees.
He hears my prayer; He’s here with me.
Whatever comes my way, I’m never alone.
Have you ever felt as Joseph did?
There were times when Joseph’s life was not turning out as he had hoped.
He no doubt wondered if he’d ever be set free from prison
or if he’d ever see his father again or his younger brother, Benjamin.
But Joseph knew that his God, Jehovah, never lost sight of him.
This surely helped him endure.
We could be in a painful situation that seems to drag on endlessly.
But when we study a Bible account like Joseph’s
—asking the six questions—
we can fully understand and apply the lessons in our life.
Then we can build the same faith that he had
—that we too are never alone.
Let’s now listen to brothers and sisters
who are using the study methods we’ve discussed.
Some learned them in Gilead School, others from Gilead graduates,
or good examples in their families and congregations.
They’ve also applied what they learned
from our publications about good study habits.
See if any of the ways they study
could help you keep “a tight grip” on God’s Word.
The more you study,
the more you understand Jehovah.
The more you understand Jehovah,
the more you love him.
Jehovah clearly tells us:
“My thoughts are not your thoughts.”
So if we want to understand Jehovah’s thinking better,
we need to dig deep in our study,
and then we share those thoughts with others.
Personal study is like fuel
that keeps you going.
Personally, I’m not a good student,
but I really learned how to study the Bible.
The Bible came alive during Gilead.
Self-discipline is involved —very much.
I overcome the tiredness aspect
of Bible study by not doing it
at a time of day when I know I’m going to be tired.
I can be tired for other things later on —but not for that.
Each session of my Bible study begins with a prayer,
“Please help me recognize it is counsel for me,
and then give me the strength to work on it.”
I have a color-coded system,
so I know what certain things stand for.
I have a particular color
for Jehovah’s good hand in people’s lives;
I have another color for warning examples;
I have another for fine examples to imitate.
You have to get behind the information,
not just focus on one verse or one chapter.
See who’s involved, the time,
the conditions, how many people are there,
and then you’ll get the true meaning of the verse.
John 1:1,
who is “the Word”?
We can go to verse 18.
“Begotten” meant
he had a beginning, a time when he started
—when he began—
in heaven with his Father.
That’s where he was.
Philippians 4:6, 7 is a scripture that I’ve read many times over.
“The peace of God that excels all thought.”
OK, how do you get that?
It’s from having a good relationship with Jehovah.
How is it that God’s peace ‘guards your heart’?
“By means of Christ Jesus” our Lord.
And I said: “Why by Jesus?
“Because Jesus paid the ransom;
that ransom is what makes possible a relationship with Jehovah.”
So it almost goes full circle.
I attended a School for Congregation Elders
that had Gilead graduates as instructors.
One of the methods is to analyze
a certain Bible account from different perspectives.
We can’t see the whole picture from one angle.
I share my research results with Bible students,
and that helps them to know Jehovah better,
and it helps them to see that what they’re studying
is of practical value.
I had studied up on Jacob;
he wrestled all night
with an angel.
And I wanted to share it with some of my friends.
One of the brothers that happened to sit around
when this discussion was going on came back to me, and he said to me:
“I had concluded my arrangements
“to quit full-time service.
“But after listening to that discussion,
I’ve decided that I’m no longer stopping.”
And that was such a wonderful moment for me.
I thanked Jehovah.
When I learned that I was going to become a mom,
I said, “Jehovah, if this little one
could love you, then I’ll get to keep him forever.”
And I began to teach everything I was learning to him.
So it’s a matter
of keeping my faith strong,
and there’s no shortcut.
Every session of study that is properly done with good meditation
adds a new pillar
to the strength of our faith.
I look forward to those times when I can, you know,
run upstairs by myself and just shut everything off,
and it’s just me and Jehovah.
Life today is very unpredictable,
but I’ve come to see that as long as I keep a tight grip on God’s Word,
nothing can “separate [me] from God’s love.”
The joy these brothers and sisters get from their personal study
is clearly heard in their expressions.
Recall what they said:
“The more you understand Jehovah, the more you love him.”
“Study is like fuel that keeps you going.”
And “I can shut everything off, and it’s just me and Jehovah.”
We also heard them ask the six questions:
who, what, where, when, why, and how.
They also used tools for research and note-taking that works for them.
Is there something you saw or that we discussed
that you’d like to add to your study routine?
If so, try it out.
Young ones, it’s true that the more you understand Jehovah,
the more you love him.
And what a blessing you have if your family worships Jehovah with you
and teaches you how to draw close to him.
But some young ones have had to build their faith
without their family’s support.
Listen to the experience of Ersi Royer from the United States.
What spiritual decision did she face at just 14 years old?
And what did she do that illustrates the value
of deep personal study?
Growing up,
it wasn’t the typical,
“My mom is a pioneer, my dad is an elder,
and we’re doing great in the congregation.”
My family life wasn’t the best,
so why would I want to do this religion that nobody is happy
in our family with?
And I think that can make you feel
very alone or odd
or awkward or secluded.
And at that time, I was graduating eighth grade.
There were dances;
friends were hanging out, going to parties.
And I remember thinking: ‘Wow, these look like really nice kids.
Why aren’t I doing that?’
I hadn’t really delved into the Bible enough to answer questions
that I really needed to know.
I went in prayer to Jehovah and said: “I’m so sorry, but today I’m not a Witness.
I’m going to try to prove everything that I’ve been taught is wrong.”
I asked him that if he’s real,
to help me understand.
So I went in my room
and shut the door.
I got every book off the shelf.
I started off organized,
but by the end of the evening,
I had books all over the place with pages open.
The more I kept reading about Jehovah,
the more the next topic would take me to then connect the scriptures.
Jesus is linked to Jehovah;
the angels are linked to Jehovah; the resurrection is linked to Jehovah.
So you can’t believe in one thing and not everything else
if you really want to know the truth.
And so that’s what did it for me,
especially the scripture in Psalms
when it said that ‘you saw even the embryo of me.’
And it was an emotional scripture for me
because I thought: ‘Wow,
‘my parents aren’t doing great in the truth right now.
‘But Jehovah found a way to find me,
‘and he knew what I could be.
‘Now I have my answer. I don’t have an excuse.
‘Jehovah gave me enough knowledge that now I’m responsible.
I now need to act on that and show my love in return for him.’
Within a week, I found another sister
in the hall that was really helpful in me getting out
in service quite often.
I don’t think to this day she ever knew how much I appreciated that.
Although things were declining in our family spiritually,
I was able to get baptized.
As I progressed spiritually,
I could see that I did not have
the support of my family,
but I had to trust that Jehovah would help me through it.
And at least by the time I got home, if there was an issue,
I had the strength of the meeting and the brothers and sisters
and joy that they couldn’t take away from me.
I remember I came home one day with some friends.
It was a nice day
—encouraging, upbuilding.
We pulled into our driveway; they dropped me off
and said good-bye.
My parents were really upset
when they came and met me at the door.
They couldn’t fully understand
why I was making my decisions
the way I was to serve Jehovah more fully.
We just could not agree
on where my relationship with Jehovah was going.
And at that point, I left with the clothes on my back.
In a matter of a few minutes,
my life forever changed.
I had a spiritual aunt that took me in,
helped me gather myself together,
and literally fed me, clothed me,
helped me spiritually.
And so then, my support became Jehovah
and the congregation.
I remember that a sister told me years ago,
“Be who you needed when you were young.”
And so when I look at those little ones,
I look at myself and say,
‘How could I have benefited
from someone taking the time for me when I was that age?’
I’ve always tried remembering the young ones
—because that’s just part of who I am—
and making sure that they know that they’re not alone.
If there is a young one out there who isn’t sure
if this is the truth or not,
I would like them to know that Jehovah knows
who they are,
and he’s finding a way for them to know him.
Jehovah is real, he knows them by name,
he wants them to live, and he’s fighting for them.
How amazing that young Ersi chose to spend an entire day studying
—proving to herself that Jehovah knew her and loved her.
But this was no onetime study marathon.
From there, she worked to develop the study habits she needed
to endure, grow, and become a spiritual person.
She pioneered for several years,
and now serves at Bethel with her husband, Jeff.
In my conversation with Ersi, she expressed her love for her family
and the hope that someday in the future
she’ll be reunited with them spiritually.
There’s no situation in life
that cannot be handled better than by seeking
Jehovah’s guidance in the Bible.
That’s certainly true in matters of conscience.
In these situations,
Jehovah does not tell us what to do with a command,
but his Word gives us the principles we use to train our conscience.
In this dramatization,
Emma has to make a difficult decision.
How is her conscience involved,
and what steps does she take to make her decision?
Every day we make choices
that can affect our relationship with Jehovah.
When there’s a clear Scriptural command,
the right choice may seem easy.
But what if there’s not?
How can we be sure we’re making a wise decision?
An invitation to our niece’s wedding arrived.
Thomas was excited about it.
I was excited too.
But the ceremony
was being held at a local church.
I wondered if it would still be OK for me to attend.
Even though Thomas wasn’t yet willing
to accept a Bible study, he gradually softened over the years
since I came into the truth.
I knew he understood why I would never enter a church for worship,
but what about attending a wedding?
Jehovah approves of weddings.
That afternoon,
I went to help Amy plan a menu
for the pioneer school lunch coming up.
She noticed I was a bit distracted,
so I told her my concerns about the wedding.
But you’re not thinking of going, are you?
Amy sure had a strong opinion on the matter,
but I didn’t feel she really understood my situation.
Although I appreciated her concern,
I felt like she was judging me.
The next day, I decided to visit Charlotte and Allan
and ask their advice.
Like me, Charlotte had come into the truth
many years before Allan, so they really understood my situation.
Is Amy right?
Would it be wrong to attend the wedding?
What would you do if you were me?
Charlotte explained that in situations
where there’s no specific Bible command,
it becomes a matter of conscience.
And what one person’s conscience allows
may be different from another.
The important thing
is that we make decisions that leave us with a good conscience.
But how do I do that?
Dear Emma, it’s really a matter of training.
Allan showed me the scripture at Hebrews 5:14,
where the apostle Paul wrote:
“Solid food belongs to mature people,
“to those who through use
“have their powers of discernment trained
to distinguish both right and wrong.”
But Paul didn’t just write those words;
he lived them.
He carefully studied the principles in God’s Word.
And as a result, he was able to make decisions
that left him with a good conscience.
So even when there’s no stated law on a matter,
we can always find a Bible principle
that can give us insight into God’s thinking.
So I made it a matter of prayer, and then I got to work.
I researched articles
in the Watch Tower Publications Index and the Research Guide.
I found a really good thought in chapter 2 of the “God’s Love” book.
I also read about others who faced similar situations
and what Bible principles they found helpful.
Then I meditated on all these.
As I kept studying, I was able to bring my conscience
in harmony with Jehovah’s spirit,
not just with my heart.
I realized that having a Bible-trained conscience
doesn’t mean everyone will always think exactly alike
—and that’s OK.
But if we train our conscience by applying Bible principles,
it will guide us along in life, so that each of us
can remain in God’s love.
What did our sister, Emma, do that we can imitate?
When she realized that she needed more information,
she got to work!
She studied in order to train her conscience
and to make a decision that left her conscience clean.
We can do the same when a conscience matter comes up.
But we can do more.
We can prepare in advance,
train our conscience on matters that do not have clear Bible commands,
and study Bible principles
that teach our conscience the rules it should work with.
Then, when we need it, it’s ready.
We can trust it and make decisions
in harmony with a Bible-trained conscience.
We urge you brothers and sisters:
Keep “a tight grip on the word of life.”
That’s what our program has been about.
We learned why it’s essential to stay close to God
and to receive his gift of everlasting life.
But what’s more, we learned practical ways to do it
using tried and true methods of personal Bible study.
We may not have an opportunity to attend Gilead
or another theocratic school,
but Jehovah shows all of us how to benefit from his written Word.
What an expression of God’s love!
To prepare this month’s program,
our team spent time with the Theocratic Schools Department
at the world headquarters facility in Patterson, New York.
This has been the home for Gilead School since 1995.
And since arriving here,
47 classes have graduated.
Gilead School began with its first class in 1943,
and since then, close to 9,000 students have been trained.
When students come to class each day,
the writings and models on display
put their mind on spiritual things
as they get ready to study God’s Word.
Isaiah 11:9 says:
“The earth will certainly be filled with the knowledge of Jehovah
as the waters cover the sea.”
Our worldwide brotherhood
works in harmony with that prophecy.
It’s fitting then that here in the classroom,
lectures cover every part of the Bible,
exploring background information
to get the sense of the account.
. . . probably still got bruises.
And Paul is telling them, very honestly,
‘we have to enter through many tribulations.’
Can you imagine, you’re sitting there and you’re looking at this man
bruised and cut,
and he’s saying,
‘We (you and I) have to go through many tribulations.’
Students participate freely,
drawing lessons that they can use in their life and assignments.
It impresses me to see that the Christian congregation in our time
follows exactly the pattern that was used back then.
Studying in the Theocratic Schools’ library
is a cherished part of their day.
In a quiet, relaxed setting,
they associate figuratively with “the faithful and discreet slave,”
searching and taking in the spiritual food
that nourishes and strengthens their relationship
with their heavenly Father, Jehovah.
Students benefit from the hard work of the school instructors.
Under the direction of the Teaching Committee
of the Governing Body,
they manage the curriculum for Gilead and other schools
that are taught here and in the field.
Through their diligent efforts and Jehovah’s blessing,
the Theocratic Schools staff count it a privilege
to serve their brothers and the Governing Body.
We send you our sincere Christian love and greetings.
Thank you for joining us this month.
This is JW Broadcasting
from the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses.

让我住在她家
她帮助我重新振作起来
她对待我就像对待自己的家人
为我提供吃的穿的
也在属灵方面帮助我
从那时起
耶和华和会众就成为我的一切了
很多年前  有位姐妹对我说
你年轻时需要怎样的帮助
那你现在就要怎样帮助那些年轻人
所以  每当我看到青少年
就对自己说
我像他们那么大的时候
如果有人愿意花时间帮我
我会得到什么益处呢?
我一直很关心会众里的年轻人
希望他们知道
他们不是孤立无援的
毕竟我也是从那个年纪过来的
如果有哪个年轻人
不确定这是不是真理
我希望他们知道
耶和华认识他们
而且正想方设法帮助他们
耶和华是真实的
他知道每个年轻人的名字
希望他们永远活下去
也会一直扶持他们
年轻的艾尔西
拨出一整天的时间来研读圣经
这让她看出耶和华了解她
也很爱她
真的值得称赞!
当然  她不是一下子读很多
以后就不读了
而是渐渐养成了研读的好习惯
这帮助她保持忍耐
在属灵方面不断进步
她做了几年先驱
现在和丈夫一起在伯特利服务
和艾尔西交谈时
她说她很爱自己的家人
她告诉我  希望有一天
能再次和家人一起事奉耶和华
在生活中  不论遇到什么情况
只要我们通过圣经
寻求耶和华的指引
就能做出最好的决定
按良心做决定的事也是这样
有些事情
耶和华没有给我们明确的指引
这时我们就需要按良心做决定
圣经里面很多原则
可以帮助我们训练自己的良心
在这个短片中
艾玛面对一个难题
她的良心怎样发挥作用呢?
为了做出明智的决定
她都采取了哪些步骤呢?
我们每天的选择
会影响到我们和耶和华的关系
如果有明确的圣经指引
做正确的决定可能就会很容易
不过  要是没有明确的指引呢?
怎么肯定自己的决定是明智的呢?
我们收到了侄女的婚礼请柬
我的丈夫托马斯非常高兴
我也很期待参加她的婚礼
但是  婚礼会在教堂举行
我不太确定  我可以去参加吗?
虽然托马斯还没有开始学圣经
但我受浸后
他越来越理解我的信仰了
我知道
他明白我为什么不去教堂做礼拜
但婚礼又怎么样呢?
耶和华并没有禁止人参加婚礼啊
那天下午
我去艾米家跟她一起商量
为先驱训练班提供什么午餐
她留意到我有些心事
我就告诉了她关于参加婚礼的事
你不会真的打算去吧?
看来艾米对这件事看法很明确
但我觉得她并不了解我的情况
我理解她的担忧
但还是觉得她有点妄断我
第二天  我去拜访了夏洛特和艾伦
想听听他们的建议
夏洛特接受真理比艾伦早很多年
和我的情况有些相似
所以他们很理解我的处境
艾米说得对吗?
我不该去参加婚礼吗?
如果你们是我  会怎么做呢?
夏洛特解释说
如果一件事圣经没有明确说怎么做
就要按良心来做决定
而每个人的良心是不同的
能接受的程度也不一样
重点是
我们的决定要让自己感到良心无愧
但我怎么才能做得到呢?
亲爱的艾玛
这是需要锻炼的
艾伦给我看了希伯来书5:14
使徒保罗写道
“只有长大成人的  才能吃固体食物”
“他们的理解力因常常运用而锻炼纯熟”
“能明辨是非”
保罗不只是说说而已
他也确实这么做了
他仔细研读上帝话语中包含的原则
所以  他做的决定总是令他良心无愧
因此
就算对某件事圣经没有明确的规定
我们也能找到相关的圣经原则
从而看出上帝的想法
我先为这件事祷告
然后开始研读
我通过《守望台出版物索引》
和《检索手册》
搜索了相关文章
《上帝的爱》第2章的一个观点
对我很有启发
另外  我也找到一些人物经历
他们面对过类似的情况
也分享了对他们有帮助的圣经原则
我仔细沉思了所有读到的內容
我越研读
就越能让自己的良心
受耶和华的圣灵指引
而不只是跟着感觉走
我看出
培养受圣经原则熏陶的良心
不代表每个人的想法都会一模一样
重要的是
我们要通过实践圣经原则来锻炼良心
这样  良心就会在生活上
不断指引我们
帮助我们留在上帝的爱里
我们从艾玛的经历学到什么呢?
她意识到自己需要查找资料
就行动起来  努力研读圣经
熏陶自己的良心  然后做出决定
结果  她能保持良心清白
我们遇到类似的事情时
也可以这样做
我们可以提前想一想
有哪些事情圣经中没有明确的指引
然后查考并沉思圣经原则
如果我们经常这样训练自己的良心
那么  当遇到
必须按良心做决定的事情时
就可以放心地根据良心发出的指引
做出符合圣经标准的决定了
亲爱的弟兄姐妹
你们一定要“紧握生命的话语”
这也是本月节目的主题
我们学到
为什么只有亲近上帝
才能得享他所赐的永生
除此之外
我们也学到了一些行之有效的方法
这些方法可以帮助我们
更好地研读圣经
也许  我们没机会参加基列学校
或组织开设的其他训练班
但是耶和华却告诉我们每个人
可以怎样从他的话语得益
这就是上帝爱我们的明证
为了准备本月节目
我们拜访了位于纽约帕特森的
圣经教育培训部
帕特森是世界总部的一部分
从1995年开始
基列学校的课程一直在这里举行
迄今为止
已经培训了47届学生
第一届基列学校开办于1943年
到现在
已有将近9000位学员
在这里接受培训
学员们每天来上课时
都能看到跟圣经有关的文献和模型
这帮助他们准备好自己的思想和內心
开始新一天的课程
以赛亚书11:9说
“认识耶和华的知识必遍满大地”
“就像水弥漫海洋一样”
正如预言所说
世界各地的弟兄姐妹
正努力学习耶和华的知识
基列学员们也不例外
他们全面系统地学习了整本圣经
查考了相关资料
从而对圣经的记载
有了更深入的认识
当时保罗身上可能还有伤
但他还是非常坦诚地告诉大家
我们必须经历许多患难
想象一下  他就坐在你面前
这个伤痕累累的弟兄告诉你
我们
你们和我
都必须经历许多患难
学员们积极评论
分享自己可以怎样把学到的
在生活和委派上用出来
让我印象深刻的是
今天  基督徒会众的运作模式
和以前完全一样
每天在图书馆学习的时间
对学员们来说特别珍贵
这里很安静  也很舒适
他们在这里查找资料
努力吸收灵粮
仿佛在跟“忠信睿智的奴隶”
共享属灵的宴席
借此加深自己和天父耶和华的关系
学员们也从导师们的悉心教导
获益良多
这些导师
在中央长老团教导委员会的督导下
除了负责基列学校的课程以外
他们也负责其他训练班的课程
培训部弟兄们的辛勤工作
得到了耶和华的赐福
能够为弟兄姐妹和中央长老团服务
我们真的感到非常荣幸
我们想把温暖的爱心和问候
带给大家
感谢大家观看本月节目
