title: 제144기 길르앗 졸업식—결론 연설 및 임명

ko.text: 노어 형제가 길르앗 졸업식의 주요 연설을 하셨습니다.
오늘의 연설 주제는 아니니까 적지 않으셔도 됩니다.
이제 중앙장로회 성원인 새뮤얼 허드 형제가
‘당신은 겸손한가요?’라고 물었는데, ‘네’라고 하면, 겸손한 게 아니죠.
연설들이 다 좋았는데, 이 연설도 그럴까요?
우리는 모두 철저히 겸손해야 한다는 걸 알고 있습니다.
여호와께서 자신의 모든 종들에게 요구하시는 건데요,
하느님을 기쁘시게 하는 이 특성에 대해 생각해 보겠습니다.
거만하거나 뽐내거나 자기를 중요하게 여기지 않습니다.
‘나는 자기를 높이는 일과 교만을 미워한다’고 말하시죠.
여러분은 길르앗 학교에 있으면서 영적인 지식을 많이 쌓았지만,
여러분이 미래에 배워 나갈 것들에 비하면
여러분은 이곳에서 몇 달을 보내면서 많은 것들에 대한 이해력이 예리해졌기 때문에
사람들에게 배운 걸 알려 주고 싶은 마음이 가득할 겁니다.
분명 그건 나쁜 게 아니죠. 좋은 일입니다.
여러분이 꼭대기에, 여러분의 지부나 회중 형제 자매들
소리가 두 배는 멀리 갈 것”이라고 윌 로저스는 말했죠.
무엇보다 여호와의 영감받은 말씀인 잠언 27:2에서는 이렇게 말합니다.
“네 입이 아니라 남이 너를 칭찬하게 하고,
네 입술이 아니라 다른 사람이 너를 칭찬하게 하여라.”
여러분만큼 많이 알진 못할 수 있지만
그들은 그만큼만 알아도 이 세상의 마지막을 생존해 신세계로 갈 겁니다.
성서 연구를 막 시작한 한 연구생의 이야깁니다.
몇 가지를 배운 그는 아는 만큼 진리를 사랑하게 됐죠.
그러다 병이 들어 거의 죽게 됐습니다.
의사는 반드시 수혈을 받아야 한다고 했지만,
그는 배운 대로 수혈은 안 된다고, 절대 안 된다고 했습니다.
믿지 않는 가족이 수혈을 좀 받으라고 해도,
“안 돼, 수혈은 안 받아”, 다른 사람이 설득해도, “안 돼”라고 했죠.
그 후 연구 사회자와 회중 사람들이
병원으로 왔는데, 그는 뭔가 말할 게 있었죠.
병상 곁에 모인 사람들은 뭔가 잘못됐다고,
연구생이 이제 수혈을 받으려 한다고 생각했는데 이렇게 말했기 때문이죠.
그는 1914년에 이방인의 때가 끝났다는 걸 모릅니다.
오늘날 사람들이 말하는 것들과 무슨 차이가 있는지도 모릅니다.
그는 하느님의 이름을 입증하는 문제나 주권 문제,
하느님의 통치의 정당성에 관해 온전히 알지 못하죠.
많이 알지 못하지만 목숨이 위태로울 때도 하느님의 법을 어기느니 죽는 쪽을 택했습니다.
여호와를 기쁘시게 하는 건 우리가 얼마나 많이 아는지가 아니라,
알게 된 것에 대해 어떻게 느끼고
그 지식을 통해 하느님에 대한 사랑을 얼마나 키웠는지 하는 겁니다.
이제 성경을 펴 보시죠, 성경 연구생인 학생 여러분.
몇 개의 구절을 볼 텐데요, 펴셨나요?
“나에게 베풀어진 과분한 친절을 통해서 그곳에 있는 여러분 모두에게 말합니다.
자기 자신에 대해 마땅히 생각해야 하는 것 이상으로 생각하지 마십시오.
오히려 하느님께서 각자에게 주신 믿음의 분량에 따라
자신과 자신이 얼마나 아는지에 몰두해선 안 됩니다.
그건 여호와께서 우리에게 바라시는 게 아니죠.
높은 것에 마음을 두지 말고 낮은 것에 이끌리십시오.
정말 멋진 조언이지 않습니까? 훌륭한 조언이죠.
하지만 마음에 이르려면 성구 몇 개보다 좀 더 많은 게 필요할 때도 있죠.
알아야 할 게 좀 더 있습니다.
여러분은 몇 개월간 교육을 받으면서 수많은 지식을 얻게 되었고
하지만 고린도 전서 8:1에선 깊이 생각해 볼 점을 알려 주죠.
“우리 모두가 지식을 가지고 있다는 것을 압니다.”
다음 보시면, “지식은 우쭐대게 하지만 사랑은 세워 줍니다.”
여러분의 많은 지식이 여러분을 우쭐대게 만들어서
회중의 형제 자매들보다 우월하다고 생각하는 일이 없도록 조심하십시오.
여호와께선 학교 교육으로 차원 높은 지식을 갖게 된
예수께서는 그 점에 대해 마태 18장에서 좀 더 알려 주십니다.
결코 하늘 왕국에 들어가지 못할 것입니다.
그러므로 누구든지 이 어린아이처럼 자기를 낮추는 사람이
시편 18편에서 ‘당신의 겸손이 나를 크게 만들어 주실 것’이라고 했죠.
하느님의 겸손은 우리도 크게 만들어 주십니다.
여호와께서 겸손하지 않으시다면, 우린 여기 없겠죠.
겸손하신 그분은 우리 모두에게 겸손할 것을 요구할 권리가 있으십니다.
그리고 우린 겸손하도록 서로 도와야 합니다.
이미 천사가 된 것처럼 보는 경우가 있기 때문인데요,
그러니 저희를 지나치게 높이지 말아 주시기 바랍니다.
부당하게 대해 왔다는 말은 아닌데, 여러분도 인간이죠.
우리는 모두 죄를 짓고 생각 없이 행동할 때가 있는 인간입니다.
그렇지만 저희도 겸손할 수 있게 도와주세요.
여호와는 “몸을 굽혀 하늘과 땅을 눈여겨보시는” 분이라고
그분은 엄격하지 않으시며 가장 높은 지위에 계시지만 겸손하시죠.
그래서 우리에게도 어느 위치에 있든 겸손하라고 가르치십니다.
우린 예수처럼 완벽해질 수 없습니다. 그저 노력할 뿐이죠.
최선을 다해 그 발걸음을 따를 뿐입니다.
그분은 타락한 소돔과 고모라를 멸하는 것이 옳은지
‘됐다. 아브라함, 이제 그만 입 좀 다물래?’
또 몇 번은 모세가 마치 사람과 대화하듯 그분을 설득하게 놔두셨습니다.
모세의 청을 들어주려면 겸손이 필요했지만, 그렇게 하셨죠.
계신 분들 중엔 아이패드나 성경이 없으신 분도 계신데,
“그리스도 예수 안에 있던 이러한 정신 태도를 여러분 안에 간직하십시오.
장악하려고 곧 하느님과 동등하게 되려고 생각하지 않으셨습니다.
오히려 자신을 비우고 종의 모습을 취하여 사람이 되셨습니다.
그뿐 아니라, 사람으로 오셨을 때에 자신을 낮추어 죽기까지,
겸손을 가르치시려고 사도들의 더러운 발을 씻겨주셨습니다.
그건 종이 하거나, 아니면 노예가 했어야 할 일이죠.
요한 13장 내용인데 그걸 묘사한 그림이 있습니다.
그 그림이 걸려 있는 걸 봤습니다.
하지만 발 쪽으로 몸을 안 숙이고 어떻게 발을 씻기겠습니까?
사도 바울도 겸손의 훌륭한 본이 되는데,
다음과 같은 말을 기록하진 않았을 겁니다.
“나는 내 속에 곧 내 육체 속에 선한 것이 자리 잡고 있지 않다는 것을 압니다.
좋은 일을 하기 원하지만 그것을 행할 능력은 없기 때문입니다.
나는 내가 원하는 선은 행하지 않고 원하지 않는 악을 행하고 있습니다.”
바울은 초자연적인 환상들을 보았고 또한 계시를 받았습니다.
사도행전 19:11-16을 보면, 그 점을 알 수 있죠.
“하느님께서는 바울의 손을 통해 비상한 기적을 계속 행하셨다.
바울의 몸에 닿았던 수건이나 앞치마를 병든 사람들에게 가져가기만 해도
그들에게서 질병이 사라지고 악한 영들이 나왔다.
그런데 떠돌아다니면서 악귀를 쫓아내던 어떤 유대인들도
악한 영이 들린 사람들에게 주 예수의 이름을 사용해 보려고 했다.
그들은 ‘바울이 전파하는 예수의 이름으로 너희에게 엄숙히 명한다’ 하고 말했다.
스게와라는 유대인 수제사장의 일곱 아들도 그런 일을 하고 있었다.
‘나는 예수도 알고 바울도 잘 아는데 너희는 누구냐?’
그러고는 악한 영이 들린 사람이 그들에게 달려들어
그들은 옷이 벗겨지고 상처를 입은 채 그 집에서 도망쳤다.”
분명 이들은 예수께서 자신의 이름을 사용해 악한 영을 쫓아내도록 하실 만큼
하지만 그는 교만해지지 않았고, 계속 겸손했죠.
네이선 H. 노어 형제가 집필부의 한 형제를 만나려고 사무실로 왔습니다.
“여기는 가장 중요하고도 가장 어려운 일을 하는 곳입니다.
그렇기 때문에 나는 이 일을 거의 하지 않아도 되지요.”
저도 중앙장로회 집필 위원회에서 일하는데, 거기 왜 있는 건지 모르겠어요.
글이라고는 쓸 줄도 모르는데 여기 있네요.
메릴랜드주 크라운스빌에서 학교에 참석했을 때가 기억납니다.
강사 중에 테드 재라스 형제는 어느 날 아침 일찍 일어나
저도 강사였는데, 그런 건 생각조차 하지 못했습니다.
아마 제가 겸손하지 않았거나 그걸 표현하지 못했나 봅니다.
사실 저는 요리의 요 자도 모르고요.
“누구든지 자기를 높이는 사람은 낮추어지고, 자기를 낮추는 사람은 높여질 것입니다.”
다른 사람이 더 낫다는 걸 힘들게 배우지 마십시오.
제가 예전에 키우던 개인 부저의 예를 들어 보죠.
원래는 작은 개를 키우던 집이었는데 그 개가 죽었죠.
부저가 뭔가 냄새를 맡고는 계속 킁킁거리는 거예요.
부저는 그 집 가까이 갔는데, 갑자기 큰 달마시안이 달려 나오더니
부저는 꼬리를 완전히 내리고서는 쏜살같이 도망쳐 버렸습니다.
몇 주 후에, 부저랑 또 같이 외출을 했죠. 걸어서요.
그런데 달마시안이 사는 집 근처에서 부저가 사라져 버렸습니다.
부저는 그 집을 저 멀리 돌아서, 시내에서 우릴 만났죠.
학생 여러분, 부저의 예의 요점을 이해하시겠죠?
제가 보증하는데 허드 형제는 정말 겸손한 분입니다.
물론 나중에 스트리밍을 통해서도 아주 많은 분들이 이 프로그램을 보시겠죠.
그러니까 그 수는 1만 명을 훨씬 넘게 될 겁니다.
여러 지부에서 아름다운 글을 보내 왔는데, 우리 학생들에게 보낸 인사말입니다.
시간 관계상 읽진 못하고, 교습 위원회의 기록 보관실로 보낼 겁니다.
제 마음 같아서는 받은 걸 전부 다 읽어 드리고 싶네요.
어떤 나라에서 이런 멋진 인사를 보내 왔는지 알려 드리도록 하죠.
앙골라, 아르헨티나, 벨기에, 볼리비아, 브라질, 영국, 불가리아, 부룬디, 캐나다, 핀란드,
프랑스, ​​조지아, 가나, 아이티, 홍콩, 이탈리아, 일본, 카자흐스탄, 한국, 마다가스카르, 모잠비크,
네덜란드, 나이지리아, 파푸아 뉴기니, 포르투갈, 시에라리온, 타이, 우크라이나입니다.
이 여러 지부에 계신 분들의 아름다운 마음이 담긴 따뜻한 글에 대해
주요 연설이 있은 후 어떤 일이 있었을까요?
‘졸업장이 담겨 있는 커다란 상자가 개봉되어 연단의 탁자 위에 놓였다.
모든 학생의 이름을 한 명씩 호명하면 앞으로 나와 졸업장을 받았다.’
네 지금, 우리도 이대로 할 겁니다. 75년 전에 했던 방식 그대로요.
기쁘게도 제 옆에 데이비드 셰이퍼 형제가 계신데,
이 학급을 처음 소개하는 프로에 참석해 보셨다면,
셰이퍼 형제가 학생들의 이름을 모두 멋지게 발음한 걸 아실 겁니다.
자 이제, 길르앗 학교 제144기 학생들을 만나 보시죠.
먼저, 아부 형제 부부는 중동으로 돌아갈 것입니다.
알로이 형제 부부는 중동에서 봉사할 것입니다.
칠튼 형제 부부는 남아프리카 공화국에서 봉사합니다.
더 로에이 형제 부부는 네덜란드로 돌아갑니다.
페투르손 형제 부부는 덴마크로 돌아갈 겁니다.
웸바롤라 형제 부부는 마다가스카르에서 봉사할 겁니다.
졸업장을 수여한 뒤에 어떤 일이 있었을까요?
기록에 의하면, 학급 대표가 편지를 낭독했는데,
길르앗에 오게 되어 고마워하는 학생들의 마음을 표현하고,
여호와와 그분의 조직에 대한 그들의 충성을 중앙장로회에게 약속했죠.
리차드 칠튼 형제가 학급을 대표해서 편지를 낭독해 주시겠습니다.
사랑하는 벗들과 영적인 주제로 뜻 깊은 토의를 나누는 것만큼
우리는 날마다 그러한 토의 속에 파묻혀 지내는 축복을 누렸습니다.
성경의 책을 한 권 한 권 살펴볼 때,
과거 충실한 남녀들의 살아 숨 쉬는 모범은
여호와의 조직의 현대 역사를 되새겨 볼 때
선구자들이 나타낸 믿음과 용기와 희생 정신은
워크숍을 통해 우리의 봉사 기술이 한층 발전되었고,
전파 활동에 참여하려는 열의가 더욱 뜨거워졌습니다.
시간이 흐르면서 학급의 학생들은 우리의 절친한 벗이 되었습니다.
우리가 헤어져야 한다는 생각에 눈물이 앞을 가리지만,
우리는 새로운 벗들 간에 서로 ‘격려를 주고받았던’ 추억을
또한 ‘영적인 것을 영적인 말로 설명해’ 주신
장성하고 헌신적인 강사 분들의 지도를 받은 것도 큰 축복이었습니다.
애정 어린 도움을 베풀어 주신 데 깊이 감사하며,
하느님의 말씀에 대한 그분들의 열심을 잊지 않겠습니다.
베델 가족을 알게 된 것도 큰 기쁨이었습니다.
사랑하는 하느님을 섬기기 위해 힘을 쏟아 활기차게 일하는 젊은이들,
그리고 수십 년간 그리스도인 원칙에 따라 살며 얻은 지혜를 나타내는
그들의 친절과 우정과 후대는 정말 감동적이었습니다.
과거에 그가 한 훌륭한 일을 더 알게 되면
그분을 알수록 우린 계속 놀라고 기뻐합니다.
그분이 현재와 과거에 하신 모든 일을 숙고하면,
우리는 감동되어 그분의 아름다운 이름을 찬양하게 됩니다.
길르앗 학교는 우리의 기대를 훨씬 뛰어넘었지만,
한편 더욱 많은 것을 바라게 만들었습니다.
우리는 의미 있는 개인 연구를 계속해 나갈 것을 다짐합니다.
하늘에 있는 것이 아니며 바다 건너편에 있는 것도 아닙니다.’
어떤 상황에서도, 우리는 언제나 빛을 밝혀 주는 성경 원칙이나,
옳은 일을 행하는 데 도움이 되는 기사를 찾게 될 것입니다.
이제 우리는 그 어느 때보다도 감사한 마음으로
출판물에 담긴 풍부한 영적 양식을 조사할 것입니다.
지난 5개월은 무엇과도 바꿀 수 없는 귀중한 시간이었습니다!
이처럼 놀라운 영적 교육의 유익을 얻도록 마련하신
다른 사람을 도울 것을 여러분께 약속합니다.
여러분의 형제 자매들인 제144기 길르앗 학급.”
여러분을 사랑하며, 여호와께서 여러분을 크게 축복하시길 기도합니다.

en.text: We go back to Wednesday,
and the principal talk of the Gilead graduation
was delivered by Brother Knorr,
who spoke on the subject
“Work, Patience, and Faith.”
Don’t write that down because that’s not the theme
that we’re going to consider today.
But we have another member of the Governing Body, Brother Sam Herd,
and he’s going to speak on the intriguing theme
“Humbly Humble.”
If I should ask you, Are you humble students?
and you say yes, then you’re not humble.
But you look humble.
It’s been a good program up until now.
We’ll see what follows.
We all know that we must be humble
through and through.
This is something that Jehovah requires of all his servants
—not proud to be humble,
but humbly humble.
That’s what pleases God.
So that’s what we’re going to talk about.
But what do we mean by humble?
Well, it’s lowliness of mind.
Certainly, it’s not pompous
—filled to the gills with self-importance.
Jehovah says at Proverbs 8:13:
“I hate self-exaltation and pride.”
So we want to let that sink into our hearts.
Pride is something that Jehovah hates,
but he is pleased with those who are humble.
Now, you’ve increased your spiritual knowledge
while attending Gilead School,
but you have not scratched the surface
of what you will know in the future.
Your understanding of many things has been sharpened
in these few months that you’ve been here,
and now you are eager to tell others about what you’ve learned.
And there’s certainly nothing wrong with that;
we can say it’s good.
But here’s a caution:
Be careful;
be extremely careful
not to become a show-off,
standing head and shoulders above your brothers and sisters
in your branches or in your congregations.
Don’t toot your horn.
“Get someone else to blow your horn
and the sound will carry twice as far,”
said Will Rogers.
Better yet, consider what Jehovah inspired
to be written at Proverbs 27:2:
“Let someone else praise you,
“and not your own mouth;
others, and not your own lips.”
Now, while it may be true
that they may not know as much as you,
what they do know will carry them
through the end of this system of things
into the new world.
Jehovah loves them just as much as he loves you.
Now, I heard an experience years ago
about a Bible student who was just starting to study.
He knows a few things and loves the truth,
as much as he knows.
Then he comes down sick unto death,
and the doctor at the hospital says, “You must have a blood transfusion.”
But he knows enough, “No blood for me, no blood transfusion.”
His family is not in the truth, “Take that blood, Boy!”
“No. No blood for me.”
Others try to get him to take blood.
“No blood for me.”
And so the doctor operates and is successful;
everyone is happy.
Then his teacher
and others in the congregation
are invited to the hospital.
He has something to say.
What is it?
After they gather around his bed,
they’re thinking that something has gone wrong.
He’s going to have to take blood, and he’s willing to do it,
when he says, “Why is it that we don’t take blood?”
Now, he does not know
that the Gentile Times ended in 1914;
he doesn’t know the difference between sovereignty
and all the other things that people talk about today.
But he knows the truth
—just a little bit of the truth.
He’s not concerned with the vindication of God’s name
and his sovereignty —the rightfulness of God’s rule.
He doesn’t know that much,
but he knows enough that when his life is on the line,
he’d rather die than break God’s law,
even if he can’t explain that law.
Now, why say all that?
It’s not how much we know that pleases Jehovah,
but how we feel about what we know
and how we have allowed that knowledge
to increase our love for Jehovah.
Now, I’m going to invite you to open your Bibles, Bible students
—Gilead students.
Let’s turn to Romans.
We’re going to read the 12th chapter.
We’re going to read a couple of verses.
Where are they found?
Well, verse 3 starts us off.
It says: “For through the undeserved kindness given to me,
“I tell everyone there among you not to think more of himself
“than it is necessary to think,
“but to think so as to have a sound mind,
“each one as God has given to him
a measure of faith.”
There it is.
We can’t get too stuck on ourselves
and how much we know.
That’s not what Jehovah wants out of us.
Now look at verse 16:
“Have the same attitude toward others as toward yourselves;
“do not set your mind on lofty things,
“but be led along with the lowly things.
Do not become wise in your own eyes.”
That’s good counsel isn’t it, Gilead students?
Excellent counsel.
But, you know, sometimes we need a little more than a couple of verses
for it to reach the heart.
We need to know a few more things.
Knowledge has been given to us
in great abundance these few months
that we’ve been here at Gilead School,
and we’ve just loved it.
But at 1 Corinthians 8:1,
it tells us something that we want to think seriously about.
It says: “We know we all have knowledge.”
Now, here it’s coming:
“Knowledge puffs up, but love builds up.”
Now, you’ve got a lot of knowledge,
so be careful that it does not puff you up
so that you stand head and shoulders higher
than your brothers and sisters in the congregation.
Jehovah loves them just as much as he loves you,
who have this advanced knowledge now
because of your schooling.
Be as humble as a little child,
and Jesus tells us a little bit about that in Matthew chapter 18.
This is what he said in verses 3 and 4:
“Truly I say to you, unless you turn around
“and become as young children,
“you will by no means enter into the Kingdom of the heavens.
“Therefore, whoever will humble himself
“like this young child
“is the one who is the greatest
in the Kingdom of the heavens.”
So we say, humbly be humble.
Jehovah God, the Most High,
the Universal Sovereign, “the King of eternity,” is humble.
This is what King David said of him
in Psalm 18,
‘Your own humility will make me great.’
And it’s God’s humility that makes us great too.
If Jehovah were not humble, we would not be here.
Not one of mankind would be alive.
He’s humble, and He has a right to expect humility
out of each and every one of us.
And we need to help each other to be humble
—not glorify a human.
So we say this because sometimes some of our brothers and sisters
look at us —as members of the Governing Body—
as if we’re already angels,
and all you have to do is ask our wives if we’re angels.
You’ll get a true story.
We’re not.
We’re just sinners like all the rest of you.
So don’t elevate us
above where we are or what we are.
If we want to elevate anything, elevate Jehovah.
Now, that doesn’t mean that we feel
that you have wronged us in some way.
No, you haven’t.
You’re just human.
And as humans, we’re filled with sin
and we get carried away.
But help us to be humble, too,
rather than elevating us.
The Bible tells us of Jehovah:
“He stoops down to look on heaven and earth”
—Psalm 113:6.
What does that mean?
Well, he unbends;
he waives the privilege of rank.
Jehovah does that.
So he’s teaching us to waive the privilege of rank.
We’re all brothers; that’s all we are.
We don’t measure up as tall as Jesus, we just try to.
We try to dog his steps as best we can.
Follow the example of Jehovah.
He allowed Abraham to question His righteousness
in purposing to destroy the wicked cities of Sodom and Gomorrah.
In Genesis chapter 18,
Abraham says, ‘If there are 50 righteous men,
are you still going to destroy everything?’
He says, ‘No, I will not.’
Then Abraham comes back, ‘45?’
He says, ‘No, I will not destroy them.’
‘No, I will not.’
‘No.’
‘No.’
‘No.’
OK, Abraham, that’s enough; close your mouth.
Now, I added that.
Do you know what the Bible really says?
It says: “When Jehovah finished speaking to Abraham,
he went his way”
—still humble.
On a couple of occasions He allowed Moses to reason with Him
as if He was another human.
It took humility for Him to grant Moses’ pleas, but He did.
Now, what about Jesus? Was he humble?
Well, let’s take a look
at Philippians 2:5-8.
Can we do that?
Philippians 2:5-8.
Now, we understand that some of you
do not have your iPad or your Bible,
but that’s all right.
You’ll have time to get it later.
Now, here in the second chapter,
we’re able to read starting with verse 5.
It says: “Keep this mental attitude in you
“that was also in Christ Jesus,
“who, although he was existing in God’s form,
“gave no consideration to a seizure,
“namely, that he should be equal to God.
“No, but he emptied himself and took a slave’s form
“and became human.
“More than that, when he came as a man,
“he humbled himself and became obedient to the point of death,
yes, death on a torture stake.”
So, yes, Jesus was humble,
and Jesus washed the feet
—the dirty feet— of his apostles
to show them how to be humble.
That was a job that a servant should have done, or a slave’s job.
He lowered himself in front of them.
Perhaps he was on his knees when he washed their feet
—John 13.
Now, why would I say that?
Well, I saw a picture—
I saw a picture
in the office building in Warwick,
a beautiful picture.
Jesus is washing the feet of his apostles.
And where is he at?
He’s on his knees.
Now, the Bible doesn’t say he was on his—
I looked that up;
it didn’t say that in John the 13th chapter.
But, how are you going to wash feet if you don’t get down toward the feet?
So there he was —on his knees—
teaching them a lesson.
The apostle Paul set a fine example of humility.
He called himself ‘a slave of Jesus Christ’
—Philippians 1:1.
Now, if he had not been humble,
he would not have written these words that I’m about to read:
“For I know that in me, that is, in my flesh,
“there dwells nothing good;
“for I have the desire to do what is fine
“but not the ability to carry it out.
“For I do not do the good that I wish,
“but the bad that I do not wish
is what I practice”
—Romans 7.
And he was given a supernatural vision,
or visions, I should say, and revelations.
He was used mightily by Jehovah God.
At Acts 19:11-16,
we’re able to see that.
It says: “And God kept performing extraordinary powerful works
“through the hands of Paul,
“so that even cloths and aprons that had touched his body
“were carried to the sick,
“and the diseases left them,
“and the wicked spirits came out.
“But some of the Jews who traveled around casting out demons
“also tried to use the name of the Lord Jesus
“over those who had wicked spirits;
“they would say: ‘I solemnly charge you
“by Jesus whom Paul preaches.’
“Now there were seven sons
“of a Jewish chief priest named Sceva doing this.
“But in answer the wicked spirit said to them:
“‘I know Jesus and I am acquainted with Paul;
“but who are you?’
“At that the man with the wicked spirit leaped on them,
“overpowered them one after the other,
“and prevailed against them,
“so that they fled naked and wounded
out of that house.”
Evidently, they were not humbly humble
for Jesus to let them use his name to cast out the wicked spirits.
Paul was inspired to write 14 of the 27 books
of the Christian Greek Scriptures.
Now, he did not get bigheaded, but he stayed humble.
He’s not the only humble soul.
Here’s another one: Nathan H. Knorr,
the third president of the Watch Tower Bible and Tract Society,
wants to visit a member of the Writing Department
in the member’s office.
And he stated, that is, Brother Knorr stated,
this—the member’s office—
this is where “the most important
“as well as the most difficult work takes place.
That’s why I do so little of it.”
Isn’t that beautiful?
That’s a humble statement.
You know what I say behind it? I say “Amen” to it.
I’m on the Writing Committee of the Governing Body
for some unknown reason.
I can’t write,
not a lick,
but there I am.
The humility shown by Brother Knorr
made me think back in time
to when a group of traveling overseers
were attending school in Crownsville, Maryland.
Brother Ted Jaracz was one of the instructors,
and he got up early one morning
and prepared a hot breakfast for all of us.
He did that on his own.
I was one of the instructors,
but it didn’t cross my mind to do a thing like that.
Maybe I wasn’t humbly humble,
or if I was, I didn’t show it.
I can’t cook either,
not a lick.
What does it take to be exalted?
Let’s let the Bible answer at Luke 14:11:
“For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled,
and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.”
What does it take?
It takes humility.
Don’t learn that others are superior
the hard way.
Take a lesson from my old hound dog named Booser.
Sometimes he would follow us to town.
And one day, we passed a home
where usually there was a little dog that lived there,
but he had died.
And something caught Booser’s nose,
and so Booser was sniffing around, sniffing around.
And he went over near the house,
and a big Dalmatian came charging around the side of the house,
and he attacked Booser.
Booser put up a fight,
but he lost,
and the Dalmatian won.
Booser tucked his tail between his legs,
and he darted out of there like a streak of lightning.
Well, a couple of weeks later,
Booser wanted to go to town with us again—walking.
But we noticed that when we got to the Dalmatian’s house,
Booser was gone.
Booser took a long trip around the house
and met us downtown.
We’re about to wrap this up.
He was humbly humble.
He viewed the Dalmatian as superior.
Now, students, do you get the point of Booser’s example?
View others as superior.
They probably are.
That was a fantastic talk
—and I assure you, Sam is a very humble person.
He just can’t cook.
Well, we have a few announcements for you.
First of all, you’ll be interested in the attendance.
In Canada, there are 902.
And here in the United States, 9,702
for a total of 10,604.
Now, of course, we know that with the streaming many,
many more are going to be looking in on the program later.
So it’s going to be a lot more than 10,000.
Now, we’ve had some beautiful expressions
from the branches —greetings to our students.
We don’t have time to read all of them.
They will go in the archives of the Teaching Committee.
If I can’t read all of them,
I don’t want to read just one or two.
But here are the countries that are represented
that have sent beautiful expressions to us:
Angola, Argentina,
Belgium, Bolivia, Brazil,
Britain, Bulgaria, Burundi, Canada,
Finland, France, Georgia,
Ghana, Haiti, Hong Kong, Italy,
Japan, Kazakhstan, Korea,
Madagascar, Mozambique,
Netherlands, Nigeria,
Papua New Guinea, Portugal,
Sierra Leone, Thailand, and Ukraine.
And that’s just about the end of the alphabet.
So we appreciate all of these greetings
—beautiful expressions of appreciation
from the folks in these branches.
Well, we go back to 1943,
and following the principal talk, what happened?
Here’s what we read —here’s the report:
‘A large case containing the diplomas
‘was opened and put on the podium table.
‘One by one all the students were called
to come forward to receive their diplomas.’
Well, we’re going to follow that pattern right now;
that pattern established 75 years ago.
And I’m very happy to have Brother David Schafer with me.
If you were present for the introductions of the class,
you know what a beautiful job David did with all the names of the students.
And so, behold
the 144th class of Gilead.
And first, we have Brother and Sister Abou
who will be returning to the Middle East.
Brother and Sister Aloi will be serving in the Middle East.
Brother and Sister Arruda will be returning to Brazil.
Brother and Sister Bascopé will be returning to Bolivia.
Brother Buchan will be returning to Britain.
Brother and Sister Chilton will be serving in South Africa.
Sister Choatkaew will be returning to Thailand.
Brother and Sister de Rooij will be returning to the Netherlands.
Brother and Sister Esabunor will be returning to Nigeria.
Brother and Sister Guillén will be returning to Venezuela.
Brother Juhtver will be returning to Estonia.
Brother and Sister Kelly will be returning to Hong Kong.
Brother Lartey will be returning to Ghana.
Brother and Sister Menjou will be returning to Britain.
Brother and Sister Miçani will be returning to Albania.
Sister Nguyễn will be returning to Asia.
Sister Ningi will be returning to Papua New Guinea.
Brother Nkurunziza will be returning to Burundi.
Brother Ouédraogo will be returning to Benin.
Brother and Sister Pétursson will be returning to Denmark.
Brother and Sister Sandy will be returning to Sierra Leone.
Brother and Sister Santos will be returning to Portugal.
Brother Scarmato will be returning to Argentina.
Brother and Sister Stepanov will be returning to Azerbaijan.
Brother Tito will be returning to Mozambique.
Brother Tugushi will be returning to Georgia.
Brother Voyevodin will be returning to Asia.
Brother and Sister Wembalola will be serving in Madagascar.
And Sister Wójcik will be returning to Poland.
And here they are.
Let’s go back to 1943.
Once all the diplomas were handed out, what happened?
Well, the report tells us that a representative of the class
read a statement expressing the students’ appreciation
for the privilege of attending Gilead
and assuring the Governing Body of their loyalty
to Jehovah and his organization.
We’re going to follow the same pattern today,
and Brother Richard Chilton is going to read
a class letter on behalf of the class.
“To the Governing Body.
“Dear Brothers:
“Few things in life bring greater satisfaction
“than meaningful discussions on spiritual topics with dear friends.
“Over the last five months,
“we have enjoyed the blessing
“of being immersed in such discussions on a daily basis.
“As we studied the Bible book by book,
“the examples of faithful men and women of the past
“came to life and touched our hearts in new ways.
“Reliving the modern-day history of Jehovah's organization,
“we marveled at the faith,
“courage, and self-sacrifice
“of those who have gone before us.
“Our skills in the ministry were refined through workshops,
“and our desire to share in the preaching work intensified.
“As the weeks passed,
“fellow students became our close friends.
“Now, as the class has come to an end,
“tears come to our eyes as we think about parting ways,
“but we will treasure the memories
“of the stimulating ‘interchange of encouragement’
“with our new group of friends.
“And what a blessing to be guided by mature, devoted instructors
“who combined ‘spiritual matters with spiritual words.’
“We are grateful for their loving support as they nurtured our spiritual growth,
“and we will never forget their example of zeal for God’s Word.
“Getting to know the Bethel family has been a real delight
“—young people who expend themselves energetically
“in the service of the God they love
“and older ones who display the wisdom
“that comes with decades of experience
“in applying Christian principles.
“Their kindness, friendship,
“and hospitality have touched our hearts.
“Sometimes we think we know our friends well,
“but our appreciation for them is enhanced
“as we find out more about good deeds they have done in the past.
“This has been the case in our relationship with our God.
“Jehovah constantly surprises and delights us.
“As we reflect on all that he is
“and all that he has done,
“we feel moved to praise his beautiful name.
“While this school has far exceeded our expectations,
“it has also left us longing for more.
“We are resolved to continue our program
“of meaningful personal study.
“As Moses said at Deuteronomy 30:11:
“‘This commandment . . . is not . . . beyond your reach.
“It is not in the heavens, . . . nor . . . on the other side of the sea.’
“In any situation, we know we will always find
“an illuminating Scriptural principle,
“an encouraging thought, or an informative article
“to help us to do what is right.
“Our Gilead course may be over,
“but we are left with an even greater appreciation
“for the wealth of spiritual food in our publications
“which remains to be explored.
“We would not exchange the past five months for anything!
“We sincerely thank the Governing Body for arranging
“for us to benefit from this magnificent spiritual education,
“and we assure you that we will do all we can
“to use these treasures to build up others.
Your brothers and sisters, the 144th class of Gilead.”
Well, what more can we add?
All we can say is that we love you,
and we pray Jehovah’s rich blessing upon you,
and may this school of Gilead
continue to serve as a symbol
of the peace and unity of Jehovah’s organization.

cn.text: 让我们回到1943年的6月23日
是星期三
在那天基列学校毕业典礼上
诺尔弟兄发表了主旨演讲
讲题是“要怀着坚忍和信心服务”
这个主题你们现在不用记
因为我们今天不会讨论这个主题
现在  中央长老团成员赫德弟兄
将会发表一个鼓舞人心的演讲
讲题是“培养真正的谦卑”
如果我问你  你谦卑吗?
你回答说是
就说明你不够谦卑
不过  你们看起来挺谦卑的
之前的演讲都很精彩
这个演讲怎么样就不知道了
我们都知道
我们必须在一切事上表现谦卑
这也是耶和华对他所有仆人的要求
不要因谦卑而骄傲
要真正谦卑
耶和华喜欢这样的思想态度
这就是我们今天要讨论的话题
谦卑是什么意思呢?
就是要自觉卑微
也就是说  谦卑的人不会骄傲
不会把自己看得太重
在箴言8:13  耶和华说
“自高  骄傲……  我都憎恨”
因此  我们都要牢记这一点
耶和华憎恨骄傲的思想态度
却喜欢谦卑的人
来基列学校以后
你们的圣经知识比以前更丰富了
但我相信  将来你们还会学到更多
通过这几个月的学习
你们对圣经真理
有了更深入  更透彻的理解
你们也很渴望跟其他朋友
分享这些宝贵的知识
我想说  这没什么不对
这样做很好
我只是想提醒大家
要小心
千万千万要小心
不要因为在这里学到很多知识
就自觉高人一等
在分部或会众的弟兄姐妹面前炫耀
不要总想表现自己
美国著名演员威尔·罗杰斯说
“要让别人吹响你的号角”
“这样声音会传得更远”
不过
耶和华早就启示人说过这样的智慧之言
请看箴言27:2
“要让外人称赞你  不要用口自夸”
“等外邦人赞赏你  不要用嘴自诩”
也许  会众的弟兄姐妹
学到的圣经知识没有你的多
但他们已有的知识足够帮助他们
渡过最后的日子  进入新世界
是的  耶和华对他们的爱
和对你的爱一样多
我以前听过一个圣经学生的经历
他当时刚学习圣经不久
虽然他的圣经知识还不多
但他非常喜欢学到的真理
后来  他生了重病  快要死了
医生跟他说  你必须输血
但是他清楚地说  我不输血!
他的家人都不是见证人
都劝他  你得输血!
但他还是说  不!
别人怎么劝  他都说
不!  我不输血!
最后医生做了不输血手术
手术很成功
大家都很高兴
后来  他邀请圣经老师
和会众的朋友去医院看他
说自己有话要跟他们说
是什么事呢?
大家围在他的病床前
担心出了什么问题
是他需要输血了吗?
他改变主意了吗?
突然  他开口说
我们为什么不输血呢?
是的
他还不知道列国的既定时期
在1914年结束
也不知道我们所学的圣经知识
与上帝的至高统治权有什么关系
他知道一些圣经真理  但非常有限
对于洗雪上帝的圣名
证明上帝的至高统治权是否正当
他都不太清楚
但在生死关头
他清楚知道该怎么做
他宁愿死去
也不愿违背上帝的律法
虽然他还不能解释
为什么要遵守这些律法
为什么讲这些呢?
耶和华喜欢的
不是我们有多少圣经知识
而是我们怎么看待这些知识
如何运用这些知识加深对耶和华的爱
现在  在座的圣经学生们
我是说基列学员们
请翻开圣经到罗马书
我们会看第12章的內容
会读出几节经文
从哪里开始呢?
从第3节开始
这里说
“我凭着所得的分外恩典吩咐你们”
“不要自视过高”
“既然上帝让各人有不同程度的信心”
“各人就要照着自己所得的信心”
“来衡量自己”
“务求思想健全”
这就是要点
不要太关注自己
以及自己有多少圣经知识
耶和华不希望我们成为这样的人
接着看第16节
“你要关心别人  像关心自己一样”
“不要心高气傲  倒要甘于卑微”
“不要自以为聪明”
多好的劝告啊!
基列学员们  要记住这个劝告
不过  有时候
只看几节经文还不足以打动內心
我们需要进一步讨论一下
在基列学校的这几个月
大家都学到了非常丰富的知识
你们一定特别高兴
然而  哥林多前书8:1提醒我们要小心
经文说“我们知道我们都有知识”
重点来了
“可是知识叫人自高自大”
“只有爱心才能强化人”
现在  你们有了非常丰富的知识
要小心  不要因此变得自高自大
在会众的弟兄姐妹面前炫耀自己
耶和华很爱你们
但他也同样深爱其他弟兄姐妹
要记得你们有这些知识
是因为接受了耶和华的教育
要像小孩一样谦卑
这是耶稣在马太福音18:3,4
教导我们的话
经文说
“我实在告诉你们”
“你们要是不回头变得像小孩一样”
“就绝不能进天上的王国”
“所以  谁像这个小孩一样谦卑自抑”
“谁在天上的王国里就是最大的”
所以说  要培养真正的谦卑
耶和华上帝是宇宙至高的主宰
是“永恒的王”
但是他非常谦卑
大卫在诗篇18:35说
“你的谦卑使我昌大”
是的  上帝的谦卑也使我们昌大
如果耶和华不谦卑
我们就不会在这里
也没有人可以活着
他是谦卑的上帝
他也期望我们每个人都表现谦卑
我们也要帮助彼此成为谦卑的人
不要把别人抬得太高
我这么说
是因为有的弟兄姐妹以为
我们中央长老团成员都是天使
去问问我们的妻子
就知道我们是不是天使了
她们会告诉你真相
我们不是天使
我们跟大家一样  也是不完美的人
不要因我们的身份或岗位就抬高我们
这一切荣耀都该归给耶和华
但我这样说
并不是觉得你们冒犯了我们
我没有这个意思
作为不完美的人
我们都有可能不加思考就说一些话
但请帮助我们也保持谦卑
请不要抬高我们
诗篇113:6描述
“上帝纡尊降贵  俯察天地”
从中看出什么呢?
耶和华没有对我们要求过高
虽然他拥有全宇宙最高的地位
却没有摆架子
我们学到  不管在什么岗位
都要表现谦卑
平等待人
我们都是亲如手足的弟兄姐妹
我们都做不到耶稣那么完美
但我们都会努力
会努力跟上他的步伐
要向耶和华学习
耶和华决定
要毁灭邪恶的所多玛和蛾摩拉时
他容许亚伯拉罕质疑他是否公正
在创世记18章
亚伯拉罕说
假如城里有五十个义人
你会毁灭那座城吗?
耶和华说  不会
亚伯拉罕又问  45个呢?  不会
40个呢?  不会
30个呢?  不会
20个呢?  不会
10个呢?  不会
够了  亚伯拉罕  闭上你的嘴吧!
最后一句是我加的
圣经说
“耶和华跟亚伯拉罕说完就走了”
多么谦卑!
摩西也跟耶和华理论过一些问题
要答应摩西提出的请求
上帝必须表现谦卑
他就是这样做的
耶稣又怎么样呢?  他谦卑吗?
请大家打开腓立比书2:5-8
看看经文怎么说
腓立比书2:5-8
我知道  在座的有些人
可能没带平板电脑或圣经
不过没关系
你们可以回去再看
我们打开第2章
从第5节开始读
第五节经文说
“基督耶稣怀有怎样的精神”
“你们也要怀有怎样的精神”
“他原先以上帝的形态存在”
“却从没有想过要攫取”
“跟上帝同等的地位”
“反而彻底舍了自己”
“取了奴隶的形态  成了人的模样”
“不但这样  他见自己成了人的样式”
“就谦卑自抑  服从至死”
“甚至死在苦刑柱上”
是的  耶稣是谦卑的典范
为了让使徒们明白什么是谦卑
耶稣就给他们洗脚
一定很脏
洗脚本来是仆人或是奴隶的工作
但耶稣却甘愿在他们面前放低身段
你可以看看约翰福音13章
耶稣也许是跪着给门徒洗脚的
为什么这样说呢?
我看过一幅画
这幅画是在沃威克的办公楼里看到的
非常漂亮的一幅画
那幅画里  耶稣正在给门徒洗脚
他是什么姿势呢?  他是跪着的
圣经没说耶稣是跪着的
我查了
约翰福音第13章没有这样说
但是  想象一下
如果你不跪下来  怎么给别人洗脚?
所以  耶稣应该是跪着的
他给门徒上了生动的一课
使徒保罗也是谦卑的好榜样
他在腓立比书1:1称自己是
“基督耶稣的奴隶”
如果保罗没有表现谦卑
他就不会受圣灵启示
写下罗马书第7章里的这些话了
他说  “我知道在我里面”
“就是在我的肉体中  没有半点良善”
“因为我有行善的愿望”
“却没有行善的能力”
“我愿意行的善  我不去行”
“我不愿意作的恶  我反而常作”
保罗有机会看到异象  不只一个异象
也得到过启示
他也受耶和华上帝重用
请打开使徒行传19:11-16
经文说
“上帝通过保罗的手”
“不断显出非凡的大能”
“甚至有人把保罗身上的手巾围裙”
“放在病人身上  病就好了”
“恶灵也出来了”
“有些周游各地驱逐邪灵的犹太人”
“也向有恶灵附身的人”
“提起主耶稣的名来”
“说  我凭着保罗所传的耶稣”
“命令你们出来”
“这样做的”
“有犹太祭司长士基瓦的七个儿子”
“可是恶灵回答他们说”
“我认识耶稣  也熟悉保罗”
“但你们是谁呢?”
“恶灵附身的人就扑到他们身上”
“逐一制伏他们  胜过他们”
“他们赤着身子”
“负伤从房子里逃出来”
显然  他们不够谦卑
所以耶稣没有允许他们
奉自己的名驱逐邪灵
另外  圣经的《希腊语经卷》
共有27卷
其中有14卷
是保罗在上帝启示下写下来的
但是  他没有因此变得自高自大
反而一直保持谦卑
我们还有其他谦卑的好榜样
比如说  內森·诺尔弟兄
他是守望台圣经书社的第三任社长
有一次
诺尔弟兄探访写作部的一位成员
他说
这是诺尔弟兄说的
社方最重要和最艰巨的工作
就在这里进行
由于这缘故  我有自知之明而很少写作

ko.text: 상당히 인기가 있는 동영상 프로가 하나 있는데요,
강사 한 분이 진행을 하시고 학급 학생들이 함께 나오는 프로입니다.
오늘 이 프로를 보여 드리게 되어 기쁩니다.
사회자로 수고해 주실 분은 강사 중 한 분인 트렌트 리폴드 형제입니다.
학생들도 카메라에 자신의 모습이 어떻게 나오는지 보게 되실 겁니다.
75년간 졸업생들은 땅끝까지 가서 여호와의 조직을 강화하고 안정시켜 왔습니다.
길르앗 졸업생들이 가서 일한 곳의 이야기가 많습니다.
오늘은 길르앗 제144기 학급 학생들의 경험에 대해 듣고 볼 특별한 기회를 갖게 되었습니다.
첫 번째 손님은 볼리비아에서 오신 알레한드로 바스코페 형제입니다.
형제는 아내와 함께 볼리비아 지부에서 봉사하시죠.
볼리비아의 전파 활동을 조직하는 일을 도왔습니다.
네, 그럼 베델에 오시기 전엔 뭘 하셨나요?
그 전에는 아내와 함께 몇 년간 순회 활동을 했고,
그곳 전파 활동이 어떻게 진행되고 있는지 잘 아실 텐데요.
볼리비아의 최근 활동을 좀 말씀해 주시겠어요?
지금 사회하고 있는 성서 연구가 4만 3000건이 넘기 때문이죠.
진리가 볼리비아 모든 곳에 전파된 것 같군요.
실제로 모든 곳은 아니지만, 확장되고 있죠.
대부분은 도시에 살지만, 3만 5000명가량은 외딴곳에 살고 있죠.
북부의 3대 하천인 마드레데디오스강, 베니강, 마모레강을 따라 점점이 흩어져 있습니다.
작년에 이런 차량으로 300대가 넘는 그룹이 이 활동에 참여했습니다.

우리가 어떻게 여호와를 섬기면서 사람들의 영적인 필요를 돌보는지 보여 줍니다.
다른 베델 봉사자들도 왕국 권익을 위해 계속 수고합니다.
이 형제는 에드워드인데, 베델 사무실에서 열심히 일합니다.
내전 중에 지부로 피신한 많은 사람 중 하나였죠.
여호와께서 어떻게 보호하고 먹이셨는지 잊지 말라고 말했습니다.
그래서 시에라리온의 형제 자매들과 함께 기쁨으로 여호와를 섬기고 있습니다.
여호와께서 시에라리온 형제 자매들을 정말 축복하셨네요.
체험을 통해 어떤 교훈을 얻으셨는지 좀 알려 주시겠어요?
저는 형제들이 제가 싫어하는 방으로 들어가라고 했을 때
사실 나중에 보니, 제가 정말로 원했던 그 방은
지부 시설 중에서 가장 심하게 파손됐더군요.
그들이 문을 부수고 안으로 들어가서, 에어컨도 망가뜨렸고,
그 방에 있던 건 모두 다 부수어 놨더라고요.
그 싫어하던 방이 이젠 제일 좋아하는 방이 됐다면서요?
우리가 숨었던 그 자리엔 빵 선반이 놓여 있죠.
임무가 아무리 힘들어 보이고 상황이 아무리 위험해 보이더라도,
여호와께서 곁에 계시고 국제적인 형제 관계가 있단 걸 배웠습니다.
형제들이 해 주는 기도가 도움이 되죠.
그와 같은 임명을 또 받게 된다 해도 우리는 기꺼이 받아들일 겁니다.
여호와께서 곁에 계시고, 또 형제들이 기도해 줄 테니까요.
감동적인 경험을 말씀해 주신 두 분께 감사드립니다.
길르앗 제144기 학생들에 대해 좀 더 알 수 있어서 기뻤습니다.
우리는 형제 자매들이 어떻게 믿음과 용기를 나타내고
여호와를 섬기면서 인내하는지 보고 듣기를 늘 고대합니다.
오늘 함께해 주신 모든 분께 감사드리며, 다음 인사이드 스토리에서 다시 뵙겠습니다.

en.text: In recent times,
a very popular segment on the Gilead graduations
has been a video presentation
that features one of the instructors along with the students
called The Inside Story.
And we’re happy to present such a program today.
The instructor who is going to serve as the moderator of this discussion
is Brother Trent Lippold,
and the students are going to get a chance to see what they look like on camera.
Enjoy the program.
February 1, 2018, marked an anniversary
for the Watchtower Bible School of Gilead.
Over the past 75 years,
Gilead graduates have been going out to the ends of the earth
to strengthen and stabilize Jehovah’s organization.
And we just love reading yearbook experiences,
and many of them are from those places that Gilead graduates have gone to.
Well, today, we have the special opportunity
to see and to hear some of the experiences
of the 144th class of Gilead.
So it’s my pleasure to welcome you to this edition of The Inside Story.
Well, we’d like to introduce, right away, our first guest,
and it’s Brother Alejandro Bascope from Bolivia.
Welcome, Alejandro.
It’s great to have you with us today.
You and your wife, Ivon, serve together at the Bolivia branch.
Can you tell us a little bit about what you do there?
For the last 11 years, I have been working in the Service Department
helping to organize the preaching efforts in the country.
Very nice.
And before you came to Bethel, what were you doing?
Before Bethel, my wife and I spent some years in the circuit work,
and before that, we were special pioneers.
Very nice.
So being at the branch, in the Service Department in Bolivia,
must give you a nice opportunity to see the work that’s going on in Bolivia.
Would you mind giving us a little update of how the work is going in Bolivia?
Of course.
Currently, we have more than 27,000 publishers in Bolivia.
And last year, we had an increase of 4 percent.
And we can see a great potential for the future
because we are conducting more than 43,000 Bible studies.
Wow, that is amazing!
It sounds like the truth is reaching everywhere in Bolivia.
Well, actually, not everywhere, but we are improving.
So, what do you mean by that, not exactly everywhere?
Bolivia has about 11 million people.
And while most live in urban areas,
there are about 35,000 living in isolated spots
along three main rivers in the north
—Madre de Dios River, Beni River, and Mamoré River.
So, what are you doing to reach those people?
Well, in 2015, brothers started to organize
the “four by four” preaching campaigns.
“Four by four” —that’s interesting.
Here we preach two by two.
So is that . . .
Yes, “four by four” refers to our vehicles.
Of course!
Last year, we had more than 300 vehicle groups
participating in this campaign.
We were able to reach many villages,
but not all of them
because some had no road access at all.
Wow, that isolated.
So how do you reach these places then that have no road access?
Well, we began renting boats.
We were able to reach many villages for the first time.
We started many Bible studies.
And after that, we reported the success
to the Service Committee of the Governing Body.
Wow, that sounds—
I mean, it sounds like you solved the problem.
Yes and no.
We realized that in order to continue preaching there,
we needed just a small thing
—our own boat.
Your own boat—
What was wrong with the rented boats?
Was there a problem?
Well, not a problem, but many problems.
Here’s an example of the boats we used to rent.
You can see they are wooden, old;
people and supplies are all crammed together.
And in order to be more effective,
we realized that we needed our own boat.
It would be a little bit safer too, I suspect.
Yes, you cannot be effective if you are squished.
So tell us, did you get your own boat?
Yeah, and we even gave it a name,
Messenger of the Kingdom, or, in Spanish,
Mensajero Del Reino.
Very nice.
So, what’s it like?
How does preaching with boats work?
Well, can I show you?
Sure!
Bolivia’s river witnessing started with wooden boats.
But Jehovah says that instead of the wood,
he would bring in better, stronger materials.
Messenger of the Kingdom is custom-made for river witnessing.
It’s small, so it can be taken to different towns
and launched closer to where we’ll preach.
The roof holds literature and supplies.
Over 200 pioneers applied to help.
They meet plenty of creatures on the river.
With some, you don’t want to get too close.
Jehovah’s beautiful creation is part of the journey.
But the brothers and sisters are looking for people,
ones “rightly disposed for everlasting life.”
They’ll often find interest in the morning,
make return visits in the afternoon,
and invite them to a meeting that same evening.
A trip lasts seven to ten days.
All the work and preparation
is worth the effort.
And before they know it, it’s back on the river
and on to the next village.
Alejandro, that looks very exciting.
Yes.
Of course, there are many potential dangers,
like animals, strong currents, rocks.
But it’s worth it.
For example, in the village of Barranquilla,
brothers met Alessandro the first time they came.
And the next time,
the whole village was waiting with Alessandro
—over 40 people.
All of them wanted to hear the good news,
and many Bible studies were started.
What a tremendous response!
I think, Alejandro,
that you’re going to have a lot more applicants
to go on these boat-preaching tours.
So, what would you say has been the effect
on the publishers who make the trips to preach?
Well, honestly, at first we were concerned
about sending pioneers to the jungle.
But they actually thanked us
because they said it was very encouraging
to share the truth with many interested people.
They said it was a spiritual gift for them.
For me and other brothers at the branch,
it was very faith-strengthening to see how Jehovah removes any obstacles
in order for the people to hear the good news.
Very nice.
And it’s faith-strengthening to us to be able to see those experiences.
I can see why those pioneers thanked you for that opportunity.
You have the nice privilege of organizing this work
by working in the Service Department.
But let me ask you, Alejandro, how many trips have you been on?
None yet.
My wife, Ivon, says that I need to become a good swimmer first.
Your wife, Ivon, is a smart woman.
Thank you very much, Alejandro, for sharing your experiences with us.
So we’d like to invite out our next guest,
and it’s Brother Arlindo Tito from Mozambique.
Welcome, Arlindo.
Arlindo, you are coming from Mozambique.
Would you mind sharing a little bit of your background with us?
Sure,
I inherited the truth from my parents and my grandparents.
And for the last seven years,
I have been working at the branch in Mozambique
—for some time, in the Audio/Video Department,
but for most of the time in the Accounting Department.
That’s a beautiful spiritual heritage that you have
—and now Gilead School.
But I understand that one of your assignments at Bethel
was connected with part of the rich spiritual history of Mozambique.
Yes, I had this privilege.
But I could say that it all started with singing.
Singing?
How was that? Could you explain that?
Well,
there was a time when singing was like a spiritual anchor
for the brothers in Mozambique.
Before 1991, we were under ban in Mozambique.
So because the brothers didn’t want to get involved in politics,
they were sent to a concentration camp.
It was a reeducation camp
—the government was trying to change their minds.
So the life there could be very difficult,
but the brothers would find a way to worship Jehovah.
They would meet secretly.
This is an example of a meeting that was held there
in the middle of the forest at that time.
It must have been very anxious for them
—anxious moments having to meet together in secret like that.
Yes, and it was at that time when singing
became like a spiritual anchor for them.
Right at the beginning, they were singing to stay courageous.
In fact, the authorities were surprised
because the brothers, instead of crying, they were singing.
And at that time, there were older brothers
who would teach other brothers to read the musical notes,
and they would memorize the songs.
And when they had no Bibles or songbooks
and they were together, they would just sing.
Wow, that is absolutely beautiful —the power of Kingdom songs.
Very nice.
So we know that after the ban in 1991,
the brothers were now free to worship.
So did singing continue to be an important part of their worship?
Well, that’s what we wanted.
It sounds like there’s a story.
Would you mind explaining that?
After the ban,
we had many new ones coming into the truth.
But in many rural areas in Mozambique,
we have no electricity, no sound system,
no recording of the songs.
So at that time, it became a real challenge
for the brothers to sing at the meetings.
What about the older ones, the ones who sang in the camps,
couldn’t they help the new ones?
Yes, but many of them had moved away,
especially to the cities.
So in rural areas, there was a great need.
OK, but what about songbooks? Surely you had songbooks.
Yes, we had them.
But most could not read the musical notes.
So they would sing, yes,
but the melody would sound a little bit different from what we know.
Yeah, so now we had freedom; they could worship Jehovah.
But because of not having a sound system,
they couldn’t fully enjoy the meetings
because they couldn’t hear clearly what was being taught at the meetings.
That must have been very discouraging in a sense.
Well, did they get the help they needed?
Yes, they did.
And this is the beauty of this organization.
Jehovah really takes care of everyone in his organization.
In 2011, the Global Purchasing Department
found a player that would really fit our needs.
What do they call the player?
We call it the unity player.
It comes from the idea of singing in unity
with our worldwide brotherhood.
OK. Unity player —what does it look like?
It’s not big. I have one here.
Can I show you?
Absolutely.
Here it is.
I was wondering what that was.
I thought it was your lunch.
Probably, my lunch would be bigger than this.
But as you can see,
it’s very easy to carry, very easy to operate,
and it’s very practical.
It can be plugged in if they have power,
but if they don’t have power, it comes with a small solar panel,
so it can be charged by the sun.
You charge it with the sun.
Yes.
OK.
Yeah, and we have plenty of sun, so that’s not a problem.
But even if the sun fails, it comes with this hand crank,
so it can be charged manually.
Charge it by hand.
Yeah, exactly.
OK. Very nice.
That’s very useful for us there in Mozambique.
And it has a little place here
where we can insert a micro SD card with all the songs.
So now it’s just play and sing.
Very nice. But it looks like that’s not all.
Yes, it comes with this microphone.
So after singing, this unity player can be used as the sound system;
so they can hear clearly what is being taught at the meeting.
It sounds like it does a lot more than your lunch would.
Exactly.
You know, I think it would be so neat to just be able to see a congregation
when they get a unity player for the first time.
Well, actually, you can see that.
Just take a look.
OK.
This is the Nhantshembene Congregation in the south part of Mozambique.
Psalm 33 tells us to “sing praises” to Jehovah,
“along with shouts of joy.”
But with no sound system, if they shout joyfully
or sing fully from the heart like they want to,
they will not hear the music.
Listening to the spiritual food can also be difficult.
To help, the brothers send a request for a unity player to the branch.
The Broadcasting Department tests the new player.
SD cards are loaded with all of the audio and video material
available to them in Changana.
Everything they need is packed inside
and is soon on its way to the congregation.
Setup is easy, and they quickly learn
how to use the solar panel to charge the unit.
This meeting will be different.
Now they are able to sing to Jehovah
the way their hearts move them.
The Nhantshembene Congregation greatly appreciates this blessing
and sends their love.
It’s beautiful to see the joy on their faces when they get a unity player
and they’re able to sing again.
So it will be interesting to see what new technology is available
that will be able to help Jehovah’s people even in the remotest parts of the earth
to benefit in their true worship.
Thank you so much, Arlindo, for being with us today.
Many of us have a favorite Kingdom song or original song,
often because it evokes in us a certain emotion.
Well, we’d like to invite some of the students to the stage now.
And they’ve specially arranged and are prepared to perform for us
one of our Kingdom songs.
Let’s listen to them.
How can we endure
When trials come, as Jesus said?
Through his pain he saw
The joy of better things ahead.
God’s promise, God’s justice,
Were thoughts on which he fed.
We need to have endurance.
Our faith we must defend.
His love is our assurance.
So we will keep enduring to the end.
Though the passing years
May bring us sorrow, bring us pain;
There beyond the tears,
We see the life that we can gain.
To be there, feel free there,
Determined we remain.
We need to have endurance.
Our faith we must defend.
His love is our assurance.
So we will keep enduring to the end.
We will not give up
Nor see the need for doubt or fear.
Faithfully we’ll serve
Until Jehovah’s day is here.
Let’s keep on enduring.
That time is very near.
We need to have endurance.
Our faith we must defend.
His love is our assurance.
So we will keep enduring to the end.
What a touching song!
And it very nicely introduces our next couple and their amazing story.
Let’s welcome Brother Laddie and Cecelia Sandy.
Brother and Sister Sandy, you are coming from Sierra Leone.
And I understand that in 1997,
you participated in the construction of the branch
and soon thereafter began serving there.
Is that correct?
Yes, very correct.
We are happily serving at the branch.
But I understand that things didn’t remain that way, did they?
No, things changed really quickly
because our country was divided into civil war,
and then just a month after the branch dedication,
the rebels attacked Freetown.
So, Laddie, what happened?
The foreign missionaries were evacuated
to a safer place in neighboring Guinea,
and the expatriate Bethelites also left the country.
So who was left at the branch then, Laddie?
Just seven of us
—Cecelia, three single brothers, a couple, and myself.
OK, so did just the seven of you then stay in the branch?
No.
As things started getting worse,
the brothers kept coming to the branch to seek refuge.
There were so many that we couldn’t keep them all at the branch.
We started distributing them
to the different missionary homes in Freetown.
So how many were you then at the branch?
We were about 70 to 80 brothers and sisters at the branch.
Wow! That’s amazing.
So, Cecelia, how did you care for all those brothers and sisters?
Well, we shared the food that we had,
and the Bethel family kept eating less and less
so our dear brothers had what they needed.
OK. Well, they look happy in that photograph.
Although, Laddie, the picture doesn’t look so good.
That’s true. It survived the war.
That’s why it has some scratches on it.
OK, right, I understand.
So when you were there, Cecelia, were you able to go out at all?
Yes, we did.
We did our best to go out in the ministry.
But before going out in the morning, we had to listen to the news
—the government’s radio and bush radio.
Ah, OK, government radio I understand but bush radio?
I’m not sure I understand what that is.
Oh, it’s the news that you get by word of mouth.
So the brothers would give their news,
passersby would give their news,
and then you decided where it was safe to go on that day.
OK, I get it. Bush radio—interesting.
Did you ever feel in danger?
Were you in danger at the branch?
Yes.
One night, a brother and myself were in the lobby
and two armed rebels appeared
demanding that we open the door to them
to get access into the branch.
We were so frightened; we ran to safety.
And they started shooting at the door —the locks on the door.
But the door remained firm,
and they didn’t think of shooting into the glass,
because the door had two glass panes
and that would help them to get easy access into the building itself.
That was a very close call.
Yes.
So was that the end of it?
No, they came again.
They jumped the fence, as you can see in the picture.
And this time, about 20 or more well-armed rebels
shot their way into the branch.
They started looting everything in the branch
that they could lay hands on.
It was a big mess.
And that must have been absolutely terrifying.
It was.
What happened is that the brothers before that time
prepared a safe room for us to hide in,
in case of any emergency.
But that room was never my favorite.
I didn’t want to go into that room.
Did you have another room that you thought you might like to go to?
I did. I had my room that I preferred.
It had food inside.
It had AC inside —very nice and clean.
It was very comfortable for me.
Cecelia, did you tell Laddie about that?
No, I didn’t tell him.
I didn’t mention it to anybody.
I just told Jehovah what I wanted to do,
and I kept telling Him that I hoped the brothers would change their decision.
But why didn’t you tell Laddie?
I really didn’t want to influence him about how I felt and what I wanted,
because it was not about us;
it was not about me;
it was about Jehovah and his people.
That’s very nice.
Laddie was responsible for many there,
and you didn’t want to put that pressure on him.
Very interesting. Thank you.
So, Laddie, what happened now?
You’re down in the room.
What happened next?
We were in that safe room trying very hard to stay out of sight,
and one of the rebels came to the door where we were hiding
trying to gain access into the room.
While he was pushing on it, forcing his way,
I heard one of the other armed men yelling at him:
“Come from that place! You seem to be too greedy.
We have more than enough. Come, let’s go!”
And they just left like that.
You came out then?
No, we were still there until the following morning.
It must have been terrifying there in that room.
So was that the end then of troubles?
No, that was not the end.
The rebels also launched another operation
known as Operation No Living Thing.
Hang on, Operation No Living Thing.
What would that mean, Laddie?
Well, this was an operation that they decided
to just kill anybody
that came their way, any living thing
—dogs, animals, humans.
They just sprayed it like that.
That was the operation that was launched.
Wow!
You said there were other refugees in the missionary homes.
How were they faring at this time?
They were not doing fine.
They were suffering just like us.
But we had some money with us at the branch.
So I decided to take some money for them
because if they have money, they can get food to survive.
Although it was expensive
and also very dangerous to take such a journey,
Cecelia decided to go with me.
Cecelia, why did you decide to go with Laddie?
I decided to go because I thought
if Laddie was willing to die for his brothers,
if that’s what it meant for him to help them,
then I might as well die with him.
I didn’t want to live and have to explain what happened.
Can you tell us, Laddie, what happened?
Were you able to reach the missionary home?
Yes. We put the money into a bag,
and because there were a series of roadblocks
—checkpoints— that we had to go through,
we decided to put some dirty clothes
and stinky rags on top of the money.
That would prevent them from going deep down
to get access to the money.
And by having access to the money,
they would either kill us or take the money.
So we made it through several of these checkpoints.
As we were approaching the missionary home,
at the last checkpoint there,
we saw a group of boys,
men, and women jubilating
—just jumping up and down in the streets.
You mean celebrating. They were celebrating.
What were they celebrating?
Well, they were chanting:
“We’ve dropped the enemy jets. We’ve dropped the enemy jets.
We’ve done it again. We’re happy.”
What did you do then to get through the checkpoint?
So we started to jump up and down with them as a strategy
just to get our way through to the missionary home.
Ah, so it’s the theocratic strategy.
Yes.
That’s a little bit like David when he went to the city of Gath
and disguised his sanity.
OK.
I wonder, though, how did you think of that?
Well, it just came spontaneously
that Jehovah directed us to do that
because this was not our plan.
And we were not expecting anything like that to happen.
Sure.
Well, Jehovah helps in every situation, excellent.
So you got through the checkpoint now.
So, what happened? You made it to the missionary home?
Yes.
As we were very close to the missionary home,
we threw the bag into the compound
—the missionary home.
The brothers came and took the bag
while we gained access safely into the missionary home
and delivered the money.
And we tried to go back to the branch.
And you were able to make it back to the branch?
Yes.
Safely?
Yes.
That is an absolutely incredible story, Laddie and Cecelia.
Thank you so much for sharing it with us.
Well, we know that in 2002, the civil war ended.
And how has Jehovah blessed the brothers and sisters in Sierra Leone
after enduring so much since that time?
We have a video that we would like to show.
Do you want to see it?
I thought you might have one. I’d love to see it.
OK, let’s watch.
Many believe that some 200 years ago,
freed American slaves founded Freetown under this cotton tree.
For nearly a hundred years,
Jehovah’s Witnesses have comforted people
with hope of a better freedom
—“the glorious freedom of the children of God.”
During the 11-year civil war,
700 people were baptized.
And since the war’s end in 2002,
the number of publishers has more than doubled.
Here at the branch, we welcome visitors
to see how we are serving Jehovah
and caring for people’s spiritual needs.
Where soldiers once ransacked,
literature is being shipped to 40 congregations.
Other Bethelites continue to work hard for Kingdom interests.
This is Edward,
a hardworking brother in the Bethel Office.
He was one of the many who found refuge at the branch.
Back then, someone told him to always remember
how Jehovah protected and fed him.
He did remember.
And he serves with joy, along with his brothers
and sisters in Sierra Leone.
Thank you so much for that.
Jehovah really has blessed the brothers and sisters in Sierra Leone.
Now, you two, through your experience, endured so much.
I wonder if you could share with us
some of the lessons that you learned from your experience.
Cecelia, what would you say?
For me, it’s obedience.
I forcefully—
I forced myself to obey when the brothers said
to go into that room that I didn’t like.
And I’m glad that I forced myself to obey
because as things turned out,
the room that I really, really preferred
was the worst damaged in the branch.
The food was all taken away.
They destroyed the door; they gained access inside;
they destroyed the air conditioner.
They destroyed everything beyond repair in that room.
Obedience saves our lives.
And we’re really happy too, Cecelia.
And I understand that that other room
now is your favorite room.
It is my favorite. That’s where the commissary is.
And the very spot where we were hiding,
that’s where they put the bread shelf.
When I collect my bread, I remember my story.
Laddie, what would you say?
What lesson did you learn?
No matter how challenging the assignments may seem
or how dangerous the situation may seem,
Jehovah is there —and the international brotherhood too.
Their prayers in our behalf help us.
And if any other assignment
like that comes our way,

현재 있는 왕국회관들, 특히 인구 밀집 지역에 있는 회관들이

그렇게 한 것은 외딴 지역에 있는 회중들에 큰 축복이 되었습니다.
스코틀랜드 북서쪽 해안에서 약 38킬로미터 떨어진 곳에는

어렸을 때는 이 섬을 별로 좋아하지 않았어요.
이 섬의 아름다운 자연 경관을 사랑하게 되었죠.
공기도 맑고, 해변도 예쁘고, 산도 멋있습니다.
섬 전체에 2만 명 정도가 살고 있죠.

왜 여호와의 조직에서 빨리 도와주지 않는지

회관에 처음 들어갈 때 얼마나 멋있을지 기대가 됐어요.
여호와의 이름에 걸맞은 숭배 장소가 생긴 거예요.
이곳의 형제 자매들은 멀리 떨어져 있지만
왕국회관 건축을 돕기 위해 멀리서 온 형제들을 보면

봉사에서 더 많은 일을 하고 싶어서 외국어를 배우기로 결정합니다.
그런데 언어를 배우는 데 너무 몰두한 나머지
모국어로 성경을 읽고 연구하는 일을 등한시하게 됩니다.
또는 도움이 필요한 곳에 가서 봉사하기로 결정을 합니다.
그러면서 그 나라의 문화나 음식 같이
그 나라에 관해 알아보는 데 너무 많은 시간을 쓰다 보니
조금씩 조금씩 가족 숭배나 개인 연구를 소홀히 하게 됩니다.
우리의 일은 아주 흥미롭고 그래서 열심히 일하죠.
하지만 일을 앞서 나가고 신속하게 처리하는 데 열중하게 되면서,
자신이 자처해서 정기적으로 오버타임을 하게 될 수 있습니다.
그러면 집회에 빠지거나 배우자와 보내는 시간이 줄어들 수 있죠.
지금 말한 상황은 모두, 가치 있는 신권 활동에서 시작되었습니다.
실제로 어떻게 우리의 정신이 나뉘게 될 수 있는지 볼 수 있지 않습니까?
예수께서 마르다에게 잘못하고 있다고 결코 말씀하지 않으셨다는 점에 유의하십시오.
예수께선 마르다가 그분을 위해 한 일에 고마워하셨죠.
하지만 그분은 음식을 준비하는 일 때문에 마르다의 주의가 나뉘고 있다고
즉 그분의 가르침을 듣는 영적인 활동을 놓치고 있었죠.
마르다는 믿음을 강하게 해 줄 특별한 기회를
이 기록에 대해 이런 설명을 합니다.
동료 신자들의 필요를 돌보기 위해 최선을 다하는 사람들이 있습니다.
그들은 실용적인 면에 주의를 기울여 신속하게 행동을 취[합니다.]
그런가 하면 마리아와 좀 더 비슷한 사람들도 있습니다.
그들이 믿음을 굳게 유지하는 데 도움이 됩니다.”
“그리스도인 회중 내에서는 이 두 부류의 사람들 모두가
영적인 것들을 가장 중요하게 여김으로 ‘좋은 몫을 택해야’ 합니다.”
균형이 필요하단 걸 알 수 있죠.
모든 성원이 순회 감독자 부부와 봉사만 같이 하려 한다면 어떨까요?
그건 균형 잡힌 게 아닐 겁니다.
반대로, 식사 초대하는 사람은 아주 많은데,
봉사하려는 사람이 없는 경우도 좋지 않을 겁니다.
따라서 요점은 자신과 다른 사람의 필요를 돌보되
그러므로 우리의 열심 때문에 주의가 나뉘지 않게 하는 비결은 무엇입니까?
“나는 여러분의 사랑이 정확한 지식과 온전한 분별력과 함께 더욱더 풍성하게 되고,
여러분이 더 중요한 것들을 확인하기를 계속 기도합니다.
흠이 없고 다른 사람들을 걸려 넘어지게 하지 않기를 바랍니다.”
우린 어떤 임명을 수행하거나 특정한 노력을 기울이기 전에
우리가 좋은 판단력을 갖고 통찰력을 사용한다면,
그걸 알게 되면 그에 따라 적절하게 생각하고 행동하고 결정할 수 있습니다.
더 중요한 것을 확인함으로 우리는 여호와의 축복과 호의를 얻을 수 있습니다.
외국어를 배우거나 필요한 구역으로 가는 것은
사실 상황만 되면 그렇게 하는 것이 좋습니다.
그리고 베델에서 임명을 열심히 수행하고, 업무를 잘 알고,
여호와께 모든 걸 드리고 싶지 않은 사람이 누가 있겠습니까?
하지만 예수께서는 우리에게 균형 잡힌 소중한 교훈을 베푸셨습니다.
가치 있는 신권 활동을 추구하는 가운데서도
우리의 영적 발전이 어떤 식으로든 방해를 받아서는 안 된다는 것입니다.
우린 믿음을 자라게 하고 형제들과의 관계를 튼튼히 하고,
가장 중요한 점으로 여호와와의 관계를 강하게 할 기회를 놓쳐서는 안 됩니다.
그럼, 예수께서 마르다에게 하신 말씀을 뭐라고 마치시는지 보실까요?
네, 마리아는 예수께서 해 주신 칭찬과 영적인 교훈을
우리도 그런 기억이 있을 수 있죠?
아마 우리도 잊을 수 없는 연설이나 집회, 대회 때 들었던 내용,
누군가와 나눈 영적인 대화가 기억날지 모릅니다.
그러한 내용이나 대화는 우리의 믿음과 여호와와의 관계에
아마 그런 경험은 아주 소중하고 특별한 기억으로 남아 있을 겁니다.
그리고 여호와와 누리는 관계를 강화하시기 바랍니다.
그렇게 할 때 여호와께선 우리의 노력을 분명 축복하실 것입니다.

en.text: Let’s consider the account that’s referred to
in our Watchtower comments.
If you turn with me in your Bibles
to the book of Luke,
we’ll read this in its entirety.
Follow with me, please,
at Luke 10:38-42.
It says: “Now as they went on their way,
“he entered into a certain village.
“Here a woman named Martha received him as a guest in her house.
“She also had a sister called Mary, who sat down at the feet of the Lord
“and kept listening to what he was saying.
“Martha, on the other hand,
“was distracted with attending to many duties.
“So she came to him and said:
“‘Lord, does it not matter to you
“‘that my sister has left me alone to attend to things?
“Tell her to come and help me.’
“In answer the Lord said to her:
“‘Martha, Martha,
“‘you are anxious and disturbed about many things.
“‘A few things, though, are needed, or just one.
“‘For her part, Mary chose the good portion,
and it will not be taken away from her.’”
Did you note in verse 40, it said that Martha
“was distracted with attending to many duties”?
It’s quite likely that Martha may not have felt that way.
After all, she was not engaged in some sort of hobby
or materialistic pursuit,
and her duties were certainly not trivial.
She was tending to the needs of Jesus.
Now, we think about that —taking care of the Messiah, the Son of God.
That had to be one of the greatest privileges
and one of the greatest honors an individual could have.
So it’s no wonder that in verse 40
she encourages Jesus to tell her sister, Mary,
to come and help her.
But this raises an interesting question:
Is it possible for Christians today
to become distracted
even while engaging in worthwhile theocratic pursuits?
Well, consider three examples.
We want to do more in the ministry,
so we decide to learn a new language.
We focus on learning the language, but in the process,
we neglect time to read and study the Bible in our mother tongue.
Or perhaps we decide we’re going to move and serve where the need is greater,
and we begin to occupy so much of our time in learning about the country
—its customs and the food—
that that begins to overshadow
our family worship and personal study.
Or how about our Bethel assignment?
We love our assignment.
Our work is very interesting.
We enjoy working hard.
But we become so absorbed in staying ahead in our work
and keeping things moving
that we begin to do self-imposed overtime work
on a regular basis,
neglecting our meeting attendance
and perhaps even time with our mate.
Did you notice that each situation
began as a worthwhile theocratic endeavor?
But can we see how it’s possible
that each hypothetical situation
could become a realistic distraction?
Now, let’s just go back for a moment to the account in Luke
because it’s important to note that Jesus never said
that what Martha was doing was wrong.
Like our text mentioned, he loved Martha.
She was a spiritual woman,
and he was very appreciative for what she was doing in his behalf.
But he very kindly reminds her and shows her
that her meal preparations were distracting her
to the point that it interfered with her receiving
what he refers to in verse 42 as “the good portion”
—a spiritual activity, listening to his teachings.
Martha was not taking advantage of a unique opportunity
to deepen her faith.
Very interestingly, the September 1, 1999, Watchtower
elaborates on this account, and it makes this comment.
It says: “Moved by love, some [today]
“—much like Martha— do their utmost to minister
“to the needs of fellow believers.
“They are practical-minded and quick to take action,
“and Jehovah promises to reward their labors of love.
“Others perhaps more closely resemble Mary.
“They are quiet and contemplative.
“Their eagerness to meditate upon God’s Word
helps them to stay solidly rooted in the faith.”
But then it says this:
“Both . . . fill a vital need in the Christian congregation.”
And by extension, we’ll just add in the Bethel family as well.
It continues: “In the end, however,
“all should ‘choose the good portion’
“by putting [spiritual or] primary emphasis
on spiritual things.”
Well, that helps us to see the balance, doesn’t it?
It makes me think, perhaps in a modern-day application,
what if the circuit overseer came to visit our congregation
and everyone wanted to go out and work with him in the ministry,
but no one was willing to stop and provide him with a meal?
That wouldn’t be good, would it, or hospitable?
Just like it wouldn’t be balanced for him to have multiple meal invitations,
and then no one showed up to support him and his wife in the ministry.
So the point is, we want to make sure
that we care for our needs and the needs of others
but also make sure that we remember our priorities.
So, what’s the key to ensuring
that our endeavors will not become distractions?
Well, notice how the Bible explains this.
Turn with me, please, to Philippians chapter 1.
At Philippians chapter 1, notice verses 9 and 10:
“And this is what I continue praying,
“that your love may abound still more and more
“with accurate knowledge and full discernment;
“that you may make sure of the more important things,
“so that you may be flawless and not stumbling others
up to the day of Christ.”
So before we undertake any endeavor, any assignment,
you notice we want to pray, reason things out,
use accurate knowledge, and discernment.
And if we’re able to use that insight —good judgment—
then it’s going to help us to discern, or perceive,
what is most important to God.
And when we know that, well, then, we can harmonize our thoughts,
our actions, and our decisions accordingly.
By making sure of the more important things,
we gain Jehovah’s blessing and favor.
So think about those situations we mentioned.
If we’re going to learn a new language
or move where the need is greater,
well, that’s amazing!
It’s appreciated, and it’s definitely needed.
In fact, we’re encouraged to do it if we have the circumstances.
And, of course, in our Bethel assignment, who of us does not want to work hard,
to get to know our work well, and give our all to Jehovah?
But we can appreciate
how Jesus shows us a valuable and balanced lesson
—that even in worthwhile theocratic pursuits,
we should not let anything distract
or impede our spiritual progress.
We don’t want to miss opportunities to strengthen our faith,
to bond with our brothers and sisters,
and, most importantly, to bond with Jehovah.
If we just go back to Luke,
notice how Jesus concluded his words to Martha.
In verse 42, he says
that because ‘Mary chose the good portion,
it will not be taken away from her.’
So, what she learned that day
—the commendation, the spiritual instruction from Jesus—
Mary would never forget that.
That would stay with her for the rest of her life.
And likely, we can recall a similar account
—maybe a talk, a meeting, something that was said at the convention,
a spiritual discussion that we had with someone—
and that conversation, or discussion,
had a profound impact on our faith and our relationship with Jehovah.
Well, if you’ve had situations like that,
you know that those are precious;
they’re very special.
And those are things that we want to hold on to.
So, what a beautiful reminder we had today.
And let’s not be distracted.
May we work to strengthen our spirituality
and relationship with Jehovah
by always choosing “the good portion,”
and if we do, we can be assured that Jehovah will bless our efforts.

cn.text: 我们会讨论一下
今天《守望台》评论的参考经文
请打开圣经到路加福音
我们会读出整段经文
请看一下路加福音10:38-42
经文说
“在路上  耶稣进了一个村庄”
“有一个女人  名叫马大”
“接耶稣到家里作客”
“她还有一个妹妹  名叫马利亚”
“坐在主的脚前  听他讲话”
“马大照顾的事多  分身不暇”
“就走过来说”
“主啊  我妹妹撇下我”
“让我一个人照顾一切”
“你觉得没关系吗?”
“请叫她来帮帮我吧”
“主回答说”
“马大  马大”
“你为太多事忧虑不安了”
“其实需要的不多”
“只要一样就够了”
“马利亚选了最好的一份”
“谁也不能从她那里夺去”
你留意到了吗?
40节说
“马大照顾的事多  分身不暇”
很可能
马大自己也没有意识到这一点
毕竟  她不是只顾着享乐
或是忙着赚钱
她忙的也不是一些琐事
而是照顾耶稣的需要
请想一想
她照顾的可是弥赛亚
上帝的儿子
这实在太光荣了  不是吗?
所以  在40节
她让耶稣叫妹妹马利亚过来帮助她
就不难理解了
这引出了一个很有意思的问题
就算我们忙于为上帝服务
有没有可能还会分心
结果忽略了更重要的事呢?
我们来想想以下三种情况
为了去外语地区扩大服务
我们可能会花很多时间和精力学习语言
结果没时间用母语研读圣经
或者
我们决定搬到需求更大的地区服务
就开始花很多时间
了解那个国家的情况
比如当地的习俗和饮食
结果没时间做家庭崇拜和个人研读
伯特利服务又怎么样呢?
我们很喜欢伯特利的工作
这里的工作很有意思
我们也喜欢努力工作
可是
如果我们一心只想着尽早完成工作
非要加班加点
而且常常这样做
结果就可能错过聚会
甚至冷落配偶
你留意到了吗?
刚才说的这几种情况
在现实生活中也可能会发生
虽然出发点是好的
都是为了多为耶和华服务
但也可能会令人分心
为什么会这样呢?
我们再看一下路加福音的记载
耶稣从没说过马大做得不对
知道这一点很重要
今天的经文也说
耶稣爱马大
马大是个属灵的女子
而耶稣也非常感激马大为他做的一切
不过  在42节
耶稣亲切地提醒马大
她为了准备食物
错过了“最好的一份”
也就是聆听耶稣的教导
马大没有好好利用这个宝贵的机会
强化自己的信心
有趣的是
《守望台》1999年9月1日刊的一篇文章
详细阐述了这个记载
文章写道
“今天有些人像马大一样”
“在爱心驱使下”
“尽力照料信徒同工的物质需要”
“他们有现实的眼光  敏于采取行动”
“耶和华应许”
“他们出于爱心的作为”
“必定会获得奖赏”
“另一些人或者较像马利亚”
“他们的性格沉静  做事深思熟虑”
“他们喜欢沉思上帝的话语”
“因此得以在信仰里扎根立稳”
文章接下来说
“两种不同的人”
“都对基督徒会众作出重大贡献”
这对伯特利家庭也适用
这篇文章继续说
“然而  归根究底来说”
“人人都应当把属灵的事看得最重要”
从这里可以看出
保持平衡很重要  对吗?
那我们怎么运用出来呢?
我想到一种情况
就是分区监督来探访会众的时候
如果每个人都想跟他一起去传道
却舍不得抽出时间请他吃饭
这样就不太好了  对吗?
也不是好客的表现
反过来  如果大家都热情地邀请他吃饭
却没有人跟他们夫妻一起传道
又怎么样呢?
所以  要点是
我们要照顾自己和其他弟兄姐妹的需要
但同时也不要忘记最重要的事
那么  我们付出努力
想为耶和华做更多服务时
怎么做才能避免分心呢?
关键是什么呢?
答案就在圣经里
请打开腓立比书1:9,10
腓立比书1:9,10
经文说
“我一直祷告求的”
“就是你们爱心多而又多”
“具有确切的知识”
“能完全明辨是非”
“又能看清哪些事更为重要”
“好叫你们清白无瑕”
“不使人失足”
“直到基督的日子”
所以
我们在追求属灵目标或是接受委派前
经文提醒我们
要先做祷告
推理  运用确切的知识和辨识力
如果我们明辨是非
运用良好的判断力
就能看出
对上帝来说  什么才是最重要的
这样  我们的思想  行动和决定
就能和耶和华的观点保持一致
我们要是看清哪些事更为重要
就会得到耶和华的赐福和悦纳
现在想一想我们刚才提到的三种情况
学习一门新的语言
或是搬到需求更大的地区服务
这都很好!
大家都很赏识这样的努力
而且确实有这个需求
其实  如果情况允许
组织也鼓励我们这样做
另外  在伯特利
我们当然都想努力工作
把工作做好
为耶和华做得更多
可是我们也要留意耶稣的劝告
学会保持平衡
就算我们在参与属灵服务
我们也要留意
不要让任何事妨碍我们
不断亲近耶和华
我们要把握机会强化信心
培养跟弟兄姐妹的友谊
更重要的是
要培养跟耶和华的亲密关系
我们再看看路加福音
请留意这个记载的最后部分
在42节  耶稣说
“马利亚选了最好的一份”
“谁也不能从她那里夺去”
对马利亚来说
那天的经历一定很宝贵
耶稣的教导和称赞
让她获益不浅
她一辈子都不会忘记
我们可能会想到类似的经历
也许是一个演讲  一次聚会
在大会里听到的一些內容
又或者是跟弟兄姐妹的一次交流
谈话的內容特别强化我们的信心
巩固了我们和耶和华的关系
这些经历真的很宝贵
特别有意义
我们很想把这些经历牢记在心
今天讨论的內容真的很及时!
提醒我们不要分心
愿我们总是选择“最好的一份”
不断强化自己的信心
巩固自己和耶和华的关系
这样  我们就可以确信
耶和华必赐福给我们

ko.text: 기억하시겠지만, 이제 JW 방송 월간 프로그램에서
6개월에 한 번 길르앗 학교 졸업식을 보여 드릴 것입니다.
제144기 길르앗 학교 졸업식의 첫 부분을 시청하실 것입니다.
성경에 근거한 흥미로운 주제의 연설들이 제공될 것인데요,
여러분 모두 이 연설들을 즐기시게 될 겁니다.
몇 주 후면 길르앗 학교 졸업식의 2부와 3부 내용도 보실 수 있습니다.
몇몇 학생들을 더 잘 알게 되실 텐데요,
인사이드 스토리에서 그들의 감동적인 이야기를 들어 보십시오.
그럼 이제, 제144기 길르앗 학교 졸업식의 1부를 함께 시청하도록 하시겠습니다.
네, 이 장면은 길르앗 학교 제1기 학급의 첫째 날에 찍은 사진입니다.
영문 신세계역 2013년 개정판에서는 이 표현이 좀 바뀌었는데요.
영어로는 두 가지 표현 사이에 차이가 있을 수 있습니다.
제가 자란 캐나다는 겨울이 되면 굉장히 추운데요,
많은 가정에서는 난방비를 아끼기 위해 겨울에 장작불을 땝니다.
가지런히 차곡차곡 쌓여 있는 장작더미를 볼 수 있죠.
특별히 꼼꼼하게 쌓아 놓는 사람들도 있습니다.
마치 예술 작품처럼, 거의 무슨 조각품처럼 보이기도 합니다.
아무렇게나 던져 놓은 모습을 연상시키는 단어를 사용할 수 없습니다.
그럼 우리가 이런 얘기를 하는 이유가 뭘까요?
그리고 여러분 졸업생들과는 어떠한 관련이 있을까요?
사실 여러분과 우리 모두와 관련이 있습니다.
우리 모두가 길르앗이라는 이 증거의 무더기에서 배울 점이 있습니다.
이 표현이 나온 곳인 창세기 31장을 보죠.
족장 야곱은 장인 라반에게 거듭해서 속임을 당하는 데 지쳤습니다.
성경을 보면 알 수 있듯이 라반은 꿍꿍이가 많은 사람이었죠.
라반한테 중고차를 사고 싶진 않으실 겁니다.
‘이 딸들은 내 딸들이고 이 아이들도 내 아이들이며
이 가축 떼도 내 가축 떼이니, 자네가 보고 있는 모든 것이 내 것이[네.]’”
“‘이제 우리가, 자네와 내가 계약을 맺도록 하세.
그것이 우리 사이에 증거가 될 것이네.’
그래서 야곱이 돌 하나를 가져다가 기둥으로 세웠다.
그런 다음 야곱이 형제들에게 ‘돌을 주워 모으시오!’ 하고 말했다.
이 “돌무더기”는 분명 상당히 가지런히 배열되어 있어서,
이 식탁에서 그들이 평화의 뜻으로 식사를 한 거죠.
라반과 야곱이 평화의 계약을 맺었다는 데 대한 기념이었죠.
이 학교의 이름을 정할 때, 라반을 따르지 않은 게 다행이죠?
그래서 갈르엣, 혹은 길르앗으로 한 겁니다.
‘이 돌무더기는 오늘 나와 자네 사이에 증거일세.’
그래서 그가 그것의 이름을 갈르엣이라고 했고,
성구에 나오는 길르앗과 “파수대” 즉 “워치타워”가 우리 학교 이름인 게 흥미롭죠?
“내가 자네를 해치려고 이 돌무더기를 넘어가지 않고
자네도 나를 해치려고 이 돌무더기와 이 기둥을 넘어오지 않겠다는 것에 대해,
라반이 야곱을 따라가서 처음 만났을 때 뭐라고 비난했는지 보셨나요?
자네가 보는 모든 것이 내 것이네.’
야곱은 열심히 일해서 그걸 다 갖게 되었습니다.
라반은 그의 삯을 열 번이나 바꾸었습니다.
따라서 라반이 다 자기 거라고 할 권리가 없었죠.
야곱은 따지고 대들 수도 있었지만 꾹 참았죠.
오늘날, 바로 그 길르앗은 우리 학교에 딱 어울리는 이름입니다.
실제로, 길르앗은 지금까지 하느님의 백성들을 연합시킨 엄청난 힘이었죠.
선교인들은 사람들이 여호와 하느님과 평화로운 관계를 맺도록 간청했죠.
그리고 그들은 세계 본부가 어떻게 일하는지 잘 알았기 때문에,
지부들이 설립되자 지부와 세계 본부가 연합해 일하도록 도왔습니다.
지부와 세계 본부 사이에 끊을 수 없는 유대를 형성하는 것입니다.
어떤 양도 다치게 해서는 안 됩니다.
평화를 이루기 위해 꾹 참아야 할 때도 있죠.
길르앗 학교 졸업생 여러분들과 우리 모두에게 말이죠.
우리 모두 왕국의 평화를 위해 일하고,
여호와의 조직의 평화를 위해 일하고 싶기 때문입니다.
다시 제1기 길르앗 학교로 돌아가 보죠.
첫 연사는 후에 중앙장로회가 된 위원회의 성원이었던
자, 오늘 제144기 학급의 졸업식에서도 첫 번째 연사가 중앙장로회 성원이신데요,
밴 엠버그 형제가 아니라 앤서니 모리스 형제입니다.
모리스 형제가 해 주실 연설의 제목은 “항상 간구하십시오!”입니다.
곧 졸업하실 여러분 모두 이미 잘 알고 계시겠지만,
성경에는 매우 다양한 형태의 기도가 나옵니다.
우선 청원의 기도로 필요한 것을 청하죠.
그리고 감사의 기도로 여호와께 감사를 표합니다.
또 여호와께서는 늘 찬양받으셔야 하기 때문에,
하지만 곧 졸업해서 임지로 떠날 여러분에게
여러분도 아시겠지만 여러분께 말씀드리고 싶은 건
그분이 남기신 정말 소중하고 완전한 본이 나옵니다.
이 말씀에서 유익을 얻을 수 있습니다.
땅에 계시는 동안 자신을 죽음에서 구하실 수 있는 분에게
강한 부르짖음과 눈물로 간구와 청원을 드리셨으며,
그의 경건한 두려움 때문에 하느님께서 그의 기도를
여기 간구에 해당하는 원어는 복수 형태이죠.
분명 예수께선 3년 반의 봉사 기간 내내 간구하셨습니다.
예수께선 간구가 정말 중요하단 걸 분명히 알려 주셨는데,
우리도 알고는 있지만 이런저런 일로 바빠서
그날이 올무처럼 닥치는 일이 없게 해야 합니다.
“그러므로 일어나게 되어 있는 이 모든 일을 피하고
‘사람의 아들’ 앞에 설 수 있도록 깨어 있고
차를 세우고 도로에서 간구해야 한다는 건 아닙니다.
예수의 말씀은 우리가 그분처럼 성공하고 싶다면
우리는 더욱 열심히 간구를 드리기 위해
끝은 올 수도 있는 게 아니라,
우리 자신이나 사랑하는 사람에게 시련이 닥칠 때 그렇죠.
온 마음을 쏟아내 간절히 기도하게 되죠.
겪고 있는 어려움 때문에 감정적으로 몰입하게 되니까요.
예를 들어, 여러분이 병에 걸려 생명이 위태롭다면
반드시 이 점에 대해서도 간구해야 한다는 걸 기억하세요.
아버지의 뜻이 하늘에서와 같이 땅에서도 이루어지게 하십시오.’”
이런 상황에 대한 여러분의 염려와 괴로움에 대해
또 그렇게 하면 자신의 문제에만 몰두하지 않게 되는데,
자기 문제에만 몰두하는 건 영적으로 해로울 수 있죠.
이 세상의 모든 문제가 사라질 것이기 때문입니다.
따라서 여러분이 꼭 기억해야 할 중요한 점은,
그분의 왕국이 오도록 간구해야 한다는 겁니다.
아주 익숙한 내용인 시편 83편을 살펴볼 텐데요.
그분의 이름이 입증되고 입증된다는 말도 틀린 게 아니죠
그렇다고 뉴스를 아예 안 볼 수도 없고요.
또 전 세계 우리 형제들에 대한 소식들도 있죠.
왕국이 이 모든 문제를 끝낼 겁니다.
시편 83편에서 특히 유의해 볼 만한 점이 있는데요.
여호와의 이름을 지닌 백성을 대적한 것인데,
여러분은 사실 큰 환난을 위해 준비하는 것입니다.
우리의 마음을 대변하는, 아버지께 간구하고 싶은 말입니다.
가장 높으신 분임을 사람들이 알게 하십시오.”
훌륭한 연설 정말 감사합니다, 모리스 형제.
제1기 길르앗 학교 졸업식에서 두 번째 연사는 큰 책임을 맡은 형제였습니다.
우리의 다음 연사도 큰 책임을 맡고 있는 헤르마뉘스 판 셀름 형제인데요,
셀름 형제가 우리에게 해 주실 흥미로운 연설의 주제는
가슴 아픈 일을 연달아 겪고 있다고 생각해 봅시다.
여호와께서 더는 날 사랑하지 않는다고 생각하죠.
이때 성령의 작용으로 여러분이 그 상황을 알게 되어,
‘여호와께서 여전히 자매를 도와주신다는 걸 어떻게 알려 주지?
자매의 삶에서 여호와의 손길을 느낄 수 있도록
그러면, 그 답을 알기 위해 룻기에 나오는 몇 구절을 보면서,
나오미와 룻과 보아스에 관한 감동적인 기록을 살펴보겠습니다.
“전능자께서 내 삶을 몹시 비통하게 만드셨기 때문입니다.”
비통해서 심한 말을 했지만 모두 사실이 아닙니다.
여호와께서는 나오미의 심한 말에 어떻게 응하셨나요?
손을 뻗어 나오미를 절망에서 부드럽게 끌어내 주셨습니다.
여호와께서는 룻과 보아스에게 바로 그분의 손,
즉 그분이 나오미를 도우실 수단이 되는 특권을 주신 것입니다.
삶에서 여호와의 손길을 느끼도록 도와줄 수 있을까요?
우리가 어려움에 처한 동료 숭배자들을 도울 때 따를 수 있는
어려움을 겪는 사람을 돕는 건 아주 힘든 일이라,
가족에 대한 사랑, 형제 사랑, 원칙에 근거한 사랑이 있죠.
너희는 각자 너희 어머니의 집으로 돌아가거라.
너희가 죽은 너희 남편과 나에게 해 준 것처럼,
커피로 치면 에스프레소 더블 샷 정도죠.
애착을 갖고 우리 형제를 계속 도와
절망감에서 끌어내 줄 수 있는 것입니다.
어려움을 겪는 형제 자매들에게 보여야 합니다.
룻이 나오미에게 도움의 손길을 내밀었을 때,
하지만 충성스러운 사랑을 가진 룻은 물러나지 않았죠.
“나오미는 룻이 기어이 자기와 함께 가려고 하는 것을 보고,
결국 그 자매가 우정의 손길을 받아 줄 걸 기대하면서
세 번째, 마음에 담아 두지 마십시오.
룻은 나오미를 도우려고 큰 희생을 치렀습니다.
나오미와 함께 몇 날 며칠을 계속 걸어 왔죠.
옆에 있는 룻의 존재를 아주 무시한 거죠.
그 말에 룻이 얼마나 마음이 아팠겠습니까?
오늘날도 어떤 형제나 자매가 사무치는 절망감에 못 이겨,
상처를 주는 말이나 행동을 할지 모릅니다.
그런 말과 행동을 마음에 담아 두지 마십시오.
“여호와여, 당신이 내민 손길을 자매가 보게 해 주십시오”라고요.
적극적인 행동을 못하고 있다는 것을 알고,
제게 호의를 베푸는 사람 뒤에서 이삭을 줍게 해 주세요.’”
상황을 개선하려고 적극적으로 행동할 힘이 없을 수 있습니다.
따라서 형제에 대한 충성스러운 사랑이 있으면
그 형제의 주변에서 실제적 도움을 베풀 겁니다.
“여호와께서 그대가 행한 일에 대해 상 주시기를 바라오.
그대가 그분의 날개 아래로 도피처를 구하려고 왔으니,
네, 룻은 오랫동안 부정적인 이야기를 들어 왔기 때문에
보아스의 그런 따뜻한 말에 깊이 감동받았을 겁니다.
당신의 종에게 안심시키는 말을 해 주셨습니다.”
보아스가 알맞은 때에 한 친절한 말은
룻이 일을 해 나가는 데 필요한 힘을 주었죠.
오늘날도 사랑 많은 장로의 친절한 말은
어려움을 겪는 형제 자매들을 돕기 위해
최선을 다하는 사람들에게 그처럼 힘이 됩니다.
여호와께서 우리에게 그분의 손이 될 특권을 주실지 모릅니다.
나오미는 보아스의 관대함에 대해 어떤 반응을 보일까요?
마침내 나오미는 그 모든 상황을 이해했고,
룻이 ‘어머니를 떠나지 않겠다, 함께 이삭을 줍겠다’고 했을 때
그리고 요구된 것보다 훨씬 더 많이 베풀어
나오미와 룻을 돌본 보아스도 여호와의 손이 된 겁니다.
여호와의 도움의 손길을 느끼게 해 준 룻과 보아스가
그처럼 상황이 완전히 바뀌어서 무척 기뻤을 겁니다.
특히 어려움에 처한 사람들에 대한 사랑이죠.
영적인 균형을 되찾는 것을 보는 기쁨을 맛보았습니다.
오늘날 우리도 어려움에 처한 형제 자매들이
영적인 힘을 되찾도록 도울 수 있을 때
그런 큰 기쁨을 맛볼 수 있습니다.
룻과 같은 자매들과 보아스 같은 형제 여러분,
이전 그 어느 때보다도 여호와의 손길을 느끼고
네, 에스프레소 더블 샷보다 훨씬 낫지 않았나요?
