그는 어디에 물이 있는지, 어디에 목초지가 있는지, 전체 상황을 알았습니다.
그래서 그에게 “눈”이 돼 달라고 한 거죠.
그의 지식과 경험을 활용해 안내자가 되어 달라고요.
가족도 친구도 여기 있고 살기도 편한데, 왜 그 사람들과 위험을 감수해야 하지?
호밥은 뚜렷한 보상에 대한 약속도 없이,
그들을 안내하려고 이스라엘 백성과 약속의 땅으로 갔습니다.
지난 5개월 동안 여러분은 성경을 구성하는 66권의 책의
창세기부터 계시록까지, 역사 수업, 지리 수업, 고고학 수업 등등,
많은 수업들과 많은 시험들을 통해 익숙해졌습니다.
여러분의 경험과 지식을 사용해서, 다른 사람을 위한 안내자로 섬기십시오.
성경의 지형에 익숙지가 않아서 그로부터 도움을 얻기가 힘들 수 있습니다.
하느님의 말씀 어디에서 영적인 물을 찾을 수 있는지,
어디서 새 힘과 활력을 얻을 수 있는지 보여 주십시오.
여러분은 이곳 학교에서 조직의 아름다운 모습들을 볼 수 있었습니다.
하느님의 조직의 이 독특한 풍경은 많은 사람이 볼 수 없는 것이죠.
여러분이 돌아가 만날 많은 사람은 여러분과 같은 경험을 하지 못할 겁니다.
여호와의 조직에 대한 그들의 신뢰심을 강화하십시오.
여러분의 지식을 나누어 주는 데 인색해지지 마십시오.
타인이 나보다 나은 사람이 되게 훈련하십시오.
여러분은 튼튼하고 연합된 조직을 만들어 나가는 데 기여하는 것입니다.
네, 우린 여호와 하느님과 그 백성을 충성스럽게 지지한
또 다른 겐 사람인 레갑의 이름이 나오는데, 그 아들은 여호나답입니다.
여호와께선 예후에게 바알 숭배를 없애라는 임무를 주셨습니다.
그는 예후를 만나길 원하고, 지원하고 싶어 합니다.
네, 여호나답은 예후가 하느님께 받은 사명을 공개적으로 지지하는 것을
여호나답은 예후의 손을 잡았고, 병거에 올라탑니다.
여호나답은 예후가 받은 임무를 지지하는 걸 영예로 여겼습니다.
여호나답처럼, 여러분도 하느님의 보이는 조직이 내린 결정들을
오늘도, 내일도, 다음 주에도, 다음 달에도,
여러분은 조직의 발전에 크게 기여할 겁니다.
겐 사람들은 왕족도 아니었고, 뚜렷한 업적도 없었습니다.
그들이 그분의 백성을 위해 한 일을 분명히 보셨고 결코 잊지 않으셨습니다.
역대기상 2:55을 보면 그들이 유다의 족보에 포함된 걸 볼 수 있습니다.
사울이 아말렉을 공격할 때 여호와께서 겐 사람들을 보호하셨는데,
그들이 충성스런 사랑을 보였기에, 피하게 해 준 겁니다.
예레미야 시대에 그분은 여호나답의 후손인 레갑 사람들과 계약을 맺으십니다.
내 앞에서 섬길 사람이 결코 끊어지지 않을 것이다.”
여호와께선 레갑 사람들의 충성스런 인내를 높게 사셨습니다.
기원전 607년에 있을 예루살렘의 멸망을 그들이 생존할 거라고 약속하셨죠.
‘그의 후손이 내 앞에서 끊어지지 않을 것이다.’
만약, 만약, 겐 사람의 후손이 예수 시대까지 남아 그분의 제자가 되고,
확실히는 알 수 없는 일이긴 하지만,
여러분이 우리의 활동이 제한되어 있거나 거의 알려져 있지 않은 곳에서 일한다면,
좀 외로운 느낌이 들 수도 있을 것입니다.
하지만 여호와께선 여러분이 인내하며 나타내는 충성과 충실을 보고 계십니다.
겐 사람들처럼 여러분이 하는 일이 주목을 받지 못할지 모릅니다.
인정받지 못하고 있다는 느낌이 들 수도 있습니다.
그리고 하늘의 아버지 여호와께서는 겐 사람들에게 하신 것처럼,
여러분이 하는 모든 일을 소중히 여기고
여러분의 충실한 봉사를 결코 잊지 않으십니다.
겐 사람들은 우리에게 소중한 교훈을 줍니다.
여러분과 제가, 여호와의 승인을 받으려면 무엇이 필요한지 가르쳐 줍니다.
이제 겐 사람들의 유산은 여러분의 겁니다.
여러분이 지위보다 왕국과 형제들을 더 사랑한다는 걸 증명하십시오.
형제들이 격려를 얻고 어려운 상황을 극복할 수 있는
‘필요한 일은 뭐든지, 얼마 동안이든 하겠다’고 결심하십시오.
묵묵히 충성스럽게 지원한 겐 사람들의 영적인 유산은
네, 지혜로운 조언을 해 주셔서 매우 감사합니다.
믿음을 강화해 준 정말 훌륭한 내용이었습니다!
불가리아에서 온 인사를 전해 드리고 싶습니다.
불가리아는 유럽 남동쪽의 산지가 많은 아름다운 나라입니다.
이 나라에선 지금도 개인 농장이 중요한 역할을 합니다.
여전히 많은 사람이 자기 집에서 와인을 빚고,
과일이나 야채로 통조림을 만들고, 추운 겨울을 나려고 장작을 팹니다.
나라 전체 전도인 수는 50명이 채 되지 않았습니다.
1991년에 처음으로 길르앗을 졸업한 선교인들이 이곳에 임명되었습니다.
탄성을 자아내는 바위, 폭포, 동굴들을 보러 많은 관광객이 모여들죠.
브라차 회중에는 전도인이 43명이며, 그중 5명은 장로로 섬깁니다.
전도인들은 매달 평균 80건의 성서 연구를 사회합니다.
유럽의 다른 나라 증인들이 전파하러 이곳으로 이주하기도 했습니다.
회중에는 14명의 정규 파이오니아, 2명의 특별 파이오니아, 2명의 선교인이 있습니다.
단지 전도 활동을 했다는 이유로 벌금을 낼 뻔했고,
몇 사람은 경찰의 괴롭힘을 받기도 했습니다.
지방 법원은 우리의 전도 활동을 제한하는 것이 헌법에 위배된다는 판결을 내렸고
우리는 불가리아에 있는 형제 자매들을 위해 계속 기도하며,
지금까지 여호와의 증인 세계 본부에서 JW 방송이었습니다.

en.text: Welcome to the June program of JW Broadcasting.
As you likely remember,
Gilead graduations are now featured
as the monthly JW Broadcasting program
once every six months.
For this program, we are excited to share with you
the first part of the graduation of the 144th class of Gilead,
which took place on March 10, 2018.
This program features Scriptural talks with intriguing themes.
We know you’ll enjoy these thought-provoking discussions.
In coming weeks, be on the lookout
for Parts 2 and 3 of the Gilead graduation.
You’ll have an opportunity to get to know some of the students better
during another heart-stirring episode
of The Inside Story.
But now, we invite you to enjoy Part 1
of the graduation of the 144th class of Gilead.
You’ll see a picture on the monitors.
Take a look at it;
take a good look.
What’s the occasion?
I’ll give you a hint.
The picture was taken 75 years ago last month.
It’s a picture of the very first day
of the very first class of Gilead.
So 75 years ago last month
was the inception of Gilead.
Now, Gilead
—that’s an interesting word, isn’t it?
What does it mean?
Well, if you answer “Heap of Witness,”
it shows that you’re very familiar
with the 1984 edition of the New World Translation.
The 2013 edition says “Witness Pile.”
Now, there can be a difference between a heap and a pile.
Where I come from in Canada, in the wintertime it gets very cold.
And to save on heating expenses,
many families heat with a woodstove.
And so you go to the backyard,
and you see a very neat pile of wood stacked up.
They’re not careless about it.
In fact, some of them are quite meticulous about their woodpile.
If you appreciate the appearance of your home,
some of them are very artistic, almost sculpted, these woodpiles.
And we’d never call it a heap because with a heap you’d think of wood
that has just been carelessly strewn right and left.
But no, this is a woodpile,
so something rather neat.
So why are we talking about a “Witness Pile”?
Well, what was it?
What was this “Heap of Witness”?
What was this “Witness Pile” in the original meaning?
What purpose did it serve,
and why does it concern you members of the graduating class?
It does.
In fact, it concerns all of us.
There’s a lesson that all of us can learn
from this “Witness Pile” called Gilead.
Let’s go to the origin, back in Genesis chapter 31
—Genesis chapter 31.
Now, a little context:
The patriarch Jacob
was tired of being cheated by his father-in-law, Laban.
And as we read the Scriptures,
we know that Laban was kind of a shady character;
you wouldn’t want to buy a used car from Laban.
And so Jacob got tired of being cheated,
and so he ran away with his wives and his children.
Well, Laban ran after him.
And when he caught up with Jacob,
Laban and Jacob made a covenant of peace.
Now, we’ll take up the reading from verse 43.
So this is Genesis 31, beginning with verse 43:
“Then Laban answered Jacob:
“‘The daughters are my daughters
“‘and the children my children
“‘and the flock my flock,
and everything you are looking at is mine.’”
It tells you what kind of a person he was, doesn’t it?
Verse 44:
“‘Now come, let us make a covenant, you and I,
“and it will serve as a witness between us.’
“So Jacob took a stone and set it up as a pillar.
“Then Jacob said to his brothers:
“‘Pick up stones!’
And they took stones and made a pile.”
And notice this:
“After that they ate there
on the pile of stones.”
So scholars tell us that this “pile of stones”
must have been quite neatly arranged,
so that it would form a kind of a table,
and they had their meal of peace on this table.
And, of course, this was to serve as a monument.
It was to be a monument of the covenant of peace
between Laban and Jacob.
Now, let’s carry on, verse 47:
“And Laban began calling it Jegar-sahadutha,
but Jacob called it Galeed.”
When the brothers were picking a name for the school,
aren’t you glad they didn’t go with Laban’s?
How would you students like to be graduates
of the Watchtower Bible School of Jegar-sahadutha?
That would be a mouthful, wouldn’t it?
So they chose Galeed, or Gilead.
Verses 48 and 49:
“Laban then said:
“‘This pile of stones is a witness
“between me and you today.’
That is why he named it Galeed, and the Watchtower.”
And isn’t it interesting that both “Watchtower” and “Gilead”
are in the name of our school?
But what was the purpose of the pile of rocks?
Verse 52:
“This pile of stones is a witness,
“and the pillar is something that bears witness,
“that I will not pass beyond this pile of stones
“to bring harm to you
“and you will not pass beyond this pile of stones and this pillar
to bring harm to me.”
So this Gilead,
this “pile of stones,”
this “Witness Pile,”
was really a monument.
It was a symbol of peace and unity.
And anytime someone would pass by that monument,
that “pile of stones,” that “witness heap,” if you like,
they would be reminded of the need for unity.
Now, the unity between Laban and Jacob
didn’t come about automatically.
We read verse 43.
Did you notice the accusations that Laban made
when he first encountered Jacob?
‘The daughters are mine;
‘the children are mine;
‘the flocks are mine;
everything you see is mine.’
Well, them were fighting words.
Jacob had worked very hard for everything he got.
He’d worked for 14 years for his wives,
and Laban changed his wages ten times.
So Laban had no right to say that it was all his,
and Jacob could have taken exception to it;
but he bit his tongue.
Why?
The goal was peace.
He wanted to make peace.
So Jacob took the high road.
Well, today, that name Gilead
is an appropriate name for our school.
And it reminds us of the blessed unity
that must pervade through the organization today.
When you think of it, Gilead has been a tremendous force
to unify God’s people.
As missionaries were sent to the far corners of the earth,
they were supplicating people to come
into a peaceful relationship with Jehovah God.
And as branches were formed,
the missionaries understood how world headquarters worked,
and they helped to promote unity
between the branches and world headquarters.
So the missionaries were agents of peace.
Now, of course, the focus of Gilead is on strengthening the congregations,
strengthening the circuits, strengthening the branches,
forging an unbreakable link
between the branches and world headquarters.
And Gilead plays a part in all this.
We are “one flock,” under “one shepherd.”
Don’t hurt any member of the flock.
Be a peacemaker.
If you want peace, you have to work for it.
And sometimes to achieve it, we have to bite our tongues.
Now, isn’t that a good lesson
that you members of the graduating class
and all of us can learn?
Because we all want to work for the peace of Jerusalem;
we all want to work for the peace of Jehovah’s organization.
Well, back to the first class of Gilead
—graduation day, June 23, 1943.
Wait a minute,
first day of class, February 1;
graduation day, June 23.
That wasn’t five months, was it?
But they had a lovely graduation day.
And the first to speak was a member
of what would later become the Governing Body,
Brother W. E. Van Amburgh.
Well, today at the graduation of the 144th class,
we have a member of the Governing Body who will be first to speak,
not Brother Van Amburgh,
but Brother Anthony Morris.
And Tony is going to speak to us on the subject
“Supplicate All the Time!”
You soon-to-be graduates are very familiar with the fact
that in Scripture there are different forms of prayer.
You have petition.
We petition Jehovah for various needs.
You have thanksgiving —so much to thank him for.
And then, of course, Jehovah always deserves praise,
so we have these prayers we offer to praise him.
However, I just want to implant in your minds,
as you get ready to graduate and go to your assignments,
this matter of supplication.
It’s unique;
it’s just full of emotion —earnest prayer.
And I think you understand that.
We want you to understand why we’re suggesting
you should supplicate all the time —all the time.
And take, for example, Christ Jesus.
He set the perfect example for us here.
And you’ll notice in Hebrews chapter 5
how priceless his perfect example was.
At least we try to reach for it.
But not just you soon-to-be graduates
but all of us can benefit from this good counsel.
Now, notice Hebrews 5:7:
“During his life on earth, Christ offered up supplications
“and also petitions, with strong outcries and tears,
“to the One who was able to save him out of death,
and he was favorably heard for his godly fear.”
Now, did you notice, though, that “supplications” is plural?
So, certainly he supplicated throughout his three-and-a-half-year ministry.
But we can only imagine the final weeks, days,
hours was with tears
—the supplication.
So this is the example for us,
and the closer we get to the end,
Jehovah wants us to imitate his Son.
In fact, Jesus made it very clear how important this was.
And you’re aware of it, but sometimes we get so busy
with the things we’re dealing with that we can forget.
Notice what he commanded in Luke.
So find Luke,
and we’re going to look at the 21st chapter.
You’ll quickly remember it
—Luke chapter 21.
Now here, just to highlight a little bit
before we read verse 36,
you’ll notice in verse 34
that these are the things we have to “pay attention to”
to avoid being “weighed down with overeating
and heavy drinking and anxieties of life,”
so that it doesn’t hit us like a snare.
Now notice verse 36:
“Keep awake, then,
“all the time making supplication
“that you may succeed in escaping all these things
that must occur and in standing before the Son of man.”
So this is what he said:
“All the time making supplication.”
Now, obviously,
it’s not going to be something where if you’re driving a car,
you’re going to stop and start supplicating on the road.
But the spirit of his counsel is,
‘Do you want to succeed like I succeeded?
You must supplicate all the time.’
It just has to be.
You can’t let a day go by that you haven’t had supplication,
and the closer we get to the end,
the more important that is.
A lot of us need to focus on supplicating
—because it’s not what might occur,
it’s what will occur.
This is a reality.
So it’s very obvious, and it’s understandable
that we will supplicate
when we or a loved one face a crisis,
something happens.
And then it’s just natural to get that intense emotion in prayer,
and there could well be tears; but it’s intense.
You’re just focused.
It’s just gripping you with the emotion
as you face different things.
So you may have a life-threatening illness in the future;
you’ll start supplicating with that news.
If you have a loved one and their life is threatened,
there’s going to be supplication.
But even though that’s appropriate
and Jehovah expects us to do that,
I just want to have you take back with you on your assignments
something that you must supplicate about too.
And I have to take the same counsel.
It means a lot to Jehovah.
It’s very basic, but look at Matthew chapter 6
—Matthew chapter 6.
And this is where Jesus gave the example of prayer,
and it certainly extends to supplicating.
You’ll notice in verse 9 where he mentions:
“You must pray . . . this way:
“‘Our Father in the heavens, let your name be sanctified.
“‘Let your Kingdom come.
Let your will take place, as in heaven, also on earth.’”
So it’s Jehovah’s name.
You look at this wicked world, and it’s getting worse.
The Bible foretold it would go “from bad to worse,”
and it’s just so reproachful to the holy name of God.
Everybody is in the face of anything Scriptural.
And how terrible that is!
Supplicate about your concern to Jehovah himself
—how that bothers you— and that will touch him.
And it’s nice because it gets your mind off yourself
(which is not always spiritually healthy)
and focused on Jehovah’s name,
because it’s his name and the Kingdom
that are going to rid the whole world of all the problems anyway.
So it’s just something we want you to take with you,
to supplicate about Jehovah’s name
and removing the reproach and that his Kingdom come.
Do that often.
All the time, if you will.
Now just some final thoughts here
in a very familiar Psalm, Psalm 83.
So if you’ll find Psalm 83 here.
And this connects with supplicating Jehovah
to have his will done
and his name vindicated (as we say in English as well now),
cleared of the reproach.
I know you feel the same way I do.
I’m way over here.
I just— It’s disgusting!
You’ve got to keep up with some of the news,
but it’s almost like, ‘Let me stop!’
But you’ve got to know a little something that’s going on.
And we have connections with our brothers
from all different parts of the earth; things are coming up all the time.
There’s so much to supplicate about,
and the Kingdom is going to finally put an end to all of it.
Now, what I thought you’d appreciate
if you look at the 83rd Psalm in context,
in the first five verses (this is interesting),
it’s about those who hate Jehovah.
These arrogant enemies of Jehovah God
hate him and hate his people.
They’re cunning; they’re despicable.
Now, it’s quite fascinating that in verse 5,
see the “b” part of the verse:
“They have made an alliance against you.”
So this was an alliance of nations
coming against Jehovah’s name people —an alliance.
What does that remind you of?
So by focusing on supplicating all the time,
you’re really getting yourself ready for the great tribulation.
We call it a coalition of nations
—Gog’s attack.
It connects with what we see here that happened in the past.
And these are beautiful thoughts here.
Notice verse 17 and verse 18
of the 83rd Psalm.
And this is from our heart.
We want to supplicate this to our Father:
“May they be put to shame and be terrified forever;
“may they be disgraced and perish;
“may people know that you, whose name is Jehovah,
you alone are the Most High over all the earth.”
Ah! What a stirring supplication!
So with whatever you face, you soon-to-be graduates,
in the future, remember the Scriptural advice:
‘Supplicate all the time,’ and you are sure to succeed.
Beautifully done.
Thank you very much, Brother Morris.
Now, at the graduation of the first class of Gilead,
the next to speak was a responsible brother.
And we have a responsible brother who is going to speak to us next,
Brother Hermanus van Selm.
He’s a helper to the Writing Committee,
and Brother van Selm is going to speak to us on the interesting theme
“See and Be Jehovah’s Hand.”
Think for a moment of your congregation back home.
Imagine that Jehovah observes there a dear elderly sister
who has suffered one painful setback after another.
As a result, she is heartbroken.
She even feels that Jehovah doesn’t love her anymore.
But then through the working of his spirit,
Jehovah makes you aware of her situation.
You want to help your dear sister, but you wonder:
‘How can I show her that Jehovah is still reaching out to her?
‘How can I help her to see
Jehovah’s supporting hand at work in her life?’
To answer, let us consider a few verses
in the Bible book of Ruth,
which relates the touching story
of Naomi, Ruth, and Boaz.
As we remember, Naomi’s husband had died.
Then her two sons got married,
but sadly, both of them also died.
Those blows caused Naomi
to sink deeper and deeper into despair.
She even felt that Jehovah had abandoned her.
Note at chapter 1, verse 13, at the end of the verse,
note what Naomi said:
“The hand of Jehovah has turned against me.”
Verse 20, at the end of the verse:
“The Almighty has made my life very bitter for me.”
Verse 21, at the end of the verse:
“Jehovah who opposed me
and the Almighty who caused me calamity.”
Now, these were strong statements,
but, of course, none of them were true.
Jehovah had not turned against her.
Jehovah had not caused her calamity.
So how did Jehovah react to Naomi’s bitter words?
Well, he did not send fire from heaven to punish her.
He did not send a prophet to reprove her.
Instead, he used Ruth and Boaz
to reach out to Naomi
and pull her gently out of her despair.
In a sense, Jehovah gave Ruth and Boaz
the privilege to serve as His hand
—that is, the means through which He could provide
support to Naomi.
In this class, we have 22 Ruth-like sisters
and 27 Boaz-like brothers.
Also, there are thousands of Ruths and Boazes in this audience.
So how can we be Jehovah’s hand?
And how can we help the Naomis in our congregation
to see Jehovah’s hand at work in their life?
To answer, we will consider five steps
mentioned in the book of Ruth
that we could follow to help our fellow worshippers who are in need.
Step number one: Have the right motivation.
Since helping those in need takes great effort,
we have to be motivated by love.
But it needs to be a special kind of love.
What do we mean?
Well, love is a bit like coffee.
Coffee? In what way?
Well, coffee comes in different types,
such as cappuccino, caffe latte, caffe mocha
—mmm.
Similarly, love comes in different types,
such as love for family, brotherly love, principled love.
But the love considered in the book of Ruth
is yet of a different type.
What is it?
It is mentioned at chapter 1, verse 8:
“Naomi said to both of her daughters-in-law:
“‘Go, return, each of you to your mother’s home.
“‘May Jehovah show loyal love to you,
just as you have shown it to the men who have died and to me.’”
“Loyal love.”
What kind of love is that?
It’s a very strong kind of love.
It’s a bit like a double espresso, undiluted.
It gives you a real boost that helps you to attach yourself to a brother in need
and to cling to him until you have pulled him out of his despair.
Now, that’s the type of love we show to our brothers and sisters in need.
Step number two: Be persistent.
When Ruth offered her helping hand to Naomi,
Naomi first refused to accept it.
But Ruth, motivated by loyal love, did not take no for an answer.
What was the result?
Chapter 1, verse 18:
“When Naomi saw that Ruth insisted on going with her,
she stopped trying to convince her.”
Similarly today, a sister in despair
may first refuse to accept our help.
Even so, loyal love will move us to cling to that sister,
hoping that she will eventually accept our hand of friendship.
Step number three: Don’t take it personally.
When Naomi and Ruth arrived in Bethlehem,
Naomi met her former neighbors.
What did she tell them?
Chapter 1, verse 21:
“I was full when I went,
but Jehovah made me return empty-handed.”
What did she tell them?
Now, put yourself in the place of Ruth.
She had gone out of her way to help Naomi.
She cried with her, she comforted her,
she walked with her for days on end.
And then, with Ruth standing next to her,
Naomi said, ‘I returned empty-handed.’
She did not even acknowledge the presence of Ruth.
How painful that must have been for our dear Ruth.
Yet, Ruth stuck with Naomi.
Likewise today, a brother or sister,
because of their bitter feelings of despair,
may speak to us or treat us in a hurtful way
in spite of all of our efforts to help them.
But we try not to take it personally.
We stick with our sister in need and pray to Jehovah:
“Please, open the sister’s eyes.
Let her see your outstretched hand.”
Step number four: Give practical help.
Ruth realized that Naomi’s depression
prevented her from taking the initiative.
So, what did Ruth do?
Chapter 2, verse 2:
“Ruth . . . said to Naomi:
“‘Let me go out, please,
“‘to the fields and glean among the ears of grain
behind whoever looks on me with favor.’”
Now, today, we also realize that the brother in despair
may lack the energy to take any initiative to help himself.
So loyal love for our brother moves us
to take the first step in giving him practical help
in and around his house.
Step number five: Get encouragement.
Ruth badly needed encouragement,
and Jehovah moved Boaz to give it to her.
Look at chapter 2, verse 12.
Boaz said to Ruth:
“May Jehovah reward you for what you have done,
“and may there be a perfect wage for you
“from Jehovah the God of Israel,
under whose wings you have come to seek refuge.”
Now, after Ruth had been hearing
negative talk for so long,
those heartwarming words of Boaz
deeply touched her.
In response, in the middle of verse 13 we read that Ruth said to Boaz:
“You have comforted me
and [you have] spoken reassuringly to your servant.”
The kind and timely words of Boaz
gave Ruth the strength she needed to carry on.
Today, the kind words of a caring elder
will have the same uplifting effect
on those who give their all
in helping brothers and sisters in need.
If we follow these five steps,
Jehovah may give us the privilege of being his hand.
With what result?
Consider what happened next to Naomi.
The Bible account continues by telling that Boaz provided
a generous gift of food for Ruth and Naomi.
What was Naomi’s reaction to Boaz’s generosity?
Chapter 2, verse 20:
“At that Naomi said to her daughter-in-law:
“‘May he be blessed by Jehovah,
“‘who has not failed in his loyal love
toward the living and the dead.’”
Now, what a turning point this was for Naomi.
Earlier she had cried out in pain,
‘Jehovah caused me calamity.’
But then she exclaimed with joy,
‘Jehovah has not failed in his loyal love!’
Finally, Naomi was able to connect the dots
and realize that when Ruth had said to her,
‘I will stick with you; I will glean with you,’
Ruth was acting as Jehovah’s hand.
And then Boaz had gone far beyond what was required
in caring for her and Ruth.
Boaz had acted as Jehovah’s hand.
‘Ahh, now I understand,’ Naomi must have thought.
‘Jehovah never left me.
‘He has been with me all the time.
‘I’m so grateful to Ruth and Boaz
that they helped me to see Jehovah’s supporting hands.’
No doubt all three of them rejoiced
over the decisive turning point
they had reached.
In summary, what gave Ruth and Boaz
the strength to pull Naomi out of her despair?
Loyal love.
A strong kind of love that we give, not to people in general,
but to our brothers and sisters, especially those who are in need.
What was the result?
Boaz and Ruth had the joy
of seeing how Naomi regained her spiritual balance.
Today, we may experience the same deep joy
when we are able to help our brothers and sisters in need,
to see Jehovah’s hand and thus regain their spiritual strength.
Therefore, our dear Ruth-like sisters
and Boaz-like brothers
of class 144,
it is our heartfelt prayer
that the precious education that you received at Gilead
may help you more than ever
to see and to be Jehovah’s hand.
Well, that was better than a double espresso, wasn’t it?
Now we’re going to have a helper to the Teaching Committee to talk to us,
and he has the interesting theme
“Be the Keel” —K-E-E-L.
So we’ll listen with interest.
Like a sailboat in the open sea, you could be sailing along
—enjoying life, enjoying your view—
but then suddenly and unexpectedly
a turbulent storm, a trialsome situation,
could be confronting you.
That could really rock your boat.
How true are the words found in The Watchtower
of the March 1, 1896, issue
where it stated:
“The Christian course of self-sacrifice
“cannot be one of ease and continuous smooth-sailing and peace.
“There may be a calm now and then,
but storms and battles are the rule.”
Now, if that was the case 122 years ago,
way before all of us were alive,
how much more so is that the rule, or the case, today.
Life in Satan’s system is anything but smooth sailing.
How can you students help others endure present storms
and prepare them for future tests —future storms?
Be the keel.
What does that mean?
The keel is a heavily-weighted fin
attached to the bottom of a sailboat.
So when strong, gusting winds fill the sail
and the vessel leans on its side,
the keel serves as the ballast —the counterweight.
It provides stability.
It prevents the sailboat from blowing sideways
and from capsizing, or keeling over.
Our brothers and sisters,
now more than ever, need to be strengthened.
They need to be stabilized so that they can face
storms of anxiety, natural disasters,
and wave after wave of ridicule and persecution.
That’s the focus of Gilead School
—to strengthen and stabilize qualified men and women like you
so that you, in turn, can strengthen
and stabilize Jehovah’s organization.
Empowered with Jehovah’s spirit,
you can be like those strengthening aids
in the first century
who proved to be someone
who could stabilize their brothers and sisters.
And there are many examples.
But let’s look at Acts 18:24,
and let’s see why the man Apollos is someone who we want to follow.
There in Acts chapter 18,
let’s read together verse 24.
And there it reads:
“Now a Jew named Apollos, a native of Alexandria,
“arrived in Ephesus;
“[and notice] he was an eloquent man who was well-versed in the Scriptures.
This man had been instructed in the way of Jehovah,”
and notice that he was “aglow with the spirit,”
which caused him to speak and teach accurately
about the things of Jesus.
“But he was acquainted only with the baptism of John.
“He began to speak boldly in the synagogue,
“and when Priscilla and Aquila heard him,
“[What did they do?]
“they took him into their company
and explained the way of God more accurately to him.”
Well, what outstanding qualities Apollos had
—qualities that you students have as well!
Now, Apollos had his strengths;
but like all of us, he also had his weaknesses
and he knew that he needed to humbly get more help,
more understanding.
So how thankful we are, and he was,
that Aquila and Priscilla filled in the gaps
—helped him to appreciate the deeper things of Jehovah
so that he could speak more accurately.
Yes, this well-grounded, spiritually mature couple
also helped Apollos learn life lessons.
Like what?
Like working as a team
—working in unity.
They also taught him life lessons about going the extra mile
in helping those who needed help spiritually
as well as materially;
what it means to be generous,
to be hospitable;
and also the key that humility is needed
in order to support others,
so that we’re content in our assignment.
Like Apollos, you accepted the invitation to come to Gilead
to receive extra schooling
to have a deeper understanding of God’s Word, the Bible.
And along the way,
you learned vital life lessons from this Bethel family,
who are supporting you.
You learned what it means to go the extra mile
—to be hospitable, generous, kind, and patient.
You also learned what it means to be a giver and not simply a taker.
You will soon graduate.
You will have a diploma in your hand.
Is that it? You walk away and that’s it?
That’s all for your instruction?
Of course not.
We know Jehovah promises
that he will continue to give you instruction.
In fact, at 1 Peter chapter 5, notice verse 10.
There at 1 Peter 5:10,
Jehovah promises that he will “finish your training.”
Well, how will he finish your training?
It goes on to say that his continued training
“will make you firm,”
it “will make you strong,”
and “he will firmly ground you.”
So just as a keel is filled with heavy weight
to keep the boat stable and upright,
so too Jehovah promises to give you his powerful holy spirit
so that you can be strengthened and stabilized
and help others to do the same
—to be firmly grounded.
Now, because Apollos was humble and he accepted the help,
he put himself in a position to be used mightily by Jehovah
and by his organization.
Now, what did he do to greatly help the congregations back then?
Notice Acts 18:27.
There at Acts 18:27,
Apollos not only helped the congregation in Achaia
but it says that “he greatly helped” them.
And it went on to say in another translation of this verse
that “he powerfully reinforced” them.
So he was really someone who took the training
and really made it happen.
In fact, if you look at verse 28,
he set an example of someone who should be zealous in the ministry.
He used the Scriptures that he had at the time,
and he used these as his authority.
And how did he speak?
Verse 28 says “with great intensity.”
So we could say
that basically Apollos was a keel with zeal.
And we look forward to seeing how you will use your Gilead training
to greatly help others in your assignments
and doing so with great intensity.
Now, when you look at a sailboat,
what’s the first thing that you normally see?
Isn’t it the sail?
Why?
Because it’s the most prominent, outstanding thing on a sailboat.
Now, the keel, on the other hand, is unseen.
It’s below the water, below the boat, but there it is.
It’s doing its job.
It’s keeping that sailboat upright, supported, and stabilized.
Now, you could hardly imagine Apollos thinking to himself:
‘I know that my assignment as a keel
‘—as a support, as a stabilizer—
‘is important, but I don’t think I’m being tapped into my true potential.
‘I don’t think the brothers can really see me down here,
‘doing all that I’m supposed to do.
‘Yes, I know that I’m not an apostle.
‘I’m not being used to write inspired letters,
‘although I would be a logical choice.
‘If only, if only, I could have a more elevated, higher position,
‘maybe like the sail.
‘If I was the sail, everyone could see me
‘and I could get more airtime.
‘And then everyone could hear me
and my words that are so eloquent.’
Well, we know that that’s ridiculous.
He never thought that, and he never acted that way toward others.
The Bible only reveals just a fraction
of all that Apollos said and that he did.
But what we do know
is that the most outstanding and most prominent thing about Apollos
was his humility.
He was willing, humble,
to do anything wherever he was sent to go.
He never allowed his strengths to become weaknesses.
Likewise, much of what you, Gilead students,
will do in the future will be unseen by others.
But you know that Jehovah sees everything you do
and all the work and the stabilizing you do
in behalf of his precious sheep.
You students have many gifts, many strengths, many abilities.
But your humility must exceed
any gifts or strengths that you have;
never allow your strengths to become your weakness.
Remember, ability without humility is a liability,
but ability with humility is stability.
And that’s the key to a keel.
And no doubt when you look back at your life,
there were many that served as a keel for you.
They were the ones who stabilized you, balanced you,
when you needed it most.
When you were going through turbulent storms in your life,
they were there for you.
Who was your Apollos?
Who was your Aquila? your Pricilla?
Remember all that they said and did for you,
and remember that you can be that person for someone else.
They can help you to be balanced, stable, even-keeled.
Now it’s your turn.
Take your Gilead training and greatly help your brothers and sisters.
Love them, support them,
strengthen them, stabilize them.
Be the keel.

There are two things that I know about you
and two things that you know about me.
The first is we want to serve Jehovah,
and we want to do so acceptably.
And the second is we want to be happy.
Wouldn’t you agree?
Now, to the first point, there’s not much of a problem
because you’ve had five months of study now.
You’ve been through the Bible.
You know what Jehovah expects —what he wants—
and you’re prepared to do it.
But, now, as to the second point,
that can be a little bit more challenging.
Why do I say that?
Well, happiness can be tricky.
We all know people who by all standards
should seem to be happy, but they’re not.
On the other hand, we know people who face
many, many difficult challenges every day,
but they just seem to radiate happiness.
We quickly realize that happiness
is not dependent on things, on circumstances,
or even on people.
Why is that?
It’s because true happiness is not an end goal;
it is a by-product.
But a by-product of what?
Well, the answer to that question lies back in time.
Open your Bibles, if you would, to Deuteronomy chapter 16.
And here, discussing one of the three annual festivals
that Jehovah required the Israelites to attend,
in verse 15 he gave these words.
He said: “Seven days you will celebrate the festival to Jehovah your God
“in the place that Jehovah chooses,
“for Jehovah your God will bless all your produce and all that you do,
and you will become nothing but joyful.”
Now, did you notice Jehovah’s words there?
“You will become nothing but joyful.”
You see, being joyful as a worshipper of Jehovah
was not an option.
He actually made it an act of worship.
But why?
It’s because imperfect humans can lose their appreciation
for things that become a routine part of life,
even if these things are a reflection of Jehovah’s loving concern.
So, what was it about these festivals that would cause all who attended them
to “become nothing but joyful”?
Well, each festival was to be a time
when the Israelites stopped what they were doing.
In other words, they would pause,
and they would go up to Jerusalem
to reflect on the blessings that they had received from Jehovah
and that they were receiving.
In other words, they would reset.
What effect did this pause and reset have on the Israelites?
One word —gratitude.
You know what happens when we feel gratitude?
Happiness always follows.
You remember Jehovah’s words:
“You will become nothing but joyful,”
and Jehovah knows that happiness is a by-product of gratitude.
Now, how does this ancient example help us today?
Well, life in this old system is filled with hardships.
Ahead of you will be challenges, uncertainties,
“time and unforeseen occurrence.”
And really, that’s true for all of us.
Jehovah knows this,
but he also knows that it is precisely during times of crisis
that we have the most to gain
by having a grateful perspective.
Gratitude reminds us that our Creator loves us and that he cares about us.
It reminds us that God’s goodness exists
even in the worst that life has to offer.
Gratitude doesn’t cure suffering, but it has the power to heal.
Gratitude doesn’t erase despair,
but it has the power to radiate hope.
Gratitude nullifies negativity.
“The joy of Jehovah [becomes our] stronghold.”
But it’s up to us.
Because gratitude is more than just a feeling,
brothers and sisters;
it’s a mind-set, it’s a disposition,
and it’s a choice.
Why do we say a choice?
It’s because we can make a conscious decision
to see blessings instead of curses.
Jehovah is called “the happy God,”
and he gives us the recipe to be happy too.
That recipe is found, in part,
in Psalm 143.
Let’s turn there,
Psalm 143:5.
David, the psalmist, said this;
he said: “I remember the days of old;
“I meditate on all your activity;
I eagerly ponder over the works of your hands.”
What’s the point?
The psalmist is basically telling us
that from time to time
we have to stop and press the pause button.
We need to take time to look around.
Jehovah has bejeweled our world with daily reminders
of his goodness, his power, but most of all, his love for us.
All we have to do is take the time to look.
We are immersed in the goodness of God,
so pause from time to time.
Take a moment to appreciate what God is giving you each day.
Contemplate the abundance
and the diversity of life.
Ponder, muse, meditate
on all the works of the true God.
Drink in the awesomeness of the universe
on a starry night.
No two sunrises and no two sunsets
are ever exactly alike.
Look up to the clouds.
What you see is ever changing.
There was nothing exactly like it before, nor will there ever be again.
The feeling you will experience is a refreshment of the soul;
it’s a reset.
Eyes see only light, and ears hear only sound;
but a grateful heart perceives meaning.
We perceive that Jehovah created all these things
as a gift for us.
That’s right; each day was to be a very special gift,
unique unto itself.
Why?
To make endless life not just special
but amazing, wondrous, and always a joy.
Connecting with Jehovah’s creation
helps to discharge anxiety.
It shifts our attention
to something safe, something enduring,
something outside ourselves.
It helps us to accept life’s uncertainties
by reassuring us that we are a part of something larger,
something everlasting,
something immensely important.
Yes, we are a part of God’s purpose.
Gratitude is important
not only because it helps us feel good
but because it inspires us to do good.
A grateful spirit will make you more loving,
more forgiving, more feeling, more thoughtful.
Thankfulness is a soil in which joy thrives.
So open your hearts to the blessings around you.
Let gratefulness flow from the inside out to others.
You too “will become nothing but joyful,”
and that joy will show in your smile,
in your eyes, in your touch,
and in your words.
Why?
Because gratitude
is the ability to experience life,
not as a test, but as a gift.
It will impact every relationship
that you have —your family,
your marriage, your work,
even your ministry.
You’ll be in a much better position to make
a real difference in the lives of others.
It will liberate you from the prison of self-preoccupation,
and it will replace a critical spirit with a sense of appreciation.
So pause regularly
to reflect on what Jehovah has given you.
Give the digital world a break.
Take a walk outside, and don’t just look
—pause and perceive.
Try to count all the blessings that you receive each day,
and you will find it easier to cope with the trials and the stresses of life.
We are never more than one grateful thought away
from increased peace of mind and greater peace of heart.
Just remember, pause and reflect.

Legacy.
The word carries the thought
of passing on something of value
to those that come after you.

So if no one knows about you,
how can you pass on anything of value to them?
Can you influence others
if your work is behind the scenes?
Yes.
The Kenites did.
They’re not included in the “cloud of witnesses”
in Hebrews chapter 11.
Yet the value of their faith,
what they’ve passed on to you,
is worth meditating on.
They never enjoyed the spotlight.
Yet, in Jehovah’s eyes,
they are so precious and unforgettable.
Let’s do some digging
and unearth the legacy of the Kenites.
And we want you to learn valuable lessons,
especially lessons that will help you
search your hearts and motives.
The first Kenite mentioned in the Bible
is Jethro, Moses’ father-in-law.
When hearing that Jehovah freed the Israelites from Egypt,
notice what Jethro said here
—his response— at Exodus 18:11.
Jethro says: “Now I know
“that Jehovah is greater than all the other gods,
“because of what he did
to those who acted arrogantly against his people.”
These are Jethro’s words.
And now in verse 12, what he did was offer up sacrifices
to Jehovah God.
You see —this Jethro, this Kenite—
he recognized that Jehovah God
was directing the nation of Israel,
and he recognized that he was to help Moses.
Jehovah God was using Moses.
Moses had been given this exhausting job
of directing some three million people.
So Jethro said, ‘How can I assist?’
He wanted to support Moses —support.
So he assisted Moses to reach a God-approved solution.
‘Select capable, trustworthy men, Moses,
‘and appoint them as chiefs
over hundreds and fifties and tens’ and so forth.
Them, not me —them.
You see, Jethro was not looking for a position for himself.
He simply gave advice to be of support to Moses.
Why?
So that Moses could continue to do Jehovah God’s work.
He wanted to be involved in helping.
He saw Jehovah’s blessing on Moses.
He didn’t criticize.
Jethro didn’t sit back and say: ‘You’re not even a fluent speaker.

He didn’t do that.
He said, ‘I want to assist.’
So the support of this Kenite proved to be invaluable

So this is your first big lesson.
Like Jethro, look for ways to support

Don’t look for position.
Positions come and go,

That’s what Jehovah is looking for.
He loves your faithful service, not position.

Help your brother succeed at their work.
Let them take the credit.
Drain the venom of position and human recognition from your mind.
Jesus said,

So prove to yourself and prove to Jehovah God
that you are more for the Kingdom than for the glory.

to travel toward the Promised Land,

Now, at this Moses says to Hobab, in verse 31:
“Please do not leave us,
“for you know where we should camp in the wilderness,

As the footnote says, our “eyes.”
You see, Moses wanted Hobab to come.
Why? He was familiar with the terrain;
he knew where to find water; he knew where to find pasturage.
Hobab saw the big picture.
Hobab, come with us; serve as our “eyes.”
Use your knowledge;
use your experience
as a scout for the nation.
We need your experience.
Hobab could have stayed home.
Why go?
‘I have a family; I have my friends; I have a comfortable life.
‘Why should I throw my lot in with some three million people?
I have no idea what’s going to happen to you.’
But he went.
Hobab, with no apparent reward for himself,
used his experience to guide the nation
as they traveled toward the Promised Land.
Now, what does this mean for you?
It means something big.
During the past five months, you have become familiar
with this spiritual terrain
of the 66 books of the Bible.
You’ve been given the big picture.
You got it from Genesis to Revelation
—history lessons, geography lessons, archaeology lessons,
lesson after lesson, day after day,
written review after written review.
You got it.
Use your experience now.
Use that knowledge —to do what?
To serve as a guide for others.
For example,
when someone faces a crisis of faith,
they might find it difficult to travel this unfamiliar terrain.
It could be challenging for them.
Show them from God’s Word where they can find spiritual water.
Where can they get refreshment? Where can they get the energy?
Help them travel that terrain.
You owe it to them.
You have been given a beautiful view, while being here at school,
of the organization
—a unique vista of God’s organization that many will never see.
You will go back to your assignments, and many will never experience
what you’ve been able to experience.
Share with them your memories, your experience.
Strengthen their confidence in Jehovah God’s organization.
Don’t be stingy by holding your knowledge hostage.
Train two to become better than you.
Then, they train two,
and then they train two,
and they train two.
Imagine, if you adopt and embrace
this healthy mind-set,
you will help forge a path
toward a strong and unified organization.
That’s your responsibility.
So now we have two —two generations of Kenites
who loyally supported Jehovah God and his people.
A legacy had begun.
Would it continue?
Well, let’s jump ahead to the time of the kings.
We have 1 Chronicles 2:55
that identifies another Kenite named Rechab,
and his son was Jehonadab.
Jehonadab lived during the time period of King Jehu,
when Jehovah God commissioned Jehu to go wipe out Baal worship.
And then Jehonadab comes out.
He meets Jehu.
Imagine, he wants to meet him; he wants to support Jehu.
At 2 Kings 10:15, what did Jehu say?
‘Jehonadab, is your heart with me?’
‘It is, my heart is with you.’
‘Then get up into this chariot.’
He pulled him up in.
Wonderful!
Jehonadab wanted to support [Jehu].
It was a privilege for Jehonadab to come out publicly
and show his loyalty for Jehu’s God-given commission
—a privilege.
I’m going to be with you.
When Jehonadab accepted Jehu’s hand,
imagine, he stepped into that chariot.
He didn’t get underneath.
He stood up.
He was proud to be a part of that process.
He in effect was saying:
“Jehu, I’m sticking with you.
“I’ll do whatever you need.
“It doesn’t matter what the job is.
I’m with you.”
Like Jehonadab, be determined to accept the privilege
of loyally supporting the decisions
made by God’s visible organization.
Support those decisions today, tomorrow,
next week, next month, next year.
Who knows?
But you’re going to be a part of this, and it’s big.
You know, from a human standpoint the Kenites had no royal lineage,
no notable accomplishments, no home.
There’s no country of Kenite.
They’re easy to miss and overlook.
Unsung as a people
but not unseen by Jehovah.
Jehovah saw these faithful Kenites and all they had done for his people,
and he never forgot them.
Jehovah didn’t forget them; he loved them.
How do we know?
Well, again, 1 Chronicles 2:55 says
that they are part of the genealogy of Judah.
They’re tacked on at the end.
Jehovah said, ‘Welcome to the family.’
Beautiful!
First Samuel 15:6 shows that Jehovah protected them
when Saul was going against the Amalekites.
And the Kenites, get out of the way.
Because of your loyal love,
move out of the way so that you don’t get hurt.
And he rewarded them.
In Jeremiah’s day, he concluded a covenant
with Jehonadab’s descendants, the Rechabites,
because of their enduring loyalty for decades.
Jehovah declared at Jeremiah 35:19:
“There will never fail to be a descendant of Jehonadab
the son of Rechab [ever]
to serve in my presence.”
Jehovah respected the loyal endurance of these Rechabites.
He promised that they would survive
the destruction of Jerusalem in 607 B.C.E.
“There will never fail to be a descendant
. . . in my presence.”
Perhaps, just perhaps,
there were descendants of the Kenites in Jesus’ time
that later became his disciples and are in heaven right now.
Now, we can’t say for a certainty,
we don’t know.
But we would not be surprised.
This is a valuable lesson for you.
If you’re in a land where our work is restricted
or an area where few know the work you are doing,
you might feel alone without an army of support.
Be assured that Jehovah’s eyes
are on your enduring loyalty,
and he so deeply appreciates your faithfulness.
You see, like the Kenites,
your work —it might not be in the spotlight.
At times, you might feel overlooked, unacknowledged,
maybe unsung by humans.
But, again, never unseen by Jehovah.
And just as Jehovah did with the Kenites,
know that your heavenly Father
cherishes and treasures everything you do
and will never forget your faithful service.
The Kenites teach us what we need to do,
what you and I,
what we need to do to be approved by Jehovah.
It’s so precious.
What do we need to do?
Nothing spectacular, just be faithful.
It’s not about fanfare.
It’s silent resilience.
The legacy of the Kenites is now yours.
What will you do with it?
Be a Jethro.
Prove that you love the Kingdom and your brothers
more than your position.
Be a Hobab.
Use your experience to help your brothers find refreshment,
bolstering their spiritual energy to climb those difficult terrains.
And be a Jehonadab.
Show your loyal support
—your loyalty for Jehovah and his organization
by saying, “I’ll do whatever you need
for however long.”
The job doesn’t matter.
By imitating the Kenites,
their example will live on in you
and their unsung loyal support will remain unforgettable.
Well, we appreciate that wise counsel very much.
What a riveting and faith-strengthening program!
Before we conclude,
we’d like to share these greetings from Bulgaria.
Bulgaria is a beautiful mountainous country
in southeastern Europe.
Individual farms are still an important part of life.
Many people still vint their own wine,
can their own fruits and vegetables,
and chop their own firewood to prepare for the cold winters.
In late 1989, when the upheaval of Communism shook Bulgaria,
there were less than 50 publishers in the entire country.
In 1991, the first Gilead-trained missionaries
were assigned there.
Today, Bulgaria has some 2,500 publishers.
Let’s visit the congregation in Vratsa,
a town where houses are built right up to the steep mountain cliffs.
The dramatic rock formations, waterfalls, and caves
attract many tourists.
The Vratsa Congregation has 43 publishers,
of which 5 serve as elders.
The publishers conduct on average
80 Bible studies each month.
Witnesses from other European countries have moved there
to help in the ministry.
The congregation has 14 regular pioneers,
2 special pioneers, and 2 missionaries.
In the recent past, the brothers and sisters in Vratsa
could be issued a fine just for participating in the preaching work,
and some were harassed by the police.
But in October 2017, the congregation rejoiced when a local court
ruled that limiting our preaching work is unconstitutional.
We keep our brothers and sisters
in Bulgaria in our prayers.
We love them very much!
From the world headquarters of Jehovah’s Witnesses,
this is JW Broadcasting.

그리고 제가 갖고 있는 희망들을 좀 사람들에게 알리고 싶은 마음들이 많았는데,

마침 회중 내에서 아침 7시부터 9시까지 편의점 봉사 마련이 있게 되었고,
그곳에 가면은 사람들을 만나서 대화를 할 수 있지 않을까,
그런 생각들을 하게 되어 그런 봉사에 참여하게 되었습니다.
편의점 봉사 전날에 늦게까지 일정들을 잡지 않는다거나
편의점 봉사에 꾸준하게 참여하기 위한 노력들을 하였습니다.
저희가 집회에서 배우게 되는 제공 방법 동영상들을 많이 전날 연습하였고,
집주인들에게 직접 사용하였을 때 과거에는 성서를 펴 보기도 힘들었는데,
이제 나중에는 성서 연구를 진행하게 되는 결과까지 이어지게 되었습니다.
편의점에서 편의점으로, 구역에서 구역으로 이동 간에
형제 자매들과 모여서 봉사 기술들을 공유하고,
또 서로 격려받으면서 굉장히 힘을 얻게 되었습니다.
계속 꾸준히 편의점 봉사에 참여하게 되면서
재방문 건수나 연구 건수가 늘어나는 걸 보면서
제 스스로도 봉사자로서 성장하고 있구나, 이런 느낌을 갖게 되었습니다.
저는 가장으로서 가족을 부양해야 하기 때문에
주말에만 야외 봉사를 지지할 수 있는데 사람들을 만날 수가 없습니다.
왜냐하면 그들이 다 야외로 나가기 때문에,
그러다 보니까, 야외 봉사에 대한 열심이 사그라드는 것 같고,
특히 가족에게도 봉사에 대한 열심을 보여야 하는데,
사람을 만나지 못하는 그런 상황이다 보니까 그런 부면에서 도전이 되는 것 같습니다.
그래서 월요일 날과 화요일, 금요일 날, 보통 저녁 봉사를 정기적으로 하고 있습니다.
제가 일을 마치게 되면, 저녁 5시경쯤 되는데,
다시금 이렇게 옷을 입고 야외 봉사 하러 나간다는 것 자체는 힘이 많이 듭니다.
관심을 나타낸 젊은 사람과 성서 연구로 이어지는
그것을 지켜본 자녀들 역시 자신의 말로
반대를 하는 사람들에게도 담대하게 성서 진리를 알리는 것을 보면
아버지로서 그런 어떤 뿌듯한 느낌도 들고,
‘야외 봉사는 이렇게 하는 것이다’라는 거를 자녀들에게 가르칠 수 있게 되어
집주인들이 아침에 일을 나가서 저녁 늦게까지 하기 때문에
저희가 호별을 가도 집주인을 만나기가 어렵고
또 만난다고 해도 성서적인 의미 있는 대화를 한다든가
재방문, 연구로 이어 가는 것이 많이 도전이 되고 있습니다.
‘정말 의미 있는 봉사를 내가 했나?’ 이런 생각을 많이 하게 돼요.
네, 시골이다 보니까 인구도 많지 않고
또 집주인들이 주변 의식을 너무 많이 하더라고요.
저희가 방문하는 것을 꺼리는 그러한 경우가 있어서,
그래서 주변 시선을 많이 의식하는 분들은
편안하게 부담 없이 서로 대화를 할 수 있어서 너무 좋았고요.
그래서 어떻게 하면 그런 연구생을 정기적으로 연구를 할 수 있을까
그러면 ‘아침, 새벽 시간은 어떠세요?’ 하고 여쭤 보니까
그분들이 조금 시간이 있으면 아무 때고 전화를 하면
80대 초반의 할머니를 밤늦게 연구를 해서 도와 드린 분이 계시는데,
그분의 필요에 맞게 도와줘서 저녁 9시나 10시에 찾아가서 연구를 하니까,
좀 피곤하고, 배도 어떨 때는 고플 때도 있고,
그래도 이제 관심자들을 도와줬다는 만족감에 기쁨을 잃지 않고 있어요.
네, 지금 제가 이제 연구를 사회하고 있는 분들이 한 열두 분 정도 되는데요.
이렇게 여러 모양이 돼서 그들의 필요에 맞게 이렇게 이제 봉사를 하다 보면
‘아, 정말 이게 하느님께서 요구하는 그 봉사를 내가 지금 하고 있구나’라는
현재 구역에선 이미 구석구석 전파했다는 생각이 들지 몰라도,
어부들이 물고기를 잡으려고 시간대를 바꾸어 낚시하는 것처럼,
우리도 사람을 만날 만한 때에 봉사해야 합니다.
물고기가 잘 잡힐 때에 그물을 치는 거죠!
성서 연구생을 만나기 위해 밤 9시나 10시에 찾아갔습니다.
하지만 좋은 소식을 전하는 시간과 장소와 방법을 융통성 있게 조정함으로,
한국에 있는 형제 자매들처럼 좋은 결과를 거둘 수 있습니다.
그렇게 하면 “영원한 생명을 얻기에 합당한 성향”을 가진 사람들을 찾는
매우 중요한 이 일을 더욱 효과적으로 수행할 수 있게 됩니다.

en.text: Out of the over 100,000 publishers in South Korea,
there are more than 40,000 zealous regular pioneers.
What efforts have they made
to reach more people in frequently worked territory?
Let’s find out.
I started pioneering less than a year after I got baptized,
so I was eager to sharpen
my preaching skills.
I really wanted to share my hope with others.
But it’s so hard to meet people
at their homes during the day.
And even if we do meet them,
it’s not easy to start a conversation.
Our congregation organized convenience store witnessing
from 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m.,
so I thought this might be a good way to reach people
and have meaningful conversations.
But the thing is that I’m not a morning person,
so getting up early was not easy.
So I had to make some adjustments.
I tried not to make plans
or to stay up late the night before.
The sample presentations from our meetings were also very helpful.
In the past, I hardly got the chance to open the Bible while I was preaching,
but now I have a few Bible studies.
Even the time we spend traveling from one convenience store to the next
is very uplifting spiritually because we use that time
to share our preaching skills and build each other up.
Having a regular share in convenience store witnessing
has allowed me to be more productive in the ministry.
I feel like I’m progressing spiritually
and becoming a better minister of the good news.
On weekdays, I work to support my family.
So I would usually go out in field service
on the weekends.
But it wasn’t easy to find people at their homes
because they usually make plans and go out.
And you know,
it’s hard to get excited about the preaching work
when you’re not meeting many people.
I wanted to set a good example for my family,
but I found it a real challenge to maintain my zeal for the ministry.
So I began to regularly participate in evening witnessing
on Mondays, Tuesdays, and Fridays.
I usually get off work around 5:00 p.m.
After a long day at work,
it’s not always easy to get dressed
to go out in the field ministry.
But I kept up with my return visits
and had some really encouraging experiences.
A young man I had been visiting
accepted a Bible study, and he’s making fine progress.
My children are able to see how much joy I get from the ministry,
and so now they too are able to give a bold witness
in their own words, even in the face of opposition.
I am very proud of my children.
Training and teaching them how to make
effective return visits and Bible studies
brings me great joy.
We serve in a small rural town
where many leave home early in the morning to work in the field,
and they return late at night.
So it’s not easy
to find people at home during the daytime.
And even if we do find them at their doors,
it’s not easy to develop a meaningful Bible-based conversation,
let alone make return visits and conduct Bible studies with them.
After returning home from preaching at night,
I would ask myself,
‘Did I have a meaningful share in the ministry today?’
It’s a small rural town.
So many people are concerned about what their neighbors
would think if they talked with us.
So even those who were interested in learning more about the Bible
were reluctant to have Bible discussions with us.
It was really unfortunate.
We tried to figure out the right time to call on people,
and we found out that many householders are more relaxed
and willing to talk about the Bible
if we visit them around nine or ten o’clock in the evening.
I gave much thought on how I could help my Bible students
have a regular intake of spiritual food.
One of my students worked from 9 a.m. to 10 p.m.,
so I asked her if we could arrange
to study early in the morning.
She agreed.
I often tell my Bible students,
‘Just call me whenever you have a little time to talk.’
When I get those calls, no matter what time it is,
it’s time to rush out that door.
There was one elderly lady who was in her early 80’s
who had attended church all her life.
To accommodate her needs,
I visited her around nine or ten o’clock in the evening
for our Bible studies.
I would come home feeling tired and hungry,
but the satisfaction of knowing
that I’ve helped her learn more about the truth
enables me to maintain my joy.
Now I am able to conduct about 12 Bible studies.
I try to “become all things to people of all sorts”
in order to look after their needs.
And it brings me great satisfaction and joy
to see my studies make progress
because that’s really how Jehovah wants us
to be carrying out our ministry.
You might feel that you’ve worked every corner of your home territory.
But just like a literal fisherman adapts to the time when the fish are biting,
we need to work when people can be found.
Cast your nets into productive waters!
Our sister arranged her schedule to call on her Bible student
at nine or ten in the evening.
Of course, we want to use good judgment
to call at times that are both practical and safe for our territory.
But by being adaptable in when, where,
or how we preach the good news,
we may yield good results like those of our fellow Witnesses in South Korea.
This will help us to have a meaningful share in the all-important work
of finding those who are “rightly disposed for everlasting life.”

대회 가는 데 드는 돈을 벌기 위해서 비누를 더 많이 만들기로 했습니다.
우리 애들 세 명이 안타나나리보에서 침례받게 됐어요.
우리 생애에서 정말 특별한 이 행사에 갈 비용을 위해 가족이 함께 벽돌을 만들고 있죠.
세계 각지의 형제 자매들을 만날 날이 정말 기대됩니다.
그렇게 돈을 벌어 비용을 마련해서, 저도 대회에 참석할 거예요.
저는 이 보아피카 콩으로 가방을 만들어서 대회에 갈 돈을 법니다.
제가 키우는 돼지인데, 팔아서 대회에 갈 거예요.
참석자들이 멀리 아홉 개 나라에서 마다가스카르까지 올 겁니다.
이곳 남아프리카 공화국의 목걸이와 팔찌를 가져가서 마다가스카르 형제 자매들에게 드릴 거예요.
도착하자마자 형제들의 따뜻한 사랑을 느낄 수 있었어요.
또 춤추는 것도 보고 맛있는 음식도 먹고요.
이곳 형제 자매들은 다 하나같이 활짝 웃고 있더라고요.
전혀 훼손되지 않은 지역에서 여호와의 창조물을 볼 수 있고,
이곳 마다가스카르에만 있는 동물과 식물을 볼 수 있다는 건 정말 큰 축복이죠.
큰 섬인 마다가스카르 내에서도 대부분 먼 여행을 합니다.
어떤 분들은 여러 날 동안 걸어서 옵니다.
많은 분들은 이곳 안타나나리보까지 오기 위해 며칠 동안 버스 여행을 하죠.
다들 마다가스카르에서 열리는 특별 지역 대회에 꼭 참석하겠다는 한 가지 마음뿐입니다.
오늘 이곳에서 우리 아이들 셋이 침례를 받았어요.
우리 회중 사람들은 3일 동안 걸었고, 그다음 버스를 탔어요.
포기하지 않았기 때문에 안타나나리보까지 무사히 도착했죠.
다들 제가 처음 보는 사람들이지만, 모두 다 여호와의 백성이니까 친해질 수 있어요.
스타디움에 이렇게 많은 사람이 모인 건 처음 봐요.
수많은 사람이 여호와께 노래하는 놀라운 장면을 보고, 이런 생각이 들었죠.
‘와! 낙원에 미리 와 있는 것 같네!’
저는 47년 동안 여호와의 백성과 연합해 왔습니다.
이렇게 큰 무리가 여호와 덕분에 많은 유익을 얻고 있는 모습을 보니 힘이 납니다.
특별 지역 대회에 온 건 처음인데, 모든 게 기대하던 것보다 훨씬 좋아요!
여호와께서 다음엔 어떤 놀라운 걸 보여 주실지 정말 궁금해요.

en.text: When we heard that there would be a special convention in Madagascar,
we were very happy.
We said, “We have to get there!”
We decided to increase
the amount of soap we make so that we could pay
for the travel to the convention.
We have three children
who are going to be baptized
in Antananarivo.
As a family, we have worked together to make bricks
so that we can pay the fare for this special event in our life.
We are looking forward to meeting
brothers and sisters from around the world.
I make earrings, and I sell them.
I will use the money to attend the convention.
I am very happy.
I make bags made with these voapika beans
to get some money to attend the convention.
This is my pig.
I will sell it so that I can attend the convention.
I am raising chickens.
I am doing laundry.
Visiting delegates are traveling far
—from nine countries— to come to Madagascar.
We are taking with us necklaces and bracelets from South Africa
to give to the brothers and sisters in Madagascar.
From the very moment that we showed up,
you could just feel the love from all of the friends.
“Welcome, welcome, welcome!” was the message we kept getting.
We really enjoyed the tour of the branch.
They also had dancing and wonderful food.
One theme that I saw with all of the local friends here
was that they were all smiling from ear to ear.
A lot of energy too
—great, happy energy!
The ministry was incredible.
We had the friends there right by our side to help us along.
Just seeing Jehovah’s creation
in an area where it’s been untouched
and getting to see some
of the plants and animals that you can’t see anywhere else in the world
is truly a nice blessing.
Even on our large island,
many people have far to travel.
Some walk on foot for several days.
Many take a bus journey of a few days to arrive here in Antananarivo.
But everyone is eager to be
at the special convention in Madagascar.
Now, when I think about my three children
who got baptized today,
I feel my heart is full of joy,
and I really thank Jehovah!
We walked for three days with our congregation,
and then we took a bus.
We arrived safely in Antananarivo because we did not give up.
We are so happy to be here!
Even though I do not know all these people from before,
they are Jehovah’s people and I can get to know them.
I’ve never been in a stadium with so many people.
Just to see that many people singing to Jehovah
was quite an experience, and it made me think:
‘Wow! This is like a taste of Paradise!’
I have been in the organization for 47 years now.
This is something that really makes me happy,
and it encourages me to see such a great crowd,
which is benefiting greatly from Jehovah himself.
This is our very first special convention,
and everything has exceeded all of my expectations!
It makes me think:
‘Wow! What does Jehovah have in store next?’

cn.text: 听到将会在马达加斯加
举行特别区域大会时
我们特别高兴
我们下定决心一定要去!
我们决定多做一些肥皂来卖
好凑足路费去参加大会
我们的三个孩子
打算在首都塔那那利佛的大会受浸
这是我们人生中非常重要的时刻
为了存钱参加这次大会
我们全家人一起做搬砖的工作
我们非常期待见到
世界各地的弟兄姐妹
我自己做耳环
然后拿去卖
我用卖耳环赚来的钱
去参加这次大会
我真的很高兴
我用这些豆子来制作手提包
然后再把赚来的钱用来参加大会
这是我养的猪
卖了它我就能参加大会了
我养鸡
我给别人洗衣服
大会代表来自9个国家
他们长途跋涉来到马达加斯加参加大会
我们会带一些南非的项链和手镯
送给来马达加斯加参加大会的弟兄姐妹们
我们一到机场
就感受到弟兄姐妹们温暖的爱心
欢迎大家的标语牌随处可见
去分部参观也特别开心
他们准备了精彩的舞蹈还有各种美食
我发现这里的弟兄姐妹有个共同点
就是每个人的脸上
都一直绽放着笑容
他们真的充满活力非常快乐!
在那里传道简直太棒了!
本地的弟兄姐妹陪我们一起传道
给我们很多帮助
这里的自然环境保护得很好
有很多稀有的动植物
是在世界其他地方无法看到的
看到耶和华这些美丽的杰作
真是我们的福分

就算生活在这里
为了参加大会也要走很远的路
有的人要走上几天才能到
还有很多人要坐好几天的长途汽车
才能到塔那那利佛
不过  每个人都非常渴望参加
在马达加斯加举行的大会

感谢耶和华!
我们和会众的弟兄姐妹走了三天的路程

特别是大家一起唱歌赞美耶和华

ko.text: 우리가 쉽지 않은 임무를 받은 경우,
여호와를 의지하는 것만큼 중요한 것도 없을 것입니다.
어떻게 그러한 신뢰심을 나타낼 수 있을까요?
제 친구이기도 한 셰인 브래디 형제를 소개해 드리고 싶은데요,
아내 아이올랜다 자매와 함께 현재 핀란드 지부에서 봉사하고 있습니다.
브래디 형제와 전 캐나다 지부에서 함께 일했었습니다.
브래디 형제는 지난 22년간 여러 나라의 형제들을 법적으로 변호하는 일을 해 왔는데,
세계 여러 나라에서 이런 임무를 맡아 수행하면서 겪는 어려움 중엔 어떤 것들이 있나요?
또, 때로는 반대자들의 적개심을 직접 경험하기도 했습니다.
그런 어려움에 직면하면서도 형제 부부는 늘 기꺼이 임무를 수행해 오셨는데,
여러 나라에서 일하시면서 어떤 상황에 직면했는지
우리가 좀 알 수 있도록 소개해 주실 수 있는 경험담이 있을까요?
네, 많은 경험들이 있었는데요, 한 가지가 떠오르네요.
몇 달 전에, 한 특별 파이오니아 형제가 소송을 당한 적이 있었습니다.
부정적인 판결이 나면 그 나라의 우리 활동에 심각한 영향을 줄 수 있었죠.
그래서 우리는 최선을 다해 강력히 변호했지만,
심리가 진행되면서 상황이 그다지 좋아 보이지 않았습니다.
그런데 심리 마지막 날, 완전히 바뀌었죠.
우린 형제에 대한 소송건을 종결해 달라고 판사에게 요청했습니다.
전 효과가 있을 거라 생각지 않았어요.
하지만 저희와 오래 일한 한 형제는
‘여호와께 축복하실 기회를 드려야 한다’고 늘 말했고, 우린 그렇게 했죠.
우리가 요청을 하자 판사는 검사를 보며 어떻게 생각하냐고 물었죠.
검사는 판사에게 이 소송을 제기한 정부 관리를 처벌해야 한다고 말했습니다.
법정을 나오면서 전 다른 형제들을 둘러봤고 우린 하나같이 말했습니다.
시간이 있으면 다 듣고 싶지만, 하나만 더 들려주실 수 있을까요?
우리의 활동이 인가되지 않은 한 나라에서,
기념식 날 밤에 여러 형제들이 소위 “불법 종교 활동”을 했다는 이유로 체포됐습니다.
모두 유죄 판결을 받았고, 그래서 소송건별로 상소했죠.
각자 다른 상소 법원 판사 앞에서 심리를 받았습니다.
시작한 지 얼마 안 돼서, 판사는 진행을 중단시키고,
성경과 여호와의 증인의 신앙에 대해 많은 질문을 하기 시작했습니다.
그래서 한동안 성경 질문들에 대답해 주고 나서야, 심리가 계속됐죠.
몇 분 후 판사는 또다시 멈추게 하더니,
“여호와의 증인이 이 지역에서 어려움을 겪는 게 바로 그 이유 때문인가요?”
심리가 몇 분간 계속되는가 싶더니 판사가 또 물었죠.
“예수께서 한 말인진 잘 모르겠지만 성경에 이런 말이 있지 않나요?
‘두세 사람이 내 이름으로 모인 곳에는 나도 그들 가운데 있습니다.’”
판사는 형제 자매들로 가득 찬 낡은 법정을 바라보며 말했습니다.
“그럼 오늘 여기 예수께서 계신 게 틀림없네요.”
그 판사는 우리의 손을 들어 주며 형제에게 무죄를 선고했고,
다른 판사들도 다 형제들의 무죄를 선고했습니다.
세계 여러 지역에서 이처럼 힘든 임무들을 받아들이고 수행해 오면서
형제 부부가 어떤 유익을 얻었는지 말씀해 주시겠습니까?
네, 정말 여러 면으로 유익을 얻었습니다.
그리고 전 세계 형제 자매들의 놀라운 사랑도 직접 경험할 수 있었는데요,
경찰이 회중 집회 중에 들이닥친 적이 있었습니다.
형제들을 심하게 구타하고 자매들을 협박했는데 끔찍했습니다!
몇 주 후 경찰은 형제들을 상대로 소송을 벌였는데,
이 소송 사건 중에 경찰은 계속해서 저와 동료 형제를 체포하려고 했습니다.
법원에 있을 때도 우릴 구금하고 체포하려 했죠.
그런 내내 아내는 상황을 지켜보고 있었습니다.
불과 몇 주 전에 바로 그 경찰관들의 손에 잔인한 취급을 받았던 우리 형제 자매들이
어려운 상황이 끝날 때까지 우리 곁을 떠나지 않았죠.
네, 정말 저희 부부는 여러 면으로 유익을 얻었고,
이 멋진 임무를 받아들인 걸 한순간도 후회한 적이 없습니다.
저희도 계속 함께 일할 수 있길 바랍니다.

en.text: When we’re faced with challenging assignments,
reliance on Jehovah is of utmost importance.
In what ways can we show that reliance?
I have the pleasure of introducing you to a friend of mine,
Shane Brady, who is presently serving along with his wife, Iolanda,
at the branch in Finland.
Brother Shane Brady and I previously worked together
at the Canada branch.
Shane has been involved in legally defending our brothers
for the past 22 years in many countries,
including Armenia, Kazakhstan, and Kyrgyzstan.
Shane, it’s good to see you. How are you doing?
I’m doing very well. It’s great to see you too, Mark.
Shane, we want to ask you,
What have been some of the challenges
that you’ve faced in accepting these assignments
in various countries in the world?
Well, there certainly have been a few challenges.
One is frequent travel.
Another is language;
each country that we assist has its own language.
Some court cases are very stressful,
and at times, we’ve faced firsthand
the hatred of our opposers.
Yes. And you know, Shane, in spite of all that,
you and your wife have always been willing to go on these assignments.
We appreciate your spirit so much.
Is there an experience that you can share with us
that would give us a taste of the kinds of situations
that you’ve had to deal with in these countries?
Well, there have been many experiences.
But one experience comes to mind.
A few months ago, there was a special pioneer,
and a case was started against him.
And if the decision was negative, it could have had very serious consequences
for our work in that country.
So we did our best to present a strong defense.
But as the trial progressed,
things didn’t seem to be going so well.
But on the last day of the trial, everything changed.
We presented a motion,
and we asked the judge to terminate the case against the brother.
Personally, I didn’t think it would actually work.
But one older brother who we’ve worked with
over the years always told us,
“We need to give Jehovah something to bless.”
And so we did, and the results were quite unexpected.
When we made the motion, the judge turned to the prosecutor and asked,
“Well, what’s your opinion?”
And to our surprise, the prosecutor agreed with our request,
and he even went beyond what we asked.
He said to the judge that the government official
that started the case against our brother should be punished.
Well, the judge agreed; the case was terminated.
When we were walking out of the courtroom,
I looked at the other brothers with me and we all said the same thing,
“What happened?”
It was obvious —Jehovah had intervened.
That’s wonderful, Shane.
I wish we had more time to hear many more experiences.
But could you just share at least one more with us?
Sure.
In another land where our work is not recognized,
on the night of the Memorial, a number of the brothers were arrested
for so-called illegal religious activity.
They were all convicted at trial.
So arrangements were made to appeal each of those cases,
and they were heard before a different appeal court judge.
What at first seemed quite negative, the loss at trial,
turned out to be an amazing result.
Let me give you just one example.
In one of the appeals, as we were presenting the appeal,
not long into the case, the appeal court judge stopped us,
and he began to ask us many questions about the Bible
and about what Jehovah’s Witnesses believe.
So for quite some time, we answered these Biblical questions,
and then the case continued.
And then after some minutes, the judge stopped us again.
And this time the judge said, “I remember reading in the Bible”—
The judge said this, “I remember reading in the Bible
“that Jesus said: ‘If they have persecuted me,
they will persecute you also.’”
So we said to the judge: “Yes, indeed. Jesus said that.”
The judge asked, “Do you think that’s the reason why
Jehovah’s Witnesses are having problems in this region?”
Well, what could we say but agree with the judge.
But that wasn’t the end of it.
As the case continued a few minutes more, the judge stopped us again.
And this time the judge said: “You know, I’m not sure if Jesus said this.
“It’s in the Bible where he said:
“‘Where there are two or three gathered together,
there I am in your midst.’”
And we assured the judge, “Indeed, those are Jesus’ words.”
The judge looked out at this old courtroom,
which was filled with our brothers and sisters, and he said,
“Well, Jesus must be in our midst today.”
We felt like breaking into applause.
At the end of the court hearing,
the judge ruled in our favor and acquitted the brother,
and the judges in all of the other cases also acquitted our brothers.
It was just a thrilling experience!
Oh, that’s wonderful; that’s wonderful, Shane.
Thank you so much for sharing those experiences.
You know, despite the challenges that you’ve had to face,
how do you feel about the way you and Iolanda have benefited
from being involved in accepting these challenging assignments
in various parts of the world?
Well, we have benefited in so many ways, Mark.
Our relationship with Jehovah has deepened.
Certainly, our trust in Jehovah
has been strengthened.
And we’ve experienced firsthand the love
of the amazing worldwide brotherhood.
Could I just share one experience about that?
Please, please do.
Two years ago, we were involved in a case
where police had raided a congregation meeting in one country.
They had brutally beaten the brothers and threatened the sisters.
It was just terrible!
Some weeks later in the court case
that started against the brothers
(that the police brought against the brothers),
during that court case, the police repeatedly tried
to arrest me and another brother I was working with.
Over two days they were trying to arrest us.
Even in the courthouse, they tried to detain and arrest us.
And all through this, my wife, Iolanda, was watching what was happening.
But do you know what was so remarkable?
It was that despite the brutal treatment
our brothers and sisters had endured just a few weeks earlier
at the hands of these very same police officers,
those dear brothers and sisters came to our aid.
They were like a wall of protection around us,
and they would not leave our side until the ordeal was done.
It was love in action.
So to answer your question, we have benefited in so many ways.
We don’t regret for a moment accepting this thrilling assignment.
Well, thank you so much, Shane.
Please give our love to Iolanda as well.
We appreciate the tremendous work that you’re accomplishing,
and may Jehovah’s spirit continue to be with you.
It’s our privilege.
We look forward to continuing to work with you, Mark.

ko.text: ‎수혈을 적게 하는 쪽으로 확연하게 바뀌고 있죠.
‎수혈을 적게 할수록 치료 결과가 더 좋다는 증거가
‎아주 복잡한 수술을 필요로 하는 환자가 있습니다.
‎정말 최선을 다해서 수혈 없이 수술을 마치죠.
‎근데 나중에 보니까 야간 당직 근무를 보던
‎마취과 의사가 환자에게 혈액 두 팩을 수혈한 겁니다.
‎피가 많이 부족한 것 같아서 그냥 혈액 두 팩을 수혈했다고 하면서요.
‎수혈을 더 많이 하는 경향이 있는 것 같습니다.
‎어린이들의 신체는 믿기 어려울 만큼 치유 능력이 아주 뛰어나죠.
‎헤모글로빈 수치가 낮아도 별문제 없이 견뎌 낼 수 있어요.

cn.text: 医学界对输血的看法有很大的改变
很明显地
现在趋势是倾向于尽可能不要输血
不只是对耶和华见证人
对其他患者也是这样
因为有越来越多的证据显示
不输血通常会带来更好的结果
我们需要教育大家
我想这样的研讨会或访谈
可以让更多人知道不输血有什么益处
输血不是绝对必要的
如果可能，最好不要输血
有时候，医护人员会遇到一种情况
医师花了很大的工夫避免输血
成功地为病人动了复杂的手术
后来发现值班的麻醉科医师
竟然给他输了两袋血
原因居然是
因为病人看起来有点脱水
所以就给他输了
这种情况真的不应该发生
所有的医护人员都需要被教育
可惜的是
我发现医师越是缺乏专业知识
随便输血的情况就越常见
所有的相关技术都可以用在儿童身上
说实在的，儿童的复原能力真的非常惊人
他们就算血红蛋白很低
也还能承受得住
而且，他们复原的速度也比大人快很多
所以，不输血疗法在他们身上是完全可行的
这是肯定的
耶和华见证人跟其他病人一样珍惜生命
也想要好好活下去
他们只是选择不接受输血
我们应该要尊重他们
